`crates/orress-academy/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! The ORRESS Academy: step-by-step lessons that check what you do in the app,
//! practice crackmes, and a CPU simulator.
//!
//! The app feeds [`Event`]s (commands run, views opened, files opened) and a
//! [`PollState`] (what is true right now) into the [`Academy`]; the academy decides
//! when the current step is done, awards XP and badges, and tells the UI what to
//! spotlight.

pub mod crackmes;
pub mod glossary;
pub mod lesson;
pub mod numbers;
pub mod progress;
pub mod sim;
mod ui;

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

pub use glossary::Term;
pub use lesson::{Check, LEVELS, Lesson, Step};
pub use progress::Progress;
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
pub use ui::{lesson_panel, overview, simulator, spotlight_overlay};

/// Something the user did, reported by the app.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Event {
    /// A command (action id) ran, e.g. `command_palette::Toggle`.
    Action(String),
    /// A view of a file got focus, e.g. "Strings".
    ViewFocused(String),
    /// A file was opened.
    FileOpened(PathBuf),
}

/// Facts about the app that some checks look at every frame.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct PollState {
    /// Name of the focused file view, e.g. "Strings".
    pub focused_view: Option<String>,
    pub cursor_in_main: bool,
    pub renamed: bool,
    pub commented: bool,
}

/// Things the academy asks the app to do.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Request {
    OpenFile(PathBuf),
    OpenSimulator,
    OpenLesson,
    /// Show the Academy tab, on the glossary.
    OpenGlossary,
    Message(String),
}

/// Feedback on an answer.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Feedback {
    pub correct: bool,
    pub text: String,
}

pub struct SimState {
    pub source: String,
    pub cpu: Option<sim::Cpu>,
    pub error: Option<sim::ParseError>,
}

impl Default for SimState {
    fn default() -> Self {
        let source =
            "; Type assembly here, then press Run or Step.\nmov rax, 5\nadd rax, 10\n".to_owned();
        let mut s = Self {
            source,
            cpu: None,
            error: None,
        };
        s.reset();
        s
    }
}

impl SimState {
    pub fn reset(&mut self) {
        match sim::Cpu::new(&self.source) {
            Ok(cpu) => {
                self.cpu = Some(cpu);
                self.error = None;
            }
            Err(e) => {
                self.cpu = None;
                self.error = Some(e);
            }
        }
    }

    pub fn load(&mut self, source: &str) {
        source.clone_into(&mut self.source);
        self.reset();
    }
}

/// Which page the Academy tab shows.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Page {
    #[default]
    Lessons,
    Glossary,
}

pub struct Academy {
    pub lessons: Vec<Lesson>,
    pub glossary: Vec<Term>,
    /// Glossary terms mentioned in the current step (indices into `glossary`).
    pub step_terms: Vec<usize>,
    pub page: Page,
    /// Search text on the glossary page.
    pub glossary_filter: String,
    /// Term to scroll to and open on the glossary page.
    pub glossary_focus: Option<usize>,
    pub progress: Progress,
    progress_file: Option<PathBuf>,
    crackme_dir: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// Active lesson index and step index.
    pub active: Option<(usize, usize)>,
    /// Hints revealed for the current step.
    pub hints_shown: usize,
    pub answer: String,
    pub feedback: Option<Feedback>,
    pub sim: SimState,
    /// Number typed into the number converter widget.
    pub converter: String,
    requests: Vec<Request>,
    opened: Vec<PathBuf>,
    /// Lesson completed just now (for a celebration message).
    pub celebrate: Option<String>,
    markdown: egui_commonmark::CommonMarkCache,
}

impl Academy {
    /// `config_dir`: where progress (`academy.json`) and extracted crackmes go.
    pub fn new(config_dir: Option<&Path>) -> Self {
        let progress_file = config_dir.map(|d| d.join("academy.json"));
        let progress = progress_file
            .as_deref()
            .map(Progress::load)
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let lessons = lesson::catalog();
        let active = progress
            .current
            .as_ref()
            .and_then(|id| lessons.iter().position(|l| &l.id == id))
            .map(|i| (i, first_open_step(&progress, &lessons[i])));
        let mut academy = Self {
            lessons,
            glossary: glossary::catalog(),
            step_terms: Vec::new(),
            page: Page::default(),
            glossary_filter: String::new(),
            glossary_focus: None,
            progress,
            progress_file,
            crackme_dir: config_dir.map(|d| d.join("academy").join("crackmes")),
            active,
            hints_shown: 0,
            answer: String::new(),
            feedback: None,
            sim: SimState::default(),
            converter: "42".into(),
            requests: Vec::new(),
            opened: Vec::new(),
            celebrate: None,
            markdown: egui_commonmark::CommonMarkCache::default(),
        };
        // Restore the current step (e.g. its simulator starting code) after a restart.
        academy.enter_step();
        academy
    }

    pub fn take_requests(&mut self) -> Vec<Request> {
        std::mem::take(&mut self.requests)
    }

    fn save(&mut self) {
        if let Some(file) = &self.progress_file
            && let Err(e) = self.progress.save(file)
        {
            self.requests.push(Request::Message(format!(
                "Could not save Academy progress: {e}"
            )));
        }
    }

    /// The lesson to continue with: the active one, or the first unfinished one.
    pub fn next_lesson(&self) -> Option<usize> {
        self.active.map(|(l, _)| l).or_else(|| {
            self.lessons
                .iter()
                .position(|l| !self.progress.lessons.contains(&l.id))
        })
    }

    pub fn start(&mut self, lesson: usize) {
        let Some(l) = self.lessons.get(lesson) else {
            return;
        };
        let step = first_open_step(&self.progress, l);
        self.progress.current = Some(l.id.clone());
        self.active = Some((lesson, step));
        self.enter_step();
        self.save();
        self.requests.push(Request::OpenLesson);
    }

    pub fn current(&self) -> Option<(&Lesson, usize, &Step)> {
        let (l, s) = self.active?;
        let lesson = self.lessons.get(l)?;
        Some((lesson, s, lesson.steps.get(s)?))
    }

    pub fn current_done(&self) -> bool {
        self.current()
            .is_some_and(|(l, s, _)| self.progress.step_done(&l.id, s))
    }

    /// UI element to highlight for the current step, while it is not done.
    pub fn spotlight(&self) -> Option<&str> {
        let (_, _, step) = self.current()?;
        (!self.current_done())
            .then_some(step.spotlight.as_deref())
            .flatten()
    }

    fn enter_step(&mut self) {
        self.hints_shown = 0;
        self.answer.clear();
        self.feedback = None;
        self.step_terms.clear();
        let Some((_, _, step)) = self.current() else {
            return;
        };
        let mut text = format!("{}\n{}", step.title, step.text);
        for line in step.instructions.iter().chain(&step.goal) {
            text.push('\n');
            text.push_str(line);
        }
        if let Check::Choice { options, .. } = &step.check {
            text.push('\n');
            text.push_str(&options.join("\n"));
        }
        let code = step.sim_code.clone();
        self.step_terms = glossary::mentioned(&self.glossary, &text);
        if let Some(code) = code {
            self.sim.load(&code);
        }
    }

    /// Opens the glossary page of the Academy tab, at `term` if given.
    pub fn show_glossary(&mut self, term: Option<usize>) {
        self.page = Page::Glossary;
        self.glossary_focus = term;
        if term.is_some() {
            self.glossary_filter.clear();
        }
        self.requests.push(Request::OpenGlossary);
    }

    pub fn go_to_step(&mut self, step: usize) {
        if let Some((l, _)) = self.active
            && step < self.lessons[l].steps.len()
        {
            self.active = Some((l, step));
            self.enter_step();
        }
    }

    pub fn next(&mut self) {
        let Some((l, s)) = self.active else {
            return;
        };
        if matches!(self.lessons[l].steps[s].check, Check::Continue) {
            self.complete();
        }
        if s + 1 < self.lessons[l].steps.len() {
            self.go_to_step(s + 1);
        }
        // On the last step the lesson stays open, so its closing text and unlocked
        // source remain visible; the panel then offers the next lesson.
    }

    /// The lesson after the active one, if any.
    pub fn following_lesson(&self) -> Option<usize> {
        let (l, _) = self.active?;
        (l + 1 < self.lessons.len()).then_some(l + 1)
    }

    pub fn previous(&mut self) {
        if let Some((_, s)) = self.active
            && s > 0
        {
            self.go_to_step(s - 1);
        }
    }

    pub fn reveal_hint(&mut self) {
        let Some((lesson, _, step)) = self.current() else {
            return;
        };
        if self.hints_shown < step.hints.len() {
            let id = lesson.id.clone();
            self.hints_shown += 1;
            *self.progress.hints_used.entry(id).or_default() += 1;
            self.save();
        }
    }

    /// Marks the current step done, and the lesson when all its steps are.
    fn complete(&mut self) {
        let Some((l, s)) = self.active else {
            return;
        };
        let id = self.lessons[l].id.clone();
        self.progress.complete_step(&id, s, progress::today());
        let all = (0..self.lessons[l].steps.len()).all(|i| self.progress.step_done(&id, i));
        if all && self.progress.complete_lesson(&id) > 0 {
            let lesson = &self.lessons[l];
            if let Some(badge) = &lesson.badge {
                self.progress.badges.insert(badge.clone());
            }
            let level = lesson.level;
            let level_done = self
                .lessons
                .iter()
                .filter(|x| x.level == level)
                .all(|x| self.progress.lessons.contains(&x.id));
            if level_done {
                self.progress
                    .badges
                    .insert(format!("Level {level}: {}", LEVELS[usize::from(level)].0));
            }
            self.celebrate = Some(lesson.title.clone());
        }
        self.save();
    }

    fn check_matches(&self, f: impl Fn(&Check) -> bool) -> bool {
        self.current()
            .is_some_and(|(_, _, step)| !self.current_done() && f(&step.check))
    }

    /// Reports a user action.
    pub fn handle(&mut self, event: &Event) {
        if let Event::FileOpened(path) = event {
            self.opened.push(path.clone());
        }
        let done = self.check_matches(|check| match (check, event) {
            (Check::Action { id }, Event::Action(a)) => id == a,
            (Check::View { view }, Event::ViewFocused(v)) => view.eq_ignore_ascii_case(v),
            (Check::OpenCrackme { name }, Event::FileOpened(path)) => crackmes::find(name)
                .is_some_and(|c| path.file_name().is_some_and(|f| f == c.file_name)),
            _ => false,
        });
        if done {
            self.complete();
        }
    }

    /// Checks conditions that are about the current state.
    pub fn poll(&mut self, state: &PollState) {
        let done = self.check_matches(|check| match check {
            Check::View { view } => state
                .focused_view
                .as_deref()
                .is_some_and(|v| v.eq_ignore_ascii_case(view)),
            Check::CursorInMain => state.cursor_in_main,
            Check::Renamed => state.renamed,
            Check::Commented => state.commented,
            _ => false,
        });
        if done {
            self.complete();
        }
    }

    /// Checks the typed answer (for answer and secret steps).
    pub fn submit_answer(&mut self) {
        let Some((_, _, step)) = self.current() else {
            return;
        };
        let given = self.answer.trim().to_owned();
        let correct = match &step.check {
            Check::Answer {
                answers,
                number,
                case_sensitive,
            } => answers.iter().any(|a| {
                if *number {
                    numbers::parse(a).is_some() && numbers::parse(a) == numbers::parse(&given)
                } else if *case_sensitive {
                    a.trim() == given
                } else {
                    a.trim().eq_ignore_ascii_case(&given)
                }
            }),
            Check::Secret { sha256 } => {
                let digest = Sha256::digest(given.as_bytes());
                let hex: String = digest.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect();
                hex.eq_ignore_ascii_case(sha256)
            }
            _ => return,
        };
        self.feedback = Some(Feedback {
            correct,
            text: if correct {
                "Correct!".into()
            } else if given.is_empty() {
                "Type an answer first.".into()
            } else {
                "Not quite. Try again, or take a hint.".into()
            },
        });
        if correct {
            self.complete();
        }
    }

    /// Checks a multiple-choice pick.
    pub fn choose(&mut self, option: usize) {
        let Some((_, _, step)) = self.current() else {
            return;
        };
        let Check::Choice {
            correct, explain, ..
        } = &step.check
        else {
            return;
        };
        let ok = option == *correct;
        let why = explain
            .get(option)
            .map(|w| format!(" {w}"))
            .unwrap_or_default();
        self.feedback = Some(Feedback {
            correct: ok,
            text: if ok {
                format!("Correct!{why}")
            } else if why.is_empty() {
                "Not that one. Read the text again, or take a hint.".into()
            } else {
                format!("Not that one.{why}")
            },
        });
        if ok {
            self.complete();
        }
    }

    /// Call after the simulator ran or stepped.
    pub fn sim_updated(&mut self) {
        let Some(cpu) = &self.sim.cpu else {
            return;
        };
        if !cpu.finished_ok() {
            return;
        }
        let Some((_, _, step)) = self.current() else {
            return;
        };
        let Check::Sim { expect, requires } = &step.check else {
            return;
        };
        let missing: Vec<&String> = requires.iter().filter(|m| !cpu.uses(m)).collect();
        let wrong: Vec<String> = expect
            .iter()
            .filter(|(reg, value)| cpu.reg(reg) != Some(*value as u64))
            .map(|(reg, value)| {
                format!(
                    "{reg} should be {value}, but it is {}",
                    cpu.reg(reg).unwrap_or(0) as i64
                )
            })
            .collect();
        let correct = missing.is_empty() && wrong.is_empty();
        let text = if correct {
            "The program does what was asked. Well done!".to_owned()
        } else if !missing.is_empty() {
            let list: Vec<&str> = missing.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();
            format!("Use {} in your program.", list.join(", "))
        } else {
            wrong.join("; ")
        };
        self.feedback = Some(Feedback { correct, text });
        if correct && !self.current_done() {
            self.complete();
        }
    }

    /// Extracts a practice program and asks the app to open it.
    pub fn open_crackme(&mut self, name: &str) {
        let Some(c) = crackmes::find(name) else {
            return;
        };
        let dir = self
            .crackme_dir
            .clone()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| std::env::temp_dir().join("orress-academy"));
        match crackmes::extract(c, &dir) {
            Ok(path) => self.requests.push(Request::OpenFile(path)),
            Err(e) => self
                .requests
                .push(Request::Message(format!("Could not extract {name}: {e}"))),
        }
    }

    pub fn total_steps(&self) -> usize {
        self.lessons.iter().map(|l| l.steps.len()).sum()
    }

    pub fn done_steps(&self) -> usize {
        self.lessons
            .iter()
            .map(|l| {
                (0..l.steps.len())
                    .filter(|&i| self.progress.step_done(&l.id, i))
                    .count()
            })
            .sum()
    }
}

fn first_open_step(progress: &Progress, lesson: &Lesson) -> usize {
    (0..lesson.steps.len())
        .find(|&i| !progress.step_done(&lesson.id, i))
        .unwrap_or(0)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn academy() -> Academy {
        Academy::new(None)
    }

    fn find_step(a: &Academy, f: impl Fn(&Check) -> bool) -> (usize, usize) {
        for (li, l) in a.lessons.iter().enumerate() {
            for (si, s) in l.steps.iter().enumerate() {
                if f(&s.check) {
                    return (li, si);
                }
            }
        }
        panic!("no such step in the built-in lessons");
    }

    #[test]
    fn action_step_completes_on_event() {
        let mut a = academy();
        let (l, s) = find_step(&a, |c| matches!(c, Check::Action { .. }));
        a.start(l);
        a.go_to_step(s);
        let Check::Action { id } = a.current().unwrap().2.check.clone() else {
            unreachable!()
        };
        a.handle(&Event::Action("something::Else".into()));
        assert!(!a.current_done());
        a.handle(&Event::Action(id));
        assert!(a.current_done());
        assert!(a.progress.xp > 0);
        assert_eq!(a.spotlight(), None, "no spotlight once done");
    }

    #[test]
    fn number_answers_accept_any_base() {
        let mut a = academy();
        let (l, s) = find_step(&a, |c| matches!(c, Check::Answer { number: true, .. }));
        a.start(l);
        a.go_to_step(s);
        let Check::Answer { answers, .. } = a.current().unwrap().2.check.clone() else {
            unreachable!()
        };
        let value = numbers::parse(&answers[0]).unwrap();
        a.answer = "definitely wrong".into();
        a.submit_answer();
        assert!(!a.feedback.as_ref().unwrap().correct);
        a.answer = format!("0x{value:x}");
        a.submit_answer();
        assert!(a.feedback.as_ref().unwrap().correct, "hex form of {value}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn crackme_passwords_match_their_secrets() {
        let mut a = academy();
        // Every practice program's password, so a typo in a lesson's sha256 is caught.
        for password in [
            "open_sesame_101",
            "R3v3rs3",
            "ORRESS42",
            "w4tch_1t_run",
            "n0_debugger_here",
            "pa7ch_0r_3mulat3",
            "flag{te4_h4s_a_g0ld_k3y}",
            "s0lv3_m3_n0w",
            "unfl4tt3",
            "vm_0wned",
            "h4ckv3rs",
            "r3g_v4lz",
            "ORR-DIFF-7",
        ] {
            let (l, s) = find_step(&a, |c| {
                matches!(c, Check::Secret { sha256 } if *sha256 == {
                    let d = Sha256::digest(password.as_bytes());
                    d.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect::<String>()
                })
            });
            a.start(l);
            a.go_to_step(s);
            a.answer = password.into();
            a.submit_answer();
            assert!(a.current_done(), "{password}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn sim_steps_complete_with_their_solution() {
        // Lesson validation already runs every solution; here the whole flow is tested:
        // load the solution into the simulator, run it, and the step completes.
        let mut a = academy();
        let steps: Vec<(usize, usize)> = a
            .lessons
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .flat_map(|(li, l)| {
                l.steps
                    .iter()
                    .enumerate()
                    .filter(|(_, s)| matches!(s.check, Check::Sim { .. }))
                    .map(move |(si, _)| (li, si))
            })
            .collect();
        assert!(steps.len() >= 4, "Level 1 has simulator exercises");
        for (l, s) in steps {
            a.start(l);
            a.go_to_step(s);
            let solution = a.current().unwrap().2.solution.clone().unwrap();
            a.sim.load(&solution);
            a.sim.cpu.as_mut().unwrap().run();
            a.sim_updated();
            assert!(a.current_done(), "lesson {l} step {s}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn completing_all_steps_completes_the_lesson() {
        let mut a = academy();
        a.start(0);
        let id = a.lessons[0].id.clone();
        for s in 0..a.lessons[0].steps.len() {
            a.go_to_step(s);
            a.complete();
        }
        assert!(a.progress.lessons.contains(&id));
        assert_eq!(a.celebrate.as_deref(), Some(a.lessons[0].title.as_str()));
    }
}

```rs
//! Number parsing and formatting for the number-systems lessons and quiz answers.

/// Parses `42`, `0x2a`, `2Ah`, `0b101010`, `-1`, `'A'`. Underscores and spaces are
/// ignored. Returns the value as i128 so both u64 and negative numbers fit.
pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Option<i128> {
    let t: String = text
        .trim()
        .chars()
        .filter(|c| *c != '_' && *c != ' ')
        .collect();
    if t.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    if let Some(c) = t.strip_prefix('\'').and_then(|r| r.strip_suffix('\'')) {
        let mut chars = c.chars();
        let ch = chars.next()?;
        return chars.next().is_none().then_some(i128::from(u32::from(ch)));
    }
    let (neg, t) = match t.strip_prefix('-') {
        Some(rest) => (true, rest.to_owned()),
        None => (false, t),
    };
    let lower = t.to_ascii_lowercase();
    let value = if let Some(hex) = lower.strip_prefix("0x") {
        i128::from_str_radix(hex, 16).ok()?
    } else if let Some(bin) = lower.strip_prefix("0b") {
        i128::from_str_radix(bin, 2).ok()?
    } else if let Some(hex) = lower.strip_suffix('h') {
        i128::from_str_radix(hex, 16).ok()?
    } else {
        lower.parse::<i128>().ok()?
    };
    Some(if neg { -value } else { value })
}

pub fn binary_grouped(value: u64, bits: u32) -> String {
    let mut s = String::new();
    for i in (0..bits).rev() {
        s.push(if value >> i & 1 == 1 { '1' } else { '0' });
        if i % 4 == 0 && i != 0 {
            s.push(' ');
        }
    }
    s
}

/// Two's complement interpretation of the low `bits` bits.
pub fn signed(value: u64, bits: u32) -> i64 {
    if bits >= 64 {
        return value as i64;
    }
    let mask = (1u64 << bits) - 1;
    let v = value & mask;
    if v >> (bits - 1) & 1 == 1 {
        (v as i64) - (1i64 << bits)
    } else {
        v as i64
    }
}

/// Bytes of the low `bits` bits, little-endian order.
pub fn le_bytes(value: u64, bits: u32) -> Vec<u8> {
    value.to_le_bytes()[..(bits / 8) as usize].to_vec()
}

pub fn char_of(value: u64) -> String {
    match value {
        0x20..=0x7e => format!("'{}'", value as u8 as char),
        0 => "NUL".into(),
        0x0a => "newline (\\n)".into(),
        0x0d => "carriage return (\\r)".into(),
        0x09 => "tab (\\t)".into(),
        _ => "not printable".into(),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn parses_all_forms() {
        assert_eq!(parse("42"), Some(42));
        assert_eq!(parse("0x2A"), Some(42));
        assert_eq!(parse("2ah"), Some(42));
        assert_eq!(parse("0b10_1010"), Some(42));
        assert_eq!(parse("-1"), Some(-1));
        assert_eq!(parse("'A'"), Some(65));
        assert_eq!(parse("0x12345678"), Some(0x1234_5678));
        assert_eq!(parse("nope"), None);
        assert_eq!(parse(""), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn formatting() {
        assert_eq!(binary_grouped(0x2a, 8), "0010 1010");
        assert_eq!(signed(0xff, 8), -1);
        assert_eq!(signed(0x7f, 8), 127);
        assert_eq!(signed(0x80, 8), -128);
        assert_eq!(le_bytes(0x1234_5678, 32), vec![0x78, 0x56, 0x34, 0x12]);
        assert_eq!(char_of(0x41), "'A'");
    }
}

`crates/orress-academy/src/progress.rs`:

```rs
//! Learner progress: completed steps and lessons, XP, badges and the daily streak.
//! Saved as `academy.json` in the config folder.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
use std::path::Path;

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

pub const XP_PER_STEP: u32 = 10;
pub const XP_PER_LESSON: u32 = 50;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct Progress {
    /// Completed step indices per lesson id.
    pub steps: BTreeMap<String, BTreeSet<usize>>,
    pub lessons: BTreeSet<String>,
    pub xp: u32,
    pub badges: BTreeSet<String>,
    /// Hints revealed per lesson id.
    pub hints_used: BTreeMap<String, u32>,
    /// Days (since 1970) on which a step was completed, for the streak.
    pub active_days: BTreeSet<u32>,
    /// Lesson to continue with.
    pub current: Option<String>,
}

impl Progress {
    pub fn load(path: &Path) -> Self {
        std::fs::read_to_string(path)
            .ok()
            .and_then(|json| serde_json::from_str(&json).ok())
            .unwrap_or_default()
    }

    pub fn save(&self, path: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
        if let Some(dir) = path.parent() {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(dir).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        }
        let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(self).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        std::fs::write(path, json).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))
    }

    pub fn step_done(&self, lesson: &str, step: usize) -> bool {
        self.steps.get(lesson).is_some_and(|s| s.contains(&step))
    }

    /// Marks a step complete. Returns the XP earned (0 if it was already done).
    pub fn complete_step(&mut self, lesson: &str, step: usize, today: u32) -> u32 {
        if !self
            .steps
            .entry(lesson.to_owned())
            .or_default()
            .insert(step)
        {
            return 0;
        }
        self.active_days.insert(today);
        self.xp += XP_PER_STEP;
        XP_PER_STEP
    }

    /// Marks a lesson complete. Returns the XP earned (0 if it was already done).
    pub fn complete_lesson(&mut self, lesson: &str) -> u32 {
        if !self.lessons.insert(lesson.to_owned()) {
            return 0;
        }
        self.xp += XP_PER_LESSON;
        XP_PER_LESSON
    }

    /// Consecutive days up to `today` with at least one completed step.
    pub fn streak(&self, today: u32) -> u32 {
        let mut day = today;
        // A streak survives until the end of the next day.
        if !self.active_days.contains(&day) {
            day = day.saturating_sub(1);
        }
        let mut n = 0;
        while self.active_days.contains(&day) {
            n += 1;
            if day == 0 {
                break;
            }
            day -= 1;
        }
        n
    }

    /// Level title for an XP amount, to make progress visible.
    pub fn rank(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self.xp {
            0..100 => "Newcomer",
            100..300 => "Bit Flipper",
            300..600 => "Byte Reader",
            600..1000 => "Assembly Apprentice",
            1000..2000 => "Crackme Cracker",
            _ => "Reverse Engineer",
        }
    }
}

pub fn today() -> u32 {
    std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map_or(0, |d| (d.as_secs() / 86_400) as u32)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn xp_and_streak() {
        let mut p = Progress::default();
        assert_eq!(p.complete_step("a", 0, 100), XP_PER_STEP);
        assert_eq!(p.complete_step("a", 0, 100), 0, "no double XP");
        p.complete_step("a", 1, 101);
        p.complete_step("a", 2, 102);
        assert_eq!(p.streak(102), 3);
        assert_eq!(p.streak(103), 3, "still alive the next day");
        assert_eq!(p.streak(105), 0);
        assert_eq!(p.complete_lesson("a"), XP_PER_LESSON);
        assert_eq!(p.xp, 3 * XP_PER_STEP + XP_PER_LESSON);
        assert_eq!(p.rank(), "Newcomer");
    }

    #[test]
    fn save_and_load() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("orress-progress-{}", std::process::id()));
        let path = dir.join("academy.json");
        let mut p = Progress::default();
        p.complete_step("l0", 0, 5);
        p.badges.insert("First steps".into());
        p.save(&path).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(Progress::load(&path), p);
        assert_eq!(
            Progress::load(&dir.join("missing.json")),
            Progress::default()
        );
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(dir).ok();
    }
}

`crates/orress-academy/src/sim.rs`:

```rs
//! A tiny x86-64 CPU simulator for lessons.
//!
//! It runs assembly text directly (no machine code), one instruction per line, so
//! learners can type a few instructions and watch registers, flags and the stack
//! change step by step. It supports the instructions the early lessons need, with
//! Intel syntax as shown in ORRESS's disassembly:
//!
//! ```text
//! start:
//!     mov rax, 5          ; comments start with ;
//!     add rax, 0x10
//!     cmp rax, 21
//!     je done
//!     push rax
//!     call double
//! done:
//!     ret
//! double:
//!     add rax, rax
//!     ret
//! ```

use std::collections::{BTreeSet, HashMap};

pub const REGS: [&str; 16] = [
    "rax", "rbx", "rcx", "rdx", "rsi", "rdi", "rbp", "rsp", "r8", "r9", "r10", "r11", "r12", "r13",
    "r14", "r15",
];
const RSP: usize = 7;
/// The stack lives at the top of this small memory region.
pub const STACK_BASE: u64 = 0x7fff_f000;
pub const STACK_SIZE: u64 = 0x1000;
pub const STACK_TOP: u64 = STACK_BASE + STACK_SIZE;
/// Return address pushed for the outermost `ret`: returning there ends the program.
const EXIT_ADDRESS: u64 = 0xdead_0000;
const MAX_STEPS: usize = 10_000;
const MAX_HISTORY: usize = 2_000;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Width {
    Q,
    D,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Operand {
    Reg(usize, Width),
    Imm(i64),
    /// `[reg + disp]`
    Mem {
        base: usize,
        disp: i64,
    },
    Label(String),
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Instr {
    pub line: usize,
    pub op: String,
    pub args: Vec<Operand>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Flags {
    /// Zero flag: the result was 0 (after cmp: the values were equal).
    pub zf: bool,
    /// Sign flag: the result was negative (top bit set).
    pub sf: bool,
    /// Carry flag: unsigned overflow / borrow (after cmp: first < second, unsigned).
    pub cf: bool,
    /// Overflow flag: signed overflow.
    pub of: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ParseError {
    pub line: usize,
    pub message: String,
}

#[derive(Clone)]
struct Snapshot {
    regs: [u64; 16],
    flags: Flags,
    stack: Vec<u8>,
    pc: usize,
    halted: Option<String>,
    steps: usize,
}

#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct Cpu {
    pub regs: [u64; 16],
    pub flags: Flags,
    pub stack: Vec<u8>,
    program: Vec<Instr>,
    labels: HashMap<String, usize>,
    /// Index into `program` of the next instruction.
    pub pc: usize,
    /// Why the program stopped (`Some` once finished or failed).
    pub halted: Option<String>,
    pub error: bool,
    pub steps: usize,
    /// Registers written by the last step, for highlighting.
    pub changed: BTreeSet<usize>,
    history: Vec<Snapshot>,
}

const MNEMONICS: &[&str] = &[
    "mov", "add", "sub", "inc", "dec", "neg", "imul", "xor", "and", "or", "not", "shl", "shr",
    "cmp", "test", "lea", "push", "pop", "call", "ret", "jmp", "je", "jz", "jne", "jnz", "jg",
    "jge", "jl", "jle", "ja", "jae", "jb", "jbe", "js", "jns", "nop", "hlt",
];

fn edit_distance(a: &str, b: &str) -> usize {
    let b: Vec<char> = b.chars().collect();
    let mut prev: Vec<usize> = (0..=b.len()).collect();
    for (i, ca) in a.chars().enumerate() {
        let mut cur = vec![i + 1];
        for (j, &cb) in b.iter().enumerate() {
            cur.push(
                (prev[j] + usize::from(ca != cb))
                    .min(prev[j + 1] + 1)
                    .min(cur[j] + 1),
            );
        }
        prev = cur;
    }
    prev[b.len()]
}

fn parse_number(text: &str) -> Option<i64> {
    let t = text.trim();
    if let Some(c) = t.strip_prefix('\'').and_then(|r| r.strip_suffix('\'')) {
        let mut chars = c.chars();
        let ch = chars.next()?;
        return chars.next().is_none().then_some(ch as i64);
    }
    let (neg, t) = match t.strip_prefix('-') {
        Some(rest) => (true, rest),
        None => (false, t),
    };
    let value = if let Some(hex) = t.strip_prefix("0x").or_else(|| t.strip_prefix("0X")) {
        u64::from_str_radix(hex, 16).ok()? as i64
    } else if let Some(hex) = t
        .strip_suffix('h')
        .filter(|h| h.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_hexdigit()))
    {
        u64::from_str_radix(hex, 16).ok()? as i64
    } else if let Some(bin) = t.strip_prefix("0b") {
        u64::from_str_radix(bin, 2).ok()? as i64
    } else {
        t.parse::<i64>().ok()?
    };
    Some(if neg { value.wrapping_neg() } else { value })
}

fn parse_register(name: &str) -> Option<(usize, Width)> {
    if let Some(i) = REGS.iter().position(|r| *r == name) {
        return Some((i, Width::Q));
    }
    let d = ["eax", "ebx", "ecx", "edx", "esi", "edi", "ebp", "esp"];
    d.iter().position(|r| *r == name).map(|i| (i, Width::D))
}

fn parse_operand(text: &str, line: usize) -> Result<Operand, ParseError> {
    let t = text.trim();
    let err = |message: String| ParseError { line, message };
    let t = t
        .strip_prefix("qword ptr")
        .or_else(|| t.strip_prefix("qword"))
        .map_or(t, str::trim);
    if let Some(inner) = t.strip_prefix('[').and_then(|r| r.strip_suffix(']')) {
        let inner = inner.replace(' ', "");
        let (reg, disp) = match inner.find(['+', '-']) {
            Some(i) => {
                let disp = parse_number(&inner[i..].replace('+', ""))
                    .ok_or_else(|| err(format!("`{}` is not a number", &inner[i..])))?;
                (&inner[..i], disp)
            }
            None => (inner.as_str(), 0),
        };
        let (base, width) =
            parse_register(reg).ok_or_else(|| err(format!("`{reg}` is not a register")))?;
        if width != Width::Q {
            return Err(err(
                "memory addresses need a 64-bit register, like [rsp+8]".into()
            ));
        }
        return Ok(Operand::Mem { base, disp });
    }
    if let Some((r, w)) = parse_register(&t.to_ascii_lowercase()) {
        return Ok(Operand::Reg(r, w));
    }
    if let Some(n) = parse_number(t) {
        return Ok(Operand::Imm(n));
    }
    if t.chars()
        .all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_' || c == '.')
        && !t.is_empty()
    {
        return Ok(Operand::Label(t.to_owned()));
    }
    Err(err(format!("cannot understand `{t}`")))
}

pub fn parse(source: &str) -> Result<(Vec<Instr>, HashMap<String, usize>), ParseError> {
    let mut program = Vec::new();
    let mut labels = HashMap::new();
    for (index, raw) in source.lines().enumerate() {
        let line = index + 1;
        let mut text = raw.split(';').next().unwrap_or("").trim();
        if let Some((label, rest)) = text.split_once(':')
            && !label.contains(' ')
            && !label.contains('[')
        {
            if labels
                .insert(label.trim().to_owned(), program.len())
                .is_some()
            {
                return Err(ParseError {
                    line,
                    message: format!("the label `{label}` is defined twice"),
                });
            }
            text = rest.trim();
        }
        if text.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let (op, rest) = text.split_once(char::is_whitespace).unwrap_or((text, ""));
        let op = op.to_ascii_lowercase();
        if !MNEMONICS.contains(&op.as_str()) {
            let suggestion = MNEMONICS
                .iter()
                .min_by_key(|m| edit_distance(&op, m))
                .filter(|m| edit_distance(&op, m) <= 2)
                .map(|m| format!(" Did you mean `{m}`?"))
                .unwrap_or_default();
            return Err(ParseError {
                line,
                message: format!("`{op}` is not an instruction this simulator knows.{suggestion}"),
            });
        }
        let args = if rest.trim().is_empty() {
            Vec::new()
        } else {
            rest.split(',')
                .map(|a| parse_operand(a, line))
                .collect::<Result<_, _>>()?
        };
        let expected = match op.as_str() {
            "ret" | "nop" | "hlt" => 0..=0,
            "inc" | "dec" | "neg" | "not" | "push" | "pop" | "call" | "jmp" | "je" | "jz"
            | "jne" | "jnz" | "jg" | "jge" | "jl" | "jle" | "ja" | "jae" | "jb" | "jbe" | "js"
            | "jns" => 1..=1,
            _ => 2..=2,
        };
        if !expected.contains(&args.len()) {
            return Err(ParseError {
                line,
                message: format!(
                    "`{op}` takes {} operand{}, found {}",
                    expected.start(),
                    if *expected.start() == 1 { "" } else { "s" },
                    args.len()
                ),
            });
        }
        program.push(Instr { line, op, args });
    }
    for instr in &program {
        for arg in &instr.args {
            if let Operand::Label(l) = arg
                && !labels.contains_key(l)
            {
                return Err(ParseError {
                    line: instr.line,
                    message: format!("there is no label called `{l}`"),
                });
            }
        }
    }
    Ok((program, labels))
}

impl Cpu {
    pub fn new(source: &str) -> Result<Self, ParseError> {
        let (program, labels) = parse(source)?;
        let mut cpu = Self {
            regs: [0; 16],
            flags: Flags::default(),
            stack: vec![0; STACK_SIZE as usize],
            program,
            labels,
            pc: 0,
            halted: None,
            error: false,
            steps: 0,
            changed: BTreeSet::new(),
            history: Vec::new(),
        };
        cpu.regs[RSP] = STACK_TOP;
        // The outermost `ret` returns to this address, which ends the program.
        cpu.regs[RSP] -= 8;
        cpu.write_mem(cpu.regs[RSP], EXIT_ADDRESS)
            .expect("stack top is valid");
        if cpu.program.is_empty() {
            cpu.halted = Some("The program is empty. Type some instructions.".into());
        }
        Ok(cpu)
    }

    pub fn line(&self) -> Option<usize> {
        self.program.get(self.pc).map(|i| i.line)
    }

    pub fn instructions(&self) -> &[Instr] {
        &self.program
    }

    pub fn reg(&self, name: &str) -> Option<u64> {
        REGS.iter().position(|r| *r == name).map(|i| self.regs[i])
    }

    pub fn read_mem(&self, addr: u64) -> Result<u64, String> {
        if !(STACK_BASE..=STACK_TOP - 8).contains(&addr) {
            return Err(format!(
                "memory address 0x{addr:x} is outside the stack (0x{STACK_BASE:x}–0x{STACK_TOP:x})"
            ));
        }
        let i = (addr - STACK_BASE) as usize;
        Ok(u64::from_le_bytes(
            self.stack[i..i + 8].try_into().expect("8 bytes"),
        ))
    }

    fn write_mem(&mut self, addr: u64, value: u64) -> Result<(), String> {
        self.read_mem(addr)?;
        let i = (addr - STACK_BASE) as usize;
        self.stack[i..i + 8].copy_from_slice(&value.to_le_bytes());
        Ok(())
    }

    fn get(&self, op: &Operand) -> Result<u64, String> {
        match op {
            Operand::Reg(r, Width::Q) => Ok(self.regs[*r]),
            Operand::Reg(r, Width::D) => Ok(self.regs[*r] & 0xffff_ffff),
            Operand::Imm(v) => Ok(*v as u64),
            Operand::Mem { base, disp } => {
                self.read_mem(self.regs[*base].wrapping_add_signed(*disp))
            }
            Operand::Label(l) => Err(format!("`{l}` is a label, not a value")),
        }
    }

    fn set(&mut self, op: &Operand, value: u64) -> Result<(), String> {
        match op {
            Operand::Reg(r, w) => {
                // Writing a 32-bit register clears the upper half, like on a real CPU.
                self.regs[*r] = if *w == Width::D {
                    value & 0xffff_ffff
                } else {
                    value
                };
                self.changed.insert(*r);
                Ok(())
            }
            Operand::Mem { base, disp } => {
                self.write_mem(self.regs[*base].wrapping_add_signed(*disp), value)
            }
            Operand::Imm(_) => Err(
                "cannot write to a number; the first operand must be a register or memory".into(),
            ),
            Operand::Label(_) => Err("cannot write to a label".into()),
        }
    }

    fn set_logic_flags(&mut self, result: u64) {
        self.flags = Flags {
            zf: result == 0,
            sf: (result as i64) < 0,
            cf: false,
            of: false,
        };
    }

    fn set_sub_flags(&mut self, a: u64, b: u64) -> u64 {
        let (result, borrow) = a.overflowing_sub(b);
        let (_, overflow) = (a as i64).overflowing_sub(b as i64);
        self.flags = Flags {
            zf: result == 0,
            sf: (result as i64) < 0,
            cf: borrow,
            of: overflow,
        };
        result
    }

    fn set_add_flags(&mut self, a: u64, b: u64) -> u64 {
        let (result, carry) = a.overflowing_add(b);
        let (_, overflow) = (a as i64).overflowing_add(b as i64);
        self.flags = Flags {
            zf: result == 0,
            sf: (result as i64) < 0,
            cf: carry,
            of: overflow,
        };
        result
    }

    fn condition(&self, op: &str) -> bool {
        let f = self.flags;
        match op {
            "je" | "jz" => f.zf,
            "jne" | "jnz" => !f.zf,
            "jg" => !f.zf && f.sf == f.of,
            "jge" => f.sf == f.of,
            "jl" => f.sf != f.of,
            "jle" => f.zf || f.sf != f.of,
            "ja" => !f.cf && !f.zf,
            "jae" => !f.cf,
            "jb" => f.cf,
            "jbe" => f.cf || f.zf,
            "js" => f.sf,
            "jns" => !f.sf,
            _ => true,
        }
    }

    fn label_target(&self, op: &Operand) -> Result<usize, String> {
        match op {
            Operand::Label(l) => self
                .labels
                .get(l)
                .copied()
                .ok_or_else(|| format!("no label `{l}`")),
            _ => Err("jumps and calls need a label, like `jmp loop`".into()),
        }
    }

    /// Executes one instruction. Returns `false` once the program has stopped.
    pub fn step(&mut self) -> bool {
        if self.halted.is_some() {
            return false;
        }
        if self.history.len() >= MAX_HISTORY {
            self.history.remove(0);
        }
        self.history.push(Snapshot {
            regs: self.regs,
            flags: self.flags,
            stack: self.stack.clone(),
            pc: self.pc,
            halted: self.halted.clone(),
            steps: self.steps,
        });
        self.changed.clear();
        let Some(instr) = self.program.get(self.pc).cloned() else {
            self.halted = Some("Reached the end of the program.".into());
            return false;
        };
        self.steps += 1;
        if let Err(message) = self.execute(&instr) {
            self.halted = Some(format!("Line {}: {message}", instr.line));
            self.error = true;
            return false;
        }
        if self.halted.is_none() && self.steps >= MAX_STEPS {
            self.halted = Some(format!(
                "Stopped after {MAX_STEPS} steps. Is there a loop that never ends?"
            ));
            self.error = true;
        }
        if self.halted.is_none() && self.pc >= self.program.len() {
            self.halted = Some("Reached the end of the program.".into());
        }
        self.halted.is_none()
    }

    fn execute(&mut self, instr: &Instr) -> Result<(), String> {
        let a = instr.args.first();
        let b = instr.args.get(1);
        let mut next = self.pc + 1;
        match instr.op.as_str() {
            "mov" => {
                let v = self.get(b.expect("2 args"))?;
                self.set(a.expect("2 args"), v)?;
            }
            "lea" => {
                let Some(Operand::Mem { base, disp }) = b else {
                    return Err("lea needs a memory operand like [rbp-8]".into());
                };
                let v = self.regs[*base].wrapping_add_signed(*disp);
                self.set(a.expect("2 args"), v)?;
            }
            "add" => {
                let (x, y) = (self.get(a.expect("args"))?, self.get(b.expect("args"))?);
                let r = self.set_add_flags(x, y);
                self.set(a.expect("args"), r)?;
            }
            "sub" => {
                let (x, y) = (self.get(a.expect("args"))?, self.get(b.expect("args"))?);
                let r = self.set_sub_flags(x, y);
                self.set(a.expect("args"), r)?;
            }
            "cmp" => {
                let (x, y) = (self.get(a.expect("args"))?, self.get(b.expect("args"))?);
                self.set_sub_flags(x, y);
            }
            "inc" | "dec" => {
                let x = self.get(a.expect("arg"))?;
                let carry = self.flags.cf; // inc/dec leave CF alone
                let r = if instr.op == "inc" {
                    self.set_add_flags(x, 1)
                } else {
                    self.set_sub_flags(x, 1)
                };
                self.flags.cf = carry;
                self.set(a.expect("arg"), r)?;
            }
            "neg" => {
                let x = self.get(a.expect("arg"))?;
                let r = self.set_sub_flags(0, x);
                self.set(a.expect("arg"), r)?;
            }
            "imul" => {
                let (x, y) = (self.get(a.expect("args"))?, self.get(b.expect("args"))?);
                let (r, overflow) = (x as i64).overflowing_mul(y as i64);
                self.set_logic_flags(r as u64);
                self.flags.of = overflow;
                self.flags.cf = overflow;
                self.set(a.expect("args"), r as u64)?;
            }
            "xor" | "and" | "or" | "test" => {
                let (x, y) = (self.get(a.expect("args"))?, self.get(b.expect("args"))?);
                let r = match instr.op.as_str() {
                    "xor" => x ^ y,
                    "or" => x | y,
                    _ => x & y,
                };
                self.set_logic_flags(r);
                if instr.op != "test" {
                    self.set(a.expect("args"), r)?;
                }
            }
            "not" => {
                let x = self.get(a.expect("arg"))?;
                self.set(a.expect("arg"), !x)?;
            }
            "shl" | "shr" => {
                let x = self.get(a.expect("args"))?;
                let n = (self.get(b.expect("args"))? & 63) as u32;
                let r = if instr.op == "shl" { x << n } else { x >> n };
                self.set_logic_flags(r);
                self.set(a.expect("args"), r)?;
            }
            "push" => {
                let v = self.get(a.expect("arg"))?;
                self.regs[RSP] = self.regs[RSP].wrapping_sub(8);
                self.changed.insert(RSP);
                self.write_mem(self.regs[RSP], v)
                    .map_err(|_| "stack overflow: too many pushes".to_owned())?;
            }
            "pop" => {
                let v = self
                    .read_mem(self.regs[RSP])
                    .map_err(|_| "nothing left on the stack to pop".to_owned())?;
                self.regs[RSP] = self.regs[RSP].wrapping_add(8);
                self.changed.insert(RSP);
                self.set(a.expect("arg"), v)?;
            }
            "call" => {
                let target = self.label_target(a.expect("arg"))?;
                self.regs[RSP] = self.regs[RSP].wrapping_sub(8);
                self.changed.insert(RSP);
                // Return "address": the index of the next instruction.
                self.write_mem(self.regs[RSP], next as u64)
                    .map_err(|_| "stack overflow: too many nested calls".to_owned())?;
                next = target;
            }
            "ret" => {
                let ret = self
                    .read_mem(self.regs[RSP])
                    .map_err(|_| "ret with an empty stack".to_owned())?;
                self.regs[RSP] = self.regs[RSP].wrapping_add(8);
                self.changed.insert(RSP);
                if ret == EXIT_ADDRESS {
                    self.halted = Some("The program returned from its last function. Done!".into());
                } else if (ret as usize) <= self.program.len() {
                    next = ret as usize;
                } else {
                    return Err(format!(
                        "ret jumped to 0x{ret:x}, which is not a return address. Did a push/pop pair not match?"
                    ));
                }
            }
            "jmp" => next = self.label_target(a.expect("arg"))?,
            "nop" => {}
            "hlt" => self.halted = Some("hlt: the program stopped.".into()),
            op => {
                if self.condition(op) {
                    next = self.label_target(a.expect("arg"))?;
                }
            }
        }
        self.pc = next;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Runs until the program stops.
    pub fn run(&mut self) {
        while self.step() {}
    }

    pub fn can_step_back(&self) -> bool {
        !self.history.is_empty()
    }

    pub fn step_back(&mut self) {
        if let Some(s) = self.history.pop() {
            self.regs = s.regs;
            self.flags = s.flags;
            self.stack = s.stack;
            self.pc = s.pc;
            self.halted = s.halted;
            self.steps = s.steps;
            self.error = false;
            self.changed.clear();
        }
    }

    /// Whether the program uses an instruction (for lesson checks like "use push").
    pub fn uses(&self, mnemonic: &str) -> bool {
        self.program.iter().any(|i| i.op == mnemonic)
    }

    /// Finished normally (not stopped by an error).
    pub fn finished_ok(&self) -> bool {
        self.halted.is_some() && !self.error
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn run(src: &str) -> Cpu {
        let mut cpu = Cpu::new(src).unwrap();
        cpu.run();
        cpu
    }

    #[test]
    fn arithmetic_and_flags() {
        let cpu = run("mov rax, 10\nadd rax, 20\nsub rax, 5\ncmp rax, 25");
        assert_eq!(cpu.reg("rax"), Some(25));
        assert!(cpu.flags.zf);
        assert!(cpu.finished_ok());
        let cpu = run("mov rax, 1\nsub rax, 2");
        assert_eq!(cpu.reg("rax"), Some(u64::MAX));
        assert!(cpu.flags.sf && cpu.flags.cf);
    }

    #[test]
    fn numbers_in_many_forms() {
        let cpu = run("mov rax, 0x10\nmov rbx, 10h\nmov rcx, 0b101\nmov rdx, 'A'\nmov rsi, -1");
        assert_eq!(cpu.reg("rax"), Some(16));
        assert_eq!(cpu.reg("rbx"), Some(16));
        assert_eq!(cpu.reg("rcx"), Some(5));
        assert_eq!(cpu.reg("rdx"), Some(65));
        assert_eq!(cpu.reg("rsi"), Some(u64::MAX));
    }

    #[test]
    fn loop_sums_one_to_five() {
        let cpu = run(
            "    xor rax, rax\n    mov rcx, 1\nloop:\n    add rax, rcx\n    inc rcx\n    cmp rcx, 6\n    jne loop\n",
        );
        assert_eq!(cpu.reg("rax"), Some(15));
    }

    #[test]
    fn stack_swap_and_calls() {
        let cpu = run("mov rax, 1\nmov rbx, 2\npush rax\npush rbx\npop rax\npop rbx");
        assert_eq!((cpu.reg("rax"), cpu.reg("rbx")), (Some(2), Some(1)));
        assert_eq!(cpu.reg("rsp"), Some(STACK_TOP - 8));

        let cpu = run("mov rax, 3\ncall double\nret\ndouble:\n  add rax, rax\n  ret");
        assert_eq!(cpu.reg("rax"), Some(6));
        assert!(cpu.halted.as_deref().unwrap().contains("Done"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn memory_operands_and_lea() {
        let cpu = run("sub rsp, 16\nmov qword ptr [rsp+8], 42\nmov rax, [rsp+8]\nlea rbx, [rsp+8]");
        assert_eq!(cpu.reg("rax"), Some(42));
        assert_eq!(cpu.reg("rbx"), Some(STACK_TOP - 8 - 16 + 8));
    }

    #[test]
    fn thirty_two_bit_writes_clear_upper_half() {
        let cpu = run("mov rax, -1\nmov eax, 5");
        assert_eq!(cpu.reg("rax"), Some(5));
    }

    #[test]
    fn signed_and_unsigned_jumps() {
        let cpu = run("mov rax, -1\ncmp rax, 1\njl less\nmov rbx, 1\nret\nless:\nmov rbx, 2\nret");
        assert_eq!(cpu.reg("rbx"), Some(2), "-1 < 1 signed");
        let cpu =
            run("mov rax, -1\ncmp rax, 1\nja above\nmov rbx, 1\nret\nabove:\nmov rbx, 2\nret");
        assert_eq!(cpu.reg("rbx"), Some(2), "0xffff... > 1 unsigned");
    }

    #[test]
    fn friendly_errors() {
        let e = Cpu::new("mvo rax, 1").err().unwrap();
        assert!(e.message.contains("Did you mean `mov`"), "{}", e.message);
        assert_eq!(e.line, 1);
        assert!(
            Cpu::new("jmp nowhere")
                .err()
                .unwrap()
                .message
                .contains("no label")
        );
        assert!(
            Cpu::new("add rax")
                .err()
                .unwrap()
                .message
                .contains("2 operands")
        );
        let cpu = run("pop rax\npop rax");
        assert!(cpu.error, "second pop has nothing to pop");
        let cpu = run("x:\njmp x");
        assert!(cpu.error && cpu.halted.unwrap().contains("never ends"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn step_back_restores_state() {
        let mut cpu = Cpu::new("mov rax, 1\nadd rax, 1").unwrap();
        cpu.step();
        cpu.step();
        assert_eq!(cpu.reg("rax"), Some(2));
        cpu.step_back();
        assert_eq!(cpu.reg("rax"), Some(1));
        assert_eq!(cpu.line(), Some(2));
    }
}
