//! Academy screens: the overview, the lesson panel, the CPU simulator, widgets, and
//! the spotlight overlay.

use egui::{Color32, Context, RichText, Ui};
use orress_ui::{ExplainExt as _, muted, spotlight};

use crate::sim::{self, STACK_TOP};
use crate::{Academy, Check, LEVELS, Page, Request, numbers, progress};

fn markdown(ui: &mut Ui, academy: &mut Academy, text: &str) {
    let mut cache = std::mem::take(&mut academy.markdown);
    egui_commonmark::CommonMarkViewer::new().show(ui, &mut cache, text);
    academy.markdown = cache;
}

/// A status dot: filled for done/current, hollow for to-do. Drawn rather than typed,
/// because the default fonts lack the circle characters.
fn dot(ui: &mut Ui, filled: bool, color: Color32) -> egui::Response {
    let (rect, response) = ui.allocate_exact_size(egui::vec2(14.0, 14.0), egui::Sense::click());
    let center = rect.center();
    if filled {
        ui.painter().circle_filled(center, 5.0, color);
    } else {
        ui.painter()
            .circle_stroke(center, 4.5, egui::Stroke::new(1.5, color));
    }
    response
}

fn success_color(ui: &Ui) -> Color32 {
    if ui.visuals().dark_mode {
        Color32::from_rgb(120, 200, 120)
    } else {
        Color32::from_rgb(40, 130, 40)
    }
}

/// The Academy tab: the lesson overview, or the glossary.
pub fn overview(ui: &mut Ui, academy: &mut Academy) {
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.selectable_value(
            &mut academy.page,
            Page::Lessons,
            RichText::new("Lessons").strong(),
        );
        ui.selectable_value(
            &mut academy.page,
            Page::Glossary,
            RichText::new("Glossary").strong(),
        )
        .explain(
            "Glossary",
            "Every technical word used in the lessons, explained in plain language.",
        );
    });
    ui.separator();
    match academy.page {
        Page::Lessons => lessons_page(ui, academy),
        Page::Glossary => glossary_page(ui, academy),
    }
}

fn glossary_page(ui: &mut Ui, academy: &mut Academy) {
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label("Search:");
        ui.add(
            egui::TextEdit::singleline(&mut academy.glossary_filter)
                .id_salt("orress::glossary_filter")
                .hint_text("a word, e.g. stack")
                .desired_width(240.0),
        );
        ui.label(muted(format!("{} words", academy.glossary.len())));
    });
    ui.add_space(4.0);
    let filter = academy.glossary_filter.trim().to_lowercase();
    let focus = academy.glossary_focus.take();
    let mut jump = None;
    egui::ScrollArea::vertical()
        .auto_shrink([false, false])
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            let mut letter = None;
            for i in 0..academy.glossary.len() {
                let term = academy.glossary[i].clone();
                let matches = filter.is_empty()
                    || term.term.to_lowercase().contains(&filter)
                    || term
                        .aliases
                        .iter()
                        .any(|a| a.to_lowercase().contains(&filter))
                    || term.short.to_lowercase().contains(&filter);
                if !matches {
                    continue;
                }
                let first = term.term.chars().next().map(|c| c.to_ascii_uppercase());
                if filter.is_empty() && first != letter {
                    letter = first;
                    ui.add_space(6.0);
                    ui.label(
                        RichText::new(first.unwrap_or(' ').to_string())
                            .strong()
                            .size(16.0),
                    );
                }
                // The term, then its one-line explanation wrapping below it in a narrow
                // panel; click the term to open the full explanation.
                let id = ui.make_persistent_id(("orress::glossary_term", i));
                let mut open = ui.data(|d| d.get_temp::<bool>(id)).unwrap_or(false);
                if focus == Some(i) {
                    open = true;
                }
                let header = ui
                    .horizontal_wrapped(|ui| {
                        let r = ui
                            .selectable_label(open, RichText::new(&term.term).strong())
                            .on_hover_text(if open { "Fold" } else { "Read more" });
                        ui.label(muted(&term.short));
                        r
                    })
                    .inner;
                if header.clicked() {
                    open = !open;
                }
                ui.data_mut(|d| d.insert_temp(id, open));
                if open {
                    ui.indent(id, |ui| {
                        if !term.aliases.is_empty() {
                            ui.label(muted(format!("Also written: {}", term.aliases.join(", "))));
                        }
                        if let Some(text) = &term.text {
                            markdown(ui, academy, text);
                        }
                        if !term.see.is_empty() {
                            ui.horizontal_wrapped(|ui| {
                                ui.label(muted("See also:"));
                                for see in &term.see {
                                    if ui.link(see).clicked() {
                                        jump = crate::glossary::find(&academy.glossary, see);
                                    }
                                }
                            });
                        }
                    });
                }
                ui.add_space(2.0);
                if focus == Some(i) {
                    header.scroll_to_me(Some(egui::Align::TOP));
                }
            }
        });
    if let Some(i) = jump {
        academy.glossary_filter.clear();
        academy.glossary_focus = Some(i);
    }
}

fn lessons_page(ui: &mut Ui, academy: &mut Academy) {
    egui::ScrollArea::vertical().auto_shrink([false, false]).show(ui, |ui| {
        ui.heading("ORRESS Academy");
        ui.label(muted(
            "Learn reverse engineering step by step, from binary numbers to cracking programs. \
             Every lesson checks what you do in ORRESS itself, and the examples are written in Rust.",
        ));
        ui.label(muted(
            "You only need to know some basic Rust. Everything else is taught here, and every \
             technical word is explained in the Glossary (the tab above).",
        ));
        ui.add_space(8.0);

        let p = &academy.progress;
        let today = progress::today();
        ui.horizontal(|ui| {
            ui.label(RichText::new(p.rank()).strong().size(16.0)).explain(
                "Rank",
                "Your title, based on the experience points (XP) you earned. Every finished step \
                 gives 10 XP, every finished lesson 50 XP more.",
            );
            ui.separator();
            ui.label(format!("{} XP", p.xp));
            ui.separator();
            let streak = p.streak(today);
            ui.label(format!("{streak} day streak")).explain(
                "Streak",
                "Days in a row on which you finished at least one step. A little every day is the \
                 fastest way to learn.",
            );
        });
        let (done, total) = (academy.done_steps(), academy.total_steps());
        ui.add(
            egui::ProgressBar::new(done as f32 / total.max(1) as f32)
                .text(format!("{done} of {total} steps"))
                .desired_width(360.0),
        );
        if !p.badges.is_empty() {
            ui.horizontal_wrapped(|ui| {
                ui.label(muted("Badges:"));
                for badge in &p.badges {
                    ui.label(RichText::new(badge).strong().color(Color32::from_rgb(230, 180, 60)));
                }
            });
        }
        ui.add_space(8.0);
        if let Some(next) = academy.next_lesson() {
            let title = academy.lessons[next].title.clone();
            if ui
                .button(RichText::new(format!("Continue: {title}")).size(16.0).strong())
                .clicked()
            {
                academy.start(next);
            }
        } else {
            ui.label(RichText::new("You finished every lesson available so far!").strong());
        }
        ui.add_space(12.0);

        for (level, (name, about)) in LEVELS.iter().enumerate() {
            let lessons: Vec<usize> = (0..academy.lessons.len())
                .filter(|&i| usize::from(academy.lessons[i].level) == level)
                .collect();
            egui::Frame::group(ui.style()).inner_margin(10.0).show(ui, |ui| {
                ui.set_width(ui.available_width());
                ui.label(RichText::new(format!("Level {level} · {name}")).strong().size(15.0));
                ui.label(muted(*about));
                if lessons.is_empty() {
                    ui.label(muted("Coming in a later version of ORRESS."));
                }
                for i in lessons {
                    let lesson = &academy.lessons[i];
                    let finished = academy.progress.lessons.contains(&lesson.id);
                    let steps_done = (0..lesson.steps.len())
                        .filter(|&s| academy.progress.step_done(&lesson.id, s))
                        .count();
                    let active = academy.active.map(|(l, _)| l) == Some(i);
                    let mut start = false;
                    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                        let (filled, color) = if finished {
                            (true, success_color(ui))
                        } else if active {
                            (true, ui.visuals().hyperlink_color)
                        } else {
                            (false, ui.visuals().weak_text_color())
                        };
                        dot(ui, filled, color);
                        ui.label(RichText::new(&lesson.title).strong());
                        ui.label(muted(format!("{steps_done}/{}", lesson.steps.len())));
                        let label = if finished {
                            "Review"
                        } else if steps_done > 0 {
                            "Continue"
                        } else {
                            "Start"
                        };
                        start = ui.small_button(label).clicked();
                    });
                    ui.label(RichText::new(&lesson.summary).small());
                    if start {
                        academy.start(i);
                    }
                }
            });
            ui.add_space(6.0);
        }
    });
}

/// The lesson panel (right dock while a lesson runs).
pub fn lesson_panel(ui: &mut Ui, academy: &mut Academy) {
    let Some((lesson, step_index, step)) =
        academy.current().map(|(l, i, s)| (l.clone(), i, s.clone()))
    else {
        ui.heading("Lessons");
        ui.label("No lesson is running. Open the Academy (Learn menu) and pick one.");
        return;
    };
    let done = academy.current_done();
    spotlight::mark(ui.ctx(), "lesson", ui.max_rect());
    // Both scrollbars: prose wraps to the panel width (pinned below), but anything that can't wrap
    // to fit — a wide table, a long unbroken token, a widget — gets a horizontal scrollbar instead
    // of being clipped by the narrow dock.
    let content_width = ui.available_width();
    egui::ScrollArea::both().auto_shrink([false, false]).show(ui, |ui| {
        ui.set_max_width(content_width);
        if let Some(title) = academy.celebrate.clone() {
            egui::Frame::new()
                .fill(success_color(ui).gamma_multiply(0.25))
                .corner_radius(6.0)
                .inner_margin(8.0)
                .show(ui, |ui| {
                    ui.label(RichText::new(format!("Lesson complete: {title}")).strong());
                    ui.label(format!("+{} XP. Great work!", progress::XP_PER_LESSON));
                    if ui.small_button("OK").clicked() {
                        academy.celebrate = None;
                    }
                });
            ui.add_space(6.0);
        }

        ui.label(muted(format!("Level {} · {}", lesson.level, LEVELS[usize::from(lesson.level)].0)));
        ui.horizontal(|ui| {
            ui.label(RichText::new(&lesson.title).strong().size(16.0));
            if ui
                .small_button("Glossary")
                .on_hover_text("Look up any word in the Academy glossary.")
                .clicked()
            {
                academy.show_glossary(None);
            }
        });
        // Step dots: click to jump to a step.
        ui.horizontal_wrapped(|ui| {
            for i in 0..lesson.steps.len() {
                let step_done = academy.progress.step_done(&lesson.id, i);
                let color = if i == step_index {
                    ui.visuals().hyperlink_color
                } else if step_done {
                    success_color(ui)
                } else {
                    ui.visuals().weak_text_color()
                };
                if dot(ui, step_done || i == step_index, color)
                    .on_hover_text(&lesson.steps[i].title)
                    .clicked()
                {
                    academy.go_to_step(i);
                }
            }
            ui.label(muted(format!("step {} of {}", step_index + 1, lesson.steps.len())));
        });
        ui.separator();

        if step_index == 0 && !lesson.goals.is_empty() {
            egui::Frame::group(ui.style()).inner_margin(8.0).show(ui, |ui| {
                ui.set_width(ui.available_width());
                ui.label(RichText::new("In this lesson you will learn to").strong());
                for goal in &lesson.goals {
                    ui.horizontal_wrapped(|ui| {
                        ui.label("-");
                        ui.label(goal);
                    });
                }
            });
            ui.add_space(4.0);
        }
        ui.label(RichText::new(&step.title).strong().size(15.0));
        if let Some(goal) = &step.goal {
            ui.label(muted(format!("Goal: {goal}")));
        }
        markdown(ui, academy, &step.text);
        if let Some(deep) = &step.deep_dive {
            ui.collapsing("Learn more", |ui| markdown(ui, academy, deep));
        }
        if let Some(widget) = &step.widget {
            ui.add_space(4.0);
            egui::Frame::group(ui.style()).show(ui, |ui| match widget.as_str() {
                "number_converter" => number_converter(ui, &mut academy.converter),
                "ascii_table" => ascii_table(ui),
                other => {
                    ui.label(muted(format!("(unknown widget {other})")));
                }
            });
        }
        ui.add_space(6.0);
        instructions(ui, academy, &step, done);
        task(ui, academy, &step, done);

        if let Some(f) = &academy.feedback {
            let color = if f.correct { success_color(ui) } else { ui.visuals().warn_fg_color };
            ui.colored_label(color, &f.text);
        }
        if done && let Some(success) = &step.success {
            egui::Frame::new()
                .fill(success_color(ui).gamma_multiply(0.15))
                .corner_radius(6.0)
                .inner_margin(8.0)
                .show(ui, |ui| markdown(ui, academy, success));
        }

        hints(ui, academy, &step, done);
        step_words(ui, academy);

        ui.add_space(8.0);
        ui.horizontal(|ui| {
            if ui.add_enabled(step_index > 0, egui::Button::new("Back")).clicked() {
                academy.previous();
            }
            let can_continue = done || matches!(step.check, Check::Continue);
            let last = step_index + 1 == lesson.steps.len();
            let finished = academy.progress.lessons.contains(&lesson.id);
            if last && finished {
                if let Some(next) = academy.following_lesson() {
                    let title = academy.lessons[next].title.clone();
                    if ui.button(RichText::new(format!("Next lesson: {title}")).strong()).clicked() {
                        academy.celebrate = None;
                        academy.start(next);
                    }
                } else {
                    ui.label(RichText::new("You finished every lesson available so far!").strong());
                }
            } else {
                let label = if last { "Finish lesson" } else { "Next" };
                if ui
                    .add_enabled(can_continue, egui::Button::new(RichText::new(label).strong()))
                    .on_disabled_hover_text("Complete the task above first.")
                    .clicked()
                {
                    academy.next();
                }
            }
        });

        if academy.progress.lessons.contains(&lesson.id)
            && let Some(name) = &lesson.reveal_source
            && let Some(c) = crate::crackmes::find(name)
        {
            ui.add_space(10.0);
            ui.collapsing("Source code of the practice program (unlocked)", |ui| {
                ui.label(muted("Now that you cracked it, compare what you saw with the original Rust code."));
                ui.add(
                    egui::TextEdit::multiline(&mut c.source.to_owned())
                        .code_editor()
                        .desired_width(f32::INFINITY)
                        .interactive(false),
                );
            });
        }
    });
}

/// The numbered "Do this" list: exactly what the learner has to do.
fn instructions(ui: &mut Ui, academy: &mut Academy, step: &crate::Step, done: bool) {
    if step.instructions.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    let accent = if done {
        success_color(ui)
    } else {
        ui.visuals().hyperlink_color
    };
    egui::Frame::new()
        .stroke(egui::Stroke::new(1.0, accent))
        .corner_radius(6.0)
        .inner_margin(8.0)
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            ui.set_width(ui.available_width());
            ui.label(
                RichText::new(if done { "Done:" } else { "Do this:" })
                    .strong()
                    .color(accent),
            );
            for (i, line) in step.instructions.iter().enumerate() {
                ui.horizontal_wrapped(|ui| {
                    ui.label(RichText::new(format!("{}.", i + 1)).strong());
                    // Instructions may use **bold** and `code`.
                    ui.vertical(|ui| markdown(ui, academy, line));
                });
            }
        });
    ui.add_space(4.0);
}

/// Glossary terms used in this step, folded away until needed.
fn step_words(ui: &mut Ui, academy: &mut Academy) {
    if academy.step_terms.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    ui.add_space(6.0);
    let terms = academy.step_terms.clone();
    let mut open = None;
    ui.collapsing(format!("Words in this step ({})", terms.len()), |ui| {
        for i in terms {
            let term = &academy.glossary[i];
            ui.horizontal_wrapped(|ui| {
                if ui
                    .link(RichText::new(&term.term).strong())
                    .on_hover_text("Open in the glossary")
                    .clicked()
                {
                    open = Some(i);
                }
                ui.label(&term.short);
            });
        }
    });
    if let Some(i) = open {
        academy.show_glossary(Some(i));
    }
}

fn task(ui: &mut Ui, academy: &mut Academy, step: &crate::Step, done: bool) {
    let status = |ui: &mut Ui, text: &str| {
        let (mark, color) = if done {
            ("Done: ", success_color(ui))
        } else {
            ("Your task: ", ui.visuals().hyperlink_color)
        };
        ui.horizontal_wrapped(|ui| {
            ui.label(RichText::new(mark).strong().color(color));
            ui.label(text);
        });
    };
    match &step.check {
        Check::Continue => {}
        Check::Action { .. } => status(
            ui,
            "follow the steps above. The lesson notices when you did it.",
        ),
        Check::View { view } => status(ui, &format!("open the {view} view (see the steps above).")),
        Check::OpenCrackme { name } => {
            status(ui, &format!("open the practice program {name}."));
            if !done && ui.button(format!("Open {name}")).clicked() {
                academy.open_crackme(name);
            }
        }
        Check::CursorInMain => status(ui, "put the cursor inside the main function."),
        Check::Renamed => status(ui, "rename something (N in the disassembly)."),
        Check::Commented => status(ui, "add a comment (; in the disassembly)."),
        Check::Answer { .. } | Check::Secret { .. } => {
            if done {
                status(ui, "answered correctly.");
            } else {
                ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                    let edit = ui.add(
                        egui::TextEdit::singleline(&mut academy.answer)
                            .id_salt("orress::lesson_answer")
                            .hint_text("Your answer")
                            .desired_width(200.0),
                    );
                    let enter = edit.lost_focus() && ui.input(|i| i.key_pressed(egui::Key::Enter));
                    if ui.button("Check").clicked() || enter {
                        academy.submit_answer();
                    }
                });
            }
        }
        Check::Choice {
            options, correct, ..
        } => {
            for (i, option) in options.iter().enumerate() {
                let text = if done && i == *correct {
                    RichText::new(format!("{option}  (correct)")).color(success_color(ui))
                } else {
                    RichText::new(option)
                };
                if ui
                    .add_enabled(!done, egui::Button::new(text).wrap())
                    .clicked()
                {
                    academy.choose(i);
                }
            }
        }
        Check::Sim { .. } => {
            status(
                ui,
                "make the program in the CPU simulator do what is asked, then Run it.",
            );
            ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                if ui.button("Open CPU simulator").clicked() {
                    academy.requests.push(Request::OpenSimulator);
                }
                if let Some(code) = &step.sim_code
                    && ui.button("Load starting code").clicked()
                {
                    academy.sim.load(code);
                    academy.requests.push(Request::OpenSimulator);
                }
            });
        }
    }
}

fn hints(ui: &mut Ui, academy: &mut Academy, step: &crate::Step, done: bool) {
    if step.hints.is_empty() && step.solution.is_none() {
        return;
    }
    ui.add_space(6.0);
    for (i, hint) in step.hints.iter().take(academy.hints_shown).enumerate() {
        ui.label(RichText::new(format!("Hint {}: {hint}", i + 1)).italics());
    }
    if done {
        return;
    }
    if academy.hints_shown < step.hints.len() {
        if ui
            .small_button(format!(
                "Show hint {} of {}",
                academy.hints_shown + 1,
                step.hints.len()
            ))
            .clicked()
        {
            academy.reveal_hint();
        }
    } else if let Some(solution) = &step.solution {
        ui.collapsing("Show a solution", |ui| {
            ui.label(muted(
                "Try it yourself first! Reading a solution teaches less than finding one.",
            ));
            ui.add(
                egui::TextEdit::multiline(&mut solution.clone())
                    .code_editor()
                    .desired_width(f32::INFINITY)
                    .interactive(false),
            );
            if ui.button("Load it into the simulator").clicked() {
                academy.sim.load(solution);
                academy.requests.push(Request::OpenSimulator);
            }
        });
    }
}

fn number_converter(ui: &mut Ui, input: &mut String) {
    ui.label(RichText::new("Number converter").strong())
        .explain(
            "Number converter",
            "Type a number as decimal (42), hexadecimal (0x2a), binary (0b101010) or a character \
         ('A'), and see it in every form at once.",
        );
    ui.add(
        egui::TextEdit::singleline(input)
            .id_salt("orress::number_converter")
            .desired_width(200.0)
            .font(egui::TextStyle::Monospace),
    );
    let Some(value) = numbers::parse(input) else {
        ui.label(muted("Not a number yet."));
        return;
    };
    let v = value as u64;
    let bits = if value < 0 {
        if value >= -128 {
            8
        } else if value >= -(1 << 31) {
            32
        } else {
            64
        }
    } else if v <= 0xff {
        8
    } else if v <= 0xffff {
        16
    } else if v <= 0xffff_ffff {
        32
    } else {
        64
    };
    let mask = if bits == 64 {
        u64::MAX
    } else {
        (1u64 << bits) - 1
    };
    let v = v & mask;
    egui::Grid::new("converter").num_columns(2).spacing([12.0, 3.0]).show(ui, |ui| {
        let mut row = |label: &str, value: String, explain: &str| {
            ui.label(muted(label)).explain(label, explain);
            ui.label(RichText::new(value).monospace());
            ui.end_row();
        };
        row("decimal", v.to_string(), "Base 10, the way people count.");
        row("hexadecimal", format!("0x{v:X}"), "Base 16: digits 0–9 and A–F. Each hex digit is exactly 4 bits, so two digits make one byte.");
        row("binary", numbers::binary_grouped(v, bits), "Base 2: only 0 and 1, the way the computer stores it. Grouped by 4 bits = one hex digit.");
        row(
            &format!("signed ({bits}-bit)"),
            numbers::signed(v, bits).to_string(),
            "The same bits read as a signed number (two's complement): if the top bit is 1, the number is negative.",
        );
        let le: Vec<String> = numbers::le_bytes(v, bits).iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02X}")).collect();
        let mut be = le.clone();
        be.reverse();
        row("bytes, little-endian", le.join(" "), "How x86 and ARM store it in memory: lowest byte first.");
        row("bytes, big-endian", be.join(" "), "Highest byte first: how people write numbers, and how network protocols send them.");
        if v <= 0xff {
            row("character", numbers::char_of(v), "The ASCII character with this code.");
        }
    });
}

fn ascii_table(ui: &mut Ui) {
    ui.label(RichText::new("ASCII table").strong());
    ui.label(muted(
        "Each printable character and its code in hex. Hover for decimal.",
    ));
    egui::Grid::new("ascii")
        .spacing([10.0, 2.0])
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            for row in 0..6u8 {
                for col in 0..16u8 {
                    let code = 0x20 + row * 16 + col;
                    if code > 0x7e {
                        ui.label("");
                        continue;
                    }
                    ui.label(RichText::new(format!("{:02X} {}", code, code as char)).monospace())
                        .on_hover_text(format!("{code} decimal"));
                }
                ui.end_row();
            }
        });
}

/// The CPU simulator tab.
pub fn simulator(ui: &mut Ui, academy: &mut Academy) {
    let mut ran = false;
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.heading("CPU simulator");
        ui.label(muted("x86-64, one instruction at a time"));
    });
    ui.label(muted(
        "Type instructions on the left. Step runs one line, Run runs to the end. Changed \
         registers light up. Labels end with ':' and comments start with ';'.",
    ));
    let running = academy.sim.cpu.as_ref().is_some_and(|c| c.steps > 0);
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        let can_run = academy.sim.cpu.as_ref().is_some_and(|c| c.halted.is_none());
        let step = ui.add_enabled(can_run, egui::Button::new("Step")).explain(
            "Step",
            "Run one instruction and see what changed. The best way to understand assembly.",
        );
        spotlight::mark(ui.ctx(), "sim.step", step.rect);
        if step.clicked()
            && let Some(cpu) = &mut academy.sim.cpu
        {
            cpu.step();
            ran = true;
        }
        let run = ui
            .add_enabled(can_run, egui::Button::new("Run"))
            .explain("Run", "Run until the program ends.");
        spotlight::mark(ui.ctx(), "sim.run", run.rect);
        if run.clicked()
            && let Some(cpu) = &mut academy.sim.cpu
        {
            cpu.run();
            ran = true;
        }
        let back = academy
            .sim
            .cpu
            .as_ref()
            .is_some_and(sim::Cpu::can_step_back);
        if ui
            .add_enabled(back, egui::Button::new("Step back"))
            .explain("Step back", "Undo the last step: time travel for learning.")
            .clicked()
            && let Some(cpu) = &mut academy.sim.cpu
        {
            cpu.step_back();
        }
        if ui
            .button("Reset")
            .explain(
                "Reset",
                "Start the program again from the first line, with all registers at 0.",
            )
            .clicked()
        {
            academy.sim.reset();
        }
        if let Some(cpu) = &academy.sim.cpu {
            ui.label(muted(format!("{} steps", cpu.steps)));
        }
    });
    if ran {
        academy.sim_updated();
    }
    if let Some(cpu) = &academy.sim.cpu
        && let Some(why) = &cpu.halted
    {
        let color = if cpu.error {
            ui.visuals().warn_fg_color
        } else {
            success_color(ui)
        };
        ui.colored_label(color, why);
    }
    if let Some(f) = &academy.feedback
        && academy
            .current()
            .is_some_and(|(_, _, s)| matches!(s.check, Check::Sim { .. }))
    {
        let color = if f.correct {
            success_color(ui)
        } else {
            ui.visuals().warn_fg_color
        };
        ui.colored_label(color, format!("Lesson: {}", f.text));
    }
    ui.separator();

    ui.columns(2, |cols| {
        let ui = &mut cols[0];
        let current_line = academy.sim.cpu.as_ref().and_then(sim::Cpu::line);
        if running {
            ui.label(RichText::new("Program (press Reset to edit)").strong());
            for (i, line) in academy.sim.source.lines().enumerate() {
                let here = current_line == Some(i + 1);
                let text = format!("{} {:>3}  {line}", if here { ">" } else { " " }, i + 1);
                let mut rt = RichText::new(text).monospace();
                if here {
                    rt = rt.background_color(ui.visuals().selection.bg_fill).strong();
                }
                ui.label(rt);
            }
        } else {
            ui.label(RichText::new("Program").strong());
            let edit = ui.add(
                egui::TextEdit::multiline(&mut academy.sim.source)
                    // A fixed id: messages above the editor come and go while typing, which
                    // would otherwise change its automatic id and drop the keyboard focus.
                    .id_salt("orress::sim_source")
                    .code_editor()
                    .desired_rows(16)
                    .desired_width(f32::INFINITY),
            );
            spotlight::mark(ui.ctx(), "sim.code", edit.rect);
            if edit.changed() {
                academy.sim.reset();
            }
            if let Some(e) = &academy.sim.error {
                ui.colored_label(ui.visuals().warn_fg_color, format!("Line {}: {}", e.line, e.message));
            }
        }

        let ui = &mut cols[1];
        let Some(cpu) = &academy.sim.cpu else {
            ui.label(muted("Fix the program to see the registers."));
            return;
        };
        let regs_rect = ui
            .scope(|ui| {
                ui.label(RichText::new("Registers").strong()).explain(
                    "Registers",
                    "Tiny, very fast storage slots inside the CPU. Instructions work on these. \
                     rax holds a function's result; rsp points at the top of the stack.",
                );
                egui::Grid::new("sim_regs").num_columns(3).spacing([10.0, 2.0]).striped(true).show(ui, |ui| {
                    // r8-r15 only when the program uses them, to keep the list short.
                    let source = academy.sim.source.to_ascii_lowercase();
                    for (i, name) in sim::REGS.iter().enumerate() {
                        let v = cpu.regs[i];
                        if i >= 8 && v == 0 && !source.contains(name) {
                            continue;
                        }
                        let changed = cpu.changed.contains(&i);
                        let color = if changed { Color32::from_rgb(255, 200, 60) } else { ui.visuals().text_color() };
                        let explain = orress_arch::explain::register(orress_arch::Isa::X64, name).unwrap_or("A general-purpose register.");
                        ui.label(RichText::new(*name).monospace().strong()).explain(name, explain);
                        ui.label(RichText::new(format!("0x{v:016x}")).monospace().color(color));
                        ui.label(RichText::new(format!("{}", v as i64)).monospace().color(color));
                        ui.end_row();
                    }
                });
            })
            .response
            .rect;
        spotlight::mark(ui.ctx(), "sim.registers", regs_rect);
        ui.add_space(6.0);
        let flags_rect = ui
            .scope(|ui| {
                ui.label(RichText::new("Flags").strong()).explain(
                    "Flags",
                    "Single bits the CPU sets after arithmetic and comparisons. Conditional jumps \
                     (je, jne, jl ...) decide by looking at them.",
                );
                ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                    let f = cpu.flags;
                    for (name, on, explain) in [
                        ("ZF", f.zf, "Zero flag: the last result was 0. After cmp a, b: a == b."),
                        ("SF", f.sf, "Sign flag: the last result was negative."),
                        ("CF", f.cf, "Carry flag: unsigned overflow. After cmp a, b: a < b as unsigned numbers."),
                        ("OF", f.of, "Overflow flag: the signed result did not fit."),
                    ] {
                        let text = RichText::new(format!("{name}={}", u8::from(on))).monospace();
                        let text = if on { text.strong().color(Color32::from_rgb(255, 200, 60)) } else { text.weak() };
                        ui.label(text).explain(name, explain);
                    }
                });
            })
            .response
            .rect;
        spotlight::mark(ui.ctx(), "sim.flags", flags_rect);
        ui.add_space(6.0);
        let stack_rect = ui
            .scope(|ui| {
                ui.label(RichText::new("Stack").strong()).explain(
                    "Stack",
                    "Memory that grows downward. push puts a value on top (rsp goes down by 8), \
                     pop takes it off (rsp goes up). call pushes the return address.",
                );
                let rsp = cpu.regs[7];
                let mut addr = rsp;
                let mut shown = 0;
                while addr < STACK_TOP && shown < 12 {
                    let value = cpu.read_mem(addr).unwrap_or(0);
                    let marker = if addr == rsp { "rsp >" } else { "     " };
                    let note = if value == 0xdead_0000 { "  (end of program)" } else { "" };
                    ui.label(RichText::new(format!("{marker} {addr:08x}: 0x{value:x}{note}")).monospace());
                    addr += 8;
                    shown += 1;
                }
            })
            .response
            .rect;
        spotlight::mark(ui.ctx(), "sim.stack", stack_rect);
    });
}

/// Draws the spotlight for the current step, if any.
pub fn spotlight_overlay(ctx: &Context, academy: &Academy) {
    let Some((_, _, step)) = academy.current() else {
        return;
    };
    if let Some(target) = academy.spotlight() {
        // Never dim the lesson itself: that is where the learner reads and answers.
        let lesson = spotlight::rect(ctx, "lesson")
            .into_iter()
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        spotlight::paint(ctx, target, &step.title, &lesson);
    }
}

```rs
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use crate::{ActionId, KeyContext, Keystroke};

/// One key binding. `action: None` unbinds the keystroke in that context
/// (written as `null` in JSON, like in Zed).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Binding {
    pub keystroke: Keystroke,
    pub context: KeyContext,
    pub action: Option<ActionId>,
}

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum KeymapError {
    #[error("invalid keymap JSON: {0}")]
    Json(#[from] serde_json::Error),
}

/// A keymap section in Zed's JSON format:
///
/// ```json
/// [
///   { "context": "Global", "bindings": { "ctrl-shift-p": "command_palette::Toggle" } },
///   { "context": "Hex",    "bindings": { "ctrl-g": "hex::GoToOffset", "ctrl-w": null } }
/// ]
/// ```
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct Section {
    #[serde(default)]
    context: KeyContext,
    bindings: BTreeMap<Keystroke, Option<ActionId>>,
}

// BTreeMap keys need Ord; order by the textual form so JSON output is stable.
impl PartialOrd for Keystroke {
    fn partial_cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Option<std::cmp::Ordering> {
        Some(self.cmp(other))
    }
}

impl Ord for Keystroke {
    fn cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> std::cmp::Ordering {
        self.to_string().cmp(&other.to_string())
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct Keymap {
    bindings: Vec<Binding>,
}

impl Keymap {
    pub fn from_json(json: &str) -> Result<Self, KeymapError> {
        let sections: Vec<Section> = serde_json::from_str(json)?;
        let mut keymap = Self::default();
        for section in sections {
            for (keystroke, action) in section.bindings {
                keymap.bind(keystroke, section.context, action);
            }
        }
        Ok(keymap)
    }

    pub fn to_json(&self) -> String {
        let mut sections: Vec<Section> = Vec::new();
        for context in KeyContext::ALL {
            let bindings: BTreeMap<_, _> = self
                .bindings
                .iter()
                .filter(|b| b.context == context)
                .map(|b| (b.keystroke, b.action.clone()))
                .collect();
            if !bindings.is_empty() {
                sections.push(Section { context, bindings });
            }
        }
        serde_json::to_string_pretty(&sections).expect("keymap serializes")
    }

    /// Adds or replaces the binding for `keystroke` in `context`.
    pub fn bind(&mut self, keystroke: Keystroke, context: KeyContext, action: Option<ActionId>) {
        self.bindings
            .retain(|b| !(b.keystroke == keystroke && b.context == context));
        self.bindings.push(Binding {
            keystroke,
            context,
            action,
        });
    }

    /// Layers `other` on top of `self`: the user keymap overrides the defaults.
    pub fn merge(&mut self, other: &Keymap) {
        for b in &other.bindings {
            self.bind(b.keystroke, b.context, b.action.clone());
        }
    }

    pub fn bindings(&self) -> &[Binding] {
        &self.bindings
    }

    /// The keystroke shown next to an action in menus and the palette.
    /// Prefers a binding in `context`, then a global one.
    pub fn keystroke_for(&self, action: &ActionId, context: KeyContext) -> Option<Keystroke> {
        let find = |ctx: KeyContext| {
            self.bindings
                .iter()
                .find(|b| b.context == ctx && b.action.as_ref() == Some(action))
                .map(|b| b.keystroke)
        };
        find(context).or_else(|| find(KeyContext::Global))
    }

    /// Like [`Keymap::keystroke_for`], but falls back to any other context that binds the action,
    /// returning that context too — so a menu or the shortcut list can show e.g. a Hex-only
    /// shortcut as "Ctrl+Shift+C (Hex)" instead of nothing.
    pub fn keystroke_anywhere(
        &self,
        action: &ActionId,
        context: KeyContext,
    ) -> Option<(Keystroke, KeyContext)> {
        if let Some(k) = self.keystroke_for(action, context) {
            let ctx = if self
                .bindings
                .iter()
                .any(|b| b.context == context && b.keystroke == k)
            {
                context
            } else {
                KeyContext::Global
            };
            return Some((k, ctx));
        }
        KeyContext::ALL.into_iter().find_map(|ctx| {
            self.bindings
                .iter()
                .find(|b| b.context == ctx && b.action.as_ref() == Some(action))
                .map(|b| (b.keystroke, ctx))
        })
    }

    /// Resolves what `keystroke` does in `context`, falling back to `Global`.
    pub fn resolve(&self, keystroke: Keystroke, context: KeyContext) -> Option<&ActionId> {
        let lookup = |ctx: KeyContext| {
            self.bindings
                .iter()
                .find(|b| b.context == ctx && b.keystroke == keystroke)
        };
        // A binding in the specific context (even `null`) shadows the global one.
        match lookup(context) {
            Some(b) => b.action.as_ref(),
            None => lookup(KeyContext::Global).and_then(|b| b.action.as_ref()),
        }
    }

    /// Consumes the first matching key press from egui's input and returns its action.
    pub fn dispatch(&self, ctx: &egui::Context, context: KeyContext) -> Option<ActionId> {
        let mut candidates: Vec<&Binding> = self
            .bindings
            .iter()
            .filter(|b| b.context == context || b.context == KeyContext::Global)
            .collect();
        // Most modifiers first: otherwise `ctrl-p` would also fire on `ctrl-shift-p`.
        candidates.sort_by_key(|b| std::cmp::Reverse(b.keystroke.specificity()));

        ctx.input_mut(|input| {
            for b in candidates {
                // Skip global bindings shadowed in this context.
                if self.resolve(b.keystroke, context) != b.action.as_ref() {
                    continue;
                }
                if input.consume_shortcut(&b.keystroke.shortcut()) {
                    return b.action.clone();
                }
            }
            None
        })
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    const JSON: &str = r#"[
        { "context": "Global", "bindings": {
            "ctrl-shift-p": "command_palette::Toggle",
            "ctrl-w": "workspace::CloseActiveTab"
        } },
        { "context": "Hex", "bindings": { "ctrl-w": null, "ctrl-g": "hex::GoTo" } }
    ]"#;

    fn ks(s: &str) -> Keystroke {
        Keystroke::parse(s).unwrap()
    }

    #[test]
    fn loads_zed_format() {
        let km = Keymap::from_json(JSON).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(km.bindings().len(), 4);
        assert_eq!(
            km.resolve(ks("ctrl-shift-p"), KeyContext::Hex),
            Some(&ActionId::from("command_palette::Toggle"))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn context_shadows_global_including_null() {
        let km = Keymap::from_json(JSON).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(km.resolve(ks("ctrl-w"), KeyContext::Hex), None);
        assert_eq!(
            km.resolve(ks("ctrl-w"), KeyContext::Notes),
            Some(&ActionId::from("workspace::CloseActiveTab"))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn merge_overrides_defaults() {
        let mut km = Keymap::from_json(JSON).unwrap();
        let user = Keymap::from_json(r#"[{ "bindings": { "ctrl-shift-p": "workspace::Open" } }]"#)
            .unwrap();
        km.merge(&user);
        assert_eq!(
            km.resolve(ks("ctrl-shift-p"), KeyContext::Global),
            Some(&ActionId::from("workspace::Open"))
        );
        assert_eq!(km.bindings().len(), 4);
    }

    #[test]
    fn json_round_trip() {
        let km = Keymap::from_json(JSON).unwrap();
        let again = Keymap::from_json(&km.to_json()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(again.bindings().len(), km.bindings().len());
    }

    #[test]
    fn keystroke_lookup_for_menus() {
        let km = Keymap::from_json(JSON).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            km.keystroke_for(&"hex::GoTo".into(), KeyContext::Hex),
            Some(ks("ctrl-g"))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn keystroke_anywhere_finds_other_contexts() {
        let km = Keymap::from_json(JSON).unwrap();
        // A Hex-only binding is found from the Workspace context, tagged with its context.
        assert_eq!(
            km.keystroke_anywhere(&"hex::GoTo".into(), KeyContext::Workspace),
            Some((ks("ctrl-g"), KeyContext::Hex))
        );
        // A global binding is reported as Global.
        assert_eq!(
            km.keystroke_anywhere(&"command_palette::Toggle".into(), KeyContext::Workspace),
            Some((ks("ctrl-shift-p"), KeyContext::Global))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            km.keystroke_anywhere(&"nothing::Here".into(), KeyContext::Workspace),
            None
        );
    }
}

`crates/orress-actions/src/keystroke.rs`:

```rs
use egui::{Key, KeyboardShortcut, Modifiers};
use serde::{Deserialize, Deserializer, Serialize, Serializer};

/// A key plus modifiers, written in Zed's keymap syntax: `ctrl-shift-p`, `alt-f4`, `f1`.
///
/// Modifier names:
/// - `ctrl`, `alt`, `shift`
/// - `cmd` / `secondary`: Ctrl on Windows and Linux, Cmd on macOS
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct Keystroke {
    pub modifiers: Modifiers,
    pub key: Key,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum KeystrokeParseError {
    #[error("empty keystroke")]
    Empty,
    #[error("unknown modifier `{0}`")]
    UnknownModifier(String),
    #[error("unknown key `{0}`")]
    UnknownKey(String),
}

impl Keystroke {
    pub const fn new(modifiers: Modifiers, key: Key) -> Self {
        Self { modifiers, key }
    }

    pub fn parse(source: &str) -> Result<Self, KeystrokeParseError> {
        let source = source.trim();
        if source.is_empty() {
            return Err(KeystrokeParseError::Empty);
        }
        // `ctrl--` means ctrl + minus: the last part may itself be "-".
        let (mods_part, key_part) = match source.strip_suffix("--") {
            Some(rest) => (rest, "-"),
            None => match source.rsplit_once('-') {
                Some((mods, key)) => (mods, key),
                None => ("", source),
            },
        };

        let mut modifiers = Modifiers::NONE;
        for part in mods_part.split('-').filter(|p| !p.is_empty()) {
            modifiers |= match part.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
                "ctrl" | "control" => Modifiers::CTRL,
                "alt" | "option" => Modifiers::ALT,
                "shift" => Modifiers::SHIFT,
                "cmd" | "secondary" | "command" => Modifiers::COMMAND,
                other => return Err(KeystrokeParseError::UnknownModifier(other.to_owned())),
            };
        }

        let key = Key::from_name(key_part)
            .or_else(|| {
                Key::ALL
                    .iter()
                    .copied()
                    .find(|k| k.name().eq_ignore_ascii_case(key_part))
            })
            .ok_or_else(|| KeystrokeParseError::UnknownKey(key_part.to_owned()))?;
        Ok(Self { modifiers, key })
    }

    pub fn shortcut(&self) -> KeyboardShortcut {
        KeyboardShortcut::new(self.modifiers, self.key)
    }

    /// Platform-aware label such as `Ctrl+Shift+P` (or `⇧⌘P` on macOS).
    pub fn label(&self, ctx: &egui::Context) -> String {
        ctx.format_shortcut(&self.shortcut())
    }

    /// Number of modifiers. Used to try more specific shortcuts first, because egui
    /// ignores a pressed Shift when the pattern does not mention it.
    pub fn specificity(&self) -> u32 {
        let m = self.modifiers;
        u32::from(m.ctrl || m.command) + u32::from(m.alt) + u32::from(m.shift)
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Display for Keystroke {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        let m = self.modifiers;
        if m.command && !m.ctrl {
            f.write_str("cmd-")?;
        } else if m.ctrl {
            f.write_str("ctrl-")?;
        }
        if m.alt {
            f.write_str("alt-")?;
        }
        if m.shift {
            f.write_str("shift-")?;
        }
        f.write_str(&self.key.name().to_ascii_lowercase())
    }
}

impl Serialize for Keystroke {
    fn serialize<S: Serializer>(&self, s: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
        s.collect_str(self)
    }
}

impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for Keystroke {
    fn deserialize<D: Deserializer<'de>>(d: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
        let s = String::deserialize(d)?;
        Self::parse(&s).map_err(serde::de::Error::custom)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn parses_zed_style_keystrokes() {
        let k = Keystroke::parse("ctrl-shift-p").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(k.key, Key::P);
        assert!(k.modifiers.ctrl && k.modifiers.shift && !k.modifiers.alt);

        assert_eq!(Keystroke::parse("f1").unwrap().key, Key::F1);
        assert_eq!(Keystroke::parse("ctrl--").unwrap().key, Key::Minus);
        assert_eq!(Keystroke::parse("ctrl-=").unwrap().key, Key::Equals);
        assert!(Keystroke::parse("cmd-b").unwrap().modifiers.command);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_garbage() {
        assert_eq!(Keystroke::parse(""), Err(KeystrokeParseError::Empty));
        assert!(matches!(
            Keystroke::parse("hyper-x"),
            Err(KeystrokeParseError::UnknownModifier(_))
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            Keystroke::parse("ctrl-nope"),
            Err(KeystrokeParseError::UnknownKey(_))
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn display_round_trips() {
        for s in [
            "ctrl-shift-p",
            "ctrl-alt-b",
            "f1",
            "ctrl-w",
            "escape",
            "ctrl--",
            "pageup",
        ] {
            let k = Keystroke::parse(s).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(Keystroke::parse(&k.to_string()).unwrap(), k, "{s}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn specificity_counts_modifiers() {
        assert_eq!(Keystroke::parse("ctrl-shift-p").unwrap().specificity(), 2);
        assert_eq!(Keystroke::parse("f1").unwrap().specificity(), 0);
    }
}

`crates/orress-actions/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! Actions, keystrokes and keymaps, modeled on Zed.
//!
//! Every user-facing operation in ORRESS is an [`Action`]: a stable string id such as
//! `"workspace::ToggleLeftDock"`, a human title, and a beginner-friendly explanation.
//! Keys never call code directly: a [`Keymap`] maps a [`Keystroke`] in a [`KeyContext`]
//! to an action id, and the app dispatches the action. This keeps the command palette,
//! menus, keyboard shortcuts and (later) scripts all going through one path.

mod keymap;
mod keystroke;
mod registry;

pub use keymap::{Binding, Keymap, KeymapError};
pub use keystroke::{Keystroke, KeystrokeParseError};
pub use registry::{Action, ActionRegistry};

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

/// Stable identifier of an action, written `namespace::Name` like in Zed.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(transparent)]
pub struct ActionId(pub String);

impl ActionId {
    pub fn new(id: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self(id.into())
    }

    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &str {
        &self.0
    }

    /// The part before `::`, used as the category in the command palette.
    pub fn namespace(&self) -> &str {
        self.0.split_once("::").map_or("", |(ns, _)| ns)
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Display for ActionId {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(&self.0)
    }
}

impl From<&str> for ActionId {
    fn from(s: &str) -> Self {
        Self(s.to_owned())
    }
}

/// Where keyboard focus is. Bindings for a specific context win over `Global` ones,
/// so the same key can mean different things in the hex view and in the code editor.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
pub enum KeyContext {
    #[default]
    Global,
    Workspace,
    Hex,
    Disassembly,
    Graph,
    Decompiler,
    Editor,
    Notes,
    Terminal,
    Debugger,
    CommandPalette,
}

impl KeyContext {
    pub const ALL: [Self; 11] = [
        Self::Global,
        Self::Workspace,
        Self::Hex,
        Self::Disassembly,
        Self::Graph,
        Self::Decompiler,
        Self::Editor,
        Self::Notes,
        Self::Terminal,
        Self::Debugger,
        Self::CommandPalette,
    ];
}

```rs
use std::collections::HashMap;

use crate::ActionId;

/// Metadata for one action. The behavior lives in the app; this describes it so the
/// command palette, menus, keybinding list and Explain Mode can all show it.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Action {
    pub id: ActionId,
    /// Short title shown in the command palette, e.g. "Toggle Left Dock".
    pub title: String,
    /// Plain-language explanation for beginners, shown in Explain Mode.
    pub explain: String,
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct ActionRegistry {
    actions: Vec<Action>,
    by_id: HashMap<ActionId, usize>,
}

impl ActionRegistry {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    /// Registers an action. Registering the same id twice replaces the metadata.
    pub fn register(&mut self, id: &str, title: &str, explain: &str) -> &mut Self {
        let action = Action {
            id: ActionId::new(id),
            title: title.to_owned(),
            explain: explain.to_owned(),
        };
        match self.by_id.get(&action.id) {
            Some(&index) => self.actions[index] = action,
            None => {
                self.by_id.insert(action.id.clone(), self.actions.len());
                self.actions.push(action);
            }
        }
        self
    }

    pub fn get(&self, id: &ActionId) -> Option<&Action> {
        self.by_id.get(id).map(|&i| &self.actions[i])
    }

    pub fn contains(&self, id: &ActionId) -> bool {
        self.by_id.contains_key(id)
    }

    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Action> {
        self.actions.iter()
    }

    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.actions.len()
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.actions.is_empty()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn register_and_replace() {
        let mut r = ActionRegistry::new();
        r.register("a::One", "One", "first");
        r.register("a::Two", "Two", "second");
        r.register("a::One", "One again", "replaced");
        assert_eq!(r.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(r.get(&"a::One".into()).unwrap().title, "One again");
        assert_eq!(ActionId::from("a::One").namespace(), "a");
    }
}

`crates/orress-ai/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! AI assistant backends for ORRESS — bring your own model.
//!
//! Four providers are supported so anyone can use their own subscription or a local model:
//!
//! - **Claude plan (CLI)** — shells out to the installed `claude` CLI (`claude -p`), which runs on
//!   whatever account Claude Code is signed into, *including a Claude Pro/Max plan* — no API key.
//! - **Claude API** — the Anthropic Messages API with an `x-api-key` (or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`).
//! - **OpenAI-compatible** — the Chat Completions protocol: OpenAI itself, Azure OpenAI, or any
//!   local server that speaks it (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM, …) via its base URL.
//! - **Offline** — no model; the caller answers from static analysis only.
//!
//! The HTTP providers use a blocking `ureq` client (rustls); callers run [`ask`] on a background
//! thread. Keys come from the config or, if blank, the matching environment variable.

use std::io::Write;
use std::process::{Command, Stdio};
use std::time::Duration;

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::{Value, json};

mod mcp;

/// Which backend to use.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Provider {
    /// The `claude` CLI (`claude -p`) on the signed-in Claude plan/account.
    ClaudeCli,
    /// The Anthropic Messages API (key).
    ClaudeApi,
    /// Any OpenAI Chat-Completions-compatible endpoint (OpenAI, Azure, Ollama, LM Studio, …).
    OpenAi,
    /// No model — answer from static analysis only.
    Offline,
}

impl Provider {
    pub fn label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::ClaudeCli => "Claude plan (CLI)",
            Self::ClaudeApi => "Claude API (key)",
            Self::OpenAi => "OpenAI-compatible / local",
            Self::Offline => "Offline (static only)",
        }
    }
    /// Default endpoint base for the HTTP providers.
    pub fn default_base(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::ClaudeApi => "https://api.anthropic.com",
            Self::OpenAi => "https://api.openai.com/v1",
            _ => "",
        }
    }
    /// Environment variable consulted when no key is configured.
    pub fn key_env(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::ClaudeApi => "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY",
            Self::OpenAi => "OPENAI_API_KEY",
            _ => "",
        }
    }
}

/// The assistant configuration. The API key is persisted only when `remember_key` is set (it is
/// then written to `ai.json` in plaintext); otherwise it is session-only and falls back to the
/// provider's environment variable.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Config {
    pub provider: Provider,
    pub model: String,
    pub base_url: String,
    /// Save the API key to disk (plaintext). Off → key is session-only / from the environment.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub remember_key: bool,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub api_key: String,
}

impl Default for Config {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            provider: Provider::ClaudeCli,
            model: String::new(),
            base_url: String::new(),
            remember_key: false,
            api_key: String::new(),
        }
    }
}

impl Config {
    fn base(&self) -> String {
        if self.base_url.trim().is_empty() {
            self.provider.default_base().to_string()
        } else {
            self.base_url.trim().trim_end_matches('/').to_string()
        }
    }
    /// The API key: the configured one, else the provider's environment variable.
    fn key(&self) -> Option<String> {
        if !self.api_key.trim().is_empty() {
            return Some(self.api_key.trim().to_string());
        }
        let env = self.provider.key_env();
        (!env.is_empty()).then(|| std::env::var(env).ok()).flatten()
    }
}

/// The Claude API model used when none is configured (the current Opus).
pub const DEFAULT_CLAUDE_MODEL: &str = "claude-opus-5-5";

/// The output-token cap for Claude API requests. Current models think before answering and the
/// thinking counts against this cap, so it must leave room for both (1024 truncated answers).
const MAX_TOKENS: u32 = 16_000;

/// The default system prompt: a focused RE assistant that answers from the provided context.
pub const SYSTEM_PROMPT: &str = "You are a reverse-engineering assistant embedded in ORRESS, a \
    reverse-engineering IDE for CTF and malware analysis. Answer the user's question about the \
    binary using only the analysis context provided in the message. Be concise and concrete, \
    prefer bullet points, cite the specific strings/APIs/addresses you reason from, and suggest \
    the next step in ORRESS. Do not ask to run tools; everything you need is in the message.";

/// Whether the `claude` CLI is available (for the Claude-plan backend).
pub fn claude_available() -> bool {
    claude_binary().is_some()
}

fn claude_binary() -> Option<String> {
    for name in ["claude", "claude.cmd", "claude.exe"] {
        if Command::new(name)
            .arg("--version")
            .stdout(Stdio::null())
            .stderr(Stdio::null())
            .stdin(Stdio::null())
            .status()
            .is_ok_and(|s| s.success())
        {
            return Some(name.to_string());
        }
    }
    None
}

/// An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server the model may use as a tool source, resolved from a Zed
/// context-server extension (its `context-server-command`). Only the `claude` CLI backend wires
/// these in; the HTTP backends ignore them.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct McpServer {
    pub name: String,
    pub command: String,
    pub args: Vec<String>,
    pub env: Vec<(String, String)>,
}

/// Builds the `--mcp-config` JSON the `claude` CLI expects:
/// `{ "mcpServers": { "<name>": { "command", "args", "env" } } }`. Pure, so it is unit-tested.
pub fn mcp_config_json(servers: &[McpServer]) -> String {
    let mut map = serde_json::Map::new();
    for s in servers {
        let env: serde_json::Map<String, Value> = s
            .env
            .iter()
            .map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), Value::String(v.clone())))
            .collect();
        map.insert(
            s.name.clone(),
            json!({ "command": s.command, "args": s.args, "env": Value::Object(env) }),
        );
    }
    json!({ "mcpServers": Value::Object(map) }).to_string()
}

/// Sends a query to the configured backend and returns the answer. Blocks (HTTP or a subprocess),
/// so run it on a background thread. `Offline` is not a model and returns an error here. `mcp` lists
/// MCP servers the model may use (honoured only by the `claude` CLI backend).
pub fn ask(cfg: &Config, system: &str, user: &str, mcp: &[McpServer]) -> Result<String, String> {
    match cfg.provider {
        Provider::ClaudeCli => {
            let model = (!cfg.model.trim().is_empty()).then(|| cfg.model.trim());
            ask_claude(model, system, user, mcp)
        }
        Provider::ClaudeApi => {
            let key = cfg
                .key()
                .ok_or("no Anthropic API key (set it, or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)")?;
            anthropic(
                &cfg.base(),
                &key,
                model_or(cfg, DEFAULT_CLAUDE_MODEL),
                system,
                user,
                mcp,
            )
        }
        Provider::OpenAi => openai(
            &cfg.base(),
            cfg.key(),
            model_or(cfg, "gpt-4o-mini"),
            system,
            user,
            mcp,
        ),
        Provider::Offline => Err("the Offline backend has no model".into()),
    }
}

fn model_or<'a>(cfg: &'a Config, default: &'a str) -> &'a str {
    if cfg.model.trim().is_empty() {
        default
    } else {
        cfg.model.trim()
    }
}

/// Runs the `claude` CLI headless, feeding the prompt on stdin. When `mcp` is non-empty the model
/// is given those MCP servers as tool sources (via a temporary `--mcp-config` file) and allowed
/// several turns so it can call a tool and then answer; with no MCP servers a single turn is used.
pub fn ask_claude(
    model: Option<&str>,
    system: &str,
    user: &str,
    mcp: &[McpServer],
) -> Result<String, String> {
    let bin = claude_binary().ok_or("the `claude` CLI was not found on PATH")?;
    let mut cmd = Command::new(bin);
    cmd.arg("-p").arg("--output-format").arg("text");
    // MCP servers need a multi-turn loop (call a tool, then answer); otherwise one turn suffices.
    let mcp_config = if mcp.is_empty() {
        cmd.arg("--max-turns").arg("1");
        None
    } else {
        let path = write_private_temp(&mcp_config_json(mcp))
            .map_err(|e| format!("could not write the MCP config: {e}"))?;
        let allowed = mcp
            .iter()
            .map(|s| format!("mcp__{}", s.name))
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join(",");
        cmd.arg("--max-turns")
            .arg("12")
            .arg("--mcp-config")
            .arg(&path);
        cmd.arg("--allowedTools").arg(allowed);
        Some(path)
    };
    cmd.arg("--append-system-prompt").arg(system);
    if let Some(m) = model {
        cmd.arg("--model").arg(m);
    }
    cmd.stdin(Stdio::piped())
        .stdout(Stdio::piped())
        .stderr(Stdio::piped());
    let result = run_claude(&mut cmd, user);
    if let Some(path) = mcp_config {
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(path);
    }
    result
}

/// Writes `contents` (which may carry secrets, e.g. MCP server env vars) to a fresh temp file only
/// the current user can read, and returns its path. The name is unique per process, time and call,
/// and the file is created exclusively, so concurrent queries never share or clobber one. The
/// caller deletes it after use.
fn write_private_temp(contents: &str) -> std::io::Result<std::path::PathBuf> {
    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
    static COUNTER: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
    let nanos = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|d| d.as_nanos())
        .unwrap_or(0);
    let n = COUNTER.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    let path = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
        "orress-mcp-{}-{nanos}-{n}.json",
        std::process::id()
    ));
    let mut opts = std::fs::OpenOptions::new();
    opts.write(true).create_new(true);
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        use std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt;
        opts.mode(0o600);
    }
    // On Windows the per-user temp directory is already private to the user.
    let mut file = opts.open(&path)?;
    if let Err(e) = file.write_all(contents.as_bytes()) {
        drop(file);
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&path);
        return Err(e);
    }
    Ok(path)
}

/// Spawns `cmd`, writes `user` to its stdin, and returns its trimmed stdout (or an error).
fn run_claude(cmd: &mut Command, user: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    let mut child = cmd
        .spawn()
        .map_err(|e| format!("could not start claude: {e}"))?;
    child
        .stdin
        .take()
        .ok_or("no stdin")?
        .write_all(user.as_bytes())
        .map_err(|e| format!("could not send the prompt: {e}"))?;
    let out = child
        .wait_with_output()
        .map_err(|e| format!("claude did not finish: {e}"))?;
    if !out.status.success() {
        return Err(format!(
            "claude failed: {}",
            String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr).trim()
        ));
    }
    Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout).trim().to_string())
}

fn agent() -> ureq::Agent {
    ureq::AgentBuilder::new()
        .timeout(Duration::from_secs(600))
        .build()
}

/// Returns the parsed JSON body of a response, or a readable error.
fn send(resp: Result<ureq::Response, ureq::Error>) -> Result<Value, String> {
    match resp {
        Ok(r) => r.into_json().map_err(|e| format!("bad JSON response: {e}")),
        Err(ureq::Error::Status(code, r)) => {
            let body: String = r
                .into_string()
                .unwrap_or_default()
                .chars()
                .take(400)
                .collect();
            Err(format!("HTTP {code}: {body}"))
        }
        Err(e) => Err(format!("request failed: {e}")),
    }
}

/// The Anthropic Messages API, with an MCP tool-use loop: discovered tools are offered to the
/// model, and when it emits `tool_use` blocks ORRESS runs them against the MCP servers and feeds
/// the `tool_result`s back, until the model answers (bounded by [`mcp::MAX_TOOL_ITERATIONS`]).
fn anthropic(
    base: &str,
    key: &str,
    model: &str,
    system: &str,
    user: &str,
    mcp: &[McpServer],
) -> Result<String, String> {
    let url = format!("{base}/v1/messages");
    let mut session = mcp::McpSession::connect(mcp);
    let tools: Vec<Value> = session.tools().iter().map(mcp::to_anthropic_tool).collect();
    let mut messages = vec![json!({ "role": "user", "content": user })];

    for _ in 0..mcp::MAX_TOOL_ITERATIONS {
        let mut body = json!({ "model": model, "max_tokens": MAX_TOKENS, "system": system, "messages": messages });
        if !tools.is_empty() {
            body["tools"] = Value::Array(tools.clone());
        }
        let resp = agent()
            .post(&url)
            .set("x-api-key", key)
            .set("anthropic-version", "2023-06-01")
            .set("content-type", "application/json")
            .send_json(body);
        let v = send(resp)?;

        let content = v["content"].as_array().cloned().unwrap_or_default();
        let tool_uses: Vec<&Value> = content.iter().filter(|b| b["type"] == "tool_use").collect();
        if tool_uses.is_empty() || v["stop_reason"] != "tool_use" {
            return parse_anthropic_response(&v);
        }
        // Echo the assistant turn, then answer each tool call with a tool_result.
        messages.push(json!({ "role": "assistant", "content": content }));
        let results: Vec<Value> = tool_uses
            .iter()
            .map(|tu| {
                let (text, is_error) =
                    match session.call(tu["name"].as_str().unwrap_or(""), tu["input"].clone()) {
                        Ok(text) => (text, false),
                        Err(e) => (e, true),
                    };
                json!({ "type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": tu["id"], "content": text, "is_error": is_error })
            })
            .collect();
        messages.push(json!({ "role": "user", "content": results }));
    }
    Err("the model kept requesting tools without answering".into())
}

/// Any OpenAI Chat-Completions-compatible endpoint, with the same MCP tool-use loop (OpenAI
/// `tools`/`tool_calls` shape).
fn openai(
    base: &str,
    key: Option<String>,
    model: &str,
    system: &str,
    user: &str,
    mcp: &[McpServer],
) -> Result<String, String> {
    let url = format!("{base}/chat/completions");
    let mut session = mcp::McpSession::connect(mcp);
    let tools: Vec<Value> = session.tools().iter().map(mcp::to_openai_tool).collect();
    let mut messages = vec![
        json!({ "role": "system", "content": system }),
        json!({ "role": "user", "content": user }),
    ];

    for _ in 0..mcp::MAX_TOOL_ITERATIONS {
        let mut body = json!({ "model": model, "messages": messages, "stream": false });
        if !tools.is_empty() {
            body["tools"] = Value::Array(tools.clone());
        }
        let mut req = agent().post(&url).set("content-type", "application/json");
        if let Some(k) = &key {
            req = req.set("authorization", &format!("Bearer {k}"));
        }
        let v = send(req.send_json(body))?;

        let message = v["choices"][0]["message"].clone();
        let tool_calls = message["tool_calls"]
            .as_array()
            .cloned()
            .unwrap_or_default();
        if tool_calls.is_empty() {
            return parse_openai_response(&v);
        }
        messages.push(message);
        for tc in &tool_calls {
            let name = tc["function"]["name"].as_str().unwrap_or("");
            let args: Value = tc["function"]["arguments"]
                .as_str()
                .and_then(|s| serde_json::from_str(s).ok())
                .unwrap_or_else(|| json!({}));
            let text = session.call(name, args).unwrap_or_else(|e| e);
            messages.push(json!({ "role": "tool", "tool_call_id": tc["id"], "content": text }));
        }
    }
    Err("the model kept requesting tools without answering".into())
}

pub fn build_openai_body(model: &str, system: &str, user: &str) -> Value {
    json!({
        "model": model,
        "messages": [
            { "role": "system", "content": system },
            { "role": "user", "content": user }
        ],
        "stream": false
    })
}

pub fn build_anthropic_body(model: &str, system: &str, user: &str) -> Value {
    json!({
        "model": model,
        "max_tokens": MAX_TOKENS,
        "system": system,
        "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": user } ]
    })
}

pub fn parse_openai_response(v: &Value) -> Result<String, String> {
    v["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
        .as_str()
        .map(|s| s.trim().to_string())
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("unexpected OpenAI response: {v}"))
}

pub fn parse_anthropic_response(v: &Value) -> Result<String, String> {
    if let Some(arr) = v["content"].as_array() {
        let text: String = arr
            .iter()
            .filter(|p| p["type"] == "text")
            .filter_map(|p| p["text"].as_str())
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join("");
        if !text.is_empty() {
            return Ok(text.trim().to_string());
        }
    }
    Err(format!("unexpected Anthropic response: {v}"))
}

/// Builds the user prompt from a question and an analysis-context block.
pub fn build_prompt(question: &str, context: &str) -> String {
    format!("# Analysis context (from ORRESS)\n{context}\n\n# Question\n{question}\n")
}

/// The form of the config actually written to disk: the API key is cleared unless `remember_key`.
fn persisted(cfg: &Config) -> Config {
    let mut c = cfg.clone();
    if !c.remember_key {
        c.api_key.clear();
    }
    c
}

/// The persisted JSON for `cfg` — used both to save and to detect changes worth saving.
pub fn config_json(cfg: &Config) -> String {
    serde_json::to_string_pretty(&persisted(cfg)).unwrap_or_default()
}

/// Loads a persisted config. A missing or broken file gives the default.
pub fn load_config(path: &std::path::Path) -> Config {
    std::fs::read_to_string(path)
        .ok()
        .and_then(|s| serde_json::from_str(&s).ok())
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

/// Persists the config (the API key only when `remember_key` is set).
pub fn save_config(path: &std::path::Path, cfg: &Config) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    if let Some(dir) = path.parent() {
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir)?;
    }
    std::fs::write(path, config_json(cfg))
}

mod tests;
