`crates/orress-ai/src/mcp.rs`:

```rs
//! A minimal MCP (Model Context Protocol) client over stdio, so ORRESS's HTTP model backends
//! (Claude API and OpenAI-compatible) can offer an extension's MCP server as tool sources. The
//! Claude-CLI backend gets MCP from the CLI instead, so this is only used by the HTTP loops.
//!
//! MCP's stdio transport is newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0: one JSON message per line. Servers log
//! to stderr, so stdout carries only protocol messages.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader, Read, Write};
use std::process::{Child, ChildStdout, Command, Stdio};
use std::sync::mpsc::{Receiver, RecvTimeoutError, channel};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use serde_json::{Value, json};

use crate::McpServer;

const PROTOCOL_VERSION: &str = "2024-11-05";
/// A safety bound on the tool-call loop, so a model that keeps asking for tools cannot spin forever.
pub const MAX_TOOL_ITERATIONS: usize = 8;

/// A tool an MCP server exposes.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct McpTool {
    pub name: String,
    pub description: String,
    /// The JSON Schema for the tool's arguments (passed straight to the model as the tool's schema).
    pub input_schema: Value,
}

/// Converts a tool to the Anthropic Messages API `tools` entry.
pub fn to_anthropic_tool(t: &McpTool) -> Value {
    json!({ "name": t.name, "description": t.description, "input_schema": t.input_schema })
}

/// Converts a tool to the OpenAI Chat-Completions `tools` entry.
pub fn to_openai_tool(t: &McpTool) -> Value {
    json!({
        "type": "function",
        "function": { "name": t.name, "description": t.description, "parameters": t.input_schema }
    })
}

/// Newline-delimited JSON-RPC write.
fn write_message(w: &mut impl Write, msg: &Value) -> Result<(), String> {
    let mut line = serde_json::to_vec(msg).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    line.push(b'\n');
    w.write_all(&line).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    w.flush().map_err(|e| e.to_string())
}

/// Reads one newline-delimited JSON-RPC message; `Ok(None)` at EOF. Blank lines are skipped.
fn read_message(r: &mut impl BufRead) -> Result<Option<Value>, String> {
    loop {
        let mut line = String::new();
        if r.read_line(&mut line).map_err(|e| e.to_string())? == 0 {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let trimmed = line.trim();
        if trimmed.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        return serde_json::from_str(trimmed)
            .map(Some)
            .map_err(|e| format!("bad MCP JSON: {e}"));
    }
}

/// Parses a `tools/list` result into tools.
fn parse_tools(result: &Value) -> Vec<McpTool> {
    result
        .get("tools")
        .and_then(Value::as_array)
        .map(|arr| {
            arr.iter()
                .filter_map(|t| {
                    Some(McpTool {
                        name: t.get("name")?.as_str()?.to_string(),
                        description: t
                            .get("description")
                            .and_then(Value::as_str)
                            .unwrap_or("")
                            .to_string(),
                        input_schema: t
                            .get("inputSchema")
                            .cloned()
                            .unwrap_or_else(|| json!({ "type": "object" })),
                    })
                })
                .collect()
        })
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

/// Extracts the text content from a `tools/call` result (joining text blocks).
fn result_text(result: &Value) -> String {
    result
        .get("content")
        .and_then(Value::as_array)
        .map(|arr| {
            arr.iter()
                .filter_map(|c| c.get("text").and_then(Value::as_str))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                .join("\n")
        })
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

/// How long to wait for a server to answer one request before giving up on it (a hung server must
/// not hang the query forever).
const REQUEST_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(120);

/// Reads messages from `stdout` on a background thread, forwarding each (or a read error) to the
/// returned channel; the channel closes at EOF. This lets [`Server::request`] wait with a timeout.
fn spawn_reader(stdout: impl Read + Send + 'static) -> Receiver<Result<Value, String>> {
    let (tx, rx) = channel();
    std::thread::spawn(move || {
        let mut reader = BufReader::new(stdout);
        loop {
            match read_message(&mut reader) {
                Ok(Some(msg)) => {
                    if tx.send(Ok(msg)).is_err() {
                        break;
                    }
                }
                Ok(None) => break,
                Err(e) => {
                    // A malformed line is reported but does not end the stream.
                    if tx.send(Err(e)).is_err() {
                        break;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    });
    rx
}

/// A single connected MCP server process and its framed stdio.
struct Server {
    child: Option<Child>,
    stdin: Box<dyn Write + Send>,
    incoming: Receiver<Result<Value, String>>,
    next_id: i64,
    timeout: Duration,
}

impl Server {
    /// Sends a request and returns its `result`. While waiting it answers requests the server
    /// sends us (`ping` → `{}`, anything else → "method not found") and skips notifications, and it
    /// gives up after the request timeout.
    fn request(&mut self, method: &str, params: Value) -> Result<Value, String> {
        let id = self.next_id;
        self.next_id += 1;
        write_message(
            &mut self.stdin,
            &json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": id, "method": method, "params": params }),
        )?;
        let deadline = Instant::now() + self.timeout;
        loop {
            let remaining = deadline.saturating_duration_since(Instant::now());
            let msg = match self.incoming.recv_timeout(remaining) {
                Ok(Ok(msg)) => msg,
                Ok(Err(_)) => continue, // an unparseable line; keep waiting for our answer
                Err(RecvTimeoutError::Timeout) => {
                    return Err(format!(
                        "the MCP server did not answer `{method}` within {}s",
                        self.timeout.as_secs()
                    ));
                }
                Err(RecvTimeoutError::Disconnected) => {
                    return Err("the MCP server closed the connection".into());
                }
            };
            // A request from the server to us (it has both a method and an id): answer it.
            if let (Some(m), Some(req_id)) =
                (msg.get("method").and_then(Value::as_str), msg.get("id"))
            {
                let reply = server_request_reply(m, req_id.clone());
                write_message(&mut self.stdin, &reply)?;
                continue;
            }
            if msg.get("id").and_then(Value::as_i64) == Some(id) {
                if let Some(err) = msg.get("error") {
                    return Err(format!("MCP error: {err}"));
                }
                return Ok(msg.get("result").cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null));
            }
            // Notifications and stray responses are ignored.
        }
    }

    fn notify(&mut self, method: &str, params: Value) -> Result<(), String> {
        write_message(
            &mut self.stdin,
            &json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": method, "params": params }),
        )
    }
}

/// Our reply to a request the server sent us: `ping` succeeds with `{}`; we offer no other client
/// capabilities (sampling, roots, …), so everything else is "method not found".
fn server_request_reply(method: &str, id: Value) -> Value {
    if method == "ping" {
        json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": id, "result": {} })
    } else {
        json!({
            "jsonrpc": "2.0",
            "id": id,
            "error": { "code": -32601, "message": format!("method not found: {method}") }
        })
    }
}

impl Drop for Server {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if let Some(child) = &mut self.child {
            let _ = child.kill();
            let _ = child.wait();
        }
    }
}

/// Spawns one MCP server and performs the handshake, returning it with its tools.
fn connect_one(s: &McpServer) -> Result<(Server, Vec<McpTool>), String> {
    let mut child = Command::new(&s.command)
        .args(&s.args)
        .envs(s.env.iter().cloned())
        .stdin(Stdio::piped())
        .stdout(Stdio::piped())
        .stderr(Stdio::null())
        .spawn()
        .map_err(|e| format!("could not start MCP server `{}`: {e}", s.name))?;
    let stdin = child.stdin.take().ok_or("no stdin")?;
    let stdout: ChildStdout = child.stdout.take().ok_or("no stdout")?;
    let mut server = Server {
        child: Some(child),
        stdin: Box::new(stdin),
        incoming: spawn_reader(stdout),
        next_id: 1,
        timeout: REQUEST_TIMEOUT,
    };
    server.request(
        "initialize",
        json!({
            "protocolVersion": PROTOCOL_VERSION,
            "capabilities": {},
            "clientInfo": { "name": "ORRESS", "version": env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION") }
        }),
    )?;
    server.notify("notifications/initialized", json!({}))?;
    let tools = parse_tools(&server.request("tools/list", json!({}))?);
    Ok((server, tools))
}

/// A set of connected MCP servers and the tools they expose, routing a tool call to its owner.
/// Best-effort: a server that fails to start or handshake is skipped rather than failing the query.
pub struct McpSession {
    servers: Vec<Server>,
    /// Tool name → index into `servers`.
    owner: HashMap<String, usize>,
    tools: Vec<McpTool>,
}

impl McpSession {
    pub fn connect(servers: &[McpServer]) -> Self {
        let mut session = McpSession {
            servers: Vec::new(),
            owner: HashMap::new(),
            tools: Vec::new(),
        };
        for s in servers {
            if let Ok((server, tools)) = connect_one(s) {
                let idx = session.servers.len();
                for t in &tools {
                    session.owner.insert(t.name.clone(), idx);
                }
                session.tools.extend(tools);
                session.servers.push(server);
            }
        }
        session
    }

    pub fn tools(&self) -> &[McpTool] {
        &self.tools
    }

    /// Calls a tool by name, returning its text output.
    pub fn call(&mut self, name: &str, arguments: Value) -> Result<String, String> {
        let idx = *self
            .owner
            .get(name)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("no MCP tool named `{name}`"))?;
        let result = self.servers[idx].request(
            "tools/call",
            json!({ "name": name, "arguments": arguments }),
        )?;
        Ok(result_text(&result))
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::io::Cursor;

    #[test]
    fn framing_round_trips_and_skips_blank_lines() {
        let mut buf = Vec::new();
        write_message(&mut buf, &json!({ "id": 1, "method": "ping" })).unwrap();
        assert!(buf.ends_with(b"\n"));
        // A blank line before the next message is skipped.
        let mut stream = Cursor::new([&buf[..], b"\n", b"{\"id\":2}\n"].concat());
        assert_eq!(
            read_message(&mut stream).unwrap().unwrap()["method"],
            "ping"
        );
        assert_eq!(read_message(&mut stream).unwrap().unwrap()["id"], 2);
        assert!(read_message(&mut stream).unwrap().is_none()); // EOF
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_tools_and_call_results() {
        let listed = json!({
            "tools": [
                { "name": "search", "description": "Search docs",
                  "inputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "q": { "type": "string" } } } },
                { "name": "noschema" }
            ]
        });
        let tools = parse_tools(&listed);
        assert_eq!(tools.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(tools[0].name, "search");
        assert_eq!(tools[0].input_schema["properties"]["q"]["type"], "string");
        // A tool with no inputSchema still gets a valid object schema.
        assert_eq!(tools[1].input_schema, json!({ "type": "object" }));

        let result = json!({ "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": "hello" }, { "type": "text", "text": "world" } ] });
        assert_eq!(result_text(&result), "hello\nworld");
    }

    /// A writer that records what the client sent.
    #[derive(Clone, Default)]
    struct Sink(std::sync::Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Vec<u8>>>);
    impl Write for Sink {
        fn write(&mut self, buf: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<usize> {
            self.0.lock().unwrap().extend_from_slice(buf);
            Ok(buf.len())
        }
        fn flush(&mut self) -> std::io::Result<()> {
            Ok(())
        }
    }

    fn fake_server(script: &str, timeout: Duration) -> (Server, Sink) {
        let sink = Sink::default();
        let server = Server {
            child: None,
            stdin: Box::new(sink.clone()),
            incoming: spawn_reader(Cursor::new(script.as_bytes().to_vec())),
            next_id: 1,
            timeout,
        };
        (server, sink)
    }

    #[test]
    fn answers_server_requests_while_waiting_for_a_response() {
        let script = concat!(
            "{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":\"s1\",\"method\":\"ping\"}\n",
            "{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"method\":\"notifications/progress\"}\n",
            "{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":\"s2\",\"method\":\"sampling/createMessage\"}\n",
            "{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":1,\"result\":{\"ok\":true}}\n",
        );
        let (mut server, sink) = fake_server(script, Duration::from_secs(5));
        assert_eq!(
            server.request("tools/list", json!({})).unwrap(),
            json!({ "ok": true })
        );
        let sent = String::from_utf8(sink.0.lock().unwrap().clone()).unwrap();
        let lines: Vec<Value> = sent
            .lines()
            .map(|l| serde_json::from_str(l).unwrap())
            .collect();
        // Our request, then the ping reply, then the method-not-found error.
        assert_eq!(lines[0]["method"], "tools/list");
        assert_eq!(
            lines[1],
            json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": "s1", "result": {} })
        );
        assert_eq!(lines[2]["id"], "s2");
        assert_eq!(lines[2]["error"]["code"], -32601);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_silent_or_closed_server_errors_instead_of_hanging() {
        // EOF with no answer → closed.
        let (mut server, _) = fake_server("", Duration::from_secs(5));
        assert!(
            server
                .request("x", json!({}))
                .unwrap_err()
                .contains("closed")
        );

        // A server that never answers → timeout (the reader stays open).
        let (tx, rx) = channel();
        let mut server = Server {
            child: None,
            stdin: Box::new(Sink::default()),
            incoming: rx,
            next_id: 1,
            timeout: Duration::from_millis(50),
        };
        let err = server.request("x", json!({})).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("did not answer"), "{err}");
        drop(tx);
    }

    #[test]
    fn tool_schema_conversions_match_each_api() {
        let t = McpTool {
            name: "search".into(),
            description: "Search".into(),
            input_schema: json!({ "type": "object" }),
        };
        let a = to_anthropic_tool(&t);
        assert_eq!(a["name"], "search");
        assert_eq!(a["input_schema"]["type"], "object");

        let o = to_openai_tool(&t);
        assert_eq!(o["type"], "function");
        assert_eq!(o["function"]["name"], "search");
        assert_eq!(o["function"]["parameters"]["type"], "object");
    }
}
```

```rs
#[test]
fn remember_key_controls_persistence() {
    let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("orress_ai_cfg_{}", std::process::id()));
    let path = dir.join("ai.json");

    // remember_key on → the key is written and loads back.
    let cfg = Config {
        provider: Provider::OpenAi,
        model: "m".into(),
        base_url: "http://x/v1".into(),
        remember_key: true,
        api_key: "sk-secret".into(),
    };
    save_config(&path, &cfg).unwrap();
    assert!(
        std::fs::read_to_string(&path)
            .unwrap()
            .contains("sk-secret")
    );
    assert_eq!(load_config(&path).api_key, "sk-secret");

    // remember_key off → the key is stripped from disk.
    let cfg2 = Config {
        remember_key: false,
        ..cfg
    };
    save_config(&path, &cfg2).unwrap();
    assert!(
        !std::fs::read_to_string(&path)
            .unwrap()
            .contains("sk-secret")
    );
    assert_eq!(load_config(&path).api_key, "");

    let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
}

/// A one-shot HTTP server that returns `body` to the first request. Returns its base URL. It reads
/// the *whole* request (headers + Content-Length body) before replying, so the client has finished
/// sending and we don't reset its connection.
fn mock_server(body: &'static str) -> String {
    let listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").unwrap();
    let port = listener.local_addr().unwrap().port();
    std::thread::spawn(move || {
        if let Ok((mut stream, _)) = listener.accept() {
            let mut req: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
            let mut tmp = [0u8; 1024];
            let mut header_end: Option<usize> = None;
            let mut content_len = 0usize;
            loop {
                match stream.read(&mut tmp) {
                    Ok(0) => break,
                    Ok(n) => {
                        req.extend_from_slice(&tmp[..n]);
                        if header_end.is_none()
                            && let Some(pos) = req.windows(4).position(|w| w == b"\r\n\r\n")
                        {
                            header_end = Some(pos + 4);
                            let headers = String::from_utf8_lossy(&req[..pos]).to_ascii_lowercase();
                            if let Some(line) =
                                headers.lines().find(|l| l.starts_with("content-length:"))
                            {
                                content_len = line[15..].trim().parse().unwrap_or(0);
                            }
                        }
                        if let Some(he) = header_end
                            && req.len() >= he + content_len
                        {
                            break;
                        }
                    }
                    Err(_) => break,
                }
            }
            use std::io::Write as _;
            let resp = format!(
                "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n{}",
                body.len(),
                body
            );
            let _ = stream.write_all(resp.as_bytes());
            let _ = stream.flush();
        }
    });
    format!("http://127.0.0.1:{port}")
}

#[test]
fn openai_round_trips_against_a_mock() {
    let base = mock_server(r#"{"choices":[{"message":{"content":"It is an XOR crackme."}}]}"#);
    let out = openai(
        &base,
        Some("test-key".into()),
        "gpt-4o-mini",
        "sys",
        "analyze this",
        &[],
    )
    .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(out, "It is an XOR crackme.");
}
```

```rs
//! Prints the analysis summary and one function of a file:
//! `cargo run -p orress-analysis --example disasm -- FILE [ADDRESS]`

use std::sync::Arc;

use orress_analysis::{Program, TokenKind};

fn main() {
    let mut args = std::env::args().skip(1);
    let path = args.next().expect("usage: disasm FILE [ADDRESS]");
    let data = Arc::new(std::fs::read(&path).expect("readable file"));
    let info = orress_loaders::triage(&data);
    let strings = orress_bytes::strings::extract(&data, 4, 500_000);
    let start = std::time::Instant::now();
    let p = Program::analyze(&info, Arc::clone(&data), &strings).expect("supported architecture");
    println!(
        "{}: {} functions, {} instructions, {} lines, main={:x?} ({:?})",
        path,
        p.functions.len(),
        p.insns.len(),
        p.lines.len(),
        p.main,
        start.elapsed()
    );
    let addr = args
        .next()
        .map(|a| u64::from_str_radix(a.trim_start_matches("0x"), 16).expect("hex address"))
        .or(p.main)
        .or(info.entry)
        .expect("an address");
    let f = p
        .function_containing(addr)
        .expect("a function at that address");
    println!(
        "\n{} ({} blocks)",
        p.name(f.entry).unwrap().text,
        f.blocks.len()
    );
    for block in &f.blocks {
        println!("  -- block {:x} -> {:x?}", block.start, block.succs);
        for &a in &block.insns {
            let insn = p.decode(a).unwrap();
            let ops: String = insn
                .operands
                .iter()
                .map(|t| match t.kind {
                    TokenKind::Address(x) => p.name(x).map_or(t.text.clone(), |n| n.text.clone()),
                    _ => t.text.clone(),
                })
                .collect();
            let comment = insn
                .data_refs
                .iter()
                .find_map(|r| p.string_refs.get(r))
                .map(|s| format!("  ; \"{s}\""))
                .unwrap_or_default();
            println!("  {a:x}  {:<8} {ops}{comment}", insn.mnemonic);
        }
    }
}

```

`crates/orress-analysis/src/dataflow.rs`:

```rs
//! Register dataflow queries over a function's instructions, built on orress-arch's per-instruction
//! register effects ([`orress_arch::reg_info`]).
//!
//! The current analysis is single-static-definition: if a register is defined exactly once in a
//! function, that definition reaches every use, so a loop-invariant pointer (such as a hoisted
//! `lea` of a jump-table or bytecode base) resolves soundly to the constant it holds. This is the
//! foundation a fuller reaching-definitions analysis would extend.

use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};

use orress_arch::{Flow, MemRef, Reg, RegInfo};

use crate::{Function, Program};

/// Registers a call may clobber: the union of the SysV (rax, rcx, rdx, rsi, rdi, r8-r11) and
/// Win64 (rax, rcx, rdx, r8-r11) caller-saved sets, so the analysis stays sound under either ABI.
const CALL_CLOBBERED: [Reg; 9] = [0, 1, 2, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11];

impl Program {
    /// Structured register effects of the instruction at `addr`.
    pub fn reg_info(&self, addr: u64) -> Option<RegInfo> {
        let bytes = self.memory.read(addr, self.isa.max_len())?;
        orress_arch::reg_info(self.isa, bytes, addr)
    }

    /// [`Self::reg_info`] for dataflow: a call also defines every caller-saved register (the
    /// decoder only reports the registers the `call` instruction itself touches).
    fn dataflow_info(&self, addr: u64) -> Option<RegInfo> {
        let mut info = self.reg_info(addr)?;
        let is_call = self
            .memory
            .read(addr, self.isa.max_len())
            .and_then(|bytes| orress_arch::decode(self.isa, bytes, addr))
            .is_some_and(|i| matches!(i.flow, Flow::Call(_) | Flow::IndirectCall { .. }));
        if is_call {
            for r in CALL_CLOBBERED {
                if !info.defs.contains(&r) {
                    info.defs.push(r);
                }
            }
        }
        Some(info)
    }

    /// The memory operand at `addr`, if the instruction has one.
    pub fn mem_ref(&self, addr: u64) -> Option<MemRef> {
        self.reg_info(addr)?.mem
    }

    /// If register `reg` has exactly one definition in `func` and that definition is
    /// `lea reg, [rip+X]`, returns `X`. A single static definition reaches every use, so this
    /// soundly resolves a loop-invariant base register (a hoisted table or bytecode pointer) to
    /// its constant address; a register written more than once (e.g. a loop counter) returns `None`.
    pub fn register_const(&self, func: &Function, reg: u8) -> Option<u64> {
        let mut defs = 0usize;
        let mut addr = None;
        for block in &func.blocks {
            for &a in &block.insns {
                let Some(info) = self.dataflow_info(a) else {
                    continue;
                };
                if info.defs.contains(&reg) {
                    defs += 1;
                    addr = info.lea_const.and_then(|(d, x)| (d == reg).then_some(x));
                }
            }
        }
        (defs == 1).then_some(addr).flatten()
    }

    /// The smallest address referenced as data anywhere in the program that is strictly greater
    /// than `after` — i.e. where the datum starting at `after` ends, bounded by the next referenced
    /// one. Used to size a blob (a jump table, a bytecode array) without a length in the code.
    pub fn next_data_ref(&self, after: u64) -> Option<u64> {
        self.data_refs
            .range(after.checked_add(1)?..)
            .next()
            .copied()
    }

    /// Reaching-definition variant of [`Self::register_const`]: if every definition of `reg` that
    /// can reach the instruction at `use_addr` is the same `lea reg, [rip+X]`, returns `X`.
    ///
    /// Unlike the whole-function version this ignores definitions that cannot reach the use — e.g.
    /// a base register reloaded with junk only on error/panic paths that lead to `exit`, never back
    /// to the use. A definition reaches the use if its block can reach the use's block in the CFG.
    pub fn register_const_at(&self, func: &Function, use_addr: u64, reg: u8) -> Option<u64> {
        let use_block = func
            .blocks
            .iter()
            .find(|b| b.insns.contains(&use_addr))?
            .start;
        let mut preds: HashMap<u64, Vec<u64>> = HashMap::new();
        for b in &func.blocks {
            for e in &b.succs {
                preds.entry(e.target).or_default().push(b.start);
            }
        }
        // Blocks that can reach the use (its predecessors, transitively) plus the use's own block.
        let mut reachers = HashSet::from([use_block]);
        let mut stack = vec![use_block];
        while let Some(n) = stack.pop() {
            for &p in preds.get(&n).into_iter().flatten() {
                if reachers.insert(p) {
                    stack.push(p);
                }
            }
        }
        let mut addr = None;
        let mut defs = 0usize;
        for block in func.blocks.iter().filter(|b| reachers.contains(&b.start)) {
            for &a in &block.insns {
                let Some(info) = self.dataflow_info(a) else {
                    continue;
                };
                if info.defs.contains(&reg) {
                    let this = info.lea_const.and_then(|(d, x)| (d == reg).then_some(x));
                    if defs == 0 {
                        addr = this;
                    } else if addr != this {
                        addr = None;
                    }
                    defs += 1;
                }
            }
        }
        (defs >= 1).then_some(addr).flatten()
    }
}

```

`crates/orress-analysis/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! Code analysis: finds functions, splits them into basic blocks, builds control-flow
//! graphs and cross-references, names things, and lays out the linear listing.
//!
//! The approach is recursive descent: start at known function entries (entry point,
//! symbols, exports, exception tables), follow every jump and call, and treat each call
//! target as a new function. Code that is never reached this way is shown as data.

mod dataflow;
mod listing;
mod main_finder;
mod memory;

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet, HashMap, HashSet};
use std::sync::Arc;

pub use listing::{Line, LineKind};
pub use memory::Memory;
pub use orress_arch::{Flow, Insn, Isa, Token, TokenKind};
use orress_bytes::strings::FoundString;
use orress_loaders::BinaryInfo;

/// Stop exploring a single function after this many instructions (obfuscated or
/// misidentified code can otherwise run away).
const MAX_FUNCTION_INSNS: usize = 200_000;
/// Overall cap on discovered functions.
const MAX_FUNCTIONS: usize = 200_000;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum EdgeKind {
    /// Unconditional jump.
    Jump,
    /// Conditional jump, taken (condition true).
    Taken,
    /// Conditional jump not taken: execution falls through to the next block.
    NotTaken,
    /// Plain fall-through into a block that starts because something jumps there.
    FallThrough,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Edge {
    pub target: u64,
    pub kind: EdgeKind,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Block {
    pub start: u64,
    /// Address after the last instruction.
    pub end: u64,
    pub insns: Vec<u64>,
    pub succs: Vec<Edge>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum FunctionKind {
    Normal,
    /// A stub that only jumps to an imported function (PLT entry, import thunk).
    Thunk,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Function {
    pub entry: u64,
    pub kind: FunctionKind,
    /// Blocks in address order; the entry block is the one starting at `entry`.
    pub blocks: Vec<Block>,
    /// Direct call targets.
    pub calls: Vec<u64>,
}

impl Function {
    pub fn size(&self) -> u64 {
        self.blocks.iter().map(|b| b.end - b.start).sum()
    }

    pub fn insn_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.blocks.iter().map(|b| b.insns.len()).sum()
    }

    pub fn block_at(&self, addr: u64) -> Option<&Block> {
        self.blocks.iter().find(|b| addr >= b.start && addr < b.end)
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum XrefKind {
    Call,
    Jump,
    /// Reads or takes the address of data (strings, globals, import slots).
    Data,
}

impl XrefKind {
    pub fn label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Call => "call",
            Self::Jump => "jump",
            Self::Data => "data",
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct Xref {
    /// Address of the referring instruction.
    pub from: u64,
    pub kind: XrefKind,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum NameKind {
    /// From the file's symbol table or exports.
    Symbol,
    /// An imported function (its import slot or a thunk to it).
    Import,
    /// Found by ORRESS (entry point, main).
    Detected,
    /// Generated: sub_401000.
    Auto,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Name {
    pub text: String,
    pub kind: NameKind,
}

/// The analyzed program.
pub struct Program {
    pub isa: Isa,
    pub memory: Memory,
    pub functions: BTreeMap<u64, Function>,
    /// Every decoded instruction: address -> length.
    pub insns: BTreeMap<u64, u8>,
    /// Block starts that are jump targets (for `loc_` labels).
    pub labels: BTreeSet<u64>,
    pub xrefs_to: HashMap<u64, Vec<Xref>>,
    /// Every address referenced as data by any instruction, program-wide. Sorted, so a jump-table
    /// read can find the next referenced datum after a table's base and stop before it — even when
    /// that datum (e.g. an adjacent table) belongs to a different function.
    data_refs: BTreeSet<u64>,
    pub names: HashMap<u64, Name>,
    /// Recovered `switch` jump tables: the address of the indirect `jmp` -> its case targets in
    /// slot (index) order, duplicates kept. The CFG edges are de-duplicated, so this is the source
    /// of truth for a decompiler that needs the exact index-to-case mapping.
    pub switch_tables: HashMap<u64, Vec<u64>>,
    /// Text of strings referenced by code, by address, for inline comments.
    pub string_refs: HashMap<u64, String>,
    pub main: Option<u64>,
    pub lines: Vec<Line>,
}

impl Program {
    /// Analyzes the code of a triaged binary. Returns `None` for architectures ORRESS
    /// cannot disassemble yet.
    pub fn analyze(info: &BinaryInfo, data: Arc<Vec<u8>>, strings: &[FoundString]) -> Option<Self> {
        let isa = Isa::from_arch_name(&info.arch)?;
        let memory = Memory::new(info, data);
        let mut p = Self {
            isa,
            memory,
            functions: BTreeMap::new(),
            insns: BTreeMap::new(),
            labels: BTreeSet::new(),
            xrefs_to: HashMap::new(),
            data_refs: BTreeSet::new(),
            switch_tables: HashMap::new(),
            names: HashMap::new(),
            string_refs: HashMap::new(),
            main: None,
            lines: Vec::new(),
        };
        p.seed_names(info);
        let imports: HashMap<u64, String> = info
            .import_slots
            .iter()
            .map(|s| (s.address, s.name.clone()))
            .collect();

        // Function entries, most trustworthy first.
        let mut seeds: Vec<u64> = Vec::new();
        seeds.extend(info.entry);
        seeds.extend(info.function_symbols.iter().map(|s| s.address));
        seeds.extend(info.exports.iter().map(|e| e.address).filter(|&a| a != 0));
        seeds.extend(info.function_starts.iter().copied());
        let known_entries: HashSet<u64> = seeds.iter().copied().collect();

        p.explore(seeds.clone(), &known_entries, &imports);
        if let Some(main) = main_finder::find_main(&p, info) {
            p.main = Some(main);
            if !p.functions.contains_key(&main) {
                p.explore(vec![main], &known_entries, &imports);
            }
            let named = p
                .names
                .get(&main)
                .is_some_and(|n| n.kind == NameKind::Symbol);
            if !named {
                p.names.insert(
                    main,
                    Name {
                        text: main_finder::main_name(&p).into(),
                        kind: NameKind::Detected,
                    },
                );
            }
            // Rust: the C-level main only hands the real `main` to the runtime.
            if let Some(user_main) = main_finder::rust_user_main(&p, info, main) {
                if !p.functions.contains_key(&user_main) {
                    p.explore(vec![user_main], &known_entries, &imports);
                }
                if p.names
                    .get(&main)
                    .is_some_and(|n| n.kind != NameKind::Symbol)
                {
                    p.names.insert(
                        main,
                        Name {
                            text: "rust_runtime_main".into(),
                            kind: NameKind::Detected,
                        },
                    );
                }
                if p.names
                    .get(&user_main)
                    .is_none_or(|n| n.kind != NameKind::Symbol)
                {
                    p.names.insert(
                        user_main,
                        Name {
                            text: "main".into(),
                            kind: NameKind::Detected,
                        },
                    );
                }
                p.main = Some(user_main);
            }
        }
        p.name_functions();
        p.collect_string_refs(info, strings);
        p.lines = listing::build(&p, info);
        Some(p)
    }

    fn seed_names(&mut self, info: &BinaryInfo) {
        for slot in &info.import_slots {
            self.names.insert(
                slot.address,
                Name {
                    text: slot.name.clone(),
                    kind: NameKind::Import,
                },
            );
        }
        for sym in &info.function_symbols {
            self.names.insert(
                sym.address,
                Name {
                    text: sym.name.clone(),
                    kind: NameKind::Symbol,
                },
            );
        }
        for export in info.exports.iter().filter(|e| e.address != 0) {
            self.names.entry(export.address).or_insert(Name {
                text: export.name.clone(),
                kind: NameKind::Symbol,
            });
        }
        if let Some(entry) = info.entry {
            self.names.entry(entry).or_insert(Name {
                text: "entry".into(),
                kind: NameKind::Detected,
            });
        }
    }

    fn add_xref(&mut self, to: u64, from: u64, kind: XrefKind) {
        let list = self.xrefs_to.entry(to).or_default();
        let xref = Xref { from, kind };
        if !list.contains(&xref) {
            list.push(xref);
        }
    }

    fn explore(
        &mut self,
        seeds: Vec<u64>,
        known_entries: &HashSet<u64>,
        imports: &HashMap<u64, String>,
    ) {
        let mut queue: Vec<u64> = seeds;
        queue.reverse();
        while let Some(entry) = queue.pop() {
            if self.functions.len() >= MAX_FUNCTIONS {
                break;
            }
            if self.functions.contains_key(&entry) || !self.memory.is_code(entry) {
                continue;
            }
            if let Some(function) = self.explore_function(entry, known_entries, imports) {
                for &target in function.calls.iter().rev() {
                    if !self.functions.contains_key(&target) {
                        queue.push(target);
                    }
                }
                // Tail calls: jumps out of this function to other function entries.
                self.functions.insert(entry, function);
            }
        }
    }

    /// Reads a jump table's target addresses, in slot order, stopping at the first entry that
    /// is not a valid code address (a heuristic bound for a dense `switch` table).
    fn read_jump_table(&self, base: u64, entry: u8) -> Vec<u64> {
        const MAX_SWITCH_CASES: usize = 1024;
        let mut targets = Vec::new();
        let mut slot = base;
        for _ in 0..MAX_SWITCH_CASES {
            let Some(bytes) = self.memory.read(slot, entry as usize) else {
                break;
            };
            // A slot cut short by the end of its region is not a table entry.
            let target = match (entry, bytes.len()) {
                (8, 8) => u64::from_le_bytes(bytes.try_into().expect("8 bytes")),
                (4, 4) => u64::from(u32::from_le_bytes(bytes.try_into().expect("4 bytes"))),
                _ => break,
            };
            if !self.memory.is_code(target) {
                break;
            }
            targets.push(target);
            let Some(next) = slot.checked_add(u64::from(entry)) else {
                break;
            };
            slot = next;
        }
        targets
    }

    /// Reads up to `max_cases` entries of an *offset-based* jump table — the form 64-bit compilers
    /// (LLVM, MSVC) emit for a position-independent `switch`: each 4-byte entry is a signed offset
    /// added to the table's own base (`.long case - table`). Stops early at the first entry that is
    /// not a code address. The cap is essential: unlike an absolute table, a random offset near the
    /// base often lands in `.text`, so without a bound the read runs away.
    fn read_offset_jump_table(&self, base: u64, max_cases: usize) -> Vec<u64> {
        let mut targets = Vec::new();
        let mut slot = base;
        for _ in 0..max_cases {
            let Some(bytes) = self.memory.read(slot, 4) else {
                break;
            };
            let Ok(bytes) = <[u8; 4]>::try_from(bytes) else {
                break; // cut short by the end of the region
            };
            let offset = i64::from(i32::from_le_bytes(bytes));
            let target = base.wrapping_add(offset as u64);
            if !self.memory.is_code(target) {
                break;
            }
            targets.push(target);
            let Some(next) = slot.checked_add(4) else {
                break;
            };
            slot = next;
        }
        targets
    }

    /// Recovers the targets of a register-indirect `jmp` that implements a `switch` through an
    /// offset table: `cmp idx, N; ja default; … lea base, [rip+table]; …; jmp reg`.
    ///
    /// The safe bound is the key. The **case count** comes from the range check in the contiguous
    /// run just before the jump: either `cmp idx, N` (`N + 1` cases) or a `and idx, MASK` that masks
    /// the index to a power-of-two range (`MASK + 1` cases). The **table base** is a `lea [rip+table]`
    /// somewhere in the function — often hoisted out of the loop, so we look across the whole decoded
    /// function, not just the run. A base is accepted only when reading exactly `N + 1` entries
    /// yields that many code targets, which both bounds the read and validates the base: a random
    /// `lea` almost never produces exactly the predicted number of consecutive code offsets. If the
    /// range check or a matching table is not found, nothing is recovered (never an unbounded read).
    fn offset_table_targets(&self, decoded: &BTreeMap<u64, Insn>, jmp_addr: u64) -> Vec<u64> {
        /// A switch's case count is small; a larger `cmp` immediate is not a range check.
        const MAX_CASES: usize = 512;
        const WINDOW: usize = 32;

        // The range check: the nearest `cmp idx, N` with a small immediate, in the run before the
        // jump (crossing block boundaries by address, since the check sits just above the dispatch).
        let mut cases = None;
        let mut cursor = jmp_addr;
        for _ in 0..WINDOW {
            let Some((&prev, insn)) = decoded.range(..cursor).next_back() else {
                break;
            };
            if prev + u64::from(insn.len) != cursor {
                break;
            }
            // `cmp idx, N; ja` guards the jump (valid 0..=N, so N + 1 cases). `and idx, MASK` masks
            // the index into a power-of-two range (valid 0..=MASK, so MASK + 1 cases).
            if insn.mnemonic == "cmp"
                && let Some(n) = last_number(&insn.operands)
                && n as usize <= MAX_CASES
            {
                cases = Some(n as usize + 1);
                break;
            }
            if insn.mnemonic == "and"
                && let Some(mask) = last_number(&insn.operands)
                && mask as usize <= MAX_CASES
                && (mask + 1).is_power_of_two()
            {
                cases = Some(mask as usize + 1);
                break;
            }
            cursor = prev;
        }
        // Candidate table bases: `lea [rip+table]` into read-only data, anywhere in the function
        // (the base is often hoisted out of the dispatch loop).
        let mut bases: Vec<u64> = decoded
            .values()
            .filter(|i| i.mnemonic == "lea")
            .flat_map(|i| i.data_refs.iter().copied())
            .filter(|&b| !self.memory.is_code(b))
            .collect();
        bases.sort_unstable();
        bases.dedup();

        if let Some(cases) = cases.filter(|&c| c >= 2) {
            // With a range check, accept a base only when reading exactly `cases` entries yields
            // that many code targets — this both bounds the read and validates the base.
            for &base in &bases {
                let targets = self.read_offset_jump_table(base, cases);
                if targets.len() == cases {
                    return targets;
                }
            }
            return Vec::new();
        }

        // No range check (an exhaustive `switch`, where the compiler proved the index in range). We
        // have no case count, so bound the table by the next referenced data address after its base
        // — an adjacent table's base is itself referenced, so this stops before it — and by the
        // first non-code entry. A real base yields a run of code offsets; unrelated data almost never
        // does, so we require several before trusting it.
        const NO_CHECK_CAP: usize = 256;
        const MIN_NO_CHECK: usize = 3;
        for &base in &bases {
            // Stop at the next referenced datum after the base — program-wide, so an adjacent table
            // owned by *any* function bounds this one; also include this function's own refs for the
            // parts not yet added to the program-wide set.
            let next = self
                .data_refs
                .range(base.saturating_add(1)..)
                .next()
                .copied()
                .into_iter()
                .chain(
                    decoded
                        .values()
                        .flat_map(|i| i.data_refs.iter().copied())
                        .filter(|&d| d > base),
                )
                .min();
            let cap = next
                .map(|n| ((n - base) / 4) as usize)
                .unwrap_or(NO_CHECK_CAP)
                .min(NO_CHECK_CAP);
            if cap < MIN_NO_CHECK {
                continue;
            }
            let targets = self.read_offset_jump_table(base, cap);
            if targets.len() >= MIN_NO_CHECK {
                return targets;
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }

    fn explore_function(
        &mut self,
        entry: u64,
        known_entries: &HashSet<u64>,
        imports: &HashMap<u64, String>,
    ) -> Option<Function> {
        // Pass 1: find every instruction reachable inside the function, and the leaders
        // (addresses that start a basic block).
        let mut leaders: BTreeSet<u64> = BTreeSet::from([entry]);
        let mut decoded: BTreeMap<u64, Insn> = BTreeMap::new();
        let mut work = vec![entry];
        let mut calls = Vec::new();
        while let Some(mut addr) = work.pop() {
            loop {
                if decoded.contains_key(&addr) || decoded.len() >= MAX_FUNCTION_INSNS {
                    break;
                }
                let Some(insn) = self.decode(addr) else {
                    break;
                };
                let next = insn.end();
                let flow = insn.flow;
                for &r in &insn.data_refs {
                    if self.memory.contains(r) || imports.contains_key(&r) {
                        self.add_xref(r, addr, XrefKind::Data);
                    }
                    if self.memory.contains(r) {
                        self.data_refs.insert(r);
                    }
                }
                match flow {
                    Flow::Call(t) => {
                        self.add_xref(t, addr, XrefKind::Call);
                        if self.memory.is_code(t) {
                            calls.push(t);
                        }
                    }
                    Flow::IndirectCall { slot: Some(s) }
                    | Flow::IndirectJump { slot: Some(s), .. } => {
                        let kind = if matches!(flow, Flow::IndirectCall { .. }) {
                            XrefKind::Call
                        } else {
                            XrefKind::Jump
                        };
                        self.add_xref(s, addr, kind);
                    }
                    // A `switch` jump table: read its targets so their blocks are discovered.
                    Flow::IndirectJump { table: Some(t), .. } => {
                        let targets = self.read_jump_table(t.base, t.entry);
                        if !targets.is_empty() {
                            self.switch_tables.insert(addr, targets.clone());
                        }
                        for tg in targets {
                            self.add_xref(tg, addr, XrefKind::Jump);
                            if self.memory.is_code(tg) {
                                leaders.insert(tg);
                                work.push(tg);
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    // A register-indirect `jmp` may be a bounded `switch` through an offset table
                    // (`cmp idx,N; ja default; lea base,[rip+table]; jmp reg`): recover its targets.
                    Flow::IndirectJump {
                        slot: None,
                        table: None,
                    } => {
                        let targets = self.offset_table_targets(&decoded, addr);
                        if !targets.is_empty() {
                            self.switch_tables.insert(addr, targets.clone());
                        }
                        for tg in targets {
                            self.add_xref(tg, addr, XrefKind::Jump);
                            leaders.insert(tg);
                            work.push(tg);
                        }
                    }
                    Flow::Jump(t) | Flow::CondJump(t) => {
                        self.add_xref(t, addr, XrefKind::Jump);
                        // A jump to another function's entry is a tail call, not part of
                        // this function.
                        let tail_call = t != entry
                            && (known_entries.contains(&t) || self.functions.contains_key(&t));
                        if self.memory.is_code(t) && !tail_call {
                            leaders.insert(t);
                            work.push(t);
                        } else if tail_call && !calls.contains(&t) {
                            calls.push(t);
                        }
                    }
                    _ => {}
                }
                decoded.insert(addr, insn);
                if flow.ends_block() && flow.falls_through() {
                    leaders.insert(next);
                }
                if !flow.falls_through() {
                    break;
                }
                addr = next;
            }
        }
        if decoded.is_empty() {
            return None;
        }

        // Pass 2: cut the instructions into blocks at the leaders.
        // Edges only go to leaders that decoded into a block: a leader whose bytes failed to decode
        // (or lie outside the image) would otherwise leave a dangling edge.
        let is_block = |a: u64| leaders.contains(&a) && decoded.contains_key(&a);
        let mut blocks = Vec::new();
        for &leader in &leaders {
            if !decoded.contains_key(&leader) {
                continue;
            }
            let mut block = Block {
                start: leader,
                end: leader,
                insns: Vec::new(),
                succs: Vec::new(),
            };
            let mut addr = leader;
            while let Some(insn) = decoded.get(&addr) {
                block.insns.push(addr);
                block.end = insn.end();
                let next = insn.end();
                match insn.flow {
                    Flow::Jump(t) => {
                        if is_block(t) {
                            block.succs.push(Edge {
                                target: t,
                                kind: EdgeKind::Jump,
                            });
                        }
                        break;
                    }
                    Flow::CondJump(t) => {
                        if is_block(t) {
                            block.succs.push(Edge {
                                target: t,
                                kind: EdgeKind::Taken,
                            });
                        }
                        if decoded.contains_key(&next) {
                            block.succs.push(Edge {
                                target: next,
                                kind: EdgeKind::NotTaken,
                            });
                        }
                        break;
                    }
                    Flow::IndirectJump { table: Some(t), .. } => {
                        let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
                        for tg in self.read_jump_table(t.base, t.entry) {
                            if is_block(tg) && seen.insert(tg) {
                                block.succs.push(Edge {
                                    target: tg,
                                    kind: EdgeKind::Jump,
                                });
                            }
                        }
                        break;
                    }
                    Flow::IndirectJump {
                        slot: None,
                        table: None,
                    } => {
                        let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
                        for tg in self.offset_table_targets(&decoded, addr) {
                            if is_block(tg) && seen.insert(tg) {
                                block.succs.push(Edge {
                                    target: tg,
                                    kind: EdgeKind::Jump,
                                });
                            }
                        }
                        break;
                    }
                    f if !f.falls_through() => break,
                    _ => {}
                }
                if is_block(next) {
                    block.succs.push(Edge {
                        target: next,
                        kind: EdgeKind::FallThrough,
                    });
                    break;
                }
                addr = next;
            }
            blocks.push(block);
        }

        for block in &blocks {
            if block.start != entry {
                self.labels.insert(block.start);
            }
        }
        for (addr, insn) in &decoded {
            self.insns.insert(*addr, insn.len);
        }

        // A function that is a single indirect jump through an import slot is a thunk.
        let first = decoded.get(&entry)?;
        let kind = match first.flow {
            Flow::IndirectJump { slot: Some(s), .. }
                if imports.contains_key(&s) && decoded.len() <= 2 =>
            {
                let name = &imports[&s];
                let text = if self.memory.is_elf {
                    format!("{name}@plt")
                } else {
                    name.clone()
                };
                self.names.entry(entry).or_insert(Name {
                    text,
                    kind: NameKind::Import,
                });
                FunctionKind::Thunk
            }
            _ => FunctionKind::Normal,
        };

        calls.sort_unstable();
        calls.dedup();
        Some(Function {
            entry,
            kind,
            blocks,
            calls,
        })
    }

    fn name_functions(&mut self) {
        for &entry in self.functions.keys() {
            self.names.entry(entry).or_insert_with(|| Name {
                text: format!("sub_{entry:x}"),
                kind: NameKind::Auto,
            });
        }
    }

    fn collect_string_refs(&mut self, info: &BinaryInfo, strings: &[FoundString]) {
        // (address, string), sorted, to also find references into the middle of a
        // string: Rust stores string literals back to back without zero bytes, so
        // "Password: Wrong password" can be two strings.
        let mut by_address: Vec<(u64, &FoundString)> = strings
            .iter()
            .filter(|s| s.encoding == orress_bytes::strings::Encoding::Ascii)
            .filter_map(|s| Some((info.offset_to_address(s.offset as u64)?, s)))
            .collect();
        by_address.sort_by_key(|(a, _)| *a);
        for &target in self.xrefs_to.keys() {
            let i = by_address.partition_point(|(a, _)| *a <= target);
            let Some(&(start, s)) = i.checked_sub(1).and_then(|i| by_address.get(i)) else {
                continue;
            };
            let skip = (target - start) as usize;
            if skip < s.byte_len {
                self.string_refs.insert(target, s.text[skip..].to_owned());
            }
        }
    }

    /// Decodes the instruction at `addr` from the file's bytes.
    pub fn decode(&self, addr: u64) -> Option<Insn> {
        let bytes = self.memory.read(addr, self.isa.max_len())?;
        orress_arch::decode(self.isa, bytes, addr)
    }

    pub fn name(&self, addr: u64) -> Option<&Name> {
        self.names.get(&addr)
    }

    /// The function whose blocks contain `addr` (the innermost by entry if several).
    pub fn function_containing(&self, addr: u64) -> Option<&Function> {
        if let Some(f) = self.functions.get(&addr) {
            return Some(f);
        }
        self.functions
            .range(..=addr)
            .rev()
            .take(64)
            .map(|(_, f)| f)
            .find(|f| f.block_at(addr).is_some())
            .or_else(|| self.functions.values().find(|f| f.block_at(addr).is_some()))
    }

    /// Start of the instruction containing `addr`, if `addr` is inside decoded code.
    pub fn insn_start(&self, addr: u64) -> Option<u64> {
        let (&start, &len) = self.insns.range(..=addr).next_back()?;
        (addr < start.saturating_add(u64::from(len))).then_some(start)
    }

    pub fn xrefs(&self, addr: u64) -> &[Xref] {
        self.xrefs_to.get(&addr).map_or(&[], Vec::as_slice)
    }

    /// Index of the listing line for `addr` (the instruction line if there is one).
    pub fn line_index(&self, addr: u64) -> Option<usize> {
        listing::find(&self.lines, addr)
    }
}

/// The last numeric-literal operand of an instruction (e.g. the immediate of `cmp idx, N`).
/// Numbers are formatted in hex, like the rest of the disassembly.
fn last_number(operands: &[Token]) -> Option<u64> {
    operands
        .iter()
        .rev()
        .find(|t| t.kind == TokenKind::Number)
        .and_then(|t| u64::from_str_radix(t.text.trim_start_matches("0x"), 16).ok())
}
```

`crates/orress-analysis/src/listing.rs`:

```rs
//! The linear disassembly listing: every byte of the executable regions, in address
//! order, as function headers, labels, instructions or raw data.

use orress_loaders::BinaryInfo;

use crate::Program;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum LineKind {
    /// Start of an executable region.
    Region,
    /// Blank separator plus the function name.
    Function,
    /// `loc_401020:` jump target inside a function.
    Label,
    Insn,
    /// Bytes that are not decoded code (`db` line), with their count.
    Data(u8),
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Line {
    pub addr: u64,
    pub kind: LineKind,
}

const DATA_PER_LINE: u64 = 8;

pub fn build(p: &Program, _info: &BinaryInfo) -> Vec<Line> {
    let mut lines = Vec::new();
    for region in p.memory.regions.iter().filter(|r| r.executable) {
        lines.push(Line {
            addr: region.start,
            kind: LineKind::Region,
        });
        let end = region.start.saturating_add(region.len);
        let mut addr = region.start;
        while addr < end {
            if p.functions.contains_key(&addr) {
                lines.push(Line {
                    addr,
                    kind: LineKind::Function,
                });
            } else if p.labels.contains(&addr) {
                lines.push(Line {
                    addr,
                    kind: LineKind::Label,
                });
            }
            if let Some(&len) = p.insns.get(&addr) {
                lines.push(Line {
                    addr,
                    kind: LineKind::Insn,
                });
                addr += u64::from(len.max(1));
                continue;
            }
            // Data up to the next instruction or line boundary.
            let next_code = p.insns.range(addr + 1..).next().map_or(end, |(&a, _)| a);
            let aligned = (addr / DATA_PER_LINE + 1) * DATA_PER_LINE;
            let stop = next_code.min(aligned).min(end);
            lines.push(Line {
                addr,
                kind: LineKind::Data((stop - addr) as u8),
            });
            addr = stop;
        }
    }
    lines
}

/// Index of the line showing `addr`: the last line starting at or before it. Header and
/// label lines come before the instruction at the same address, so this is the
/// instruction (or data) line.
pub fn find(lines: &[Line], addr: u64) -> Option<usize> {
    lines.partition_point(|l| l.addr <= addr).checked_sub(1)
}
```

`crates/orress-analysis/src/main_finder.rs`:

```rs
//! Finding `main`. The entry point of a C program is runtime start-up code, not the
//! programmer's main function. Recognizing the start-up pattern saves beginners from
//! getting lost in it.

use orress_loaders::BinaryInfo;

use crate::{Flow, NameKind, Program};

pub fn find_main(p: &Program, info: &BinaryInfo) -> Option<u64> {
    // A symbol named main wins.
    if let Some((&addr, _)) = p
        .names
        .iter()
        .find(|(_, n)| n.kind == NameKind::Symbol && (n.text == "main" || n.text == "_main"))
    {
        return Some(addr);
    }
    info.entry
        .and_then(|entry| libc_start_main(p, entry))
        .or_else(|| msvc_main(p).map(|(addr, _)| addr))
}

/// Rust programs have a small C-level `main` that passes the address of the real
/// `main` to the standard library's start-up code (`std::rt::lang_start`). Returns
/// that address when `c_main` looks like this shim.
pub fn rust_user_main(p: &Program, info: &BinaryInfo, c_main: u64) -> Option<u64> {
    let is_rust = info.detections.iter().any(|d| d.name == "Rust");
    if !is_rust {
        return None;
    }
    let mut addr = c_main;
    for _ in 0..24 {
        let insn = p.decode(addr)?;
        if matches!(
            insn.mnemonic.as_str(),
            "lea" | "mov" | "adrp" | "adr" | "add"
        ) && let Some(&target) = insn
            .data_refs
            .iter()
            .find(|&&r| p.memory.is_code(r) && r != c_main)
        {
            return Some(target);
        }
        if !insn.flow.falls_through() {
            return None;
        }
        addr = insn.end();
    }
    None
}

fn is_thunk(p: &Program, addr: u64) -> bool {
    p.functions
        .get(&addr)
        .is_some_and(|f| f.kind == crate::FunctionKind::Thunk)
}

/// Instructions that call an import, directly through its slot or through a stub
/// (`jmp [slot]`) that the compiler placed in between.
fn call_sites(p: &Program, slot: u64) -> Vec<u64> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for xref in p.xrefs(slot) {
        if is_thunk(p, xref.from) {
            out.extend(p.xrefs(xref.from).iter().map(|x| x.from));
        } else {
            out.push(xref.from);
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Name for the detected main: `WinMain` for GUI programs, `main` otherwise.
pub fn main_name(p: &Program) -> &'static str {
    match msvc_main(p) {
        Some((_, true)) => "WinMain",
        _ => "main",
    }
}

/// MSVC C runtime: `invoke_main` fetches argc/argv (or the WinMain command line) from
/// the CRT DLL right before calling main, so the first direct call after those
/// imports is main. Returns the address and whether it is WinMain.
fn msvc_main(p: &Program) -> Option<(u64, bool)> {
    const ARGS: [&str; 4] = [
        "__p___argc",
        "__p___argv",
        "__p___wargv",
        "_get_initial_narrow_environment",
    ];
    const WINMAIN: [&str; 2] = [
        "_get_wide_winmain_command_line",
        "_get_narrow_winmain_command_line",
    ];
    for (&slot, name) in p.names.iter().filter(|(_, n)| n.kind == NameKind::Import) {
        let crt = crt_name(&name.text);
        let winmain = WINMAIN.contains(&crt);
        if !winmain && !ARGS.contains(&crt) {
            continue;
        }
        for from in call_sites(p, slot) {
            let Some(mut addr) = p.decode(from).map(|i| i.end()) else {
                continue;
            };
            for _ in 0..16 {
                let Some(insn) = p.decode(addr) else {
                    break;
                };
                match insn.flow {
                    Flow::Call(target) if p.memory.is_code(target) && !is_thunk(p, target) => {
                        return Some((target, winmain));
                    }
                    f if !f.falls_through() => break,
                    _ => {}
                }
                addr = insn.end();
            }
        }
    }
    exit_after_main(p).map(|addr| (addr, false))
}

/// Older and other C runtimes: `exit(main(argc, argv, envp))`. The last direct call
/// shortly before the call to `exit` is main.
fn exit_after_main(p: &Program) -> Option<u64> {
    for (&slot, _) in p.names.iter().filter(|(_, n)| {
        n.kind == NameKind::Import && matches!(crt_name(&n.text), "exit" | "_exit" | "_cexit")
    }) {
        for from in call_sites(p, slot) {
            let Some(function) = p.function_containing(from) else {
                continue;
            };
            let mut insns: Vec<u64> = function
                .blocks
                .iter()
                .flat_map(|b| b.insns.iter().copied())
                .collect();
            insns.sort_unstable();
            let Some(at) = insns.iter().position(|&a| a == from) else {
                continue;
            };
            let found = insns[at.saturating_sub(8)..at].iter().rev().find_map(|&a| {
                match p.decode(a)?.flow {
                    Flow::Call(t)
                        if p.memory.is_code(t)
                            && p.functions.get(&t).is_some_and(|f| f.insn_count() > 3) =>
                    {
                        Some(t)
                    }
                    _ => None,
                }
            });
            if found.is_some() {
                return found;
            }
        }
    }
    None
}

/// glibc start-up: `_start` loads the address of main into the first argument register
/// (rdi on x86-64, a push on 32-bit x86, x0 on ARM64) and calls __libc_start_main.
fn libc_start_main(p: &Program, entry: u64) -> Option<u64> {
    let mut candidate = None;
    // ARM64 `adrp x0, page`: the page base itself need not be code (it can lie below `.text`);
    // only the full address after the following `add` is validated.
    let mut page = None;
    let mut addr = entry;
    for _ in 0..40 {
        let insn = p.decode(addr)?;
        let ops = insn.text();
        let to_x0 = ops.contains(" x0,");
        // Track the last address-like value placed where main's address goes.
        let first_arg = matches!(insn.mnemonic.as_str(), "lea" | "mov")
            && (ops.contains(" rdi,") || ops.contains(" edi,"))
            || insn.mnemonic == "push"
            || (insn.mnemonic == "adr" && to_x0);
        if first_arg && let Some(&r) = insn.data_refs.first().filter(|&&r| p.memory.is_code(r)) {
            candidate = Some(r);
        }
        if insn.mnemonic == "adrp" && to_x0 {
            page = insn.data_refs.first().copied();
        }
        if insn.mnemonic == "add" && to_x0 {
            // ARM64: adrp x0, page; add x0, x0, #off
            if let (Some(pg), Some(off)) = (
                page.take(),
                insn.operands.last().and_then(|t| parse_imm(&t.text)),
            ) {
                candidate = pg.checked_add(off).filter(|&c| p.memory.is_code(c));
            }
        }
        // ARM64 `ldr x0, =main`: a PC-relative load of main's address from a literal pool.
        if insn.mnemonic == "ldr"
            && to_x0
            && let Some(&lit) = insn.data_refs.first()
            && let Some(bytes) = p.memory.read(lit, 8)
            && let Ok(bytes) = <[u8; 8]>::try_from(bytes)
        {
            let value = u64::from_le_bytes(bytes);
            if p.memory.is_code(value) {
                candidate = Some(value);
            }
        }
        let calls_start_main = match insn.flow {
            Flow::Call(t) => p
                .name(t)
                .is_some_and(|n| n.text.contains("__libc_start_main")),
            Flow::IndirectCall { slot: Some(s) } => p
                .name(s)
                .is_some_and(|n| n.text.contains("__libc_start_main")),
            _ => false,
        };
        if calls_start_main {
            return candidate.filter(|&c| p.memory.is_code(c));
        }
        if !insn.flow.falls_through() {
            return None;
        }
        addr = insn.end();
    }
    None
}

/// Windows' own programs import the C runtime from a private DLL whose functions carry
/// an `_o_` prefix (`_o_exit`, `_o__get_wide_winmain_command_line`).
fn crt_name(name: &str) -> &str {
    name.strip_prefix("_o_").unwrap_or(name)
}

fn parse_imm(text: &str) -> Option<u64> {
    let t = text.trim_start_matches('#');
    match t.strip_prefix("0x") {
        Some(hex) => u64::from_str_radix(hex, 16).ok(),
        None => t.parse().ok(),
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-analysis/src/memory.rs`:

```rs
//! The program's memory image as far as the file defines it: which addresses map to
//! which bytes, and which of them are code.

use std::sync::Arc;

use orress_loaders::{BinaryInfo, Format};

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Region {
    pub start: u64,
    pub file_offset: u64,
    pub len: u64,
    pub executable: bool,
    pub name: String,
}

#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct Memory {
    data: Arc<Vec<u8>>,
    /// Sorted by start address.
    pub regions: Vec<Region>,
    pub is_elf: bool,
}

impl Memory {
    pub fn new(info: &BinaryInfo, data: Arc<Vec<u8>>) -> Self {
        let mut regions: Vec<Region> = info
            .sections
            .iter()
            .filter(|s| s.file_size > 0 && s.address != 0)
            .map(|s| Region {
                start: s.address,
                file_offset: s.offset,
                // Raw data past the virtual size (PE file-alignment padding) is not mapped; a zero
                // virtual size means "unknown", so the file size stands.
                len: if s.virtual_size > 0 {
                    s.file_size.min(s.virtual_size)
                } else {
                    s.file_size
                },
                executable: s.perms.execute,
                name: s.name.clone(),
            })
            .collect();
        // ELF files without section headers: fall back to the loadable segments.
        if regions.is_empty() {
            regions = info
                .segments
                .iter()
                .filter(|s| s.file_size > 0)
                .map(|s| Region {
                    start: s.address,
                    file_offset: s.offset,
                    len: s.file_size,
                    executable: s.perms.execute,
                    name: s
                        .name
                        .clone()
                        .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("segment_{:x}", s.address)),
                })
                .collect();
        }
        let size = data.len() as u64;
        // Drop regions whose file range runs past the data, or whose address range wraps past the
        // top of the address space (a malformed header), so `start + len` never overflows later.
        regions.retain(|r| {
            r.file_offset
                .checked_add(r.len)
                .is_some_and(|end| end <= size)
                && r.start.checked_add(r.len).is_some()
        });
        regions.sort_by_key(|r| r.start);
        Self {
            data,
            regions,
            is_elf: info.format == Format::Elf,
        }
    }

    pub fn region(&self, addr: u64) -> Option<&Region> {
        let i = self.regions.partition_point(|r| r.start <= addr);
        let r = self.regions.get(i.checked_sub(1)?)?;
        (addr - r.start < r.len).then_some(r)
    }

    pub fn contains(&self, addr: u64) -> bool {
        self.region(addr).is_some()
    }

    pub fn is_code(&self, addr: u64) -> bool {
        self.region(addr).is_some_and(|r| r.executable)
    }

    /// Up to `len` bytes at `addr`, stopping at the end of the region.
    pub fn read(&self, addr: u64, len: usize) -> Option<&[u8]> {
        let r = self.region(addr)?;
        let skip = addr - r.start;
        let available = (r.len - skip) as usize;
        let start = (r.file_offset + skip) as usize;
        self.data.get(start..start + len.min(available))
    }

    pub fn offset_of(&self, addr: u64) -> Option<u64> {
        let r = self.region(addr)?;
        Some(r.file_offset + (addr - r.start))
    }

    pub fn address_of(&self, offset: u64) -> Option<u64> {
        self.regions
            .iter()
            .find(|r| offset >= r.file_offset && offset - r.file_offset < r.len)
            .map(|r| r.start + (offset - r.file_offset))
    }
}
```
