`crates/orress-analysis/src/tests.rs`:

```rs
use std::sync::Arc;

use orress_loaders::{BinaryInfo, Format, Kind, NamedAddress, Perms, Section};

use crate::*;

const BASE: u64 = 0x40_1000;
const DATA: u64 = 0x40_2000;

/// A tiny hand-assembled x86-64 crackme:
///
/// ```text
/// 401000 main:  push rbp
///               mov rbp, rsp
///               lea rdi, [rip -> 402000 "Wrong password"]
///               call check
///               test eax, eax
///               jz fail
///               call [rip -> 402100 (import slot: puts)]
///               xor eax, eax
///               pop rbp
///               ret
///        fail:  mov eax, 1
///               pop rbp
///               ret
///        check: xor eax, eax
///               ret
/// ```
fn crackme() -> (BinaryInfo, Arc<Vec<u8>>) {
    let mut code: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
    code.push(0x55); // push rbp
    code.extend([0x48, 0x89, 0xe5]); // mov rbp, rsp
    let lea_at = BASE + code.len() as u64;
    let rel = (DATA as i64 - (lea_at as i64 + 7)) as i32;
    code.extend([0x48, 0x8d, 0x3d]);
    code.extend(rel.to_le_bytes()); // lea rdi, [rip+rel]
    let call_at = code.len();
    code.extend([0xe8, 0, 0, 0, 0]); // call check (patched below)
    code.extend([0x85, 0xc0]); // test eax, eax
    let jz_at = code.len();
    code.extend([0x74, 0]); // jz fail (patched below)
    let icall_at = BASE + code.len() as u64;
    let rel = (DATA as i64 + 0x100 - (icall_at as i64 + 6)) as i32;
    code.extend([0xff, 0x15]);
    code.extend(rel.to_le_bytes()); // call [rip+rel]
    code.extend([0x31, 0xc0, 0x5d, 0xc3]); // xor eax,eax; pop rbp; ret
    let fail = code.len();
    code.extend([0xb8, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0x5d, 0xc3]); // mov eax,1; pop rbp; ret
    let check = code.len();
    code.extend([0x31, 0xc0, 0xc3]); // xor eax,eax; ret
    code[jz_at + 1] = (fail - (jz_at + 2)) as u8;
    let rel = (check as i32) - (call_at as i32 + 5);
    code[call_at + 1..call_at + 5].copy_from_slice(&rel.to_le_bytes());
    code.resize(0x100, 0xcc);

    let mut data = vec![0u8; 0x200];
    data[..15].copy_from_slice(b"Wrong password\0");

    let mut file = vec![0u8; 0x200]; // headers
    file.extend(&code); // offset 0x200 -> 0x401000
    file.extend(&data); // offset 0x300 -> 0x402000

    let info = BinaryInfo {
        format: Format::Elf,
        kind: Kind::Executable,
        arch: "x86-64".into(),
        bits: Some(64),
        entry: Some(BASE),
        image_base: 0x40_0000,
        sections: vec![
            Section {
                name: ".text".into(),
                offset: 0x200,
                file_size: 0x100,
                address: BASE,
                virtual_size: 0x100,
                perms: Perms {
                    read: true,
                    write: false,
                    execute: true,
                },
                entropy: None,
            },
            Section {
                name: ".rodata".into(),
                offset: 0x300,
                file_size: 0x200,
                address: DATA,
                virtual_size: 0x200,
                perms: Perms {
                    read: true,
                    write: false,
                    execute: false,
                },
                entropy: None,
            },
        ],
        import_slots: vec![NamedAddress {
            address: DATA + 0x100,
            name: "puts".into(),
        }],
        function_symbols: vec![NamedAddress {
            address: BASE,
            name: "main".into(),
        }],
        ..BinaryInfo::default()
    };
    (info, Arc::new(file))
}

fn analyzed() -> Program {
    let (info, data) = crackme();
    let strings = orress_bytes::strings::extract(&data, 4, 1000);
    Program::analyze(&info, data, &strings).expect("x86-64 is supported")
}

#[test]
fn finds_functions_and_blocks() {
    let p = analyzed();
    assert_eq!(p.functions.len(), 2, "main and check");
    let main = &p.functions[&BASE];
    assert_eq!(main.blocks.len(), 3, "entry, success path, fail path");
    let entry = main.block_at(BASE).unwrap();
    let kinds: Vec<EdgeKind> = entry.succs.iter().map(|e| e.kind).collect();
    assert_eq!(kinds, vec![EdgeKind::Taken, EdgeKind::NotTaken]);
    assert_eq!(main.calls.len(), 1);
    let check = main.calls[0];
    assert_eq!(p.name(check).unwrap().text, format!("sub_{check:x}"));
    assert_eq!(p.main, Some(BASE));
    assert_eq!(p.name(BASE).unwrap().text, "main");
}

#[test]
fn cross_references() {
    let p = analyzed();
    // The string is referenced by the lea, and shows up as a string comment.
    let refs = p.xrefs(DATA);
    assert_eq!(refs.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(refs[0].kind, XrefKind::Data);
    assert_eq!(p.string_refs[&DATA], "Wrong password");
    // The import slot is called.
    let slot_refs = p.xrefs(DATA + 0x100);
    assert_eq!(slot_refs.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(slot_refs[0].kind, XrefKind::Call);
    assert_eq!(p.name(DATA + 0x100).unwrap().text, "puts");
    // check() is called once.
    let check = p.functions[&BASE].calls[0];
    assert_eq!(p.xrefs(check)[0].kind, XrefKind::Call);
}

#[test]
fn listing_covers_code_and_padding() {
    let p = analyzed();
    assert_eq!(p.lines[0].kind, LineKind::Region);
    assert_eq!(
        p.lines[1],
        Line {
            addr: BASE,
            kind: LineKind::Function
        }
    );
    assert_eq!(
        p.lines[2],
        Line {
            addr: BASE,
            kind: LineKind::Insn
        }
    );
    assert!(p.lines.iter().any(|l| l.kind == LineKind::Label));
    assert!(
        matches!(p.lines.last().unwrap().kind, LineKind::Data(_)),
        "int3 padding is data"
    );
    // Lookup lands on the instruction line, not the header.
    let i = p.line_index(BASE).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(p.lines[i].kind, LineKind::Insn);
    // Lines are sorted and cover the region without gaps.
    assert!(p.lines.windows(2).all(|w| w[0].addr <= w[1].addr));
    assert_eq!(
        p.insn_start(BASE + 2),
        Some(BASE + 1),
        "inside mov rbp, rsp"
    );
}

#[test]
fn unsupported_arch_is_none() {
    let (mut info, data) = crackme();
    info.arch = "MIPS (32-bit)".into();
    assert!(Program::analyze(&info, data, &[]).is_none());
}

/// The test binary itself is a large real program.
#[test]
fn analyzes_host_executable() {
    let data = Arc::new(std::fs::read(std::env::current_exe().unwrap()).unwrap());
    let info = orress_loaders::triage(&data);
    let start = std::time::Instant::now();
    let p = Program::analyze(&info, Arc::clone(&data), &[]).expect("host arch supported");
    assert!(
        p.functions.len() > 200,
        "found {} functions",
        p.functions.len()
    );
    assert!(p.functions.contains_key(&info.entry.unwrap()));
    assert!(!p.lines.is_empty());
    // Import slots are called from code.
    let called_imports = info
        .import_slots
        .iter()
        .filter(|s| !p.xrefs(s.address).is_empty())
        .count();
    assert!(called_imports > 5, "{called_imports} imports have xrefs");
    eprintln!(
        "analyzed {} functions, {} instructions in {:?}",
        p.functions.len(),
        p.insns.len(),
        start.elapsed()
    );
}

#[test]
fn calls_clobber_caller_saved_registers() {
    let p = analyzed();
    let main = &p.functions[&BASE];
    // `lea rdi, [rip->DATA]` is rdi's only explicit definition, but `call check` follows and may
    // overwrite rdi, so it is not a function-wide constant.
    assert_eq!(p.register_const(main, 7), None);
    // The use right after the lea (the call itself) is in the same block as the call, so the
    // call's clobber reaches it too: still not provably constant at any point after the call.
    let after_call = main.blocks[0].insns[4]; // test eax, eax
    assert_eq!(p.register_const_at(main, after_call, 7), None);
}

/// An x86-64 or ARM64 program with one executable section of `code` at `addr`.
fn tiny(arch: &str, addr: u64, code: &[u8], symbols: &[(u64, &str)]) -> Program {
    let mut file = vec![0u8; 0x200];
    file.extend(code);
    let info = BinaryInfo {
        format: Format::Elf,
        kind: Kind::Executable,
        arch: arch.into(),
        bits: Some(64),
        entry: Some(addr),
        image_base: 0x40_0000,
        sections: vec![Section {
            name: ".text".into(),
            offset: 0x200,
            file_size: code.len() as u64,
            address: addr,
            virtual_size: code.len() as u64,
            perms: Perms {
                read: true,
                write: false,
                execute: true,
            },
            entropy: None,
        }],
        function_symbols: symbols
            .iter()
            .map(|&(address, name)| NamedAddress {
                address,
                name: name.into(),
            })
            .collect(),
        ..BinaryInfo::default()
    };
    Program::analyze(&info, Arc::new(file), &[]).expect("supported arch")
}

#[test]
fn syscall_does_not_end_the_function() {
    // mov eax, 60; syscall; mov eax, 1; ret
    let code = [0xb8, 60, 0, 0, 0, 0x0f, 0x05, 0xb8, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0xc3];
    let p = tiny("x86-64", BASE, &code, &[(BASE, "f")]);
    assert_eq!(p.functions[&BASE].insn_count(), 4);
}

#[test]
fn arm64_main_from_adrp_add_with_unmapped_page() {
    // .text starts mid-page at 0x401800, so `adrp x0`'s page base 0x401000 is not mapped.
    const TEXT: u64 = 0x40_1800;
    let words: [u32; 20] = [
        0x9000_0000, // adrp x0, 0x401000
        0x9121_0000, // add x0, x0, #0x840
        0x9400_0006, // bl __libc_start_main (0x401820)
        0xd65f_03c0, // ret
        0,
        0,
        0,
        0,
        0xd65f_03c0, // 0x401820: __libc_start_main: ret
        0,
        0,
        0,
        0,
        0,
        0,
        0,
        0xd280_0000, // 0x401840: main: mov x0, #0
        0xd65f_03c0, // ret
        0,
        0,
    ];
    let code: Vec<u8> = words.iter().flat_map(|w| w.to_le_bytes()).collect();
    let p = tiny(
        "ARM64 (AArch64)",
        TEXT,
        &code,
        &[(0x40_1820, "__libc_start_main")],
    );
    assert_eq!(p.main, Some(0x40_1840));
}

#[test]
fn arm64_main_from_literal_pool() {
    const TEXT: u64 = 0x40_1000;
    let mut words = [0u32; 32];
    words[0] = 0x5800_0300; // ldr x0, 0x401060 (literal)
    words[1] = 0x9400_0007; // bl __libc_start_main (0x401020)
    words[2] = 0xd65f_03c0; // ret
    words[8] = 0xd65f_03c0; // 0x401020: __libc_start_main
    words[16] = 0xd280_0000; // 0x401040: main
    words[17] = 0xd65f_03c0;
    words[24] = 0x0040_1040; // 0x401060: literal = main
    let code: Vec<u8> = words.iter().flat_map(|w| w.to_le_bytes()).collect();
    let p = tiny(
        "ARM64 (AArch64)",
        TEXT,
        &code,
        &[(0x40_1020, "__libc_start_main")],
    );
    assert_eq!(p.main, Some(0x40_1040));
}

#[test]
fn region_length_honours_virtual_size() {
    let (mut info, data) = crackme();
    // PE-style: raw data padded past the virtual size; only the virtual part is mapped.
    info.sections[1].virtual_size = 0x20;
    let m = Memory::new(&info, Arc::clone(&data));
    assert!(m.contains(DATA + 0x1f) && !m.contains(DATA + 0x20));
    // Zero virtual size: the file size stands.
    info.sections[1].virtual_size = 0;
    assert!(Memory::new(&info, Arc::clone(&data)).contains(DATA + 0x1ff));
    // A section whose address range wraps the address space is rejected.
    info.sections[1].address = u64::MAX - 0x10;
    assert!(!Memory::new(&info, data).contains(u64::MAX - 0x8));
}

/// The Academy's Rust crackmes: real-world Rust start-up code and string layout.
#[test]
fn rust_crackmes() {
    for (bytes, check_fn_cmp) in [
        (
            &include_bytes!("../../../academy/crackmes/bin/crackme01.exe")[..],
            None,
        ),
        (
            &include_bytes!("../../../academy/crackmes/bin/crackme02.exe")[..],
            Some(0x52u64),
        ),
    ] {
        let data = Arc::new(bytes.to_vec());
        let info = orress_loaders::triage(&data);
        let strings = orress_bytes::strings::extract(&data, 4, 100_000);
        let p = Program::analyze(&info, Arc::clone(&data), &strings).unwrap();
        let main = p.main.expect("main found");
        assert_eq!(p.name(main).unwrap().text, "main");
        assert!(
            p.names.values().any(|n| n.text == "rust_runtime_main"),
            "the C-level shim is named"
        );
        // main references "Wrong password", which sits in the middle of merged strings.
        let f = &p.functions[&main];
        let texts: Vec<&String> = f
            .blocks
            .iter()
            .flat_map(|b| &b.insns)
            .filter_map(|&a| p.decode(a))
            .flat_map(|i| i.data_refs)
            .filter_map(|r| p.string_refs.get(&r))
            .collect();
        assert!(
            texts.iter().any(|t| t.starts_with("Wrong password")),
            "{texts:?}"
        );
        // crackme02: the check function compares the first byte with 'R' (0x52).
        if let Some(byte) = check_fn_cmp {
            let found = p.insns.keys().any(|&a| {
                p.decode(a).is_some_and(|i| {
                    i.mnemonic == "cmp"
                        && i.operands.iter().any(|t| t.text == format!("0x{byte:x}"))
                })
            });
            assert!(found, "cmp with 'R' present");
        }
    }
}

`crates/orress-arch/src/arm64.rs`:

```rs
use yaxpeax_arch::{Decoder, U8Reader};
use yaxpeax_arm::armv8::a64::{InstDecoder, Instruction, Opcode, Operand};

use crate::{Flow, Insn, Token, TokenKind};

fn pc_offset(ins: &Instruction) -> Option<i64> {
    ins.operands.iter().find_map(|op| match op {
        Operand::PCOffset(off) => Some(*off),
        _ => None,
    })
}

pub fn decode(bytes: &[u8], address: u64) -> Option<Insn> {
    let word = bytes.get(..4)?;
    let mut reader = U8Reader::new(word);
    let ins = InstDecoder::default().decode(&mut reader).ok()?;
    let target = pc_offset(&ins).map(|off| address.wrapping_add_signed(off));

    let flow = match ins.opcode {
        Opcode::B => target.map_or(Flow::Stop, Flow::Jump),
        Opcode::BL => target.map_or(Flow::Stop, Flow::Call),
        Opcode::Bcc(_) | Opcode::CBZ | Opcode::CBNZ | Opcode::TBZ | Opcode::TBNZ => {
            target.map_or(Flow::Next, Flow::CondJump)
        }
        // Pointer-authenticated (PAC) variants branch exactly like their plain forms.
        Opcode::BR | Opcode::BRAA | Opcode::BRAAZ | Opcode::BRAB | Opcode::BRABZ => {
            Flow::IndirectJump {
                slot: None,
                table: None,
            }
        }
        Opcode::BLR | Opcode::BLRAA | Opcode::BLRAAZ | Opcode::BLRAB | Opcode::BLRABZ => {
            Flow::IndirectCall { slot: None }
        }
        Opcode::RET
        | Opcode::RETAA
        | Opcode::RETAB
        | Opcode::RETAASPPC
        | Opcode::RETABSPPC
        | Opcode::RETAASPPCR
        | Opcode::RETABSPPCR
        | Opcode::ERET
        | Opcode::ERETAA
        | Opcode::ERETAB => Flow::Return,
        Opcode::BRK | Opcode::HLT | Opcode::UDF => Flow::Stop,
        _ => Flow::Next,
    };

    let mut data_refs = Vec::new();
    match ins.opcode {
        // ADRP forms the address of a 4 KiB page; the next instruction adds the offset.
        Opcode::ADRP => {
            if let Some(off) = pc_offset(&ins) {
                data_refs.push((address & !0xfff).wrapping_add_signed(off));
            }
        }
        Opcode::ADR | Opcode::LDR => {
            if let Some(t) = target {
                data_refs.push(t);
            }
        }
        _ => {}
    }

    // yaxpeax prints PC-relative operands as `$+0x10`; show absolute addresses instead.
    let text = ins.to_string();
    let (mnemonic, rest) = text.split_once(' ').unwrap_or((text.as_str(), ""));
    let shown = match ins.opcode {
        Opcode::ADRP => data_refs.first().copied(),
        _ => target,
    };
    let operands = tokenize(rest, shown);

    Some(Insn {
        address,
        len: 4,
        mnemonic: mnemonic.to_owned(),
        operands,
        flow,
        data_refs,
    })
}

fn tokenize(text: &str, pc_target: Option<u64>) -> Vec<Token> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for (i, part) in text.split(", ").enumerate() {
        if i > 0 {
            out.push(Token {
                kind: TokenKind::Punct,
                text: ",".into(),
            });
        }
        let part = part.trim();
        let (kind, text) = if part.starts_with('$') || part.starts_with("#$") {
            match pc_target {
                Some(t) => (TokenKind::Address(t), format!("0x{t:x}")),
                None => (TokenKind::Number, part.to_owned()),
            }
        } else if part.starts_with('#')
            || part.starts_with("0x")
            || part.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit())
        {
            (TokenKind::Number, part.to_owned())
        } else if is_register(part) {
            (TokenKind::Register, part.to_owned())
        } else {
            (TokenKind::Text, part.to_owned())
        };
        out.push(Token { kind, text });
    }
    out.retain(|t| !t.text.is_empty());
    out
}

fn is_register(s: &str) -> bool {
    matches!(s, "sp" | "wsp" | "xzr" | "wzr" | "lr" | "fp")
        || (s.len() >= 2
            && matches!(
                s.as_bytes()[0],
                b'x' | b'w' | b'v' | b'q' | b'd' | b's' | b'h' | b'b'
            )
            && s[1..].chars().take_while(char::is_ascii_digit).count() > 0)
}

`crates/orress-arch/src/explain.rs`:

```rs
//! Plain-language explanations of instructions and registers, for Explain Mode.

use crate::Isa;

/// Explains a mnemonic, e.g. `"jnz"`. Prefixes such as `rep` are explained separately.
pub fn mnemonic(isa: Isa, mnemonic: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
    let m = mnemonic.rsplit(' ').next().unwrap_or(mnemonic);
    match isa {
        Isa::X86 | Isa::X64 => x86(m),
        Isa::Arm64 => arm64(m),
    }
}

fn x86(m: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
    Some(match m {
        "mov" => "Copy a value: mov dst, src puts src into dst. The most common instruction.",
        "movzx" => {
            "Copy a small value into a bigger register, filling the rest with zeros (zero-extend). Typical for reading one byte or character."
        }
        "movsx" | "movsxd" => {
            "Copy a small value into a bigger register, keeping its sign (sign-extend)."
        }
        "lea" => {
            "Load Effective Address: computes an address (or any a+b*c+d arithmetic) without reading memory. Often loads a pointer to a string."
        }
        "push" => {
            "Put a value on top of the stack (rsp/esp goes down). Also used to pass arguments in 32-bit code."
        }
        "pop" => "Take the value from the top of the stack into a register (rsp/esp goes up).",
        "call" => {
            "Call a function: push the return address, then jump to it. When the function returns, execution continues after this call."
        }
        "ret" | "retn" => {
            "Return from the function: pop the return address from the stack and jump back to the caller. The return value is in rax/eax."
        }
        "jmp" => "Jump: continue execution at another address, always.",
        "cmp" => {
            "Compare: computes a - b to set the flags, without storing the result. A conditional jump right after decides what happens."
        }
        "test" => {
            "Bitwise AND to set the flags, without storing the result. `test eax, eax` checks whether eax is zero."
        }
        "je" | "jz" => {
            "Jump if equal / zero (ZF=1): taken when the previous cmp found both values equal, or the result was zero."
        }
        "jne" | "jnz" => {
            "Jump if not equal / not zero (ZF=0). In a crackme this is often the jump to \"Wrong password\"."
        }
        "jg" | "jnle" => "Jump if greater (signed comparison).",
        "jge" | "jnl" => "Jump if greater or equal (signed).",
        "jl" | "jnge" => "Jump if less (signed).",
        "jle" | "jng" => "Jump if less or equal (signed).",
        "ja" | "jnbe" => "Jump if above (unsigned comparison).",
        "jae" | "jnb" | "jnc" => "Jump if above or equal (unsigned); also: jump if no carry.",
        "jb" | "jnae" | "jc" => "Jump if below (unsigned); also: jump if carry.",
        "jbe" | "jna" => "Jump if below or equal (unsigned).",
        "js" => "Jump if the result was negative (sign flag set).",
        "jns" => "Jump if the result was not negative.",
        "jo" | "jno" => "Jump on (no) signed overflow.",
        "jp" | "jpe" | "jnp" | "jpo" => {
            "Jump on parity flag; rare in normal code, often from floating-point compares."
        }
        "jcxz" | "jecxz" | "jrcxz" => "Jump if the counter register is zero.",
        "loop" => "Decrement rcx/ecx and jump if it is not zero yet.",
        "xor" => {
            "Exclusive OR. `xor eax, eax` sets eax to 0. XOR with a key is the most common simple encryption in CTFs."
        }
        "and" => "Bitwise AND: keeps only the bits set in both values. Used for masking.",
        "or" => "Bitwise OR: sets bits.",
        "not" => "Flips every bit.",
        "neg" => "Negates a number (two's complement): x becomes -x.",
        "add" => "Addition: dst = dst + src.",
        "sub" => {
            "Subtraction: dst = dst - src. `sub rsp, N` reserves N bytes of stack for local variables."
        }
        "inc" => "Add 1.",
        "dec" => "Subtract 1.",
        "imul" => "Signed multiplication.",
        "mul" => "Unsigned multiplication (result in rdx:rax).",
        "idiv" => "Signed division: rdx:rax / operand; quotient in rax, remainder in rdx.",
        "div" => "Unsigned division: quotient in rax, remainder (modulo) in rdx.",
        "shl" | "sal" => "Shift bits left: multiplies by a power of two.",
        "shr" => "Shift bits right (unsigned): divides by a power of two.",
        "sar" => "Shift bits right keeping the sign (signed division by a power of two).",
        "rol" => {
            "Rotate bits left: bits pushed out on the left come back on the right. Common in hash and crypto code."
        }
        "ror" => "Rotate bits right. ror 13 is the classic shellcode API-hash.",
        "nop" => {
            "No operation: does nothing. Used as padding; patching a check with NOPs removes it."
        }
        "int3" => {
            "Breakpoint trap. Debuggers place this byte (0xCC) to stop the program. Padding between functions also uses it."
        }
        "int" => "Software interrupt. `int 0x80` is a Linux system call in 32-bit code.",
        "syscall" => {
            "Ask the operating system kernel to do something (read, write, exit ...). The call number is in rax."
        }
        "sysenter" => "Fast system call (32-bit).",
        "hlt" => "Halt the processor. Crashes a normal program; marks unreachable code.",
        "ud2" => {
            "Undefined instruction: always crashes. Compilers put it after code that must never be reached."
        }
        "leave" => {
            "Function epilogue: restores the stack pointer and rbp/ebp (mov rsp, rbp; pop rbp)."
        }
        "enter" => "Function prologue that sets up a stack frame (rarely used).",
        "cdq" | "cdqe" | "cqo" | "cwde" | "cbw" | "cwd" => {

        }
        "sete" | "setz" | "setne" | "setnz" | "setg" | "setl" | "setge" | "setle" | "seta"

    match isa {

}

`crates/orress-arch/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! Instruction decoding behind one interface, for every supported architecture.
//!
//! [`decode`] returns an [`Insn`]: its length, its text as colored tokens, how it
//! affects control flow (needed to build control-flow graphs) and which addresses it
//! refers to (needed for cross-references). [`explain`] has plain-language
//! explanations of mnemonics and registers for Explain Mode.

mod arm64;
pub mod explain;
pub mod patch;
mod x86;

/// Instruction set architecture.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum Isa {
    X86,
    X64,
    Arm64,
}

impl Isa {
    /// Picks the ISA from the loader's architecture name.
    pub fn from_arch_name(arch: &str) -> Option<Self> {
        match arch {
            "x86 (32-bit)" => Some(Self::X86),
            "x86-64" | "x86-64 (x32 ABI)" => Some(Self::X64),
            "ARM64 (AArch64)" => Some(Self::Arm64),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::X86 => "x86",
            Self::X64 => "x86-64",
            Self::Arm64 => "ARM64",
        }
    }

    /// Longest possible instruction, for reading enough bytes.
    pub fn max_len(self) -> usize {
        match self {
            Self::X86 | Self::X64 => 15,
            Self::Arm64 => 4,
        }
    }

    pub fn pointer_size(self) -> u64 {
        match self {
            Self::X86 => 4,
            Self::X64 | Self::Arm64 => 8,
        }
    }
}

/// A statically-addressable jump table `[base + index*entry]`: `base` is the absolute address
/// of slot 0 and `entry` is the entry size in bytes (4 or 8). Used to recover `switch`/`match`.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct JumpTable {
    pub base: u64,
    pub entry: u8,
}

/// How an instruction affects the flow of execution.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Flow {
    /// Continues with the next instruction.
    Next,
    /// Always jumps to the target.
    Jump(u64),
    /// Jumps to the target if a condition holds, otherwise continues.
    CondJump(u64),
    /// Calls a function and continues after it returns.
    Call(u64),
    /// Jumps to a computed address. `slot` is the memory slot read, if known
    /// (e.g. `jmp [rip+0x2000]`, used by PLT stubs and import thunks). `table` describes a
    /// statically-addressable jump table `[base + index*entry]`, for switch recovery.
    IndirectJump {
        slot: Option<u64>,
        table: Option<JumpTable>,
    },
    /// Calls a computed address, e.g. `call [IsDebuggerPresent]` through the IAT.
    IndirectCall {
        slot: Option<u64>,
    },
    Return,
    /// Stops execution here (int3, hlt, ud2, brk ...).
    Stop,
}

impl Flow {
    /// Whether execution can continue with the next instruction.
    pub fn falls_through(self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            self,
            Self::Next | Self::CondJump(_) | Self::Call(_) | Self::IndirectCall { .. }
        )
    }

    /// Whether this instruction ends a basic block.
    pub fn ends_block(self) -> bool {
        !matches!(self, Self::Next | Self::Call(_) | Self::IndirectCall { .. })
    }
}

/// What a piece of instruction text is, for coloring and interaction.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum TokenKind {
    Mnemonic,
    Register,
    Number,
    /// A number that is an address in the program; the UI may show a name instead and
    /// makes it clickable.
    Address(u64),
    Keyword,
    Punct,
    Text,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Token {
    pub kind: TokenKind,
    pub text: String,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Insn {
    pub address: u64,
    pub len: u8,
    pub mnemonic: String,
    /// Operand text as tokens (without the mnemonic).
    pub operands: Vec<Token>,
    pub flow: Flow,
    /// Addresses this instruction refers to as data (memory operands, address-like
    /// immediates, ADRP/ADR results).
    pub data_refs: Vec<u64>,
}

impl Insn {
    pub fn text(&self) -> String {
        let ops: String = self.operands.iter().map(|t| t.text.as_str()).collect();
        if ops.is_empty() {
            self.mnemonic.clone()
        } else {
            format!("{} {ops}", self.mnemonic)
        }
    }

    pub fn end(&self) -> u64 {
        self.address + u64::from(self.len)
    }

    /// Code target of a direct jump or call.
    pub fn branch_target(&self) -> Option<u64> {
        match self.flow {
            Flow::Jump(t) | Flow::CondJump(t) | Flow::Call(t) => Some(t),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// Decodes one instruction at `address` from `bytes`. `None` for invalid encodings or
/// too few bytes.
pub fn decode(isa: Isa, bytes: &[u8], address: u64) -> Option<Insn> {
    match isa {
        Isa::X86 => x86::decode(32, bytes, address),
        Isa::X64 => x86::decode(64, bytes, address),
        Isa::Arm64 => arm64::decode(bytes, address),
    }
}

/// A general-purpose register, numbered 0..16 in a stable order (the 64-bit register that a
/// narrower access belongs to). Only the ordering's consistency matters to analyses.
pub type Reg = u8;

/// The memory operand of an instruction, reduced to the registers that form its address.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MemRef {
    pub base: Option<Reg>,
    pub index: Option<Reg>,
    /// Access size in bytes.
    pub size: u8,
    /// The memory operand is read (a load) rather than only written.
    pub is_load: bool,
}

/// Structured register effects of one instruction, for register dataflow analysis — which GP
/// registers it writes and reads, any memory operand's address registers, and whether it is a
/// `lea reg, [rip+addr]` that loads a constant address. Only general-purpose registers are tracked.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RegInfo {
    pub defs: Vec<Reg>,
    pub uses: Vec<Reg>,
    pub mem: Option<MemRef>,
    /// `(dest, addr)` when the instruction is `lea dest, [rip+addr]`.
    pub lea_const: Option<(Reg, u64)>,
    /// `(reg, imm)` when the instruction is `cmp reg, imm` — the register compared against a
    /// constant, e.g. the loop bound a virtual program counter is checked against.
    pub cmp_imm: Option<(Reg, u64)>,
    /// `(reg, delta)` when the instruction adds a constant to a register in place: `add`/`sub`/
    /// `inc`/`dec reg, imm`, or `lea reg, [reg+disp]`. Used to measure how far a handler advances a
    /// virtual program counter.
    pub delta: Option<(Reg, i64)>,
}

/// Register effects of the instruction at `address`. `None` for invalid encodings, or for an ISA
/// whose register model is not yet extracted (currently only x86/x86-64).
pub fn reg_info(isa: Isa, bytes: &[u8], address: u64) -> Option<RegInfo> {
    match isa {
        Isa::X86 => x86::reg_info(32, bytes, address),
        Isa::X64 => x86::reg_info(64, bytes, address),
        Isa::Arm64 => None,
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn d(isa: Isa, bytes: &[u8], addr: u64) -> Insn {
        decode(isa, bytes, addr).expect("valid instruction")
    }

    #[test]
    fn x64_basics() {
        let i = d(Isa::X64, &[0x48, 0x83, 0xec, 0x28], 0x1000);
        assert_eq!(i.text(), "sub rsp,0x28");
        assert_eq!(i.len, 4);
        assert_eq!(i.flow, Flow::Next);
        assert_eq!(i.operands[0].kind, TokenKind::Register);

        // call rel32 to 0x1000 + 5 + 0x10
        let call = d(Isa::X64, &[0xe8, 0x10, 0, 0, 0], 0x1000);
        assert_eq!(call.flow, Flow::Call(0x1015));
        assert!(
            call.operands
                .iter()
                .any(|t| t.kind == TokenKind::Address(0x1015))
        );

        // jz short +2
        let jz = d(Isa::X64, &[0x74, 0x02], 0x2000);
        assert_eq!(jz.flow, Flow::CondJump(0x2004));
        assert!(jz.flow.falls_through() && jz.flow.ends_block());

        assert_eq!(d(Isa::X64, &[0xc3], 0).flow, Flow::Return);
        assert_eq!(d(Isa::X64, &[0xcc], 0).flow, Flow::Stop);
    }

    #[test]
    fn x64_rip_relative_refs() {
        // lea rcx, [rip+0x100] at 0x1000 (7 bytes) -> 0x1107
        let lea = d(Isa::X64, &[0x48, 0x8d, 0x0d, 0x00, 0x01, 0, 0], 0x1000);
        assert_eq!(lea.data_refs, vec![0x1107]);
        assert!(
            lea.operands
                .iter()
                .any(|t| t.kind == TokenKind::Address(0x1107))
        );
        // call [rip+0x2000] at 0x1000 (6 bytes): an import call through a slot
        let call = d(Isa::X64, &[0xff, 0x15, 0x00, 0x20, 0, 0], 0x1000);
        assert_eq!(call.flow, Flow::IndirectCall { slot: Some(0x3006) });
        // jmp [rip+0x10]: a PLT/thunk-style indirect jump
        let jmp = d(Isa::X64, &[0xff, 0x25, 0x10, 0, 0, 0], 0x1000);
        assert_eq!(
            jmp.flow,
            Flow::IndirectJump {
                slot: Some(0x1016),
                table: None
            }
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn x86_32_absolute_memory() {
        // call dword ptr [0x402000]
        let call = d(Isa::X86, &[0xff, 0x15, 0x00, 0x20, 0x40, 0x00], 0x401000);
        assert_eq!(
            call.flow,
            Flow::IndirectCall {
                slot: Some(0x402000)
            }
        );
        // push 0x403000 (a string address, typically)
        let push = d(Isa::X86, &[0x68, 0x00, 0x30, 0x40, 0x00], 0x401000);
        assert_eq!(push.data_refs, vec![0x403000]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn invalid_is_none() {
        // `push es` does not exist in 64-bit mode.
        assert!(decode(Isa::X64, &[0x06], 0).is_none());
        assert_eq!(decode(Isa::X86, &[0x06], 0).unwrap().mnemonic, "push");
        assert!(decode(Isa::X64, &[], 0).is_none());
        assert!(decode(Isa::Arm64, &[0, 0], 0).is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn arm64_branches() {
        // bl #+0x100  (0x94000040)
        let bl = d(Isa::Arm64, &0x9400_0040u32.to_le_bytes(), 0x1000);
        assert_eq!(bl.flow, Flow::Call(0x1100));
        // ret (0xd65f03c0)
        assert_eq!(
            d(Isa::Arm64, &0xd65f_03c0u32.to_le_bytes(), 0).flow,
            Flow::Return
        );
        // b.eq #+0x8 (0x54000040)
        let beq = d(Isa::Arm64, &0x5400_0040u32.to_le_bytes(), 0x2000);
        assert_eq!(beq.flow, Flow::CondJump(0x2008));
        // cbz x0, #+0x10 (0xb4000080)
        let cbz = d(Isa::Arm64, &0xb400_0080u32.to_le_bytes(), 0x3000);
        assert_eq!(cbz.flow, Flow::CondJump(0x3010));
        // b #-0x4 (0x17ffffff)
        let b = d(Isa::Arm64, &0x17ff_ffffu32.to_le_bytes(), 0x4000);
        assert_eq!(b.flow, Flow::Jump(0x3ffc));
        // adrp x0, page +1 (0x90000000 | immlo/immhi for 1 page = 0xb0000000)
        let adrp = d(Isa::Arm64, &0xb000_0000u32.to_le_bytes(), 0x4123);
        assert_eq!(adrp.data_refs, vec![0x5000]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn x64_syscall_falls_through() {
        // syscall, vmcall, sysenter (32-bit): the kernel/hypervisor returns to the next insn.
        assert_eq!(d(Isa::X64, &[0x0f, 0x05], 0x1000).flow, Flow::Next);
        assert_eq!(d(Isa::X64, &[0x0f, 0x01, 0xc1], 0x1000).flow, Flow::Next);
        assert_eq!(d(Isa::X64, &[0x0f, 0x01, 0xd9], 0x1000).flow, Flow::Next);
        assert_eq!(d(Isa::X86, &[0x0f, 0x34], 0x1000).flow, Flow::Next);
        // A real far call still stops.
        assert_eq!(
            d(Isa::X86, &[0x9a, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0x08, 0], 0x1000).flow,
            Flow::Stop
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn arm64_pac_branches() {
        let flow = |w: u32| d(Isa::Arm64, &w.to_le_bytes(), 0x1000).flow;
        let ij = Flow::IndirectJump {
            slot: None,
            table: None,
        };
        let ic = Flow::IndirectCall { slot: None };
        assert_eq!(flow(0xd65f_0bff), Flow::Return); // retaa
        assert_eq!(flow(0xd65f_0fff), Flow::Return); // retab
        assert_eq!(flow(0xd69f_0bff), Flow::Return); // eretaa
        assert_eq!(flow(0xd69f_0fff), Flow::Return); // eretab
        assert_eq!(flow(0xd61f_081f), ij); // braaz x0
        assert_eq!(flow(0xd61f_0c1f), ij); // brabz x0
        assert_eq!(flow(0xd71f_0c01), ij); // brab x0, x1
        assert_eq!(flow(0xd63f_081f), ic); // blraaz x0
        assert_eq!(flow(0xd63f_0c1f), ic); // blrabz x0
        assert_eq!(flow(0xd73f_0c01), ic); // blrab x0, x1
        assert_eq!(flow(0x0000_0000), Flow::Stop); // udf #0
    }
}

`crates/orress-arch/src/patch.rs`:

```rs
//! Byte patches for common edits: remove an instruction, invert a condition, or make a
//! conditional jump unconditional. These are the classic crackme patches.

use crate::Isa;

/// Bytes that replace an instruction of `len` bytes with "do nothing".
///
/// ARM64 instructions are 4 bytes each: a `len` that is not a multiple of 4 cannot be
/// filled with NOPs, so this returns an empty patch (no change) rather than covering only
/// part of the range. Use [`try_nop`] to detect that case.
pub fn nop(isa: Isa, len: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    try_nop(isa, len).unwrap_or_default()
}

/// Like [`nop`], but `None` when `len` cannot be covered exactly by NOPs (ARM64 with a
/// length that is not a multiple of 4).
pub fn try_nop(isa: Isa, len: usize) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    match isa {
        Isa::X86 | Isa::X64 => Some(vec![0x90; len]),
        // ARM64 instructions are 4 bytes; NOP is d503201f.
        Isa::Arm64 => len
            .is_multiple_of(4)
            .then(|| 0xd503_201fu32.to_le_bytes().repeat(len / 4)),
    }
}

/// `b.cond` (B.cond: `0101_0100 imm19 0 cond`).
fn is_bcond(word: u32) -> bool {
    word & 0xff00_0010 == 0x5400_0000
}

/// `cbz`/`cbnz` (32- or 64-bit).
fn is_cbz(word: u32) -> bool {
    word & 0x7e00_0000 == 0x3400_0000
}

/// `tbz`/`tbnz`.
fn is_tbz(word: u32) -> bool {
    word & 0x7e00_0000 == 0x3600_0000
}

/// Sign-extends the `bits`-wide field of `word` starting at bit 5 (the branch offset in
/// instruction units).
fn branch_field(word: u32, bits: u32) -> i32 {
    let raw = (word >> 5) & ((1 << bits) - 1);
    ((raw << (32 - bits)) as i32) >> (32 - bits)
}

/// Inverts a conditional jump (je <-> jne, jl <-> jge, ...). `None` if the instruction
/// is not a conditional jump this function knows.
pub fn invert(isa: Isa, bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    let mut out = bytes.to_vec();
    match isa {
        Isa::X86 | Isa::X64 => match bytes {
            // Short jcc: 70..7F rel8. Opcodes come in pairs that differ in the low bit.
            [op @ 0x70..=0x7f, _] => out[0] = op ^ 1,
            // Near jcc: 0F 80..8F rel32.
            [0x0f, op @ 0x80..=0x8f, _, _, _, _] => out[1] = op ^ 1,
            _ => return None,
        },
        Isa::Arm64 => {
            let word = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes.get(..4)?.try_into().ok()?);
            let new = if is_bcond(word) {
                // b.al / b.nv (condition 111x) always branch: there is no inverse.
                if word & 0xe == 0xe {
                    return None;
                }
                // b.cond: the lowest condition bit flips the condition.
                word ^ 1
            } else if is_cbz(word) || is_tbz(word) {
                // cbz <-> cbnz, tbz <-> tbnz: bit 24.
                word ^ (1 << 24)
            } else {
                return None;
            };
            out[..4].copy_from_slice(&new.to_le_bytes());
        }
    }
    Some(out)
}

/// Turns a conditional jump into an unconditional one with the same target.
pub fn force(isa: Isa, bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    match isa {
        Isa::X86 | Isa::X64 => match bytes {
            [0x70..=0x7f, rel] => Some(vec![0xeb, *rel]),
            // jcc rel32 is 6 bytes, jmp rel32 is 5: a NOP first keeps the same end address,
            // so the relative offset stays valid.
            [0x0f, 0x80..=0x8f, r0, r1, r2, r3] => Some(vec![0x90, 0xe9, *r0, *r1, *r2, *r3]),
            _ => None,
        },
        Isa::Arm64 => {
            let word = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes.get(..4)?.try_into().ok()?);
            let new = if is_bcond(word) {
                // b.cond with condition AL (0b1110) always branches.
                (word & !0xf) | 0xe
            } else if is_cbz(word) || is_tbz(word) {
                // cbz/cbnz (imm19) and tbz/tbnz (imm14) become `b` (imm26) with the same
                // PC-relative offset: same address, same target.
                let off = if is_cbz(word) {
                    branch_field(word, 19)
                } else {
                    branch_field(word, 14)
                };
                0x1400_0000 | (off as u32 & 0x03ff_ffff)
            } else {
                return None;
            };
            Some(new.to_le_bytes().to_vec())
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::{Flow, decode};

    #[test]
    fn x86_jump_patches_keep_targets() {
        // je +0x10 at 0x1000 (short) and jne +0x100 (near).
        let short = [0x74, 0x10];
        let near = [0x0f, 0x85, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00];
        let inv = invert(Isa::X64, &short).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(decode(Isa::X64, &inv, 0x1000).unwrap().mnemonic, "jne");
        let forced = force(Isa::X64, &short).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            decode(Isa::X64, &forced, 0x1000).unwrap().flow,
            Flow::Jump(0x1012)
        );

        let inv = invert(Isa::X64, &near).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(decode(Isa::X64, &inv, 0x1000).unwrap().mnemonic, "je");
        // Forced near jump: NOP then jmp, landing on the original target 0x1106.
        let forced = force(Isa::X64, &near).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(decode(Isa::X64, &forced, 0x1000).unwrap().mnemonic, "nop");
        assert_eq!(
            decode(Isa::X64, &forced[1..], 0x1001).unwrap().flow,
            Flow::Jump(0x1106)
        );

        assert_eq!(invert(Isa::X64, &[0x90]), None);
        assert_eq!(nop(Isa::X64, 3), vec![0x90; 3]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn arm64_patches() {
        // b.eq +8 -> b.ne +8
        let beq = 0x5400_0040u32.to_le_bytes();
        let bne = invert(Isa::Arm64, &beq).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(decode(Isa::Arm64, &bne, 0).unwrap().mnemonic, "b.ne");
        // cbz -> cbnz
        let cbz = 0xb400_0080u32.to_le_bytes();
        assert_eq!(
            decode(Isa::Arm64, &invert(Isa::Arm64, &cbz).unwrap(), 0)
                .unwrap()
                .mnemonic,
            "cbnz"
        );
        let forced = force(Isa::Arm64, &beq).unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(
            decode(Isa::Arm64, &forced, 0).unwrap().flow,
            Flow::Jump(8) | Flow::CondJump(8)
        ));
        assert_eq!(
            decode(Isa::Arm64, &nop(Isa::Arm64, 4), 0).unwrap().mnemonic,
            "nop"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn arm64_always_branches_do_not_invert() {
        // b.al +8 and b.nv +8 always branch; flipping the low bit would not invert them.
        assert_eq!(invert(Isa::Arm64, &0x5400_004eu32.to_le_bytes()), None);
        assert_eq!(invert(Isa::Arm64, &0x5400_004fu32.to_le_bytes()), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn arm64_force_compare_branches() {
        // cbz x0, +0x10 at 0x1000 -> b 0x1010
        let cbz = 0xb400_0080u32.to_le_bytes();
        let forced = force(Isa::Arm64, &cbz).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            decode(Isa::Arm64, &forced, 0x1000).unwrap().flow,
            Flow::Jump(0x1010)
        );
        // cbnz w1, -0x8 at 0x1000 -> b 0xff8
        let cbnz = (0x3500_0001u32 | ((0x7fffe & 0x7ffff) << 5)).to_le_bytes();
        let forced = force(Isa::Arm64, &cbnz).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            decode(Isa::Arm64, &forced, 0x1000).unwrap().flow,
            Flow::Jump(0xff8)
        );
        // tbnz x2, #3, +0x20 at 0x2000 -> b 0x2020
        let tbnz = (0x3718_0002u32 | (8 << 5)).to_le_bytes();
        assert_eq!(decode(Isa::Arm64, &tbnz, 0x2000).unwrap().mnemonic, "tbnz");
        let forced = force(Isa::Arm64, &tbnz).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            decode(Isa::Arm64, &forced, 0x2000).unwrap().flow,
            Flow::Jump(0x2020)
        );
        // Not a conditional branch.
        assert_eq!(force(Isa::Arm64, &0xd503_201fu32.to_le_bytes()), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn arm64_nop_requires_whole_instructions() {
        assert_eq!(try_nop(Isa::Arm64, 6), None);
        assert!(nop(Isa::Arm64, 6).is_empty());
        assert_eq!(try_nop(Isa::Arm64, 8).map(|b| b.len()), Some(8));
        assert_eq!(try_nop(Isa::X64, 3), Some(vec![0x90; 3]));
    }
}

`crates/orress-arch/src/x86.rs`:

```rs
use iced_x86::{
    Decoder, DecoderOptions, FlowControl, Formatter, FormatterOutput, FormatterTextKind,
    Instruction, InstructionInfoFactory, IntelFormatter, Mnemonic, OpAccess, OpKind, Register,
};

use crate::{Flow, Insn, MemRef, Reg, RegInfo, Token, TokenKind};

/// Maps an iced register to a stable 0..16 general-purpose index (by its full 64-bit register),
/// or `None` for non-GP registers (xmm, flags, rip, segment, ...).
fn gp(r: Register) -> Option<Reg> {
    use Register::*;
    Some(match r.full_register() {
        RAX => 0,
        RCX => 1,
        RDX => 2,
        RBX => 3,
        RSP => 4,
        RBP => 5,
        RSI => 6,
        RDI => 7,
        R8 => 8,
        R9 => 9,
        R10 => 10,
        R11 => 11,
        R12 => 12,
        R13 => 13,
        R14 => 14,
        R15 => 15,
        _ => return Option::None,
    })
}

fn is_imm(ins: &Instruction, op: u32) -> bool {
    matches!(
        ins.op_kind(op),
        OpKind::Immediate8
            | OpKind::Immediate16
            | OpKind::Immediate32
            | OpKind::Immediate64
            | OpKind::Immediate8to16
            | OpKind::Immediate8to32
            | OpKind::Immediate8to64
            | OpKind::Immediate32to64
    )
}

fn push_unique(v: &mut Vec<Reg>, r: Reg) {
    if !v.contains(&r) {
        v.push(r);
    }
}

pub fn reg_info(bitness: u32, bytes: &[u8], address: u64) -> Option<RegInfo> {
    if bytes.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let mut decoder = Decoder::with_ip(bitness, bytes, address, DecoderOptions::NONE);
    let ins = decoder.decode();
    if ins.is_invalid() {
        return None;
    }
    let mut info = RegInfo::default();
    let mut factory = InstructionInfoFactory::new();
    for ur in factory.info(&ins).used_registers() {
        let Some(r) = gp(ur.register()) else { continue };
        match ur.access() {
            OpAccess::Read | OpAccess::CondRead => push_unique(&mut info.uses, r),
            OpAccess::Write | OpAccess::CondWrite => push_unique(&mut info.defs, r),
            OpAccess::ReadWrite | OpAccess::ReadCondWrite => {
                push_unique(&mut info.uses, r);
                push_unique(&mut info.defs, r);
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    if ins.mnemonic() == Mnemonic::Cmp
        && let Some(reg) = gp(ins.op0_register())
        && matches!(
            ins.op1_kind(),
            OpKind::Immediate8
                | OpKind::Immediate16
                | OpKind::Immediate32
                | OpKind::Immediate64
                | OpKind::Immediate8to32
                | OpKind::Immediate8to64
                | OpKind::Immediate32to64
        )
    {
        info.cmp_imm = Some((reg, ins.immediate(1)));
    }
    // A constant delta applied to a register in place (how a handler advances a counter).
    let imm1 = || ins.immediate(1) as i64;
    info.delta = match ins.mnemonic() {
        Mnemonic::Add => gp(ins.op0_register())
            .filter(|_| is_imm(&ins, 1))
            .map(|r| (r, imm1())),
        Mnemonic::Sub => gp(ins.op0_register())
            .filter(|_| is_imm(&ins, 1))
            .map(|r| (r, -imm1())),
        Mnemonic::Inc => gp(ins.op0_register()).map(|r| (r, 1)),
        Mnemonic::Dec => gp(ins.op0_register()).map(|r| (r, -1)),
        // `lea reg, [reg+disp]` with no index is an in-place add of `disp`.
        Mnemonic::Lea
            if gp(ins.op0_register()) == gp(ins.memory_base())
                && ins.memory_index() == Register::None
                && !ins.is_ip_rel_memory_operand() =>
        {
            gp(ins.op0_register()).map(|r| (r, ins.memory_displacement64() as i64))
        }
        _ => None,
    };

    if ins.mnemonic() == Mnemonic::Lea {
        // `lea` computes an address; it is not a memory access, and when rip-relative it loads a
        // constant address into its destination register.
        if ins.is_ip_rel_memory_operand()
            && let Some(dest) = gp(ins.op0_register())
        {
            info.lea_const = Some((dest, ins.ip_rel_memory_address()));
        }
    } else if let Some(mem_op) = (0..ins.op_count()).find(|&i| ins.op_kind(i) == OpKind::Memory) {
        info.mem = Some(MemRef {
            base: gp(ins.memory_base()),
            index: gp(ins.memory_index()),
            size: ins.memory_size().size() as u8,
            // The memory operand is a pure store only when it is the written destination (op0 of a
            // write); otherwise it is read.
            is_load: mem_op != 0 || ins.op_count() == 1,
        });
    }
    Some(info)
}

struct Output {
    tokens: Vec<Token>,
}

impl FormatterOutput for Output {
    fn write(&mut self, text: &str, kind: FormatterTextKind) {
        let kind = match kind {
            FormatterTextKind::Mnemonic | FormatterTextKind::Prefix => TokenKind::Mnemonic,
            FormatterTextKind::Register => TokenKind::Register,
            FormatterTextKind::Number => TokenKind::Number,
            FormatterTextKind::LabelAddress | FormatterTextKind::FunctionAddress => {
                match parse_hex(text) {
                    Some(v) => TokenKind::Address(v),
                    None => TokenKind::Number,
                }
            }
            FormatterTextKind::Keyword | FormatterTextKind::Directive => TokenKind::Keyword,
            FormatterTextKind::Punctuation | FormatterTextKind::Operator => TokenKind::Punct,
            _ => TokenKind::Text,
        };
        self.tokens.push(Token {
            kind,
            text: text.to_owned(),
        });
    }
}

fn parse_hex(text: &str) -> Option<u64> {
    let t = text.trim_start_matches("0x");
    u64::from_str_radix(t, 16).ok()
}

fn formatter() -> IntelFormatter {
    let mut f = IntelFormatter::new();
    let o = f.options_mut();
    o.set_hex_prefix("0x");
    o.set_hex_suffix("");
    o.set_uppercase_hex(false);
    o.set_space_after_operand_separator(false);
    // `false` shows `[0x140003000]` instead of `[rip+0x2000]`: the absolute address is
    // what you look up and what a name can replace.
    o.set_rip_relative_addresses(false);
    o.set_branch_leading_zeros(false);
    o.set_show_branch_size(false);
    f
}

thread_local! {
    static FORMATTER: std::cell::RefCell<IntelFormatter> = std::cell::RefCell::new(formatter());
}

pub fn decode(bitness: u32, bytes: &[u8], address: u64) -> Option<Insn> {
    if bytes.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let mut decoder = Decoder::with_ip(bitness, bytes, address, DecoderOptions::NONE);
    let ins: Instruction = decoder.decode();
    if ins.is_invalid() {
        return None;
    }

    // Absolute address of the memory operand, when it can be known statically.
    let mem_addr = memory_address(&ins, bitness);

    let flow = match ins.flow_control() {
        FlowControl::Next | FlowControl::XbeginXabortXend => Flow::Next,
        FlowControl::UnconditionalBranch => Flow::Jump(ins.near_branch_target()),
        FlowControl::ConditionalBranch => Flow::CondJump(ins.near_branch_target()),
        FlowControl::Call => Flow::Call(ins.near_branch_target()),
        FlowControl::IndirectBranch => Flow::IndirectJump {
            slot: mem_addr,
            table: jump_table(&ins),
        },
        FlowControl::IndirectCall => Flow::IndirectCall { slot: mem_addr },
        FlowControl::Return => Flow::Return,
        FlowControl::Interrupt => match ins.mnemonic() {
            // `int 0x80` / syscall continue after the kernel returns.
            Mnemonic::Int | Mnemonic::Into => Flow::Next,
            _ => Flow::Stop,
        },
        FlowControl::Exception => Flow::Stop,
    };
    // syscall/sysenter and the hypervisor calls are `FlowControl::Call` in iced, but they
    // return to the next instruction and have no near target: plain fall-through.
    let flow = match ins.mnemonic() {
        Mnemonic::Syscall | Mnemonic::Sysenter | Mnemonic::Vmcall | Mnemonic::Vmmcall => Flow::Next,
        _ => flow,
    };
    // Far branches have no near target; treat them as stops.
    let flow = match flow {
        Flow::Jump(0) | Flow::Call(0) if ins.near_branch_target() == 0 && !is_near_branch(&ins) => {
            Flow::Stop
        }
        other => other,
    };

    let mut data_refs = Vec::new();
    if let Some(a) = mem_addr
        && !matches!(flow, Flow::IndirectJump { .. } | Flow::IndirectCall { .. })
    {
        data_refs.push(a);
    }
    for i in 0..ins.op_count() {
        let value = match ins.op_kind(i) {
            OpKind::Immediate32 => u64::from(ins.immediate32()),
            OpKind::Immediate64 => ins.immediate64(),
            OpKind::Immediate32to64 => ins.immediate32to64() as u64,
            _ => continue,
        };
        // Small constants are counters and flags, not addresses.
        if value >= 0x1_0000 {
            data_refs.push(value);
        }
    }

    let mut out = Output { tokens: Vec::new() };
    FORMATTER.with(|f| f.borrow_mut().format(&ins, &mut out));
    let mut tokens = out.tokens.into_iter().peekable();
    let mut mnemonic = String::new();
    while let Some(t) = tokens.peek() {
        if t.kind == TokenKind::Mnemonic
            || (t.kind == TokenKind::Text && t.text.trim().is_empty() && mnemonic.is_empty())
        {
            let t = tokens.next().expect("peeked");
            if t.kind == TokenKind::Mnemonic {
                if !mnemonic.is_empty() {
                    mnemonic.push(' ');
                }
                mnemonic.push_str(&t.text);
            }
        } else if t.kind == TokenKind::Text && t.text.trim().is_empty() {
            tokens.next();
            break;
        } else {
            break;
        }
    }
    // Memory operands shown with an absolute address become clickable addresses too.
    let operands = tokens
        .map(|mut t| {
            if t.kind == TokenKind::Number
                && let Some(v) = parse_hex(&t.text)
                && (Some(v) == mem_addr || data_refs.contains(&v))
            {
                t.kind = TokenKind::Address(v);
            }
            t
        })
        .collect();

    Some(Insn {
        address,
        len: ins.len() as u8,
        mnemonic,
        operands,
        flow,
        data_refs,
    })
}

fn is_near_branch(ins: &Instruction) -> bool {
    matches!(
        ins.op0_kind(),
        OpKind::NearBranch16 | OpKind::NearBranch32 | OpKind::NearBranch64
    )
}

/// A statically-addressable jump table `[base + index*entry]` (no base register, a scaled
/// index, and a 4- or 8-byte entry) — the non-PIE `switch` form. PIE tables add the loaded
/// value to a runtime base, so they stay unresolved.
fn jump_table(ins: &Instruction) -> Option<crate::JumpTable> {
    if ins.memory_base() != Register::None || ins.memory_index() == Register::None {
        return None;
    }
    let entry = ins.memory_index_scale();
    if !matches!(entry, 4 | 8) {
        return None;
    }
    Some(crate::JumpTable {
        base: ins.memory_displacement64(),
        entry: entry as u8,
    })
}

fn memory_address(ins: &Instruction, bitness: u32) -> Option<u64> {
    let has_mem = (0..ins.op_count()).any(|i| ins.op_kind(i) == OpKind::Memory);
    if !has_mem {
        return None;
    }
    if ins.is_ip_rel_memory_operand() {
        return Some(ins.ip_rel_memory_address());
    }
    // `[disp32]` with no base or index register: an absolute address (32-bit code).
    if ins.memory_base() == Register::None && ins.memory_index() == Register::None {
        let disp = ins.memory_displacement64();
        if bitness == 32 {
            return Some(disp & 0xffff_ffff);
        }
        return Some(disp);
    }
    None
}

`crates/orress-archive/examples/archive_info.rs`:

```rs
//! Lists a ZIP/JAR's entries and prints the JAR manifest, if present.
//!
//! Run with: `cargo run -p orress-archive --example archive_info -- path/to/app.jar`

fn main() {
    let path = std::env::args()
        .nth(1)
        .expect("usage: archive_info <file.zip|.jar>");
    let data = std::fs::read(&path).expect("read file");
    let ar = match orress_archive::Archive::open(&data) {
        Ok(a) => a,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("{path}: {e}");
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
    };
    println!("{path} — {} entries", ar.entries.len());
    for e in &ar.entries {
        if e.is_dir() {
            println!("  {}/", e.name.trim_end_matches('/'));
        } else {
            println!(
                "  {:<40} {:>8} bytes  ({} -> {})",
                e.name,
                e.uncompressed_size,
                e.method_name(),
                e.compressed_size
            );
        }
    }
    if let Some(entry) = ar.by_name("META-INF/MANIFEST.MF")
        && let Ok(mf) = ar.read(entry)
    {
        println!("\nManifest:");
        for (k, v) in orress_archive::parse_manifest(&mf) {
            println!("  {k}: {v}");
        }
    }
}

`crates/orress-archive/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! A pure-Rust ZIP archive reader for ORRESS — the basis for JAR (Java), APK (Android) and the
//! many ZIP-based container formats. It reads the central directory to list entries and extracts
//! stored (method 0) or deflated (method 8) members (deflate via `miniz_oxide`). It never runs
//! anything and tolerates hostile input (bounded sizes, errors instead of panics).
//!
//! Scope: standard ZIP and ZIP64 (the 64-bit end-of-directory record and the per-entry `0x0001`
//! extra field). Other compression methods are listed but not decompressed, and encrypted
//! members are reported as such rather than inflated as ciphertext.

const EOCD_SIG: u32 = 0x0605_4b50;
const ZIP64_EOCD_SIG: u32 = 0x0606_4b50;
const ZIP64_LOCATOR_SIG: u32 = 0x0706_4b50;
/// The fixed part of a central-directory record; real entries are at least this long.
const CEN_LEN: usize = 46;
const CEN_SIG: u32 = 0x0201_4b50;
const LOC_SIG: u32 = 0x0403_4b50;
/// Cap on a single extracted member, so a crafted header can't exhaust memory.
const MAX_EXTRACT: usize = 512 * 1024 * 1024;

/// One archive member (from the central directory).
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Entry {
    pub name: String,
    /// Compression method: 0 = stored, 8 = deflate (others are listed but not extractable).
    pub method: u16,
    pub compressed_size: u64,
    pub uncompressed_size: u64,
    pub crc32: u32,
    pub local_header_offset: u64,
    /// General-purpose bit flags (bit 0 = encrypted).
    pub flags: u16,
}

impl Entry {
    /// True if the member is encrypted (traditional PKWARE or strong encryption).
    pub fn is_encrypted(&self) -> bool {
        self.flags & 1 != 0
    }
    /// A directory entry (its name ends with `/`).
    pub fn is_dir(&self) -> bool {
        self.name.ends_with('/')
    }
    /// A human name for the compression method.
    pub fn method_name(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self.method {
            0 => "store",
            8 => "deflate",
            12 => "bzip2",
            14 => "lzma",
            93 => "zstd",
            _ => "other",
        }
    }
}

/// A parsed ZIP archive borrowing the file bytes.
pub struct Archive<'a> {
    data: &'a [u8],
    pub entries: Vec<Entry>,
}

fn u16_at(data: &[u8], off: usize) -> Option<u16> {
    data.get(off..off.checked_add(2)?)
        .map(|s| u16::from_le_bytes([s[0], s[1]]))
}
fn u32_at(data: &[u8], off: usize) -> Option<u32> {
    data.get(off..off.checked_add(4)?)
        .map(|s| u32::from_le_bytes([s[0], s[1], s[2], s[3]]))
}
fn u64_at(data: &[u8], off: usize) -> Option<u64> {
    data.get(off..off.checked_add(8)?)
        .map(|s| u64::from_le_bytes(s.try_into().expect("8 bytes")))
}

/// Reads the ZIP64 end-of-central-directory record via its locator (just before the EOCD).
/// Returns `(total entries, central directory size, central directory offset)`.
fn zip64_eocd(data: &[u8], eocd: usize) -> Result<(u64, u64, u64), String> {
    let loc = eocd
        .checked_sub(20)
        .filter(|&l| u32_at(data, l) == Some(ZIP64_LOCATOR_SIG))
        .ok_or("ZIP64 archive without a ZIP64 end-of-directory locator")?;
    let rec = usize::try_from(u64_at(data, loc + 8).ok_or("truncated ZIP64 locator")?)
        .map_err(|_| "ZIP64 record offset out of range")?;
    if u32_at(data, rec) != Some(ZIP64_EOCD_SIG) {
        return Err("bad ZIP64 end-of-central-directory record".into());
    }
    let total = u64_at(data, rec + 32).ok_or("truncated ZIP64 record")?;
    let cd_size = u64_at(data, rec + 40).ok_or("truncated ZIP64 record")?;
    let cd_offset = u64_at(data, rec + 48).ok_or("truncated ZIP64 record")?;
    Ok((total, cd_size, cd_offset))
}

/// Applies a central-directory entry's ZIP64 extended-information extra field (id `0x0001`):
/// it holds a `u64` for each of uncompressed size, compressed size and local-header offset —
/// in that order, and only for the fields whose 32-bit value is the `0xFFFFFFFF` sentinel.
fn apply_zip64_extra(extra: &[u8], uncomp: &mut u64, comp: &mut u64, lho: &mut u64) {
    let mut p = 0;
    while let (Some(id), Some(len)) = (u16_at(extra, p), u16_at(extra, p + 2)) {
        let body_start = p + 4;
        let body = extra
            .get(body_start..body_start + len as usize)
            .unwrap_or(&[]);
        if id == 0x0001 {
            let mut q = 0;
            for field in [uncomp, comp, lho] {
                if *field == 0xFFFF_FFFF {
                    let Some(v) = u64_at(body, q) else {
                        return;
                    };
                    *field = v;
                    q += 8;
                }
            }
            return;
        }
        p = body_start + len as usize;
    }
}

/// True if `data` looks like a ZIP (local-file or empty-archive signature at the start).
pub fn looks_like_zip(data: &[u8]) -> bool {
    matches!(u32_at(data, 0), Some(LOC_SIG) | Some(EOCD_SIG))
}

impl<'a> Archive<'a> {
    /// Opens an archive, reading its central directory.
    pub fn open(data: &'a [u8]) -> Result<Self, String> {
        let eocd =
            find_eocd(data).ok_or("not a ZIP archive (no end-of-central-directory record)")?;
        let cd_entries = u16_at(data, eocd + 8).ok_or("truncated EOCD")?;
        let total16 = u16_at(data, eocd + 10).ok_or("truncated EOCD")?;
        let cd_size32 = u32_at(data, eocd + 12).ok_or("truncated EOCD")?;
        let cd_offset32 = u32_at(data, eocd + 16).ok_or("truncated EOCD")?;

        // Any sentinel means the real values live in the ZIP64 end-of-directory record.
        let (total, cd_size, cd_offset) = if total16 == 0xFFFF
            || cd_entries == 0xFFFF
            || cd_size32 == 0xFFFF_FFFF
            || cd_offset32 == 0xFFFF_FFFF
        {
            zip64_eocd(data, eocd)?
        } else {
            (
                u64::from(total16),
                u64::from(cd_size32),
                u64::from(cd_offset32),
            )
        };

        // Each record is at least 46 bytes, so the directory size bounds the entry count (and the
        // file size bounds the directory) — a hostile count can't drive a huge allocation.
        let max_entries = cd_size.min(data.len() as u64) / CEN_LEN as u64;
        let total = total.min(max_entries) as usize;
        let mut entries = Vec::with_capacity(total.min(1 << 16));
        let mut p = usize::try_from(cd_offset).map_err(|_| "central directory out of range")?;
        for _ in 0..total {
            if u32_at(data, p) != Some(CEN_SIG) {
                break; // Tolerate a short/garbled directory.
            }
            let flags = u16_at(data, p + 8).ok_or("truncated central directory")?;
            let method = u16_at(data, p + 10).ok_or("truncated central directory")?;
            let crc32 = u32_at(data, p + 16).ok_or("truncated central directory")?;
            let mut comp = u32_at(data, p + 20).ok_or("truncated central directory")? as u64;
            let mut uncomp = u32_at(data, p + 24).ok_or("truncated central directory")? as u64;
            let name_len = u16_at(data, p + 28).ok_or("truncated central directory")? as usize;
            let extra_len = u16_at(data, p + 30).ok_or("truncated central directory")? as usize;
            let comment_len = u16_at(data, p + 32).ok_or("truncated central directory")? as usize;
            let mut lho = u32_at(data, p + 42).ok_or("truncated central directory")? as u64;
            let name_end = p + CEN_LEN + name_len;
            let name_bytes = data
                .get(p + CEN_LEN..name_end)
                .ok_or("truncated entry name")?;
            if comp == 0xFFFF_FFFF || uncomp == 0xFFFF_FFFF || lho == 0xFFFF_FFFF {
                let extra = data
                    .get(name_end..name_end + extra_len)
                    .ok_or("truncated extra field")?;
                apply_zip64_extra(extra, &mut uncomp, &mut comp, &mut lho);
            }
            entries.push(Entry {
                name: String::from_utf8_lossy(name_bytes).into_owned(),
                method,
                compressed_size: comp,
                uncompressed_size: uncomp,
                crc32,
                local_header_offset: lho,
                flags,
            });
            p = name_end + extra_len + comment_len;
        }

        Ok(Archive { data, entries })
    }

    /// Finds an entry by exact name.
    pub fn by_name(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&Entry> {
        self.entries.iter().find(|e| e.name == name)
    }

    /// Extracts (decompresses) a member's bytes.
    pub fn read(&self, entry: &Entry) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
        if entry.is_encrypted() {
            return Err(format!(
                "`{}` is encrypted (password-protected); ORRESS does not decrypt ZIP members",
                entry.name
            ));
        }
        let lho = usize::try_from(entry.local_header_offset)
            .map_err(|_| "local header offset out of range")?;
        if u32_at(self.data, lho) != Some(LOC_SIG) {
            return Err("bad local file header".into());
        }
        let name_len = u16_at(self.data, lho + 26).ok_or("truncated local header")? as usize;
        let extra_len = u16_at(self.data, lho + 28).ok_or("truncated local header")? as usize;
        let start = lho + 30 + name_len + extra_len;
        let raw = usize::try_from(entry.compressed_size)
            .ok()
            .and_then(|comp| start.checked_add(comp))
            .and_then(|end| self.data.get(start..end))
            .ok_or("compressed data out of bounds")?;

        match entry.method {
            0 if raw.len() > MAX_EXTRACT => Err("stored member too large to extract".into()),
            0 => Ok(raw.to_vec()),
            8 => {
                let limit = usize::try_from(entry.uncompressed_size)
                    .unwrap_or(MAX_EXTRACT)
                    .clamp(1, MAX_EXTRACT);
                miniz_oxide::inflate::decompress_to_vec_with_limit(raw, limit)
                    .map_err(|e| format!("deflate failed: {e:?}"))
            }
            m => Err(format!("compression method {m} not supported")),
        }
    }
}

/// Scans backward for the end-of-central-directory signature (allowing a trailing comment).
fn find_eocd(data: &[u8]) -> Option<usize> {
    if data.len() < 22 {
        return None;
    }
    // The EOCD is the last 22 bytes plus an optional comment of up to 65535 bytes.
    let last = data.len() - 22;
    let min = last.saturating_sub(0xFFFF);
    (min..=last)
        .rev()
        .find(|&off| u32_at(data, off) == Some(EOCD_SIG))
}

/// Parses a JAR/`MANIFEST.MF` into `(key, value)` pairs, joining 72-column continuation lines
/// (which start with a single space).
pub fn parse_manifest(bytes: &[u8]) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(bytes);
    let mut out: Vec<(String, String)> = Vec::new();
    for line in text.lines() {
        let line = line.strip_suffix('\r').unwrap_or(line);
        if let Some(cont) = line.strip_prefix(' ') {
            if let Some(last) = out.last_mut() {
                last.1.push_str(cont);
            }
        } else if let Some((k, v)) = line.split_once(": ") {
            out.push((k.to_string(), v.to_string()));
        }
    }
    out
}

use super::*;

/// A real JAR built by `jar 17` containing a manifest and `Check.class`.
const JAR: &[u8] = include_bytes!("../tests/fixtures/app.jar");

#[test]
fn detects_and_lists_entries() {
    assert!(looks_like_zip(JAR));
    assert!(!looks_like_zip(b"MZ\x90\x00"));

    let ar = Archive::open(JAR).unwrap();
    let names: Vec<&str> = ar.entries.iter().map(|e| e.name.as_str()).collect();
    assert!(names.contains(&"META-INF/MANIFEST.MF"));
    assert!(names.contains(&"Check.class"));
    // The META-INF/ directory entry is recognised as a directory.
    assert!(
        ar.entries
            .iter()
            .any(|e| e.name == "META-INF/" && e.is_dir())
    );
}

#[test]
fn extracts_class_and_parses_manifest() {
    let ar = Archive::open(JAR).unwrap();

    // The stored/deflated Check.class round-trips to a valid class file.
    let class_entry = ar.by_name("Check.class").unwrap();
    let class_bytes = ar.read(class_entry).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(class_bytes.len() as u64, class_entry.uncompressed_size);
    assert_eq!(&class_bytes[..4], &[0xCA, 0xFE, 0xBA, 0xBE]);

    // The manifest names the main class we set when building the jar.
    let mf = ar
        .read(ar.by_name("META-INF/MANIFEST.MF").unwrap())
        .unwrap();
    let fields = parse_manifest(&mf);
    assert_eq!(
        fields
            .iter()
            .find(|(k, _)| k == "Main-Class")
            .map(|(_, v)| v.as_str()),
        Some("Check")
    );
}

#[test]
fn rejects_non_zip() {
    assert!(Archive::open(b"not a zip at all, just some text").is_err());
}

fn le16(out: &mut Vec<u8>, v: u16) {
    out.extend(v.to_le_bytes());
}
fn le32(out: &mut Vec<u8>, v: u32) {
    out.extend(v.to_le_bytes());
}
fn le64(out: &mut Vec<u8>, v: u64) {
    out.extend(v.to_le_bytes());
}

/// Hand-builds a one-member stored archive. With `zip64`, every size/offset/count is a sentinel
/// and the real values live in ZIP64 extra fields and the ZIP64 end-of-directory record.
fn build_zip(name: &str, body: &[u8], flags: u16, zip64: bool) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut z = Vec::new();
    let len = body.len() as u64;
    let (size32, extra_local) = if zip64 {
        let mut e = Vec::new();
        le16(&mut e, 0x0001);
        le16(&mut e, 16);
        le64(&mut e, len);
        le64(&mut e, len);
        (0xFFFF_FFFF, e)
    } else {
        (len as u32, Vec::new())
    };
    // Local file header.
    le32(&mut z, 0x0403_4b50);
    le16(&mut z, 45);
    le16(&mut z, flags);
    le16(&mut z, 0); // stored
    le32(&mut z, 0); // time/date
    le32(&mut z, 0); // crc (not checked)
    le32(&mut z, size32);
    le32(&mut z, size32);
    le16(&mut z, name.len() as u16);
    le16(&mut z, extra_local.len() as u16);
    z.extend(name.as_bytes());
    z.extend(&extra_local);
    z.extend(body);

    // Central directory.
    let cd_off = z.len() as u64;
    let extra_cd = if zip64 {
        let mut e = Vec::new();
        le16(&mut e, 0x0001);
        le16(&mut e, 24);
        le64(&mut e, len); // uncompressed
        le64(&mut e, len); // compressed
        le64(&mut e, 0); // local header offset
        e
    } else {
        Vec::new()
    };
    le32(&mut z, 0x0201_4b50);
    le16(&mut z, 45);
    le16(&mut z, 45);
    le16(&mut z, flags);
    le16(&mut z, 0);
    le32(&mut z, 0);
    le32(&mut z, 0);
    le32(&mut z, size32);
    le32(&mut z, size32);
    le16(&mut z, name.len() as u16);
    le16(&mut z, extra_cd.len() as u16);
    le16(&mut z, 0); // comment
    le16(&mut z, 0); // disk
    le16(&mut z, 0); // internal attrs
    le32(&mut z, 0); // external attrs
    le32(&mut z, if zip64 { 0xFFFF_FFFF } else { 0 });
    z.extend(name.as_bytes());
    z.extend(&extra_cd);
    let cd_size = z.len() as u64 - cd_off;

    if zip64 {
        let rec = z.len() as u64;
        le32(&mut z, 0x0606_4b50);
        le64(&mut z, 44); // size of the rest of the record
        le16(&mut z, 45);
        le16(&mut z, 45);
        le32(&mut z, 0);
        le32(&mut z, 0);
        le64(&mut z, 1); // entries on this disk
        le64(&mut z, 1); // total entries
        le64(&mut z, cd_size);
        le64(&mut z, cd_off);
        // Locator.
        le32(&mut z, 0x0706_4b50);
        le32(&mut z, 0);
        le64(&mut z, rec);
        le32(&mut z, 1);
    }
    // Classic EOCD.
    le32(&mut z, 0x0605_4b50);
    le16(&mut z, 0);
    le16(&mut z, 0);
    let (n16, cs, co) = if zip64 {
        (0xFFFF, 0xFFFF_FFFF, 0xFFFF_FFFF)
    } else {
        (1, cd_size as u32, cd_off as u32)
    };
    le16(&mut z, n16);
    le16(&mut z, n16);
    le32(&mut z, cs);
    le32(&mut z, co);
    le16(&mut z, 0);
    z
}

#[test]
fn reads_zip64_archives() {
    let zip = build_zip("big.bin", b"zip64 payload", 0, true);
    let ar = Archive::open(&zip).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(ar.entries.len(), 1);
    let e = &ar.entries[0];
    assert_eq!(e.name, "big.bin");
    assert_eq!(e.uncompressed_size, 13);
    assert_eq!(e.compressed_size, 13);
    assert_eq!(e.local_header_offset, 0);
    assert_eq!(ar.read(e).unwrap(), b"zip64 payload");

    // Sentinels without a locator are a clean error.
    let mut broken = zip.clone();
    let loc = broken.len() - 22 - 20;
    broken[loc] = 0;
    assert!(Archive::open(&broken).is_err());
}

#[test]
fn plain_builder_archive_round_trips() {
    let zip = build_zip("a.txt", b"hello", 0, false);
    let ar = Archive::open(&zip).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(ar.read(&ar.entries[0]).unwrap(), b"hello");
}

#[test]
fn encrypted_members_are_reported() {
    let zip = build_zip("secret.txt", b"\x01\x02ciphertext", 1, false);
    let ar = Archive::open(&zip).unwrap();
    let e = &ar.entries[0];
    assert!(e.is_encrypted());
    let err = ar.read(e).unwrap_err();
    assert!(err.contains("encrypted"), "{err}");
}

#[test]
fn hostile_entry_counts_are_capped() {
    // A ZIP64 record claiming 2^60 entries in a tiny directory.
    let mut zip = build_zip("x", b"y", 0, true);
    let rec = zip.len() - 22 - 20 - 56;
    zip[rec + 32..rec + 40].copy_from_slice(&(1u64 << 60).to_le_bytes());
    let ar = Archive::open(&zip).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(ar.entries.len(), 1);

    // A locator pointing at u64::MAX, and a directory offset at u64::MAX: errors, no panics.
    let mut zip = build_zip("x", b"y", 0, true);
    let loc = zip.len() - 22 - 20;
    zip[loc + 8..loc + 16].copy_from_slice(&u64::MAX.to_le_bytes());
    assert!(Archive::open(&zip).is_err());
    let mut zip = build_zip("x", b"y", 0, true);
    zip[rec + 48..rec + 56].copy_from_slice(&u64::MAX.to_le_bytes());
    let _ = Archive::open(&zip);
}
