`crates/orress-challenge/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! The authoring side of the CTF "Forge": scaffold a `challenge-kit` challenge from a template,
//! and submit its source + metadata to ctf.okiedocus.nl for review. The platform owns the flag, the
//! build and the challenge id — the author writes only the `check()` logic (see
//! `challenge_kit::assigned_id`), so nothing here touches flags.
//!
//! This crate is pure logic (template generation, file scaffolding, HTTP submit). The egui panel in
//! `orress-views` drives it and runs the build/submit on a background thread.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::time::Duration;

/// Everything about a challenge except its source.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Meta {
    pub title: String,
    pub category: String,
    pub technique: String,
    /// Difficulty 1..=5.
    pub level: u8,
    pub brief: String,
    pub input_label: String,
    pub hints: Vec<String>,
    pub writeup: String,
    pub bonus_points: u32,
}

impl Default for Meta {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            title: "My Challenge".into(),
            category: "crackme".into(),
            technique: String::new(),
            level: 1,
            brief: "Find the secret and recover the flag.".into(),
            input_label: "Answer".into(),
            hints: Vec::new(),
            writeup: String::new(),
            bonus_points: 0,
        }
    }
}

/// The bundled `challenge-kit` library source, vendored into a scaffolded project so it builds
/// offline, with no dependency on the (private) CTF platform repository.
const KIT_LIB_RS: &str = include_str!("../kit/lib.rs");
/// The bundled `challenge-kit` manifest (named `.in` so it is not itself a cargo manifest).
const KIT_CARGO_TOML: &str = include_str!("../kit/Cargo.toml.in");

/// The `challenge-kit` dependency spec body for a project that uses the vendored built-in kit.
pub const BUILTIN_KIT_DEP: &str = "path = \"challenge-kit\"";

/// Where a scaffolded challenge gets its `challenge-kit` dependency.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum KitSource {
    /// Vendor the bundled kit into the project (a `challenge-kit/` subfolder) and depend on it by
    /// path. Self-contained and offline; the default.
    #[default]
    BuiltIn,
    /// A custom Cargo dependency spec body, e.g. `git = "https://…"` or `path = "../checkout"`,
    /// for authors who keep their own `challenge-kit` checkout.
    External(String),
}

impl KitSource {
    /// The dependency spec body to write into the project's `Cargo.toml`.
    fn dep_spec(&self) -> &str {
        match self {
            Self::BuiltIn => BUILTIN_KIT_DEP,
            Self::External(s) => s,
        }
    }
}

/// The generated `main.rs` for a challenge, pre-filled from `meta`.
pub fn template(meta: &Meta) -> String {
    let title = rust_str(&meta.title);
    let brief = rust_str(&meta.brief);
    let label = rust_str(&meta.input_label);
    format!(
        r#"// Hide the Windows console in release builds.
#![cfg_attr(not(debug_assertions), windows_subsystem = "windows")]

//! {title_comment}
//!
//! Write your reverse-engineering puzzle below. The player types an input; your `check()` decides
//! whether it is correct. On `Verdict::Accept` the platform reveals that player's personal flag —
//! you never see or set the flag. Keep `id()` returning `challenge_kit::assigned_id()`.

use challenge_kit::{{Challenge, Verdict}};

struct MyChallenge;

impl Challenge for MyChallenge {{
    // The platform assigns the id at build time — leave this as-is.
    fn id(&self) -> &str {{ challenge_kit::assigned_id() }}
    fn title(&self) -> &str {{ {title} }}
    fn brief(&self) -> &str {{ {brief} }}
    fn input_label(&self) -> &str {{ {label} }}

    fn check(&mut self, input: &str) -> Verdict {{
        // TODO: your logic. Return Verdict::Accept(..) when the input is correct.
        if input.trim() == "open-sesame" {{
            Verdict::Accept("Correct!".into())
        }} else {{
            Verdict::Reject("Not quite — keep reversing.".into())
        }}
    }}
}}

fn main() {{
    let _ = challenge_kit::run(MyChallenge);
}}
"#,
        title_comment = one_line(&meta.title),
    )
}

/// The generated `Cargo.toml` for a scaffolded challenge. `kit_dep` is the dependency spec body
/// for `challenge-kit` (e.g. [`BUILTIN_KIT_DEP`] or `git = "..."`). The empty `[workspace]` table
/// makes the project its own workspace root, so it builds the same wherever it is placed (and the
/// vendored `challenge-kit` path dependency resolves without joining a surrounding workspace).
pub fn cargo_toml(kit_dep: &str) -> String {
    format!(
        r#"[package]
name = "challenge"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[[bin]]
name = "challenge"
path = "src/main.rs"

[dependencies]
challenge-kit = {{ {kit_dep} }}

[workspace]
"#
    )
}

/// Scaffolds a challenge project at `dir`: `Cargo.toml`, `src/main.rs` (from the template), a
/// `challenge.json` snapshot of the metadata, and — when `kit` is [`KitSource::BuiltIn`] — a
/// vendored `challenge-kit/` so the project builds offline. Returns the path to `src/main.rs`
/// (open it in the editor). Does not overwrite an existing `src/main.rs`.
pub fn scaffold(dir: &Path, meta: &Meta, kit: &KitSource) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
    let src_dir = dir.join("src");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&src_dir)
        .map_err(|e| format!("could not create {}: {e}", src_dir.display()))?;
    write_if_absent(&dir.join("Cargo.toml"), &cargo_toml(kit.dep_spec()))?;
    if *kit == KitSource::BuiltIn {
        vendor_kit(dir)?;
    }
    let main_rs = src_dir.join("main.rs");
    write_if_absent(&main_rs, &template(meta))?;
    // A metadata snapshot, for reference / re-submission.
    let meta_json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(meta).unwrap_or_default();
    let _ = std::fs::write(dir.join("challenge.json"), meta_json);
    Ok(main_rs)
}

/// Writes the bundled `challenge-kit` into `dir/challenge-kit/`, overwriting it so the vendored
/// copy always matches this build of ORRESS.
fn vendor_kit(dir: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
    let kit_dir = dir.join("challenge-kit");
    let kit_src = kit_dir.join("src");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&kit_src)
        .map_err(|e| format!("could not create {}: {e}", kit_src.display()))?;
    std::fs::write(kit_dir.join("Cargo.toml"), KIT_CARGO_TOML)
        .map_err(|e| format!("could not write the kit manifest: {e}"))?;
    std::fs::write(kit_src.join("lib.rs"), KIT_LIB_RS)
        .map_err(|e| format!("could not write the kit source: {e}"))?;
    Ok(())
}

fn write_if_absent(path: &Path, contents: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    if path.exists() {
        return Ok(());
    }
    std::fs::write(path, contents).map_err(|e| format!("could not write {}: {e}", path.display()))
}

/// Submit a challenge's source + metadata to the site's Forge for review. Logs in with the given
/// credentials (session cookie kept on the agent), verifies the session, then posts the form.
pub fn submit(
    base_url: &str,
    username: &str,
    password: &str,
    meta: &Meta,
    source: &str,
) -> Result<String, String> {
    let base = base_url.trim().trim_end_matches('/');
    if base.is_empty() {
        return Err("set the CTF site URL first".into());
    }
    let agent = ureq::AgentBuilder::new()
        .timeout(Duration::from_secs(60))
        .build();

    // Log in (the 303 redirect carries the session cookie; the agent's cookie store keeps it).
    agent
        .post(&format!("{base}/login"))
        .send_form(&[("username", username), ("password", password)])
        .map_err(describe)?;
    // Confirm the session took (login failures redirect back without a usable cookie).
    match agent.get(&format!("{base}/api/me")).call() {
        Ok(_) => {}
        Err(_) => {
            return Err(
                "login failed — check your username/password, and that your email is verified"
                    .into(),
            );
        }
    }

    let level = meta.level.to_string();
    let bonus = meta.bonus_points.to_string();
    let hints = meta.hints.join("\n");
    let fields: Vec<(&str, &str)> = vec![
        ("title", meta.title.as_str()),
        ("category", meta.category.as_str()),
        ("technique", meta.technique.as_str()),
        ("brief", meta.brief.as_str()),
        ("level", level.as_str()),
        ("bonus_points", bonus.as_str()),
        ("hints", hints.as_str()),
        ("writeup", meta.writeup.as_str()),
        ("source", source),
    ];
    let resp = agent
        .post(&format!("{base}/forge/submit"))
        .send_form(&fields)
        .map_err(describe)?;
    // On success the site redirects to /forge?msg=submitted; validation errors bounce back to the
    // form (/forge/submit?msg=...).
    if resp.get_url().contains("/forge/submit") {
        return Err("the site rejected the submission — check the fields and that the source is a challenge-kit challenge".into());
    }
    Ok("Submitted for review. Track it on the site's Forge page.".into())
}

fn describe(e: ureq::Error) -> String {
    match e {
        ureq::Error::Status(code, r) => {
            let body: String = r
                .into_string()
                .unwrap_or_default()
                .chars()
                .take(200)
                .collect();
            format!("HTTP {code}: {body}")
        }
        other => format!("request failed: {other}"),
    }
}

/// `s` made safe for a single `//!` comment line: newlines (which would end the comment and turn
/// the rest of the title into code) and other control characters (a bare CR is a compile error in
/// a doc comment) become spaces.
fn one_line(s: &str) -> String {
    s.chars()
        .map(|c| if c.is_control() { ' ' } else { c })
        .collect()
}

fn rust_str(s: &str) -> String {
    format!("{s:?}") // debug-formats a &str into a valid Rust string literal
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn template_bakes_in_metadata_and_uses_assigned_id() {
        let m = Meta {
            title: "Nibble \"Shuffle\"".into(),
            ..Meta::default()
        };
        let src = template(&m);
        assert!(src.contains("challenge_kit::assigned_id()"));
        // The title is embedded as a properly-escaped Rust string literal.
        assert!(src.contains(r#""Nibble \"Shuffle\"""#));
        assert!(src.contains("impl Challenge for MyChallenge"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_multiline_title_cannot_escape_the_doc_comment() {
        let m = Meta {
            title: "Line one\nfn evil() {}\r\nmore".into(),
            ..Meta::default()
        };
        let src = template(&m);
        assert!(src.contains("//! Line one fn evil() {}  more\n"), "{src}");
        // Every line that mentions `evil` is a comment or a string literal.
        for line in src.lines().filter(|l| l.contains("evil")) {
            let t = line.trim_start();
            assert!(t.starts_with("//!") || t.contains("\\n"), "{line}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn cargo_toml_uses_the_chosen_kit_dependency() {
        let builtin = cargo_toml(KitSource::BuiltIn.dep_spec());
        assert!(builtin.contains("challenge-kit = {"));
        assert!(builtin.contains(r#"path = "challenge-kit""#));
        assert!(builtin.contains("[workspace]"));
        // The built-in kit is vendored by path: it must not pull in any git repository.
        assert!(!builtin.contains("git ="));

        let external = cargo_toml(KitSource::External(r#"git = "https://x/y""#.into()).dep_spec());
        assert!(external.contains(r#"git = "https://x/y""#));
    }

    #[test]
    fn builtin_scaffold_vendors_the_kit_offline() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("orress-cw-test-{}", std::process::id()));
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
        let meta = Meta::default();
        let main = scaffold(&dir, &meta, &KitSource::BuiltIn).expect("scaffold");
        assert!(main.ends_with("main.rs"));
        assert!(dir.join("Cargo.toml").exists());
        assert!(dir.join("src/main.rs").exists());
        assert!(dir.join("challenge.json").exists());
        // The kit is vendored in, so the project needs no external repo to build.
        let kit_lib = dir.join("challenge-kit/src/lib.rs");
        assert!(dir.join("challenge-kit/Cargo.toml").exists());
        assert!(kit_lib.exists());
        let kit = std::fs::read_to_string(&kit_lib).unwrap();
        assert!(kit.contains("pub trait Challenge"));
        assert!(kit.contains("pub fn assigned_id()"));
        let src = std::fs::read_to_string(&main).unwrap();
        assert!(src.contains("challenge_kit::assigned_id()"));
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }

    #[test]
    fn external_scaffold_does_not_vendor_the_kit() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("orress-cw-ext-{}", std::process::id()));
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
        let kit = KitSource::External(r#"path = "../my-kit""#.into());
        scaffold(&dir, &Meta::default(), &kit).expect("scaffold");
        let toml = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("Cargo.toml")).unwrap();
        assert!(toml.contains(r#"path = "../my-kit""#));
        assert!(!dir.join("challenge-kit").exists());
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }
}

`crates/orress-cli/src/main.rs`:

```rs
//! orress-cli: ORRESS's engines on the command line.
//!
//! Inputs are files, or standard input when the file is omitted or `-`, so commands
//! chain with pipes:
//!
//! ```text
//! orress-cli slice crackme.exe 0x1840 64 | orress-cli xor -k 0x42 | orress-cli hex
//! orress-cli recipe "from_base64 | zlib_inflate" payload.txt
//! ```

use std::io::{Read, Write};
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::Arc;

use anyhow::{Context, Result, bail};
use clap::{Parser, Subcommand};
use orress_transforms::{Recipe, Step};

#[derive(Parser)]
#[command(
    name = "orress-cli",
    version,
    about = "ORRESS reverse-engineering tools on the command line"
)]
struct Cli {
    #[command(subcommand)]
    command: Command,
}

#[derive(Subcommand)]
enum Command {
    /// What is this file? Format, protections, detections, hashes, tips.
    Info {
        file: PathBuf,
        /// Machine-readable output.
        #[arg(long)]
        json: bool,
    },
    /// Readable strings in a file.
    Strings {
        file: PathBuf,
        /// Minimum length.
        #[arg(short = 'n', long, default_value_t = 4)]
        min: usize,
        /// Only strings that look like CTF flags.
        #[arg(long)]
        flags: bool,
        /// Print the file offset of each string.
        #[arg(short = 'o', long)]
        offsets: bool,
    },
    /// List the functions ORRESS finds.
    Funcs { file: PathBuf },
    /// Detect VM-based obfuscation: functions whose shape is a bytecode interpreter dispatch loop.
    Vm { file: PathBuf },
    /// Disassemble a function: `main` (default), `entry`, a name or a hex address.
    Disasm {
        file: PathBuf,
        target: Option<String>,
    },
    /// Decompile a function to Rust-style pseudocode: `main` (default), `entry`, a name
    /// or a hex address.
    Decompile {
        file: PathBuf,
        target: Option<String>,
    },
    /// Run a Rhai script against a binary's analysis (functions, strings, bytes, disassembly).
    Script {
        file: PathBuf,
        /// Path to a `.rhai` script, or `-e CODE` to run inline code.
        script: PathBuf,
        /// Treat `script` as inline code rather than a file path.
        #[arg(short = 'e', long)]
        eval: bool,
    },
    /// Run a pwntools-style exploit script against a binary (tubes, packing, cyclic, ROP).
    Exploit {
        file: PathBuf,
        /// Path to a `.rhai` script, or `-e CODE` to run inline code.
        script: PathBuf,
        /// Treat `script` as inline code rather than a file path.
        #[arg(short = 'e', long)]
        eval: bool,
    },
    /// List the ROP gadgets in a binary (sequences ending in ret/syscall).
    Gadgets {
        file: PathBuf,
        /// Only show gadgets whose text contains this (case-insensitive).
        #[arg(long)]
        filter: Option<String>,
    },
    /// Find one-shot execve("/bin/sh") gadgets in a libc.
    OneGadget { file: PathBuf },
    /// Run a Workbench recipe, e.g. "from_base64 | xor key=0x41".
    Recipe {
        recipe: String,
        file: Option<PathBuf>,
    },
    /// Try to find a decoding recipe automatically.
    Magic {
        file: Option<PathBuf>,
        /// Maximum number of steps.
        #[arg(short, long, default_value_t = 3)]
        depth: usize,
    },
    /// List all Workbench operations and their parameters.
    Ops,
    /// XOR with a repeating key (text, 0x41..., or hex:41 42).
    Xor {
        #[arg(short, long)]
        key: String,
        file: Option<PathBuf>,
    },
    /// Base64 encode, or decode with -d.
    B64 {
        #[arg(short, long)]
        decode: bool,
        file: Option<PathBuf>,
    },
    /// Hex encode, or decode with -d.
    Hex {
        #[arg(short, long)]
        decode: bool,
        file: Option<PathBuf>,
    },
    /// URL encode, or decode with -d.
    Url {
        #[arg(short, long)]
        decode: bool,
        file: Option<PathBuf>,
    },
    /// RC4 encrypt/decrypt.
    Rc4 {
        #[arg(short, long)]
        key: String,
        file: Option<PathBuf>,
    },
    /// MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256 and CRC-32 of the input.
    Hash { file: Option<PathBuf> },
    /// Entropy of the input, overall and per block.
    Entropy {
        file: Option<PathBuf>,
        /// Block size for the per-block view (0 = overall only).
        #[arg(short, long, default_value_t = 0)]
        block: usize,
    },
    /// Copy bytes: OFFSET and optional LENGTH (decimal or 0x hex).
    Slice {
        file: PathBuf,
        offset: String,
        length: Option<String>,
    },
    /// Search files for a byte pattern (hex with ?? wildcards) or text (-t).
    Bgrep {
        pattern: String,
        files: Vec<PathBuf>,
        /// Search for text instead of hex bytes.
        #[arg(short, long)]
        text: bool,
    },
    /// Decode a timestamp: Unix seconds or Windows FILETIME.
    Tsdec { value: String },
    /// Write a patched copy: OFFSET HEXBYTES -o OUTPUT.
    Patch {
        file: PathBuf,
        offset: String,
        bytes: String,
        #[arg(short, long)]
        output: PathBuf,
    },
}

fn read_input(file: Option<&PathBuf>) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
    match file {
        Some(path) if path.as_os_str() != "-" => {
            std::fs::read(path).with_context(|| format!("reading {}", path.display()))
        }
        _ => {
            let mut buf = Vec::new();
            std::io::stdin()
                .read_to_end(&mut buf)
                .context("reading standard input")?;
            Ok(buf)
        }
    }
}

fn write_out(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<()> {
    let mut out = std::io::stdout().lock();
    out.write_all(bytes)?;
    out.flush()?;
    Ok(())
}

fn number(text: &str) -> Result<u64> {
    let t = text.trim().replace('_', "");
    let value = match t.strip_prefix("0x").or_else(|| t.strip_prefix("0X")) {
        Some(hex) => u64::from_str_radix(hex, 16),
        None => t.parse(),
    };
    value.with_context(|| format!("`{text}` is not a number"))
}

fn transform(step: Step, file: Option<&PathBuf>) -> Result<()> {
    let input = read_input(file)?;
    let out = step.apply(&input).map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)?;
    write_out(&out)
}

fn main() -> Result<()> {
    let cli = Cli::parse();
    match cli.command {
        Command::Info { file, json } => info(&file, json),
        Command::Strings {
            file,
            min,
            flags,
            offsets,
        } => {
            let data = read_input(Some(&file))?;
            for s in orress_bytes::strings::extract(&data, min, usize::MAX) {
                if flags && !orress_bytes::strings::looks_like_flag(&s.text) {
                    continue;
                }
                if offsets {
                    println!("0x{:08x}  {}", s.offset, s.text);
                } else {
                    println!("{}", s.text);
                }
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        Command::Funcs { file } => funcs(&file),
        Command::Vm { file } => vm(&file),
        Command::Script { file, script, eval } => run_script(&file, &script, eval),
        Command::Exploit { file, script, eval } => run_exploit(&file, &script, eval),
        Command::Gadgets { file, filter } => list_gadgets(&file, filter.as_deref()),
        Command::OneGadget { file } => one_gadget(&file),
        Command::Disasm { file, target } => disasm(&file, target.as_deref().unwrap_or("main")),
        Command::Decompile { file, target } => {
            let (info, p) = analyze(&file)?;
            let addr = resolve(&info, &p, target.as_deref().unwrap_or("main"))?;
            let conv = orress_decompiler::convention(info.format);
            let out =
                orress_decompiler::decompile(&p, addr, conv).map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("{e}"))?;
            print!("{}", out.text());
            Ok(())
        }
        Command::Recipe { recipe, file } => {
            let recipe = Recipe::parse(&recipe).map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)?;
            let input = read_input(file.as_ref())?;
            let out = recipe.output(&input).map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)?;
            write_out(&out)
        }
        Command::Magic { file, depth } => {
            let input = read_input(file.as_ref())?;
            let suggestions = orress_transforms::magic(&input, depth);
            if suggestions.is_empty() {
                println!("Nothing found that is more readable than the input.");
            }
            for s in suggestions {
                let preview: String = String::from_utf8_lossy(&s.output)
                    .chars()
                    .take(70)
                    .collect();
                println!(
                    "{:<45}  {}  ({})",
                    s.recipe.to_string(),
                    preview.escape_debug(),
                    s.why
                );
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        Command::Ops => {
            for op in orress_transforms::ops() {
                let params: Vec<String> = op
                    .params
                    .iter()
                    .map(|p| format!("{}={}", p.name, p.default))
                    .collect();
                println!("{:<18} {:<12} {}", op.id, op.category.name(), op.explain);
                if !params.is_empty() {
                    let shown: Vec<String> = params
                        .iter()
                        .map(|p| p.chars().take(40).collect())
                        .collect();
                    println!("{:<31} params: {}", "", shown.join(", "));
                }
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        Command::Xor { key, file } => transform(Step::new("xor").with("key", &key), file.as_ref()),
        Command::B64 { decode, file } => transform(
            Step::new(if decode { "from_base64" } else { "to_base64" }),
            file.as_ref(),
        ),
        Command::Hex { decode, file } => transform(
            if decode {
                Step::new("from_hex")
            } else {
                Step::new("to_hex").with("separator", "")
            },
            file.as_ref(),
        ),
        Command::Url { decode, file } => transform(
            Step::new(if decode { "from_url" } else { "to_url" }),
            file.as_ref(),
        ),
        Command::Rc4 { key, file } => transform(Step::new("rc4").with("key", &key), file.as_ref()),
        Command::Hash { file } => {
            let input = read_input(file.as_ref())?;
            for op in ["md5", "sha1", "sha256", "crc32"] {
                let out = Step::new(op).apply(&input).map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)?;
                println!("{op:<7} {}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&out));
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        Command::Entropy { file, block } => {
            let input = read_input(file.as_ref())?;
            let e = orress_bytes::entropy::shannon(&input);
            println!(
                "{e:.3} bits per byte: {}",
                orress_bytes::entropy::describe(e)
            );
            if block > 0 {
                for (i, e) in orress_bytes::entropy::blocks(&input, block)
                    .iter()
                    .enumerate()
                {
                    let bar = "#".repeat((e * 4.0).round() as usize);
                    println!("0x{:08x}  {e:5.2}  {bar}", i * block);
                }
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        Command::Slice {
            file,
            offset,
            length,
        } => {
            let data = read_input(Some(&file))?;
            let start = number(&offset)? as usize;
            if start > data.len() {
                bail!(
                    "offset 0x{start:x} is past the end of the file (0x{:x} bytes)",
                    data.len()
                );
            }
            let end = match length {
                // A length past the end (even one that would overflow) is clamped to EOF.
                Some(l) => start.saturating_add(number(&l)? as usize).min(data.len()),
                None => data.len(),
            };
            write_out(&data[start..end])
        }
        Command::Bgrep {
            pattern,
            files,
            text,
        } => {
            let p = if text {
                orress_bytes::search::Pattern::text(&pattern, false)
            } else {
                orress_bytes::search::Pattern::parse_hex(&pattern)
            }
            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("{e}"))?;
            let mut found = false;
            for file in &files {
                let data = read_input(Some(file))?;
                let mut pos = 0;
                while let Some(at) = p.find_from(&data, pos) {
                    println!("{}: 0x{at:08x}", file.display());
                    found = true;
                    pos = at + 1;
                }
            }
            if !found {
                std::process::exit(1);
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        Command::Tsdec { value } => {
            let v = number(&value)?;
            println!(
                "as Unix time (seconds): {}",
                orress_bytes::inspect::format_unix(v as i64)
            );
            if v > 11_644_473_600 * 10_000_000 {
                let secs = (v / 10_000_000) as i64 - 11_644_473_600;
                println!(
                    "as Windows FILETIME:    {}",
                    orress_bytes::inspect::format_unix(secs)
                );
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        Command::Patch {
            file,
            offset,
            bytes,
            output,
        } => {
            if output == file {
                bail!("refusing to overwrite the input; choose another --output");
            }
            let mut data = read_input(Some(&file))?;
            let start = number(&offset)? as usize;
            let new = orress_transforms::parse_key(&format!("hex:{bytes}"))
                .map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)?;
            let end = start
                .checked_add(new.len())
                .context("the patch offset is out of range")?;
            if end > data.len() {
                bail!("the patch goes past the end of the file");
            }
            data[start..end].copy_from_slice(&new);
            std::fs::write(&output, &data)
                .with_context(|| format!("writing {}", output.display()))?;
            eprintln!(
                "patched {} byte(s) at 0x{start:x}, wrote {}",
                new.len(),
                output.display()
            );
            Ok(())
        }
    }
}

fn info(file: &PathBuf, json: bool) -> Result<()> {
    let data = read_input(Some(file))?;
    let i = orress_loaders::triage(&data);
    if json {
        let value = serde_json::json!({
            "file": file.display().to_string(),
            "size": i.size,
            "format": i.format.name(),
            "kind": i.kind.name(),
            "arch": i.arch,
            "entry": i.entry,
            "image_base": i.image_base,
            "entropy": i.entropy,
            "hashes": { "md5": i.hashes.md5, "sha1": i.hashes.sha1, "sha256": i.hashes.sha256, "imphash": i.hashes.imphash },
            "sections": i.sections.iter().map(|s| serde_json::json!({
                "name": s.name, "offset": s.offset, "size": s.file_size, "address": s.address,
                "perms": s.perms.label(), "entropy": s.entropy,
            })).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            "imports": i.imports.iter().map(|x| format!("{}!{}", x.library, x.name)).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            "protections": i.protections.iter().map(|p| serde_json::json!({
                "name": p.name, "state": format!("{:?}", p.state), "detail": p.detail,
            })).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            "detections": i.detections.iter().map(|d| serde_json::json!({
                "category": d.category.name(), "name": d.name, "evidence": d.evidence,
            })).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            "insights": i.insights.iter().map(|x| serde_json::json!({
                "level": format!("{:?}", x.level), "title": x.title, "body": x.body,
            })).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        });
        println!("{}", serde_json::to_string_pretty(&value)?);
        return Ok(());
    }
    println!("{}", file.display());
    println!("  {} · {} · {}", i.format.name(), i.kind.name(), i.arch);
    println!(
        "  size {} bytes, entropy {:.2} ({})",
        i.size,
        i.entropy,
        orress_bytes::entropy::describe(i.entropy)
    );
    if let Some(e) = i.entry {
        println!("  entry point 0x{e:x}");
    }
    println!("  sha256 {}", i.hashes.sha256);
    for s in &i.sections {
        println!(
            "  section {:<10} {} offset 0x{:<8x} size 0x{:<8x} entropy {:.2}",
            s.name,
            s.perms.label(),
            s.offset,
            s.file_size,
            s.entropy.unwrap_or(0.0)
        );
    }
    for p in &i.protections {
        println!("  {:<26} {:?} ({})", p.name, p.state, p.detail);
    }
    for d in &i.detections {
        println!(
            "  detected {}: {} [{}]",
            d.category.name(),
            d.name,
            d.evidence
        );
    }
    for x in &i.insights {
        println!("  {:?}: {}", x.level, x.title);
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn analyze(file: &PathBuf) -> Result<(orress_loaders::BinaryInfo, orress_analysis::Program)> {
    let data = Arc::new(read_input(Some(file))?);
    let info = orress_loaders::triage(&data);
    let strings = orress_bytes::strings::extract(&data, 4, 500_000);
    let program = orress_analysis::Program::analyze(&info, Arc::clone(&data), &strings)
        .with_context(|| format!("cannot disassemble {} ({})", info.arch, file.display()))?;
    Ok((info, program))
}

fn run_script(file: &PathBuf, script: &PathBuf, eval: bool) -> Result<()> {
    let src = if eval {
        script.to_string_lossy().into_owned()
    } else {
        std::fs::read_to_string(script)
            .with_context(|| format!("cannot read script {}", script.display()))?
    };
    let data = Arc::new(read_input(Some(file))?);
    let info = orress_loaders::triage(&data);
    let strings = orress_bytes::strings::extract(&data, 4, 500_000);
    let program = orress_analysis::Program::analyze(&info, Arc::clone(&data), &strings)
        .with_context(|| format!("cannot analyze {}", file.display()))?;
    let strs: Vec<&str> = strings.iter().map(|s| s.text.as_str()).collect();
    match orress_script::run(&src, &program, &strs) {
        Ok(out) => {
            print!("{out}");
            if !out.ends_with('\n') {
                println!();
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        Err(e) => anyhow::bail!("script error: {e}"),
    }
}

fn run_exploit(file: &PathBuf, script: &PathBuf, eval: bool) -> Result<()> {
    let src = if eval {
        script.to_string_lossy().into_owned()
    } else {
        std::fs::read_to_string(script)
            .with_context(|| format!("cannot read script {}", script.display()))?
    };
    let data = Arc::new(read_input(Some(file))?);
    let info = orress_loaders::triage(&data);
    let strings = orress_bytes::strings::extract(&data, 4, 500_000);
    let program = orress_analysis::Program::analyze(&info, Arc::clone(&data), &strings)
        .with_context(|| format!("cannot analyze {}", file.display()))?;
    let ctx = exploit_ctx(&info, &program, &data);

    // Stream the script's output to stdout as it runs.
    let (tx, rx) = std::sync::mpsc::channel::<String>();
    let printer = std::thread::spawn(move || {
        for line in rx {
            print!("{line}");
        }
    });
    let cancel = std::sync::Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false));
    let result = orress_script::run_exploit(&src, ctx, tx, cancel);
    let _ = printer.join();
    match result {
        Ok(()) => Ok(()),
        Err(e) => anyhow::bail!("exploit error: {e}"),
    }
}

/// Builds the scripting context (symbols/GOT/PLT/exec sections) from a binary's analysis.
fn exploit_ctx(
    info: &orress_loaders::BinaryInfo,
    program: &orress_analysis::Program,
    data: &[u8],
) -> orress_script::ExploitCtx {
    use std::collections::HashMap;
    let mut symbols: HashMap<String, u64> = HashMap::new();
    for s in &info.function_symbols {
        symbols.entry(s.name.clone()).or_insert(s.address);
    }
    for e in &info.exports {
        if e.address != 0 {
            symbols.entry(e.name.clone()).or_insert(e.address);
        }
    }
    let got = info
        .import_slots
        .iter()
        .map(|s| (s.name.clone(), s.address))
        .collect();
    let mut plt: HashMap<String, u64> = HashMap::new();
    for f in program.functions.values() {
        if f.kind == orress_analysis::FunctionKind::Thunk
            && let Some(name) = program.name(f.entry)
            && let Some(base_name) = name.text.strip_suffix("@plt")
        {
            plt.entry(base_name.to_string()).or_insert(f.entry);
        }
    }
    let exec = info
        .sections
        .iter()
        .filter(|s| s.perms.execute)
        .filter_map(|s| Some((s.address, data.get(s.file_range()?)?.to_vec())))
        .collect();
    let binsh = orress_bytes::search::Pattern::text("/bin/sh", false)
        .ok()
        .and_then(|p| p.find_from(data, 0))
        .and_then(|off| info.offset_to_address(off as u64));
    let sections = info
        .sections
        .iter()
        .map(|s| (s.name.clone(), s.address))
        .collect();
    orress_script::ExploitCtx {
        base: info.image_base,
        isa: program.isa,
        symbols,
        got,
        plt,
        exec,
        binsh,
        sections,
    }
}

fn one_gadget(file: &PathBuf) -> Result<()> {
    let data = Arc::new(read_input(Some(file))?);
    let info = orress_loaders::triage(&data);
    let strings = orress_bytes::strings::extract(&data, 4, 500_000);
    let program = orress_analysis::Program::analyze(&info, Arc::clone(&data), &strings)
        .with_context(|| format!("cannot analyze {}", file.display()))?;
    let ctx = exploit_ctx(&info, &program, &data);
    let Some(binsh) = ctx.binsh else {
        anyhow::bail!("no \"/bin/sh\" string found in {}", file.display());
    };
    let execve: Vec<u64> = ["execve", "system"]
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|n| ctx.symbols.get(*n).copied())
        .collect();
    let sections: Vec<(u64, &[u8])> = ctx.exec.iter().map(|(a, b)| (*a, b.as_slice())).collect();
    let gadgets = orress_pwn::find_one_gadgets(&sections, binsh, &execve, ctx.isa);
    if gadgets.is_empty() {
        println!("no one_gadgets found");
    }
    for g in gadgets {
        let cons = if g.constraints.is_empty() {
            "(no outstanding constraints)".to_string()
        } else {
            g.constraints.join(", ")
        };
        println!("{:#x}  {cons}", g.addr);
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn list_gadgets(file: &PathBuf, filter: Option<&str>) -> Result<()> {
    let data = read_input(Some(file))?;
    let info = orress_loaders::triage(&data);
    let isa = orress_arch::Isa::from_arch_name(&info.arch).unwrap_or(orress_arch::Isa::X64);
    let sections: Vec<(u64, &[u8])> = info
        .sections
        .iter()
        .filter(|s| s.perms.execute)
        .filter_map(|s| Some((s.address, data.get(s.file_range()?)?)))
        .collect();
    let needle = filter.map(str::to_lowercase);
    for g in orress_pwn::find_gadgets(&sections, isa, 6) {
        if needle
            .as_deref()
            .is_none_or(|n| g.text.to_lowercase().contains(n))
        {
            println!("{:#x}  {}", g.addr, g.text);
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn vm(file: &PathBuf) -> Result<()> {
    let (_, p) = analyze(file)?;
    let reports = orress_vm::scan(&p);
    if reports.is_empty() {
        println!("No VM-based obfuscation detected (no interpreter dispatch loop found).");
        return Ok(());
    }
    println!("{} likely VM interpreter(s):", reports.len());
    for r in &reports {
        let name = p
            .name(r.entry)
            .map_or_else(|| format!("sub_{:x}", r.entry), |n| n.text.clone());
        println!(
            "  {name} @ {:#x}: dispatcher {:#x}, {} handlers / {} blocks (fan-in {}), {:.0}% confidence",
            r.entry,
            r.dispatcher,
            r.handlers,
            r.blocks,
            r.max_fan_in,
            r.confidence * 100.0
        );
        let dis = orress_vm::disassemble(&p, r);
        if let Some(bc) = orress_vm::bytecode(&p, r) {
            // The program's true length is where its disassembly ends (at a halt), not the raw blob
            // extent (which can run into trailing data).
            let prog_len = dis
                .as_ref()
                .and_then(|d| d.last())
                .map_or(bc.len.unwrap_or(0) as usize, |i| {
                    i.offset + 1 + i.operands.len()
                });
            println!("    bytecode blob at {:#x} ({prog_len} bytes):", bc.base);
            if let Some(bytes) = p.memory.read(bc.base, prog_len) {
                for (i, chunk) in bytes.chunks(16).enumerate() {
                    let hex: Vec<String> = chunk.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect();
                    println!("      {:04x}: {}", i * 16, hex.join(" "));
                }
            }
        }
        if let Some(dis) = &dis {
            println!("    bytecode disassembly ({} instructions):", dis.len());
            for ins in dis {
                let ops: Vec<String> = ins.operands.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:#04x}")).collect();
                println!(
                    "      {:04x}: op{:<3} {:<13} {}",
                    ins.offset,
                    ins.opcode,
                    ins.op,
                    ops.join(", ")
                );
            }
        }
        // The opcode table: the first step of devirtualization.
        let table = orress_vm::handlers(&p, r);
        if !table.is_empty() {
            println!("    opcode table ({} entries):", table.len());
            for h in &table {
                let ops = if h.ops.is_empty() {
                    "-".to_string()
                } else {
                    h.ops.join(", ")
                };
                println!(
                    "      op {:>3}: {:<13} handler {:#x} ({} insns)  [{ops}]",
                    h.opcode,
                    orress_vm::operation(h),
                    h.address,
                    h.insns
                );
            }
        }
        // The devirtualization payoff: concolically solve for the key that passes the interpreter.
        if let Some(sol) = orress_vm::solve(&p, r) {
            let shown = String::from_utf8_lossy(&sol.key);
            let status = if sol.complete { "verified" } else { "partial" };
            println!(
                "    recovered key ({status}, {} constraints): {:?}",
                sol.constraints, shown
            );
            if !sol.checks.is_empty() {
                println!("    lifted checks:");
                for c in &sol.checks {
                    println!("      {c}");
                }
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn funcs(file: &PathBuf) -> Result<()> {
    let (_, p) = analyze(file)?;
    for (entry, f) in &p.functions {
        let name = p
            .name(*entry)
            .map_or_else(|| format!("sub_{entry:x}"), |n| n.text.clone());
        println!(
            "0x{entry:x}  {name:<40} {:>6} bytes  {:>4} blocks  {:>4} callers",
            f.size(),
            f.blocks.len(),
            p.xrefs(*entry).len()
        );
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn resolve(
    info: &orress_loaders::BinaryInfo,
    p: &orress_analysis::Program,
    target: &str,
) -> Result<u64> {
    Ok(match target {
        "main" => p.main.context("no main function found; try `entry`")?,
        "entry" => info.entry.context("the file has no entry point")?,
        t => match p.names.iter().find(|(_, n)| n.text == t) {
            Some((&a, _)) => a,
            None => number(t)?,
        },
    })
}

fn disasm(file: &PathBuf, target: &str) -> Result<()> {
    let (info, p) = analyze(file)?;
    let addr = resolve(&info, &p, target)?;
    let f = p
        .function_containing(addr)
        .with_context(|| format!("no function at 0x{addr:x}"))?;
    let name = p
        .name(f.entry)
        .map_or_else(|| format!("sub_{:x}", f.entry), |n| n.text.clone());
    println!("{name}:  ; {} blocks", f.blocks.len());
    for block in &f.blocks {
        if block.start != f.entry {
            println!("loc_{:x}:", block.start);
        }
        for &a in &block.insns {
            let insn = p.decode(a).context("decode")?;
            let ops: String = insn
                .operands
                .iter()
                .map(|t| match t.kind {
                    orress_analysis::TokenKind::Address(x) => p.name(x).map_or_else(
                        || {
                            if p.labels.contains(&x) {
                                format!("loc_{x:x}")
                            } else {
                                t.text.clone()
                            }
                        },
                        |n| n.text.clone(),
                    ),
                    _ => t.text.clone(),
                })
                .collect();
            let comment = insn
                .data_refs
                .iter()
                .find_map(|r| p.string_refs.get(r))
                .map(|s| {
                    format!(
                        "  ; \"{}\"",
                        s.chars().take(50).collect::<String>().escape_debug()
                    )
                })
                .unwrap_or_default();
            println!("  {a:x}  {:<8} {ops}{comment}", insn.mnemonic);
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

`crates/orress-cli/tests/cli.rs`:

//! Runs the real orress-cli binary.

use std::io::Write;
use std::process::{Command, Stdio};

fn run(args: &[&str], stdin: &[u8]) -> (bool, Vec<u8>) {
    let mut child = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_orress-cli"))
        .args(args)
        .stdin(Stdio::piped())
        .stdout(Stdio::piped())
        .stderr(Stdio::piped())
        .spawn()
        .expect("binary runs");
    child.stdin.take().unwrap().write_all(stdin).unwrap();
    let out = child.wait_with_output().unwrap();
    (out.status.success(), out.stdout)
}

fn crackme(name: &str) -> String {
    format!(
        "{}/../../academy/crackmes/bin/{name}",
        env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")
    )
}

#[test]
fn recipe_and_shortcuts() {
    let (ok, out) = run(&["recipe", "to_base64 | from_base64 | rot13"], b"Hello");
    assert!(ok);
    assert_eq!(out, b"Uryyb");
    let (_, out) = run(&["xor", "-k", "0x01"], b"AB");
    assert_eq!(out, b"@C");
    let (_, out) = run(&["hex", "-d"], b"48 69");
    assert_eq!(out, b"Hi");
    let (ok, _) = run(&["recipe", "no_such_op"], b"");
    assert!(!ok, "bad recipes fail");
}

#[test]
fn magic_finds_the_flag() {
    let (_, encoded) = run(
        &["recipe", "xor key=0x33 | to_base64"],
        b"flag{piped_through_the_cli}",
    );
    let (ok, out) = run(&["magic"], &encoded);
    assert!(ok);
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out);
    assert!(text.contains("flag{piped_through_the_cli}"), "{text}");
}

#[test]
fn analysis_commands_on_a_crackme() {
    let file = crackme("crackme02.exe");
    let (ok, out) = run(&["disasm", &file, "main"], b"");
    assert!(ok);
    assert!(String::from_utf8_lossy(&out).starts_with("main:"));
    let (ok, out) = run(&["info", &file, "--json"], b"");
    assert!(ok);
    let json: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&out).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(json["arch"], "x86-64");
    let (found, _) = run(&["bgrep", "4D 5A", &file], b"");
    assert!(found);
    let (found, _) = run(&["bgrep", "-t", "definitely not inside", &file], b"");
    assert!(!found, "bgrep exits with failure when nothing matches");
}

#[test]
fn patch_writes_a_copy() {
    let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("orress-cli-{}", std::process::id()));
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
    let input = dir.join("in.bin");
    let output = dir.join("out.bin");
    std::fs::write(&input, b"\x74\x05AAAA").unwrap();
    let (ok, _) = run(
        &[
            "patch",
            input.to_str().unwrap(),
            "0",
            "75",
            "-o",
            output.to_str().unwrap(),
        ],
        b"",
    );
    assert!(ok);
    assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&output).unwrap(), b"\x75\x05AAAA");
    let (ok, _) = run(
        &[
            "patch",
            input.to_str().unwrap(),
            "0",
            "75",
            "-o",
            input.to_str().unwrap(),
        ],
        b"",
    );
    assert!(!ok, "never overwrites the input");
    std::fs::remove_dir_all(dir).ok();
}

#[test]
fn huge_offsets_and_lengths_error_or_clamp_instead_of_panicking() {
    let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("orress-cli-ovf-{}", std::process::id()));
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
    let input = dir.join("in.bin");
    std::fs::write(&input, b"ABCDEF").unwrap();
    let file = input.to_str().unwrap();

    // A length that would overflow `start + length` is clamped to the end of the file.
    let (ok, out) = run(&["slice", file, "2", "0xffffffffffffffff"], b"");
    assert!(ok);
    assert_eq!(out, b"CDEF");

    // A patch offset that would overflow is a clean error, not a panic.
    let out = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_orress-cli"))
        .args([
            "patch",
            file,
            "0xffffffffffffffff",
            "7575",
            "-o",
            dir.join("out.bin").to_str().unwrap(),
        ])
        .output()
        .unwrap();
    assert!(!out.status.success());
    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr);
    assert!(!stderr.contains("panicked"), "{stderr}");
    std::fs::remove_dir_all(dir).ok();
}

#[test]
fn decompile_prints_rust() {
    let file = crackme("crackme01.exe");
    let (ok, out) = run(&["decompile", &file], b"");
    assert!(ok);
    let text = String::from_utf8(out).unwrap();
    assert!(text.starts_with("fn main()"), "{text}");
    assert!(text.contains("\"open_sesame_101\""), "{text}");
}

`crates/orress-collab/src/client.rs`:

```rs
//! The relay client: connects to an [`orress-relay`](../orress_relay) over a WebSocket on a
//! background thread (blocking `tungstenite`, like the LSP/DAP transports), joins a room, and
//! bridges between the app and the wire — sealing outgoing [`ClientMessage`]s with the room key
//! into `Data` frames, and opening incoming `Data` frames back into `ClientMessage`s.
//!
//! Both `ws://` and `wss://` are supported (TLS via rustls with bundled webpki roots); the payloads
//! are end-to-end encrypted regardless, so `wss://` only adds transport privacy/integrity on top.

use std::net::TcpStream;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
use std::sync::mpsc::{Receiver, Sender, channel};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::Duration;

use tungstenite::Message;
use tungstenite::stream::MaybeTlsStream;

use crate::crypto::RoomKey;
use crate::protocol::{ClientMessage, Envelope};

const POLL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(40);

/// A connected relay client. Dropping it signals the worker thread to stop.
pub struct RelayClient {
    outgoing: Sender<ClientMessage>,
    incoming: Receiver<ClientMessage>,
    connected: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    error: Arc<Mutex<Option<String>>>,
    stop: Arc<AtomicBool>,
}

impl RelayClient {
    /// Connects to `url` (`ws://` or `wss://`, e.g. `ws://host:8787`) and joins `room`, sealing
    /// traffic with the key derived from `room` + `passphrase`. The connect, TLS and WebSocket
    /// handshakes happen here (so a bad URL fails fast); the send/receive loop then runs on a
    /// background thread.
    pub fn connect(url: &str, room: &str, passphrase: &str) -> Result<RelayClient, String> {
        let key = RoomKey::derive(room, passphrase)?;
        let url = normalize_url(url)?;
        let (mut ws, _resp) =
            tungstenite::connect(&url).map_err(|e| format!("could not reach relay {url}: {e}"))?;
        ws.send(Message::Binary(
            Envelope::Join {
                room: room.to_string(),
            }
            .encode(),
        ))
        .map_err(|e| format!("could not join the room: {e}"))?;
        set_read_timeout(ws.get_mut(), POLL);

        let (out_tx, out_rx) = channel::<ClientMessage>();
        let (in_tx, in_rx) = channel::<ClientMessage>();
        let connected = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(true));
        let error = Arc::new(Mutex::new(None));
        let stop = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));

        let worker = Worker {
            ws,
            key,
            out_rx,
            in_tx,
            connected: Arc::clone(&connected),
            error: Arc::clone(&error),
            stop: Arc::clone(&stop),
        };
        std::thread::spawn(move || worker.run());

        Ok(RelayClient {
            outgoing: out_tx,
            incoming: in_rx,
            connected,
            error,
            stop,
        })
    }

    /// Queues a message to seal and broadcast (non-blocking).
    pub fn send(&self, msg: ClientMessage) {
        let _ = self.outgoing.send(msg);
    }

    /// The next decrypted message from a peer, if any (non-blocking).
    pub fn try_recv(&self) -> Option<ClientMessage> {
        self.incoming.try_recv().ok()
    }

    pub fn is_connected(&self) -> bool {
        self.connected.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
    }

    pub fn error(&self) -> Option<String> {
        self.error.lock().unwrap().clone()
    }
}

impl Drop for RelayClient {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.stop.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }
}

struct Worker {
    ws: tungstenite::WebSocket<MaybeTlsStream<TcpStream>>,
    key: RoomKey,
    out_rx: Receiver<ClientMessage>,
    in_tx: Sender<ClientMessage>,
    connected: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    error: Arc<Mutex<Option<String>>>,
    stop: Arc<AtomicBool>,
}

impl Worker {
    fn run(mut self) {
        use std::io::ErrorKind;
        while !self.stop.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
            // Seal and send anything the app queued.
            let mut ok = true;
            while let Ok(msg) = self.out_rx.try_recv() {
                match msg.seal(&self.key) {
                    Ok(payload) => {
                        if let Err(e) = self
                            .ws
                            .send(Message::Binary(Envelope::Data { payload }.encode()))
                        {
                            self.fail(format!("relay connection lost while sending: {e}"));
                            ok = false;
                            break;
                        }
                    }
                    Err(e) => self.fail(e),
                }
            }
            if !ok {
                break;
            }
            match self.ws.read() {
                Ok(Message::Binary(bytes)) => {
                    // A message we cannot open (wrong key / noise) is skipped, not fatal.
                    if let Some(Envelope::Data { payload }) = Envelope::decode(&bytes)
                        && let Ok(msg) = ClientMessage::open(&payload, &self.key)
                    {
                        let _ = self.in_tx.send(msg);
                    }
                }
                Ok(Message::Close(_)) => break,
                // Pings are answered by tungstenite itself (the queued Pong is flushed on the next
                // read/write), so nothing to do here.
                Ok(_) => {}
                Err(tungstenite::Error::Io(e))
                    if matches!(e.kind(), ErrorKind::WouldBlock | ErrorKind::TimedOut) => {}
                Err(e) => {
                    self.fail(format!("relay connection lost: {e}"));
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        self.connected.store(false, Ordering::Relaxed);
        let _ = self.ws.close(None);
    }

    fn fail(&self, message: String) {
        *self.error.lock().unwrap() = Some(message);
    }
}

/// Sets a read timeout on the underlying TCP socket (through TLS if present) so the worker can poll
/// reads and interleave sends. A plain stream and a rustls stream both reach the `TcpStream`.
fn set_read_timeout(stream: &mut MaybeTlsStream<TcpStream>, timeout: Duration) {
    match stream {
        MaybeTlsStream::Plain(s) => {
            s.set_read_timeout(Some(timeout)).ok();
        }
        MaybeTlsStream::Rustls(tls) => {
            tls.get_ref().set_read_timeout(Some(timeout)).ok();
        }
        _ => {}
    }
}

/// Normalises a relay URL for `tungstenite::connect`: defaults the scheme to `ws://` and, when no
/// port is given, appends the relay's default port 8787 (`wss://` without a port keeps 443 via the
/// scheme default only if one is written, matching how servers are addressed).
fn normalize_url(url: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    let (scheme, rest) = if let Some(r) = url.strip_prefix("wss://") {
        ("wss://", r)
    } else if let Some(r) = url.strip_prefix("ws://") {
        ("ws://", r)
    } else {
        ("ws://", url)
    };
    let (authority, path) = match rest.find('/') {
        Some(i) => rest.split_at(i),
        None => (rest, ""),
    };
    if authority.is_empty() {
        return Err(format!("no host in relay URL `{url}`"));
    }
    let authority = if authority.contains(':') || scheme == "wss://" {
        authority.to_string()
    } else {
        format!("{authority}:8787")
    };
    Ok(format!("{scheme}{authority}{path}"))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::normalize_url;

    #[test]
    fn normalizes_relay_urls() {
        assert_eq!(
            normalize_url("ws://10.0.0.5:9000").unwrap(),
            "ws://10.0.0.5:9000"
        );
        // Bare ws:// host with no port gets the relay default.
        assert_eq!(
            normalize_url("ws://relay.example/room").unwrap(),
            "ws://relay.example:8787/room"
        );
        // No scheme defaults to ws:// (+ default port).
        assert_eq!(
            normalize_url("127.0.0.1:1234").unwrap(),
            "ws://127.0.0.1:1234"
        );
        // wss:// is preserved (port left to the scheme/explicit value).
        assert_eq!(
            normalize_url("wss://relay.example/r").unwrap(),
            "wss://relay.example/r"
        );
        assert!(normalize_url("ws://").is_err());
    }
}

`crates/orress-collab/src/crypto.rs`:

```rs
//! End-to-end encryption for a collaboration room. The relay only ever sees ciphertext: every
//! message peers exchange is sealed with a key derived from the room's passphrase, so a hosted or
//! self-hosted relay (and anyone on the wire) cannot read renames, comments, chat or presence —
//! important when the team is reversing malware.
//!
//! The key is Argon2id over the passphrase with a salt derived deterministically from the room
//! name (so every peer in the room derives the same key); messages use XChaCha20Poly1305 with a
//! random 192-bit nonce prepended to each ciphertext.

use argon2::Argon2;
use chacha20poly1305::aead::{Aead, AeadCore, KeyInit, OsRng};
use chacha20poly1305::{XChaCha20Poly1305, XNonce};

const NONCE_LEN: usize = 24;

/// A room's symmetric key, ready to seal/open messages.
pub struct RoomKey {
    cipher: XChaCha20Poly1305,
}

impl RoomKey {
    /// Derives the room key from its name and passphrase (Argon2id). Every peer that joins the same
    /// room with the same passphrase derives the same key; a wrong passphrase derives a different
    /// key, so its messages simply fail to open.
    pub fn derive(room: &str, passphrase: &str) -> Result<Self, String> {
        let salt = derive_salt(room);
        let mut key = [0u8; 32];
        Argon2::default()
            .hash_password_into(passphrase.as_bytes(), &salt, &mut key)
            .map_err(|e| format!("key derivation failed: {e}"))?;
        let cipher =
            XChaCha20Poly1305::new_from_slice(&key).map_err(|e| format!("bad key length: {e}"))?;
        Ok(Self { cipher })
    }

    /// Encrypts `plaintext`, returning `nonce || ciphertext`.
    pub fn seal(&self, plaintext: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
        let nonce = XChaCha20Poly1305::generate_nonce(&mut OsRng);
        let ciphertext = self
            .cipher
            .encrypt(&nonce, plaintext)
            .map_err(|_| "encryption failed".to_string())?;
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(NONCE_LEN + ciphertext.len());
        out.extend_from_slice(&nonce); // GenericArray derefs to &[u8]
        out.extend_from_slice(&ciphertext);
        Ok(out)
    }

    /// Decrypts a `nonce || ciphertext` blob. Fails on a wrong key or any tampering (AEAD).
    pub fn open(&self, sealed: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
        if sealed.len() < NONCE_LEN {
            return Err("sealed message too short".to_string());
        }
        let (nonce_bytes, ciphertext) = sealed.split_at(NONCE_LEN);
        let mut nonce = XNonce::default();
        nonce.copy_from_slice(nonce_bytes);
        self.cipher
            .decrypt(&nonce, ciphertext)
            .map_err(|_| "could not decrypt (wrong passphrase or tampered message)".to_string())
    }
}

/// A 16-byte Argon2 salt derived deterministically from the room name (FNV-1a expanded), so all
/// peers in a room agree without exchanging a salt.
fn derive_salt(room: &str) -> [u8; 16] {
    let mut salt = [0u8; 16];
    let mut hash: u64 = 1469598103934665603;
    for (i, slot) in salt.iter_mut().enumerate() {
        for b in room.as_bytes() {
            hash ^= u64::from(*b);
            hash = hash.wrapping_mul(1099511628211);
        }
        hash = hash.wrapping_add(i as u64 + 1);
        *slot = (hash >> ((i % 8) * 8)) as u8;
    }
    salt
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn same_room_and_passphrase_round_trips() {
        let a = RoomKey::derive("ctf-2026/web", "correct horse battery staple").unwrap();
        let b = RoomKey::derive("ctf-2026/web", "correct horse battery staple").unwrap();
        let sealed = a.seal(b"rename 0x401000 = check_flag").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(b.open(&sealed).unwrap(), b"rename 0x401000 = check_flag");
        // The nonce makes each sealing distinct even for the same plaintext.
        assert_ne!(a.seal(b"x").unwrap(), a.seal(b"x").unwrap());
    }

    #[test]
    fn wrong_passphrase_cannot_open() {
        let good = RoomKey::derive("room", "hunter2").unwrap();
        let bad = RoomKey::derive("room", "hunter3").unwrap();
        let sealed = good.seal(b"secret").unwrap();
        assert!(bad.open(&sealed).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_different_room_derives_a_different_key() {
        let one = RoomKey::derive("room-a", "pw").unwrap();
        let two = RoomKey::derive("room-b", "pw").unwrap();
        let sealed = one.seal(b"hi").unwrap();
        assert!(two.open(&sealed).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn tampering_is_detected() {
        let k = RoomKey::derive("r", "p").unwrap();
        let mut sealed = k.seal(b"important").unwrap();
        let last = sealed.len() - 1;
        sealed[last] ^= 0xff; // flip a ciphertext byte
        assert!(k.open(&sealed).is_err());
    }
}

`crates/orress-collab/src/doc.rs`:

```rs
//! The shared CRDT document: the collaborative state a team edits together over a relay. Built on
//! a Yjs ([`yrs`]) document, so concurrent edits from every peer merge deterministically without a
//! central authority. Everything a team shares while solving a CTF lives here — renames, comments,
//! recovered types, free-form notes, bookmarks, challenge claims and chat.
//!
//! Sync is update-based: a peer encodes the changes the other side is missing ([`CollabDoc::encode_update`]
//! from a remote [`CollabDoc::state_vector`]) and applies incoming updates ([`CollabDoc::apply_update`]);
//! the result converges regardless of order or duplication.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::sync::Mutex;

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use yrs::updates::decoder::Decode;
use yrs::updates::encoder::Encode;
use yrs::{
    Any, Array, ArrayRef, Doc, Map, MapRef, Out, ReadTxn, StateVector, Transact, TransactionMut,
    Update,
};

/// An error from decoding or applying a sync message.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum CollabError {
    Decode(String),
    Apply(String),
}

impl std::fmt::Display for CollabError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            CollabError::Decode(e) => write!(f, "could not decode sync message: {e}"),
            CollabError::Apply(e) => write!(f, "could not apply sync update: {e}"),
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for CollabError {}

/// A chat message, with an optional address so teammates can jump to what is being discussed.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ChatMessage {
    pub peer: String,
    pub text: String,
    /// Unix-millis timestamp (set by the sender).
    pub ts: u64,
    /// An address this message refers to, rendered as a clickable link in the UI.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub addr: Option<u64>,
}

/// The team's shared CRDT state.
pub struct CollabDoc {
    doc: Doc,
    /// address -> user-chosen name.
    renames: MapRef,
    /// address -> comment text.
    comments: MapRef,
    /// address -> bookmark label.
    bookmarks: MapRef,
    /// key (caller-chosen, e.g. a function address) -> recovered type / signature.
    types: MapRef,
    /// key -> free-form note.
    notes: MapRef,
    /// challenge id -> the peer who claimed it.
    claims: MapRef,
    /// Append-only chat log (each entry a JSON [`ChatMessage`]).
    chat: ArrayRef,
    /// Updates produced by local edits (through this type's mutators) not yet taken for broadcast.
    /// Remote updates applied via [`CollabDoc::apply_update`] are never recorded here, so they are
    /// not echoed back to the room.
    outbox: Mutex<Vec<Vec<u8>>>,
}

impl Default for CollabDoc {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

/// Reads a string value out of a yrs map entry (ignoring non-string values).
fn as_string(out: Option<Out>) -> Option<String> {
    match out {
        Some(Out::Any(Any::String(s))) => Some(s.to_string()),
        _ => None,
    }
}

impl CollabDoc {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        let doc = Doc::new();
        let renames = doc.get_or_insert_map("renames");
        let comments = doc.get_or_insert_map("comments");
        let bookmarks = doc.get_or_insert_map("bookmarks");
        let types = doc.get_or_insert_map("types");
        let notes = doc.get_or_insert_map("notes");
        let claims = doc.get_or_insert_map("claims");
        let chat = doc.get_or_insert_array("chat");
        Self {
            doc,
            renames,
            comments,
            bookmarks,
            types,
            notes,
            claims,
            chat,
            outbox: Mutex::new(Vec::new()),
        }
    }

    /// Queues the changes made in `txn` (a local edit) for broadcast, if it changed anything.
    fn record(&self, txn: &TransactionMut) {
        let update = txn.encode_update_v1();
        if !update_is_empty(&update) {
            self.outbox
                .lock()
                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
                .push(update);
        }
    }

    fn set(&self, map: &MapRef, key: String, value: &str) {
        let mut txn = self.doc.transact_mut();
        map.insert(&mut txn, key, value.to_string());
        self.record(&txn);
    }

    fn remove(&self, map: &MapRef, key: &str) {
        let mut txn = self.doc.transact_mut();
        map.remove(&mut txn, key);
        self.record(&txn);
    }

    fn string_map(&self, map: &MapRef) -> BTreeMap<String, String> {
        let txn = self.doc.transact();
        map.iter(&txn)
            .filter_map(|(k, v)| match v {
                Out::Any(Any::String(s)) => Some((k.to_string(), s.to_string())),
                _ => None,
            })
            .collect()
    }

    fn addr_map(&self, map: &MapRef) -> BTreeMap<u64, String> {
        self.string_map(map)
            .into_iter()
            .filter_map(|(k, v)| parse_addr(&k).map(|a| (a, v)))
            .collect()
    }

    // --- Renames / comments / bookmarks (keyed by address). --------------------------------
    pub fn set_rename(&self, addr: u64, name: &str) {
        self.set(&self.renames, addr_key(addr), name);
    }
    pub fn rename(&self, addr: u64) -> Option<String> {
        as_string(self.renames.get(&self.doc.transact(), &addr_key(addr)))
    }
    pub fn renames(&self) -> BTreeMap<u64, String> {
        self.addr_map(&self.renames)
    }

    pub fn remove_rename(&self, addr: u64) {
        self.remove(&self.renames, &addr_key(addr));
    }

    pub fn set_comment(&self, addr: u64, text: &str) {
        self.set(&self.comments, addr_key(addr), text);
    }
    pub fn comments(&self) -> BTreeMap<u64, String> {
        self.addr_map(&self.comments)
    }
    pub fn remove_comment(&self, addr: u64) {
        self.remove(&self.comments, &addr_key(addr));
    }

    pub fn set_bookmark(&self, addr: u64, label: &str) {
        self.set(&self.bookmarks, addr_key(addr), label);
    }
    pub fn remove_bookmark(&self, addr: u64) {
        self.remove(&self.bookmarks, &addr_key(addr));
    }
    pub fn bookmarks(&self) -> BTreeMap<u64, String> {
        self.addr_map(&self.bookmarks)
    }

    // --- Types / notes (keyed by a caller-chosen string). ----------------------------------
    pub fn set_type(&self, key: &str, ty: &str) {
        self.set(&self.types, key.to_string(), ty);
    }
    pub fn types(&self) -> BTreeMap<String, String> {
        self.string_map(&self.types)
    }

    pub fn set_note(&self, key: &str, text: &str) {
        self.set(&self.notes, key.to_string(), text);
    }
    pub fn notes(&self) -> BTreeMap<String, String> {
        self.string_map(&self.notes)
    }

    // --- Claims ("taking challenge 3"), keyed by challenge id. ------------------------------
    pub fn claim(&self, challenge: &str, peer: &str) {
        self.set(&self.claims, challenge.to_string(), peer);
    }
    pub fn release_claim(&self, challenge: &str) {
        self.remove(&self.claims, challenge);
    }
    pub fn claims(&self) -> BTreeMap<String, String> {
        self.string_map(&self.claims)
    }

    // --- Chat. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    pub fn post_chat(&self, msg: &ChatMessage) {
        let json = serde_json::to_string(msg).unwrap_or_default();
        let mut txn = self.doc.transact_mut();
        self.chat.push_back(&mut txn, json);
        self.record(&txn);
    }
    pub fn chat(&self) -> Vec<ChatMessage> {
        let txn = self.doc.transact();
        (0..self.chat.len(&txn))
            .filter_map(|i| self.chat.get(&txn, i))
            .filter_map(|out| match out {
                Out::Any(Any::String(s)) => serde_json::from_str(&s).ok(),
                _ => None,
            })
            .collect()
    }

    // --- Sync. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    /// This document's state vector (what it already has), for a peer to diff against.
    pub fn state_vector(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
        self.doc.transact().state_vector().encode_v1()
    }

    /// The update carrying everything the holder of `remote_state_vector` is missing.
    pub fn encode_update(&self, remote_state_vector: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CollabError> {
        let sv = StateVector::decode_v1(remote_state_vector)
            .map_err(|e| CollabError::Decode(e.to_string()))?;
        Ok(self.doc.transact().encode_diff_v1(&sv))
    }

    /// The full state as a single update (for a peer that is just joining).
    pub fn encode_full(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
        self.doc
            .transact()
            .encode_state_as_update_v1(&StateVector::default())
    }

    /// Takes the updates produced by local edits since the last call, merged into one (`None` if
    /// nothing changed locally). Unlike diffing state vectors this also catches pure deletions,
    /// which do not advance the state vector.
    pub fn take_local_update(&self) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
        let pending = std::mem::take(&mut *self.outbox.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()));
        match pending.len() {
            0 => None,
            1 => pending.into_iter().next(),
            _ => match yrs::merge_updates_v1(&pending) {
                Ok(merged) => Some(merged),
                // Merging should not fail on our own updates; if it does, fall back to the full
                // state (idempotent on the receiving side).
                Err(_) => Some(self.encode_full()),
            },
        }
    }

    /// Applies an update produced by [`CollabDoc::encode_update`]/[`CollabDoc::encode_full`] on
    /// another peer.
    pub fn apply_update(&self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), CollabError> {
        let update = Update::decode_v1(bytes).map_err(|e| CollabError::Decode(e.to_string()))?;
        self.doc
            .transact_mut()
            .apply_update(update)
            .map_err(|e| CollabError::Apply(e.to_string()))
    }
}

/// Whether an encoded (v1) update carries no changes at all (an empty yrs update still encodes
/// to a couple of bytes, so `bytes.is_empty()` is not enough). Undecodable bytes count as
/// non-empty so the caller surfaces the decode error instead of silently dropping them.
pub(crate) fn update_is_empty(bytes: &[u8]) -> bool {
    Update::decode_v1(bytes).is_ok_and(|u| u.is_empty())
}

/// Addresses are stored as fixed-width lowercase hex so they sort and round-trip cleanly.
fn addr_key(addr: u64) -> String {
    format!("{addr:016x}")
}

fn parse_addr(key: &str) -> Option<u64> {
    u64::from_str_radix(key, 16).ok()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn two_peers_converge_after_exchanging_updates() {
        let alice = CollabDoc::new();
        let bob = CollabDoc::new();

        // Concurrent, independent edits on each side.
        alice.set_rename(0x401000, "check_flag");
        alice.set_comment(0x401000, "validates the password");
        bob.set_bookmark(0x401200, "key schedule");
        bob.claim("web-3", "bob");

        // Exchange only what each side is missing, in both directions.
        let a_to_b = alice.encode_update(&bob.state_vector()).unwrap();
        let b_to_a = bob.encode_update(&alice.state_vector()).unwrap();
        bob.apply_update(&a_to_b).unwrap();
        alice.apply_update(&b_to_a).unwrap();

        // Both documents now hold the union.
        for doc in [&alice, &bob] {
            assert_eq!(doc.rename(0x401000).as_deref(), Some("check_flag"));
            assert_eq!(
                doc.comments().get(&0x401000).map(String::as_str),
                Some("validates the password")
            );
            assert_eq!(
                doc.bookmarks().get(&0x401200).map(String::as_str),
                Some("key schedule")
            );
            assert_eq!(doc.claims().get("web-3").map(String::as_str), Some("bob"));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn concurrent_edits_to_the_same_key_converge_to_one_value() {
        let alice = CollabDoc::new();
        let bob = CollabDoc::new();
        alice.set_rename(0x1000, "alpha");
        bob.set_rename(0x1000, "beta");

        // Full-state exchange both ways; a map key is last-writer-wins, and both pick the SAME winner.
        let a_full = alice.encode_full();
        let b_full = bob.encode_full();
        alice.apply_update(&b_full).unwrap();
        bob.apply_update(&a_full).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(alice.rename(0x1000), bob.rename(0x1000));
        assert!(matches!(
            alice.rename(0x1000).as_deref(),
            Some("alpha") | Some("beta")
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn chat_is_an_ordered_append_log_that_merges() {
        let alice = CollabDoc::new();
        let bob = CollabDoc::new();
        alice.post_chat(&ChatMessage {
            peer: "alice".into(),
            text: "look at 0x401000".into(),
            ts: 1,
            addr: Some(0x401000),
        });
        bob.post_chat(&ChatMessage {
            peer: "bob".into(),
            text: "on it".into(),
            ts: 2,
            addr: None,
        });

        bob.apply_update(&alice.encode_update(&bob.state_vector()).unwrap())
            .unwrap();
        alice
            .apply_update(&bob.encode_update(&alice.state_vector()).unwrap())
            .unwrap();

        for doc in [&alice, &bob] {
            let chat = doc.chat();
            assert_eq!(chat.len(), 2);
            assert!(
                chat.iter()
                    .any(|m| m.peer == "alice" && m.addr == Some(0x401000))
            );
            assert!(chat.iter().any(|m| m.peer == "bob" && m.text == "on it"));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn local_updates_are_recorded_only_for_real_changes() {
        let alice = CollabDoc::new();
        let bob = CollabDoc::new();
        assert_eq!(
            alice.take_local_update(),
            None,
            "a fresh doc has nothing to send"
        );
        // An empty diff still encodes to bytes; it must not count as a change.
        assert!(update_is_empty(
            &alice.encode_update(&alice.state_vector()).unwrap()
        ));

        alice.set_rename(0x10, "a");
        alice.set_comment(0x10, "c");
        let u = alice.take_local_update().expect("edits produce an update");
        assert_eq!(
            alice.take_local_update(),
            None,
            "taken updates are not resent"
        );
        bob.apply_update(&u).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(bob.rename(0x10).as_deref(), Some("a"));
        // Applying a remote update is not a local change (no echo).
        assert_eq!(bob.take_local_update(), None);

        // A pure delete does not advance the state vector but must still be broadcast.
        let sv = alice.state_vector();
        alice.remove_comment(0x10);
        assert_eq!(alice.state_vector(), sv);
        let del = alice.take_local_update().expect("a delete is a change");
        bob.apply_update(&del).unwrap();
        assert!(bob.comments().is_empty());

        // Removing something that is not there changes nothing.
        alice.remove_comment(0x999);
        assert_eq!(alice.take_local_update(), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn applying_the_same_update_twice_is_idempotent() {
        let alice = CollabDoc::new();
        let bob = CollabDoc::new();
        alice.set_note("plan", "diff the two firmware dumps");
        let u = alice.encode_full();
        bob.apply_update(&u).unwrap();
        bob.apply_update(&u).unwrap(); // duplicate delivery is harmless
        assert_eq!(
            bob.notes().get("plan").map(String::as_str),
            Some("diff the two firmware dumps")
        );
    }
}
