`crates/orress-collab/src/presence.rs`:

```rs
//! Presence and follow mode: the *ephemeral* awareness layer (separate from the CRDT, which holds
//! durable state). Each peer periodically broadcasts where it is looking — its name, a stable
//! colour, and the address it is viewing — so the team sees presence avatars ("Alice is at
//! `check_flag`") and can **follow** a teammate's cursor through the binary.
//!
//! Awareness is last-write-wins per peer and self-expiring: a peer not heard from within a TTL is
//! pruned, so a crashed client disappears on its own.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

/// One peer's current awareness state (broadcast as-is).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Peer {
    /// Stable per-session id (also used to route follow mode).
    pub id: String,
    pub name: String,
    /// Avatar colour as `0xRRGGBB` (derived from the id if not set).
    pub color: u32,
    /// The address this peer is currently viewing, if any.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub addr: Option<u64>,
    /// Sender's unix-millis timestamp; used for TTL pruning and last-write-wins.
    pub last_seen: u64,
}

impl Peer {
    /// A new peer with a colour derived from its id.
    pub fn new(id: impl Into<String>, name: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        let id = id.into();
        let color = color_for(&id);
        Self {
            id,
            name: name.into(),
            color,
            addr: None,
            last_seen: 0,
        }
    }
}

/// A deterministic, readable avatar colour for an id (stable across peers and sessions): the id is
/// hashed to a hue, with fixed high saturation/value so colours stay distinct and legible.
pub fn color_for(id: &str) -> u32 {
    let mut hash: u64 = 1469598103934665603; // FNV-1a
    for b in id.as_bytes() {
        hash ^= u64::from(*b);
        hash = hash.wrapping_mul(1099511628211);
    }
    let hue = (hash % 360) as f32;
    hsv_to_rgb(hue, 0.65, 0.95)
}

fn hsv_to_rgb(h: f32, s: f32, v: f32) -> u32 {
    let c = v * s;
    let x = c * (1.0 - ((h / 60.0) % 2.0 - 1.0).abs());
    let m = v - c;
    let (r, g, b) = match h as u32 / 60 {
        0 => (c, x, 0.0),
        1 => (x, c, 0.0),
        2 => (0.0, c, x),
        3 => (0.0, x, c),
        4 => (x, 0.0, c),
        _ => (c, 0.0, x),
    };
    let to = |f: f32| ((f + m) * 255.0).round() as u32;
    (to(r) << 16) | (to(g) << 8) | to(b)
}

/// The team's awareness: this session's own peer plus the remote peers last heard from.
pub struct Presence {
    local: Peer,
    remote: BTreeMap<String, Peer>,
    /// peer id -> when *we* last heard from it (our clock, unix millis). Pruning uses this rather
    /// than the sender's `last_seen`, so clock skew between machines cannot expire (or immortalise)
    /// a peer.
    received: BTreeMap<String, u64>,
    following: Option<String>,
}

impl Presence {
    pub fn new(local: Peer) -> Self {
        Self {
            local,
            remote: BTreeMap::new(),
            received: BTreeMap::new(),
            following: None,
        }
    }

    pub fn local(&self) -> &Peer {
        &self.local
    }

    /// Updates where this session is looking and stamps it `now` (unix millis), returning the
    /// update to broadcast.
    pub fn set_local_addr(&mut self, addr: Option<u64>, now: u64) -> Peer {
        self.local.addr = addr;
        self.local.last_seen = now;
        self.local.clone()
    }

    /// A fresh copy of the local peer to broadcast as a heartbeat, stamped `now`.
    pub fn heartbeat(&mut self, now: u64) -> Peer {
        self.local.last_seen = now;
        self.local.clone()
    }

    /// Records a remote peer's broadcast (ignoring our own echo and older timestamps). Without a
    /// local receive time, the sender's own `last_seen` stands in for it; prefer
    /// [`Presence::apply_at`], which is immune to clock skew between machines.
    pub fn apply(&mut self, peer: Peer) {
        let at = peer.last_seen;
        self.apply_at(peer, at);
    }

    /// Records a remote peer's broadcast received at `received_at` (unix millis on *our* clock),
    /// ignoring our own echo and updates older (by the sender's clock) than what we hold.
    pub fn apply_at(&mut self, peer: Peer, received_at: u64) {
        if peer.id == self.local.id {
            return;
        }
        // Any broadcast proves the peer is alive, even a reordered stale one.
        let seen = self.received.entry(peer.id.clone()).or_insert(received_at);
        *seen = (*seen).max(received_at);
        match self.remote.get(&peer.id) {
            Some(existing) if existing.last_seen > peer.last_seen => {}
            _ => {
                self.remote.insert(peer.id.clone(), peer);
            }
        }
    }

    /// Drops remote peers not heard from within `ttl_ms` of `now` (our clock, compared against
    /// when we received their last broadcast). If the followed peer expires, following stops.
    pub fn prune(&mut self, now: u64, ttl_ms: u64) {
        let received = &self.received;
        self.remote.retain(|id, p| {
            let at = received.get(id).copied().unwrap_or(p.last_seen);
            now.saturating_sub(at) <= ttl_ms
        });
        let remote = &self.remote;
        self.received.retain(|id, _| remote.contains_key(id));
        if let Some(id) = &self.following
            && !self.remote.contains_key(id)
        {
            self.following = None;
        }
    }

    /// Remote peers, ordered by id (stable for rendering avatars).
    pub fn peers(&self) -> Vec<&Peer> {
        self.remote.values().collect()
    }

    pub fn peer(&self, id: &str) -> Option<&Peer> {
        self.remote.get(id)
    }

    // --- Follow mode. -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    pub fn follow(&mut self, id: &str) {
        self.following = Some(id.to_string());
    }

    pub fn unfollow(&mut self) {
        self.following = None;
    }

    pub fn following(&self) -> Option<&str> {
        self.following.as_deref()
    }

    /// The address to jump to when following: the followed peer's current address. `None` if not
    /// following, the peer is gone, or it has no address.
    pub fn follow_addr(&self) -> Option<u64> {
        let id = self.following.as_ref()?;
        self.remote.get(id).and_then(|p| p.addr)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn colors_are_deterministic_and_vary_by_id() {
        assert_eq!(color_for("alice"), color_for("alice"));
        assert_ne!(color_for("alice"), color_for("bob"));
        assert!(color_for("x") <= 0xFFFFFF);
    }

    #[test]
    fn apply_ignores_self_and_keeps_the_newest() {
        let mut p = Presence::new(Peer::new("me", "Me"));
        p.apply(Peer {
            id: "me".into(),
            name: "echo".into(),
            color: 0,
            addr: Some(1),
            last_seen: 9,
        });
        assert!(p.peers().is_empty(), "own echo is ignored");

        let mut bob = Peer::new("bob", "Bob");
        bob.addr = Some(0x1000);
        bob.last_seen = 10;
        p.apply(bob.clone());
        assert_eq!(p.peer("bob").unwrap().addr, Some(0x1000));

        // An older update does not clobber a newer one.
        let mut stale = bob.clone();
        stale.addr = Some(0x9999);
        stale.last_seen = 5;
        p.apply(stale);
        assert_eq!(p.peer("bob").unwrap().addr, Some(0x1000));
    }

    #[test]
    fn prune_drops_stale_peers_and_stops_following_them() {
        let mut p = Presence::new(Peer::new("me", "Me"));
        let mut bob = Peer::new("bob", "Bob");
        bob.addr = Some(0x2000);
        bob.last_seen = 1000;
        p.apply(bob);
        p.follow("bob");
        assert_eq!(p.follow_addr(), Some(0x2000));

        p.prune(1500, 1000); // within TTL
        assert_eq!(p.peers().len(), 1);
        p.prune(3000, 1000); // now stale
        assert!(p.peers().is_empty());
        assert_eq!(p.following(), None, "following a gone peer stops");
        assert_eq!(p.follow_addr(), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn prune_uses_the_local_receive_time_not_the_senders_clock() {
        let mut p = Presence::new(Peer::new("me", "Me"));
        // Bob's clock is an hour behind ours; he is still alive.
        let mut bob = Peer::new("bob", "Bob");
        bob.last_seen = 1_000;
        p.apply_at(bob, 3_601_000);
        p.prune(3_602_000, 12_000);
        assert_eq!(p.peers().len(), 1, "a skewed but live peer is kept");
        // ... and is pruned once *we* have not heard from him for longer than the TTL.
        p.prune(3_601_000 + 12_001, 12_000);
        assert!(p.peers().is_empty());

        // Carol's clock runs ahead: she is still pruned after going quiet locally.
        let mut carol = Peer::new("carol", "Carol");
        carol.last_seen = 99_999_999;
        p.apply_at(carol, 10_000);
        p.prune(10_000 + 12_001, 12_000);
        assert!(p.peers().is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn follow_tracks_the_peers_moving_cursor() {
        let mut p = Presence::new(Peer::new("me", "Me"));
        let mut bob = Peer::new("bob", "Bob");
        bob.last_seen = 1;
        p.apply(bob.clone());
        assert_eq!(p.follow_addr(), None, "not following yet");
        p.follow("bob");
        assert_eq!(p.follow_addr(), None, "bob has no address yet");

        bob.addr = Some(0x401000);
        bob.last_seen = 2;
        p.apply(bob);
        assert_eq!(p.follow_addr(), Some(0x401000));
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-collab/src/protocol.rs`:

```rs
//! The two wire layers used over the relay's WebSocket:
//!
//! - [`Envelope`] — the **relay-visible** framing. A client first sends `Join { room }`, then
//!   `Data { payload }` frames the relay broadcasts to every other member of the room. The relay
//!   never looks inside `payload`; it only routes by room. Encoded as a compact tagged binary blob.
//! - [`ClientMessage`] — the **end-to-end** payload, sealed with the room [`RoomKey`] before it
//!   becomes an `Envelope::Data`. It carries CRDT sync (`StateVector`/`Update`) and ephemeral
//!   `Presence`.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use crate::crypto::RoomKey;
use crate::presence::Peer;

/// The relay-visible frame. Binary: a 1-byte tag then the content (room name, or opaque payload).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Envelope {
    /// Join (or create) a room. Sent once, first.
    Join { room: String },
    /// An opaque, end-to-end-encrypted payload to broadcast to the rest of the room.
    Data { payload: Vec<u8> },
}

const TAG_JOIN: u8 = 0;
const TAG_DATA: u8 = 1;

impl Envelope {
    pub fn encode(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
        match self {
            Envelope::Join { room } => {
                let mut out = vec![TAG_JOIN];
                out.extend_from_slice(room.as_bytes());
                out
            }
            Envelope::Data { payload } => {
                let mut out = vec![TAG_DATA];
                out.extend_from_slice(payload);
                out
            }
        }
    }

    pub fn decode(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<Envelope> {
        let (&tag, rest) = bytes.split_first()?;
        match tag {
            TAG_JOIN => Some(Envelope::Join {
                room: String::from_utf8(rest.to_vec()).ok()?,
            }),
            TAG_DATA => Some(Envelope::Data {
                payload: rest.to_vec(),
            }),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// The end-to-end message peers actually exchange (inside an encrypted `Envelope::Data`).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "t", content = "v", rename_all = "kebab-case")]
pub enum ClientMessage {
    /// "Here is what I already have" — on join, so a peer can reply with the diff I am missing.
    StateVector(Vec<u8>),
    /// A CRDT update (from `CollabDoc::encode_update`/`encode_full`).
    Update(Vec<u8>),
    /// An ephemeral presence broadcast.
    Presence(Peer),
}

impl ClientMessage {
    /// Serializes and seals this message into an `Envelope::Data` payload with the room key.
    pub fn seal(&self, key: &RoomKey) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
        let json = serde_json::to_vec(self).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        key.seal(&json)
    }

    /// Opens and deserializes a sealed payload.
    pub fn open(payload: &[u8], key: &RoomKey) -> Result<ClientMessage, String> {
        let json = key.open(payload)?;
        serde_json::from_slice(&json).map_err(|e| format!("bad client message: {e}"))
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn envelope_round_trips() {
        let join = Envelope::Join {
            room: "ctf/web".into(),
        };
        assert_eq!(Envelope::decode(&join.encode()), Some(join));
        let data = Envelope::Data {
            payload: vec![1, 2, 3, 0, 255],
        };
        assert_eq!(Envelope::decode(&data.encode()), Some(data));
        assert_eq!(Envelope::decode(&[]), None); // empty frame
        assert_eq!(Envelope::decode(&[9, 9]), None); // unknown tag
    }

    #[test]
    fn client_message_seals_and_opens_with_the_room_key() {
        let key = RoomKey::derive("room", "pw").unwrap();
        let msg = ClientMessage::Update(vec![10, 20, 30]);
        let sealed = msg.seal(&key).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(ClientMessage::open(&sealed, &key).unwrap(), msg);

        // A different key cannot open it (end-to-end).
        let other = RoomKey::derive("room", "nope").unwrap();
        assert!(ClientMessage::open(&sealed, &other).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn presence_message_carries_the_peer() {
        let key = RoomKey::derive("r", "p").unwrap();
        let peer = Peer::new("bob", "Bob");
        let sealed = ClientMessage::Presence(peer.clone()).seal(&key).unwrap();
        match ClientMessage::open(&sealed, &key).unwrap() {
            ClientMessage::Presence(p) => assert_eq!(p, peer),
            other => panic!("expected presence, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-collab/src/session.rs`:

```rs
//! A live collaboration session: the glue the app drives. It owns the shared [`CollabDoc`], the
//! [`Presence`] awareness and the [`RelayClient`], and reconciles them each frame via [`poll`]:
//!
//! - local CRDT edits (made directly on [`CollabSession::doc`]) are recorded as they happen and
//!   broadcast once; an idle session sends no document traffic at all,
//! - incoming updates are applied, incoming state-vectors are answered with the diff they lack,
//! - presence is broadcast on a heartbeat and pruned when peers go quiet.
//!
//! [`poll`]: CollabSession::poll

use crate::client::RelayClient;
use crate::doc::{CollabDoc, update_is_empty};
use crate::presence::{Peer, Presence};
use crate::protocol::ClientMessage;

/// How often to re-announce our presence, and how long before a silent peer is pruned (millis).
const HEARTBEAT_MS: u64 = 3_000;
const PRESENCE_TTL_MS: u64 = 12_000;

/// A connected collaboration session for one room.
pub struct CollabSession {
    /// The shared state. Mutate it directly (e.g. `session.doc.set_rename(..)`); [`CollabSession::poll`]
    /// broadcasts the changes.
    pub doc: CollabDoc,
    presence: Presence,
    client: RelayClient,
    last_heartbeat: u64,
}

impl CollabSession {
    /// Connects to `url` and joins `room` (sealed with `passphrase`), announcing our presence and
    /// state so peers send us what we are missing.
    pub fn connect(
        url: &str,
        room: &str,
        passphrase: &str,
        local: Peer,
    ) -> Result<CollabSession, String> {
        let client = RelayClient::connect(url, room, passphrase)?;
        let doc = CollabDoc::new();
        let presence = Presence::new(local);
        // Tell the room what we have (they reply with the diff we lack) and who we are.
        client.send(ClientMessage::StateVector(doc.state_vector()));
        client.send(ClientMessage::Presence(presence.local().clone()));
        Ok(CollabSession {
            doc,
            presence,
            client,
            last_heartbeat: 0,
        })
    }

    /// Reconciles local and remote state once. Call every UI frame with `now` in unix-millis.
    /// Returns whether anything changed (so the UI can repaint).
    pub fn poll(&mut self, now: u64) -> bool {
        let mut changed = false;

        // 1. Broadcast local edits made since the last poll. These are recorded by the doc's
        //    mutators as they happen (not by diffing state vectors, which deletions do not
        //    advance), so an idle session sends nothing.
        if let Some(update) = self.doc.take_local_update() {
            self.client.send(ClientMessage::Update(update));
        }

        // 2. Apply everything peers sent us. Remote updates are not recorded as local edits, so
        //    they are not echoed back.
        while let Some(msg) = self.client.try_recv() {
            match msg {
                ClientMessage::StateVector(sv) => {
                    if let Ok(diff) = self.doc.encode_update(&sv)
                        && !update_is_empty(&diff)
                    {
                        self.client.send(ClientMessage::Update(diff));
                    }
                }
                ClientMessage::Update(update) => {
                    if !update_is_empty(&update) && self.doc.apply_update(&update).is_ok() {
                        changed = true;
                    }
                }
                ClientMessage::Presence(peer) => {
                    self.presence.apply_at(peer, now);
                    changed = true;
                }
            }
        }

        // 3. Heartbeat our presence and prune peers that have gone quiet.
        if now.saturating_sub(self.last_heartbeat) >= HEARTBEAT_MS {
            let peer = self.presence.heartbeat(now);
            self.client.send(ClientMessage::Presence(peer));
            self.last_heartbeat = now;
        }
        self.presence.prune(now, PRESENCE_TTL_MS);

        changed
    }

    /// Updates where this session is looking and broadcasts it immediately (so follow mode is
    /// responsive), without waiting for the heartbeat.
    pub fn set_local_addr(&mut self, addr: Option<u64>, now: u64) {
        let peer = self.presence.set_local_addr(addr, now);
        self.client.send(ClientMessage::Presence(peer));
    }

    pub fn presence(&self) -> &Presence {
        &self.presence
    }

    pub fn follow(&mut self, id: &str) {
        self.presence.follow(id);
    }
    pub fn unfollow(&mut self) {
        self.presence.unfollow();
    }
    /// The address to jump to when following a teammate, if any.
    pub fn follow_addr(&self) -> Option<u64> {
        self.presence.follow_addr()
    }

    pub fn is_connected(&self) -> bool {
        self.client.is_connected()
    }

    pub fn error(&self) -> Option<String> {
        self.client.error()
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-ctf/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! CTF platform integration (M13): import a competition's challenges and submit flags from inside
//! ORRESS, so a team's triage, claims and flag submissions all live in one place. Supports the two
//! common self-hosted platforms — **CTFd** and **rCTF** — authenticated with an API token.
//!
//! Blocking `ureq` on a background thread (like the AI backends); the response parsers are pure and
//! unit-tested, and the request wiring is tested against a mock server.

use std::time::Duration;

use serde_json::Value;

/// Which platform's API shape to speak.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Platform {
    Ctfd,
    Rctf,
}

/// A challenge as shown in the browser.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Challenge {
    /// Platform id (numeric on CTFd, opaque string on rCTF) — kept as a string so both fit.
    pub id: String,
    pub name: String,
    pub category: String,
    pub value: i64,
    pub solved: bool,
}

/// The result of submitting a flag.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SubmitOutcome {
    pub correct: bool,
    pub already_solved: bool,
    pub message: String,
}

/// A configured client for one platform instance.
pub struct CtfClient {
    platform: Platform,
    /// Base URL, e.g. `https://ctf.example.com` (no trailing slash).
    base: String,
    token: String,
}

impl CtfClient {
    pub fn new(platform: Platform, base: impl Into<String>, token: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        let base = base.into().trim_end_matches('/').to_string();
        Self {
            platform,
            base,
            token: token.into(),
        }
    }

    fn agent() -> ureq::Agent {
        ureq::AgentBuilder::new()
            .timeout(Duration::from_secs(30))
            .build()
    }

    /// Adds the platform's auth header.
    fn auth(&self, req: ureq::Request) -> ureq::Request {
        match self.platform {
            Platform::Ctfd => req.set("Authorization", &format!("Token {}", self.token)),
            Platform::Rctf => req.set("Authorization", &format!("Bearer {}", self.token)),
        }
    }

    /// Lists the competition's challenges.
    pub fn challenges(&self) -> Result<Vec<Challenge>, String> {
        let path = match self.platform {
            Platform::Ctfd => "/api/v1/challenges",
            Platform::Rctf => "/api/v1/challs",
        };
        let url = format!("{}{path}", self.base);
        let value = into_json(self.auth(Self::agent().get(&url)).call())?;
        match self.platform {
            Platform::Ctfd => Ok(parse_ctfd_challenges(&value)),
            Platform::Rctf => {
                let mut challenges = parse_rctf_challenges(&value);
                // rCTF challenge objects carry no "solved" flag; the team's solves come from its
                // profile. Best-effort: if the profile cannot be fetched, nothing is marked solved.
                let me = format!("{}/api/v1/users/me", self.base);
                if let Ok(profile) = into_json(self.auth(Self::agent().get(&me)).call()) {
                    let solved = parse_rctf_solved_ids(&profile);
                    for c in &mut challenges {
                        c.solved |= solved.contains(&c.id);
                    }
                }
                Ok(challenges)
            }
        }
    }

    /// Submits `flag` for a challenge, returning the platform's verdict.
    pub fn submit(&self, challenge_id: &str, flag: &str) -> Result<SubmitOutcome, String> {
        match self.platform {
            Platform::Ctfd => {
                let url = format!("{}/api/v1/challenges/attempt", self.base);
                let body = serde_json::json!({ "challenge_id": numeric(challenge_id), "submission": flag });
                let value = into_json(self.auth(Self::agent().post(&url)).send_json(body))?;
                Ok(parse_ctfd_attempt(&value))
            }
            Platform::Rctf => {
                let url = format!(
                    "{}/api/v1/challs/{}/submit",
                    self.base,
                    encode_path_segment(challenge_id)
                );
                let body = serde_json::json!({ "flag": flag });
                // rCTF answers a wrong flag (400 `badFlag`) or a repeat solve (409
                // `badAlreadySolved`) with a non-2xx status *and* a normal JSON verdict body.
                let value = match self.auth(Self::agent().post(&url)).send_json(body) {
                    Err(ureq::Error::Status(code, r)) => {
                        let text = r.into_string().unwrap_or_default();
                        match serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&text) {
                            Ok(v) if is_rctf_verdict(&v) => v,
                            _ => {
                                let body: String = text.chars().take(300).collect();
                                return Err(format!("HTTP {code}: {body}"));
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    other => into_json(other)?,
                };
                Ok(parse_rctf_submit(&value))
            }
        }
    }
}

/// CTFd challenge ids are numeric; pass a number when the id parses, else the raw string.
fn numeric(id: &str) -> Value {
    id.parse::<i64>()
        .map(Value::from)
        .unwrap_or_else(|_| Value::from(id))
}

/// Whether an rCTF error body is a flag verdict (a wrong or repeated flag) rather than a real
/// failure such as a bad token.
fn is_rctf_verdict(v: &Value) -> bool {
    matches!(v["kind"].as_str(), Some("badFlag" | "badAlreadySolved"))
}

/// Percent-encodes `s` for use as one URL path segment (everything but RFC 3986 unreserved
/// characters), so an id cannot add path segments or a query.
fn encode_path_segment(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    for b in s.bytes() {
        if b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(b, b'-' | b'.' | b'_' | b'~') {
            out.push(b as char);
        } else {
            out.push_str(&format!("%{b:02X}"));
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Shared response handling: a non-2xx or network error becomes a readable message.
fn into_json(resp: Result<ureq::Response, ureq::Error>) -> Result<Value, String> {
    match resp {
        Ok(r) => r
            .into_json()
            .map_err(|e| format!("bad JSON from the CTF platform: {e}")),
        Err(ureq::Error::Status(code, r)) => {
            let body: String = r
                .into_string()
                .unwrap_or_default()
                .chars()
                .take(300)
                .collect();
            Err(format!("HTTP {code}: {body}"))
        }
        Err(e) => Err(format!("request failed: {e}")),
    }
}

pub fn parse_ctfd_challenges(v: &Value) -> Vec<Challenge> {
    v["data"]
        .as_array()
        .map(|arr| {
            arr.iter()
                .filter_map(|c| {
                    let id = c.get("id")?;
                    let id = id
                        .as_i64()
                        .map(|n| n.to_string())
                        .or_else(|| id.as_str().map(str::to_string))?;
                    Some(Challenge {
                        id,
                        name: c["name"].as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string(),
                        category: c["category"].as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string(),
                        value: c["value"].as_i64().unwrap_or(0),
                        solved: c["solved_by_me"].as_bool().unwrap_or(false),
                    })
                })
                .collect()
        })
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

pub fn parse_ctfd_attempt(v: &Value) -> SubmitOutcome {
    let status = v["data"]["status"].as_str().unwrap_or("");
    SubmitOutcome {
        correct: status == "correct",
        already_solved: status == "already_solved",
        message: v["data"]["message"]
            .as_str()
            .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
            .unwrap_or(status)
            .to_string(),
    }
}

pub fn parse_rctf_challenges(v: &Value) -> Vec<Challenge> {
    v["data"]
        .as_array()
        .map(|arr| {
            arr.iter()
                .filter_map(|c| {
                    Some(Challenge {
                        id: c.get("id")?.as_str()?.to_string(),
                        name: c["name"].as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string(),
                        category: c["category"].as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string(),
                        value: c["points"].as_i64().unwrap_or(0),
                        solved: c["solved"].as_bool().unwrap_or(false),
                    })
                })
                .collect()
        })
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

/// The ids of the challenges the team has solved, from rCTF's `/api/v1/users/me` profile
/// (`data.solves[].id`).
pub fn parse_rctf_solved_ids(v: &Value) -> std::collections::HashSet<String> {
    v["data"]["solves"]
        .as_array()
        .map(|arr| {
            arr.iter()
                .filter_map(|s| s.get("id")?.as_str().map(str::to_string))
                .collect()
        })
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

pub fn parse_rctf_submit(v: &Value) -> SubmitOutcome {
    let kind = v["kind"].as_str().unwrap_or("");
    SubmitOutcome {
        correct: kind == "goodFlag",
        already_solved: kind == "badAlreadySolved",
        message: v["message"]
            .as_str()
            .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
            .unwrap_or(kind)
            .to_string(),
    }
}
```

```rs
use std::io::{Read, Write};

#[test]
fn parses_ctfd_challenges_and_verdicts() {
    let listing = serde_json::json!({
        "success": true,
        "data": [
            { "id": 1, "type": "standard", "name": "Sanity", "value": 50, "category": "misc", "solved_by_me": true },
            { "id": 2, "name": "RE 101", "value": 200, "category": "rev" }
        ]
    });
    let chs = parse_ctfd_challenges(&listing);
    assert_eq!(chs.len(), 2);
    assert_eq!(chs[0].id, "1");
    assert_eq!(chs[0].category, "misc");
    assert!(chs[0].solved);
    assert_eq!(chs[1].value, 200);
    assert!(!chs[1].solved);

    let correct = parse_ctfd_attempt(
        &serde_json::json!({ "success": true, "data": { "status": "correct", "message": "Correct!" } }),
    );
    assert!(correct.correct && !correct.already_solved && correct.message == "Correct!");
    let wrong = parse_ctfd_attempt(&serde_json::json!({ "data": { "status": "incorrect" } }));
    assert!(!wrong.correct);
    let dup = parse_ctfd_attempt(&serde_json::json!({ "data": { "status": "already_solved" } }));
    assert!(dup.already_solved);
}

#[test]
fn parses_rctf_challenges_and_verdicts() {
    let listing = serde_json::json!({
        "kind": "goodChallenges",
        "message": "ok",
        "data": [ { "id": "abc123", "name": "pwnme", "category": "pwn", "points": 300, "solved": false } ]
    });
    let chs = parse_rctf_challenges(&listing);
    assert_eq!(chs.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(chs[0].id, "abc123");
    assert_eq!(chs[0].value, 300);

    assert!(
        parse_rctf_submit(&serde_json::json!({ "kind": "goodFlag", "message": "nice" })).correct
    );
    assert!(
        parse_rctf_submit(&serde_json::json!({ "kind": "badAlreadySolved", "message": "dup" }))
            .already_solved
    );
    assert!(
        !parse_rctf_submit(&serde_json::json!({ "kind": "badFlag", "message": "nope" })).correct
    );
}

/// A one-shot HTTP server: serves `body` to the first request, capturing it, and returns the base
/// URL plus a handle to read the captured request.
fn one_shot(body: &'static str) -> (String, std::thread::JoinHandle<String>) {
    one_shot_status("200 OK", body)
}

/// [`one_shot`] answering with an explicit HTTP status line (e.g. `"400 Bad Request"`).
fn one_shot_status(
    status: &'static str,
    body: &'static str,
) -> (String, std::thread::JoinHandle<String>) {
    let listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").unwrap();
    let addr = listener.local_addr().unwrap();
    let handle = std::thread::spawn(move || {
        let (mut stream, _) = listener.accept().unwrap();
        // Read until the full request (headers + any Content-Length body) has arrived — the body
        // may land in a later segment than the request line.
        let mut data = Vec::new();
        let mut chunk = [0u8; 1024];
        loop {
            let n = stream.read(&mut chunk).unwrap();
            if n == 0 {
                break;
            }
            data.extend_from_slice(&chunk[..n]);
            let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&data);
            if let Some(hdr_end) = text.find("\r\n\r\n") {
                let content_len = text
                    .lines()
                    .find_map(|l| {
                        l.to_ascii_lowercase()
                            .strip_prefix("content-length:")
                            .map(|v| v.trim().parse::<usize>().unwrap_or(0))
                    })
                    .unwrap_or(0);
                if data.len() >= hdr_end + 4 + content_len {
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        let request = String::from_utf8_lossy(&data).to_string();
        let resp = format!(
            "HTTP/1.1 {status}\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n{}",
            body.len(),
            body
        );
        stream.write_all(resp.as_bytes()).unwrap();
        request
    });
    (format!("http://{addr}"), handle)
}

#[test]
fn ctfd_client_sends_the_token_and_parses_the_listing() {
    let (base, handle) =
        one_shot(r#"{"success":true,"data":[{"id":7,"name":"x","value":10,"category":"misc"}]}"#);
    let client = CtfClient::new(Platform::Ctfd, base, "secrettoken");
    let chs = client.challenges().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(chs.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(chs[0].id, "7");

    let request = handle.join().unwrap();
    assert!(request.starts_with("GET /api/v1/challenges "), "{request}");
    assert!(
        request.contains("Authorization: Token secrettoken"),
        "{request}"
    );
}

#[test]
fn rctf_wrong_and_repeat_flags_are_verdicts_not_errors() {
    let (base, handle) = one_shot_status(
        "400 Bad Request",
        r#"{"kind":"badFlag","message":"The flag was incorrect."}"#,
    );
    let client = CtfClient::new(Platform::Rctf, base, "tok");
    let outcome = client.submit("chall/../x y", "flag{no}").unwrap();
    assert!(!outcome.correct && !outcome.already_solved);
    assert_eq!(outcome.message, "The flag was incorrect.");
    let request = handle.join().unwrap();
    // The id is percent-encoded into a single path segment.
    assert!(
        request.starts_with("POST /api/v1/challs/chall%2F..%2Fx%20y/submit "),
        "{request}"
    );

    let (base, _h) = one_shot_status(
        "409 Conflict",
        r#"{"kind":"badAlreadySolved","message":"already solved"}"#,
    );
    let outcome = CtfClient::new(Platform::Rctf, base, "tok")
        .submit("a", "f")
        .unwrap();
    assert!(outcome.already_solved);

    // A real failure (bad token) is still an error.
    let (base, _h) = one_shot_status(
        "401 Unauthorized",
        r#"{"kind":"badToken","message":"bad token"}"#,
    );
    assert!(
        CtfClient::new(Platform::Rctf, base, "tok")
            .submit("a", "f")
            .is_err()
    );
}

#[test]
fn rctf_solves_come_from_the_profile() {
    let profile = serde_json::json!({
        "kind": "goodUserData",
        "data": { "solves": [ { "id": "abc", "name": "x" }, { "id": "def" } ] }
    });
    let ids = parse_rctf_solved_ids(&profile);
    assert!(ids.contains("abc") && ids.contains("def") && ids.len() == 2);
    assert!(parse_rctf_solved_ids(&serde_json::json!({})).is_empty());
}

fn ctfd_client_submits_a_flag() {

        one_shot(r#"{"success":true,"data":{"status":"correct","message":"Correct"}}"#);
    let client = CtfClient::new(Platform::Ctfd, base, "tok");

    let request = handle.join().unwrap();
    assert!(
        request.starts_with("POST /api/v1/challenges/attempt "),
        "{request}"
    );
    assert!(request.contains("\"challenge_id\":7"), "{request}");
    assert!(request.contains("flag{abc}"), "{request}");
}
```

`crates/orress-dap/src/bin/orress_dap_mock.rs`:

```rs
//! A tiny mock DAP adapter used only by tests: it speaks enough of the protocol to drive
//! the client through a full stop (initialize -> launch -> initialized -> breakpoints ->
//! stopped -> stackTrace -> scopes -> variables), with canned data.

use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader, Write};

use serde_json::{Value, json};

fn main() {
    let stdin = std::io::stdin();
    let mut reader = BufReader::new(stdin.lock());
    let mut out = std::io::stdout();
    let mut seq = 1i64;
    let send = |out: &mut std::io::Stdout, v: Value| {
        let body = serde_json::to_vec(&v).unwrap();
        let _ = write!(out, "Content-Length: {}\r\n\r\n", body.len());
        let _ = out.write_all(&body);
        let _ = out.flush();
    };
    let next = |seq: &mut i64| {
        let s = *seq;
        *seq += 1;
        s
    };

    while let Some(msg) = read_message(&mut reader) {
        let command = msg
            .get("command")
            .and_then(Value::as_str)
            .unwrap_or("")
            .to_string();
        let req_seq = msg.get("seq").and_then(Value::as_i64).unwrap_or(0);
        let resp = |seq: &mut i64, body: Value| json!({ "seq": next(seq), "type": "response", "request_seq": req_seq, "success": true, "command": command, "body": body });
        match command.as_str() {
            "initialize" => {
                send(
                    &mut out,
                    resp(
                        &mut seq,
                        json!({ "supportsConfigurationDoneRequest": true }),
                    ),
                );
            }
            "launch" => {
                send(&mut out, resp(&mut seq, Value::Null));
                // Ask for configuration.
                send(
                    &mut out,
                    json!({ "seq": next(&mut seq), "type": "event", "event": "initialized", "body": {} }),
                );
            }
            "setBreakpoints" => {
                send(
                    &mut out,
                    resp(
                        &mut seq,
                        json!({ "breakpoints": [{ "verified": true, "line": 3 }] }),
                    ),
                );
            }
            "configurationDone" => {
                send(&mut out, resp(&mut seq, Value::Null));
                // Now "hit" the breakpoint.
                send(
                    &mut out,
                    json!({ "seq": next(&mut seq), "type": "event", "event": "stopped", "body": { "reason": "breakpoint", "threadId": 1 } }),
                );
            }
            "stackTrace" => {
                send(
                    &mut out,
                    resp(
                        &mut seq,
                        json!({ "stackFrames": [{ "id": 1000, "name": "main", "line": 3, "source": { "path": "/tmp/demo.rs" } }], "totalFrames": 1 }),
                    ),
                );
            }
            "scopes" => {
                send(
                    &mut out,
                    resp(
                        &mut seq,
                        json!({ "scopes": [{ "name": "Locals", "variablesReference": 2000 }] }),
                    ),
                );
            }
            "variables" => {
                send(
                    &mut out,
                    resp(
                        &mut seq,
                        json!({ "variables": [{ "name": "a", "value": "41", "type": "i32" }] }),
                    ),
                );
            }
            "continue" | "next" | "stepIn" | "stepOut" | "pause" => {
                send(
                    &mut out,
                    resp(&mut seq, json!({ "allThreadsContinued": true })),
                );
            }
            "terminate" => send(&mut out, resp(&mut seq, Value::Null)),
            "disconnect" => {
                send(&mut out, resp(&mut seq, Value::Null));
                break;
            }
            _ => send(&mut out, resp(&mut seq, Value::Null)),
        }
    }
}

fn read_message(reader: &mut impl BufRead) -> Option<Value> {
    let mut len = None;
    loop {
        let mut line = String::new();
        if reader.read_line(&mut line).ok()? == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        let line = line.trim_end_matches(['\r', '\n']);
        if line.is_empty() {
            break;
        }
        if let Some(v) = line.strip_prefix("Content-Length:") {
            len = v.trim().parse().ok();
        }
    }
    let mut buf = vec![0u8; len?];
    std::io::Read::read_exact(reader, &mut buf).ok()?;
    serde_json::from_slice(&buf).ok()
}
```

`crates/orress-dap/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! A Debug Adapter Protocol (DAP) client for source-level debugging of programs you write
//! in ORRESS (via an adapter such as `lldb-dap`). Like the LSP client it is thread-based
//! with Content-Length framing and no async runtime — the UI polls shared state.
//!
//! The transport runs the whole launch handshake and event loop on its thread
//! (initialize -> launch -> setBreakpoints -> configurationDone, then stop/continue/output
//! events; on each stop it fetches the call stack and the top frame's variables). This
//! module is the thin public surface: launch and the step controls.

mod transport;

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use transport::Transport;

pub use transport::Notify;

/// Where the debuggee is in its life cycle.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Status {
    Starting,
    Running,
    Stopped,
    Exited,
    Failed,
}

/// One stack frame.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct Frame {
    pub id: i64,
    pub name: String,
    pub source: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub line: u32,
}

/// One variable (name = value).
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Variable {
    pub name: String,
    pub value: String,
    pub ty: Option<String>,
}

/// A snapshot of the debug session for the UI.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct DapState {
    pub status: Option<Status>,
    pub stop_reason: Option<String>,
    pub frames: Vec<Frame>,
    pub variables: Vec<Variable>,
    pub output: Vec<String>,
    pub last_error: Option<String>,
    /// The current stopped source file and line.
    pub current: Option<(PathBuf, u32)>,
    pub generation: u64,
}

impl DapState {
    pub fn is_stopped(&self) -> bool {
        self.status == Some(Status::Stopped)
    }
    pub fn is_alive(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            self.status,
            Some(Status::Starting | Status::Running | Status::Stopped)
        )
    }
}

/// How to start a debug session: the adapter process to spawn and the `launch` request to send.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct LaunchConfig {
    /// The adapter executable (e.g. "lldb-dap") and its arguments.
    pub adapter: String,
    pub adapter_args: Vec<String>,
    /// Extra environment and working directory for the adapter process itself.
    pub adapter_env: Vec<(String, String)>,
    pub adapter_cwd: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// The `adapterID` sent in `initialize` (e.g. "lldb", "CodeLLDB", "debugpy").
    pub adapter_id: String,
    /// The raw `launch` request arguments, passed through as given (adapter-specific keys such
    /// as `program`, `cwd`, `args`, `env`, `type`, `stopOnEntry`, …).
    pub launch_arguments: serde_json::Value,
}

impl LaunchConfig {
    /// The plain lldb-style launch of `program` (in `cwd`) under `adapter`.
    pub fn lldb(
        adapter: &str,
        adapter_args: &[String],
        program: &Path,
        cwd: Option<&Path>,
    ) -> Self {
        let mut args = serde_json::json!({
            "name": "orress",
            "type": "lldb",
            "request": "launch",
            "program": program.to_string_lossy(),
            "stopOnEntry": false,
        });
        if let Some(cwd) = cwd {
            args["cwd"] = serde_json::json!(cwd.to_string_lossy());
        }
        Self {
            adapter: adapter.to_string(),
            adapter_args: adapter_args.to_vec(),
            adapter_env: Vec::new(),
            adapter_cwd: None,
            adapter_id: "lldb".into(),
            launch_arguments: args,
        }
    }
}

/// A running (or finished) source-debug session.
pub struct DapSession {
    tx: Transport,
}

impl DapSession {
    /// Launches `program` under the adapter at `adapter` (e.g. "lldb-dap"), stopping at the
    /// given source breakpoints (1-based line numbers per file).
    pub fn launch(
        adapter: &str,
        adapter_args: &[String],
        program: &Path,
        cwd: Option<&Path>,
        breakpoints: HashMap<PathBuf, Vec<u32>>,
        notify: Notify,
    ) -> std::io::Result<Self> {
        Self::launch_with(
            LaunchConfig::lldb(adapter, adapter_args, program, cwd),
            breakpoints,
            notify,
        )
    }

    /// Launches a session from a full [`LaunchConfig`] (adapter id, raw launch arguments, the
    /// adapter's own environment and working directory), stopping at the given breakpoints.
    pub fn launch_with(
        config: LaunchConfig,
        breakpoints: HashMap<PathBuf, Vec<u32>>,
        notify: Notify,
    ) -> std::io::Result<Self> {
        Ok(Self {
            tx: Transport::start(config, breakpoints, notify)?,
        })
    }

    /// Replaces the breakpoints of one source file (1-based lines). Sent to the adapter at once
    /// when the session is configured; before that they are sent with the initial set.
    pub fn set_breakpoints(&self, source: &Path, lines: Vec<u32>) {
        self.tx.set_breakpoints(source, lines);
    }

    pub fn state(&self) -> DapState {
        self.tx.state()
    }

    pub fn resume(&self) {
        self.tx.control("continue");
    }
    pub fn step_over(&self) {
        self.tx.control("next");
    }
    pub fn step_in(&self) {
        self.tx.control("stepIn");
    }
    pub fn step_out(&self) {
        self.tx.control("stepOut");
    }
    pub fn pause(&self) {
        self.tx.control("pause");
    }
    pub fn stop(&self) {
        self.tx.terminate();
    }
}

pub(crate) fn parse_frames_body(body: &serde_json::Value) -> Vec<Frame> {
    body.get("stackFrames")
        .and_then(|v| v.as_array())
        .map(|arr| {
            arr.iter()
                .map(|f| Frame {
                    id: f.get("id").and_then(|v| v.as_i64()).unwrap_or(0),
                    name: f
                        .get("name")
                        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
                        .unwrap_or("")
                        .to_string(),
                    source: f
                        .get("source")
                        .and_then(|s| s.get("path"))
                        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
                        .map(PathBuf::from),
                    line: f.get("line").and_then(|v| v.as_u64()).unwrap_or(0) as u32,
                })
                .collect()
        })
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

pub(crate) fn parse_variables_body(body: &serde_json::Value) -> Vec<Variable> {
    body.get("variables")
        .and_then(|v| v.as_array())
        .map(|arr| {
            arr.iter()
                .map(|v| Variable {
                    name: v
                        .get("name")
                        .and_then(|x| x.as_str())
                        .unwrap_or("")
                        .to_string(),
                    value: v
                        .get("value")
                        .and_then(|x| x.as_str())
                        .unwrap_or("")
                        .to_string(),
                    ty: v.get("type").and_then(|x| x.as_str()).map(str::to_string),
                })
                .collect()
        })
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

/// Finds a DAP adapter: `lldb-dap` on PATH, or the LLVM install on Windows.
pub fn find_adapter() -> Option<(String, Vec<String>)> {
    for cand in ["lldb-dap", "lldb-vscode"] {
        if which(cand) {
            return Some((cand.to_string(), Vec::new()));
        }
    }
    if cfg!(windows) {
        let p = "C:/Program Files/LLVM/bin/lldb-dap.exe";
        if Path::new(p).exists() {
            return Some((p.to_string(), Vec::new()));
        }
    }
    None
}

fn which(cmd: &str) -> bool {
    std::process::Command::new(cmd)
        .arg("--version")
        .stdout(std::process::Stdio::null())
        .stderr(std::process::Stdio::null())
        .status()
        .map(|s| s.success())
        .unwrap_or(false)
}
```

`crates/orress-dap/src/transport.rs`:

```rs
//! DAP JSON framing, a background reader thread, and the protocol state machine. All the
//! sequencing (initialize -> launch, the `initialized` event -> setBreakpoints, a `stopped`
//! event -> stackTrace -> scopes -> variables) runs on the reader thread.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader, Write};
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::process::{Child, ChildStdin, Command, Stdio};
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicI64, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

use serde_json::{Value, json};

use crate::{DapState, LaunchConfig, Status, parse_frames_body, parse_variables_body};

pub type Notify = Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>;

struct Shared {
    state: DapState,
    thread_id: i64,
    /// Whether the initial breakpoints and `configurationDone` have been sent, after which a
    /// breakpoint change goes straight to the adapter.
    configured: bool,
}

struct Inner {
    writer: Mutex<ChildStdin>,
    next_seq: AtomicI64,
    pending: Mutex<HashMap<i64, String>>,
    shared: Mutex<Shared>,
    notify: Notify,
    /// The `launch` request arguments, sent as given.
    launch_arguments: Value,
    /// Breakpoints per source file; updated live by [`Transport::set_breakpoints`].
    breakpoints: Mutex<HashMap<PathBuf, Vec<u32>>>,
}

impl Inner {
    fn bump(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut DapState)) {
        {
            let mut s = self.shared.lock().expect("dap state");
            f(&mut s.state);
            s.state.generation += 1;
        }
        (self.notify)();
    }

    fn send(&self, msg: &Value) {
        if std::env::var("ORRESS_DAP_DEBUG").is_ok() {
            eprintln!(
                "[dap] -> {} {}",
                msg.get("command").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or(""),
                msg
            );
        }
        if let Ok(mut w) = self.writer.lock() {
            let _ = write_message(&mut *w, msg);
        }
    }

    fn request(&self, command: &str, arguments: Value) -> i64 {
        let seq = self.next_seq.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
        if let Ok(mut p) = self.pending.lock() {
            p.insert(seq, command.to_string());
        }
        self.send(
            &json!({ "seq": seq, "type": "request", "command": command, "arguments": arguments }),
        );
        seq
    }

    fn launch_program(&self) {
        self.request("launch", self.launch_arguments.clone());
    }

    fn send_breakpoints(&self, src: &std::path::Path, lines: &[u32]) {
        self.request(
            "setBreakpoints",
            json!({
                "source": { "path": src.to_string_lossy(), "name": src.file_name().map(|n| n.to_string_lossy()) },
                "breakpoints": lines.iter().map(|l| json!({ "line": l })).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
                "lines": lines,
            }),
        );
    }

    fn set_breakpoints(&self) {
        let all = self
            .breakpoints
            .lock()
            .map(|b| b.clone())
            .unwrap_or_default();
        for (src, lines) in &all {
            self.send_breakpoints(src, lines);
        }
        if let Ok(mut s) = self.shared.lock() {
            s.configured = true;
        }
        self.request("configurationDone", json!({}));
    }
}

pub struct Transport {
    inner: Arc<Inner>,
    /// The adapter process (taken on drop, to be reaped off the UI thread).
    child: Option<Child>,
    _reader: std::thread::JoinHandle<()>,
}

impl Transport {
    pub fn start(
        config: LaunchConfig,
        breakpoints: HashMap<PathBuf, Vec<u32>>,
        notify: Notify,
    ) -> std::io::Result<Self> {
        let adapter = config.adapter.as_str();
        let mut cmd = Command::new(adapter);
        cmd.args(&config.adapter_args)
            .envs(config.adapter_env.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k, v)))
            .stdin(Stdio::piped())
            .stdout(Stdio::piped())
            .stderr(Stdio::null());
        if let Some(cwd) = &config.adapter_cwd {
            cmd.current_dir(cwd);
        }
        // The adapter may need its own directory on PATH to find its shared libraries
        // (e.g. lldb-dap needs liblldb next to it).
        if let Some(dir) = std::path::Path::new(adapter)
            .parent()
            .filter(|d| !d.as_os_str().is_empty())
        {
            let mut paths = vec![dir.to_path_buf()];
            if let Some(existing) = std::env::var_os("PATH") {
                paths.extend(std::env::split_paths(&existing));
            }
            if let Ok(joined) = std::env::join_paths(paths) {
                cmd.env("PATH", joined);
            }
        }
        let mut child = cmd.spawn()?;
        let stdin = child.stdin.take().expect("adapter stdin");
        let stdout = child.stdout.take().expect("adapter stdout");
        let inner = Arc::new(Inner {
            writer: Mutex::new(stdin),
            next_seq: AtomicI64::new(1),
            pending: Mutex::new(HashMap::new()),
            shared: Mutex::new(Shared {
                state: DapState {
                    status: Some(Status::Starting),
                    ..DapState::default()
                },
                thread_id: 0,
                configured: false,
            }),
            notify,
            launch_arguments: config.launch_arguments,
            breakpoints: Mutex::new(breakpoints),
        });
        let reader_inner = Arc::clone(&inner);
        let reader = std::thread::Builder::new()
            .name("orress-dap-read".into())
            .spawn(move || read_loop(BufReader::new(stdout), &reader_inner))
            .expect("spawn dap reader");

        // Kick off the handshake.
        inner.request(
            "initialize",
            json!({
                "clientID": "orress",
                "adapterID": config.adapter_id,
                "linesStartAt1": true,
                "columnsStartAt1": true,
                "pathFormat": "path",
                "supportsRunInTerminalRequest": false,
            }),
        );

        Ok(Self {
            inner,
            child: Some(child),
            _reader: reader,
        })
    }

    /// Replaces one file's breakpoints; sends them right away once the session is configured
    /// (before that, the `initialized` event sends the whole updated set).
    pub fn set_breakpoints(&self, source: &std::path::Path, lines: Vec<u32>) {
        if let Ok(mut b) = self.inner.breakpoints.lock() {
            b.insert(source.to_path_buf(), lines.clone());
        }
        let configured = self.inner.shared.lock().is_ok_and(|s| s.configured);
        let alive = self.state().is_alive();
        if configured && alive {
            self.inner.send_breakpoints(source, &lines);
        }
    }

    pub fn state(&self) -> DapState {
        self.inner.shared.lock().expect("dap state").state.clone()
    }

    pub fn control(&self, command: &str) {
        let tid = self.inner.shared.lock().map(|s| s.thread_id).unwrap_or(0);
        self.inner.request(command, json!({ "threadId": tid }));
        if matches!(command, "continue" | "next" | "stepIn" | "stepOut") {
            self.inner.bump(|s| s.status = Some(Status::Running));
        }
    }

    pub fn terminate(&self) {
        self.inner.request("terminate", json!({}));
        self.inner
            .request("disconnect", json!({ "terminateDebuggee": true }));
    }
}

impl Drop for Transport {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.inner
            .request("disconnect", json!({ "terminateDebuggee": true }));
        if let Some(mut child) = self.child.take() {
            let _ = child.kill();
            // Reap it (no zombie on Unix) without blocking the UI thread on the wait.
            let _ = std::thread::Builder::new()
                .name("orress-dap-reap".into())
                .spawn(move || {
                    let _ = child.wait();
                });
        }
    }
}

fn read_loop(mut reader: impl BufRead, inner: &Arc<Inner>) {
    loop {
        match read_message(&mut reader) {
            Ok(Some(msg)) => {
                if std::env::var("ORRESS_DAP_DEBUG").is_ok() {
                    let kind = msg.get("type").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or("");
                    let what = msg
                        .get("event")
                        .or_else(|| msg.get("command"))
                        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
                        .unwrap_or("");
                    eprintln!(
                        "[dap] <- {kind} {what} success={:?} msg={}",
                        msg.get("success"),
                        serde_json::to_string(&msg)
                            .unwrap_or_default()
                            .chars()
                            .take(240)
                            .collect::<String>()
                    );
                }
                handle(&msg, inner)
            }
            Ok(None) => break,
            Err(_) => break,
        }
    }
    inner.bump(|s| match s.status {
        // Exiting before we ever got going means the adapter itself failed to start.
        Some(Status::Starting) => {
            s.status = Some(Status::Failed);
            s.last_error = Some(
                "the debug adapter exited before starting — is it installed and working?".into(),
            );
        }
        Some(Status::Exited) => {}
        _ => s.status = Some(Status::Exited),
    });
}

fn handle(msg: &Value, inner: &Arc<Inner>) {
    match msg.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str) {
        Some("response") => {
            let req_seq = msg.get("request_seq").and_then(Value::as_i64).unwrap_or(-1);
            let command = inner
                .pending
                .lock()
                .ok()
                .and_then(|mut p| p.remove(&req_seq))
                .or_else(|| {
                    msg.get("command")
                        .and_then(Value::as_str)
                        .map(str::to_string)
                })
                .unwrap_or_default();
            let body = msg.get("body").cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null);
            let success = msg.get("success").and_then(Value::as_bool).unwrap_or(false);
            if !success {
                let err = msg
                    .get("message")
                    .and_then(Value::as_str)
                    .unwrap_or("request failed");
                if matches!(command.as_str(), "launch" | "initialize") {
                    inner.bump(|s| {
                        s.status = Some(Status::Failed);
                        s.last_error = Some(format!("{command}: {err}"));
                    });
                }
                return;
            }
            handle_response(&command, &body, inner);
        }
        Some("event") => handle_event(msg, inner),
        _ => {}
    }
}

fn handle_response(command: &str, body: &Value, inner: &Arc<Inner>) {
    match command {
        "initialize" => inner.launch_program(),
        "stackTrace" => {
            let frames = parse_frames_body(body);
            let current = frames
                .first()
                .and_then(|f| f.source.clone().map(|p| (p, f.line)));
            let top = frames.first().map(|f| f.id);
            inner.bump(|s| {
                s.frames = frames;
                s.current = current;
            });
            if let Some(id) = top {
                inner.request("scopes", json!({ "frameId": id }));
            }
        }
        "scopes" => {
            let reference = body
                .get("scopes")
                .and_then(Value::as_array)
                .and_then(|scopes| {
                    scopes
                        .iter()
                        .find(|s| s.get("name").and_then(Value::as_str) == Some("Locals"))
                        .or_else(|| scopes.first())
                })
                .and_then(|s| s.get("variablesReference"))
                .and_then(Value::as_i64);
            if let Some(reference) = reference {
                inner.request("variables", json!({ "variablesReference": reference }));
            } else {
                inner.bump(|s| s.status = Some(Status::Stopped));
            }
        }
        "variables" => {
            let vars = parse_variables_body(body);
            inner.bump(|s| {
                s.variables = vars;
                s.status = Some(Status::Stopped);
            });
        }
        _ => {}
    }
}

fn handle_event(msg: &Value, inner: &Arc<Inner>) {
    let event = msg.get("event").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
    let body = msg.get("body").cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null);
    match event {
        "initialized" => inner.set_breakpoints(),
        "stopped" => {
            let tid = body.get("threadId").and_then(Value::as_i64).unwrap_or(0);
            let reason = body
                .get("reason")
                .and_then(Value::as_str)
                .unwrap_or("stopped")
                .to_string();
            {
                let mut s = inner.shared.lock().expect("dap state");
                s.thread_id = tid;
                s.state.stop_reason = Some(reason);
            }
            inner.request(
                "stackTrace",
                json!({ "threadId": tid, "startFrame": 0, "levels": 40 }),
            );
        }
        "continued" => inner.bump(|s| s.status = Some(Status::Running)),
        "output" => {
            if let Some(text) = body.get("output").and_then(Value::as_str) {
                let text = text.to_string();
                inner.bump(|s| s.output.push(text));
            }
        }
        "terminated" | "exited" => inner.bump(|s| s.status = Some(Status::Exited)),
        _ => {}
    }
}

fn write_message(w: &mut impl Write, v: &Value) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let body = serde_json::to_vec(v)?;
    write!(w, "Content-Length: {}\r\n\r\n", body.len())?;
    w.write_all(&body)?;
    w.flush()
}

fn read_message(reader: &mut impl BufRead) -> std::io::Result<Option<Value>> {
    let mut content_length: Option<usize> = None;
    loop {
        let mut line = String::new();
        if reader.read_line(&mut line)? == 0 {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let line = line.trim_end_matches(['\r', '\n']);
        if line.is_empty() {
            break;
        }
        if let Some(v) = line.strip_prefix("Content-Length:") {
            content_length = v.trim().parse().ok();
        }
    }
    let len = content_length.ok_or_else(|| {
        std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, "missing Content-Length")
    })?;
    let mut buf = vec![0u8; len];
    std::io::Read::read_exact(reader, &mut buf)?;
    Ok(Some(serde_json::from_slice(&buf)?))
}
```

`crates/orress-dap/tests/mock.rs`:

```rs
//! Verifies the full DAP client state machine against the mock adapter.
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use orress_dap::{DapSession, Status};

#[test]
fn drives_to_a_stop_with_variables() {
    let adapter = env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_orress_dap_mock");
    let hits = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
    let h = Arc::clone(&hits);
    let notify: Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync> = Arc::new(move || {
        h.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
    });

    let mut bps = HashMap::new();
    bps.insert(PathBuf::from("/tmp/demo.rs"), vec![3u32]);
    let session = DapSession::launch(adapter, &[], &PathBuf::from("/tmp/demo"), None, bps, notify)
        .expect("launch");

    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(10);
    loop {
        let st = session.state();
        if st.status == Some(Status::Stopped) && !st.frames.is_empty() {
            assert_eq!(st.stop_reason.as_deref(), Some("breakpoint"));
            assert_eq!(st.current.as_ref().map(|(_, l)| *l), Some(3));
            assert_eq!(st.frames[0].name, "main");
            assert!(
                st.variables
                    .iter()
                    .any(|v| v.name == "a" && v.value == "41"),
                "vars: {:?}",
                st.variables
            );
            break;
        }
        assert!(
            st.status != Some(Status::Failed),
            "failed: {:?}",
            st.last_error
        );
        assert!(
            Instant::now() < deadline,
            "timed out; status {:?}",
            st.status
        );
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20));
    }
    assert!(hits.load(Ordering::SeqCst) > 0);
    session.stop();
}
```

`crates/orress-debug/src/backend.rs`:

```rs
//! The platform-agnostic debugger back end: the small set of primitives every target
//! (a native Windows process now; ptrace and GDB-remote later) must provide. The
//! controller in `lib.rs` drives one of these on its own thread.

use std::fmt;

use crate::regs::Registers;

pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, DebugError>;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum DebugError {
    /// This platform has no native debugger yet.
    Unsupported(&'static str),
    /// The target is not running (already exited, or never launched).
    NotRunning,
    /// The program file could not be started.
    Launch(String),
    /// An OS call failed, with its message.
    Os(String),
}

impl fmt::Display for DebugError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Self::Unsupported(p) => write!(f, "debugging is not supported on {p} yet"),
            Self::NotRunning => write!(f, "the program is not running"),
            Self::Launch(e) => write!(f, "could not start the program: {e}"),
            Self::Os(e) => write!(f, "{e}"),
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for DebugError {}

/// A loaded module (the executable or a DLL / shared object).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Module {
    pub name: String,
    pub base: u64,
}

/// Why the target stopped.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum StopReason {
    /// Hit a breakpoint the user set, at this address.
    Breakpoint(u64),
    /// Completed a single instruction step.
    Step,
    /// Paused by the user.
    Paused,
    /// An exception the debugger did not plant (access violation, divide by zero …),
    /// with a plain-language description.
    Exception {
        code: u32,
        address: u64,
        text: String,
    },
    /// The process exited with this code.
    Exited(i32),
}

impl StopReason {
    /// A short, friendly description for the status line.
    pub fn summary(&self) -> String {
        match self {
            Self::Breakpoint(a) => format!("stopped at breakpoint 0x{a:x}"),
            Self::Step => "stepped one instruction".into(),
            Self::Paused => "paused".into(),
            Self::Exception { text, address, .. } => format!("{text} at 0x{address:x}"),
            Self::Exited(code) => format!("the program exited (code {code})"),
        }
    }

    pub fn is_exit(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Self::Exited(_))
    }
}

/// What a back end's `poll` produced.
pub enum Event {
    /// The target stopped and is ready for inspection.
    Stopped(StopReason),
    /// The target is still running; nothing to report yet.
    Running,
}

/// The primitives a debugger back end provides. Every method is called only from the
/// controller thread, so implementations need not be `Sync`.
pub trait Backend {
    /// Plants a software breakpoint. It takes effect on the next resume.
    fn add_breakpoint(&mut self, addr: u64) -> Result<()>;
    /// Removes a software breakpoint.
    fn remove_breakpoint(&mut self, addr: u64) -> Result<()>;
    /// Advances the OS debug loop, waiting up to `timeout_ms`. Returns `Running` if the
    /// target is still going, or `Stopped` with the reason.
    fn poll(&mut self, timeout_ms: u32) -> Result<Event>;
    /// Lets the target run until the next event.
    fn resume(&mut self) -> Result<()>;
    /// Executes a single instruction, then stops.
    fn step(&mut self) -> Result<()>;
    /// Asks a running target to stop as soon as possible.
    fn request_pause(&mut self) -> Result<()>;
    fn registers(&mut self) -> Result<Registers>;
    fn set_register(&mut self, name: &str, value: u64) -> Result<()>;
    fn read_memory(&mut self, addr: u64, len: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>>;
    fn write_memory(&mut self, addr: u64, data: &[u8]) -> Result<()>;
    fn modules(&self) -> Vec<Module>;
    /// The base address the main executable was loaded at, once known.
    fn image_base(&self) -> Option<u64>;
    /// The target process id, for pid-based memory reads (`None` for back ends without one).
    fn pid(&self) -> Option<u32> {
        None
    }
    /// Terminates the target.
    fn kill(&mut self) -> Result<()>;
}

/// The back end used on platforms without native debugging yet. Every call fails with a
/// clear message so the UI can explain the situation.
pub struct Unsupported(pub &'static str);

impl Backend for Unsupported {
    fn add_breakpoint(&mut self, _addr: u64) -> Result<()> {
        Err(DebugError::Unsupported(self.0))
    }
    fn remove_breakpoint(&mut self, _addr: u64) -> Result<()> {
        Err(DebugError::Unsupported(self.0))
    }
```
