`crates/orress-debug/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! The ORRESS debugger.
//!
//! Native debugging has a hard rule on Windows: the thread that creates the debuggee is
//! the only one allowed to wait for and continue its debug events. So the debugger runs
//! on its own thread, which owns the [`Backend`]. The UI holds a [`Debugger`] handle and
//! talks to that thread through a command channel; the thread publishes the target's
//! state into a shared snapshot and calls `notify` so the UI repaints.
//!
//! Back ends (x86-64 only): a native Windows one (the Win32 Debug API) and a Linux one
//! (`ptrace`); GDB-remote is planned. Other platforms/architectures get a clean
//! "unsupported" error. A [`MockTarget`] drives the controller in tests on any platform.
//!
//! Start-up: every back end's first stop is reported through `poll`. The Linux back end
//! reports the exec stop as `Paused` (set breakpoints, then continue); the Windows back end
//! runs through the loader breakpoint to the first user breakpoint (or exit).

mod backend;
mod mock;
pub mod procmem;
mod regs;

#[cfg(all(windows, target_arch = "x86_64"))]
mod windows;

#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "x86_64"))]
mod linux;

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests;

use std::sync::mpsc::{Receiver, Sender, channel};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::thread::JoinHandle;

pub use backend::{Backend, DebugError, Event, Module, StopReason, Unsupported};
pub use mock::MockTarget;
pub use procmem::{MapRegion, MemRegion, memory_map, read_all_memory, read_mem};
pub use regs::{FLAGS, FlagInfo, GP_NAMES, Registers, flag_set};

/// Where the target is in its life cycle.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Status {
    /// Starting up (the back end is being created).
    Starting,
    /// Executing.
    Running,
    /// Stopped and ready to inspect.
    Stopped,
    /// The process has ended.
    Exited,
    /// The back end failed; see `last_error`.
    Failed,
}

/// A snapshot of the target for the UI. Cloned out of the shared state each frame.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct DebugState {
    pub status: Status,
    pub reason: Option<StopReason>,
    pub registers: Registers,
    /// Previous registers, so the UI can highlight what just changed.
    pub prev_registers: Registers,
    pub modules: Vec<Module>,
    pub image_base: Option<u64>,
    /// The target process id, once launched (for pid-based memory reads).
    pub pid: Option<u32>,
    /// Breakpoint address -> enabled.
    pub breakpoints: std::collections::BTreeMap<u64, bool>,
    pub last_error: Option<String>,
    /// A cached block of target memory the UI last asked for: (address, bytes).
    pub memory: Option<(u64, Vec<u8>)>,
    /// A cached block around the stack pointer: (address, bytes).
    pub stack: Option<(u64, Vec<u8>)>,
    /// Bumps on every change, so the UI can tell when to refresh derived data.
    pub generation: u64,
}

impl DebugState {
    fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            status: Status::Starting,
            reason: None,
            registers: Registers::default(),
            prev_registers: Registers::default(),
            modules: Vec::new(),
            image_base: None,
            pid: None,
            breakpoints: std::collections::BTreeMap::new(),
            last_error: None,
            memory: None,
            stack: None,
            generation: 0,
        }
    }

    pub fn is_stopped(&self) -> bool {
        self.status == Status::Stopped
    }

    pub fn is_alive(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            self.status,
            Status::Starting | Status::Running | Status::Stopped
        )
    }
}

enum Command {
    Continue,
    Step,
    Pause,
    AddBreakpoint(u64),
    RemoveBreakpoint(u64),
    SetRegister(String, u64),
    WriteMemory(u64, Vec<u8>),
    ReadMemory(u64, usize),
    ReadStack(u64, usize),
    Kill,
    Shutdown,
}

/// A factory that builds the back end on the debugger thread.
type Factory = Box<dyn FnOnce() -> backend::Result<Box<dyn Backend>> + Send>;

/// A handle to a running (or finished) debug session.
pub struct Debugger {
    tx: Sender<Command>,
    shared: Arc<Mutex<DebugState>>,
    thread: Option<JoinHandle<()>>,
}

impl Debugger {
    /// Starts a debug session on a native target. `notify` is called whenever the
    /// target's state changes, so the UI can repaint.
    pub fn launch(
        path: std::path::PathBuf,
        args: Vec<String>,
        notify: Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>,
    ) -> Self {
        Self::spawn(Box::new(move || native_backend(&path, &args)), notify)
    }

    /// Starts a session against a caller-provided back end (used for the mock target).
    pub fn with_backend(
        make: impl FnOnce() -> backend::Result<Box<dyn Backend>> + Send + 'static,
        notify: Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>,
    ) -> Self {
        Self::spawn(Box::new(make), notify)
    }

    fn spawn(make: Factory, notify: Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>) -> Self {
        let shared = Arc::new(Mutex::new(DebugState::new()));
        let (tx, rx) = channel();
        let thread_shared = Arc::clone(&shared);
        let thread = std::thread::Builder::new()
            .name("orress-debug".into())
            .spawn(move || run(make, rx, thread_shared, notify))
            .expect("spawn debugger thread");
        Self {
            tx,
            shared,
            thread: Some(thread),
        }
    }

    /// The current state of the target.
    pub fn state(&self) -> DebugState {
        self.shared.lock().expect("debug state lock").clone()
    }

    pub fn resume(&self) {
        let _ = self.tx.send(Command::Continue);
    }
    pub fn step(&self) {
        let _ = self.tx.send(Command::Step);
    }
    pub fn pause(&self) {
        let _ = self.tx.send(Command::Pause);
    }
    pub fn add_breakpoint(&self, addr: u64) {
        let _ = self.tx.send(Command::AddBreakpoint(addr));
    }
    pub fn remove_breakpoint(&self, addr: u64) {
        let _ = self.tx.send(Command::RemoveBreakpoint(addr));
    }
    pub fn set_register(&self, name: impl Into<String>, value: u64) {
        let _ = self.tx.send(Command::SetRegister(name.into(), value));
    }
    pub fn write_memory(&self, addr: u64, data: Vec<u8>) {
        let _ = self.tx.send(Command::WriteMemory(addr, data));
    }
    /// Asks the thread to cache `len` bytes of memory at `addr` into the snapshot.
    pub fn read_memory(&self, addr: u64, len: usize) {
        let _ = self.tx.send(Command::ReadMemory(addr, len));
    }
    /// Caches `len` bytes around the stack pointer into the snapshot.
    pub fn read_stack(&self, addr: u64, len: usize) {
        let _ = self.tx.send(Command::ReadStack(addr, len));
    }
    pub fn kill(&self) {
        let _ = self.tx.send(Command::Kill);
    }
}

impl Drop for Debugger {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let _ = self.tx.send(Command::Kill);
        let _ = self.tx.send(Command::Shutdown);
        if let Some(t) = self.thread.take() {
            let _ = t.join();
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(all(windows, target_arch = "x86_64"))]
fn native_backend(path: &std::path::Path, args: &[String]) -> backend::Result<Box<dyn Backend>> {
    Ok(Box::new(windows::WindowsBackend::launch(path, args)?))
}

#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "x86_64"))]
fn native_backend(path: &std::path::Path, args: &[String]) -> backend::Result<Box<dyn Backend>> {
    Ok(Box::new(linux::LinuxBackend::launch(path, args)?))
}

#[cfg(not(any(
    all(windows, target_arch = "x86_64"),
    all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "x86_64")
)))]
fn native_backend(_path: &std::path::Path, _args: &[String]) -> backend::Result<Box<dyn Backend>> {
    Err(DebugError::Unsupported("this platform"))
}

/// Updates the shared snapshot and asks the UI to repaint.
fn publish(shared: &Mutex<DebugState>, notify: &dyn Fn(), f: impl FnOnce(&mut DebugState)) {
    {
        let mut s = shared.lock().expect("debug state lock");
        f(&mut s);
        s.generation += 1;
    }
    notify();
}

fn snapshot(
    backend: &mut dyn Backend,
    shared: &Mutex<DebugState>,
    notify: &dyn Fn(),
    reason: StopReason,
) {
    let regs = backend.registers().unwrap_or_default();
    let modules = backend.modules();
    let image_base = backend.image_base();
    let pid = backend.pid();
    let exited = reason.is_exit();
    publish(shared, notify, |s| {
        s.prev_registers = s.registers;
        s.registers = regs;
        s.modules = modules;
        s.image_base = image_base;
        s.pid = pid;
        s.status = if exited {
            Status::Exited
        } else {
            Status::Stopped
        };
        s.reason = Some(reason);
        // A clean stop clears any earlier transient warning.
        s.last_error = None;
    });
}

fn run(
    make: Factory,
    rx: Receiver<Command>,
    shared: Arc<Mutex<DebugState>>,
    notify: Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>,
) {
    let mut backend = match make() {
        Ok(b) => b,
        Err(e) => {
            publish(&shared, &*notify, |s| {
                s.status = Status::Failed;
                s.last_error = Some(e.to_string());
            });
            return;
        }
    };
    // The target starts suspended at the initial breakpoint the OS reports; drive it to
    // that first stop so the user sees registers immediately.
    let mut running = true;
    loop {
        if running {
            match backend.poll(50) {
                Ok(Event::Running) => {
                    // Still executing: handle commands that are safe while the target
                    // runs (breakpoints, memory, pause, kill). Run/step wait for a stop.
                    while let Ok(cmd) = rx.try_recv() {
                        match cmd {
                            Command::Pause => {
                                let _ = backend.request_pause();
                            }
                            Command::AddBreakpoint(addr) => {
                                let ok =
                                    report_err(&backend.add_breakpoint(addr), &shared, &*notify);
                                if ok {
                                    publish(&shared, &*notify, |s| {
                                        s.breakpoints.insert(addr, true);
                                    });
                                }
                            }
                            Command::RemoveBreakpoint(addr) => {
                                let _ = backend.remove_breakpoint(addr);
                                publish(&shared, &*notify, |s| {
                                    s.breakpoints.remove(&addr);
                                });
                            }
                            Command::WriteMemory(addr, data) => {
                                report_err(&backend.write_memory(addr, &data), &shared, &*notify);
                            }
                            Command::Kill | Command::Shutdown => {
                                let _ = backend.kill();
                                publish(&shared, &*notify, |s| s.status = Status::Exited);
                                return;
                            }
                            _ => {} // continue/step/edit-register wait until the target stops
                        }
                    }
                    // The image base and module list become known while running; publish
                    // them so the UI can place breakpoints by runtime address.
                    let base = backend.image_base();
                    let mods = backend.modules();
                    let changed = {
                        let s = shared.lock().expect("debug state lock");
                        s.image_base != base || s.modules.len() != mods.len()
                    };
                    if changed {
                        publish(&shared, &*notify, |s| {
                            s.image_base = base;
                            s.modules = mods;
                        });
                    }
                }
                Ok(Event::Stopped(reason)) => {
                    running = false;
                    snapshot(&mut *backend, &shared, &*notify, reason);
                }
                Err(e) => {
                    running = false;
                    publish(&shared, &*notify, |s| {
                        s.status = Status::Failed;
                        s.last_error = Some(e.to_string());
                    });
                }
            }
            continue;
        }
        // Stopped: block until the user asks for something.
        let Ok(cmd) = rx.recv() else {
            let _ = backend.kill();
            return;
        };
        match cmd {
            Command::Continue => {
                if report_err(&backend_resume(&mut *backend), &shared, &*notify) {
                    set_running(&shared, &*notify);
                    running = true;
                }
            }
            Command::Step => {
                if report_err(&backend.step(), &shared, &*notify) {
                    running = true;
                }
            }
            Command::Pause => {}
            Command::AddBreakpoint(addr) => {
                let ok = report_err(&backend.add_breakpoint(addr), &shared, &*notify);
                if ok {
                    publish(&shared, &*notify, |s| {
                        s.breakpoints.insert(addr, true);
                    });
                }
            }
            Command::RemoveBreakpoint(addr) => {
                let _ = backend.remove_breakpoint(addr);
                publish(&shared, &*notify, |s| {
                    s.breakpoints.remove(&addr);
                });
            }
            Command::SetRegister(name, value) => {
                if report_err(&backend.set_register(&name, value), &shared, &*notify) {
                    let regs = backend.registers().unwrap_or_default();
                    publish(&shared, &*notify, |s| s.registers = regs);
                }
            }
            Command::WriteMemory(addr, data) => {
                report_err(&backend.write_memory(addr, &data), &shared, &*notify);
            }
            Command::ReadMemory(addr, len) => match backend.read_memory(addr, len) {
                Ok(bytes) => publish(&shared, &*notify, |s| s.memory = Some((addr, bytes))),
                Err(e) => publish(&shared, &*notify, |s| s.last_error = Some(e.to_string())),
            },
            Command::ReadStack(addr, len) => {
                if let Ok(bytes) = backend.read_memory(addr, len) {
                    publish(&shared, &*notify, |s| s.stack = Some((addr, bytes)));
                }
            }
            Command::Kill => {
                let _ = backend.kill();
                publish(&shared, &*notify, |s| s.status = Status::Exited);
            }
            Command::Shutdown => {
                let _ = backend.kill();
                return;
            }
        }
    }
}

fn set_running(shared: &Mutex<DebugState>, notify: &dyn Fn()) {
    publish(shared, notify, |s| {
        s.status = Status::Running;
        s.reason = None;
    });
}

/// `resume` is its own fn so the `report_err` borrow is clean.
fn backend_resume(backend: &mut dyn Backend) -> backend::Result<()> {
    backend.resume()
}

/// Records an error in the snapshot. Returns true on success.
fn report_err<T>(r: &backend::Result<T>, shared: &Mutex<DebugState>, notify: &dyn Fn()) -> bool {
    match r {
        Ok(_) => true,
        Err(e) => {
            let msg = e.to_string();
            publish(shared, notify, |s| s.last_error = Some(msg));
            false
        }
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-debug/src/linux.rs`:

```rs
//! The Linux debugger back end, built on `ptrace(2)` (via `nix` and raw `libc`). It launches the
//! target under trace, plants `int3` software breakpoints, single-steps with `PTRACE_SINGLESTEP`,
//! and reads/writes the live process through `/proc/<pid>/mem` — the same primitives as the
//! Windows back end, so the controller in `lib.rs` drives it identically. `unsafe` is confined
//! here (the `fork`/`exec`, raw `waitpid` and raw `ptrace` resume calls), as the workspace allows
//! for a platform back end. x86-64 only (the register file is x86-64's).
//!
//! Breakpoint protocol (standard, gdb-style): save the original byte, write `0xCC`. When an
//! `int3` traps (`si_code == SI_KERNEL`) the instruction pointer is one past it, so we rewind it
//! to the breakpoint address. To run past a breakpoint we are sitting on, restore the original
//! byte, single-step that one instruction, then re-plant `0xCC` when the step completes. A
//! single-step trap (`si_code == TRAP_TRACE`) is never rewound: a step that *lands* on a planted
//! breakpoint just records that we are sitting on it.
//!
//! Signals: a fault the program caused (SIGSEGV, SIGILL, …) is reported first and then
//! **delivered** on the next continue/step, so the program's own handlers run (and an unhandled
//! fault terminates it, as it would without a debugger) instead of re-faulting forever.
//! Housekeeping signals (SIGCHLD, SIGALRM, SIGWINCH, real-time signals …) are passed through
//! silently. A user pause is a `SIGSTOP` we send and then swallow.
//!
//! Threads: `PTRACE_O_TRACECLONE` auto-attaches every new thread, so a breakpoint hit in any
//! thread is caught and reported with that thread's registers. The model is "non-stop": only the
//! thread that reported the stop is halted; other threads keep running. While a breakpoint's
//! byte is restored for a step-over, another thread can run through that address without
//! stopping. `fork`ed child processes are not traced (and inherit any planted `0xCC` bytes).
//! `PTRACE_O_EXITKILL` makes the kernel kill the target if the debugger itself dies.

use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};
use std::ffi::{CString, c_char, c_void};
use std::fs::{File, OpenOptions};
use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
use std::os::unix::fs::FileExt;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use nix::errno::Errno;
use nix::libc;
use nix::sys::ptrace::{self, Options};
use nix::sys::signal::Signal;
use nix::unistd::{ForkResult, Pid, fork};

use crate::backend::{Backend, DebugError, Event, Module, Result, StopReason};
use crate::regs::Registers;

impl From<nix::errno::Errno> for DebugError {
    fn from(e: nix::errno::Errno) -> Self {
        DebugError::Os(e.to_string())
    }
}

/// `si_code` of a `SIGTRAP` raised by an `int3` instruction.
const SI_KERNEL: i32 = libc::SI_KERNEL;
/// `PTRACE_EVENT_*` codes (the high byte of a stop status).
const EVENT_CLONE: i32 = libc::PTRACE_EVENT_CLONE;
const EVENT_EXEC: i32 = libc::PTRACE_EVENT_EXEC;

/// How a `SIGTRAP` was raised, from its `si_code`.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum TrapKind {
    /// An `int3` executed (ours or the program's).
    Int3,
    /// A hardware debug trap — for us, a completed single step.
    Trace,
    /// Sent by a process (`kill`/`raise`/`tgkill`): a genuine signal for the program.
    User,
}

pub struct LinuxBackend {
    /// The process (thread-group leader).
    pid: Pid,
    /// `/proc/<pid>/mem`, opened read+write (ptrace access reaches read-only code pages).
    mem: File,
    exe: PathBuf,
    image_base: Option<u64>,
    /// addr -> the original byte we overwrote with `0xCC`.
    breakpoints: HashMap<u64, u8>,
    /// Every traced thread (the leader included).
    threads: Vec<Pid>,
    /// New threads whose initial `SIGSTOP` has not been consumed yet.
    fresh: HashSet<Pid>,
    /// The thread of the current stop: registers are read from / written to it, and it is the
    /// one resumed by continue/step.
    current: Pid,
    /// We are stopped exactly on this breakpoint (its `0xCC` is still in memory); the next resume
    /// must step over it.
    at_bp: Option<u64>,
    /// A thread is single-stepping over this breakpoint (its original byte is in memory);
    /// re-plant `0xCC` once that thread stops again.
    step_over: Option<(Pid, u64)>,
    /// The user asked this thread for one instruction; its next trace trap is a `Step` stop.
    user_step: Option<Pid>,
    /// Signals to deliver to a thread when it is next resumed (faults we reported, or
    /// pass-through signals that arrived mid-step).
    pending_signal: HashMap<Pid, i32>,
    /// The process is still in its exec stop and the first poll has not reported it yet.
    pending_initial_stop: bool,
    /// The user asked to pause; the next `SIGSTOP` is ours and is reported as `Paused`.
    pause_requested: bool,
    /// True after a `cont`/`step`, until the target stops again.
    running: bool,
    exited: bool,
}

/// `waitpid` on one thread (`__WALL`, so clone children count), retrying on `EINTR`. Returns the
/// raw status, or `None` if `nohang` and the thread has nothing to report.
fn wait_raw(tid: Pid, nohang: bool) -> std::result::Result<Option<i32>, Errno> {
    let flags = libc::__WALL | if nohang { libc::WNOHANG } else { 0 };
    let mut status: libc::c_int = 0;
    loop {
        // SAFETY: plain waitpid on a specific pid with a valid out-pointer.
        let r = unsafe { libc::waitpid(tid.as_raw(), &mut status, flags) };
        match r {
            -1 => match Errno::last() {
                Errno::EINTR => continue,
                e => return Err(e),
            },
            0 => return Ok(None),
            _ => return Ok(Some(status)),
        }
    }
}

/// Resumes a stopped tracee, either running or single-stepping, delivering `sig` (0 = none).
/// Raw `libc` so real-time signals (which `nix::Signal` cannot represent) can be delivered.
fn ptrace_resume(tid: Pid, step: bool, sig: i32) -> Result<()> {
    let req = if step {
        libc::PTRACE_SINGLESTEP
    } else {
        libc::PTRACE_CONT
    };
    // SAFETY: a resume request on a ptrace-stopped tracee of ours; `addr` is ignored and `data`
    // carries the signal number, exactly as ptrace(2) specifies. No memory is passed.
    let r = unsafe {
        libc::ptrace(
            req,
            tid.as_raw(),
            std::ptr::null_mut::<c_void>(),
            std::ptr::without_provenance_mut::<c_void>(sig as usize),
        )
    };
    Errno::result(r).map(drop).map_err(Into::into)
}

/// Signals that are routine process housekeeping: pass them to the program without stopping.
fn is_passthrough(sig: i32) -> bool {
    // glibc uses real-time signals internally (thread cancellation, setxid), so all of them
    // must reach the program.
    sig >= 32
        || [
            libc::SIGCHLD,
            libc::SIGWINCH,
            libc::SIGALRM,
            libc::SIGVTALRM,
            libc::SIGPROF,
            libc::SIGURG,
            libc::SIGIO,
            libc::SIGCONT,
        ]
        .contains(&sig)
}

/// Stop signals we must not deliver: they would put the whole process into a group-stop.
fn is_job_control_stop(sig: i32) -> bool {
    [libc::SIGSTOP, libc::SIGTSTP, libc::SIGTTIN, libc::SIGTTOU].contains(&sig)
}

fn signal_name(sig: i32) -> String {
    Signal::try_from(sig).map_or_else(|_| format!("signal {sig}"), |s| s.as_str().to_string())
}

impl LinuxBackend {
    pub fn launch(path: &Path, args: &[String]) -> Result<Self> {
        // Build every C string and the argv pointer array *before* forking: the debugger is a
        // multi-threaded process, so after `fork` the child may only call async-signal-safe
        // functions — no allocation (another thread may have held the malloc lock at the fork).
        let abs = std::fs::canonicalize(path)
            .map_err(|e| DebugError::Launch(format!("{}: {e}", path.display())))?;
        let c_path = CString::new(abs.as_os_str().as_bytes())
            .map_err(|e| DebugError::Launch(e.to_string()))?;
        let mut argv: Vec<CString> = Vec::with_capacity(args.len() + 1);
        argv.push(c_path.clone());
        for a in args {
            argv.push(CString::new(a.as_bytes()).map_err(|e| DebugError::Launch(e.to_string()))?);
        }
        let argv_ptrs: Vec<*const c_char> = argv
            .iter()
            .map(|a| a.as_ptr())
            .chain(std::iter::once(std::ptr::null()))
            .collect();

        // SAFETY: the child branch below only makes raw syscalls that are async-signal-safe
        // (ptrace, personality, execv, _exit) on memory prepared before the fork; it never
        // allocates, locks, or returns into Rust code that could.
        match unsafe { fork() }.map_err(|e| DebugError::Launch(e.to_string()))? {
            ForkResult::Child => {
                // SAFETY: async-signal-safe syscalls only (see above). `c_path`/`argv_ptrs` are
                // valid, NUL-terminated, and outlive the exec.
                unsafe {
                    // Become traceable, drop ASLR so addresses are stable across runs, then exec.
                    libc::ptrace(
                        libc::PTRACE_TRACEME,
                        0,
                        std::ptr::null_mut::<c_void>(),
                        std::ptr::null_mut::<c_void>(),
                    );
                    let current = libc::personality(0xffff_ffff);
                    if current != -1 {
                        libc::personality(
                            (current as libc::c_ulong) | libc::ADDR_NO_RANDOMIZE as libc::c_ulong,
                        );
                    }
                    libc::execv(c_path.as_ptr(), argv_ptrs.as_ptr());
                    // execv only returns on failure.
                    libc::_exit(127);
                }
            }
            ForkResult::Parent { child } => {
                // The child stops with SIGTRAP at the execve; wait for it.
                let status = wait_raw(child, false)
                    .map_err(|e| DebugError::Launch(e.to_string()))?
                    .unwrap_or(0);
                if libc::WIFEXITED(status) {
                    let code = libc::WEXITSTATUS(status);
                    let why = if code == 127 {
                        " (could not execute it)"
                    } else {
                        ""
                    };
                    return Err(DebugError::Launch(format!(
                        "exited early with code {code}{why}"
                    )));
                }
                if !(libc::WIFSTOPPED(status) && libc::WSTOPSIG(status) == libc::SIGTRAP) {
                    return Err(DebugError::Launch(format!(
                        "unexpected start (wait status {status:#x})"
                    )));
                }
                // Follow new threads and new images, and have the kernel kill the target if the
                // debugger dies. EXITKILL needs Linux 3.8; fall back without it.
                let follow = Options::PTRACE_O_TRACECLONE | Options::PTRACE_O_TRACEEXEC;
                if ptrace::setoptions(child, follow | Options::PTRACE_O_EXITKILL).is_err() {
                    let _ = ptrace::setoptions(child, follow);
                }
                let mem = open_mem(child)?;
                let mut me = Self {
                    pid: child,
                    mem,
                    exe: abs,
                    image_base: None,
                    breakpoints: HashMap::new(),
                    threads: vec![child],
                    fresh: HashSet::new(),
                    current: child,
                    at_bp: None,
                    step_over: None,
                    user_step: None,
                    pending_signal: HashMap::new(),
                    pending_initial_stop: true,
                    pause_requested: false,
                    running: false,
                    exited: false,
                };
                me.image_base = me.find_image_base();
                Ok(me)
            }
        }
    }

    /// The load address of the main executable, from `/proc/<pid>/maps` (the lowest mapping backed
    /// by the executable's own path).
    fn find_image_base(&self) -> Option<u64> {
        let maps = std::fs::read_to_string(format!("/proc/{}/maps", self.pid)).ok()?;
        let exe = self.exe.to_string_lossy();
        maps.lines()
            .filter(|l| l.ends_with(exe.as_ref()))
            .filter_map(|l| l.split('-').next())
            .filter_map(|a| u64::from_str_radix(a, 16).ok())
            .min()
    }

    fn read_raw(&self, addr: u64, buf: &mut [u8]) -> Result<()> {
        self.mem
            .read_exact_at(buf, addr)
            .map_err(|e| DebugError::Os(format!("read {addr:#x}: {e}")))
    }

    fn write_raw(&self, addr: u64, data: &[u8]) -> Result<()> {
        self.mem
            .write_all_at(data, addr)
            .map_err(|e| DebugError::Os(format!("write {addr:#x}: {e}")))
    }

    fn get_regs(&self, tid: Pid) -> Result<Registers> {
        let r = ptrace::getregs(tid)?;
        Ok(Registers {
            rax: r.rax,
            rbx: r.rbx,
            rcx: r.rcx,
            rdx: r.rdx,
            rsi: r.rsi,
            rdi: r.rdi,
            rbp: r.rbp,
            rsp: r.rsp,
            r8: r.r8,
            r9: r.r9,
            r10: r.r10,
            r11: r.r11,
            r12: r.r12,
            r13: r.r13,
            r14: r.r14,
            r15: r.r15,
            rip: r.rip,
            rflags: r.eflags,
        })
    }

    /// Whether `tid` is in the middle of a single step (a user step or a breakpoint step-over).
    fn is_stepping(&self, tid: Pid) -> bool {
        self.user_step == Some(tid) || self.step_over.is_some_and(|(t, _)| t == tid)
    }

    /// `tid` stopped for some reason other than its step finishing: if it was stepping over a
    /// breakpoint, put the `0xCC` back now (and note we're sitting on it if `rip` is still
    /// there), and forget any user step.
    fn abandon_step(&mut self, tid: Pid, rip: Option<u64>) {
        if let Some((t, addr)) = self.step_over
            && t == tid
        {
            self.step_over = None;
            if self.breakpoints.contains_key(&addr) {
                let _ = self.write_raw(addr, &[0xCC]);
                if rip == Some(addr) {
                    self.at_bp = Some(addr);
                }
            }
        }
        if self.user_step == Some(tid) {
            self.user_step = None;
        }
    }

    /// Records a reported stop on `tid` and builds the event.
    fn stop(&mut self, tid: Pid, reason: StopReason) -> Option<Event> {
        self.running = false;
        self.current = tid;
        Some(Event::Stopped(reason))
    }

    /// The process has gone (exited, killed, or lost).
    fn gone(&mut self, code: i32) -> Option<Event> {
        self.exited = true;
        self.running = false;
        self.at_bp = None;
        self.step_over = None;
        self.user_step = None;
        self.threads.clear();
        self.fresh.clear();
        Some(Event::Stopped(StopReason::Exited(code)))
    }

    /// The process replaced its image (execve): the old breakpoints, threads and memory handle
    /// are gone with the old address space.
    fn on_exec(&mut self) -> Option<Event> {
        // After a multi-threaded exec the surviving thread takes over the leader's id; the other
        // threads are gone and get reaped (or dropped on ECHILD) by the next sweeps.
        if !self.threads.contains(&self.pid) {
            self.threads.push(self.pid);
        }
        self.fresh.clear();
        self.pending_signal.clear();
        self.breakpoints.clear();
        self.at_bp = None;
        self.step_over = None;
        self.user_step = None;
        if let Ok(mem) = open_mem(self.pid) {
            self.mem = mem;
        }
        if let Ok(exe) = std::fs::read_link(format!("/proc/{}/exe", self.pid)) {
            self.exe = exe;
        }
        self.image_base = self.find_image_base();
        let address = ptrace::getregs(self.pid).map(|r| r.rip).unwrap_or(0);
        self.stop(
            self.pid,
            StopReason::Exception {
                code: libc::SIGTRAP as u32,
                address,
                text: "the program started a new executable (execve); its breakpoints were cleared"
                    .into(),
            },
        )
    }

    /// Classifies a `SIGTRAP` stop of `tid` by its `si_code`.
    fn trap_kind(&self, tid: Pid) -> TrapKind {
        match ptrace::getsiginfo(tid) {
            Ok(info) if info.si_code == SI_KERNEL => TrapKind::Int3,
            Ok(info) if info.si_code > 0 => TrapKind::Trace,
            Ok(_) => TrapKind::User,
            // No siginfo: fall back on what we asked the thread to do.
            Err(_) if self.is_stepping(tid) => TrapKind::Trace,
            Err(_) => TrapKind::Int3,
        }
    }

    /// Handles one wait status from `tid`. Returns the event to report, or `None` if the
    /// target keeps running (the status was consumed internally).
    fn handle_status(&mut self, tid: Pid, status: i32) -> Result<Option<Event>> {
        if libc::WIFEXITED(status) || libc::WIFSIGNALED(status) {
            let code = if libc::WIFEXITED(status) {
                libc::WEXITSTATUS(status)
            } else {
                128 + libc::WTERMSIG(status)
            };
            if tid == self.pid {
                return Ok(self.gone(code));
            }
            // A thread ended.
            self.threads.retain(|&t| t != tid);
            self.fresh.remove(&tid);
            self.pending_signal.remove(&tid);
            self.abandon_step(tid, None);
            return Ok(None);
        }
        if !libc::WIFSTOPPED(status) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let sig = libc::WSTOPSIG(status);
        let event = status >> 16;

        // ptrace event stops.
        if sig == libc::SIGTRAP && event != 0 {
            if event == EVENT_EXEC {
                return Ok(self.on_exec());
            }
            if event == EVENT_CLONE
                && let Ok(new) = ptrace::getevent(tid)
            {
                let new = Pid::from_raw(new as libc::pid_t);
                if !self.threads.contains(&new) {
                    self.threads.push(new);
                    self.fresh.insert(new);
                }
            }
            // Resume the creator in whatever mode it was in.
            ptrace_resume(tid, self.is_stepping(tid), 0)?;
            return Ok(None);
        }

        // A new thread's initial stop: let it run.
        if sig == libc::SIGSTOP && self.fresh.remove(&tid) {
            ptrace_resume(tid, false, 0)?;
            return Ok(None);
        }

        let rip = ptrace::getregs(tid).map(|r| r.rip).ok();

        if sig == libc::SIGTRAP {
            match self.trap_kind(tid) {
                TrapKind::Int3 => {
                    let bp = rip.unwrap_or(0).wrapping_sub(1);
                    // Stepping over a breakpoint placed on a genuine `int3` byte executes the
                    // program's own int3: that one must not be rewound (it would loop forever).
                    let own_int3 = self.step_over == Some((tid, bp));
                    self.abandon_step(tid, rip);
                    if !own_int3
                        && self.breakpoints.contains_key(&bp)
                        && let Ok(mut r) = ptrace::getregs(tid)
                    {
                        r.rip = bp;
                        ptrace::setregs(tid, r)?;
                        self.at_bp = Some(bp);
                        return Ok(self.stop(tid, StopReason::Breakpoint(bp)));
                    }
                    // The program's own int3: report it; continuing resumes after it (as on
                    // Windows).
                    return Ok(self.stop(
                        tid,
                        StopReason::Exception {
                            code: libc::SIGTRAP as u32,
                            address: bp,
                            text: "a breakpoint (int3) in the program".into(),
                        },
                    ));
                }
                TrapKind::Trace if self.is_stepping(tid) => {
                    // A completed single step: re-plant the breakpoint we stepped over.
                    if let Some((t, addr)) = self.step_over
                        && t == tid
                    {
                        self.step_over = None;
                        if self.breakpoints.contains_key(&addr) {
                            self.write_raw(addr, &[0xCC])?;
                        }
                    }
                    if self.user_step == Some(tid) {
                        self.user_step = None;
                        // Landing *on* a planted breakpoint: don't rewind (nothing executed it),
                        // just remember we're on it so the next resume steps over it.
                        if let Some(r) = rip
                            && self.breakpoints.contains_key(&r)
                        {
                            self.at_bp = Some(r);
                            return Ok(self.stop(tid, StopReason::Breakpoint(r)));
                        }
                        return Ok(self.stop(tid, StopReason::Step));
                    }
                    // The step only moved us off a breakpoint: carry on with the continue.
                    let pending = self.pending_signal.remove(&tid).unwrap_or(0);
                    ptrace_resume(tid, false, pending)?;
                    return Ok(None);
                }
                TrapKind::Trace => {
                    // A trace trap we didn't ask for: the program set the trap flag itself.
                    // Report it and hand the SIGTRAP to the program, as the CPU/kernel would.
                    self.pending_signal.insert(tid, libc::SIGTRAP);
                    return Ok(self.stop(
                        tid,
                        StopReason::Exception {
                            code: libc::SIGTRAP as u32,
                            address: rip.unwrap_or(0),
                            text: "a trace trap (the program set the trap flag)".into(),
                        },
                    ));
                }
                TrapKind::User => {
                    self.abandon_step(tid, rip);
                    self.pending_signal.insert(tid, libc::SIGTRAP);
                    return Ok(self.stop(
                        tid,
                        StopReason::Exception {
                            code: libc::SIGTRAP as u32,
                            address: rip.unwrap_or(0),
                            text: "SIGTRAP sent to the program".into(),
                        },
                    ));
                }
            }
        }

        if sig == libc::SIGSTOP && self.pause_requested {
            // Our own pause: swallow the SIGSTOP.
            self.pause_requested = false;
            self.abandon_step(tid, rip);
            return Ok(self.stop(tid, StopReason::Paused));
        }

        if is_passthrough(sig) {
            if self.is_stepping(tid) {
                // Keep the step on its instruction; deliver the signal on the next resume.
                self.pending_signal.insert(tid, sig);
                ptrace_resume(tid, true, 0)?;
            } else {
                ptrace_resume(tid, false, sig)?;
            }
            return Ok(None);
        }

        // A real fault (SIGSEGV, SIGILL, SIGFPE, SIGBUS…) or another stopping signal: report it
        // with the faulting address and deliver it on the next resume (job-control stops are
        // swallowed — delivering them would freeze the whole process).
        self.abandon_step(tid, rip);
        if !is_job_control_stop(sig) {
            self.pending_signal.insert(tid, sig);
        }
        let text = match sig {
            libc::SIGSEGV => "segmentation fault (invalid memory access)".to_string(),
            libc::SIGILL => "illegal instruction".to_string(),
            libc::SIGFPE => "arithmetic exception (e.g. divide by zero)".to_string(),
            libc::SIGBUS => "bus error (misaligned or bad memory access)".to_string(),
            libc::SIGABRT => "aborted".to_string(),
            _ => format!("stopped by {}", signal_name(sig)),
        };
        Ok(self.stop(
            tid,
            StopReason::Exception {
                code: sig as u32,
                address: rip.unwrap_or(0),
                text,
            },
        ))
    }

    /// One non-blocking sweep over every traced thread. Returns the first reportable event.
    fn sweep(&mut self) -> Result<Option<Event>> {
        let tids = self.threads.clone();
        for tid in tids {
            match wait_raw(tid, true) {
                Ok(Some(status)) => {
                    if let Some(ev) = self.handle_status(tid, status)? {
                        return Ok(Some(ev));
                    }
                }
                Ok(None) => {}
                Err(Errno::ECHILD) => {
                    // Not (or no longer) ours to wait for.
                    if tid == self.pid {
                        return Ok(self.gone(-1));
                    }
                    self.threads.retain(|&t| t != tid);
                    self.fresh.remove(&tid);
                    self.abandon_step(tid, None);
                }
                Err(e) => return Err(e.into()),
            }
            if self.exited {
                break;
            }
        }
        Ok(None)
    }
}

fn open_mem(pid: Pid) -> Result<File> {
    OpenOptions::new()
        .read(true)
        .write(true)
        .open(format!("/proc/{pid}/mem"))
        .map_err(|e| DebugError::Os(format!("open /proc/{pid}/mem: {e}")))
}

impl Backend for LinuxBackend {
    fn add_breakpoint(&mut self, addr: u64) -> Result<()> {
        if self.breakpoints.contains_key(&addr) {
            return Ok(());
        }
        if self.exited {
            return Err(DebugError::NotRunning);
        }
        let mut orig = [0u8; 1];
        self.read_raw(addr, &mut orig)?;
        self.write_raw(addr, &[0xCC])?;
        self.breakpoints.insert(addr, orig[0]);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn remove_breakpoint(&mut self, addr: u64) -> Result<()> {
        if let Some(orig) = self.breakpoints.remove(&addr) {
            // Only restore if the target is alive; a dead process has no memory.
            if !self.exited {
                let _ = self.write_raw(addr, &[orig]);
            }
            if self.at_bp == Some(addr) {
                self.at_bp = None;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn poll(&mut self, timeout_ms: u32) -> Result<Event> {
        if self.pending_initial_stop && !self.exited {
            // The target is parked at its exec stop: report that first so the controller leaves
            // its start-up state and the user can set breakpoints before running.
            self.pending_initial_stop = false;
            self.running = false;
            return Ok(Event::Stopped(StopReason::Paused));
        }
        if self.exited || !self.running {
            return Ok(Event::Running);
        }
        let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_millis(u64::from(timeout_ms));
        loop {
            if let Some(ev) = self.sweep()? {
                return Ok(ev);
            }
            if self.exited || Instant::now() >= deadline {
                return Ok(Event::Running);
            }
            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(2));
        }
    }

    fn resume(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
        if self.exited {
            return Err(DebugError::NotRunning);
        }
        self.pending_initial_stop = false;
        let tid = self.current;
        if let Some(addr) = self.at_bp.take()
            && let Some(&orig) = self.breakpoints.get(&addr)
        {
            // Step the real instruction first; the step's completion re-plants the 0xCC and
            // continues (delivering any pending signal then).
            self.write_raw(addr, &[orig])?;
            self.step_over = Some((tid, addr));
            ptrace_resume(tid, true, 0)?;
        } else {
            let sig = self.pending_signal.remove(&tid).unwrap_or(0);
            ptrace_resume(tid, false, sig)?;
        }
        self.running = true;
        Ok(())
    }

    fn step(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
        if self.exited {
            return Err(DebugError::NotRunning);
        }
        self.pending_initial_stop = false;
        let tid = self.current;
        // If on a breakpoint, restore the real byte for this one instruction and re-plant after.
        if let Some(addr) = self.at_bp.take()
            && let Some(&orig) = self.breakpoints.get(&addr)
        {
            self.write_raw(addr, &[orig])?;
            self.step_over = Some((tid, addr));
        }
        self.user_step = Some(tid);
        let sig = self.pending_signal.remove(&tid).unwrap_or(0);
        ptrace_resume(tid, true, sig)?;
        self.running = true;
        Ok(())
    }

    fn request_pause(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
        if !self.exited && self.running {
            self.pause_requested = true;
            let _ = nix::sys::signal::kill(self.pid, Signal::SIGSTOP);
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn registers(&mut self) -> Result<Registers> {
        if self.exited {
            return Err(DebugError::NotRunning);
        }
        self.get_regs(self.current)
    }

    fn set_register(&mut self, name: &str, value: u64) -> Result<()> {
        if self.exited {
            return Err(DebugError::NotRunning);
        }
        let mut r = ptrace::getregs(self.current)?;
        match name {
            "rax" => r.rax = value,
            "rbx" => r.rbx = value,
            "rcx" => r.rcx = value,
            "rdx" => r.rdx = value,
            "rsi" => r.rsi = value,
            "rdi" => r.rdi = value,
            "rbp" => r.rbp = value,
            "rsp" => r.rsp = value,
            "r8" => r.r8 = value,
            "r9" => r.r9 = value,
            "r10" => r.r10 = value,
            "r11" => r.r11 = value,
            "r12" => r.r12 = value,
            "r13" => r.r13 = value,
            "r14" => r.r14 = value,
            "r15" => r.r15 = value,
            "rip" | "pc" => r.rip = value,
            "rflags" | "eflags" => r.eflags = value,
            _ => return Err(DebugError::Os(format!("unknown register {name}"))),
        }
        ptrace::setregs(self.current, r)?;
        if matches!(name, "rip" | "pc") && self.at_bp.is_some_and(|a| a != value) {
            // Moved off the breakpoint we were sitting on.
            self.at_bp = None;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn read_memory(&mut self, addr: u64, len: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
        let end = addr
            .checked_add(len as u64)
            .ok_or_else(|| DebugError::Os(format!("read {addr:#x}+{len:#x}: address overflow")))?;
        let mut bytes = vec![0u8; len];
        self.read_raw(addr, &mut bytes)?;
        // Show the real instructions, not our planted 0xCC bytes.
        for (&a, &orig) in &self.breakpoints {
            if a >= addr && a < end {
                bytes[(a - addr) as usize] = orig;
            }
        }
        Ok(bytes)
    }

    fn write_memory(&mut self, addr: u64, data: &[u8]) -> Result<()> {
        self.write_raw(addr, data)
    }

    fn modules(&self) -> Vec<Module> {
        let Ok(maps) = std::fs::read_to_string(format!("/proc/{}/maps", self.pid)) else {
            return Vec::new();
        };
        let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        for line in maps.lines() {
            // addr-range perms offset dev inode path
            let mut it = line.split_whitespace();
            let range = it.next().unwrap_or("");
            let path = it.nth(4).unwrap_or("");
            if path.is_empty() || path.starts_with('[') {
                continue;
            }
            if let Some(base) = range
                .split('-')
                .next()
                .and_then(|a| u64::from_str_radix(a, 16).ok())
                && seen.insert(path.to_string())
            {
                let name = path.rsplit('/').next().unwrap_or(path).to_string();
                out.push(Module { name, base });
            }
        }
        out
    }

    fn image_base(&self) -> Option<u64> {
        self.image_base
    }

    fn pid(&self) -> Option<u32> {
        Some(self.pid.as_raw() as u32)
    }

    fn kill(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
        if self.exited {
            return Ok(());
        }
        // SIGKILL works whether the tracee is running or ptrace-stopped (PTRACE_KILL does not
        // on a running tracee). Then reap every thread, bounded so a lost thread can't hang us.
        let _ = nix::sys::signal::kill(self.pid, Signal::SIGKILL);
        let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(2);
        'reap: while Instant::now() < deadline {
            // Threads we haven't seen a clone event for yet are still ours to reap.
            if let Ok(dir) = std::fs::read_dir(format!("/proc/{}/task", self.pid)) {
                for e in dir.flatten() {
                    if let Some(t) = e.file_name().to_str().and_then(|s| s.parse().ok()) {
                        let t = Pid::from_raw(t);
                        if !self.threads.contains(&t) {
                            self.threads.push(t);
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            // Non-leader threads first: the leader is only reported once they are reaped.
            let mut tids = self.threads.clone();
            tids.sort_by_key(|&t| t == self.pid);
            for tid in tids {
                match wait_raw(tid, true) {
                    Ok(Some(st)) if libc::WIFEXITED(st) || libc::WIFSIGNALED(st) => {
                        if tid == self.pid {
                            break 'reap;
                        }
                        self.threads.retain(|&t| t != tid);
                    }
                    Ok(_) => {}
                    Err(_) => {
                        if tid == self.pid {
                            break 'reap;
                        }
                        self.threads.retain(|&t| t != tid);
                    }
                }
            }
            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(2));
        }
        let _ = self.gone(-1);
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Drop for LinuxBackend {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let _ = self.kill();
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-debug/src/mock.rs`:

```rs
//! A fake target for tests and for platforms without a native back end. It "runs" a
//! scripted trace of addresses, so the controller's breakpoint, step and continue logic
//! can be tested deterministically on any OS.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashSet};

use crate::backend::{Backend, DebugError, Event, Module, Result, StopReason};
use crate::regs::Registers;

pub struct MockTarget {
    /// The instruction addresses the program executes, in order.
    trace: Vec<u64>,
    /// How far through `trace` we are.
    pc: usize,
    exit_code: i32,
    breakpoints: HashSet<u64>,
    memory: BTreeMap<u64, u8>,
    regs: Registers,
    running: bool,
    step_mode: bool,
    started: bool,
    exited: bool,
}

impl MockTarget {
    /// A target that will execute `trace` and then exit with `exit_code`.
    pub fn new(trace: Vec<u64>, exit_code: i32) -> Self {
        let rip = trace.first().copied().unwrap_or(0);
        Self {
            trace,
            pc: 0,
            exit_code,
            breakpoints: HashSet::new(),
            memory: BTreeMap::new(),
            regs: Registers {
                rip,
                rsp: 0x7000,
                ..Registers::default()
            },
            running: false,
            step_mode: false,
            started: false,
            exited: false,
        }
    }

    fn at_end(&self) -> bool {
        self.pc >= self.trace.len()
    }

    /// Advances one step of the trace, updating rip. Returns the new stop, if any.
    fn advance(&mut self, honor_breakpoints: bool) -> StopReason {
        loop {
            if self.at_end() {
                self.exited = true;
                return StopReason::Exited(self.exit_code);
            }
            self.pc += 1;
            if self.at_end() {
                self.exited = true;
                return StopReason::Exited(self.exit_code);
            }
            let addr = self.trace[self.pc];
            self.regs.rip = addr;
            // rax counts instructions executed, so tests can read a changing register.
            self.regs.rax = self.pc as u64;
            if honor_breakpoints && self.breakpoints.contains(&addr) {
                return StopReason::Breakpoint(addr);
            }
            if !honor_breakpoints {
                return StopReason::Step;
            }
        }
    }
}

impl Backend for MockTarget {
    fn add_breakpoint(&mut self, addr: u64) -> Result<()> {
        self.breakpoints.insert(addr);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn remove_breakpoint(&mut self, addr: u64) -> Result<()> {
        self.breakpoints.remove(&addr);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn poll(&mut self, _timeout_ms: u32) -> Result<Event> {
        if !self.started {
            // Like a real target that the loader leaves stopped at its entry.
            self.started = true;
            return Ok(Event::Stopped(StopReason::Step));
        }
        if !self.running {
            return Ok(Event::Running);
        }
        self.running = false;
        let reason = if self.step_mode {
            self.advance(false)
        } else {
            self.advance(true)
        };
        Ok(Event::Stopped(reason))
    }

    fn resume(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
        if self.exited {
            return Err(DebugError::NotRunning);
        }
        self.running = true;
        self.step_mode = false;
        Ok(())
    }

    fn step(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
        if self.exited {
            return Err(DebugError::NotRunning);
        }
        self.running = true;
        self.step_mode = true;
        Ok(())
    }

    fn request_pause(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }

    fn registers(&mut self) -> Result<Registers> {
        Ok(self.regs)
    }

    fn set_register(&mut self, name: &str, value: u64) -> Result<()> {
        if self.regs.set(name, value) {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(DebugError::Os(format!("no register named {name}")))
        }
    }

    fn read_memory(&mut self, addr: u64, len: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
        Ok((0..len as u64)
            .map(|i| self.memory.get(&(addr + i)).copied().unwrap_or(0))
            .collect())
    }

    fn write_memory(&mut self, addr: u64, data: &[u8]) -> Result<()> {
        for (i, b) in data.iter().enumerate() {
            self.memory.insert(addr + i as u64, *b);
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn modules(&self) -> Vec<Module> {
        vec![Module {
            name: "mock.exe".into(),
            base: 0x1000,
        }]
    }

    fn image_base(&self) -> Option<u64> {
        Some(0x1000)
    }

    fn kill(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
        self.exited = true;
        self.running = false;
        Ok(())
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-debug/src/procmem.rs`:

```rs
//! Reading a (possibly non-debugged) process's memory, for in-memory YARA scanning. Enumerates
//! the committed, readable regions of a process by PID and copies them out: on Windows via
//! `VirtualQueryEx` + `ReadProcessMemory`, on Linux via `/proc/<pid>/maps` + `/proc/<pid>/mem`;
//! other platforms return an error.

/// A snapshot of one readable memory region.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct MemRegion {
    pub base: u64,
    pub data: Vec<u8>,
}

/// One entry of a process's memory map (name includes `[heap]`, `[stack]` and file paths on Linux).
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct MapRegion {
    pub base: u64,
    pub size: u64,
    pub perms: String,
    pub name: String,
}

#[cfg(windows)]
pub fn read_all_memory(pid: u32, max_total: usize) -> Result<Vec<MemRegion>, String> {
    use core::ffi::c_void;

    use windows::Win32::Foundation::CloseHandle;
    use windows::Win32::System::Diagnostics::Debug::ReadProcessMemory;
    use windows::Win32::System::Memory::{
        MEM_COMMIT, MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION, PAGE_GUARD, PAGE_NOACCESS, VirtualQueryEx,
    };
    use windows::Win32::System::Threading::{
        OpenProcess, PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION, PROCESS_VM_READ,
    };

    // SAFETY: a standard OpenProcess for read access; fails cleanly on protected processes.
    let handle = unsafe { OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION | PROCESS_VM_READ, false, pid) }
        .map_err(|e| e.message())?;

    let mut regions = Vec::new();
    let mut total = 0usize;
    let mut addr: usize = 0;
    loop {
        let mut mbi = MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION::default();
        // SAFETY: `handle` is valid; `mbi` is a correctly-sized out buffer.
        let written = unsafe {
            VirtualQueryEx(
                handle,
                Some(addr as *const c_void),
                &mut mbi,
                std::mem::size_of::<MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION>(),
            )
        };
        if written == 0 {
            break;
        }
        let base = mbi.BaseAddress as usize;
        let size = mbi.RegionSize;
        let readable = mbi.State == MEM_COMMIT
            && (mbi.Protect.0 & PAGE_NOACCESS.0) == 0
            && (mbi.Protect.0 & PAGE_GUARD.0) == 0;
        if readable && size > 0 && total < max_total {
            let to_read = size.min(max_total - total);
            let mut buf = vec![0u8; to_read];
            let mut read = 0usize;
            // SAFETY: valid handle; `buf` has `to_read` bytes; `read` receives the count.
            let _ = unsafe {
                ReadProcessMemory(
                    handle,
                    base as *const c_void,
                    buf.as_mut_ptr() as *mut c_void,
                    to_read,
                    Some(&mut read),
                )
            };
            // A region with an unreadable tail fails with ERROR_PARTIAL_COPY yet still
            // copies the readable prefix: keep whatever was read.
            if read > 0 {
                buf.truncate(read);
                total += read;
                regions.push(MemRegion {
                    base: base as u64,
                    data: buf,
                });
            }
        }
        match base.checked_add(size) {
            Some(next) if next > addr => addr = next,
            _ => break,
        }
        if total >= max_total {
            break;
        }
    }
    // SAFETY: `handle` came from OpenProcess and is closed exactly once.
    unsafe {
        let _ = CloseHandle(handle);
    }
    Ok(regions)
}

/// Windows: enumerate committed regions (no file names; used only for parity — the glibc heap
/// view is Linux-only).
#[cfg(windows)]
pub fn memory_map(pid: u32) -> Result<Vec<MapRegion>, String> {
    use core::ffi::c_void;
    use windows::Win32::Foundation::CloseHandle;
    use windows::Win32::System::Memory::{MEM_COMMIT, MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION, VirtualQueryEx};
    use windows::Win32::System::Threading::{OpenProcess, PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION};

    // SAFETY: a standard query-only OpenProcess; fails cleanly on protected processes.
    let handle =
        unsafe { OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION, false, pid) }.map_err(|e| e.message())?;
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut addr: usize = 0;
    loop {
        let mut mbi = MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION::default();
        // SAFETY: `handle` is valid; `mbi` is a correctly-sized out buffer.
        let written = unsafe {
            VirtualQueryEx(
                handle,
                Some(addr as *const c_void),
                &mut mbi,
                std::mem::size_of::<MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION>(),
            )
        };
        if written == 0 {
            break;
        }
        let base = mbi.BaseAddress as u64;
        let size = mbi.RegionSize as u64;
        if mbi.State == MEM_COMMIT && size > 0 {
            out.push(MapRegion {
                base,
                size,
                perms: format!("{:#x}", mbi.Protect.0),
                name: String::new(),
            });
        }
        match (base as usize).checked_add(mbi.RegionSize) {
            Some(next) if next > addr => addr = next,
            _ => break,
        }
    }
    // SAFETY: `handle` came from OpenProcess and is closed exactly once.
    unsafe {
        let _ = CloseHandle(handle);
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// Windows: read `len` bytes at `addr` from process `pid`.
#[cfg(windows)]
pub fn read_mem(pid: u32, addr: u64, len: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    use core::ffi::c_void;
    use windows::Win32::Foundation::CloseHandle;
    use windows::Win32::System::Diagnostics::Debug::ReadProcessMemory;
    use windows::Win32::System::Threading::{OpenProcess, PROCESS_VM_READ};

    // SAFETY: a standard read-only OpenProcess.
    let handle = unsafe { OpenProcess(PROCESS_VM_READ, false, pid) }.map_err(|e| e.message())?;
    let mut buf = vec![0u8; len];
    let mut read = 0usize;
    // SAFETY: valid handle; `buf` has `len` bytes; `read` receives the count.
    let _ = unsafe {
        ReadProcessMemory(
            handle,
            addr as *const c_void,
            buf.as_mut_ptr() as *mut c_void,
            len,
            Some(&mut read),
        )
    };
    // SAFETY: handle closed exactly once.
    unsafe {
        let _ = CloseHandle(handle);
    }
    buf.truncate(read);
    Ok(buf)
}

/// Linux: the process's memory map from `/proc/<pid>/maps`, including `[heap]` and file paths.
#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
pub fn memory_map(pid: u32) -> Result<Vec<MapRegion>, String> {
    let maps = std::fs::read_to_string(format!("/proc/{pid}/maps"))
        .map_err(|e| format!("/proc/{pid}/maps: {e}"))?;
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for line in maps.lines() {
        let mut it = line.split_whitespace();
        let (Some(range), Some(perms)) = (it.next(), it.next()) else {
            continue;
        };
        // After perms: offset, dev, inode, then the optional path.
        let name = it.nth(3).unwrap_or("").to_string();
        let Some((start, end)) = range.split_once('-').and_then(|(s, e)| {
            Some((
                u64::from_str_radix(s, 16).ok()?,
                u64::from_str_radix(e, 16).ok()?,
            ))
        }) else {
            continue;
        };
        out.push(MapRegion {
            base: start,
            size: end.saturating_sub(start),
            perms: perms.to_string(),
            name,
        });
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// Linux: read `len` bytes at `addr` from `/proc/<pid>/mem` (chunked; returns the readable prefix).
#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
pub fn read_mem(pid: u32, addr: u64, len: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    use std::os::unix::fs::FileExt;
    let mem = std::fs::File::open(format!("/proc/{pid}/mem"))
        .map_err(|e| format!("/proc/{pid}/mem: {e}"))?;
    let mut buf = vec![0u8; len];
    let mut got = 0usize;
    while got < len {
        let chunk = (len - got).min(1 << 20);
        match mem.read_at(&mut buf[got..got + chunk], addr + got as u64) {
            Ok(0) | Err(_) => break,
            Ok(n) => got += n,
        }
    }
    buf.truncate(got);
    Ok(buf)
}

/// Linux: walk `/proc/<pid>/maps` and copy each readable mapping out of `/proc/<pid>/mem`.
/// Needs ptrace-read access to the process (same user, and Yama's `ptrace_scope` permitting).
#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
pub fn read_all_memory(pid: u32, max_total: usize) -> Result<Vec<MemRegion>, String> {
    use std::os::unix::fs::FileExt;

    let maps = std::fs::read_to_string(format!("/proc/{pid}/maps"))
        .map_err(|e| format!("/proc/{pid}/maps: {e}"))?;
    let mem = std::fs::File::open(format!("/proc/{pid}/mem"))
        .map_err(|e| format!("/proc/{pid}/mem: {e}"))?;

    let mut regions = Vec::new();
    let mut total = 0usize;
    for line in maps.lines() {
        if total >= max_total {
            break;
        }
        // start-end perms offset dev inode [path]
        let mut it = line.split_whitespace();
        let (Some(range), Some(perms)) = (it.next(), it.next()) else {
            continue;
        };
        let path = it.nth(3).unwrap_or("");
        // Unreadable, or a kernel page that can't be read through /proc/<pid>/mem.
        if !perms.starts_with('r') || path == "[vvar]" || path == "[vsyscall]" {
            continue;
        }
        let Some((start, end)) = range.split_once('-').and_then(|(s, e)| {
            Some((
                u64::from_str_radix(s, 16).ok()?,
                u64::from_str_radix(e, 16).ok()?,
            ))
        }) else {
            continue;
        };
        let size = usize::try_from(end.saturating_sub(start)).unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
        let to_read = size.min(max_total - total);
        if to_read == 0 {
            continue;
        }
        // Read in chunks so an unreadable page part-way through keeps the prefix.
        let mut buf = vec![0u8; to_read];
        let mut got = 0usize;
        while got < to_read {
            let chunk = (to_read - got).min(1 << 20);
            match mem.read_at(&mut buf[got..got + chunk], start + got as u64) {
                Ok(0) | Err(_) => break,
                Ok(n) => got += n,
            }
        }
        if got > 0 {
            buf.truncate(got);
            total += got;
            regions.push(MemRegion {
                base: start,
                data: buf,
            });
        }
    }
    Ok(regions)
}

#[cfg(not(any(windows, target_os = "linux")))]
pub fn read_all_memory(_pid: u32, _max_total: usize) -> Result<Vec<MemRegion>, String> {
    Err("reading process memory is only implemented on Windows and Linux".into())
}

    Err("reading process memory is only implemented on Windows and Linux".into())
}

#[cfg(all(test, any(windows, target_os = "linux")))]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn reads_own_memory_and_finds_a_marker() {
        // A unique marker on the heap (committed, readable) — we should read it back.
        let marker: &[u8] = b"ORRESS_PROCMEM_MARKER_7a3f91";
        let held: Vec<u8> = marker.to_vec();
        std::hint::black_box(&held);

        let regions = read_all_memory(std::process::id(), 512 * 1024 * 1024).unwrap();
        assert!(!regions.is_empty(), "should read some committed regions");
        let found = regions
            .iter()
            .any(|r| r.data.windows(marker.len()).any(|w| w == marker));
        assert!(found, "should find our marker in our own memory");
        std::hint::black_box(&held);
    }
}
```

```rs
//! The x86-64 register set as the debugger reports it, plus plain-language flag meanings
//! so beginners can read the processor state.

/// The general-purpose registers, instruction pointer and flags of a stopped thread.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Registers {
    pub rax: u64,
    pub rbx: u64,
    pub rcx: u64,
    pub rdx: u64,
    pub rsi: u64,
    pub rdi: u64,
    pub rbp: u64,

    pub r13: u64,

    pub r15: u64,
    pub rip: u64,

}

/// The 16 general-purpose registers in the usual display order, with their names.
pub const GP_NAMES: [&str; 16] = [
    "rax", "rbx", "rcx", "rdx", "rsi", "rdi", "rbp", "rsp", "r8", "r9", "r10", "r11", "r12", "r13",
    "r14", "r15",

            ("r14", self.r14),
            ("r15", self.r15),
        ]
    }

    /// Reads a general-purpose register by name (lower-case), plus `rip`/`rsp`/`rbp`.
    pub fn get(&self, name: &str) -> Option<u64> {
        Some(match name {
            "rax" => self.rax,
            "rbx" => self.rbx,
            "rcx" => self.rcx,
            "rdx" => self.rdx,
            "rsi" => self.rsi,
            "rdi" => self.rdi,
            "rbp" => self.rbp,
            "rsp" => self.rsp,
            "r8" => self.r8,
            "r9" => self.r9,
            "r10" => self.r10,
            "r11" => self.r11,
            "r12" => self.r12,
            "r13" => self.r13,
            "r14" => self.r14,
            "r15" => self.r15,
            "rip" | "pc" => self.rip,
            "rflags" | "eflags" => self.rflags,
            _ => return None,
        })
    }

    /// Writes a general-purpose register by name. Returns false for an unknown name.
    pub fn set(&mut self, name: &str, value: u64) -> bool {
        match name {
            "rax" => self.rax = value,
            "rbx" => self.rbx = value,
            "rcx" => self.rcx = value,
            "rdx" => self.rdx = value,
            "rsi" => self.rsi = value,
            "rdi" => self.rdi = value,
            "rbp" => self.rbp = value,
            "rsp" => self.rsp = value,
            "r8" => self.r8 = value,
            "r9" => self.r9 = value,
            "r10" => self.r10 = value,
            "r11" => self.r11 = value,
            "r12" => self.r12 = value,
            "r13" => self.r13 = value,
            "r14" => self.r14 = value,
            "r15" => self.r15 = value,
            "rip" | "pc" => self.rip = value,
            "rflags" | "eflags" => self.rflags = value,
            _ => return false,
        }
        true
    }
}

/// One CPU status flag with its bit, short name and meaning.
pub struct FlagInfo {
    pub bit: u32,
    pub short: &'static str,
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub meaning: &'static str,
}

/// The status flags ORRESS shows, most useful first.
pub const FLAGS: [FlagInfo; 7] = [
    FlagInfo {
        bit: 0,
        short: "CF",
        name: "Carry",
        meaning: "unsigned overflow or borrow (after a compare: the first value was smaller, unsigned)",
    },
    FlagInfo {
        bit: 6,
        short: "ZF",
        name: "Zero",
        meaning: "the result was zero (after a compare: the two values were equal)",
    },
    FlagInfo {
        bit: 7,
        short: "SF",
        name: "Sign",
        meaning: "the result was negative (its top bit is set)",
    },
    FlagInfo {
        bit: 11,
        short: "OF",
        name: "Overflow",
        meaning: "signed overflow: the result did not fit as a signed number",
    },
    FlagInfo {
        bit: 2,
        short: "PF",
        name: "Parity",
        meaning: "the low byte has an even number of set bits",
    },
    FlagInfo {
        bit: 10,
        short: "DF",
        name: "Direction",
        meaning: "string instructions step backwards when set",
    },
    FlagInfo {
        bit: 8,
        short: "TF",
        name: "Trap",
        meaning: "single-step mode: the CPU traps after each instruction (the debugger uses this to step)",
    },

/// Whether a flag bit is set in `rflags`.
pub fn flag_set(rflags: u64, bit: u32) -> bool {
    (rflags >> bit) & 1 == 1
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn get_set_roundtrip() {
        let mut r = Registers::default();
        for name in GP_NAMES {
            assert!(r.set(name, 0x1234));
            assert_eq!(r.get(name), Some(0x1234));
        }
        assert!(r.set("rip", 0x4000));
        assert_eq!(r.get("rip"), Some(0x4000));
        assert_eq!(r.get("nope"), None);
        assert!(!r.set("nope", 1));
    }

    #[test]
    fn flags_decode() {
        // ZF (bit 6) and CF (bit 0) set.
        let f = (1 << 6) | 1;
        assert!(flag_set(f, 0));
        assert!(flag_set(f, 6));
        assert!(!flag_set(f, 7));
    }
}
```
