`crates/orress-decompiler/src/arm64.rs`:

```rs
//! Lifting ARM64 (AArch64) machine code into the shared decompiler IR.
//!
//! The x86 and ARM64 front ends produce the same [`Block`]/[`Stmt`]/[`Expr`] IR, so the
//! simplify → structure → types → print pipeline is entirely shared. Registers map to
//! `Var::Reg(n)`: `x0`..`x30` are 0..30, and `x0` (register 0) is the result register, which the
//! pipeline already treats as the return value (like x86's `rax`). The zero register `xzr`/`wzr`
//! becomes a constant `0`; the stack pointer and `[sp, #off]` slots become `Var::Stack`.

use std::collections::{HashMap, VecDeque};

use orress_analysis::{EdgeKind, Function, Program};
use yaxpeax_arch::{Decoder, U8Reader};
use yaxpeax_arm::armv8::a64::{
    InstDecoder, Instruction, Opcode, Operand, SIMDSizeCode, ShiftStyle, SizeCode,
};

use crate::ir::*;
use crate::lift::{Convention, import_noreturn, import_params};

/// What the last flag-setting instruction (`cmp`/`subs`/`adds`/`ands`/`tst`) computed.
#[derive(Clone)]
enum Flags {
    /// `cmp`/`subs`: the comparison `a` vs `b`.
    Sub(Expr, Expr),
    /// `tst`/`ands` with a discarded result: the bitwise `a & b`.
    Test(Expr, Expr),
    /// Any other result whose sign/zero a condition may read.
    Result(Expr),
    /// `fcmp`: a floating-point comparison `a` vs `b`.
    FSub(Expr, Expr),
}

struct State {
    flags: Option<Flags>,
    /// Argument registers written since the last call (to count a call's arguments).
    written: Vec<u8>,
}

pub struct Arm64Lifter<'a> {
    pub program: &'a Program,
    pub param_counts: &'a HashMap<u64, usize>,
}

fn wsz(sz: SizeCode) -> Width {
    match sz {
        SizeCode::X => Width::B64,
        SizeCode::W => Width::B32,
    }
}

impl Arm64Lifter<'_> {
    fn decode(&self, addr: u64) -> Option<Instruction> {
        let bytes = self.program.memory.read(addr, 4)?;
        let mut reader = U8Reader::new(bytes.get(..4)?);
        InstDecoder::default().decode(&mut reader).ok()
    }

    /// Lifts every block of `f`.
    pub fn lift(&self, f: &Function) -> Vec<Block> {
        let mut out: HashMap<u64, Block> = HashMap::new();
        let mut queue: VecDeque<usize> = VecDeque::from([0]);
        let mut seen = vec![false; f.blocks.len()];
        // Walk in reachable order so an argument-written set carries across fall-through.
        for (i, b) in f.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
            if b.start == f.entry {
                queue.clear();
                queue.push_back(i);
                break;
            }
        }
        while let Some(index) = queue.pop_front() {
            if seen[index] {
                continue;
            }
            seen[index] = true;
            let block = self.lift_block(f, index);
            for e in &f.blocks[index].succs {
                if let Some(j) = f.blocks.iter().position(|b| b.start == e.target) {
                    queue.push_back(j);
                }
            }
            out.insert(f.blocks[index].start, block);
        }
        for (i, b) in f.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
            out.entry(b.start).or_insert_with(|| self.lift_block(f, i));
        }
        let mut blocks: Vec<Block> = out.into_values().collect();
        blocks.sort_by_key(|b| b.addr);
        blocks
    }

    fn lift_block(&self, f: &Function, index: usize) -> Block {
        let fb = &f.blocks[index];
        let mut st = State {
            flags: None,
            written: Vec::new(),
        };
        let mut stmts = Vec::new();
        let mut term = None;
        let mut term_addr = fb.start;
        for &addr in &fb.insns {
            let Some(ins) = self.decode(addr) else {
                stmts.push((addr, Stmt::Asm("(undecodable)".into(), Vec::new())));
                continue;
            };
            term_addr = addr;
            if let Some(t) = self.lift_insn(&ins, addr, &mut st, &mut stmts) {
                term = Some(t);
            }
        }
        let term = term.unwrap_or_else(|| {
            match fb
                .succs
                .iter()
                .find(|e| matches!(e.kind, EdgeKind::FallThrough | EdgeKind::Jump))
            {
                Some(e) => Term::Jump(e.target),
                None => Term::Stop,
            }
        });
        Block {
            addr: fb.start,
            stmts,
            term,
            term_addr,
        }
    }

    /// A source operand as an expression.
    fn val(&self, op: &Operand) -> Expr {
        match op {
            Operand::Register(sz, 31) => Expr::konst(0, wsz(*sz)),
            Operand::Register(sz, n) => Expr::Var(Var::Reg(*n as u8), wsz(*sz)),
            Operand::RegisterOrSP(_, 31) => Expr::StackAddr(0),
            Operand::RegisterOrSP(sz, n) => Expr::Var(Var::Reg(*n as u8), wsz(*sz)),
            Operand::Immediate(i) => Expr::konst(u64::from(*i), Width::B64),
            Operand::Imm64(i) => Expr::konst(*i, Width::B64),
            Operand::Imm16(i) => Expr::konst(u64::from(*i), Width::B64),
            Operand::ImmShift(base, sh) => Expr::konst(u64::from(*base) << sh, Width::B64),
            Operand::RegShift(style, amt, sz, n) => {
                let r = if *n == 31 {
                    Expr::konst(0, wsz(*sz))
                } else {
                    Expr::Var(Var::Reg(*n as u8), wsz(*sz))
                };
                shift_expr(*style, u32::from(*amt), r, wsz(*sz))
            }
            _ => Expr::Unknown("op".into()),
        }
    }

    /// The destination register of operand 0, unless it is the zero register (then the result is
    /// discarded, which for the `*s` forms means a flag-only compare).
    fn dest(op: &Operand) -> Option<(Var, Width)> {
        match op {
            Operand::Register(sz, n) | Operand::RegisterOrSP(sz, n) if *n != 31 => {
                Some((Var::Reg(*n as u8), wsz(*sz)))
            }
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// Writes `value` to a destination register (a 32-bit `w` write narrows, matching the
    /// zero-extend-to-64 hardware semantics the rest of the IR already assumes).
    fn write(dst: (Var, Width), value: Expr, addr: u64, out: &mut Vec<(u64, Stmt)>) {
        let (v, w) = dst;
        let value = if value.width() > w {
            Expr::Cast(Box::new(value), w, false)
        } else {
            value
        };
        out.push((addr, Stmt::Assign(v, value)));
    }

    /// A data-processing `Rd = Rn OP op2` (operands Rd, Rn, op2).
    fn dp(&self, ins: &Instruction, op: BinOp, addr: u64, out: &mut Vec<(u64, Stmt)>) {
        let Some(dst) = Self::dest(&ins.operands[0]) else {
            return;
        };
        let w = dst.1;
        let a = self.val(&ins.operands[1]);
        let b = self.val(&ins.operands[2]);
        Self::write(dst, Expr::bin(op, a, b, w), addr, out);
    }

    /// A bitwise op whose second source is complemented (`bic`/`orn`/`eon`): `Rd = Rn OP !op2`.
    fn dp_not(&self, ins: &Instruction, op: BinOp, addr: u64, out: &mut Vec<(u64, Stmt)>) {
        let Some(dst) = Self::dest(&ins.operands[0]) else {
            return;
        };
        let w = dst.1;
        let a = self.val(&ins.operands[1]);
        let b = Expr::Not(Box::new(self.val(&ins.operands[2])), w);
        Self::write(dst, Expr::bin(op, a, b, w), addr, out);
    }

    /// A flag-setting data-processing op (`adds`/`subs`/`ands`). With a `zr` destination it is a
    /// `cmp`/`cmn`/`tst` that only sets the flags.
    fn dp_flags(
        &self,
        ins: &Instruction,
        op: BinOp,
        addr: u64,
        st: &mut State,
        out: &mut Vec<(u64, Stmt)>,
    ) {
        let a = self.val(&ins.operands[1]);
        let b = self.val(&ins.operands[2]);
        match Self::dest(&ins.operands[0]) {
            Some(dst) => {
                let w = dst.1;
                Self::write(dst, Expr::bin(op, a, b, w), addr, out);
                // The flags reflect the stored result, so a following `b.ne` reads `dst != 0`
                // (this is what a `subs`/`b.ne` loop counter decrements to zero).
                st.flags = Some(Flags::Result(Expr::Var(dst.0, w)));
            }
            None => {
                st.flags = Some(match op {
                    BinOp::Sub => Flags::Sub(a, b),
                    BinOp::And => Flags::Test(a, b),
                    _ => Flags::Result(Expr::bin(op, a, b, Width::B64)),
                });
            }
        }
    }

    fn lift_insn(
        &self,
        ins: &Instruction,
        addr: u64,
        st: &mut State,
        out: &mut Vec<(u64, Stmt)>,
    ) -> Option<Term> {
        use Opcode as O;
        // Record a write to an argument register, for counting an unknown call's arguments.
        if let Some((Var::Reg(r), _)) = Self::dest(&ins.operands[0])
            && r < 8
        {
            st.written.push(r);
        }
        if self.lift_fp(ins, addr, st, out) {
            return None;
        }
        match ins.opcode {
            // Pointer-authentication and branch-target hints: no effect on the recovered logic.
            O::HINT
            | O::PACIASP
            | O::PACIBSP
            | O::AUTIASP
            | O::AUTIBSP
            | O::PACIAZ
            | O::PACIBZ
            | O::AUTIAZ
            | O::AUTIBZ
            | O::PACIA
            | O::PACIB
            | O::AUTIA
            | O::AUTIB
            | O::PACM
            | O::XPACLRI => {}
            O::ADD => self.dp(ins, BinOp::Add, addr, out),
            O::SUB => self.dp(ins, BinOp::Sub, addr, out),
            O::AND => self.dp(ins, BinOp::And, addr, out),
            O::ORR => self.dp(ins, BinOp::Or, addr, out),
            O::EOR => self.dp(ins, BinOp::Xor, addr, out),
            O::BIC => self.dp_not(ins, BinOp::And, addr, out),
            O::ORN => self.dp_not(ins, BinOp::Or, addr, out),
            O::EON => self.dp_not(ins, BinOp::Xor, addr, out),
            O::ADDS => self.dp_flags(ins, BinOp::Add, addr, st, out),
            O::SUBS => self.dp_flags(ins, BinOp::Sub, addr, st, out),
            O::ANDS => self.dp_flags(ins, BinOp::And, addr, st, out),
            O::BICS => {
                // `Rd = Rn & !op2`, setting flags.
                if let Some(dst) = Self::dest(&ins.operands[0]) {
                    let w = dst.1;
                    let a = self.val(&ins.operands[1]);
                    let b = Expr::Not(Box::new(self.val(&ins.operands[2])), w);
                    Self::write(dst, Expr::bin(BinOp::And, a, b, w), addr, out);
                }
                st.flags = None;
            }
            O::NEG => {
                if let Some(dst) = Self::dest(&ins.operands[0]) {
                    let w = dst.1;
                    Self::write(
                        dst,
                        Expr::Neg(Box::new(self.val(&ins.operands[1])), w),
                        addr,
                        out,
                    );
                }
            }
            O::MUL => self.dp(ins, BinOp::Mul, addr, out),
            O::MADD | O::MSUB => {
                // Rd = Ra ± (Rn * Rm); `mul` is `madd` with a zero addend.
                if let Some(dst) = Self::dest(&ins.operands[0]) {
                    let w = dst.1;
                    let n = self.val(&ins.operands[1]);
                    let m = self.val(&ins.operands[2]);
                    let prod = Expr::bin(BinOp::Mul, n, m, w);
                    let value = if matches!(ins.operands[3], Operand::Register(_, 31)) {
                        prod
                    } else {
                        let a = self.val(&ins.operands[3]);
                        let op = if ins.opcode == O::MADD {
                            BinOp::Add
                        } else {
                            BinOp::Sub
                        };
                        Expr::bin(op, a, prod, w)
                    };
                    Self::write(dst, value, addr, out);
                }
            }
            O::SDIV | O::UDIV => {
                if let Some(dst) = Self::dest(&ins.operands[0]) {
                    let w = dst.1;
                    let (mut a, mut b) = (self.val(&ins.operands[1]), self.val(&ins.operands[2]));
                    if ins.opcode == O::SDIV {
                        a = Expr::Cast(Box::new(a), w, true);
                        b = Expr::Cast(Box::new(b), w, true);
                    }
                    Self::write(dst, Expr::bin(BinOp::Div, a, b, w), addr, out);
                }
            }
            O::LSLV | O::LSRV | O::ASRV => {
                if let Some(dst) = Self::dest(&ins.operands[0]) {
                    let w = dst.1;
                    let op = match ins.opcode {
                        O::LSLV => BinOp::Shl,
                        O::LSRV => BinOp::Shr,
                        _ => BinOp::Sar,
                    };
                    let a = self.val(&ins.operands[1]);
                    let b = self.val(&ins.operands[2]);
                    Self::write(dst, Expr::bin(op, a, b, w), addr, out);
                }
            }
            O::RORV => {
                if let Some(dst) = Self::dest(&ins.operands[0]) {
                    let w = dst.1;
                    let a = self.val(&ins.operands[1]);
                    let b = self.val(&ins.operands[2]);
                    Self::write(dst, Expr::method(a, "rotate_right", vec![b], w), addr, out);
                }
            }
            O::UBFM | O::SBFM => return self.bitfield(ins, addr, out),
            O::MOVZ => {
                if let Some(dst) = Self::dest(&ins.operands[0]) {
                    let w = dst.1;
                    Self::write(dst, self.val(&ins.operands[1]), addr, out);
                    let _ = w;
                }
            }
            O::MOVN => {
                if let Some(dst) = Self::dest(&ins.operands[0]) {
                    let w = dst.1;
                    Self::write(
                        dst,
                        Expr::Not(Box::new(self.val(&ins.operands[1])), w),
                        addr,
                        out,
                    );
                }
            }
            O::MOVK => {
                // Insert a 16-bit field, keeping the rest: `Rd = (Rd & !mask) | (imm << s)`.
                if let (Some(dst), Operand::ImmShift(base, sh)) =
                    (Self::dest(&ins.operands[0]), &ins.operands[1])
                {
                    let w = dst.1;
                    let mask = !(0xffffu64 << sh);
                    let kept = Expr::bin(BinOp::And, Expr::Var(dst.0, w), Expr::konst(mask, w), w);
                    let ins_val = Expr::konst(u64::from(*base) << sh, w);
                    Self::write(dst, Expr::bin(BinOp::Or, kept, ins_val, w), addr, out);
                }
            }
            O::CSEL | O::CSINC | O::CSINV | O::CSNEG => return self.csel(ins, addr, out, st),
            O::LDR | O::LDRB | O::LDRH | O::LDRSW | O::LDRSB | O::LDRSH => {
                self.load(ins, addr, out)
            }
            O::STR | O::STRB | O::STRH => self.store(ins, addr, out),
            O::STP | O::LDP => self.pair(ins, addr, out),
            O::ADRP => {
                if let (Some(dst), Some(t)) =
                    (Self::dest(&ins.operands[0]), self.pc_target(ins, addr))
                {
                    out.push((addr, Stmt::Assign(dst.0, Expr::Addr(t & !0xfff))));
                }
            }
            O::ADR => {
                if let (Some(dst), Some(t)) =
                    (Self::dest(&ins.operands[0]), self.pc_target(ins, addr))
                {
                    out.push((addr, Stmt::Assign(dst.0, Expr::Addr(t))));
                }
            }
            O::B => {
                return Some(match self.pc_target(ins, addr) {
                    Some(t) if self.program.functions.contains_key(&t) => {
                        Term::TailCall(Expr::Call(CallTarget::Direct(t), Vec::new()))
                    }
                    Some(t) => Term::Jump(t),
                    None => Term::Stop,
                });
            }
            O::Bcc(c) => {
                let next = addr + 4;
                let t = self.pc_target(ins, addr).unwrap_or(next);
                return Some(Term::Branch(self.condition(c, st), t, next));
            }
            O::CBZ | O::CBNZ => {
                let next = addr + 4;
                let t = self.pc_target(ins, addr).unwrap_or(next);
                let v = self.val(&ins.operands[0]);
                let op = if ins.opcode == O::CBZ {
                    CmpOp::Eq
                } else {
                    CmpOp::Ne
                };
                return Some(Term::Branch(
                    Expr::cmp(op, v, Expr::konst(0, Width::B64), false),
                    t,
                    next,
                ));
            }
            O::TBZ | O::TBNZ => {
                let next = addr + 4;
                let t = self.pc_target(ins, addr).unwrap_or(next);
                let v = self.val(&ins.operands[0]);
                let bit = self.val(&ins.operands[1]);
                let w = v.width();
                let test = Expr::bin(
                    BinOp::And,
                    Expr::bin(BinOp::Shr, v, bit, w),
                    Expr::konst(1, w),
                    w,
                );
                let op = if ins.opcode == O::TBZ {
                    CmpOp::Eq
                } else {
                    CmpOp::Ne
                };
                return Some(Term::Branch(
                    Expr::cmp(op, test, Expr::konst(0, w), false),
                    t,
                    next,
                ));
            }
            O::BL => {
                return self.call(
                    ins,
                    addr,
                    self.pc_target(ins, addr).map(CallTarget::Direct),
                    st,
                    out,
                );
            }
            // PAC (pointer-authenticated) forms behave like their plain counterparts.
            O::BLR | O::BLRAA | O::BLRAAZ | O::BLRAB | O::BLRABZ => {
                let t = CallTarget::Indirect(Box::new(self.val(&ins.operands[0])));
                return self.call(ins, addr, Some(t), st, out);
            }
            O::RET
            | O::RETAA
            | O::RETAB
            | O::RETAASPPC
            | O::RETABSPPC
            | O::RETAASPPCR
            | O::RETABSPPCR
            | O::ERET
            | O::ERETAA
            | O::ERETAB => {
                return Some(Term::Return(Some(Expr::Var(Var::Reg(0), Width::B64))));
            }
            O::BR | O::BRAA | O::BRAAZ | O::BRAB | O::BRABZ => {
                return Some(Term::TailCall(Expr::Call(
                    CallTarget::Indirect(Box::new(self.val(&ins.operands[0]))),
                    Vec::new(),
                )));
            }
            O::BRK | O::HLT | O::UDF => return Some(Term::Stop),
            _ => {
                out.push((addr, Stmt::Asm(ins.to_string(), Vec::new())));
                st.flags = None;
            }
        }
        None
    }

    /// `UBFM`/`SBFM` cover the shift/extend aliases. The common `lsl`/`lsr`/`asr` immediates and
    /// `uxt*`/`sxt*` extends are recovered; a general bitfield move stays `asm!`.
    fn bitfield(&self, ins: &Instruction, addr: u64, out: &mut Vec<(u64, Stmt)>) -> Option<Term> {
        let dst = Self::dest(&ins.operands[0])?;
        let w = dst.1;
        let bits = u32::from(w.0) * 8;
        let rn = self.val(&ins.operands[1]);
        let imm = |o: &Operand| match o {
            Operand::Immediate(i) => Some(*i),
            Operand::Imm16(i) => Some(u32::from(*i)),
            _ => None,
        };
        let (Some(immr), Some(imms)) = (imm(&ins.operands[2]), imm(&ins.operands[3])) else {
            out.push((addr, Stmt::Asm(ins.to_string(), Vec::new())));
            return None;
        };
        let signed = ins.opcode == Opcode::SBFM;
        let value = if imms >= immr {
            if signed && immr == 0 && matches!(imms, 7 | 15 | 31) {
                // sxtb / sxth / sxtw: sign-extend the low (imms+1) bits.
                let small = Width(((imms + 1) / 8) as u8);
                Expr::Cast(
                    Box::new(Expr::Cast(Box::new(rn), small, true)),
                    Width::B64,
                    true,
                )
            } else if signed && imms == bits - 1 {
                // asr #immr.
                Expr::bin(BinOp::Sar, rn, Expr::konst(u64::from(immr), w), w)
            } else if !signed && immr == 0 && matches!(imms, 7 | 15) {
                // uxtb / uxth.
                Expr::Cast(Box::new(rn), Width(((imms + 1) / 8) as u8), false)
            } else if !signed {
                // lsr / ubfx: (Rn >> immr) & mask(imms-immr+1).
                let width = imms - immr + 1;
                let shifted = if immr > 0 {
                    Expr::bin(BinOp::Shr, rn, Expr::konst(u64::from(immr), w), w)
                } else {
                    rn
                };
                if width < bits {
                    Expr::bin(BinOp::And, shifted, Expr::konst((1u64 << width) - 1, w), w)
                } else {
                    shifted
                }
            } else {
                out.push((addr, Stmt::Asm(ins.to_string(), Vec::new())));
                return None;
            }
        } else {
            // lsl #(bits - immr).
            Expr::bin(BinOp::Shl, rn, Expr::konst(u64::from(bits - immr), w), w)
        };
        Self::write(dst, value, addr, out);
        None
    }

    /// `csel`/`cset`/`csinc`/`csinv`/`csneg`: `Rd = cond ? Rn : else(Rm)`.
    fn csel(
        &self,
        ins: &Instruction,
        addr: u64,
        out: &mut Vec<(u64, Stmt)>,
        st: &State,
    ) -> Option<Term> {
        let dst = Self::dest(&ins.operands[0])?;
        let w = dst.1;
        let n = self.val(&ins.operands[1]);
        let m = self.val(&ins.operands[2]);
        let cond = ins.operands.iter().find_map(|o| match o {
            Operand::ConditionCode(c) => Some(self.condition(*c, st)),
            _ => None,
        });
        let cond = cond?;
        let other = match ins.opcode {
            Opcode::CSINC => Expr::bin(BinOp::Add, m, Expr::konst(1, w), w),
            Opcode::CSINV => Expr::Not(Box::new(m), w),
            Opcode::CSNEG => Expr::Neg(Box::new(m), w),
            _ => m,
        };
        Self::write(
            dst,
            Expr::Select(Box::new(cond), Box::new(n), Box::new(other), w),
            addr,
            out,
        );
        None
    }

    fn load(&self, ins: &Instruction, addr: u64, out: &mut Vec<(u64, Stmt)>) {
        // A floating-point load (`ldr d0, [x0]`) targets a NEON register.
        if let Some(fd) = Self::fdest(&ins.operands[0])
            && ins.opcode == Opcode::LDR
        {
            if let Some(mem) = self.mem(&ins.operands[1]) {
                let value = match mem {
                    Mem::Stack(slot) => Expr::Var(Var::Stack(slot), fd.1),
                    Mem::Addr(a) => Expr::Load(Box::new(a), fd.1),
                };
                out.push((addr, Stmt::Assign(fd.0, value)));
                Self::writeback(&ins.operands[1], addr, out);
            } else {
                out.push((addr, Stmt::Asm(ins.to_string(), Vec::new())));
            }
            return;
        }
        let Some(dst) = Self::dest(&ins.operands[0]) else {
            return;
        };
        let rt_w = dst.1;
        let (w, signed) = match ins.opcode {
            Opcode::LDRB => (Width::B8, false),
            Opcode::LDRH => (Width::B16, false),
            Opcode::LDRSB => (Width::B8, true),
            Opcode::LDRSH => (Width::B16, true),
            Opcode::LDRSW => (Width::B32, true),
            _ => (rt_w, false),
        };
        let Some(mem) = self.mem(&ins.operands[1]) else {
            out.push((addr, Stmt::Asm(ins.to_string(), Vec::new())));
            return;
        };
        let mut value = match mem {
            Mem::Stack(slot) => Expr::Var(Var::Stack(slot), w),
            Mem::Addr(a) => Expr::Load(Box::new(a), w),
        };
        if signed {
            // Sign-extend to the DESTINATION width (B32 for a W-form load, B64 for X), then let
            // `write` apply register-write semantics (a W write zeros the upper 32 bits).
            // Previously this always extended to B64, so `ldrsb w0,..` wrongly filled x0's top half.
            value = Expr::Cast(Box::new(value), rt_w, true);
        }
        Self::write(dst, value, addr, out);
        Self::writeback(&ins.operands[1], addr, out);
    }

    /// A pre-/post-indexed addressing mode writes the adjusted address back to the base register
    /// (`x8 += 4` after `ldr w0, [x8], #4`), which is what advances a pointer-walking loop.
    fn writeback(op: &Operand, addr: u64, out: &mut Vec<(u64, Stmt)>) {
        let (base, delta) = match op {
            Operand::RegPreIndex(base, off, true) => (*base, i64::from(*off)),
            Operand::RegPostIndex(base, off) => (*base, i64::from(*off)),
            _ => return,
        };
        if base == 31 || delta == 0 {
            return;
        }
        let v = Var::Reg(base as u8);
        out.push((
            addr,
            Stmt::Assign(v, add_off(Expr::Var(v, Width::B64), delta)),
        ));
    }

    fn store(&self, ins: &Instruction, addr: u64, out: &mut Vec<(u64, Stmt)>) {
        // A floating-point store (`str d0, [x0]`) from a NEON register.
        if let Some(fd) = Self::fdest(&ins.operands[0])
            && ins.opcode == Opcode::STR
        {
            let v = Expr::Var(fd.0, fd.1);
            if let Some(mem) = self.mem(&ins.operands[1]) {
                match mem {
                    Mem::Stack(slot) => out.push((addr, Stmt::Assign(Var::Stack(slot), v))),
                    Mem::Addr(a) => out.push((addr, Stmt::Store(a, v, fd.1))),
                }
                Self::writeback(&ins.operands[1], addr, out);
            } else {
                out.push((addr, Stmt::Asm(ins.to_string(), Vec::new())));
            }
            return;
        }
        let w = match ins.opcode {
            Opcode::STRB => Width::B8,
            Opcode::STRH => Width::B16,
            _ => match &ins.operands[0] {
                Operand::Register(sz, _) => wsz(*sz),
                _ => Width::B64,
            },
        };
        let v = self.val(&ins.operands[0]);
        let v = if v.width() > w {
            Expr::Cast(Box::new(v), w, false)
        } else {
            v
        };
        let Some(mem) = self.mem(&ins.operands[1]) else {
            out.push((addr, Stmt::Asm(ins.to_string(), Vec::new())));
            return;
        };
        match mem {
            Mem::Stack(slot) => out.push((addr, Stmt::Assign(Var::Stack(slot), v))),
            Mem::Addr(a) => out.push((addr, Stmt::Store(a, v, w))),
        }
        Self::writeback(&ins.operands[1], addr, out);
    }

    /// `ldp`/`stp`. A save/restore of the frame pair (`x29`/`x30`) around `sp` is prologue
    /// bookkeeping; otherwise the pair becomes two loads/stores at consecutive slots.
    fn pair(&self, ins: &Instruction, addr: u64, out: &mut Vec<(u64, Stmt)>) {
        let regs: Vec<&Operand> = ins.operands[..2].iter().collect();
        if regs
            .iter()
            .all(|o| matches!(o, Operand::Register(_, 29 | 30)))
        {
            return;
        }
        let is_load = ins.opcode == Opcode::LDP;
        let Some(mem) = self.mem(&ins.operands[2]) else {
            out.push((addr, Stmt::Asm(ins.to_string(), Vec::new())));
            return;
        };
        let (base_slot, base_addr) = match mem {
            Mem::Stack(slot) => (Some(slot), None),
            Mem::Addr(a) => (None, Some(a)),
        };
        for (k, op) in ins.operands[..2].iter().enumerate() {
            let w = match op {
                Operand::Register(sz, _) => wsz(*sz),
                _ => Width::B64,
            };
            let off = (k as i64) * i64::from(w.0);
            if is_load {
                let Some((v, _)) = Self::dest(op) else {
                    continue;
                };
                let value = match (&base_slot, &base_addr) {
                    (Some(slot), _) => Expr::Var(Var::Stack(slot + off), w),
                    (_, Some(a)) => Expr::Load(Box::new(add_off(a.clone(), off)), w),
                    _ => continue,
                };
                out.push((addr, Stmt::Assign(v, value)));
            } else {
                let v = self.val(op);
                match (&base_slot, &base_addr) {
                    (Some(slot), _) => out.push((addr, Stmt::Assign(Var::Stack(slot + off), v))),
                    (_, Some(a)) => out.push((addr, Stmt::Store(add_off(a.clone(), off), v, w))),
                    _ => {}
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// A memory operand as either a stack slot or an address expression.
    fn mem(&self, op: &Operand) -> Option<Mem> {
        match op {
            Operand::RegPreIndex(31, off, _) => Some(Mem::Stack(i64::from(*off))),
            Operand::RegPreIndex(base, off, _) => Some(Mem::Addr(add_off(
                Expr::Var(Var::Reg(*base as u8), Width::B64),
                i64::from(*off),
            ))),
            Operand::RegPostIndex(31, _) => Some(Mem::Stack(0)),
            Operand::RegPostIndex(base, _) => {
                Some(Mem::Addr(Expr::Var(Var::Reg(*base as u8), Width::B64)))
            }
            Operand::RegRegOffset(base, idx, sz, style, amt) => {
                let b = Expr::Var(Var::Reg(*base as u8), Width::B64);
                let i = shift_expr(
                    *style,
                    u32::from(*amt),
                    Expr::Var(Var::Reg(*idx as u8), wsz(*sz)),
                    Width::B64,
                );
                Some(Mem::Addr(Expr::bin(BinOp::Add, b, i, Width::B64)))
            }
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    fn pc_target(&self, ins: &Instruction, addr: u64) -> Option<u64> {
        ins.operands.iter().find_map(|op| match op {
            Operand::PCOffset(off) => Some(addr.wrapping_add_signed(*off)),
            _ => None,
        })
    }

    fn call(
        &self,
        ins: &Instruction,
        addr: u64,
        target: Option<CallTarget>,
        st: &mut State,
        out: &mut Vec<(u64, Stmt)>,
    ) -> Option<Term> {
        let _ = ins;
        let Some(target) = target else {
            out.push((addr, Stmt::Asm("blr".into(), Vec::new())));
            return None;
        };
        let name = match &target {
            CallTarget::Direct(a) => self.program.name(*a).map(|n| n.text.clone()),
            _ => None,
        };
        let regs = Convention::Aarch64.arg_regs();
        let count = match &target {
            CallTarget::Direct(a) => self
                .param_counts
                .get(a)
                .copied()
                .or_else(|| name.as_deref().and_then(import_params)),
            _ => None,
        }
        .unwrap_or_else(|| regs.iter().take_while(|r| st.written.contains(r)).count());
        let args = regs
            .iter()
            .take(count)
            .map(|&r| Expr::Var(Var::Reg(r), Width::B64))
            .collect();
        out.push((addr, Stmt::Assign(Var::Reg(0), Expr::Call(target, args))));
        for &r in Convention::Aarch64.clobbered() {
            out.push((
                addr,
                Stmt::Assign(Var::Reg(r), Expr::Unknown("clobbered".into())),
            ));
        }
        st.written.clear();
        st.flags = None;
        if name.as_deref().is_some_and(import_noreturn) {
            return Some(Term::Stop);
        }
        None
    }

    /// A scalar floating-point (NEON) register's width, if operand `op` is one (`s`→f32, `d`→f64).
    fn fdest(op: &Operand) -> Option<(Var, Width)> {
        match op {
            Operand::SIMDRegister(SIMDSizeCode::S, n) => Some((Var::Xmm(*n as u8), Width::B32)),
            Operand::SIMDRegister(SIMDSizeCode::D, n) => Some((Var::Xmm(*n as u8), Width::B64)),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// A floating-point source operand (SIMD register, GPR for a conversion, or an immediate at
    /// the given width).
    fn fval(&self, op: &Operand, w: Width) -> Expr {
        match op {
            Operand::SIMDRegister(SIMDSizeCode::S, n) => Expr::Var(Var::Xmm(*n as u8), Width::B32),
            Operand::SIMDRegister(SIMDSizeCode::D, n) => Expr::Var(Var::Xmm(*n as u8), Width::B64),
            Operand::Register(sz, 31) => Expr::konst(0, wsz(*sz)),
            Operand::Register(sz, n) => Expr::Var(Var::Reg(*n as u8), wsz(*sz)),
            Operand::ImmediateDouble(d) => {
                let bits = if w.0 == 4 {
                    u64::from((*d as f32).to_bits())
                } else {
                    d.to_bits()
                };
                Expr::FConst(bits, w)
            }
            _ => Expr::Unknown("fop".into()),
        }
    }

    /// Lifts the scalar NEON floating-point instructions (`fadd`, `fmul`, `fcvt*`, `fcmp`,
    /// `fcsel`, …) into float IR. Returns `true` if it handled the instruction.
    fn lift_fp(
        &self,
        ins: &Instruction,
        addr: u64,
        st: &mut State,
        out: &mut Vec<(u64, Stmt)>,
    ) -> bool {
        use Opcode as O;
        let fwrite = |d: (Var, Width), value: Expr, out: &mut Vec<(u64, Stmt)>| {
            out.push((addr, Stmt::Assign(d.0, value)));
        };
        let bin = |op: BinOp, s: &Self, out: &mut Vec<(u64, Stmt)>| {
            if let Some(d) = Self::fdest(&ins.operands[0]) {
                let (a, b) = (s.fval(&ins.operands[1], d.1), s.fval(&ins.operands[2], d.1));
                fwrite(d, Expr::fbin(op, a, b, d.1), out);
            }
        };
        let unary = |op: FUnOp, s: &Self, out: &mut Vec<(u64, Stmt)>| {
            if let Some(d) = Self::fdest(&ins.operands[0]) {
                let a = s.fval(&ins.operands[1], d.1);
                fwrite(d, Expr::FUn(op, Box::new(a), d.1), out);
            }
        };
        match ins.opcode {
            O::FADD => bin(BinOp::Add, self, out),
            O::FSUB => bin(BinOp::Sub, self, out),
            O::FMUL => bin(BinOp::Mul, self, out),
            O::FDIV => bin(BinOp::Div, self, out),
            O::FSQRT => unary(FUnOp::Sqrt, self, out),
            O::FABS => unary(FUnOp::Abs, self, out),
            O::FNEG => unary(FUnOp::Neg, self, out),
            O::FMAX | O::FMAXNM | O::FMIN | O::FMINNM => {
                if let Some(d) = Self::fdest(&ins.operands[0]) {
                    let name = if matches!(ins.opcode, O::FMAX | O::FMAXNM) {
                        "max"
                    } else {
                        "min"
                    };
                    let (a, b) = (
                        self.fval(&ins.operands[1], d.1),
                        self.fval(&ins.operands[2], d.1),
                    );
                    fwrite(d, Expr::method(a, name, vec![b], d.1), out);
                }
            }
            O::FMADD | O::FMSUB | O::FNMADD => {
                if let Some(d) = Self::fdest(&ins.operands[0]) {
                    let w = d.1;
                    let n = self.fval(&ins.operands[1], w);
                    let m = self.fval(&ins.operands[2], w);
                    let a = self.fval(&ins.operands[3], w);
                    let prod = Expr::fbin(BinOp::Mul, n, m, w);
                    let value = match ins.opcode {
                        O::FMADD => Expr::fbin(BinOp::Add, a, prod, w),
                        O::FMSUB => Expr::fbin(BinOp::Sub, a, prod, w),
                        _ => Expr::FUn(FUnOp::Neg, Box::new(Expr::fbin(BinOp::Add, a, prod, w)), w),
                    };
                    fwrite(d, value, out);
                }
            }
            O::FMOV => {
                // reg<-imm, reg<-reg, or a GPR<->FP bit reinterpret.
                if let Some(d) = Self::fdest(&ins.operands[0]) {
                    match &ins.operands[1] {
                        Operand::Register(_, n) if *n != 31 => {
                            // GPR -> FP: bit reinterpret as a float.
                            let name = if d.1.0 == 4 {
                                "f32::from_bits"
                            } else {
                                "f64::from_bits"
                            };
                            let g = Expr::Var(Var::Reg(*n as u8), d.1);
                            fwrite(d, Expr::Call(CallTarget::Builtin(name), vec![g]), out);
                        }
                        other => fwrite(d, self.fval(other, d.1), out),
                    }
                } else if let Some((g, gw)) = Self::dest(&ins.operands[0]) {
                    // FP -> GPR: `x.to_bits()`.
                    let fv = self.fval(&ins.operands[1], gw);
                    fwrite((g, gw), Expr::method(fv, "to_bits", Vec::new(), gw), out);
                }
            }
            O::FCMP | O::FCMPE => {
                let w = Self::fdest(&ins.operands[0]).map_or(Width::B64, |d| d.1);
                let a = self.fval(&ins.operands[0], w);
                let b = self.fval(&ins.operands[1], w);
                st.flags = Some(Flags::FSub(a, b));
            }
            O::FCSEL => {
                if let Some(d) = Self::fdest(&ins.operands[0]) {
                    let cond = ins.operands.iter().find_map(|o| match o {
                        Operand::ConditionCode(c) => Some(self.condition(*c, st)),
                        _ => None,
                    });
                    if let Some(cond) = cond {
                        let (a, b) = (
                            self.fval(&ins.operands[1], d.1),
                            self.fval(&ins.operands[2], d.1),
                        );
                        fwrite(
                            d,
                            Expr::Select(Box::new(cond), Box::new(a), Box::new(b), d.1),
                            out,
                        );
                    }
                }
            }
            O::SCVTF | O::UCVTF => {
                // Integer -> float (dest is the FP register).
                if let Some(d) = Self::fdest(&ins.operands[0]) {
                    let src = self.fval(&ins.operands[1], d.1);
                    fwrite(d, Expr::FCast(Box::new(src), d.1, FCast::SIntToFloat), out);
                }
            }
            O::FCVTZS | O::FCVTZU => {
                // Float -> integer, truncating (dest is a GPR).
                if let Some((g, gw)) = Self::dest(&ins.operands[0]) {
                    let sw = Self::fdest(&ins.operands[1]).map_or(Width::B64, |d| d.1);
                    let src = self.fval(&ins.operands[1], sw);
                    fwrite(
                        (g, gw),
                        Expr::FCast(Box::new(src), gw, FCast::FloatToSInt),
                        out,
                    );
                }
            }
            O::FCVT => {
                // Float -> float of a different width.
                if let Some(d) = Self::fdest(&ins.operands[0]) {
                    let sw = Self::fdest(&ins.operands[1]).map_or(Width::B64, |x| x.1);
                    let src = self.fval(&ins.operands[1], sw);
                    fwrite(d, Expr::FCast(Box::new(src), d.1, FCast::FloatToFloat), out);
                }
            }
            _ => return false,
        }
        true
    }

    /// An ARM condition code as an IR condition, read from the pending flags.
    fn condition(&self, cc: u8, st: &State) -> Expr {
        use CmpOp::*;
        let unknown = || Expr::Unknown(format!("cond_{cc}"));
        match &st.flags {
            Some(Flags::Sub(a, b)) => {
                let (a, b) = (a.clone(), b.clone());
                match cc {
                    0 => Expr::cmp(Eq, a, b, false),
                    1 => Expr::cmp(Ne, a, b, false),
                    2 => Expr::cmp(Ge, a, b, false), // hs / cs
                    3 => Expr::cmp(Lt, a, b, false), // lo / cc
                    8 => Expr::cmp(Gt, a, b, false), // hi
                    9 => Expr::cmp(Le, a, b, false), // ls
                    10 => Expr::cmp(Ge, a, b, true), // ge
                    11 => Expr::cmp(Lt, a, b, true), // lt
                    12 => Expr::cmp(Gt, a, b, true), // gt
                    13 => Expr::cmp(Le, a, b, true), // le
                    4 => {
                        let w = a.width();
                        Expr::cmp(Lt, Expr::bin(BinOp::Sub, a, b, w), Expr::konst(0, w), true)
                    }
                    5 => {
                        let w = a.width();
                        Expr::cmp(Ge, Expr::bin(BinOp::Sub, a, b, w), Expr::konst(0, w), true)
                    }
                    _ => unknown(),
                }
            }
            Some(Flags::Test(a, b)) => {
                let w = a.width();
                let x = if a == b {
                    a.clone()
                } else {
                    Expr::bin(BinOp::And, a.clone(), b.clone(), w)
                };
                let zero = Expr::konst(0, w);
                match cc {
                    0 => Expr::cmp(Eq, x, zero, false),
                    1 => Expr::cmp(Ne, x, zero, false),
                    4 => Expr::cmp(Lt, x, zero, true),
                    5 => Expr::cmp(Ge, x, zero, true),
                    _ => unknown(),
                }
            }
            Some(Flags::Result(r)) => {
                let w = r.width();
                let (r, zero) = (r.clone(), Expr::konst(0, w));
                match cc {
                    0 => Expr::cmp(Eq, r, zero, false),
                    1 => Expr::cmp(Ne, r, zero, false),
                    4 | 11 => Expr::cmp(Lt, r, zero, true),
                    5 | 10 => Expr::cmp(Ge, r, zero, true),
                    12 => Expr::cmp(Gt, r, zero, true),
                    13 => Expr::cmp(Le, r, zero, true),
                    _ => unknown(),
                }
            }
            Some(Flags::FSub(a, b)) => {
                use CmpOp::*;
                let (a, b) = (a.clone(), b.clone());
                match cc {
                    0 => Expr::fcmp(Eq, a, b),
                    1 => Expr::fcmp(Ne, a, b),
                    8 | 12 => Expr::fcmp(Gt, a, b), // hi / gt
                    2 | 10 => Expr::fcmp(Ge, a, b), // hs / ge
                    3 | 11 => Expr::fcmp(Lt, a, b), // lo / lt
                    9 | 13 => Expr::fcmp(Le, a, b), // ls / le
                    _ => Expr::Unknown(format!("fcond_{cc}")), // mi/pl/vs/vc (NaN handling)
                }
            }
            None => unknown(),
        }
    }
}

enum Mem {
    Stack(i64),
    Addr(Expr),
}

fn add_off(base: Expr, off: i64) -> Expr {
    match off.cmp(&0) {
        std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => base,
        std::cmp::Ordering::Greater => Expr::bin(
            BinOp::Add,
            base,
            Expr::konst(off as u64, Width::B64),
            Width::B64,
        ),
        std::cmp::Ordering::Less => Expr::bin(
            BinOp::Sub,
            base,
            Expr::konst(off.unsigned_abs(), Width::B64),
            Width::B64,
        ),
    }
}

fn shift_expr(style: ShiftStyle, amt: u32, r: Expr, w: Width) -> Expr {
    match style {
        ShiftStyle::LSL => Expr::bin(BinOp::Shl, r, Expr::konst(u64::from(amt), w), w),
        ShiftStyle::LSR => Expr::bin(BinOp::Shr, r, Expr::konst(u64::from(amt), w), w),
        ShiftStyle::ASR => Expr::bin(BinOp::Sar, r, Expr::konst(u64::from(amt), w), w),
        ShiftStyle::ROR => Expr::method(r, "rotate_right", vec![Expr::konst(u64::from(amt), w)], w),
        ShiftStyle::UXTB => Expr::Cast(Box::new(r), Width::B8, false),
        ShiftStyle::UXTH => Expr::Cast(Box::new(r), Width::B16, false),
        ShiftStyle::UXTW => Expr::Cast(Box::new(r), Width::B32, false),
        ShiftStyle::SXTB => Expr::Cast(
            Box::new(Expr::Cast(Box::new(r), Width::B8, true)),
            Width::B64,
            true,
        ),
        ShiftStyle::SXTH => Expr::Cast(
            Box::new(Expr::Cast(Box::new(r), Width::B16, true)),
            Width::B64,
            true,
        ),
        ShiftStyle::SXTW => Expr::Cast(
            Box::new(Expr::Cast(Box::new(r), Width::B32, true)),
            Width::B64,
            true,
        ),
        ShiftStyle::UXTX | ShiftStyle::SXTX => r,
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-decompiler/src/compile.rs`:

```rs
//! Optional self-contained compile check: feed a generated Rust port to `rustc` and
//! report whether it compiles.
//!
//! Enabled by the `compile-check` cargo feature, so the default build never shells out to
//! a compiler. The check is metadata-only (`--emit=metadata`): it type-checks the scaffold
//! without producing an object file, and it never panics — a missing `rustc` is reported
//! as [`CompileStatus::ToolMissing`], not an error.

use std::process::Command;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};

use orress_analysis::Program;

use crate::{Convention, Error};

/// The outcome of running `rustc` over a port.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum CompileStatus {
    /// `rustc` accepted the port.
    Compiles,
    /// `rustc` reported errors.
    Errors,
    /// No `rustc` on `PATH`, so the check could not run.
    ToolMissing,
}

/// A compile check's result: its [`CompileStatus`] and `rustc`'s diagnostics.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct CompileReport {
    pub status: CompileStatus,
    /// `rustc`'s stderr — the errors to fix (empty when it compiled or the tool is missing).
    pub diagnostics: String,
}

impl CompileReport {
    /// Whether the port compiled.
    pub fn ok(&self) -> bool {
        self.status == CompileStatus::Compiles
    }
}

/// Type-checks `src` as a library with `rustc` (edition 2021, metadata only) and reports
/// the result. Writes to a unique temporary directory that is removed afterwards.
pub fn check_source(src: &str) -> CompileReport {
    static N: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);
    let uniq = N.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("orress_compile_{}_{uniq}", std::process::id()));
    let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir);
    let file = dir.join("port.rs");
    let report = match std::fs::write(&file, src) {
        Ok(()) => {
            let out = Command::new("rustc")
                .args([
                    "--edition",
                    "2021",
                    "--crate-type",
                    "lib",
                    "--emit=metadata",
                    "-o",
                ])
                .arg(dir.join("port.meta"))
                .arg(&file)
                .output();
            match out {
                Ok(o) if o.status.success() => CompileReport {
                    status: CompileStatus::Compiles,
                    diagnostics: String::new(),
                },
                Ok(o) => CompileReport {
                    status: CompileStatus::Errors,
                    diagnostics: String::from_utf8_lossy(&o.stderr).into_owned(),
                },
                Err(_) => CompileReport {
                    status: CompileStatus::ToolMissing,
                    diagnostics: "rustc was not found on PATH".to_owned(),
                },
            }
        }
        Err(e) => CompileReport {
            status: CompileStatus::ToolMissing,
            diagnostics: format!("could not write a temporary file: {e}"),
        },
    };
    let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    report
}

/// Ports the function at `addr` and checks that the scaffold compiles, returning both the
/// port source and the report.
pub fn check_port(
    program: &Program,
    addr: u64,
    conv: Convention,
) -> Result<(String, CompileReport), Error> {
    let src = crate::port(program, addr, conv)?;
    let report = check_source(&src);
    Ok((src, report))
}
```

`crates/orress-decompiler/src/deobfuscate.rs`:

```rs
//! Opaque-predicate deobfuscation via a known-bits abstraction. Obfuscators guard real code with
//! predicates that always evaluate the same way but are not literal constants — e.g. `(x & 1) == 2`
//! (always false) or `(x | 1) != 0` (always true). A bitwise known-bits analysis proves many of
//! these, folding the comparison to a constant so the existing constant-branch and dead-code passes
//! remove the bogus edge and its unreachable arm.
//!
//! The analysis is *sound* (never claims a bit is known unless it provably is), so a fold only ever
//! happens when the predicate is genuinely constant — it cannot change a program's meaning.
//! `known_bits_are_sound` differential-tests it against concrete evaluation.

use crate::ir::{BinOp, Block, CmpOp, Expr, Stmt, Term, Var, Width};

/// A bit set in `zeros` is provably 0; a bit set in `ones` is provably 1; a bit in neither is
/// unknown. Both are confined to the value's width, and `zeros & ones == 0`.
pub fn known_bits(e: &Expr) -> (u64, u64) {
    let m = e.width().mask();
    match e {
        Expr::Const(v, _) => (!v & m, v & m),
        Expr::Not(a, _) => {
            let (z, o) = known_bits(a);
            (o & m, z & m)
        }
        Expr::Bin(op, a, b, _) => bin_bits(*op, a, b, m),
        Expr::Cast(a, w, signed) => cast_bits(a, *w, *signed),
        // Booleans are 0 or 1, so bits above bit 0 are always known-zero.
        Expr::Cmp(..) | Expr::LNot(_) | Expr::LAnd(..) | Expr::LOr(..) | Expr::FCmp(..) => {
            match opaque_value(e) {
                Some(true) => (m & !1, 1),
                Some(false) => (m, 0),
                None => (m & !1, 0),
            }
        }
        // Everything else (loads, calls, multiplies, …) is treated as fully unknown — sound.
        _ => (0, 0),
    }
}

fn bin_bits(op: BinOp, a: &Expr, b: &Expr, m: u64) -> (u64, u64) {
    let (za, oa) = known_bits(a);
    let (zb, ob) = known_bits(b);
    match op {
        BinOp::And => ((za | zb) & m, (oa & ob) & m),
        BinOp::Or => ((za & zb) & m, (oa | ob) & m),
        BinOp::Xor => (((oa & ob) | (za & zb)) & m, ((oa & zb) | (za & ob)) & m),
        BinOp::Shl | BinOp::Shr => {
            let Expr::Const(k, _) = b else { return (0, 0) };
            let k = *k;
            if k >= 64 {
                return (m, 0); // everything shifted out → all zero
            }
            if op == BinOp::Shl {
                let vacated = (1u64 << k) - 1; // low k bits become 0
                (((za << k) | vacated) & m, (oa << k) & m)
            } else {
                let vacated = m & !(m >> k); // high k bits become 0
                (((za >> k) | vacated) & m, (oa >> k) & m)
            }
        }
        // Add/Sub/Mul/Div/Rem/Sar propagate carries or signs across bits — stay sound by claiming
        // nothing.
        _ => (0, 0),
    }
}

fn cast_bits(a: &Expr, w: Width, signed: bool) -> (u64, u64) {
    let (za, oa) = known_bits(a);
    let am = a.width().mask();
    let m = w.mask();
    if w.bits() <= a.width().bits() {
        return (za & m, oa & m); // truncation (or same width)
    }
    let high = m & !am; // the newly added high bits
    if !signed {
        return ((za & am) | high, oa & am); // zero-extend: new bits are 0
    }
    // Sign-extend: the new bits copy the source's top bit, if it is known.
    let sign = 1u64 << (a.width().bits() - 1);
    if oa & sign != 0 {
        (za & am, (oa & am) | high)
    } else if za & sign != 0 {
        ((za & am) | high, oa & am)
    } else {
        (za & am, oa & am)
    }
}

/// If a boolean expression is provably constant, the value it always takes.
pub fn opaque_value(e: &Expr) -> Option<bool> {
    match e {
        Expr::Const(v, _) => Some(*v != 0),
        Expr::Cmp(op, a, b, signed) => cmp_value(*op, a, b, *signed),
        Expr::LNot(a) => opaque_value(a).map(|v| !v),
        Expr::LAnd(a, b) => match (opaque_value(a), opaque_value(b)) {
            (Some(false), _) | (_, Some(false)) => Some(false),
            (Some(true), Some(true)) => Some(true),
            _ => None,
        },
        Expr::LOr(a, b) => match (opaque_value(a), opaque_value(b)) {
            (Some(true), _) | (_, Some(true)) => Some(true),
            (Some(false), Some(false)) => Some(false),
            _ => None,
        },
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn cmp_value(op: CmpOp, a: &Expr, b: &Expr, signed: bool) -> Option<bool> {
    let (za, oa) = known_bits(a);
    let (zb, ob) = known_bits(b);
    let ma = a.width().mask();
    let mb = b.width().mask();
    let a_known = (za | oa) == ma;
    let b_known = (zb | ob) == mb;
    match op {
        CmpOp::Eq | CmpOp::Ne => {
            // A bit where one side is known 1 and the other known 0 makes equality impossible.
            let disagree = (oa & zb) | (za & ob);
            let eq = if disagree != 0 {
                Some(false)
            } else if a_known && b_known {
                Some(oa == ob)
            } else {
                None
            };
            eq.map(|v| if op == CmpOp::Eq { v } else { !v })
        }
        // Ordering only when both sides are fully known (otherwise the result genuinely varies).
        _ if a_known && b_known => {
            let (x, y) = if signed {
                (sign_ext(oa, a.width()), sign_ext(ob, b.width()))
            } else {
                (oa as i64, ob as i64)
            };
            // For unsigned, compare as u64 (both masked, non-negative); for signed, as i64.
            Some(if signed {
                match op {
                    CmpOp::Lt => x < y,
                    CmpOp::Le => x <= y,
                    CmpOp::Gt => x > y,
                    CmpOp::Ge => x >= y,
                    _ => unreachable!(),
                }
            } else {
                match op {
                    CmpOp::Lt => oa < ob,
                    CmpOp::Le => oa <= ob,
                    CmpOp::Gt => oa > ob,
                    CmpOp::Ge => oa >= ob,
                    _ => unreachable!(),
                }
            })
        }
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn sign_ext(v: u64, w: Width) -> i64 {
    let bits = w.bits();
    if bits >= 64 {
        return v as i64;
    }
    let shift = 64 - bits;
    ((v << shift) as i64) >> shift
}

/// Folds a provably-constant boolean expression to `true`/`false`; leaves everything else as is.
/// Called from the main `fold` pass, so it runs on every expression bottom-up.
pub fn fold_bool(e: Expr) -> Expr {
    match &e {
        Expr::Cmp(..) | Expr::LNot(_) | Expr::LAnd(..) | Expr::LOr(..) => match opaque_value(&e) {
            Some(b) => Expr::konst(u64::from(b), Width::B8),
            None => e,
        },
        _ => e,
    }
}

// --- control-flow-flattening unflattening ---------------------------------

/// Undoes control-flow flattening (OLLVM-style): a central dispatcher — a dense `switch(state)` or
/// a chain of `if (state == cᵢ) goto Bᵢ` compares — that every real block jumps back to after
/// setting `state` to a constant for the next block. We relink each such block directly to its real
/// successor, so the dispatcher's bogus hub edges disappear and the later dead-code/merge passes
/// drop the dispatcher.
///
/// Sound and conservative: a predecessor is relinked only when its last write to the dispatcher's
/// state variable is a constant (one successor) or a `select` of two constants (a recovered
/// conditional) — the recovered edge is then exactly what the flattened code does. Anything that
/// cannot be resolved that precisely is left flattened (still a correct CFG, just not simplified).
/// Returns whether it changed the CFG.
pub fn unflatten(blocks: &mut [Block]) -> bool {
    let Some(d) = find_dispatcher(blocks) else {
        return false;
    };
    let target = |v: u64| d.map.get(&v).copied();
    let mut changed = false;
    for b in blocks.iter_mut() {
        // Redirect any edge that lands on the dispatcher, from a block that set the state to a
        // value the dispatcher resolves — the edge then goes straight to the real successor.
        if b.addr == d.entry || !crate::simplify::successors(&b.term).contains(&d.entry) {
            continue;
        }
        match last_state_value(b, d.state) {
            Some(StateVal::Const(c)) => {
                if let Some(t) = target(c) {
                    redirect_edge(&mut b.term, d.entry, t);
                    changed = true;
                }
            }
            // A select-of-constants only decodes to a branch when the whole edge is a plain jump
            // to the dispatcher (otherwise we would be grafting a branch onto a branch).
            Some(StateVal::Select(cond, c1, c2)) if b.term == Term::Jump(d.entry) => {
                if let (Some(t1), Some(t2)) = (target(c1), target(c2)) {
                    b.term = Term::Branch(cond, t1, t2);
                    changed = true;
                }
            }
            _ => {} // unresolved: leave this edge routed through the dispatcher
        }
    }
    changed
}

/// Redirects the edge(s) in `term` that target `from` to `to`, preserving the terminator's shape
/// (a branch keeps its other edge; a branch both of whose edges pointed at `from` collapses to a
/// jump).
fn redirect_edge(term: &mut Term, from: u64, to: u64) {
    let swap = |t: u64| if t == from { to } else { t };
    *term = match std::mem::replace(term, Term::Stop) {
        Term::Jump(t) => Term::Jump(swap(t)),
        Term::Branch(c, a, b) => {
            let (a, b) = (swap(a), swap(b));
            if a == b {
                Term::Jump(a)
            } else {
                Term::Branch(c, a, b)
            }
        }
        Term::Switch(e, cases) => Term::Switch(e, cases.into_iter().map(swap).collect()),
        other => other,
    };
}

/// A recovered dispatcher: the address real blocks jump back to, the state variable it reads, and
/// the state-value → real-block map.
struct Dispatcher {
    entry: u64,
    state: Var,
    map: std::collections::HashMap<u64, u64>,
}

/// Finds a flattening dispatcher the real blocks route through — either a dense `switch(state)`
/// block or the head of an `if (state == cᵢ)` compare chain — requiring at least three blocks to
/// jump back to it (an ordinary switch/if has one predecessor, so it is never mistaken for a hub).
fn find_dispatcher(blocks: &[Block]) -> Option<Dispatcher> {
    // A hub: at least three blocks have a CFG edge landing on it (a flattened function's blocks all
    // route back; an ordinary switch/if has one predecessor). Edges include branch arms, not just
    // jumps, because a handler often reaches the dispatcher on one side of its own test.
    let hub = |addr: u64| {
        blocks
            .iter()
            .filter(|p| crate::simplify::successors(&p.term).contains(&addr))
            .count()
            >= 3
    };
    // Dense jump-table form: `switch(state)`. The dispatcher may compute the jump index from the
    // state (a scrutinee copy + a table load), as long as it has no side effects and the values it
    // defines are used only for its own dispatch — then bypassing it to the resolved case is exact.
    for b in blocks {
        if let Term::Switch(Expr::Var(sw, _), cases) = &b.term
            && hub(b.addr)
            && is_pure_hub(b)
            && switch_local(blocks, b)
            && let Some(state) = trace_state(b, *sw)
        {
            let map = cases
                .iter()
                .enumerate()
                .map(|(i, &t)| (i as u64, t))
                .collect();
            return Some(Dispatcher {
                entry: b.addr,
                state,
                map,
            });
        }
    }
    // Compare-chain form: a run of pure `if (state == cᵢ) goto Bᵢ else <next compare>` blocks.
    for b in blocks {
        if b.stmts.is_empty()
            && hub(b.addr)
            && let Some((state, map)) = walk_chain(blocks, b.addr)
            && map.len() >= 3
        {
            return Some(Dispatcher {
                entry: b.addr,
                state,
                map,
            });
        }
    }
    None
}

/// The dispatcher must compute only its dispatch: no stores, calls, or un-lifted instructions
/// (which could have observable effects we would skip by bypassing it).
fn is_pure_hub(b: &Block) -> bool {
    b.stmts.iter().all(|(_, s)| match s {
        Stmt::Assign(_, e) => !contains_call(e),
        Stmt::Store(..) | Stmt::Eval(_) | Stmt::Asm(..) => false,
    })
}

fn contains_call(e: &Expr) -> bool {
    let mut found = false;
    e.clone().map(&mut |x| {
        if matches!(x, Expr::Call(..)) {
            found = true;
        }
        x
    });
    found
}

/// Every variable the dispatcher defines is read only inside the dispatcher itself (its scrutinee
/// copies and jump-index temporaries), so relinking around it drops nothing a successor needs.
fn switch_local(blocks: &[Block], d: &Block) -> bool {
    let defs: std::collections::HashSet<Var> = d.stmts.iter().flat_map(|(_, s)| s.defs()).collect();
    if defs.is_empty() {
        return true;
    }
    !blocks.iter().filter(|o| o.addr != d.addr).any(|o| {
        o.stmts
            .iter()
            .any(|(_, s)| defs.iter().any(|&v| s.reads(v)))
            || crate::simplify::term_exprs(&o.term)
                .iter()
                .any(|e| defs.iter().any(|&v| e.reads(v)))
    })
}

/// Resolves the real state variable the dispatcher switches on, following scrutinee copies
/// (`sel = s3`, `s3 = state`) back to the variable that is live into the dispatcher. Returns `None`
/// if the switch variable is produced by anything other than a chain of copies inside the block.
fn trace_state(d: &Block, sw: Var) -> Option<Var> {
    let mut v = sw;
    // Each copy's source is read *at* that copy, so the next definition to follow is strictly
    // earlier in the block. Searching only before the current definition guarantees termination,
    // even through a copy cycle (`y = x; x = y`).
    let mut end = d.stmts.len();
    loop {
        match d.stmts[..end]
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .rev()
            .find(|(_, (_, s))| s.defs().contains(&v))
        {
            Some((i, (_, Stmt::Assign(_, Expr::Var(u, _))))) => {
                v = *u;
                end = i;
            }
            Some(_) => return None, // defined by a non-copy here — can't trace through soundly
            None => return Some(v), // not defined in the dispatcher → it is the live-in state
        }
    }
}

/// Walks a compare chain from `head`, collecting the state-value → target map while every block is
/// a pure `if (state == const)` test on the same variable. Stops at the first block that is not.
fn walk_chain(blocks: &[Block], head: u64) -> Option<(Var, std::collections::HashMap<u64, u64>)> {
    let mut map = std::collections::HashMap::new();
    let mut state: Option<Var> = None;
    let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
    let mut cur = head;
    while seen.insert(cur) {
        let Some(b) = blocks.iter().find(|x| x.addr == cur) else {
            break;
        };
        let (Term::Branch(cond, eq, next), true) = (&b.term, b.stmts.is_empty()) else {
            break;
        };
        let Some((sv, c)) = eq_state_const(cond) else {
            break;
        };
        match state {
            None => state = Some(sv),
            Some(s) if s != sv => break,
            _ => {}
        }
        map.entry(c).or_insert(*eq);
        cur = *next;
    }
    state.map(|s| (s, map))
}

/// Matches `state == const` (either operand order), returning the variable and constant.
fn eq_state_const(cond: &Expr) -> Option<(Var, u64)> {
    let Expr::Cmp(CmpOp::Eq, a, b, _) = cond else {
        return None;
    };
    match (&**a, &**b) {
        (Expr::Var(v, _), Expr::Const(c, _)) | (Expr::Const(c, _), Expr::Var(v, _)) => {
            Some((*v, *c))
        }
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// The value a block leaves in `state` on its way out: the last assignment to it, when that is a
/// constant or a `select` of two constants.
enum StateVal {
    Const(u64),
    Select(Expr, u64, u64),
}

fn last_state_value(block: &Block, state: Var) -> Option<StateVal> {
    let (_, last) = block
        .stmts
        .iter()
        .rev()
        .find(|(_, s)| s.defs().contains(&state))?;
    let Stmt::Assign(_, e) = last else {
        return None;
    };
    match e {
        Expr::Const(c, _) => Some(StateVal::Const(*c)),
        Expr::Select(cond, a, b, _) => match (&**a, &**b) {
            (Expr::Const(c1, _), Expr::Const(c2, _)) => {
                Some(StateVal::Select((**cond).clone(), *c1, *c2))
            }
            _ => None,
        },
        _ => None,
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// A tiny concrete evaluator over the integer/boolean subset known_bits reasons about, with
    /// `Var(0)` bound to `x`. Used only to differential-test the abstraction.
    fn eval(e: &Expr, x: u64) -> u64 {
        let m = e.width().mask();
        match e {
            Expr::Const(v, _) => v & m,
            Expr::Var(..) => x & m,
            Expr::Not(a, _) => !eval(a, x) & m,
            Expr::Bin(op, a, b, _) => {
                let (l, r) = (eval(a, x), eval(b, x));
                let v = match op {
                    BinOp::Add => l.wrapping_add(r),
                    BinOp::Sub => l.wrapping_sub(r),
                    BinOp::Mul => l.wrapping_mul(r),
                    BinOp::And => l & r,
                    BinOp::Or => l | r,
                    BinOp::Xor => l ^ r,
                    BinOp::Shl => l.wrapping_shl(r as u32),
                    BinOp::Shr => l.wrapping_shr(r as u32),
                    _ => 0,
                };
                v & m
            }
            Expr::Cast(a, w, signed) => {
                let v = eval(a, x);
                if *signed && w.bits() > a.width().bits() {
                    (sign_ext(v, a.width()) as u64) & m
                } else {
                    v & m
                }
            }
            Expr::Cmp(op, a, b, _) => {
                let (l, r) = (eval(a, x), eval(b, x));
                u64::from(match op {
                    CmpOp::Eq => l == r,
                    CmpOp::Ne => l != r,
                    CmpOp::Lt => l < r,
                    CmpOp::Le => l <= r,
                    CmpOp::Gt => l > r,
                    CmpOp::Ge => l >= r,
                })
            }
            _ => 0,
        }
    }

    fn c(v: u64) -> Expr {
        Expr::konst(v, Width::B32)
    }
    fn x() -> Expr {
        Expr::Var(crate::ir::Var::Reg(0), Width::B32)
    }
    fn bin(op: BinOp, a: Expr, b: Expr) -> Expr {
        Expr::bin(op, a, b, Width::B32)
    }

    #[test]
    fn known_bits_are_sound() {
        // For every concrete x, the bits known_bits claims must actually hold. Exhaustive over a
        // byte of entropy in the low bits plus some spread-out values.
        let exprs = vec![
            bin(BinOp::And, x(), c(1)),
            bin(BinOp::Or, x(), c(0xff)),
            bin(BinOp::Xor, bin(BinOp::And, x(), c(0xf0)), c(0x0f)),
            bin(BinOp::Shl, bin(BinOp::And, x(), c(0xff)), c(8)),
            bin(BinOp::Shr, x(), c(28)),
            Expr::Cast(
                Box::new(Expr::Var(crate::ir::Var::Reg(0), Width::B8)),
                Width::B32,
                false,
            ),
            bin(BinOp::And, bin(BinOp::Shl, x(), c(4)), c(0xf)),
        ];
        for e in &exprs {
            let (z, o) = known_bits(e);
            assert_eq!(z & o, 0, "zeros and ones overlap for {e:?}");
            for x in (0u64..=0x3ff).chain([0x5555_5555, 0xffff_ffff, 0xdead_beef]) {
                let v = eval(e, x);
                assert_eq!(v & z, 0, "claimed-zero bit was 1: {e:?} at x={x:#x}");
                assert_eq!(v & o, o, "claimed-one bit was 0: {e:?} at x={x:#x}");
            }
        }
    }

    fn cmp(op: CmpOp, a: Expr, b: Expr) -> Expr {
        Expr::Cmp(op, Box::new(a), Box::new(b), false)
    }

    #[test]
    fn folds_opaque_predicates() {
        // (x & 1) == 2 is always false; != always true.
        let lo = bin(BinOp::And, x(), c(1));
        assert_eq!(opaque_value(&cmp(CmpOp::Eq, lo.clone(), c(2))), Some(false));
        assert_eq!(opaque_value(&cmp(CmpOp::Ne, lo, c(2))), Some(true));
        // (x | 1) == 0 is always false (bit 0 is forced to 1).
        let hi = bin(BinOp::Or, x(), c(1));
        assert_eq!(opaque_value(&cmp(CmpOp::Eq, hi, c(0))), Some(false));
        // ((x << 4) & 0xf) == 0 is always true (the low nibble is shifted-in zeros).
        let masked = bin(BinOp::And, bin(BinOp::Shl, x(), c(4)), c(0xf));
        assert_eq!(opaque_value(&cmp(CmpOp::Eq, masked, c(0))), Some(true));
        // A genuine data-dependent predicate must NOT be folded.
        assert_eq!(opaque_value(&cmp(CmpOp::Eq, x(), c(7))), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn fold_bool_rewrites_only_constants() {
        let lo = bin(BinOp::And, x(), c(1));
        assert_eq!(
            fold_bool(cmp(CmpOp::Eq, lo.clone(), c(2))),
            Expr::konst(0, Width::B8)
        );
        // Data-dependent: left untouched.
        let live = cmp(CmpOp::Eq, x(), c(7));
        assert_eq!(fold_bool(live.clone()), live);
    }

    fn blk(addr: u64, stmts: Vec<Stmt>, term: Term) -> Block {
        Block {
            addr,
            stmts: stmts.into_iter().map(|s| (addr, s)).collect(),
            term,
            term_addr: addr,
        }
    }
    const SV: Var = Var::Reg(1);
    fn set_state(v: u64) -> Stmt {
        Stmt::Assign(SV, Expr::konst(v, Width::B32))
    }

    #[test]
    fn unflatten_relinks_constant_state_transitions() {
        // entry -> D; D switches on state; B0/B1 set the next state and loop back; B2 returns.
        let mut blocks = vec![
            blk(0x10, vec![set_state(0)], Term::Jump(0x100)),
            blk(
                0x100,
                vec![],
                Term::Switch(Expr::Var(SV, Width::B32), vec![0x20, 0x30, 0x40]),
            ),
            blk(0x20, vec![set_state(1)], Term::Jump(0x100)),
            blk(0x30, vec![set_state(2)], Term::Jump(0x100)),
            blk(0x40, vec![], Term::Return(None)),
        ];
        assert!(unflatten(&mut blocks));
        // entry -> cases[0]=0x20; B0 -> cases[1]=0x30; B1 -> cases[2]=0x40. Dispatcher bypassed.
        assert_eq!(blocks[0].term, Term::Jump(0x20));
        assert_eq!(blocks[2].term, Term::Jump(0x30));
        assert_eq!(blocks[3].term, Term::Jump(0x40));
    }

    #[test]
    fn unflatten_recovers_a_conditional_as_a_branch() {
        // A block whose next state is `cond ? 1 : 2` is a flattened if/else.
        let cond = cmp(CmpOp::Lt, x(), c(5));
        let sel = Expr::Select(
            Box::new(cond.clone()),
            Box::new(Expr::konst(1, Width::B32)),
            Box::new(Expr::konst(2, Width::B32)),
            Width::B32,
        );
        let mut blocks = vec![
            blk(0x10, vec![set_state(0)], Term::Jump(0x100)),
            blk(
                0x100,
                vec![],
                Term::Switch(Expr::Var(SV, Width::B32), vec![0x20, 0x30, 0x40, 0x50]),
            ),
            blk(0x20, vec![Stmt::Assign(SV, sel)], Term::Jump(0x100)),
            blk(0x30, vec![set_state(3)], Term::Jump(0x100)), // a third hub edge
            blk(0x40, vec![], Term::Return(None)),
            blk(0x50, vec![], Term::Return(None)),
        ];
        assert!(unflatten(&mut blocks));
        // cases[1]=0x30, cases[2]=0x40 → the recovered conditional branches to those.
        assert_eq!(blocks[2].term, Term::Branch(cond, 0x30, 0x40));
    }

    #[test]
    fn unflatten_handles_a_compare_chain_dispatcher() {
        // A dispatcher lowered as `if (state==0) B0; else if (state==1) B1; else if (state==2) B2`.
        let chain = |addr: u64, sval: u64, eq: u64, next: u64| {
            let cond = cmp(CmpOp::Eq, Expr::Var(SV, Width::B32), c(sval));
            blk(addr, vec![], Term::Branch(cond, eq, next))
        };
        let mut blocks = vec![
            blk(0x10, vec![set_state(0)], Term::Jump(0x100)),
            chain(0x100, 0, 0x20, 0x101),
            chain(0x101, 1, 0x30, 0x102),
            chain(0x102, 2, 0x40, 0x103),
            blk(0x103, vec![], Term::Return(None)), // default
            blk(0x20, vec![set_state(1)], Term::Jump(0x100)),
            blk(0x30, vec![set_state(2)], Term::Jump(0x100)),
            blk(0x40, vec![], Term::Return(None)),
        ];
        assert!(unflatten(&mut blocks));
        assert_eq!(blocks[0].term, Term::Jump(0x20)); // entry: state 0 -> B0
        assert_eq!(blocks[5].term, Term::Jump(0x30)); // B0: state 1 -> B1
        assert_eq!(blocks[6].term, Term::Jump(0x40)); // B1: state 2 -> B2
    }

    #[test]
    fn unflatten_leaves_an_ordinary_switch_alone() {
        // A normal switch (one predecessor, not a hub) must not be touched.
        let mut blocks = vec![
            blk(0x10, vec![set_state(1)], Term::Jump(0x100)),
            blk(
                0x100,
                vec![],
                Term::Switch(Expr::Var(SV, Width::B32), vec![0x20, 0x30]),
            ),
            blk(0x20, vec![], Term::Return(None)),
            blk(0x30, vec![], Term::Return(None)),
        ];
        assert!(!unflatten(&mut blocks));
        assert_eq!(blocks[0].term, Term::Jump(0x100));
    }

    #[test]
    fn trace_state_terminates_on_a_copy_cycle() {
        use crate::ir::Var;
        let (x, y) = (Var::Reg(1), Var::Reg(2));
        let copy = |d: Var, s: Var| Stmt::Assign(d, Expr::Var(s, Width::B32));
        // y = x; x = y; switch on x — the cycle resolves to the live-in x.
        let d = blk(
            0x100,
            vec![copy(y, x), copy(x, y)],
            Term::Switch(Expr::Var(x, Width::B32), vec![0x20]),
        );
        assert_eq!(trace_state(&d, x), Some(x));
        // A self-copy (x = x) as well.
        let d = blk(
            0x100,
            vec![copy(x, x)],
            Term::Switch(Expr::Var(x, Width::B32), vec![0x20]),
        );
        assert_eq!(trace_state(&d, x), Some(x));
    }
}
```
