```rs
                let op = match ins.mnemonic() {
                    M::Shlx => BinOp::Shl,
                    M::Shrx => BinOp::Shr,
                    _ => BinOp::Sar,
                };
                self.write(ins, 0, Expr::bin(op, src, count, w0), st, out);
            }
            // BMI2: `rorx dst, src, imm` → `rotate_right`.
            M::Rorx => {
                let src = self.read(ins, 1, st);
                let n = Expr::Cast(Box::new(self.read(ins, 2, st)), Width::B32, false);
                self.write(
                    ins,
                    0,
                    Expr::method(src, "rotate_right", vec![n], w0),
                    st,
                    out,
                );
            }
            // Sign-extend the accumulator's low half (al→ax, ax→eax; `cdqe` does eax→rax).
            M::Cbw => out.push((
                addr,
                Stmt::Assign(
                    Var::Reg(RAX),
                    Expr::Cast(
                        Box::new(Expr::Var(Var::Reg(RAX), Width::B8)),
                        Width::B16,
                        true,
                    ),
                ),
            )),
            M::Cwde => out.push((
                addr,
                Stmt::Assign(
                    Var::Reg(RAX),
                    Expr::Cast(
                        Box::new(Expr::Var(Var::Reg(RAX), Width::B16)),
                        Width::B32,
                        true,
                    ),
                ),
            )),
            // Double-precision shifts expand to a shift/or expression.
            M::Shld | M::Shrd => {
                let dst = self.read(ins, 0, st);
                let src = self.read(ins, 1, st);
                let n = self.read(ins, 2, st);
                let bits = Expr::konst(u64::from(w0.bits()), w0);
                let inv = Expr::bin(BinOp::Sub, bits, n.clone(), w0);
                let (main, fill) = if ins.mnemonic() == M::Shld {
                    (
                        Expr::bin(BinOp::Shl, dst, n, w0),
                        Expr::bin(BinOp::Shr, src, inv, w0),
                    )
                } else {
                    (
                        Expr::bin(BinOp::Shr, dst, n, w0),
                        Expr::bin(BinOp::Shl, src, inv, w0),
                    )
                };
                self.write(ins, 0, Expr::bin(BinOp::Or, main, fill, w0), st, out);
                st.flags = None;
            }
            // Exchange: swap the two operands' values (read both first, then write).
            M::Xchg => {
                let a = self.read(ins, 0, st);
                let b = self.read(ins, 1, st);
                self.write(ins, 0, b, st, out);
                self.write(ins, 1, a, st, out);
            }
            // Exchange-and-add: dst gets dst+src, src gets the old dst.
            M::Xadd => {
                let a = self.read(ins, 0, st);
                let b = self.read(ins, 1, st);
                self.write(ins, 1, a.clone(), st, out);
                self.write(ins, 0, Expr::bin(BinOp::Add, a, b, w0), st, out);
                st.flags = None;
            }
            // Bit test (+ set/reset/complement): CF = bit `n` of the operand before any change.
            M::Bt | M::Bts | M::Btr | M::Btc => {
                let x = self.read(ins, 0, st);
                let n = self.read(ins, 1, st);
                st.flags = Some(Flags::Bit(x.clone(), n.clone()));
                let bit = || Expr::bin(BinOp::Shl, Expr::konst(1, w0), n.clone(), w0);
                match ins.mnemonic() {
                    M::Bts => {
                        self.write(ins, 0, Expr::bin(BinOp::Or, x, bit(), w0), st, out);
                    }
                    M::Btr => {
                        let mask = Expr::Not(Box::new(bit()), w0);
                        self.write(ins, 0, Expr::bin(BinOp::And, x, mask, w0), st, out);
                    }
                    M::Btc => {
                        self.write(ins, 0, Expr::bin(BinOp::Xor, x, bit(), w0), st, out);
                    }
                    _ => {} // Bt only tests.
                }
            }
            // Repeated string moves / stores → C `memcpy` / `memset` over `rcx` elements
            // (forward direction, the usual `cld` case). `rsi`/`rdi` advance past the block
            // and `rcx` is consumed, so later reads of them stay sound.
            M::Movsb
            | M::Movsw
            | M::Movsd
            | M::Movsq
            | M::Stosb
            | M::Stosw
            | M::Stosd
            | M::Stosq
                if ins.has_rep_prefix() || ins.has_repe_prefix() =>
            {
                let ew: u64 = match ins.mnemonic() {
                    M::Movsb | M::Stosb => 1,
                    M::Movsw | M::Stosw => 2,
                    M::Movsd | M::Stosd => 4,
                    _ => 8, // movsq / stosq
                };
                let rcx = Expr::Var(Var::Reg(RCX), Width::B64);
                let bytes = if ew == 1 {
                    rcx
                } else {
                    Expr::bin(BinOp::Mul, rcx, Expr::konst(ew, Width::B64), Width::B64)
                };
                let dst = Expr::Var(Var::Reg(RDI), Width::B64);
                let is_move = matches!(ins.mnemonic(), M::Movsb | M::Movsw | M::Movsd | M::Movsq);
                if is_move {
                    let src = Expr::Var(Var::Reg(RSI), Width::B64);
                    out.push((
                        addr,
                        Stmt::Eval(Expr::Call(
                            CallTarget::Builtin("memcpy"),
                            vec![dst.clone(), src.clone(), bytes.clone()],
                        )),
                    ));
                    out.push((
                        addr,
                        Stmt::Assign(
                            Var::Reg(RSI),
                            Expr::bin(BinOp::Add, src, bytes.clone(), Width::B64),
                        ),
                    ));
                } else {
                    let val = Expr::Var(Var::Reg(RAX), Width(ew as u8));
                    out.push((
                        addr,
                        Stmt::Eval(Expr::Call(
                            CallTarget::Builtin("memset"),
                            vec![dst.clone(), val, bytes.clone()],
                        )),
                    ));
                }
                out.push((
                    addr,
                    Stmt::Assign(Var::Reg(RDI), Expr::bin(BinOp::Add, dst, bytes, Width::B64)),
                ));
                out.push((
                    addr,
                    Stmt::Assign(Var::Reg(RCX), Expr::konst(0, Width::B64)),
                ));
                st.flags = None;
            }
            // Repeated compare → C `memcmp`: the flags become `memcmp(rsi, rdi, n) <=> 0`, so a
            // following `je`/`jne`/`jl`/… reads as `memcmp(..) == 0` and friends.
            M::Cmpsb | M::Cmpsw | M::Cmpsd | M::Cmpsq
                if ins.has_rep_prefix() || ins.has_repe_prefix() || ins.has_repne_prefix() =>
            {
                let ew: u64 = match ins.mnemonic() {
                    M::Cmpsb => 1,
                    M::Cmpsw => 2,
                    M::Cmpsd => 4,
                    _ => 8,
                };
                let rcx = Expr::Var(Var::Reg(RCX), Width::B64);
                let bytes = if ew == 1 {
                    rcx
                } else {
                    Expr::bin(BinOp::Mul, rcx, Expr::konst(ew, Width::B64), Width::B64)
                };
                let memcmp = Expr::Call(
                    CallTarget::Builtin("memcmp"),
                    vec![
                        Expr::Var(Var::Reg(RSI), Width::B64),
                        Expr::Var(Var::Reg(RDI), Width::B64),
                        bytes,
                    ],
                );
                st.flags = Some(Flags::Sub(memcmp, Expr::konst(0, Width::B32)));
            }
            // Repeated scan for a byte. Modelled as `__scasb(ptr, value)` = the number of
            // bytes examined up to and including the match, decrementing `rcx` by it — so the
            // classic `or rcx,-1; xor al,al; repne scasb; not rcx; dec rcx` idiom folds to
            // `strlen(ptr)` (see `simplify::fold`).
            M::Scasb | M::Scasw | M::Scasd | M::Scasq
                if ins.has_rep_prefix() || ins.has_repe_prefix() || ins.has_repne_prefix() =>
            {
                let ew: u64 = match ins.mnemonic() {
                    M::Scasb => 1,
                    M::Scasw => 2,
                    M::Scasd => 4,
                    _ => 8,
                };
                let scan = Expr::Call(
                    CallTarget::Builtin("__scasb"),
                    vec![
                        Expr::Var(Var::Reg(RDI), Width::B64),
                        Expr::Var(Var::Reg(RAX), Width(ew as u8)),
                    ],
                );
                out.push((
                    addr,
                    Stmt::Assign(
                        Var::Reg(RCX),
                        Expr::bin(
                            BinOp::Sub,
                            Expr::Var(Var::Reg(RCX), Width::B64),
                            scan,
                            Width::B64,
                        ),
                    ),
                ));
                st.flags = None;
            }
            M::Cmp => st.flags = Some(Flags::Sub(self.read(ins, 0, st), self.read(ins, 1, st))),
            M::Test => st.flags = Some(Flags::Test(self.read(ins, 0, st), self.read(ins, 1, st))),
            M::Push => {
                let v = self.read(ins, 0, st);
                st.rsp -= 8;
                // Saving a register in the prologue is bookkeeping, not program logic.
                if !(st.prologue && ins.op_kind(0) == OpKind::Register) {
                    out.push((addr, Stmt::Assign(Var::Stack(st.rsp), v)));
                }
            }
            M::Pop => {
                let v = Expr::Var(Var::Stack(st.rsp), Width::B64);
                st.rsp += 8;
                if is_rbp(ins, 0) {
                    st.rbp = None;
                }
                self.write(ins, 0, v, st, out);
            }
            M::Leave => {
                if let Some(b) = st.rbp {
                    st.rsp = b + 8;
                }
                st.rbp = None;
            }
            M::Cdqe => out.push((
                addr,
                Stmt::Assign(
                    Var::Reg(RAX),
                    Expr::Cast(
                        Box::new(Expr::Var(Var::Reg(RAX), Width::B32)),
                        Width::B64,
                        true,
                    ),
                ),
            )),
            M::Cdq | M::Cqo | M::Cwd => {} // sign bits for a division; the division reads rax
            M::Call => return self.lift_call(ins, st, out),
            M::Ret | M::Retf => {
                return Some(Term::Return(Some(Expr::Var(Var::Reg(RAX), Width::B64))));
            }
            M::Jmp => {
                // A `switch` jump table `jmp [base + index*entry]` → a multi-way `Switch`.
                if ins.op0_kind() == OpKind::Memory
                    && ins.memory_base() == Register::None
                    && ins.memory_index() != Register::None
                    && matches!(ins.memory_index_scale(), 4 | 8)
                    && let Some((idx, _)) = reg(ins.memory_index())
                    && let Some(cases) =
                        self.jump_table(ins.memory_displacement64(), ins.memory_index_scale() as u8)
                {
                    return Some(Term::Switch(Expr::Var(Var::Reg(idx), Width::B64), cases));
                }
                return Some(match ins.op0_kind() {
                    OpKind::NearBranch16 | OpKind::NearBranch32 | OpKind::NearBranch64 => {
                        let t = ins.near_branch_target();
                        if self.program.functions.contains_key(&t) {
                            Term::TailCall(Expr::Call(CallTarget::Direct(t), Vec::new()))
                        } else {
                            Term::Jump(t)
                        }
                    }
                    _ => Term::TailCall(Expr::Call(self.call_target(ins, st), Vec::new())),
                });
            }
            M::Int3 | M::Ud2 | M::Hlt => return Some(Term::Stop),
            // `jcxz`/`jecxz`/`jrcxz`: branch if the count register is zero. These have
            // condition_code() == None, so they'd otherwise fall through to `unmodeled` and lose
            // the conditional edge entirely.
            M::Jcxz | M::Jecxz | M::Jrcxz => {
                let w = match ins.mnemonic() {
                    M::Jrcxz => Width::B64,
                    M::Jcxz => Width::B16,
                    _ => Width::B32,
                };
                let c = Expr::cmp(
                    CmpOp::Eq,
                    Expr::Var(Var::Reg(RCX), w),
                    Expr::konst(0, w),
                    false,
                );
                return Some(Term::Branch(c, ins.near_branch_target(), next));
            }
            // `loop`/`loope`/`loopne`: `--rcx; branch if rcx != 0` (and ZF for loope / !ZF for
            // loopne). The decrement does not touch flags, so the ZF test reads the loop body's
            // last flag-setting instruction.
            M::Loop | M::Loope | M::Loopne => {
                out.push((
                    addr,
                    Stmt::Assign(
                        Var::Reg(RCX),
                        Expr::bin(
                            BinOp::Sub,
                            Expr::Var(Var::Reg(RCX), Width::B64),
                            Expr::konst(1, Width::B64),
                            Width::B64,
                        ),
                    ),
                ));
                let nz = Expr::cmp(
                    CmpOp::Ne,
                    Expr::Var(Var::Reg(RCX), Width::B64),
                    Expr::konst(0, Width::B64),
                    false,
                );
                let cond = match ins.mnemonic() {
                    M::Loope => {
                        Expr::LAnd(Box::new(nz), Box::new(self.condition(ConditionCode::e, st)))
                    }
                    M::Loopne => Expr::LAnd(
                        Box::new(nz),
                        Box::new(self.condition(ConditionCode::ne, st)),
                    ),
                    _ => nz,
                };
                return Some(Term::Branch(cond, ins.near_branch_target(), next));
            }
            m if ins.condition_code() != ConditionCode::None
                && ins.flow_control() == iced_x86::FlowControl::ConditionalBranch =>
            {
                let _ = m;
                let cond = self.condition(ins.condition_code(), st);
                return Some(Term::Branch(cond, ins.near_branch_target(), next));
            }
            m if ins.condition_code() != ConditionCode::None
                && format!("{m:?}").starts_with("Set") =>
            {
                let cond = self.condition(ins.condition_code(), st);
                self.write(ins, 0, cond, st, out);
            }
            m if ins.condition_code() != ConditionCode::None
                && format!("{m:?}").starts_with("Cmov") =>
            {
                let cond = self.condition(ins.condition_code(), st);
                let old = self.read(ins, 0, st);
                let new = self.read(ins, 1, st);
                self.write(
                    ins,
                    0,
                    Expr::Select(Box::new(cond), Box::new(new), Box::new(old), w0),
                    st,
                    out,
                );
            }
            _ => return self.unmodeled(ins, st, out),
        }
        None
    }

    /// Reads a floating-point source operand of `w` bytes: an XMM register as the scalar value,
    /// a general-purpose register as its integer (for `cvtsi2*`), or a memory load.
    fn fread(&self, ins: &Instruction, op: u32, st: &State, w: Width) -> Expr {
        match ins.op_kind(op) {
            OpKind::Register => {
                let r = ins.op_register(op);
                if let Some(x) = xmm(r) {
                    Expr::Var(Var::Xmm(x), w)
                } else if let Some((g, gw)) = reg(r) {
                    Expr::Var(Var::Reg(g), gw)
                } else {
                    Expr::Unknown(format!("{r:?}").to_lowercase())
                }
            }
            OpKind::Memory => {
                // A compiler keeps float literals in a read-only constant pool, loaded
                // rip-relative. Recover the actual value so it reads `x * 2.5` not a raw read.
                if ins.is_ip_rel_memory_operand()
                    && let Some(v) = self.float_const(ins.ip_rel_memory_address(), w)
                {
                    return Expr::FConst(v, w);
                }
                match self.mem_addr(ins, st) {
                    Ok(a) => Expr::Load(Box::new(a), w),
                    Err((v, vw)) => Expr::Var(v, vw),
                }
            }
            _ => Expr::Unknown(String::from("?")),
        }
    }

    /// Reads a `w`-byte float literal from a read-only constant pool, as raw bits.
    fn float_const(&self, addr: u64, w: Width) -> Option<u64> {
        let r = self.program.memory.region(addr)?;
        let n = r.name.to_ascii_lowercase();
        if !(n.contains("rodata")
            || n.contains("rdata")
            || n.contains("text")
            || n.contains("const"))
        {
            return None;
        }
        let bytes = self.program.memory.read(addr, usize::from(w.0))?;
        if bytes.len() < usize::from(w.0) {
            return None;
        }
        let mut v = 0u64;
        for (i, &b) in bytes.iter().enumerate() {
            v |= u64::from(b) << (8 * i);
        }
        Some(v & w.mask())
    }

    /// Writes a floating-point `value` to operand `op` (an XMM register, a general register for
    /// a float→int conversion, or memory).
    fn fwrite(
        &self,
        ins: &Instruction,
        op: u32,
        value: Expr,
        st: &State,
        out: &mut Vec<(u64, Stmt)>,
    ) {
        let addr = ins.ip();
        match ins.op_kind(op) {
            OpKind::Register => {
                let r = ins.op_register(op);
                if let Some(x) = xmm(r) {
                    out.push((addr, Stmt::Assign(Var::Xmm(x), value)));
                } else if let Some((g, _)) = reg(r) {
                    out.push((addr, Stmt::Assign(Var::Reg(g), value)));
                }
            }
            OpKind::Memory => {
                let w = value.width();
                match self.mem_addr(ins, st) {
                    Ok(a) => out.push((addr, Stmt::Store(a, value, w))),
                    Err((v, _)) => out.push((addr, Stmt::Assign(v, value))),
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }

    /// Lifts the scalar SSE/SSE2 floating-point instructions (`addsd`, `mulss`, `cvtsi2sd`,
    /// `comisd`, `sqrtsd`, …) into float IR nodes. Returns `true` if it handled the instruction.
    fn lift_float(&self, ins: &Instruction, st: &mut State, out: &mut Vec<(u64, Stmt)>) -> bool {
        use Mnemonic as M;
        let m = ins.mnemonic();
        // `movsd` is also a string instruction; the SSE form always has an XMM operand.
        let has_xmm = (0..ins.op_count())
            .any(|op| ins.op_kind(op) == OpKind::Register && xmm(ins.op_register(op)).is_some());
        // Arithmetic `dst = dst OP src`.
        let arith = |op: BinOp, w: Width, s: &Self, out: &mut Vec<(u64, Stmt)>| {
            let a = s.fread(ins, 0, st, w);
            let b = s.fread(ins, 1, st, w);
            s.fwrite(ins, 0, Expr::fbin(op, a, b, w), st, out);
        };
        match m {
            M::Addss => arith(BinOp::Add, Width::B32, self, out),
            M::Addsd => arith(BinOp::Add, Width::B64, self, out),
            M::Subss => arith(BinOp::Sub, Width::B32, self, out),
            M::Subsd => arith(BinOp::Sub, Width::B64, self, out),
            M::Mulss => arith(BinOp::Mul, Width::B32, self, out),
            M::Mulsd => arith(BinOp::Mul, Width::B64, self, out),
            M::Divss => arith(BinOp::Div, Width::B32, self, out),
            M::Divsd => arith(BinOp::Div, Width::B64, self, out),
            M::Sqrtss | M::Sqrtsd => {
                let w = if m == M::Sqrtss {
                    Width::B32
                } else {
                    Width::B64
                };
                let src = self.fread(ins, 1, st, w);
                self.fwrite(ins, 0, Expr::FUn(FUnOp::Sqrt, Box::new(src), w), st, out);
            }
            M::Minss | M::Minsd | M::Maxss | M::Maxsd => {
                let w = if matches!(m, M::Minss | M::Maxss) {
                    Width::B32
                } else {
                    Width::B64
                };
                let name = if matches!(m, M::Minss | M::Minsd) {
                    "min"
                } else {
                    "max"
                };
                let a = self.fread(ins, 0, st, w);
                let b = self.fread(ins, 1, st, w);
                self.fwrite(ins, 0, Expr::method(a, name, vec![b], w), st, out);
            }
            // Compare → floating-point flags for the following `ja`/`jb`/`je`/….
            M::Comiss | M::Ucomiss | M::Comisd | M::Ucomisd => {
                let w = if matches!(m, M::Comiss | M::Ucomiss) {
                    Width::B32
                } else {
                    Width::B64
                };
                st.flags = Some(Flags::FSub(
                    self.fread(ins, 0, st, w),
                    self.fread(ins, 1, st, w),
                ));
            }
            // Integer → float.
            M::Cvtsi2ss | M::Cvtsi2sd => {
                let w = if m == M::Cvtsi2ss {
                    Width::B32
                } else {
                    Width::B64
                };
                let src = self.fread(ins, 1, st, self.op_width(ins, 1, st));
                self.fwrite(
                    ins,
                    0,
                    Expr::FCast(Box::new(src), w, FCast::SIntToFloat),
                    st,
                    out,
                );
            }
            // Float → integer (truncating).
            M::Cvttss2si | M::Cvttsd2si | M::Cvtss2si | M::Cvtsd2si => {
                let sw = if matches!(m, M::Cvttss2si | M::Cvtss2si) {
                    Width::B32
                } else {
                    Width::B64
                };
                let dw = self.op_width(ins, 0, st);
                let src = self.fread(ins, 1, st, sw);
                self.fwrite(
                    ins,
                    0,
                    Expr::FCast(Box::new(src), dw, FCast::FloatToSInt),
                    st,
                    out,
                );
            }
            // Float → float.
            M::Cvtss2sd => {
                let src = self.fread(ins, 1, st, Width::B32);
                self.fwrite(
                    ins,
                    0,
                    Expr::FCast(Box::new(src), Width::B64, FCast::FloatToFloat),
                    st,
                    out,
                );
            }
            M::Cvtsd2ss => {
                let src = self.fread(ins, 1, st, Width::B64);
                self.fwrite(
                    ins,
                    0,
                    Expr::FCast(Box::new(src), Width::B32, FCast::FloatToFloat),
                    st,
                    out,
                );
            }
            // Scalar float moves. `movss`/`movsd` are always scalar; the packed moves
            // (`movaps`/`movups`/…) are scalar only as a register↔register copy — with a memory
            // operand they move a full 128-bit vector, so they fall through to `lift_simd`.
            M::Movss if has_xmm => {
                let v = self.fread(ins, 1, st, Width::B32);
                self.fwrite(ins, 0, v, st, out);
            }
            M::Movsd if has_xmm => {
                let v = self.fread(ins, 1, st, Width::B64);
                self.fwrite(ins, 0, v, st, out);
            }
            M::Movaps | M::Movups
                if has_xmm
                    && ins.op_kind(0) == OpKind::Register
                    && ins.op_kind(1) == OpKind::Register =>
            {
                let v = self.fread(ins, 1, st, Width::B32);
                self.fwrite(ins, 0, v, st, out);
            }
            M::Movapd | M::Movupd
                if has_xmm
                    && ins.op_kind(0) == OpKind::Register
                    && ins.op_kind(1) == OpKind::Register =>
            {
                let v = self.fread(ins, 1, st, Width::B64);
                self.fwrite(ins, 0, v, st, out);
            }
            // `xorps`/`xorpd xmm, xmm` with the same register is the zero-a-float idiom. (`pxor`
            // is the integer form and is handled by `lift_simd` as a zero vector.)
            M::Xorps | M::Xorpd
                if has_xmm
                    && ins.op_kind(0) == OpKind::Register
                    && ins.op_kind(1) == OpKind::Register
                    && ins.op_register(0) == ins.op_register(1) =>
            {
                let w = if m == M::Xorps {
                    Width::B32
                } else {
                    Width::B64
                };
                self.fwrite(ins, 0, Expr::FConst(0, w), st, out);
            }
            // `movd`/`movq` between a GPR and an XMM register reinterpret the bits as a float
            // (`f64::from_bits` / `.to_bits()`), e.g. returning a float computed in a GPR.
            M::Movd | M::Movq
                if ins.op_kind(0) == OpKind::Register && ins.op_kind(1) == OpKind::Register =>
            {
                let w = if m == M::Movq { Width::B64 } else { Width::B32 };
                let (r0, r1) = (ins.op_register(0), ins.op_register(1));
                match (xmm(r0), reg(r1), reg(r0), xmm(r1)) {
                    // GPR -> XMM: xmm = fN::from_bits(gpr).
                    (Some(_), Some((g, _)), _, _) => {
                        let name = if w == Width::B64 {
                            "f64::from_bits"
                        } else {
                            "f32::from_bits"
                        };
                        let bits = Expr::Var(Var::Reg(g), w);
                        self.fwrite(
                            ins,
                            0,
                            Expr::Call(CallTarget::Builtin(name), vec![bits]),
                            st,
                            out,
                        );
                    }
                    // XMM -> GPR: gpr = xmm.to_bits().
                    (_, _, Some((g, _)), Some(x)) => {
                        let fv = Expr::Var(Var::Xmm(x), w);
                        out.push((
                            ins.ip(),
                            Stmt::Assign(Var::Reg(g), Expr::method(fv, "to_bits", Vec::new(), w)),
                        ));
                    }
                    _ => return false,
                }
            }
            _ => return false,
        }
        true
    }

    /// Reads a packed-vector source operand: an XMM register (as the whole vector) or a memory
    /// load of `lanes`×`lane`.
    fn vread(&self, ins: &Instruction, op: u32, lanes: u8, lane: Lane, st: &State) -> Expr {
        match ins.op_kind(op) {
            OpKind::Register => match xmm(ins.op_register(op)) {
                Some(x) => Expr::Var(Var::Xmm(x), Width::B64),
                None => Expr::Unknown(String::from("vec")),
            },
            OpKind::Memory => match self.mem_addr(ins, st) {
                Ok(a) => Expr::VecLoad(Box::new(a), lanes, lane),
                Err((v, _)) => Expr::Var(v, Width::B64),
            },
            _ => Expr::Unknown(String::from("?")),
        }
    }

    /// Writes a packed-vector `value` to operand `op` (an XMM register or memory).
    fn vwrite(
        &self,
        ins: &Instruction,
        op: u32,
        value: Expr,
        st: &State,
        out: &mut Vec<(u64, Stmt)>,
    ) {
        let addr = ins.ip();
        match ins.op_kind(op) {
            OpKind::Register => {
                if let Some(x) = xmm(ins.op_register(op)) {
                    out.push((addr, Stmt::Assign(Var::Xmm(x), value)));
                }
            }
            OpKind::Memory => match self.mem_addr(ins, st) {
                Ok(a) => out.push((addr, Stmt::Store(a, value, Width::B64))),
                Err((v, _)) => out.push((addr, Stmt::Assign(v, value))),
            },
            _ => {}
        }
    }

    /// Lifts the common packed-integer SSE2 instructions (`paddd`, `pxor`, `movdqu`, `pshufd`, …)
    /// into packed-vector IR. Returns `true` if it handled the instruction. This is the vector-IR
    /// groundwork; a later pass folds a vectorised reduction into `s.iter().sum()`.
    fn lift_simd(&self, ins: &Instruction, st: &State, out: &mut Vec<(u64, Stmt)>) -> bool {
        use Mnemonic as M;
        let i32 = Lane::int(Width::B32);
        let (lanes, lane, op) = match ins.mnemonic() {
            // Packed integer arithmetic / logic.
            M::Paddb => (16u8, Lane::int(Width::B8), Some(BinOp::Add)),
            M::Psubb => (16, Lane::int(Width::B8), Some(BinOp::Sub)),
            M::Paddw => (8, Lane::int(Width::B16), Some(BinOp::Add)),
            M::Psubw => (8, Lane::int(Width::B16), Some(BinOp::Sub)),
            M::Pmullw => (8, Lane::int(Width::B16), Some(BinOp::Mul)),
            M::Paddd => (4, i32, Some(BinOp::Add)),
            M::Psubd => (4, i32, Some(BinOp::Sub)),
            M::Pmulld => (4, i32, Some(BinOp::Mul)),
            M::Paddq => (2, Lane::int(Width::B64), Some(BinOp::Add)),
            M::Psubq => (2, Lane::int(Width::B64), Some(BinOp::Sub)),
            M::Pand => (4, i32, Some(BinOp::And)),
            M::Por => (4, i32, Some(BinOp::Or)),
            M::Pxor => (4, i32, Some(BinOp::Xor)),
            // Packed single/double floating-point arithmetic (addps/mulps/divps …): same shape as
            // the integer ops but float lanes, so they render as `[f32; 4]` / `[f64; 2]`.
            M::Addps => (4, Lane::float(Width::B32), Some(BinOp::Add)),
            M::Subps => (4, Lane::float(Width::B32), Some(BinOp::Sub)),
            M::Mulps => (4, Lane::float(Width::B32), Some(BinOp::Mul)),
            M::Divps => (4, Lane::float(Width::B32), Some(BinOp::Div)),
            M::Addpd => (2, Lane::float(Width::B64), Some(BinOp::Add)),
            M::Subpd => (2, Lane::float(Width::B64), Some(BinOp::Sub)),
            M::Mulpd => (2, Lane::float(Width::B64), Some(BinOp::Mul)),
            M::Divpd => (2, Lane::float(Width::B64), Some(BinOp::Div)),
            // 128-bit moves. Integer domain (movdqa/movdqu) → int lanes; the float domain
            // (movaps/movups, movapd/movupd) → float lanes.
            M::Movdqu | M::Movdqa => {
                let v = self.vread(ins, 1, 4, i32, st);
                self.vwrite(ins, 0, v, st, out);
                return true;
            }
            M::Movups | M::Movaps => {
                let v = self.vread(ins, 1, 4, Lane::float(Width::B32), st);
                self.vwrite(ins, 0, v, st, out);
                return true;
            }
            M::Movupd | M::Movapd => {
                let v = self.vread(ins, 1, 2, Lane::float(Width::B64), st);
                self.vwrite(ins, 0, v, st, out);
                return true;
            }
            M::Pshufd => {
                let src = self.vread(ins, 1, 4, i32, st);
                self.vwrite(
                    ins,
                    0,
                    Expr::VecShuffle(Box::new(src), ins.immediate8(), 4, i32),
                    st,
                    out,
                );
                return true;
            }
            // Packed float max/min (`maxps`/`minps`, `maxpd`/`minpd`) — a direct lane-wise max/min.
            M::Maxps | M::Minps | M::Maxpd | M::Minpd => {
                let (n, l) = if matches!(ins.mnemonic(), M::Maxpd | M::Minpd) {
                    (2, Lane::float(Width::B64))
                } else {
                    (4, Lane::float(Width::B32))
                };
                let a = self.vread(ins, 0, n, l, st);
                let b = self.vread(ins, 1, n, l, st);
                let v = if matches!(ins.mnemonic(), M::Maxps | M::Maxpd) {
                    Expr::VecMax(Box::new(a), Box::new(b), n, l)
                } else {
                    Expr::VecMin(Box::new(a), Box::new(b), n, l)
                };
                self.vwrite(ins, 0, v, st, out);
                return true;
            }
            // `pcmpgtd dst, src` → a lane-wise greater-than mask; `pandn dst, src` → `!dst & src`.
            // These feed the compare-and-blend that `simplify::fold` recovers as `VecMax`/`VecMin`.
            M::Pcmpgtd | M::Pandn => {
                let a = self.vread(ins, 0, 4, i32, st);
                let b = self.vread(ins, 1, 4, i32, st);
                let v = if ins.mnemonic() == M::Pcmpgtd {
                    Expr::VecGt(Box::new(a), Box::new(b), 4, i32)
                } else {
                    Expr::VecAndn(Box::new(a), Box::new(b), 4, i32)
                };
                self.vwrite(ins, 0, v, st, out);
                return true;
            }
            _ => return false,
        };
        let Some(op) = op else {
            return false;
        };
        // `pxor xmm, xmm` with the same register zeroes it.
        if op == BinOp::Xor
            && ins.op_kind(0) == OpKind::Register
            && ins.op_kind(1) == OpKind::Register
            && ins.op_register(0) == ins.op_register(1)
        {
            self.vwrite(ins, 0, Expr::VecImm(0, lanes, lane), st, out);
            return true;
        }
        let a = self.vread(ins, 0, lanes, lane, st);
        let b = self.vread(ins, 1, lanes, lane, st);
        self.vwrite(
            ins,
            0,
            Expr::VecBin(op, Box::new(a), Box::new(b), lanes, lane),
            st,
            out,
        );
        true
    }

    /// An instruction the IR has no model for is kept as `asm!`.
    fn unmodeled(
        &self,
        ins: &Instruction,
        st: &mut State,
        out: &mut Vec<(u64, Stmt)>,
    ) -> Option<Term> {
        let addr = ins.ip();
        // The general-purpose registers the instruction reads and writes (including implicit
        // ones, e.g. `cpuid` reads eax and writes eax/ebx/ecx/edx with no explicit operands).
        let mut info = InstructionInfoFactory::new();
        let mut reads: std::collections::BTreeSet<u8> = Default::default();
        let mut writes: std::collections::BTreeSet<u8> = Default::default();
        for u in info.info(ins).used_registers() {
            let Some((r, _)) = reg(u.register().full_register()) else {
                continue;
            };
            if r == RSP || (r as usize) >= REG_NAMES.len() {
                continue;
            }
            match u.access() {
                OpAccess::Read | OpAccess::CondRead => {
                    reads.insert(r);
                }
                OpAccess::Write | OpAccess::CondWrite => {
                    writes.insert(r);
                }
                OpAccess::ReadWrite | OpAccess::ReadCondWrite => {
                    reads.insert(r);
                    writes.insert(r);
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        // rbx and rbp cannot be `asm!` operands (LLVM reserves them), so they get no operand and
        // their writes stay modelled as `reg = unknown(...)` afterwards.
        const RBX: u8 = 3;
        let can_bind = |r: u8| r != RBX && r != RBP;
        let mut ops = Vec::new();
        let all: std::collections::BTreeSet<u8> = reads.union(&writes).copied().collect();
        for &r in &all {
            if !can_bind(r) {
                continue;
            }
            let name = REG_NAMES[r as usize];
            let input = Expr::Var(Var::Reg(r), Width::B64);
            let output = Var::Reg(r);
            ops.push(match (reads.contains(&r), writes.contains(&r)) {
                (true, true) => AsmOp::InOut(name, input, output),
                (false, true) => AsmOp::Out(name, output),
                (true, false) => AsmOp::In(name, input),
                (false, false) => unreachable!(),
            });
        }
        out.push((addr, Stmt::Asm(format!("{ins}"), ops)));
        // Writes to registers that cannot be `asm!` operands are still unknown afterwards.
        let what = format!("{:?}", ins.mnemonic()).to_lowercase();
        for r in writes {
            if !can_bind(r) {
                out.push((addr, Stmt::Assign(Var::Reg(r), Expr::Unknown(what.clone()))));
            }
        }
        st.flags = None;
        None
    }
}

/// Partial-register fix. An x86 8/16-bit register write PRESERVES the upper bits (unlike a 32-bit
/// write, which zeroes them). The lifter models a narrow write as a plain replace, which is only
/// correct when those upper bits do not carry a meaningful live value. This pass rewrites a narrow
/// write to `(old & !mask) | (val & mask)` exactly when the register's upper bits are:
///   * DEFINED by a reaching write (a prior >=16-bit write, or a parameter at entry) — forward
///     max-merge dataflow; and
///   * LIVE — read later at a width > w before being fully redefined — backward liveness; and
///   * NOT known-zero — the reaching value is not a `xor r,r` / `mov r,0` zeroing — forward
///     and-merge dataflow (a zeroed register's upper bits are 0, so the clean replace is already
///     right, which also keeps bool/byte returns clean).
///
/// So `mov al,X; ret` (undefined), `setb al; movzx eax,al` (dead) and `xor eax,eax; setz al; ret`
/// (zeroed) all stay clean; only a genuine `mov eax,V; mov al,Y; <use eax>` gets the RMW.
pub fn restore_partial_writes(blocks: &mut [Block], entry: u64, params: &[u8]) {
    use std::collections::HashMap;
    // Register file size: x86-64 uses 0..16, ARM64 `x0`..`x30` plus 31 (sp/zr).
    const NREG: usize = 32;
    type State = [u8; NREG];
    type Flags = [bool; NREG];

    fn gen_reads(live: &mut State, e: &Expr) {
        e.walk(&mut |x| {
            if let Expr::Var(Var::Reg(r), w) = x {
                live[*r as usize] = live[*r as usize].max(w.0);
            }
        });
    }
    fn term_reads(live: &mut State, t: &Term) {
        match t {
            // NB: Return is deliberately excluded. The IR models a return as reading rax at 64
            // bits, but the real return width is the (not-yet-inferred) return type; counting it
            // would mark the upper bits of a bool/byte return live and wrap it in a spurious RMW.
            // A genuine wide use of a partially-written register is a computation, caught below.
            Term::Branch(e, ..) | Term::TailCall(e) | Term::Switch(e, _) => gen_reads(live, e),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    fn kill(live: &mut State, s: &Stmt) {
        match s {
            Stmt::Assign(Var::Reg(r), v) if v.width().0 >= 4 => live[*r as usize] = 0,
            Stmt::Assign(Var::Reg(_), _) => {}
            _ => {
                for d in s.defs() {
                    if let Var::Reg(r) = d {
                        live[r as usize] = 0;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    fn def_step(st: &mut State, s: &Stmt) {
        if let Stmt::Assign(Var::Reg(r), v) = s {
            let wv = v.width().0;
            st[*r as usize] = st[*r as usize].max(if wv >= 4 { 8 } else { wv });
        } else {
            for d in s.defs() {
                if let Var::Reg(r) = d {
                    st[r as usize] = 8;
                }
            }
        }
    }
    // A write that leaves the register all-zero: `mov r,0`, `xor r,r`, `sub r,r`.
    fn is_zero_write(v: &Expr) -> bool {
        match v {
            Expr::Const(0, _) => true,
            Expr::Bin(BinOp::Xor | BinOp::Sub, a, b, _) => a == b,
            _ => false,
        }
    }
    fn zero_step(z: &mut Flags, s: &Stmt) {
        if let Stmt::Assign(Var::Reg(r), v) = s {
            z[*r as usize] = is_zero_write(v);
        } else {
            for d in s.defs() {
                if let Var::Reg(r) = d {
                    z[r as usize] = false;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    let idx: HashMap<u64, usize> = blocks
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(i, b)| (b.addr, i))
        .collect();
    let n = blocks.len();
    let (mut preds, mut succs): (Vec<Vec<usize>>, Vec<Vec<usize>>) =
        (vec![Vec::new(); n], vec![Vec::new(); n]);
    for (i, b) in blocks.iter().enumerate() {
        for s in crate::simplify::successors(&b.term) {
            if let Some(&j) = idx.get(&s) {
                preds[j].push(i);
                succs[i].push(j);
            }
        }
    }
    let mut entry_def: State = [0; NREG];
    for &p in params {
        entry_def[p as usize] = 8;
    }

    let mut def_in = vec![[0u8; NREG]; n];
    let mut def_out = vec![[0u8; NREG]; n];
    let mut zero_in = vec![[false; NREG]; n];
    let mut zero_out = vec![[false; NREG]; n];
    let mut live_in = vec![[0u8; NREG]; n];
    let mut changed = true;
    while changed {
        changed = false;
        for i in 0..n {
            let mut d = if blocks[i].addr == entry {
                entry_def
            } else {
                [0u8; NREG]
            };
            for &p in &preds[i] {
                for r in 0..16 {
                    d[r] = d[r].max(def_out[p][r]);
                }
            }
            let mut z = if blocks[i].addr == entry || preds[i].is_empty() {
                [false; NREG]
            } else {
                [true; NREG]
            };
            for &p in &preds[i] {
                for r in 0..16 {
                    z[r] &= zero_out[p][r];
                }
            }
            if d != def_in[i] || z != zero_in[i] {
                def_in[i] = d;
                zero_in[i] = z;
                changed = true;
            }
            let (mut od, mut oz) = (def_in[i], zero_in[i]);
            for (_, s) in &blocks[i].stmts {
                def_step(&mut od, s);
                zero_step(&mut oz, s);
            }
            if od != def_out[i] || oz != zero_out[i] {
                def_out[i] = od;
                zero_out[i] = oz;
                changed = true;
            }
            let mut live = [0u8; NREG];
            for &j in &succs[i] {
                for r in 0..16 {
                    live[r] = live[r].max(live_in[j][r]);
                }
            }
            term_reads(&mut live, &blocks[i].term);
            for (_, s) in blocks[i].stmts.iter().rev() {
                kill(&mut live, s);
                for e in s.exprs() {
                    gen_reads(&mut live, e);
                }
            }
            if live != live_in[i] {
                live_in[i] = live;
                changed = true;
            }
        }
    }

    for i in 0..n {
        let mut live_out = [0u8; NREG];
        for &j in &succs[i] {
            for r in 0..16 {
                live_out[r] = live_out[r].max(live_in[j][r]);
            }
        }
        let mut live_after = vec![[0u8; NREG]; blocks[i].stmts.len()];
        {
            let mut live = live_out;
            term_reads(&mut live, &blocks[i].term);
            for k in (0..blocks[i].stmts.len()).rev() {
                live_after[k] = live;
                kill(&mut live, &blocks[i].stmts[k].1);
                for e in blocks[i].stmts[k].1.exprs() {
                    gen_reads(&mut live, e);
                }
            }
        }
        let (mut st, mut z) = (def_in[i], zero_in[i]);
        for (k, (_, s)) in blocks[i].stmts.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            if let Stmt::Assign(Var::Reg(r), v) = s {
                let w = v.width().0;
                if (w == 1 || w == 2)
                    && st[*r as usize] > w
                    && live_after[k][*r as usize] > w
                    && !z[*r as usize]
                {
                    let mask = Width(w).mask();
                    let old = Expr::Var(Var::Reg(*r), Width::B64);
                    let val = std::mem::replace(v, Expr::Unknown(String::new()));
                    *v = Expr::bin(
                        BinOp::Or,
                        Expr::bin(BinOp::And, old, Expr::konst(!mask, Width::B64), Width::B64),
                        Expr::bin(
                            BinOp::And,
                            Expr::Cast(Box::new(val), Width::B64, false),
                            Expr::konst(mask, Width::B64),
                            Width::B64,
                        ),
                        Width::B64,
                    );
                }
            }
            def_step(&mut st, s);
            zero_step(&mut z, s);
        }
    }
}

```

`crates/orress-decompiler/src/print.rs`:

```rs
//! Printing structured IR as Rust-syntax pseudocode, as coloured tokens with the
//! machine address each line came from (so the view can follow the cursor).

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashMap};

use orress_analysis::Program;

use crate::ir::*;
use crate::structure::Node;
use crate::types::{Signature, Ty, base_param};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum TokKind {
    Keyword,
    Type,
    /// A function name; `Span::target` holds its address.
    Function,
    Variable,
    Param,
    Number,
    Str,
    Comment,
    Punct,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Span {
    pub text: String,
    pub kind: TokKind,
    /// The address this token refers to (a function or global), for navigation.
    pub target: Option<u64>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct Line {
    /// The first machine instruction this line was produced from.
    pub addr: Option<u64>,
    pub indent: usize,
    pub spans: Vec<Span>,
}

impl Line {
    pub fn text(&self) -> String {
        let mut s = "    ".repeat(self.indent);
        for sp in &self.spans {
            s.push_str(&sp.text);
        }
        s
    }
}

pub struct Printer<'a> {
    pub program: &'a Program,
    pub sig: &'a Signature,
    pub locals: &'a BTreeMap<Var, (Width, bool)>,
    /// Local stack slots that hold a floating-point value (declared `f32`/`f64`).
    pub float_locals: &'a std::collections::BTreeSet<Var>,
    /// Locals that hold a packed vector, with their `[T; N]` shape (lanes, lane width).
    pub vec_locals: &'a std::collections::BTreeMap<Var, (u8, Lane)>,
    /// Locals that are slice indices/lengths, declared `usize`.
    pub usize_locals: &'a std::collections::BTreeSet<Var>,
    pub returns: bool,
    lines: Vec<Line>,
    cur: Line,
    indent: usize,
    /// Lengths of string literals, from the (pointer, length) pairs Rust passes around.
    str_lens: HashMap<u64, usize>,
    /// Port mode: emit compilable Rust (qualified `orress_rt::` helpers, real inline `asm!`)
    /// rather than readable pseudocode.
    port: bool,
    /// Element bindings of the enclosing `for x in s.iter_mut()` loops: a load/store through
    /// one of these prints as `*x` / `*x = v`.
    iter_mut: Vec<Var>,
}

/// Binding strength, higher binds tighter (Rust's operator precedence).
/// Whether any `BreakLabel`/`ContinueLabel` within `nodes` targets loop `header` (recursing into
/// nested control-flow), i.e. whether that loop needs a printed Rust label.
fn body_has_label(nodes: &[Node], header: u64) -> bool {
    nodes.iter().any(|n| match n {
        Node::BreakLabel(h) | Node::ContinueLabel(h) => *h == header,
        Node::If { then, els, .. } => body_has_label(then, header) || body_has_label(els, header),
        Node::Loop { body, .. } | Node::While { body, .. } | Node::For { body, .. } => {
            body_has_label(body, header)
        }
        Node::Match { arms, .. } => arms.iter().any(|(_, b)| body_has_label(b, header)),
        _ => false,
    })
}

fn prec(e: &Expr) -> u8 {
    match e {
        Expr::LOr(..) => 1,
        Expr::LAnd(..) => 2,
        Expr::Cmp(..) => 3,
        Expr::Bin(op, ..) => match op {
            BinOp::Or => 4,
            BinOp::Xor => 5,
            BinOp::And => 6,
            BinOp::Shl | BinOp::Shr | BinOp::Sar => 7,
            BinOp::Add | BinOp::Sub => 8,
            BinOp::Mul | BinOp::Div | BinOp::Rem => 9,
        },
        Expr::FCmp(..) => 3,
        Expr::FBin(op, ..) => match op {
            BinOp::Or => 4,
            BinOp::Xor => 5,
            BinOp::And => 6,
            BinOp::Shl | BinOp::Shr | BinOp::Sar => 7,
            BinOp::Add | BinOp::Sub => 8,
            BinOp::Mul | BinOp::Div | BinOp::Rem => 9,
        },
        Expr::Cast(..) | Expr::FCast(..) => 10,
        Expr::Neg(..) | Expr::Not(..) | Expr::LNot(..) | Expr::FUn(FUnOp::Neg, ..) => 11,
        Expr::Select(..) | Expr::Closure(..) => 0,
        _ => 12,
    }
}

pub fn param_name(i: usize) -> String {
    format!("a{}", i + 1)
}

/// A Rust float literal from raw bits, suffixed with its type (`3.5f64`, `1.5f32`), or a named
/// constant for a non-finite value.
fn float_literal(bits: u64, w: Width) -> String {
    let (v, ty) = if w.0 == 4 {
        (f64::from(f32::from_bits(bits as u32)), "f32")
    } else {
        (f64::from_bits(bits), "f64")
    };
    if !v.is_finite() {
        return if v.is_nan() {
            format!("{ty}::NAN")
        } else if v > 0.0 {
            format!("{ty}::INFINITY")
        } else {
            format!("{ty}::NEG_INFINITY")
        };
    }
    let mut s = format!("{v:?}");
    if !s.contains(['.', 'e', 'E']) {
        s.push_str(".0");
    }
    // `f64` is Rust's default float type, so a bare literal already infers it; only `f32`
    // literals need the suffix to type-check (and to read unambiguously).
    if ty == "f32" {
        s.push_str(ty);
    }
    s
}

fn escape(s: &str) -> String {
    s.chars().flat_map(char::escape_default).collect()
}

impl<'a> Printer<'a> {
    pub fn new(
        program: &'a Program,
        sig: &'a Signature,
        locals: &'a BTreeMap<Var, (Width, bool)>,
        float_locals: &'a std::collections::BTreeSet<Var>,
        vec_locals: &'a std::collections::BTreeMap<Var, (u8, Lane)>,
        usize_locals: &'a std::collections::BTreeSet<Var>,
        returns: bool,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            program,
            sig,
            locals,
            float_locals,
            vec_locals,
            usize_locals,
            returns,
            lines: Vec::new(),
            cur: Line::default(),
            indent: 0,
            str_lens: HashMap::new(),
            port: false,
            iter_mut: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Switches to port mode: the output is a compilable Rust scaffold.
    pub fn port_mode(mut self) -> Self {
        self.port = true;
        self
    }

    /// The module path prefix for memory helpers (`orress_rt::` in port mode, nothing otherwise).
    fn rt(&self) -> &'static str {
        if self.port { "orress_rt::" } else { "" }
    }

    fn tok(&mut self, text: impl Into<String>, kind: TokKind) {
        self.cur.spans.push(Span {
            text: text.into(),
            kind,
            target: None,
        });
    }

    fn link(&mut self, text: impl Into<String>, kind: TokKind, target: u64) {
        self.cur.spans.push(Span {
            text: text.into(),
            kind,
            target: Some(target),
        });
    }

    fn p(&mut self, text: &str) {
        self.tok(text, TokKind::Punct);
    }

    fn kw(&mut self, text: &str) {
        self.tok(text, TokKind::Keyword);
    }

    fn start(&mut self, addr: Option<u64>) {
        self.cur.addr = addr;
        self.cur.indent = self.indent;
    }

    fn end(&mut self) {
        let line = std::mem::take(&mut self.cur);
        self.lines.push(line);
    }

    /// A variable's printed name. Registers are named per architecture (ARM64 `x0`… vs x86
    /// `rax`…); stack slots and synthesised bindings are architecture-neutral.
    fn var_name(&self, v: &Var) -> String {
        match v {
            _ if self.program.isa != orress_analysis::Isa::Arm64 => v.to_string(),
            Var::Reg(r) => format!("x{r}"),
            Var::Split(r, v) => format!("x{r}_{v}"),
            Var::Xmm(r) => format!("d{r}"),
            Var::XmmSplit(r, v) => format!("d{r}_{v}"),
            _ => v.to_string(),
        }
    }

    fn func_name(&self, addr: u64) -> String {
        self.program
            .name(addr)
            .map_or_else(|| format!("sub_{addr:x}"), |n| n.text.clone())
    }

    fn number(&mut self, v: u64, w: Width) {
        // Print the true unsigned value. An all-ones constant is NOT rendered as `-1` here: this
        // path has no signedness context, and `-1` is wrong (value and port type) in an unsigned
        // position such as `x & 0xffffffff` or an unsigned `x == 0xff`. Signed contexts that want a
        // negative literal (e.g. a signed comparison) render it themselves before calling here.
        let _ = w;
        let text = if v < 10 {
            v.to_string()
        } else if v >= 0x100 || v.is_multiple_of(0x10) && v >= 0x10 {
            format!("{v:#x}")
        } else {
            v.to_string()
        };
        self.tok(text, TokKind::Number);
    }

    fn byte_or_number(&mut self, e: &Expr) {
        if let Expr::Const(v, w) = e
            && w.0 == 1
            && (0x20..0x7f).contains(v)
        {
            let c = char::from(*v as u8);
            let lit = match c {
                '\'' => "b'\\''".to_owned(),
                '\\' => "b'\\\\'".to_owned(),
                c => format!("b'{c}'"),
            };
            self.tok(lit, TokKind::Str);
            return;
        }
        self.expr(e, 0);
    }

    fn param(&mut self, i: usize) {
        let ty = self.sig.params.get(i);
        if ty == Some(&Ty::SliceLen) && i > 0 {
            self.tok(param_name(i - 1), TokKind::Param);
            self.p(".");
            self.tok("len", TokKind::Function);
            self.p("()");
        } else {
            self.tok(param_name(i), TokKind::Param);
        }
    }

    /// Whether an inline-asm input value can be bound: a constant, parameter or computed value
    /// that simplification resolved to a register-sized integer. A bare register that stayed
    /// unresolved has no known value (risking an uninitialised-variable port), and a non-integer
    /// parameter (a slice or reference) is not a register value, so both are left unbound.
    fn asm_input_ok(&self, e: &Expr) -> bool {
        match e {
            Expr::Var(Var::Reg(_), _) => false,
            Expr::Param(i, _) => matches!(self.sig.params.get(*i), Some(Ty::Int(..)) | None),
            _ => true,
        }
    }

    /// Prints an inline-asm input value cast to the register width (`… as u64`), so the input
    /// type matches the output register.
    fn asm_input(&mut self, e: &Expr) {
        self.expr(e, 11);
        self.kw(" as ");
        self.tok("u64", TokKind::Type);
    }

    /// Prints a slice index expression — cast to `usize` in port mode (a slice index must be
    /// `usize`, but the recovered arithmetic is a register width). Readable mode keeps `x`.
    fn idx(&mut self, e: &Expr) {
        if self.port {
            self.expr(e, 11);
            self.kw(" as ");
            self.tok("usize", TokKind::Type);
        } else {
            self.expr(e, 0);
        }
    }

    /// If `addr` is a slice parameter plus some byte offset, returns that parameter's index and
    /// the offset expression (a vector access base that should read/write slice-relatively).
    fn vec_slice_base(&self, addr: &Expr) -> Option<(usize, Expr)> {
        fn peel(e: &Expr) -> Option<(usize, Expr)> {
            match e {
                Expr::Param(i, _) => Some((*i, Expr::konst(0, Width::B64))),
                Expr::Bin(BinOp::Add, a, b, w) => peel(a)
                    .map(|(i, off)| (i, Expr::bin(BinOp::Add, off, (**b).clone(), *w)))
                    .or_else(|| {
                        peel(b).map(|(i, off)| (i, Expr::bin(BinOp::Add, off, (**a).clone(), *w)))
                    }),
                _ => None,
            }
        }
        let (i, off) = peel(addr)?;
        matches!(self.sig.params.get(i), Some(Ty::Slice(..))).then_some((i, off))
    }

    /// Prints a vector access's element index from its byte offset: `(off / elem) as usize`,
    /// or `0` when the offset is zero.
    fn vec_index(&mut self, byte_off: &Expr, elem: Width) {
        let byte_off = crate::simplify::fold(byte_off.clone());
        if matches!(byte_off, Expr::Const(0, _)) {
            self.number(0, Width::B64);
            return;
        }
        self.p("(");
        self.expr(&byte_off, 9);
        self.p(" / ");
        self.number(u64::from(elem.0), Width::B64);
        self.p(")");
        self.kw(" as ");
        self.tok("usize", TokKind::Type);
    }

    /// `s[i]` for an element read from a slice / reference parameter.
    fn element(&mut self, addr: &Expr, w: Width) -> bool {
        let Some((i, off)) = base_param(addr) else {
            return false;
        };
        match self.sig.params.get(i) {
            Some(Ty::Slice(ew, _, _, _)) if *ew == w => {
                self.tok(param_name(i), TokKind::Param);
                self.p("[");
                match off {
                    None => self.number(0, Width::B64),
                    Some(Expr::Const(k, cw)) => self.number(k / u64::from(w.0), *cw),
                    Some(Expr::Bin(BinOp::Mul, x, k, _)) if matches!(&**k, Expr::Const(n, _) if *n == u64::from(w.0)) => {
                        self.idx(x)
                    }
                    Some(x) if w.0 == 1 => self.idx(x),
                    Some(x) => {
                        // A scaled offset `x / w`, cast to `usize` in port mode.
                        if self.port {
                            self.p("(");
                        }
                        self.expr(x, 9);
                        self.p(" / ");
                        self.number(u64::from(w.0), Width::B64);
                        if self.port {
                            self.p(")");
                            self.kw(" as ");
                            self.tok("usize", TokKind::Type);
                        }
                    }
                }
                self.p("]");
                true
            }
            Some(Ty::Ref(rw, _)) if *rw == w && off.is_none() => {
                self.p("*");
                self.tok(param_name(i), TokKind::Param);
                true
            }
            // `p.field_8` for a field access of a struct pointer parameter.
            Some(Ty::Struct(layout, _)) => {
                let o = match off {
                    None => 0,
                    Some(Expr::Const(k, _)) => *k,
                    _ => return false,
                };
                let Some(f) = layout.fields.iter().find(|f| f.offset == o && f.width == w) else {
                    return false;
                };
                self.tok(param_name(i), TokKind::Param);
                self.p(".");
                self.tok(layout.field_name(f), TokKind::Variable);
                true
            }
            _ => false,
        }
    }

    pub fn expr(&mut self, e: &Expr, min: u8) {
        let paren = prec(e) < min;
        if paren {
            self.p("(");
        }
        match e {
            Expr::Const(v, w) => self.number(*v, *w),
            Expr::Var(v, _) => self.tok(self.var_name(v), TokKind::Variable),
            Expr::Param(i, _) => self.param(*i),
            Expr::Load(a, w) => {
                if let Expr::Var(v, _) = &**a
                    && self.iter_mut.contains(v)
                {
                    // `*x` for a read through an `iter_mut` element binding.
                    self.p("*");
                    self.tok(self.var_name(v), TokKind::Variable);
                } else if !self.element(a, *w) {
                    self.tok(format!("{}read", self.rt()), TokKind::Function);
                    self.p("::<");
                    self.tok(w.rust(false), TokKind::Type);
                    self.p(">(");
                    self.expr(a, 0);
                    self.p(")");
                }
            }
            Expr::Bin(op, a, b, _) => {
                let pr = prec(e);
                // `Sar` is an arithmetic shift-right; Rust `>>` is arithmetic only when the left
                // operand is signed, so cast it (`(a as iN) >> b`). `Shr` stays logical.
                if matches!(op, BinOp::Sar) {
                    self.signed(a);
                } else {
                    self.value(a, pr);
                }
                self.p(&format!(" {} ", op.symbol()));
                self.value(b, pr + 1);
            }
            Expr::Neg(a, _) => {
                self.p("-");
                self.expr(a, 11);
            }
            Expr::Not(a, _) => {
                self.p("!");
                self.expr(a, 11);
            }
            Expr::LNot(a) => {
                self.p("!");
                self.expr(a, 11);
            }
            Expr::Cmp(op, a, b, signed) => {
                let (a, b) = (strip_trivial_cast(a), strip_trivial_cast(b));
                // In a signed comparison the left operand must be signed. Type inference already
                // types plain Var/Param operands (`mark_signed_cmps`), but not a Load or other
                // expression — cast those explicitly, including when the RHS is a constant (the
                // `x < 5` signed case, which previously printed an unsigned compare).
                if *signed
                    && (!matches!(a, Expr::Var(..) | Expr::Param(..))
                        || !matches!(b, Expr::Const(..)))
                {
                    self.signed(a);
                } else {
                    self.expr(a, 4);
                }
                self.p(&format!(" {} ", op.symbol()));
                if *signed && matches!(b, Expr::Const(v, w) if *v > w.mask() >> 1) {
                    // Negative constant in a signed comparison.
                    if let Expr::Const(v, w) = b {
                        let neg = (w.mask() - v + 1) & w.mask();
                        self.tok(format!("-{neg}"), TokKind::Number);
                    }
                } else if *signed && !matches!(b, Expr::Const(..)) {
                    self.signed(b);
                } else {
                    self.byte_or_number_at(b, 4);
                }
            }
            Expr::LAnd(a, b) => {
                self.expr(a, 2);
                self.p(" && ");
                self.expr(b, 3);
            }
            Expr::LOr(a, b) => {
                self.expr(a, 1);
                self.p(" || ");
                self.expr(b, 2);
            }
            // The low half of a call result (`eax` after a call) is just the call — but in
            // port mode keep the `as` cast, since the stub returns a fixed-width `u64`.
            Expr::Cast(a, _, _) if !self.port && matches!(&**a, Expr::Call(..)) => {
                self.expr(a, min)
            }
            // A signed cast of a parameter already of that signed type is redundant (e.g. a
            // signed-division operand whose parameter was inferred `iN`).
            Expr::Cast(a, w, true)
                if matches!(&**a, Expr::Param(i, pw)
                    if pw == w && self.sig.params.get(*i) == Some(&Ty::Int(*w, true))) =>
            {
                if let Expr::Param(i, _) = &**a {
                    self.param(*i);
                }
            }
            Expr::Cast(a, w, s) => {
                self.expr(a, 10);
                self.kw(" as ");
                self.tok(w.rust(*s), TokKind::Type);
            }
            Expr::Call(t, args) => self.call(t, args),
            Expr::Addr(a) => self.global(*a),
            Expr::StackAddr(off) => {
                self.p("&mut ");
                self.tok(Var::Stack(*off).to_string(), TokKind::Variable);
            }
            Expr::Select(c, a, b, _) => {
                self.kw("if ");
                self.expr(c, 0);
                self.p(" { ");
                self.expr(a, 0);
                self.p(" } ");
                self.kw("else");
                self.p(" { ");
                self.expr(b, 0);
                self.p(" }");
            }
            // `movd eax, xmm` (lifted as `xmm.to_bits()`) where `xmm` is a vector local extracts
            // lane 0.
            Expr::Method(recv, "to_bits", args, _)
                if args.is_empty()
                    && matches!(&**recv, Expr::Var(v, _) if self.vec_locals.contains_key(v)) =>
            {
                self.value(recv, 12);
                self.p("[0]");
            }
            Expr::Method(recv, name, args, _) => {
                // The receiver binds tightest; parenthesise it if it's looser. A `Load` can
                // render as a deref (`*a1`), which must be parenthesised before `.method()`.
                if matches!(&**recv, Expr::Load(..)) {
                    self.p("(");
                    self.expr(recv, 0);
                    self.p(")");
                } else {
                    self.value(recv, 12);
                }
                self.p(".");
                self.tok(*name, TokKind::Function);
                self.p("(");
                for (i, a) in args.iter().enumerate() {
                    if i > 0 {
                        self.p(", ");
                    }
                    self.expr(a, 0);
                }
                self.p(")");
            }
            Expr::Closure(params, body) => {
                self.p("|");
                for (i, (v, by_ref)) in params.iter().enumerate() {
                    if i > 0 {
                        self.p(", ");
                    }
                    if *by_ref {
                        self.p("&");
                    }
                    self.tok(self.var_name(v), TokKind::Variable);
                }
                self.p("| ");
                self.expr(body, 0);
            }
            Expr::FConst(bits, w) => {
                self.tok(float_literal(*bits, *w), TokKind::Number);
            }
            Expr::FBin(op, a, b, _) => {
                let pr = prec(e);
                self.fexpr(a, pr);
                self.p(&format!(" {} ", op.symbol()));
                self.fexpr(b, pr + 1);
            }
            Expr::FUn(FUnOp::Neg, a, _) => {
                self.p("-");
                self.fexpr(a, 11);
            }
            Expr::FUn(op, a, _) => {
                self.fexpr(a, 12);
                self.p(".");
                self.tok(
                    if *op == FUnOp::Abs { "abs" } else { "sqrt" },
                    TokKind::Function,
                );
                self.p("()");
            }
            Expr::FCmp(op, a, b) => {
                self.fexpr(a, 4);
                self.p(&format!(" {} ", op.symbol()));
                self.fexpr(b, 4);
            }
            // Float → float (`cvtss2sd`): `x as f64`. Int → float and float → int are the same
            // `as` surface syntax; the result width and kind pick the target type.
            Expr::FCast(a, w, kind) => {
                let ty = match kind {
                    FCast::FloatToSInt => w.rust(true),
                    FCast::SIntToFloat | FCast::FloatToFloat => {
                        if w.0 == 4 {
                            "f32"
                        } else {
                            "f64"
                        }
                    }
                };
                // Int → float casts from a plain integer operand; float → * from a float one.
                if matches!(kind, FCast::SIntToFloat) {
                    self.expr(a, 10);
                } else {
                    self.fexpr(a, 10);
                }
                self.kw(" as ");
                self.tok(ty, TokKind::Type);
            }
            // Packed-vector (SIMD) values, modelled as `[T; N]` lane arrays with `orress_rt`
            // element-wise helpers (the vector-IR groundwork; a later pass folds a vectorised
            // reduction into `.iter().sum()`).
            Expr::VecImm(v, n, w) => {
                self.p("[");
                self.number(*v, w.width);
                self.kw(" as ");
                self.tok(w.rust(), TokKind::Type);
                self.p(&format!("; {n}]"));
            }
            Expr::VecSplat(a, n, w) => {
                self.p("[");
                self.expr(a, 10);
                self.kw(" as ");
                self.tok(w.rust(), TokKind::Type);
                self.p(&format!("; {n}]"));
            }
            Expr::VecLoad(a, n, w) => {
                // A vector load whose base is a slice parameter reads slice-relatively
                // (`vload_slice(a1, i)`), so the one `&[T]` type serves the vector and element
                // uses; otherwise it is a raw-address load.
                if let Some((i, byte_off)) = self.vec_slice_base(a) {
                    self.tok(format!("{}vload_slice", self.rt()), TokKind::Function);
                    self.p("::<");
                    self.tok(w.rust(), TokKind::Type);
                    self.p(&format!(", {n}>("));
                    self.tok(param_name(i), TokKind::Param);
                    self.p(", ");
                    self.vec_index(&byte_off, w.width);
                    self.p(")");
                } else {
                    self.tok(format!("{}vload", self.rt()), TokKind::Function);
                    self.p("::<");
                    self.tok(w.rust(), TokKind::Type);
                    self.p(&format!(", {n}>("));
                    self.expr(a, 0);
                    self.p(")");
                }
            }
            Expr::VecBin(op, a, b, _, _) => {
                let name = match op {
                    BinOp::Add => "vadd",
                    BinOp::Sub => "vsub",
                    BinOp::Mul => "vmul",
                    BinOp::Div => "vdiv",
                    BinOp::And => "vand",
                    BinOp::Or => "vor",
                    _ => "vxor",
                };
                self.tok(format!("{}{name}", self.rt()), TokKind::Function);
                self.p("(");
                self.expr(a, 0);
                self.p(", ");
                self.expr(b, 0);
                self.p(")");
            }
            Expr::VecShuffle(a, imm, _, w) => {
                self.tok(format!("{}vshuffle", self.rt()), TokKind::Function);
                self.p("::<");
                self.tok(w.rust(), TokKind::Type);
                self.p(">(");
                self.expr(a, 0);
                self.p(", ");
                self.number(u64::from(*imm), Width::B8);
                self.p(")");
            }
            Expr::VecExtract(a, lane, _) => {
                self.value(a, 12);
                self.p(&format!("[{lane}]"));
            }
            // Packed lane-wise max/min and the compare/blend primitives.
            Expr::VecMax(a, b, _, _) => self.vec_call("vmax", a, b),
            Expr::VecMin(a, b, _, _) => self.vec_call("vmin", a, b),
            Expr::VecGt(a, b, _, _) => self.vec_call("vgt", a, b),
            Expr::VecAndn(a, b, _, _) => self.vec_call("vandn", a, b),
            // A horizontal lane reduction: `v.iter().sum::<T>()` / `.product::<T>()`, or
            // `v.iter().copied().max()/.min().unwrap()` (a lane array is non-empty, so `unwrap`).
            Expr::VecReduce(op, a, w) => {
                self.value(a, 12);
                self.p(".");
                self.tok("iter", TokKind::Function);
                self.p("()");
                match op {
                    ReduceOp::Add | ReduceOp::Mul => {
                        self.p(".");
                        let name = if *op == ReduceOp::Mul {
                            "product"
                        } else {
                            "sum"
                        };
                        self.tok(name, TokKind::Function);
                        self.p("::<");
                        self.tok(w.rust(), TokKind::Type);
                        self.p(">()");
                    }
                    ReduceOp::Max | ReduceOp::Min => {
                        self.p(".");
                        self.tok("copied", TokKind::Function);
                        self.p("().");
                        self.tok(
                            if *op == ReduceOp::Max { "max" } else { "min" },
                            TokKind::Function,
                        );
                        self.p("().");
                        self.tok("unwrap", TokKind::Function);
                        self.p("()");
                    }
                }
            }
            Expr::Unknown(s) => {
                let what = if s == "clobbered" {
                    "changed by the call above"
                } else {
                    s.as_str()
                };
                self.tok(format!("{}unknown", self.rt()), TokKind::Function);
                self.p("(");
                self.tok(format!("\"{}\"", escape(what)), TokKind::Str);
                self.p(")");
            }
        }
        if paren {
            self.p(")");
        }
    }

    /// Prints an expression known to be floating-point. A raw memory `Load` becomes a typed
    /// float read (`read::<f64>(addr)`); every other float value already carries its type (a
    /// float node, a float parameter, a register value), so it prints normally.
    fn fexpr(&mut self, e: &Expr, min: u8) {
        if let Expr::Load(a, w) = e {
            // A float element of a float slice parameter reads as `s[i]` (already `f32`/`f64`),
            // not a raw `read::<f32>(ptr)`.
            if self.is_float_slice_base(a) && self.element(a, *w) {
                return;
            }
            self.tok(format!("{}read", self.rt()), TokKind::Function);
            self.p("::<");
            self.tok(if w.0 == 4 { "f32" } else { "f64" }, TokKind::Type);
            self.p(">(");
            self.expr(a, 0);
            self.p(")");
        } else {
            self.expr(e, min);
        }
    }

    /// Whether `addr` is an element of a floating-point slice parameter (`&[f32]` / `&[f64]`).
    fn is_float_slice_base(&self, addr: &Expr) -> bool {
        base_param(addr)
            .is_some_and(|(i, _)| matches!(self.sig.params.get(i), Some(Ty::Slice(_, _, true, _))))
    }

    /// A two-operand packed-vector helper call `rt::name(a, b)`.
    fn vec_call(&mut self, name: &str, a: &Expr, b: &Expr) {
        self.tok(format!("{}{name}", self.rt()), TokKind::Function);
        self.p("(");
        self.expr(a, 0);
        self.p(", ");
        self.expr(b, 0);
        self.p(")");
    }

    /// A condition used as a number: `(a < b) as u64`.
    fn value(&mut self, e: &Expr, min: u8) {
        if e.is_condition() {
            self.p("(");
            self.expr(e, 0);
            self.p(")");
            self.kw(" as ");
            self.tok("u64", TokKind::Type);
        } else {
            self.expr(e, min);
        }
    }

    fn byte_or_number_at(&mut self, e: &Expr, min: u8) {
        if matches!(e, Expr::Const(..)) {
            self.byte_or_number(e);
        } else {
            self.expr(e, min);
        }
    }

    fn signed(&mut self, e: &Expr) {
        match e {
            Expr::Param(i, w) if matches!(self.sig.params.get(*i), Some(Ty::Int(_, true))) => {
                let _ = w;
                self.param(*i);
            }
            Expr::Const(..) => self.expr(e, 4),
            other => {
                // Parenthesize the cast: as a comparison LHS, `x as i32 < y` is otherwise parsed
                // by Rust as generic arguments to `i32` and fails to compile.
                self.p("(");
                self.expr(other, 10);
                self.kw(" as ");
                self.tok(other.width().rust(true), TokKind::Type);
                self.p(")");
            }
        }
    }

    fn global(&mut self, a: u64) {
        if let Some(s) = self.program.string_refs.get(&a) {
            let text = match self.str_lens.get(&a) {
                Some(&n) if n <= s.len() && s.is_char_boundary(n) => s[..n].to_owned(),
                // One past the end: the text ended in a newline the string scan stopped at.
                Some(&n) if n == s.len() + 1 => format!(
                    "{s}
"
                ),
                _ => s.clone(),
            };
            self.link(format!("\"{}\"", escape(&text)), TokKind::Str, a);
        } else if let Some(n) = self.program.name(a) {
            let text = n.text.clone();
            let kind = if self.program.functions.contains_key(&a) {
                TokKind::Function
            } else {
                TokKind::Variable
            };
            if kind == TokKind::Variable {
                self.p("&");
            }
            self.link(text, kind, a);
        } else if self.program.functions.contains_key(&a) {
            self.link(format!("sub_{a:x}"), TokKind::Function, a);
        } else {
            self.p("&");
            self.link(format!("data_{a:x}"), TokKind::Variable, a);
        }
    }

    fn call(&mut self, t: &CallTarget, args: &[Expr]) {
        match t {
            CallTarget::Direct(a) | CallTarget::Import(a) => {
                let name = self.func_name(*a);
                self.link(name, TokKind::Function, *a);
            }
            CallTarget::Indirect(e) => {
                self.p("(");
                self.expr(e, 0);
                self.p(")");
            }
            CallTarget::Builtin(name) => self.tok(*name, TokKind::Function),
        }
        self.p("(");
        for (i, a) in args.iter().enumerate() {
            if i > 0 {
                self.p(", ");
            }
            self.expr(a, 0);
        }
        self.p(")");
    }

    fn stmt(&mut self, addr: u64, s: &Stmt) {
        self.start(Some(addr));
        match s {
            Stmt::Assign(v, e) => {
                self.tok(self.var_name(v), TokKind::Variable);
                // `x = x + 1` -> `x += 1`
                if let Expr::Bin(op, a, b, _) = e
                    && matches!(&**a, Expr::Var(av, _) if av == v)
                    && !matches!(op, BinOp::Sar)
                {
                    self.p(&format!(" {}= ", op.symbol()));
                    if b.is_condition() {
                        self.value(b, 0);
                    } else {
                        self.byte_or_number_at(b, 0);
                    }
                } else {
                    self.p(" = ");
                    self.value(e, 0);
                }
            }
            Stmt::Store(a, v, w) => {
                if let Expr::Var(bind, _) = a
                    && self.iter_mut.contains(bind)
                {
                    // `*x = v` for a write through an `iter_mut` element binding.
                    self.p("*");
                    self.tok(self.var_name(bind), TokKind::Variable);
                    // `*x = *x OP k` → `*x OP= k` (the read is the deref of the same binding).
                    let deref_of_bind = |e: &Expr| {
                        matches!(e, Expr::Load(la, _)
                            if matches!(&**la, Expr::Var(b2, _) if b2 == bind))
                    };
                    match v {
```
