```rs
#[test]
fn vectorised_max_blend_folds_to_reduction() {
    // The full integer max pipeline: the SSE2 compare-and-blend (pcmpgtd/pand/pandn/por) lifts to
    // `VecMax`, and the semantic reducer then proves the whole function is a slice max and folds it
    // to `s.iter().copied().reduce(|a, b| a.max(b)).unwrap()` — the vector scaffold is discarded.
    let code: &[u8] = &[
        0x8b, 0x07, 0x83, 0xfe, 0x02, 0x0f, 0x82, 0xe5, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x89, 0xf1, 0xba, 0x01,
        0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x83, 0xfe, 0x09, 0x0f, 0x82, 0xc5, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x48, 0x8d, 0x71,
        0xff, 0x49, 0x89, 0xf0, 0x49, 0x83, 0xe0, 0xf8, 0x49, 0x8d, 0x50, 0x01, 0x66, 0x0f, 0x6e,
        0xc0, 0x66, 0x0f, 0x70, 0xc0, 0x00, 0x31, 0xc0, 0x66, 0x0f, 0x6f, 0xc8, 0x0f, 0x1f, 0x80,
        0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xf3, 0x0f, 0x6f, 0x54, 0x87, 0x04, 0xf3, 0x0f, 0x6f, 0x5c, 0x87,
        0x14, 0x66, 0x0f, 0x6f, 0xe2, 0x66, 0x0f, 0x66, 0xe0, 0x66, 0x0f, 0xdb, 0xd4, 0x66, 0x0f,
        0xdf, 0xe0, 0x66, 0x0f, 0x6f, 0xc4, 0x66, 0x0f, 0xeb, 0xc2, 0x66, 0x0f, 0x6f, 0xd3, 0x66,
        0x0f, 0x66, 0xd1, 0x66, 0x0f, 0xdb, 0xda, 0x66, 0x0f, 0xdf, 0xd1, 0x66, 0x0f, 0x6f, 0xca,
        0x66, 0x0f, 0xeb, 0xcb, 0x48, 0x83, 0xc0, 0x08, 0x49, 0x39, 0xc0, 0x75, 0xbb, 0x66, 0x0f,
        0x6f, 0xd0, 0x66, 0x0f, 0x66, 0xd1, 0x66, 0x0f, 0xdb, 0xc2, 0x66, 0x0f, 0xdf, 0xd1, 0x66,
        0x0f, 0xeb, 0xd0, 0x66, 0x0f, 0x70, 0xc2, 0xee, 0x66, 0x0f, 0x6f, 0xca, 0x66, 0x0f, 0x66,
        0xc8, 0x66, 0x0f, 0xdb, 0xd1, 0x66, 0x0f, 0xdf, 0xc8, 0x66, 0x0f, 0xeb, 0xca, 0x66, 0x0f,
        0x70, 0xc1, 0x55, 0x66, 0x0f, 0x6f, 0xd1, 0x66, 0x0f, 0x66, 0xd0, 0x66, 0x0f, 0xdb, 0xca,
        0x66, 0x0f, 0xdf, 0xd0, 0x66, 0x0f, 0xeb, 0xd1, 0x66, 0x0f, 0x7e, 0xd0, 0x4c, 0x39, 0xc6,
        0x74, 0x1c, 0x66, 0x66, 0x66, 0x2e, 0x0f, 0x1f, 0x84, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x8b,
        0x34, 0x97, 0x39, 0xc6, 0x0f, 0x4f, 0xc6, 0x48, 0xff, 0xc2, 0x48, 0x39, 0xd1, 0x75, 0xf0,
        0xc3,
    ];
    let text = decompiled(&[("maxv", code)], 0);
    // The whole function folds to a slice max reduction (proving blend → VecMax → reduction).
    assert!(
        text.contains("fn maxv(a1: &[i32]) -> i32"),
        "signature wrong:\n{text}"
    );
    assert!(
        text.contains("a1.iter().copied().reduce(|a, b| a.max(b)).unwrap()"),
        "max reduction not recovered:\n{text}"
    );
    // The vector scaffold, blend ops and raw asm are all discarded.
    assert!(
        !text.contains("loop") && !text.contains("vmax(") && !text.contains("vgt("),
        "scaffold not discarded:\n{text}"
    );
    assert!(
        !text.contains("pcmpgtd") && !text.contains("asm!(\"pand"),
        "{text}"
    );
    assert!(
        rustc_compiles(&ported(&[("maxv", code)], 0)),
        "folded max port must compile"
    );
}

#[test]
fn packed_float_elementwise_multiply() {
    // clang -O2 of `void mulv(float* c, const float* a, const float* b, unsigned n)` with
    // `c[i] = a[i] * b[i]`: a packed `mulps` loop (movups/mulps/movups) + a scalar `mulss` tail.
    // The packed body lifts to `vmul` over **f32** lanes (not u32) — the packed-float lifting.
    // (Typing the slice parameters themselves as `&[f32]` so the whole port compiles is the next
    // step: it needs float-aware slice inference and float scalar-tail indexing.)
    let code: &[u8] = &[
        0x85, 0xC9, 0x74, 0x63, 0x89, 0xC8, 0x83, 0xF9, 0x04, 0x73, 0x04, 0x31, 0xC9, 0xEB, 0x41,
        0x89, 0xC1, 0x83, 0xE1, 0xFC, 0x4C, 0x8D, 0x04, 0x85, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x49, 0x83,
        0xE0, 0xF0, 0x45, 0x31, 0xC9, 0x66, 0x66, 0x66, 0x66, 0x2E, 0x0F, 0x1F, 0x84, 0x00, 0x00,
        0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x42, 0x0F, 0x10, 0x04, 0x0E, 0x42, 0x0F, 0x10, 0x0C, 0x0A, 0x0F, 0x59,
        0xC8, 0x42, 0x0F, 0x11, 0x0C, 0x0F, 0x49, 0x83, 0xC1, 0x10, 0x4D, 0x39, 0xC8, 0x75, 0xE5,
        0x39, 0xC1, 0x74, 0x18, 0x90, 0xF3, 0x0F, 0x10, 0x04, 0x8E, 0xF3, 0x0F, 0x59, 0x04, 0x8A,
        0xF3, 0x0F, 0x11, 0x04, 0x8F, 0x48, 0xFF, 0xC1, 0x48, 0x39, 0xC8, 0x75, 0xE9, 0xC3, 0x0F,
        0x1F, 0x84, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
    ];
    let text = decompiled(&[("mulv", code)], 0);
    // The packed float multiply lifts to `vmul` over f32 lanes (vload_slice typed `::<f32, 4>`),
    // not an integer op and not left as inline asm.
    assert!(
        text.contains("vmul("),
        "packed float multiply not lifted:\n{text}"
    );
    assert!(
        text.contains("vload_slice::<f32, 4>"),
        "float vector load not typed f32:\n{text}"
    );
    assert!(!text.contains("asm!(\"mulps"), "mulps left as asm:\n{text}");
    // The slice parameters are typed as float slices from the packed-float access…
    assert!(
        text.contains("&mut [f32]") && text.contains("&[f32]"),
        "slices not typed f32:\n{text}"
    );
    // …and the scalar remainder reads/writes them as float slice elements (`a[i]`), not raw
    // `read::<f32>(ptr + i*4)`.
    assert!(
        text.contains("a2[rcx_1] * a3[rcx_1]")
            || text.contains("a2[rcx_1 as usize] * a3[rcx_1 as usize]"),
        "scalar float tail not slice-indexed:\n{text}"
    );
    assert!(
        !text.contains("read::<f32>"),
        "float element left as a raw pointer read:\n{text}"
    );
    // The function is void — it writes through `a1`, so the leftover register the trailing `ret`
    // reads is not a result: no `-> …` return type and no spurious `return <scratch>`.
    assert!(
        text.contains("fn mulv(a1: &mut [f32], a2: &[f32], a3: &[f32]) {"),
        "not void:\n{text}"
    );
    assert!(
        rustc_compiles(&ported(&[("mulv", code)], 0)),
        "void float port must compile"
    );
}

#[test]
fn float_vectorised_sum_recovers() {
    // clang -O3 -ffast-math of `float sumf(const float* s, unsigned n){ acc=0; for.. acc+=s[i]; }`:
    // an `addps` reduction loop + an `unpckhpd`/`shufps`/`addss` horizontal reduce + a scalar
    // remainder, result returned in xmm0. The semantic reduction analysis proves the whole thing
    // computes the slice sum and folds it to `s.iter().sum()` with an `f32` return — the messy
    // float horizontal-reduce idiom is discarded, not matched.
    let code: &[u8] = &[
        0x85, 0xF6, 0x74, 0x0E, 0x89, 0xF0, 0x83, 0xFE, 0x04, 0x73, 0x0B, 0x0F, 0x57, 0xC0, 0x31,
        0xC9, 0xEB, 0x4E, 0x0F, 0x57, 0xC0, 0xC3, 0x89, 0xC1, 0x83, 0xE1, 0xFC, 0x48, 0x8D, 0x14,
        0x85, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x48, 0x83, 0xE2, 0xF0, 0x0F, 0x57, 0xC0, 0x31, 0xF6, 0x0F,
        0x1F, 0x40, 0x00, 0x0F, 0x10, 0x0C, 0x37, 0x0F, 0x58, 0xC1, 0x48, 0x83, 0xC6, 0x10, 0x48,
        0x39, 0xF2, 0x75, 0xF0, 0x0F, 0x28, 0xC8, 0x66, 0x0F, 0x15, 0xC8, 0x0F, 0x58, 0xC8, 0x0F,
        0x28, 0xC1, 0x0F, 0xC6, 0xC1, 0x55, 0xF3, 0x0F, 0x58, 0xC1, 0x39, 0xC1, 0x74, 0x14, 0x0F,
        0x1F, 0x80, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xF3, 0x0F, 0x58, 0x04, 0x8F, 0x48, 0xFF, 0xC1, 0x48,
        0x39, 0xC8, 0x75, 0xF3, 0xC3,
    ];
    let text = decompiled(&[("sumf", code)], 0);
    assert!(

    assert!(
        text.contains("a1.iter().sum()"),
        "float sum not folded:

    );
    assert!(
        !text.contains("asm!") && !text.contains("loop") && !text.contains("unpckhpd"),
        "hsum not discarded:
{text}"
    );
    assert!(
        rustc_compiles(&ported(&[("sumf", code)], 0)),
        "folded float-sum port must compile"
    );
}

#[test]
fn vectorised_pmuludq_product_recovers() {
    // clang -O3 of an unsigned product `p=1; for i.. p*=s[i]`. SSE2 has no packed 32-bit multiply,
    // so the packed loop emulates it with the `pmuludq`/`pshufd`/`punpckldq` dance, plus a
    // `pshufd`/`pmuludq` horizontal product and a scalar `imull` remainder. The semantic reducer
    // recognises the whole as a slice product and folds it — the emulation dance is discarded, not
    // matched (so the gnarly `pmuludq` idiom never needs lifting).
    let code: &[u8] = &[
        0x85, 0xF6, 0x74, 0x13, 0x89, 0xF1, 0x83, 0xFE, 0x04, 0x73, 0x12, 0xB8, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00,
        0x00, 0x31, 0xD2, 0xE9, 0x89, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xB8, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xC3, 0x89,
        0xCA, 0x83, 0xE2, 0xFC, 0x48, 0x8D, 0x04, 0x8D, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x48, 0x83, 0xE0,
        0xF0, 0x66, 0x0F, 0x6F, 0x05, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x31, 0xF6, 0x0F, 0x1F, 0x84, 0x00,
        0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xF3, 0x0F, 0x6F, 0x0C, 0x37, 0x66, 0x0F, 0x70, 0xD1, 0xF5, 0x66,
        0x0F, 0xF4, 0xC8, 0x66, 0x0F, 0x70, 0xC0, 0xF5, 0x66, 0x0F, 0x70, 0xC9, 0xE8, 0x66, 0x0F,
        0xF4, 0xC2, 0x66, 0x0F, 0x70, 0xD0, 0xE8, 0x66, 0x0F, 0x6F, 0xC1, 0x66, 0x0F, 0x62, 0xC2,
        0x48, 0x83, 0xC6, 0x10, 0x48, 0x39, 0xF0, 0x75, 0xCE, 0x66, 0x0F, 0x70, 0xC8, 0xEE, 0x66,
        0x0F, 0x70, 0xD0, 0xFF, 0x66, 0x0F, 0x70, 0xD8, 0xF5, 0x66, 0x0F, 0xF4, 0xDA, 0x66, 0x0F,
        0xF4, 0xC8, 0x66, 0x0F, 0xF4, 0xCB, 0x66, 0x0F, 0x7E, 0xC8, 0x39, 0xCA, 0x74, 0x17, 0x66,
        0x66, 0x2E, 0x0F, 0x1F, 0x84, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x0F, 0xAF, 0x04, 0x97, 0x48,
        0xFF, 0xC2, 0x48, 0x39, 0xD1, 0x75, 0xF4, 0xC3,
    ];
    let text = decompiled(&[("prod", code)], 0);
    assert!(
        text.contains("fn prod(a1: &[u32]) -> u32"),
        "signature wrong:
{text}"
    );
    assert!(
        text.contains("a1.iter().product()"),
        "product not recovered:
{text}"
    );
    assert!(
        !text.contains("asm!") && !text.contains("loop") && !text.contains("pmuludq"),
        "dance not discarded:
{text}"
    );
    assert!(
        rustc_compiles(&ported(&[("prod", code)], 0)),
        "folded product port must compile"
    );
}

#[test]
fn opaque_predicate_branch_is_removed() {
    // An opaque guard: `if ((x & 1) == 2) { return 0xdead } return 1`. `x & 1` is 0 or 1, never 2,
    // so the branch is dead. The known-bits deobfuscation pass folds the comparison and the dead
    // arm (returning 0xdead) disappears; the function reduces to `return 1`.
    //   89 F8            mov eax, edi
    //   83 E0 01         and eax, 1
    //   83 F8 02         cmp eax, 2
    //   75 06            jne +6 (-> real)
    //   B8 AD DE 00 00   mov eax, 0xdead   ; dead
    //   C3               ret
    //   B8 01 00 00 00   mov eax, 1        ; real
    //   C3               ret
    let code: &[u8] = &[
        0x89, 0xF8, 0x83, 0xE0, 0x01, 0x83, 0xF8, 0x02, 0x75, 0x06, 0xB8, 0xAD, 0xDE, 0x00, 0x00,
        0xC3, 0xB8, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xC3,
    ];
    let text = decompiled(&[("guard", code)], 0);
    assert!(
        !text.contains("0xdead") && !text.to_lowercase().contains("57005"),
        "dead opaque-predicate arm was not removed:\n{text}"
    );
}

#[test]
fn nested_signed_then_unsigned_cast_keeps_inner_sign() {
    // Cast(Cast(x:B8, B32, signed), B16, unsigned): the outer narrow is a truncation, so the
    // result bits are the INNER signed extension — the collapse must keep signed=true.
    use crate::ir::{Expr, Width};
    let e = Expr::Cast(
        Box::new(Expr::Cast(
            Box::new(Expr::Param(0, Width::B8)),
            Width::B32,
            true,
        )),
        Width::B16,
        false,
    );
    let f = crate::simplify::fold(e);
    assert!(
        matches!(f, Expr::Cast(_, Width::B16, true)),
        "inner sign-extension must survive the collapse: {f:?}"
    );
}

#[test]
fn lea_multiply_fold_does_not_overflow() {
    // x + x*0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF  ->  x * (k+1); k+1 wraps to 0 and must not panic.
    use crate::ir::{BinOp, Expr, Width};
    let x = Expr::Param(0, Width::B64);
    let e = Expr::bin(
        BinOp::Add,
        x.clone(),
        Expr::bin(BinOp::Mul, x, Expr::konst(u64::MAX, Width::B64), Width::B64),
        Width::B64,
    );
    let _ = crate::simplify::fold(e); // must not panic in a debug build
}

#[test]
fn sar_prints_as_arithmetic_shift() {
    // mov eax, edi ; sar eax, 31 ; ret  — an arithmetic shift-right of a signed value.
    let code: &[u8] = &[0x89, 0xF8, 0xC1, 0xF8, 0x1F, 0xC3];
    let s = decompiled(&[("sar", code)], 0);
    assert!(s.contains("as i32"), "SAR operand must be cast signed: {s}");
    assert!(s.contains(">>"), "{s}");
    assert!(
        rustc_compiles(&ported(&[("sar", code)], 0)),
        "the SAR port must compile"
    );
}

#[test]
fn allones_constant_respects_signedness() {
    // Unsigned compare against all-ones must print the true value (0xffffffff), not -1
    // (which is the wrong value for a u32 and won't compile in port mode).
    let unsigned: &[u8] = &[
        0x89, 0xF8, 0x3D, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x0F, 0x92, 0xC0, 0x0F, 0xB6, 0xC0, 0xC3,
    ]; // mov eax,edi; cmp eax,0xffffffff; setb al; movzx eax,al; ret
    let u = decompiled(&[("u", unsigned)], 0);
    assert!(u.contains("0xffffffff") && !u.contains("-1"), "{u}");
    assert!(rustc_compiles(&ported(&[("u", unsigned)], 0)), "{u}");
    // A signed compare still renders the negative literal.
    let signed: &[u8] = &[
        0x89, 0xF8, 0x3D, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x0F, 0x9C, 0xC0, 0x0F, 0xB6, 0xC0, 0xC3,
    ]; // ...; setl al
    let s = decompiled(&[("s", signed)], 0);
    assert!(s.contains("-1"), "signed compare should keep -1: {s}");
}

#[test]
fn signed_compare_of_load_is_signed_and_compiles() {
    // cmp dword [rdi], 5 ; setl al ; movzx eax,al ; ret  — a SIGNED `< 5` of a memory load.
    // The load operand must be cast signed, and the cast must be parenthesized or Rust parses
    // `*a1 as i32 < 5` as generic arguments to i32 and rejects it.
    let code: &[u8] = &[0x83, 0x3F, 0x05, 0x0F, 0x9C, 0xC0, 0x0F, 0xB6, 0xC0, 0xC3];
    let s = decompiled(&[("f", code)], 0);
    assert!(s.contains("as i32") && s.contains("< 5"), "{s}");
    assert!(
        rustc_compiles(&ported(&[("f", code)], 0)),
        "signed load compare must compile: {s}"
    );
}

#[test]
fn loop_instruction_keeps_its_back_edge() {
    // mov rcx,rdi; xor eax,eax; top: inc rax; loop top; ret
    // The `loop` must model the rcx decrement and the conditional back-edge — previously it fell
    // through to `asm!` with no terminator and the loop structure was lost.
    let code: &[u8] = &[
        0x48, 0x89, 0xF9, 0x31, 0xC0, 0x48, 0xFF, 0xC0, 0xE2, 0xFB, 0xC3,
    ];
    let s = decompiled(&[("f", code)], 0);
    assert!(
        s.contains("loop {") || s.contains("while"),
        "expected a loop: {s}"
    );
    assert!(
        s.contains("rcx -= 1") || s.contains("rcx - 1"),
        "expected the decrement: {s}"
    );
    assert!(!s.contains("asm!"), "loop should be modelled, not asm: {s}");
    assert!(rustc_compiles(&ported(&[("f", code)], 0)), "{s}");
}

#[test]
fn inner_loop_break_of_outer_uses_a_label() {
    // Nested loops; the inner body's `je end` jumps clear out of BOTH loops — a break of the
    // OUTER loop. It must become a labeled `break 'l..`, not a dropped `// goto`.
    //   acc=0; for i in 0..n { for j in 0..m { acc++; if acc==100 { break outer } } }
    let code: &[u8] = &[
        0x31, 0xC0, 0x31, 0xC9, 0x48, 0x39, 0xF9, 0x73, 0x1D, 0x31, 0xD2, 0x48, 0x39, 0xF2, 0x73,
        0x11, 0x48, 0x83, 0xC0, 0x01, 0x48, 0x3D, 0x64, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x74, 0x0A, 0x48, 0xFF,
        0xC2, 0xEB, 0xEA, 0x48, 0xFF, 0xC1, 0xEB, 0xDE, 0xC3,
    ];
    let s = decompiled(&[("f", code)], 0);
    assert!(s.contains("break 'l"), "expected a labeled break: {s}");
    assert!(
        !s.contains("goto"),
        "the outer break must not degrade to a goto: {s}"
    );
    assert!(
        rustc_compiles(&ported(&[("f", code)], 0)),
        "labeled-break port must compile: {s}"
    );
}

#[test]
fn self_loop_structures_cleanly() {
    // mov rax,rdi; self: dec rax; jnz self; ret  — a block that branches to itself must become a
    // clean loop with no dangling goto.
    let code: &[u8] = &[0x48, 0x89, 0xF8, 0x48, 0xFF, 0xC8, 0x75, 0xFB, 0xC3];
    let s = decompiled(&[("f", code)], 0);
    assert!(s.contains("loop {") || s.contains("while"), "{s}");
    assert!(
        !s.contains("goto"),
        "self-loop should not leave a goto: {s}"
    );
    assert!(rustc_compiles(&ported(&[("f", code)], 0)), "{s}");
}

#[test]
fn multi_exit_loop_is_correct_and_has_no_dead_code() {
    // A loop with two distinct exits that merge afterwards. The merge tail is duplicated into
    // each exit path (allowed: never drop), and there must be no unreachable statement after an
    // unconditional `continue`/`break`.
    // i=0; loop { if i>=n {rax=1; goto merge} if i==5 {rax=2; fall} i++ } merge: rax+=i; ret
    let code: &[u8] = &[
        0x31, 0xC9, 0x48, 0x39, 0xF9, 0x73, 0x0B, 0x48, 0x83, 0xF9, 0x05, 0x74, 0x0E, 0x48, 0xFF,
        0xC1, 0xEB, 0xF0, 0x48, 0xC7, 0xC0, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xEB, 0x07, 0x48, 0xC7, 0xC0,
        0x02, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x48, 0x01, 0xC8, 0xC3,
    ];
    let s = decompiled(&[("f", code)], 0);
    // No dead `break;` immediately after a `continue;`.
    let dense: String = s.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" ");
    assert!(
        !dense.contains("continue; break;"),
        "dead code after continue: {s}"
    );
    assert!(rustc_compiles(&ported(&[("f", code)], 0)), "{s}");
}

#[test]
fn one_operand_mul_keeps_the_high_half() {
    // mov rax,rdi; mul rsi; mov rax,rdx; ret  — returns the HIGH 64 bits of the product. The
    // one-operand mul previously dropped rdx, leaving it stale.
    let umul: &[u8] = &[0x48, 0x89, 0xF8, 0x48, 0xF7, 0xE6, 0x48, 0x89, 0xD0, 0xC3];
    let u = decompiled(&[("f", umul)], 0);
    assert!(u.contains("as u128") && u.contains(">> 0x40"), "{u}");
    assert!(rustc_compiles(&ported(&[("f", umul)], 0)), "{u}");
    // Signed imul: high half via i128 (arithmetic shift), params typed signed.
    let imul: &[u8] = &[0x48, 0x89, 0xF8, 0x48, 0xF7, 0xEE, 0x48, 0x89, 0xD0, 0xC3];
    let i = decompiled(&[("f", imul)], 0);
    assert!(
        i.contains("as i128"),
        "signed imul high half should widen to i128: {i}"
    );
    assert!(rustc_compiles(&ported(&[("f", imul)], 0)), "{i}");
}

#[test]
fn partial_register_write_preserves_upper_bits() {
    // mov eax,0x1122 ; mov al,5 ; add eax,0x10000 ; ret
    // `mov al,5` must preserve eax's upper bits (eax -> 0x1105), so the add gives 0x11105.
    // (The clean-replace model would clobber eax to 5 and give 0x10005.)
    let code: &[u8] = &[
        0xB8, 0x22, 0x11, 0x00, 0x00, 0xB0, 0x05, 0x05, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0xC3,
    ];
    let s = decompiled(&[("f", code)], 0);
    assert!(
        s.contains("0x11105"),
        "upper bits must survive the al write: {s}"
    );
    assert!(rustc_compiles(&ported(&[("f", code)], 0)), "{s}");
    // A byte return must NOT be wrapped in a read-modify-write (upper bits are dead).
    let br: &[u8] = &[0xB0, 0x07, 0xC3]; // mov al,7; ret
    let b = decompiled(&[("g", br)], 0);
    assert!(!b.contains("& 0xff"), "byte return should stay clean: {b}");
}

#[test]
fn max_min_preserves_comparison_signedness() {
    // mov rax,rdi; cmp rax,rsi; cmovl rax,rsi; ret  — a SIGNED max (cmovl) -> i64 types.
    let smax: &[u8] = &[
        0x48, 0x89, 0xF8, 0x48, 0x39, 0xF0, 0x48, 0x0F, 0x4C, 0xC6, 0xC3,
    ];
    let s = decompiled(&[("f", smax)], 0);
    assert!(
        s.contains("i64") && s.contains(".max(a2)"),
        "signed max must be i64: {s}"
    );
    assert!(rustc_compiles(&ported(&[("f", smax)], 0)), "{s}");
    // Same shape with cmovb is an UNSIGNED max -> u64.
    let umax: &[u8] = &[
        0x48, 0x89, 0xF8, 0x48, 0x39, 0xF0, 0x48, 0x0F, 0x42, 0xC6, 0xC3,
    ];
    let u = decompiled(&[("g", umax)], 0);
    assert!(
        u.contains("u64") && !u.contains("i64"),
        "unsigned max must stay u64: {u}"
    );
    assert!(rustc_compiles(&ported(&[("g", umax)], 0)), "{u}");
}

```

`crates/orress-decompiler/src/types.rs`:

```rs
//! Type recovery, in the spirit of decy's ownership inference: how a value is *used*
//! decides its Rust type. A parameter that is dereferenced is a reference; one that is
//! written through is `&mut`; a pointer followed by a length that the code compares
//! is a slice (`&[u8]` / `&str` arrive as exactly such a pair); a function that only
//! returns comparisons and 0/1 returns `bool`.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashMap};

use crate::ir::*;

/// A recovered struct field: its byte offset from the start of the struct, its access width,
/// and whether it is used as a signed value.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Field {
    pub offset: u64,
    pub width: Width,
    pub signed: bool,
}

impl Field {
    /// The field's Rust name, which encodes its byte offset (`field_8`).
    pub fn name(&self) -> String {
        format!("field_{}", self.offset)
    }
}

/// A recovered struct layout: the fields a pointer parameter is accessed through, by offset.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct StructLayout {
    pub name: String,
    pub fields: Vec<Field>,
    /// User-supplied names by field offset, overriding `field_N` when a user type is applied.
    pub field_names: BTreeMap<u64, String>,
}

impl StructLayout {
    /// The printed name of a field: the user's name if one was applied, else `field_N`.
    pub fn field_name(&self, f: &Field) -> String {
        self.field_names
            .get(&f.offset)
            .cloned()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| f.name())
    }
}

/// Type information the user has supplied, lowered into decompiler terms by the caller. It
/// names recovered struct parameters and their fields, and overrides a function's signature.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct TypeHints {
    /// User struct layouts, used to name a recovered struct parameter and its fields.
    pub structs: Vec<StructDef>,
    /// Function prototypes by entry address: override return and parameter types.
    pub prototypes: BTreeMap<u64, Proto>,
}

impl TypeHints {
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.structs.is_empty() && self.prototypes.is_empty()
    }
}

/// A user struct, as `(offset, width, signed, name)` fields.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct StructDef {
    pub name: String,
    pub fields: Vec<(u64, Width, bool, String)>,
}

/// A user function prototype, already lowered to decompiler types.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct Proto {
    pub ret: Option<Ty>,
    pub params: Vec<Ty>,
}

/// Applies user type hints to a recovered signature in place: names recovered struct
/// parameters whose layout a user struct covers, then overlays any function prototype.
pub fn apply_hints(sig: &mut Signature, entry: u64, hints: &TypeHints) {
    if hints.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    for ty in &mut sig.params {
        if let Ty::Struct(layout, _) = ty
            && let Some(def) = best_struct_match(&hints.structs, layout)
        {
            layout.name = def.name.clone();
            layout.field_names = def
                .fields
                .iter()
                .map(|(off, _, _, name)| (*off, name.clone()))
                .collect();
        }
    }
    if let Some(proto) = hints.prototypes.get(&entry) {
        if let Some(ret) = &proto.ret {
            sig.ret = Some(ret.clone());
        }
        for (i, pty) in proto.params.iter().enumerate() {
            if let Some(slot) = sig.params.get_mut(i) {
                *slot = pty.clone();
            }
        }
    }
}

/// The one user struct whose fields cover every recovered `(offset, width)` field, if that
/// match is unique (no guessing between two equally plausible structs).
fn best_struct_match<'a>(defs: &'a [StructDef], layout: &StructLayout) -> Option<&'a StructDef> {
    let covers = |d: &StructDef| {
        layout.fields.iter().all(|f| {
            d.fields
                .iter()
                .any(|(off, w, _, _)| *off == f.offset && *w == f.width)
        })
    };
    let mut matches = defs.iter().filter(|d| covers(d));
    let first = matches.next()?;
    matches.next().is_none().then_some(first)
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Ty {
    Int(Width, bool),
    Bool,
    /// `&T` / `&mut T` where T is an integer of this width.
    Ref(Width, bool),
    /// `&[T]` / `&mut [T]`; the length is the next parameter. The bools are, in order: `&mut`,
    /// floating-point element (`&[f32]` / `&[f64]`, set when accessed as a packed-float vector),
    /// and signed element (`&[i32]` vs `&[u32]`, set when an element feeds a signed operation).
    Slice(Width, bool, bool, bool),
    /// The length half of a slice parameter.
    SliceLen,
    /// A floating-point value (`f32` for width 4, `f64` for width 8).
    Float(Width),
    /// `&Struct` / `&mut Struct`: a pointer accessed through constant field offsets.
    Struct(StructLayout, bool),
}

impl Ty {
    pub fn rust(&self) -> String {
        match self {
            Self::Int(w, s) => w.rust(*s).to_owned(),
            Self::Bool => "bool".to_owned(),
            Self::Ref(w, m) => format!("&{}{}", if *m { "mut " } else { "" }, w.rust(false)),
            Self::Slice(w, m, f, s) => {
                let elem = if *f {
                    if w.0 == 4 { "f32" } else { "f64" }
                } else {
                    w.rust(*s)
                };
                format!("&{}[{}]", if *m { "mut " } else { "" }, elem)
            }
            Self::SliceLen => "usize".to_owned(),
            Self::Float(w) => if w.0 == 4 { "f32" } else { "f64" }.to_owned(),
            Self::Struct(l, m) => format!("&{}{}", if *m { "mut " } else { "" }, l.name),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Signature {
    pub params: Vec<Ty>,
    pub ret: Option<Ty>,
}

#[derive(Default, Clone, Copy)]
struct Use {
    width: u8,
    deref: Option<Width>,
    written: bool,
    indexed: bool,
    signed: bool,
    compared: bool,
    /// The parameter's elements are accessed as floating-point (a packed-float vector load/store),
    /// so a slice of it is `&[f32]` / `&[f64]`.
    float: bool,
}

/// The parameter index an address is ultimately based on, seeing through nested offsets such as
/// `(p + i*4) + 4` (a vector loop that starts at element 1). Used for the float-element signal,
/// where only *which* parameter the access is on matters, not the exact offset form.
pub fn addr_param(addr: &Expr) -> Option<usize> {
    let mut found = None;
    addr.walk(&mut |x| {
        if let Expr::Param(i, _) = x {
            found = Some(*i);
        }
    });
    found
}

/// The parameter an address is based on: `p`, `p + x` or `x + p`.
pub fn base_param(addr: &Expr) -> Option<(usize, Option<&Expr>)> {
    match addr {
        Expr::Param(i, _) => Some((*i, None)),
        Expr::Bin(BinOp::Add, a, b, _) => match (&**a, &**b) {
            (Expr::Param(i, _), x) | (x, Expr::Param(i, _)) => Some((*i, Some(x))),
            _ => None,
        },
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn strip_cast(e: &Expr) -> &Expr {
    match e {
        Expr::Cast(a, _, _) => strip_cast(a),
        other => other,
    }
}

/// Records a dereference of a pointer parameter at a byte offset: a constant offset is a struct
/// field (widening the field if seen at multiple widths); a variable offset marks the parameter
/// as array-indexed instead.
fn record_field(
    map: &mut BTreeMap<u64, Width>,
    var_indexed: &mut bool,
    off: Option<&Expr>,
    w: Width,
) {
    let k = match off {
        None => 0,
        Some(Expr::Const(k, _)) => *k,
        Some(_) => {
            *var_indexed = true;
            return;
        }
    };
    let e = map.entry(k).or_insert(w);
    *e = (*e).max(w);
}

fn all_exprs(blocks: &[Block]) -> Vec<(&Expr, bool)> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for b in blocks {
        for (_, s) in &b.stmts {
            match s {
                // The address of a store is written through.
                Stmt::Store(a, v, _) => {
                    out.push((a, true));
                    out.push((v, false));
                }
                other => out.extend(other.exprs().into_iter().map(|e| (e, false))),
            }
        }
        match &b.term {
            Term::Branch(c, _, _) => out.push((c, false)),
            Term::Return(Some(e)) | Term::TailCall(e) => out.push((e, false)),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    out
}

fn is_boolish(e: &Expr) -> bool {
    e.is_condition()
        || matches!(e, Expr::Const(0 | 1, _))
        || matches!(e, Expr::Cast(a, _, false) if a.is_condition())
}

/// Infers the signature of a simplified function.
/// Recovers the function signature. `n_int` is how many of the `params` are passed in integer
/// registers; the rest (`params - n_int`) are floating-point parameters in XMM registers.
/// `float_ret`, when set, is the width of a floating-point return value (in xmm0).
pub fn infer(
    blocks: &[Block],
    params: usize,
    returns: bool,
    n_int: usize,
    float_ret: Option<Width>,
) -> Signature {
    let mut uses = vec![Use::default(); params];
    // Per-parameter struct evidence: the constant offsets it is dereferenced at (with their
    // widths), and whether it is ever indexed by a variable (which makes it an array, not a
    // struct).
    let mut field_map: Vec<BTreeMap<u64, Width>> = vec![BTreeMap::new(); params];
    let mut field_signed: Vec<BTreeMap<u64, bool>> = vec![BTreeMap::new(); params];
    let mut var_indexed = vec![false; params];
    for b in blocks {
        for (_, s) in &b.stmts {
            if let Stmt::Store(a, val, w) = s
                && !val.is_vector()
                && let Some((i, off)) = base_param(a)
                && i < params
            {
                uses[i].deref = Some(uses[i].deref.map_or(*w, |d| d.max(*w)));
                uses[i].written = true;
                uses[i].indexed |= off.is_some_and(|o| !matches!(o, Expr::Const(..)));
                record_field(&mut field_map[i], &mut var_indexed[i], off, *w);
            }
            // A packed *float* store to a parameter marks the element type float, so that — once
            // the parameter is a slice from its scalar-element evidence — it types as `&[f32]`.
            // (Slice-vs-pointer is still decided by the scalar/length evidence, so a pure-vector
            // pointer with no length stays a raw pointer.)
            if let Stmt::Store(a, val, _) = s
                && val.vec_shape().is_some_and(|(_, l)| l.float)
                && let Some(i) = addr_param(a)
                && i < params
            {
                uses[i].float = true;
            }
        }
    }
    for (e, _) in all_exprs(blocks) {
        e.walk(&mut |x| match x {
            Expr::Param(i, w) if *i < params => uses[*i].width = uses[*i].width.max(w.0),
            Expr::Load(a, w) => {
                if let Some((i, off)) = base_param(a)
                    && i < params
                {
                    uses[i].deref = Some(uses[i].deref.map_or(*w, |d| d.max(*w)));
                    uses[i].indexed |= off.is_some_and(|o| !matches!(o, Expr::Const(..)));
                    // A constant offset beyond the first element also means "array".
                    uses[i].indexed |=
                        off.is_some_and(|o| matches!(o, Expr::Const(k, _) if *k > 0));
                    record_field(&mut field_map[i], &mut var_indexed[i], off, *w);
                }
            }
            // A packed *float* load from a parameter marks its element type float (so a slice of
            // it is `&[f32]`); slice-vs-pointer stays decided by the scalar/length evidence.
            Expr::VecLoad(a, _, lane) if lane.float => {
                if let Some(i) = addr_param(a)
                    && i < params
                {
                    uses[i].float = true;
                }
            }
            Expr::Cmp(_, a, c, signed) => {
                for side in [a, c] {
                    if let Expr::Param(i, _) = strip_cast(side)
                        && *i < params
                    {
                        uses[*i].compared = true;
                        uses[*i].signed |= *signed;
                    }
                }
            }
            // A parameter reinterpreted by a signed cast (e.g. a signed-division operand), or
            // converted to a float by the signed `cvtsi2*`, is itself signed.
            Expr::Cast(a, _, true) | Expr::FCast(a, _, FCast::SIntToFloat) => {
                if let Expr::Param(i, _) = strip_cast(a)
                    && *i < params
                {
                    uses[*i].signed = true;
                }
                // A sign-extended field load (`movsx eax, byte [rdi+4]`) → that field is signed.
                if let Expr::Load(addr, _) = strip_cast(a)
                    && let Some((i, off)) = base_param(addr)
                    && i < params
                {
                    let k = match off {
                        Some(Expr::Const(k, _)) => *k,
                        None => 0,
                        // A variable index is a slice element, not a fixed field: the slice's
                        // element type is signed (`&[i32]`).
                        _ => {
                            uses[i].signed = true;
                            return;
                        }
                    };
                    field_signed[i].insert(k, true);
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        });
    }

    let mut tys: Vec<Ty> = uses
        .iter()
        .map(|u| match u.deref {
            Some(w) if u.indexed => Ty::Slice(w, u.written, u.float, u.signed),
            Some(w) => Ty::Ref(w, u.written),
            None => Ty::Int(Width(if u.width == 0 { 8 } else { u.width }), u.signed),
        })
        .collect();
    // A pointer dereferenced through constant offsets with *mixed widths* (which an array
    // cannot express), or at a single non-zero offset, is a struct: `&Struct` / `&mut Struct`.
    // Uniform-width offsets stay an array/slice (ambiguous, and `p[0]`/`p[1]` reads fine). A
    // variable index is a definite array, never a struct.
    let mut next_struct = 0;
    for i in 0..params {
        if var_indexed[i] {
            continue;
        }
        let fm = &field_map[i];
        let widths: std::collections::BTreeSet<u8> = fm.values().map(|w| w.0).collect();
        let has_nonzero = fm.keys().any(|&k| k > 0);
        if !fm.is_empty() && (widths.len() > 1 || (fm.len() == 1 && has_nonzero)) {
            next_struct += 1;
            let fields = fm
                .iter()
                .map(|(&offset, &width)| Field {
                    offset,
                    width,
                    signed: field_signed[i].get(&offset).copied().unwrap_or(false),
                })
                .collect();
            let name = format!("Struct{next_struct}");
            tys[i] = Ty::Struct(
                StructLayout {
                    name,
                    fields,
                    field_names: BTreeMap::new(),
                },
                uses[i].written,
            );
        }
    }
    // (pointer, length) pairs become one slice parameter.
    for i in 0..tys.len().saturating_sub(1) {
        let as_slice = match &tys[i] {
            Ty::Ref(w, m) => Some((*w, *m, uses[i].float, uses[i].signed)),
            Ty::Slice(w, m, f, s) => Some((*w, *m, *f, *s)),
            _ => None,
        };
        if let Some((w, m, f, s)) = as_slice
            && matches!(tys[i + 1], Ty::Int(..))
            && uses[i + 1].compared
        {
            tys[i] = Ty::Slice(w, m, f, s);
            tys[i + 1] = Ty::SliceLen;
        }
    }
    // Floating-point parameters (the trailing XMM arguments) are `f32`/`f64`; their width
    // comes from how they are used (an `sd` op reads 8 bytes, `ss` 4).
    for (i, ty) in tys.iter_mut().enumerate().skip(n_int) {
        *ty = Ty::Float(Width(if uses[i].width == 0 { 8 } else { uses[i].width }));
    }

    if let Some(w) = float_ret {
        return Signature {
            params: tys,
            ret: Some(Ty::Float(w)),
        };
    }

    let ret = returns.then(|| {
        let mut rets = Vec::new();
        let mut rax_defs = Vec::new();
        for b in blocks {
            if let Term::Return(Some(e)) = &b.term {
                rets.push(e);
            }
            for (_, s) in &b.stmts {
                if let Stmt::Assign(Var::Reg(RAX), e) = s {
                    rax_defs.push(e);
                }
            }
        }
        let boolish = |e: &&Expr| match e {
            Expr::Var(Var::Reg(RAX), _) => {
                !rax_defs.is_empty() && rax_defs.iter().all(|d| is_boolish(d))
            }
            other => is_boolish(other),
        };
        if !rets.is_empty()
            && rets.iter().all(boolish)
            && rets
                .iter()
                .chain(&rax_defs)
                .any(|e| !matches!(e, Expr::Const(..)) || matches!(e, Expr::Const(1, _)))
        {
            Ty::Bool
        } else {
            // The width of the actual computed value pins the return type; a bare `return rax`
            // takes it from rax's definitions. Constants (e.g. a `return 0` fallthrough, which
            // the lifter widens to the register) do not pin it, since a small constant fits any
            // integer width. Only if every return is constant do the constants decide.
            let defs_width = |consts: bool| {
                rax_defs
                    .iter()
                    .filter(|d| consts || !matches!(d, Expr::Const(..)))
                    .map(|d| d.width())
                    .max()
            };
            let value_width = |e: &&Expr, consts: bool| match e {
                Expr::Var(Var::Reg(RAX), _) => defs_width(consts),
                Expr::Const(..) if !consts => None,
                other => Some(other.width()),
            };
            let w = rets
                .iter()
                .filter_map(|e| value_width(e, false))
                .max()
                .or_else(|| rets.iter().filter_map(|e| value_width(e, true)).max())
                .unwrap_or(Width::B64);
            // Signed when the returned value is produced by a signed operation (a bare
            // `return rax` takes it from rax's definitions).
            let signed = rax_defs.iter().any(|e| is_signed_expr(e))
                || rets
                    .iter()
                    .any(|e| !matches!(e, Expr::Var(Var::Reg(RAX), _)) && is_signed_expr(e));
            Ty::Int(w, signed)
        }
    });
    Signature { params: tys, ret }
}

/// Local variables that are slice indices or lengths and so should be `usize`: a value derived
/// from a slice-length parameter, used to index a slice, or compared against either (propagated
/// through `==`/`!=` comparisons to a fixpoint).
pub fn usize_locals(blocks: &[Block], sig: &Signature) -> std::collections::BTreeSet<Var> {
    use std::collections::BTreeSet;
    let is_len = |i: usize| matches!(sig.params.get(i), Some(Ty::SliceLen));
    let is_slice = |i: usize| matches!(sig.params.get(i), Some(Ty::Slice(..)));
    let reads_len = |e: &Expr| {
        let mut hit = false;
        e.walk(&mut |x| {
            if let Expr::Param(i, _) = x
                && is_len(*i)
            {
                hit = true;
            }
        });
        hit
    };
    // The variable used to index `off` (`v` or `v * stride`).
    let index_var = |off: &Expr| -> Option<Var> {
        match off {
            Expr::Var(v, _) => Some(*v),
            Expr::Bin(BinOp::Mul, a, _, _) => match &**a {
                Expr::Var(v, _) => Some(*v),
                _ => None,
            },
            _ => None,
        }
    };
    let mut set: BTreeSet<Var> = BTreeSet::new();
    // `==`/`!=` comparisons link two operands' usize-ness; a SliceLen operand seeds it.
    let mut edges: Vec<(Var, Option<Var>)> = Vec::new(); // (local, other local or None = a length)
    let note_cmp =
        |a: &Expr, b: &Expr, set: &mut BTreeSet<Var>, edges: &mut Vec<(Var, Option<Var>)>| {
            let var = |e: &Expr| {
                matches!(strip_cast(e), Expr::Var(_, _)).then(|| match strip_cast(e) {
                    Expr::Var(v, _) => *v,
                    _ => unreachable!(),
                })
            };
            let len = |e: &Expr| matches!(strip_cast(e), Expr::Param(i, _) if is_len(*i));
            match (var(a), var(b)) {
                (Some(va), Some(vb)) => edges.push((va, Some(vb))),
                (Some(va), None) if len(b) => {
                    set.insert(va);
                }
                (None, Some(vb)) if len(a) => {
                    set.insert(vb);
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        };
    let scan_expr = |e: &Expr, set: &mut BTreeSet<Var>, edges: &mut Vec<(Var, Option<Var>)>| {
        e.walk(&mut |x| match x {
            Expr::Load(a, _) => {
                if let Some((i, Some(off))) = base_param(a)
                    && is_slice(i)
                    && let Some(v) = index_var(off)
                {
                    set.insert(v);
                }
            }
            Expr::Cmp(CmpOp::Eq | CmpOp::Ne, a, b, _) => note_cmp(a, b, set, edges),
            _ => {}
        });
    };
    for b in blocks {
        for (_, s) in &b.stmts {
            if let Stmt::Assign(v, e) = s
                && reads_len(e)
            {
                set.insert(*v);
            }
            if let Stmt::Store(a, _, _) = s
                && let Some((i, Some(off))) = base_param(a)
                && is_slice(i)
                && let Some(iv) = index_var(off)
            {
                set.insert(iv);
            }
            for e in s.exprs() {
                scan_expr(e, &mut set, &mut edges);
            }
        }
        if let Term::Branch(e, _, _) = &b.term {
            scan_expr(e, &mut set, &mut edges);
        }
    }
    // Propagate usize-ness across comparison edges to a fixpoint.
    let mut changed = true;
    while changed {
        changed = false;
        for &(a, b) in &edges {
            let (ina, inb) = (set.contains(&a), b.is_some_and(|v| set.contains(&v)));
            if ina != inb {
                if ina && let Some(v) = b {
                    changed |= set.insert(v);
                } else if inb {
                    changed |= set.insert(a);
                }
            }
        }
    }
    set
}

/// Whether an expression is floating-point: a float literal, float arithmetic, a conversion
/// whose result is a float, or an XMM-register value.
pub fn is_float_expr(e: &Expr) -> bool {
    matches!(
        e,
        Expr::FConst(..)
            | Expr::FBin(..)
            | Expr::FUn(..)
            | Expr::FCast(_, _, FCast::SIntToFloat | FCast::FloatToFloat)
            | Expr::Var(Var::Xmm(_), _)
    )
}

/// Local variables (stack slots) that hold a floating-point value, so they declare as `f32`/`f64`
/// rather than an integer. The width comes from [`locals`].
pub fn float_locals(blocks: &[Block]) -> std::collections::BTreeSet<Var> {
    let mut out = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
    for b in blocks {
        for (_, s) in &b.stmts {
            if let Stmt::Assign(v, e) = s
                && is_float_expr(e)
            {
                out.insert(*v);
            }
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Local variables (registers/stack slots) that hold a packed vector, with their `[T; N]`
/// shape (lane count, lane width) — so they declare as a lane array.
pub fn vec_locals(blocks: &[Block]) -> std::collections::BTreeMap<Var, (u8, Lane)> {
    let mut out = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
    for b in blocks {
        for (_, s) in &b.stmts {
            if let Stmt::Assign(v, e) = s
                && let Some(shape) = e.vec_shape()
            {
                out.insert(*v, shape);
            }
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Whether an expression produces a signed value: a sign-extending cast, an arithmetic
/// shift, a negation, or signed arithmetic built from those.
pub fn is_signed_expr(e: &Expr) -> bool {
    match e {
        Expr::Cast(_, _, true) | Expr::Neg(..) => true,
        // A float → integer truncation (`cvttsd2si`) yields a signed integer.
        Expr::FCast(_, _, FCast::FloatToSInt) => true,
        Expr::Bin(BinOp::Sar, ..) => true,
        Expr::Bin(_, a, b, _) => is_signed_expr(a) || is_signed_expr(b),
        // A signed max/min (built with signed-cast operands) yields a signed value.
        Expr::Method(recv, "max" | "min", ..) => is_signed_expr(recv),
        _ => false,
    }
}

/// Marks variables compared with a signed comparison as signed.
fn mark_signed_cmps(e: &Expr, signed: &mut std::collections::HashSet<Var>) {
    e.walk(&mut |x| {
        if let Expr::Cmp(_, a, b, true) = x {
            for side in [&**a, &**b] {
                if let Expr::Var(v, _) = strip_cast(side) {
                    signed.insert(*v);
                }
            }
        }
    });
}

/// Declared types of the local variables (stack slots and leftover registers): width, and
/// whether the variable is used as a signed value.
pub fn locals(blocks: &[Block]) -> BTreeMap<Var, (Width, bool)> {
    let mut out: HashMap<Var, Width> = HashMap::new();
    let mut signed: std::collections::HashSet<Var> = std::collections::HashSet::new();
    let widen = |e: &Expr, out: &mut HashMap<Var, Width>| {
        e.walk(&mut |x| {
            if let Expr::Var(v, w) = x {
                let cur = out.entry(*v).or_insert(*w);
                *cur = (*cur).max(*w);
            }
        });
    };
    for b in blocks {
        for (_, s) in &b.stmts {
            if let Stmt::Assign(v, e) = s {
                let w = out.entry(*v).or_insert(e.width());
                *w = (*w).max(e.width());
                if is_signed_expr(e) {
                    signed.insert(*v);
                }
            }
            // A register captured as an `asm!` output is a 64-bit local too.
            for v in s.defs() {
                out.entry(v).or_insert(Width::B64);
            }
            for e in s.exprs() {
                widen(e, &mut out);
                mark_signed_cmps(e, &mut signed);
            }
        }
        match &b.term {
            // A bare `return reg` reads the whole register, so its width is the ABI
            // register width (always 64-bit from the lifter), not the variable's. Letting
            // it widen the local inflates e.g. a `u32` accumulator to `u64`, so the port's
            // `acc += x as u32` and `return acc;` no longer type-check. The function's
            // return type (from `infer`) governs what is returned, so skip the bare case.
            Term::Return(Some(Expr::Var(..))) => {}
            Term::Branch(e, _, _) | Term::Return(Some(e)) => {
                widen(e, &mut out);
                mark_signed_cmps(e, &mut signed);
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    out.into_iter()
        .map(|(v, w)| (v, (w, signed.contains(&v))))
        .collect()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod hint_tests {
    use super::*;

    fn struct_param(offsets: &[(u64, u8)]) -> Signature {
        let fields = offsets
            .iter()
            .map(|&(offset, w)| Field {
                offset,
                width: Width(w),
                signed: false,
            })
            .collect();
        Signature {
            params: vec![Ty::Struct(
                StructLayout {
                    name: "Struct1".into(),
                    fields,
                    field_names: BTreeMap::new(),
                },
                false,
            )],
            ret: None,
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn user_struct_names_recovered_fields() {
        let mut sig = struct_param(&[(0, 4), (4, 2)]);
        let hints = TypeHints {
            structs: vec![StructDef {
                name: "Packet".into(),
                fields: vec![
                    (0, Width(4), false, "magic".into()),
                    (4, Width(2), false, "len".into()),
                ],
            }],
            prototypes: BTreeMap::new(),
        };
        apply_hints(&mut sig, 0x1000, &hints);
        let Ty::Struct(layout, _) = &sig.params[0] else {
            panic!("expected struct");
        };
        assert_eq!(layout.name, "Packet");
        assert_eq!(layout.field_name(&layout.fields[0]), "magic");
        assert_eq!(layout.field_name(&layout.fields[1]), "len");
    }

    #[test]
    fn ambiguous_match_is_left_alone() {
        let mut sig = struct_param(&[(0, 4)]);
        // Two structs both cover the single recovered field: no unique match, so no rename.
        let def = |n: &str| StructDef {
            name: n.into(),
            fields: vec![(0, Width(4), false, "x".into())],
        };
        let hints = TypeHints {
            structs: vec![def("A"), def("B")],
            prototypes: BTreeMap::new(),
        };
        apply_hints(&mut sig, 0x1000, &hints);
        let Ty::Struct(layout, _) = &sig.params[0] else {
            panic!();
        };
        assert_eq!(layout.name, "Struct1");
    }

    #[test]
    fn prototype_overrides_return_and_params() {
        let mut sig = Signature {
            params: vec![Ty::Int(Width(4), false)],
            ret: None,
        };
        let mut prototypes = BTreeMap::new();
        prototypes.insert(
            0x2000,
            Proto {
                ret: Some(Ty::Bool),
                params: vec![Ty::Int(Width(8), true)],
            },
        );
        let hints = TypeHints {
            structs: vec![],
            prototypes,
        };
        apply_hints(&mut sig, 0x2000, &hints);
        assert_eq!(sig.ret, Some(Ty::Bool));
        assert_eq!(sig.params[0], Ty::Int(Width(8), true));
    }

    #[test]
    fn empty_hints_change_nothing() {
        let mut sig = struct_param(&[(0, 4)]);
        let before = format!("{sig:?}");
        apply_hints(&mut sig, 0x1000, &TypeHints::default());
        assert_eq!(before, format!("{sig:?}"));
    }
}
```

```rs
//! Turn a mangled linker symbol into a readable name. Tries Rust (legacy `_ZN…E` and v0 `_R…`),
//! MSVC (`?…`) and C++ Itanium (`_Z…`/`__Z…`), in that order. Pure Rust — no C `__cxa_demangle`.
//!
//! [`demangle`] returns `Some(readable)` only when a demangler recognises the name and produces
//! something different; a plain or auto-generated name (`main`, `sub_1400`, `puts`) returns `None`,
//! so callers can keep the original.

/// Demangles `name`, or `None` if it is not a recognised mangled symbol.
pub fn demangle(name: &str) -> Option<String> {
    // Rust: `{:#}` omits the trailing hash (`...::h1a2b3c` -> `...`).
    if let Ok(d) = rustc_demangle::try_demangle(name) {
        let s = format!("{d:#}");
        if s != name {
            return Some(s);
        }
    }
    // MSVC C++ (`?` prefix).
    if name.starts_with('?') {
        let flags =
            msvc_demangler::DemangleFlags::COMPLETE | msvc_demangler::DemangleFlags::NO_MS_KEYWORDS;
        if let Ok(s) = msvc_demangler::demangle(name, flags)
            && s != name
        {
            return Some(s);
        }
    }
    // C++ Itanium (`_Z` / `__Z`).
    if (name.starts_with("_Z") || name.starts_with("__Z"))
        && let Ok(sym) = cpp_demangle::Symbol::new(name)
    {
        let s = sym.to_string();
        if s != name {
            return Some(s);
        }
    }
    None
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn rust_legacy_and_v0() {
        // Legacy Rust mangling.
        let d = demangle("_ZN4core3fmt9Formatter3pad17h0123456789abcdefE").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(d, "core::fmt::Formatter::pad");
        // v0 Rust mangling (`_R…`): core::panicking::panic.
        let d = demangle("_RNvNtCs1234_4core9panicking5panic").unwrap();
        assert!(d.contains("panicking") && d.contains("panic"), "{d}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn cpp_itanium() {
        // int foo(int, int)
        assert_eq!(demangle("_Z3fooii").unwrap(), "foo(int, int)");
    }

    #[test]
    fn msvc() {
        // `int __cdecl foo(int)` mangled by MSVC.
        let d = demangle("?foo@@YAHH@Z").unwrap();
        assert!(d.contains("foo"), "{d}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn plain_names_are_left_alone() {
        assert_eq!(demangle("main"), None);
        assert_eq!(demangle("sub_140001100"), None);
        assert_eq!(demangle("puts"), None);
        assert_eq!(demangle("check_password"), None);
    }
}
```

```rs
//! The Dalvik opcode table: each opcode's mnemonic, instruction format and the kind of constant-
//! pool reference it carries (if any). The decoder in `lib.rs` uses this to walk a method's code.
//! Instructions are measured in 16-bit code units; every format's size is fixed, so decoding stays
//! aligned even across opcodes ORRESS doesn't render in detail.

/// A Dalvik instruction format (named as in the Dalvik spec: `AABBCC`-style).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Fmt {
    F10x,
    F12x,
    F11n,
    F11x,
    F10t,
    F20t,
    F22x,
    F21t,
    F21s,
    F21h,
    /// `const-wide/high16`: like 21h, but the literal is the top 16 bits of a 64-bit value.
    F21hw,
    F21c,
    F23x,
    F22b,
    F22t,
    F22s,
    F22c,
    F30t,
    F31t,
    F31i,
    F31c,
    F32x,
    F35c,
    F3rc,
    F51l,
    F45cc,
    F4rcc,
    /// Unused/unknown opcode (decoded as one unit so we stay aligned).
    Unknown,
}

impl Fmt {
    /// Size of this format in 16-bit code units.
    pub fn units(self) -> usize {
        use Fmt::*;
        match self {
            F10x | F12x | F11n | F11x | F10t => 1,
            F20t | F22x | F21t | F21s | F21h | F21hw | F21c | F23x | F22b | F22t | F22s | F22c => 2,
            F30t | F31t | F31i | F31c | F32x | F35c | F3rc => 3,
            F45cc | F4rcc => 4,
            F51l => 5,
            Unknown => 1,
        }
    }
}

/// What a referencing instruction's index points at.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Ref {
    None,
    Str,
    Type,
    Field,
    Method,
    /// Call site / method handle / prototype — rendered as a raw index.
    Other,
}
```

`crates/orress-dex/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! Android DEX (Dalvik Executable) loading for ORRESS.
//!
//! [`parse`] reads a `classes.dex` header and its **string pool** — the single most useful thing
//! in a DEX for triage, since every class name, method name, field name, type descriptor and
//! string constant lives there (URLs, commands and secrets included). It also resolves type and
//! method names from the id tables. Pure `std`, no dependencies, tolerant of hostile input.
//!
//! This is the DEX inside an APK (which is a ZIP — see `orress-archive`). [`Dex::classes`] lists
//! each class's methods and [`Dex::disassemble_method`] decodes a method's Dalvik bytecode, with
//! string/type/field/method references resolved.

mod dis;

use std::collections::HashSet;

/// Offsets of the `u32` fields in the 112-byte DEX header.
mod hdr {
    pub const STRING_IDS_SIZE: usize = 56;
    pub const STRING_IDS_OFF: usize = 60;
    pub const TYPE_IDS_SIZE: usize = 64;
    pub const TYPE_IDS_OFF: usize = 68;
    pub const PROTO_IDS_SIZE: usize = 72;
    pub const FIELD_IDS_SIZE: usize = 80;
    pub const FIELD_IDS_OFF: usize = 84;
    pub const METHOD_IDS_SIZE: usize = 88;
    pub const METHOD_IDS_OFF: usize = 92;
    pub const CLASS_DEFS_SIZE: usize = 96;
    pub const CLASS_DEFS_OFF: usize = 100;
}

/// A parsed DEX file (header counts, the string pool, and resolved type/method names).
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Dex {
    /// Version from the magic, e.g. `035`.
    pub version: String,
    pub string_count: u32,
    pub type_count: u32,
    pub proto_count: u32,
    pub field_count: u32,
    pub method_count: u32,
    pub class_def_count: u32,
    /// The decoded string pool, in index order.
    pub strings: Vec<String>,
    /// Type descriptors (`Lcom/example/Foo;`), resolved from the type-id table.
    pub types: Vec<String>,
    /// Fully-qualified method names (`Lcom/example/Foo;.bar`), resolved from the method-id table.
    pub methods: Vec<String>,
    /// Fully-qualified field names (`Lcom/example/Foo;.bar`), from the field-id table.
    pub fields: Vec<String>,
    /// Classes with their methods (name + code offset), for disassembly.
    pub classes: Vec<DexClass>,
}

/// A class and its methods.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct DexClass {
    pub name: String,
    pub methods: Vec<DexMethod>,
}

/// A method and the file offset of its `code_item` (0 if abstract/native).
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct DexMethod {
    pub name: String,
    pub code_off: u32,
}

/// One decoded Dalvik instruction.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct DalvikInsn {
    /// Offset in 16-bit code units from the start of the method's code (matches `dexdump`).
    pub offset: usize,
    pub opcode: u8,
    pub mnemonic: &'static str,
    /// Rendered operands (registers, literals, resolved references, branch targets).
    pub operand: String,
    pub branch_target: Option<usize>,
    pub is_branch_target: bool,
}

fn u32_at(d: &[u8], off: usize) -> Option<u32> {
    d.get(off..off + 4)
        .map(|s| u32::from_le_bytes([s[0], s[1], s[2], s[3]]))
}
fn u16_at(d: &[u8], off: usize) -> Option<u16> {
    d.get(off..off + 2)
        .map(|s| u16::from_le_bytes([s[0], s[1]]))
}

/// True if `data` starts with the DEX magic (`dex\n`).
pub fn is_dex(data: &[u8]) -> bool {
    data.len() >= 8 && &data[..4] == b"dex\n"
}

/// Reads an unsigned LEB128 value at `*pos`, advancing it. `None` if the stream ends first.
fn read_uleb128(d: &[u8], pos: &mut usize) -> Option<u32> {
    let mut result: u32 = 0;
    let mut shift = 0;
    loop {
        let byte = *d.get(*pos)?;
        *pos += 1;
        result |= ((byte & 0x7f) as u32) << shift;
        if byte & 0x80 == 0 {
            return Some(result);
        }
        shift += 7;
        if shift >= 32 {
            return Some(result);
        }
    }
}

/// Decodes a MUTF-8 string_data item at `off` (a ULEB128 code-unit count, then UTF-8 bytes up to a
/// NUL terminator).
fn read_string_data(d: &[u8], off: usize) -> String {
    let mut pos = off;
    let _utf16_len = read_uleb128(d, &mut pos);
    let start = pos;
    while d.get(pos).is_some_and(|&b| b != 0) {
        pos += 1;
    }
    decode_mutf8(&d[start..pos.min(d.len())])
}

/// Decodes Java/Dalvik "modified UTF-8" (1/2/3-byte forms, `C0 80` NUL, 6-byte surrogate pairs).
fn decode_mutf8(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(bytes.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < bytes.len() {
        let b = bytes[i];
        if b & 0x80 == 0 {
            out.push(b as char);
            i += 1;
        } else if b & 0xE0 == 0xC0 {
            if i + 1 < bytes.len() {
                let c = ((b as u32 & 0x1F) << 6) | (bytes[i + 1] as u32 & 0x3F);
                out.push(char::from_u32(c).unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}'));
            }
            i += 2;
        } else if b & 0xF0 == 0xE0 {
            if i + 5 < bytes.len()
                && b == 0xED
                && (bytes[i + 1] & 0xF0) == 0xA0
                && bytes[i + 3] == 0xED
            {
                let hi = ((bytes[i + 1] as u32 & 0x0F) << 6) | (bytes[i + 2] as u32 & 0x3F);
                let lo = ((bytes[i + 4] as u32 & 0x0F) << 6) | (bytes[i + 5] as u32 & 0x3F);
                out.push(char::from_u32(0x10000 + (hi << 10) + lo).unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}'));
                i += 6;
            } else {
                if i + 2 < bytes.len() {
                    let c = ((b as u32 & 0x0F) << 12)
                        | ((bytes[i + 1] as u32 & 0x3F) << 6)
                        | (bytes[i + 2] as u32 & 0x3F);
                    out.push(char::from_u32(c).unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}'));
                }
                i += 3;
            }
        } else {
            out.push('\u{FFFD}');
            i += 1;
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Cap on table sizes, so a crafted header can't make us allocate wildly.
const MAX_ITEMS: u32 = 20_000_000;

/// Parses a DEX file.
pub fn parse(data: &[u8]) -> Result<Dex, String> {
    if !is_dex(data) {
        return Err("not a DEX file (missing \"dex\\n\" magic)".into());
    }
    if data.len() < 112 {
        return Err("file too small for a DEX header".into());
    }
    let version = String::from_utf8_lossy(&data[4..7]).into_owned();

    let get = |off: usize| u32_at(data, off).ok_or("truncated header");
    let string_count = get(hdr::STRING_IDS_SIZE)?;
    let string_off = get(hdr::STRING_IDS_OFF)? as usize;
    let type_count = get(hdr::TYPE_IDS_SIZE)?;
    let type_off = get(hdr::TYPE_IDS_OFF)? as usize;
    let proto_count = get(hdr::PROTO_IDS_SIZE)?;
    let field_count = get(hdr::FIELD_IDS_SIZE)?;
    let field_off = get(hdr::FIELD_IDS_OFF)? as usize;
    let method_count = get(hdr::METHOD_IDS_SIZE)?;
    let method_off = get(hdr::METHOD_IDS_OFF)? as usize;
    let class_def_count = get(hdr::CLASS_DEFS_SIZE)?;
    let class_def_off = get(hdr::CLASS_DEFS_OFF)? as usize;

    if string_count
        .max(type_count)
        .max(field_count)
        .max(method_count)
        .max(class_def_count)
        > MAX_ITEMS
    {
        return Err("implausible table size".into());
    }
    // Never walk more entries than the file can actually hold from each table's offset.
    let fits = |count: u32, off: usize, item: usize| -> usize {
        (count as usize).min(data.len().saturating_sub(off) / item)
    };

    // String pool: string_ids[i] is a u32 offset to a string_data item.
    let mut strings = Vec::with_capacity(string_count.min(1 << 16) as usize);
    for i in 0..fits(string_count, string_off, 4) {
        match u32_at(data, string_off + i * 4) {
            Some(off) if (off as usize) < data.len() => {
                strings.push(read_string_data(data, off as usize))
            }
            _ => strings.push(String::new()),
        }
    }

    // Type descriptors: type_ids[i] is a u32 index into the string pool.
    let mut types = Vec::with_capacity(type_count.min(1 << 16) as usize);
    for i in 0..fits(type_count, type_off, 4) {
        let s = u32_at(data, type_off + i * 4)
            .and_then(|idx| strings.get(idx as usize))
            .cloned()
            .unwrap_or_default();
        types.push(s);
    }

    // Methods: method_id = { class_idx: u16, proto_idx: u16, name_idx: u32 }.
    let mut methods = Vec::with_capacity(method_count.min(1 << 16) as usize);
    for i in 0..fits(method_count, method_off, 8) {
        let base = method_off + i * 8;
        let class = u16_at(data, base)
            .and_then(|idx| types.get(idx as usize))
            .cloned();
        let name = u32_at(data, base + 4)
            .and_then(|idx| strings.get(idx as usize))
            .cloned();
        match (class, name) {
            (Some(c), Some(n)) => methods.push(format!("{c}.{n}")),
            (None, Some(n)) => methods.push(n),
            _ => methods.push(String::new()),
        }
    }

    // Fields: field_id = { class_idx: u16, type_idx: u16, name_idx: u32 }.
    let mut fields = Vec::with_capacity(field_count.min(1 << 16) as usize);
    for i in 0..fits(field_count, field_off, 8) {
        let base = field_off + i * 8;
        let class = u16_at(data, base)
            .and_then(|idx| types.get(idx as usize))
            .cloned();
        let name = u32_at(data, base + 4)
            .and_then(|idx| strings.get(idx as usize))
            .cloned();
        fields.push(match (class, name) {
            (Some(c), Some(n)) => format!("{c}.{n}"),
            (_, Some(n)) => n,
            _ => String::new(),
        });
    }

    // Classes and their methods (from class_defs -> class_data).
    let classes = parse_classes(
        data,
        class_def_off,
        fits(class_def_count, class_def_off, 32) as u32,
        &types,
        &methods,
    );

    Ok(Dex {
        version,
        string_count,
        type_count,
        proto_count,
        field_count,
        method_count,
        class_def_count,
        strings,
        types,
        methods,
        fields,
        classes,
    })
}

/// Walks the class_defs table and each present class_data to collect methods + their code offsets.
fn parse_classes(
    d: &[u8],
    off: usize,
    count: u32,
    types: &[String],
    methods: &[String],
) -> Vec<DexClass> {
    let count = (count as usize).min(1 << 20);
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(count.min(1 << 16));
    for i in 0..count {
        let base = off + i * 32; // class_def_item is 32 bytes
        let Some(class_idx) = u32_at(d, base) else {
            break;
        };
        let name = types.get(class_idx as usize).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
        let data_off = u32_at(d, base + 24).unwrap_or(0) as usize;
        let mut ms = Vec::new();
        if data_off != 0 {
            ms = parse_class_methods(d, data_off, methods);
        }
        out.push(DexClass { name, methods: ms });
    }
    out
}

/// Parses a class_data_item's method lists (fields are skipped). Method indices are delta-encoded.
fn parse_class_methods(d: &[u8], off: usize, methods: &[String]) -> Vec<DexMethod> {
    let mut p = off;
    let static_fields = read_uleb128(d, &mut p);
    let instance_fields = read_uleb128(d, &mut p);
    let direct_methods = read_uleb128(d, &mut p);
    let virtual_methods = read_uleb128(d, &mut p);
    let (Some(sf), Some(inf), Some(dm), Some(vm)) = (
        static_fields,
        instance_fields,
        direct_methods,
        virtual_methods,
    ) else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    // Reject implausible counts (junk or hostile offsets) before looping on them.
    const CAP: u32 = 1 << 20;
    if sf > CAP || inf > CAP || dm > CAP || vm > CAP {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    // Skip encoded_field lists (each: field_idx_diff, access_flags).
    for _ in 0..(sf + inf) {
        read_uleb128(d, &mut p);
        read_uleb128(d, &mut p);
    }
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for group in [dm, vm] {
        let mut method_idx: u32 = 0;
        let mut first = true;
        for _ in 0..group {
            let Some(diff) = read_uleb128(d, &mut p) else {
                return out;
            };
            let _access = read_uleb128(d, &mut p);
            let Some(code_off) = read_uleb128(d, &mut p) else {
                return out;
            };
            method_idx = if first {
                diff
            } else {
                method_idx.wrapping_add(diff)
            };
            first = false;
            let name = methods
                .get(method_idx as usize)
                .cloned()
                .unwrap_or_default();
            out.push(DexMethod { name, code_off });
        }
    }
    out
}

fn sign4(x: u16) -> i32 {
    let x = (x & 0xf) as i32;
    if x >= 8 { x - 16 } else { x }
}
fn sign8(x: u16) -> i32 {
    (x & 0xff) as u8 as i8 as i32
}
fn sign16(x: u16) -> i32 {
    x as i16 as i32
}

impl Dex {
    fn resolve_ref(&self, kind: dis::Ref, idx: usize) -> String {
        match kind {
            dis::Ref::Str => self.strings.get(idx).map(|s| format!("{s:?}")),
            dis::Ref::Type => self.types.get(idx).cloned(),
            dis::Ref::Method => self.methods.get(idx).cloned(),
            dis::Ref::Field => self.fields.get(idx).cloned(),
            dis::Ref::Other => Some(format!("@{idx}")),
            dis::Ref::None => None,
        }
        .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("@{idx}"))
    }

    /// Disassembles the Dalvik bytecode of the `code_item` at file offset `code_off`.
    pub fn disassemble_method(
        &self,
        data: &[u8],
        code_off: u32,
    ) -> Result<Vec<DalvikInsn>, String> {
        if code_off == 0 {
            return Err("method has no code (abstract or native)".into());
        }
        let base = code_off as usize;
        let insns_size = u32_at(data, base + 12).ok_or("truncated code_item")? as usize;
        if insns_size > 10_000_000 {
            return Err("implausible code size".into());
        }
        let start = base + 16;
        let mut units = Vec::with_capacity(insns_size.min(1 << 16));
        for k in 0..insns_size {
            units.push(u16_at(data, start + k * 2).ok_or("truncated instructions")?);
        }
        Ok(self.decode(&units))
    }

    fn decode(&self, units: &[u16]) -> Vec<DalvikInsn> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        let mut targets = HashSet::new();
        let mut i = 0;
        while i < units.len() {
            let op = (units[i] & 0xff) as u8;
            // A `nop` unit with a non-zero high byte may start switch/array payload data, which
            // sits inline in the code: skip it by its encoded size and keep decoding after it.
            if op == 0x00
                && let Some((mnemonic, size, operand)) = payload(units, i)
            {
                out.push(DalvikInsn {
                    offset: i,
                    opcode: op,
                    mnemonic,
                    operand,
                    branch_target: None,
                    is_branch_target: false,
                });
                i = i.saturating_add(size);
                continue;
            }
            let (mnemonic, fmt, refkind) = dis::info(op);
            let (operand, target) = self.decode_fmt(units, i, fmt, refkind);
            if let Some(t) = target {
                targets.insert(t);
            }
            out.push(DalvikInsn {
                offset: i,
                opcode: op,
                mnemonic,
                operand,
                branch_target: target,
                is_branch_target: false,
            });
            i += fmt.units().max(1);
        }
        for ins in &mut out {
            if targets.contains(&ins.offset) {
                ins.is_branch_target = true;
            }
        }
        out
    }

    fn decode_fmt(
        &self,
        units: &[u16],
        i: usize,
        fmt: dis::Fmt,
        refkind: dis::Ref,
    ) -> (String, Option<usize>) {
        use dis::Fmt::*;
        let u = |j: usize| units.get(i + j).copied().unwrap_or(0);
        let a8 = ((u(0) >> 8) & 0xff) as u32;
        let a4 = ((u(0) >> 8) & 0xf) as u32;
        let b4 = ((u(0) >> 12) & 0xf) as u32;
        let branch = |off: i32| {
            let t = (i as i64 + off as i64) as usize;
            (format!("{t:04x}"), Some(t))
        };
        let reff = |idx: u16| self.resolve_ref(refkind, idx as usize);

        match fmt {
            F10x | Unknown => (String::new(), None),
            F12x => (format!("v{a4}, v{b4}"), None),
            F11n => (format!("v{a4}, #{}", sign4(u(0) >> 12)), None),
            F11x => (format!("v{a8}"), None),
            F10t => branch(sign8(u(0) >> 8)),
            F20t => branch(sign16(u(1))),
            F22x => (format!("v{a8}, v{}", u(1)), None),
            F21t => {
                let (t, tgt) = branch(sign16(u(1)));
                (format!("v{a8}, {t}"), tgt)
            }
            F21s => (format!("v{a8}, #{}", sign16(u(1))), None),
            F21h => (format!("v{a8}, #{:#x}", (u(1) as u32) << 16), None),
            F21hw => (format!("v{a8}, #{:#x}", (u(1) as u64) << 48), None),
            F21c => (format!("v{a8}, {}", reff(u(1))), None),
            F23x => (format!("v{a8}, v{}, v{}", u(1) & 0xff, u(1) >> 8), None),
            F22b => (
                format!("v{a8}, v{}, #{}", u(1) & 0xff, sign8(u(1) >> 8)),
                None,
            ),
            F22t => {
                let (t, tgt) = branch(sign16(u(1)));
                (format!("v{a4}, v{b4}, {t}"), tgt)
            }
            F22s => (format!("v{a4}, v{b4}, #{}", sign16(u(1))), None),
            F22c => (format!("v{a4}, v{b4}, {}", reff(u(1))), None),
            F30t => branch((u(1) as u32 | ((u(2) as u32) << 16)) as i32),
            F31t => {
                let (t, tgt) = branch((u(1) as u32 | ((u(2) as u32) << 16)) as i32);
                (format!("v{a8}, {t}"), tgt)
            }
            F31i => (
                format!("v{a8}, #{}", (u(1) as u32 | ((u(2) as u32) << 16)) as i32),
                None,
            ),
            F31c => (
                format!(
                    "v{a8}, {}",
                    reff_wide(self, refkind, u(1) as u32 | ((u(2) as u32) << 16))
                ),
                None,
            ),
            F32x => (format!("v{}, v{}", u(1), u(2)), None),
            F35c => (
                format!("{{{}}}, {}", list_regs(u(0), u(2)), reff(u(1))),
                None,
            ),
            F3rc => {
                let count = (u(0) >> 8) & 0xff;
                let list = range_regs(u(2), count);
                (format!("{{{list}}}, {}", reff(u(1))), None)
            }
            F51l => {
                let v = (u(1) as u64)
                    | ((u(2) as u64) << 16)
                    | ((u(3) as u64) << 32)
                    | ((u(4) as u64) << 48);
                (format!("v{a8}, #{}", v as i64), None)
            }
            // invoke-polymorphic: like 35c/3rc plus a trailing proto index.
            F45cc => (
                format!(
                    "{{{}}}, {}, proto@{}",
                    list_regs(u(0), u(2)),
                    reff(u(1)),
                    u(3)
                ),
                None,
            ),
            F4rcc => (
                format!(
                    "{{{}}}, {}, proto@{}",
                    range_regs(u(2), (u(0) >> 8) & 0xff),
                    reff(u(1)),
                    u(3)
                ),
                None,
            ),
        }
    }
}

/// The register list of a 35c/45cc instruction (`A|G|op ... F|E|D|C`).
fn list_regs(u0: u16, u2: u16) -> String {
    let count = (u0 >> 12) & 0xf;
    let g = (u0 >> 8) & 0xf;
    let regs = [
        u2 & 0xf,
        (u2 >> 4) & 0xf,
        (u2 >> 8) & 0xf,
        (u2 >> 12) & 0xf,
        g,
    ];
    regs[..(count as usize).min(5)]
        .iter()
        .map(|r| format!("v{r}"))
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join(", ")
}

/// The register range of a 3rc/4rcc instruction: `count` registers starting at `first`.
fn range_regs(first: u16, count: u16) -> String {
    (0..u32::from(count))
        .map(|k| format!("v{}", u32::from(first) + k))
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join(", ")
}

/// If the code unit at `i` starts a switch/array payload pseudo-instruction, returns its
/// mnemonic, total size in code units and a short description.
fn payload(units: &[u16], i: usize) -> Option<(&'static str, usize, String)> {
    let u = |j: usize| u64::from(units.get(i + j).copied().unwrap_or(0));
    let (mnemonic, size, desc) = match units[i] {
        0x0100 => {
            let n = u(1);
            ("packed-switch-payload", n * 2 + 4, format!("{n} entries"))
        }
        0x0200 => {
            let n = u(1);
            ("sparse-switch-payload", n * 4 + 2, format!("{n} entries"))
        }
        0x0300 => {
            let width = u(1);
            let n = u(2) | (u(3) << 16);
            (
                "fill-array-data-payload",
                (n * width).div_ceil(2) + 4,
                format!("{n} x {width}-byte elements"),
            )
        }
        _ => return None,
    };
    Some((mnemonic, usize::try_from(size).unwrap_or(usize::MAX), desc))
}

/// Resolves a 32-bit reference index (jumbo string / wide const).
fn reff_wide(dex: &Dex, kind: dis::Ref, idx: u32) -> String {
    dex.resolve_ref(kind, idx as usize)
}
```
