```rs
use super::*;

fn uleb(mut v: u32) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    loop {
        let mut b = (v & 0x7f) as u8;
        v >>= 7;
        if v != 0 {
            b |= 0x80;
        }
        out.push(b);
        if v == 0 {
            break;
        }
    }
    out
}

fn string_data(s: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut d = uleb(s.chars().count() as u32);
    d.extend_from_slice(s.as_bytes());
    d.push(0);
    d
}

fn put(out: &mut [u8], off: usize, v: u32) {
    out[off..off + 4].copy_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
}

/// Hand-builds a minimal but structurally valid DEX: a 4-string pool, one type and one method.
/// (Checksum/signature are left zero — the parser reads structure, not integrity fields.)
fn build_dex() -> Vec<u8> {
    let strings = ["Hello", "Lcom/evil/Main;", "http://c2.example", "doEvil"];
    let (n, t, m) = (strings.len(), 1usize, 1usize);
    let string_ids_off = 112;
    let type_ids_off = string_ids_off + n * 4;
    let method_ids_off = type_ids_off + t * 4;
    let data_off = method_ids_off + m * 8;

    let mut blocks = Vec::new();
    let mut offsets = Vec::new();
    let mut cur = data_off;
    for s in strings {
        let b = string_data(s);
        offsets.push(cur as u32);
        cur += b.len();
        blocks.push(b);
    }
    let file_size = cur;

    let mut out = vec![0u8; data_off];
    out[0..8].copy_from_slice(b"dex\n035\0");
    put(&mut out, 32, file_size as u32);
    put(&mut out, 36, 112); // header_size
    put(&mut out, 40, 0x1234_5678); // endian tag
    put(&mut out, 56, n as u32);
    put(&mut out, 60, string_ids_off as u32);
    put(&mut out, 64, t as u32);
    put(&mut out, 68, type_ids_off as u32);
    put(&mut out, 88, m as u32);
    put(&mut out, 92, method_ids_off as u32);
    put(&mut out, 96, 2); // class_defs_size (fictional, for display)

    for (i, off) in offsets.iter().enumerate() {
        put(&mut out, string_ids_off + i * 4, *off);
    }
    put(&mut out, type_ids_off, 1); // type[0] -> string[1] "Lcom/evil/Main;"
    // method[0] = { class_idx: 0 (u16), proto_idx: 0 (u16), name_idx: 3 (u32) }
    put(&mut out, method_ids_off + 4, 3);

    for b in blocks {
        out.extend_from_slice(&b);
    }
    out
}

#[test]
fn detects_dex_magic() {
    let dex = build_dex();
    assert!(is_dex(&dex));
    assert!(!is_dex(b"PK\x03\x04"));
}

#[test]
fn parses_header_and_string_pool() {
    let d = parse(&build_dex()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(d.version, "035");
    assert_eq!(d.string_count, 4);
    assert_eq!(d.class_def_count, 2);
    assert_eq!(
        d.strings,
        ["Hello", "Lcom/evil/Main;", "http://c2.example", "doEvil"]
    );
}

#[test]
fn resolves_types_and_methods() {
    let d = parse(&build_dex()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(d.types, ["Lcom/evil/Main;"]);
    assert_eq!(d.methods, ["Lcom/evil/Main;.doEvil"]);
}

/// Builds a DEX with one class whose one method has a real `code_item`:
///   const/4 v0, #1 ; const-string v0, "http://c2.example" ; return-void
fn build_dex_with_code() -> Vec<u8> {
    let strings = ["Hello", "Lcom/evil/Main;", "http://c2.example", "doEvil"];
    let (n, t, m, c) = (strings.len(), 1usize, 1usize, 1usize);
    let sio = 112;
    let tio = sio + n * 4;
    let mio = tio + t * 4;
    let cio = mio + m * 8;
    let data_off = cio + c * 32;

    // Data section: string blocks, then (4-aligned) the code_item, then the class_data.
    let mut data: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
    let mut cur = data_off;
    let mut soff = Vec::new();
    for s in strings {
        let b = string_data(s);
        soff.push(cur as u32);
        cur += b.len();
        data.extend(b);
    }
    while cur % 4 != 0 {
        data.push(0);
        cur += 1;
    }
    let code_item_off = cur;
    let mut ci = Vec::new();
    ci.extend(1u16.to_le_bytes()); // registers_size
    ci.extend(0u16.to_le_bytes()); // ins_size
    ci.extend(0u16.to_le_bytes()); // outs_size
    ci.extend(0u16.to_le_bytes()); // tries_size
    ci.extend(0u32.to_le_bytes()); // debug_info_off
    ci.extend(4u32.to_le_bytes()); // insns_size (units)
    for inst in [0x1012u16, 0x001a, 0x0002, 0x000e] {
        ci.extend(inst.to_le_bytes());
    }
    data.extend(&ci);
    cur += ci.len();

    let class_data_off = cur;
    let mut cd = Vec::new();
    for v in [0u32, 0, 1, 0] {
        cd.extend(uleb(v)); // static/instance fields, direct(1)/virtual methods
    }
    cd.extend(uleb(0)); // method_idx_diff (-> method 0)
    cd.extend(uleb(0x9)); // access_flags
    cd.extend(uleb(code_item_off as u32)); // code_off
    data.extend(&cd);

    let file_size = data_off + data.len();
    let mut out = vec![0u8; data_off];
    out[0..8].copy_from_slice(b"dex\n035\0");
    put(&mut out, 32, file_size as u32);
    put(&mut out, 36, 112);
    put(&mut out, 40, 0x1234_5678);
    put(&mut out, 56, n as u32);
    put(&mut out, 60, sio as u32);
    put(&mut out, 64, t as u32);
    put(&mut out, 68, tio as u32);
    put(&mut out, 88, m as u32);
    put(&mut out, 92, mio as u32);
    put(&mut out, 96, c as u32);
    put(&mut out, 100, cio as u32);
    for (i, o) in soff.iter().enumerate() {
        put(&mut out, sio + i * 4, *o);
    }
    put(&mut out, tio, 1); // type[0] -> string[1]
    put(&mut out, mio + 4, 3); // method[0] name_idx -> "doEvil"
    put(&mut out, cio, 0); // class_def class_idx -> type[0]
    put(&mut out, cio + 24, class_data_off as u32);
    out.extend(data);
    out
}

#[test]
fn disassembles_method() {
    let dex = build_dex_with_code();
    let d = parse(&dex).unwrap();

    // The class and its method were recovered from class_defs -> class_data.
    let class = d
        .classes
        .iter()
        .find(|c| c.name == "Lcom/evil/Main;")
        .expect("class");
    let method = class
        .methods
        .iter()
        .find(|m| m.name.ends_with("doEvil"))
        .expect("method");

    let il = d.disassemble_method(&dex, method.code_off).unwrap();
    let got: Vec<(usize, &str)> = il.iter().map(|i| (i.offset, i.mnemonic)).collect();
    assert_eq!(
        got,
        [(0, "const/4"), (1, "const-string"), (3, "return-void")]
    );

    assert_eq!(il[0].operand, "v0, #1");
    // const-string resolves the referenced string from the pool.
    assert_eq!(il[1].operand, "v0, \"http://c2.example\"");
    assert_eq!(il[2].operand, "");
}

#[test]
fn rejects_non_dex() {
    assert!(parse(b"not a dex file at all, padding padding padding").is_err());
}

#[test]
fn hostile_table_counts_are_bounded() {
    // A field count above the cap is rejected outright (it used to be missing from the check).
    let mut dex = build_dex();
    put(&mut dex, 80, 0xFFFF_FFFF);
    assert!(parse(&dex).is_err());

    // Large-but-under-cap counts only walk what the file can actually hold.
    let mut dex = build_dex();
    put(&mut dex, 80, 19_000_000); // field_ids_size
    put(&mut dex, 84, 112); // field_ids_off
    put(&mut dex, 88, 19_000_000); // method_ids_size
    let d = parse(&dex).unwrap();
    assert!(d.fields.len() <= dex.len() / 8);
    assert!(d.methods.len() <= dex.len() / 8);
    assert_eq!(d.field_count, 19_000_000);
}

#[test]
fn class_data_method_index_wraps_instead_of_panicking() {
    let mut cd = Vec::new();
    for v in [0, 0, 2, 0] {
        cd.extend(uleb(v)); // static/instance fields, direct/virtual methods
    }
    for diff in [0xFFFF_FFFF, 5] {
        cd.extend(uleb(diff));
        cd.extend(uleb(1)); // access flags
        cd.extend(uleb(0)); // code_off
    }
    let ms = parse_class_methods(&cd, 0, &[]);
    assert_eq!(ms.len(), 2);
}

fn decode_units(units: &[u16]) -> Vec<DalvikInsn> {
    let d = parse(&build_dex()).unwrap();
    d.decode(units)
}

#[test]
fn payloads_are_skipped_and_decoding_continues() {
    let units = [
        0x0000, // nop
        0x0100, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, // packed-switch-payload: 1 entry → 6 units
        0x0300, 1, 3, 0, 0x4241, 0x0043, // fill-array-data-payload: 3 x 1 byte → 6 units
        0x0200, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0,      // sparse-switch-payload: 1 entry → 6 units
        0x000e, // return-void
    ];
    let got: Vec<(usize, &str)> = decode_units(&units)
        .iter()
        .map(|i| (i.offset, i.mnemonic))
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(
        got,
        [
            (0, "nop"),
            (1, "packed-switch-payload"),
            (7, "fill-array-data-payload"),
            (13, "sparse-switch-payload"),
            (19, "return-void"),
        ]
    );
    // A payload with an absurd size just ends decoding, without panicking.
    let got = decode_units(&[0x0300, 0xFFFF, 0xFFFF, 0xFFFF, 0x000e]);
    assert_eq!(got.len(), 1);
}

#[test]
fn wide_and_range_operands() {
    // const-wide/high16 v1, #0x4000 << 48
    let il = decode_units(&[0x0119, 0x4000]);
    assert_eq!(il[0].mnemonic, "const-wide/high16");
    assert_eq!(il[0].operand, "v1, #0x4000000000000000");
    // const/high16 keeps its 16-bit shift.
    let il = decode_units(&[0x0115, 0x4000]);
    assert_eq!(il[0].operand, "v1, #0x40000000");

    // invoke-static/range with a first register near u16::MAX must not overflow.
    let il = decode_units(&[0x0377, 0, 0xFFFF]);
    assert_eq!(
        il[0].operand,
        "{v65535, v65536, v65537}, Lcom/evil/Main;.doEvil"
    );

    // invoke-polymorphic {v0, v1}, meth@0, proto@5
    let il = decode_units(&[0x20fa, 0, 0x0010, 5]);
    assert_eq!(il[0].operand, "{v0, v1}, Lcom/evil/Main;.doEvil, proto@5");
    // invoke-polymorphic/range {v7, v8}, meth@0, proto@2
    let il = decode_units(&[0x02fb, 0, 7, 2]);
    assert_eq!(il[0].operand, "{v7, v8}, Lcom/evil/Main;.doEvil, proto@2");
}
```

`crates/orress-diff/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! Binary diffing (M14): BinDiff-style function matching between two analyzed programs — for patch
//! diffing ("what changed between these two builds?") and malware-variant comparison.
//!
//! Each function is reduced to a **position-independent signature**: CFG shape (instruction / basic
//! block / edge / call counts) plus an *opcode hash* (the sequence of decoded mnemonics with their
//! registers and small immediates, but not addresses or branch targets — so it survives relocation
//! and address shifts, while a `jz` -> `jnz` patch still changes it). Functions are
//! then matched one-to-one in order of confidence — by name, then identical opcode hash, then CFG
//! shape, then a greedy best-similarity pass — and each pair is classed **identical** or
//! **changed**; unmatched functions are **added** (only in B) or **removed** (only in A).

use std::collections::HashMap;

use orress_analysis::{Program, TokenKind};

const FNV_OFFSET: u64 = 1469598103934665603;
const FNV_PRIME: u64 = 1099511628211;
/// A greedy match is only accepted above this similarity, so unrelated functions stay unmatched.
const GREEDY_THRESHOLD: f32 = 0.5;
/// The greedy pass compares each function with at most this many unmatched candidates (those with
/// the nearest instruction counts), so it stays near-linear on large binaries.
const GREEDY_CANDIDATES: usize = 256;
/// Immediates at or above this are treated as (relocatable) addresses and left out of the hash —
/// the same cut-off the disassembler uses for data references.
const ADDRESS_LIKE: u64 = 0x1_0000;

/// A function reduced to features that do not depend on its address.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct FuncSig {
    pub entry: u64,
    /// A reliable name (symbol/import/detected — never an auto `sub_xxx`), used as the strongest
    /// matching key.
    pub name: Option<String>,
    pub insns: u32,
    pub blocks: u32,
    pub edges: u32,
    pub calls: u32,
    /// Hash of the instruction sequence (mnemonics, registers, small immediates), in address order.
    pub opcode_hash: u64,
}

impl FuncSig {
    fn fingerprint(&self) -> (u32, u32, u32, u32) {
        (self.insns, self.blocks, self.edges, self.calls)
    }

    fn reference(&self) -> FuncRef {
        FuncRef {
            entry: self.entry,
            name: self.name.clone(),
        }
    }
}

/// How a matched pair of functions relates.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MatchKind {
    /// Same code (identical opcode hash and instruction count).
    Identical,
    /// Matched, but the code differs.
    Changed,
}

/// A reference to a function in one program (for the added/removed lists and match endpoints).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct FuncRef {
    pub entry: u64,
    pub name: Option<String>,
}

/// A matched pair of functions across the two programs.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct Match {
    pub a: FuncRef,
    pub b: FuncRef,
    pub kind: MatchKind,
    /// 0.0–1.0 (1.0 when identical).
    pub similarity: f32,
}

/// The result of diffing two programs.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct Diff {
    pub matches: Vec<Match>,
    /// Functions only in B.
    pub added: Vec<FuncRef>,
    /// Functions only in A.
    pub removed: Vec<FuncRef>,
}

impl Diff {
    /// (identical, changed, added, removed) counts.
    pub fn summary(&self) -> (usize, usize, usize, usize) {
        let identical = self
            .matches
            .iter()
            .filter(|m| m.kind == MatchKind::Identical)
            .count();
        (
            identical,
            self.matches.len() - identical,
            self.added.len(),
            self.removed.len(),
        )
    }
}

/// Extracts a position-independent signature for every function in `program`.
pub fn signatures(program: &Program) -> Vec<FuncSig> {
    program
        .functions
        .values()
        .map(|f| {
            let edges = f.blocks.iter().map(|b| b.succs.len()).sum::<usize>() as u32;
            let mut hash = FNV_OFFSET;
            for block in &f.blocks {
                for &insn_addr in &block.insns {
                    hash_insn(program, insn_addr, &mut hash);
                }
            }
            FuncSig {
                entry: f.entry,
                name: reliable_name(program, f.entry),
                insns: f.insn_count() as u32,
                blocks: f.blocks.len() as u32,
                edges,
                calls: f.calls.len() as u32,
                opcode_hash: hash,
            }
        })
        .collect()
}

fn fnv(hash: &mut u64, bytes: &[u8]) {
    for &b in bytes {
        *hash ^= u64::from(b);
        *hash = hash.wrapping_mul(FNV_PRIME);
    }
}

/// Folds one instruction into `hash`: its mnemonic and operands, with addresses (branch targets,
/// RIP-relative/absolute data references, address-sized immediates) replaced by a placeholder so
/// the hash does not depend on where the code or its data was placed.
fn hash_insn(program: &Program, addr: u64, hash: &mut u64) {
    let len = program
        .insns
        .get(&addr)
        .map_or(program.isa.max_len(), |&l| usize::from(l));
    let Some(bytes) = program.memory.read(addr, len) else {
        return;
    };
    let Some(insn) = orress_arch::decode(program.isa, bytes, addr) else {
        // Undecodable: fall back to the first byte.
        fnv(hash, &bytes[..bytes.len().min(1)]);
        return;
    };
    fnv(hash, insn.mnemonic.as_bytes());
    for t in &insn.operands {
        match t.kind {
            TokenKind::Address(_) => fnv(hash, b"\x01"),
            TokenKind::Number if number(&t.text).is_some_and(|v| v >= ADDRESS_LIKE) => {
                fnv(hash, b"\x01")
            }
            _ => fnv(hash, t.text.as_bytes()),
        }
    }
    fnv(hash, b"\x00");
}

/// The value of a numeric operand token (`0x10`, `#0x10]`, `-8`, `16`), ignoring sign.
fn number(text: &str) -> Option<u64> {
    let t = text.trim_matches(|c: char| matches!(c, '#' | '[' | ']' | '!' | ' '));
    let t = t.trim_start_matches('-');
    match t.strip_prefix("0x") {
        Some(hex) => u64::from_str_radix(hex, 16).ok(),
        None => t.parse().ok(),
    }
}

/// A name usable as a matching key — present and not an auto-generated `sub_xxx`.
fn reliable_name(program: &Program, entry: u64) -> Option<String> {
    use orress_analysis::NameKind;
    program.names.get(&entry).and_then(|n| match n.kind {
        NameKind::Auto => None,
        _ => Some(n.text.clone()),
    })
}

/// Diffs two analyzed programs.
pub fn diff_programs(a: &Program, b: &Program) -> Diff {
    diff(&signatures(a), &signatures(b))
}

/// The core matcher over extracted signatures (pure; the engine's tested surface).
pub fn diff(a: &[FuncSig], b: &[FuncSig]) -> Diff {
    let mut a_used = vec![false; a.len()];
    let mut b_used = vec![false; b.len()];
    let mut matches = Vec::new();

    // Passes in decreasing confidence; each matches only one-to-one *unique* keys.
    match_unique(a, b, &mut a_used, &mut b_used, &mut matches, |s| {
        s.name.clone()
    });
    match_unique(a, b, &mut a_used, &mut b_used, &mut matches, |s| {
        Some(s.opcode_hash)
    });
    match_unique(a, b, &mut a_used, &mut b_used, &mut matches, |s| {
        Some(s.fingerprint())
    });
    greedy(a, b, &mut a_used, &mut b_used, &mut matches);

    let removed = a
        .iter()
        .zip(&a_used)
        .filter(|(_, u)| !**u)
        .map(|(s, _)| s.reference())
        .collect();
    let added = b
        .iter()
        .zip(&b_used)
        .filter(|(_, u)| !**u)
        .map(|(s, _)| s.reference())
        .collect();
    matches.sort_by_key(|m| m.a.entry); // stable order by A's entry
    Diff {
        matches,
        added,
        removed,
    }
}

/// Pairs functions whose `key` is present exactly once on each side (so a match is unambiguous).
fn match_unique<K: Eq + std::hash::Hash>(
    a: &[FuncSig],
    b: &[FuncSig],
    a_used: &mut [bool],
    b_used: &mut [bool],
    matches: &mut Vec<Match>,
    key: impl Fn(&FuncSig) -> Option<K>,
) {
    let index = |sigs: &[FuncSig], used: &[bool]| {
        let mut map: HashMap<K, Vec<usize>> = HashMap::new();
        for (i, s) in sigs.iter().enumerate() {
            if !used[i]
                && let Some(k) = key(s)
            {
                map.entry(k).or_default().push(i);
            }
        }
        map
    };
    let a_map = index(a, a_used);
    let b_map = index(b, b_used);
    for (k, ais) in &a_map {
        if ais.len() != 1 {
            continue;
        }
        if let Some(bjs) = b_map.get(k)
            && bjs.len() == 1
        {
            let (i, j) = (ais[0], bjs[0]);
            a_used[i] = true;
            b_used[j] = true;
            matches.push(make_match(&a[i], &b[j]));
        }
    }
}

/// Matches leftovers by best similarity above the threshold (one-to-one). Each A function is
/// compared with at most [`GREEDY_CANDIDATES`] unmatched B functions — those nearest in instruction
/// count — so this is not quadratic on large binaries. Ties go to the lowest B index.
fn greedy(
    a: &[FuncSig],
    b: &[FuncSig],
    a_used: &mut [bool],
    b_used: &mut [bool],
    matches: &mut Vec<Match>,
) {
    // Unmatched B functions sorted by instruction count (then index, for determinism).
    let mut order: Vec<usize> = (0..b.len()).filter(|&j| !b_used[j]).collect();
    order.sort_by_key(|&j| (b[j].insns, j));
    for i in 0..a.len() {
        if a_used[i] {
            continue;
        }
        let mut best: Option<usize> = None;
        let mut best_sim = GREEDY_THRESHOLD;
        let mut consider = |j: usize| {
            let s = similarity(&a[i], &b[j]);
            if s > best_sim || (s == best_sim && best.is_some_and(|k| j < k)) {
                best_sim = s;
                best = Some(j);
            }
        };
        // Walk outwards from A's instruction count, nearest first, over unmatched candidates.
        let pos = order.partition_point(|&j| b[j].insns < a[i].insns);
        let (mut lo, mut hi) = (pos, pos);
        let mut seen = 0;
        while seen < GREEDY_CANDIDATES && (lo > 0 || hi < order.len()) {
            let take_hi = match (lo > 0, hi < order.len()) {
                (true, true) => {
                    b[order[hi]].insns - a[i].insns.min(b[order[hi]].insns)
                        <= a[i].insns - b[order[lo - 1]].insns.min(a[i].insns)
                }
                (false, _) => true,
                (true, false) => false,
            };
            let j = if take_hi {
                hi += 1;
                order[hi - 1]
            } else {
                lo -= 1;
                order[lo]
            };
            if !b_used[j] {
                consider(j);
                seen += 1;
            }
        }
        if let Some(j) = best {
            a_used[i] = true;
            b_used[j] = true;
            matches.push(make_match(&a[i], &b[j]));
        }
    }
}

fn make_match(a: &FuncSig, b: &FuncSig) -> Match {
    let identical = a.opcode_hash == b.opcode_hash && a.insns == b.insns;
    Match {
        a: a.reference(),
        b: b.reference(),
        kind: if identical {
            MatchKind::Identical
        } else {
            MatchKind::Changed
        },
        similarity: if identical { 1.0 } else { similarity(a, b) },
    }
}

/// Feature-weighted similarity in 0.0–1.0 (1.0 when the opcode hashes match).
fn similarity(a: &FuncSig, b: &FuncSig) -> f32 {
    if a.opcode_hash == b.opcode_hash {
        return 1.0;
    }
    let ratio = |x: u32, y: u32| {
        if x == 0 && y == 0 {
            1.0
        } else {
            1.0 - (f64::from(x) - f64::from(y)).abs() as f32 / x.max(y) as f32
        }
    };
    0.4 * ratio(a.insns, b.insns)
        + 0.3 * ratio(a.blocks, b.blocks)
        + 0.2 * ratio(a.edges, b.edges)
        + 0.1 * ratio(a.calls, b.calls)
}
```

```rs
use super::*;

fn sig(
    entry: u64,
    name: Option<&str>,
    insns: u32,
    blocks: u32,
    edges: u32,
    calls: u32,
    hash: u64,
) -> FuncSig {
    FuncSig {
        entry,
        name: name.map(str::to_string),
        insns,
        blocks,
        edges,
        calls,
        opcode_hash: hash,
    }
}

#[test]
fn identical_program_matches_everything() {
    let a = vec![
        sig(0x1000, Some("main"), 20, 4, 5, 2, 0xaa),
        sig(0x1100, Some("helper"), 8, 1, 0, 1, 0xbb),
    ];
    // Same code at shifted addresses (a rebuild): matched by name/opcode-hash, all identical.
    let b = vec![
        sig(0x2000, Some("main"), 20, 4, 5, 2, 0xaa),
        sig(0x2100, Some("helper"), 8, 1, 0, 1, 0xbb),
    ];
    let d = diff(&a, &b);
    assert_eq!(d.summary(), (2, 0, 0, 0));
    assert!(
        d.matches
            .iter()
            .all(|m| m.kind == MatchKind::Identical && m.similarity == 1.0)
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_changed_function_is_matched_by_name_and_marked_changed() {
    let a = vec![sig(0x1000, Some("check"), 20, 4, 5, 2, 0xaa)];
    // Same name, different code/shape -> Changed (not identical).
    let b = vec![sig(0x2000, Some("check"), 24, 5, 7, 3, 0xcc)];
    let d = diff(&a, &b);
    assert_eq!(d.summary(), (0, 1, 0, 0));
    assert_eq!(d.matches[0].kind, MatchKind::Changed);
    assert!(d.matches[0].similarity > 0.0 && d.matches[0].similarity < 1.0);
}

#[test]
fn added_and_removed_functions_are_reported() {
    let a = vec![
        sig(0x1000, Some("main"), 20, 4, 5, 2, 0xaa),
        sig(0x1100, Some("gone"), 8, 1, 0, 1, 0xbb),
    ];
    let b = vec![
        sig(0x2000, Some("main"), 20, 4, 5, 2, 0xaa),
        sig(0x2100, Some("fresh"), 30, 6, 9, 4, 0xdd),
    ];
    let d = diff(&a, &b);
    assert_eq!(d.summary(), (1, 0, 1, 1));
    assert_eq!(d.removed[0].name.as_deref(), Some("gone"));
    assert_eq!(d.added[0].name.as_deref(), Some("fresh"));
}

#[test]
fn identical_code_matches_even_when_renamed() {
    // No reliable names (both auto): matched by opcode hash -> identical, despite moving.
    let a = vec![sig(0x1000, None, 12, 2, 2, 0, 0x55)];
    let b = vec![sig(0x9000, None, 12, 2, 2, 0, 0x55)];
    let d = diff(&a, &b);
    assert_eq!(d.summary(), (1, 0, 0, 0));
    assert_eq!(d.matches[0].a.entry, 0x1000);
    assert_eq!(d.matches[0].b.entry, 0x9000);
}

#[test]
fn greedy_matches_a_moved_tweaked_function_but_not_unrelated_ones() {
    // Nameless, different hash, but near-identical CFG shape -> greedy Changed match.
    let a = vec![sig(0x1000, None, 100, 10, 14, 5, 0x1)];
    let b = vec![sig(0x2000, None, 101, 10, 14, 5, 0x2)];
    let d = diff(&a, &b);
    assert_eq!(d.summary().1, 1); // one changed match
    assert!(d.added.is_empty() && d.removed.is_empty());

    // Wildly different shapes stay unmatched (below threshold).
    let a2 = vec![sig(0x1000, None, 100, 20, 40, 10, 0x1)];
    let b2 = vec![sig(0x2000, None, 3, 1, 0, 0, 0x2)];
    let d2 = diff(&a2, &b2);
    assert_eq!(d2.summary(), (0, 0, 1, 1)); // added + removed, no match
}

#[test]
fn name_match_wins_over_an_ambiguous_shape() {
    // Two B functions share the fingerprint; the name pass disambiguates `main` first.
    let a = vec![sig(0x1000, Some("main"), 10, 2, 2, 1, 0xaa)];
    let b = vec![
        sig(0x2000, Some("other"), 10, 2, 2, 1, 0xff),
        sig(0x2100, Some("main"), 10, 2, 2, 1, 0xaa),
    ];
    let d = diff(&a, &b);
    assert_eq!(d.matches.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(d.matches[0].b.name.as_deref(), Some("main"));
    assert_eq!(d.matches[0].kind, MatchKind::Identical);
    assert_eq!(d.added.len(), 1); // "other" is B-only
}

/// An ELF-like x86-64 program with `code` at `base` and a `check` symbol at its start.
fn program(code: &[u8], base: u64) -> orress_analysis::Program {
    use orress_loaders::{BinaryInfo, Format, Kind, NamedAddress, Perms, Section};
    let mut text = vec![0xccu8; 0x100];
    text[..code.len()].copy_from_slice(code);
    let mut file = vec![0u8; 0x200];
    file.extend(&text);
    let info = BinaryInfo {
        format: Format::Elf,
        kind: Kind::Executable,
        arch: "x86-64".into(),
        bits: Some(64),
        entry: Some(base),
        image_base: base & !0xfff,
        sections: vec![Section {
            name: ".text".into(),
            offset: 0x200,
            file_size: 0x100,
            address: base,
            virtual_size: 0x100,
            perms: Perms {
                read: true,
                write: false,
                execute: true,
            },
            entropy: None,
        }],
        function_symbols: vec![NamedAddress {
            address: base,
            name: "check".into(),
        }],
        ..BinaryInfo::default()
    };
    orress_analysis::Program::analyze(&info, std::sync::Arc::new(file), &[]).expect("x86-64")
}

#[test]
fn a_patched_condition_is_reported_changed() {
    // test eax,eax; jz (near, 0f 84) +6; mov eax,1; ret; xor eax,eax; ret — vs. the same with
    // jnz (0f 85): only the second opcode byte differs, and the CFG shape is identical.
    let original = [
        0x85, 0xc0, 0x0f, 0x84, 0x06, 0, 0, 0, 0xb8, 0x01, 0, 0, 0, 0xc3, 0x31, 0xc0, 0xc3,
    ];
    let mut patched = original;
    patched[3] = 0x85;
    let a = program(&original, 0x40_1000);
    let b = program(&patched, 0x40_1000);
    let d = diff_programs(&a, &b);
    assert_eq!(d.summary(), (0, 1, 0, 0), "{d:?}");

    // The same code moved to another address is still identical.
    let moved = program(&original, 0x50_2000);
    assert_eq!(diff_programs(&a, &moved).summary(), (1, 0, 0, 0));
}

#[test]
fn greedy_scales_and_still_matches_the_closest_shape() {
    // Many unrelated nameless functions on both sides; the tweaked one still pairs up.
    let mut a: Vec<FuncSig> = (0..2000)
        .map(|i| sig(0x1000 + i * 0x10, None, 5 + i as u32, 1, 0, 0, 0x1_0000 + i))
        .collect();
    let mut b: Vec<FuncSig> = (0..2000)
        .map(|i| sig(0x9000 + i * 0x10, None, 5 + i as u32, 1, 0, 0, 0x9_0000 + i))
        .collect();
    a.push(sig(0x80_0000, None, 100_000, 50, 70, 9, 0x77));
    b.push(sig(0x90_0000, None, 100_010, 50, 70, 9, 0x78));
    let d = diff(&a, &b);
    let m = d
        .matches
        .iter()
        .find(|m| m.a.entry == 0x80_0000)
        .expect("matched");
    assert_eq!(m.b.entry, 0x90_0000);
}
```

```rs
//! Prints a .NET assembly's metadata and the IL of each method.
//! Run: cargo run -p orress-dotnet --example dotnet_info -- File.dll
fn main() {
    let p = std::env::args()
        .nth(1)
        .expect("usage: dotnet_info <File.dll>");
    let d = std::fs::read(&p).unwrap();
    let a = orress_dotnet::parse(&d).expect("parse");
    println!(
        "{} module={} asm={:?} · {} types · {} user strings",
        a.runtime_version,
        a.module_name,
        a.assembly_name,
        a.types.len(),
        a.user_strings.len()
    );
    for t in &a.types {
        if t.methods.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        println!("\ntype {}", t.full_name());
        for m in &t.methods {
            println!("  {} (rva {:#x})", m.name, m.rva);
            if let Ok(il) = a.disassemble(&d, m.rva) {
                for i in il.iter().take(40) {
                    let mark = if i.is_branch_target { ">>" } else { "  " };
                    println!(
                        "    {mark} IL_{:04x}: {:<12} {}",
                        i.offset, i.opcode, i.operand
                    );
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-dotnet/src/il.rs`:

```rs
//! CIL (MSIL) disassembly: decode a method body's bytecode into instructions, resolving metadata
//! tokens and user-string tokens through caller-provided closures. The opcode table is the stable
//! ECMA-335 set (single-byte plus the `0xFE` two-byte prefix); every opcode's operand size is
//! known, so decoding stays aligned.

/// The operand that follows an opcode.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Opr {
    None,
    /// 1-byte unsigned (prefix operands: `unaligned.`, `no.`).
    U8,
    /// 1-/2-byte local/arg index.
    Var8,
    Var16,
    /// Inline integers.
    ShortI,
    I,
    I8,
    /// Inline floats.
    ShortR,
    R,
    /// Branch offsets (relative to the next instruction).
    ShortBr,
    Br,
    Switch,
    /// A 4-byte metadata token (method/field/type/tok/sig).
    Tok,
    /// A 4-byte user-string token.
    Str,
}

/// One decoded CIL instruction.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct Il {
    /// Offset within the method body's code (matches ildasm `IL_xxxx`).
    pub offset: usize,
    pub opcode: &'static str,
    /// Rendered operand (token resolved to a name, string to its literal, branch to a target).
    pub operand: String,
    pub branch_target: Option<usize>,
    pub is_branch_target: bool,
}

/// Disassembles a method body's `code`. `resolve_tok` turns a metadata token into a name;
/// `resolve_str` turns a user-string token into the quoted literal.
pub fn disassemble(
    code: &[u8],
    resolve_tok: impl Fn(u32) -> String,
    resolve_str: impl Fn(u32) -> String,
) -> Vec<Il> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut targets: std::collections::HashSet<usize> = std::collections::HashSet::new();
    let mut i = 0usize;

    let u8 = |c: &[u8], i: &mut usize| -> Option<u8> {
        let v = *c.get(*i)?;
        *i += 1;
        Some(v)
    };
    let u16 = |c: &[u8], i: &mut usize| -> Option<u16> {
        let v = u16::from_le_bytes([*c.get(*i)?, *c.get(*i + 1)?]);
        *i += 2;
        Some(v)
    };
    let u32r = |c: &[u8], i: &mut usize| -> Option<u32> {
        let v = u32::from_le_bytes([
            *c.get(*i)?,
            *c.get(*i + 1)?,
            *c.get(*i + 2)?,
            *c.get(*i + 3)?,
        ]);
        *i += 4;
        Some(v)
    };

    while i < code.len() {
        let start = i;
        let b = code[i];
        i += 1;
        let (name, opr) = if b == 0xFE {
            match u8(code, &mut i) {
                Some(b2) => op2(b2),
                None => break,
            }
        } else {
            op1(b)
        }
        .unwrap_or(("unknown", Opr::None));

        let mut operand = String::new();
        let mut branch_target = None;
        let ok = (|| -> Option<()> {
            match opr {
                Opr::None => {}
                Opr::U8 => operand = u8(code, &mut i)?.to_string(),
                Opr::Var8 => operand = u8(code, &mut i)?.to_string(),
                Opr::Var16 => operand = u16(code, &mut i)?.to_string(),
                Opr::ShortI => operand = (u8(code, &mut i)? as i8).to_string(),
                Opr::I => operand = (u32r(code, &mut i)? as i32).to_string(),
                Opr::I8 => {
                    let lo = u32r(code, &mut i)? as u64;
                    let hi = u32r(code, &mut i)? as u64;
                    operand = ((lo | (hi << 32)) as i64).to_string();
                }
                Opr::ShortR => operand = f32::from_bits(u32r(code, &mut i)?).to_string(),
                Opr::R => {
                    let lo = u32r(code, &mut i)? as u64;
                    let hi = u32r(code, &mut i)? as u64;
                    operand = f64::from_bits(lo | (hi << 32)).to_string();
                }
                Opr::ShortBr => {
                    let rel = u8(code, &mut i)? as i8 as isize;
                    let t = (i as isize + rel) as usize;
                    branch_target = Some(t);
                    targets.insert(t);
                    operand = format!("IL_{t:04x}");
                }
                Opr::Br => {
                    let rel = u32r(code, &mut i)? as i32 as isize;
                    let t = (i as isize + rel) as usize;
                    branch_target = Some(t);
                    targets.insert(t);
                    operand = format!("IL_{t:04x}");
                }
                Opr::Switch => {
                    let n = u32r(code, &mut i)? as usize;
                    let mut rels = Vec::with_capacity(n.min(4096));
                    for _ in 0..n {
                        rels.push(u32r(code, &mut i)? as i32 as isize);
                    }
                    let base = i as isize;
                    let ts: Vec<String> = rels
                        .iter()
                        .map(|r| {
                            let t = (base + r) as usize;
                            targets.insert(t);
                            format!("IL_{t:04x}")
                        })
                        .collect();
                    operand = format!("({})", ts.join(", "));
                }
                Opr::Tok => operand = resolve_tok(u32r(code, &mut i)?),
                Opr::Str => operand = resolve_str(u32r(code, &mut i)?),
            }
            Some(())
        })();
        if ok.is_none() {
            out.push(Il {
                offset: start,
                opcode: name,
                operand: "(truncated)".into(),
                branch_target: None,
                is_branch_target: false,
            });
            break;
        }

        out.push(Il {
            offset: start,
            opcode: name,
            operand,
            branch_target,
            is_branch_target: false,
        });
    }

    for il in &mut out {
        if targets.contains(&il.offset) {
            il.is_branch_target = true;
        }
    }
    out
}
```

`crates/orress-dotnet/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! .NET (CLI) assembly loading for ORRESS.
//!
//! A .NET executable is a PE whose CLI header (data directory 14) points at a metadata region: a
//! root, a set of streams (`#~` tables, `#Strings`, `#US` user strings, `#GUID`, `#Blob`), and the
//! metadata tables themselves. [`parse`] walks all of that with no dependencies and recovers the
//! assembly/module names, the type and method names, and the **user-string heap** — the literal
//! strings in the IL, where .NET malware hides URLs, commands and keys.
//!
//! Row sizes are computed from the ECMA-335 schema in `tables` plus the heap-index and
//! table-row sizes, so it reads real assemblies, not just a fixed layout. Tolerant of hostile
//! input (bounded, errors instead of panics). [`DotNet::disassemble`] decodes a method's IL body
//! with tokens and user strings resolved.

mod il;
mod sig;
mod tables;

pub use il::Il;
use tables::{Coded, Col, columns, table_name};

/// A method: its name, decoded signature and the RVA of its body (0 if it has no body).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Method {
    pub name: String,
    /// `(params) : ret`, decoded from the signature blob (empty if unavailable).
    pub signature: String,
    pub rva: u32,
}

/// A type and the methods defined on it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct TypeInfo {
    pub namespace: String,
    pub name: String,
    pub methods: Vec<Method>,
}

impl TypeInfo {
    /// `Namespace.Name` (or just `Name` with no namespace).
    pub fn full_name(&self) -> String {
        if self.namespace.is_empty() {
            self.name.clone()
        } else {
            format!("{}.{}", self.namespace, self.name)
        }
    }
}

/// A parsed .NET assembly.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct DotNet {
    /// CLI runtime version string, e.g. `v4.0.30319`.
    pub runtime_version: String,
    pub module_name: String,
    pub assembly_name: Option<String>,
    pub types: Vec<TypeInfo>,
    /// `#US` user strings — the string literals in the code.
    pub user_strings: Vec<String>,
    /// `(table name, row count)` for present tables.
    pub table_rows: Vec<(&'static str, u32)>,
    /// Everything needed to resolve tokens and locate method bodies for IL disassembly.
    resolver: Resolver,
}

fn u16a(d: &[u8], o: usize) -> Option<u16> {
    d.get(o..o + 2).map(|s| u16::from_le_bytes([s[0], s[1]]))
}
fn u32a(d: &[u8], o: usize) -> Option<u32> {
    d.get(o..o + 4)
        .map(|s| u32::from_le_bytes([s[0], s[1], s[2], s[3]]))
}

/// True if `data` is a PE with a CLI (.NET) header.
pub fn is_dotnet(data: &[u8]) -> bool {
    metadata_offset(data).is_ok()
}

/// A PE section mapping entry: `(virtual_address, size, raw_file_pointer)`.
type Section = (u32, u32, u32);

fn rva_to_off(sections: &[Section], rva: u32) -> Option<usize> {
    sections
        .iter()
        .find(|&&(va, size, _)| rva >= va && u64::from(rva) < u64::from(va) + u64::from(size))
        .and_then(|&(va, _, ptr)| usize::try_from(u64::from(ptr) + u64::from(rva - va)).ok())
}

/// Finds the metadata root's file offset and the PE section table (via the CLI header).
fn metadata_offset(d: &[u8]) -> Result<(usize, Vec<Section>), String> {
    if d.len() < 0x40 || &d[0..2] != b"MZ" {
        return Err("not a PE (no MZ)".into());
    }
    let pe = u32a(d, 0x3c).ok_or("truncated")? as usize;
    if d.get(pe..pe + 4) != Some(b"PE\0\0") {
        return Err("not a PE (no PE signature)".into());
    }
    let nsec = u16a(d, pe + 6).ok_or("truncated")? as usize;
    let optsize = u16a(d, pe + 20).ok_or("truncated")? as usize;
    let opt = pe + 24;
    let magic = u16a(d, opt).ok_or("truncated")?;
    let dd = match magic {
        0x10b => opt + 96,  // PE32
        0x20b => opt + 112, // PE32+
        _ => return Err("unknown optional-header magic".into()),
    };
    let cor_rva = u32a(d, dd + 14 * 8).ok_or("truncated")?;
    if cor_rva == 0 {
        return Err("not a .NET assembly (no CLI header)".into());
    }

    let sec0 = opt + optsize;
    let mut sections = Vec::with_capacity(nsec.min(96));
    for i in 0..nsec {
        let s = sec0 + i * 40;
        let vsz = u32a(d, s + 8).ok_or("truncated section")?;
        let va = u32a(d, s + 12).ok_or("truncated section")?;
        let rsz = u32a(d, s + 16).ok_or("truncated section")?;
        let ptr = u32a(d, s + 20).ok_or("truncated section")?;
        sections.push((va, vsz.max(rsz), ptr));
    }

    let cor = rva_to_off(&sections, cor_rva).ok_or("CLI header RVA not in any section")?;
    let md_rva = u32a(d, cor + 8).ok_or("truncated CLI header")?;
    let md = rva_to_off(&sections, md_rva).ok_or("metadata RVA not in any section")?;
    if u32a(d, md) != Some(0x424a_5342) {
        return Err("bad metadata signature (expected BSJB)".into());
    }
    Ok((md, sections))
}

/// A located metadata stream: absolute file offset and size.
struct Stream {
    off: usize,
    size: usize,
}

/// Parses a .NET assembly.
pub fn parse(data: &[u8]) -> Result<DotNet, String> {
    let (md, sections) = metadata_offset(data)?;

    let ver_len = u32a(data, md + 12).ok_or("truncated metadata root")? as usize;
    let runtime_version = {
        let s = data
            .get(md + 16..md + 16 + ver_len)
            .ok_or("truncated version")?;
        String::from_utf8_lossy(s)
            .trim_end_matches('\0')
            .to_string()
    };
    let mut p = md + 16 + ((ver_len + 3) & !3);
    let nstreams = u16a(data, p + 2).ok_or("truncated stream count")?;
    p += 4;

    let mut streams: std::collections::HashMap<String, Stream> = std::collections::HashMap::new();
    for _ in 0..nstreams {
        let off = u32a(data, p).ok_or("truncated stream header")? as usize;
        let size = u32a(data, p + 4).ok_or("truncated stream header")? as usize;
        p += 8;
        let start = p;
        while data.get(p).is_some_and(|&b| b != 0) {
            p += 1;
        }
        let name = String::from_utf8_lossy(&data[start..p]).into_owned();
        p += 1;
        p = (p + 3) & !3; // pad to 4
        streams.insert(
            name,
            Stream {
                off: md + off,
                size,
            },
        );
    }

    let strings = streams.get("#Strings").ok_or("no #Strings heap")?;
    let tilde = streams
        .get("#~")
        .or_else(|| streams.get("#-"))
        .ok_or("no table stream")?;

    let md_tables = MdTables::parse(data, tilde.off, tilde.size)?;
    let string_at =
        |idx: u32| read_cstr(data, strings.off + idx as usize, strings.off + strings.size);

    // Module name (Module table, row 1, Name column = index 1).
    let module_name = md_tables
        .cell(data, 0x00, 1, 1)
        .map(|i| string_at(i as u32))
        .unwrap_or_default();

    // Assembly name (Assembly table, row 1, Name is column 7).
    let assembly_name = (md_tables.rows[0x20] > 0)
        .then(|| {
            md_tables
                .cell(data, 0x20, 1, 7)
                .map(|i| string_at(i as u32))
        })
        .flatten();

    // Types and their methods (with decoded signatures from the blob heap).
    let blob_off = streams.get("#Blob").map(|s| s.off);
    let types = collect_types(data, &md_tables, &string_at, blob_off);

    // User strings (#US).
    let user_strings = streams
        .get("#US")
        .map(|s| read_user_strings(data, s.off, s.size))
        .unwrap_or_default();

    let table_rows = (0u8..=0x2c)
        .filter(|&id| md_tables.rows[id as usize] > 0)
        .map(|id| (table_name(id), md_tables.rows[id as usize]))
        .collect();

    let resolver = Resolver {
        tables: md_tables,
        strings_off: strings.off,
        strings_size: strings.size,
        us_off: streams.get("#US").map(|s| s.off),
        sections,
    };

    Ok(DotNet {
        runtime_version,
        module_name,
        assembly_name,
        types,
        user_strings,
        table_rows,
        resolver,
    })
}

/// Walks TypeDef (name/namespace + its method range) and MethodDef (name, signature, RVA).
fn collect_types(
    data: &[u8],
    t: &MdTables,
    string_at: &impl Fn(u32) -> String,
    blob_off: Option<usize>,
) -> Vec<TypeInfo> {
    let n_types = t.rows[0x02];
    let n_methods = t.rows[0x06];
    // Resolve a type reference (TypeDef/TypeRef/TypeSpec) to a readable name, for signatures.
    let resolve_type = |table: u8, row: u32| type_full_name(t, data, string_at, table, row);

    // Row counts are validated against the stream size in `MdTables::parse`, but keep the
    // up-front reservation modest anyway.
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity((n_types as usize).min(4096));
    // Method lists are monotonic (ECMA-335 II.22.37); clamping each type's start to the previous
    // type's end keeps hostile, overlapping lists linear instead of quadratic.
    let mut prev_end = 1u32;
    for r in 1..=n_types {
        let name = t
            .cell(data, 0x02, r, 1)
            .map(|i| string_at(i as u32))
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let ns = t
            .cell(data, 0x02, r, 2)
            .map(|i| string_at(i as u32))
            .unwrap_or_default();
        // MethodList (column 5) is the first method row; the type owns up to the next type's start.
        let end_of_table = n_methods.saturating_add(1);
        let first = (t.cell(data, 0x02, r, 5).unwrap_or(0) as u32)
            .max(prev_end)
            .min(end_of_table);
        let last = if r < n_types {
            t.cell(data, 0x02, r + 1, 5).unwrap_or(0) as u32
        } else {
            end_of_table
        }
        .clamp(first, end_of_table);
        prev_end = last;
        let mut methods = Vec::new();
        for m in first..last {
            if let Some(ni) = t.cell(data, 0x06, m, 3) {
                let rva = t.cell(data, 0x06, m, 0).unwrap_or(0) as u32;
                let signature = blob_off
                    .and_then(|bo| {
                        t.cell(data, 0x06, m, 4)
                            .and_then(|bi| blob_at(data, bo, bi as u32))
                    })
                    .and_then(|b| sig::decode_method(b, &resolve_type))
                    .map(|s| format!("({}) : {}", s.params.join(", "), s.ret))
                    .unwrap_or_default();
                methods.push(Method {
                    name: string_at(ni as u32),
                    signature,
                    rva,
                });
            }
        }
        out.push(TypeInfo {
            namespace: ns,
            name,
            methods,
        });
    }
    out
}

/// `Namespace.Name` of a TypeDef (0x02)/TypeRef (0x01) row (TypeSpec is shown as a placeholder).
fn type_full_name(
    t: &MdTables,
    d: &[u8],
    string_at: &impl Fn(u32) -> String,
    table: u8,
    row: u32,
) -> String {
    if table == 0x1b {
        return format!("TypeSpec#{row}");
    }
    let name = t
        .cell(d, table, row, 1)
        .map(|i| string_at(i as u32))
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let ns = t
        .cell(d, table, row, 2)
        .map(|i| string_at(i as u32))
        .unwrap_or_default();
    if ns.is_empty() {
        name
    } else {
        format!("{ns}.{name}")
    }
}

/// Reads a blob-heap entry (`compressed length` + bytes) at `blob_off + idx`.
fn blob_at(d: &[u8], blob_off: usize, idx: u32) -> Option<&[u8]> {
    let at = blob_off + idx as usize;
    let (len, hdr) = compressed_uint(d, at, d.len().saturating_sub(at))?;
    let start = at + hdr;
    d.get(start..start + len as usize)
}

/// The `#~` table stream: row counts and the geometry needed to address any cell.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
struct MdTables {
    rows: [u32; 64],
    /// Heap index sizes in bytes (Strings, GUID, Blob).
    str_sz: usize,
    guid_sz: usize,
    blob_sz: usize,
    /// Byte size of each table's row.
    row_size: [usize; 64],
    /// Absolute file offset of each present table's first row.
    base: [usize; 64],
}

impl MdTables {
    /// Parses the `#~` stream header at `off` (`size` bytes long) and checks that every table
    /// lies inside the stream, so hostile row counts can't drive huge allocations or loops.
    fn parse(d: &[u8], off: usize, size: usize) -> Result<Self, String> {
        let heapsizes = *d.get(off + 6).ok_or("truncated table header")?;
        let valid = u64::from_le_bytes(
            d.get(off + 8..off + 16)
                .ok_or("truncated")?
                .try_into()
                .unwrap(),
        );
        let str_sz = if heapsizes & 1 != 0 { 4 } else { 2 };
        let guid_sz = if heapsizes & 2 != 0 { 4 } else { 2 };
        let blob_sz = if heapsizes & 4 != 0 { 4 } else { 2 };

        let mut rows = [0u32; 64];
        let mut rc = off + 24;
        for (id, slot) in rows.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            if valid >> id & 1 == 1 {
                *slot = u32a(d, rc).ok_or("truncated row counts")?;
                rc += 4;
            }
        }
        // HeapSizes bit 0x40: four bytes of extra data follow the row counts.
        if heapsizes & 0x40 != 0 {
            rc += 4;
        }

        let mut t = MdTables {
            rows,
            str_sz,
            guid_sz,
            blob_sz,
            row_size: [0; 64],
            base: [0; 64],
        };

        // First pass: row sizes (needs row counts, already known).
        for id in 0u8..64 {
            if t.rows[id as usize] > 0 {
                t.row_size[id as usize] = columns(id).iter().map(|c| t.col_size(*c)).sum();
            }
        }
        // Second pass: table base offsets, in ascending id order.
        let end = off.saturating_add(size).min(d.len());
        let mut cur = rc;
        for id in 0u8..64 {
            if t.rows[id as usize] > 0 {
                t.base[id as usize] = cur;
                cur = (t.row_size[id as usize] as u64)
                    .checked_mul(u64::from(t.rows[id as usize]))
                    .and_then(|len| (cur as u64).checked_add(len))
                    .filter(|&e| e <= end as u64)
                    .ok_or_else(|| {
                        format!(
                            "table {} ({} rows) extends past the #~ stream",
                            table_name(id),
                            t.rows[id as usize]
                        )
                    })? as usize;
            }
        }
        Ok(t)
    }

    /// Size in bytes of a column, from heap and table sizes.
    fn col_size(&self, c: Col) -> usize {
        match c {
            Col::U16 => 2,
            Col::U32 => 4,
            Col::Str => self.str_sz,
            Col::Guid => self.guid_sz,
            Col::Blob => self.blob_sz,
            Col::Idx(table) => {
                if self.rows[table as usize] >= 0x1_0000 {
                    4
                } else {
                    2
                }
            }
            Col::CodedIdx(code) => self.coded_size(code),
        }
    }

    fn coded_size(&self, code: Coded) -> usize {
        let (tag_bits, tables) = code.info();
        let max = tables
            .iter()
            .filter(|&&t| t != 0xff)
            .map(|&t| self.rows[t as usize])
            .max()
            .unwrap_or(0);
        if (max as u64) < (1u64 << (16 - tag_bits)) {
            2
        } else {
            4
        }
    }

    /// Reads column `col` (0-based) of row `row` (1-based) in table `id` as an integer. `None` if
    /// out of range.
    fn cell(&self, d: &[u8], id: u8, row: u32, col: usize) -> Option<u64> {
        if row == 0 || row > self.rows[id as usize] {
            return None;
        }
        let cols = columns(id);
        let mut coloff = 0usize;
        for c in &cols[..col.min(cols.len())] {
            coloff += self.col_size(*c);
        }
        let size = self.col_size(*cols.get(col)?);
        let at = self.base[id as usize] + (row as usize - 1) * self.row_size[id as usize] + coloff;
        match size {
            2 => u16a(d, at).map(|v| v as u64),
            4 => u32a(d, at).map(|v| v as u64),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// Reads a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string at `start`, bounded by `end`.
fn read_cstr(d: &[u8], start: usize, end: usize) -> String {
    let mut p = start;
    while p < end && d.get(p).is_some_and(|&b| b != 0) {
        p += 1;
    }
    String::from_utf8_lossy(d.get(start..p).unwrap_or(&[])).into_owned()
}

/// Enumerates the `#US` heap: blob-style, each entry a compressed length then UTF-16LE + a flag.
fn read_user_strings(d: &[u8], off: usize, size: usize) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut i = 1; // the heap starts with a single 0 byte
    while i < size {
        let (len, hdr) = match compressed_uint(d, off + i, size - i) {
            Some(v) => v,
            None => break,
        };
        i += hdr;
        if len == 0 {
            continue;
        }
        let bytes = match d.get(off + i..off + i + len as usize) {
            Some(b) => b,
            None => break,
        };
        i += len as usize;
        // The last byte is a flag; the rest is UTF-16LE.
        let body = &bytes[..bytes.len().saturating_sub(1)];
        let mut units = Vec::with_capacity(body.len() / 2);
        let mut k = 0;
        while k + 1 < body.len() {
            units.push(u16::from_le_bytes([body[k], body[k + 1]]));
            k += 2;
        }
        let s = String::from_utf16_lossy(&units);
        if !s.is_empty() {
            out.push(s);
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Reads an ECMA-335 compressed unsigned integer. Returns `(value, bytes_read)`.
fn compressed_uint(d: &[u8], off: usize, avail: usize) -> Option<(u32, usize)> {
    let b0 = *d.get(off)? as u32;
    if avail == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    if b0 & 0x80 == 0 {
        Some((b0, 1))
    } else if b0 & 0xC0 == 0x80 {
        let b1 = *d.get(off + 1)? as u32;
        Some((((b0 & 0x3f) << 8) | b1, 2))
    } else {
        let b1 = *d.get(off + 1)? as u32;
        let b2 = *d.get(off + 2)? as u32;
        let b3 = *d.get(off + 3)? as u32;
        Some((((b0 & 0x1f) << 24) | (b1 << 16) | (b2 << 8) | b3, 4))
    }
}

/// Holds what IL disassembly needs: the tables, heap locations and section map.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
struct Resolver {
    tables: MdTables,
    strings_off: usize,
    strings_size: usize,
    us_off: Option<usize>,
    sections: Vec<Section>,
}

impl Resolver {
    fn string(&self, d: &[u8], idx: u32) -> String {
        read_cstr(
            d,
            self.strings_off + idx as usize,
            self.strings_off + self.strings_size,
        )
    }

    /// `Namespace.Name` for a TypeDef (0x02) or TypeRef (0x01) row.
    fn type_name(&self, d: &[u8], table: u8, row: u32) -> String {
        let (name_col, ns_col) = (1, 2);
        let name = self
            .tables
            .cell(d, table, row, name_col)
            .map(|i| self.string(d, i as u32))
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let ns = self
            .tables
            .cell(d, table, row, ns_col)
            .map(|i| self.string(d, i as u32))
            .unwrap_or_default();
        if ns.is_empty() {
            name
        } else {
            format!("{ns}.{name}")
        }
    }

    /// Decodes a coded index value into `(table_id, row)`.
    fn decode_coded(code: Coded, value: u64) -> Option<(u8, u32)> {
        let (bits, group) = code.info();
        let tag = (value & ((1 << bits) - 1)) as usize;
        let table = *group.get(tag)?;
        if table == 0xff {
            return None;
        }
        Some((table, (value >> bits) as u32))
    }
}

impl DotNet {
    /// Resolves a metadata token (`table << 24 | row`) to a readable name.
    fn resolve_token(&self, d: &[u8], tok: u32) -> String {
        let r = &self.resolver;
        let table = (tok >> 24) as u8;
        let row = tok & 0x00ff_ffff;
        match table {
            0x06 => r
                .tables
                .cell(d, 0x06, row, 3)
                .map(|i| r.string(d, i as u32))
                .unwrap_or_default(),
            0x04 => r
                .tables
                .cell(d, 0x04, row, 1)
                .map(|i| r.string(d, i as u32))
                .unwrap_or_default(),
            0x01 => r.type_name(d, 0x01, row),
            0x02 => r.type_name(d, 0x02, row),
            0x0a => {
                // MemberRef: Parent.Name
                let name = r
                    .tables
                    .cell(d, 0x0a, row, 1)
                    .map(|i| r.string(d, i as u32))
                    .unwrap_or_default();
                let parent = r
                    .tables
                    .cell(d, 0x0a, row, 0)
                    .and_then(|v| Resolver::decode_coded(Coded::MemberRefParent, v))
                    .map(|(t, rr)| match t {
                        0x01 | 0x02 => r.type_name(d, t, rr),
                        _ => String::new(),
                    })
                    .unwrap_or_default();
                if parent.is_empty() {
                    name
                } else {
                    format!("{parent}.{name}")
                }
            }
            0x1b => format!("TypeSpec#{row}"),
            0x11 => format!("StandAloneSig#{row}"),
            _ => format!("token 0x{tok:08x}"),
        }
    }

    /// Resolves a user-string token (`0x70 << 24 | heap_offset`) to the quoted literal.
    fn resolve_string(&self, d: &[u8], tok: u32) -> String {
        if (tok >> 24) != 0x70 {
            return format!("token 0x{tok:08x}");
        }
        let Some(base) = self.resolver.us_off else {
            return String::new();
        };
        let off = base + (tok & 0x00ff_ffff) as usize;
        let Some((len, hdr)) = compressed_uint(d, off, d.len().saturating_sub(off)) else {
            return String::new();
        };
        if len == 0 {
            return "\"\"".into();
        }
        let start = off + hdr;
        let bytes = d.get(start..start + len as usize).unwrap_or(&[]);
        let body = &bytes[..bytes.len().saturating_sub(1)];
        let mut units = Vec::with_capacity(body.len() / 2);
        let mut k = 0;
        while k + 1 < body.len() {
            units.push(u16::from_le_bytes([body[k], body[k + 1]]));
            k += 2;
        }
        format!("{:?}", String::from_utf16_lossy(&units))
    }

    /// Disassembles the IL of the method body at `rva`. `data` must be the same bytes `parse`
    /// received. Returns an error if the method has no body or the body is malformed.
    pub fn disassemble(&self, data: &[u8], rva: u32) -> Result<Vec<Il>, String> {
        if rva == 0 {
            return Err("method has no body (abstract, native or P/Invoke)".into());
        }
        let off =
            rva_to_off(&self.resolver.sections, rva).ok_or("method RVA not in any section")?;
        let b0 = *data.get(off).ok_or("truncated method header")?;
        let (code_off, code_size) = match b0 & 0x03 {
            0x02 => (off + 1, (b0 >> 2) as usize), // tiny header
            0x03 => {
                let code_size = u32a(data, off + 4).ok_or("truncated fat header")? as usize;
                (off + 12, code_size) // fat header is 12 bytes
            }
            _ => return Err("unknown method-header format".into()),
        };
        let code = data
            .get(code_off..code_off + code_size)
            .ok_or("method code out of bounds")?;
        Ok(il::disassemble(
            code,
            |t| self.resolve_token(data, t),
            |t| self.resolve_string(data, t),
        ))
    }
}
```

```rs
//! Decodes ECMA-335 method signature blobs (`#Blob` heap) into readable return/parameter types.
//! A signature is a calling-convention byte, an optional generic-parameter count, a parameter
//! count, then the return type and each parameter type — each a recursive `ELEMENT_TYPE_*` form.

/// A decoded method signature.
pub struct MethodSig {
    pub ret: String,
    pub params: Vec<String>,
}

struct Cursor<'a> {
    b: &'a [u8],
    i: usize,
}

impl Cursor<'_> {
    fn u8(&mut self) -> Option<u8> {
        let v = *self.b.get(self.i)?;
        self.i += 1;
        Some(v)
    }

    /// ECMA-335 compressed unsigned integer.
    fn cuint(&mut self) -> Option<u32> {
        let b0 = self.u8()? as u32;
        if b0 & 0x80 == 0 {
            Some(b0)
        } else if b0 & 0xC0 == 0x80 {
            let b1 = self.u8()? as u32;
            Some(((b0 & 0x3f) << 8) | b1)
        } else {
            let b1 = self.u8()? as u32;
            let b2 = self.u8()? as u32;
            let b3 = self.u8()? as u32;
            Some(((b0 & 0x1f) << 24) | (b1 << 16) | (b2 << 8) | b3)
        }
    }

    /// A `TypeDefOrRef` coded token (2 tag bits select the table).
    fn ctoken(&mut self) -> Option<(u8, u32)> {
        let v = self.cuint()?;
        let table = match v & 3 {
            0 => 0x02, // TypeDef
            1 => 0x01, // TypeRef
            2 => 0x1b, // TypeSpec
            _ => return None,
        };
        Some((table, v >> 2))
    }
}

/// Decodes a method signature blob. `resolve` turns a `(table, row)` type reference into a name.
pub fn decode_method(bytes: &[u8], resolve: &impl Fn(u8, u32) -> String) -> Option<MethodSig> {
    let mut c = Cursor { b: bytes, i: 0 };
    let cc = c.u8()?;
    if cc & 0x10 != 0 {
        c.cuint()?; // generic parameter count
    }
    let nparams = c.cuint()? as usize;
    let ret = read_type(&mut c, resolve, 0)?;
    let mut params = Vec::new();
    for _ in 0..nparams.min(1024) {
        match read_type(&mut c, resolve, 0) {
            Some(t) => params.push(t),
            None => break,
        }
    }
    Some(MethodSig { ret, params })
}

fn read_type(c: &mut Cursor, resolve: &impl Fn(u8, u32) -> String, depth: u32) -> Option<String> {
    if depth > 32 {
        return Some("…".into());
    }
    let et = c.u8()?;
    Some(match et {
        0x01 => "void".into(),
        0x02 => "bool".into(),
        0x03 => "char".into(),
        0x04 => "sbyte".into(),
        0x05 => "byte".into(),
        0x06 => "short".into(),
        0x07 => "ushort".into(),
        0x08 => "int".into(),
        0x09 => "uint".into(),
        0x0a => "long".into(),
        0x0b => "ulong".into(),
        0x0c => "float".into(),
        0x0d => "double".into(),
        0x0e => "string".into(),
        0x16 => "TypedReference".into(),
        0x18 => "IntPtr".into(),
        0x19 => "UIntPtr".into(),
        0x1c => "object".into(),
        0x0f => format!("{}*", read_type(c, resolve, depth + 1)?), // PTR
        0x10 => format!("ref {}", read_type(c, resolve, depth + 1)?), // BYREF
        0x1d => format!("{}[]", read_type(c, resolve, depth + 1)?), // SZARRAY
        0x11 | 0x12 => {
            // VALUETYPE / CLASS
            let (table, row) = c.ctoken()?;
            resolve(table, row)
        }
        0x13 => format!("!{}", c.cuint()?), // VAR (class generic param)
        0x1e => format!("!!{}", c.cuint()?), // MVAR (method generic param)
        0x15 => {
            // GENERICINST <type> <argc> <args…>
            let base = read_type(c, resolve, depth + 1)?;
            let argc = c.cuint()? as usize;
            let args: Vec<String> = (0..argc.min(64))
                .map(|_| read_type(c, resolve, depth + 1).unwrap_or_else(|| "?".into()))
                .collect();
            format!("{base}<{}>", args.join(", "))
        }
        0x14 => {
            // ARRAY <type> <rank> <numsizes> sizes… <numlobounds> lobounds…
            let t = read_type(c, resolve, depth + 1)?;
            let rank = c.cuint()?;
            let nsizes = c.cuint()? as usize;
            for _ in 0..nsizes.min(64) {
                c.cuint();
            }
            let nlo = c.cuint()? as usize;
            for _ in 0..nlo.min(64) {
                c.cuint();
            }
            format!("{t}[{}]", ",".repeat(rank.saturating_sub(1) as usize))
        }
        // Custom modifiers / pinned / sentinel: skip and continue to the real type.
        0x1f | 0x20 => {
            c.ctoken()?;
            read_type(c, resolve, depth + 1)?
        }
        0x41 | 0x45 => read_type(c, resolve, depth + 1)?,
        0x1b => "fnptr".into(), // FNPTR (signature not expanded)
        other => format!("type#{other:#x}"),
    })
}
```

`crates/orress-dotnet/src/tables.rs`:

```rs
//! ECMA-335 metadata table schema: the column layout of every `#~` table, used to compute row
//! sizes and locate a column within a row. This is data, transcribed from the spec.

/// A coded index: a table reference tagged with a few low bits selecting which table.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub enum Coded {
    TypeDefOrRef,
    HasConstant,
    HasCustomAttribute,
    HasFieldMarshal,
    HasDeclSecurity,
    MemberRefParent,
    HasSemantics,
    MethodDefOrRef,
    MemberForwarded,
    Implementation,
    CustomAttributeType,
    ResolutionScope,
    TypeOrMethodDef,
}

impl Coded {
    /// `(tag_bits, member_tables)`. A `0xff` entry is an unused tag slot.
    pub fn info(self) -> (u32, &'static [u8]) {
        match self {
            Coded::TypeDefOrRef => (2, &[0x02, 0x01, 0x1b]),
            Coded::HasConstant => (2, &[0x04, 0x08, 0x17]),
            Coded::HasCustomAttribute => (
                5,
                &[
                    0x06, 0x04, 0x01, 0x02, 0x08, 0x09, 0x0a, 0x00, 0x0e, 0x17, 0x14, 0x11, 0x1a,
                    0x1b, 0x20, 0x23, 0x26, 0x27, 0x28, 0x2a, 0x2b, 0x2c,
                ],
            ),
            Coded::HasFieldMarshal => (1, &[0x04, 0x08]),
            Coded::HasDeclSecurity => (2, &[0x02, 0x06, 0x20]),
            Coded::MemberRefParent => (3, &[0x02, 0x01, 0x1a, 0x06, 0x1b]),
            Coded::HasSemantics => (1, &[0x14, 0x17]),
            Coded::MethodDefOrRef => (1, &[0x06, 0x0a]),
            Coded::MemberForwarded => (1, &[0x04, 0x06]),
            Coded::Implementation => (2, &[0x26, 0x23, 0x27]),
            Coded::CustomAttributeType => (3, &[0xff, 0xff, 0x06, 0x0a, 0xff]),
            Coded::ResolutionScope => (2, &[0x00, 0x1a, 0x23, 0x01]),
            Coded::TypeOrMethodDef => (1, &[0x02, 0x06]),
        }
    }
}

/// A column's type.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub enum Col {
    U16,
    U32,
    /// `#Strings` heap index.
    Str,
    /// `#GUID` heap index.
    Guid,
    /// `#Blob` heap index.
    Blob,
    /// Simple index into a single table.
    Idx(u8),
    /// A coded index (table reference tagged in its low bits).
    CodedIdx(Coded),
}

/// The columns of table `id`, in order. An empty slice means an unknown/absent table.
pub fn columns(id: u8) -> &'static [Col] {
    use Coded::*;
    use Col::CodedIdx as C;
    use Col::{Blob, Guid, Idx, Str, U16, U32};
    match id {
        0x00 => &[U16, Str, Guid, Guid, Guid],   // Module
        0x01 => &[C(ResolutionScope), Str, Str], // TypeRef
        0x02 => &[U32, Str, Str, C(TypeDefOrRef), Idx(0x04), Idx(0x06)], // TypeDef
        0x03 => &[Idx(0x04)],                    // FieldPtr
        0x04 => &[U16, Str, Blob],               // Field
        0x05 => &[Idx(0x06)],                    // MethodPtr
        0x06 => &[U32, U16, U16, Str, Blob, Idx(0x08)], // MethodDef
        0x07 => &[Idx(0x08)],                    // ParamPtr
        0x08 => &[U16, U16, Str],                // Param
        0x09 => &[Idx(0x02), C(TypeDefOrRef)],   // InterfaceImpl
        0x0a => &[C(MemberRefParent), Str, Blob], // MemberRef
        0x0b => &[U16, C(HasConstant), Blob],    // Constant
        0x0c => &[C(HasCustomAttribute), C(CustomAttributeType), Blob], // CustomAttribute
        0x0d => &[C(HasFieldMarshal), Blob],     // FieldMarshal
        0x0e => &[U16, C(HasDeclSecurity), Blob], // DeclSecurity
        0x0f => &[U16, U32, Idx(0x02)],          // ClassLayout
        0x10 => &[U32, Idx(0x04)],               // FieldLayout
        0x11 => &[Blob],                         // StandAloneSig
        0x12 => &[Idx(0x02), Idx(0x14)],         // EventMap
        0x13 => &[Idx(0x14)],                    // EventPtr
        0x14 => &[U16, Str, C(TypeDefOrRef)],    // Event
        0x15 => &[Idx(0x02), Idx(0x17)],         // PropertyMap
        0x16 => &[Idx(0x17)],                    // PropertyPtr
        0x17 => &[U16, Str, Blob],               // Property
        0x18 => &[U16, Idx(0x06), C(HasSemantics)], // MethodSemantics
        0x19 => &[Idx(0x02), C(MethodDefOrRef), C(MethodDefOrRef)], // MethodImpl
        0x1a => &[Str],                          // ModuleRef
        0x1b => &[Blob],                         // TypeSpec
        0x1c => &[U16, C(MemberForwarded), Str, Idx(0x1a)], // ImplMap
        0x1d => &[U32, Idx(0x04)],               // FieldRVA
        0x1e => &[U32, U32],                     // EncLog
        0x1f => &[U32],                          // EncMap
        0x20 => &[U32, U16, U16, U16, U16, U32, Blob, Str, Str], // Assembly
        0x21 => &[U32],                          // AssemblyProcessor
        0x22 => &[U32, U32, U32],                // AssemblyOS
        0x23 => &[U16, U16, U16, U16, U32, Blob, Str, Str, Blob], // AssemblyRef
        0x24 => &[U32, Idx(0x23)],               // AssemblyRefProcessor
        0x25 => &[U32, U32, U32, Idx(0x23)],     // AssemblyRefOS
        0x26 => &[U32, Str, Blob],               // File
        0x27 => &[U32, U32, Str, Str, C(Implementation)], // ExportedType
        0x28 => &[U32, U32, Str, C(Implementation)], // ManifestResource
        0x29 => &[Idx(0x02), Idx(0x02)],         // NestedClass
        0x2a => &[U16, U16, C(TypeOrMethodDef), Str], // GenericParam
        0x2b => &[C(MethodDefOrRef), Blob],      // MethodSpec
        0x2c => &[Idx(0x2a), C(TypeDefOrRef)],   // GenericParamConstraint
        _ => &[],
    }
}

/// The readable name of a table id (for the overview).
pub fn table_name(id: u8) -> &'static str {
    match id {
        0x00 => "Module",
        0x01 => "TypeRef",
        0x02 => "TypeDef",
        0x04 => "Field",
        0x06 => "MethodDef",
        0x08 => "Param",
        0x0a => "MemberRef",
        0x0b => "Constant",
        0x0c => "CustomAttribute",
        0x11 => "StandAloneSig",
        0x14 => "Event",
        0x17 => "Property",
        0x1a => "ModuleRef",
        0x1b => "TypeSpec",
        0x20 => "Assembly",
        0x23 => "AssemblyRef",
        0x26 => "File",
        0x27 => "ExportedType",
        0x28 => "ManifestResource",
        0x2a => "GenericParam",
        0x2b => "MethodSpec",
        _ => "Table",
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-dotnet/src/tests.rs`:

```rs
use super::*;

/// A controlled assembly compiled by the .NET Framework C# compiler (`Add-Type -OutputAssembly`).
const DLL: &[u8] = include_bytes!("../tests/fixtures/Check.dll");

fn parsed() -> DotNet {
    parse(DLL).expect("parse Check.dll")
}

#[test]
fn detects_dotnet() {
    assert!(is_dotnet(DLL));
    assert!(!is_dotnet(b"MZ\x90\x00 not really a PE"));
    assert!(!is_dotnet(&[0u8; 4]));
}

#[test]
fn reads_names_and_runtime() {
    let a = parsed();
    assert_eq!(a.runtime_version, "v4.0.30319");
    assert_eq!(a.module_name, "Check.dll");
    assert_eq!(a.assembly_name.as_deref(), Some("Check"));
}

#[test]
fn recovers_types_and_methods() {
    let a = parsed();
    // The special <Module> type plus our Check class.
    assert!(a.types.iter().any(|t| t.name == "<Module>"));
    let check = a
        .types
        .iter()
        .find(|t| t.name == "Check")
        .expect("Check type");
    assert_eq!(check.full_name(), "Check");
    for m in ["Verify", "Main", ".ctor"] {
        assert!(
            check.methods.iter().any(|x| x.name == m),
            "missing method {m} in {:?}",
            check.methods
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn decodes_method_signatures() {
    let a = parsed();
    let check = a.types.iter().find(|t| t.name == "Check").unwrap();
    let sig = |name: &str| {
        check
            .methods
            .iter()
            .find(|m| m.name == name)
            .unwrap()
            .signature
            .as_str()
    };
    assert_eq!(sig("Verify"), "(string) : bool");
    assert_eq!(sig("Main"), "() : void");
    assert_eq!(sig(".ctor"), "() : void");
}

#[test]
fn disassembles_il() {
    let a = parsed();
    let check = a.types.iter().find(|t| t.name == "Check").unwrap();

    // Main() { Console.WriteLine("enter password:"); } — a clean, predictable body.
    let main = check.methods.iter().find(|m| m.name == "Main").unwrap();
    let il = a.disassemble(DLL, main.rva).unwrap();
    let ops: Vec<&str> = il.iter().map(|i| i.opcode).collect();
    assert!(ops.contains(&"ldstr"), "{ops:?}");
    assert!(ops.contains(&"call"), "{ops:?}");
    assert!(ops.last() == Some(&"ret"), "{ops:?}");

    // ldstr resolves the literal; call resolves the method name.
    let ldstr = il.iter().find(|i| i.opcode == "ldstr").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(ldstr.operand, "\"enter password:\"");
    let call = il.iter().find(|i| i.opcode == "call").unwrap();
    assert!(
        call.operand.contains("WriteLine"),
        "call operand was {:?}",
        call.operand
    );

    // Verify() has a real loop, so it must contain at least one branch with a target.
    let verify = check.methods.iter().find(|m| m.name == "Verify").unwrap();
    let vil = a.disassemble(DLL, verify.rva).unwrap();
    assert!(vil.iter().any(|i| i.branch_target.is_some()));
    assert!(vil.iter().any(|i| i.is_branch_target));
}

#[test]
fn recovers_user_strings() {
    let a = parsed();
    // The one string literal in the IL — where real malware hides its C2/commands.
    assert_eq!(a.user_strings, ["enter password:"]);
}

#[test]
fn reports_table_rows() {
    let a = parsed();
    let find = |n: &str| {
        a.table_rows
            .iter()
            .find(|(name, _)| *name == n)
            .map(|(_, c)| *c)
    };
    assert_eq!(find("TypeDef"), Some(2));
    assert_eq!(find("MethodDef"), Some(3));
    assert_eq!(find("Assembly"), Some(1));
    assert_eq!(find("AssemblyRef"), Some(1)); // references mscorlib
}

#[test]
fn rejects_non_dotnet() {
    assert!(parse(b"not a PE at all").is_err());
}

/// A synthetic `#~` stream: header, row counts for the tables in `valid`, then `body`.
fn tilde(heapsizes: u8, valid: u64, rows: &[u32], extra: &[u8], body: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut d = vec![0u8; 6];
    d.push(heapsizes);
    d.push(1);
    d.extend(valid.to_le_bytes());
    d.extend(0u64.to_le_bytes()); // sorted
    for r in rows {
        d.extend(r.to_le_bytes());
    }
    d.extend(extra);
    d.extend(body);
    d
}

#[test]
fn heapsizes_extra_data_is_skipped() {
    // Module row: Generation u16, Name str(2), Mvid/EncId/EncBaseId guid(2 each) = 10 bytes.
    let row = [0, 0, 0x2a, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0];
    let d = tilde(0x40, 1, &[1], &[0xEE; 4], &row);
    let t = MdTables::parse(&d, 0, d.len()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(t.base[0], 24 + 4 + 4);
    assert_eq!(t.cell(&d, 0x00, 1, 1), Some(0x2a));
}

#[test]
fn hostile_row_counts_are_rejected() {
    // Four billion TypeDef rows in a 40-byte stream: must be an error, not a 4 GB allocation.
    let d = tilde(0, 1 << 2, &[0xFFFF_FFFF], &[], &[0; 16]);
    assert!(MdTables::parse(&d, 0, d.len()).is_err());

    // Same thing through the full parser: patch the fixture's TypeDef row count.
    let mut dll = DLL.to_vec();
    let (md, _) = metadata_offset(&dll).unwrap();
    let ver_len = u32a(&dll, md + 12).unwrap() as usize;
    let mut p = md + 16 + ((ver_len + 3) & !3);
    let nstreams = u16a(&dll, p + 2).unwrap();
    p += 4;
    let mut tilde_off = None;
    for _ in 0..nstreams {
        let off = u32a(&dll, p).unwrap() as usize;
        p += 8;
        let start = p;
        while dll[p] != 0 {
            p += 1;
        }
        if &dll[start..p] == b"#~" {
            tilde_off = Some(md + off);
        }
        p = (p + 1 + 3) & !3;
    }
    let off = tilde_off.unwrap();
    let valid = u64::from_le_bytes(dll[off + 8..off + 16].try_into().unwrap());
    let idx = (valid & 0b11).count_ones() as usize; // row-count slot of table 0x02
    dll[off + 24 + idx * 4..off + 28 + idx * 4].copy_from_slice(&0xFFFF_FFF0u32.to_le_bytes());
    assert!(parse(&dll).is_err());
}

#[test]
fn rva_mapping_does_not_overflow() {
    let sections = [(0xFFFF_F000, 0x2000, 0xFFFF_FFF0)];
    assert_eq!(
        rva_to_off(&sections, 0xFFFF_FFF0).map(|o| o as u64),
        Some(0xFFFF_FFF0u64 + 0xFF0)
    );
    assert_eq!(rva_to_off(&sections, 0x10), None);
}
```

`crates/orress-editor/src/highlight.rs`:

```rs
//! A small, dependency-free syntax highlighter: a generic lexer driven by a per-language
//! spec. It colours comments, strings, numbers, keywords, types, functions and (for Rust)
//! macros, attributes and lifetimes. Good enough to read and write solver scripts and
//! crackmes; a tree-sitter backend is the planned richer upgrade (same `Token` output).

use crate::Language;

/// What a highlighted span represents. Punctuation and plain identifiers are left out
/// (rendered in the default text colour), so the output is sparse.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Tok {
    Keyword,
    Type,
    Function,
    Macro,
    Attribute,
    String,
    Char,
    Number,
    Comment,
    Lifetime,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Token {
    pub start: usize,
    pub end: usize,
    pub kind: Tok,
}

struct Spec {
    line_comments: &'static [&'static str],
    block_comment: Option<(&'static str, &'static str)>,
    /// String delimiters as (open, close). Longer delimiters must come first.
    strings: &'static [(&'static str, &'static str)],
    char_lit: bool,
    keywords: &'static [&'static str],
    types: &'static [&'static str],
    /// Rust-style extras: `name!` macros, `#[attr]`, `'lifetime`, CamelCase as a type.
    rust_like: bool,
    /// A leading decorator character (`@` in Python).
    decorator: Option<char>,
}

fn spec(lang: Language) -> Option<Spec> {
    Some(match lang {
        Language::Rust => Spec {
            line_comments: &["//"],
            block_comment: Some(("/*", "*/")),
            strings: &[("\"", "\"")],
            char_lit: true,
            keywords: RUST_KEYWORDS,
            types: RUST_TYPES,
            rust_like: true,
            decorator: None,
        },
        Language::Python => Spec {
            line_comments: &["#"],
            block_comment: None,
            strings: &[
                ("\"\"\"", "\"\"\""),
                ("'''", "'''"),
                ("\"", "\""),
                ("'", "'"),
            ],
            char_lit: false,
            keywords: PYTHON_KEYWORDS,
            types: PYTHON_TYPES,
            rust_like: false,
            decorator: Some('@'),
        },
        // C and C++ are highlighted by tree-sitter; this spec is only the fallback if that fails.
        Language::C => Spec {
            line_comments: &["//"],
            block_comment: Some(("/*", "*/")),
            strings: &[("\"", "\"")],
            char_lit: true,
            keywords: C_KEYWORDS,
            types: C_TYPES,
            rust_like: false,
            decorator: Some('#'),
        },
        Language::Cpp => Spec {
            line_comments: &["//"],
            block_comment: Some(("/*", "*/")),
            strings: &[("\"", "\"")],
            char_lit: true,
            keywords: CPP_KEYWORDS,
            types: C_TYPES,
            rust_like: false,
            decorator: Some('#'),
        },
        Language::Asm => Spec {
            line_comments: &[";", "#"],
            block_comment: None,
            strings: &[("\"", "\""), ("'", "'")],
            char_lit: false,
            keywords: ASM_MNEMONICS,
            types: ASM_REGISTERS,
            rust_like: false,
            decorator: None,
        },
        Language::Toml => Spec {
            line_comments: &["#"],
            block_comment: None,
            strings: &[
                ("\"\"\"", "\"\"\""),
                ("'''", "'''"),
                ("\"", "\""),
                ("'", "'"),
            ],
            char_lit: false,
            keywords: &["true", "false"],
            types: &[],
            rust_like: false,
            decorator: None,
        },
        Language::Json => Spec {
            line_comments: &[],
            block_comment: None,
            strings: &[("\"", "\"")],
            char_lit: false,
            keywords: &["true", "false", "null"],
            types: &[],
            rust_like: false,
            decorator: None,
        },
        Language::Markdown | Language::PlainText => return None,
    })
}
```
