```rs
/// Highlights `text` of the given language into sparse, non-overlapping tokens in order.
pub(crate) fn tokenizer(text: &str, lang: Language) -> Vec<Token> {
    let Some(spec) = spec(lang) else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    let bytes = text.as_bytes();
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut i = 0;
    let n = text.len();
    // Byte offsets of the start of the current line, to spot line-leading constructs.
    let mut at_line_start = true;

    while i < n {
        let rest = &text[i..];
        let c = bytes[i];

        if c == b'\n' {
            i += 1;
            at_line_start = true;
            continue;
        }
        if c == b' ' || c == b'\t' || c == b'\r' {
            i += 1;
            continue;
        }

        // Comments.
        if let Some((open, close)) = spec.block_comment
            && rest.starts_with(open)
        {
            let end = text[i + open.len()..]
                .find(close)
                .map_or(n, |p| i + open.len() + p + close.len());
            out.push(Token {
                start: i,
                end,
                kind: Tok::Comment,
            });
            i = end;
            at_line_start = false;
            continue;
        }
        if spec.line_comments.iter().any(|p| rest.starts_with(p)) {
            let end = rest.find('\n').map_or(n, |p| i + p);
            out.push(Token {
                start: i,
                end,
                kind: Tok::Comment,
            });
            i = end;
            continue;
        }

        // Rust attributes: `#[ ... ]` or `#![ ... ]` to the end of the line.
        if spec.rust_like && c == b'#' && (rest.starts_with("#[") || rest.starts_with("#![")) {
            let end = rest.find('\n').map_or(n, |p| i + p);
            out.push(Token {
                start: i,
                end,
                kind: Tok::Attribute,
            });
            i = end;
            continue;
        }

        // Python decorators at the start of a line: `@name`.
        if let Some(dec) = spec.decorator
            && at_line_start
            && c == dec as u8
        {
            let mut j = i + 1;
            while j < n
                && (bytes[j].is_ascii_alphanumeric() || bytes[j] == b'_' || bytes[j] == b'.')
            {
                j += 1;
            }
            out.push(Token {
                start: i,
                end: j,
                kind: Tok::Attribute,
            });
            i = j;
            at_line_start = false;
            continue;
        }

        // Strings (including Rust raw/byte string prefixes handled loosely).
        if let Some(tok) = string_at(text, i, &spec) {
            out.push(tok);
            i = tok.end;
            at_line_start = false;
            continue;
        }

        // Char literal vs. Rust lifetime.
        if spec.char_lit && c == b'\'' {
            if let Some(end) = char_literal_end(text, i) {
                out.push(Token {
                    start: i,
                    end,
                    kind: Tok::Char,
                });
                i = end;
            } else if spec.rust_like {
                // `'ident` lifetime.
                let mut j = i + 1;
                while j < n && (bytes[j].is_ascii_alphanumeric() || bytes[j] == b'_') {
                    j += 1;
                }
                out.push(Token {
                    start: i,
                    end: j,
                    kind: Tok::Lifetime,
                });
                i = j.max(i + 1);
            } else {
                i += 1;
            }
            at_line_start = false;
            continue;
        }

        // Numbers.
        if c.is_ascii_digit() || (c == b'.' && i + 1 < n && bytes[i + 1].is_ascii_digit()) {
            let end = number_end(text, i);
            out.push(Token {
                start: i,
                end,
                kind: Tok::Number,
            });
            i = end;
            at_line_start = false;
            continue;
        }

        // Identifiers / keywords / types / functions / macros.
        if c.is_ascii_alphabetic() || c == b'_' {
            let mut j = i + 1;
            while j < n && (bytes[j].is_ascii_alphanumeric() || bytes[j] == b'_') {
                j += 1;
            }
            let word = &text[i..j];
            // Look past spaces for a following `(` (function) or `!` (macro).
            let mut k = j;
            while k < n && (bytes[k] == b' ' || bytes[k] == b'\t') {
                k += 1;
            }
            let next = bytes.get(k).copied();

            let kind = if spec.keywords.contains(&word) {
                Some(Tok::Keyword)
            } else if spec.types.contains(&word) || (spec.rust_like && starts_upper(word)) {
                Some(Tok::Type)
            } else if spec.rust_like && bytes.get(j) == Some(&b'!') {
                // macro: include the `!`.
                out.push(Token {
                    start: i,
                    end: j + 1,
                    kind: Tok::Macro,
                });
                i = j + 1;
                at_line_start = false;
                continue;
            } else if next == Some(b'(') {
                Some(Tok::Function)
            } else {
                None
            };
            if let Some(kind) = kind {
                out.push(Token {
                    start: i,
                    end: j,
                    kind,
                });
            }
            i = j;
            at_line_start = false;
            continue;
        }

        // Anything else (punctuation/operators): default colour.
        i += next_char_len(rest);
        at_line_start = false;
    }
    out
}

fn next_char_len(rest: &str) -> usize {
    rest.chars().next().map_or(1, char::len_utf8)
}

fn starts_upper(word: &str) -> bool {
    word.chars().next().is_some_and(|c| c.is_ascii_uppercase())
}

/// Matches a string starting at `i`, honouring the spec's delimiters and backslash
/// escapes (for single-char delimiters).
fn string_at(text: &str, i: usize, spec: &Spec) -> Option<Token> {
    let rest = &text[i..];
    // Rust raw/byte-string prefixes: r"...", b"...", br"...", r#"..."#.
    let prefix = if spec.rust_like {
        ["br#\"", "b r", "br\"", "r#\"", "b\"", "r\""]
            .iter()
            .find(|p| rest.starts_with(**p) && p.ends_with('"'))
            .map_or(0, |p| p.len() - 1) // length up to the opening quote
    } else {
        0
    };
    let body = &text[i + prefix..];
    for (open, close) in spec.strings {
        if body.starts_with(open) {
            let start_search = i + prefix + open.len();
            let mut j = start_search;
            let bytes = text.as_bytes();
            while j < text.len() {
                if open.len() == 1 && bytes[j] == b'\\' {
                    // Skip the backslash and the whole escaped character (which may be
                    // multi-byte, e.g. `\é`), so `j` stays on a char boundary.
                    j += 1;
                    if j < text.len() {
                        j += next_char_len(&text[j..]);
                    }
                    continue;
                }
                if text[j..].starts_with(close) {
                    return Some(Token {
                        start: i,
                        end: j + close.len(),
                        kind: Tok::String,
                    });
                }
                j += next_char_len(&text[j..]);
            }
            // Unterminated string runs to EOF (or end of line for 1-char quotes).
            let end = if open.len() == 1 {
                text[start_search..]
                    .find('\n')
                    .map_or(text.len(), |p| start_search + p)
            } else {
                text.len()
            };
            return Some(Token {
                start: i,
                end,
                kind: Tok::String,
            });
        }
    }
    None
}

/// If `text[i..]` is a char literal `'x'` or `'\n'`, returns its end.
fn char_literal_end(text: &str, i: usize) -> Option<usize> {
    let bytes = text.as_bytes();
    let n = text.len();
    debug_assert_eq!(bytes[i], b'\'');
    let mut j = i + 1;
    if j >= n {
        return None;
    }
    if bytes[j] == b'\\' {
        j += 2; // escape: \n, \t, \', \\, \xNN (loose)
        while j < n && bytes[j] != b'\'' && bytes[j] != b'\n' {
            j += 1;
        }
    } else {
        j += next_char_len(&text[j..]);
    }
    (j < n && bytes[j] == b'\'').then_some(j + 1)
}

fn number_end(text: &str, i: usize) -> usize {
    let bytes = text.as_bytes();
    let n = text.len();
    let mut j = i;
    // 0x / 0b / 0o prefixes, then hex/alnum digits, underscores, a dot and an exponent.
    if bytes[j] == b'0'
        && j + 1 < n
        && matches!(bytes[j + 1], b'x' | b'X' | b'b' | b'B' | b'o' | b'O')
    {
        j += 2;
    }
    while j < n {
        let c = bytes[j];
        if c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == b'_' || c == b'.' {
            // Stop at a `..` range operator.
            if c == b'.' && j + 1 < n && bytes[j + 1] == b'.' {
                break;
            }
            j += 1;
        } else {
            break;
        }
    }
    j.max(i + 1)
}
```

`crates/orress-editor/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! The ORRESS code editor model: an in-memory text buffer, language detection, syntax
//! highlighting and build/run tasks. UI-agnostic, so it is testable on its own; the egui
//! editor view in `orress-views` renders it.
//!
//! The buffer is a `ropey` rope (O(log n) edits and index math, cheap snapshot clones for
//! undo) with a dependency-free tokenizer fallback plus incremental `tree-sitter` for
//! highlighting, rendered by a custom multi-cursor editor widget in `orress-views` and driven
//! by an LSP client. This mirrors Zed's layering so each piece upgrades locally.

mod highlight;
mod task;
mod ts;

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests;

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use ropey::Rope;

pub use highlight::{Tok, Token};
pub use task::{Command, Task, tasks_for};

/// Highlights `text` of the given language into sparse, ordered, non-overlapping tokens.
/// Uses tree-sitter for Rust, Python, C and C++, falling back to the built-in tokenizer for other
/// languages and if a grammar is unavailable.
pub fn highlight(text: &str, lang: Language) -> Vec<Token> {
    if ts::supported(lang)
        && let Some(tokens) = ts::highlight(text, lang)
    {
        return tokens;
    }
    highlight::tokenizer(text, lang)
}

/// Highlights `text` using an *imported* tree-sitter highlight query (e.g. a Zed grammar
/// extension's `highlights.scm`) over the bundled grammar for `lang`, falling back to the built-in
/// query — then the tokenizer — if the imported query does not compile or parsing fails. This is
/// the query half of Zed grammar/query compatibility.
pub fn highlight_with_query(text: &str, lang: Language, query: &str) -> Vec<Token> {
    if ts::supported(lang)
        && let Some(tokens) = ts::highlight_with_query(text, lang, query)
    {
        return tokens;
    }
    highlight(text, lang)
}

/// Whether ORRESS bundles a tree-sitter grammar for `lang` (so an imported query can be applied).
pub fn has_grammar(lang: Language) -> bool {
    ts::supported(lang)
}

/// A language ORRESS can highlight and (for some) run.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum Language {
    Rust,
    Python,
    C,
    Cpp,
    Asm,
    Toml,
    Json,
    Markdown,
    PlainText,
}

impl Language {
    /// Every language, in declaration order.
    pub const ALL: [Self; 9] = [
        Self::Rust,
        Self::Python,
        Self::C,
        Self::Cpp,
        Self::Asm,
        Self::Toml,
        Self::Json,
        Self::Markdown,
        Self::PlainText,
    ];

    /// The language whose [`name`](Self::name) is `name` (case-insensitive), e.g. the language an
    /// extension's grammar declares.
    pub fn from_name(name: &str) -> Option<Self> {
        Self::ALL
            .into_iter()
            .find(|l| l.name().eq_ignore_ascii_case(name))
    }

    /// Guesses the language from a file name's extension.
    pub fn from_path(path: &Path) -> Self {
        match path
            .extension()
            .and_then(|e| e.to_str())
            .map(str::to_ascii_lowercase)
            .as_deref()
        {
            Some("rs") => Self::Rust,
            Some("py" | "pyw") => Self::Python,
            // `.h` is ambiguous C/C++; default to C (the C grammar also parses most headers).
            Some("c" | "h") => Self::C,
            Some("cpp" | "cc" | "cxx" | "c++" | "hpp" | "hh" | "hxx") => Self::Cpp,
            Some("asm" | "s" | "nasm" | "inc") => Self::Asm,
            Some("toml") => Self::Toml,
            Some("json") => Self::Json,
            Some("md" | "markdown") => Self::Markdown,
            _ => Self::PlainText,
        }
    }

    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Rust => "Rust",
            Self::Python => "Python",
            Self::C => "C",
            Self::Cpp => "C++",
            Self::Asm => "Assembly",
            Self::Toml => "TOML",
            Self::Json => "JSON",
            Self::Markdown => "Markdown",
            Self::PlainText => "Plain text",
        }
    }
}

/// An editable text document.
///
/// The text is a `ropey::Rope`: the editor widget edits it in place (O(log n) splices, cheap
/// snapshot clones for undo), and index math (char/byte/line) is O(log n). Consumers that
/// need a contiguous `&str` — tree-sitter, the LSP client, egui's galley — materialize one
/// per frame via `as_string()`.
pub struct Buffer {
    pub path: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub language: Language,
    /// A display name for an untitled buffer (e.g. a generated scratch), shown as the tab title
    /// until it is saved and gains a path. `None` for a plain untitled buffer.
    name: Option<String>,
    /// The text, edited in place by the editor widget.
    pub text: Rope,
    /// The text as last loaded or saved, to tell whether there are unsaved changes.
    saved_text: Rope,
}

impl Buffer {
    /// A new, empty, untitled buffer.
    pub fn untitled() -> Self {
        Self {
            path: None,
            language: Language::PlainText,
            name: None,
            text: Rope::new(),
            saved_text: Rope::new(),
        }
    }

    /// A named, pre-filled buffer with no file on disk yet (e.g. a decompiler port opened for
    /// editing). The language is inferred from `name`'s extension, and it starts out dirty so the
    /// title shows it is unsaved.
    pub fn scratch(name: &str, text: &str) -> Self {
        Self {
            path: None,
            language: Language::from_path(Path::new(name)),
            name: Some(name.to_string()),
            text: Rope::from_str(text),
            saved_text: Rope::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Loads a file into a buffer.
    pub fn open(path: &Path) -> std::io::Result<Self> {
        let text = std::fs::read_to_string(path)?;
        let rope = Rope::from_str(&text);
        Ok(Self {
            path: Some(path.to_path_buf()),
            language: Language::from_path(path),
            name: None,
            saved_text: rope.clone(),
            text: rope,
        })
    }

    /// The whole buffer as a `String` (O(n); callers cache it per frame).
    pub fn as_string(&self) -> String {
        self.text.to_string()
    }

    /// Whether the text differs from what is on disk.
    pub fn is_dirty(&self) -> bool {
        self.text != self.saved_text
    }

    /// Saves to the buffer's path. Returns an error if the buffer is untitled.
    pub fn save(&mut self) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        let path = self.path.clone().ok_or_else(|| {
            std::io::Error::new(
                std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput,
                "this buffer has no file name yet",
            )
        })?;
        self.save_as(&path)
    }

    /// Saves to a specific path and adopts it.
    pub fn save_as(&mut self, path: &Path) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        let mut file = std::io::BufWriter::new(std::fs::File::create(path)?);
        self.text.write_to(&mut file)?;
        std::io::Write::flush(&mut file)?;
        self.saved_text = self.text.clone();
        self.path = Some(path.to_path_buf());
        self.language = Language::from_path(path);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// A file name to seed a Save-As dialog: the current file's name, else a scratch's name,
    /// else a plain default.
    pub fn suggested_name(&self) -> String {
        self.path
            .as_ref()
            .and_then(|p| p.file_name())
            .map(|n| n.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
            .or_else(|| self.name.clone())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "untitled.txt".into())
    }

    /// A short title for the tab: the file name (or "untitled"), with `*` when dirty.
    pub fn title(&self) -> String {
        let name = self
            .path
            .as_ref()
            .and_then(|p| p.file_name())
            .map(|n| n.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
            .or_else(|| self.name.clone())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "untitled".into());
        if self.is_dirty() {
            format!("{name} *")
        } else {
            name
        }
    }

    /// Highlight tokens for the current text.
    pub fn tokens(&self) -> Vec<Token> {
        highlight(&self.as_string(), self.language)
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-editor/src/task.rs`:

```rs
//! Build / run tasks for the open file, in the spirit of Zed's `tasks.json`: a small set
//! of commands derived from the file's language and project. Pure data — the editor view
//! spawns the processes and streams the output.
//!
//! A task is a *sequence* of commands run in order, stopping if one fails. That models
//! "compile, then run the result" (`rustc` then the produced executable) without any shell.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use crate::Language;

/// One command to execute.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Command {
    pub program: String,
    pub args: Vec<String>,
    pub cwd: PathBuf,
}

/// A named task: one or more commands run in sequence.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Task {
    /// Shown on the button / in the menu, e.g. "cargo run".
    pub label: String,
    pub steps: Vec<Command>,
}

/// The nearest ancestor directory containing a `Cargo.toml`, if any.
fn cargo_root(path: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    let mut dir = path.parent();
    while let Some(d) = dir {
        if d.join("Cargo.toml").is_file() {
            return Some(d.to_path_buf());
        }
        dir = d.parent();
    }
    None
}

/// Tasks offered for a file, best/most-common first. Empty for files we cannot run.
pub fn tasks_for(path: &Path, language: Language) -> Vec<Task> {
    let dir = path.parent().unwrap_or(Path::new(".")).to_path_buf();
    let file = path.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
    match language {
        Language::Rust => {
            if let Some(root) = cargo_root(path) {
                vec![
                    one("cargo run", "cargo", &["run"], &root),
                    one("cargo build", "cargo", &["build"], &root),
                    one("cargo test", "cargo", &["test"], &root),
                ]
            } else {
                // A standalone .rs file: compile next to it, then run the result.
                let out = standalone_output(path);
                let out_s = out.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
                vec![
                    Task {
                        label: "rustc & run".into(),
                        steps: vec![
                            cmd(
                                "rustc",
                                &[
                                    "--edition",
                                    "2024",
                                    "-C",
                                    "opt-level=0",
                                    &file,
                                    "-o",
                                    &out_s,
                                ],
                                &dir,
                            ),
                            cmd(&out_s, &[], &dir),
                        ],
                    },
                    one(
                        "rustc (check only)",
                        "rustc",
                        &["--edition", "2024", "--emit=metadata", &file],
                        &dir,
                    ),
                ]
            }
        }
        Language::Python => vec![one("python", "python", &[&file], &dir)],
        _ => Vec::new(),
    }
}

/// Where a standalone `.rs` file compiles to.
fn standalone_output(path: &Path) -> PathBuf {
    let stem = path
        .file_stem()
        .map(|s| s.to_os_string())
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let mut out = path.with_file_name(stem);
    if cfg!(windows) {
        out.set_extension("exe");
    }
    out
}

fn cmd(program: &str, args: &[&str], cwd: &Path) -> Command {
    Command {
        program: program.into(),
        args: args.iter().map(|s| (*s).to_string()).collect(),
        cwd: cwd.to_path_buf(),
    }
}

fn one(label: &str, program: &str, args: &[&str], cwd: &Path) -> Task {
    Task {
        label: label.into(),
        steps: vec![cmd(program, args, cwd)],
    }
}
```

```rs
#[test]
fn imported_highlight_query_is_applied() {
    // A minimal "Zed" highlights.scm that colours only `return` as a keyword and strings. Using it
    // over the bundled C grammar proves imported queries drive the highlighting (the query half of
    // Zed grammar compatibility). A capture the query omits (e.g. `int` as a type) is not coloured.
    let query = "(return_statement) @keyword\n(string_literal) @string\n";
    let src = "int f() { return \"hi\"; }";
    let toks = highlight_with_query(src, Language::C, query);
    let kinds: Vec<_> = toks
        .iter()
        .map(|t| (&src[t.start..t.end], t.kind))
        .collect();
    assert!(
        kinds.iter().any(|(_, k)| *k == Tok::String),
        "string not from imported query: {kinds:?}"
    );
    // The imported query does not capture `int` as a type, so it is not coloured as one.
    assert!(
        !kinds.iter().any(|(t, k)| *k == Tok::Type && *t == "int"),
        "{kinds:?}"
    );
    // A query that does not compile falls back to the built-in highlighting (so `int` is a type).
    let fallback = highlight_with_query(src, Language::C, "(this_node_does_not_exist) @keyword");
    let fk: Vec<_> = fallback
        .iter()
        .map(|t| (&src[t.start..t.end], t.kind))
        .collect();
    assert!(
        fk.iter().any(|(t, k)| *k == Tok::Type && *t == "int"),
        "no fallback: {fk:?}"
    );
}

#[test]
fn highlights_rust() {

#[test]
fn escaped_multibyte_char_in_a_string_does_not_panic() {
    // `\é`: the escaped character is two bytes; skipping a fixed 2 bytes used to land mid-char.
    for (src, lang) in [
        ("s = \"\\é\"\nx = 1\n", Language::Python),
        ("let s = \"a\\é\\😀b\"; let t = 2;", Language::Rust),
        ("x = \"\\é", Language::Python), // unterminated, backslash-escape at EOF
        ("x = \"\\", Language::Python),
    ] {
        let toks = crate::highlight::tokenizer(src, lang);
        for t in &toks {
            assert!(src.is_char_boundary(t.start) && src.is_char_boundary(t.end));
        }
        assert!(toks.iter().any(|t| t.kind == Tok::String), "{src:?}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn imported_query_configs_are_cached() {
    let query = "(return_statement) @keyword
(string_literal) @string
";
    let src = "int f() { return \"hi\"; }";
    // The second lookup reuses the first compiled configuration rather than recompiling.
    let first = crate::ts::cached_config(Language::C, query).expect("compiles");
    let second = crate::ts::cached_config(Language::C, query).expect("cached");
    assert!(std::sync::Arc::ptr_eq(&first, &second));
    // A different query (or language) gets its own entry.
    let other = crate::ts::cached_config(
        Language::C,
        "(string_literal) @string
",
    )
    .unwrap();
    assert!(!std::sync::Arc::ptr_eq(&first, &other));
    // Cached output is identical to compiling the query afresh.
    let fresh = crate::ts::build_config_with(Language::C, query).unwrap();
    let uncached = crate::ts::run(src, &fresh).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(highlight_with_query(src, Language::C, query), uncached);
    assert_eq!(highlight_with_query(src, Language::C, query), uncached);
    // A query that does not compile is cached as a miss (and highlighting falls back).
    assert!(crate::ts::cached_config(Language::C, "(no_such_node) @keyword").is_none());
    assert!(crate::ts::cached_config(Language::C, "(no_such_node) @keyword").is_none());
}
```

`crates/orress-editor/src/ts.rs`:

```rs
//! Tree-sitter syntax highlighting for Rust, Python, C and C++ — the scalable highlighter that
//! replaces the built-in tokenizer for those languages. It produces the same [`Token`] stream, so
//! nothing downstream changes (the tokenizer stays as the fallback for other languages and if a
//! grammar fails to load).
//!
//! Each language pairs a compiled-in grammar with a highlight query (`.scm`). The grammar set is a
//! table, so adding a language is one arm; and [`highlight_with_query`] highlights a built-in
//! grammar with an *imported* query — e.g. a Zed grammar extension's `highlights.scm` — which is
//! the query half of Zed grammar/query compatibility (the grammar half, loading Zed's WASM
//! parsers, waits for the wasmtime host). Imported queries are compiled once and cached per
//! (language, query), so highlighting with one on every edit costs no more than the built-in query.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::hash::{Hash, Hasher};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex, OnceLock};

use tree_sitter_highlight::{HighlightConfiguration, HighlightEvent, Highlighter};

use crate::{Language, Tok, Token};

/// Capture names we ask tree-sitter to recognise, mapped to our token kinds by index.
const NAMES: &[&str] = &[
    "keyword",
    "type",
    "type.builtin",
    "constructor",
    "function",
    "function.method",
    "function.macro",
    "string",
    "string.special",
    "escape",
    "character",
    "number",
    "boolean",
    "constant",
    "constant.builtin",
    "comment",
    "attribute",
    "label",
];

fn tok_for(idx: usize) -> Option<Tok> {
    Some(match *NAMES.get(idx)? {
        "keyword" | "boolean" => Tok::Keyword,
        "constant.builtin" => Tok::Number,
        "type" | "type.builtin" | "constructor" | "constant" => Tok::Type,
        "function" | "function.method" => Tok::Function,
        "function.macro" => Tok::Macro,
        "string" | "string.special" | "escape" => Tok::String,
        "character" => Tok::Char,
        "number" => Tok::Number,
        "comment" => Tok::Comment,
        "attribute" => Tok::Attribute,
        "label" => Tok::Lifetime,
        _ => return None,
    })
}

/// The compiled-in grammar for a language, if ORRESS bundles one.
fn grammar(lang: Language) -> Option<tree_sitter::Language> {
    Some(match lang {
        Language::Rust => tree_sitter::Language::new(tree_sitter_rust::LANGUAGE),
        Language::Python => tree_sitter::Language::new(tree_sitter_python::LANGUAGE),
        Language::C => tree_sitter::Language::new(tree_sitter_c::LANGUAGE),
        Language::Cpp => tree_sitter::Language::new(tree_sitter_cpp::LANGUAGE),
        _ => return None,
    })
}

/// The highlight query shipped with each bundled grammar. C++ inherits C's query (its grammar is a
/// superset), as editors do with `; inherits: c`, then adds the C++-specific captures.
fn default_query(lang: Language) -> Option<&'static str> {
    Some(match lang {
        Language::Rust => tree_sitter_rust::HIGHLIGHTS_QUERY,
        Language::Python => tree_sitter_python::HIGHLIGHTS_QUERY,
        Language::C => tree_sitter_c::HIGHLIGHT_QUERY,
        Language::Cpp => {
            static CPP: OnceLock<String> = OnceLock::new();
            CPP.get_or_init(|| {
                format!(
                    "{}\n{}",
                    tree_sitter_c::HIGHLIGHT_QUERY,
                    tree_sitter_cpp::HIGHLIGHT_QUERY
                )
            })
        }
        _ => return None,
    })
}

/// Builds a highlighter for `lang`'s bundled grammar from a specific query — the bundled one, or a
/// query imported from an extension (e.g. a Zed grammar's `highlights.scm`). Returns `None` if the
/// grammar is unavailable or the query does not compile against it.
pub fn build_config_with(lang: Language, query: &str) -> Option<HighlightConfiguration> {
    let language = grammar(lang)?;
    let mut config = HighlightConfiguration::new(language, lang.name(), query, "", "").ok()?;
    config.configure(NAMES);
    Some(config)
}

fn config(lang: Language) -> Option<&'static HighlightConfiguration> {
    // One default configuration per language, built once.
    static RUST: OnceLock<Option<HighlightConfiguration>> = OnceLock::new();
    static PYTHON: OnceLock<Option<HighlightConfiguration>> = OnceLock::new();
    static C: OnceLock<Option<HighlightConfiguration>> = OnceLock::new();
    static CPP: OnceLock<Option<HighlightConfiguration>> = OnceLock::new();
    let build = || build_config_with(lang, default_query(lang)?);
    match lang {
        Language::Rust => RUST.get_or_init(build).as_ref(),
        Language::Python => PYTHON.get_or_init(build).as_ref(),
        Language::C => C.get_or_init(build).as_ref(),
        Language::Cpp => CPP.get_or_init(build).as_ref(),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Whether tree-sitter can highlight this language (ORRESS bundles a grammar for it).
pub fn supported(lang: Language) -> bool {
    grammar(lang).is_some()
}

/// Highlights with an imported highlight query (e.g. a Zed grammar extension's `highlights.scm`)
/// over the bundled grammar for `lang`, instead of the built-in query. Returns `None` if the
/// grammar is unavailable, the query does not compile, or parsing fails — so the caller can fall
/// back to the built-in query or the tokenizer.
pub fn highlight_with_query(text: &str, lang: Language, query: &str) -> Option<Vec<Token>> {
    let config = cached_config(lang, query)?;
    run(text, &config)
}

/// How many compiled imported-query configurations are kept. Each installed grammar extension
/// contributes one per language, so this is generous; on overflow the cache simply starts over.
const QUERY_CACHE_CAP: usize = 32;

/// A compiled imported query, or `None` when it does not compile against the bundled grammar
/// (cached too, so a broken query is not recompiled on every edit).
type CachedConfig = Option<Arc<HighlightConfiguration>>;

/// The compiled highlight configuration for `lang`'s bundled grammar with `query`, compiled on first
/// use and cached per (language, query hash) — compiling a query is far slower than highlighting,
/// so doing it per edit would make typing lag. Thread-safe and bounded ([`QUERY_CACHE_CAP`]).
pub(crate) fn cached_config(lang: Language, query: &str) -> CachedConfig {
    static CACHE: OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<(Language, u64), CachedConfig>>> = OnceLock::new();
    let key = (lang, query_hash(query));
    let cache = CACHE.get_or_init(Default::default);
    if let Some(hit) = cache.lock().ok()?.get(&key) {
        return hit.clone();
    }
    // Compile outside the lock, so other threads highlighting meanwhile are not held up.
    let built = build_config_with(lang, query).map(Arc::new);
    let mut map = cache.lock().ok()?;
    if map.len() >= QUERY_CACHE_CAP && !map.contains_key(&key) {
        map.clear();
    }
    // If another thread compiled it first, keep (and return) that one.
    map.entry(key).or_insert(built).clone()
}

fn query_hash(query: &str) -> u64 {
    let mut h = std::collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher::new();
    query.hash(&mut h);
    h.finish()
}

/// Highlights with tree-sitter's built-in query for the language. Returns `None` if the grammar is
/// unavailable or parsing fails, so the caller can fall back to the tokenizer.
pub fn highlight(text: &str, lang: Language) -> Option<Vec<Token>> {
    run(text, config(lang)?)
}

/// Runs a prepared highlight configuration over `text`, collecting the [`Token`] spans.
pub(crate) fn run(text: &str, config: &HighlightConfiguration) -> Option<Vec<Token>> {
    let mut highlighter = Highlighter::new();
    let events = highlighter
        .highlight(config, text.as_bytes(), None, |_| None)
        .ok()?;
    let mut out: Vec<Token> = Vec::new();
    let mut stack: Vec<Option<Tok>> = Vec::new();
    for event in events {
        match event.ok()? {
            HighlightEvent::HighlightStart(h) => stack.push(tok_for(h.0)),
            HighlightEvent::HighlightEnd => {
                stack.pop();
            }
            HighlightEvent::Source { start, end } => {
                if let Some(Some(kind)) = stack.last() {
                    // Merge with the previous span if it is the same kind and adjacent.
                    if let Some(last) = out.last_mut()
                        && last.kind == *kind
                        && last.end == start
                    {
                        last.end = end;
                    } else {
                        out.push(Token {
                            start,
                            end,
                            kind: *kind,
                        });
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    Some(out)
}
```

`crates/orress-emu/src/cpu.rs`:

```rs
//! The CPU state: 16 general-purpose registers (iced-x86 encoding order), the instruction
//! pointer, and the arithmetic flags. Register reads/writes respect sub-register widths and
//! the x86-64 rule that a 32-bit write zeroes the upper 32 bits.

use iced_x86::Register;

/// The six arithmetic flags an integer emulator needs.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Flags {
    pub cf: bool,
    pub pf: bool,
    pub af: bool,
    pub zf: bool,
    pub sf: bool,
    pub of: bool,
}

impl Flags {
    /// Packs into the low bits of RFLAGS (bit 1 is the reserved, always-1 bit).
    pub fn to_rflags(self) -> u64 {
        let mut v = 0b10u64;
        v |= u64::from(self.cf);
        v |= u64::from(self.pf) << 2;
        v |= u64::from(self.af) << 4;
        v |= u64::from(self.zf) << 6;
        v |= u64::from(self.sf) << 7;
        v |= u64::from(self.of) << 11;
        v
    }
}

/// x86-64 integer register file plus RIP and flags.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct Cpu {
    /// Indexed in iced-x86 order: rax, rcx, rdx, rbx, rsp, rbp, rsi, rdi, r8..r15.
    pub regs: [u64; 16],
    /// The 128-bit SSE registers xmm0..xmm15 (enough for the SSE2 subset that Rust emits for
    /// slice comparisons and small `memset`/`memcpy`). AVX (ymm/zmm) upper halves are not modelled.
    pub xmm: [u128; 16],
    pub rip: u64,
    pub flags: Flags,
    /// The FS segment base (SysV thread pointer: `fs:[0x28]` is the stack canary).
    pub fs_base: u64,
    /// The GS segment base (Win64 TEB: `gs:[0x30]` is the TEB self-pointer, `gs:[0x60]` the PEB).
    pub gs_base: u64,
}

/// The 64-bit container index (0..16) for a general-purpose register, or `None` for a
/// non-GPR (segment, xmm, rip, ...).
fn gpr_index(full: Register) -> Option<usize> {
    use Register::*;
    Some(match full {
        RAX => 0,
        RCX => 1,
        RDX => 2,
        RBX => 3,
        RSP => 4,
        RBP => 5,
        RSI => 6,
        RDI => 7,
        R8 => 8,
        R9 => 9,
        R10 => 10,
        R11 => 11,
        R12 => 12,
        R13 => 13,
        R14 => 14,
        R15 => 15,
        // `use Register::*` brings `Register::None` into scope, so qualify the Option here.
        _ => return Option::None,
    })
}

/// The index (0..16) of an SSE register xmm0..xmm15, or `None` for anything else.
fn xmm_index(r: Register) -> Option<usize> {
    r.is_xmm().then(|| r.number())
}

/// The four legacy high-byte registers (bits 8..16 of their container).
fn is_high_byte(reg: Register) -> bool {
    matches!(
        reg,
        Register::AH | Register::CH | Register::DH | Register::BH
    )
}

impl Cpu {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    /// Reads a register, honouring its width (and the AH/CH/DH/BH high-byte regs).
    pub fn reg(&self, r: Register) -> u64 {
        if r == Register::RIP || r == Register::EIP {
            return self.rip;
        }
        let Some(idx) = gpr_index(r.full_register()) else {
            return 0;
        };
        let v = self.regs[idx];
        if is_high_byte(r) {
            return (v >> 8) & 0xff;
        }
        match r.size() {
            1 => v & 0xff,
            2 => v & 0xffff,
            4 => v & 0xffff_ffff,
            _ => v,
        }
    }

    /// Writes a register, honouring width rules (32-bit writes zero the upper 32 bits).
    pub fn set_reg(&mut self, r: Register, val: u64) {
        if r == Register::RIP || r == Register::EIP {
            self.rip = val;
            return;
        }
        let Some(idx) = gpr_index(r.full_register()) else {
            return;
        };
        let cur = self.regs[idx];
        self.regs[idx] = if is_high_byte(r) {
            (cur & !0xff00) | ((val & 0xff) << 8)
        } else {
            match r.size() {
                1 => (cur & !0xff) | (val & 0xff),
                2 => (cur & !0xffff) | (val & 0xffff),
                4 => val & 0xffff_ffff, // zero-extend to 64
                _ => val,
            }
        };
    }

    /// Reads a 128-bit SSE register (xmm0..xmm15); 0 for anything that is not one.
    pub fn xmm(&self, r: Register) -> u128 {
        xmm_index(r).map_or(0, |i| self.xmm[i])
    }

    /// Writes a 128-bit SSE register (xmm0..xmm15); ignored for anything that is not one.
    pub fn set_xmm(&mut self, r: Register, val: u128) {
        if let Some(i) = xmm_index(r) {
            self.xmm[i] = val;
        }
    }

    // Named accessors for the registers the harness touches directly.
    pub fn rsp(&self) -> u64 {
        self.regs[4]
    }
    pub fn set_rsp(&mut self, v: u64) {
        self.regs[4] = v;
    }
    pub fn rax(&self) -> u64 {
        self.regs[0]
    }
}

```

`crates/orress-emu/src/exec.rs`:

```rs
//! The instruction interpreter: operand access, flag computation, and the per-mnemonic
//! dispatch. Covers the integer/branch/stack/memory subset that real check and decryption
//! routines use; anything else returns [`EmuError::Unsupported`] so gaps are visible.

use iced_x86::{Instruction, Mnemonic, OpKind, Register};

use crate::{EmuError, Emulator};

/// A condition code, shared by the Jcc / SETcc / CMOVcc families.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum Cc {
    O,
    No,
    B,
    Ae,
    E,
    Ne,
    Be,
    A,
    S,
    Ns,
    P,
    Np,
    L,
    Ge,
    Le,
    G,
}

fn mask(size: usize) -> u64 {
    if size >= 8 {
        u64::MAX
    } else {
        (1u64 << (size * 8)) - 1
    }
}

fn sign_bit(size: usize) -> u64 {
    1u64 << (size * 8 - 1)
}

/// Even parity of the low byte (x86 PF is computed on the low 8 bits only).
fn parity(v: u64) -> bool {
    (v as u8).count_ones().is_multiple_of(2)
}

/// Sign-extends the low `size` bytes of `v` to a full i64.
fn sign_extend(v: u64, size: usize) -> i64 {
    if size >= 8 {
        return v as i64;
    }
    let shift = 64 - size * 8;
    ((v << shift) as i64) >> shift
}

/// Sign-extends the low `bits` bits of a u128 to a full i128 (for the double-width DIV dividend).
fn sign_extend128(v: u128, bits: u32) -> i128 {
    if bits >= 128 {
        return v as i128;
    }
    let shift = 128 - bits;
    ((v << shift) as i128) >> shift
}

impl Emulator {
    // --- operands ---------------------------------------------------------

    /// The linear address of a memory operand: its offset plus the FS/GS segment base when the
    /// operand uses one (`fs:[0x28]` canary loads, `gs:[0x30]` TEB access). Other segments have
    /// a zero base in 64-bit mode.
    fn ea(&self, instr: &Instruction) -> u64 {
        let seg = match instr.memory_segment() {
            Register::FS => self.cpu.fs_base,
            Register::GS => self.cpu.gs_base,
            _ => 0,
        };
        self.offset(instr).wrapping_add(seg)
    }

    /// The offset (segment-relative address) of a memory operand — what `lea` computes, since
    /// `lea` never applies a segment base.
    fn offset(&self, instr: &Instruction) -> u64 {
        let base = instr.memory_base();
        let disp = instr.memory_displacement64();
        if base == Register::RIP || base == Register::EIP {
            return disp; // iced resolves RIP-relative to an absolute address
        }
        let mut addr = disp;
        if base != Register::None {
            addr = addr.wrapping_add(self.cpu.reg(base));
        }
        let index = instr.memory_index();
        if index != Register::None {
            let scale = u64::from(instr.memory_index_scale());
            addr = addr.wrapping_add(self.cpu.reg(index).wrapping_mul(scale));
        }
        addr
    }

    /// The operation width in bytes, taken from operand 0 (the destination for binary ops,
    /// the operand itself for unary ops).
    fn width(&self, instr: &Instruction) -> usize {
        match instr.op0_kind() {
            OpKind::Register => instr.op_register(0).size(),
            OpKind::Memory => instr.memory_size().size(),
            _ => 8,
        }
    }

    fn read_op(&self, instr: &Instruction, i: u32, size: usize) -> Result<u64, EmuError> {
        Ok(match instr.op_kind(i) {
            OpKind::Register => self.cpu.reg(instr.op_register(i)),
            OpKind::Memory => self.mem.read(self.ea(instr), size)?,
            OpKind::NearBranch16 | OpKind::NearBranch32 | OpKind::NearBranch64 => {
                instr.near_branch_target()
            }
            _ => instr.immediate(i) & mask(size),
        })
    }

    fn write_op(
        &mut self,
        instr: &Instruction,
        i: u32,
        val: u64,
        size: usize,
    ) -> Result<(), EmuError> {
        match instr.op_kind(i) {
            OpKind::Register => self.cpu.set_reg(instr.op_register(i), val),
            OpKind::Memory => self.mem.write(self.ea(instr), val & mask(size), size)?,
            _ => {}
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    // --- SSE / 128-bit operands -------------------------------------------

    /// Reads a 128-bit (xmmword) operand: a whole XMM register, or 16 bytes of memory.
    fn read_xmm(&self, instr: &Instruction, i: u32) -> Result<u128, EmuError> {
        match instr.op_kind(i) {
            OpKind::Register => Ok(self.cpu.xmm(instr.op_register(i))),
            OpKind::Memory => self.read128(self.ea(instr)),
            _ => Ok(0),
        }
    }

    /// Writes a 128-bit (xmmword) operand: a whole XMM register, or 16 bytes of memory.
    fn write_xmm(&mut self, instr: &Instruction, i: u32, val: u128) -> Result<(), EmuError> {
        match instr.op_kind(i) {
            OpKind::Register => self.cpu.set_xmm(instr.op_register(i), val),
            OpKind::Memory => self.write128(self.ea(instr), val)?,
            _ => {}
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Reads 16 bytes little-endian (an XMM-width memory load).
    fn read128(&self, addr: u64) -> Result<u128, EmuError> {
        let lo = self.mem.read(addr, 8)?;
        let hi = self.mem.read(addr.wrapping_add(8), 8)?;
        Ok((u128::from(hi) << 64) | u128::from(lo))
    }

    /// Writes 16 bytes little-endian (an XMM-width memory store).
    fn write128(&mut self, addr: u64, val: u128) -> Result<(), EmuError> {
        self.mem.write(addr, val as u64, 8)?;
        self.mem
            .write(addr.wrapping_add(8), (val >> 64) as u64, 8)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Reads a scalar operand (`bytes` wide) that may be a GPR, an XMM register (its low bytes),
    /// memory, or an immediate — for MOVD/MOVQ, which shuttle 4 or 8 bytes between an XMM and a
    /// GPR, memory or another XMM.
    fn read_scalar(&self, instr: &Instruction, i: u32, bytes: usize) -> Result<u64, EmuError> {
        Ok(match instr.op_kind(i) {
            OpKind::Register => {
                let r = instr.op_register(i);
                if r.is_xmm() {
                    (self.cpu.xmm(r) as u64) & mask(bytes)
                } else {
                    self.cpu.reg(r) & mask(bytes)
                }
            }
            OpKind::Memory => self.mem.read(self.ea(instr), bytes)?,
            _ => instr.immediate(i) & mask(bytes),
        })
    }

    /// Writes a scalar operand (`bytes` wide) that may be a GPR, an XMM register (zero-extending
    /// the rest of the 128 bits), or memory — the destination side of MOVD/MOVQ.
    fn write_scalar(
        &mut self,
        instr: &Instruction,
        i: u32,
        val: u64,
        bytes: usize,
    ) -> Result<(), EmuError> {
        match instr.op_kind(i) {
            OpKind::Register => {
                let r = instr.op_register(i);
                if r.is_xmm() {
                    self.cpu.set_xmm(r, u128::from(val & mask(bytes))); // zero-extends xmm
                } else {
                    self.cpu.set_reg(r, val); // set_reg applies the register's own width rules
                }
            }
            OpKind::Memory => self.mem.write(self.ea(instr), val & mask(bytes), bytes)?,
            _ => {}
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    // --- stack ------------------------------------------------------------

    fn push(&mut self, val: u64) -> Result<(), EmuError> {
        let sp = self.cpu.rsp().wrapping_sub(8);
        self.mem.write(sp, val, 8)?;
        self.cpu.set_rsp(sp);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn pop(&mut self) -> Result<u64, EmuError> {
        let sp = self.cpu.rsp();
        let val = self.mem.read(sp, 8)?;
        self.cpu.set_rsp(sp.wrapping_add(8));
        Ok(val)
    }

    // --- flag helpers -----------------------------------------------------

    fn set_szp(&mut self, res: u64, size: usize) {
        let r = res & mask(size);
        self.cpu.flags.zf = r == 0;
        self.cpu.flags.sf = r & sign_bit(size) != 0;
        self.cpu.flags.pf = parity(r);
    }

    /// `a + b`, setting all arithmetic flags.
    fn do_add(&mut self, a: u64, b: u64, size: usize) -> u64 {
        let m = mask(size);
        let (a, b) = (a & m, b & m);
        let sum = u128::from(a) + u128::from(b);
        let res = (sum as u64) & m;
        let f = &mut self.cpu.flags;
        f.cf = (sum >> (size * 8)) & 1 == 1;
        f.af = ((a & 0xf) + (b & 0xf)) > 0xf;
        f.of = (!(a ^ b) & (a ^ res) & sign_bit(size)) != 0;
        self.set_szp(res, size);
        res
    }

    /// `a - b`, setting all arithmetic flags (shared by SUB and CMP).
    fn do_sub(&mut self, a: u64, b: u64, size: usize) -> u64 {
        let m = mask(size);
        let (a, b) = (a & m, b & m);
        let res = a.wrapping_sub(b) & m;
        let f = &mut self.cpu.flags;
        f.cf = a < b;
        f.af = (a & 0xf) < (b & 0xf);
        f.of = ((a ^ b) & (a ^ res) & sign_bit(size)) != 0;
        self.set_szp(res, size);
        res
    }

    /// `a + b + carry`, setting all arithmetic flags for the full three-input add (OF/AF must
    /// reflect `a + b + carry`, not just one of two chained adds).
    fn do_adc(&mut self, a: u64, b: u64, carry: u64, size: usize) -> u64 {
        let m = mask(size);
        let (a, b, c) = (a & m, b & m, carry & 1);
        let sum = u128::from(a) + u128::from(b) + u128::from(c);
        let res = (sum as u64) & m;
        let f = &mut self.cpu.flags;
        f.cf = (sum >> (size * 8)) & 1 == 1;
        f.af = ((a & 0xf) + (b & 0xf) + c) > 0xf;
        f.of = (!(a ^ b) & (a ^ res) & sign_bit(size)) != 0;
        self.set_szp(res, size);
        res
    }

    /// `a - b - borrow`, setting all arithmetic flags for the full three-input subtract.
    fn do_sbb(&mut self, a: u64, b: u64, borrow: u64, size: usize) -> u64 {
        let m = mask(size);
        let (a, b, c) = (a & m, b & m, borrow & 1);
        let res = a.wrapping_sub(b).wrapping_sub(c) & m;
        let f = &mut self.cpu.flags;
        f.cf = u128::from(a) < u128::from(b) + u128::from(c);
        f.af = (a & 0xf) < (b & 0xf) + c;
        f.of = ((a ^ b) & (a ^ res) & sign_bit(size)) != 0;
        self.set_szp(res, size);
        res
    }

    /// Bitwise result flags (AND/OR/XOR/TEST): CF = OF = 0, AF cleared, SF/ZF/PF from result.
    fn do_logic(&mut self, res: u64, size: usize) {
        self.cpu.flags.cf = false;
        self.cpu.flags.of = false;
        self.cpu.flags.af = false;
        self.set_szp(res, size);
    }

    fn eval_cc(&self, cc: Cc) -> bool {
        let f = &self.cpu.flags;
        match cc {
            Cc::O => f.of,
            Cc::No => !f.of,
            Cc::B => f.cf,
            Cc::Ae => !f.cf,
            Cc::E => f.zf,
            Cc::Ne => !f.zf,
            Cc::Be => f.cf || f.zf,
            Cc::A => !f.cf && !f.zf,
            Cc::S => f.sf,
            Cc::Ns => !f.sf,
            Cc::P => f.pf,
            Cc::Np => !f.pf,
            Cc::L => f.sf != f.of,
            Cc::Ge => f.sf == f.of,
            Cc::Le => f.zf || (f.sf != f.of),
            Cc::G => !f.zf && (f.sf == f.of),
        }
    }

    // --- dispatch ---------------------------------------------------------

    pub(crate) fn exec(&mut self, instr: &Instruction) -> Result<(), EmuError> {
        use Mnemonic as M;
        let size = self.width(instr);
        let addr = instr.ip();

        if let Some(cc) = jcc(instr.mnemonic()) {
            if self.eval_cc(cc) {
                self.cpu.rip = instr.near_branch_target();
            }
            return Ok(());
        }
        if let Some(cc) = setcc(instr.mnemonic()) {
            let v = u64::from(self.eval_cc(cc));
            return self.write_op(instr, 0, v, 1);
        }
        if let Some(cc) = cmovcc(instr.mnemonic()) {
            if self.eval_cc(cc) {
                let v = self.read_op(instr, 1, size)?;
                self.write_op(instr, 0, v, size)?;
            } else if size == 4 {
                // A 32-bit CMOVcc writes its destination even when the condition is false, so
                // the upper 32 bits are zeroed regardless (rewriting the low half does exactly that).
                let r = instr.op_register(0);
                self.cpu.set_reg(r, self.cpu.reg(r));
            }
            return Ok(());
        }

        match instr.mnemonic() {
            M::Mov => {
                let v = self.read_op(instr, 1, size)?;
                self.write_op(instr, 0, v, size)?;
            }
            M::Movzx => {
                let src = self.src_size(instr);
                let v = self.read_op(instr, 1, src)? & mask(src);
                self.write_op(instr, 0, v, size)?;
            }
            M::Movsx | M::Movsxd => {
                let src = self.src_size(instr);
                let v = self.read_op(instr, 1, src)?;
                let ext = sign_extend(v, src) as u64;
                self.write_op(instr, 0, ext, size)?;
            }
            M::Lea => {
                let a = self.offset(instr);
                self.write_op(instr, 0, a, size)?;
            }
            M::Add => {
                let (a, b) = self.two(instr, size)?;
                let r = self.do_add(a, b, size);
                self.write_op(instr, 0, r, size)?;
            }
            M::Sub => {
                let (a, b) = self.two(instr, size)?;
                let r = self.do_sub(a, b, size);
                self.write_op(instr, 0, r, size)?;
            }
            M::Cmp => {
                let (a, b) = self.two(instr, size)?;
                self.do_sub(a, b, size);
            }
            M::Adc => {
                let (a, b) = self.two(instr, size)?;
                let carry = u64::from(self.cpu.flags.cf);
                let r = self.do_adc(a, b, carry, size);
                self.write_op(instr, 0, r, size)?;
            }
            M::Sbb => {
                let (a, b) = self.two(instr, size)?;
                let borrow = u64::from(self.cpu.flags.cf);
                let r = self.do_sbb(a, b, borrow, size);
                self.write_op(instr, 0, r, size)?;
            }
            M::And => {
                let (a, b) = self.two(instr, size)?;
                let r = a & b;
                self.do_logic(r, size);
                self.write_op(instr, 0, r, size)?;
            }
            M::Or => {
                let (a, b) = self.two(instr, size)?;
                let r = a | b;
                self.do_logic(r, size);
                self.write_op(instr, 0, r, size)?;
            }
            M::Xor => {
                let (a, b) = self.two(instr, size)?;
                let r = a ^ b;
                self.do_logic(r, size);
                self.write_op(instr, 0, r, size)?;
            }
            M::Test => {
                let (a, b) = self.two(instr, size)?;
                self.do_logic(a & b, size);
            }
            M::Not => {
                let a = self.read_op(instr, 0, size)?;
                self.write_op(instr, 0, !a, size)?;
            }
            M::Neg => {
                let a = self.read_op(instr, 0, size)?;
                let r = self.do_sub(0, a, size);
                self.write_op(instr, 0, r, size)?;
            }
            M::Inc => {
                let a = self.read_op(instr, 0, size)?;
                let saved_cf = self.cpu.flags.cf;
                let r = self.do_add(a, 1, size);
                self.cpu.flags.cf = saved_cf; // INC preserves CF
                self.write_op(instr, 0, r, size)?;
            }
            M::Dec => {
                let a = self.read_op(instr, 0, size)?;
                let saved_cf = self.cpu.flags.cf;
                let r = self.do_sub(a, 1, size);
                self.cpu.flags.cf = saved_cf; // DEC preserves CF
                self.write_op(instr, 0, r, size)?;
            }
            M::Shl | M::Sal => self.shift(instr, size, Shift::Left)?,
            M::Shr => self.shift(instr, size, Shift::Right)?,
            M::Sar => self.shift(instr, size, Shift::Arith)?,
            M::Rol => self.rotate(instr, size, true)?,
            M::Ror => self.rotate(instr, size, false)?,
            M::Imul => self.imul(instr, size)?,
            M::Mul => self.mul(instr, size)?,
            M::Div => self.div(instr, size, false)?,
            M::Idiv => self.div(instr, size, true)?,
            M::Clc => self.cpu.flags.cf = false,
            M::Stc => self.cpu.flags.cf = true,
            M::Cmc => self.cpu.flags.cf = !self.cpu.flags.cf,
            M::Cdqe => {
                let v = sign_extend(self.cpu.reg(Register::EAX), 4) as u64;
                self.cpu.set_reg(Register::RAX, v);
            }
            M::Cwde => {
                let v = (sign_extend(self.cpu.reg(Register::AX), 2) as u64) & 0xffff_ffff;
                self.cpu.set_reg(Register::EAX, v);
            }
            M::Cdq => {
                let rax = self.cpu.reg(Register::EAX);
                let hi = if rax & 0x8000_0000 != 0 {
                    0xffff_ffff
                } else {
                    0
                };
                self.cpu.set_reg(Register::EDX, hi);
            }
            M::Cqo => {
                let hi = if self.cpu.rax() & sign_bit(8) != 0 {
                    u64::MAX
                } else {
                    0
                };
                self.cpu.set_reg(Register::RDX, hi);
            }
            M::Push => {
                let v = self.read_op(instr, 0, 8)?;
                self.push(v)?;
            }
            M::Pop => {
                let v = self.pop()?;
                self.write_op(instr, 0, v, 8)?;
            }
            M::Call => {
                let slot_stub = self.slot_hook(instr);
                let target = if slot_stub.is_some() {
                    0
                } else {
                    self.read_op(instr, 0, 8)?
                };
                self.push(self.cpu.rip)?; // RIP already points past the call
                match slot_stub {
                    // `call [IAT slot]`: run the import's stub (it pops the return address).
                    Some(stub) => self.apply_stub(&stub)?,
                    None => self.cpu.rip = target,
                }
            }
            M::Jmp => match self.slot_hook(instr) {
                // `jmp [GOT/IAT slot]` (a PLT stub or tail call): the caller's return address is
                // already on the stack, so the stub returns straight to it.
                Some(stub) => self.apply_stub(&stub)?,
                None => self.cpu.rip = self.read_op(instr, 0, 8)?,
            },
            M::Ret => {
                let ret = self.pop()?;
                self.cpu.rip = ret;
                if instr.op_count() == 1 {
                    let extra = instr.immediate(0);
                    self.cpu.set_rsp(self.cpu.rsp().wrapping_add(extra));
                }
            }
            M::Leave => {
                let rbp = self.cpu.reg(Register::RBP);
                self.cpu.set_rsp(rbp);
                let v = self.pop()?;
                self.cpu.set_reg(Register::RBP, v);
            }
            // --- SSE2 (128-bit) ---
            // Every 128-bit move is the same here: copy 16 bytes, reg or memory, either way.
            // (Alignment is not enforced, so movdqa/movaps on unaligned memory do not fault.)
            M::Movdqu | M::Movdqa | M::Movups | M::Movaps | M::Movupd | M::Movapd => {
                let v = self.read_xmm(instr, 1)?;
                self.write_xmm(instr, 0, v)?;
            }
            // MOVD moves 4 bytes, MOVQ 8, between an XMM register and a GPR, memory or XMM.
            M::Movd | M::Movq => {
                let bytes = if instr.mnemonic() == M::Movq { 8 } else { 4 };
                let v = self.read_scalar(instr, 1, bytes)?;
                self.write_scalar(instr, 0, v, bytes)?;
            }
            M::Pxor | M::Xorps | M::Xorpd => {
                let r = self.read_xmm(instr, 0)? ^ self.read_xmm(instr, 1)?;
                self.write_xmm(instr, 0, r)?;
            }
            M::Pand | M::Andps | M::Andpd => {
                let r = self.read_xmm(instr, 0)? & self.read_xmm(instr, 1)?;
                self.write_xmm(instr, 0, r)?;
            }
            M::Por | M::Orps | M::Orpd => {
                let r = self.read_xmm(instr, 0)? | self.read_xmm(instr, 1)?;
                self.write_xmm(instr, 0, r)?;
            }
            // PANDN: dest = (NOT dest) AND src.
            M::Pandn => {
                let r = !self.read_xmm(instr, 0)? & self.read_xmm(instr, 1)?;
                self.write_xmm(instr, 0, r)?;
            }
            // Packed compare-equal: each lane becomes all-ones on a match, all-zeros otherwise.
            M::Pcmpeqb => self.pcmpeq(instr, 1)?,
            M::Pcmpeqw => self.pcmpeq(instr, 2)?,
            M::Pcmpeqd => self.pcmpeq(instr, 4)?,
            // PMOVMSKB: gather the top bit of each of the 16 bytes into a GPR.
            M::Pmovmskb => {
                let v = self.read_xmm(instr, 1)?;
                let mut m = 0u64;
                for k in 0..16 {
                    if (v >> (k * 8 + 7)) & 1 == 1 {
                        m |= 1u64 << k;
                    }
                }
                self.write_op(instr, 0, m, size)?;
            }
            M::Nop | M::Endbr64 | M::Endbr32 | M::Pause => {}
            other => {
                return Err(EmuError::Unsupported {
                    addr,
                    mnemonic: format!("{other:?}"),
                });
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// The stub for an indirect `call`/`jmp` through a hooked import slot. Import names are keyed
    /// by the IAT/GOT *slot* address, but `call [slot]` loads the slot's contents — in the file
    /// image that is a hint/name RVA (PE) or a lazy-binding PLT address (ELF), not code — so the
    /// slot address itself has to be matched here or the hook would never fire.
    fn slot_hook(&self, instr: &Instruction) -> Option<crate::Stub> {
        if instr.op0_kind() != OpKind::Memory || self.hooks.is_empty() {
            return None;
        }
        self.hooks.get(&self.ea(instr)).cloned()
    }

    /// Reads both operands of a binary instruction (dst, src), at the operation width.
    fn two(&self, instr: &Instruction, size: usize) -> Result<(u64, u64), EmuError> {
        Ok((self.read_op(instr, 0, size)?, self.read_op(instr, 1, size)?))
    }

    /// Packed compare-equal over `lane`-byte lanes (PCMPEQB/W/D): each lane of the destination
    /// becomes all-ones when the two lanes are equal, all-zeros otherwise.
    fn pcmpeq(&mut self, instr: &Instruction, lane: usize) -> Result<(), EmuError> {
        let a = self.read_xmm(instr, 0)?;
        let b = self.read_xmm(instr, 1)?;
        let lane_mask = (1u128 << (lane * 8)) - 1;
        let mut res = 0u128;
        let mut k = 0;
        while k < 16 {
            let shift = k * 8;
            if (a >> shift) & lane_mask == (b >> shift) & lane_mask {
                res |= lane_mask << shift;
            }
            k += lane;
        }
        self.write_xmm(instr, 0, res)
    }

    /// The width of the *source* operand (for MOVZX/MOVSX, where it differs from the dest).
    fn src_size(&self, instr: &Instruction) -> usize {
        match instr.op_kind(1) {
            OpKind::Register => instr.op_register(1).size(),
            OpKind::Memory => instr.memory_size().size(),
            _ => 1,
        }
    }

    fn shift(&mut self, instr: &Instruction, size: usize, kind: Shift) -> Result<(), EmuError> {
        let a = self.read_op(instr, 0, size)? & mask(size);
        let bits = (size * 8) as u32;
        // x86 masks the count to 5 bits for 8/16/32-bit operands, 6 bits only for 64-bit.
        let count_mask = if size >= 8 { 0x3f } else { 0x1f };
        let cnt = (self.read_op(instr, 1, 1)? & count_mask) as u32;
        if cnt == 0 {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let (res, cf) = match kind {
            Shift::Left => {
                // Guard bits - cnt: a left shift by >= width shifts every bit out (CF = 0),
                // and `bits - cnt` would otherwise underflow and panic in debug builds.
                let cf = if cnt <= bits {
                    (a >> (bits - cnt)) & 1 == 1
                } else {
                    false
                };
                (a.wrapping_shl(cnt) & mask(size), cf)
            }
            Shift::Right => {
                // a has only `bits` significant bits, so `a >> cnt` is 0 once cnt >= bits (cnt < 64).
                let cf = if cnt <= bits {
                    (a >> (cnt - 1)) & 1 == 1
                } else {
                    false
                };
                (a >> cnt, cf)
            }
            Shift::Arith => {
                let cf = (a >> (cnt - 1).min(bits - 1)) & 1 == 1;
                ((sign_extend(a, size) >> cnt) as u64 & mask(size), cf)
            }
        };
        self.cpu.flags.cf = cf;
        // OF is defined by x86 only for a 1-bit shift; it is left undefined (unchanged) otherwise.
        if cnt == 1 {
            self.cpu.flags.of = match kind {
                Shift::Left => cf ^ (res & sign_bit(size) != 0),
                Shift::Right => a & sign_bit(size) != 0,
                Shift::Arith => false,
            };
        }
        self.set_szp(res, size);
        self.write_op(instr, 0, res, size)
    }

    /// `rol`/`ror`: rotate `op0` by the count in `op1` (masked), setting CF to the bit rotated
    /// out. The rotate amount wraps to the operand width (`cnt % bits`).
    fn rotate(&mut self, instr: &Instruction, size: usize, left: bool) -> Result<(), EmuError> {
        let a = self.read_op(instr, 0, size)? & mask(size);
        let bits = (size * 8) as u32;
        let cnt = (self.read_op(instr, 1, 1)? & 0x3f) as u32 % bits;
        if cnt == 0 {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let res = if left {
            ((a << cnt) | (a >> (bits - cnt))) & mask(size)
        } else {
            ((a >> cnt) | (a << (bits - cnt))) & mask(size)
        };
        // CF = the bit that wrapped around (LSB after rol, MSB after ror).
        self.cpu.flags.cf = if left {
            res & 1 == 1
        } else {
            (res >> (bits - 1)) & 1 == 1
        };
        self.write_op(instr, 0, res, size)
    }

    fn imul(&mut self, instr: &Instruction, size: usize) -> Result<(), EmuError> {
        match instr.op_count() {
            1 => {
                // RDX:RAX = RAX * src (signed)
                let src = sign_extend(self.read_op(instr, 0, size)?, size) as i128;
                let a = sign_extend(self.cpu.reg(acc(size)), size) as i128;
                let full = a * src;
                self.store_wide(full as u128, size);
                let truncated = sign_extend(full as u64, size) as i128;
                self.cpu.flags.cf = full != truncated;
                self.cpu.flags.of = self.cpu.flags.cf;
            }
            2 => {
                let a = sign_extend(self.read_op(instr, 0, size)?, size) as i128;
                let b = sign_extend(self.read_op(instr, 1, size)?, size) as i128;
                let full = a * b;
                self.write_op(instr, 0, full as u64, size)?;
                let truncated = sign_extend(full as u64, size) as i128;
                self.cpu.flags.cf = full != truncated;
                self.cpu.flags.of = self.cpu.flags.cf;
            }
            _ => {
                let a = sign_extend(self.read_op(instr, 1, size)?, size) as i128;
                let b = sign_extend(instr.immediate(2), size) as i128;
                let full = a * b;
                self.write_op(instr, 0, full as u64, size)?;
                let truncated = sign_extend(full as u64, size) as i128;
                self.cpu.flags.cf = full != truncated;
                self.cpu.flags.of = self.cpu.flags.cf;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn mul(&mut self, instr: &Instruction, size: usize) -> Result<(), EmuError> {
        let src = self.read_op(instr, 0, size)? & mask(size);
        let a = self.cpu.reg(acc(size)) & mask(size);
        let full = u128::from(a) * u128::from(src);
        self.store_wide(full, size);
        let hi_nonzero = (full >> (size * 8)) != 0;
        self.cpu.flags.cf = hi_nonzero;
        self.cpu.flags.of = hi_nonzero;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Stores a double-width product into RAX (low) and RDX (high), or AX for byte ops.
    fn store_wide(&mut self, full: u128, size: usize) {
        let m = mask(size) as u128;
        let lo = (full & m) as u64;
        let hi = ((full >> (size * 8)) & m) as u64;
        if size == 1 {
            self.cpu.set_reg(Register::AX, (hi << 8) | lo);
        } else {
            self.cpu.set_reg(acc(size), lo);
            self.cpu.set_reg(hireg(size), hi);
        }
    }

    fn div(&mut self, instr: &Instruction, size: usize, signed: bool) -> Result<(), EmuError> {
        let ip = instr.ip();
        let divisor = self.read_op(instr, 0, size)? & mask(size);
        if divisor == 0 {
            return Err(EmuError::DivideByZero(ip));
        }
        let bits = (size * 8) as u32;
        if size == 1 {
            // 8-bit: dividend is AX (16-bit), quotient -> AL, remainder -> AH.
            let dividend = self.cpu.reg(Register::AX) & 0xffff;
            let (q, r) = if signed {
                let d = dividend as i16 as i32;
                let v = sign_extend(divisor, 1) as i32;
                let q = d.checked_div(v).ok_or(EmuError::DivideOverflow(ip))?;
                if q < i32::from(i8::MIN) || q > i32::from(i8::MAX) {
                    return Err(EmuError::DivideOverflow(ip));
                }
                ((q as u64) & 0xff, (d % v) as u64 & 0xff)
            } else {
                let q = dividend / divisor;
                if q > 0xff {
                    return Err(EmuError::DivideOverflow(ip));
                }
                (q, dividend % divisor)
            };
            self.cpu.set_reg(Register::AL, q);
            self.cpu.set_reg(Register::AH, r);
            return Ok(());
        }
        // 16/32/64-bit: dividend is the double-width hi:lo (DX:AX / EDX:EAX / RDX:RAX).
        let lo = self.cpu.reg(acc(size)) & mask(size);
        let hi = self.cpu.reg(hireg(size)) & mask(size);
        let dividend = (u128::from(hi) << (size * 8)) | u128::from(lo);
        let (q, r) = if signed {
            // The dividend is a signed value of 2*bits width — sign-extend it (not zero-extend,
            // which silently made negative DX:AX / EDX:EAX dividends positive).
            let d = sign_extend128(dividend, bits * 2);
            let v = i128::from(sign_extend(divisor, size));
            // checked_div/rem trap INT_MIN / -1 as #DE instead of panicking.
            let q = d.checked_div(v).ok_or(EmuError::DivideOverflow(ip))?;
            let r = d.checked_rem(v).ok_or(EmuError::DivideOverflow(ip))?;
            let qmin = -(1i128 << (bits - 1));
            let qmax = (1i128 << (bits - 1)) - 1;
            if q < qmin || q > qmax {
                return Err(EmuError::DivideOverflow(ip));
            }
            (q as u128, r as u128)
        } else {
            let v = u128::from(divisor);
            let q = dividend / v;
            if q > u128::from(mask(size)) {
                return Err(EmuError::DivideOverflow(ip));
            }
            (q, dividend % v)
        };
        self.cpu.set_reg(acc(size), (q as u64) & mask(size));
        self.cpu.set_reg(hireg(size), (r as u64) & mask(size));
        Ok(())
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum Shift {
    Left,
    Right,
    Arith,
}

/// The accumulator register of a given width (AL/AX/EAX/RAX).
fn acc(size: usize) -> Register {
    match size {
        1 => Register::AL,
        2 => Register::AX,
        4 => Register::EAX,
        _ => Register::RAX,
    }
}

/// The high register for wide mul/div (DX/EDX/RDX).
fn hireg(size: usize) -> Register {
    match size {
        2 => Register::DX,
        4 => Register::EDX,
        _ => Register::RDX,
    }
}
```
