`crates/orress-emu/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! A small, pure-Rust x86-64 emulator built on iced-x86's decoder.
//!
//! It exists for the reverse-engineering jobs that need to *run* code, not just read it:
//! "run this function with these arguments" (string decryptors, CTF check functions), counting
//! instructions per input for side-channel solving, and single-stepping. It is deliberately
//! dependency-light (only iced-x86) and interprets a pragmatic integer/branch/stack/memory
//! subset — the instructions real crackme check routines use — faulting clearly on anything it
//! does not yet model, so coverage gaps are visible rather than silently wrong.
//!
//! This is the Rust-first counterpart to a Unicorn/QEMU back end: it composes with the rest of
//! ORRESS (no C toolchain) and is the base the side-channel and symbolic solvers build on.

#![allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation)]

mod cpu;
mod exec;
mod mem;
mod solve;
pub mod trace;

pub use cpu::{Cpu, Flags};
pub use mem::Memory;
pub use solve::{MAX_SOLVE_LEN, Solution, SolveStep, solve_by_count};
pub use trace::{Trace, TraceStep};

/// Something the emulator could not do.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum EmuError {
    /// Access to unmapped memory at this address.
    Fault(u64),
    /// The bytes at this address did not decode to a valid instruction.
    InvalidInstruction(u64),
    /// A decoded instruction the interpreter does not model yet.
    Unsupported { addr: u64, mnemonic: String },
    /// Division by zero.
    DivideByZero(u64),
    /// The quotient did not fit the destination (x86 #DE), including INT_MIN / -1.
    DivideOverflow(u64),
}

impl std::fmt::Display for EmuError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Self::Fault(a) => write!(f, "memory fault at {a:#x}"),
            Self::InvalidInstruction(a) => write!(f, "invalid instruction at {a:#x}"),
            Self::Unsupported { addr, mnemonic } => {
                write!(f, "unsupported instruction {mnemonic} at {addr:#x}")
            }
            Self::DivideByZero(a) => write!(f, "divide by zero at {a:#x}"),
            Self::DivideOverflow(a) => write!(f, "divide overflow at {a:#x}"),
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for EmuError {}

/// Why a run stopped.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Stop {
    /// Reached the requested stop address (e.g. a function returned to the sentinel).
    Target(u64),
    /// Hit a set breakpoint.
    Breakpoint(u64),
    /// Ran out of the step budget.
    StepLimit,
}

/// Upper bound on bytes a single libc-stub (malloc/memset/…) will allocate or touch, so a
/// guest-controlled size can't exhaust host memory or spin an effectively unbounded loop.
const STUB_MAX_BYTES: u64 = 256 * 1024 * 1024;

/// A stub that stands in for an imported library function, so calls into code we don't have
/// (libc / WinAPI) return something sensible instead of faulting. Arguments are read from the
/// current ABI's argument registers; the result goes in RAX.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Stub {
    /// Set RAX to a constant and return (the catch-all for unmodelled imports).
    Return(u64),
    /// `strlen(s)`.
    Strlen,
    /// `strcmp(a, b)` → 0 if equal.
    Strcmp,
    /// `strncmp(a, b, n)`.
    Strncmp,
    /// `memcmp(a, b, n)`.
    Memcmp,
    /// `memcpy(dst, src, n)` → dst.
    Memcpy,
    /// `memset(dst, c, n)` → dst.
    Memset,
    /// `strcpy(dst, src)` → dst.
    Strcpy,
    /// `atoi(s)` → parsed decimal integer.
    Atoi,
    /// `malloc(n)` → a fresh zeroed region (bump-allocated).
    Malloc,
}

/// The stub for an imported function, by name (leading underscores ignored): the libc routines a
/// check function typically calls get a real model, everything else returns 0. Shared by every
/// front end that seeds an emulator from a loaded program (see `orress_vm::import_hooks`).
pub fn stub_for(name: &str) -> Stub {
    match name.trim_start_matches('_') {
        "strlen" => Stub::Strlen,
        "strcmp" => Stub::Strcmp,
        "strncmp" => Stub::Strncmp,
        "memcmp" | "bcmp" => Stub::Memcmp,
        "memcpy" | "memmove" => Stub::Memcpy,
        "memset" => Stub::Memset,
        "strcpy" => Stub::Strcpy,
        "atoi" | "strtol" => Stub::Atoi,
        "malloc" | "calloc" => Stub::Malloc,
        _ => Stub::Return(0),
    }
}

/// C `atoi`: skips leading whitespace, takes an optional sign, then the leading decimal digits
/// (`"123abc"` -> 123, `"  -42"` -> -42, `"x1"` -> 0). Overflow wraps rather than panicking.
pub fn parse_atoi(s: &[u8]) -> i64 {
    let mut it = s
        .iter()
        .copied()
        .skip_while(|c| matches!(c, b' ' | b'\t' | b'\n' | b'\r' | 0x0b | 0x0c))
        .peekable();
    let neg = match it.peek() {
        Some(b'-') => {
            it.next();
            true
        }
        Some(b'+') => {
            it.next();
            false
        }
        _ => false,
    };
    let mut v: i64 = 0;
    for c in it.take_while(u8::is_ascii_digit) {
        v = v.wrapping_mul(10).wrapping_add(i64::from(c - b'0'));
    }
    if neg { v.wrapping_neg() } else { v }
}

/// Where [`setup_tls`] places the SysV thread block (`fs_base`).
pub const TLS_BASE: u64 = 0x7ffd_0000_0000;
/// Where [`setup_tls`] places the fake Win64 TEB (`gs_base`).
pub const TEB_BASE: u64 = 0x7ffd_0001_0000;
/// Where [`setup_tls`] places the (zeroed) fake Win64 PEB that `gs:[0x60]` points at.
pub const PEB_BASE: u64 = 0x7ffd_0002_0000;
/// The stack-protector canary stored at `fs:[0x28]` (low byte 0, like glibc's).
pub const STACK_CANARY: u64 = 0x5ca1_ab1e_c0de_7700;

/// Maps a minimal thread environment so segment-relative loads don't fault: a SysV TCB at
/// [`TLS_BASE`] (self-pointer at `fs:0`/`fs:0x10`, canary at `fs:0x28`) and a Win64 TEB at
/// [`TEB_BASE`] (self-pointer at `gs:0x30`, PEB pointer at `gs:0x60`). Returns `(fs_base, gs_base)`.
/// Used by [`Emulator::setup_stack`] and by the symbolic executor.
pub fn setup_tls(mem: &mut Memory) -> (u64, u64) {
    mem.map_zeroed(TLS_BASE, 0x1000);
    mem.map_zeroed(TEB_BASE, 0x2000);
    mem.map_zeroed(PEB_BASE, 0x1000);
    // Every page was just mapped, so these writes cannot fault.
    let _ = mem.write(TLS_BASE, TLS_BASE, 8);
    let _ = mem.write(TLS_BASE + 0x10, TLS_BASE, 8);
    let _ = mem.write(TLS_BASE + 0x28, STACK_CANARY, 8);
    let _ = mem.write(TEB_BASE + 0x30, TEB_BASE, 8);
    let _ = mem.write(TEB_BASE + 0x60, PEB_BASE, 8);
    (TLS_BASE, TEB_BASE)
}

/// Calling convention for [`Emulator::call`].
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Abi {
    /// Windows x64: rcx, rdx, r8, r9.
    Win64,
    /// System V (Linux/macOS): rdi, rsi, rdx, rcx, r8, r9.
    SysV,
}

/// C-style comparison result (0 equal, 1 / -1 as u64) for strcmp/memcmp stubs.
fn cmp_result(a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> u64 {
    match a.cmp(b) {
        std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => 0,
        std::cmp::Ordering::Less => (-1i64) as u64,
        std::cmp::Ordering::Greater => 1,
    }
}

impl Abi {
    /// The register carrying integer/pointer argument `i` (0-based), or `None` past the
    /// register-argument count (the rest would come from the stack).
    pub fn arg_reg(self, i: usize) -> Option<iced_x86::Register> {
        use iced_x86::Register::*;
        let regs: &[iced_x86::Register] = match self {
            Self::Win64 => &[RCX, RDX, R8, R9],
            Self::SysV => &[RDI, RSI, RDX, RCX, R8, R9],
        };
        regs.get(i).copied()
    }

    /// How many integer arguments travel in registers.
    pub fn reg_arg_count(self) -> usize {
        match self {
            Self::Win64 => 4,
            Self::SysV => 6,
        }
    }

    /// Bytes the caller reserves above the return address before the stack arguments (Win64's
    /// 32-byte home/shadow space; none for System V).
    pub fn shadow_space(self) -> u64 {
        match self {
            Self::Win64 => 32,
            Self::SysV => 0,
        }
    }
}

/// The address a called function "returns to"; the run stops when RIP reaches it.
const SENTINEL: u64 = 0x1337_0000_0000_0000;
/// Where [`Emulator::setup_stack`] puts the stack top by default.
const DEFAULT_STACK_TOP: u64 = 0x7fff_0000_0000;
const DEFAULT_STACK_SIZE: u64 = 0x10_0000; // 1 MiB

/// The emulator: a CPU, its memory, and a running instruction count.
pub struct Emulator {
    pub cpu: Cpu,
    pub mem: Memory,
    /// Total instructions executed since the last reset (the side-channel signal).
    pub steps: u64,
    /// Addresses to stop at before executing.
    pub breakpoints: Vec<u64>,
    /// The per-run step budget, to bound runaway loops.
    pub budget: u64,
    /// The ABI the current run uses (how stubs read their arguments).
    pub abi: Abi,
    /// Import stubs, keyed by the address a call to that import lands on.
    pub hooks: std::collections::HashMap<u64, Stub>,
    /// The next address `malloc` hands out (a simple bump allocator).
    heap: u64,
}

impl Default for Emulator {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl Emulator {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            cpu: Cpu::new(),
            mem: Memory::new(),
            steps: 0,
            breakpoints: Vec::new(),
            budget: 10_000_000,
            abi: Abi::SysV,
            hooks: std::collections::HashMap::new(),
            heap: 0x2000_0000,
        }
    }

    /// Registers an import stub at `addr` (the address a call to that import reaches).
    pub fn hook(&mut self, addr: u64, stub: Stub) {
        self.hooks.insert(addr, stub);
    }

    /// Reads a NUL-terminated string from guest memory (bounded), for stubs and results.
    pub fn read_cstr(&self, addr: u64, max: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        for i in 0..max as u64 {
            match self.mem.read_u8(addr.wrapping_add(i)) {
                Ok(0) | Err(_) => break,
                Ok(b) => out.push(b),
            }
        }
        out
    }

    fn arg(&self, i: usize) -> u64 {
        self.abi.arg_reg(i).map(|r| self.cpu.reg(r)).unwrap_or(0)
    }

    /// Applies an import stub: reads arguments, computes the result into RAX, and returns to
    /// the caller (popping the return address the `call` pushed).
    pub(crate) fn apply_stub(&mut self, stub: &Stub) -> Result<(), EmuError> {
        let result = match stub {
            Stub::Return(v) => *v,
            Stub::Strlen => self.read_cstr(self.arg(0), 1 << 20).len() as u64,
            Stub::Strcmp => {
                let a = self.read_cstr(self.arg(0), 1 << 20);
                let b = self.read_cstr(self.arg(1), 1 << 20);
                cmp_result(&a, &b)
            }
            Stub::Strncmp => {
                let n = self.arg(2) as usize;
                let a = self.read_cstr(self.arg(0), n);
                let b = self.read_cstr(self.arg(1), n);
                cmp_result(&a, &b)
            }
            Stub::Memcmp => {
                let n = self.arg(2) as usize;
                let a = self.mem.read_vec(self.arg(0), n)?;
                let b = self.mem.read_vec(self.arg(1), n)?;
                cmp_result(&a, &b)
            }
            Stub::Memcpy => {
                let (dst, src, n) = (self.arg(0), self.arg(1), self.arg(2) as usize);
                let bytes = self.mem.read_vec(src, n)?;
                self.mem.write_slice(dst, &bytes)?;
                dst
            }
            Stub::Memset => {
                // Cap the guest-controlled length so a bogus size can't spin a multi-GB loop.
                let (dst, c, n) = (
                    self.arg(0),
                    self.arg(1) as u8,
                    self.arg(2).min(STUB_MAX_BYTES),
                );
                for i in 0..n {
                    self.mem.write_u8(dst.wrapping_add(i), c)?;
                }
                dst
            }
            Stub::Strcpy => {
                let (dst, src) = (self.arg(0), self.arg(1));
                let bytes = self.read_cstr(src, 1 << 20);
                self.mem.write_slice(dst, &bytes)?;
                // wrapping_add: dst + len can overflow u64 (debug panic) for a wild pointer.
                self.mem.write_u8(dst.wrapping_add(bytes.len() as u64), 0)?;
                dst
            }
            Stub::Atoi => {
                let s = self.read_cstr(self.arg(0), 64);
                parse_atoi(&s) as u64
            }
            Stub::Malloc => {
                // Cap the request and use saturating math so a huge/overflowing size can't OOM
                // or panic; real crackme allocations are tiny.
                let size = self.arg(0).clamp(1, STUB_MAX_BYTES);
                let addr = self.heap;
                self.heap = self.heap.saturating_add(size).saturating_add(15) & !15;
                self.mem.map_zeroed(addr, size);
                addr
            }
        };
        let ret = self.pop_ret()?;
        self.cpu.regs[0] = result; // RAX
        self.cpu.rip = ret;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Pops the return address (used by stubs; mirrors a `ret`).
    fn pop_ret(&mut self) -> Result<u64, EmuError> {
        let sp = self.cpu.rsp();
        let v = self.mem.read(sp, 8)?;
        self.cpu.set_rsp(sp.wrapping_add(8));
        Ok(v)
    }

    /// Loads code or data bytes at `addr`.
    pub fn map(&mut self, addr: u64, bytes: &[u8]) {
        self.mem.write_bytes(addr, bytes);
    }

    /// Reserves a zero-filled stack and points RSP near its top (16-byte aligned, with some
    /// headroom so a prologue's `sub rsp` / pushes stay in bounds). Also maps the thread
    /// environment ([`setup_tls`]) and points FS/GS at it, unless a base was already set.
    /// Returns the stack top.
    pub fn setup_stack(&mut self) -> u64 {
        let top = DEFAULT_STACK_TOP;
        self.mem
            .map_zeroed(top - DEFAULT_STACK_SIZE, DEFAULT_STACK_SIZE);
        let sp = (top - 0x100) & !0xf;
        self.cpu.set_rsp(sp);
        if self.cpu.fs_base == 0 && self.cpu.gs_base == 0 {
            let (fs, gs) = setup_tls(&mut self.mem);
            self.cpu.fs_base = fs;
            self.cpu.gs_base = gs;
        }
        top
    }

    /// Executes one instruction at RIP.
    pub fn step(&mut self) -> Result<(), EmuError> {
        let ip = self.cpu.rip;
        let mut buf = [0u8; 16];
        let mut n = 0;
        while n < 16 {
            match self.mem.read_u8(ip.wrapping_add(n as u64)) {
                Ok(b) => {
                    buf[n] = b;
                    n += 1;
                }
                Err(_) => break,
            }
        }
        if n == 0 {
            return Err(EmuError::Fault(ip));
        }
        let mut dec = iced_x86::Decoder::with_ip(64, &buf[..n], ip, iced_x86::DecoderOptions::NONE);
        let instr = dec.decode();
        if instr.is_invalid() {
            return Err(EmuError::InvalidInstruction(ip));
        }
        self.cpu.rip = instr.next_ip();
        self.steps += 1;
        self.exec(&instr)
    }

    /// Runs until RIP reaches `stop` (if given), a breakpoint, or the step budget.
    pub fn run_until(&mut self, stop: Option<u64>) -> Result<Stop, EmuError> {
        for _ in 0..self.budget {
            let ip = self.cpu.rip;
            if Some(ip) == stop {
                return Ok(Stop::Target(ip));
            }
            if self.breakpoints.contains(&ip) {
                return Ok(Stop::Breakpoint(ip));
            }
            if let Some(stub) = self.hooks.get(&ip).cloned() {
                self.apply_stub(&stub)?;
                self.steps += 1;
                continue;
            }
            self.step()?;
        }
        Ok(Stop::StepLimit)
    }

    /// Calls `func` with `args`, returning the value in RAX. Sets up the stack if RSP is 0,
    /// passes the arguments per `abi` (registers first, the rest on the stack), pushes a sentinel
    /// return address, and runs until the function returns to it.
    pub fn call(&mut self, func: u64, args: &[u64], abi: Abi) -> Result<u64, EmuError> {
        self.prepare_call(func, args, abi)?;
        self.run_until(Some(SENTINEL))?;
        Ok(self.cpu.rax())
    }

    /// The common call setup: ABI, stack, argument registers, stack arguments, the sentinel
    /// return address, and RIP.
    ///
    /// Stack layout at entry (RSP = 8 mod 16, as after a real `call`): `[rsp]` = return address,
    /// then (Win64 only) the 32-byte shadow space, then the stack arguments in ascending addresses.
    fn prepare_call(&mut self, func: u64, args: &[u64], abi: Abi) -> Result<(), EmuError> {
        self.abi = abi;
        if self.cpu.rsp() == 0 {
            self.setup_stack();
        }
        let nregs = abi.reg_arg_count();
        for (i, &a) in args.iter().take(nregs).enumerate() {
            if let Some(r) = abi.arg_reg(i) {
                self.cpu.set_reg(r, a);
            }
        }
        let extra = args.get(nregs..).unwrap_or(&[]);
        // The argument area (shadow space + stack args), kept a multiple of 16 so the callee sees
        // the ABI's entry alignment.
        let area = (abi.shadow_space() + 8 * extra.len() as u64 + 15) & !15;
        let base = (self.cpu.rsp() & !0xf).wrapping_sub(area);
        for (i, &a) in extra.iter().enumerate() {
            let slot = base
                .wrapping_add(abi.shadow_space())
                .wrapping_add(8 * i as u64);
            self.mem.write(slot, a, 8)?;
        }
        // Push the sentinel return address.
        let sp = base.wrapping_sub(8);
        self.mem.write(sp, SENTINEL, 8)?;
        self.cpu.set_rsp(sp);
        self.cpu.rip = func;
        self.steps = 0;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Runs from the current state like [`Emulator::run_until`], but records a per-instruction CPU
    /// snapshot for time-travel debugging (bounded by `max_steps`). See [`trace::Trace`].
    ///
    /// A fault is returned as an error and the recorded steps are dropped; prefer
    /// [`Emulator::record_with_fault`], which keeps them.
    pub fn record(
        &mut self,
        stop: Option<u64>,
        max_steps: usize,
    ) -> Result<trace::Trace, EmuError> {
        let t = self.record_with_fault(stop, max_steps);
        match t.fault {
            Some(e) => Err(e),
            None => Ok(t),
        }
    }

    /// Like [`Emulator::record`], but never discards the recording: if a step faults, the
    /// returned trace holds every step executed before it and the error in [`trace::Trace::fault`].
    pub fn record_with_fault(&mut self, stop: Option<u64>, max_steps: usize) -> trace::Trace {
        let initial = self.cpu.clone();
        let mut steps = Vec::new();
        let mut outcome = Stop::StepLimit;
        let mut fault = None;
        for _ in 0..max_steps {
            let ip = self.cpu.rip;
            if Some(ip) == stop {
                outcome = Stop::Target(ip);
                break;
            }
            if self.breakpoints.contains(&ip) {
                outcome = Stop::Breakpoint(ip);
                break;
            }
            let r = if let Some(stub) = self.hooks.get(&ip).cloned() {
                self.apply_stub(&stub).map(|()| self.steps += 1)
            } else {
                self.step()
            };
            if let Err(e) = r {
                fault = Some(e);
                break;
            }
            steps.push(trace::TraceStep {
                addr: ip,
                cpu: self.cpu.clone(),
            });
        }
        trace::Trace {
            initial,
            steps,
            stop: outcome,
            fault,
        }
    }

    /// Calls `func` like [`Emulator::call`] but records the whole execution as a [`trace::Trace`].
    /// A fault is an error (the steps are dropped); see [`Emulator::record_call_with_fault`].
    pub fn record_call(
        &mut self,
        func: u64,
        args: &[u64],
        abi: Abi,
        max_steps: usize,
    ) -> Result<trace::Trace, EmuError> {
        self.prepare_call(func, args, abi)?;
        self.record(Some(SENTINEL), max_steps)
    }

    /// Calls `func` like [`Emulator::record_call`], keeping the recorded steps when the run
    /// faults (the error is in [`trace::Trace::fault`]). `Err` only if the call could not be set
    /// up at all (e.g. the stack is unmapped).
    pub fn record_call_with_fault(
        &mut self,
        func: u64,
        args: &[u64],
        abi: Abi,
        max_steps: usize,
    ) -> Result<trace::Trace, EmuError> {
        self.prepare_call(func, args, abi)?;
        Ok(self.record_with_fault(Some(SENTINEL), max_steps))
    }
}

`crates/orress-emu/src/mem.rs`:

```rs
//! Sparse paged guest memory. Pages are allocated only by the *loader* paths
//! ([`Memory::write_bytes`] / [`Memory::map_zeroed`]); guest reads and writes
//! ([`Memory::read`] / [`Memory::write`] / [`Memory::write_u8`] / [`Memory::write_slice`]) are
//! little-endian, may cross page boundaries, and fault on an unmapped page — so a null or wild
//! pointer write is caught instead of silently allocating (a striding write loop could otherwise
//! allocate gigabytes of host memory).

use std::collections::HashMap;

use crate::EmuError;

const PAGE_BITS: u64 = 12;
const PAGE_SIZE: usize = 1 << PAGE_BITS;
const PAGE_MASK: u64 = (PAGE_SIZE as u64) - 1;

/// Sparse guest address space, one 4 KiB page at a time.
#[derive(Default, Clone)]
pub struct Memory {
    pages: HashMap<u64, Box<[u8; PAGE_SIZE]>>,
}

impl Memory {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    fn page_mut(&mut self, page: u64) -> &mut [u8; PAGE_SIZE] {
        self.pages
            .entry(page)
            .or_insert_with(|| Box::new([0u8; PAGE_SIZE]))
    }

    /// Maps `bytes` at `addr`, allocating pages as needed (used to load code/data/stack).
    pub fn write_bytes(&mut self, addr: u64, bytes: &[u8]) {
        for (i, &b) in bytes.iter().enumerate() {
            let a = addr.wrapping_add(i as u64);
            self.page_mut(a >> PAGE_BITS)[(a & PAGE_MASK) as usize] = b;
        }
    }

    /// Reserves a zero-filled region (e.g. a stack), so reads there don't fault.
    pub fn map_zeroed(&mut self, addr: u64, len: u64) {
        let first = addr >> PAGE_BITS;
        let last = (addr.wrapping_add(len.saturating_sub(1))) >> PAGE_BITS;
        for page in first..=last {
            self.page_mut(page);
        }
    }

    /// Whether `addr` is in an allocated page.
    pub fn is_mapped(&self, addr: u64) -> bool {
        self.pages.contains_key(&(addr >> PAGE_BITS))
    }

    pub fn read_u8(&self, addr: u64) -> Result<u8, EmuError> {
        self.pages
            .get(&(addr >> PAGE_BITS))
            .map(|p| p[(addr & PAGE_MASK) as usize])
            .ok_or(EmuError::Fault(addr))
    }

    /// Guest write of one byte; faults on an unmapped page (it never allocates).
    pub fn write_u8(&mut self, addr: u64, val: u8) -> Result<(), EmuError> {
        let page = self
            .pages
            .get_mut(&(addr >> PAGE_BITS))
            .ok_or(EmuError::Fault(addr))?;
        page[(addr & PAGE_MASK) as usize] = val;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Guest write of a byte slice (e.g. a `memcpy` stub). All-or-nothing: if any byte falls on
    /// an unmapped page it faults at the first such address and writes nothing.
    pub fn write_slice(&mut self, addr: u64, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), EmuError> {
        if let Some(bad) = (0..bytes.len() as u64)
            .map(|i| addr.wrapping_add(i))
            .find(|&a| !self.is_mapped(a))
        {
            return Err(EmuError::Fault(bad));
        }
        for (i, &b) in bytes.iter().enumerate() {
            self.write_u8(addr.wrapping_add(i as u64), b)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Reads a little-endian value of `size` (1/2/4/8) bytes.
    pub fn read(&self, addr: u64, size: usize) -> Result<u64, EmuError> {
        let mut val: u64 = 0;
        for i in 0..size as u64 {
            val |= u64::from(self.read_u8(addr.wrapping_add(i))?) << (8 * i);
        }
        Ok(val)
    }

    /// Writes the low `size` (1/2/4/8) bytes of `val`, little-endian.
    /// Faults (writing nothing) if any byte is unmapped.
    pub fn write(&mut self, addr: u64, val: u64, size: usize) -> Result<(), EmuError> {
        if let Some(bad) = (0..size as u64)
            .map(|i| addr.wrapping_add(i))
            .find(|&a| !self.is_mapped(a))
        {
            return Err(EmuError::Fault(bad));
        }
        for i in 0..size as u64 {
            self.write_u8(addr.wrapping_add(i), (val >> (8 * i)) as u8)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Reads `len` bytes into a `Vec` (for pulling a result buffer back out after a run).
    pub fn read_vec(&self, addr: u64, len: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>, EmuError> {
        (0..len as u64)
            .map(|i| self.read_u8(addr.wrapping_add(i)))
            .collect()
    }
}

`crates/orress-emu/src/solve.rs`:

```rs
//! The instruction-counting side-channel solver.
//!
//! Many check routines bail out on the first wrong input byte, so a correct byte makes the
//! routine run *further* before failing. By emulating a candidate input and counting executed
//! instructions, the correct byte at each position is the one that maximises the count — so a
//! flag can be recovered one byte at a time without ever satisfying the final check. This is
//! the classic CTF "instruction counting" trick, and it is why the emulator tracks `steps`.

/// A step recorded during a solve, for the step-by-step explanation the UI shows learners.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct SolveStep {
    /// The position being recovered.
    pub index: usize,
    /// The byte chosen for this position.
    pub byte: u8,
    /// Its instruction count (the winning, highest count).
    pub count: u64,
    /// The runner-up count, so the UI can show how clear the signal was.
    pub runner_up: u64,
}

/// The result of a side-channel solve.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Solution {
    pub input: Vec<u8>,
    pub steps: Vec<SolveStep>,
}

/// Longest input [`solve_by_count`] recovers; longer requests are clamped to this, so a typo
/// in a length field cannot allocate gigabytes or run for days.
pub const MAX_SOLVE_LEN: usize = 0x1_0000;

/// Recovers `len` input bytes by maximising executed instructions per position.
/// `len` is clamped to [`MAX_SOLVE_LEN`].
///
/// `trial(input)` runs the check routine against `input` and returns the number of
/// instructions executed; `candidates` are the byte values to try at each position (e.g.
/// printable ASCII). The recovered prefix is fixed as the search moves right.
pub fn solve_by_count<F>(len: usize, candidates: &[u8], mut trial: F) -> Solution
where
    F: FnMut(&[u8]) -> u64,
{
    let len = len.min(MAX_SOLVE_LEN);
    let mut input = vec![0u8; len];
    let mut steps = Vec::with_capacity(len);
    for index in 0..len {
        let mut best_byte = candidates.first().copied().unwrap_or(0);
        let mut best = 0u64;
        let mut runner_up = 0u64;
        for &c in candidates {
            input[index] = c;
            let count = trial(&input);
            if count > best {
                runner_up = best;
                best = count;
                best_byte = c;
            } else if count > runner_up {
                runner_up = count;
            }
        }
        input[index] = best_byte;
        steps.push(SolveStep {
            index,
            byte: best_byte,
            count: best,
            runner_up,
        });
    }
    Solution { input, steps }
}

`crates/orress-emu/src/trace.rs`:

```rs
//! Time-travel debugging (M14): a recorded execution trace you can scrub backward and forward.
//!
//! The emulator is deterministic, so instead of a heavyweight record/replay engine we capture a
//! lightweight per-instruction snapshot of the CPU (registers + flags + the address executed). The
//! UI (or a test) can then jump to any step, watch a register's value evolve, and find exactly
//! where it changed — the core time-travel experience. (Memory rewind is not recorded; it can be
//! reconstructed by deterministic replay from the start, a later extension.)

use crate::cpu::Cpu;
use crate::{EmuError, Stop};

/// One executed instruction: the address it was at, and the CPU state immediately after it ran.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct TraceStep {
    pub addr: u64,
    pub cpu: Cpu,
}

/// A full recorded run, navigable in both directions.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Trace {
    /// The CPU state before the first instruction (step index "before 0").
    pub initial: Cpu,
    pub steps: Vec<TraceStep>,
    /// Why recording stopped. When `fault` is set this is [`Stop::StepLimit`] (the run neither
    /// reached its stop address nor a breakpoint).
    pub stop: Stop,
    /// The error that ended the run early, if any (memory fault, unsupported instruction, ...).
    /// The steps recorded up to the fault are kept, so the UI can scrub to the faulting point.
    pub fault: Option<EmuError>,
}

impl Trace {
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.steps.len()
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.steps.is_empty()
    }

    /// The address of the instruction executed at step `i`.
    pub fn addr_at(&self, i: usize) -> Option<u64> {
        self.steps.get(i).map(|s| s.addr)
    }

    /// The CPU state after step `i`, or the initial state when `i` is out of range below 0 — call
    /// with `i` in `0..len()`.
    pub fn cpu_at(&self, i: usize) -> &Cpu {
        self.steps.get(i).map_or(&self.initial, |s| &s.cpu)
    }

    /// The general-purpose registers whose value changed at step `i` (vs. the previous state), as
    /// (register index 0..16, new value) — for highlighting in the UI.
    pub fn changed_regs(&self, i: usize) -> Vec<(usize, u64)> {
        let prev = if i == 0 {
            &self.initial
        } else {
            self.cpu_at(i - 1)
        };
        let Some(cur) = self.steps.get(i).map(|s| &s.cpu) else {
            return Vec::new();
        };
        (0..16)
            .filter(|&r| prev.regs[r] != cur.regs[r])
            .map(|r| (r, cur.regs[r]))
            .collect()
    }

    /// The first step at which general-purpose register `reg` (0..16) holds `value`, if any — the
    /// "when did this register become X?" query.
    pub fn first_step_with(&self, reg: usize, value: u64) -> Option<usize> {
        self.steps
            .iter()
            .position(|s| s.cpu.regs.get(reg) == Some(&value))
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use crate::{Abi, Emulator, Stop};

    #[test]
    fn records_a_navigable_trace() {
        let mut emu = Emulator::new();
        // mov eax, 5 ; add eax, 3 ; ret
        emu.map(
            0x1000,
            &[0xB8, 0x05, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x83, 0xC0, 0x03, 0xC3],
        );
        let t = emu.record_call(0x1000, &[], Abi::SysV, 100).unwrap();

        assert!(
            matches!(t.stop, Stop::Target(_)),
            "function returned to the sentinel"
        );
        assert_eq!(t.len(), 3); // mov, add, ret
        assert_eq!(t.addr_at(0), Some(0x1000));
        assert_eq!(t.addr_at(1), Some(0x1005));
        assert_eq!(t.cpu_at(0).regs[0], 5); // rax after `mov eax, 5`
        assert_eq!(t.cpu_at(1).regs[0], 8); // rax after `add eax, 3`
        // Scrub: the register that changed at step 0 is rax -> 5.
        assert_eq!(t.changed_regs(0), vec![(0, 5)]);
        // "When did rax become 8?" -> step 1.
        assert_eq!(t.first_step_with(0, 8), Some(1));
        assert_eq!(t.fault, None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_fault_keeps_the_recorded_steps() {
        let mut emu = Emulator::new();
        // mov eax, 5 ; add eax, 3 ; mov [0], eax (null write faults) ; ret
        emu.map(
            0x1000,
            &[
                0xB8, 0x05, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x83, 0xC0, 0x03, 0x89, 0x04, 0x25, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
                0x00, 0xC3,
            ],
        );
        let t = emu
            .record_call_with_fault(0x1000, &[], Abi::SysV, 100)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(t.fault, Some(crate::EmuError::Fault(0)));
        assert_eq!(t.len(), 2, "the two steps before the fault survive");
        assert_eq!(t.cpu_at(1).regs[0], 8);
        // The legacy API still reports the fault as an error.
        let mut emu2 = Emulator::new();
        emu2.map(0x1000, &[0x89, 0x04, 0x25, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xC3]);
        assert_eq!(
            emu2.record_call(0x1000, &[], Abi::SysV, 100).unwrap_err(),
            crate::EmuError::Fault(0)
        );
    }
}

`crates/orress-emu/tests/emu.rs`:

```rs
//! End-to-end emulator tests. Each test assembles a real function with iced-x86's assembler,
//! loads it, and runs it through the emulator — exercising the operand, flag and control-flow
//! paths the interpreter implements.

use iced_x86::code_asm::*;
use orress_emu::{Abi, Emulator, Stub};

/// Assembles `build` at `ip` and returns the machine code.
fn asm(ip: u64, build: impl FnOnce(&mut CodeAssembler)) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut a = CodeAssembler::new(64).unwrap();
    build(&mut a);
    a.assemble(ip).unwrap()
}

#[test]
fn adds_two_arguments() {
    // fn add(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 { a + b }
    let code = asm(0x1000, |a| {
        a.mov(eax, edi).unwrap();
        a.add(eax, esi).unwrap();
        a.ret().unwrap();
    });
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.map(0x1000, &code);
    assert_eq!(emu.call(0x1000, &[3, 4], Abi::SysV).unwrap(), 7);
    assert_eq!(emu.call(0x1000, &[100, 23], Abi::SysV).unwrap(), 123);
}

#[test]
fn sums_a_loop() {
    // fn sum(n: u32) -> u32 { let mut s = 0; while n > 0 { s += n; n -= 1; } s }
    let code = asm(0x2000, |a| {
        let mut loop_l = a.create_label();
        let mut done_l = a.create_label();
        a.xor(eax, eax).unwrap();
        a.set_label(&mut loop_l).unwrap();
        a.test(edi, edi).unwrap();
        a.jz(done_l).unwrap();
        a.add(eax, edi).unwrap();
        a.dec(edi).unwrap();
        a.jmp(loop_l).unwrap();
        a.set_label(&mut done_l).unwrap();
        a.ret().unwrap();
    });
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.map(0x2000, &code);
    assert_eq!(emu.call(0x2000, &[10], Abi::SysV).unwrap(), 55);
    assert_eq!(emu.call(0x2000, &[100], Abi::SysV).unwrap(), 5050);
}

#[test]
fn xor_decrypts_a_buffer_in_memory() {
    // fn xor(ptr: *mut u8, len: usize, key: u8) { for i in 0..len { ptr[i] ^= key; } }
    let code = asm(0x3000, |a| {
        let mut loop_l = a.create_label();
        let mut done_l = a.create_label();
        a.xor(ecx, ecx).unwrap(); // i = 0
        a.set_label(&mut loop_l).unwrap();
        a.cmp(rcx, rsi).unwrap();
        a.jae(done_l).unwrap();
        a.mov(al, byte_ptr(rdi + rcx)).unwrap();
        a.xor(al, dl).unwrap();
        a.mov(byte_ptr(rdi + rcx), al).unwrap();
        a.inc(rcx).unwrap();
        a.jmp(loop_l).unwrap();
        a.set_label(&mut done_l).unwrap();
        a.ret().unwrap();
    });
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.map(0x3000, &code);
    let buf = 0x5000;
    let data = b"Secret message";
    emu.map(buf, data);
    let key = 0x42u64;
    emu.call(0x3000, &[buf, data.len() as u64, key], Abi::SysV)
        .unwrap();
    let out = emu.mem.read_vec(buf, data.len()).unwrap();
    let expected: Vec<u8> = data.iter().map(|b| b ^ 0x42).collect();
    assert_eq!(out, expected);
    // And it round-trips: xor again restores the plaintext.
    emu.call(0x3000, &[buf, data.len() as u64, key], Abi::SysV)
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(emu.mem.read_vec(buf, data.len()).unwrap(), data);
}

#[test]
fn check_function_returns_bool() {
    // fn check(c: u8) -> bool { c == b'A' }
    let code = asm(0x4000, |a| {
        a.cmp(dil, 0x41).unwrap();
        a.sete(al).unwrap();
        a.movzx(eax, al).unwrap();
        a.ret().unwrap();
    });
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.map(0x4000, &code);
    assert_eq!(emu.call(0x4000, &[u64::from(b'A')], Abi::SysV).unwrap(), 1);
    assert_eq!(emu.call(0x4000, &[u64::from(b'B')], Abi::SysV).unwrap(), 0);
}

#[test]
fn instruction_count_is_the_side_channel_signal() {
    // The sum loop runs more instructions for larger n — the signal a side-channel solver reads.
    let code = asm(0x2000, |a| {
        let mut loop_l = a.create_label();
        let mut done_l = a.create_label();
        a.xor(eax, eax).unwrap();
        a.set_label(&mut loop_l).unwrap();
        a.test(edi, edi).unwrap();
        a.jz(done_l).unwrap();
        a.add(eax, edi).unwrap();
        a.dec(edi).unwrap();
        a.jmp(loop_l).unwrap();
        a.set_label(&mut done_l).unwrap();
        a.ret().unwrap();
    });
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.map(0x2000, &code);
    emu.call(0x2000, &[5], Abi::SysV).unwrap();
    let five = emu.steps;
    emu.call(0x2000, &[20], Abi::SysV).unwrap();
    let twenty = emu.steps;
    assert!(twenty > five, "more iterations => more instructions");
}

#[test]
fn signed_multiply_and_negative_args() {
    // fn mul(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { a * b }
    let code = asm(0x6000, |a| {
        a.mov(rax, rdi).unwrap();
        a.imul_2(rax, rsi).unwrap();
        a.ret().unwrap();
    });
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.map(0x6000, &code);
    let r = emu.call(0x6000, &[6, 7], Abi::SysV).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(r, 42);
    // -3 * 4 = -12 (two's complement)
    let neg3 = (-3i64) as u64;
    let r = emu.call(0x6000, &[neg3, 4], Abi::SysV).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(r as i64, -12);
}

#[test]
fn calls_a_stubbed_import() {
    // fn check(s: *const u8) -> bool { strcmp(s, SECRET) == 0 }
    const SECRET_ADDR: u64 = 0xb000;
    const STRCMP: u64 = 0xa000;
    let code = asm(0x8000, |a| {
        a.mov(rsi, SECRET_ADDR).unwrap(); // arg1 = secret
        a.call(STRCMP).unwrap(); // arg0 = rdi (the input, already in place)
        a.test(rax, rax).unwrap();
        a.sete(al).unwrap();
        a.movzx(eax, al).unwrap();
        a.ret().unwrap();
    });
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.map(0x8000, &code);
    emu.hook(STRCMP, Stub::Strcmp);
    emu.map(SECRET_ADDR, b"hunter2\0");
    emu.map(0xc000, b"hunter2\0");
    emu.map(0xd000, b"wrong\0");
    assert_eq!(emu.call(0x8000, &[0xc000], Abi::SysV).unwrap(), 1);
    assert_eq!(emu.call(0x8000, &[0xd000], Abi::SysV).unwrap(), 0);
}

#[test]
fn win64_abi_uses_rcx_rdx() {
    let code = asm(0x7000, |a| {
        // Win64: arg0=rcx, arg1=rdx
        a.mov(rax, rcx).unwrap();
        a.add(rax, rdx).unwrap();
        a.ret().unwrap();
    });
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.map(0x7000, &code);
    assert_eq!(emu.call(0x7000, &[40, 2], Abi::Win64).unwrap(), 42);
}

// --- QA regression tests (flags, shift/div edge cases) --------------------

use orress_emu::EmuError;

/// `shl al, 10`: the masked count (10) exceeds the 8-bit width. Must not panic (it did:
/// `bits - cnt` underflowed) and the result is 0.
#[test]
fn shl_count_over_width_does_not_panic() {
    let code = asm(0x1000, |a| {
        a.mov(eax, edi).unwrap();
        a.shl(al, 10i32).unwrap();
        a.movzx(eax, al).unwrap();
        a.ret().unwrap();
    });
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.map(0x1000, &code);
    assert_eq!(emu.call(0x1000, &[0xff], Abi::SysV).unwrap(), 0);
}

/// `shl eax, 32`: x86 masks the count for 32-bit operands to 5 bits, so 32 & 0x1f == 0 (a no-op).
/// The old code masked to 0x3f and shifted by 32, zeroing eax.
#[test]
fn shl_eax_by_32_is_a_noop() {
    let code = asm(0x1100, |a| {
        a.mov(eax, edi).unwrap();
        a.shl(eax, 32i32).unwrap();
        a.ret().unwrap();
    });
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.map(0x1100, &code);
    assert_eq!(
        emu.call(0x1100, &[0x1234_5678], Abi::SysV).unwrap(),
        0x1234_5678
    );
}

/// 64-bit `idiv` of INT_MIN by -1 must trap as #DE (DivideOverflow), not panic on i128 overflow.
#[test]
fn idiv_int_min_by_neg_one_traps() {
    let code = asm(0x1200, |a| {
        a.mov(rdx, 0x8000_0000_0000_0000u64).unwrap(); // dividend high
        a.xor(rax, rax).unwrap(); // dividend low -> rdx:rax = 2^127
        a.mov(rcx, rdi).unwrap(); // divisor = arg0 (-1)
        a.idiv(rcx).unwrap();
        a.ret().unwrap();
    });
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.map(0x1200, &code);
    assert!(matches!(
        emu.call(0x1200, &[u64::MAX], Abi::SysV),
        Err(EmuError::DivideOverflow(_))
    ));
}

/// 16-bit `div` whose quotient doesn't fit AX must raise #DE, not silently truncate.
#[test]
fn div_quotient_overflow_traps() {
    let code = asm(0x1300, |a| {
        a.mov(edx, 1u32).unwrap(); // dx = 1
        a.xor(eax, eax).unwrap(); // ax = 0 -> dx:ax = 0x1_0000
        a.mov(ebx, 1u32).unwrap(); // bx = 1
        a.div(bx).unwrap(); // quotient 0x10000 doesn't fit AX
        a.ret().unwrap();
    });
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.map(0x1300, &code);
    assert!(matches!(
        emu.call(0x1300, &[], Abi::SysV),
        Err(EmuError::DivideOverflow(_))
    ));
}

/// 32-bit signed `idiv` with a negative dividend (-8 / 2 = -4). The old code treated the
/// EDX:EAX dividend as unsigned, giving a huge positive quotient.
#[test]
fn idiv_negative_dividend_32bit() {
    let code = asm(0x1400, |a| {
        a.mov(eax, edi).unwrap(); // eax = arg0 (-8)
        a.cdq().unwrap(); // sign-extend into edx
        a.mov(ecx, 2u32).unwrap();
        a.idiv(ecx).unwrap();
        a.ret().unwrap();
    });
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.map(0x1400, &code);
    // arg0 = -8 as a 32-bit value; result is -4 = 0xFFFF_FFFC (upper 32 of rax zeroed).
    assert_eq!(
        emu.call(0x1400, &[0xFFFF_FFF8], Abi::SysV).unwrap(),
        0xFFFF_FFFC
    );
}

/// ADC 0x7f + 0x7f with CF=0 overflows signed -> OF=1. The old chained-add set OF from the
/// second (+carry) micro-op, yielding OF=0.
#[test]
fn adc_sets_overflow_flag() {
    let code = asm(0x1500, |a| {
        a.mov(eax, edi).unwrap();
        a.mov(ebx, esi).unwrap();
        a.clc().unwrap();
        a.adc(al, bl).unwrap();
        a.ret().unwrap();
    });
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.map(0x1500, &code);
    let _ = emu.call(0x1500, &[0x7f, 0x7f], Abi::SysV).unwrap();
    assert!(emu.cpu.flags.of, "ADC 0x7f+0x7f must set OF");
    assert_eq!(emu.cpu.rax() & 0xff, 0xfe);
}

/// SBB 0x00 - 0x00 - borrow(1): AF/OF must reflect the full a-b-borrow. Here 0-0-1 = 0xff,
/// borrow out (CF) = 1, AF = 1.
#[test]
fn sbb_borrow_flags() {
    let code = asm(0x1600, |a| {
        a.mov(eax, edi).unwrap();
        a.mov(ebx, esi).unwrap();
        a.stc().unwrap(); // CF = 1 -> borrow
        a.sbb(al, bl).unwrap();
        a.ret().unwrap();
    });
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.map(0x1600, &code);
    let _ = emu.call(0x1600, &[0, 0], Abi::SysV).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(emu.cpu.rax() & 0xff, 0xff);
    assert!(emu.cpu.flags.cf, "0-0-1 borrows");
    assert!(emu.cpu.flags.af, "0-0-1 half-borrows");
}

// --- audit regression tests (import slots, faults, segments, ABI, stubs) ----

/// `call [IAT slot]` loads the slot's contents (a hint/name RVA in a PE file image), so the hook
/// must match the slot address itself — before, execution jumped into the RVA and faulted.
#[test]
fn call_through_a_hooked_import_slot_runs_the_stub() {
    const SLOT: u64 = 0x9000;
    const SECRET_ADDR: u64 = 0xb000;
    let code = asm(0x8000, |a| {
        a.mov(rsi, SECRET_ADDR).unwrap();
        a.call(qword_ptr(SLOT)).unwrap();
        a.test(rax, rax).unwrap();
        a.sete(al).unwrap();
        a.movzx(eax, al).unwrap();
        a.ret().unwrap();
    });
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.map(0x8000, &code);
    // The slot holds what a PE file image holds there: a hint/name RVA, not code.
    emu.map(SLOT, &0x0001_2345u64.to_le_bytes());
    emu.hook(SLOT, Stub::Strcmp);
    emu.map(SECRET_ADDR, b"hunter2\0");
    emu.map(0xc000, b"hunter2\0");
    emu.map(0xd000, b"wrong\0");
    assert_eq!(emu.call(0x8000, &[0xc000], Abi::SysV).unwrap(), 1);
    assert_eq!(emu.call(0x8000, &[0xd000], Abi::SysV).unwrap(), 0);
}

/// A PLT stub `jmp [GOT]` whose GOT slot is hooked: the file image's GOT holds the lazy-binding
/// address (PLT+6), so the hook must fire on the `jmp` and return to the original caller.
#[test]
fn jmp_through_a_hooked_got_slot_returns_to_the_caller() {
    const GOT: u64 = 0x9000;
    const PLT: u64 = 0xa000;
    let code = asm(0x8000, |a| {
        a.call(PLT).unwrap();
        a.add(rax, 1).unwrap();
        a.ret().unwrap();
    });
    let plt = asm(PLT, |a| {
        a.jmp(qword_ptr(GOT)).unwrap();
        a.push(0).unwrap(); // the lazy-binding path (never reached)
    });
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.map(0x8000, &code);
    emu.map(PLT, &plt);
    emu.map(GOT, &(PLT + 6).to_le_bytes());
    emu.hook(GOT, Stub::Return(41));
    assert_eq!(emu.call(0x8000, &[], Abi::SysV).unwrap(), 42);
}

/// Guest writes fault on unmapped memory instead of allocating a page: a null-pointer store is
/// caught, and a striding write loop can't balloon host memory.
#[test]
fn writes_to_unmapped_memory_fault() {
    let code = asm(0x1000, |a| {
        a.mov(dword_ptr(rdi), 7).unwrap();
        a.ret().unwrap();
    });
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.map(0x1000, &code);
    assert_eq!(emu.call(0x1000, &[0], Abi::SysV), Err(EmuError::Fault(0)));
    emu.cpu = orress_emu::Cpu::new();
    assert_eq!(
        emu.call(0x1000, &[0x4000_0000], Abi::SysV),
        Err(EmuError::Fault(0x4000_0000))
    );
    assert!(
        !emu.mem.is_mapped(0),
        "the faulting write did not map a page"
    );
    assert!(!emu.mem.is_mapped(0x4000_0000));
    // Mapped memory is still writable.
    emu.cpu = orress_emu::Cpu::new();
    emu.mem.map_zeroed(0x5000, 0x1000);
    emu.call(0x1000, &[0x5000], Abi::SysV).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(emu.mem.read(0x5000, 4).unwrap(), 7);
}

/// `fs:[0x28]` (SysV stack canary) and `gs:[0x30]` (Win64 TEB self-pointer) honour the segment
/// base; before, the override was ignored and the load hit address 0x28 / 0x30.
#[test]
fn fs_and_gs_segment_overrides_use_the_segment_base() {
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    // mov rax, fs:[0x28] ; ret
    emu.map(0x1000, &[0x64, 0x48, 0x8B, 0x04, 0x25, 0x28, 0, 0, 0, 0xC3]);
    // mov rax, gs:[0x30] ; mov rax, [rax+0x60] ; ret   (TEB -> PEB)
    emu.map(
        0x2000,
        &[
            0x65, 0x48, 0x8B, 0x04, 0x25, 0x30, 0, 0, 0, 0x48, 0x8B, 0x40, 0x60, 0xC3,
        ],
    );
    assert_eq!(
        emu.call(0x1000, &[], Abi::SysV).unwrap(),
        orress_emu::STACK_CANARY
    );
    assert_eq!(
        emu.call(0x2000, &[], Abi::Win64).unwrap(),
        orress_emu::PEB_BASE
    );
    // `lea` never applies a segment base.
    // lea rax, fs:[0x28] ; ret
    emu.map(0x3000, &[0x64, 0x48, 0x8D, 0x04, 0x25, 0x28, 0, 0, 0, 0xC3]);
    assert_eq!(emu.call(0x3000, &[], Abi::SysV).unwrap(), 0x28);
}

/// A 32-bit CMOVcc with a false condition still zero-extends its destination.
#[test]
fn cmov32_false_condition_zeroes_upper_half() {
    let code = asm(0x1000, |a| {
        a.mov(rax, -1i64).unwrap();
        a.cmp(edi, edi).unwrap(); // ZF = 1, so cmovne is false
        a.cmovne(eax, esi).unwrap();
        a.ret().unwrap();
    });
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.map(0x1000, &code);
    assert_eq!(emu.call(0x1000, &[1, 2], Abi::SysV).unwrap(), 0xffff_ffff);
}

/// Arguments past the register count go on the stack: SysV right after the return address,
/// Win64 after the 32-byte shadow space.
#[test]
fn stack_arguments_follow_the_abi() {
    // SysV: return arg7 * 1000 + arg8  (args 7 and 8 at [rsp+8], [rsp+16])
    let sysv = asm(0x1000, |a| {
        a.imul_3(rax, qword_ptr(rsp + 8), 1000).unwrap();
        a.add(rax, qword_ptr(rsp + 16)).unwrap();
        a.ret().unwrap();
    });
    // Win64: return arg5 * 1000 + arg6  (at [rsp+0x28], [rsp+0x30])
    let win = asm(0x2000, |a| {
        a.imul_3(rax, qword_ptr(rsp + 0x28), 1000).unwrap();
        a.add(rax, qword_ptr(rsp + 0x30)).unwrap();
        a.ret().unwrap();
    });
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.map(0x1000, &sysv);
    emu.map(0x2000, &win);
    let args = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8];
    assert_eq!(emu.call(0x1000, &args, Abi::SysV).unwrap(), 7008);
    assert_eq!(emu.call(0x2000, &args[..6], Abi::Win64).unwrap(), 5006);
    // At entry RSP is 8 mod 16, as after a real `call`.
    let probe = asm(0x3000, |a| {
        a.mov(rax, rsp).unwrap();
        a.ret().unwrap();
    });
    emu.map(0x3000, &probe);
    for n in 0..10 {
        let args: Vec<u64> = (0..n).collect();
        assert_eq!(emu.call(0x3000, &args, Abi::SysV).unwrap() % 16, 8);
        assert_eq!(emu.call(0x3000, &args, Abi::Win64).unwrap() % 16, 8);
    }
}

/// `atoi` parses leading whitespace, a sign, and the leading digits only.
#[test]
fn atoi_stub_parses_a_numeric_prefix() {
    const ATOI: u64 = 0xa000;
    let code = asm(0x1000, |a| {
        a.call(ATOI).unwrap();
        a.ret().unwrap();
    });
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.map(0x1000, &code);
    emu.hook(ATOI, Stub::Atoi);
    for (s, want) in [
        (&b"123abc\0"[..], 123i64),
        (b"  -42\0", -42),
        (b"+7 apples\0", 7),
        (b"abc\0", 0),
        (b"\t\n99\0", 99),
    ] {
        emu.map(0x5000, s);
        assert_eq!(
            emu.call(0x1000, &[0x5000], Abi::SysV).unwrap() as i64,
            want,
            "{s:?}"
        );
    }
}

/// `stub_for` is the shared import-name -> stub mapping.
#[test]
fn stub_for_maps_libc_names() {
    assert_eq!(orress_emu::stub_for("_strcmp"), Stub::Strcmp);
    assert_eq!(orress_emu::stub_for("memmove"), Stub::Memcpy);
    assert_eq!(orress_emu::stub_for("puts"), Stub::Return(0));
}

/// SSE2: a 16-byte slice comparison, exactly the shape Rust emits for `a == b` on `[u8; 16]`
/// (movdqu / pcmpeqb / pmovmskb). Equal buffers give al = 1, any difference gives 0.
#[test]
fn sse2_compares_sixteen_bytes() {
    // fn eq16(a: *const u8, b: *const u8) -> bool  (SysV: a=rdi, b=rsi)
    let code = asm(0x1000, |a| {
        a.movdqu(xmm0, xmmword_ptr(rdi)).unwrap();
        a.movdqu(xmm1, xmmword_ptr(rsi)).unwrap();
        a.pcmpeqb(xmm1, xmm0).unwrap();
        a.pmovmskb(eax, xmm1).unwrap();
        a.cmp(eax, 0xffff).unwrap();
        a.sete(al).unwrap();
        a.movzx(eax, al).unwrap();
        a.ret().unwrap();
    });
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.map(0x1000, &code);
    emu.map(0x4000, b"n0_debugger_here"); // 16 bytes
    emu.map(0x5000, b"n0_debugger_here");
    emu.map(0x6000, b"n0_debugger_XXXX");
    assert_eq!(emu.call(0x1000, &[0x4000, 0x5000], Abi::SysV).unwrap(), 1);
    assert_eq!(emu.call(0x1000, &[0x4000, 0x6000], Abi::SysV).unwrap(), 0);
}

/// SSE2 moves and bitwise ops: pxor zeros a register, a 128-bit store/load round-trips, and
/// movd/movq shuttle a scalar in and back out of an xmm register.
#[test]
fn sse2_move_xor_and_scalar() {
    let code = asm(0x1000, |a| {
        a.pxor(xmm0, xmm0).unwrap(); // xmm0 = 0
        a.movdqu(xmmword_ptr(0x5000u64), xmm0).unwrap(); // store 16 zero bytes
        a.movd(xmm1, edi).unwrap(); // xmm1.low32 = arg0
        a.movq(rax, xmm1).unwrap(); // rax = xmm1.low64 (upper zero from movd)
        a.ret().unwrap();
    });
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.map(0x1000, &code);
    emu.mem.map_zeroed(0x5000, 16);
    emu.mem.write_bytes(0x5000, &[0xff; 16]);
    assert_eq!(
        emu.call(0x1000, &[0x1234_5678], Abi::SysV).unwrap(),
        0x1234_5678
    );
    // the pxor'd register was stored over the 0xff bytes, zeroing them
    assert_eq!(emu.mem.read(0x5000, 8).unwrap(), 0);
    assert_eq!(emu.mem.read(0x5008, 8).unwrap(), 0);
}

`crates/orress-emu/tests/solve.rs`:

```rs
//! Proves the instruction-counting side-channel solver recovers a secret from a check routine
//! that bails on the first wrong byte — without ever producing a passing input.

use iced_x86::code_asm::*;
use orress_emu::{Abi, Cpu, Emulator, solve_by_count};

const CODE: u64 = 0x1000;
const SECRET_ADDR: u64 = 0x8000;
const BUF: u64 = 0x9000;

/// A byte-by-byte comparison that returns early on the first mismatch — the classic shape a
/// side channel defeats.
fn build_check(secret_len: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut a = CodeAssembler::new(64).unwrap();
    let mut loop_l = a.create_label();
    let mut pass_l = a.create_label();
    let mut fail_l = a.create_label();
    a.mov(r8, SECRET_ADDR).unwrap(); // secret base
    a.xor(ecx, ecx).unwrap(); // i = 0
    a.set_label(&mut loop_l).unwrap();
    a.cmp(rcx, secret_len as i32).unwrap();
    a.jae(pass_l).unwrap();
    a.mov(al, byte_ptr(rdi + rcx)).unwrap(); // input[i]
    a.mov(dl, byte_ptr(r8 + rcx)).unwrap(); // secret[i]
    a.cmp(al, dl).unwrap();
    a.jne(fail_l).unwrap();
    a.inc(rcx).unwrap();
    a.jmp(loop_l).unwrap();
    a.set_label(&mut pass_l).unwrap();
    a.mov(eax, 1).unwrap();
    a.ret().unwrap();
    a.set_label(&mut fail_l).unwrap();
    a.xor(eax, eax).unwrap();
    a.ret().unwrap();
    a.assemble(CODE).unwrap()
}

#[test]
fn side_channel_recovers_the_secret() {
    let secret = b"R3v3rs3!";
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.map(CODE, &build_check(secret.len()));
    emu.map(SECRET_ADDR, secret);

    let candidates: Vec<u8> = (0x20u8..=0x7e).collect(); // printable ASCII
    let solution = solve_by_count(secret.len(), &candidates, |input| {
        emu.map(BUF, input);
        emu.cpu = Cpu::new(); // fresh registers/flags each trial
        emu.call(CODE, &[BUF], Abi::SysV).unwrap();
        emu.steps
    });

    assert_eq!(&solution.input, secret);
    // The winning byte at each position beat the runner-up (a clean signal).
    for step in &solution.steps {
        assert!(
            step.count > step.runner_up,
            "position {} had no clear winner",
            step.index
        );
    }

    // Sanity: the recovered input actually passes the real check.
    emu.map(BUF, &solution.input);
    emu.cpu = Cpu::new();
    assert_eq!(emu.call(CODE, &[BUF], Abi::SysV).unwrap(), 1);
}

`crates/orress-ext/fixtures/README.md`:

```md
# Extension host test fixtures

`demo-guest.wasm` is a tiny WASM **component** implementing the `orress:extension` WIT world
(`../wit/world.wit`). The host test `runs_a_real_guest_extension_over_the_wit_world` loads it to
verify the component host end to end: host imports, exported functions, records and strings.

It is checked in (≈22 KB) so the test needs no WASM toolchain. To regenerate it after changing the
WIT world or the guest, with the stable Rust toolchain plus the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target
(`rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown`) — no external binaries, cargo only:

```sh
# 1. Build the guest to a core module (wit-bindgen embeds the component type).
cd guest && cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown && cd ..
# 2. Wrap the core module into a component and write ../demo-guest.wasm.
cd encode && cargo run --release && cd ..
```

`guest/` and `encode/` are each their own detached workspace, so the main ORRESS build ignores
them; their `target/` directories are git-ignored.

## Zed extension fixture

`zed-guest.wasm` is a *real* Zed extension built with the `zed_extension_api` crate
(`zed-guest/`), used by `runs_a_real_zed_extension_and_resolves_its_language_server` to verify the
clean-room Zed host. Regenerate it with:

```sh
cd zed-guest && cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown && cd ..
cd encode && cargo run --release -- \
  ../zed-guest/target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/orress_zed_demo_guest.wasm \
  ../zed-guest.wasm && cd ..
```

## Older Zed API version fixture

`zed-guest-old.wasm` is a Zed extension built against the **pre-`dap`** `since_v0.5.0` WIT world
(the last `zed:extension` world before `since_v0.6.0` added the `dap` interface). It is hand-written
with `wit-bindgen` against that vendored WIT (`zed-guest-old/wit/`) rather than `zed_extension_api`,
so it compiles for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` without a WASI runtime — isolating the one property
under test in `runs_an_older_api_version_zed_extension`: that the host (whose linker exposes the
newer `since_v0.6.0` import surface) still instantiates and drives a component that neither imports
`dap` nor exports the five `dap-*` functions. It also implements the context-server and
slash-command exports with real values, so the host's wiring for those
(`runs_context_server_and_slash_command_exports`) is tested against it too. Regenerate it with:

```sh
cd zed-guest-old && cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown && cd ..
cd encode && cargo run --release -- \
  ../zed-guest-old/target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/orress_zed_old_guest.wasm \
  ../zed-guest-old.wasm && cd ..
```

## WASI extension fixture

`zed-guest-wasi.wasm` is the **same** real extension as `zed-guest/`, but built for
**`wasm32-wasip1`** — the target Zed actually ships extensions in. Its `init-extension` touches
`std::env`/the C runtime cwd, so it only runs if the host provides a WASI runtime (`wasmtime-wasi`)
with `$PWD` set. The test `runs_a_wasi_zed_extension` proves exactly that. The `encode` tool
auto-detects a WASI preview1 core (one importing `wasi_snapshot_preview1`) and splices in the WASI
preview1 **reactor** adapter (from the `wasi-preview1-component-adapter-provider` crate, pinned to
the wasmtime version), producing a component that imports the componentized `wasi:*` interfaces.
Needs the target (`rustup target add wasm32-wasip1`):

```sh
cd zed-guest && cargo build --release --target wasm32-wasip1 && cd ..
cd encode && cargo run --release -- \
  ../zed-guest/target/wasm32-wasip1/release/orress_zed_demo_guest.wasm \
  ../zed-guest-wasi.wasm && cd ..
```

`crates/orress-ext/fixtures/encode/src/main.rs`:

```rs
//! Wraps a guest core wasm module into a component and writes it. Defaults to the demo guest;
//! pass `<core.wasm> <out.wasm>` to encode another (e.g. the Zed guest). See `../README.md`.
//!
//! A `wasm32-unknown-unknown` core is wrapped directly. A `wasm32-wasip1` core (one that imports
//! the `wasi_snapshot_preview1` module) additionally has the WASI preview1 **reactor** adapter
//! spliced in, so the result is a component importing the componentized `wasi:*` interfaces — the
//! shape real Zed extensions ship in.

use wasi_preview1_component_adapter_provider::{
    WASI_SNAPSHOT_PREVIEW1_ADAPTER_NAME, WASI_SNAPSHOT_PREVIEW1_REACTOR_ADAPTER,
};

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();
    let (input, output) = match args.as_slice() {
        [] => (
            "../guest/target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/orress_ext_demo_guest.wasm".to_string(),
            "../demo-guest.wasm".to_string(),
        ),
        [i, o] => (i.clone(), o.clone()),
        _ => return Err("usage: encode [<core.wasm> <out.wasm>]".into()),
    };
    let core = std::fs::read(&input)?;
    let mut encoder = wit_component::ComponentEncoder::default().validate(true).module(&core)?;
    // A WASI preview1 core imports the `wasi_snapshot_preview1` module; give it the reactor adapter.
    let targets_wasi = core
        .windows(WASI_SNAPSHOT_PREVIEW1_ADAPTER_NAME.len())
        .any(|w| w == WASI_SNAPSHOT_PREVIEW1_ADAPTER_NAME.as_bytes());
    if targets_wasi {
        encoder = encoder
            .adapter(WASI_SNAPSHOT_PREVIEW1_ADAPTER_NAME, WASI_SNAPSHOT_PREVIEW1_REACTOR_ADAPTER)?;
    }
    let component = encoder.encode()?;
    std::fs::write(&output, &component)?;
    println!(
        "wrote {output} ({} bytes{})",
        component.len(),
        if targets_wasi { ", WASI preview1 adapter spliced in" } else { "" }
    );
    Ok(())
}

`crates/orress-ext/fixtures/guest/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! A tiny ORRESS extension guest, used only to test the component host. It implements the
//! `orress:extension` world: reports metadata and uppercases text while logging via the host.

wit_bindgen::generate!({
    world: "extension",
    path: "../../wit",
});

struct Component;

impl Guest for Component {
    fn info() -> Info {
        Info {
            name: "demo".to_string(),
            version: "0.1.0".to_string(),
        }
    }

    fn shout(text: String) -> String {
        orress::extension::host::log(&format!("shouting: {text}"));
        text.to_uppercase()
    }
}

export!(Component);

```

`crates/orress-ext/fixtures/zed-guest-old/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! A Zed extension guest built directly against the vendored **`since_v0.5.0`** WIT world (the
//! last `zed:extension` world before `since_v0.6.0` added the `dap` interface). It is hand-written
//! with `wit-bindgen` rather than `zed_extension_api` so it compiles for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`
//! without a WASI runtime, isolating the one thing under test: that ORRESS's host (whose linker
//! exposes the newer `since_v0.6.0` import surface) still instantiates and drives a component that
//! neither imports `dap` nor exports the five `dap-*` functions.
//!
//! `init-extension` and `language-server-command` carry behaviour, as do the context-server and
//! slash-command exports (`context-server-command`/`-configuration`, `run-slash-command`,
//! `complete-slash-command-argument`) so the host's wiring for those can be tested end to end. The
//! remaining exports are present (a valid component must export them all) but return empty results.

wit_bindgen::generate!({
    world: "extension",
    path: "wit",
});

// `SlashCommandOutputSection` is nested inside a record (not a direct export signature), so it
// stays in its interface module rather than being re-exported at the root like `Range`.
use zed::extension::slash_command::SlashCommandOutputSection;

struct OldExt;

impl Guest for OldExt {
    fn init_extension() {}

    fn language_server_command(
        _language_server_id: String,
        _worktree: &Worktree,
    ) -> Result<Command, String> {
        Ok(Command {
            command: "old-language-server".to_string(),
            args: vec!["--stdio".to_string()],
            env: vec![],
        })
    }

    fn language_server_initialization_options(
        _language_server_id: String,
        _worktree: &Worktree,
    ) -> Result<Option<String>, String> {
        Ok(None)
    }

    fn language_server_workspace_configuration(
        _language_server_id: String,
        _worktree: &Worktree,
    ) -> Result<Option<String>, String> {
        Ok(None)
    }

    fn language_server_additional_initialization_options(
        _language_server_id: String,
        _target_language_server_id: String,
        _worktree: &Worktree,
    ) -> Result<Option<String>, String> {
        Ok(None)
    }

    fn language_server_additional_workspace_configuration(
        _language_server_id: String,
        _target_language_server_id: String,
        _worktree: &Worktree,
    ) -> Result<Option<String>, String> {
        Ok(None)
    }

    fn labels_for_completions(
        _language_server_id: String,
        _completions: Vec<Completion>,
    ) -> Result<Vec<Option<CodeLabel>>, String> {
        Ok(vec![])
    }

    fn labels_for_symbols(
        _language_server_id: String,
        _symbols: Vec<Symbol>,
    ) -> Result<Vec<Option<CodeLabel>>, String> {
        Ok(vec![])
    }

    fn complete_slash_command_argument(
        _command: SlashCommand,
        _args: Vec<String>,
    ) -> Result<Vec<SlashCommandArgumentCompletion>, String> {
        Ok(vec![SlashCommandArgumentCompletion {
            label: "greet".to_string(),
            new_text: "greet".to_string(),
            run_command: true,
        }])
    }

    fn run_slash_command(
        command: SlashCommand,
        args: Vec<String>,
        _worktree: Option<&Worktree>,
    ) -> Result<SlashCommandOutput, String> {
        let text = format!("/{} {}", command.name, args.join(" "));
        let section = SlashCommandOutputSection {
            range: Range { start: 0, end: text.len() as u32 },
            label: "demo".to_string(),
        };
        Ok(SlashCommandOutput { text, sections: vec![section] })
    }

    fn context_server_command(
        _context_server_id: String,
        _project: &Project,
    ) -> Result<Command, String> {
        Ok(Command {
            command: "mcp-server".to_string(),
            args: vec!["--stdio".to_string()],
            env: vec![],
        })
    }

    fn context_server_configuration(
        _context_server_id: String,
        _project: &Project,
    ) -> Result<Option<ContextServerConfiguration>, String> {
        Ok(Some(ContextServerConfiguration {
            installation_instructions: "Install with npm".to_string(),
            settings_schema: "{}".to_string(),
            default_settings: "{}".to_string(),
        }))
    }

    fn suggest_docs_packages(_provider_name: String) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
        Ok(vec![])
    }

    fn index_docs(
        _provider_name: String,
        _package_name: String,
        _database: &KeyValueStore,
    ) -> Result<(), String> {
        Err("not supported".to_string())
    }
}

export!(OldExt);
