`crates/orress-ext/wit/zed/dap.wit`:

```wit
interface dap {
    use common.{env-vars};

    /// Resolves a specified TcpArgumentsTemplate into TcpArguments
    resolve-tcp-template: func(template: tcp-arguments-template) -> result<tcp-arguments, string>;

    record launch-request {
        program: string,
        cwd: option<string>,
        args: list<string>,
        envs: env-vars,
    }

    record attach-request {
        process-id: option<u32>,
    }

    variant debug-request {
        launch(launch-request),
        attach(attach-request)
    }

    record tcp-arguments {
        port: u16,
        host: u32,
        timeout: option<u64>,
    }

    record tcp-arguments-template {
        port: option<u16>,
        host: option<u32>,
        timeout: option<u64>,
    }

    /// Debug Config is the "highest-level" configuration for a debug session.
    /// It comes from a new process modal UI; thus, it is essentially debug-adapter-agnostic.
    /// It is expected of the extension to translate this generic configuration into something that can be debugged by the adapter (debug scenario).
    record debug-config {
        /// Name of the debug task
        label: string,
        /// The debug adapter to use
        adapter: string,
        request: debug-request,
        stop-on-entry: option<bool>,
    }

    record task-template {
        /// Human readable name of the task to display in the UI.
        label: string,
        /// Executable command to spawn.
        command: string,
        args: list<string>,
        env: env-vars,
        cwd: option<string>,
    }

    /// A task template with substituted task variables.
    type resolved-task = task-template;

    /// A task template for building a debug target.
    type build-task-template = task-template;

    variant build-task-definition {
        by-name(string),
        template(build-task-definition-template-payload )
    }
    record build-task-definition-template-payload {
        locator-name: option<string>,
        template: build-task-template
    }

    /// Debug Scenario is the user-facing configuration type (used in debug.json). It is still concerned with what to debug and not necessarily how to do it (except for any
    /// debug-adapter-specific configuration options).
    record debug-scenario {
        /// Unsubstituted label for the task.DebugAdapterBinary
        label: string,
        /// Name of the Debug Adapter this configuration is intended for.
        adapter: string,
        /// An optional build step to be ran prior to starting a debug session. Build steps are used by Zed's locators to locate the executable to debug.
        build: option<build-task-definition>,
        /// JSON-encoded configuration for a given debug adapter.
        config: string,
        /// TCP connection parameters (if they were specified by user)
        tcp-connection: option<tcp-arguments-template>,
    }

    enum start-debugging-request-arguments-request {
        launch,
        attach,
    }

    record debug-task-definition {
        /// Unsubstituted label for the task.DebugAdapterBinary
        label: string,
        /// Name of the Debug Adapter this configuration is intended for.
        adapter: string,
        /// JSON-encoded configuration for a given debug adapter.
        config: string,
        /// TCP connection parameters (if they were specified by user)
        tcp-connection: option<tcp-arguments-template>,
    }

    record start-debugging-request-arguments {
        /// JSON-encoded configuration for a given debug adapter. It is specific to each debug adapter.
        /// `configuration` will have it's Zed variable references substituted prior to being passed to the debug adapter.
        configuration: string,
        request: start-debugging-request-arguments-request,
    }

    /// The lowest-level representation of a debug session, which specifies:
    /// - How to start a debug adapter process
    /// - How to start a debug session with it (using DAP protocol)
    /// for a given debug scenario.
    record debug-adapter-binary {
        command: option<string>,
        arguments: list<string>,
        envs: env-vars,
        cwd: option<string>,
        /// Zed will use TCP transport if `connection` is specified.
        connection: option<tcp-arguments>,
        request-args: start-debugging-request-arguments
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-ext/wit/zed/http-client.wit`:

```wit
interface http-client {
    /// An HTTP request.
    record http-request {
        /// The HTTP method for the request.
        method: http-method,
        /// The URL to which the request should be made.
        url: string,
        /// The headers for the request.
        headers: list<tuple<string, string>>,
        /// The request body.
        body: option<list<u8>>,
        /// The policy to use for redirects.
        redirect-policy: redirect-policy,
    }

    /// HTTP methods.
    enum http-method {
        /// `GET`
        get,
        /// `HEAD`
        head,
        /// `POST`
        post,
        /// `PUT`
        put,
        /// `DELETE`
        delete,
        /// `OPTIONS`
        options,
        /// `PATCH`
        patch,
    }

    /// The policy for dealing with redirects received from the server.
    variant redirect-policy {
        /// Redirects from the server will not be followed.
        ///
        /// This is the default behavior.
        no-follow,
        /// Redirects from the server will be followed up to the specified limit.
        follow-limit(u32),
        /// All redirects from the server will be followed.
        follow-all,
    }

    /// An HTTP response.
    record http-response {
        /// The response headers.
        headers: list<tuple<string, string>>,
        /// The response body.
        body: list<u8>,
    }

    /// Performs an HTTP request and returns the response.
    fetch: func(req: http-request) -> result<http-response, string>;

    /// An HTTP response stream.
    resource http-response-stream {
        /// Retrieves the next chunk of data from the response stream.
        ///
        /// Returns `Ok(None)` if the stream has ended.
        next-chunk: func() -> result<option<list<u8>>, string>;
    }

    /// Performs an HTTP request and returns a response stream.
    fetch-stream: func(req: http-request) -> result<http-response-stream, string>;
}
```

`crates/orress-heap/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! A glibc (ptmalloc) heap parser for 64-bit targets. Given a memory snapshot — the `[heap]`
//! region's bytes, and optionally the `main_arena` bytes — it walks the malloc chunks and the
//! free lists (tcache, fastbins, unsorted/small/large bins). Pure logic: no process and no OS, so
//! it is fully unit-testable; the live Heap view reads the bytes from the debugger and calls in.
//!
//! Assumptions (the common modern case, matching nightmare's challenges): little-endian x86-64,
//! glibc >= 2.30 for the tcache layout (`uint16_t counts[64]`), and glibc >= 2.27 for the
//! `malloc_state` layout (a `have_fastchunks` word before `fastbinsY`). `mangled` selects
//! safe-linking (glibc >= 2.32), which XORs free-list `fd` pointers with `pos >> 12`.

use std::collections::HashSet;

/// Chunk header flag bits (the low 3 bits of the `size` field).
const PREV_INUSE: u64 = 1;
const IS_MMAPPED: u64 = 2;
const NON_MAIN_ARENA: u64 = 4;
/// Smallest real chunk; anything below this ends the walk.
const MIN_CHUNK: u64 = 0x20;
/// Number of tcache / fastbin bins.
const TCACHE_BINS: usize = 64;
const FASTBINS: usize = 10;
/// `malloc_state` field offsets (glibc >= 2.27, x86-64): fastbinsY, then bins.
const FASTBINSY_OFF: usize = 0x10;
const BINS_OFF: usize = 0x70;
/// Guard against runaway walks / cyclic free lists.
const MAX_CHUNKS: usize = 200_000;
const MAX_LIST: usize = 4000;

/// A single malloc chunk.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Chunk {
    pub addr: u64,
    /// Total chunk size in bytes (flag bits masked off).
    pub size: u64,
    pub prev_inuse: bool,
    pub is_mmapped: bool,
    pub non_main_arena: bool,
    /// Whether the chunk is allocated (the next chunk's PREV_INUSE bit is set).
    pub in_use: bool,
    /// For a free chunk, its `fd`/`bk` (0 for an allocated chunk).
    pub fd: u64,
    pub bk: u64,
}

/// Which free list a [`Bin`] came from.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum BinKind {
    Tcache,
    Fastbin,
    Unsorted,
    Small,
    Large,
}

impl BinKind {
    pub fn label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Tcache => "tcache",
            Self::Fastbin => "fastbin",
            Self::Unsorted => "unsorted",
            Self::Small => "small",
            Self::Large => "large",
        }
    }
}

/// One free list: its kind, index, the chunk size it holds (when fixed), and the chunk addresses.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Bin {
    pub kind: BinKind,
    pub index: usize,
    pub size: Option<u64>,
    /// Chunk header addresses on the list, in list order.
    pub entries: Vec<u64>,
}

/// A parsed heap.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct Heap {
    pub chunks: Vec<Chunk>,
    pub bins: Vec<Bin>,
    pub notes: Vec<String>,
}

fn rd_u64(bytes: &[u8], off: usize) -> u64 {
    bytes
        .get(off..off + 8)
        .map(|s| u64::from_le_bytes(s.try_into().unwrap()))
        .unwrap_or(0)
}

/// Reads a u64 at an absolute address from a region starting at `base`, if in range.
fn read_at(bytes: &[u8], base: u64, addr: u64) -> Option<u64> {
    let off = addr.checked_sub(base)? as usize;
    bytes
        .get(off..off + 8)
        .map(|s| u64::from_le_bytes(s.try_into().unwrap()))
}

/// Walks the chunks of a heap region linearly from `heap_base`.
pub fn walk_chunks(heap: &[u8], heap_base: u64) -> Vec<Chunk> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut off = 0usize;
    while off + 16 <= heap.len() && out.len() < MAX_CHUNKS {
        let raw_size = rd_u64(heap, off + 8);
        let size = raw_size & !0x7;
        if size < MIN_CHUNK {
            break;
        }
        let next_off = off + size as usize;
        let in_use = if next_off + 16 <= heap.len() {
            rd_u64(heap, next_off + 8) & PREV_INUSE != 0
        } else {
            true // the top chunk (last) is treated as in use
        };
        let (fd, bk) = (rd_u64(heap, off + 16), rd_u64(heap, off + 24));
        out.push(Chunk {
            addr: heap_base + off as u64,
            size,
            prev_inuse: raw_size & PREV_INUSE != 0,
            is_mmapped: raw_size & IS_MMAPPED != 0,
            non_main_arena: raw_size & NON_MAIN_ARENA != 0,
            in_use,
            fd: if in_use { 0 } else { fd },
            bk: if in_use { 0 } else { bk },
        });
        if next_off <= off {
            break;
        }
        off = next_off;
    }
    out
}

/// Follows a singly-linked free list (tcache / fastbin) from `head`, reading the next pointer at
/// each node's `fd` and de-mangling under safe-linking. `user_offset` is where the `fd` lives
/// relative to the node value (0 for tcache entries, which point at user data; 16 for fastbins,
/// which point at the chunk header). Returns chunk header addresses.
fn follow_singly(
    heap: &[u8],
    heap_base: u64,
    head: u64,
    chunk_from_node: u64,
    fd_offset: u64,
    mangled: bool,
) -> Vec<u64> {
    let mut entries = Vec::new();
    let mut seen = HashSet::new();
    let mut node = head;
    while node != 0 && entries.len() < MAX_LIST && seen.insert(node) {
        entries.push(node.wrapping_sub(chunk_from_node));
        let fd_addr = node + fd_offset;
        let Some(raw) = read_at(heap, heap_base, fd_addr) else {
            break;
        };
        node = if mangled { raw ^ (fd_addr >> 12) } else { raw };
    }
    entries
}

/// Parses the tcache bins from the tcache_perthread_struct (the first chunk of the heap).
pub fn parse_tcache(heap: &[u8], heap_base: u64, mangled: bool) -> Vec<Bin> {
    let counts_off = 16usize; // user data of the first chunk
    let entries_off = counts_off + TCACHE_BINS * 2; // uint16_t counts[64] (glibc >= 2.30)
    let mut bins = Vec::new();
    for i in 0..TCACHE_BINS {
        let head = rd_u64(heap, entries_off + i * 8);
        if head == 0 {
            continue;
        }
        // tcache entries point at user data; the chunk header is 16 bytes earlier.
        let entries = follow_singly(heap, heap_base, head, 16, 0, mangled);
        if entries.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        bins.push(Bin {
            kind: BinKind::Tcache,
            index: i,
            size: Some(0x20 + i as u64 * 0x10),
            entries,
        });
    }
    bins
}

/// Parses the fastbins from `main_arena`.
pub fn parse_fastbins(arena: &[u8], heap: &[u8], heap_base: u64, mangled: bool) -> Vec<Bin> {
    let mut bins = Vec::new();
    for i in 0..FASTBINS {
        let head = rd_u64(arena, FASTBINSY_OFF + i * 8);
        if head == 0 {
            continue;
        }
        // fastbin pointers reference the chunk header; the `fd` is at chunk+16.
        let entries = follow_singly(heap, heap_base, head, 0, 16, mangled);
        if entries.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        bins.push(Bin {
            kind: BinKind::Fastbin,
            index: i,
            size: Some(0x20 + i as u64 * 0x10),
            entries,
        });
    }
    bins
}

/// Parses the unsorted/small/large bins from `main_arena` (circular doubly-linked lists whose
/// heads live in the arena; chunks link via `fd`).
pub fn parse_arena_bins(arena: &[u8], arena_addr: u64, heap: &[u8], heap_base: u64) -> Vec<Bin> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for k in 1..=127usize {
        let fd_off = BINS_OFF + (2 * k - 2) * 8;
        let head_fd = rd_u64(arena, fd_off);
        // A bin's head acts as a fake chunk whose fd/bk are at +16/+24.
        let bin_chunk = arena_addr + fd_off as u64 - 16;
        if head_fd == 0 || head_fd == bin_chunk {
            continue; // empty bin points to itself
        }
        let mut entries = Vec::new();
        let mut seen = HashSet::new();
        let mut node = head_fd;
        while node != 0 && node != bin_chunk && entries.len() < MAX_LIST && seen.insert(node) {
            entries.push(node);
            match read_at(heap, heap_base, node + 16) {
                Some(next) => node = next,
                None => break,
            }
        }
        if entries.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let kind = match k {
            1 => BinKind::Unsorted,
            2..=63 => BinKind::Small,
            _ => BinKind::Large,
        };
        out.push(Bin {
            kind,
            index: k,
            size: None,
            entries,
        });
    }
    out
}

/// The unsorted-bin "fake chunk" head offset within `main_arena` (glibc >= 2.27, x86-64).
const UNSORTED_BIN_OFFSET: u64 = 0x60;

/// Best-effort `main_arena` address from a free chunk sitting alone in the unsorted bin: such a
/// chunk's `fd == bk` points at the unsorted-bin head (`main_arena + 0x60`), which lies in libc's
/// data. `libc` is the libc mapping's address range. Reliable for the common "one freed chunk in
/// the unsorted bin" setup; returns `None` otherwise (the user can supply the address).
pub fn guess_main_arena(chunks: &[Chunk], libc: std::ops::Range<u64>) -> Option<u64> {
    chunks.iter().find_map(|c| {
        (!c.in_use && c.fd != 0 && c.fd == c.bk && libc.contains(&c.fd))
            .then(|| c.fd - UNSORTED_BIN_OFFSET)
    })
}

/// Parses a whole heap: chunks + tcache, plus the arena bins when the arena snapshot is given.
pub fn parse(heap: &[u8], heap_base: u64, arena: Option<(&[u8], u64)>, mangled: bool) -> Heap {
    let chunks = walk_chunks(heap, heap_base);
    let mut bins = parse_tcache(heap, heap_base, mangled);
    let mut notes = Vec::new();
    match arena {
        Some((abytes, aaddr)) => {
            bins.extend(parse_fastbins(abytes, heap, heap_base, mangled));
            bins.extend(parse_arena_bins(abytes, aaddr, heap, heap_base));
        }
        None => notes.push(
            "main_arena not located — fastbins and unsorted/small/large bins are not shown \
             (chunks and tcache only)."
                .into(),
        ),
    }
    Heap {
        chunks,
        bins,
        notes,
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// A little builder for a synthetic heap region.
    struct Builder {
        base: u64,
        bytes: Vec<u8>,
    }
    impl Builder {
        fn new(base: u64) -> Self {
            Self {
                base,
                bytes: Vec::new(),
            }
        }
        fn put_u64(&mut self, off: usize, v: u64) {
            if self.bytes.len() < off + 8 {
                self.bytes.resize(off + 8, 0);
            }
            self.bytes[off..off + 8].copy_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
        }
        fn put_u16(&mut self, off: usize, v: u16) {
            if self.bytes.len() < off + 2 {
                self.bytes.resize(off + 2, 0);
            }
            self.bytes[off..off + 2].copy_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn walks_allocated_and_free_chunks() {
        // Three 0x20 chunks, the middle one free (its next chunk clears PREV_INUSE).
        let mut b = Builder::new(0x5000);
        // chunk0 @ off 0, size 0x20, prev_inuse set
        b.put_u64(8, 0x20 | PREV_INUSE);
        // chunk1 @ 0x20, size 0x20, prev_inuse set
        b.put_u64(0x20 + 8, 0x20 | PREV_INUSE);
        // chunk2 @ 0x40, size 0x20, PREV_INUSE cleared -> chunk1 is free
        b.put_u64(0x40 + 8, 0x20);
        // top @ 0x60
        b.put_u64(0x60 + 8, 0x20 | PREV_INUSE);
        b.put_u64(0x80 + 8, 0); // terminate

        let chunks = walk_chunks(&b.bytes, b.base);
        assert_eq!(chunks.len(), 4);
        assert_eq!(chunks[0].addr, 0x5000);
        assert_eq!(chunks[0].size, 0x20);
        assert!(chunks[0].in_use);
        assert!(!chunks[1].in_use, "middle chunk is free");
    }

    #[test]
    fn tcache_list_unmangled_and_mangled() {
        // Two chunks past the tcache struct; tcache bin 0 links them (user data = chunk+16).
        let base = 0x5000u64;
        let (c0, c1) = (0x5300u64, 0x5380u64);
        let (u0, u1) = (c0 + 16, c1 + 16);
        let mut b = Builder::new(base);
        // tcache struct: counts[64] u16 at off16, entries[64] at off 16+128.
        let entries_off = 16 + 64 * 2;
        b.put_u16(16, 2); // counts[0] = 2 (cosmetic)
        b.put_u64(entries_off, u0); // entries[0] -> first user data
        b.put_u64((u0 - base) as usize, u1); // first.fd -> second
        b.put_u64((u1 - base) as usize, 0); // second.fd -> NULL
        let bins = parse_tcache(&b.bytes, base, false);
        assert_eq!(bins.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(bins[0].entries, vec![c0, c1]);

        // Mangled (safe-linking): store fd ^ (fd_addr >> 12).
        let mut m = Builder::new(base);
        m.put_u64(entries_off, u0);
        m.put_u64((u0 - base) as usize, u1 ^ (u0 >> 12));
        // Last entry: fd is 0 (end of list), so its mangled value is just 0 ^ (addr>>12).
        m.put_u64((u1 - base) as usize, u1 >> 12);
        let bins = parse_tcache(&m.bytes, base, true);
        assert_eq!(bins[0].entries, vec![c0, c1]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn fastbin_list_from_arena() {
        let base = 0x5000u64;
        let arena_addr = 0x7f0000u64;
        let (c0, c1) = (0x5100u64, 0x5200u64);
        let mut heap = Builder::new(base);
        heap.put_u64((c0 - base) as usize + 16, c1); // c0.fd -> c1
        heap.put_u64((c1 - base) as usize + 16, 0); // c1.fd -> NULL
        let mut arena = Builder::new(arena_addr);
        arena.put_u64(FASTBINSY_OFF, c0); // fastbinsY[0] -> c0
        let bins = parse_fastbins(&arena.bytes, &heap.bytes, base, false);
        assert_eq!(bins.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(bins[0].entries, vec![c0, c1]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn unsorted_bin_circular_walk() {
        let base = 0x5000u64;
        let arena_addr = 0x7f0000u64;
        let c0 = 0x5100u64;
        let fd_off = BINS_OFF; // bin 1 (unsorted) fd
        let bin_chunk = arena_addr + fd_off as u64 - 16;
        let mut arena = Builder::new(arena_addr);
        arena.put_u64(fd_off, c0); // unsorted.fd -> c0
        let mut heap = Builder::new(base);
        heap.put_u64((c0 - base) as usize + 16, bin_chunk); // c0.fd -> back to bin head
        let bins = parse_arena_bins(&arena.bytes, arena_addr, &heap.bytes, base);
        let unsorted: Vec<_> = bins
            .iter()
            .filter(|b| b.kind == BinKind::Unsorted)
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(unsorted.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(unsorted[0].entries, vec![c0]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn guesses_main_arena_from_unsorted_chunk() {
        let libc_base = 0x7f_0000_0000u64;
        let arena = libc_base + 0x1000;
        // A free chunk whose fd == bk points at the unsorted-bin head (arena + 0x60).
        let chunks = vec![
            Chunk {
                addr: 0x5000,
                size: 0x30,
                prev_inuse: true,
                is_mmapped: false,
                non_main_arena: false,
                in_use: false,
                fd: arena + UNSORTED_BIN_OFFSET,
                bk: arena + UNSORTED_BIN_OFFSET,
            },
            Chunk {
                addr: 0x5030,
                size: 0x30,
                prev_inuse: true,
                is_mmapped: false,
                non_main_arena: false,
                in_use: true,
                fd: 0,
                bk: 0,
            },
        ];
        let got = guess_main_arena(&chunks, libc_base..libc_base + 0x200000);
        assert_eq!(got, Some(arena));
    }

    #[test]
    fn cycle_guard_terminates() {
        // A self-referential tcache entry must not loop forever.
        let base = 0x5000u64;
        let c0 = 0x5300u64;
        let u0 = c0 + 16;
        let entries_off = 16 + 64 * 2;
        let mut b = Builder::new(base);
        b.put_u64(entries_off, u0);
        b.put_u64((u0 - base) as usize, u0); // points to itself
        let bins = parse_tcache(&b.bytes, base, false);
        assert_eq!(bins[0].entries, vec![c0]); // visited once, then stops
    }
}
```

```rs
//! Prints a `.class` file's header, fields and methods with a JVM disassembly.
//!
//! Run with: `cargo run -p orress-java --example class_info -- path/to/File.class`

fn main() {
    let path = std::env::args()
        .nth(1)
        .expect("usage: class_info <File.class>");
    let data = std::fs::read(&path).expect("read file");
    let cf = match orress_java::parse(&data) {
        Ok(c) => c,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("{path}: {e}");
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
    };
    let flags = orress_java::access_flag_names(cf.access & !0x0020).join(" ");
    println!("{flags} class {} ({})", cf.this_class, cf.java_version());
    if let Some(s) = &cf.super_class {
        println!("  extends {s}");
    }
    for f in &cf.fields {
        let fl = orress_java::access_flag_names(f.access).join(" ");
        let cv = f
            .constant_value
            .map(|i| format!(" = {}", cf.cp.resolve(i)))
            .unwrap_or_default();
        println!("  field: {fl} {}: {}{cv}", f.name, f.descriptor);
    }
    for m in &cf.methods {
        let fl = orress_java::access_flag_names(m.access).join(" ");
        println!("\n  method: {fl} {}{}", m.name, m.descriptor);
        if let Some(code) = &m.code {
            for ins in orress_java::disassemble(code, &cf.cp) {
                let mark = if ins.is_branch_target { ">>" } else { "  " };
                println!(
                    "    {mark} {:>4}: {:<16} {}",
                    ins.offset, ins.mnemonic, ins.operands
                );
            }
        }
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-java/src/dis.rs`:

```rs
//! Disassembles JVM bytecode (a method's `Code` attribute) into instructions, resolving
//! constant-pool references and branch targets. The opcode set is stable across all class
//! versions, so this needs no per-version table.

use crate::{Code, ConstantPool};

/// One decoded JVM instruction.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct Insn {
    /// Byte offset in the method's `code[]` (matches `javap`).
    pub offset: usize,
    pub opcode: u8,
    pub mnemonic: &'static str,
    /// Rendered operands (indices resolved, with `// comment`), empty if the op takes none.
    pub operands: String,
    /// Absolute target offset for a branch instruction.
    pub branch_target: Option<usize>,
    /// True if some branch lands on this instruction.
    pub is_branch_target: bool,
}

/// Disassembles a method's bytecode.
pub fn disassemble(code: &Code, cp: &ConstantPool) -> Vec<Insn> {
    let b = &code.bytecode;
    let mut insns: Vec<Insn> = Vec::new();
    let mut targets: std::collections::HashSet<usize> = std::collections::HashSet::new();
    let mut i = 0usize;

    while i < b.len() {
        let start = i;
        let op = b[i];
        i += 1;
        let (operands, target) = match operands(op, b, &mut i, start, cp) {
            Some(x) => x,
            None => {
                // Truncated or malformed operand stream — stop cleanly.
                insns.push(Insn {
                    offset: start,
                    opcode: op,
                    mnemonic: mnemonic(op),
                    operands: "(truncated)".into(),
                    branch_target: None,
                    is_branch_target: false,
                });
                break;
            }
        };
        if let Some(t) = target {
            targets.insert(t);
        }
        insns.push(Insn {
            offset: start,
            opcode: op,
            mnemonic: mnemonic(op),
            operands,
            branch_target: target,
            is_branch_target: false,
        });
    }

    for ins in &mut insns {
        if targets.contains(&ins.offset) {
            ins.is_branch_target = true;
        }
    }
    insns
}

/// Reads an opcode's operands, advancing `*i`. Returns `(rendered, branch_target)`, or `None` on a
/// truncated/invalid stream. For switches it also records targets via the returned string only;
/// the caller's single `target` is the primary one (switches render all targets inline).
fn operands(
    op: u8,
    b: &[u8],
    i: &mut usize,
    start: usize,
    cp: &ConstantPool,
) -> Option<(String, Option<usize>)> {
    let u1 = |i: &mut usize| -> Option<u8> {
        let v = *b.get(*i)?;
        *i += 1;
        Some(v)
    };
    let u2 = |i: &mut usize| -> Option<u16> {
        let v = u16::from_be_bytes([*b.get(*i)?, *b.get(*i + 1)?]);
        *i += 2;
        Some(v)
    };
    let i2 = |i: &mut usize| -> Option<i16> { u2(i).map(|v| v as i16) };
    let i4 = |i: &mut usize| -> Option<i32> {
        let v = i32::from_be_bytes([
            *b.get(*i)?,
            *b.get(*i + 1)?,
            *b.get(*i + 2)?,
            *b.get(*i + 3)?,
        ]);
        *i += 4;
        Some(v)
    };

    Some(match op {
        // Immediate pushes.
        0x10 => (format!("{}", u1(i)? as i8), None), // bipush
        0x11 => (format!("{}", i2(i)?), None),       // sipush
        // Constant-pool loads (1- and 2-byte index).
        0x12 => cp_ref(u1(i)? as u16, cp), // ldc
        0x13 | 0x14 => cp_ref(u2(i)?, cp), // ldc_w, ldc2_w
        // Local-variable access (1-byte index).
        0x15..=0x19 | 0x36..=0x3a | 0xa9 => (format!("{}", u1(i)?), None),
        0x84 => {
            // iinc index, const
            let idx = u1(i)?;
            let c = u1(i)? as i8;
            (format!("{idx}, {c}"), None)
        }
        // Conditional/unconditional branches (2-byte signed, relative to the opcode).
        0x99..=0xa8 | 0xc6 | 0xc7 => {
            let t = (start as isize + i2(i)? as isize) as usize;
            (t.to_string(), Some(t))
        }
        // Wide branches (4-byte).
        0xc8 | 0xc9 => {
            let t = (start as isize + i4(i)? as isize) as usize;
            (t.to_string(), Some(t))
        }
        // Field/method/type references (2-byte index).
        0xb2..=0xb8 | 0xbb | 0xbd | 0xc0 | 0xc1 => cp_ref(u2(i)?, cp),
        0xb9 => {
            // invokeinterface: index, count, 0
            let (txt, _) = cp_ref(u2(i)?, cp);
            let count = u1(i)?;
            let _zero = u1(i)?;
            (format!("{txt}, {count}"), None)
        }
        0xba => {
            // invokedynamic: index, 0, 0
            let (txt, _) = cp_ref(u2(i)?, cp);
            let _ = u2(i)?;
            (txt, None)
        }
        0xbc => (newarray_type(u1(i)?).to_string(), None), // newarray
        0xc5 => {
            // multianewarray: index, dimensions
            let (txt, _) = cp_ref(u2(i)?, cp);
            let dims = u1(i)?;
            (format!("{txt}, dim {dims}"), None)
        }
        0xaa => tableswitch(b, i, start)?,
        0xab => lookupswitch(b, i, start)?,
        0xc4 => wide(b, i, cp)?,
        _ => (String::new(), None),
    })
}

fn cp_ref(idx: u16, cp: &ConstantPool) -> (String, Option<usize>) {
    (format!("#{idx}  // {}", cp.resolve(idx)), None)
}

fn newarray_type(atype: u8) -> &'static str {
    match atype {
        4 => "boolean",
        5 => "char",
        6 => "float",
        7 => "double",
        8 => "byte",
        9 => "short",
        10 => "int",
        11 => "long",
        _ => "?",
    }
}

fn tableswitch(b: &[u8], i: &mut usize, start: usize) -> Option<(String, Option<usize>)> {
    // 0-3 bytes padding so the default operand is 4-byte aligned from the code start.
    *i += (4 - (*i % 4)) % 4;
    let rd4 = |i: &mut usize| -> Option<i32> {
        let v = i32::from_be_bytes([
            *b.get(*i)?,
            *b.get(*i + 1)?,
            *b.get(*i + 2)?,
            *b.get(*i + 3)?,
        ]);
        *i += 4;
        Some(v)
    };
    let default = start as isize + rd4(i)? as isize;
    let low = rd4(i)?;
    let high = rd4(i)?;
    let n = (high as i64 - low as i64 + 1).max(0) as usize;
    let mut cases = Vec::new();
    for k in 0..n {
        let t = start as isize + rd4(i)? as isize;
        cases.push(format!("{}: {}", low as i64 + k as i64, t));
    }
    Some((
        format!("default: {default}, {} case(s) [{}]", n, cases.join(", ")),
        Some(default as usize),
    ))
}

fn lookupswitch(b: &[u8], i: &mut usize, start: usize) -> Option<(String, Option<usize>)> {
    *i += (4 - (*i % 4)) % 4;
    let rd4 = |i: &mut usize| -> Option<i32> {
        let v = i32::from_be_bytes([
            *b.get(*i)?,
            *b.get(*i + 1)?,
            *b.get(*i + 2)?,
            *b.get(*i + 3)?,
        ]);
        *i += 4;
        Some(v)
    };
    let default = start as isize + rd4(i)? as isize;
    let npairs = rd4(i)?.max(0) as usize;
    let mut cases = Vec::new();
    for _ in 0..npairs {
        let m = rd4(i)?;
        let t = start as isize + rd4(i)? as isize;
        cases.push(format!("{m}: {t}"));
    }
    Some((
        format!(
            "default: {default}, {npairs} pair(s) [{}]",
            cases.join(", ")
        ),
        Some(default as usize),
    ))
}

fn wide(b: &[u8], i: &mut usize, _cp: &ConstantPool) -> Option<(String, Option<usize>)> {
    let op = *b.get(*i)?;
    *i += 1;
    let idx = u16::from_be_bytes([*b.get(*i)?, *b.get(*i + 1)?]);
    *i += 2;
    if op == 0x84 {
        // wide iinc: index (2), const (2)
        let c = i16::from_be_bytes([*b.get(*i)?, *b.get(*i + 1)?]);
        *i += 2;
        Some((format!("{} {idx}, {c}", mnemonic(op)), None))
    } else {
        Some((format!("{} {idx}", mnemonic(op)), None))
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-java/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! Java class-file (`.class`) loading for ORRESS.
//!
//! [`parse`] reads the JVM class-file format — the constant pool, this/super class, interfaces,
//! fields and methods with their descriptors and attributes — and [`disassemble`] turns a method's
//! `Code` attribute into JVM bytecode instructions with constant-pool references resolved. Pure
//! `std`, no dependencies, and tolerant of hostile input (errors rather than panics; counts and
//! sizes are bounded).
//!
//! Java bytecode is common in CTF (and Android work starts here before DEX); the format and opcode
//! set are stable, so this covers every class version. Part of ORRESS's M10 managed-code track.

mod dis;

pub use dis::{Insn, disassemble};

/// A constant-pool entry (1-indexed in the file; `Unusable` fills index 0 and the second slot of
/// `Long`/`Double`).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum Constant {
    Unusable,
    Utf8(String),
    Integer(i32),
    Float(f32),
    Long(i64),
    Double(f64),
    Class(u16),
    String(u16),
    FieldRef { class: u16, nat: u16 },
    MethodRef { class: u16, nat: u16 },
    InterfaceMethodRef { class: u16, nat: u16 },
    NameAndType { name: u16, desc: u16 },
    MethodHandle { kind: u8, index: u16 },
    MethodType(u16),
    Dynamic { bootstrap: u16, nat: u16 },
    InvokeDynamic { bootstrap: u16, nat: u16 },
    Module(u16),
    Package(u16),
}

/// The constant pool: resolves indices to strings, names and references.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct ConstantPool(Vec<Constant>);

impl ConstantPool {
    pub fn get(&self, i: u16) -> Option<&Constant> {
        self.0.get(i as usize)
    }

    /// The UTF-8 text at `i`, if that entry is a `Utf8`.
    pub fn utf8(&self, i: u16) -> Option<&str> {
        match self.get(i)? {
            Constant::Utf8(s) => Some(s),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// The class name at `i` (a `Class` entry → its `Utf8` name).
    pub fn class_name(&self, i: u16) -> Option<String> {
        match self.get(i)? {
            Constant::Class(n) => self.utf8(*n).map(str::to_string),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    fn name_and_type(&self, i: u16) -> Option<(String, String)> {
        match self.get(i)? {
            Constant::NameAndType { name, desc } => {
                Some((self.utf8(*name)?.to_string(), self.utf8(*desc)?.to_string()))
            }
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// A human rendering of the entry at `i` — used for instruction-operand comments. References
    /// render as `Class.name:descriptor`, strings quoted, numbers as literals.
    pub fn resolve(&self, i: u16) -> String {
        match self.get(i) {
            None => format!("#{i}?"),
            Some(c) => match c {
                Constant::Utf8(s) => s.clone(),
                Constant::Integer(v) => v.to_string(),
                Constant::Float(v) => format!("{v}f"),
                Constant::Long(v) => format!("{v}L"),
                Constant::Double(v) => v.to_string(),
                Constant::Class(n) => self.utf8(*n).unwrap_or("?").to_string(),
                Constant::String(n) => format!("{:?}", self.utf8(*n).unwrap_or("?")),
                Constant::FieldRef { class, nat }
                | Constant::MethodRef { class, nat }
                | Constant::InterfaceMethodRef { class, nat } => {
                    let cls = self.class_name(*class).unwrap_or_else(|| "?".into());
                    match self.name_and_type(*nat) {
                        Some((n, d)) => format!("{cls}.{n}:{d}"),
                        None => format!("{cls}.#{nat}"),
                    }
                }
                Constant::NameAndType { name, desc } => format!(
                    "{}:{}",
                    self.utf8(*name).unwrap_or("?"),
                    self.utf8(*desc).unwrap_or("?")
                ),
                Constant::MethodHandle { kind, index } => format!("handle kind {kind} #{index}"),
                Constant::MethodType(d) => self.utf8(*d).unwrap_or("?").to_string(),
                Constant::Dynamic { nat, .. } | Constant::InvokeDynamic { nat, .. } => {
                    match self.name_and_type(*nat) {
                        Some((n, d)) => format!("{n}:{d}"),
                        None => format!("#{nat}"),
                    }
                }
                Constant::Module(n) | Constant::Package(n) => {
                    self.utf8(*n).unwrap_or("?").to_string()
                }
                Constant::Unusable => "(unusable)".to_string(),
            },
        }
    }
}

/// A caught-exception entry in a method's `Code`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct Exception {
    pub start: u16,
    pub end: u16,
    pub handler: u16,
    /// Caught class name, or `None` for a `finally` (catch-all).
    pub catch_type: Option<String>,
}

/// A method's executable code.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Code {
    pub max_stack: u16,
    pub max_locals: u16,
    pub bytecode: Vec<u8>,
    pub exceptions: Vec<Exception>,
}

/// A field or method.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Member {
    pub access: u16,
    pub name: String,
    pub descriptor: String,
    /// Methods: the decoded `Code` attribute, if present (absent for abstract/native).
    pub code: Option<Code>,
    /// Fields: the constant-pool index of a `ConstantValue` attribute (compile-time constant).
    pub constant_value: Option<u16>,
}

/// A parsed Java class file.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ClassFile {
    pub minor: u16,
    pub major: u16,
    pub access: u16,
    pub this_class: String,
    /// `None` only for `java/lang/Object`.
    pub super_class: Option<String>,
    pub interfaces: Vec<String>,
    pub fields: Vec<Member>,
    pub methods: Vec<Member>,
    pub source_file: Option<String>,
    pub cp: ConstantPool,
}

impl ClassFile {
    /// A readable Java platform version from the major version (`61` → `Java 17`).
    pub fn java_version(&self) -> String {
        match self.major {
            45 => "Java 1.1".into(),
            46 => "Java 1.2".into(),
            47 => "Java 1.3".into(),
            48 => "Java 1.4".into(),
            m if m >= 49 => format!("Java {}", m - 44),
            m => format!("class v{m}"),
        }
    }
}

/// True if `data` starts with the JVM class-file magic `0xCAFEBABE`.
pub fn is_class(data: &[u8]) -> bool {
    data.len() >= 4 && data[..4] == [0xCA, 0xFE, 0xBA, 0xBE]
}

/// Decodes class/field/method access flags into readable names.
pub fn access_flag_names(access: u16) -> Vec<&'static str> {
    const FLAGS: &[(u16, &str)] = &[
        (0x0001, "public"),
        (0x0002, "private"),
        (0x0004, "protected"),
        (0x0008, "static"),
        (0x0010, "final"),
        (0x0020, "synchronized"), // also ACC_SUPER on classes
        (0x0040, "volatile"),     // also ACC_BRIDGE on methods
        (0x0080, "transient"),    // also ACC_VARARGS
        (0x0100, "native"),
        (0x0200, "interface"),
        (0x0400, "abstract"),
        (0x0800, "strictfp"),
        (0x1000, "synthetic"),
        (0x2000, "annotation"),
        (0x4000, "enum"),
    ];
    FLAGS
        .iter()
        .filter(|&&(bit, _)| access & bit != 0)
        .map(|&(_, n)| n)
        .collect()
}

struct Reader<'a> {
    data: &'a [u8],
    pos: usize,
}

impl<'a> Reader<'a> {
    fn new(data: &'a [u8]) -> Self {
        Self { data, pos: 0 }
    }
    fn u1(&mut self) -> Result<u8, String> {
        let b = *self
            .data
            .get(self.pos)
            .ok_or("unexpected end of class file")?;
        self.pos += 1;
        Ok(b)
    }
    fn u2(&mut self) -> Result<u16, String> {
        Ok(u16::from_be_bytes([self.u1()?, self.u1()?]))
    }
    fn u4(&mut self) -> Result<u32, String> {
        Ok(u32::from_be_bytes([
            self.u1()?,
            self.u1()?,
            self.u1()?,
            self.u1()?,
        ]))
    }
    fn u8v(&mut self) -> Result<u64, String> {
        Ok((self.u4()? as u64) << 32 | self.u4()? as u64)
    }
    fn bytes(&mut self, n: usize) -> Result<&'a [u8], String> {
        let end = self.pos.checked_add(n).ok_or("length overflow")?;
        let s = self.data.get(self.pos..end).ok_or("truncated data")?;
        self.pos = end;
        Ok(s)
    }
    fn skip(&mut self, n: usize) -> Result<(), String> {
        self.bytes(n).map(|_| ())
    }
}

/// Parses a `.class` file.
pub fn parse(data: &[u8]) -> Result<ClassFile, String> {
    let mut r = Reader::new(data);
    if r.u4()? != 0xCAFE_BABE {
        return Err("not a Java class file (missing 0xCAFEBABE magic)".into());
    }
    let minor = r.u2()?;
    let major = r.u2()?;

    let cp = parse_constant_pool(&mut r)?;

    let access = r.u2()?;
    let this_idx = r.u2()?;
    let this_class = cp.class_name(this_idx).unwrap_or_else(|| "?".into());
    let super_idx = r.u2()?;
    let super_class = if super_idx == 0 {
        None
    } else {
        cp.class_name(super_idx)
    };

    let icount = r.u2()? as usize;
    let mut interfaces = Vec::with_capacity(icount.min(256));
    for _ in 0..icount {
        let idx = r.u2()?;
        interfaces.push(cp.class_name(idx).unwrap_or_else(|| "?".into()));
    }

    let fields = parse_members(&mut r, &cp, false)?;
    let methods = parse_members(&mut r, &cp, true)?;

    // Class-level attributes: pick up SourceFile; skip the rest.
    let mut source_file = None;
    let acount = r.u2()? as usize;
    for _ in 0..acount {
        let name = cp.utf8(r.u2()?).unwrap_or("").to_string();
        let len = r.u4()? as usize;
        if name == "SourceFile" && len == 2 {
            source_file = cp.utf8(r.u2()?).map(str::to_string);
        } else {
            r.skip(len)?;
        }
    }

    Ok(ClassFile {
        minor,
        major,
        access,
        this_class,
        super_class,
        interfaces,
        fields,
        methods,
        source_file,
        cp,
    })
}

fn parse_constant_pool(r: &mut Reader) -> Result<ConstantPool, String> {
    let count = r.u2()? as usize;
    if count == 0 {
        return Err("invalid constant pool count 0".into());
    }
    let mut pool = vec![Constant::Unusable]; // index 0 is unused
    let mut i = 1;
    while i < count {
        let tag = r.u1()?;
        let c = match tag {
            1 => {
                let len = r.u2()? as usize;
                Constant::Utf8(decode_mutf8(r.bytes(len)?))
            }
            3 => Constant::Integer(r.u4()? as i32),
            4 => Constant::Float(f32::from_bits(r.u4()?)),
            5 => Constant::Long(r.u8v()? as i64),
            6 => Constant::Double(f64::from_bits(r.u8v()?)),
            7 => Constant::Class(r.u2()?),
            8 => Constant::String(r.u2()?),
            9 => Constant::FieldRef {
                class: r.u2()?,
                nat: r.u2()?,
            },
            10 => Constant::MethodRef {
                class: r.u2()?,
                nat: r.u2()?,
            },
            11 => Constant::InterfaceMethodRef {
                class: r.u2()?,
                nat: r.u2()?,
            },
            12 => Constant::NameAndType {
                name: r.u2()?,
                desc: r.u2()?,
            },
            15 => Constant::MethodHandle {
                kind: r.u1()?,
                index: r.u2()?,
            },
            16 => Constant::MethodType(r.u2()?),
            17 => Constant::Dynamic {
                bootstrap: r.u2()?,
                nat: r.u2()?,
            },
            18 => Constant::InvokeDynamic {
                bootstrap: r.u2()?,
                nat: r.u2()?,
            },
            19 => Constant::Module(r.u2()?),
            20 => Constant::Package(r.u2()?),
            other => return Err(format!("unknown constant-pool tag {other}")),
        };
        let wide = matches!(c, Constant::Long(_) | Constant::Double(_));
        pool.push(c);
        i += 1;
        if wide {
            // Long/Double take two pool slots.
            pool.push(Constant::Unusable);
            i += 1;
        }
    }
    Ok(ConstantPool(pool))
}

fn parse_members(r: &mut Reader, cp: &ConstantPool, methods: bool) -> Result<Vec<Member>, String> {
    let count = r.u2()? as usize;
    if count > 65_535 {
        return Err("implausible member count".into());
    }
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(count.min(1024));
    for _ in 0..count {
        let access = r.u2()?;
        let name = cp.utf8(r.u2()?).unwrap_or("?").to_string();
        let descriptor = cp.utf8(r.u2()?).unwrap_or("?").to_string();
        let mut code = None;
        let mut constant_value = None;
        let acount = r.u2()? as usize;
        for _ in 0..acount {
            let aname = cp.utf8(r.u2()?).unwrap_or("").to_string();
            let len = r.u4()? as usize;
            match aname.as_str() {
                "Code" if methods => code = Some(parse_code(r, cp, len)?),
                "ConstantValue" if !methods && len == 2 => constant_value = Some(r.u2()?),
                _ => r.skip(len)?,
            }
        }
        out.push(Member {
            access,
            name,
            descriptor,
            code,
            constant_value,
        });
    }
    Ok(out)
}

fn parse_code(r: &mut Reader, cp: &ConstantPool, attr_len: usize) -> Result<Code, String> {
    let end = r.pos + attr_len;
    let max_stack = r.u2()?;
    let max_locals = r.u2()?;
    let code_len = r.u4()? as usize;
    let bytecode = r.bytes(code_len)?.to_vec();
    let ecount = r.u2()? as usize;
    let mut exceptions = Vec::with_capacity(ecount.min(256));
    for _ in 0..ecount {
        let start = r.u2()?;
        let end_pc = r.u2()?;
        let handler = r.u2()?;
        let ct = r.u2()?;
        exceptions.push(Exception {
            start,
            end: end_pc,
            handler,
            catch_type: (ct != 0).then(|| cp.class_name(ct).unwrap_or_else(|| "?".into())),
        });
    }
    // Skip the Code attribute's own sub-attributes (LineNumberTable, etc.).
    if end >= r.pos {
        r.skip(end - r.pos)?;
    }
    Ok(Code {
        max_stack,
        max_locals,
        bytecode,
        exceptions,
    })
}

/// Decodes Java's "modified UTF-8" to a Rust `String` (best-effort; invalid sequences become
/// U+FFFD). Handles 1/2/3-byte forms and the 6-byte supplementary-pair encoding, and `C0 80` NUL.
fn decode_mutf8(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(bytes.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < bytes.len() {
        let b = bytes[i];
        if b & 0x80 == 0 {
            out.push(b as char);
            i += 1;
        } else if b & 0xE0 == 0xC0 {
            if i + 1 < bytes.len() {
                let c = ((b as u32 & 0x1F) << 6) | (bytes[i + 1] as u32 & 0x3F);
                out.push(char::from_u32(c).unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}'));
            }
            i += 2;
        } else if b & 0xF0 == 0xE0 {
            // Could be a normal 3-byte char or half of a 6-byte surrogate pair.
            if i + 5 < bytes.len()
                && b == 0xED
                && (bytes[i + 1] & 0xF0) == 0xA0
                && bytes[i + 3] == 0xED
            {
                let hi = ((bytes[i + 1] as u32 & 0x0F) << 6) | (bytes[i + 2] as u32 & 0x3F);
                let lo = ((bytes[i + 4] as u32 & 0x0F) << 6) | (bytes[i + 5] as u32 & 0x3F);
                let c = 0x10000 + (hi << 10) + lo;
                out.push(char::from_u32(c).unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}'));
                i += 6;
            } else {
                if i + 2 < bytes.len() {
                    let c = ((b as u32 & 0x0F) << 12)
                        | ((bytes[i + 1] as u32 & 0x3F) << 6)
                        | (bytes[i + 2] as u32 & 0x3F);
                    out.push(char::from_u32(c).unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}'));
                }
                i += 3;
            }
        } else {
            out.push('\u{FFFD}');
            i += 1;
        }
    }
    out
}
```

```rs
use super::*;

/// A real class compiled by `javac 17` from `tests/fixtures/Check.java`.
const CLASS: &[u8] = include_bytes!("../tests/fixtures/Check.class");

fn parsed() -> ClassFile {
    parse(CLASS).expect("parse Check.class")
}

fn method<'a>(cf: &'a ClassFile, name: &str) -> &'a Member {
    cf.methods.iter().find(|m| m.name == name).expect("method")
}

#[test]
fn detects_and_parses_header() {
    assert!(is_class(CLASS));
    assert!(!is_class(b"MZ\x90\x00"));

    let cf = parsed();
    assert_eq!(cf.major, 61);
    assert_eq!(cf.minor, 0);
    assert_eq!(cf.java_version(), "Java 17");
    assert_eq!(cf.this_class, "Check");
    assert_eq!(cf.super_class.as_deref(), Some("java/lang/Object"));
    assert_eq!(cf.source_file.as_deref(), Some("Check.java"));
}

#[test]
fn recovers_fields_with_constant_value() {
    let cf = parsed();
    let names: Vec<&str> = cf.fields.iter().map(|f| f.name.as_str()).collect();
    assert_eq!(names, ["SECRET", "total"]);

    let secret = cf.fields.iter().find(|f| f.name == "SECRET").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(secret.descriptor, "Ljava/lang/String;");
    assert_eq!(access_flag_names(secret.access), ["static", "final"]);
    // The compile-time constant value is recovered — often where a flag hides.
    let cv = secret.constant_value.expect("ConstantValue");
    assert_eq!(cf.cp.resolve(cv), "\"flag{jvm_r3v3rs3}\"");

    let total = cf.fields.iter().find(|f| f.name == "total").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(total.descriptor, "I");
    assert!(total.constant_value.is_none());
}

#[test]
fn recovers_methods_and_descriptors() {
    let cf = parsed();
    let sigs: Vec<(&str, &str)> = cf
        .methods
        .iter()
        .map(|m| (m.name.as_str(), m.descriptor.as_str()))

#[test]
fn resolves_operands_and_branch_targets() {
    let cf = parsed();
    let code = method(&cf, "check").code.as_ref().unwrap();
    let ins = disassemble(code, &cf.cp);
    let at = |off: usize| ins.iter().find(|i| i.offset == off).unwrap();

    // Constant-pool references resolve to Class.name:descriptor.
    assert!(at(6).operands.contains("java/lang/String.length:()I"));
    assert!(at(15).operands.contains("java/lang/String.charAt:(I)C"));
    // Immediate operands.
    assert_eq!(at(19).operands, "7"); // bipush 7
    assert_eq!(at(32).operands, "1337"); // sipush 1337
    assert_eq!(at(25).operands, "3, 1"); // iinc 3, 1

    // Branch targets are absolute (relative offset + instruction address).
    assert_eq!(at(9).branch_target, Some(31)); // if_icmpge 31
    assert_eq!(at(28).branch_target, Some(4)); // goto 4 (loop back)
    assert_eq!(at(35).branch_target, Some(42)); // if_icmpne 42
    assert_eq!(at(39).branch_target, Some(43)); // goto 43

    // Landing sites are flagged.
    assert!(at(4).is_branch_target);
    assert!(at(31).is_branch_target);
    assert!(at(42).is_branch_target);
    assert!(at(43).is_branch_target);
    assert!(!at(0).is_branch_target);
}

#[test]
fn main_loads_the_string_literal() {
    let cf = parsed();
    let code = method(&cf, "main").code.as_ref().unwrap();
    let ins = disassemble(code, &cf.cp);
    // println("enter password:") → a ldc of the String constant.
    assert!(
        ins.iter()
            .any(|i| i.mnemonic == "ldc" && i.operands.contains("enter password:"))
    );
    assert!(ins.iter().any(
        |i| i.mnemonic == "invokevirtual" && i.operands.contains("java/io/PrintStream.println")
    ));
}

}
```
