`crates/orress-js/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! JavaScript deobfuscation and beautifying for ORRESS.
//!
//! Obfuscated JavaScript is a staple of CTF and of malware droppers (droppers hide URLs, commands
//! and payloads behind `\xNN` escapes, `String.fromCharCode(...)` and string concatenation). This
//! crate, built on a tokenizer (not a full parser), offers string-level transforms that reveal the
//! hidden text, a string extractor, and a beautifier that re-indents minified code. Pure `std`,
//! never panics, always produces output.
//!
//! The transforms are deliberately conservative: they only rewrite what they can decode certainly
//! (string literals, numeric `fromCharCode`, literal concatenation), leaving everything else
//! verbatim — so the result stays valid and nothing is silently lost.

mod token;

pub use token::{Tok, Token, tokenize};

/// Decodes the escape sequences inside a string's content (without the surrounding quotes):
/// `\xNN`, `\uNNNN`, `\u{…}`, octal `\NNN`, the named escapes and line continuations.
pub fn decode_escapes(inner: &str) -> String {
    let c: Vec<char> = inner.chars().collect();
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(c.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < c.len() {
        if c[i] != '\\' {
            out.push(c[i]);
            i += 1;
            continue;
        }
        i += 1;
        if i >= c.len() {
            out.push('\\');
            break;
        }
        let e = c[i];
        match e {
            'n' => out.push('\n'),
            't' => out.push('\t'),
            'r' => out.push('\r'),
            'b' => out.push('\u{08}'),
            'f' => out.push('\u{0C}'),
            'v' => out.push('\u{0B}'),
            'x' => {
                if let Some(ch) = take_hex(&c, i + 1, 2) {
                    out.push(ch);
                    i += 2;
                } else {
                    out.push('x');
                }
            }
            'u' => {
                if c.get(i + 1) == Some(&'{') {
                    // \u{H+}
                    let mut j = i + 2;
                    let mut v: u32 = 0;
                    let mut any = false;
                    while j < c.len() && c[j] != '}' {
                        match c[j].to_digit(16) {
                            Some(d) => {
                                v = v.saturating_mul(16) + d;
                                any = true;
                            }
                            None => break,
                        }
                        j += 1;
                    }
                    if any && c.get(j) == Some(&'}') {
                        out.push(char::from_u32(v).unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}'));
                        i = j;
                    } else {
                        out.push('u');
                    }
                } else if let Some(ch) = take_hex(&c, i + 1, 4) {
                    out.push(ch);
                    i += 4;
                } else {
                    out.push('u');
                }
            }
            '0'..='7' => {
                // Octal escape \NNN (1–3 octal digits); `\0` alone decodes to NUL.
                let mut v = e.to_digit(8).unwrap();
                let mut taken = 0;
                while taken < 2 && c.get(i + 1).and_then(|d| d.to_digit(8)).is_some() {
                    v = v * 8 + c[i + 1].to_digit(8).unwrap();
                    i += 1;
                    taken += 1;
                }
                out.push(char::from_u32(v).unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}'));
            }
            '\n' => {} // line continuation
            other => out.push(other),
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    out
}

fn take_hex(c: &[char], start: usize, len: usize) -> Option<char> {
    if start + len > c.len() {
        return None;
    }
    let mut v: u32 = 0;
    for &ch in &c[start..start + len] {
        v = v * 16 + ch.to_digit(16)?;
    }
    char::from_u32(v)
}

/// Re-quotes decoded text as a double-quoted JS string literal, re-escaping what must be escaped.
fn requote(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len() + 2);
    out.push('"');
    for ch in s.chars() {
        match ch {
            '"' => out.push_str("\\\""),
            '\\' => out.push_str("\\\\"),
            '\n' => out.push_str("\\n"),
            '\r' => out.push_str("\\r"),
            '\t' => out.push_str("\\t"),
            c if (c as u32) < 0x20 => out.push_str(&format!("\\x{:02x}", c as u32)),
            c => out.push(c),
        }
    }
    out.push('"');
    out
}

/// Strips a string/template token's surrounding quotes, returning the inner content.
fn inner_of(text: &str) -> &str {
    let b = text.as_bytes();
    if b.len() >= 2 && (b[b.len() - 1] == b[0]) {
        &text[1..text.len() - 1]
    } else {
        &text[1..] // unterminated
    }
}

/// Rewrites every string literal to its escape-decoded form (templates keep their backticks).
pub fn decode_string_literals(src: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(src.len());
    for t in tokenize(src) {
        match t.kind {
            Tok::Str => out.push_str(&requote(&decode_escapes(inner_of(&t.text)))),
            Tok::Template => out.push_str(&decode_template(&t.text)),
            _ => out.push_str(&t.text),
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Escape-decodes a template literal's literal text while keeping it a valid template: `${…}`
/// interpolations are copied verbatim, and in the decoded text the characters that would end or
/// interpolate the template (`` ` ``, `\`, `${`) are re-escaped, so repeated passes are stable.
fn decode_template(text: &str) -> String {
    let c: Vec<char> = inner_of(text).chars().collect();
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len());
    out.push('`');
    let mut lit = String::new();
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < c.len() {
        if c[i] == '\\' {
            lit.push(c[i]);
            if let Some(&n) = c.get(i + 1) {
                lit.push(n);
            }
            i += 2;
            continue;
        }
        if c[i] == '$' && c.get(i + 1) == Some(&'{') {
            out.push_str(&escape_template(&decode_escapes(&lit)));
            lit.clear();
            // Copy the interpolation through its matching `}` (nested braces counted).
            let mut depth = 0usize;
            while i < c.len() {
                out.push(c[i]);
                match c[i] {
                    '{' => depth += 1,
                    '}' => {
                        depth -= 1;
                        if depth == 0 {
                            i += 1;
                            break;
                        }
                    }
                    _ => {}
                }
                i += 1;
            }
            continue;
        }
        lit.push(c[i]);
        i += 1;
    }
    out.push_str(&escape_template(&decode_escapes(&lit)));
    out.push('`');
    out
}

/// Escapes decoded text for the literal part of a template.
fn escape_template(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    let mut it = s.chars().peekable();
    while let Some(ch) = it.next() {
        match ch {
            '`' => out.push_str("\\`"),
            '\\' => out.push_str("\\\\"),
            '$' if it.peek() == Some(&'{') => out.push_str("\\$"),
            '\r' => out.push_str("\\r"),
            c if (c as u32) < 0x20 && c != '\n' && c != '\t' => {
                out.push_str(&format!("\\x{:02x}", c as u32))
            }
            c => out.push(c),
        }
    }
    out
}

fn is_trivia(t: &Token) -> bool {
    matches!(t.kind, Tok::Space | Tok::LineComment | Tok::BlockComment)
}

/// Folds every call `[recv.]name(args)` whose arguments `f` can decode into a string literal
/// (a plain identifier receiver chain such as `window.String.` is replaced too). Works on tokens,
/// so text inside strings, comments and regexes is never touched. Calls `f` returns `None` for —
/// and calls on a computed receiver (`x["String"].fromCharCode(…)`, `f().atob(…)`) — are left
/// verbatim.
fn fold_calls(src: &str, name: &str, f: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<String>) -> String {
    let toks = tokenize(src);
    let prev_sig = |from: usize| (0..from).rev().find(|&i| !is_trivia(&toks[i]));
    let next_sig = |from: usize| (from..toks.len()).find(|&i| !is_trivia(&toks[i]));
    let is_punct = |i: usize, p: &str| toks[i].kind == Tok::Punct && toks[i].text == p;

    let mut out = String::with_capacity(src.len());
    // `marks[i]` = length of `out` before token `i` was emitted, so a receiver chain that was
    // already emitted can be taken back.
    let mut marks = Vec::with_capacity(toks.len());
    let mut ti = 0;
    while ti < toks.len() {
        marks.push(out.len());
        let t = &toks[ti];
        if t.kind == Tok::Ident
            && t.text == name
            && let Some(open) = next_sig(ti + 1)
            && is_punct(open, "(")
        {
            // Walk the receiver chain back: `a.b.name` → start at `a`.
            let mut start = ti;
            let mut computed = false;
            while let Some(dot) = prev_sig(start)
                && is_punct(dot, ".")
            {
                match prev_sig(dot) {
                    Some(r) if toks[r].kind == Tok::Ident => start = r,
                    _ => {
                        computed = true; // `]`, `)`, `?.`, … — not a plain name chain
                        break;
                    }
                }
            }
            if !computed && let Some(close) = matching_paren_tok(&toks, open) {
                let args: String = toks[open + 1..close]
                    .iter()
                    .map(|t| t.text.as_str())
                    .collect();
                if let Some(decoded) = f(&args) {
                    out.truncate(marks[start]);
                    out.push_str(&requote(&decoded));
                    // Keep `marks` aligned for the tokens being skipped.
                    marks.resize(close + 1, out.len());
                    ti = close + 1;
                    continue;
                }
            }
        }
        out.push_str(&t.text);
        ti += 1;
    }
    out
}

/// Index of the token closing the bracket opened at `open` (counting nested brackets).
fn matching_paren_tok(toks: &[Token], open: usize) -> Option<usize> {
    let mut depth = 0usize;
    for (i, t) in toks.iter().enumerate().skip(open) {
        if t.kind != Tok::Punct {
            continue;
        }
        match t.text.as_str() {
            "(" | "[" | "{" => depth += 1,
            ")" | "]" | "}" => {
                depth = depth.checked_sub(1)?;
                if depth == 0 {
                    return Some(i);
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    None
}

/// Folds `X.fromCharCode(n, n, …)` with integer arguments into the decoded string literal.
pub fn fold_fromcharcode(src: &str) -> String {
    fold_calls(src, "fromCharCode", decode_char_codes)
}

/// Folds `atob("…")` (base64 decode) into the decoded string, when the result is valid UTF-8.
pub fn fold_atob(src: &str) -> String {
    fold_calls(src, "atob", |inner| {
        let bytes = base64_decode(&single_string_arg(inner)?)?;
        String::from_utf8(bytes).ok()
    })
}

/// Folds `unescape("…")` / `decodeURIComponent("…")` (percent-decode) into the decoded string.
pub fn fold_unescape(src: &str) -> String {
    let unescape = |inner: &str| single_string_arg(inner).map(|s| unescape_decode(&s));
    let uri = |inner: &str| single_string_arg(inner).and_then(|s| uri_decode(&s));
    fold_calls(
        &fold_calls(src, "unescape", unescape),
        "decodeURIComponent",
        uri,
    )
}

/// If `inner` is exactly one string literal, returns its escape-decoded content.
fn single_string_arg(inner: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let sig: Vec<Token> = tokenize(inner)
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|t| t.kind != Tok::Space)
        .collect();
    match sig.as_slice() {
        [t] if t.kind == Tok::Str => Some(decode_escapes(inner_of(&t.text))),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Decodes standard base64 (padding optional; whitespace ignored). `None` on invalid input.
fn base64_decode(s: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    fn val(c: u8) -> Option<u32> {
        match c {
            b'A'..=b'Z' => Some((c - b'A') as u32),
            b'a'..=b'z' => Some((c - b'a' + 26) as u32),
            b'0'..=b'9' => Some((c - b'0' + 52) as u32),
            b'+' => Some(62),
            b'/' => Some(63),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
    let mut acc = 0u32;
    let mut bits = 0;
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for &c in s.as_bytes() {
        if c == b'=' || c.is_ascii_whitespace() {
            continue;
        }
        let v = val(c)?;
        acc = (acc << 6) | v;
        bits += 6;
        if bits >= 8 {
            bits -= 8;
            out.push((acc >> bits) as u8);
        }
    }
    Some(out)
}

/// `hex` digits starting at `start` as a number (exactly `len` of them), or `None`.
fn hex_value(c: &[char], start: usize, len: usize) -> Option<u32> {
    let digits = c.get(start..start + len)?;
    digits
        .iter()
        .try_fold(0u32, |v, ch| Some(v * 16 + ch.to_digit(16)?))
}

/// JS `unescape`: `%xx` is a Latin-1 code unit and `%uXXXX` a UTF-16 code unit (so surrogate
/// pairs combine); malformed sequences and other characters pass through.
fn unescape_decode(s: &str) -> String {
    let c: Vec<char> = s.chars().collect();
    let mut units: Vec<u16> = Vec::with_capacity(c.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < c.len() {
        if c[i] == '%' {
            if c.get(i + 1) == Some(&'u')
                && let Some(v) = hex_value(&c, i + 2, 4)
            {
                units.push(v as u16);
                i += 6;
                continue;
            }
            if let Some(v) = hex_value(&c, i + 1, 2) {
                units.push(v as u16);
                i += 3;
                continue;
            }
        }
        let mut buf = [0u16; 2];
        units.extend_from_slice(c[i].encode_utf16(&mut buf));
        i += 1;
    }
    decode_utf16_lossy(&units)
}

/// JS `decodeURIComponent`: `%xx` sequences are UTF-8 bytes. `None` where JS would throw a
/// `URIError` (malformed `%`, invalid UTF-8), so the call is left as written.
fn uri_decode(s: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let c: Vec<char> = s.chars().collect();
    let mut bytes: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(c.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < c.len() {
        if c[i] == '%' {
            bytes.push(hex_value(&c, i + 1, 2)? as u8);
            i += 3;
            continue;
        }
        let mut buf = [0u8; 4];
        bytes.extend_from_slice(c[i].encode_utf8(&mut buf).as_bytes());
        i += 1;
    }
    String::from_utf8(bytes).ok()
}

/// UTF-16 code units to a string; lone surrogates become U+FFFD.
fn decode_utf16_lossy(units: &[u16]) -> String {
    char::decode_utf16(units.iter().copied())
        .map(|r| r.unwrap_or(char::REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER))
        .collect()
}

/// Decodes a comma-separated list of integer literals to a string, or `None` if any arg isn't a
/// plain integer (so a `fromCharCode` with computed arguments is left untouched). Like JS, each
/// value is truncated to a UTF-16 code unit (`v & 0xFFFF`) and surrogate pairs combine.
fn decode_char_codes(args: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let args = args.trim();
    if args.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let mut units = Vec::new();
    for part in args.split(',') {
        let p = part.trim();
        let v = if let Some(hex) = p.strip_prefix("0x").or_else(|| p.strip_prefix("0X")) {
            u64::from_str_radix(hex, 16).ok()?
        } else {
            p.parse::<u64>().ok()?
        };
        units.push((v & 0xFFFF) as u16);
    }
    Some(decode_utf16_lossy(&units))
}

/// Folds adjacent string-literal concatenations (`"a" + "b"` → `"ab"`) at the token level.
pub fn fold_concat(src: &str) -> String {
    let toks = tokenize(src);
    // Build a list of significant-token indices for easy lookahead.
    let mut out: Vec<Token> = Vec::with_capacity(toks.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < toks.len() {
        if toks[i].kind == Tok::Str {
            // Look ahead for ( Space* '+' Space* Str )+ chains.
            let mut combined = decode_escapes(inner_of(&toks[i].text));
            let mut j = i + 1;
            let mut matched_any = false;
            loop {
                let plus = skip_space(&toks, j);
                if toks.get(plus).map(|t| (t.kind, t.text.as_str())) != Some((Tok::Punct, "+")) {
                    break;
                }
                let next = skip_space(&toks, plus + 1);
                match toks.get(next) {
                    Some(t) if t.kind == Tok::Str => {
                        combined.push_str(&decode_escapes(inner_of(&t.text)));
                        j = next + 1;
                        matched_any = true;
                    }
                    _ => break,
                }
            }
            if matched_any {
                out.push(Token {
                    kind: Tok::Str,
                    text: requote(&combined),
                });
                i = j;
                continue;
            }
        }
        out.push(toks[i].clone());
        i += 1;
    }
    out.iter().map(|t| t.text.as_str()).collect()
}

fn skip_space(toks: &[Token], mut i: usize) -> usize {
    while toks.get(i).map(|t| t.kind) == Some(Tok::Space) {
        i += 1;
    }
    i
}

/// Methods that mutate an array in place; calling one on the table makes it unsafe to inline.
const ARRAY_MUTATORS: &[&str] = &[
    "push",
    "pop",
    "shift",
    "unshift",
    "splice",
    "reverse",
    "sort",
    "fill",
    "copyWithin",
];

/// Replaces `NAME[i]` with the literal from a single top-level literal string array
/// (`var NAME = ['a','b',…];`). This is the common string-table obfuscation (the non-rotated
/// form). Any sign that the table might not hold its initial contents at a use site poisons the
/// name and leaves every use alone: a reassignment (`NAME = …`, `NAME += …`, `++NAME`), an element
/// write (`NAME[…] = …`, `delete NAME[…]`), a mutating method call (`NAME.push(…)`, `.shift()`,
/// `.splice()`, …), a second declaration, the name appearing as a function/arrow/catch parameter
/// (shadowing), or appearing as a property (`obj.NAME`).
pub fn fold_string_array(src: &str) -> String {
    use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};
    let toks = tokenize(src);
    let sig: Vec<usize> = (0..toks.len()).filter(|&i| !is_trivia(&toks[i])).collect();
    let at = |k: usize| sig.get(k).map(|&i| &toks[i]);
    let kv = |k: usize| at(k).map(|t| (t.kind, t.text.as_str()));
    let punct = |k: usize, p: &str| kv(k) == Some((Tok::Punct, p));
    let ident = |k: usize| {
        at(k)
            .filter(|t| t.kind == Tok::Ident)
            .map(|t| t.text.as_str())
    };
    let prev_punct = |k: usize, p: &str| k > 0 && punct(k - 1, p);
    // Sig index of the bracket closing the one opened at sig index `open`.
    let close_of = |open: usize| {
        let mut depth = 0usize;
        for j in open..sig.len() {
            match kv(j) {
                Some((Tok::Punct, "(" | "[" | "{")) => depth += 1,
                Some((Tok::Punct, ")" | "]" | "}")) => {
                    depth = depth.checked_sub(1)?;
                    if depth == 0 {
                        return Some(j);
                    }
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        None
    };
    // Sig index of the bracket opening the one closed at sig index `close`.
    let open_of = |close: usize| {
        let mut depth = 0usize;
        for j in (0..=close).rev() {
            match kv(j) {
                Some((Tok::Punct, ")" | "]" | "}")) => depth += 1,
                Some((Tok::Punct, "(" | "[" | "{")) => {
                    depth = depth.checked_sub(1)?;
                    if depth == 0 {
                        return Some(j);
                    }
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        None
    };
    // Whether an assignment / update operator starts at sig index `j` (`=`, `+=`, `>>>=`, `??=`,
    // `++`, `--`, … but not `==`, `!=`, `<=`, `=>`).
    let assigns = |j: usize| {
        let mut op = String::new();
        let mut j = j;
        while let Some((Tok::Punct, p)) = kv(j) {
            if !"+-*/%<>&|^?!=".contains(p) || op.len() >= 4 {
                break;
            }
            op.push_str(p);
            j += 1;
            if p == "=" {
                break;
            }
        }
        if op.starts_with("++") || op.starts_with("--") {
            return true;
        }
        let Some(prefix) = op.strip_suffix('=') else {
            return false;
        };
        !punct(j, "=")
            && !punct(j, ">")
            && matches!(
                prefix,
                "" | "+"
                    | "-"
                    | "*"
                    | "/"
                    | "%"
                    | "**"
                    | "<<"
                    | ">>"
                    | ">>>"
                    | "&"
                    | "|"
                    | "^"
                    | "&&"
                    | "||"
                    | "??"
            )
    };

    // Pass A: collect literal arrays by name; `None` marks a second definition.
    let mut arrays: HashMap<String, Option<Vec<String>>> = HashMap::new();
    let mut poisoned: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
    let mut declarations: HashMap<String, usize> = HashMap::new();
    let poison_idents = |from: usize, to: usize, poisoned: &mut HashSet<String>| {
        for j in from..=to {
            if let Some(n) = ident(j) {
                poisoned.insert(n.to_string());
            }
        }
    };
    let mut k = 0;
    while k < sig.len() {
        // Parameters shadow outer names: `function f(a, b)`, `catch (e)`, `(a, b) =>`, `a =>`.
        if punct(k, "=") && punct(k + 1, ">") && k > 0 {
            if ident(k - 1).is_some() {
                poison_idents(k - 1, k - 1, &mut poisoned);
            } else if punct(k - 1, ")")
                && let Some(open) = open_of(k - 1)
            {
                poison_idents(open, k - 1, &mut poisoned);
            }
        }
        let Some(name) = ident(k) else {
            k += 1;
            continue;
        };
        if matches!(name, "function" | "catch") {
            let open = if punct(k + 1, "(") { k + 1 } else { k + 2 };
            if punct(open, "(")
                && let Some(close) = close_of(open)
            {
                poison_idents(k + 1, close, &mut poisoned); // name + params
            }
            k += 1;
            continue;
        }
        let name = name.to_string();
        if prev_punct(k, ".") {
            // `obj.NAME` is some other object's property; don't guess, poison.
            poisoned.insert(name);
            k += 1;
            continue;
        }
        if k > 0 && matches!(ident(k - 1), Some("var" | "let" | "const")) {
            *declarations.entry(name.clone()).or_default() += 1;
        }
        if k >= 2
            && ((punct(k - 1, "+") && punct(k - 2, "+"))
                || (punct(k - 1, "-") && punct(k - 2, "-")))
        {
            poisoned.insert(name.clone()); // ++NAME / --NAME
        }
        if punct(k + 1, ".") && ident(k + 2).is_some_and(|m| ARRAY_MUTATORS.contains(&m)) {
            poisoned.insert(name.clone());
        }
        if punct(k + 1, "[") {
            // Element write: `NAME[…] = …`, `NAME[…]++`, `delete NAME[…]`.
            let writes = close_of(k + 1).is_some_and(|close| assigns(close + 1))
                || (k > 0 && ident(k - 1) == Some("delete"));
            if writes {
                poisoned.insert(name.clone());
            }
        }
        if punct(k + 1, "=") && punct(k + 2, "[") {
            let mut vals = Vec::new();
            let mut j = k + 3;
            let mut expect_str = true;
            let mut ok = true;
            loop {
                match kv(j) {
                    Some((Tok::Punct, "]")) => break,
                    Some((Tok::Str, _)) if expect_str => {
                        vals.push(decode_escapes(inner_of(&at(j).unwrap().text)));
                        expect_str = false;
                        j += 1;
                    }
                    Some((Tok::Punct, ",")) if !expect_str => {
                        expect_str = true;
                        j += 1;
                    }
                    _ => {
                        ok = false;
                        break;
                    }
                }
            }
            if ok {
                arrays
                    .entry(name)
                    .and_modify(|e| *e = None) // second definition → poison
                    .or_insert(Some(vals));
                k = j + 1;
                continue;
            }
            poisoned.insert(name);
        } else if assigns(k + 1) {
            // Any other assignment to (or update of) the name poisons it.
            poisoned.insert(name);
        }
        k += 1;
    }
    for (name, n) in declarations {
        if n > 1 {
            poisoned.insert(name);
        }
    }
    let clean: HashMap<String, Vec<String>> = arrays
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|(k, _)| !poisoned.contains(k))
        .filter_map(|(k, v)| v.map(|vv| (k, vv)))
        .collect();
    if clean.is_empty() {
        return src.to_string();
    }

    // Pass B: replace `NAME[int]` (read positions only) with the literal.
    let mut sig_of = vec![usize::MAX; toks.len()];
    for (s, &ti) in sig.iter().enumerate() {
        sig_of[ti] = s;
    }
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(src.len());
    let mut ti = 0;
    while ti < toks.len() {
        let t = &toks[ti];
        let s = sig_of[ti];
        if t.kind == Tok::Ident
            && let Some(arr) = clean.get(&t.text)
            && !prev_punct(s, ".")
            && punct(s + 1, "[")
            && kv(s + 2).map(|(k, _)| k) == Some(Tok::Number)
            && punct(s + 3, "]")
            && !assigns(s + 4)
            && let Ok(idx) = at(s + 2).unwrap().text.parse::<usize>()
            && let Some(val) = arr.get(idx)
        {
            out.push_str(&requote(val));
            ti = sig[s + 3] + 1;
            continue;
        }
        out.push_str(&t.text);
        ti += 1;
    }
    out
}

/// Applies the deobfuscation transforms repeatedly until the source stops changing (bounded), so
/// layered obfuscation (array lookups → fromCharCode → escapes → concatenation) is unwound.
pub fn deobfuscate(src: &str) -> String {
    let mut cur = src.to_string();
    for _ in 0..6 {
        let step = fold_string_array(&cur);
        let step = fold_fromcharcode(&step);
        let step = fold_atob(&step);
        let step = fold_unescape(&step);
        let step = fold_concat(&step);
        let next = decode_string_literals(&step);
        if next == cur {
            break;
        }
        cur = next;
    }
    cur
}

/// Every string literal's decoded text, in source order (deduplicated, blanks dropped).
pub fn extract_strings(src: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut seen = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for t in tokenize(src) {
        if matches!(t.kind, Tok::Str | Tok::Template) {
            let d = decode_escapes(inner_of(&t.text));
            if !d.trim().is_empty() && seen.insert(d.clone()) {
                out.push(d);
            }
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Re-indents minified JavaScript. Not a pretty-printer — it adds newlines around `{}` and after
/// `;`, indents blocks, and spaces word boundaries, enough to read the structure. The token stream
/// is preserved (only whitespace changes).
pub fn beautify(src: &str) -> String {
    // Drop whitespace, but remember what separated each token from the previous one: a space
    // (so `a - -b` doesn't fuse into `a--b`) or a newline (so ASI after `return` is kept).
    let mut toks: Vec<Token> = Vec::new();
    let mut gap: Vec<Gap> = Vec::new();
    let mut pending = Gap::None;
    for t in tokenize(src) {
        if t.kind == Tok::Space {
            pending = if t.text.contains('\n') || pending == Gap::Newline {
                Gap::Newline
            } else {
                Gap::Space
            };
            continue;
        }
        toks.push(t);
        gap.push(std::mem::replace(&mut pending, Gap::None));
    }
    let mut out = String::new();
    let mut indent: usize = 0;
    let nl = |out: &mut String, indent: usize| {
        out.push('\n');
        out.push_str(&"  ".repeat(indent));
    };
    for idx in 0..toks.len() {
        let t = &toks[idx];
        let prev = idx.checked_sub(1).map(|i| &toks[i]);
        let next = toks.get(idx + 1);
        match (t.kind, t.text.as_str()) {
            (Tok::Punct, "{") => {
                if needs_space_before_brace(prev) {
                    out.push(' ');
                }
                out.push('{');
                indent += 1;
                nl(&mut out, indent);
            }
            (Tok::Punct, "}") => {
                indent = indent.saturating_sub(1);
                trim_trailing_ws(&mut out);
                nl(&mut out, indent);
                out.push('}');
                // Start a new line after a block, unless a continuation follows it.
                let continues = matches!(
                    next.map(|n| (n.kind, n.text.as_str())),
                    Some((Tok::Punct, ";" | "," | ")" | "]" | "."))
                        | Some((Tok::Ident, "else" | "catch" | "finally" | "while"))
                );
                if next.is_some() && !continues {
                    nl(&mut out, indent);
                }
            }
            (Tok::Punct, ";") => {
                out.push(';');
                if next.map(|n| n.text.as_str()) != Some("}") {
                    nl(&mut out, indent);
                }
            }
            (Tok::Punct, ",") => out.push_str(", "),
            (Tok::LineComment, _) => {
                out.push_str(&t.text);
                nl(&mut out, indent);
            }
            _ => {
                if keeps_line_break(prev, t, next, gap[idx]) {
                    trim_trailing_ws(&mut out);
                    nl(&mut out, indent);
                } else if needs_space(prev, t, gap[idx]) {
                    out.push(' ');
                }
                out.push_str(&t.text);
            }
        }
    }
    out.trim().to_string()
}

/// What separated a token from the previous one in the source.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Gap {
    None,
    Space,
    Newline,
}

/// A source line break that automatic semicolon insertion depends on: after `return`, `break`,
/// `continue`, `throw` or `yield` (a newline there ends the statement), and before a prefix
/// `++`/`--`.
fn keeps_line_break(prev: Option<&Token>, cur: &Token, next: Option<&Token>, gap: Gap) -> bool {
    if gap != Gap::Newline {
        return false;
    }
    let Some(p) = prev else { return false };
    let restricted = p.kind == Tok::Ident
        && matches!(
            p.text.as_str(),
            "return" | "break" | "continue" | "throw" | "yield"
        );
    let prefix_update = cur.kind == Tok::Punct
        && matches!(cur.text.as_str(), "+" | "-")
        && next.is_some_and(|n| n.kind == Tok::Punct && n.text == cur.text);
    restricted || prefix_update
}

fn trim_trailing_ws(out: &mut String) {
    while out.ends_with(' ') || out.ends_with('\n') {
        out.pop();
    }
}

fn needs_space_before_brace(prev: Option<&Token>) -> bool {
    matches!(prev, Some(t) if t.kind == Tok::Ident || matches!(t.text.as_str(), ")" | "="))
}

fn is_word(t: &Token) -> bool {
    matches!(
        t.kind,
        Tok::Ident | Tok::Number | Tok::Str | Tok::Template | Tok::Regex
    )
}

fn needs_space(prev: Option<&Token>, cur: &Token, gap: Gap) -> bool {
    let Some(p) = prev else { return false };
    // Keep word tokens apart, and put a space after control keywords before `(`.
    if is_word(p) && is_word(cur) {
        return true;
    }
    if gap != Gap::None {
        // Operators are single-character tokens; ones that were apart in the source must stay
        // apart (`a - -b`, `a + +b`, `x = /re/` after `/`), or they would fuse into another.
        const OPS: &str = "+-*/%<>=!&|^?.";
        if p.kind == Tok::Punct
            && cur.kind == Tok::Punct
            && OPS.contains(p.text.as_str())
            && OPS.contains(cur.text.as_str())
        {
            return true;
        }
        // Anything else that would re-lex differently when joined (`1 .x` → `1.x`, `a / /re/`).
        let joined = format!("{}{}", p.text, cur.text);
        let relexed = tokenize(&joined);
        if relexed.len() != 2 || relexed[0] != *p || relexed[1] != *cur {
            return true;
        }
    }
    if p.kind == Tok::Ident
        && cur.kind == Tok::Punct
        && cur.text == "("
        && matches!(
            p.text.as_str(),
            "if" | "for" | "while" | "switch" | "catch" | "return" | "function" | "do"
        )
    {
        return true;
    }
    false
}
```

```rs
use super::*;

#[test]
fn tokenizes_strings_regex_and_division() {
    // `/` after `=` is a regex; after `)` it is division.
    let raw = tokenize("var x = /ab\\/c/g; y = (a)/b");
    let toks: Vec<(Tok, &str)> = raw
        .iter()
        .filter(|t| t.kind != Tok::Space)
        .map(|t| (t.kind, t.text.as_str()))
        .collect();
    assert!(toks.contains(&(Tok::Regex, "/ab\\/c/g")));
    // The second slash is division (Punct), not a regex.
    assert_eq!(toks.iter().filter(|(k, _)| *k == Tok::Regex).count(), 1);
    assert!(toks.contains(&(Tok::Punct, "/")));
}

#[test]
fn decodes_hex_unicode_and_octal_escapes() {
    assert_eq!(decode_escapes("\\x66\\x6c\\x61\\x67"), "flag");
    assert_eq!(decode_escapes("\\u0041\\u{1F600}"), "A\u{1F600}");
    assert_eq!(decode_escapes("\\110\\151"), "Hi"); // octal H, i
    assert_eq!(decode_escapes("a\\tb\\nc"), "a\tb\nc");
}

#[test]
fn decodes_string_literals_in_place() {
    let src = "var u = \"\\x68\\x74\\x74\\x70://evil\"; call(u)";
    let out = decode_string_literals(src);
    assert!(out.contains("\"http://evil\""), "{out}");
    // Non-string text is preserved verbatim.
    assert!(out.contains("var u = "));
    assert!(out.contains("; call(u)"));
}

#[test]
fn folds_fromcharcode() {
    assert_eq!(
        fold_fromcharcode("var s=String.fromCharCode(102,108,97,103);"),
        "var s=\"flag\";"
    );
    // Hex args work too.
    assert_eq!(
        fold_fromcharcode("x=String.fromCharCode(0x41,0x42)"),
        "x=\"AB\""
    );
    // Non-integer args are left untouched.
    let keep = "String.fromCharCode(a,b)";
    assert_eq!(fold_fromcharcode(keep), keep);
}

#[test]
fn folds_string_concatenation() {
    assert_eq!(
        fold_concat("x = \"ab\" + \"cd\" + \"ef\";"),
        "x = \"abcdef\";"
    );
    // A non-string operand stops the fold.
    assert_eq!(fold_concat("\"a\" + b + \"c\""), "\"a\" + b + \"c\"");
}

#[test]
fn deobfuscate_unwinds_layered_obfuscation() {
    // fromCharCode builds "ev", concatenated with an escaped "al(1)".
    let src = "var f = String.fromCharCode(101,118) + \"\\x61\\x6c(1)\";";
    let out = deobfuscate(src);
    assert!(out.contains("\"eval(1)\""), "{out}");
}

#[test]
fn folds_atob_base64() {
    // atob("ZXZpbC5jb20=") == "evil.com"
    assert_eq!(
        fold_atob("var h=atob(\"ZXZpbC5jb20=\");"),
        "var h=\"evil.com\";"
    );
    // window.atob receiver is replaced too.
    assert_eq!(fold_atob("x=window.atob(\"QUI=\")"), "x=\"AB\"");
    // Non-base64 / binary result is left alone.
    let keep = "atob(someVar)";
    assert_eq!(fold_atob(keep), keep);
}

#[test]
fn folds_unescape_percent() {
    assert_eq!(fold_unescape("unescape(\"%41%42%43\")"), "\"ABC\"");
    assert_eq!(fold_unescape("decodeURIComponent(\"a%20b\")"), "\"a b\"");
    assert_eq!(fold_unescape("unescape(\"%u0041!\")"), "\"A!\"");
}

#[test]
fn dereferences_literal_string_array() {
    let src = "var _a=['ht','tp','://x'];var u=_a[0]+_a[1]+_a[2];";
    let out = fold_string_array(src);
    assert_eq!(
        out,
        "var _a=['ht','tp','://x'];var u=\"ht\"+\"tp\"+\"://x\";"
    );
    // And the full pipeline collapses it to one URL string.
    assert!(deobfuscate(src).contains("\"http://x\""));
}

#[test]
fn reassigned_array_is_left_alone() {
    // _a is reassigned, so indexing must not be substituted (unsound otherwise).
    let src = "var _a=['x','y'];_a=getArray();f(_a[0]);";
    assert_eq!(fold_string_array(src), src);
}

#[test]
fn deobfuscate_combines_array_atob_and_escapes() {
    let src = "var s=['ZXZhbA==','\\x28\\x31\\x29'];var r=atob(s[0])+s[1];";
    let out = deobfuscate(src);
    assert!(out.contains("\"eval(1)\""), "{out}");
}

#[test]
fn extracts_decoded_strings() {
    let src = "a(\"\\x66\\x6c\\x61\\x67{js}\"); b('plain'); c(\"\")";
    let strings = extract_strings(src);
    assert!(strings.contains(&"flag{js}".to_string()));
    assert!(strings.contains(&"plain".to_string()));
    // Empty strings are dropped.
    assert!(!strings.iter().any(|s| s.is_empty()));
}

#[test]
fn beautify_indents_and_preserves_tokens() {
    let src = "function f(a){if(a){return a+1;}return 0;}";
    let pretty = beautify(src);
    // It added structure.
    assert!(pretty.contains('\n'));
    assert!(pretty.contains("  return")); // indented body

    // Crucially, beautifying must not change the significant token stream.
    let sig = |s: &str| -> Vec<(Tok, String)> {
        tokenize(s)
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|t| t.kind != Tok::Space)
            .map(|t| (t.kind, t.text))
            .collect()
    };
    assert_eq!(sig(src), sig(&pretty));
}

#[test]
fn template_literals_stay_valid_and_stable() {
    // `\`` , `\\` and `\${` must stay escaped; real interpolations stay live.
    let src = r"x = `a\`b \\ c \${no} ${yes} \x41`;";
    let once = decode_string_literals(src);
    assert_eq!(once, r"x = `a\`b \\ c \${no} ${yes} A`;");
    // Repeated passes don't decay the escapes.
    assert_eq!(decode_string_literals(&once), once);
    assert_eq!(deobfuscate(src), once);
}

#[test]
fn fold_calls_ignores_strings_comments_and_computed_receivers() {
    // Inside a string or a comment nothing is rewritten.
    let s = r#"a = "String.fromCharCode(72)"; // atob("QUI=")"#;
    assert_eq!(fold_fromcharcode(s), s);
    assert_eq!(fold_atob(s), s);
    // A computed receiver can't be dropped (it would leave `window[...]"H"`).
    let c = r#"x = window["String"].fromCharCode(72); y = f().atob("QUI=");"#;
    assert_eq!(fold_fromcharcode(c), c);
    assert_eq!(fold_atob(c), c);
    // A longer identifier is not a match.
    assert_eq!(fold_atob(r#"myatob("QUI=")"#), r#"myatob("QUI=")"#);
    // Nested calls: the inner one folds, the outer one on a later pass.
    assert_eq!(fold_atob(r#"atob(atob("VVVrOQ=="))"#), r#"atob("UUk9")"#);
}

#[test]
fn fromcharcode_and_uri_decoding_follow_js() {
    // Values are truncated to 16 bits; surrogate pairs combine.
    assert_eq!(fold_fromcharcode("String.fromCharCode(65601)"), "\"A\"");
    assert_eq!(
        fold_fromcharcode("String.fromCharCode(0xD83D, 0xDE00)"),
        "\"\u{1F600}\""
    );
    // decodeURIComponent decodes UTF-8 byte sequences …
    assert_eq!(
        fold_unescape(r#"decodeURIComponent("%C3%A9t%C3%A9")"#),
        "\"été\""
    );
    // … and leaves calls JS would reject alone.
    let bad = r#"decodeURIComponent("%E9")"#;
    assert_eq!(fold_unescape(bad), bad);
    // unescape keeps its Latin-1 / UTF-16 semantics.
    assert_eq!(
        fold_unescape(r#"unescape("%E9%uD83D%uDE00")"#),
        "\"é\u{1F600}\""
    );
}

#[test]
fn string_array_poisoning() {
    for src in [
        // Element write.
        "var _a=['x','y'];_a[0]='z';f(_a[0]);",
        // Compound element write and update.
        "var _a=['x','y'];_a[1]+='z';f(_a[0]);",
        "var _a=['x','y'];delete _a[0];f(_a[0]);",
        // Mutating methods (the rotate-the-table trick).
        "var _a=['x','y'];_a.push(_a.shift());f(_a[0]);",
        "var _a=['x','y'];_a.reverse();f(_a[0]);",
        // Shadowing by a parameter or a re-declaration.
        "var _a=['x','y'];function g(_a){return _a[0];}",
        "var _a=['x','y'];var h=(_a)=>_a[0];",
        "var _a=['x','y'];var h=_a=>_a[0];",
        "var _a=['x','y'];{let _a;f(_a[0]);}",
        // Compound assignment of the name itself.
        "var _a=['x','y'];_a+='';f(_a[0]);",
    ] {
        assert_eq!(fold_string_array(src), src, "{src}");
    }
    // Comparisons are reads, not writes.
    let src = "var _a=['x','y'];if(_a[0]==_a[1]){f(_a[1])}";
    assert_eq!(
        fold_string_array(src),
        "var _a=['x','y'];if(\"x\"==\"y\"){f(\"y\")}"
    );
    // A property of another object is never substituted.
    let src = "var _a=['x'];o._a[0];";
    assert_eq!(fold_string_array(src), src);
}

#[test]
fn beautify_keeps_operators_apart_and_asi_line_breaks() {
    let pretty = beautify("x = a - -b; y = c + +d; z = e+ ++f;");
    assert!(pretty.contains("- -b"), "{pretty}");
    assert!(pretty.contains("+ +d"), "{pretty}");
    assert!(!pretty.contains("+++"), "{pretty}");
    // `return\nvalue` returns undefined; joining the lines would change that.
    let pretty = beautify("function f(){return\n42}");
    assert!(pretty.contains("return\n"), "{pretty}");
    assert!(!pretty.contains("return 42"), "{pretty}");
    // `1 .toString()` must not become `1.toString()`.
    let pretty = beautify("x = 1 .toString()");
    assert!(pretty.contains("1 ."), "{pretty}");
}
```

`crates/orress-js/src/token.rs`:

```rs
//! A JavaScript tokenizer good enough for beautifying and string-level deobfuscation. It is not a
//! full parser: it splits source into strings, template literals, regex literals, comments,
//! numbers, identifiers and single-character punctuation, which is what the transforms need. It
//! never panics and always consumes the whole input (an unterminated string/comment runs to EOF).

/// The kind of a lexical token.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Tok {
    /// A `'…'` or `"…"` string literal (text includes the quotes).
    Str,
    /// A `` `…` `` template literal (text includes the backticks).
    Template,
    /// A `/…/flags` regular-expression literal.
    Regex,
    Number,
    Ident,
    /// One punctuation character (operators are emitted char-by-char).
    Punct,
    LineComment,
    BlockComment,
    /// A run of whitespace (kept so transforms can reproduce the original source verbatim).
    Space,
}

/// A lexical token: its kind and exact source text.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Token {
    pub kind: Tok,
    pub text: String,
}

fn is_ident_start(c: char) -> bool {
    c.is_ascii_alphabetic() || c == '_' || c == '$' || (c as u32) > 127
}
fn is_ident_part(c: char) -> bool {
    is_ident_start(c) || c.is_ascii_digit()
}

/// The last token that isn't whitespace or a comment.
fn last_significant(out: &[Token]) -> Option<&Token> {
    out.iter()
        .rev()
        .find(|t| !matches!(t.kind, Tok::Space | Tok::LineComment | Tok::BlockComment))
}

/// Whether a `/` after the previous significant token begins a regex (vs. division). A regex can't
/// follow a value: an identifier, number, string, `)`, `]`, or `}` (close of a block/value).
fn regex_allowed(prev: Option<&Token>) -> bool {
    match prev {
        None => true,
        Some(t) => match t.kind {
            Tok::Ident => matches!(
                t.text.as_str(),
                "return"
                    | "typeof"
                    | "instanceof"
                    | "in"
                    | "of"
                    | "new"
                    | "delete"
                    | "void"
                    | "do"
                    | "else"
                    | "yield"
                    | "await"
                    | "case"
            ),
            Tok::Number | Tok::Str | Tok::Template | Tok::Regex => false,
            Tok::Punct => !matches!(t.text.as_str(), ")" | "]" | "}"),
            _ => true,
        },
    }
}

/// Tokenizes JavaScript source. Every character lands in exactly one token: whitespace runs
/// become [`Tok::Space`] tokens and comments are kept, so concatenating the token texts
/// reproduces the input exactly.
pub fn tokenize(src: &str) -> Vec<Token> {
    let chars: Vec<char> = src.chars().collect();
    let mut i = 0;
    let n = chars.len();
    let mut out: Vec<Token> = Vec::new();

    let push = |out: &mut Vec<Token>, kind: Tok, s: String| out.push(Token { kind, text: s });

    while i < n {
        let c = chars[i];
        if c.is_whitespace() {
            let start = i;
            while i < n && chars[i].is_whitespace() {
                i += 1;
            }
            push(&mut out, Tok::Space, chars[start..i].iter().collect());
            continue;
        }
        // Comments.
        if c == '/' && i + 1 < n && chars[i + 1] == '/' {
            let start = i;
            while i < n && chars[i] != '\n' {
                i += 1;
            }
            push(&mut out, Tok::LineComment, chars[start..i].iter().collect());
            continue;
        }
        if c == '/' && i + 1 < n && chars[i + 1] == '*' {
            let start = i;
            i += 2;
            while i + 1 < n && !(chars[i] == '*' && chars[i + 1] == '/') {
                i += 1;
            }
            i = (i + 2).min(n);
            push(
                &mut out,
                Tok::BlockComment,
                chars[start..i].iter().collect(),
            );
            continue;
        }
        // Strings.
        if c == '"' || c == '\'' {
            let start = i;
            i += 1;
            while i < n && chars[i] != c {
                if chars[i] == '\\' {
                    i += 1;
                }
                i += 1;
            }
            i = (i + 1).min(n);
            push(&mut out, Tok::Str, chars[start..i].iter().collect());
            continue;
        }
        // Template literals (interpolation boundaries are not tracked).
        if c == '`' {
            let start = i;
            i += 1;
            while i < n && chars[i] != '`' {
                if chars[i] == '\\' {
                    i += 1;
                }
                i += 1;
            }
            i = (i + 1).min(n);
            push(&mut out, Tok::Template, chars[start..i].iter().collect());
            continue;
        }
        // Regex vs. division.
        if c == '/' && regex_allowed(last_significant(&out)) {
            let start = i;
            i += 1;
            let mut in_class = false;
            while i < n {
                let d = chars[i];
                if d == '\\' {
                    i += 2;
                    continue;
                }
                if d == '[' {
                    in_class = true;
                } else if d == ']' {
                    in_class = false;
                } else if d == '/' && !in_class {
                    break;
                } else if d == '\n' {
                    break; // unterminated; bail
                }
                i += 1;
            }
            i = (i + 1).min(n); // consume closing '/'
            while i < n && chars[i].is_ascii_alphabetic() {
                i += 1; // flags
            }
            push(&mut out, Tok::Regex, chars[start..i].iter().collect());
            continue;
        }
        // Numbers.
        if c.is_ascii_digit() || (c == '.' && i + 1 < n && chars[i + 1].is_ascii_digit()) {
            let start = i;
            i += 1;
            while i < n {
                let d = chars[i];
                let exponent_sign = (d == '+' || d == '-') && matches!(chars[i - 1], 'e' | 'E');
                if d.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || d == '.' || d == '_' || exponent_sign {
                    i += 1;
                } else {
                    break;
                }
            }
            push(&mut out, Tok::Number, chars[start..i].iter().collect());
            continue;
        }
        // Identifiers / keywords.
        if is_ident_start(c) {
            let start = i;
            i += 1;
            while i < n && is_ident_part(chars[i]) {
                i += 1;
            }
            push(&mut out, Tok::Ident, chars[start..i].iter().collect());
            continue;
        }
        // Everything else: one punctuation character.
        push(&mut out, Tok::Punct, c.to_string());
        i += 1;
    }
    out
}
```

```rs
//! Lists the imports of a file: `cargo run -p orress-loaders --example imports -- FILE`

fn main() {
    let path = std::env::args().nth(1).expect("usage: imports FILE");
    let info = orress_loaders::triage(&std::fs::read(&path).expect("readable file"));
    for i in &info.imports {
        println!("{}!{}", i.library, i.name);
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-loaders/examples/triage.rs`:

```rs
//! Prints the triage summary of a file: `cargo run -p orress-loaders --example triage -- FILE`

fn main() {
    let Some(path) = std::env::args().nth(1) else {
        eprintln!("usage: triage FILE");
        std::process::exit(2);
    };
    let data = std::fs::read(&path).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{path}: {e}"));
    let info = orress_loaders::triage(&data);
    println!("{path}");
    println!(
        "  format   {} / {} / {}",
        info.format.name(),
        info.kind.name(),
        info.arch
    );
    println!(
        "  entry    {:x?} (file offset {:x?})",
        info.entry,
        info.entry_offset()
    );
    println!("  sha256   {}", info.hashes.sha256);
    if let Some(imphash) = &info.hashes.imphash {
        println!("  imphash  {imphash}");
    }
    println!("  entropy  {:.2}", info.entropy);
    for s in &info.sections {
        println!(
            "  section  {:<10} off {:>8x} size {:>8x} va {:>12x} {} H={:.2}",
            s.name,
            s.offset,
            s.file_size,
            s.address,
            s.perms.label(),
            s.entropy.unwrap_or(0.0)
        );
    }
    println!(
        "  imports  {} / exports {}",
        info.imports.len(),
        info.exports.len()
    );
    for p in &info.protections {
        println!("  protect  {:<26} {:?} ({})", p.name, p.state, p.detail);
    }
    for d in &info.detections {
        println!(
            "  detect   {}: {} [{}]",
            d.category.name(),
            d.name,
            d.evidence
        );
    }
    for i in &info.insights {
        println!("  insight  {:?}: {}", i.level, i.title);
    }
    if let Some(e) = &info.parse_error {
        println!("  error    {e}");
    }
}
```

```rs
//! A small knowledge base of library functions that matter in reverse engineering.
//! Used to explain imports and to spot what a program is likely to do.

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub enum ApiCategory {
    Input,
    Compare,
    Crypto,
    AntiDebug,
    Network,
    Injection,
    Process,
    File,
    Registry,
    DynamicLoading,
    Memory,
}

impl ApiCategory {
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Input => "Input",
            Self::Compare => "Comparison",
            Self::Crypto => "Crypto",
            Self::AntiDebug => "Anti-debugging",
            Self::Network => "Network",
            Self::Injection => "Code injection",
            Self::Process => "Processes",
            Self::File => "Files",
            Self::Registry => "Registry",
            Self::DynamicLoading => "Dynamic loading",
            Self::Memory => "Memory",
        }
    }

    /// Whether this category deserves attention in a malware context.
    pub fn suspicious(self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            self,
            Self::AntiDebug | Self::Injection | Self::Network | Self::DynamicLoading
        )
    }
}

/// Looks up a function name. Ignores a leading `_` (32-bit Windows decoration) and a
/// trailing `@N` (stdcall suffix).
pub fn lookup(name: &str) -> Option<&'static ApiInfo> {
    let trimmed = name.trim_start_matches('_');
    let trimmed = trimmed.split('@').next().unwrap_or(trimmed);
    let find = |n: &str| APIS.iter().find(|a| a.name.trim_start_matches('_') == n);
    APIS.iter()
        .find(|a| a.name == name)
        .or_else(|| find(trimmed))
        .or_else(|| {
            // Windows APIs come as ...A (ANSI) and ...W (wide) variants; the knowledge
            // base often lists only one of them.
            let base = trimmed
                .strip_suffix('A')
                .or_else(|| trimmed.strip_suffix('W'))?;
            find(&format!("{base}A")).or_else(|| find(&format!("{base}W")))
        })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn lookup_handles_decorations() {
        assert_eq!(lookup("strcmp").unwrap().category, Compare);
        assert_eq!(lookup("_IsDebuggerPresent@0").unwrap().category, AntiDebug);
        assert!(lookup("totally_unknown").is_none());
        // A/W variants map to each other.
        assert_eq!(lookup("RegOpenKeyExW").unwrap().name, "RegOpenKeyExA");
        assert_eq!(lookup("InternetOpenW").unwrap().name, "InternetOpenA");
        assert!(lookup("SHOW").is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn no_duplicate_names() {
        let mut names: Vec<_> = APIS.iter().map(|a| a.name).collect();
        names.sort_unstable();
        let before = names.len();
        names.dedup();
        assert_eq!(before, names.len());
    }
}
```

```rs
//! Facts the code analysis needs from the file format: where imported function pointers
//! live, named function symbols, and function starts from exception tables.

use object::macho;
use object::read::macho::{MachHeader, MachOFile, Nlist, Section as _};
use object::read::pe::{ImageNtHeaders, ImageThunkData, PeFile};
use object::{
    LittleEndian as LE, Object, ObjectSymbol, ObjectSymbolTable, ReadRef, RelocationTarget,
    SymbolIndex, SymbolKind, U32,
};

use crate::model::*;

/// PE: one slot per imported function in the Import Address Table. The program calls
/// imports indirectly through these slots: `call [IAT slot]`.
pub fn pe_import_slots<Pe: ImageNtHeaders>(
    pe: &PeFile<'_, Pe>,
    image_base: u64,
) -> Vec<NamedAddress> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let Ok(Some(table)) = pe.import_table() else {
        return out;
    };
    let Ok(mut descriptors) = table.descriptors() else {
        return out;
    };
    let slot_size: u64 = if pe.is_64() { 8 } else { 4 };
    while let Ok(Some(desc)) = descriptors.next() {
        let library = table
            .name(desc.name.get(LE))
            .map(|n| String::from_utf8_lossy(n).into_owned())
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let first_thunk = desc.first_thunk.get(LE);
        // Names come from the original thunks; the IAT itself may be pre-bound.
        let names_at = match desc.original_first_thunk.get(LE) {
            0 => first_thunk,
            oft => oft,
        };
        let Ok(mut thunks) = table.thunks(names_at) else {
            continue;
        };
        let mut index = 0u64;
        while let Ok(Some(thunk)) = thunks.next::<Pe>() {
            let name = match table.import::<Pe>(thunk) {
                Ok(object::read::pe::Import::Name(_, name)) => {
                    String::from_utf8_lossy(name).into_owned()
                }
                Ok(object::read::pe::Import::Ordinal(o)) => format!("{library}#{o}"),
                Err(_) => format!("import_{:x}", thunk.raw()),
            };
            out.push(NamedAddress {
                address: image_base + u64::from(first_thunk) + index * slot_size,
                name,
            });
            index += 1;
        }
    }
    out
}

/// ELF: GOT slots filled in by the dynamic linker (JUMP_SLOT / GLOB_DAT relocations).
/// PLT stubs jump through these: `jmp [GOT slot]`.
pub fn elf_import_slots(file: &object::File<'_>) -> Vec<NamedAddress> {
    let Some(relocations) = file.dynamic_relocations() else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    let Some(symbols) = file.dynamic_symbol_table() else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    relocations
        .filter_map(|(offset, reloc)| match reloc.target() {
            RelocationTarget::Symbol(index) => {
                let symbol = symbols.symbol_by_index(index).ok()?;
                let name = symbol.name().ok()?;
                (!name.is_empty() && symbol.is_undefined()).then(|| NamedAddress {
                    address: offset,
                    name: name.to_owned(),
                })
            }
            _ => None,
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Mach-O: the indirect symbol table names every entry of the symbol-stub (`__stubs`) and
/// symbol-pointer (`__got`, `__la_symbol_ptr`) sections. Code calls an import with
/// `bl`/`call <stub>` or loads its pointer from the GOT, so those entries are the import slots.
pub fn macho_import_slots<'data, Mach: MachHeader, R: ReadRef<'data>>(
    file: &MachOFile<'data, Mach, R>,
) -> Vec<NamedAddress> {
    let endian = file.endian();
    let Ok(mut commands) = file.macho_load_commands() else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    let mut dysymtab = None;
    while let Ok(Some(command)) = commands.next() {
        if let Ok(Some(d)) = command.dysymtab() {
            dysymtab = Some(d);
            break;
        }
    }
    let Some(dysymtab) = dysymtab else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    let Ok(indirect) = file.data().read_slice_at::<U32<Mach::Endian>>(
        u64::from(dysymtab.indirectsymoff.get(endian)),
        dysymtab.nindirectsyms.get(endian) as usize,
    ) else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    let symbols = file.macho_symbol_table();
    let pointer_size = if file.is_64() { 8 } else { 4 };
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for section in file.sections() {
        let section = section.macho_section();
        let entry_size = match section.flags(endian).typ() {
            macho::S_SYMBOL_STUBS => u64::from(section.reserved2(endian)),
            macho::S_NON_LAZY_SYMBOL_POINTERS | macho::S_LAZY_SYMBOL_POINTERS => pointer_size,
            _ => continue,
        };
        if entry_size == 0 {
            continue;
        }
        let address: u64 = section.addr(endian).into();
        let size: u64 = section.size(endian).into();
        let first = section.reserved1(endian) as usize;
        // Bounded by the indirect table: a hostile section size cannot make this loop long.
        for i in 0..size / entry_size {
            let Some(entry) = first
                .checked_add(i as usize)
                .and_then(|index| indirect.get(index))
            else {
                break;
            };
            let index = entry.get(endian);
            // INDIRECT_SYMBOL_LOCAL / INDIRECT_SYMBOL_ABS: not an import.
            if index & 0xc000_0000 != 0 {
                continue;
            }
            let Ok(nlist) = symbols.symbol(SymbolIndex(index as usize)) else {
                continue;
            };
            let Ok(name) = nlist.name(endian, symbols.strings()) else {
                continue;
            };
            if !name.is_empty() {
                out.push(NamedAddress {
                    address: address + i * entry_size,
                    name: String::from_utf8_lossy(name).into_owned(),
                });
            }
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Defined function symbols (static and dynamic), one name per address.
pub fn function_symbols(file: &object::File<'_>) -> Vec<NamedAddress> {
    let mut out: Vec<NamedAddress> = file
        .symbols()
        .chain(file.dynamic_symbols())
        .filter(|s| s.is_definition() && s.kind() == SymbolKind::Text && s.address() != 0)
        .filter_map(|s| {
            let name = s.name().ok()?;
            (!name.is_empty()).then(|| NamedAddress {
                address: s.address(),
                name: orress_demangle::demangle(name).unwrap_or_else(|| name.to_owned()),
            })
        })
        .collect();
    out.sort_by_key(|n| n.address);
    out.dedup_by_key(|n| n.address);
    out
}

/// x64 PE: every non-leaf function has a RUNTIME_FUNCTION entry in the exception
/// directory (.pdata), so this lists function starts even in stripped binaries.
pub fn pe_pdata_starts(
    info: &BinaryInfo,
    data: &[u8],
    exception_dir: Option<(u32, u32)>,
) -> Vec<u64> {
    let Some((rva, size)) = exception_dir else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    let Some(offset) = info.address_to_offset(info.image_base + u64::from(rva)) else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    let start = offset as usize;
    let Some(bytes) = data.get(start..start.saturating_add(size as usize)) else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    let mut out: Vec<u64> = bytes
        // RUNTIME_FUNCTION: begin RVA, end RVA, unwind info RVA (3 x u32).
        .as_chunks::<12>()
        .0
        .iter()
        .map(|entry| u32::from_le_bytes([entry[0], entry[1], entry[2], entry[3]]))
        .filter(|&begin| begin != 0)
        .map(|begin| info.image_base + u64::from(begin))
        .collect();
    out.sort_unstable();
    out.dedup();
    out
}
```

```rs
/// Signatures for non-executable files, checked at offset 0.
const MAGIC: &[(&[u8], &str, &str)] = &[

        "Script",
        "A script with an interpreter line (#!/bin/sh, #!/usr/bin/python ...). Read it as text.",
    ),
    (
        b"L\x00\x00\x00\x01\x14\x02\x00",
        "Windows shortcut (LNK)",
        "A Windows shortcut. Malicious LNK files run hidden commands.",

    (

        "ELF (damaged)",
        "Starts like an ELF file but could not be parsed: the header may be corrupted on purpose to break tools.",

pub fn detect(data: &[u8], info: &BinaryInfo) -> Vec<Detection> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();

    for rule in RULES {
        let by_section = info
            .sections
            .iter()
            .find(|s| rule.sections.contains(&s.name.as_str()))
            .map(|s| format!("section \"{}\"", s.name));
        let by_marker = || {
            rule.markers
                .iter()
                .find(|m| contains(data, m))
                .map(|m| format!("bytes \"{}\"", m.escape_ascii()))
        };
        if let Some(evidence) = by_section.or_else(by_marker) {
            out.push(Detection {
                category: rule.category,
                name: rule.name.to_owned(),
                evidence,
                explain: rule.explain,
            });
        }
    }

    if let Some(pe) = &info.pe {
        if pe.is_dotnet {
            out.push(Detection {
                category: DetectionCategory::Language,
                name: ".NET (C#, VB.NET, F#)".into(),
                evidence: "CLR runtime header present".into(),
                explain: "A .NET program: the code is CIL bytecode, not machine code. A .NET \
                    decompiler (dnSpy, ILSpy) gives you near-original C#. Native disassembly \
                    only shows a tiny loader.",
            });
        }
        if !pe.rich.is_empty() {
            out.push(Detection {
                category: DetectionCategory::Compiler,
                name: "Microsoft Visual C++".into(),
                evidence: format!("Rich header with {} tool entries", pe.rich.len()),
                explain: "Built with Microsoft's toolchain. The Rich header lists the tool \
                    versions used; malware families often share the same build setup.",
            });
        }
    }

    // Packed-code heuristic: an executable section with near-random contents.
    let packed_section = info
        .sections
        .iter()
        .find(|s| s.perms.execute && s.file_size > 1024 && s.entropy.unwrap_or(0.0) > 7.2);
    let already_packer = out.iter().any(|d| d.category == DetectionCategory::Packer);
    if let Some(s) = packed_section
        && !already_packer
    {
        out.push(Detection {
            category: DetectionCategory::Packer,
            name: "Unknown packer or encryption (heuristic)".into(),
            evidence: format!(
                "executable section \"{}\" has entropy {:.2}",
                s.name,
                s.entropy.unwrap_or(0.0)
            ),
            explain: "Code normally has an entropy around 5–6.5. Close to 8 means the bytes \
                are compressed or encrypted, so the real code only appears in memory at run \
                time. Run it in a debugger or emulator and dump it after unpacking.",
        });
    }

    if info.format == Format::Unknown
        && let Some((_, name, explain)) = MAGIC.iter().find(|(magic, _, _)| data.starts_with(magic))
    {
        out.push(Detection {
            category: DetectionCategory::FileType,
            name: (*name).to_owned(),
            evidence: "file signature (magic bytes) at offset 0".into(),
            explain,
        });
    }

    out.sort_by_key(|d| d.category);
    out
}
```

```rs
use md5::Md5;
use sha1::Sha1;
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};

use crate::Import;

/// File hashes, used to look samples up in threat-intel databases and to tell
/// files apart.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Hashes {
    pub md5: String,
    pub sha1: String,
    pub sha256: String,
    /// Import hash (PE only): MD5 of the imported functions. Malware built from the
    /// same source often shares it even when the file hash differs.
    pub imphash: Option<String>,
}

fn hex(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    use std::fmt::Write;
    bytes
        .iter()
        .fold(String::with_capacity(bytes.len() * 2), |mut s, b| {
            let _ = write!(s, "{b:02x}");
            s
        })
}

impl Hashes {
    pub fn compute(data: &[u8], imports: &[Import], is_pe: bool) -> Self {
        Self {
            md5: hex(&Md5::digest(data)),
            sha1: hex(&Sha1::digest(data)),
            sha256: hex(&Sha256::digest(data)),
            imphash: (is_pe && !imports.is_empty()).then(|| imphash(imports)),
        }
    }
}

/// pefile's `ordlookup` table for `ws2_32.dll` (also used for `wsock32.dll`): the classic
/// Winsock ordinals. Only the stable, well-documented ordinals are listed here (1–23, 51–57,
/// 101–116, 151, 500); pefile's table has more entries in 24–50 / 58–100, which fall back to
/// `ord<N>` below, so imphashes of samples importing those by ordinal may still differ.
const WS2_32_ORDINALS: &[(u32, &str)] = &[
    (1, "accept"),
    (2, "bind"),
    (3, "closesocket"),
    (4, "connect"),
    (5, "getpeername"),
    (6, "getsockname"),
    (7, "getsockopt"),
    (8, "htonl"),
    (9, "htons"),
    (10, "ioctlsocket"),
    (11, "inet_addr"),
    (12, "inet_ntoa"),
    (13, "listen"),
    (14, "ntohl"),
    (15, "ntohs"),
    (16, "recv"),
    (17, "recvfrom"),
    (18, "select"),
    (19, "send"),
    (20, "sendto"),
    (21, "setsockopt"),
    (22, "shutdown"),
    (23, "socket"),
    (51, "gethostbyaddr"),
    (52, "gethostbyname"),
    (53, "getprotobyname"),
    (54, "getprotobynumber"),
    (55, "getservbyname"),
    (56, "getservbyport"),
    (57, "gethostname"),
    (101, "WSAAsyncSelect"),
    (102, "WSAAsyncGetHostByAddr"),
    (103, "WSAAsyncGetHostByName"),
    (104, "WSAAsyncGetProtoByNumber"),
    (105, "WSAAsyncGetProtoByName"),
    (106, "WSAAsyncGetServByPort"),
    (107, "WSAAsyncGetServByName"),
    (108, "WSACancelAsyncRequest"),
    (109, "WSASetBlockingHook"),
    (110, "WSAUnhookBlockingHook"),
    (111, "WSAGetLastError"),
    (112, "WSASetLastError"),
    (113, "WSACancelBlockingCall"),
    (114, "WSAIsBlocking"),
    (115, "WSAStartup"),
    (116, "WSACleanup"),
    (151, "__WSAFDIsSet"),
    (500, "WEP"),
];

/// pefile's `ordlookup` table for `oleaut32.dll`, limited to the ordinals that are certain (the
/// BSTR/VARIANT basics that VB/COM binaries import by ordinal). Others fall back to `ord<N>`.
const OLEAUT32_ORDINALS: &[(u32, &str)] = &[
    (2, "SysAllocString"),
    (3, "SysReAllocString"),
    (4, "SysAllocStringLen"),
    (5, "SysReAllocStringLen"),
    (6, "SysFreeString"),
    (7, "SysStringLen"),
    (8, "VariantInit"),
    (9, "VariantClear"),
    (10, "VariantCopy"),
    (11, "VariantCopyInd"),
    (12, "VariantChangeType"),
    (15, "SafeArrayCreate"),
    (16, "SafeArrayDestroy"),
    (149, "SysStringByteLen"),
    (150, "SysAllocStringByteLen"),
];

/// pefile's `ordLookup`: an ordinal import's name for the few libraries it knows, keyed by the
/// full lowercase DLL name (as pefile does).
fn ord_lookup(library_lower: &str, ordinal: u32) -> Option<&'static str> {
    let table = match library_lower {
        "ws2_32.dll" | "wsock32.dll" => WS2_32_ORDINALS,
        "oleaut32.dll" => OLEAUT32_ORDINALS,
        _ => return None,
    };
    table
        .binary_search_by_key(&ordinal, |&(o, _)| o)
        .ok()
        .map(|i| table[i].1)
}

/// The pefile/VirusTotal imphash: `library.function` pairs, lowercase, library without
/// its extension, joined with commas, then MD5. Ordinal imports are resolved to names for
/// `ws2_32`/`wsock32`/`oleaut32` (pefile's `ordlookup`), and use `ord<N>` otherwise.
pub fn imphash(imports: &[Import]) -> String {
    let joined = imports
        .iter()
        .map(|i| {
            let full = i.library.to_ascii_lowercase();
            let lib = ["dll", "ocx", "sys"]
                .iter()
                .find_map(|ext| full.strip_suffix(&format!(".{ext}")))
                .unwrap_or(&full)
                .to_owned();
            let func = match i.name.strip_prefix('#') {
                Some(ordinal) => ordinal
                    .parse::<u32>()
                    .ok()
                    .and_then(|o| ord_lookup(&full, o))
                    .map(str::to_ascii_lowercase)
                    .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("ord{ordinal}")),
                None => i.name.to_ascii_lowercase(),
            };
            format!("{lib}.{func}")
        })
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join(",");
    hex(&Md5::digest(joined.as_bytes()))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn known_digests() {
        let h = Hashes::compute(b"abc", &[], false);
        assert_eq!(h.md5, "900150983cd24fb0d6963f7d28e17f72");
        assert_eq!(h.sha1, "a9993e364706816aba3e25717850c26c9cd0d89d");
        assert_eq!(
            h.sha256,
            "ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad"
        );
        assert_eq!(h.imphash, None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn imphash_normalizes_names() {
        let imports = [
            Import {
                library: "KERNEL32.dll".into(),
                name: "ExitProcess".into(),
            },
            Import {
                library: "ws2_32.dll".into(),
                name: "#115".into(),
            },
            Import {
                library: "OLEAUT32.dll".into(),
                name: "#6".into(),
            },
            Import {
                library: "WSOCK32.dll".into(),
                name: "#9999".into(),
            },
            Import {
                library: "mylib.dll".into(),
                name: "#3".into(),
            },
        ];
        // Like pefile: known ordinals resolve to lowercase names, unknown ones stay `ord<N>`.
        let expected = hex(&Md5::digest(
            b"kernel32.exitprocess,ws2_32.wsastartup,oleaut32.sysfreestring,\
              wsock32.ord9999,mylib.ord3",
        ));
        assert_eq!(imphash(&imports), expected);
    }

    #[test]
    fn ordinal_tables_are_sorted() {
        for t in [WS2_32_ORDINALS, OLEAUT32_ORDINALS] {
            assert!(t.windows(2).all(|w| w[0].0 < w[1].0));
        }
        assert_eq!(ord_lookup("wsock32.dll", 23), Some("socket"));
        assert_eq!(ord_lookup("ws2_32", 23), None);
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-loaders/src/insights.rs`:

```rs
//! Beginner-friendly observations and next steps, derived from the triage results.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;

use crate::apis::{self, ApiCategory};
use crate::model::*;

pub fn insights(info: &BinaryInfo) -> Vec<Insight> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut push = |level, title: &str, body: String| {
        out.push(Insight {
            level,
            title: title.to_owned(),
            body,
        });
    };

    let mut by_category: BTreeMap<ApiCategory, Vec<&str>> = BTreeMap::new();
    for import in &info.imports {
        if let Some(api) = apis::lookup(&import.name) {
            let list = by_category.entry(api.category).or_default();
            if !list.contains(&api.name) {
                list.push(api.name);
            }
        }
    }
    let names = |c: ApiCategory| by_category.get(&c).map(|v| v.join(", "));

    let packed = info
        .detections
        .iter()
        .find(|d| d.category == DetectionCategory::Packer);
    if let Some(p) = packed {
        push(
            InsightLevel::Warning,
            "The program is packed",
            format!(
                "{} detected ({}). What you see in the file is mostly the unpacker; the real \
                 code is created in memory at run time. Unpack it first, then analyze the result.",
                p.name, p.evidence
            ),
        );
    }

    if let Some(list) = names(ApiCategory::AntiDebug) {
        // The Microsoft C runtime start-up code imports these two in nearly every Windows
        // program (also Rust ones), so on their own they are not a red flag.
        let runtime_only = info.format == Format::Pe
            && by_category.get(&ApiCategory::AntiDebug).is_some_and(|l| {
                l.iter()
                    .all(|n| matches!(*n, "IsDebuggerPresent" | "QueryPerformanceCounter"))
            });
        if runtime_only {
            push(
                InsightLevel::Info,
                "Debugger checks (probably harmless)",
                format!(
                    "Imports {list}. Microsoft's C runtime imports these in almost every Windows \
                     program for its own start-up and crash handling. They only matter if the \
                     program's own code calls them: check their cross-references."
                ),
            );
        } else {
            push(
                InsightLevel::Warning,
                "Anti-debugging",
                format!(
                    "Imports {list}. The program may act differently when it notices a debugger. \
                     Find where these are called and patch the check, or hide the debugger."
                ),
            );
        }
    }

    if let Some(list) = names(ApiCategory::Compare) {
        push(
            InsightLevel::Tip,
            "It compares strings",
            format!(
                "Imports {list}. In a crackme, your input is often compared with the expected \
                 password here. Find the calls (cross-references), or break on them in a \
                 debugger and read both arguments."
            ),
        );
    }

    if let Some(list) = names(ApiCategory::Input) {
        push(
            InsightLevel::Info,
            "Where input comes from",
            format!("Reads input with {list}. Follow the buffer it fills to find the check."),
        );
    }

    if let Some(list) = names(ApiCategory::Crypto) {
        push(
            InsightLevel::Info,
            "Cryptography",
            format!(
                "Imports {list}. Encrypted strings, configuration or network traffic are likely. \
                 The key is usually nearby: look at the arguments."
            ),
        );
    }

    if let Some(list) = names(ApiCategory::Injection) {
        push(
            InsightLevel::Warning,
            "Code injection capability",
            format!(
                "Imports {list}. Together these can write code into another process and run \
                 it, a common malware technique. Analyze only in an isolated VM."
            ),
        );
    }

    if let Some(list) = names(ApiCategory::Network) {
        push(
            InsightLevel::Info,
            "Network activity",
            format!("Imports {list}. Look for IP addresses, domains and URLs in the strings."),
        );
    }

    let few_imports = info.format == Format::Pe && info.imports.len() < 10;
    if few_imports && info.imports_api(&["GetProcAddress", "LoadLibraryA", "LoadLibraryW"]) {
        push(
            InsightLevel::Warning,
            "Imports resolved at run time",
            format!(
                "Only {} imports, including LoadLibrary/GetProcAddress. The program looks up \
                 the functions it really uses while running, which hides them from this list. \
                 Typical for packers and malware.",
                info.imports.len()
            ),
        );
    }

    if let Some(pe) = &info.pe
        && pe.has_tls
    {
        push(
            InsightLevel::Tip,
            "TLS callbacks",
            "This file has a TLS directory. TLS callbacks run before the entry point, so code \
             there runs before a debugger that breaks on the entry point stops. Check them for \
             hidden checks."
                .to_owned(),
        );
    }

    let stripped = info
        .protections
        .iter()
        .any(|p| p.name == "Stripped" && p.state == ProtectionState::On);
    if stripped && info.format != Format::Unknown {
        push(
            InsightLevel::Info,
            "No function names",
            "The binary is stripped. Functions will show up as sub_401000 and similar. Start \
             from the entry point or from interesting strings and imports, and name functions \
             as you understand them."
                .to_owned(),
        );
    }

    if info.format == Format::Unknown {
        push(
            InsightLevel::Info,
            "Not an executable",
            "ORRESS could not parse this as a program. Check the detected file type, the \
             strings and the entropy graph to work out what it is."
                .to_owned(),
        );
    } else {
        push(
            InsightLevel::Tip,
            "Suggested first steps",
            "1. Open Strings and look for messages like \"Correct!\", \"Wrong\" or flag-like \
             text.\n2. Check Imports for what the program can do.\n3. Press Ctrl+Shift+M to jump \
             to main and read the disassembly."
                .to_owned(),
        );
    }

    out.sort_by_key(|i| i.level);
    out
}
```
