`crates/orress-loaders/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! Executable format loading and file triage.
//!
//! [`triage`] turns raw bytes into a [`BinaryInfo`]: format, architecture, sections,
//! imports and exports, security protections, compiler and packer detections, hashes,
//! and beginner-friendly insights ("this program compares strings: set a breakpoint on
//! strcmp"). It never executes anything and works on hostile input.

pub mod apis;
mod code_hints;
mod detect;
mod hashes;
mod insights;
mod model;
mod parse;
mod protections;
pub mod sections;

pub use apis::{ApiCategory, ApiInfo};
pub use hashes::Hashes;
pub use model::*;

/// Analyzes `data`. Parse errors are recorded in [`BinaryInfo::parse_error`], so this
/// always returns something useful (at least hashes, entropy and a format guess).
pub fn triage(data: &[u8]) -> BinaryInfo {
    let mut info = parse::parse(data);
    info.size = data.len() as u64;
    info.hashes = Hashes::compute(data, &info.imports, info.format == Format::Pe);
    info.entropy = orress_bytes::entropy::shannon(data);
    for section in &mut info.sections {
        section.entropy = section
            .file_range()
            .and_then(|r| data.get(r))
            .map(orress_bytes::entropy::shannon);
    }
    info.detections = detect::detect(data, &info);
    info.insights = insights::insights(&info);
    info
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests;
```

```rs
use std::ops::Range;

pub use orress_bytes::Endian;

use crate::Hashes;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum Format {
    Pe,
    Elf,
    MachO,
    Coff,
    Wasm,
    Xcoff,
    /// Not an executable format ORRESS can parse (yet). See the detections for a guess.
    #[default]
    Unknown,
}

impl Format {
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Pe => "PE (Windows executable)",
            Self::Elf => "ELF (Linux/Unix executable)",
            Self::MachO => "Mach-O (macOS/iOS executable)",
            Self::Coff => "COFF object file",
            Self::Wasm => "WebAssembly module",
            Self::Xcoff => "XCOFF (AIX executable)",
            Self::Unknown => "Unknown format",
        }
    }

    pub fn explain(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Pe => {
                "Portable Executable: the format of Windows programs (.exe), libraries (.dll) \
                 and drivers (.sys). It starts with \"MZ\" (an old DOS header), followed by \
                 a \"PE\" header that describes sections, imports and the entry point."
            }
            Self::Elf => {
                "Executable and Linkable Format: used by Linux, BSD, Android native code and \
                 most embedded systems. It starts with the bytes 7F 45 4C 46 (\".ELF\"). \
                 Most CTF reversing challenges are ELF files."
            }
            Self::MachO => {
                "Mach-O: the format of macOS and iOS programs. It contains load commands \
                 that describe segments, libraries and the entry point."
            }
            Self::Coff => {
                "COFF: an object file produced by a compiler before linking (.obj on \
                 Windows). It contains code but is not a runnable program yet."
            }
            Self::Wasm => {
                "WebAssembly: portable bytecode that runs in browsers and in runtimes like \
                 wasmtime. It starts with \"\\0asm\"."
            }
            Self::Xcoff => "XCOFF: the executable format of IBM AIX.",
            Self::Unknown => {
                "ORRESS could not parse this as an executable. It may be data, an archive, \
                 a document or something packed or encrypted. The hex view and the strings \
                 list still work."
            }
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Kind {
    Executable,
    Library,
    Object,
    Core,
    #[default]
    Unknown,
}

impl Kind {
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Executable => "Executable program",
            Self::Library => "Shared library (DLL / .so / .dylib)",
            Self::Object => "Object file (not linked)",
            Self::Core => "Core dump",
            Self::Unknown => "Unknown",
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Perms {
    pub read: bool,
    pub write: bool,
    pub execute: bool,
}

impl Perms {
    pub fn label(self) -> String {
        format!(
            "{}{}{}",
            if self.read { 'R' } else { '-' },
            if self.write { 'W' } else { '-' },
            if self.execute { 'X' } else { '-' }
        )
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct Section {
    pub name: String,
    /// File offset and size of the section's bytes in the file (0 size for `.bss`-like
    /// sections that only exist in memory).
    pub offset: u64,
    pub file_size: u64,
    /// Address when loaded in memory (virtual address).
    pub address: u64,
    pub virtual_size: u64,
    pub perms: Perms,
    pub entropy: Option<f32>,
}

impl Section {
    pub fn file_range(&self) -> Option<Range<usize>> {
        if self.file_size == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        let start = usize::try_from(self.offset).ok()?;
        let end = start.checked_add(usize::try_from(self.file_size).ok()?)?;
        Some(start..end)
    }

    pub fn contains_offset(&self, offset: u64) -> bool {
        offset >= self.offset && offset - self.offset < self.file_size
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct Segment {
    pub name: Option<String>,
    pub offset: u64,
    pub file_size: u64,
    pub address: u64,
    pub virtual_size: u64,
    pub perms: Perms,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Import {
    /// DLL or shared library name. Empty for ELF, where the library is not recorded
    /// per symbol.
    pub library: String,
    /// Function name, or `#123` for imports by ordinal number.
    pub name: String,
}

/// A name for an address (symbol, import slot ...).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct NamedAddress {
    pub address: u64,
    pub name: String,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Export {
    pub name: String,
    pub address: u64,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PeDetails {
    /// Link time from the PE header (seconds since 1970). Often faked by malware, and
    /// replaced by a hash in reproducible builds.
    pub timestamp: u32,
    pub subsystem: String,
    pub linker_version: (u8, u8),
    pub is_dotnet: bool,
    pub has_signature: bool,
    pub has_tls: bool,
    /// Rich header entries (product id, build, count): tools that built the file.
    pub rich: Vec<(u16, u16, u32)>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ProtectionState {
    On,
    Partial,
    Off,
}

pub struct Protection {

    pub state: ProtectionState,
    pub detail: String,

}

pub enum DetectionCategory {
    Packer,
    Language,
    Compiler,
    Installer,
    FileType,
}

impl DetectionCategory {
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Packer => "Packer / protector",
            Self::Language => "Language",
            Self::Compiler => "Compiler",
            Self::Installer => "Installer / bundler",
            Self::FileType => "File type",
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]

    /// What was found, e.g. `section "UPX0"`.
    pub evidence: String,
    pub explain: &'static str,
}

pub enum InsightLevel {
    Warning,
    Tip,
    Info,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Insight {
    pub level: InsightLevel,
    pub title: String,
    pub body: String,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct BinaryInfo {
    pub format: Format,
    pub kind: Kind,
    /// Human-readable architecture, e.g. "x86-64".
    pub arch: String,
    pub bits: Option<u8>,
    pub endian: Endian,
    /// Entry point address (where execution starts), if any.
    pub entry: Option<u64>,
    /// Preferred load address (PE image base, lowest ELF segment address).
    pub image_base: u64,
    pub sections: Vec<Section>,
    pub segments: Vec<Segment>,
    pub imports: Vec<Import>,
    pub exports: Vec<Export>,
    /// Memory slots holding imported function addresses (PE IAT, ELF GOT).
    pub import_slots: Vec<NamedAddress>,
    /// Named functions from symbol tables, sorted by address.
    pub function_symbols: Vec<NamedAddress>,
    /// Function start addresses from exception tables (x64 PE .pdata).
    pub function_starts: Vec<u64>,
    pub symbol_count: usize,
    pub has_debug_info: bool,
    pub pe: Option<PeDetails>,
    pub protections: Vec<Protection>,
    pub detections: Vec<Detection>,
    pub insights: Vec<Insight>,
    pub hashes: Hashes,
    /// Entropy of the whole file.
    pub entropy: f32,
    pub size: u64,
    pub parse_error: Option<String>,
}

impl BinaryInfo {
    /// File ranges that map to memory: sections first, then segments (ELF files
    /// without section headers only have segments).
    fn mappings(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (u64, u64, u64)> + '_ {
        self.sections
            .iter()
            .filter(|s| s.address != 0)
            .map(|s| (s.offset, s.file_size, s.address))
            .chain(
                self.segments
                    .iter()
                    .map(|s| (s.offset, s.file_size, s.address)),
            )
            .filter(|&(_, size, _)| size > 0)
    }

    /// Virtual address where the byte at file `offset` is loaded, if it is loaded.
    pub fn offset_to_address(&self, offset: u64) -> Option<u64> {
        self.mappings()
            .find(|&(off, size, _)| offset >= off && offset - off < size)
            .and_then(|(off, _, addr)| addr.checked_add(offset - off))
    }

    /// File offset of virtual address `address`, if that address is backed by the file.
    pub fn address_to_offset(&self, address: u64) -> Option<u64> {
        self.mappings()
            .find(|&(_, size, addr)| address >= addr && address - addr < size)
            .and_then(|(off, _, addr)| off.checked_add(address - addr))
    }

    pub fn section_at_offset(&self, offset: u64) -> Option<&Section> {
        self.sections.iter().find(|s| s.contains_offset(offset))
    }

    pub fn entry_offset(&self) -> Option<u64> {
        self.entry.and_then(|e| self.address_to_offset(e))
    }

    pub fn imports_api(&self, names: &[&str]) -> bool {
        self.imports
            .iter()
            .any(|i| names.iter().any(|n| i.name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(n)))
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-loaders/src/parse.rs`:

```rs
//! Turns bytes into the format-independent model using the `object` crate.

use object::read::elf::{ElfFile, FileHeader};
use object::read::pe::{ImageNtHeaders, ImageOptionalHeader, PeFile};
use object::{
    Architecture, BinaryFormat, ExportTarget, NameOrOrdinal, Object, ObjectKind, ObjectSection,
    ObjectSegment, SectionFlags, SectionKind,
};

use crate::model::*;
use crate::{code_hints, protections};

pub fn parse(data: &[u8]) -> BinaryInfo {
    let file = match object::File::parse(data) {
        Ok(file) => file,
        Err(e) => {
            return BinaryInfo {
                parse_error: Some(e.to_string()),
                ..BinaryInfo::default()
            };
        }
    };

    let format = match file.format() {
        BinaryFormat::Pe => Format::Pe,
        BinaryFormat::Elf => Format::Elf,
        BinaryFormat::MachO => Format::MachO,
        BinaryFormat::Coff => Format::Coff,
        BinaryFormat::Wasm => Format::Wasm,
        BinaryFormat::Xcoff => Format::Xcoff,
        _ => Format::Unknown,
    };

    let mut info = BinaryInfo {
        format,
        kind: match file.kind() {
            ObjectKind::Executable => Kind::Executable,
            ObjectKind::Dynamic => Kind::Library,
            ObjectKind::Relocatable => Kind::Object,
            ObjectKind::Core => Kind::Core,
            _ => Kind::Unknown,
        },
        arch: arch_name(file.architecture()).to_owned(),
        bits: Some(if file.is_64() { 64 } else { 32 }),
        endian: if file.is_little_endian() {
            Endian::Little
        } else {
            Endian::Big
        },
        entry: Some(file.entry()).filter(|&e| e != 0),
        image_base: file.relative_address_base(),
        has_debug_info: file.has_debug_symbols(),
        symbol_count: file.symbols().count() + file.dynamic_symbols().count(),
        ..BinaryInfo::default()
    };

    // Mach-O's LC_MAIN stores the entry point as a *file offset* (`entryoff`), and `object`
    // reports it as-is; turn it into a virtual address through the segment that maps it.
    if format == Format::MachO
        && let Some(off) = info.entry
    {
        info.entry = file.segments().find_map(|seg| {
            let (start, size) = seg.file_range();
            (size > 0 && off >= start && off - start < size).then(|| seg.address() + (off - start))
        });
    }

    for section in file.sections() {
        let name = section.name().unwrap_or("").to_owned();
        let (offset, file_size) = section.file_range().unwrap_or((0, 0));
        info.sections.push(Section {
            perms: section_perms(section.flags(), section.kind()),
            name,
            offset,
            file_size,
            address: section.address(),
            virtual_size: section.size(),
            entropy: None,
        });
    }

    for segment in file.segments() {
        let (offset, file_size) = segment.file_range();
        let p = segment.permissions();
        info.segments.push(Segment {
            name: segment.name().ok().flatten().map(str::to_owned),
            offset,
            file_size,
            address: segment.address(),
            virtual_size: segment.size(),
            perms: Perms {
                read: p.readable(),
                write: p.writable(),
                execute: p.executable(),
            },
        });
    }
    if info.format == Format::Elf
        && let Some(lowest) = info
            .segments
            .iter()
            .filter(|s| s.file_size > 0)
            .map(|s| s.address)
            .min()
    {
        info.image_base = lowest;
    }

    if let Ok(imports) = file.imports() {
        // Malformed entries are skipped; the rest of the table is still useful.
        info.imports = imports
            .filter_map(Result::ok)
            .map(|i| Import {
                library: String::from_utf8_lossy(i.library()).into_owned(),
                name: match i.name() {
                    NameOrOrdinal::Name(n) => {
                        let raw = String::from_utf8_lossy(n);
                        orress_demangle::demangle(&raw).unwrap_or_else(|| raw.into_owned())
                    }
                    NameOrOrdinal::Ordinal(o) => format!("#{o}"),
                },
            })
            .collect();
    }
    if let Ok(exports) = file.exports() {
        info.exports = exports
            .filter_map(Result::ok)
            .map(|e| Export {
                name: match e.name() {
                    NameOrOrdinal::Name(n) => {
                        let raw = String::from_utf8_lossy(n);
                        orress_demangle::demangle(&raw).unwrap_or_else(|| raw.into_owned())
                    }
                    NameOrOrdinal::Ordinal(o) => format!("#{o}"),
                },
                // Forwarded exports (to another DLL) have no address in this file.
                address: match e.target() {
                    ExportTarget::Address { address } => address,
                    ExportTarget::Absolute { value } => value,
                    _ => 0,
                },
            })
            .collect();
    }

    info.function_symbols = code_hints::function_symbols(&file);
    match &file {
        object::File::Pe32(pe) => {
            info.import_slots = code_hints::pe_import_slots(pe, info.image_base);
            pe_details(pe, &mut info);
        }
        object::File::Pe64(pe) => {
            info.import_slots = code_hints::pe_import_slots(pe, info.image_base);
            let exception = pe.data_directory(3).map(|d| {
                (
                    d.virtual_address.get(object::LittleEndian),
                    d.size.get(object::LittleEndian),
                )
            });
            info.function_starts = code_hints::pe_pdata_starts(&info, data, exception);
            pe_details(pe, &mut info);
        }
        object::File::Elf32(elf) => {
            info.import_slots = code_hints::elf_import_slots(&file);
            protections::elf(elf, data, &mut info);
        }
        object::File::Elf64(elf) => {
            info.import_slots = code_hints::elf_import_slots(&file);
            protections::elf(elf, data, &mut info);
        }
        object::File::MachO32(macho) => {
            info.import_slots = code_hints::macho_import_slots(macho);
            protections::macho(&file, &mut info);
        }
        object::File::MachO64(macho) => {
            info.import_slots = code_hints::macho_import_slots(macho);
            protections::macho(&file, &mut info);
        }
        _ => {}
    }
    info
}

fn section_perms(flags: SectionFlags, kind: SectionKind) -> Perms {
    match flags {
        SectionFlags::Coff { characteristics } => {
            let c = characteristics.0;
            Perms {
                read: c & 0x4000_0000 != 0,
                write: c & 0x8000_0000 != 0,
                execute: c & 0x2000_0000 != 0,
            }
        }
        SectionFlags::Elf { sh_flags, .. } => {
            let f = sh_flags.0;
            Perms {
                read: f & 0x2 != 0, // SHF_ALLOC: loaded into memory, so readable
                write: f & 0x1 != 0,
                execute: f & 0x4 != 0,
            }
        }
        _ => Perms {
            read: true,
            write: matches!(kind, SectionKind::Data | SectionKind::UninitializedData),
            execute: kind == SectionKind::Text,
        },
    }
}

fn pe_details<Pe: ImageNtHeaders>(pe: &PeFile<'_, Pe>, info: &mut BinaryInfo) {
    let nt = pe.nt_headers();
    let opt = nt.optional_header();
    let dir_present = |index: usize| {
        pe.data_directory(index)
            .is_some_and(|d| d.virtual_address.get(object::LittleEndian) != 0)
    };
    let rich = pe
        .rich_header_info()
        .map(|r| {
            r.unmasked_entries()
                .map(|e| {
                    (
                        (e.comp_id >> 16) as u16,
                        (e.comp_id & 0xffff) as u16,
                        e.count,
                    )
                })
                .collect()
        })
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let details = PeDetails {
        timestamp: nt.file_header().time_date_stamp.get(object::LittleEndian),
        subsystem: subsystem_name(opt.subsystem().0).to_owned(),
        linker_version: (opt.major_linker_version(), opt.minor_linker_version()),
        is_dotnet: dir_present(14),
        has_signature: dir_present(4),
        has_tls: dir_present(9),
        rich,
    };
    protections::pe(
        opt.dll_characteristics().0,
        info.bits == Some(64),
        &details,
        info,
    );
    info.pe = Some(details);
}

fn subsystem_name(subsystem: u16) -> &'static str {
    match subsystem {
        1 => "Native (driver or boot program)",
        2 => "Windows GUI",
        3 => "Windows console",
        9 => "Windows CE GUI",
        10 => "EFI application",
        11 => "EFI boot driver",
        12 => "EFI runtime driver",
        14 => "Xbox",
        16 => "Windows boot application",
        _ => "Other",
    }
}

fn arch_name(arch: Architecture) -> &'static str {
    match arch {
        Architecture::I386 => "x86 (32-bit)",
        Architecture::X86_64 => "x86-64",
        Architecture::X86_64_X32 => "x86-64 (x32 ABI)",
        Architecture::Arm => "ARM (32-bit)",
        Architecture::Aarch64 => "ARM64 (AArch64)",
        Architecture::Aarch64_Ilp32 => "ARM64 (ILP32)",
        Architecture::Mips => "MIPS (32-bit)",
        Architecture::Mips64 => "MIPS64",
        Architecture::PowerPc => "PowerPC (32-bit)",
        Architecture::PowerPc64 => "PowerPC64",
        Architecture::Riscv32 => "RISC-V (32-bit)",
        Architecture::Riscv64 => "RISC-V (64-bit)",
        Architecture::Avr => "AVR (microcontroller)",
        Architecture::Wasm32 => "WebAssembly (32-bit)",
        Architecture::Wasm64 => "WebAssembly (64-bit)",
        Architecture::S390x => "IBM Z (s390x)",
        Architecture::Sparc | Architecture::Sparc32Plus => "SPARC",
        Architecture::Sparc64 => "SPARC64",
        Architecture::LoongArch64 => "LoongArch64",
        Architecture::Msp430 => "MSP430 (microcontroller)",
        Architecture::Bpf => "eBPF",
        _ => "Unknown architecture",
    }
}

// Used by protections.rs for ELF.
pub(crate) fn elf_type<Elf: FileHeader>(elf: &ElfFile<'_, Elf>) -> u16 {
    elf.elf_header().e_type(elf.endian()).0
}
```

`crates/orress-loaders/src/protections.rs`:

```rs
//! Security protections ("checksec"). Each one changes what a reverse engineer or
//! exploit writer sees, so each comes with an explanation of why it matters.

use object::read::elf::{ElfFile, FileHeader, ProgramHeader};
use object::{FileFlags, Object};

use crate::model::*;

const ASLR: &str = "Address Space Layout Randomization: the program is loaded at a random \
    address each run. Addresses you see in a debugger change between runs; ORRESS shows \
    addresses relative to the image base so they stay comparable.";
const DEP: &str = "Data Execution Prevention / NX: memory is either writable or executable, \
    never both. Injected code (shellcode) on the stack or heap cannot run directly.";
const CFG: &str = "Control Flow Guard: indirect calls are checked against a list of valid \
    targets, which makes hijacking function pointers harder.";
const SIGNED: &str = "Authenticode signature: the file carries a code-signing certificate. \
    A valid signature says who published it; malware sometimes uses stolen certificates.";
const SAFESEH: &str = "SafeSEH: 32-bit Windows programs list their valid exception handlers, \
    so an overwritten handler pointer on the stack cannot be used to take control.";
const PIE: &str = "Position Independent Executable: the program can be loaded at any \
    address, so ASLR randomizes it. In the file you see small addresses (from 0); at run \
    time a random base is added.";
const RELRO: &str = "RELocation Read-Only: after loading, the dynamic linker makes the \
    Global Offset Table read-only (Full RELRO), so overwriting GOT entries is impossible. \
    Partial RELRO protects only part of it.";
const CANARY: &str = "Stack canary: a secret value placed before the return address and \
    checked before the function returns. A buffer overflow that changes it crashes the \
    program (__stack_chk_fail) instead of being exploitable.";
const FORTIFY: &str = "FORTIFY_SOURCE: the compiler replaced risky functions like memcpy \
    and sprintf with checked versions (__memcpy_chk ...) that stop on overflows.";
const STRIPPED: &str = "Symbols are the names of functions and variables. A stripped binary \
    has them removed, so you must work out and name functions yourself. Most CTF \
    challenges and almost all malware are stripped.";

fn add(
    info: &mut BinaryInfo,
    name: &'static str,
    state: ProtectionState,
    detail: impl Into<String>,
    explain: &'static str,
) {
    info.protections.push(Protection {
        name,
        state,
        detail: detail.into(),
        explain,
    });
}

fn on_off(on: bool) -> ProtectionState {
    if on {
        ProtectionState::On
    } else {
        ProtectionState::Off
    }
}

pub fn pe(dll_flags: u16, is_64: bool, details: &PeDetails, info: &mut BinaryInfo) {
    const DYNAMIC_BASE: u16 = 0x0040;
    const HIGH_ENTROPY_VA: u16 = 0x0020;
    const NX_COMPAT: u16 = 0x0100;
    const NO_SEH: u16 = 0x0400;
    const GUARD_CF: u16 = 0x4000;

    let aslr = dll_flags & DYNAMIC_BASE != 0;
    let high = dll_flags & HIGH_ENTROPY_VA != 0;
    let (state, detail) = match (aslr, is_64 && high) {
        (true, true) => (ProtectionState::On, "DYNAMIC_BASE + HIGH_ENTROPY_VA"),
        (true, false) => (ProtectionState::On, "DYNAMIC_BASE"),
        _ => (ProtectionState::Off, "fixed load address"),
    };
    add(info, "ASLR", state, detail, ASLR);
    add(
        info,
        "DEP / NX",
        on_off(dll_flags & NX_COMPAT != 0),
        "NX_COMPAT flag",
        DEP,
    );
    add(
        info,
        "Control Flow Guard",
        on_off(dll_flags & GUARD_CF != 0),
        "GUARD_CF flag",
        CFG,
    );
    if !is_64 {
        let no_seh = dll_flags & NO_SEH != 0;
        add(
            info,
            "SafeSEH / no SEH",
            on_off(no_seh),
            if no_seh {
                "NO_SEH flag"
            } else {
                "not marked (needs load config to confirm)"
            },
            SAFESEH,
        );
    }
    add(
        info,
        "Signed",
        on_off(details.has_signature),
        if details.has_signature {
            "has a certificate table (not verified)"
        } else {
            "no embedded certificate (system files may be catalog-signed)"
        },
        SIGNED,
    );
    stripped(info);
}

pub fn elf<Elf: FileHeader>(elf: &ElfFile<'_, Elf>, data: &[u8], info: &mut BinaryInfo) {
    const ET_DYN: u16 = 3;
    const PT_DYNAMIC: u32 = 2;
    const PT_INTERP: u32 = 3;
    const PT_GNU_STACK: u32 = 0x6474_e551;
    const PT_GNU_RELRO: u32 = 0x6474_e552;
    const PF_X: u32 = 1;
    const DT_NULL: u64 = 0;
    const DT_BIND_NOW: u64 = 24;
    const DT_FLAGS: u64 = 30;
    const DT_FLAGS_1: u64 = 0x6fff_fffb;
    const DF_BIND_NOW: u64 = 0x8;
    const DF_1_NOW: u64 = 0x1;
    const DF_1_PIE: u64 = 0x0800_0000;

    let endian = elf.endian();
    let headers = elf.elf_program_headers();
    let find = |kind: u32| headers.iter().find(|h| h.p_type(endian).0 == kind);

    // Dynamic section entries, read straight from the PT_DYNAMIC segment.
    let mut dynamic = Vec::new();
    if let Some(h) = find(PT_DYNAMIC) {
        let offset: u64 = h.p_offset(endian).into();
        let size: u64 = h.p_filesz(endian).into();
        let entry = if elf.is_64() { 16 } else { 8 };
        let bytes = usize::try_from(offset)
            .ok()
            .zip(usize::try_from(size).ok())
            .and_then(|(o, s)| data.get(o..o.checked_add(s)?));
        for chunk in bytes.unwrap_or(&[]).chunks_exact(entry) {
            let read = |b: &[u8]| -> u64 {
                let mut buf = [0u8; 8];
                let n = b.len();
                if info.endian == Endian::Little {
                    buf[..n].copy_from_slice(b);
                    u64::from_le_bytes(buf)
                } else {
                    buf[8 - n..].copy_from_slice(b);
                    u64::from_be_bytes(buf)
                }
            };
            let half = entry / 2;
            let (tag, val) = (read(&chunk[..half]), read(&chunk[half..]));
            if tag == DT_NULL {
                break;
            }
            dynamic.push((tag, val));
        }
    }
    let dyn_val = |tag: u64| dynamic.iter().find(|(t, _)| *t == tag).map(|(_, v)| *v);
    let flags_1 = dyn_val(DT_FLAGS_1).unwrap_or(0);

    let is_dyn = crate::parse::elf_type(elf) == ET_DYN;
    // A PIE executable is ET_DYN just like a shared library, so `object` reports it as
    // `Dynamic`. It is a program if it asks for a dynamic loader (PT_INTERP) or is flagged PIE.
    if is_dyn
        && info.kind == Kind::Library
        && (find(PT_INTERP).is_some() || flags_1 & DF_1_PIE != 0)
    {
        info.kind = Kind::Executable;
    }
    let pie = is_dyn && (flags_1 & DF_1_PIE != 0 || elf.entry() != 0);
    add(
        info,
        "PIE",
        on_off(pie),
        if pie {
            "ET_DYN with entry point"
        } else {
            "fixed load address (ET_EXEC)"
        },
        PIE,
    );

    let nx = find(PT_GNU_STACK).is_none_or(|h| h.p_flags(endian).0 & PF_X == 0);
    add(
        info,
        "NX (non-executable stack)",
        on_off(nx),
        if nx {
            "stack is not executable"
        } else {
            "PT_GNU_STACK is executable"
        },
        DEP,
    );

    let bind_now = dyn_val(DT_BIND_NOW).is_some()
        || dyn_val(DT_FLAGS).is_some_and(|f| f & DF_BIND_NOW != 0)
        || flags_1 & DF_1_NOW != 0;
    let (state, detail) = match (find(PT_GNU_RELRO).is_some(), bind_now) {
        (true, true) => (ProtectionState::On, "Full RELRO"),
        (true, false) => (ProtectionState::Partial, "Partial RELRO"),
        _ => (ProtectionState::Off, "No RELRO"),
    };
    add(info, "RELRO", state, detail, RELRO);

    let names = symbol_names(elf);
    let canary = names
        .iter()
        .any(|n| n == "__stack_chk_fail" || n == "__stack_chk_guard");
    add(
        info,
        "Stack canary",
        on_off(canary),
        if canary {
            "uses __stack_chk_fail"
        } else {
            "no __stack_chk_fail"
        },
        CANARY,
    );
    let fortified = names
        .iter()
        .filter(|n| n.starts_with("__") && n.ends_with("_chk"))
        .count();
    add(
        info,
        "FORTIFY_SOURCE",
        on_off(fortified > 0),
        format!("{fortified} checked function(s)"),
        FORTIFY,
    );
    stripped(info);
}

pub fn macho(file: &object::File<'_>, info: &mut BinaryInfo) {
    const MH_PIE: u32 = 0x0020_0000;
    const MH_NO_HEAP_EXECUTION: u32 = 0x0100_0000;
    if let FileFlags::MachO { flags } = file.flags() {
        let pie = flags.0 & MH_PIE != 0;
        add(info, "PIE", on_off(pie), "MH_PIE flag", PIE);
        let nx_heap = flags.0 & MH_NO_HEAP_EXECUTION != 0;
        add(
            info,
            "Non-executable heap",
            on_off(nx_heap),
            "MH_NO_HEAP_EXECUTION flag",
            DEP,
        );
    }
    stripped(info);
}

fn symbol_names<Elf: FileHeader>(elf: &ElfFile<'_, Elf>) -> Vec<String> {
    use object::ObjectSymbol;
    elf.symbols()
        .chain(elf.dynamic_symbols())
        .filter_map(|s| s.name().ok().map(str::to_owned))
        .collect()
}

fn stripped(info: &mut BinaryInfo) {
    let has_symbols =
        info.symbol_count > info.imports.len() + info.exports.len() || info.has_debug_info;
    add(
        info,
        "Stripped",
        on_off(!has_symbols),
        if info.has_debug_info {
            "debug info present"
        } else if has_symbols {
            "function names present"
        } else {
            "stripped: only imports/exports are named"
        },
        STRIPPED,
    );
}
```

```rs
//! Plain-language explanations of common section names.

/// Explains what a section with this name usually contains.
pub fn explain(name: &str) -> &'static str {
    match name {
        ".text" | "__text" | "CODE" | ".code" => {
            "Machine code: the program's instructions. This is where you will spend most \
             of your time."
        }
        ".data" | "__data" | "DATA" => "Initialized global variables that the program can change.",
        ".rdata" | ".rodata" | "__const" | "__cstring" => {
            "Read-only data: constant strings, tables and numbers. Passwords and flag \
             fragments are often here."
        }
        ".bss" | "__bss" | "BSS" => {
            "Global variables that start as zero. Takes no space in the file, only in memory."
        }
        ".idata" => "Import table: which DLL functions the program uses.",
        ".edata" => "Export table: functions this file offers to other programs.",
        ".rsrc" => {
            "Resources: icons, dialogs, version info and sometimes embedded files. Malware \
             likes to hide payloads here."
        }
        ".reloc" => "Relocations: fix-ups needed when the program loads at a different address.",
        "fothk" => {
            "Hot-patching thunks used by Microsoft system files. Normal in Windows binaries."
        }
        ".didat" => "Delay-load import table: DLLs loaded only when first used.",
        ".pdata" | ".xdata" => {
            "Exception handling tables (64-bit Windows). They also reveal where functions start."
        }
        ".tls" => {
            "Thread Local Storage. TLS callbacks run before the entry point: a known anti-debug trick."
        }
        ".plt" | ".plt.got" | ".plt.sec" | "__stubs" => {
            "Procedure Linkage Table: small stubs that jump to library functions. A call to \
             puts@plt calls puts."
        }
        ".got" | ".got.plt" | "__got" | "__la_symbol_ptr" => {
            "Global Offset Table: addresses of library functions, filled in at load time."
        }
        ".init" | ".fini" | ".init_array" | ".fini_array" | "__mod_init_func" => {
            "Code or function pointers that run before main starts or after it ends. Hidden \
             checks sometimes live here."
        }
        ".symtab" => {
            "Symbol table: names of functions and variables. Missing in stripped binaries."
        }
        ".dynsym" => "Dynamic symbols: names needed to link with shared libraries.",
        ".strtab" | ".dynstr" | ".shstrtab" => "String table: the names used by other tables.",
        ".dynamic" => "Dynamic linking information: needed libraries and loader settings.",
        ".interp" => "Path of the dynamic loader (e.g. /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2).",
        ".comment" => "Compiler version strings, e.g. \"GCC: (Ubuntu ...)\".",
        ".eh_frame" | ".eh_frame_hdr" | ".gcc_except_table" => {
            "Stack unwinding information for exceptions; also reveals function boundaries."
        }
        ".gopclntab" | "__gopclntab" => {
            "Go runtime table that maps code to function names and line numbers. Lets \
             ORRESS recover names even in stripped Go binaries."
        }
        ".go.buildinfo" => "Go build information: Go version and module paths.",
        "UPX0" | "UPX1" | "UPX2" | ".UPX0" | ".UPX1" => {
            "Created by the UPX packer. UPX0 is empty in the file and receives the unpacked \
             code at run time; UPX1 holds the compressed program."
        }
        n if n.starts_with(".debug") || n.starts_with("__debug") => {
            "Debug information (DWARF): names, types and line numbers. A gift for reversers."
        }
        n if n.starts_with(".note") => "Notes such as the build ID and ABI version.",
        n if n.starts_with(".rela") || n.starts_with(".rel.") => {
            "Relocation entries for the dynamic linker."
        }
        _ => {
            "No standard meaning. Custom or unusual section names can be a sign of a packer or protector."
        }
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-loaders/src/tests.rs`:

```rs
//! Format tests. Fixtures are generated with `object::write`, so the tests need no
//! binary files and run on every platform.

use object::write::{Object as WObject, StandardSection, Symbol, SymbolSection};
use object::{Architecture, BinaryFormat, Endianness, SymbolFlags, SymbolKind, SymbolScope};

use crate::*;

fn object_file(format: BinaryFormat, arch: Architecture) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut obj = WObject::new(format, arch, Endianness::Little);
    let text = obj.section_id(StandardSection::Text);
    obj.append_section_data(text, &[0x55, 0x48, 0x89, 0xe5, 0xc3], 16);
    let rodata = obj.section_id(StandardSection::ReadOnlyData);
    obj.append_section_data(rodata, b"flag{generated_fixture}\0Wrong password\0", 1);
    obj.add_symbol(Symbol {
        name: b"main".to_vec(),
        value: 0,
        size: 5,
        kind: SymbolKind::Text,
        scope: SymbolScope::Linkage,
        weak: false,
        section: SymbolSection::Section(text),
        flags: SymbolFlags::None,
    });
    obj.add_symbol(Symbol {
        name: b"strcmp".to_vec(),
        value: 0,
        size: 0,
        kind: SymbolKind::Text,
        scope: SymbolScope::Unknown,
        weak: false,
        section: SymbolSection::Undefined,
        flags: SymbolFlags::None,
    });
    obj.write().unwrap()
}

#[test]
fn elf_object_is_recognized() {
    let data = object_file(BinaryFormat::Elf, Architecture::X86_64);
    let info = triage(&data);
    assert_eq!(info.format, Format::Elf);
    assert_eq!(info.kind, Kind::Object);
    assert_eq!(info.arch, "x86-64");
    assert_eq!(info.bits, Some(64));
    let text = info.sections.iter().find(|s| s.name == ".text").unwrap();
    assert!(text.perms.execute && !text.perms.write);
    assert_eq!(text.file_size, 5);
    assert!(info.parse_error.is_none());
    assert_eq!(info.hashes.sha256.len(), 64);
    assert!(info.protections.iter().any(|p| p.name == "PIE"));
}

#[test]
fn coff_and_macho_objects_parse() {
    let coff = triage(&object_file(BinaryFormat::Coff, Architecture::I386));
    assert_eq!(coff.format, Format::Coff);
    assert_eq!(coff.arch, "x86 (32-bit)");
    let macho = triage(&object_file(BinaryFormat::MachO, Architecture::Aarch64));
    assert_eq!(macho.format, Format::MachO);
    assert_eq!(macho.arch, "ARM64 (AArch64)");
}

/// A minimal 64-bit ARM64 Mach-O executable laid out like a real one: `__PAGEZERO`, a `__TEXT`
/// segment mapping the first 16 KiB at 0x1_0000_0000 with a `__stubs` section (two 12-byte
/// stubs at file offset 0x3000), an `LC_MAIN` whose `entryoff` is a *file offset*, and a
/// symbol table plus indirect symbol table naming the stubs `_printf` and `_exit`.
fn macho_executable(entryoff: u64) -> Vec<u8> {
    const TEXT_SIZE: u64 = 0x4000;
    const STUBS: u64 = 0x3000;
    const SYMTAB: u32 = 0x3100;
    const STRTAB: u32 = 0x3200;
    const INDIRECT: u32 = 0x3300;
    let strings = b"␀_printf␀_exit␀";
    let le32 = |out: &mut Vec<u8>, values: &[u32]| {
        for v in values {
            out.extend(v.to_le_bytes());
        }
    };
    let name16 = |name: &str| {
        let mut field = [0u8; 16];
        field[..name.len()].copy_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
        field
    };

    let mut cmds = Vec::new();
    // LC_SEGMENT_64 __PAGEZERO, no sections.
    le32(&mut cmds, &[0x19, 72]);
    cmds.extend(name16("__PAGEZERO"));
    for v in [0u64, 0x1_0000_0000, 0, 0] {
        cmds.extend(v.to_le_bytes());
    }
    le32(&mut cmds, &[0, 0, 0, 0]); // maxprot, initprot, nsects, flags
    // LC_SEGMENT_64 __TEXT with one section, __stubs (S_SYMBOL_STUBS, 12-byte entries).
    le32(&mut cmds, &[0x19, 72 + 80]);
    cmds.extend(name16("__TEXT"));
    for v in [0x1_0000_0000u64, TEXT_SIZE, 0, TEXT_SIZE] {
        cmds.extend(v.to_le_bytes());
    }
    le32(&mut cmds, &[5, 5, 1, 0]);
    cmds.extend(name16("__stubs"));
    cmds.extend(name16("__TEXT"));
    for v in [0x1_0000_0000 + STUBS, 24] {
        cmds.extend(v.to_le_bytes());
    }
    // offset, align, reloff, nreloc, flags, reserved1 (first indirect index), reserved2 (stub size), reserved3
    le32(&mut cmds, &[STUBS as u32, 2, 0, 0, 0x8000_0408, 0, 12, 0]);
    // LC_MAIN
    le32(&mut cmds, &[0x8000_0028, 24]);
    cmds.extend(entryoff.to_le_bytes());
    cmds.extend(0u64.to_le_bytes());
    // LC_SYMTAB: symoff, nsyms, stroff, strsize
    le32(
        &mut cmds,
        &[0x2, 24, SYMTAB, 2, STRTAB, strings.len() as u32],
    );
    // LC_DYSYMTAB: two undefined symbols; indirect table at INDIRECT with two entries.
    let mut dysymtab = [0u32; 18];
    dysymtab[4] = 0; // iundefsym
    dysymtab[5] = 2; // nundefsym
    dysymtab[12] = INDIRECT; // indirectsymoff
    dysymtab[13] = 2; // nindirectsyms
    le32(&mut cmds, &[0xb, 80]);
    le32(&mut cmds, &dysymtab);

    let mut out = Vec::new();
    // magic, cputype (ARM64), cpusubtype, filetype (MH_EXECUTE), ncmds, sizeofcmds, flags, reserved
    le32(
        &mut out,
        &[0xfeed_facf, 0x0100_000c, 0, 2, 5, cmds.len() as u32, 0, 0],
    );
    out.extend(cmds);
    out.resize(TEXT_SIZE as usize, 0);
    // nlist_64 entries: n_strx, n_type (N_UNDF | N_EXT), n_sect, n_desc, n_value.
    for (i, strx) in [1u32, 9].into_iter().enumerate() {
        let at = SYMTAB as usize + i * 16;
        out[at..at + 4].copy_from_slice(&strx.to_le_bytes());
        out[at + 4] = 0x01;
    }
    out[STRTAB as usize..STRTAB as usize + strings.len()].copy_from_slice(strings);
    for (i, symbol) in [0u32, 1].into_iter().enumerate() {
        let at = INDIRECT as usize + i * 4;
        out[at..at + 4].copy_from_slice(&symbol.to_le_bytes());
    }
    out
}

#[test]
fn garbage_does_not_panic() {
    for len in [0usize, 1, 2, 4, 64, 4096] {
        let data: Vec<u8> = (0..len).map(|i| (i * 31 % 251) as u8).collect();
        let _ = triage(&data);
    }
    // Truncated headers of every supported format.
    for format in [BinaryFormat::Elf, BinaryFormat::Coff, BinaryFormat::MachO] {
        let data = object_file(format, Architecture::X86_64);
        for cut in [4, 16, 52, 64, 100, data.len() / 2] {
            let _ = triage(&data[..cut.min(data.len())]);
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn address_mapping_round_trips() {
    let info = BinaryInfo {
        sections: vec![Section {
            name: ".text".into(),
            offset: 0x400,
            file_size: 0x200,
            address: 0x40_1000,
            virtual_size: 0x200,
            perms: Perms::default(),
            entropy: None,
        }],
        ..BinaryInfo::default()
    };
    assert_eq!(info.offset_to_address(0x410), Some(0x40_1010));
    assert_eq!(info.address_to_offset(0x40_1010), Some(0x410));
    assert_eq!(info.offset_to_address(0x10), None);
    assert_eq!(info.address_to_offset(0x40_1200), None);
    assert_eq!(
        info.section_at_offset(0x5ff).map(|s| s.name.as_str()),
        Some(".text")
    );
}

#[test]
fn address_mapping_does_not_overflow() {
    // A hostile section mapped at the very top of the address space.
    let info = BinaryInfo {
        sections: vec![Section {
            name: ".evil".into(),
            offset: u64::MAX - 0x10,
            file_size: 0x100,
            address: u64::MAX - 0x10,
            virtual_size: 0x100,
            perms: Perms::default(),
            entropy: None,
        }],
        ..BinaryInfo::default()
    };
    assert_eq!(info.offset_to_address(u64::MAX - 0x8), Some(u64::MAX - 0x8));
    let info = BinaryInfo {
        sections: vec![Section {
            offset: 0,
            address: u64::MAX - 0x10,
            ..info.sections[0].clone()
        }],
        ..BinaryInfo::default()
    };
    assert_eq!(info.offset_to_address(0x80), None);
    let info = BinaryInfo {
        sections: vec![Section {
            offset: u64::MAX - 0x10,
            address: 0x1000,
            ..info.sections[0].clone()
        }],
        ..BinaryInfo::default()
    };
    assert_eq!(info.address_to_offset(0x1080), None);
}

/// The test binary itself is a real linked executable for the host platform
/// (PE on Windows, ELF on Linux, Mach-O on macOS).
#[test]
fn host_executable_parses() {
    let exe = std::env::current_exe().unwrap();
    let data = std::fs::read(exe).unwrap();
    let info = triage(&data);
    let expected = if cfg!(windows) {
        Format::Pe
    } else if cfg!(target_os = "macos") {
        Format::MachO
    } else {
        Format::Elf
    };
    assert_eq!(info.format, expected);
    assert_eq!(info.kind, Kind::Executable);
    assert!(info.entry.is_some());
    assert!(
        info.entry_offset().is_some(),
        "entry point maps to a file offset"
    );
    assert!(!info.imports.is_empty());
    assert!(info.detections.iter().any(|d| d.name == "Rust"));
    if cfg!(windows) {
        assert!(info.pe.is_some());
        assert!(
            info.protections
                .iter()
                .any(|p| p.name == "ASLR" && p.state == ProtectionState::On)
        );
        assert!(info.hashes.imphash.is_some());
        assert!(
            info.import_slots.len() >= info.imports.len() / 2,
            "IAT slots found for imports"
        );
        assert!(
            info.function_starts.len() > 100,
            "x64 .pdata lists functions"
        );
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-lsp/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! The ORRESS language-server client.
//!
//! A thread-based LSP client (JSON-RPC over the server's stdio) with a manager that keeps one
//! server per language, started on demand. It provides live **diagnostics**, **hover**,
//! **go-to-definition** and **completion** — the features that matter most when writing a
//! solver (source-level debugging lives in `orress-dap`). No async runtime: results arrive on
//! channels the UI polls, which suits egui.
//!
//! Positions: we offer UTF-8 and UTF-16 (`positionEncodings`) and read the encoding the server
//! picks from its `initialize` result (UTF-16 when it names none — pyright and older clangd).
//! [`LspManager::encoding`] reports it; [`position_at_enc`] / [`byte_at_enc`] convert.
//!
//! User settings (`lsp.<server>` in settings.json: binary path/arguments/env, settings,
//! initialization options) apply to every adapter — built-in, imported or extension-provided —
//! matched by server name; see [`LspManager::set_server_settings`]. An adapter may carry its own
//! environment, `initializationOptions` and workspace configuration (e.g. what a Zed extension's
//! WASM returned); the user's settings are deep-merged on top of them, as in Zed.

mod transport;

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests;

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashMap, HashSet};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::{Command, Stdio};
use std::sync::Arc;

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::{Value, json};
use transport::{Notify, RpcResult, Transport, normalize_uri};

pub use lsp_types::{
    CompletionItem, CompletionItemKind, Diagnostic, DiagnosticSeverity, Hover, HoverContents,
    Location, MarkedString, MarkupContent, Position, Range, Url,
};

/// How a server counts the `character` of a position: in UTF-8 bytes, UTF-16 code units (the
/// protocol default) or Unicode scalar values.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PositionEncoding {
    Utf8,
    #[default]
    Utf16,
    Utf32,
}

/// How to launch a language server for a language.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct ServerSpec {
    /// A key identifying the server instance: the adapter key (usually the language, e.g.
    /// "rust"), plus the workspace root when there is one — so files from two projects get two
    /// servers, each rooted in its own project.
    pub key: String,
    pub command: String,
    pub args: Vec<String>,
    /// Extra environment for the server process.
    pub env: Vec<(String, String)>,
    /// The LSP language id, e.g. "rust" or "python".
    pub language_id: String,
    /// The user's `initializationOptions` for this server, if configured.
    pub initialization_options: Option<Value>,
    /// The user's server settings, the answer to `workspace/configuration`.
    pub settings: Option<Value>,
}

/// The user's configuration for one language server — the `lsp.<server>` section of
/// settings.json, in Zed's shape.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct ServerSettings {
    pub binary: Option<BinarySettings>,
    pub settings: Option<Value>,
    pub initialization_options: Option<Value>,
}

/// A server binary override (`lsp.<server>.binary`).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct BinarySettings {
    pub path: Option<String>,
    pub arguments: Option<Vec<String>>,
    pub env: Option<BTreeMap<String, String>>,
}

/// A language-server **adapter manifest**: how to launch a server for a language, as data. The
/// built-in set covers rust-analyzer, pyright and clangd; the same shape is loaded from JSON files
/// (a single object or an array) so an adapter can be added or overridden without a rebuild — the
/// no-WASM slice of Zed's language-server extensions (Zed ships the equivalent in `extension.toml`).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct LspAdapter {
    /// The ORRESS language this serves (e.g. `"Rust"`, `"C"`, `"C++"`), matched case-insensitively.
    pub language: String,
    /// The server executable (found on `PATH`).
    pub command: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub args: Vec<String>,
    /// The LSP `languageId` for `didOpen`; defaults to the lowercased language name.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub language_id: Option<String>,
    /// Ancestor files that mark the workspace root (e.g. `["Cargo.toml"]`,
    /// `["compile_commands.json", ".clangd", "CMakeLists.txt"]`). The nearest match is the root; if
    /// none is found the file is analysed standalone (detached).
    #[serde(default)]
    pub root_markers: Vec<String>,
    /// A stable key for the server instance; defaults to the lowercased language name.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub key: Option<String>,
    /// Extra environment for the server process (e.g. a toolchain on `PATH` a Zed extension asked
    /// for). The user's `lsp.<server>.binary.env` wins per variable.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")]
    pub env: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    /// The adapter's own `initializationOptions` (e.g. from a Zed extension's
    /// `language-server-initialization-options`). The user's `lsp.<server>.initialization_options`
    /// are deep-merged on top.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub initialization_options: Option<Value>,
    /// The adapter's own workspace configuration, the base answer to `workspace/configuration`
    /// (e.g. from a Zed extension's `language-server-workspace-configuration`). The user's
    /// `lsp.<server>.settings` are deep-merged on top.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub workspace_configuration: Option<Value>,
}

impl LspAdapter {
    /// The server-instance key (explicit, else the lowercased language name).
    pub fn key(&self) -> String {
        self.key
            .clone()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| self.language.to_ascii_lowercase())
    }

    /// The LSP `languageId` (explicit, else the lowercased language name).
    pub fn language_id(&self) -> String {
        self.language_id
            .clone()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| self.language.to_ascii_lowercase())
    }

    /// The nearest ancestor directory of `path` that contains one of `root_markers`, or `None`
    /// (the file is analysed standalone).
    pub fn root_for(&self, path: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf> {
        if self.root_markers.is_empty() {
            return None;
        }
        let mut dir = path.parent();
        while let Some(d) = dir {
            if self.root_markers.iter().any(|m| d.join(m).exists()) {
                return Some(d.to_path_buf());
            }
            dir = d.parent();
        }
        None
    }

    /// The names a user may configure this server under in `lsp.<server>`: its key, its
    /// executable's name (`rust-analyzer`, `clangd`), that name without a `-langserver` suffix
    /// (`pyright`), and the language.
    fn settings_names(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut names = vec![self.key()];
        if let Some(stem) = Path::new(&self.command)
            .file_stem()
            .map(|s| s.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
        {
            if let Some(short) = stem.strip_suffix("-langserver") {
                names.push(short.to_string());
            }
            names.push(stem);
        }
        names.push(self.language.to_ascii_lowercase());
        names
    }

    fn spec(&self) -> ServerSpec {
        ServerSpec {
            key: self.key(),
            command: self.command.clone(),
            args: self.args.clone(),
            env: self
                .env
                .iter()
                .map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), v.clone()))
                .collect(),
            language_id: self.language_id(),
            initialization_options: self.initialization_options.clone(),
            settings: self.workspace_configuration.clone(),
        }
    }
}

/// The built-in language-server adapters.
pub fn builtin_adapters() -> Vec<LspAdapter> {
    let a = |language: &str, command: &str, args: &[&str], markers: &[&str]| LspAdapter {
        language: language.into(),
        command: command.into(),
        args: args.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect(),
        language_id: None,
        root_markers: markers.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect(),
        ..LspAdapter::default()
    };
    vec![
        a("Rust", "rust-analyzer", &[], &["Cargo.toml"]),
        a(
            "Python",
            "pyright-langserver",
            &["--stdio"],
            &["pyproject.toml", "setup.py", "setup.cfg"],
        ),
        // clangd serves both C and C++ (the grammars added in the tree-sitter step).
        a(
            "C",
            "clangd",
            &[],
            &["compile_commands.json", ".clangd", "CMakeLists.txt"],
        ),
        a(
            "C++",
            "clangd",
            &[],
            &["compile_commands.json", ".clangd", "CMakeLists.txt"],
        ),
        // asm-lsp (cargo install asm-lsp): hover with instruction reference docs, completion and
        // diagnostics for assembly. Launched over stdio; analysed standalone when there is no root.
        LspAdapter {
            language: "Assembly".into(),
            command: "asm-lsp".into(),
            args: Vec::new(),
            language_id: Some("asm".into()),
            root_markers: vec![".asm-lsp.toml".into(), "asm-lsp.toml".into()],
            ..LspAdapter::default()
        },
    ]
}

/// Loads LSP-adapter manifests from a directory of `*.json` files (each a single adapter object or
/// an array of them). Returns the adapters and any per-file parse errors (to surface, not fail on).
pub fn load_adapters(dir: &Path) -> (Vec<LspAdapter>, Vec<String>) {
    let mut adapters = Vec::new();
    let mut errors = Vec::new();
    let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(dir) else {
        return (adapters, errors);
    };
    for entry in entries.flatten() {
        let path = entry.path();
        if path.extension().is_none_or(|e| e != "json") {
            continue;
        }
        match std::fs::read_to_string(&path) {
            // Accept either one adapter or an array of them.
            Ok(json) => match serde_json::from_str::<OneOrMany>(&json) {
                Ok(OneOrMany::One(a)) => adapters.push(*a),
                Ok(OneOrMany::Many(v)) => adapters.extend(v),
                Err(e) => errors.push(format!("LSP adapter {} ignored: {e}", path.display())),
            },
            Err(e) => errors.push(format!("LSP adapter {} ignored: {e}", path.display())),
        }
    }
    (adapters, errors)
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
#[serde(untagged)]
enum OneOrMany {
    One(Box<LspAdapter>),
    Many(Vec<LspAdapter>),
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Status {
    NotStarted,
    Starting,
    Ready,
    Failed,
}

struct Server {
    transport: Transport,
    open: HashSet<String>,
    versions: HashMap<String, i32>,
    hashes: HashMap<String, u64>,
}

/// Manages language servers and routes document events to them.
pub struct LspManager {
    servers: HashMap<String, Result<Server, String>>,
    notify: Notify,
    /// Language-server adapters, built-ins first, then any imported ones (which override by
    /// language, since `adapter_for` takes the last match).
    adapters: Vec<LspAdapter>,
    /// The user's per-server settings (`lsp.<server>`), by server name.
    server_settings: HashMap<String, ServerSettings>,
}

/// A pending request result the UI polls.
pub struct Pending {
    rx: std::sync::mpsc::Receiver<RpcResult>,
}

impl Pending {
    /// `None` while still waiting; `Some(result)` once the server replies.
    pub fn poll(&self) -> Option<RpcResult> {
        self.rx.try_recv().ok()
    }
}

impl LspManager {
    pub fn new(notify: Notify) -> Self {
        Self {
            servers: HashMap::new(),
            notify,
            adapters: builtin_adapters(),
            server_settings: HashMap::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Sets the user's per-server configuration from the `lsp` section of settings.json (an
    /// object of `"<server>": { "binary": …, "settings": …, "initialization_options": … }`).
    /// Entries that do not parse are skipped. Applies to servers started from now on.
    pub fn set_server_settings(&mut self, lsp: &Value) {
        self.server_settings = lsp
            .as_object()
            .map(|map| {
                map.iter()
                    .filter_map(|(name, v)| {
                        serde_json::from_value::<ServerSettings>(v.clone())
                            .ok()
                            .map(|s| (name.clone(), s))
                    })
                    .collect()
            })
            .unwrap_or_default();
    }

    /// The user's settings for `adapter`, looked up by its server names.
    fn settings_for(&self, adapter: &LspAdapter) -> Option<&ServerSettings> {
        adapter
            .settings_names()
            .iter()
            .find_map(|name| self.server_settings.get(name))
    }

    /// Registers imported adapters (from manifests). They are appended, so an adapter for a
    /// language already covered by a built-in overrides it.
    pub fn add_adapters(&mut self, more: Vec<LspAdapter>) {
        self.adapters.extend(more);
    }

    /// Replaces all imported adapters: the set becomes the built-ins plus `more`. Used to
    /// re-register after an extension is installed or removed.
    pub fn reset_adapters(&mut self, more: Vec<LspAdapter>) {
        self.adapters = builtin_adapters();
        self.adapters.extend(more);
    }

    /// The adapter serving `language` (case-insensitive), preferring the most recently added.
    pub fn adapter_for(&self, language: &str) -> Option<&LspAdapter> {
        self.adapters
            .iter()
            .rev()
            .find(|a| a.language.eq_ignore_ascii_case(language))
    }

    /// Resolves the launch spec, workspace root and working directory for `language` at `path`,
    /// from the matching adapter. `None` when no adapter serves the language.
    pub fn resolve(
        &self,
        language: &str,
        path: &Path,
    ) -> Option<(ServerSpec, Option<PathBuf>, PathBuf)> {
        let adapter = self.adapter_for(language)?;
        let root = adapter.root_for(path);
        let cwd = root
            .clone()
            .or_else(|| path.parent().map(Path::to_path_buf))?;
        let mut spec = adapter.spec();
        if let Some(user) = self.settings_for(adapter) {
            apply_settings(&mut spec, user);
        }
        // One server per (adapter, project root): a second project's files must not be analysed
        // under the first project's root.
        if let Some(root) = &root {
            spec.key = format!("{}@{}", spec.key, root.display());
        }
        Some((spec, root, cwd))
    }

    /// The position encoding the server for `spec_key` negotiated (UTF-16 until it is ready).
    pub fn encoding(&self, spec_key: &str) -> PositionEncoding {
        match self.servers.get(spec_key) {
            Some(Ok(server)) => server
                .transport
                .inner
                .shared
                .lock()
                .map(|s| s.encoding)
                .unwrap_or_default(),
            _ => PositionEncoding::default(),
        }
    }

    /// Sends `didClose` for every open document `keep` rejects (e.g. files whose editor tab was
    /// closed), so servers stop tracking them.
    pub fn close_documents(&mut self, mut keep: impl FnMut(&Path) -> bool) {
        for server in self.servers.values_mut().flatten() {
            let closing: Vec<String> = server
                .open
                .iter()
                .filter(|uri| {
                    Url::parse(uri)
                        .ok()
                        .and_then(|u| u.to_file_path().ok())
                        .is_some_and(|p| !keep(&p))
                })
                .cloned()
                .collect();
            for uri in closing {
                server.open.remove(&uri);
                server.versions.remove(&uri);
                server.hashes.remove(&uri);
                server.transport.inner.notify_server(
                    "textDocument/didClose",
                    json!({"textDocument": {"uri": uri}}),
                );
            }
        }
    }

    /// Ensures the server for `spec` is running and the document is open and up to date.
    /// `workspace` is the project root (a Cargo project) when the file belongs to one, or
    /// `None` for a standalone file — then the server runs in detached-file mode and only
    /// analyses the open file, rather than indexing `cwd`. `cwd` is where the server runs.
    pub fn sync(
        &mut self,
        spec: &ServerSpec,
        workspace: Option<&Path>,
        cwd: &Path,
        path: &Path,
        text: &str,
    ) {
        let Ok(uri) = Url::from_file_path(path) else {
            return;
        };
        let uri_s = uri.to_string();
        if !self.servers.contains_key(&spec.key) {
            let started = start_server(spec, workspace, cwd, path, &self.notify);
            self.servers.insert(spec.key.clone(), started);
        }
        let Some(Ok(server)) = self.servers.get_mut(&spec.key) else {
            return;
        };
        let hash = hash(text);
        if !server.open.contains(&uri_s) {
            server.open.insert(uri_s.clone());
            server.versions.insert(uri_s.clone(), 1);
            server.hashes.insert(uri_s.clone(), hash);
            server.transport.inner.notify_server(
                "textDocument/didOpen",
                json!({"textDocument": {"uri": uri, "languageId": spec.language_id, "version": 1, "text": text}}),
            );
        } else if server.hashes.get(&uri_s) != Some(&hash) {
            let v = server.versions.entry(uri_s.clone()).or_insert(1);
            *v += 1;
            server.hashes.insert(uri_s.clone(), hash);
            server.transport.inner.notify_server(
                "textDocument/didChange",
                json!({"textDocument": {"uri": uri, "version": *v}, "contentChanges": [{"text": text}]}),
            );
        }
    }

    /// Tells the server the document was saved.
    pub fn did_save(&self, spec_key: &str, path: &Path) {
        if let Some(Ok(server)) = self.servers.get(spec_key)
            && let Ok(uri) = Url::from_file_path(path)
        {
            server.transport.inner.notify_server(
                "textDocument/didSave",
                json!({"textDocument": {"uri": uri}}),
            );
        }
    }

    pub fn status(&self, spec_key: &str) -> Status {
        match self.servers.get(spec_key) {
            None => Status::NotStarted,
            Some(Err(_)) => Status::Failed,
            Some(Ok(server)) => match server.transport.inner.shared.lock() {
                Ok(s) if s.error.is_some() => Status::Failed,
                Ok(s) if s.ready => Status::Ready,
                _ => Status::Starting,
            },
        }
    }

    /// Any error that stopped the server for this language.
    pub fn error(&self, spec_key: &str) -> Option<String> {
        match self.servers.get(spec_key)? {
            Err(e) => Some(e.clone()),
            Ok(server) => server
                .transport
                .inner
                .shared
                .lock()
                .ok()
                .and_then(|s| s.error.clone()),
        }
    }

    /// Current diagnostics for a file.
    pub fn diagnostics(&self, spec_key: &str, path: &Path) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
        let Some(Ok(server)) = self.servers.get(spec_key) else {
            return Vec::new();
        };
        let Ok(uri) = Url::from_file_path(path) else {
            return Vec::new();
        };
        server
            .transport
            .inner
            .shared
            .lock()
            .ok()
            .and_then(|s| s.diagnostics.get(&normalize_uri(uri.as_ref())).cloned())
            .unwrap_or_default()
    }

    /// Every diagnostic across all servers, as (file path, diagnostic).
    pub fn all_diagnostics(&self) -> Vec<(PathBuf, Diagnostic)> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        for server in self.servers.values().flatten() {
            if let Ok(shared) = server.transport.inner.shared.lock() {
                for (uri, diags) in &shared.diagnostics {
                    if diags.is_empty() {
                        continue;
                    }
                    let path = Url::parse(uri).ok().and_then(|u| u.to_file_path().ok());
                    if let Some(path) = path {
                        for d in diags {
                            out.push((path.clone(), d.clone()));
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        out
    }

    /// A monotone counter that advances whenever any server publishes new data.
    pub fn generation(&self, spec_key: &str) -> u64 {
        match self.servers.get(spec_key) {
            Some(Ok(server)) => server
                .transport
                .inner
                .shared
                .lock()
                .map(|s| s.generation)
                .unwrap_or(0),
            _ => 0,
        }
    }

    pub fn hover(&self, spec_key: &str, path: &Path, pos: Position) -> Option<Pending> {
        self.request(spec_key, "textDocument/hover", path, pos)
    }

    pub fn definition(&self, spec_key: &str, path: &Path, pos: Position) -> Option<Pending> {
        self.request(spec_key, "textDocument/definition", path, pos)
    }

    pub fn completion(&self, spec_key: &str, path: &Path, pos: Position) -> Option<Pending> {
        self.request(spec_key, "textDocument/completion", path, pos)
    }

    fn request(&self, spec_key: &str, method: &str, path: &Path, pos: Position) -> Option<Pending> {
        let Some(Ok(server)) = self.servers.get(spec_key) else {
            return None;
        };
        // Until `initialize` returns the position encoding is unknown, so a position computed
        // now could be wrong; the caller simply asks again on a later frame.
        if !server.transport.inner.shared.lock().is_ok_and(|s| s.ready) {
            return None;
        }
        let uri = Url::from_file_path(path).ok()?;
        let rx = server.transport.inner.request(
            method,
            json!({"textDocument": {"uri": uri}, "position": {"line": pos.line, "character": pos.character}}),
        );
        Some(Pending { rx })
    }
}

fn start_server(
    spec: &ServerSpec,
    workspace: Option<&Path>,
    cwd: &Path,
    doc: &Path,
    notify: &Notify,
) -> Result<Server, String> {
    let child = Command::new(&spec.command)
        .args(&spec.args)
        .envs(spec.env.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k, v)))
        .current_dir(cwd)
        .stdin(Stdio::piped())
        .stdout(Stdio::piped())
        .stderr(Stdio::null())
        .spawn()
        .map_err(|e| format!("could not start {} ({e})", spec.command))?;

    // A real workspace gets a rootUri + workspace folder; a standalone file gets neither,
    // so rust-analyzer analyses just the opened file instead of indexing the folder.
    let root_uri = workspace.and_then(|w| Url::from_directory_path(w).ok());
    let folders = match &root_uri {
        Some(uri) => json!([{ "uri": uri, "name": "root" }]),
        None => Value::Null,
    };
    let init_options = init_options(spec.initialization_options.clone(), workspace, doc);
    let init_id = 0i64;
    let init = json!({
        "jsonrpc": "2.0",
        "id": init_id,
        "method": "initialize",
        "params": {
            "processId": std::process::id(),
            "rootUri": root_uri,
            "capabilities": {
                "general": { "positionEncodings": ["utf-8", "utf-16"] },
                "textDocument": {
                    "synchronization": { "didSave": true, "dynamicRegistration": false },
                    "publishDiagnostics": { "relatedInformation": false },
                    "hover": { "contentFormat": ["markdown", "plaintext"] },
                    "definition": { "linkSupport": false },
                    "completion": { "completionItem": { "snippetSupport": false } }
                },
                "workspace": {
                    "configuration": true,
                    "workspaceFolders": true,
                    "applyEdit": false
                }
            },
            "workspaceFolders": folders,
            // For a standalone file (no Cargo workspace) rust-analyzer needs it listed as a
            // detached file, or it reports "failed to discover workspace" and no diagnostics.
            "initializationOptions": init_options
        }
    });
    let transport = Transport::new(
        child,
        init_id,
        Vec::new(),
        spec.settings.clone(),
        Arc::clone(notify),
    );
    // Send initialize immediately (the reader flips `ready` and flushes the rest).
    transport.inner.notify_raw(init);
    Ok(Server {
        transport,
        open: HashSet::new(),
        versions: HashMap::new(),
        hashes: HashMap::new(),
    })
}

/// Layers the user's `lsp.<server>` configuration over an adapter's launch spec: a binary
/// path/arguments override, extra environment, and initialization options and server settings
/// deep-merged over the adapter's own (the user's values win, as in Zed).
fn apply_settings(spec: &mut ServerSpec, user: &ServerSettings) {
    if let Some(binary) = &user.binary {
        if let Some(path) = binary.path.as_ref().filter(|p| !p.is_empty()) {
            spec.command.clone_from(path);
        }
        if let Some(args) = &binary.arguments {
            spec.args.clone_from(args);
        }
        if let Some(env) = &binary.env {
            for (k, v) in env {
                spec.env.retain(|(key, _)| key != k);
                spec.env.push((k.clone(), v.clone()));
            }
        }
    }
    merge_option(
        &mut spec.initialization_options,
        user.initialization_options.as_ref(),
    );
    merge_option(&mut spec.settings, user.settings.as_ref());
}

/// Deep-merges `overlay` (when present) over `base`, or adopts it when `base` is empty.
fn merge_option(base: &mut Option<Value>, overlay: Option<&Value>) {
    let Some(overlay) = overlay else {
        return;
    };
    match base {
        Some(base) => merge_json(base, overlay),
        None => *base = Some(overlay.clone()),
    }
}

/// Deep-merges `overlay` into `base`: objects merge key by key (recursively), anything else —
/// scalars, arrays, mismatched types — is replaced by the overlay's value.
pub fn merge_json(base: &mut Value, overlay: &Value) {
    match (base, overlay) {
        (Value::Object(base), Value::Object(overlay)) => {
            for (key, value) in overlay {
                match base.get_mut(key) {
                    Some(existing) => merge_json(existing, value),
                    None => {
                        base.insert(key.clone(), value.clone());
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        (base, overlay) => *base = overlay.clone(),
    }
}

/// The `initializationOptions` to send: the user's, plus — for a standalone file (no workspace)
/// — the file listed as a detached file, which rust-analyzer needs to analyse it at all.
fn init_options(user: Option<Value>, workspace: Option<&Path>, doc: &Path) -> Value {
    let mut options = user.unwrap_or_else(|| json!({}));
    if workspace.is_none()
        && let Some(map) = options.as_object_mut()
        && !map.contains_key("detachedFiles")
    {
        map.insert("detachedFiles".into(), json!([doc.to_string_lossy()]));
    }
    options
}

/// The LSP position (line, UTF-8 character) for a byte offset in `text`.
pub fn position_at(text: &str, byte: usize) -> Position {
    position_at_enc(text, byte, PositionEncoding::Utf8)
}

/// The byte offset in `text` for an LSP position whose character is in UTF-8 bytes.
pub fn byte_at(text: &str, pos: Position) -> usize {
    byte_at_enc(text, pos, PositionEncoding::Utf8)
}

/// The LSP position for a byte offset in `text`, with the character counted in `encoding`.
/// An offset inside a character counts from that character's start.
pub fn position_at_enc(text: &str, byte: usize, encoding: PositionEncoding) -> Position {
    let mut byte = byte.min(text.len());
    while !text.is_char_boundary(byte) {
        byte -= 1;
    }
    let before = &text[..byte];
    let line = before.matches('\n').count() as u32;
    let line_start = before.rfind('\n').map_or(0, |p| p + 1);
    let column = &text[line_start..byte];
    let character = match encoding {
        PositionEncoding::Utf8 => column.len(),
        PositionEncoding::Utf16 => column.encode_utf16().count(),
        PositionEncoding::Utf32 => column.chars().count(),
    } as u32;
    Position { line, character }
}

/// The byte offset in `text` for an LSP position whose character is counted in `encoding`.
/// Always a char boundary within the text: a line past the end gives the end of the text, a
/// character past the end of its line gives the line end, and a column inside a character
/// (e.g. half a UTF-16 surrogate pair) gives that character's start.
pub fn byte_at_enc(text: &str, pos: Position, encoding: PositionEncoding) -> usize {
    let mut line_start = 0;
    for _ in 0..pos.line {
        match text[line_start..].find('\n') {
            Some(p) => line_start += p + 1,
            None => return text.len(),
        }
    }
    let line_end = text[line_start..]
        .find('\n')
        .map_or(text.len(), |p| line_start + p);
    let line = &text[line_start..line_end];
    let want = pos.character as usize;
    let mut units = 0usize;
    for (offset, ch) in line.char_indices() {
        let width = match encoding {
            PositionEncoding::Utf8 => ch.len_utf8(),
            PositionEncoding::Utf16 => ch.len_utf16(),
            PositionEncoding::Utf32 => 1,
        };
        if units + width > want {
            return line_start + offset;
        }
        units += width;
    }
    line_end
}

/// Plain text from a hover result, if any.
pub fn hover_text(value: &Value) -> Option<String> {
    let hover: Hover = serde_json::from_value(value.clone()).ok()?;
    let text = match hover.contents {
        HoverContents::Scalar(MarkedString::String(s)) => s,
        HoverContents::Scalar(MarkedString::LanguageString(ls)) => ls.value,
        HoverContents::Markup(MarkupContent { value, .. }) => value,
        HoverContents::Array(items) => items
            .into_iter()
            .map(|m| match m {
                MarkedString::String(s) => s,
                MarkedString::LanguageString(ls) => ls.value,
            })
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join("\n"),
    };
    (!text.trim().is_empty()).then_some(text)
}

/// The first location from a definition result.
pub fn definition_location(value: &Value) -> Option<Location> {
    // The result is a Location, a Location[] or a LocationLink[].
    if let Ok(loc) = serde_json::from_value::<Location>(value.clone()) {
        return Some(loc);
    }
    if let Ok(locs) = serde_json::from_value::<Vec<Location>>(value.clone()) {
        return locs.into_iter().next();
    }
    if let Some(arr) = value.as_array()
        && let Some(first) = arr.first()
        && let (Some(uri), Some(range)) = (
            first.get("targetUri"),
            first
                .get("targetSelectionRange")
                .or_else(|| first.get("targetRange")),
        )
    {
        let uri: Url = serde_json::from_value(uri.clone()).ok()?;
        let range: Range = serde_json::from_value(range.clone()).ok()?;
        return Some(Location { uri, range });
    }
    None
}

/// The completion items from a completion result (a list or a bare array).
pub fn completion_items(value: &Value) -> Vec<CompletionItem> {
    if let Ok(list) = serde_json::from_value::<lsp_types::CompletionList>(value.clone()) {
        return list.items;
    }
    serde_json::from_value::<Vec<CompletionItem>>(value.clone()).unwrap_or_default()
}

fn hash(text: &str) -> u64 {
    use std::hash::{Hash, Hasher};
    let mut h = std::collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher::new();
    text.hash(&mut h);
    h.finish()
}

/// Finds the nearest ancestor with a `Cargo.toml` (the Rust workspace root).
pub fn cargo_root(path: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    let mut dir = path.parent();
    while let Some(d) = dir {
        if d.join("Cargo.toml").is_file() {
            return Some(d.to_path_buf());
        }
        dir = d.parent();
    }
    None
}
```

```rs
use serde_json::json;

use crate::*;

#[test]
fn position_byte_roundtrip() {
    let text = "fn main() {\n    let x = 1;\n}\n";
    // Start of line 1 (the `let`): byte offset of 'l'.
    let byte = text.find("let").unwrap();
    let pos = position_at(text, byte);
    assert_eq!(
        pos,
        Position {
            line: 1,
            character: 4
        }
    );
    assert_eq!(byte_at(text, pos), byte);
}

#[test]
fn position_utf8_characters() {
    // "café" + newline, then a token: character offsets are UTF-8 bytes.
    let text = "// café\nx";
    let byte = text.find('x').unwrap();
    let pos = position_at(text, byte);
    assert_eq!(pos.line, 1);
    assert_eq!(pos.character, 0);
    assert_eq!(byte_at(text, pos), byte);
}

#[test]
fn parses_markup_hover() {

    assert_eq!(hover_text(&v).unwrap(), "```rust\nfn main()\n```");
}
```
