```rs
    assert_eq!(hover_text(&json!({"contents": "u32"})).unwrap(), "u32");
    assert!(hover_text(&json!({"contents": "   "})).is_none());
}

#[test]
fn parses_definition_forms() {
    let loc = json!({"uri": "file:///tmp/a.rs", "range": {"start": {"line": 1, "character": 2}, "end": {"line": 1, "character": 5}}});
    assert!(definition_location(&loc).is_some());
    let arr = json!([loc]);
    assert!(definition_location(&arr).is_some());
    // LocationLink form.
    let link = json!([{
        "targetUri": "file:///tmp/b.rs",
        "targetRange": {"start": {"line": 0, "character": 0}, "end": {"line": 0, "character": 1}},
        "targetSelectionRange": {"start": {"line": 0, "character": 0}, "end": {"line": 0, "character": 1}}
    }]);
    let got = definition_location(&link).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(got.uri.to_string(), "file:///tmp/b.rs");
    assert!(definition_location(&json!(null)).is_none());
}

#[test]
fn cargo_root_detection() {
    // This crate lives in a Cargo workspace, so a root is found above its source.
    let here = std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("src/lib.rs");
    assert!(cargo_root(&here).is_some());
}

#[test]
fn builtin_adapters_cover_the_bundled_languages() {
    let m = LspManager::new(Arc::new(|| {}));
    assert_eq!(m.adapter_for("Rust").unwrap().command, "rust-analyzer");
    assert_eq!(
        m.adapter_for("Python").unwrap().command,
        "pyright-langserver"
    );
    // C and C++ (the tree-sitter grammars just added) are both served by clangd.
    assert_eq!(m.adapter_for("C").unwrap().command, "clangd");
    assert_eq!(m.adapter_for("c++").unwrap().command, "clangd"); // case-insensitive
    assert!(m.adapter_for("Haskell").is_none());
}

#[test]
fn imported_adapter_overrides_a_builtin() {
    let json = r#"[
        { "language": "Rust", "command": "my-rust-ls", "args": ["--stdio"] },
        { "language": "Go", "command": "gopls", "root_markers": ["go.mod"] }
    ]"#;
    let parsed: Vec<LspAdapter> = match serde_json::from_str::<super::OneOrMany>(json).unwrap() {
        super::OneOrMany::Many(v) => v,
        super::OneOrMany::One(a) => vec![*a],
    };
    let mut m = LspManager::new(Arc::new(|| {}));
    m.add_adapters(parsed);
    // The imported Rust adapter wins over the built-in rust-analyzer.
    assert_eq!(m.adapter_for("Rust").unwrap().command, "my-rust-ls");
    // A new language is added; its languageId/key default to the lowercased name.
    let go = m.adapter_for("Go").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(go.command, "gopls");
    assert_eq!(go.language_id(), "go");
}

#[test]
fn root_markers_find_the_workspace() {
    let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("orress_lsp_root_{}", std::process::id()));
    let sub = dir.join("src");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&sub).unwrap();
    std::fs::write(dir.join("compile_commands.json"), "[]").unwrap();
    let adapter = &builtin_adapters()[2]; // C (clangd)
    let root = adapter.root_for(&sub.join("main.c"));
    assert_eq!(root.as_deref(), Some(dir.as_path()));
    // No marker above an unrelated path → standalone (None).
    assert!(
        adapter
            .root_for(std::path::Path::new("/nowhere/x.c"))
            .is_none()
    );
    let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
}

#[test]
fn byte_at_clamps_and_snaps_to_char_boundaries() {
    let text = "aé\nb";
    let at = |line, character| byte_at(text, Position { line, character });
    // A character past the end of the line lands on the line end, not in the next line.
    assert_eq!(at(0, 99), 3);
    // A UTF-8 column in the middle of `é` snaps back to its start (no mid-char slicing).
    assert_eq!(at(0, 2), 1);
    // A line past the end is the end of the text.
    assert_eq!(at(7, 0), text.len());
}

#[test]
fn utf16_positions_round_trip() {
    // `é` is 2 UTF-8 bytes / 1 UTF-16 unit; the crab is 4 bytes / 2 UTF-16 units.
    let text = "é🦀x";
    let x = text.find('x').unwrap();
    let pos = position_at_enc(text, x, PositionEncoding::Utf16);
    assert_eq!(pos.character, 3);
    assert_eq!(byte_at_enc(text, pos, PositionEncoding::Utf16), x);
    // Half a surrogate pair snaps to the crab's start.
    let half = Position {
        line: 0,
        character: 2,
    };
    assert_eq!(
        byte_at_enc(text, half, PositionEncoding::Utf16),
        text.find('🦀').unwrap()
    );
    // UTF-32 counts scalar values.
    assert_eq!(
        position_at_enc(text, x, PositionEncoding::Utf32).character,
        2
    );
    // A byte offset inside a character is treated as that character's start.
    assert_eq!(
        position_at_enc(text, 1, PositionEncoding::Utf8).character,
        0
    );
}

#[test]

#[test]
fn user_settings_merge_over_adapter_options_and_configuration() {
    let mut m = LspManager::new(Arc::new(|| {}));
    // What a Zed extension resolved for its server.
    m.add_adapters(vec![LspAdapter {
        language: "Gleam".into(),
        command: "gleam".into(),
        key: Some("gleam".into()),
        env: [("PATH".to_string(), "/ext/bin".to_string())].into(),
        initialization_options: Some(json!({ "a": 1, "nested": { "x": 1, "y": 2 } })),
        workspace_configuration: Some(json!({ "gleam": { "lint": true, "list": [1, 2] } })),
        ..LspAdapter::default()
    }]);
    let file = std::path::Path::new("/nowhere/a.gleam");

    // Without user settings the adapter's own values are used as-is.
    let (spec, _, _) = m.resolve("Gleam", file).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        spec.initialization_options,
        Some(json!({ "a": 1, "nested": { "x": 1, "y": 2 } }))
    );
    assert_eq!(spec.settings.as_ref().unwrap()["gleam"]["lint"], true);

    // User settings win key by key; untouched adapter keys survive; arrays are replaced.
    m.set_server_settings(&json!({
        "gleam": {
            "binary": { "env": { "PATH": "/user/bin" } },
            "initialization_options": { "nested": { "y": 20, "z": 30 } },
            "settings": { "gleam": { "list": [9] } }
        }
    }));
    let (spec, _, _) = m.resolve("Gleam", file).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        spec.initialization_options,
        Some(json!({ "a": 1, "nested": { "x": 1, "y": 20, "z": 30 } }))
    );
    assert_eq!(
        spec.settings,
        Some(json!({ "gleam": { "lint": true, "list": [9] } }))
    );
    assert_eq!(
        spec.env,
        vec![("PATH".to_string(), "/user/bin".to_string())]
    );
}

```

`crates/orress-lsp/src/transport.rs`:

```rs
//! JSON-RPC over a language server's stdio: Content-Length framing, a background reader
//! thread, request/response correlation and notification dispatch. No async runtime — the
//! UI polls results through channels, which fits egui.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader, Write};
use std::process::{Child, ChildStdin};
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicI64, Ordering};
use std::sync::mpsc::Sender;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

use serde_json::{Value, json};

use crate::PositionEncoding;

pub type Notify = Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>;

/// A response to a request: `Ok(result)` or `Err(error object)`.
pub type RpcResult = Result<Value, Value>;

/// Shared state the reader thread writes and the UI reads.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Shared {
    /// Diagnostics by document URI.
    pub diagnostics: HashMap<String, Vec<lsp_types::Diagnostic>>,
    /// Whether `initialize` has completed.
    pub ready: bool,
    /// A fatal transport error, if any.
    pub error: Option<String>,
    /// Whether the server has gone away (exited, crashed or failed `initialize`). Requests made
    /// after that fail at once instead of waiting forever.
    pub dead: bool,
    /// The position encoding negotiated in `initialize` (UTF-16, the LSP default, until then).
    pub encoding: PositionEncoding,
    /// Bumps on every change, so the UI can tell when to refresh.
    pub generation: u64,
}

pub struct Inner {
    stdin: Mutex<ChildStdin>,
    next_id: AtomicI64,
    pending: Mutex<HashMap<i64, Sender<RpcResult>>>,
    /// Notifications queued until the server is initialized.
    queue: Mutex<Vec<Value>>,
    pub shared: Mutex<Shared>,
    pub notify: Notify,
    /// The id of the `initialize` request, handled specially by the reader.
    init_id: i64,
    /// The `initialized` + initial didOpen messages to send once initialize returns.
    on_ready: Mutex<Vec<Value>>,
    /// The user's settings for this server (`lsp.<server>.settings`), the answer to the server's
    /// `workspace/configuration` requests.
    settings: Option<Value>,
}

impl Inner {
    fn bump(&self) {
        if let Ok(mut s) = self.shared.lock() {
            s.generation += 1;
        }
        (self.notify)();
    }

    fn write(&self, msg: &Value) {
        if let Ok(mut stdin) = self.stdin.lock() {
            let _ = write_message(&mut *stdin, msg);
        }
    }

    /// Writes a message directly, bypassing the ready-queue (used for `initialize`).
    pub fn notify_raw(&self, msg: Value) {
        self.write(&msg);
    }

    /// Sends a notification, queuing it until the server is ready.
    pub fn notify_server(&self, method: &str, params: Value) {
        let msg = json!({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": method, "params": params});
        let ready = self.shared.lock().map(|s| s.ready).unwrap_or(false);
        if ready {
            self.write(&msg);
        } else if let Ok(mut q) = self.queue.lock() {
            q.push(msg);
        }
    }

    /// Sends a request; its result arrives on the returned receiver. If the server is gone, the
    /// receiver gets an error straight away.
    pub fn request(&self, method: &str, params: Value) -> std::sync::mpsc::Receiver<RpcResult> {
        let id = self.next_id.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
        let (tx, rx) = std::sync::mpsc::channel();
        if self.shared.lock().map(|s| s.dead).unwrap_or(true) {
            let _ = tx.send(Err(
                json!({"message": "the language server is not running"}),
            ));
            return rx;
        }
        if let Ok(mut p) = self.pending.lock() {
            p.insert(id, tx);
        }
        let msg = json!({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": id, "method": method, "params": params});
        // Requests also wait for readiness (except initialize, sent directly at startup).
        let ready = self.shared.lock().map(|s| s.ready).unwrap_or(false);
        if ready || id == self.init_id {
            self.write(&msg);
        } else if let Ok(mut q) = self.queue.lock() {
            q.push(msg);
        }
        rx
    }

    /// Marks the server gone and fails every request still waiting for a reply, so callers
    /// polling a [`crate::Pending`] see an error instead of waiting forever.
    fn fail_pending(&self, why: &str) {
        if let Ok(mut s) = self.shared.lock() {
            s.dead = true;
        }
        let waiting: Vec<Sender<RpcResult>> = self
            .pending
            .lock()
            .map(|mut p| p.drain().map(|(_, tx)| tx).collect())
            .unwrap_or_default();
        for tx in waiting {
            let _ = tx.send(Err(json!({ "message": why })));
        }
    }
}

pub struct Transport {
    pub inner: Arc<Inner>,
    /// The server process (taken on drop, to be reaped off the UI thread).
    child: Option<Child>,
    _reader: std::thread::JoinHandle<()>,
}

impl Transport {
    /// Starts the reader thread over `child`'s stdout. `init_id` is the id used for the
    /// `initialize` request; `on_ready` are messages to flush once it returns; `settings` answers
    /// the server's `workspace/configuration` requests.
    pub fn new(
        mut child: Child,
        init_id: i64,
        on_ready: Vec<Value>,
        settings: Option<Value>,
        notify: Notify,
    ) -> Self {
        let stdin = child.stdin.take().expect("server stdin");
        let stdout = child.stdout.take().expect("server stdout");
        let inner = Arc::new(Inner {
            stdin: Mutex::new(stdin),
            next_id: AtomicI64::new(init_id + 1),
            pending: Mutex::new(HashMap::new()),
            queue: Mutex::new(Vec::new()),
            shared: Mutex::new(Shared::default()),
            notify,
            init_id,
            on_ready: Mutex::new(on_ready),
            settings,
        });
        let reader_inner = Arc::clone(&inner);
        let reader = std::thread::Builder::new()
            .name("orress-lsp-read".into())
            .spawn(move || read_loop(BufReader::new(stdout), &reader_inner))
            .expect("spawn lsp reader");
        Self {
            inner,
            child: Some(child),
            _reader: reader,
        }
    }
}

impl Drop for Transport {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // Best-effort graceful shutdown, then kill.
        self.inner
            .write(&json!({"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":-1,"method":"shutdown","params":null}));
        self.inner
            .write(&json!({"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"exit","params":null}));
        if let Some(mut child) = self.child.take() {
            let _ = child.kill();
            // Reap it (no zombie on Unix) without blocking the UI thread on the wait.
            let _ = std::thread::Builder::new()
                .name("orress-lsp-reap".into())
                .spawn(move || {
                    let _ = child.wait();
                });
        }
    }
}

fn read_loop(mut reader: impl BufRead, inner: &Arc<Inner>) {
    loop {
        match read_message(&mut reader) {
            Ok(Some(msg)) => {
                if std::env::var("ORRESS_LSP_DEBUG").is_ok() {
                    let m = msg.get("method").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or("");
                    if m == "window/showMessage"
                        || m == "textDocument/publishDiagnostics"
                        || m == "window/logMessage"
                    {
                        eprintln!(
                            "[lsp] <- {m}: {}",
                            msg.get("params")
                                .map(|p| p.to_string())
                                .unwrap_or_default()
                                .chars()
                                .take(300)
                                .collect::<String>()
                        );
                    } else {
                        eprintln!(
                            "[lsp] <- id={:?} method={:?}",
                            msg.get("id"),
                            msg.get("method")
                        );
                    }
                }
                handle(&msg, inner);
            }
            Ok(None) => {
                // EOF: the server exited. If it never became ready, surface that.
                if let Ok(mut s) = inner.shared.lock()
                    && !s.ready
                    && s.error.is_none()
                {
                    s.error = Some(
                        "the language server exited before it was ready (is it installed?)".into(),
                    );
                }
                inner.fail_pending("the language server exited");
                inner.bump();
                break;
            }
            Err(e) => {
                if let Ok(mut s) = inner.shared.lock() {
                    s.error = Some(e.to_string());
                }
                inner.fail_pending(&format!("the language server connection failed: {e}"));
                inner.bump();
                break;
            }
        }
    }
}

fn handle(msg: &Value, inner: &Arc<Inner>) {
    // A response to one of our requests.
    if let Some(id) = msg.get("id").and_then(Value::as_i64)
        && (msg.get("result").is_some() || msg.get("error").is_some())
        && msg.get("method").is_none()
    {
        if id == inner.init_id {
            match msg.get("error") {
                // A failed `initialize` leaves the server unusable: report it, don't proceed.
                Some(err) => {
                    let text = err
                        .get("message")
                        .and_then(Value::as_str)
                        .unwrap_or("unknown error");
                    if let Ok(mut s) = inner.shared.lock() {
                        s.error = Some(format!("the language server failed to initialize: {text}"));
                    }
                    inner.fail_pending("the language server failed to initialize");
                    inner.bump();
                }
                None => on_initialized(inner, msg.get("result").unwrap_or(&Value::Null)),
            }
            return;
        }
        let result: RpcResult = match msg.get("error") {
            Some(e) => Err(e.clone()),
            None => Ok(msg.get("result").cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null)),
        };
        if let Ok(mut p) = inner.pending.lock()
            && let Some(tx) = p.remove(&id)
        {
            let _ = tx.send(result);
        }
        inner.bump();
        return;
    }

    // A request from the server to us: reply so it does not stall.
    if let (Some(id), Some(method)) = (msg.get("id"), msg.get("method").and_then(Value::as_str)) {
        let result = match method {
            "workspace/configuration" => {
                // One config object per requested item, from the user's settings for this server.
                let items = msg
                    .get("params")
                    .and_then(|p| p.get("items"))
                    .and_then(Value::as_array)
                    .cloned()
                    .unwrap_or_default();
                Value::Array(
                    items
                        .iter()
                        .map(|item| {
                            configuration_for(
                                inner.settings.as_ref(),
                                item.get("section").and_then(Value::as_str),
                            )
                        })
                        .collect(),
                )
            }
            // We never apply server-initiated edits, and must say so rather than reply null.
            "workspace/applyEdit" => json!({ "applied": false }),
            _ => Value::Null, // registerCapability, workDoneProgress/create, …
        };
        inner.write(&json!({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": id, "result": result}));
        return;
    }

    // A notification from the server.
    if let Some(method) = msg.get("method").and_then(Value::as_str)
        && method == "textDocument/publishDiagnostics"
        && let Some(params) = msg.get("params")
        && let Ok(pdp) =
            serde_json::from_value::<lsp_types::PublishDiagnosticsParams>(params.clone())
    {
        if let Ok(mut s) = inner.shared.lock() {
            s.diagnostics
                .insert(normalize_uri(pdp.uri.as_ref()), pdp.diagnostics);
        }
        inner.bump();
    }
    // Other notifications ($/progress, window/logMessage, …) are ignored.
}

/// The answer to one `workspace/configuration` item: the value at `section` (a dotted path such
/// as `python.analysis`) in the user's settings for this server. A section the settings do not
/// nest under is answered with the whole settings object (users often write a server's settings
/// without the server-name wrapper, e.g. `lsp.rust-analyzer.settings = { "check": … }`).
pub(crate) fn configuration_for(settings: Option<&Value>, section: Option<&str>) -> Value {
    let Some(settings) = settings else {
        return Value::Null;
    };
    let Some(section) = section.filter(|s| !s.is_empty()) else {
        return settings.clone();
    };
    let mut node = settings;
    for part in section.split('.') {
        match node.get(part) {
            Some(next) => node = next,
            None => return settings.clone(),
        }
    }
    node.clone()
}

/// The position encoding the server picked in its `initialize` result (UTF-16 when it names
/// none, as the protocol specifies).
pub(crate) fn negotiated_encoding(result: &Value) -> PositionEncoding {
    match result
        .get("capabilities")
        .and_then(|c| c.get("positionEncoding"))
        .and_then(Value::as_str)
    {
        Some("utf-8") => PositionEncoding::Utf8,
        Some("utf-32") => PositionEncoding::Utf32,
        _ => PositionEncoding::Utf16,
    }
}

fn on_initialized(inner: &Arc<Inner>, result: &Value) {
    if std::env::var("ORRESS_LSP_DEBUG").is_ok() {
        eprintln!("[lsp] on_initialized");
    }
    inner.write(&json!({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "initialized", "params": {}}));
    if let Ok(mut s) = inner.shared.lock() {
        s.ready = true;
        s.encoding = negotiated_encoding(result);
    }
    // Flush the didOpen queued at startup, then anything queued while initializing.
    let ready_msgs = inner
        .on_ready
        .lock()
        .map(|mut v| std::mem::take(&mut *v))
        .unwrap_or_default();
    for m in ready_msgs {
        inner.write(&m);
    }
    let queued = inner
        .queue
        .lock()
        .map(|mut v| std::mem::take(&mut *v))
        .unwrap_or_default();
    for m in queued {
        inner.write(&m);
    }
    inner.bump();
}

/// Normalises a document URI for map keys. Windows paths are case-insensitive and
/// rust-analyzer lower-cases the drive letter, so fold case there.
pub fn normalize_uri(uri: &str) -> String {
    if cfg!(windows) {
        uri.to_lowercase()
    } else {
        uri.to_string()
    }
}

fn write_message(w: &mut impl Write, v: &Value) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let body = serde_json::to_vec(v)?;
    write!(w, "Content-Length: {}\r\n\r\n", body.len())?;
    w.write_all(&body)?;
    w.flush()
}

/// Reads one framed message; `Ok(None)` on EOF.
fn read_message(reader: &mut impl BufRead) -> std::io::Result<Option<Value>> {
    let mut content_length: Option<usize> = None;
    loop {
        let mut line = String::new();
        if reader.read_line(&mut line)? == 0 {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let line = line.trim_end_matches(['\r', '\n']);
        if line.is_empty() {
            break;
        }
        if let Some(v) = line.strip_prefix("Content-Length:") {
            content_length = v.trim().parse().ok();
        }
    }
    let len = content_length.ok_or_else(|| {
        std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, "missing Content-Length")
    })?;
    let mut buf = vec![0u8; len];
    reader.read_exact(&mut buf)?;
    let value = serde_json::from_slice(&buf)?;
    Ok(Some(value))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::io::Cursor;

    #[test]
    fn frames_round_trip() {
        let mut buf = Vec::new();
        write_message(&mut buf, &json!({"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"hi"})).unwrap();
        let text = String::from_utf8(buf.clone()).unwrap();
        assert!(text.starts_with("Content-Length: "));
        let mut cur = Cursor::new(buf);
        let msg = read_message(&mut cur).unwrap().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(msg["id"], 1);
        assert_eq!(msg["method"], "hi");
    }

    #[test]
    fn eof_returns_none() {
        let mut cur = Cursor::new(Vec::new());
        assert!(read_message(&mut cur).unwrap().is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn configuration_sections_resolve_from_settings() {
        let settings = json!({ "python": { "analysis": { "typeCheckingMode": "strict" } } });
        assert_eq!(
            configuration_for(Some(&settings), Some("python.analysis")),
            json!({ "typeCheckingMode": "strict" })
        );
        // A section the settings do not nest under gets the whole object.
        assert_eq!(
            configuration_for(Some(&settings), Some("rust-analyzer")),
            settings
        );
        assert_eq!(configuration_for(None, Some("python")), Value::Null);
    }

    #[test]
    fn pending_requests_fail_when_the_server_exits() {
        use std::process::{Command, Stdio};
        // `rustc --version` stands in for a server that prints something and exits at once.
        let child = Command::new("rustc")
            .arg("--version")
            .stdin(Stdio::piped())
            .stdout(Stdio::piped())
            .stderr(Stdio::null())
            .spawn()
            .expect("rustc runs");
        let transport = Transport::new(child, 0, Vec::new(), None, Arc::new(|| {}));
        let rx = transport.inner.request("textDocument/hover", json!({}));
        let result = rx
            .recv_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(20))
            .expect("the request is answered, not left hanging");
        assert!(result.is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn encoding_defaults_to_utf16() {
        assert_eq!(negotiated_encoding(&json!({})), PositionEncoding::Utf16);
        assert_eq!(
            negotiated_encoding(&json!({"capabilities": {"positionEncoding": "utf-8"}})),
            PositionEncoding::Utf8
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn reads_two_messages() {
        let mut buf = Vec::new();
        write_message(&mut buf, &json!({"n":1})).unwrap();
        write_message(&mut buf, &json!({"n":2})).unwrap();
        let mut cur = Cursor::new(buf);
        assert_eq!(read_message(&mut cur).unwrap().unwrap()["n"], 1);
        assert_eq!(read_message(&mut cur).unwrap().unwrap()["n"], 2);
        assert!(read_message(&mut cur).unwrap().is_none());
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-lsp/tests/rust_analyzer.rs`:

```rs
//! Live test against a real rust-analyzer in a small Cargo project (skipped if the
//! rust-analyzer component is not installed).
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use orress_lsp::{LspManager, ServerSpec, Status};

fn ra_command() -> String {
    // Prefer the rustup proxy in CARGO_HOME/.cargo, else rely on PATH.
    if cfg!(windows)
        && let Ok(home) = std::env::var("USERPROFILE")
    {
        let p = format!("{home}/.cargo/bin/rust-analyzer.exe");
        if std::path::Path::new(&p).exists() {
            return p;
        }
    }
    "rust-analyzer".to_string()
}

fn have_ra() -> bool {
    std::process::Command::new(ra_command())
        .arg("--version")
        .output()
        .map(|o| o.status.success() && String::from_utf8_lossy(&o.stdout).contains("rust-analyzer"))
        .unwrap_or(false)
}

#[test]
fn rust_analyzer_diagnostics_in_cargo_project() {
    if !have_ra() {
        eprintln!("rust-analyzer not installed; skipping");
        return;
    }
    let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("orress-ra-{}", std::process::id()));
    let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join("src")).unwrap();
    // `[workspace]` makes this an explicit workspace root: without it, cargo (and so
    // rust-analyzer's project load) walks up to `%TEMP%`/`$TMPDIR` and fails if any ancestor holds
    // a stray or malformed `Cargo.toml` — which the shared system temp dir may well contain. With
    // it, `cargo metadata` resolves here and flycheck can run.
    std::fs::write(
        dir.join("Cargo.toml"),
        "[package]\nname = \"t\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\nedition = \"2021\"\n\n[workspace]\n",
    )
    .unwrap();
    let file = dir.join("src/main.rs");
    std::fs::write(&file, "fn main() {\n    let _y: &str = 10;\n}\n").unwrap();

    let notify: Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync> = Arc::new(|| {});
    let mut lsp = LspManager::new(notify);
    let spec = ServerSpec {
        key: "rust".into(),
        command: ra_command(),
        args: vec![],
        language_id: "rust".into(),
        ..ServerSpec::default()
    };
    let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&file).unwrap();

    // rust-analyzer reports a type error like this one via flycheck (`cargo check`, whose message
    // is rustc's "mismatched types"), which runs on save — so open, wait for readiness, then save.
    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(90);
    let mut ready = false;
    let mut saved = false;
    while Instant::now() < deadline {
        lsp.sync(&spec, Some(&dir), &dir, &file, &text);
        match lsp.status("rust") {
            Status::Ready => ready = true,
            Status::Failed => panic!("rust-analyzer failed: {:?}", lsp.error("rust")),
            _ => {}
        }
        if ready && !saved {
            saved = true;
            lsp.did_save("rust", &file);
        }
        if ready
            && lsp
                .diagnostics("rust", &file)
                .iter()
                .any(|d| d.message.contains("mismatched types"))
        {
            break;
        }
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(400));
    }
    assert!(ready, "rust-analyzer never became ready");
    let diags = lsp.diagnostics("rust", &file);
    eprintln!(
        "diagnostics: {:#?}",
        diags.iter().map(|d| &d.message).collect::<Vec<_>>()
    );
    assert!(
        diags.iter().any(|d| d.message.contains("mismatched types")),
        "expected a mismatched-types diagnostic, got {diags:?}"
    );
    let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
}
```

`crates/orress-mcp/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that exposes ORRESS's analysis engines to external
//! agents — Claude Code and the like — over stdio JSON-RPC. It lets an agent drive ORRESS: triage
//! a file, pull its strings, disassemble managed/bytecode formats, deobfuscate JavaScript and list
//! archive contents, all through the same pure-Rust engines the GUI uses.
//!
//! The transport is newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 (the MCP stdio transport). [`dispatch`] handles
//! one message and returns the response (or `None` for a notification), so it is easy to test.

use serde_json::{Value, json};

pub mod tools;

/// Handles one JSON-RPC message, returning the response value (or `None` for a notification).
pub fn dispatch(req: &Value) -> Option<Value> {
    let id = req.get("id").cloned();
    let method = req.get("method").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");

    match method {
        "initialize" => reply(
            id,
            json!({
                "protocolVersion": "2024-11-05",
                "capabilities": { "tools": {} },
                "serverInfo": { "name": "orress-mcp", "version": env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION") }
            }),
        ),
        "ping" => reply(id, json!({})),
        "tools/list" => reply(id, json!({ "tools": tool_schemas() })),
        "tools/call" => {
            let params = req.get("params");
            let name = params
                .and_then(|p| p.get("name"))
                .and_then(Value::as_str)
                .unwrap_or("");
            let empty = json!({});
            let args = params.and_then(|p| p.get("arguments")).unwrap_or(&empty);
            // A panic inside an engine (malformed input tripping a bug) must not kill the server;
            // report it as a tool error instead.
            let outcome =
                std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| run_tool(name, args)))
                    .unwrap_or_else(|panic| {
                        Err(format!(
                            "tool `{name}` panicked: {}",
                            panic_message(panic.as_ref())
                        ))
                    });
            match outcome {
                Ok(text) => reply(id, json!({ "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": text }] })),
                Err(e) => reply(
                    id,
                    json!({ "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": format!("error: {e}") }], "isError": true }),
                ),
            }
        }
        // Notifications (no id) are silently accepted.
        _ if id.is_none() => None,
        _ => error(id, -32601, &format!("method not found: {method}")),
    }
}

/// The message of a caught panic payload (a `&str` or `String`), or a generic note.
fn panic_message(payload: &(dyn std::any::Any + Send)) -> String {
    payload
        .downcast_ref::<&str>()
        .map(|s| s.to_string())
        .or_else(|| payload.downcast_ref::<String>().cloned())
        .unwrap_or_else(|| "unknown panic".to_string())
}

fn reply(id: Option<Value>, result: Value) -> Option<Value> {
    Some(json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": id.unwrap_or(Value::Null), "result": result }))
}

fn error(id: Option<Value>, code: i64, message: &str) -> Option<Value> {
    Some(
        json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": id.unwrap_or(Value::Null), "error": { "code": code, "message": message } }),
    )
}

fn run_tool(name: &str, args: &Value) -> Result<String, String> {
    // The diff tool takes two paths rather than one.
    if name == "binary_diff" {
        let a = args
            .get("path_a")
            .and_then(Value::as_str)
            .ok_or("missing required 'path_a'")?;
        let b = args
            .get("path_b")
            .and_then(Value::as_str)
            .ok_or("missing required 'path_b'")?;
        return tools::binary_diff(a, b);
    }
    let path = args
        .get("path")
        .and_then(Value::as_str)
        .ok_or("missing required 'path' argument")?;
    match name {
        "triage" => tools::triage(path),
        "strings" => {
            let min = args.get("min_length").and_then(Value::as_u64).unwrap_or(5) as usize;
            tools::strings(path, min)
        }
        "disassemble" => tools::disassemble(path),
        "detect_vm" => tools::detect_vm(path),
        "deobfuscate_js" => tools::deobfuscate_js(path),
        "archive_list" => tools::archive_list(path),
        other => Err(format!("unknown tool: {other}")),
    }
}

/// The tool definitions advertised via `tools/list`.
fn tool_schemas() -> Value {
    let path_arg = json!({
        "type": "object",
        "properties": { "path": { "type": "string", "description": "Path to the file to analyze" } },
        "required": ["path"]
    });
    json!([
        { "name": "triage", "description": "Static triage of a file: format, architecture, hashes, protections, imports by behaviour (MITRE ATT&CK) and defanged IOCs, as Markdown.", "inputSchema": path_arg },
        { "name": "strings", "description": "Printable ASCII strings in a file.", "inputSchema": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "path": { "type": "string", "description": "Path to the file" },
                "min_length": { "type": "integer", "description": "Minimum run length (default 5)" }
            },
            "required": ["path"]
        }},
        { "name": "disassemble", "description": "Auto-detects and disassembles a managed/bytecode file: WebAssembly (WAT), Python .pyc, Java .class, .NET (IL) or Android .dex.", "inputSchema": path_arg },
        { "name": "detect_vm", "description": "Flags functions that look like a VM interpreter (bytecode dispatch loop) — the signature of VM-based obfuscation (VMProtect/Themida/custom CTF VMs).", "inputSchema": path_arg },
        { "name": "deobfuscate_js", "description": "Deobfuscates JavaScript (escapes, fromCharCode, atob, string arrays), beautifies it and lists its strings.", "inputSchema": path_arg },
        { "name": "archive_list", "description": "Lists the entries of a ZIP/JAR/APK and a JAR's Main-Class.", "inputSchema": path_arg },
        { "name": "binary_diff", "description": "BinDiff-style comparison of two native binaries: identical / changed / added / removed functions (patch diffing, malware-variant comparison).", "inputSchema": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "path_a": { "type": "string", "description": "Path to the first (older) binary" },
                "path_b": { "type": "string", "description": "Path to the second (newer) binary" }
            },
            "required": ["path_a", "path_b"]
        }}
    ])
}

mod tests;
```

`crates/orress-mcp/src/main.rs`:

```rs
//! The ORRESS MCP server binary: a newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 loop over stdio. Point an MCP
//! client (e.g. Claude Code) at this program to let an agent drive ORRESS's analysis engines.

use std::io::{BufRead, Write};

use serde_json::{Value, json};

fn main() {
    let stdin = std::io::stdin();
    let mut stdout = std::io::stdout();
    for line in stdin.lock().lines() {
        let Ok(line) = line else { break };
        if line.trim().is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let resp = match serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&line) {
            Ok(req) => orress_mcp::dispatch(&req),
            Err(e) => Some(json!({
                "jsonrpc": "2.0",
                "id": Value::Null,
                "error": { "code": -32700, "message": format!("parse error: {e}") }
            })),
        };
        if let Some(resp) = resp {
            let _ = writeln!(stdout, "{resp}");
            let _ = stdout.flush();
        }
    }
}
```

```rs
use super::*;

fn call(method: &str, params: Value) -> Value {
    dispatch(&json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": method, "params": params }))
        .expect("a response")

#[test]
fn extract_strings_finds_runs() {

    let s = tools::extract_strings(data, 5);
    assert!(s.contains(&"hello".to_string()));

#[test]
fn cap_truncates_on_a_char_boundary() {
    // A multi-byte character straddling the limit must not panic.
    let s = format!("{}{}", "a".repeat(59_999), "é".repeat(10));
    let out = tools::cap(s);
    assert!(out.ends_with("(truncated)"));
    assert!(out.starts_with(&"a".repeat(59_999)));
}

#[test]
fn panic_payloads_become_messages() {
    let caught = std::panic::catch_unwind(|| panic!("boom {}", 1)).unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(panic_message(caught.as_ref()), "boom 1");
    let caught = std::panic::catch_unwind(|| std::panic::panic_any(7u8)).unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(panic_message(caught.as_ref()), "unknown panic");
}
```

`crates/orress-mcp/src/tools.rs`:

```rs
//! The analysis tools the MCP server exposes, each reusing an ORRESS engine crate. Every tool
//! takes a file path, reads it, and returns a text result (or an error string). Output is capped so
//! a huge binary can't flood the agent.

use std::fmt::Write as _;

/// Largest text result returned to the agent.
const MAX_OUT: usize = 60_000;

fn read(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    std::fs::read(path).map_err(|e| format!("cannot read {path}: {e}"))
}

pub(crate) fn cap(mut s: String) -> String {
    if s.len() > MAX_OUT {
        // Cut at a char boundary at or below the limit (`truncate` panics mid-character).
        let mut end = MAX_OUT;
        while !s.is_char_boundary(end) {
            end -= 1;
        }
        s.truncate(end);
        s.push_str("\n… (truncated)");
    }
    s
}

/// Extracts printable ASCII runs of at least `min` characters.
pub fn extract_strings(data: &[u8], min: usize) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut cur = String::new();
    for &b in data {
        if (0x20..0x7f).contains(&b) {
            cur.push(b as char);
        } else {
            if cur.len() >= min {
                out.push(std::mem::take(&mut cur));
            } else {
                cur.clear();
            }
        }
    }
    if cur.len() >= min {
        out.push(cur);
    }
    out
}

/// A static triage report (format, hashes, protections, behaviours, IOCs) as Markdown.
pub fn triage(path: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    let data = read(path)?;
    let info = orress_loaders::triage(&data);
    let strings = extract_strings(&data, 5);
    let sref: Vec<&str> = strings.iter().map(String::as_str).collect();
    let report = orress_triage::build(&info, &sref, &data);
    Ok(cap(report.markdown))
}

/// Printable strings in the file.
pub fn strings(path: &str, min: usize) -> Result<String, String> {
    let data = read(path)?;
    let min = min.clamp(3, 200);
    let s = extract_strings(&data, min);
    Ok(cap(s.join("\n")))
}

/// Deobfuscates a JavaScript file and lists its strings.
pub fn deobfuscate_js(path: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    let data = read(path)?;
    let src = String::from_utf8_lossy(&data);
    let deob = orress_js::beautify(&orress_js::deobfuscate(&src));
    let mut out = String::from("=== deobfuscated ===\n");
    out.push_str(&deob);
    out.push_str("\n\n=== strings ===\n");
    for s in orress_js::extract_strings(&orress_js::deobfuscate(&src)) {
        let _ = writeln!(out, "{s:?}");
    }
    Ok(cap(out))
}

/// Lists a ZIP/JAR/APK's entries and (for a JAR) its Main-Class.
pub fn archive_list(path: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    let data = read(path)?;
    let ar = orress_archive::Archive::open(&data)?;
    let mut out = format!("{} entries\n", ar.entries.len());
    for e in &ar.entries {
        if e.is_dir() {
            let _ = writeln!(out, "  {}/", e.name.trim_end_matches('/'));
        } else {
            let _ = writeln!(
                out,
                "  {:<48} {:>9} bytes  ({})",
                e.name,
                e.uncompressed_size,
                e.method_name()
            );
        }
    }
    if let Some(entry) = ar.by_name("META-INF/MANIFEST.MF")
        && let Ok(mf) = ar.read(entry)
    {
        for (k, v) in orress_archive::parse_manifest(&mf) {
            if k == "Main-Class" {
                let _ = writeln!(out, "\nMain-Class: {v}");
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(cap(out))
}

/// Analyzes a native binary into a `Program` (loaders + analysis + disassembly).
fn analyze_program(path: &str) -> Result<orress_analysis::Program, String> {
    let data = std::sync::Arc::new(read(path)?);
    let analysis = orress_project::Analysis::run(&data);
    orress_analysis::Program::analyze(
        &analysis.info,
        std::sync::Arc::clone(&data),
        &analysis.strings,
    )
    .ok_or_else(|| format!("{path}: no native code to diff (architecture not supported)"))
}

/// BinDiff-style comparison of two native binaries: identical/changed/added/removed functions.
pub fn binary_diff(path_a: &str, path_b: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    let (a, b) = (analyze_program(path_a)?, analyze_program(path_b)?);
    let diff = orress_diff::diff_programs(&a, &b);
    let (identical, changed, added, removed) = diff.summary();
    let name = |r: &orress_diff::FuncRef| {
        r.name
            .clone()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("sub_{:x}", r.entry))
    };

    let mut out = String::new();
    let _ = writeln!(out, "A: {path_a} ({} functions)", a.functions.len());
    let _ = writeln!(out, "B: {path_b} ({} functions)", b.functions.len());
    let _ = writeln!(
        out,
        "identical {identical}  changed {changed}  added {added}  removed {removed}\n"
    );
    if changed > 0 {
        out.push_str("Changed:\n");
        for m in diff
            .matches
            .iter()
            .filter(|m| m.kind == orress_diff::MatchKind::Changed)
        {
            let _ = writeln!(
                out,
                "  {} -> {}  ~{:.0}%",
                name(&m.a),
                name(&m.b),
                m.similarity * 100.0
            );
        }
    }
    if added > 0 {
        out.push_str("Added (only in B):\n");
        for r in &diff.added {
            let _ = writeln!(out, "  {}", name(r));
        }
    }
    if removed > 0 {
        out.push_str("Removed (only in A):\n");
        for r in &diff.removed {
            let _ = writeln!(out, "  {}", name(r));
        }
    }
    Ok(cap(out))
}

/// Flags functions that look like a VM interpreter (bytecode dispatch loop) — the signature of
/// VM-based obfuscation (VMProtect/Themida/custom CTF VMs).
pub fn detect_vm(path: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    let program = analyze_program(path)?;
    let reports = orress_vm::scan(&program);
    if reports.is_empty() {
        return Ok("No VM-based obfuscation detected (no interpreter dispatch loop found).".into());
    }
    let mut out = format!("{} likely VM interpreter(s):\n", reports.len());
    for r in &reports {
        let _ = writeln!(
            out,
            "  fn {:#x}: dispatcher {:#x}, {} handlers / {} blocks (fan-in {}), confidence {:.0}%",
            r.entry,
            r.dispatcher,
            r.handlers,
            r.blocks,
            r.max_fan_in,
            r.confidence * 100.0
        );
    }
    Ok(cap(out))
}

/// Auto-detects a managed/bytecode format and disassembles it.
pub fn disassemble(path: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    let data = read(path)?;
    if orress_wasm::is_wasm(&data) {
        return orress_wasm::disassemble(&data).map(cap);
    }
    if orress_pyc::looks_like_pyc(&data) {
        return dis_pyc(&data);
    }
    if orress_java::is_class(&data) {
        return dis_java(&data);
    }
    if orress_dotnet::is_dotnet(&data) {
        return dis_dotnet(&data);
    }
    if orress_dex::is_dex(&data) {
        return dis_dex(&data);
    }
    Err("no bytecode disassembler for this format (try the `triage` tool)".into())
}

fn dis_pyc(data: &[u8]) -> Result<String, String> {
    let pyc = orress_pyc::parse(data)?;
    let mut out = format!("{}\n", pyc.version_label());
    fn walk(c: &orress_pyc::CodeObject, depth: usize, v: Option<(u8, u8)>, out: &mut String) {
        let pad = "  ".repeat(depth);
        let _ = writeln!(out, "{pad}{}", c.signature());
        if let Some(insns) = orress_pyc::disassemble(c, v) {
            for i in insns.iter().take(60) {
                let arg = i
                    .argval
                    .clone()
                    .or_else(|| i.arg.map(|a| a.to_string()))
                    .unwrap_or_default();
                let _ = writeln!(out, "{pad}  {:>4} {:<20} {arg}", i.offset, i.opname);
            }
        }
        for n in c.nested() {
            walk(n, depth + 1, v, out);
        }
    }
    walk(&pyc.top, 0, pyc.version, &mut out);
    Ok(cap(out))
}

fn dis_java(data: &[u8]) -> Result<String, String> {
    let cf = orress_java::parse(data)?;
    let mut out = format!("class {} ({})\n", cf.this_class, cf.java_version());
    for m in &cf.methods {
        let Some(code) = &m.code else { continue };
        let _ = writeln!(out, "\n  {}{}", m.name, m.descriptor);
        for ins in orress_java::disassemble(code, &cf.cp) {
            let _ = writeln!(
                out,
                "    {:>4}: {:<16} {}",
                ins.offset, ins.mnemonic, ins.operands
            );
        }
    }
    Ok(cap(out))
}

fn dis_dotnet(data: &[u8]) -> Result<String, String> {
    let a = orress_dotnet::parse(data)?;
    let mut out = format!("{} module {}\n", a.runtime_version, a.module_name);
    for t in &a.types {
        for m in &t.methods {
            let _ = writeln!(out, "\n  {}.{}{}", t.full_name(), m.name, m.signature);
            if let Ok(il) = a.disassemble(data, m.rva) {
                for i in il.iter().take(80) {
                    let _ = writeln!(
                        out,
                        "    IL_{:04x}: {:<12} {}",
                        i.offset, i.opcode, i.operand
                    );
                }
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(cap(out))
}

fn dis_dex(data: &[u8]) -> Result<String, String> {
    let dex = orress_dex::parse(data)?;
    let mut out = format!("DEX {} · {} strings\n", dex.version, dex.string_count);
    for c in &dex.classes {
        for m in &c.methods {
            if m.code_off == 0 {
                continue;
            }
            let _ = writeln!(out, "\n  {}", m.name);
            if let Ok(il) = dex.disassemble_method(data, m.code_off) {
                for i in il.iter().take(80) {
                    let _ = writeln!(
                        out,
                        "    {:04x}: {:<22} {}",
                        i.offset, i.mnemonic, i.operand
                    );
                }
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(cap(out))
}
```

`crates/orress-mcp/tests/cff_unflatten.rs`:

```rs
//! End-to-end guard for control-flow-flattening unflattening. crackme08 is a real rustc-compiled
//! binary whose password check is control-flow-flattened (a `match state` dispatch loop). This
//! decompiles it and verifies the decompiler recovers the original straight-line check — i.e. the
//! unflattening pass fires on genuine compiler output, not just hand-built IR.

use std::sync::Arc;

fn analyze(name: &str) -> orress_analysis::Program {
    let path = format!(
        "{}/../../academy/crackmes/bin/{}.exe",
        env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"),
        name
    );
    let data = Arc::new(std::fs::read(&path).expect("read crackme"));
    let a = orress_project::Analysis::run(&data);
    orress_analysis::Program::analyze(&a.info, Arc::clone(&data), &a.strings).expect("analyze")
}

#[test]
fn crackme08_control_flow_flattening_is_undone() {
    let p = analyze("crackme08");
    let conv = orress_decompiler::convention(orress_loaders::Format::Pe);

    let mut noted = Vec::new();
    for f in p.functions.values() {
        // The flattened check is ~36 blocks; skip the large std/runtime functions for speed.
        if f.blocks.len() > 80 {
            continue;
        }
        let Ok(out) = orress_decompiler::decompile(&p, f.entry, conv) else {
            continue;
        };
        let text = out.text();
        if text.contains("deobfuscated by ORRESS: control-flow flattening") {
            noted.push((f.entry, text));
        }
    }

    assert!(
        !noted.is_empty(),
        "unflattening should fire on crackme08's control-flow-flattened check"
    );
    // The recovered function must read as a real check (the dispatcher and its `match` are gone,
    // replaced by straight-line control flow that returns true/false).
    let (entry, text) = &noted[0];
    assert!(
        text.contains("return true") && text.contains("return false"),
        "the unflattened function at {entry:#x} should be a recovered check:\n{text}"
    );
    assert!(
        !text.contains("match "),
        "the dispatcher's match should be gone after unflattening:\n{text}"
    );
}
```

`crates/orress-mcp/tests/perf_budget.rs`:

```rs
//! Performance-budget guard for the "open" path. PLAN §16: opening a 50 MB binary with interactive
//! navigation must take < 2 s (full disassembly then runs in the background). Opening is dominated
//! by `triage` (format/sections/imports) over the whole file, so this asserts triage stays linear
//! and fast on a large input.
//!
//! Measured on this dev machine (release): triage of a 50 MB blob ~166 ms, of real 8–13 MB PEs
//! 26–38 ms — a ~12× margin under the 2 s budget. This test runs in a debug build and on arbitrary
//! CI hardware, so its threshold is deliberately generous: its job is to catch an algorithmic
//! regression (an accidental O(n²) or a hang), not to re-measure the exact budget.

use std::time::Instant;

/// A deterministic ~size-byte pseudo-random blob (no `rand` dependency).
fn blob(size: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut x = 0x1234_5678_9abc_def0u64;
    (0..size)
        .map(|_| {
            x ^= x << 13;
            x ^= x >> 7;
            x ^= x << 17;
            (x >> 24) as u8
        })
        .collect()
}

#[test]
fn opening_a_large_binary_is_fast() {
    let data = blob(50 * 1_048_576); // 50 MB — the budget's reference size
    let t = Instant::now();
    let _ = orress_loaders::triage(&data);
    let elapsed = t.elapsed();
    // Generous ceiling for a debug build on slow CI; a linear triage is well under this (hundreds
    // of ms in release, ~1 s in debug), while an O(n²) regression would take minutes.
    assert!(
        elapsed.as_secs_f64() < 5.0,
        "triage of 50 MB took {elapsed:?} — far over budget, likely an algorithmic regression"
    );
}
```

`crates/orress-mcp/tests/robustness.rs`:

```rs
//! Robustness ("fuzz-style") tests: every loader/parser must handle hostile input — truncated,
//! bit-flipped and random bytes — without panicking, hanging or over-allocating. True coverage-
//! guided fuzzing (cargo-fuzz/libFuzzer) needs a nightly toolchain that isn't available in this
//! dev environment, so this is a deterministic stand-in (seeded PRNG, committed and cross-platform)
//! that exercises the same hostile-input paths. A panic in any parser fails the owning test with a
//! reproducible input; a hang or OOM points at an unbounded read/allocation to cap.

use std::sync::Arc;

/// A tiny deterministic xorshift PRNG — no `rand` dependency, reproducible across runs/platforms.
struct Rng(u64);
impl Rng {
    fn next(&mut self) -> u64 {
        let mut x = self.0;
        x ^= x << 13;
        x ^= x >> 7;
        x ^= x << 17;
        self.0 = x;
        x
    }
    fn below(&mut self, n: usize) -> usize {
        (self.next() % n as u64) as usize
    }
    fn byte(&mut self) -> u8 {
        (self.next() >> 24) as u8
    }
}

/// Real samples plus bare format magics, as mutation seeds.
fn seeds() -> Vec<Vec<u8>> {
    let mut v: Vec<Vec<u8>> = Vec::new();
    for name in ["crackme01", "crackme05", "crackme08"] {
        let p = format!(
            "{}/../../academy/crackmes/bin/{name}.exe",
            env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")
        );
        if let Ok(b) = std::fs::read(&p) {
            v.push(b);
        }
    }
    v.extend([
        b"\x00asm\x01\x00\x00\x00".to_vec(),          // wasm
        b"\xCA\xFE\xBA\xBE\x00\x00\x00\x34".to_vec(), // java class
        b"PK\x03\x04\x14\x00\x00\x00".to_vec(),       // zip local header
        b"dex\n035\x00".to_vec(),                     // dex
        b"MZ\x90\x00\x03\x00\x00\x00".to_vec(),       // PE/DOS
        b"\x7fELF\x02\x01\x01\x00".to_vec(),          // ELF64
        b"\xa7\x0d\x0d\x0a".to_vec(),                 // pyc-ish magic
    ]);
    v
}

/// A hostile corpus: the empty input, every truncation of each seed (sampled), several bit-flip
/// mutations per seed, and pure-random blobs. `per` scales the mutation/random counts.
fn corpus(per: usize) -> Vec<Vec<u8>> {
    let mut rng = Rng(0x9e37_79b9_7f4a_7c15);
    let mut out: Vec<Vec<u8>> = vec![Vec::new()];
    for seed in seeds() {
        let step = (seed.len() / 256).max(1);
        let mut i = 0;
        while i <= seed.len() {
            out.push(seed[..i].to_vec());
            i += step;
        }
        for _ in 0..per {
            let mut m = seed.clone();
            if m.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            for _ in 0..1 + rng.below(8) {
                let p = rng.below(m.len());
                m[p] ^= 1 << (rng.next() % 8);
            }
            out.push(m);
        }
    }
    for _ in 0..per {
        let len = 1 + rng.below(512);
        out.push((0..len).map(|_| rng.byte()).collect());
    }
    out
}

#[test]
fn loaders_triage_handles_hostile_input() {
    for d in corpus(150) {
        let _ = orress_loaders::triage(&d);
    }
}

#[test]
fn wasm_parser_handles_hostile_input() {
    for d in corpus(150) {
        let _ = orress_wasm::is_wasm(&d);
        let _ = orress_wasm::parse(&d);
        let _ = orress_wasm::disassemble(&d);
    }
}

#[test]
fn pyc_parser_handles_hostile_input() {
    for d in corpus(150) {
        let _ = orress_pyc::looks_like_pyc(&d);
        let _ = orress_pyc::parse(&d);
    }
}

#[test]
fn java_parser_handles_hostile_input() {
    for d in corpus(150) {
        let _ = orress_java::is_class(&d);
        if let Ok(cf) = orress_java::parse(&d) {
            for m in cf.methods.iter().take(32) {
                if let Some(code) = &m.code {
                    let _ = orress_java::disassemble(code, &cf.cp);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn dotnet_parser_handles_hostile_input() {
    for d in corpus(150) {
        let _ = orress_dotnet::is_dotnet(&d);
        let _ = orress_dotnet::parse(&d);
    }
}

#[test]
fn dex_parser_handles_hostile_input() {
    for d in corpus(150) {
        let _ = orress_dex::is_dex(&d);
        let _ = orress_dex::parse(&d);
    }
}

    for d in corpus(150) {
        let _ = orress_archive::looks_like_zip(&d);
        let _ = orress_archive::parse_manifest(&d);
        if let Ok(a) = orress_archive::Archive::open(&d) {
            for e in a.entries.iter().take(32) {
                let _ = a.read(e);
            }
        }
    }
```

`crates/orress-mcp/tests/vm_detection.rs`:

```rs
//! Integration guard: on the bundled crackmes, VM detection is precise (the VM crackme is flagged,
//! the others are not) and jump-table recovery stays bounded (no phantom-block explosion). These
//! run against the real analysis + disassembly, so they catch jump-table over-recovery regressions
//! that unit tests on synthetic CFGs cannot.

fn analyze(name: &str) -> orress_analysis::Program {
    let path = format!(
        "{}/../../academy/crackmes/bin/{}.exe",
        env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"),
        name
    );
    let data = std::sync::Arc::new(std::fs::read(&path).expect("read crackme"));
    let analysis = orress_project::Analysis::run(&data);
    orress_analysis::Program::analyze(
        &analysis.info,
        std::sync::Arc::clone(&data),
        &analysis.strings,
    )
    .expect("analyze crackme")
}

#[test]
fn vm_crackme_is_detected_and_others_are_not() {
    assert_eq!(
        orress_vm::scan(&analyze("crackme05")).len(),
        1,
        "the VM crackme should be flagged"
    );
    for name in ["crackme01", "crackme02", "crackme03", "crackme04"] {
        assert!(
            orress_vm::scan(&analyze(name)).is_empty(),
            "{name} is not a VM and must not be flagged (false positive)"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn vm_opcode_table_is_recovered() {
    // The first devirtualization step: crackme05's 10-opcode dispatch yields a 10-entry opcode
    // table, and the handlers' recovered operations include the VM's distinctive ops (xor, rotate).
    let p = analyze("crackme05");
    let report = &orress_vm::scan(&p)[0];
    let table = orress_vm::handlers(&p, report);
    assert_eq!(table.len(), 10, "crackme05's VM has 10 opcodes");
    let ops: std::collections::HashSet<&str> = table
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|h| h.ops.iter().map(String::as_str))
        .collect();
    assert!(ops.contains("xor"), "a handler should XOR: {ops:?}");
    assert!(ops.contains("rol"), "a handler should rotate: {ops:?}");
    // The named virtual operations single out the distinctive opcodes (ISA skeleton).
    let named: std::collections::HashSet<&str> = table.iter().map(orress_vm::operation).collect();
    for op in ["xor", "subtract", "rotate", "halt/return", "push"] {
        assert!(
            named.contains(op),
            "opcode table should name a `{op}` op: {named:?}"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn vm_bytecode_blob_is_located() {
    // Register dataflow traces the opcode-fetch's base register to the bytecode blob. We verify the
    // right blob by reading its first bytes: crackme05's CODE array begins [8, 8, 0, 0, 1, ...]
    // (LEN 8, PUSHIN 0, ...), independent of where the linker placed it.
    let p = analyze("crackme05");
    let report = &orress_vm::scan(&p)[0];
    let bc = orress_vm::bytecode(&p, report).expect("bytecode blob located");
    let head = p.memory.read(bc.base, 5).expect("blob readable");
    assert_eq!(
        head,
        [8, 8, 0, 0, 1],
        "blob at {:#x} is crackme05's bytecode",
        bc.base
    );
    // The disassembly recovers the exact program: crackme05's is 83 bytes ending in a HALT (op 9).
    let dis = orress_vm::disassemble(&p, report).expect("disassembled");
    let last = dis.last().expect("instructions");
    assert_eq!(
        last.offset + 1 + last.operands.len(),
        83,
        "recovered program length"
    );
    assert_eq!(last.opcode, 9, "the bytecode ends in a HALT opcode");
}

#[test]
fn vm_bytecode_disassembles() {
    // The bytecode disassembles into the per-byte check pattern crackme05 uses:
    // PUSHIN i, PUSHIM k, XOR, ROL n, PUSHIM c, EQ ... x8, then HALT. We verify the recovered
    // operand sizes and operations: the XOR/ROL opcodes land where expected, and it ends in a halt.
    let p = analyze("crackme05");
    let report = &orress_vm::scan(&p)[0];
    let dis = orress_vm::disassemble(&p, report).expect("bytecode disassembled");
    assert!(
        dis.last().is_some_and(|i| i.op == "halt/return"),
        "ends in halt: {dis:?}"
    );
    // The first XOR is at offset 6 with no operand; the first rotate follows with a 1-byte operand.
    let xor = dis
        .iter()
        .find(|i| i.op == "xor")
        .expect("an xor instruction");
    assert!(xor.operands.is_empty(), "xor takes no operand");
    let rot = dis
        .iter()
        .find(|i| i.op == "rotate")
        .expect("a rotate instruction");
    assert_eq!(
        rot.operands.len(),
        1,
        "rotate takes a 1-byte operand (the amount)"
    );
    assert!(
        dis.len() >= 40,
        "the full program decodes: {} instructions",
        dis.len()
    );
}

#[test]
fn second_vm_crackme06_generalises() {
    // A structurally different VM (16-bit stack, 2-byte immediate operand, different opcodes) must
    // flow through the same pipeline — proof the analysis isn't over-fit to crackme05.
    let p = analyze("crackme06");
    let reports = orress_vm::scan(&p);
    assert_eq!(reports.len(), 1, "crackme06's VM is detected");
    let report = &reports[0];

    let named: std::collections::HashSet<&str> = orress_vm::handlers(&p, report)
        .iter()
        .map(orress_vm::operation)
        .collect();
    assert!(
        named.contains("multiply"),
        "its MUL opcode is named: {named:?}"
    );
    assert!(
        named.contains("push") && named.contains("xor"),
        "push/xor recovered: {named:?}"
    );

    orress_vm::bytecode(&p, report).expect("bytecode located despite a reused base register");

    let dis = orress_vm::disassemble(&p, report).expect("disassembled");
    let last = dis.last().expect("instructions");
    assert_eq!(
        last.offset + 1 + last.operands.len(),
        113,
        "recovered program length"
    );
    // PUSHI carries a 2-byte immediate: the operand-size recovery handles a 3-byte instruction.
    assert!(
        dis.iter().any(|i| i.operands.len() == 2),
        "a 2-byte-operand instruction decodes: {dis:?}"
    );
}

#[test]
fn third_vm_crackme07_register_machine_generalises() {
    // A register-based VM (no operand stack, uniform 3-byte instructions) — the hardest shape for
    // the stack-oriented assumptions. The pipeline must still detect it, locate and fully
    // disassemble the bytecode with correct operand sizes, and name its arithmetic opcodes.
    let p = analyze("crackme07");
    let reports = orress_vm::scan(&p);
    assert_eq!(reports.len(), 1, "register VM is detected");
    let report = &reports[0];

    let named: std::collections::HashSet<&str> = orress_vm::handlers(&p, report)
        .iter()
        .map(orress_vm::operation)
        .collect();
    assert!(
        named.contains("rotate") && named.contains("xor"),
        "arith ops named: {named:?}"
    );
    // A register machine has no operand stack, so nothing should be mislabeled "push".
    assert!(
        !named.contains("push"),
        "no spurious push on a register VM: {named:?}"
    );

    let dis = orress_vm::disassemble(&p, report).expect("disassembled");
    let last = dis.last().expect("instructions");
    assert_eq!(
        last.offset + 1 + last.operands.len(),
        99,
        "exact program length (33 x 3 bytes)"
    );
    // Every instruction is 3 bytes: a uniform 2-operand encoding, recovered from the shared advance.
    assert!(
        dis.iter().all(|i| i.operands.len() == 2),
        "uniform 2-operand decode: {dis:?}"
    );
}

#[test]
fn vm_keys_are_recovered_by_concolic_lift() {
    // The devirtualization payoff: symbolically executing each interpreter over its concrete
    // bytecode captures the per-byte constraints and solves a key that passes the real binary.
    // Ground truth: the keys the crackmes were built with. Three structurally-different VMs.
    for (name, key) in [
        ("crackme05", "vm_0wned"),
        ("crackme06", "h4ckv3rs"),
        ("crackme07", "r3g_v4lz"),
        // crackme08 is control-flow-flattened, not a bytecode VM, but its dispatch loop is the same
        // shape, so the concolic engine devirtualizes it the same way.
        ("crackme08", "unfl4tt3"),
    ] {
        let p = analyze(name);
        let report = &orress_vm::scan(&p)[0];
        let sol = orress_vm::solve(&p, report).unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{name}: no solution"));
        assert!(
            sol.complete,
            "{name}: incomplete solve ({} constraints), got {:?}",
            sol.constraints,
            String::from_utf8_lossy(&sol.key)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            String::from_utf8_lossy(&sol.key),
            key,
            "{name}: recovered key must match the real one"
        );
        // Each byte yields one lifted check mentioning that input byte (the devirtualized logic).
        assert_eq!(
            sol.checks.len(),
            key.len(),
            "{name}: one lifted check per byte"
        );
        for (j, c) in sol.checks.iter().enumerate() {
            assert!(
                c.contains(&format!("in[{j}]")),
                "{name}: check {j} should read in[{j}]: {c}"
            );
            assert!(
                c.contains("=="),
                "{name}: check {j} should be an equality: {c}"
            );
        }
    }
    // crackme05's lifted checks are exactly the per-byte rotate-xor the bytecode encodes.
    let p = analyze("crackme05");
    let sol = orress_vm::solve(&p, &orress_vm::scan(&p)[0]).expect("solved");
    assert_eq!(sol.checks[0], "rol((in[0] ^ 0x3b), 1) == 0x9a");
    assert_eq!(sol.checks[7], "rol((in[7] ^ 0x10), 2) == 0xd1");
}

#[test]
fn jump_table_recovery_stays_bounded() {
    // A runaway offset-table read inflates a function with hundreds of phantom blocks (seen at ~888
    // before the fix). These binaries top out near ~220 blocks; 400 leaves margin while still
    // catching an over-recovery regression.
    for name in ["crackme01", "crackme05"] {
        let program = analyze(name);
        let max_blocks = program
            .functions
            .values()
            .map(|f| f.blocks.len())
            .max()
            .unwrap_or(0);
        assert!(
            max_blocks < 400,
            "{name}: a function has {max_blocks} blocks — jump-table over-recovery?"
        );
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-project/Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[package]
name = "orress-project"
description = "Open documents, background analysis and shared cursor state for ORRESS"
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true
license.workspace = true
publish.workspace = true
rust-version.workspace = true
```

`crates/orress-project/src/annotations.rs`:

```rs
//! Your work on a file: renamed functions, comments and bookmarks.
//!
//! Annotations are saved automatically as JSON, one file per analyzed binary, named by
//! the binary's SHA-256. Opening the same file again (from any folder) brings your
//! names and comments back.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use crate::types::{FuncProto, TypeRef, UserType};

pub const EXTENSION: &str = "orress";
const VERSION: u32 = 2;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct Annotations {
    pub version: u32,
    /// SHA-256 of the file these annotations belong to.
    pub sha256: String,
    /// Path the file was last opened from (informational).
    pub last_path: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// User names by address.
    pub names: BTreeMap<u64, String>,
    /// User comments by address.
    pub comments: BTreeMap<u64, String>,
    pub bookmarks: BTreeSet<u64>,
    /// Patched bytes: file offset -> new value. Applied on top of the original file.
    pub patches: BTreeMap<u64, u8>,
    /// User-defined types, by name.
    pub types: BTreeMap<String, UserType>,
    /// A type applied to a data address: "a value of this type lives here".
    pub data_types: BTreeMap<u64, TypeRef>,
    /// A function prototype pinned to a function address (consumed by the decompiler).
    pub func_prototypes: BTreeMap<u64, FuncProto>,
}

impl Annotations {
    pub fn new(sha256: &str, path: &Path) -> Self {
        Self {
            version: VERSION,
            sha256: sha256.to_owned(),
            last_path: Some(path.to_path_buf()),
            ..Self::default()
        }
    }

    pub fn file_for(dir: &Path, sha256: &str) -> PathBuf {
        dir.join(format!("{sha256}.{EXTENSION}"))
    }

    /// Loads annotations from `path`; a missing file is not an error.
    pub fn load(path: &Path) -> Result<Option<Self>, String> {
        match std::fs::read_to_string(path) {
            Ok(json) => serde_json::from_str(&json)
                .map(Some)
                .map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display())),
            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(None),
            Err(e) => Err(format!("{}: {e}", path.display())),
        }
    }

    pub fn save(&self, path: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
        if let Some(dir) = path.parent() {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(dir).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", dir.display()))?;
        }
        let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(self).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        // Write to a temporary file first so a crash cannot leave half a file behind.
        let tmp = path.with_extension("tmp");
        std::fs::write(&tmp, json).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", tmp.display()))?;
        std::fs::rename(&tmp, path).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.names.is_empty()
            && self.comments.is_empty()
            && self.bookmarks.is_empty()
            && self.patches.is_empty()
            && self.types.is_empty()
            && self.data_types.is_empty()
            && self.func_prototypes.is_empty()
    }
}

/// Checks a user-chosen name: letters, digits, `_`, `@`, `$`, `.`, `:`, and no spaces,
/// so it reads well in the listing.
pub fn validate_name(name: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    let name = name.trim();
    if name.is_empty() {
        return Ok(()); // empty removes the name
    }
    if name.len() > 200 {
        return Err("names can be at most 200 characters".into());
    }
    if name.chars().next().is_some_and(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) {
        return Err("names cannot start with a digit".into());
    }
    match name
        .chars()
        .find(|c| !(c.is_alphanumeric() || "_@$.:?<>~".contains(*c)))
    {
        Some(c) => Err(format!(
            "`{c}` is not allowed in names; use letters, digits and _"
        )),
        None => Ok(()),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn round_trip() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("orress-annotations-{}", std::process::id()));
        let path = Annotations::file_for(&dir, "abc");
        let mut a = Annotations::new("abc", Path::new("C:/x.exe"));
        a.names.insert(0x401000, "check_password".into());
        a.comments
            .insert(0x401005, "compares with \"s3cret\"".into());
        a.bookmarks.insert(0x401000);
        a.save(&path).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(Annotations::load(&path).unwrap(), Some(a));
        assert_eq!(
            Annotations::load(&dir.join("missing.orress")).unwrap(),
            None
        );
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(dir).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn types_round_trip_and_v1_still_loads() {
        use crate::types::{FieldDef, Prim, TypeRef, UserType};
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("orress-types-{}", std::process::id()));
        let path = Annotations::file_for(&dir, "t1");
        let mut a = Annotations::new("t1", Path::new("C:/x.exe"));
        a.types.insert(
            "Packet".into(),
            UserType::Struct {
                name: "Packet".into(),
                fields: vec![FieldDef {
                    name: "magic".into(),
                    ty: TypeRef::Prim(Prim::U32),
                    count: 1,
                }],
            },
        );
        a.data_types
            .insert(0x0040_4060, TypeRef::Named("Packet".into()));
        a.save(&path).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(Annotations::load(&path).unwrap(), Some(a));

        // A pre-types (v1) file has no type fields; `#[serde(default)]` fills them in.
        let v1 = r#"{"version":1,"sha256":"old","names":{"4096":"main"}}"#;
        let legacy = dir.join("old.orress");
        std::fs::write(&legacy, v1).unwrap();
        let loaded = Annotations::load(&legacy).unwrap().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(loaded.names.get(&4096).map(String::as_str), Some("main"));
        assert!(loaded.types.is_empty() && loaded.data_types.is_empty());
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(dir).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn name_rules() {
        assert!(validate_name("check_password").is_ok());
        assert!(validate_name("").is_ok());
        assert!(validate_name("has space").is_err());
        assert!(validate_name("1abc").is_err());
    }
}
```
