`crates/orress-pwn/src/srop.rs`:

```rs
//! Sigreturn-oriented-programming frames (x86-64): build the `rt_sigframe` that `rt_sigreturn`
//! restores, so a single `sigreturn` call sets every register at once. Byte offsets follow the
//! Linux `struct sigcontext` inside the frame, as pwntools' `SigreturnFrame` uses them.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;

/// Total frame length we emit (through the signal mask).
const FRAME_LEN: usize = 248;
/// `csgsfs` default: `cs = 0x33` (64-bit user code segment), required for a valid return.
const CSGSFS_OFFSET: usize = 184;
const DEFAULT_CSGSFS: u64 = 0x33;

/// Byte offset of each saved register within the frame.
fn reg_offset(name: &str) -> Option<usize> {
    Some(match name {
        "r8" => 40,
        "r9" => 48,
        "r10" => 56,
        "r11" => 64,
        "r12" => 72,
        "r13" => 80,
        "r14" => 88,
        "r15" => 96,
        "rdi" => 104,
        "rsi" => 112,
        "rbp" => 120,
        "rbx" => 128,
        "rdx" => 136,
        "rax" => 144,
        "rcx" => 152,
        "rsp" => 160,
        "rip" => 168,
        "eflags" => 176,
        "csgsfs" => CSGSFS_OFFSET,
        _ => return None,
    })
}

/// Builds a sigreturn frame with the given registers set (names as in `reg_offset`); unset
/// registers are zero, except `csgsfs` which defaults to `0x33`.
pub fn sigreturn_frame(regs: &BTreeMap<String, u64>) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut frame = vec![0u8; FRAME_LEN];
    frame[CSGSFS_OFFSET..CSGSFS_OFFSET + 8].copy_from_slice(&DEFAULT_CSGSFS.to_le_bytes());
    for (name, &value) in regs {
        if let Some(off) = reg_offset(name) {
            frame[off..off + 8].copy_from_slice(&value.to_le_bytes());
        }
    }
    frame
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn rd(frame: &[u8], off: usize) -> u64 {
        u64::from_le_bytes(frame[off..off + 8].try_into().unwrap())
    }

    #[test]
    fn registers_land_at_their_offsets() {
        let mut regs = BTreeMap::new();
        regs.insert("rip".into(), 0x401000);
        regs.insert("rsp".into(), 0x7fff_0000);
        regs.insert("rdi".into(), 0xdead);
        let frame = sigreturn_frame(&regs);
        assert_eq!(frame.len(), FRAME_LEN);
        assert_eq!(rd(&frame, 168), 0x401000); // rip
        assert_eq!(rd(&frame, 160), 0x7fff_0000); // rsp
        assert_eq!(rd(&frame, 104), 0xdead); // rdi
        assert_eq!(rd(&frame, CSGSFS_OFFSET), DEFAULT_CSGSFS); // cs defaulted
        assert_eq!(rd(&frame, 144), 0); // rax untouched
    }

    #[test]
    fn csgsfs_is_overridable() {
        let mut regs = BTreeMap::new();
        regs.insert("csgsfs".into(), 0x0);
        let frame = sigreturn_frame(&regs);
        assert_eq!(rd(&frame, CSGSFS_OFFSET), 0);
    }
}

`crates/orress-pwn/src/tube.rs`:

```rs
//! Tubes: talk to a target over its standard I/O (a spawned local process) or over a TCP socket
//! (a remote service), with the pwntools `send`/`recvuntil`/… surface. A background reader thread
//! fills a shared buffer so `recvuntil` can wait for a delimiter with a timeout.
//!
//! Every call blocks (bounded by the timeout), so a tube is only ever driven from a worker thread,
//! never the UI thread.

use std::io::{Read, Write};
use std::net::TcpStream;
use std::process::{Child, Command, Stdio};
use std::sync::{Arc, Condvar, Mutex};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

const DEFAULT_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5);

/// The bytes read so far, and whether the far end has closed.
#[derive(Default)]
struct Buffer {
    data: Vec<u8>,
    closed: bool,
}

type Shared = Arc<(Mutex<Buffer>, Condvar)>;

/// A connection to a target. Dropping it kills a spawned child.
pub struct Tube {
    shared: Shared,
    writer: Box<dyn Write + Send>,
    child: Option<Child>,
    timeout: Duration,
}

impl Tube {
    /// Spawns `path` with `args` and talks to it over its stdin/stdout (stderr is discarded).
    pub fn process(path: &str, args: &[String]) -> std::io::Result<Self> {
        let mut child = Command::new(path)
            .args(args)
            .stdin(Stdio::piped())
            .stdout(Stdio::piped())
            .stderr(Stdio::null())
            .spawn()?;
        let stdout = child
            .stdout
            .take()
            .ok_or_else(|| std::io::Error::other("no stdout"))?;
        let writer = child
            .stdin
            .take()
            .ok_or_else(|| std::io::Error::other("no stdin"))?;
        Ok(Self::from_parts(
            Box::new(stdout),
            Box::new(writer),
            Some(child),
        ))
    }

    /// Connects to a remote `host:port` over TCP.
    pub fn remote(host: &str, port: u16) -> std::io::Result<Self> {
        let stream = TcpStream::connect((host, port))?;
        let reader = stream.try_clone()?;
        Ok(Self::from_parts(Box::new(reader), Box::new(stream), None))
    }

    fn from_parts(
        mut reader: Box<dyn Read + Send>,
        writer: Box<dyn Write + Send>,
        child: Option<Child>,
    ) -> Self {
        let shared: Shared = Arc::new((Mutex::new(Buffer::default()), Condvar::new()));
        let worker = Arc::clone(&shared);
        let _ = std::thread::Builder::new()
            .name("tube-reader".into())
            .spawn(move || {
                let (lock, cv) = &*worker;
                let mut buf = [0u8; 8192];
                loop {
                    match reader.read(&mut buf) {
                        Ok(0) | Err(_) => break,
                        Ok(n) => {
                            lock.lock()
                                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
                                .data
                                .extend_from_slice(&buf[..n]);
                            cv.notify_all();
                        }
                    }
                }
                lock.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).closed = true;
                cv.notify_all();
            });
        Self {
            shared,
            writer,
            child,
            timeout: DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
        }
    }

    /// Sets the receive timeout in seconds.
    pub fn set_timeout(&mut self, secs: f64) {
        self.timeout = Duration::from_secs_f64(secs.max(0.0));
    }

    pub fn send(&mut self, data: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        self.writer.write_all(data)?;
        self.writer.flush()
    }

    pub fn sendline(&mut self, data: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        self.writer.write_all(data)?;
        self.writer.write_all(b"\n")?;
        self.writer.flush()
    }

    /// Receives up to `n` bytes (fewer if that is all that arrives before the timeout).
    pub fn recv(&mut self, n: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
        self.wait_until(|b| !b.data.is_empty() || b.closed);
        let (lock, _) = &*self.shared;
        let mut b = lock.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        let take = n.min(b.data.len());
        b.data.drain(..take).collect()
    }

    /// Receives until `delim` appears (inclusive). On timeout or close, returns what is buffered.
    pub fn recvuntil(&mut self, delim: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        let deadline = Instant::now() + self.timeout;
        let (lock, cv) = &*self.shared;
        let mut b = lock.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        loop {
            if let Some(pos) = memchr::memmem::find(&b.data, delim) {
                return b.data.drain(..pos + delim.len()).collect();
            }
            if b.closed {
                return std::mem::take(&mut b.data);
            }
            let now = Instant::now();
            if now >= deadline {
                return std::mem::take(&mut b.data);
            }
            b = cv
                .wait_timeout(b, deadline - now)
                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
                .0;
        }
    }

    pub fn recvline(&mut self) -> Vec<u8> {
        self.recvuntil(b"\n")
    }

    /// Receives everything until the far end closes (bounded by the timeout).
    pub fn recvall(&mut self) -> Vec<u8> {
        self.wait_until(|b| b.closed);
        let (lock, _) = &*self.shared;
        let mut b = lock.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        std::mem::take(&mut b.data)
    }

    /// Closes the connection (and kills a spawned child).
    pub fn close(&mut self) {
        if let Some(mut c) = self.child.take() {
            let _ = c.kill();
            let _ = c.wait();
        }
    }

    fn wait_until(&self, done: impl Fn(&Buffer) -> bool) {
        let deadline = Instant::now() + self.timeout;
        let (lock, cv) = &*self.shared;
        let mut b = lock.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        while !done(&b) {
            let now = Instant::now();
            if now >= deadline {
                break;
            }
            b = cv
                .wait_timeout(b, deadline - now)
                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
                .0;
        }
    }
}

impl Drop for Tube {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if let Some(mut c) = self.child.take() {
            let _ = c.kill();
            let _ = c.wait();
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader};
    use std::net::TcpListener;

    #[test]
    fn remote_tube_echoes_a_line() {
        let listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").unwrap();
        let port = listener.local_addr().unwrap().port();
        // A one-shot echo server: read a line, write it back with a prompt.
        let server = std::thread::spawn(move || {
            let (stream, _) = listener.accept().unwrap();
            let mut reader = BufReader::new(stream.try_clone().unwrap());
            let mut w = stream;
            w.write_all(b"> ").unwrap();
            let mut line = String::new();
            reader.read_line(&mut line).unwrap();
            w.write_all(format!("you said: {line}").as_bytes()).unwrap();
        });

        let mut t = Tube::remote("127.0.0.1", port).unwrap();
        t.set_timeout(5.0);
        let prompt = t.recvuntil(b"> ");
        assert_eq!(prompt, b"> ");
        t.sendline(b"hello").unwrap();
        let reply = t.recvuntil(b"\n");
        assert_eq!(reply, b"you said: hello\n");
        server.join().unwrap();
    }
}

`crates/orress-pyc/examples/pyc_info.rs`:

```rs
//! Prints a `.pyc` file's version, code-object tree and (for supported versions) a disassembly.
//!
//! Run with: `cargo run -p orress-pyc --example pyc_info -- path/to/module.pyc`

use orress_pyc::CodeObject;

fn main() {
    let path = std::env::args().nth(1).expect("usage: pyc_info <file.pyc>");
    let data = std::fs::read(&path).expect("read file");
    let pyc = match orress_pyc::parse(&data) {
        Ok(p) => p,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("{path}: {e}");
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
    };
    println!("{} — {}", path, pyc.version_label());

    fn walk(c: &CodeObject, depth: usize, version: Option<(u8, u8)>) {
        let pad = "  ".repeat(depth);
        println!(
            "{pad}{} (args {}, {} consts, {} names, {} bytes)",
            c.qualname,
            c.argcount,
            c.consts.len(),
            c.names.len(),
            c.code.len()
        );
        if let Some(insns) = orress_pyc::disassemble(c, version) {
            for ins in insns.iter().take(12) {
                let arg = ins
                    .argval
                    .clone()
                    .or_else(|| ins.arg.map(|a| a.to_string()))
                    .unwrap_or_default();
                println!("{pad}    {:>4}  {:<24} {arg}", ins.offset, ins.opname);
            }
            if insns.len() > 12 {
                println!("{pad}    … {} more", insns.len() - 12);
            }
        }
        for n in c.nested() {
            walk(n, depth + 1, version);
        }
    }
    walk(&pyc.top, 0, pyc.version);
}

`crates/orress-pyc/src/dis.rs`:

```rs
//! Disassembles CPython 3.11+ "wordcode" (2-byte code units) into instructions.
//!
//! Since 3.11 the bytecode stream is interleaved with inline `CACHE` units (opcode 0) used by the
//! adaptive interpreter. A marshaled `.pyc` holds the *un-specialized* opcodes, and every unit is
//! two bytes, so a linear walk that skips `CACHE` units reproduces CPython's own instruction
//! offsets exactly. Opcode *names* and operand classes are version-specific; the bundled table is
//! authoritative for CPython 3.14 (see [`crate::opcodes_314`]), so named disassembly is offered
//! only for that version — other versions still get the full structure and raw bytecode.

use std::collections::HashSet;

use crate::marshal::CodeObject;
use crate::opcodes_314 as op;

/// One decoded instruction.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct Insn {
    /// Byte offset in `co_code` (matches CPython `dis`).
    pub offset: usize,
    pub opcode: u8,
    pub opname: String,
    /// The operand, if the opcode takes one (and after folding any `EXTENDED_ARG`).
    pub arg: Option<u32>,
    /// A resolved operand (const value, name, local, jump target), where ORRESS knows how.
    pub argval: Option<String>,
    /// True if some jump lands here.
    pub is_jump_target: bool,
}

fn in_set(set: &[u8], op: u8) -> bool {
    set.contains(&op)
}

/// Disassembles a code object with the CPython 3.14 opcode table.
pub fn disassemble_314(code: &CodeObject) -> Vec<Insn> {
    let b = &code.code;

    // Pass 1: fold caches + EXTENDED_ARG into (start_offset, opcode, full_arg).
    let mut raw: Vec<(usize, u8, u32)> = Vec::new();
    let mut i = 0;
    let mut ext: u32 = 0;
    let mut ext_start: Option<usize> = None;
    while i + 1 < b.len() {
        let opcode = b[i];
        let argbyte = b[i + 1] as u32;
        if opcode == op::CACHE {
            i += 2;
            continue;
        }
        if opcode == op::EXTENDED_ARG {
            if ext_start.is_none() {
                ext_start = Some(i);
            }
            ext = (ext << 8) | argbyte;
            i += 2;
            continue;
        }
        let start = ext_start.take().unwrap_or(i);
        raw.push((start, opcode, (ext << 8) | argbyte));
        ext = 0;
        i += 2;
    }

    // Pass 2: names, operands and jump targets.
    let mut insns: Vec<Insn> = Vec::with_capacity(raw.len());
    let mut targets: HashSet<usize> = HashSet::new();
    for (k, &(offset, opcode, full)) in raw.iter().enumerate() {
        let opname = op::opname(opcode)
            .map(String::from)
            .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("<op {opcode}>"));
        let has_arg = opcode >= op::HAVE_ARGUMENT;
        let arg = has_arg.then_some(full);

        // The unit after this instruction + its caches = the next instruction's start.
        let after = raw.get(k + 1).map(|n| n.0).unwrap_or(b.len());
        let mut jump_target = None;
        if in_set(op::HASJREL, opcode) {
            let delta = (full as usize).saturating_mul(2);
            let t = if opname.contains("JUMP_BACKWARD") {
                after.saturating_sub(delta)
            } else {
                after + delta
            };
            jump_target = Some(t);
            targets.insert(t);
        }

        let argval = arg.and_then(|a| resolve(code, opcode, &opname, a, jump_target));
        insns.push(Insn {
            offset,
            opcode,
            opname,
            arg,
            argval,
            is_jump_target: false,
        });
    }
    for ins in &mut insns {
        if targets.contains(&ins.offset) {
            ins.is_jump_target = true;
        }
    }
    insns
}

fn resolve(
    code: &CodeObject,
    opcode: u8,
    opname: &str,
    arg: u32,
    jump_target: Option<usize>,
) -> Option<String> {
    let a = arg as usize;
    // A few opcodes pack flags into the low bit of the operand (3.12+).
    if matches!(opname, "LOAD_GLOBAL" | "LOAD_ATTR" | "LOAD_SUPER_ATTR") {
        // LOAD_SUPER_ATTR packs two flags (method load, two-arg super) below the name index.
        let shift = if opname == "LOAD_SUPER_ATTR" { 2 } else { 1 };
        let name = code.names.get(arg as usize >> shift).cloned();
        let extra = if arg & 1 != 0 {
            match opname {
                "LOAD_GLOBAL" => " + NULL",
                "LOAD_SUPER_ATTR" => " + NULL|self",
                _ => " + self",
            }
        } else {
            ""
        };
        return name.map(|n| format!("{n}{extra}"));
    }
    if opname == "LOAD_SMALL_INT" {
        return Some(arg.to_string());
    }
    // Operators encoded in the operand (authoritative for CPython 3.14).
    match opname {
        "COMPARE_OP" => {
            // 3.12+: the comparison is in the high bits; the low bits are a cache flag.
            const CMP: [&str; 6] = ["<", "<=", "==", "!=", ">", ">="];
            return CMP.get((arg >> 5) as usize).map(|s| s.to_string());
        }
        "BINARY_OP" => return binary_op_symbol(arg).map(str::to_string),
        "IS_OP" => return Some(if arg == 0 { "is" } else { "is not" }.to_string()),
        "CONTAINS_OP" => return Some(if arg == 0 { "in" } else { "not in" }.to_string()),
        _ => {}
    }
    if in_set(op::HASCONST, opcode) {
        return code.consts.get(a).map(crate::marshal::Obj::render);
    }
    if in_set(op::HASNAME, opcode) {
        return code.names.get(a).cloned();
    }
    if in_set(op::HASLOCAL, opcode) || in_set(op::HASFREE, opcode) {
        return code.localsplus.get(a).cloned();
    }
    if let Some(t) = jump_target {
        return Some(format!("to {t}"));
    }
    None
}

/// The operator symbol for a `BINARY_OP` operand (CPython 3.14 `_nb_ops` order).
fn binary_op_symbol(arg: u32) -> Option<&'static str> {
    const OPS: [&str; 27] = [
        "+", "&", "//", "<<", "@", "*", "%", "|", "**", ">>", "-", "/", "^", // 0..=12
        "+=", "&=", "//=", "<<=", "@=", "*=", "%=", "|=", "**=", ">>=", "-=", "/=",
        "^=", // 13..=25
        "[]", // 26 NB_SUBSCR
    ];
    OPS.get(arg as usize).copied()
}

`crates/orress-pyc/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! Python compiled-bytecode (`.pyc`) loading for ORRESS.
//!
//! A `.pyc` is a short header (a version magic, flags, and a timestamp or source hash) followed by
//! a `marshal`-serialized module code object. [`parse`] recovers the whole code-object tree —
//! every function, comprehension and class body, with their names, constants and raw bytecode —
//! and [`disassemble`] turns a code object's bytecode into instructions. Pure `std`, no external
//! dependencies, and tolerant of hostile input.
//!
//! The marshal reader and the code-object field layout work across Python 3.x (the layout is
//! selected from the detected version). Named disassembly is currently bundled for the host's
//! CPython (3.14); other versions still yield the full structure, constants, strings and raw
//! bytecode — only the opcode *names* wait on their own bundled table.

mod dis;
mod marshal;
mod opcodes_314;

pub use dis::Insn;
pub use marshal::{CodeObject, Obj, Unmarshal};

/// How a code object is laid out in the marshal stream, which changed across Python versions.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct CodeLayout {
    /// 3.11+: `localsplusnames`/`localspluskinds`, `qualname`, exception table, no `nlocals`.
    pub modern: bool,
    /// 3.8+: a `posonlyargcount` field.
    pub has_posonly: bool,
    /// < 3.11: an `nlocals` field.
    pub has_nlocals: bool,
}

impl CodeLayout {
    fn for_version(v: Option<(u8, u8)>) -> Self {
        // Default to the modern layout when the version is unknown (most .pyc today are 3.11+).
        let (_maj, min) = v.unwrap_or((3, 11));
        let modern = min >= 11;
        Self {
            modern,
            has_posonly: min >= 8,
            has_nlocals: !modern,
        }
    }
}

/// A parsed `.pyc` file.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Pyc {
    /// Detected `(major, minor)` Python version, if the magic is known.
    pub version: Option<(u8, u8)>,
    /// The raw 16-bit magic number.
    pub magic: u16,
    /// 3.7+ hash-based pyc (otherwise timestamp-based).
    pub hash_based: bool,
    /// Length of the header before the marshal body.
    pub header_len: usize,
    pub layout: CodeLayout,
    /// The module-level code object (its constants hold the nested functions/classes).
    pub top: CodeObject,
}

impl Pyc {
    /// A short version label such as `Python 3.14` or `Python (unknown magic 1234)`.
    pub fn version_label(&self) -> String {
        match self.version {
            Some((a, b)) => format!("Python {a}.{b}"),
            None => format!("Python (unknown magic {})", self.magic),
        }
    }

    /// Whether ORRESS can name this version's opcodes (so a disassembly is meaningful).
    pub fn can_disassemble(&self) -> bool {
        self.version == Some((3, 14))
    }
}

/// CPython 3.x magic-number ranges, inclusive. Each range runs from a minor version's first
/// development magic up to just before the next minor's, so alpha/beta/point-release bumps map to
/// the right version. Anything outside (Python 2's 62211-style magics, versions newer than the
/// last known one, garbage) is reported as unknown rather than guessed.
const MAGIC_RANGES: &[(u16, u16, u8, u8)] = &[
    (3000, 3140, 3, 0),
    (3141, 3159, 3, 1),
    (3160, 3189, 3, 2),
    (3190, 3249, 3, 3),
    (3250, 3319, 3, 4),
    (3320, 3359, 3, 5),
    (3360, 3389, 3, 6),
    (3390, 3399, 3, 7),
    (3400, 3419, 3, 8),
    (3420, 3429, 3, 9),
    (3430, 3449, 3, 10),
    (3450, 3499, 3, 11),
    (3500, 3549, 3, 12),
    (3550, 3599, 3, 13),
    (3600, 3649, 3, 14),
];

fn version_from_magic(magic: u16) -> Option<(u8, u8)> {
    MAGIC_RANGES
        .iter()
        .find(|&&(lo, hi, _, _)| (lo..=hi).contains(&magic))
        .map(|&(_, _, a, b)| (a, b))
}

/// A quick check: a `.pyc` carries `\r\n` at bytes 2–3 after the 2-byte magic.
pub fn looks_like_pyc(data: &[u8]) -> bool {
    data.len() >= 16 && data[2] == 0x0d && data[3] == 0x0a
}

/// Parses a `.pyc` file into its header and code-object tree.
pub fn parse(data: &[u8]) -> Result<Pyc, String> {
    if data.len() < 16 {
        return Err("file too small to be a .pyc".into());
    }
    let magic = u16::from_le_bytes([data[0], data[1]]);
    if data[2] != 0x0d || data[3] != 0x0a {
        return Err("not a .pyc file (missing \\r\\n after the magic number)".into());
    }
    let version = version_from_magic(magic);
    let layout = CodeLayout::for_version(version);
    // Unknown magics get the current (3.7+) 16-byte header as a best guess.
    let min = version.map(|v| v.1).unwrap_or(11);

    // Header length and flags by version: 3.7+ magic/flags/(mtime+size | hash) = 16 bytes,
    // 3.3–3.6 magic/mtime/size = 12 bytes, 3.0–3.2 magic/mtime = 8 bytes.
    let (header_len, hash_based) = if min >= 7 {
        let flags = u32::from_le_bytes([data[4], data[5], data[6], data[7]]);
        (16, flags & 1 != 0)
    } else if min >= 3 {
        (12, false)
    } else {
        (8, false)
    };

    let body = data
        .get(header_len..)
        .ok_or("file truncated before the marshal body")?;
    let obj = Unmarshal::new(body, layout).read()?;
    let top = match obj {
        Obj::Code(c) => *c,
        other => {
            return Err(format!(
                "top-level object is not a code object: {}",
                other.render()
            ));
        }
    };

    Ok(Pyc {
        version,
        magic,
        hash_based,
        header_len,
        layout,
        top,
    })
}

/// Disassembles a code object, if ORRESS has the opcode table for `version`.
pub fn disassemble(code: &CodeObject, version: Option<(u8, u8)>) -> Option<Vec<Insn>> {
    (version == Some((3, 14))).then(|| dis::disassemble_314(code))
}

/// Decodes the `co_flags` bitfield into readable flag names.
pub fn flag_names(flags: u32) -> Vec<&'static str> {
    const FLAGS: &[(u32, &str)] = &[
        (0x0001, "OPTIMIZED"),
        (0x0002, "NEWLOCALS"),
        (0x0004, "VARARGS"),
        (0x0008, "VARKEYWORDS"),
        (0x0010, "NESTED"),
        (0x0020, "GENERATOR"),
        (0x0040, "NOFREE"),
        (0x0080, "COROUTINE"),
        (0x0100, "ITERABLE_COROUTINE"),
        (0x0200, "ASYNC_GENERATOR"),
    ];
    FLAGS
        .iter()
        .filter(|&&(bit, _)| flags & bit != 0)
        .map(|&(_, name)| name)
        .collect()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests;

`crates/orress-pyc/src/marshal.rs`:

```rs
//! A reader for CPython's `marshal` serialization format (the body of a `.pyc` file). It recovers
//! the object tree — code objects, constants, names, strings, numbers, containers — needed to
//! inspect and disassemble compiled Python. Pure `std`; tolerant of bad input (returns `Err`
//! rather than panicking, and caps recursion/sizes).
//!
//! The format is a stream of tagged objects. The high bit (`FLAG_REF`, 0x80) of a tag means the
//! decoded object is appended to a reference table that later `TYPE_REF` tags point back into.

use crate::CodeLayout;

const FLAG_REF: u8 = 0x80;
/// Guard against hostile/looping input.
const MAX_DEPTH: u32 = 100;
const MAX_ITEMS: usize = 50_000_000;
/// Total decode budget (objects + string/bytes payload in 16-byte units), charged again every
/// time a `TYPE_REF` back-reference is materialized. Without it a hostile stream can nest refs to
/// refs and blow up memory exponentially from a few hundred input bytes.
const MAX_BUDGET: u64 = 4_000_000;

/// A decoded marshal object.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum Obj {
    Null,
    None,
    Bool(bool),
    StopIter,
    Ellipsis,
    Int(i64),
    /// An integer too large for `i64`, rendered in decimal.
    BigInt(String),
    Float(f64),
    Complex(f64, f64),
    Bytes(Vec<u8>),
    Str(String),
    Tuple(Vec<Obj>),
    List(Vec<Obj>),
    Set(Vec<Obj>),
    FrozenSet(Vec<Obj>),
    Dict(Vec<(Obj, Obj)>),
    Code(Box<CodeObject>),
    /// A `slice(start, stop, step)` constant (`TYPE_SLICE`, marshal v5 / Python 3.14+).
    Slice(Box<(Obj, Obj, Obj)>),
    /// A tag ORRESS doesn't decode; carries the raw type byte.
    Unknown(u8),
}

impl Obj {
    /// A short human rendering for a constant/argument (strings quoted, code objects named).
    pub fn render(&self) -> String {
        match self {
            Obj::Null => "NULL".into(),
            Obj::None => "None".into(),
            Obj::Bool(b) => if *b { "True" } else { "False" }.into(),
            Obj::StopIter => "StopIteration".into(),
            Obj::Ellipsis => "...".into(),
            Obj::Int(i) => i.to_string(),
            Obj::BigInt(s) => s.clone(),
            Obj::Float(f) => f.to_string(),
            Obj::Complex(r, i) => format!("{r}+{i}j"),
            Obj::Bytes(b) => format!("b{:?}", String::from_utf8_lossy(b)),
            Obj::Str(s) => format!("{s:?}"),
            Obj::Tuple(v) => format!("({})", render_list(v)),
            Obj::List(v) => format!("[{}]", render_list(v)),
            Obj::Set(v) => format!("{{{}}}", render_list(v)),
            Obj::FrozenSet(v) => format!("frozenset({{{}}})", render_list(v)),
            Obj::Dict(_) => "{...}".into(),
            Obj::Code(c) => format!("<code {}>", c.name),
            Obj::Slice(s) => format!(
                "slice({}, {}, {})",
                s.0.render(),
                s.1.render(),
                s.2.render()
            ),
            Obj::Unknown(t) => format!("<unknown 0x{t:02x}>"),
        }
    }

    fn as_string(&self) -> String {
        match self {
            Obj::Str(s) => s.clone(),
            Obj::Bytes(b) => String::from_utf8_lossy(b).into_owned(),
            _ => "?".into(),
        }
    }

    /// Flattens a tuple/list of strings to `Vec<String>` (for names/varnames).
    fn as_string_vec(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        match self {
            Obj::Tuple(v) | Obj::List(v) => v.iter().map(Obj::as_string).collect(),
            _ => Vec::new(),
        }
    }
}

fn render_list(v: &[Obj]) -> String {
    v.iter()
        .take(8)
        .map(Obj::render)
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join(", ")
}

/// A decoded Python code object (one function / module / comprehension body).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct CodeObject {
    pub argcount: u32,
    pub posonlyargcount: u32,
    pub kwonlyargcount: u32,
    pub stacksize: u32,
    pub flags: u32,
    /// Raw bytecode (`co_code`).
    pub code: Vec<u8>,
    pub consts: Vec<Obj>,
    pub names: Vec<String>,
    /// 3.11+: `co_localsplusnames` (args, locals, cells, frees). Earlier: varnames + cell + free.
    pub localsplus: Vec<String>,
    pub filename: String,
    pub name: String,
    /// 3.11+ qualified name; equal to `name` on older versions.
    pub qualname: String,
    pub firstlineno: u32,
}

impl CodeObject {
    /// A `def`-style signature reconstructed from the argument count and local names
    /// (`def check(pw)`), with `/` for positional-only and `*` before keyword-only args.
    pub fn signature(&self) -> String {
        if self.name == "<module>" {
            return "<module>".to_string();
        }
        let mut parts: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
        let pos = self.argcount as usize;
        for (i, name) in self.localsplus.iter().take(pos).enumerate() {
            parts.push(name.clone());
            if i + 1 == self.posonlyargcount as usize {
                parts.push("/".to_string());
            }
        }
        if self.kwonlyargcount > 0 {
            parts.push("*".to_string());
            for name in self
                .localsplus
                .iter()
                .skip(pos)
                .take(self.kwonlyargcount as usize)
            {
                parts.push(name.clone());
            }
        }
        format!("def {}({})", self.name, parts.join(", "))
    }

    /// The function/module docstring: `co_consts[0]` when it is a string.
    pub fn docstring(&self) -> Option<&str> {
        match self.consts.first() {
            Some(Obj::Str(s)) => Some(s),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// Nested code objects found in this object's constants (inner functions, comprehensions).
    pub fn nested(&self) -> Vec<&CodeObject> {
        self.consts
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|c| match c {
                Obj::Code(c) => Some(c.as_ref()),
                _ => None,
            })
            .collect()
    }
}

/// Reads a marshal stream.
pub struct Unmarshal<'a> {
    data: &'a [u8],
    pos: usize,
    /// Back-reference table: each object with the cost charged to decode it.
    refs: Vec<(Obj, u64)>,
    /// Budget units spent so far (see [`MAX_BUDGET`]).
    spent: u64,
    layout: CodeLayout,
}

impl<'a> Unmarshal<'a> {
    pub fn new(data: &'a [u8], layout: CodeLayout) -> Self {
        Self {
            data,
            pos: 0,
            refs: Vec::new(),
            spent: 0,
            layout,
        }
    }

    pub fn read(&mut self) -> Result<Obj, String> {
        self.r_object(0)
    }

    fn u8(&mut self) -> Result<u8, String> {
        let b = *self
            .data
            .get(self.pos)
            .ok_or("unexpected end of marshal data")?;
        self.pos += 1;
        Ok(b)
    }

    fn u32(&mut self) -> Result<u32, String> {
        let end = self.pos + 4;
        let s = self.data.get(self.pos..end).ok_or("truncated u32")?;
        self.pos = end;
        Ok(u32::from_le_bytes([s[0], s[1], s[2], s[3]]))
    }

    fn i32(&mut self) -> Result<i32, String> {
        Ok(self.u32()? as i32)
    }

    fn bytes(&mut self, n: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
        if n > MAX_ITEMS {
            return Err(format!("implausible length {n}"));
        }
        let end = self.pos.checked_add(n).ok_or("length overflow")?;
        let s = self.data.get(self.pos..end).ok_or("truncated bytes")?;
        self.pos = end;
        Ok(s.to_vec())
    }

    fn charge(&mut self, units: u64) -> Result<(), String> {
        self.spent = self.spent.saturating_add(units);
        if self.spent > MAX_BUDGET {
            return Err("marshal data expands too much (reference bomb?)".into());
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn count(&mut self) -> Result<usize, String> {
        let n = self.i32()?;
        if n < 0 || n as usize > MAX_ITEMS {
            return Err(format!("implausible count {n}"));
        }
        Ok(n as usize)
    }

    fn r_object(&mut self, depth: u32) -> Result<Obj, String> {
        if depth > MAX_DEPTH {
            return Err("marshal nesting too deep".into());
        }
        let tag = self.u8()?;
        let flag_ref = tag & FLAG_REF != 0;
        let ty = tag & !FLAG_REF;

        // Reserve a reference slot before decoding, so back-references resolve.
        let slot = if flag_ref {
            let i = self.refs.len();
            self.refs.push((Obj::Null, 1));
            Some(i)
        } else {
            None
        };

        let start = self.spent;
        self.charge(1)?;
        let obj = self.decode(ty, depth)?;
        if let Some(i) = slot {
            // The cost of this subtree (including any refs it materialized) is what a later
            // `TYPE_REF` to it costs again.
            self.refs[i] = (obj.clone(), self.spent - start);
        }
        Ok(obj)
    }

    fn decode(&mut self, ty: u8, depth: u32) -> Result<Obj, String> {
        let obj = match ty {
            b'0' => Obj::Null,
            b'N' => Obj::None,
            b'F' => Obj::Bool(false),
            b'T' => Obj::Bool(true),
            b'S' => Obj::StopIter,
            b'.' => Obj::Ellipsis,
            b'i' => Obj::Int(self.i32()? as i64),
            b'I' => Obj::Int(self.u32()? as i64 | ((self.u32()? as i64) << 32)),
            b'l' => self.r_long()?,
            b'g' => {
                let b = self.bytes(8)?;
                Obj::Float(f64::from_le_bytes(b.try_into().unwrap()))
            }
            b'y' => {
                let r = self.bytes(8)?;
                let i = self.bytes(8)?;
                Obj::Complex(
                    f64::from_le_bytes(r.try_into().unwrap()),
                    f64::from_le_bytes(i.try_into().unwrap()),
                )
            }
            // Byte strings.
            b's' => {
                let n = self.count()?;
                self.charge(n as u64 / 16)?;
                Obj::Bytes(self.bytes(n)?)
            }
            // Unicode / ASCII strings (various interning + length encodings).
            b'u' | b't' | b'a' | b'A' => {
                let n = self.count()?;
                self.charge(n as u64 / 16)?;
                let b = self.bytes(n)?;
                Obj::Str(String::from_utf8_lossy(&b).into_owned())
            }
            b'z' | b'Z' => {
                let n = self.u8()? as usize;
                let b = self.bytes(n)?;
                Obj::Str(String::from_utf8_lossy(&b).into_owned())
            }
            b'r' => {
                let i = self.count()?;
                let cost = self.refs.get(i).ok_or("marshal ref out of range")?.1;
                self.charge(cost)?;
                self.refs[i].0.clone()
            }
            b')' => {
                let n = self.u8()? as usize;
                Obj::Tuple(self.items(n, depth)?)
            }
            b'(' => {
                let n = self.count()?;
                Obj::Tuple(self.items(n, depth)?)
            }
            b'[' => {
                let n = self.count()?;
                Obj::List(self.items(n, depth)?)
            }
            b'<' => {
                let n = self.count()?;
                Obj::Set(self.items(n, depth)?)
            }
            b'>' => {
                let n = self.count()?;
                Obj::FrozenSet(self.items(n, depth)?)
            }
            b'{' => Obj::Dict(self.r_dict(depth)?),
            b'c' => Obj::Code(Box::new(self.r_code(depth)?)),
            b':' => {
                let start = self.r_object(depth + 1)?;
                let stop = self.r_object(depth + 1)?;
                let step = self.r_object(depth + 1)?;
                Obj::Slice(Box::new((start, stop, step)))
            }
            other => {
                return Err(format!(
                    "unsupported marshal type 0x{other:02x} ('{}')",
                    other as char
                ));
            }
        };
        Ok(obj)
    }

    fn items(&mut self, n: usize, depth: u32) -> Result<Vec<Obj>, String> {
        if n > MAX_ITEMS {
            return Err(format!("implausible item count {n}"));
        }
        let mut v = Vec::with_capacity(n.min(1024));
        for _ in 0..n {
            v.push(self.r_object(depth + 1)?);
        }
        Ok(v)
    }

    fn r_dict(&mut self, depth: u32) -> Result<Vec<(Obj, Obj)>, String> {
        let mut v = Vec::new();
        loop {
            // A NULL key terminates the dict.
            let key = self.r_object(depth + 1)?;
            if key == Obj::Null {
                break;
            }
            let val = self.r_object(depth + 1)?;
            v.push((key, val));
        }
        Ok(v)
    }

    /// Arbitrary-precision integer (`TYPE_LONG`): a signed digit count, then 15-bit little-endian
    /// digits. Values beyond `i128` are rendered to a decimal string.
    fn r_long(&mut self) -> Result<Obj, String> {
        let n = self.i32()?;
        let negative = n < 0;
        let ndigits = n.unsigned_abs() as usize;
        if ndigits > 1_000_000 {
            return Err("implausible bigint size".into());
        }
        let mut value: i128 = 0;
        let mut overflow = false;
        for i in 0..ndigits {
            let digit = {
                let s = self
                    .data
                    .get(self.pos..self.pos + 2)
                    .ok_or("truncated bigint")?;
                self.pos += 2;
                u16::from_le_bytes([s[0], s[1]]) as i128
            };
            if !overflow {
                // `checked_shl` only rejects shift amounts >= 128, not bits shifted out, so check
                // the magnitude explicitly: the digit's bits shifted by `i*15` must stay within
                // 126 bits (i128 holds 127; one bit of headroom keeps the sum safe).
                let shift = (i as u32).saturating_mul(15);
                let width = 128 - digit.leading_zeros();
                if digit != 0 && shift.saturating_add(width) > 126 {
                    overflow = true;
                } else if digit != 0 {
                    match value.checked_add(digit << shift) {
                        Some(v) => value = v,
                        None => overflow = true,
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        if overflow {
            // Rare; report rather than lose precision silently.
            return Ok(Obj::BigInt(format!("<big int, {ndigits} digits>")));
        }
        if negative {
            value = -value;
        }
        match i64::try_from(value) {
            Ok(v) => Ok(Obj::Int(v)),
            Err(_) => Ok(Obj::BigInt(value.to_string())),
        }
    }

    fn r_code(&mut self, depth: u32) -> Result<CodeObject, String> {
        let argcount = self.u32()?;
        let posonlyargcount = if self.layout.has_posonly {
            self.u32()?
        } else {
            0
        };
        let kwonlyargcount = self.u32()?;
        if self.layout.has_nlocals {
            let _nlocals = self.u32()?;
        }
        let stacksize = self.u32()?;
        let flags = self.u32()?;
        let code = match self.r_object(depth + 1)? {
            Obj::Bytes(b) => b,
            other => return Err(format!("co_code is not bytes: {}", other.render())),
        };
        let consts = match self.r_object(depth + 1)? {
            Obj::Tuple(v) | Obj::List(v) => v,
            other => vec![other],
        };
        let names = self.r_object(depth + 1)?.as_string_vec();
        let localsplus = if self.layout.modern {
            let lp = self.r_object(depth + 1)?.as_string_vec();
            let _kinds = self.r_object(depth + 1)?; // co_localspluskinds (bytes)
            lp
        } else {
            let varnames = self.r_object(depth + 1)?.as_string_vec();
            let freevars = self.r_object(depth + 1)?.as_string_vec();
            let cellvars = self.r_object(depth + 1)?.as_string_vec();
            // Fast-locals index space on <3.11: varnames, then cells, then frees.
            let mut lp = varnames;
            lp.extend(cellvars);
            lp.extend(freevars);
            lp
        };
        let filename = self.r_object(depth + 1)?.as_string();
        let name = self.r_object(depth + 1)?.as_string();
        let qualname = if self.layout.modern {
            self.r_object(depth + 1)?.as_string()
        } else {
            name.clone()
        };
        let firstlineno = self.u32()?;
        // Line table / lnotab, and (3.11+) the exception table — read and discard.
        let _linetable = self.r_object(depth + 1)?;
        if self.layout.modern {
            let _exctable = self.r_object(depth + 1)?;
        }

        Ok(CodeObject {
            argcount,
            posonlyargcount,
            kwonlyargcount,
            stacksize,
            flags,
            code,
            consts,
            names,
            localsplus,
            filename,
            name,
            qualname,
            firstlineno,
        })
    }
}

/// A real `.pyc` compiled by CPython 3.14 from `tests/fixtures/sample_src.py`.

    p.top
        .nested()
        .into_iter()
        .find(|c| c.name == "check")
        .expect("check function")

#[test]

#[test]
fn disassembly_matches_cpython_dis() {
    let p = parse(PYC).unwrap();
    let check = check_fn(&p);
    let ins = disassemble(check, p.version).unwrap();

    // Offsets + opcodes must match `dis.get_instructions` exactly (including cache skipping).

        (110, "LOAD_FAST_BORROW", Some(1)),
        (112, "LOAD_CONST", Some(1)),
        (114, "COMPARE_OP", Some(72)),

#[test]
fn resolves_operands_and_jump_targets() {
    let p = parse(PYC).unwrap();
    let check = check_fn(&p);
    let ins = disassemble(check, p.version).unwrap();
    let at = |off: usize| ins.iter().find(|i| i.offset == off).unwrap();

    assert_eq!(at(4).argval.as_deref(), Some("total")); // STORE_FAST 1
    assert_eq!(at(6).argval.as_deref(), Some("enumerate + NULL")); // LOAD_GLOBAL 1
    assert_eq!(at(40).argval.as_deref(), Some("ord + NULL")); // LOAD_GLOBAL 3
    assert_eq!(at(112).argval.as_deref(), Some("1337")); // LOAD_CONST 1
    assert_eq!(at(62).argval.as_deref(), Some("7")); // LOAD_SMALL_INT 7

    // FOR_ITER @28 jumps forward to 106; JUMP_BACKWARD @102 jumps back to 28.
    assert_eq!(at(28).argval.as_deref(), Some("to 106"));
    assert_eq!(at(102).argval.as_deref(), Some("to 28"));
    assert!(at(28).is_jump_target); // JUMP_BACKWARD lands here
    assert!(at(106).is_jump_target); // FOR_ITER lands here
    assert!(!at(4).is_jump_target);
}

#[test]
fn resolves_operators() {
    let p = parse(PYC).unwrap();
    let check = check_fn(&p);
    let ins = disassemble(check, p.version).unwrap();
    let at = |off: usize| ins.iter().find(|i| i.offset == off).unwrap();
    // BINARY_OP and COMPARE_OP operands resolve to their symbols (matching CPython dis).
    assert_eq!(at(64).argval.as_deref(), Some("+")); // i + 7
    assert_eq!(at(76).argval.as_deref(), Some("^")); // ord(c) ^ ...
    assert_eq!(at(88).argval.as_deref(), Some("+=")); // total += ...
    assert_eq!(at(114).argval.as_deref(), Some("==")); // total == 1337
}

#[test]
fn version_from_older_magics() {
    // The range table maps a magic to the right (major, minor).
    assert_eq!(version_from_magic(3627), Some((3, 14)));
    assert_eq!(version_from_magic(3495), Some((3, 11)));
    assert_eq!(version_from_magic(3500), Some((3, 12))); // 3.12a1's first magic
    assert_eq!(version_from_magic(3379), Some((3, 6)));
    assert_eq!(version_from_magic(3230), Some((3, 3)));
    assert_eq!(version_from_magic(3131), Some((3, 0)));
    assert_eq!(version_from_magic(1000), None);
    // Python 2 magics and future versions are unknown, not "3.14".
    assert_eq!(version_from_magic(62211), None);
    assert_eq!(version_from_magic(3700), None);
}

/// A minimal pre-3.8 code object body (`'c'` + fields) whose name is `name`.
fn legacy_code_object(name: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut b = vec![b'c'];
    for _ in 0..5 {
        b.extend(0u32.to_le_bytes()); // argcount kwonly nlocals stacksize flags
    }
    b.extend([b's', 0, 0, 0, 0]); // co_code
    for _ in 0..5 {
        b.extend([b')', 0]); // consts names varnames freevars cellvars
    }
    b.extend([b'z', 1, b'f']); // filename
    b.push(b'z');
    b.push(name.len() as u8);
    b.extend(name.as_bytes());
    b.extend(1u32.to_le_bytes()); // firstlineno
    b.extend([b's', 0, 0, 0, 0]); // lnotab
    b
}

#[test]
fn header_sizes_follow_the_version() {
    // 3.6 (magic 3379): 12-byte header.
    let mut py36 = vec![0x33, 0x0d, 0x0d, 0x0a, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0];
    py36.extend(legacy_code_object("m36"));
    let p = parse(&py36).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(p.version, Some((3, 6)));
    assert_eq!(p.header_len, 12);
    assert_eq!(p.top.name, "m36");
    assert!(!p.can_disassemble());

    // 3.2 (magic 3180): 8-byte header.
    let mut py32 = vec![0x6c, 0x0c, 0x0d, 0x0a, 0, 0, 0, 0];
    py32.extend(legacy_code_object("m32"));
    py32.extend([0; 8]); // pad past the 16-byte minimum
    let p = parse(&py32).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(p.version, Some((3, 2)));
    assert_eq!(p.header_len, 8);
    assert_eq!(p.top.name, "m32");

    // A Python 2 magic is unknown and can't be disassembled.
    let mut py2 = PYC.to_vec();
    py2[..2].copy_from_slice(&62211u16.to_le_bytes());
    if let Ok(p) = parse(&py2) {
        assert_eq!(p.version, None);
        assert!(!p.can_disassemble());
    }
}

#[test]
fn reference_bombs_are_bounded() {
    // A list whose element i is a FLAG_REF tuple holding two refs to element i-1: the tree it
    // describes has 2^60 nodes, from under a kilobyte of input. Must fail fast, not OOM.
    let levels: u32 = 60;
    let mut b = vec![b'['];
    b.extend(levels.to_le_bytes());
    b.extend([b'(' | 0x80, 2, 0, 0, 0, b'N', b'N']);
    for i in 1..levels {
        b.extend([b'(' | 0x80, 2, 0, 0, 0]);
        for _ in 0..2 {
            b.push(b'r');
            b.extend((i - 1).to_le_bytes());
        }
    }
    let layout = CodeLayout::for_version(Some((3, 14)));
    let err = Unmarshal::new(&b, layout).read().unwrap_err();
    assert!(err.contains("expands"), "{err}");

    // Ordinary sharing still works.
    let ok = [b'(', 2, 0, 0, 0, b'z' | 0x80, 1, b'x', b'r', 0, 0, 0, 0];
    let obj = Unmarshal::new(&ok, layout).read().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(obj.render(), "(\"x\", \"x\")");
}

#[test]
fn decodes_slices_and_big_ints() {
    let layout = CodeLayout::for_version(Some((3, 14)));
    // TYPE_SLICE: slice(1, None, 2)
    let s = [b':', b'i', 1, 0, 0, 0, b'N', b'i', 2, 0, 0, 0];
    let obj = Unmarshal::new(&s, layout).read().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(obj.render(), "slice(1, None, 2)");

    // 2^120 as 9 15-bit digits: fits i128 exactly.
    let mut l = vec![b'l'];
    l.extend(9i32.to_le_bytes());
    for d in 0..9 {
        let digit: u16 = if d == 8 { 1 } else { 0 };
        l.extend(digit.to_le_bytes());
    }
    let obj = Unmarshal::new(&l, layout).read().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(obj, Obj::BigInt((1i128 << 120).to_string()));

    // 0x7fff << 120 needs 135 bits: must be reported as too big, not silently wrapped.
    let mut l = vec![b'l'];
    l.extend(9i32.to_le_bytes());
    for d in 0..9 {
        let digit: u16 = if d == 8 { 0x7fff } else { 0 };
        l.extend(digit.to_le_bytes());
    }
    let obj = Unmarshal::new(&l, layout).read().unwrap();
    assert!(
        matches!(obj, Obj::BigInt(ref s) if s.starts_with("<big int")),
        "{obj:?}"
    );
}

#[test]
fn load_super_attr_name_index() {
    // LOAD_SUPER_ATTR (96) with oparg 0b1011: name index 2, two-arg form, method load.
    let code = CodeObject {
        argcount: 0,
        posonlyargcount: 0,
        kwonlyargcount: 0,
        stacksize: 0,
        flags: 0,
        code: vec![96, 0b1011],
        consts: vec![],
        names: vec!["a".into(), "b".into(), "meth".into(), "zzz".into()],
        localsplus: vec![],
        filename: String::new(),
        name: "f".into(),
        qualname: "f".into(),
        firstlineno: 1,
    };
    let ins = disassemble(&code, Some((3, 14))).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(ins[0].argval.as_deref(), Some("meth + NULL|self"));
}

`crates/orress-relay/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! A self-hostable collaboration relay: a WebSocket server that routes end-to-end-encrypted room
//! traffic between team members. It is deliberately dumb — it reads each client's [`Envelope`],
//! routes `Data` frames to the other members of the same room, and never decrypts anything (the
//! payloads are sealed with the room key, which the relay does not have). That keeps a hosted or
//! self-hosted relay unable to read the team's work, which matters for malware analysis.
//!
//! Blocking and thread-per-connection (no async runtime): each connection polls its socket with a
//! short read timeout and, between reads, flushes anything queued for it by other connections.
//!
//! Because a relay is meant to be internet-facing, it is bounded everywhere ([`RelayConfig`]): a
//! cap on concurrent connections, a handshake deadline, a maximum message/frame size, a bounded
//! per-member outgoing queue (a peer too slow to drain it is disconnected rather than buffering
//! without limit), and an idle timeout backed by WebSocket pings.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::io::ErrorKind;
use std::net::{TcpListener, TcpStream};
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
use std::sync::mpsc::{Receiver, SyncSender, TryRecvError, TrySendError, sync_channel};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use orress_collab::Envelope;
use tungstenite::Message;
use tungstenite::protocol::WebSocketConfig;

/// How long a connection blocks on a read before looping to flush its outgoing queue.
const POLL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(40);

/// Limits that keep an internet-facing relay from being exhausted by misbehaving clients.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct RelayConfig {
    /// Maximum simultaneous connections; further connections are closed immediately.
    pub max_connections: usize,
    /// Maximum size of one incoming WebSocket message (and frame), in bytes.
    pub max_message_size: usize,
    /// How long a client has to complete the WebSocket handshake.
    pub handshake_timeout: Duration,
    /// How many messages may wait in a member's outgoing queue. A member whose queue is full (it
    /// is not reading fast enough) is disconnected instead of buffering without bound.
    pub queue_capacity: usize,
    /// After this long without hearing from a client the relay pings it; after
    /// [`RelayConfig::idle_timeout`] of silence it is disconnected.
    pub ping_interval: Duration,
    /// Disconnect a client that has sent nothing (not even a pong) for this long.
    pub idle_timeout: Duration,
    /// Blocking-write deadline, so a peer that stops reading cannot wedge its connection thread.
    pub write_timeout: Duration,
}

impl Default for RelayConfig {
    fn default() -> Self {
        RelayConfig {
            max_connections: 512,
            max_message_size: 4 << 20,
            handshake_timeout: Duration::from_secs(10),
            queue_capacity: 1024,
            ping_interval: Duration::from_secs(30),
            idle_timeout: Duration::from_secs(90),
            write_timeout: Duration::from_secs(10),
        }
    }
}

impl RelayConfig {
    fn websocket(&self) -> WebSocketConfig {
        WebSocketConfig {
            max_message_size: Some(self.max_message_size),
            max_frame_size: Some(self.max_message_size),
            // Bound what can pile up in tungstenite's own write buffer behind a stalled peer.
            max_write_buffer_size: (self.max_message_size * 4).max(256 * 1024),
            ..WebSocketConfig::default()
        }
    }
}

type Members = HashMap<usize, SyncSender<Vec<u8>>>;

/// The live rooms and their members' outgoing queues.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Rooms {
    inner: Mutex<HashMap<String, Members>>,
}

impl Rooms {
    fn join(&self, room: &str, id: usize, tx: SyncSender<Vec<u8>>) {
        self.inner
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
            .entry(room.to_string())
            .or_default()
            .insert(id, tx);
    }

    fn leave(&self, room: &str, id: usize) {
        let mut rooms = self.inner.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        if let Some(members) = rooms.get_mut(room) {
            members.remove(&id);
            if members.is_empty() {
                rooms.remove(room);
            }
        }
    }

    /// Queues `payload` for every member of `room` except the sender. A member whose queue is full
    /// (too slow) or gone is removed from the room; dropping its sender makes its connection
    /// thread see the queue disconnect and close the socket.
    fn broadcast(&self, room: &str, from: usize, payload: &[u8]) {
        let mut rooms = self.inner.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        let Some(members) = rooms.get_mut(room) else {
            return;
        };
        members.retain(|&id, tx| {
            id == from
                || match tx.try_send(payload.to_vec()) {
                    Ok(()) => true,
                    Err(TrySendError::Full(_) | TrySendError::Disconnected(_)) => false,
                }
        });
        if members.is_empty() {
            rooms.remove(room);
        }
    }

    /// Number of live rooms (for tests / status).
    pub fn room_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.inner.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).len()
    }
}

/// Decrements the live-connection count when a connection thread ends (however it ends).
struct ConnectionSlot(Arc<AtomicUsize>);

impl Drop for ConnectionSlot {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.0.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
    }
}

/// Serves connections on `listener` with the default [`RelayConfig`] until it stops yielding (i.e.
/// forever for a normal listener). Each connection is handled on its own thread.
pub fn run(listener: TcpListener) {
    run_with(listener, RelayConfig::default());
}

/// [`run`] with explicit limits.
pub fn run_with(listener: TcpListener, config: RelayConfig) {
    let config = Arc::new(config);
    let rooms = Arc::new(Rooms::default());
    let ids = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
    let live = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
    for stream in listener.incoming() {
        let stream = match stream {
            Ok(s) => s,
            Err(_) => {
                // e.g. out of file descriptors: back off instead of spinning.
                std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50));
                continue;
            }
        };
        if live.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel) >= config.max_connections {
            live.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
            let _ = stream.shutdown(std::net::Shutdown::Both);
            continue;
        }
        let slot = ConnectionSlot(Arc::clone(&live));
        let rooms = Arc::clone(&rooms);
        let config = Arc::clone(&config);
        let id = ids.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        std::thread::spawn(move || {
            let _slot = slot;
            handle(stream, id, &rooms, &config);
        });
    }
}

fn handle(stream: TcpStream, id: usize, rooms: &Rooms, config: &RelayConfig) {
    // Bound the handshake: a client that connects and never speaks times out here.
    stream.set_read_timeout(Some(config.handshake_timeout)).ok();
    stream.set_write_timeout(Some(config.write_timeout)).ok();
    let Ok(mut ws) = tungstenite::accept_with_config(stream, Some(config.websocket())) else {
        return;
    };
    // After the handshake, poll with a short timeout so we can interleave fan-out.
    ws.get_ref().set_read_timeout(Some(POLL)).ok();
    let (tx, rx): (SyncSender<Vec<u8>>, Receiver<Vec<u8>>) =
        sync_channel(config.queue_capacity.max(1));
    // Handed to the room on join; after that the room holds the only sender, so the room dropping
    // it (slow member) disconnects `rx` and ends this connection.
    let mut tx = Some(tx);
    let mut room: Option<String> = None;
    let mut last_heard = Instant::now();
    let mut pinged = false;

    'conn: loop {
        // Flush anything other members queued for us.
        loop {
            match rx.try_recv() {
                Ok(payload) => {
                    if ws
                        .send(Message::Binary(Envelope::Data { payload }.encode()))
                        .is_err()
                    {
                        break 'conn;
                    }
                }
                Err(TryRecvError::Empty) => break,
                // Removed from the room for being too slow.
                Err(TryRecvError::Disconnected) => break 'conn,
            }
        }

        // Liveness: ping a quiet client, drop one that stays silent.
        let quiet = last_heard.elapsed();
        if quiet >= config.idle_timeout {
            break;
        }
        if quiet >= config.ping_interval && !pinged {
            if ws.send(Message::Ping(Vec::new())).is_err() {
                break;
            }
            pinged = true;
        }

        match ws.read() {
            Ok(msg) => {
                last_heard = Instant::now();
                pinged = false;
                match msg {
                    Message::Binary(bytes) => match Envelope::decode(&bytes) {
                        Some(Envelope::Join { room: r }) => {
                            if room.is_none()
                                && let Some(tx) = tx.take()
                            {
                                rooms.join(&r, id, tx);
                                room = Some(r);
                            }
                        }
                        Some(Envelope::Data { payload }) => {
                            if let Some(r) = &room {
                                rooms.broadcast(r, id, &payload);
                            }
                        }
                        None => {}
                    },
                    // Pings are answered by tungstenite itself (flushed on the next read/write).
                    Message::Close(_) => break,
                    _ => {}
                }
            }
            // Idle (read timed out): loop back to flush the outgoing queue.
            Err(tungstenite::Error::Io(e))
                if matches!(e.kind(), ErrorKind::WouldBlock | ErrorKind::TimedOut) => {}
            Err(_) => break,
        }
    }

    if let Some(r) = &room {
        rooms.leave(r, id);
    }
    let _ = ws.close(None);
    let _ = ws.flush();
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn a_member_with_a_full_queue_is_dropped_from_the_room() {
        let rooms = Rooms::default();
        let (fast_tx, fast_rx) = sync_channel(8);
        let (slow_tx, slow_rx) = sync_channel(1);
        rooms.join("r", 1, fast_tx);
        rooms.join("r", 2, slow_tx);
        rooms.broadcast("r", 0, b"a");
        rooms.broadcast("r", 0, b"b"); // slow member's queue (cap 1) is full -> removed
        assert_eq!(fast_rx.try_recv().unwrap(), b"a");
        assert_eq!(fast_rx.try_recv().unwrap(), b"b");
        assert_eq!(slow_rx.try_recv().unwrap(), b"a");
        // The room dropped the slow member's sender, so its connection sees the disconnect.
        assert!(matches!(
            slow_rx.try_recv(),
            Err(TryRecvError::Disconnected)
        ));
        assert_eq!(rooms.room_count(), 1);
    }
}

`crates/orress-relay/src/main.rs`:

```rs
//! The ORRESS collaboration relay server. Run it to let a team share a project:
//!
//! ```text
//! orress-relay 0.0.0.0:8787
//! ```
//!
//! It only forwards end-to-end-encrypted room traffic; it never sees the team's data. Pair it with
//! a TLS-terminating reverse proxy for `wss://` if you want transport encryption on top.
//!
//! Limits can be tuned with environment variables: `ORRESS_RELAY_MAX_CONNECTIONS` (default 512)
//! and `ORRESS_RELAY_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES` (default 4 MiB).

use std::net::TcpListener;

fn main() {
    let addr = std::env::args()
        .nth(1)
        .unwrap_or_else(|| "127.0.0.1:8787".to_string());
    match TcpListener::bind(&addr) {
        Ok(listener) => {
            let actual = listener.local_addr().map(|a| a.to_string()).unwrap_or(addr);
            println!("ORRESS relay listening on ws://{actual}");
            orress_relay::run_with(listener, config_from_env());
        }
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("could not bind {addr}: {e}");
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
    }
}

/// The default [`orress_relay::RelayConfig`], with limits overridden from the environment.
fn config_from_env() -> orress_relay::RelayConfig {
    let mut config = orress_relay::RelayConfig::default();
    let num = |name: &str| {
        std::env::var(name)
            .ok()
            .and_then(|v| v.trim().parse::<usize>().ok())
            .filter(|&n| n > 0)
    };
    if let Some(n) = num("ORRESS_RELAY_MAX_CONNECTIONS") {
        config.max_connections = n;
    }
    if let Some(n) = num("ORRESS_RELAY_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES") {
        config.max_message_size = n;
    }
    config
}

`crates/orress-relay/tests/relay.rs`:

```rs
//! Integration test: a real relay over loopback. Two clients join a room; one broadcasts, the
//! other receives it; a third client in a different room does not.

use std::net::{TcpListener, TcpStream};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use orress_collab::{ClientMessage, CollabSession, Envelope, Peer, RoomKey};
use tungstenite::{Message, WebSocket};

type Client = WebSocket<TcpStream>;

fn connect(addr: &str) -> Client {
    let stream = TcpStream::connect(addr).expect("connect");
    let (ws, _resp) = tungstenite::client(format!("ws://{addr}/"), stream).expect("handshake");
    // Poll reads (after the blocking handshake) so read_data can wait with a deadline.
    ws.get_ref()
        .set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_millis(100)))
        .ok();
    ws
}

fn join(ws: &mut Client, room: &str) {
    ws.send(Message::Binary(
        Envelope::Join {
            room: room.to_string(),
        }
        .encode(),
    ))
    .unwrap();
}

/// Reads until a `Data` frame arrives or `timeout` elapses.
fn read_data(ws: &mut Client, timeout: Duration) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    let deadline = Instant::now() + timeout;
    while Instant::now() < deadline {
        match ws.read() {
            Ok(Message::Binary(bytes)) => {
                if let Some(Envelope::Data { payload }) = Envelope::decode(&bytes) {
                    return Some(payload);
                }
            }
            Ok(_) => {}
            Err(tungstenite::Error::Io(_)) => {} // read timed out; keep waiting
            Err(_) => break,
        }
    }
    None
}

#[test]
fn broadcasts_within_a_room_but_not_across_rooms() {
    let listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").unwrap();
    let addr = listener.local_addr().unwrap().to_string();
    std::thread::spawn(move || orress_relay::run(listener));

    let mut alice = connect(&addr);
    let mut bob = connect(&addr);
    let mut eve = connect(&addr); // a different room

    join(&mut alice, "ctf/web");
    join(&mut bob, "ctf/web");
    join(&mut eve, "ctf/pwn");
    // Let the server register all three joins.
    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(150));

    let payload = b"sealed-update".to_vec();
    alice
        .send(Message::Binary(
            Envelope::Data {
                payload: payload.clone(),
            }
            .encode(),
        ))
        .unwrap();

    // Bob (same room) receives the opaque payload verbatim.
    assert_eq!(read_data(&mut bob, Duration::from_secs(3)), Some(payload));
    // Eve (other room) does not.
    assert_eq!(read_data(&mut eve, Duration::from_millis(400)), None);
}

fn now_ms() -> u64 {
    std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .unwrap()
        .as_millis() as u64
}

#[test]
fn two_sessions_sync_crdt_and_presence_over_the_relay() {
    let listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").unwrap();
    let url = format!("ws://{}", listener.local_addr().unwrap());
    std::thread::spawn(move || orress_relay::run(listener));

    let mut alice =
        CollabSession::connect(&url, "ctf/re", "team-pw", Peer::new("alice", "Alice")).unwrap();
    let mut bob =
        CollabSession::connect(&url, "ctf/re", "team-pw", Peer::new("bob", "Bob")).unwrap();

    // Alice renames a function and marks where she is looking.
    alice.doc.set_rename(0x401000, "check_flag");
    alice.set_local_addr(Some(0x401000), now_ms());

    // Pump both sessions until Bob converges (or a deadline).
    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(5);
    let mut synced = false;
    while Instant::now() < deadline {
        alice.poll(now_ms());
        bob.poll(now_ms());
        if bob.doc.rename(0x401000).as_deref() == Some("check_flag")
            && bob.presence().peer("alice").and_then(|p| p.addr) == Some(0x401000)
        {
            synced = true;
            break;
        }
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20));
    }
    assert!(
        synced,
        "bob should see alice's rename and presence over the relay"
    );

    // Follow mode: Bob follows Alice and lands on her address.
    bob.follow("alice");
    assert_eq!(bob.follow_addr(), Some(0x401000));
}

#[test]
fn an_idle_session_sends_no_document_updates() {
    let listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").unwrap();
    let addr = listener.local_addr().unwrap().to_string();
    std::thread::spawn(move || orress_relay::run(listener));

    // A raw observer in the room that can open the sealed traffic.
    let key = RoomKey::derive("ctf/idle", "pw").unwrap();
    let mut observer = connect(&addr);
    join(&mut observer, "ctf/idle");
    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(150));

    let mut alice = CollabSession::connect(
        &format!("ws://{addr}"),
        "ctf/idle",
        "pw",
        Peer::new("alice", "Alice"),
    )
    .unwrap();
    // Many idle frames at a fixed time (so only the first heartbeat fires).
    let now = now_ms();
    for _ in 0..50 {
        alice.poll(now);
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(5));
    }
    let count_updates = |observer: &mut Client, wait: Duration| {
        let mut updates = 0;
        while let Some(payload) = read_data(observer, wait) {
            if let Ok(ClientMessage::Update(_)) = ClientMessage::open(&payload, &key) {
                updates += 1;
            }
        }
        updates
    };
    assert_eq!(
        count_updates(&mut observer, Duration::from_millis(400)),
        0,
        "an idle session must not broadcast document updates"
    );

    // A real edit is broadcast exactly once.
    alice.doc.set_rename(0x1000, "main");
    for _ in 0..20 {
        alice.poll(now);
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(5));
    }
    assert_eq!(count_updates(&mut observer, Duration::from_millis(400)), 1);
}

#[test]
fn connections_beyond_the_cap_are_refused() {
    let listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").unwrap();
    let addr = listener.local_addr().unwrap().to_string();
    let config = orress_relay::RelayConfig {
        max_connections: 1,
        ..Default::default()
    };
    std::thread::spawn(move || orress_relay::run_with(listener, config));

    let _first = connect(&addr);
    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
    let stream = TcpStream::connect(&addr).expect("tcp connect");
    stream
        .set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(3)))
        .unwrap();
    assert!(
        tungstenite::client(format!("ws://{addr}/"), stream).is_err(),
        "the second connection exceeds the cap"
    );
}

#[test]
fn oversized_messages_close_the_connection() {
    let listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").unwrap();
    let addr = listener.local_addr().unwrap().to_string();
    let config = orress_relay::RelayConfig {
        max_message_size: 1024,
        ..Default::default()
    };
    std::thread::spawn(move || orress_relay::run_with(listener, config));

    let mut alice = connect(&addr);
    let mut bob = connect(&addr);
    join(&mut alice, "r");
    join(&mut bob, "r");
    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(150));
    let _ = alice.send(Message::Binary(
        Envelope::Data {
            payload: vec![0u8; 4096],
        }
        .encode(),
    ));
    // The oversized frame is never relayed.
    assert_eq!(read_data(&mut bob, Duration::from_millis(500)), None);
}
