`crates/orress-resources/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! Pull the contents out of an executable: native Win32 resources (icons, bitmaps, manifest,
//! version info, string tables, RCDATA…), embedded files found by magic-byte signatures
//! (PNG/JPEG/GIF/BMP/ZIP/GZIP/PDF/WAV…), each PE section, and any overlay (bytes appended after
//! the image). The input is only read, never executed.
//!
//! [`extract`] lists what it finds as [`Resource`]s (each with its own bytes); [`write_all`]
//! writes a selection to a folder with sequence-numbered names and a manifest.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use object::LittleEndian as LE;
use object::read::pe::{ImageNtHeaders, PeFile};

/// The biggest single item we will hold/extract (guards against a corrupt size field).
const MAX_ITEM: usize = 256 * 1024 * 1024;
/// The most items we will list (guards against a pathological resource tree).
const MAX_ITEMS: usize = 4000;
/// When an embedded file's end cannot be determined, carve at most this many bytes.
const CARVE_FALLBACK: usize = 16 * 1024 * 1024;

// Resource type ids (level 0 of the resource tree). `object` only exposes these behind its
// `names` feature, so we spell them out.
const RT_CURSOR: u16 = 1;
const RT_BITMAP: u16 = 2;
const RT_ICON: u16 = 3;
const RT_MENU: u16 = 4;
const RT_DIALOG: u16 = 5;
const RT_STRING: u16 = 6;
const RT_RCDATA: u16 = 10;
const RT_GROUP_CURSOR: u16 = 12;
const RT_GROUP_ICON: u16 = 14;
const RT_VERSION: u16 = 16;
const RT_HTML: u16 = 23;
const RT_MANIFEST: u16 = 24;

/// What an extracted item is.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ResourceKind {
    /// A native Win32 resource from the `.rsrc` directory.
    Resource,
    /// A whole PE section's bytes.
    Section,
    /// Data appended after the image (installers, self-extractors, signatures).
    Overlay,
    /// A file found inside the binary by its magic-byte signature.
    Embedded,
}

impl ResourceKind {
    pub fn label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Resource => "resource",
            Self::Section => "section",
            Self::Overlay => "overlay",
            Self::Embedded => "embedded",
        }
    }
}

/// One extractable item.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct Resource {
    pub kind: ResourceKind,
    /// A human label, e.g. `manifest`, `.text` or `icon_1`.
    pub name: String,
    /// The file extension to save it under (no dot), e.g. `ico`, `bmp`, `bin`.
    pub ext: &'static str,
    /// File offset in the source, when known.
    pub offset: Option<u64>,
    /// The item's bytes.
    pub data: Vec<u8>,
}

impl Resource {
    fn new(
        kind: ResourceKind,
        name: impl Into<String>,
        ext: &'static str,
        offset: Option<u64>,
        data: Vec<u8>,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            kind,
            name: name.into(),
            ext,
            offset,
            data,
        }
    }

    /// The suggested file name (`<index>_<name>.<ext>`), used by [`write_all`].
    fn file_name(&self, index: usize) -> String {
        let safe: String = self
            .name
            .chars()
            .map(|c| {
                if c.is_alphanumeric() || c == '.' || c == '-' || c == '_' {
                    c
                } else {
                    '_'
                }
            })
            .collect();
        format!("{index:03}_{safe}.{}", self.ext)
    }
}

/// Finds everything extractable in `data`.
pub fn extract(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<Resource> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    // Record the file ranges already covered, so carving does not re-report them.
    let mut covered: Vec<(usize, usize)> = Vec::new();

    if let Ok(file) = object::File::parse(data) {
        match file {
            object::File::Pe32(pe) => pe_items(&pe, data, &mut out, &mut covered),
            object::File::Pe64(pe) => pe_items(&pe, data, &mut out, &mut covered),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    carve(data, &covered, &mut out);
    out.truncate(MAX_ITEMS);
    out
}

/// Writes the chosen resources to `dest`, with an `export_manifest.txt`. Returns the paths written.
pub fn write_all(resources: &[Resource], dest: &Path) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>, String> {
    std::fs::create_dir_all(dest).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", dest.display()))?;
    let mut written = Vec::new();
    let mut manifest = String::from("ORRESS resource export\n\n");
    for (i, res) in resources.iter().enumerate() {
        let name = res.file_name(i + 1);
        let path = dest.join(&name);
        std::fs::write(&path, &res.data).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))?;
        let off = res
            .offset
            .map(|o| format!("0x{o:x}"))
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "-".into());
        manifest.push_str(&format!(
            "{name}\t{}\t{} bytes\toffset {off}\n",
            res.kind.label(),
            res.data.len()
        ));
        written.push(path);
    }
    let _ = std::fs::write(dest.join("export_manifest.txt"), manifest);
    Ok(written)
}

// --- PE resources, sections, overlay ---------------------------------------

fn pe_items<Pe: ImageNtHeaders>(
    pe: &PeFile<Pe>,
    data: &[u8],
    out: &mut Vec<Resource>,
    covered: &mut Vec<(usize, usize)>,
) {
    let sections = pe.section_table();

    // 1. Native resources.
    if let Ok(Some(dir)) = pe.data_directories().resource_directory(data, &sections)
        && let Ok(root) = dir.root()
    {
        let mut icons: Vec<Vec<u8>> = Vec::new();
        for type_entry in root.entries {
            let Some(type_id) = type_entry.name_or_id().id() else {
                continue;
            };
            let Some(names) = type_entry.data(dir).ok().and_then(|d| d.table()) else {
                continue;
            };
            for name_entry in names.entries {
                let Some(langs) = name_entry.data(dir).ok().and_then(|d| d.table()) else {
                    continue;
                };
                for lang_entry in langs.entries {
                    let Some(leaf) = lang_entry.data(dir).ok().and_then(|d| d.data()) else {
                        continue;
                    };
                    let rva = leaf.offset_to_data.get(LE);
                    let size = leaf.size.get(LE) as usize;
                    if size == 0 || size > MAX_ITEM {
                        continue;
                    }
                    let Some(bytes) = sections.pe_data_at(data, rva).and_then(|b| b.get(..size))
                    else {
                        continue;
                    };
                    let file_off = sections.pe_file_range_at(rva).map(|(o, _)| u64::from(o));
                    if let Some(start) = file_off {
                        covered.push((start as usize, start as usize + size));
                    }
                    let id = name_entry.name_or_id().id().unwrap_or(0);
                    emit_resource(type_id, id, bytes, file_off, out, &mut icons);
                }
            }
        }
        for (n, ico) in icons.into_iter().enumerate() {
            out.push(Resource::new(
                ResourceKind::Resource,
                format!("icon_{}", n + 1),
                "ico",
                None,
                ico,
            ));
        }
    }

    // 2. Sections.
    let mut image_end = 0u64;
    for section in sections.iter() {
        let (off, size) = section.pe_file_range();
        if size == 0 {
            continue;
        }
        image_end = image_end.max(u64::from(off) + u64::from(size));
        let name = String::from_utf8_lossy(&section.name)
            .trim_end_matches('\0')
            .to_string();
        if let Some(bytes) = data.get(off as usize..(off as usize).saturating_add(size as usize)) {
            out.push(Resource::new(
                ResourceKind::Section,
                format!("section_{}", name.trim_start_matches('.')),
                "bin",
                Some(u64::from(off)),
                bytes.to_vec(),
            ));
        }
    }

    // 3. Overlay (bytes after the last section).
    if (image_end as usize) < data.len() {
        let overlay = &data[image_end as usize..];
        covered.push((image_end as usize, data.len()));
        out.push(Resource::new(
            ResourceKind::Overlay,
            "overlay",
            "bin",
            Some(image_end),
            overlay.to_vec(),
        ));
    }
}

/// Classifies one native resource and pushes it (icons are collected to rebuild `.ico` files).
fn emit_resource(
    type_id: u16,
    id: u16,
    bytes: &[u8],
    offset: Option<u64>,
    out: &mut Vec<Resource>,
    icons: &mut Vec<Vec<u8>>,
) {
    match type_id {
        RT_ICON => icons.push(wrap_icon(bytes)),
        RT_BITMAP => out.push(Resource::new(
            ResourceKind::Resource,
            format!("bitmap_{id}"),
            "bmp",
            offset,
            wrap_bmp(bytes),
        )),
        RT_MANIFEST => out.push(Resource::new(
            ResourceKind::Resource,
            format!("manifest_{id}"),
            "manifest",
            offset,
            bytes.to_vec(),
        )),
        RT_VERSION => {
            let text = utf16_strings(bytes).join("\n");
            out.push(Resource::new(
                ResourceKind::Resource,
                format!("version_{id}"),
                "txt",
                offset,
                text.into_bytes(),
            ));
        }
        RT_STRING => {
            let text = string_table(bytes);
            if !text.is_empty() {
                out.push(Resource::new(
                    ResourceKind::Resource,
                    format!("strings_{id}"),
                    "txt",
                    offset,
                    text.into_bytes(),
                ));
            }
        }
        RT_HTML => out.push(Resource::new(
            ResourceKind::Resource,
            format!("html_{id}"),
            "html",
            offset,
            bytes.to_vec(),
        )),
        other => {
            let base = match other {
                RT_RCDATA => "rcdata",
                RT_GROUP_ICON => "group_icon",
                RT_GROUP_CURSOR => "group_cursor",
                RT_CURSOR => "cursor",
                RT_MENU => "menu",
                RT_DIALOG => "dialog",
                _ => "resource",
            };
            out.push(Resource::new(
                ResourceKind::Resource,
                format!("{base}_{id}"),
                "bin",
                offset,
                bytes.to_vec(),
            ));
        }
    }
}

/// Wraps a single RT_ICON image (a DIB or PNG) in a one-image `.ico` container.
fn wrap_icon(payload: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let (mut w, mut h, mut bits) = (0u8, 0u8, 0u16);
    if payload.len() >= 40
        && u32::from_le_bytes([payload[0], payload[1], payload[2], payload[3]]) == 40
    {
        let biw = i32::from_le_bytes([payload[4], payload[5], payload[6], payload[7]]);
        let bih = i32::from_le_bytes([payload[8], payload[9], payload[10], payload[11]]);
        bits = u16::from_le_bytes([payload[14], payload[15]]);
        w = (biw & 0xff) as u8;
        h = ((bih / 2) & 0xff) as u8; // icon DIB height counts the AND mask twice
    }
    let mut ico = Vec::with_capacity(22 + payload.len());
    ico.extend_from_slice(&[0, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0]); // ICONDIR: reserved, type=1, count=1
    ico.push(w);
    ico.push(h);
    ico.push(0); // color count
    ico.push(0); // reserved
    ico.extend_from_slice(&1u16.to_le_bytes()); // planes
    ico.extend_from_slice(&bits.to_le_bytes()); // bit count
    ico.extend_from_slice(&(payload.len() as u32).to_le_bytes()); // bytes in resource
    ico.extend_from_slice(&22u32.to_le_bytes()); // offset to image
    ico.extend_from_slice(payload);
    ico
}

/// Prepends a 14-byte `BITMAPFILEHEADER` to a DIB so RT_BITMAP data opens as a `.bmp`.
fn wrap_bmp(dib: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut pixel_offset = 14u32;
    if dib.len() >= 40 {
        let header_size = u32::from_le_bytes([dib[0], dib[1], dib[2], dib[3]]);
        let bit_count = u16::from_le_bytes([dib[14], dib[15]]);
        let mut clr_used = u32::from_le_bytes([dib[32], dib[33], dib[34], dib[35]]);
        if clr_used == 0 && bit_count <= 8 {
            clr_used = 1 << bit_count;
        }
        pixel_offset = 14 + header_size + clr_used * 4;
    }
    let file_size = 14u32.saturating_add(dib.len() as u32);
    let mut bmp = Vec::with_capacity(14 + dib.len());
    bmp.extend_from_slice(b"BM");
    bmp.extend_from_slice(&file_size.to_le_bytes());
    bmp.extend_from_slice(&0u32.to_le_bytes()); // reserved
    bmp.extend_from_slice(&pixel_offset.to_le_bytes());
    bmp.extend_from_slice(dib);
    bmp
}

/// Decodes an RT_STRING block: 16 UTF-16LE strings, each a u16 length then that many code units.
fn string_table(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    let mut i = 0usize;
    for _ in 0..16 {
        if i + 2 > bytes.len() {
            break;
        }
        let len = u16::from_le_bytes([bytes[i], bytes[i + 1]]) as usize;
        i += 2;
        if len == 0 {
            continue;
        }
        let end = (i + len * 2).min(bytes.len());
        let s = utf16_to_string(&bytes[i..end]);
        i = end;
        if !s.trim().is_empty() {
            out.push_str(s.trim());
            out.push('\n');
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Pulls printable UTF-16LE runs (length >= 3) out of a blob — a pragmatic read of version info.
fn utf16_strings(bytes: &[u8]) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut cur = String::new();
    let mut i = 0;
    while i + 1 < bytes.len() {
        let c = u16::from_le_bytes([bytes[i], bytes[i + 1]]);
        i += 2;
        match char::from_u32(u32::from(c)) {
            Some(ch) if !ch.is_control() => cur.push(ch),
            _ => {
                if cur.trim().chars().count() >= 3 {
                    out.push(cur.trim().to_string());
                }
                cur.clear();
            }
        }
    }
    if cur.trim().chars().count() >= 3 {
        out.push(cur.trim().to_string());
    }
    out
}

fn utf16_to_string(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    let (pairs, _) = bytes.as_chunks::<2>();
    let units: Vec<u16> = pairs.iter().map(|c| u16::from_le_bytes(*c)).collect();
    String::from_utf16_lossy(&units)
}

// --- signature carving -----------------------------------------------------

/// A magic-byte signature for an embedded file.
struct Sig {
    magic: &'static [u8],
    ext: &'static str,
    name: &'static str,
}

const SIGS: &[Sig] = &[
    Sig {
        magic: b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n",
        ext: "png",
        name: "png",
    },
    Sig {
        magic: b"\xff\xd8\xff",
        ext: "jpg",
        name: "jpeg",
    },
    Sig {
        magic: b"GIF87a",
        ext: "gif",
        name: "gif",
    },
    Sig {
        magic: b"GIF89a",
        ext: "gif",
        name: "gif",
    },
    Sig {
        magic: b"BM",
        ext: "bmp",
        name: "bmp",
    },
    Sig {
        magic: b"RIFF",
        ext: "wav",
        name: "riff",
    },
    Sig {
        magic: b"PK\x03\x04",
        ext: "zip",
        name: "zip",
    },
    Sig {
        magic: b"\x1f\x8b\x08",
        ext: "gz",
        name: "gzip",
    },
    Sig {
        magic: b"%PDF",
        ext: "pdf",
        name: "pdf",
    },
    Sig {
        magic: b"7z\xbc\xaf\x27\x1c",
        ext: "7z",
        name: "7z",
    },
    Sig {
        magic: b"Rar!\x1a\x07",
        ext: "rar",
        name: "rar",
    },
    Sig {
        magic: b"OggS",
        ext: "ogg",
        name: "ogg",
    },
    Sig {
        magic: b"fLaC",
        ext: "flac",
        name: "flac",
    },
    Sig {
        magic: b"\x25\x21PS",
        ext: "ps",
        name: "postscript",
    },
];

fn carve(data: &[u8], covered: &[(usize, usize)], out: &mut Vec<Resource>) {
    let mut ranges: Vec<(usize, usize)> = covered.to_vec();
    let mut found = 0usize;
    for sig in SIGS {
        for pos in memchr::memmem::find_iter(data, sig.magic) {
            // Skip offset 0 (that is the host file itself) and anything inside an already
            // reported range (a resource, a section, the overlay, or an earlier carve).
            if pos == 0 || ranges.iter().any(|&(s, e)| pos >= s && pos < e) {
                continue;
            }
            let Some(end) = carve_end(sig, data, pos) else {
                continue;
            };
            if end <= pos || end - pos > MAX_ITEM {
                continue;
            }
            ranges.push((pos, end));
            out.push(Resource::new(
                ResourceKind::Embedded,
                format!("{}_{:x}", sig.name, pos),
                sig.ext,
                Some(pos as u64),
                data[pos..end].to_vec(),
            ));
            found += 1;
            if found >= MAX_ITEMS {
                return;
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Best-effort end offset of an embedded file starting at `pos`.
fn carve_end(sig: &Sig, data: &[u8], pos: usize) -> Option<usize> {
    let rest = &data[pos..];
    match sig.ext {
        "png" => memchr::memmem::find(rest, b"IEND").map(|i| pos + i + 8),
        "jpg" => memchr::memmem::find(&rest[2..], b"\xff\xd9").map(|i| pos + 2 + i + 2),
        "pdf" => rfind(rest, b"%%EOF").map(|i| pos + i + 5),
        "gif" => rest.iter().position(|&b| b == 0x3b).map(|i| pos + i + 1),
        "bmp" => read_u32(rest, 2)
            .map(|n| pos + n as usize)
            .filter(|&e| e <= data.len()),
        "wav" => {
            if rest.len() < 12 || &rest[8..12] != b"WAVE" {
                return None;
            }
            read_u32(rest, 4)
                .map(|n| pos + 8 + n as usize)
                .filter(|&e| e <= data.len())
        }
        "zip" => zip_end(rest).map(|n| pos + n),
        _ => Some((pos + CARVE_FALLBACK).min(data.len())),
    }
}

/// End of a ZIP: locate the End Of Central Directory record (PK\x05\x06) and add its comment.
fn zip_end(rest: &[u8]) -> Option<usize> {
    let eocd = rfind(rest, b"PK\x05\x06")?;
    let comment_len = read_u16(rest, eocd + 20)? as usize;
    Some((eocd + 22 + comment_len).min(rest.len()))
}

fn rfind(hay: &[u8], needle: &[u8]) -> Option<usize> {
    memchr::memmem::rfind(hay, needle)
}

fn read_u16(data: &[u8], at: usize) -> Option<u16> {
    data.get(at..at + 2)
        .map(|b| u16::from_le_bytes([b[0], b[1]]))
}

fn read_u32(data: &[u8], at: usize) -> Option<u32> {
    data.get(at..at + 4)
        .map(|b| u32::from_le_bytes([b[0], b[1], b[2], b[3]]))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn string_table_decodes_utf16() {
        // Two strings "hi" and "yo" in one RT_STRING block.
        let mut b = Vec::new();
        for s in ["hi", "yo"] {
            b.extend_from_slice(&(s.len() as u16).to_le_bytes());
            for ch in s.encode_utf16() {
                b.extend_from_slice(&ch.to_le_bytes());
            }
        }
        let text = string_table(&b);
        assert!(text.contains("hi") && text.contains("yo"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn carve_finds_embedded_png_and_zip() {
        let mut data = vec![0u8; 64]; // some header-ish filler
        let png_start = data.len();
        data.extend_from_slice(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n");
        data.extend_from_slice(&[1, 2, 3, 4]);
        data.extend_from_slice(b"IEND\xae\x42\x60\x82"); // IEND + CRC
        let after_png = data.len();
        // A tiny ZIP: a local-file-header signature, then the EOCD record (comment length 0).
        let zip_start = data.len();
        data.extend_from_slice(b"PK\x03\x04");
        data.extend_from_slice(&[0u8; 8]);
        data.extend_from_slice(b"PK\x05\x06");
        data.extend_from_slice(&[0u8; 18]); // disk numbers … + comment length 0
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        carve(&data, &[], &mut out);
        let png = out.iter().find(|r| r.ext == "png").expect("png carved");
        assert_eq!(png.offset, Some(png_start as u64));
        assert_eq!(png.data.len(), after_png - png_start);
        assert!(
            out.iter()
                .any(|r| r.ext == "zip" && r.offset == Some(zip_start as u64))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn wrap_bmp_adds_a_file_header() {
        let mut dib = vec![40, 0, 0, 0]; // biSize = 40
        dib.extend_from_slice(&[0u8; 36]);
        let bmp = wrap_bmp(&dib);
        assert_eq!(&bmp[..2], b"BM");
        assert_eq!(bmp.len(), dib.len() + 14);
    }

    #[test]
    fn write_all_writes_files_and_manifest() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("orress-res-test-{}", std::process::id()));
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
        let res = vec![Resource::new(
            ResourceKind::Embedded,
            "png_0",
            "png",
            Some(0),
            vec![1, 2, 3],
        )];
        let written = write_all(&res, &dir).expect("write");
        assert_eq!(written.len(), 1);
        assert!(dir.join("export_manifest.txt").exists());
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&written[0]).unwrap(), vec![1, 2, 3]);
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }
}
```

```rs
//! Probes the ETW activity monitor: starts it, captures for ~2s, prints a summary. On a non-admin
//! shell this should fail cleanly with the "run as administrator" hint; elevated it prints events.
//!
//! Run with: `cargo run -p orress-sandbox --example etw_probe`

fn main() {
    match orress_sandbox::etw::start() {
        Err(e) => {
            println!("monitor did not start (expected without admin):\n  {e}");
        }
        Ok(mut monitor) => {
            println!("monitor started — capturing for 2s…");
            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(2));
            let events = monitor.events();
            println!("captured {} event(s)", events.len());
            for e in events.iter().take(15) {
                println!(
                    "  [{:>8}] pid {:<6} {} {}",
                    e.category.label(),
                    e.pid,
                    e.op,
                    e.detail
                );
            }
            monitor.stop();
        }
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-sandbox/src/etw.rs`:

```rs
//! A kernel-level activity monitor via ETW (Event Tracing for Windows). While a sample runs, it
//! records process, file, registry, network and image-load events system-wide; the UI filters to
//! the sample's PID. The NT Kernel Logger requires **administrator** privileges, so starting the
//! trace fails cleanly (with that hint) when ORRESS is not elevated. Windows-only; other
//! platforms return an error.

#[cfg(windows)]
use std::sync::Mutex;

#[cfg(windows)]
use crate::event_log::EventLog;

/// The kind of activity an event represents.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Category {
    Process,
    File,
    Registry,
    Network,
    Image,
    Other,
}

impl Category {
    pub fn label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Process => "Process",
            Self::File => "File",
            Self::Registry => "Registry",
            Self::Network => "Network",
            Self::Image => "Image",
            Self::Other => "Other",
        }
    }
}

/// One recorded activity event.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ActivityEvent {
    pub seq: usize,
    pub pid: u32,
    pub category: Category,
    pub op: String,
    pub detail: String,
}

/// The largest number of events kept in memory.
#[cfg(windows)]
const MAX_EVENTS: usize = 50_000;

#[cfg(windows)]
pub use imp::Monitor;

/// Starts the activity monitor (Windows + admin only).
#[cfg(windows)]
pub fn start() -> Result<Monitor, String> {
    imp::start()
}

#[cfg(not(windows))]
pub struct Monitor;

#[cfg(not(windows))]
impl Monitor {
    pub fn events(&self) -> Vec<ActivityEvent> {
        Vec::new()
    }
    pub fn with_events<R>(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&[ActivityEvent]) -> R) -> R {
        f(&[])
    }
    pub fn events_since(&self, seen: usize) -> (Vec<ActivityEvent>, usize) {
        (Vec::new(), seen)
    }
    pub fn stop(&mut self) {}
}

#[cfg(not(windows))]
pub fn start() -> Result<Monitor, String> {
    Err("the ETW activity monitor is only available on Windows".into())
}

/// Appends an event, capping the log so it can't grow without bound.
#[cfg(windows)]
fn record(log: &Mutex<EventLog<ActivityEvent>>, ev: ActivityEvent) {
    log.lock().unwrap().push(ev, MAX_EVENTS);
}

#[cfg(windows)]
mod imp {
    use std::collections::HashMap;
    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
    use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
    use std::thread::JoinHandle;

    use ferrisetw::parser::Parser;
    use ferrisetw::provider::Provider;
    use ferrisetw::provider::kernel_providers::{
        FILE_IO_PROVIDER, IMAGE_LOAD_PROVIDER, PROCESS_PROVIDER, REGISTRY_PROVIDER,
        TCP_IP_PROVIDER, THREAD_PROVIDER,
    };
    use ferrisetw::trace::{TraceTrait, stop_trace_by_name};
    use ferrisetw::{EventRecord, GUID, KernelTrace, SchemaLocator};

    use super::{ActivityEvent, Category};
    use crate::event_log::EventLog;

    const TRACE_NAME: &str = "ORRESS-Activity";

    /// A running ETW activity monitor. Stops on drop.
    pub struct Monitor {
        log: Arc<Mutex<EventLog<ActivityEvent>>>,
        trace: Option<KernelTrace>,
        thread: Option<JoinHandle<()>>,
    }

    impl Monitor {
        /// A copy of every retained event. Prefer [`events_since`](Self::events_since) for
        /// periodic refreshes, or [`with_events`](Self::with_events) to read without copying.
        pub fn events(&self) -> Vec<ActivityEvent> {
            self.log.lock().unwrap().events().to_vec()
        }

        /// Runs `f` over the retained events (oldest first) without copying them. The log is
        /// locked meanwhile, so keep `f` short.
        pub fn with_events<R>(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&[ActivityEvent]) -> R) -> R {
            f(self.log.lock().unwrap().events())
        }

        /// The events recorded since a reader had seen `seen` of them (start at 0), and the count
        /// to pass next time — so a periodic refresh copies only what is new.
        pub fn events_since(&self, seen: usize) -> (Vec<ActivityEvent>, usize) {
            self.log.lock().unwrap().since(seen)
        }

        pub fn stop(&mut self) {
            if let Some(trace) = self.trace.take() {
                let _ = trace.stop();
            }
            if let Some(t) = self.thread.take() {
                let _ = t.join();
            }
        }
    }

    impl Drop for Monitor {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            self.stop();
        }
    }

    fn categorize(guid: GUID) -> Category {
        for (provider, cat) in [
            (&PROCESS_PROVIDER, Category::Process),
            (&FILE_IO_PROVIDER, Category::File),
            (&REGISTRY_PROVIDER, Category::Registry),
            (&TCP_IP_PROVIDER, Category::Network),
            (&IMAGE_LOAD_PROVIDER, Category::Image),
        ] {
            if provider.guid == guid {
                return cat;
            }
        }
        Category::Other
    }

    /// Best-effort extraction of the most useful string field for a category.
    fn detail_for(cat: Category, parser: &Parser) -> String {
        let fields: &[&str] = match cat {
            Category::Image => &["FileName"],
            Category::Process => &["ImageFileName", "ProcessName", "CommandLine"],
            Category::File => &["FileName", "OpenPath"],
            Category::Registry => &["KeyName", "RelativeName", "ValueName"],
            Category::Network => &["daddr", "DestinationIp"],
            Category::Other => &[],
        };
        for f in fields {
            if let Ok(v) = parser.try_parse::<String>(f)
                && !v.is_empty()
            {
                return v;
            }
        }
        String::new()
    }

    /// The header PID kernel events carry when they were logged outside any process context
    /// (common for FileIo, which the kernel logs from wherever the I/O completes).
    const NO_PID: u32 = u32::MAX;
    /// Bound on the thread→process map (cleared and relearned if a trace churns past it).
    const MAX_THREADS: usize = 200_000;

    /// Thread id -> owning process id, learned from Thread events and from every event whose
    /// header names both, so context-less events can be attributed to the right process.
    type ThreadMap = Mutex<HashMap<u32, u32>>;

    fn learn(threads: &ThreadMap, tid: u32, pid: u32) {
        if tid == NO_PID || pid == NO_PID || pid == 0 {
            return;
        }
        let mut m = threads.lock().unwrap();
        if m.len() >= MAX_THREADS {
            m.clear();
        }
        m.insert(tid, pid);
    }

    fn handle(
        record: &EventRecord,
        locator: &SchemaLocator,
        log: &Arc<Mutex<EventLog<ActivityEvent>>>,
        seq: &AtomicUsize,
        threads: &ThreadMap,
    ) {
        let schema = locator.event_schema(record).ok();
        let parser = schema.as_ref().map(|s| Parser::create(record, s));

        // Thread events only feed the thread→process map; they aren't activity themselves.
        if record.provider_id() == THREAD_PROVIDER.guid {
            if let Some(p) = &parser
                && let (Ok(pid), Ok(tid)) = (
                    p.try_parse::<u32>("ProcessId"),
                    p.try_parse::<u32>("TThreadId"),
                )
            {
                learn(threads, tid, pid);
            }
            return;
        }

        let mut pid = record.process_id();
        learn(threads, record.thread_id(), pid);
        if pid == NO_PID {
            // No process context in the header: attribute the event through the issuing
            // thread (FileIo payloads carry it as TTID) if we know which process owns it.
            let tid = Some(record.thread_id())
                .filter(|&t| t != NO_PID)
                .or_else(|| parser.as_ref()?.try_parse::<u32>("TTID").ok());
            if let Some(owner) = tid.and_then(|t| threads.lock().unwrap().get(&t).copied()) {
                pid = owner;
            }
        }

        let category = categorize(record.provider_id());
        let (op, detail) = match (&schema, &parser) {
            (Some(schema), Some(parser)) => {
                let name = schema.opcode_name();
                let op = if name.is_empty() {
                    format!("opcode {}", record.opcode())
                } else {
                    name
                };
                (op, detail_for(category, parser))
            }
            _ => (format!("opcode {}", record.opcode()), String::new()),
        };
        let ev = ActivityEvent {
            seq: seq.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst),
            pid,
            category,
            op,
            detail,
        };
        super::record(log, ev);
    }

    pub fn start() -> Result<Monitor, String> {
        // Clean up a leftover session from a previous (crashed) run.
        let _ = stop_trace_by_name(TRACE_NAME);

        let log = Arc::new(Mutex::new(EventLog::default()));
        let seq = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
        let threads: Arc<ThreadMap> = Arc::new(Mutex::new(HashMap::new()));
        let provider = |kp| {
            let (log, seq, threads) = (Arc::clone(&log), Arc::clone(&seq), Arc::clone(&threads));
            Provider::kernel(kp)
                .add_callback(move |rec: &EventRecord, loc: &SchemaLocator| {
                    handle(rec, loc, &log, &seq, &threads)
                })
                .build()
        };

        let (trace, handle) = KernelTrace::new()
            .named(TRACE_NAME.to_string())
            // Thread start/end (and the rundown of existing threads) map thread ids to
            // processes, for events that arrive without a process context.
            .enable(provider(&THREAD_PROVIDER))
            .enable(provider(&PROCESS_PROVIDER))
            .enable(provider(&FILE_IO_PROVIDER))
            .enable(provider(&REGISTRY_PROVIDER))
            .enable(provider(&TCP_IP_PROVIDER))
            .enable(provider(&IMAGE_LOAD_PROVIDER))
            .start()
            .map_err(|e| {
                let raw = format!("{e:?}");
                // 0x80070005 / errno 5 is ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED — by far the most common cause.
                if raw.contains("-2147024891") || raw.to_lowercase().contains("denied") {
                    "ETW kernel tracing requires running ORRESS as administrator (access denied)."
                        .to_string()
                } else {
                    format!("could not start ETW kernel trace: {raw}")
                }
            })?;

        let thread = std::thread::spawn(move || {
            let _ = KernelTrace::process_from_handle(handle);
        });

        Ok(Monitor {
            log,
            trace: Some(trace),
            thread: Some(thread),
        })
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-sandbox/src/event_log.rs`:

```rs
//! A capped, append-only event log shared between recorder threads and the UI. Besides the
//! retained events it counts every event ever recorded, so a reader can fetch only what is new
//! since its last read ([`EventLog::since`]) even after the oldest entries were dropped — instead
//! of copying the whole (up to tens of thousands of entries) log on every refresh.

/// A capped event log: the retained events plus a running total of all events recorded.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) struct EventLog<T> {
    events: Vec<T>,
    total: usize,
}

impl<T> Default for EventLog<T> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            events: Vec::new(),
            total: 0,
        }
    }
}

impl<T: Clone> EventLog<T> {
    /// Appends `ev`; once `cap` events are retained the oldest fifth is dropped first, so the log
    /// can't grow without bound.
    pub(crate) fn push(&mut self, ev: T, cap: usize) {
        if self.events.len() >= cap {
            self.events.drain(0..(cap / 5).max(1));
        }
        self.events.push(ev);
        self.total += 1;
    }

    /// The retained events, oldest first.
    pub(crate) fn events(&self) -> &[T] {
        &self.events
    }

    /// The events recorded after the first `seen` (counting every event ever recorded), and the
    /// new count to pass next time. Events that were already dropped from the log are skipped.
    pub(crate) fn since(&self, seen: usize) -> (Vec<T>, usize) {
        let dropped = self.total - self.events.len();
        let from = seen.saturating_sub(dropped).min(self.events.len());
        (self.events[from..].to_vec(), self.total)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::EventLog;

    #[test]
    fn since_returns_only_new_events_across_drops() {
        let mut log = EventLog::default();
        for i in 0..4 {
            log.push(i, 10);
        }
        let (new, seen) = log.since(0);
        assert_eq!((new, seen), (vec![0, 1, 2, 3], 4));
        log.push(4, 10);
        assert_eq!(log.since(seen), (vec![4], 5));
        assert_eq!(log.since(5), (vec![], 5));
        // Fill past the cap: the oldest are dropped, yet `since` still lines up.
        for i in 5..12 {
            log.push(i, 10);
        }
        assert_eq!(log.events().len(), 10);
        assert_eq!(log.since(5), (vec![5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11], 12));
        // A reader that fell behind the drop just gets everything retained.
        assert_eq!(log.since(0).0.first(), Some(&2));
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-sandbox/src/fakenet.rs`:

```rs
//! A tiny fake-network responder (INetSim / FakeNet-NG style). A detonated sample, with its VM
//! network pointed here, gets an answer for every DNS query and HTTP request — so instead of
//! reaching real infrastructure it talks to us, and we **log** exactly what it tried to do.
//!
//! Pure `std` networking: a minimal DNS A-record responder and an HTTP responder that returns a
//! canned 200. Ports are configurable (the real `53`/`80` need privileges; tests use ephemeral
//! ports). Listeners run on background threads and stop on drop; each HTTP connection gets its
//! own (bounded) thread, and the event log is capped.

use std::io::{Read, Write};
use std::net::{Ipv4Addr, SocketAddr, TcpListener, TcpStream, UdpSocket};
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicUsize, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::thread::JoinHandle;
use std::time::Duration;

use crate::event_log::EventLog;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum NetKind {
    Dns,
    Http,
}

/// One observed network attempt.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct NetEvent {
    pub seq: usize,
    pub kind: NetKind,
    pub summary: String,
}

/// Fake-network configuration.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct Config {
    /// The IPv4 address every DNS A query is answered with.
    pub answer_ip: Ipv4Addr,
    pub dns_port: u16,
    pub http_port: u16,
}

impl Default for Config {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            answer_ip: Ipv4Addr::new(127, 0, 0, 1),
            dns_port: 53,
            http_port: 80,
        }
    }
}

/// A running fake network. Dropping it stops the listeners.
pub struct FakeNet {
    log: Arc<Mutex<EventLog<NetEvent>>>,
    shutdown: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    threads: Vec<JoinHandle<()>>,
    pub dns_addr: Option<SocketAddr>,
    pub http_addr: Option<SocketAddr>,
    pub errors: Vec<String>,
}

impl FakeNet {
    /// Binds the responders and starts serving. Bind failures (e.g. no privilege for port 53)
    /// are recorded in `errors` rather than failing the whole start.
    pub fn start(cfg: Config) -> Self {
        let log = Arc::new(Mutex::new(EventLog::default()));
        let seq = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
        let shutdown = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
        let mut threads = Vec::new();
        let mut errors = Vec::new();
        let mut dns_addr = None;
        let mut http_addr = None;

        match UdpSocket::bind((Ipv4Addr::UNSPECIFIED, cfg.dns_port)) {
            Ok(sock) => {
                sock.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_millis(100))).ok();
                dns_addr = sock.local_addr().ok();
                let (log, seq, shutdown) = (log.clone(), seq.clone(), shutdown.clone());
                let answer = cfg.answer_ip;
                threads.push(std::thread::spawn(move || {
                    dns_loop(&sock, answer, &log, &seq, &shutdown)
                }));
            }
            Err(e) => errors.push(format!("DNS :{} — {e}", cfg.dns_port)),
        }

        match TcpListener::bind((Ipv4Addr::UNSPECIFIED, cfg.http_port)) {
            Ok(listener) => {
                listener.set_nonblocking(true).ok();
                http_addr = listener.local_addr().ok();
                let (log, seq, shutdown) = (log.clone(), seq.clone(), shutdown.clone());
                threads.push(std::thread::spawn(move || {
                    http_loop(&listener, &log, &seq, &shutdown)
                }));
            }
            Err(e) => errors.push(format!("HTTP :{} — {e}", cfg.http_port)),
        }

        FakeNet {
            log,
            shutdown,
            threads,
            dns_addr,
            http_addr,
            errors,
        }
    }

    /// A snapshot of the captured network events. Prefer [`events_since`](Self::events_since)
    /// for periodic refreshes, or [`with_events`](Self::with_events) to read without copying.
    pub fn events(&self) -> Vec<NetEvent> {
        self.log.lock().unwrap().events().to_vec()
    }

    /// Runs `f` over the retained events (oldest first) without copying them. The log is locked
    /// meanwhile, so keep `f` short.
    pub fn with_events<R>(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&[NetEvent]) -> R) -> R {
        f(self.log.lock().unwrap().events())
    }

    /// The events captured since a reader had seen `seen` of them (start at 0), and the count to
    /// pass next time — so a periodic refresh copies only what is new.
    pub fn events_since(&self, seen: usize) -> (Vec<NetEvent>, usize) {
        self.log.lock().unwrap().since(seen)
    }

    /// Whether any listener is serving.
    pub fn is_listening(&self) -> bool {
        self.dns_addr.is_some() || self.http_addr.is_some()
    }

    /// Stops the listeners and joins their threads.
    pub fn stop(&mut self) {
        self.shutdown.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
        for t in self.threads.drain(..) {
            let _ = t.join();
        }
    }
}

impl Drop for FakeNet {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.stop();
    }
}

/// The most events kept; beyond this the oldest are dropped (a chatty sample can't exhaust
/// memory).
const MAX_EVENTS: usize = 50_000;
/// The most HTTP connections served at once; more are closed unanswered.
const MAX_HTTP_CONNECTIONS: usize = 64;

fn record(log: &Mutex<EventLog<NetEvent>>, seq: &AtomicUsize, kind: NetKind, summary: String) {
    let n = seq.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
    log.lock().unwrap().push(
        NetEvent {
            seq: n,
            kind,
            summary,
        },
        MAX_EVENTS,
    );
}

// --- DNS ------------------------------------------------------------------

fn dns_loop(
    sock: &UdpSocket,
    answer: Ipv4Addr,
    log: &Mutex<EventLog<NetEvent>>,
    seq: &AtomicUsize,
    shutdown: &AtomicBool,
) {
    let mut buf = [0u8; 512];
    while !shutdown.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
        match sock.recv_from(&mut buf) {
            Ok((n, src)) => {
                if let Some((domain, resp)) = dns_reply(&buf[..n], answer) {
                    let _ = sock.send_to(&resp, src);
                    record(log, seq, NetKind::Dns, format!("A? {domain}  →  {answer}"));
                }
            }
            Err(e) if is_timeout(&e) => continue,
            Err(_) => break,
        }
    }
}

/// Parses a DNS query and builds an A-record reply, returning the queried name and the response.
fn dns_reply(query: &[u8], answer: Ipv4Addr) -> Option<(String, Vec<u8>)> {
    if query.len() < 12 {
        return None;
    }
    // QR set: this is a response, not a query — never answer it (that could loop two
    // responders against each other).
    if query[2] & 0x80 != 0 {
        return None;
    }
    let qdcount = u16::from_be_bytes([query[4], query[5]]);
    if qdcount == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    // Parse QNAME starting at offset 12.
    let mut i = 12;
    let mut labels = Vec::new();
    let mut name_len = 0usize;
    loop {
        let len = *query.get(i)?;
        if len == 0 {
            i += 1;
            break;
        }
        // The top two bits mark a compression pointer (0xC0) or a reserved label type; a
        // query's own question name never needs one, so reject rather than misread it as a
        // length.
        if len & 0xC0 != 0 {
            return None;
        }
        let start = i + 1;
        let end = start + len as usize;
        let label = query.get(start..end)?;
        name_len += len as usize + 1;
        if name_len > 255 {
            return None;
        }
        labels.push(String::from_utf8_lossy(label).into_owned());
        i = end;
    }
    let qtype = u16::from_be_bytes([*query.get(i)?, *query.get(i + 1)?]);
    let question_end = i + 4; // QTYPE(2) + QCLASS(2)
    let domain = labels.join(".");

    let mut resp = Vec::with_capacity(question_end + 16);
    resp.extend_from_slice(&query[0..2]); // ID
    resp.extend_from_slice(&[0x81, 0x80]); // flags: QR=1, RD=1, RA=1
    resp.extend_from_slice(&[0x00, 0x01]); // QDCOUNT = 1
    let is_a = qtype == 1;
    resp.extend_from_slice(if is_a { &[0x00, 0x01] } else { &[0x00, 0x00] }); // ANCOUNT
    resp.extend_from_slice(&[0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00]); // NSCOUNT, ARCOUNT
    resp.extend_from_slice(query.get(12..question_end)?); // the question
    if is_a {
        resp.extend_from_slice(&[0xc0, 0x0c]); // NAME: pointer to qname
        resp.extend_from_slice(&[0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0x01]); // TYPE A, CLASS IN
        resp.extend_from_slice(&[0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x3c]); // TTL 60
        resp.extend_from_slice(&[0x00, 0x04]); // RDLENGTH
        resp.extend_from_slice(&answer.octets()); // RDATA
    }
    Some((domain, resp))
}

// --- HTTP -----------------------------------------------------------------

fn http_loop(
    listener: &TcpListener,
    log: &Arc<Mutex<EventLog<NetEvent>>>,
    seq: &Arc<AtomicUsize>,
    shutdown: &AtomicBool,
) {
    // Each connection is served on its own thread, so one slow client (the read waits up to
    // 2 s) can't stall the rest; the count is bounded.
    let active = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
    while !shutdown.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
        match listener.accept() {
            Ok((stream, src)) => {
                if active.load(Ordering::SeqCst) >= MAX_HTTP_CONNECTIONS {
                    drop(stream);
                    continue;
                }
                active.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
                let (log, seq, slot) = (Arc::clone(log), Arc::clone(seq), Arc::clone(&active));
                let spawned = std::thread::Builder::new()
                    .name("fakenet-http".into())
                    .spawn(move || {
                        handle_http(stream, src, &log, &seq);
                        slot.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
                    });
                if spawned.is_err() {
                    active.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
                }
            }
            Err(ref e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => {
                std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20));
            }
            Err(_) => break,
        }
    }
}

fn handle_http(
    mut stream: TcpStream,
    src: SocketAddr,
    log: &Mutex<EventLog<NetEvent>>,
    seq: &AtomicUsize,
) {
    stream.set_nonblocking(false).ok();
    stream.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(2))).ok();
    // Read until the end of the headers (or the buffer fills, or the client stops sending).
    let mut buf = [0u8; 8192];
    let mut n = 0;
    while n < buf.len() {
        match stream.read(&mut buf[n..]) {
            Ok(0) | Err(_) => break,
            Ok(k) => {
                n += k;
                if buf[..n].windows(4).any(|w| w == b"\r\n\r\n") {
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
    }
    let req = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf[..n]);
    let line = req.lines().next().unwrap_or("").trim().to_string();
    let host = header(&req, "host");
    let agent = header(&req, "user-agent");
    let mut summary = format!("{line}  (from {src})");
    if let Some(h) = host {
        summary.push_str(&format!("  Host: {h}"));
    }
    if let Some(a) = agent {
        summary.push_str(&format!("  UA: {a}"));
    }
    record(log, seq, NetKind::Http, summary);

    let body = b"OK";
    let _ = write!(
        stream,
        "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n",
        body.len()
    );
    let _ = stream.write_all(body);
}

fn header<'a>(req: &'a str, name: &str) -> Option<&'a str> {
    req.lines()
        .find(|l| l.to_ascii_lowercase().starts_with(&format!("{name}:")))
        .and_then(|l| l.split_once(':'))
        .map(|(_, v)| v.trim())
}

fn is_timeout(e: &std::io::Error) -> bool {
    matches!(
        e.kind(),
        std::io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock | std::io::ErrorKind::TimedOut
    )
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::net::Ipv4Addr;

    fn ephemeral() -> Config {
        Config {
            answer_ip: Ipv4Addr::new(10, 1, 2, 3),
            dns_port: 0,
            http_port: 0,
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn dns_answers_and_logs() {
        let net = FakeNet::start(ephemeral());
        let addr = net.dns_addr.expect("dns bound");
        let client = UdpSocket::bind((Ipv4Addr::LOCALHOST, 0)).unwrap();
        client
            .set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(2)))
            .unwrap();
        // Query "evil.example.com" A: id=0x1234, flags=0x0100, qd=1, name, A/IN.
        let query = [
            0x12, 0x34, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 4, b'e', b'v', b'i', b'l', 7,
            b'e', b'x', b'a', b'm', b'p', b'l', b'e', 3, b'c', b'o', b'm', 0, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00,
            0x01,
        ];
        client
            .send_to(&query, (Ipv4Addr::LOCALHOST, addr.port()))
            .unwrap();
        let mut resp = [0u8; 512];
        let n = client.recv(&mut resp).unwrap();
        // The answer's last 4 bytes are the A record IP we configured.
        assert_eq!(&resp[n - 4..n], &[10, 1, 2, 3]);
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50));
        let events = net.events();
        assert!(
            events
                .iter()
                .any(|e| e.kind == NetKind::Dns && e.summary.contains("evil.example.com"))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn dns_ignores_responses_and_pointer_labels() {
        let ip = Ipv4Addr::new(10, 0, 0, 1);
        let query = [
            0x12, 0x34, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, b'a', 0, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00,
            0x01,
        ];
        assert!(dns_reply(&query, ip).is_some());
        // The same packet with QR set is a response: no answer.
        let mut response = query;
        response[2] |= 0x80;
        assert!(dns_reply(&response, ip).is_none());
        // A compression pointer in the question name is rejected, not read as a length.
        let pointer = [
            0x12, 0x34, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0xC0, 0x0C, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00,
            0x01,
        ];
        assert!(dns_reply(&pointer, ip).is_none());
        // A truncated name is rejected too.
        assert!(dns_reply(&query[..14], ip).is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn http_serves_connections_concurrently() {
        let net = FakeNet::start(ephemeral());
        let addr = net.http_addr.expect("http bound");
        // A client that connects and sends nothing must not block the next one.
        let _idle = TcpStream::connect((Ipv4Addr::LOCALHOST, addr.port())).unwrap();
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
        let start = std::time::Instant::now();
        let mut stream = TcpStream::connect((Ipv4Addr::LOCALHOST, addr.port())).unwrap();
        stream.write_all(b"GET /x HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n").unwrap();
        stream
            .set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(5)))
            .unwrap();
        let mut resp = String::new();
        let _ = stream.read_to_string(&mut resp);
        assert!(resp.starts_with("HTTP/1.1 200"));
        assert!(start.elapsed() < Duration::from_millis(1500));
    }

    #[test]
    fn http_responds_and_logs() {
        let net = FakeNet::start(ephemeral());
        let addr = net.http_addr.expect("http bound");
        let mut stream = TcpStream::connect((Ipv4Addr::LOCALHOST, addr.port())).unwrap();
        stream
            .write_all(
                b"GET /gate.php HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: c2.bad.example\r\nUser-Agent: EvilBot\r\n\r\n",
            )
            .unwrap();
        let mut resp = String::new();
        stream
            .set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(2)))
            .unwrap();
        let _ = stream.read_to_string(&mut resp);
        assert!(resp.starts_with("HTTP/1.1 200"));
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50));
        let events = net.events();
        let http = events
            .iter()
            .find(|e| e.kind == NetKind::Http)
            .expect("http event");
        assert!(http.summary.contains("/gate.php"));
        assert!(http.summary.contains("c2.bad.example"));
        assert!(http.summary.contains("EvilBot"));
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-sandbox/src/guard.rs`:

```rs
//! The execution guard. Running a flagged sample is gated: by default it is refused on a
//! bare-metal host and requires an explicit confirmation even inside a VM. The caller enforces
//! the [`Decision`] — this module only decides.

/// What running a sample requires.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Policy {
    /// Refuse to run unless we appear to be inside a VM.
    pub require_vm: bool,
    /// Require an explicit user confirmation for each run.
    pub require_confirmation: bool,
}

impl Default for Policy {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            require_vm: true,
            require_confirmation: true,
        }
    }
}

/// The guard's decision.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Decision {
    Allowed,
    /// Allowed in principle, but the user has not confirmed yet.
    NeedsConfirmation,
    /// Refused: policy requires a VM and we are on bare metal.
    RefusedNotInVm,
}

impl Decision {
    pub fn is_allowed(self) -> bool {
        self == Decision::Allowed
    }

    pub fn explain(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Decision::Allowed => "ready to run (in a VM, confirmed)",
            Decision::NeedsConfirmation => "confirm you want to run this sample",
            Decision::RefusedNotInVm => {
                "refused: not running inside a VM — enable a VM or disable the VM requirement"
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Decides whether a sample may run under `policy`, given whether we are in a VM and whether the
/// user has confirmed.
pub fn guard(policy: &Policy, in_vm: bool, confirmed: bool) -> Decision {
    if policy.require_vm && !in_vm {
        return Decision::RefusedNotInVm;
    }
    if policy.require_confirmation && !confirmed {
        return Decision::NeedsConfirmation;
    }
    Decision::Allowed
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn refuses_on_bare_metal_by_default() {
        let p = Policy::default();
        assert_eq!(guard(&p, false, true), Decision::RefusedNotInVm);
    }

    #[test]
    fn needs_confirmation_in_vm() {
        let p = Policy::default();
        assert_eq!(guard(&p, true, false), Decision::NeedsConfirmation);
        assert_eq!(guard(&p, true, true), Decision::Allowed);
    }

    #[test]
    fn can_relax_vm_requirement() {
        let p = Policy {
            require_vm: false,
            require_confirmation: false,
        };
        assert!(guard(&p, false, false).is_allowed());
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-sandbox/src/job.rs`:

```rs
//! Windows Job Objects, so a sample's whole process tree can be contained and killed. The rest
//! of this crate forbids `unsafe`; this module is the one place that opts in, because Job
//! Objects are only reachable through raw Win32 FFI. Every call documents why it is sound.

#![allow(unsafe_code)]

use std::os::windows::io::AsRawHandle;
use std::process::Child;

use windows::Win32::Foundation::{CloseHandle, HANDLE};
use windows::Win32::System::Diagnostics::ToolHelp::{
    CreateToolhelp32Snapshot, TH32CS_SNAPTHREAD, THREADENTRY32, Thread32First, Thread32Next,
};
use windows::Win32::System::JobObjects::{
    AssignProcessToJobObject, CreateJobObjectW, JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE,
    JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_INFORMATION, JobObjectExtendedLimitInformation,
    SetInformationJobObject, TerminateJobObject,
};
use windows::Win32::System::Threading::{OpenThread, ResumeThread, THREAD_SUSPEND_RESUME};
use windows::core::PCWSTR;

/// `CREATE_SUSPENDED`, for `CommandExt::creation_flags`.
pub const CREATE_SUSPENDED: u32 = 0x0000_0004;

/// An anonymous job object that kills every process in it when terminated or closed.
pub struct Job(HANDLE);

// The handle is a plain kernel object handle; using it from another thread is fine.
unsafe impl Send for Job {}

impl Job {
    /// Creates a kill-on-close job, or `None` if the OS refuses.
    pub fn new() -> Option<Job> {
        // SAFETY: default security, no name; the returned handle is owned by `Job`.
        let h = unsafe { CreateJobObjectW(None, PCWSTR::null()) }.ok()?;
        let job = Job(h);
        let mut info = JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_INFORMATION::default();
        info.BasicLimitInformation.LimitFlags = JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE;
        // SAFETY: `info` is a correctly sized, initialized extended-limit struct for this
        // information class, and outlives the call.
        unsafe {
            SetInformationJobObject(
                job.0,
                JobObjectExtendedLimitInformation,
                &info as *const _ as *const core::ffi::c_void,
                std::mem::size_of::<JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_INFORMATION>() as u32,
            )
        }
        .ok()?;
        Some(job)
    }

    /// Puts `child` (and, from now on, everything it spawns) into the job.
    pub fn assign(&self, child: &Child) -> bool {
        let process = HANDLE(child.as_raw_handle());
        // SAFETY: both handles are live: the job is owned by `self`, the process by `child`.
        unsafe { AssignProcessToJobObject(self.0, process) }.is_ok()
    }

    /// Kills every process in the job.
    pub fn terminate(&self) {
        // SAFETY: `self.0` is a live job handle.
        unsafe {
            let _ = TerminateJobObject(self.0, 1);
        }
    }
}

impl Drop for Job {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: closing the handle we own, exactly once. KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE then ends any
        // process still in the job.
        unsafe {
            let _ = CloseHandle(self.0);
        }
    }
}

/// Resumes every thread of a process started with `CREATE_SUSPENDED` (std's `Child` doesn't
/// expose the primary thread handle, so find its threads by snapshot).
pub fn resume_process(pid: u32) {
    // SAFETY: a thread snapshot of the whole system; the handle is closed below.
    let Ok(snap) = (unsafe { CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(TH32CS_SNAPTHREAD, 0) }) else {
        return;
    };
    let mut entry = THREADENTRY32 {
        dwSize: std::mem::size_of::<THREADENTRY32>() as u32,
        ..Default::default()
    };
    // SAFETY: `snap` is a live snapshot handle and `entry` has `dwSize` set as required.
    let mut more = unsafe { Thread32First(snap, &mut entry) }.is_ok();
    while more {
        if entry.th32OwnerProcessID == pid {
            // SAFETY: opening a thread of our own child just to resume it; the handle is
            // closed right after.
            if let Ok(t) = unsafe { OpenThread(THREAD_SUSPEND_RESUME, false, entry.th32ThreadID) } {
                // SAFETY: `t` is the live thread handle just opened; closed exactly once.
                unsafe {
                    ResumeThread(t);
                    let _ = CloseHandle(t);
                }
            }
        }
        // SAFETY: as for Thread32First.
        more = unsafe { Thread32Next(snap, &mut entry) }.is_ok();
    }
    // SAFETY: closing the snapshot handle we own, exactly once.
    unsafe {
        let _ = CloseHandle(snap);
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-sandbox/src/launch.rs`:

```rs
//! A minimal process launcher that records a sample's lifecycle (start, output, exit) with a
//! timeout. This is the safe foundation for dynamic analysis; richer monitoring (file/registry/
//! network via ETW, a fake network, in-memory YARA) builds on top. Callers must pass the
//! guard before calling [`run`].
//!
//! Containment: the sample runs with no stdin, and its whole process tree is tracked — a Job
//! Object on Windows (the process starts suspended and is assigned before it runs a single
//! instruction; the job kills everything in it when closed), its own process group on Unix.
//! When the run ends (the timeout, or the sample exits) whatever is left of the tree is killed,
//! so a sample can't leave children running behind. (On Unix a descendant that leaves the
//! process group — `setsid` — escapes this.) Output is read as raw bytes (invalid UTF-8 is
//! replaced, never dropped) and capped, and the run never blocks forever on a pipe an escaped
//! process still holds.

use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader, Read};
use std::path::Path;
use std::process::{Child, Command, Stdio};
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
use std::sync::mpsc::{Receiver, RecvTimeoutError, Sender, channel};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::thread::JoinHandle;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

/// Total bytes of stdout + stderr recorded per run; the rest is drained and dropped.
const MAX_OUTPUT: usize = 8 * 1024 * 1024;
/// The longest single line recorded; longer lines are split.
const MAX_LINE: usize = 64 * 1024;
/// After the tree is killed, how long to wait for the output readers to see end-of-file.
const READER_GRACE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2);

/// An event observed while a sample ran.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum RunEvent {
    Started(u32),
    Stdout(String),
    Stderr(String),
    Exited(i32),
    Timeout,
    Error(String),
}

/// The record of one sandboxed run.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct RunLog {
    pub events: Vec<RunEvent>,
    pub exit_code: Option<i32>,
    pub timed_out: bool,
    pub duration: Duration,
}

type Events = Arc<Mutex<Vec<RunEvent>>>;

/// The sample's whole process tree.
struct Tree {
    #[cfg(windows)]
    job: Option<crate::job::Job>,
    #[cfg(unix)]
    pgid: i32,
}

impl Tree {
    /// Starts tracking `child`'s tree (and, on Windows, lets the suspended child run).
    fn attach(child: &Child) -> Tree {
        #[cfg(windows)]
        {
            let job = crate::job::Job::new().filter(|j| j.assign(child));
            // Always resume: a child left suspended would just sit until the timeout.
            crate::job::resume_process(child.id());
            Tree { job }
        }
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            Tree {
                pgid: child.id() as i32,
            }
        }
        #[cfg(not(any(windows, unix)))]
        {
            let _ = child;
            Tree {}
        }
    }

    /// Kills every process still in the tree.
    fn kill(&self) {
        #[cfg(windows)]
        if let Some(job) = &self.job {
            job.terminate();
        }
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            use nix::sys::signal::{Signal, killpg};
            use nix::unistd::Pid;
            let _ = killpg(Pid::from_raw(self.pgid), Signal::SIGKILL);
        }
    }
}

/// Runs `exe` with `args` (in `cwd` if given), capturing its output and exit, killing it after
/// `timeout`. The caller is responsible for having passed the execution guard first.
pub fn run(exe: &Path, args: &[String], cwd: Option<&Path>, timeout: Duration) -> RunLog {
    let events: Events = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
    let push = |e: RunEvent| events.lock().unwrap().push(e);
    let start = Instant::now();
    let deadline = start + timeout;

    let mut cmd = Command::new(exe);
    cmd.args(args)
        .stdin(Stdio::null())
        .stdout(Stdio::piped())
        .stderr(Stdio::piped());
    if let Some(dir) = cwd {
        cmd.current_dir(dir);
    }
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        use std::os::unix::process::CommandExt;
        // Its own process group, so the whole tree can be killed at once.
        cmd.process_group(0);
    }
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        use std::os::windows::process::CommandExt;
        // Suspended until it is inside the job, so nothing it spawns can escape the job.
        cmd.creation_flags(crate::job::CREATE_SUSPENDED);
    }
    let mut child = match cmd.spawn() {
        Ok(c) => c,
        Err(e) => {
            push(RunEvent::Error(format!("could not start: {e}")));
            return RunLog {
                events: take_events(&events),
                duration: start.elapsed(),
                ..Default::default()
            };
        }
    };
    let tree = Tree::attach(&child);
    push(RunEvent::Started(child.id()));

    // Stream stdout/stderr on helper threads into the shared log.
    let budget = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
    let (done_tx, done_rx) = channel();
    let mut readers = Vec::new();
    if let Some(out) = child.stdout.take() {
        readers.push(spawn_reader(
            out,
            RunEvent::Stdout,
            Arc::clone(&events),
            Arc::clone(&budget),
            done_tx.clone(),
        ));
    }
    if let Some(err) = child.stderr.take() {
        readers.push(spawn_reader(
            err,
            RunEvent::Stderr,
            Arc::clone(&events),
            Arc::clone(&budget),
            done_tx.clone(),
        ));
    }
    drop(done_tx);

    // Wait with a timeout (std has no wait-with-timeout, so poll).
    let mut exit_code = None;
    let mut timed_out = false;
    loop {
        match child.try_wait() {
            Ok(Some(status)) => {
                exit_code = status.code();
                break;
            }
            Ok(None) => {
                if Instant::now() >= deadline {
                    tree.kill();
                    let _ = child.kill();
                    let _ = child.wait();
                    timed_out = true;
                    break;
                }
                std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(40));
            }
            Err(e) => {
                events.lock().unwrap().push(RunEvent::Error(e.to_string()));
                break;
            }
        }
    }

    let mut pending = readers.len();
    if !timed_out {
        // The sample exited, but processes it started may still be writing to the pipes:
        // they get the rest of the time budget too.
        pending -= wait_readers(&done_rx, pending, deadline);
        if pending > 0 {
            timed_out = true;
        }
    }
    // Nothing the sample started outlives the run.
    tree.kill();
    pending -= wait_readers(&done_rx, pending, Instant::now() + READER_GRACE);
    for r in readers {
        // A reader still blocked (a pipe held by a process that escaped the tree) is left
        // detached rather than hanging the run.
        if pending == 0 || r.is_finished() {
            let _ = r.join();
        }
    }

    if let Some(code) = exit_code {
        events.lock().unwrap().push(RunEvent::Exited(code));
    }
    if timed_out {
        events.lock().unwrap().push(RunEvent::Timeout);
    }

    RunLog {
        events: take_events(&events),
        exit_code,
        timed_out,
        duration: start.elapsed(),
    }
}

/// Moves the recorded events out (a detached reader may still hold the `Arc`).
fn take_events(events: &Events) -> Vec<RunEvent> {
    std::mem::take(&mut *events.lock().unwrap())
}

/// Waits until `pending` readers have finished or `until` passes; returns how many finished.
fn wait_readers(done: &Receiver<()>, pending: usize, until: Instant) -> usize {
    let mut finished = 0;
    while finished < pending {
        let left = until.saturating_duration_since(Instant::now());
        match done.recv_timeout(left) {
            Ok(()) => finished += 1,
            Err(RecvTimeoutError::Timeout | RecvTimeoutError::Disconnected) => break,
        }
    }
    finished
}

/// Reads `src` line by line into the log on its own thread. Lines are raw bytes up to `\n`
/// (lossily decoded, so invalid UTF-8 never stops the capture), split at [`MAX_LINE`]; once
/// the shared `budget` passes [`MAX_OUTPUT`] the rest is drained without being recorded.
fn spawn_reader<R: Read + Send + 'static>(
    src: R,
    wrap: fn(String) -> RunEvent,
    events: Events,
    budget: Arc<AtomicUsize>,
    done: Sender<()>,
) -> JoinHandle<()> {
    std::thread::spawn(move || {
        read_lines(src, wrap, &events, &budget);
        let _ = done.send(());
    })
}

fn read_lines<R: Read>(
    src: R,
    wrap: fn(String) -> RunEvent,
    events: &Mutex<Vec<RunEvent>>,
    budget: &AtomicUsize,
) {
    let mut reader = BufReader::new(src);
    let mut line = Vec::new();
    let mut truncated = false;
    loop {
        line.clear();
        match reader
            .by_ref()
            .take(MAX_LINE as u64)
            .read_until(b'\n', &mut line)
        {
            Ok(0) => break,
            Ok(n) => {
                let used = budget.fetch_add(n, Ordering::SeqCst);
                if used.saturating_add(n) > MAX_OUTPUT {
                    if !truncated {
                        truncated = true;
                        events
                            .lock()
                            .unwrap()
                            .push(wrap("[output truncated]".into()));
                    }
                    continue;
                }
                if line.last() == Some(&b'\n') {
                    line.pop();
                    if line.last() == Some(&b'\r') {
                        line.pop();
                    }
                }
                let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&line).into_owned();
                events.lock().unwrap().push(wrap(text));
            }
            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::Interrupted => continue,
            Err(_) => break,
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[cfg(windows)]
    fn echo() -> (&'static str, Vec<String>) {
        ("cmd", vec!["/c".into(), "echo sandbox_ok".into()])
    }
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    fn echo() -> (&'static str, Vec<String>) {
        ("echo", vec!["sandbox_ok".into()])
    }

    #[test]
    fn captures_output_and_exit() {
        let (exe, args) = echo();
        let log = run(Path::new(exe), &args, None, Duration::from_secs(10));
        assert_eq!(log.exit_code, Some(0));
        assert!(!log.timed_out);
        assert!(
            log.events
                .iter()
                .any(|e| matches!(e, RunEvent::Stdout(s) if s.contains("sandbox_ok")))
        );
        assert!(matches!(log.events.first(), Some(RunEvent::Started(_))));
    }

    #[test]
    fn reports_a_missing_binary() {
        let log = run(
            Path::new("this_binary_does_not_exist_orress"),
            &[],
            None,
            Duration::from_secs(2),
        );
        assert!(log.events.iter().any(|e| matches!(e, RunEvent::Error(_))));
    }

    /// A grandchild holding the output pipe must not hang the run past its timeout.
    #[test]
    fn timeout_kills_the_whole_tree() {
        #[cfg(windows)]
        let (exe, args) = (
            "cmd",
            vec!["/c".to_string(), "ping -n 30 127.0.0.1".to_string()],
        );
        #[cfg(not(windows))]
        let (exe, args) = (
            "sh",
            vec!["-c".to_string(), "sleep 30; echo done".to_string()],
        );
        let log = run(Path::new(exe), &args, None, Duration::from_millis(800));
        assert!(log.timed_out);
        assert!(
            log.duration < Duration::from_secs(10),
            "took {:?}",
            log.duration
        );
        assert!(log.events.contains(&RunEvent::Timeout));
    }

    #[test]
    fn invalid_utf8_does_not_stop_the_capture() {
        let events = Mutex::new(Vec::new());
        let budget = AtomicUsize::new(0);
        let src = std::io::Cursor::new(b"first\r\n\xff\xfe bad\nafter\nno newline".to_vec());
        read_lines(src, RunEvent::Stdout, &events, &budget);
        let got = events.into_inner().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            got,
            vec![
                RunEvent::Stdout("first".into()),
                RunEvent::Stdout("\u{fffd}\u{fffd} bad".into()),
                RunEvent::Stdout("after".into()),
                RunEvent::Stdout("no newline".into()),
            ]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn output_is_capped() {
        let events = Mutex::new(Vec::new());
        let budget = AtomicUsize::new(MAX_OUTPUT - 3);
        let src = std::io::Cursor::new(b"ab\ncd\nef\n".to_vec());
        read_lines(src, RunEvent::Stdout, &events, &budget);
        let got = events.into_inner().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            got,
            vec![
                RunEvent::Stdout("ab".into()),
                RunEvent::Stdout("[output truncated]".into()),
            ]
        );
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-sandbox/src/store.rs`:

```rs
//! Defanged-at-rest storage. A flagged sample is never written to disk as a runnable file: it
//! is XOR-obfuscated behind a magic header, so a double-click or an on-access AV scanner sees
//! inert data. Refang only in memory, right before a gated run.

use std::io;
use std::path::Path;

const MAGIC: &[u8; 4] = b"ODF1";
const KEY: &[u8] = b"ORRESS-infected";

fn xor(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    data.iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(i, b)| b ^ KEY[i % KEY.len()])
        .collect()
}

/// Obfuscates `data` for storage (magic header + XOR).
pub fn defang(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out = MAGIC.to_vec();
    out.extend(xor(data));
    out
}

/// Recovers the original bytes from a defanged blob, or `None` if the header is wrong.
pub fn refang(blob: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    blob.strip_prefix(MAGIC.as_slice()).map(xor)
}

/// Writes `data` to `path` in defanged form.
pub fn store(path: &Path, data: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()> {
    std::fs::write(path, defang(data))
}

/// Reads and refangs a defanged file.
pub fn load(path: &Path) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>> {
    let blob = std::fs::read(path)?;
    refang(&blob).ok_or_else(|| io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, "not a defanged sample"))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn round_trips() {
        let original = b"MZ\x90\x00this is a dangerous payload\xff\xfe";
        let blob = defang(original);
        // The stored blob is not the original (no MZ header at offset 0).
        assert_ne!(&blob[..2], b"MZ");
        assert_eq!(refang(&blob).as_deref(), Some(original.as_slice()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_foreign_data() {
        assert!(refang(b"not a defanged blob").is_none());
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-sandbox/src/vbox.rs`:

```rs
//! VirtualBox control, by driving the `VBoxManage` CLI. This lets ORRESS orchestrate an analysis
//! VM from the host — list VMs, snapshot, revert, start/stop — for the "revert to clean, run the
//! sample, collect results, revert" workflow. The output parsers are pure (and unit-tested); the
//! wrappers shell out.

use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::process::Command;

/// A VirtualBox VM.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Vm {
    pub name: String,
    pub uuid: String,
}

/// Finds the `VBoxManage` executable (PATH, then the default install location).
pub fn vboxmanage() -> Option<PathBuf> {
    if let Ok(paths) = std::env::var("PATH") {
        for dir in std::env::split_paths(&paths) {
            for exe in ["VBoxManage", "VBoxManage.exe"] {
                let p = dir.join(exe);
                if p.is_file() {
                    return Some(p);
                }
            }
        }
    }
    for cand in [
        r"C:\Program Files\Oracle\VirtualBox\VBoxManage.exe",
        "/usr/bin/VBoxManage",
        "/usr/local/bin/VBoxManage",
        "/Applications/VirtualBox.app/Contents/MacOS/VBoxManage",
    ] {
        let p = PathBuf::from(cand);
        if p.is_file() {
            return Some(p);
        }
    }
    None
}

/// Whether VirtualBox is available.
pub fn available() -> bool {
    vboxmanage().is_some()
}

/// Runs `VBoxManage` with `args`, returning stdout or an error string.
fn run(args: &[&str]) -> Result<String, String> {
    let exe = vboxmanage().ok_or("VBoxManage not found — is VirtualBox installed?")?;
    let out = Command::new(exe)
        .args(args)
        .output()
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    if out.status.success() {
        Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout).into_owned())
    } else {
        Err(String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr)
            .lines()
            .find(|l| !l.trim().is_empty())
            .unwrap_or("VBoxManage failed")
            .to_string())
    }
}

// --- pure parsers ---------------------------------------------------------

/// Parses `VBoxManage list vms` output: lines like `"Name" {uuid}`.
pub fn parse_vms(output: &str) -> Vec<Vm> {
    output
        .lines()
        .filter_map(|line| {
            let line = line.trim();
            let name_end = line.rfind('"')?;
            let name = line.get(1..name_end)?.to_string();
            let brace = line.find('{')?;
            let close = line.find('}')?;
            let uuid = line.get(brace + 1..close)?.to_string();
            (!name.is_empty()).then_some(Vm { name, uuid })
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Parses `VMState="..."` from `showvminfo --machinereadable` output.
pub fn parse_state(machinereadable: &str) -> Option<String> {
    machinereadable
        .lines()
        .find_map(|l| l.strip_prefix("VMState="))
        .map(|v| v.trim_matches('"').to_string())
}

/// Parses `SnapshotName*="..."` entries from `snapshot <vm> list --machinereadable`.
pub fn parse_snapshots(machinereadable: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    machinereadable
        .lines()
        .filter(|l| l.starts_with("SnapshotName"))
        .filter_map(|l| l.split_once('='))
        .map(|(_, v)| v.trim_matches('"').to_string())
        .collect()
}

// --- wrappers -------------------------------------------------------------

pub fn list_vms() -> Result<Vec<Vm>, String> {
    Ok(parse_vms(&run(&["list", "vms"])?))
}

pub fn state(vm: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    Ok(parse_state(&run(&["showvminfo", vm, "--machinereadable"])?)
        .unwrap_or_else(|| "unknown".into()))
}

pub fn snapshots(vm: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
    // `snapshot list` errors when a VM has none; treat that as an empty list.
    match run(&["snapshot", vm, "list", "--machinereadable"]) {
        Ok(out) => Ok(parse_snapshots(&out)),
        Err(e) if e.to_lowercase().contains("does not have any snapshot") => Ok(Vec::new()),
        Err(e) => Err(e),
    }
}

pub fn take_snapshot(vm: &str, name: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    run(&["snapshot", vm, "take", name]).map(|_| ())
}

pub fn restore_snapshot(vm: &str, name: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    run(&["snapshot", vm, "restore", name]).map(|_| ())
}

pub fn restore_current(vm: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    run(&["snapshot", vm, "restorecurrent"]).map(|_| ())
}

pub fn start(vm: &str, headless: bool) -> Result<(), String> {
    let kind = if headless { "headless" } else { "gui" };
    run(&["startvm", vm, "--type", kind]).map(|_| ())
}

pub fn poweroff(vm: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    run(&["controlvm", vm, "poweroff"]).map(|_| ())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn parses_vm_list() {
        let out = "\"Kali-Linux\" {b3d301da-f47e-45e3-865e-70f8e88ecd5a}\n\"Linux-Mint\" {1ae66575-e681-4c44-9d71-ae4089cfad5d}\n";
        let vms = parse_vms(out);
        assert_eq!(vms.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(vms[0].name, "Kali-Linux");
        assert_eq!(vms[0].uuid, "b3d301da-f47e-45e3-865e-70f8e88ecd5a");
```
