`crates/orress-sandbox/src/vm.rs`:

```rs
//! Am I running inside a virtual machine? The execution guard refuses to run flagged samples on
//! a bare-metal host, so this needs to be reasonably reliable. The primary signal is the CPUID
//! hypervisor-present bit (and the hypervisor vendor string); file artifacts of common guest
//! additions and the firmware's SMBIOS/DMI system identity (Linux `/sys/class/dmi/id`, the
//! Windows registry's BIOS key) are secondary hints. The firmware identity is what tells a
//! genuine Hyper-V guest ("Virtual Machine" by Microsoft Corporation) apart from VBS on a
//! physical host, where CPUID alone reports "Microsoft Hv" either way.

#[cfg(windows)]
use std::path::Path;

/// What the VM check found.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct VmEvidence {
    /// The CPUID hypervisor-present bit was set.
    pub hypervisor: bool,
    /// The hypervisor vendor string (e.g. "VMwareVMware", "VBoxVBoxVBox", "Microsoft Hv").
    pub vendor: Option<String>,
    /// Secondary hints (guest-additions files, etc.).
    pub hints: Vec<String>,
}

impl VmEvidence {
    /// Whether this is a confident VM determination. A bare hypervisor bit is **not** enough on
    /// Windows: virtualization-based security reports vendor "Microsoft Hv" on physical hosts
    /// too, so we only trust an unambiguous guest hypervisor vendor or a guest-additions file.
    pub fn looks_like_vm(&self) -> bool {
        (self.hypervisor && self.vendor.as_deref().is_some_and(is_vm_vendor))
            || !self.hints.is_empty()
    }

    /// A hypervisor is present but the evidence is ambiguous (likely VBS on a physical host).
    pub fn ambiguous(&self) -> bool {
        self.hypervisor && !self.looks_like_vm()
    }
}

/// Whether the hypervisor vendor string names a guest VM (not host-side VBS).
fn is_vm_vendor(vendor: &str) -> bool {
    let v = vendor.to_ascii_lowercase();
    [
        "vmware",
        "vbox",
        "kvm",
        "xen",
        "qemu",
        "tcg",
        "prl",
        "bhyve",
        "virtualapple",
    ]
    .iter()
    .any(|m| v.contains(m))
}

/// Collects VM evidence.
pub fn detect() -> VmEvidence {
    let (hypervisor, vendor) = cpuid_hypervisor();
    let mut hints = file_hints();
    hints.extend(firmware_hint());
    VmEvidence {
        hypervisor,
        vendor,
        hints,
    }
}

/// Classifies the firmware's (SMBIOS/DMI) system identity — manufacturer, product name, and
/// board vendor — into a VM hint. Only unambiguous virtual-hardware identities count: in
/// particular Hyper-V is recognised solely by Microsoft's "Virtual Machine" product, so a
/// physical Microsoft device (a Surface) running virtualization-based security does not.
// Firmware identity is only read on Windows and Linux; elsewhere this is used by tests alone.
#[cfg_attr(not(any(windows, target_os = "linux")), allow(dead_code))]
fn classify_firmware(manufacturer: &str, product: &str, board_vendor: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let m = manufacturer.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    let p = product.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    let b = board_vendor.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    let any = |needle: &str| m.contains(needle) || p.contains(needle) || b.contains(needle);
    let name = if any("innotek") || any("virtualbox") {
        "VirtualBox"
    } else if any("vmware") {
        "VMware"
    } else if p.contains("kvm") || m == "kvm" {
        "KVM"
    } else if any("qemu") {
        "QEMU"
    } else if m == "xen" || p.contains("hvm domu") {
        "Xen"
    } else if any("parallels") {
        "Parallels"
    } else if m == "bochs" || p == "bochs" {
        "Bochs"
    } else if m == "microsoft corporation" && p == "virtual machine" {
        "Hyper-V"
    } else {
        return None;
    };
    Some(format!(
        "{name} virtual hardware (firmware reports \"{}\" / \"{}\")",
        manufacturer.trim(),
        product.trim()
    ))
}

/// Linux: the DMI identity the kernel exposes under `/sys/class/dmi/id`.
#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
fn firmware_hint() -> Option<String> {
    let read = |f: &str| {
        std::fs::read_to_string(format!("/sys/class/dmi/id/{f}"))
            .map(|s| s.trim().to_string())
            .unwrap_or_default()
    };
    classify_firmware(
        &read("sys_vendor"),
        &read("product_name"),
        &read("board_vendor"),
    )
}

/// Windows: the SMBIOS identity the OS caches in the registry under
/// `HKLM\HARDWARE\DESCRIPTION\System\BIOS` (read via `reg.exe` — no WMI, no FFI).
#[cfg(windows)]
fn firmware_hint() -> Option<String> {
    use std::os::windows::process::CommandExt;
    const CREATE_NO_WINDOW: u32 = 0x0800_0000;
    let root = std::env::var_os("SystemRoot").unwrap_or_else(|| r"C:\Windows".into());
    let reg = Path::new(&root).join(r"System32\reg.exe");
    let out = std::process::Command::new(reg)
        .args(["query", r"HKLM\HARDWARE\DESCRIPTION\System\BIOS"])
        .creation_flags(CREATE_NO_WINDOW)
        .stdin(std::process::Stdio::null())
        .stderr(std::process::Stdio::null())
        .output()
        .ok()?;
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout);
    let value = |name: &str| reg_value(&text, name).unwrap_or_default();
    classify_firmware(
        &value("SystemManufacturer"),
        &value("SystemProductName"),
        &value("BaseBoardManufacturer"),
    )
}

#[cfg(not(any(windows, target_os = "linux")))]
fn firmware_hint() -> Option<String> {
    None
}

/// Extracts a `REG_SZ` value from `reg query` output (`    Name    REG_SZ    Data`).
#[cfg(any(windows, test))]
fn reg_value(output: &str, name: &str) -> Option<String> {
    output.lines().find_map(|line| {
        let line = line.trim_start();
        let rest = line
            .strip_prefix(name)
            .filter(|r| r.starts_with(char::is_whitespace))?;
        let (_, data) = rest.trim_start().split_once("REG_SZ")?;
        Some(data.trim().to_string())
    })
}

/// Whether we appear to be *confidently* inside a VM (see [`VmEvidence::looks_like_vm`]).
pub fn in_vm() -> bool {
    detect().looks_like_vm()
}

#[cfg(any(target_arch = "x86", target_arch = "x86_64"))]
fn cpuid_hypervisor() -> (bool, Option<String>) {
    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86")]
    use core::arch::x86::__cpuid;
    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
    use core::arch::x86_64::__cpuid;

    // __cpuid only reads CPU identification registers (no side effects) and is callable safely
    // on the x86-64 baseline where CPUID is always present.
    let leaf1 = __cpuid(1);
    let present = (leaf1.ecx >> 31) & 1 == 1;
    if !present {
        return (false, None);
    }
    let v = __cpuid(0x4000_0000);
    let mut bytes = Vec::with_capacity(12);
    bytes.extend_from_slice(&v.ebx.to_le_bytes());
    bytes.extend_from_slice(&v.ecx.to_le_bytes());
    bytes.extend_from_slice(&v.edx.to_le_bytes());
    let vendor = String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes)
        .trim_matches(|c: char| c == '\0' || c.is_whitespace())
        .to_string();
    (true, (!vendor.is_empty()).then_some(vendor))
}

#[cfg(not(any(target_arch = "x86", target_arch = "x86_64")))]
fn cpuid_hypervisor() -> (bool, Option<String>) {
    (false, None)
}

#[cfg(windows)]
fn file_hints() -> Vec<String> {
    const FILES: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
        (r"C:\Windows\System32\drivers\vmmouse.sys", "VMware"),
        (r"C:\Windows\System32\drivers\vmhgfs.sys", "VMware"),
        (r"C:\Windows\System32\drivers\VBoxMouse.sys", "VirtualBox"),
        (r"C:\Windows\System32\drivers\VBoxGuest.sys", "VirtualBox"),
        (r"C:\Windows\System32\vboxservice.exe", "VirtualBox"),
        (r"C:\Windows\System32\drivers\vioscsi.sys", "QEMU/KVM"),
    ];
    FILES
        .iter()
        .filter(|(p, _)| Path::new(p).exists())
        .map(|(_, name)| format!("{name} guest file present"))
        .collect()
}

#[cfg(not(windows))]
fn file_hints() -> Vec<String> {
    Vec::new()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn microsoft_hv_alone_is_not_a_confirmed_vm() {
        let e = VmEvidence {
            hypervisor: true,
            vendor: Some("Microsoft Hv".into()),
            hints: Vec::new(),
        };
        assert!(
            !e.looks_like_vm(),
            "VBS on a physical host must not count as a VM"
        );
        assert!(e.ambiguous());
    }

    #[test]
    fn known_vm_vendor_counts() {
        let e = VmEvidence {
            hypervisor: true,
            vendor: Some("VMwareVMware".into()),
            hints: Vec::new(),
        };
        assert!(e.looks_like_vm());
        assert!(!e.ambiguous());
    }

    #[test]
    fn guest_files_count() {
        let e = VmEvidence {
            hypervisor: false,
            vendor: None,
            hints: vec!["VirtualBox guest file present".into()],
        };
        assert!(e.looks_like_vm());
    }

    #[test]
    fn firmware_identities_of_known_hypervisors() {
        let hit = |m, p, b| classify_firmware(m, p, b);
        assert!(
            hit("innotek GmbH", "VirtualBox", "Oracle Corporation")
                .unwrap()
                .starts_with("VirtualBox")
        );
        assert!(
            hit(
                "VMware, Inc.",
                "VMware Virtual Platform",
                "Intel Corporation"
            )
            .unwrap()
            .starts_with("VMware")
        );
        assert!(
            hit("VMware, Inc.", "VMware20,1", "")
                .unwrap()
                .starts_with("VMware")
        );
        assert!(
            hit("QEMU", "Standard PC (Q35 + ICH9, 2009)", "")
                .unwrap()
                .starts_with("QEMU")
        );
        assert!(hit("Red Hat", "KVM", "").unwrap().starts_with("KVM"));
        assert!(hit("Xen", "HVM domU", "").unwrap().starts_with("Xen"));
        assert!(
            hit(
                "Parallels Software International Inc.",
                "Parallels Virtual Platform",
                ""
            )
            .unwrap()
            .starts_with("Parallels")
        );
        assert!(
            hit(
                "Microsoft Corporation",
                "Virtual Machine",
                "Microsoft Corporation"
            )
            .unwrap()
            .starts_with("Hyper-V")
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn physical_machines_are_not_flagged() {
        // A Surface is Microsoft hardware but not a VM — VBS on it must stay ambiguous.
        assert_eq!(
            classify_firmware(
                "Microsoft Corporation",
                "Surface Pro 7",
                "Microsoft Corporation"
            ),
            None
        );
        assert_eq!(
            classify_firmware("Dell Inc.", "XPS 15 9520", "Dell Inc."),
            None
        );
        assert_eq!(classify_firmware("LENOVO", "20XW0026GE", "LENOVO"), None);
        assert_eq!(
            classify_firmware("ASUS", "System Product Name", "ASUSTeK COMPUTER INC."),
            None
        );
        assert_eq!(classify_firmware("", "", ""), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn hyper_v_guest_is_confirmed_by_firmware() {
        let e = VmEvidence {
            hypervisor: true,
            vendor: Some("Microsoft Hv".into()),
            hints: classify_firmware("Microsoft Corporation", "Virtual Machine", "")
                .into_iter()
                .collect(),
        };
        assert!(e.looks_like_vm());
        assert!(!e.ambiguous());
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_reg_query_output() {
        let out = "\r\nHKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\\HARDWARE\\DESCRIPTION\\System\\BIOS\r\n    \
                   BaseBoardManufacturer    REG_SZ    Microsoft Corporation\r\n    \
                   BiosMajorRelease    REG_DWORD    0x4\r\n    \
                   SystemManufacturer    REG_SZ    Microsoft Corporation\r\n    \
                   SystemProductName    REG_SZ    Virtual Machine\r\n";
        assert_eq!(
            reg_value(out, "SystemManufacturer").as_deref(),
            Some("Microsoft Corporation")
        );
        assert_eq!(
            reg_value(out, "SystemProductName").as_deref(),
            Some("Virtual Machine")
        );
        assert_eq!(reg_value(out, "BiosMajorRelease"), None);
        assert_eq!(reg_value(out, "Missing"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn detect_runs_without_panicking() {
        // We can't assert the value (depends where the test runs), only that it works.
        let e = detect();
        if e.hypervisor {
            // A vendor string is usually, but not always, present.
            let _ = &e.vendor;
        }
        let _ = in_vm();
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-script/src/exploit.rs`:

```rs
//! Exploit-mode scripting: the pwntools-style builtins (packing, cyclic patterns, shellcode
//! assembly, symbol/GOT/PLT lookups, ROP gadget search, and process/remote tubes) exposed to Rhai,
//! plus a worker-thread runner that streams `print` output to the UI and can be cancelled.
//!
//! Unlike the read-only analysis scripting in [`crate::run`], an exploit script blocks on I/O
//! (`recvuntil`, connecting to a remote), so [`run_exploit`] is meant to be called *on a worker
//! thread* — the Rhai engine (which is `!Send` under default features) is built and run entirely
//! inside the worker; only the owned, `Send` inputs cross the thread boundary.

use std::cell::RefCell;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::rc::Rc;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
use std::sync::mpsc::Sender;

use orress_arch::Isa;
use orress_pwn::cyclic::{DEFAULT_ALPHABET, DEFAULT_N};
use orress_pwn::{
    Gadget, Tube, cyclic, find_gadgets, find_one_gadgets, fmtstr_payload, pack, sigreturn_frame,
};
use rhai::{Array, Blob, Dynamic, Engine, EvalAltResult, ImmutableString, Map};

/// An owned, `Send` snapshot of the open binary that exploit builtins need.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct ExploitCtx {
    pub base: u64,
    pub isa: Isa,
    pub symbols: HashMap<String, u64>,
    pub got: HashMap<String, u64>,
    pub plt: HashMap<String, u64>,
    /// Executable sections as `(virtual base, bytes)`, for gadget search.
    pub exec: Vec<(u64, Vec<u8>)>,
    /// The address of the `"/bin/sh"` string, if present (for one_gadget search).
    pub binsh: Option<u64>,
    /// Section name -> virtual address (for ret2dlresolve: `.dynsym`/`.dynstr`/`.rela.plt`).
    pub sections: HashMap<String, u64>,
}

impl Default for ExploitCtx {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            base: 0,
            isa: Isa::X64,
            symbols: HashMap::new(),
            got: HashMap::new(),
            plt: HashMap::new(),
            exec: Vec::new(),
            binsh: None,
            sections: HashMap::new(),
        }
    }
}

/// Runs an exploit script to completion, streaming `print`/`debug` lines to `out`. Call on a
/// worker thread; set `cancel` to abort (checked between Rhai operations — a blocking `recv`
/// finishes its current timeout first).
pub fn run_exploit(
    src: &str,
    ctx: ExploitCtx,
    out: Sender<String>,
    cancel: Arc<AtomicBool>,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    let mut engine = Engine::new();
    engine.set_max_operations(0); // exploits legitimately loop; cancellation is via `cancel`
    engine.set_max_string_size(0);
    engine.set_max_array_size(0);

    let print_out = out.clone();
    engine.on_print(move |s| {
        let _ = print_out.send(format!("{s}\n"));
    });
    let dbg_out = out.clone();
    engine.on_debug(move |s, _, _| {
        let _ = dbg_out.send(format!("{s}\n"));
    });
    let stop = Arc::clone(&cancel);
    engine.on_progress(move |_| {
        if stop.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
            Some(Dynamic::UNIT)
        } else {
            None
        }
    });

    register(&mut engine, ctx);

    match engine.run(src) {
        Ok(()) => Ok(()),
        Err(e) if cancel.load(Ordering::Relaxed) => {
            let _ = out.send("[stopped]\n".into());
            let _ = e;
            Ok(())
        }
        Err(e) => Err(e.to_string()),
    }
}

/// A Rhai handle to a live tube (shared so methods can mutate it).
#[derive(Clone)]
struct TubeHandle(Rc<RefCell<Tube>>);

fn err(msg: impl Into<String>) -> Box<EvalAltResult> {
    msg.into().into()
}

/// Assembles amd64 source to bytes, mapping errors to a Rhai error.
fn assemble(src: &str) -> Result<Blob, Box<EvalAltResult>> {
    orress_asm::assemble(src, orress_asm::Arch::X64, 0)
        .map(|a| a.bytes)
        .map_err(|d| {
            err(d
                .first()
                .map(|x| format!("asm error: {}", x.message))
                .unwrap_or_else(|| "asm error".into()))
        })
}

/// Parses a `0x…` or decimal integer from a map key.
fn parse_u64(s: &str) -> Option<u64> {
    let s = s.trim();
    s.strip_prefix("0x")
        .or_else(|| s.strip_prefix("0X"))
        .map_or_else(|| s.parse().ok(), |h| u64::from_str_radix(h, 16).ok())
}

fn register(engine: &mut Engine, ctx: ExploitCtx) {
    let ctx = Rc::new(ctx);
    let gadgets: Rc<RefCell<Option<Vec<Gadget>>>> = Rc::new(RefCell::new(None));

    // --- packing ---
    engine.register_fn("p8", |v: i64| -> Blob { pack::p8(v as u64) });
    engine.register_fn("p16", |v: i64| -> Blob { pack::p16(v as u64) });
    engine.register_fn("p32", |v: i64| -> Blob { pack::p32(v as u64) });
    engine.register_fn("p64", |v: i64| -> Blob { pack::p64(v as u64) });
    engine.register_fn("u8", |b: Blob| -> i64 { pack::u8v(&b) as i64 });
    engine.register_fn("u16", |b: Blob| -> i64 { pack::u16v(&b) as i64 });
    engine.register_fn("u32", |b: Blob| -> i64 { pack::u32v(&b) as i64 });
    engine.register_fn("u64", |b: Blob| -> i64 { pack::u64v(&b) as i64 });
    engine.register_fn("flat", |arr: Array| -> Blob { flatten(arr) });

    // --- cyclic ---
    engine.register_fn("cyclic", |n: i64| -> Blob {
        cyclic::cyclic(n.max(0) as usize, DEFAULT_ALPHABET, DEFAULT_N)
    });
    engine.register_fn("cyclic_find", |v: i64| -> i64 {
        find_offset(&pack::p32(v as u64))
    });
    engine.register_fn("cyclic_find", |b: Blob| -> i64 { find_offset(&b) });

    // --- shellcode ---
    engine.register_fn("asm", |src: &str| -> Result<Blob, Box<EvalAltResult>> {
        assemble(src)
    });
    // execve("/bin/sh", 0, 0) shellcode (amd64, null-free).
    engine.register_fn("sh", || -> Result<Blob, Box<EvalAltResult>> {
        assemble(
            "xor rsi, rsi\npush rsi\nmov rdi, 0x68732f2f6e69622f\npush rdi\npush rsp\npop rdi\n\
             xor edx, edx\npush 0x3b\npop rax\nsyscall",
        )
    });

    // --- payload builders ---
    // fmtstr(offset, addr, value): a %hn format-string payload writing `value` to `addr`.
    engine.register_fn("fmtstr", |offset: i64, addr: i64, value: i64| -> Blob {
        fmtstr_payload(offset.max(0) as usize, &[(addr as u64, value as u64)])
    });
    // fmtstr(offset, #{ addr: value, ... }) for several writes at once.
    engine.register_fn("fmtstr", |offset: i64, writes: Map| -> Blob {
        let writes: Vec<(u64, u64)> = writes
            .into_iter()
            .filter_map(|(k, v)| Some((parse_u64(k.as_str())?, v.as_int().ok()? as u64)))
            .collect();
        fmtstr_payload(offset.max(0) as usize, &writes)
    });
    // srop(#{ rip:.., rsp:.., rdi:.. }): an x86-64 sigreturn frame.
    engine.register_fn("srop", |regs: Map| -> Blob {
        let regs: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, u64> = regs
            .into_iter()
            .filter_map(|(k, v)| Some((k.to_string(), v.as_int().ok()? as u64)))
            .collect();
        sigreturn_frame(&regs)
    });

    // --- bytes <-> text ---
    engine.register_fn("str", |b: Blob| -> String {
        String::from_utf8_lossy(&b).into_owned()
    });
    engine.register_fn("bytes", |s: &str| -> Blob { s.as_bytes().to_vec() });

    // --- hex ---
    engine.register_fn("hex", |b: Blob| -> String {
        b.iter().map(|x| format!("{x:02x}")).collect()
    });
    engine.register_fn("unhex", |s: &str| -> Blob {
        let s: String = s.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace()).collect();
        (0..s.len())
            .step_by(2)
            .filter_map(|i| u8::from_str_radix(s.get(i..i + 2)?, 16).ok())
            .collect()
    });

    // --- symbols / GOT / PLT / base ---
    let c = Rc::clone(&ctx);
    engine.register_fn("sym", move |name: &str| lookup(&c.symbols, name));
    let c = Rc::clone(&ctx);
    engine.register_fn("got", move |name: &str| lookup(&c.got, name));
    let c = Rc::clone(&ctx);
    engine.register_fn("plt", move |name: &str| lookup(&c.plt, name));
    let base = ctx.base;
    engine.register_fn("base", move || -> i64 { base as i64 });

    // --- ROP gadgets ---
    // ret2dlresolve(write_to, symbol): forge dl-resolve structures at write_to to resolve `symbol`.
    // Returns #{ reloc_index, payload }.
    let c = Rc::clone(&ctx);
    engine.register_fn(
        "ret2dlresolve",
        move |write_to: i64, symbol: &str| -> Result<rhai::Map, Box<EvalAltResult>> {
            let sec = |name: &str| c.sections.get(name).copied();
            let dynsym = sec(".dynsym").ok_or_else(|| err("no .dynsym section"))?;
            let dynstr = sec(".dynstr").ok_or_else(|| err("no .dynstr section"))?;
            let relaplt = sec(".rela.plt")
                .or_else(|| sec(".rel.plt"))
                .ok_or_else(|| err("no .rela.plt section"))?;
            let w = write_to as u64;
            let p = orress_pwn::ret2dlresolve::build(dynsym, dynstr, relaplt, w, w, symbol)
                .ok_or_else(|| {
                    err("could not build a ret2dlresolve payload for these addresses")
                })?;
            let mut m = rhai::Map::new();
            m.insert("reloc_index".into(), Dynamic::from(p.reloc_index as i64));
            m.insert("payload".into(), Dynamic::from(p.bytes));
            Ok(m)
        },
    );

    // ret2csu(call_ptr, a1, a2, a3, ret_after): a chain calling *call_ptr(a1,a2,a3) via the
    // __libc_csu_init universal gadget.
    let c = Rc::clone(&ctx);
    engine.register_fn(
        "ret2csu",
        move |call_ptr: i64,
              a1: i64,
              a2: i64,
              a3: i64,
              ret_after: i64|
              -> Result<Blob, Box<EvalAltResult>> {
            let secs: Vec<(u64, &[u8])> = c.exec.iter().map(|(a, b)| (*a, b.as_slice())).collect();
            let (pop6, mov_call) = orress_pwn::ret2csu::find_csu(&secs, c.isa)
                .ok_or_else(|| err("no __libc_csu_init ret2csu gadgets found in this binary"))?;
            Ok(orress_pwn::ret2csu::chain(
                pop6,
                mov_call,
                call_ptr as u64,
                [a1 as u64, a2 as u64, a3 as u64],
                ret_after as u64,
            ))
        },
    );

    // one_gadgets(): candidate one-shot execve("/bin/sh") gadget addresses in the open binary.
    let c = Rc::clone(&ctx);
    engine.register_fn("one_gadgets", move || -> Array {
        let Some(binsh) = c.binsh else {
            return Array::new();
        };
        let execve: Vec<u64> = ["execve", "system"]
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|n| c.symbols.get(*n).copied())
            .collect();
        let secs: Vec<(u64, &[u8])> = c.exec.iter().map(|(a, b)| (*a, b.as_slice())).collect();
        find_one_gadgets(&secs, binsh, &execve, c.isa)
            .into_iter()
            .map(|g| Dynamic::from(g.addr as i64))
            .collect()
    });

    let c = Rc::clone(&ctx);
    let cache = Rc::clone(&gadgets);
    engine.register_fn("find_gadget", move |q: &str| -> i64 {
        let mut slot = cache.borrow_mut();
        if slot.is_none() {
            let secs: Vec<(u64, &[u8])> = c.exec.iter().map(|(a, b)| (*a, b.as_slice())).collect();
            *slot = Some(find_gadgets(&secs, c.isa, 6));
        }
        let want = normalize(q);
        slot.as_ref()
            .unwrap()
            .iter()
            .find(|g| normalize(&g.text) == want)
            .map_or(-1, |g| g.addr as i64)
    });

    register_tubes(engine);
}

fn register_tubes(engine: &mut Engine) {
    engine.register_type_with_name::<TubeHandle>("Tube");

    engine.register_fn(
        "process",
        |path: &str| -> Result<TubeHandle, Box<EvalAltResult>> {
            make_tube(Tube::process(path, &[]))
        },
    );
    engine.register_fn(
        "process",
        |path: &str, args: Array| -> Result<TubeHandle, Box<EvalAltResult>> {
            let args: Vec<String> = args
                .into_iter()
                .map(|d| d.into_string().unwrap_or_default())
                .collect();
            make_tube(Tube::process(path, &args))
        },
    );
    engine.register_fn(
        "remote",
        |host: &str, port: i64| -> Result<TubeHandle, Box<EvalAltResult>> {
            make_tube(Tube::remote(host, port as u16))
        },
    );

    engine.register_fn("send", |t: &mut TubeHandle, data: Blob| send(t, &data));
    engine.register_fn("send", |t: &mut TubeHandle, data: &str| {
        send(t, data.as_bytes())
    });
    engine.register_fn("sendline", |t: &mut TubeHandle, data: Blob| {
        sendline(t, &data)
    });
    engine.register_fn("sendline", |t: &mut TubeHandle, data: &str| {
        sendline(t, data.as_bytes())
    });
    engine.register_fn("recv", |t: &mut TubeHandle, n: i64| -> Blob {
        t.0.borrow_mut().recv(n.max(0) as usize)
    });
    engine.register_fn("recvuntil", |t: &mut TubeHandle, d: Blob| -> Blob {
        t.0.borrow_mut().recvuntil(&d)
    });
    engine.register_fn("recvuntil", |t: &mut TubeHandle, d: &str| -> Blob {
        t.0.borrow_mut().recvuntil(d.as_bytes())
    });
    engine.register_fn("recvline", |t: &mut TubeHandle| -> Blob {
        t.0.borrow_mut().recvline()
    });
    engine.register_fn("recvall", |t: &mut TubeHandle| -> Blob {
        t.0.borrow_mut().recvall()
    });
    engine.register_fn("set_timeout", |t: &mut TubeHandle, s: f64| {
        t.0.borrow_mut().set_timeout(s)
    });
    engine.register_fn("close", |t: &mut TubeHandle| t.0.borrow_mut().close());
}

fn make_tube(r: std::io::Result<Tube>) -> Result<TubeHandle, Box<EvalAltResult>> {
    r.map(|t| TubeHandle(Rc::new(RefCell::new(t))))
        .map_err(|e| err(e.to_string()))
}

fn send(t: &mut TubeHandle, data: &[u8]) -> Result<(), Box<EvalAltResult>> {
    t.0.borrow_mut().send(data).map_err(|e| err(e.to_string()))
}

fn sendline(t: &mut TubeHandle, data: &[u8]) -> Result<(), Box<EvalAltResult>> {
    t.0.borrow_mut()
        .sendline(data)
        .map_err(|e| err(e.to_string()))
}

fn lookup(map: &HashMap<String, u64>, name: &str) -> Result<i64, Box<EvalAltResult>> {
    map.get(name)
        .map(|&a| a as i64)
        .ok_or_else(|| err(format!("unknown name: {name}")))
}

fn find_offset(window: &[u8]) -> i64 {
    cyclic::cyclic_find(window, DEFAULT_ALPHABET, DEFAULT_N).map_or(-1, |o| o as i64)
}

/// Concatenates an array of blobs, strings and integers (each int becomes one byte).
fn flatten(arr: Array) -> Blob {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for d in arr {
        if let Some(b) = d.clone().try_cast::<Blob>() {
            out.extend_from_slice(&b);
        } else if let Some(s) = d.clone().try_cast::<ImmutableString>() {
            out.extend_from_slice(s.as_bytes());
        } else if let Ok(i) = d.as_int() {
            out.push(i as u8);
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Normalises gadget text so `"pop rdi ; ret"` matches regardless of spacing around separators.
fn normalize(text: &str) -> String {
    text.split([';', ' ', '\t'])
        .filter(|p| !p.is_empty())
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join(" ")
}

        "#;
        let (out, res) = run(src, ExploitCtx::default());
        assert!(res.is_ok(), "{res:?}");
        assert!(out.contains("4847464544434241"), "out: {out}");

    }

        "#;
        let (out, res) = run(src, ExploitCtx::default());
        assert!(res.is_ok(), "{res:?}");
        assert!(out.contains("srop=248"), "srop frame length; out: {out}");

        ctx.sections.insert(".rela.plt".into(), 0x400460);
        let (out, res) = run(
            r#"let r = ret2dlresolve(0x601000, "system"); print("idx=" + r.reloc_index + " len=" + r.payload.len());"#,
            ctx,
        );
        assert!(res.is_ok(), "{res:?}");
        assert!(out.contains("idx=") && out.contains("len="), "out: {out}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn remote_tube_through_rhai() {
        use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader, Write};
        use std::net::TcpListener;
        let listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").unwrap();
        let port = listener.local_addr().unwrap().port();
        let server = std::thread::spawn(move || {
            let (stream, _) = listener.accept().unwrap();
            let mut reader = BufReader::new(stream.try_clone().unwrap());
            let mut w = stream;
            w.write_all(b"> ").unwrap();
            let mut line = String::new();
            reader.read_line(&mut line).unwrap();
            w.write_all(format!("hi {line}").as_bytes()).unwrap();
        });
        let src = format!(

            io.recvuntil("> ");
            io.sendline("bob");
            print(str(io.recvline()));
        "#
        );
        let (out, res) = run(&src, ExploitCtx::default());
        assert!(res.is_ok(), "{res:?}");
        assert!(out.contains("hi bob"), "out: {out}");
        server.join().unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn sym_lookup_and_find_gadget() {
        let mut ctx = ExploitCtx::default();
        ctx.symbols.insert("main".into(), 0x401136);
        // a `pop rdi ; ret` blob at base 0x401000
        let bytes = orress_asm::assemble("pop rdi\nret", orress_asm::Arch::X64, 0)
            .unwrap()
            .bytes;
        ctx.exec.push((0x401000, bytes));
        let (out, res) = run(
            r#"print(sym("main")); print(find_gadget("pop rdi ; ret"));"#,
            ctx,
        );
        assert!(res.is_ok(), "{res:?}");
        assert!(out.contains(&0x401136.to_string()), "out: {out}");
        assert!(
            out.contains(&0x401000.to_string()),
            "gadget addr; out: {out}"
        );
    }
```

`crates/orress-script/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! Scripting for ORRESS: a sandboxed, pure-Rust [Rhai](https://rhai.rs) engine that exposes the
//! analysis of the open binary to a script, so analysts (and third-party extensions) can automate
//! queries and transforms without recompiling — "iterate every function, flag the ones that call
//! `strcpy`", "dump the bytes at this address", "disassemble the entry point", etc.
//!
//! The engine is read-only over an owned snapshot of the analysis and is bounded (operation,
//! recursion, string and array limits) so a runaway or hostile script cannot hang or exhaust the
//! UI. It links no C and uses no `unsafe`. PyO3/CPython embedding is intentionally *not* used — it
//! is a C dependency, which this project avoids; Rhai (and the WASM-component extension host in
//! `orress-ext`) cover scripting and extensibility in pure Rust.

#![allow(
    clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
    clippy::cast_possible_wrap,
    clippy::cast_sign_loss
)]

use std::cell::RefCell;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::rc::Rc;

use orress_analysis::{Memory, Program};
use orress_arch::Isa;
use rhai::{Array, Dynamic, Engine};

pub mod exploit;
pub use exploit::{ExploitCtx, run_exploit};

/// An owned, read-only snapshot of the analysis the script queries.
struct Ctx {
    memory: Memory,
    isa: Isa,
    /// (entry, name, block count) per function, in address order.
    funcs: Vec<(u64, String, i64)>,
    names: HashMap<u64, String>,
    strings: Vec<String>,
}

impl Ctx {
    fn new(p: &Program, strings: &[&str]) -> Self {
        let funcs = p
            .functions
            .iter()
            .map(|(&e, f)| {
                let name = p
                    .name(e)
                    .map_or_else(|| format!("sub_{e:x}"), |n| n.text.clone());
                (e, name, f.blocks.len() as i64)
            })
            .collect();
        let names = p.names.iter().map(|(&a, n)| (a, n.text.clone())).collect();
        Self {
            memory: p.memory.clone(),
            isa: p.isa,
            funcs,
            names,
            strings: strings.iter().map(|s| (*s).to_string()).collect(),
        }
    }

    fn disasm(&self, mut addr: u64, count: usize) -> String {
        let mut out = String::new();
        for _ in 0..count.min(4096) {
            let Some(bytes) = self.memory.read(addr, 16) else {
                break;
            };
            let Some(ins) = orress_arch::decode(self.isa, bytes, addr) else {
                break;
            };
            out.push_str(&format!("{addr:#x}: {}\n", ins.text()));
            if ins.len == 0 {
                break;
            }
            addr += u64::from(ins.len);
        }
        out
    }
}

/// Runs `src` against the analysis of `program` (with the recovered `strings`), returning whatever
/// the script printed followed by its final value. Errors carry the Rhai diagnostic.
pub fn run(src: &str, program: &Program, strings: &[&str]) -> Result<String, String> {
    let ctx = Rc::new(Ctx::new(program, strings));
    let out = Rc::new(RefCell::new(String::new()));
    let mut engine = Engine::new();
    // Bound a runaway or hostile script so it can never hang or exhaust the UI.
    engine.set_max_operations(5_000_000);
    engine.set_max_call_levels(64);
    engine.set_max_string_size(2_000_000);
    engine.set_max_array_size(2_000_000);

    let line = out.clone();
    engine.on_print(move |s| {
        let mut b = line.borrow_mut();
        b.push_str(s);
        b.push('\n');
    });
    let dbg = out.clone();
    engine.on_debug(move |s, _, _| {
        let mut b = dbg.borrow_mut();
        b.push_str(s);
        b.push('\n');
    });

    register(&mut engine, &ctx);

    let result = engine.eval::<Dynamic>(src).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let mut text = out.borrow().clone();
    if !result.is_unit() {
        text.push_str(&result.to_string());
    }
    Ok(text)
}

/// Registers the read-only analysis API on the engine.
fn register(engine: &mut Engine, ctx: &Rc<Ctx>) {
    let c = ctx.clone();
    engine.register_fn("function_count", move || c.funcs.len() as i64);

    let c = ctx.clone();
    engine.register_fn("functions", move || {
        c.funcs
            .iter()
            .map(|f| Dynamic::from(f.0 as i64))
            .collect::<Array>()
    });

    let c = ctx.clone();
    engine.register_fn("func_name", move |addr: i64| {
        c.funcs
            .iter()
            .find(|f| f.0 == addr as u64)
            .map_or_else(String::new, |f| f.1.clone())
    });

    let c = ctx.clone();
    engine.register_fn("func_blocks", move |addr: i64| {
        c.funcs
            .iter()
            .find(|f| f.0 == addr as u64)
            .map_or(0, |f| f.2)
    });

    let c = ctx.clone();
    engine.register_fn("name", move |addr: i64| {
        c.names.get(&(addr as u64)).cloned().unwrap_or_default()
    });

    let c = ctx.clone();
    engine.register_fn("strings", move || {
        c.strings
            .iter()
            .map(|s| Dynamic::from(s.clone()))
            .collect::<Array>()
    });

    let c = ctx.clone();
    engine.register_fn("string_count", move || c.strings.len() as i64);

    let c = ctx.clone();
    engine.register_fn("read", move |addr: i64, len: i64| {
        let bytes = c
            .memory
            .read(addr as u64, len.max(0) as usize)
            .unwrap_or(&[]);
        bytes
            .iter()
            .map(|&b| Dynamic::from(i64::from(b)))
            .collect::<Array>()
    });

    let c = ctx.clone();
    engine.register_fn("disasm", move |addr: i64, count: i64| {
        c.disasm(addr as u64, count.max(0) as usize)
    });
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use orress_loaders::{BinaryInfo, Format, Kind, Perms, Section};
    use std::sync::Arc;

    /// A tiny one-function x86-64 program: `xor eax,eax; ret` at 0x1000.
    fn tiny_program() -> Program {
        let base = 0x1000u64;
        let mut file = vec![0u8; 0x200];
        file.extend_from_slice(&[0x31, 0xC0, 0xC3]); // xor eax,eax ; ret
        let info = BinaryInfo {
            format: Format::Elf,
            kind: Kind::Executable,
            arch: "x86-64".into(),
            bits: Some(64),
            entry: Some(base),
            image_base: 0,
            sections: vec![Section {
                name: ".text".into(),
                offset: 0x200,
                file_size: 3,
                address: base,
                virtual_size: 3,
                perms: Perms {
                    read: true,
                    write: false,
                    execute: true,
                },
                entropy: None,
            }],
            ..BinaryInfo::default()
        };
        Program::analyze(&info, Arc::new(file), &[]).expect("analyze")
    }

    #[test]
    fn evaluates_and_captures_output() {
        let p = tiny_program();
        let out = run("print(\"hi\"); 1 + 2", &p, &[]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out, "hi\n3");
    }

    #[test]
    fn exposes_functions_and_bytes() {
        let p = tiny_program();
        // One function was discovered at the entry.
        assert_eq!(run("function_count()", &p, &[]).unwrap(), "1");
        // Its first two bytes are the `xor eax,eax` opcode 0x31 0xc0.
        let out = run("let b = read(0x1000, 2); b[0] + \", \" + b[1]", &p, &[]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out, "49, 192");
        // And it disassembles.
        let dis = run("disasm(0x1000, 2)", &p, &[]).unwrap();
        assert!(dis.contains("xor") && dis.contains("ret"), "disasm: {dis}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn exposes_strings() {
        let p = tiny_program();
        let out = run(
            "strings()[0] + \"/\" + string_count()",
            &p,
            &["hello", "world"],
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out, "hello/2");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_runaway_loop_is_bounded_not_hung() {
        let p = tiny_program();
        // An infinite loop must terminate with an error (operation budget), never hang.
        let err = run("let i = 0; loop { i += 1; }", &p, &[]).unwrap_err();
        assert!(
            err.to_lowercase().contains("operation"),
            "expected a budget error, got: {err}"
        );
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-settings/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! User settings, stored as `settings.json` in the platform config directory
//! (on Windows: `%APPDATA%\okiedocus\ORRESS\config\`). A user keymap sits next to it
//! as `keymap.json`, and custom themes go in `themes/*.json`.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use anyhow::Context as _;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct Settings {
    /// Name of the active theme.
    pub theme: String,
    /// UI zoom factor (1.0 = 100%).
    pub ui_scale: f32,
    /// Explain Mode: plain-language tooltips on everything. On by default, because
    /// ORRESS is meant to teach.
    pub explain_mode: bool,
    /// Last opened files, newest first.
    pub recent_files: Vec<PathBuf>,
    /// The open project folder (Zed-style), if any. Restored on startup so the folder tree
    /// reappears. `None` when no folder is open.
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub project_root: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// Per-language-server configuration, keyed by server name/id. Mirrors Zed's `lsp` settings
    /// section, so it both configures ORRESS's own LSP client and is handed to Zed language
    /// extensions (via `get-settings`) when they resolve a server. Empty by default.
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")]
    pub lsp: BTreeMap<String, LspServerSettings>,
}

impl Default for Settings {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            theme: "ORRESS Dark".into(),
            ui_scale: 1.0,
            explain_mode: true,
            recent_files: Vec::new(),
            project_root: None,
            lsp: BTreeMap::new(),
        }
    }
}

/// Per-server LSP configuration, in the same shape Zed uses for `lsp.<server>`: a binary override,
/// server settings (LSP workspace configuration) and initialization options.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct LspServerSettings {
    /// Override the server binary (path / arguments / environment).
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub binary: Option<LspBinarySettings>,
    /// Server-specific settings (sent as the LSP workspace configuration).
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub settings: Option<serde_json::Value>,
    /// The LSP `initializationOptions`.
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub initialization_options: Option<serde_json::Value>,
}

/// A language-server binary override (Zed's `lsp.<server>.binary`).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct LspBinarySettings {
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub path: Option<String>,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub arguments: Option<Vec<String>>,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub env: Option<BTreeMap<String, String>>,
}

const MAX_RECENT: usize = 10;

impl Settings {
    pub const MIN_SCALE: f32 = 0.5;
    pub const MAX_SCALE: f32 = 3.0;

    pub fn from_json(json: &str) -> anyhow::Result<Self> {
        let mut s: Self = serde_json::from_str(json).context("parsing settings.json")?;
        s.ui_scale = s.ui_scale.clamp(Self::MIN_SCALE, Self::MAX_SCALE);
        Ok(s)
    }

    pub fn to_json(&self) -> String {
        serde_json::to_string_pretty(self).expect("settings serialize")
    }

    /// Loads settings from `path`. A missing file gives defaults; a broken file gives
    /// defaults plus the error, so the app still starts and can tell the user.
    pub fn load(path: &Path) -> (Self, Option<anyhow::Error>) {
        match std::fs::read_to_string(path) {
            Ok(json) => match Self::from_json(&json) {
                Ok(s) => (s, None),
                Err(e) => (Self::default(), Some(e)),
            },
            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => (Self::default(), None),
            Err(e) => (
                Self::default(),
                Some(anyhow::Error::new(e).context(format!("reading {}", path.display()))),
            ),
        }
    }

    pub fn save(&self, path: &Path) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        if let Some(dir) = path.parent() {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(dir).with_context(|| format!("creating {}", dir.display()))?;
        }
        std::fs::write(path, self.to_json()).with_context(|| format!("writing {}", path.display()))
    }

    pub fn push_recent(&mut self, path: PathBuf) {
        self.recent_files.retain(|p| p != &path);
        self.recent_files.insert(0, path);
        self.recent_files.truncate(MAX_RECENT);
    }

    /// The editor settings in the JSON shape a Zed language extension reads via `get-settings`:
    /// `{ "lsp": { "<server>": { "binary": {…}, "settings": {…}, "initialization_options": {…} } } }`.
    /// Handed to the extension host so extensions honour the user's configured server binary,
    /// settings and initialization options (category `"lsp"`, key = the language-server name).
    pub fn zed_extension_settings(&self) -> serde_json::Value {
        serde_json::json!({ "lsp": self.lsp })
    }
}

/// Where ORRESS keeps its configuration files.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Paths {
    pub config_dir: PathBuf,
}

impl Paths {
    pub fn from_platform() -> Option<Self> {
        let dirs = directories::ProjectDirs::from("nl", "okiedocus", "ORRESS")?;
        Some(Self {
            config_dir: dirs.config_dir().to_path_buf(),
        })
    }

    pub fn settings_file(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.config_dir.join("settings.json")
    }

    pub fn keymap_file(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.config_dir.join("keymap.json")
    }

    pub fn themes_dir(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.config_dir.join("themes")
    }

    /// Imported language-server adapter manifests (`*.json`).
    pub fn lsp_dir(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.config_dir.join("lsp")
    }

    /// Installed extensions, one directory each (with an `extension.toml`).
    pub fn extensions_dir(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.config_dir.join("extensions")
    }

    /// Saved annotations (names, comments, bookmarks), one file per analyzed binary.
    pub fn projects_dir(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.config_dir.join("projects")
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn partial_json_fills_defaults_and_clamps() {
        let s = Settings::from_json(r#"{ "ui_scale": 9.0, "explain_mode": false }"#).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(s.ui_scale, Settings::MAX_SCALE);
        assert!(!s.explain_mode);
        assert_eq!(s.theme, "ORRESS Dark");
    }

    #[test]
    fn lsp_settings_round_trip_to_zed_shape() {
        // A user configures one server's binary + init options in settings.json.
        let s = Settings::from_json(
            r#"{ "lsp": { "rust-analyzer": {
                "binary": { "path": "/opt/ra", "arguments": ["--stdio"] },
                "initialization_options": { "cargo": { "allFeatures": true } }
            } } }"#,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let ra = s.lsp.get("rust-analyzer").expect("server configured");
        assert_eq!(ra.binary.as_ref().unwrap().path.as_deref(), Some("/opt/ra"));

        // zed_extension_settings() nests it under "lsp" exactly as a Zed extension reads it: the
        // section at ["lsp"]["rust-analyzer"] carries the binary and init options, and `None`
        // fields (here `settings`) are omitted rather than serialized as null.
        let zed = s.zed_extension_settings();
        let server = &zed["lsp"]["rust-analyzer"];
        assert_eq!(server["binary"]["path"], "/opt/ra");
        assert_eq!(server["binary"]["arguments"][0], "--stdio");
        assert_eq!(
            server["initialization_options"]["cargo"]["allFeatures"],
            true
        );
        assert!(server.get("settings").is_none());

        // No LSP config → an empty `lsp` object (extensions tolerate the absence of a server key).
        assert_eq!(
            Settings::default().zed_extension_settings(),
            serde_json::json!({ "lsp": {} })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn save_and_load_round_trip() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("orress-settings-test-{}", std::process::id()));
        let path = dir.join("settings.json");
        let s = Settings {
            theme: "High Contrast".into(),
            ..Settings::default()
        };
        s.save(&path).unwrap();
        let (loaded, err) = Settings::load(&path);
        assert!(err.is_none());
        assert_eq!(loaded, s);
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(dir).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn broken_file_gives_defaults_and_error() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("orress-settings-bad-{}", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        let path = dir.join("settings.json");
        std::fs::write(&path, "{ not json").unwrap();
        let (s, err) = Settings::load(&path);
        assert_eq!(s, Settings::default());
        assert!(err.is_some());
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(dir).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn recent_files_dedupe_and_cap() {
        let mut s = Settings::default();
        for i in 0..15 {
            s.push_recent(PathBuf::from(format!("f{i}")));
        }
        s.push_recent(PathBuf::from("f10"));
        assert_eq!(s.recent_files.len(), MAX_RECENT);
        assert_eq!(s.recent_files[0], PathBuf::from("f10"));
        assert_eq!(
            s.recent_files
                .iter()
                .filter(|p| p.as_os_str() == "f10")
                .count(),
            1
        );
    }
}
```

```rs
//! x86 condition codes shared by the Jcc / SETcc families.

use iced_x86::Mnemonic;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Cc {
    O,
    No,
    B,
    Ae,
    E,
    Ne,
    Be,
    A,
    S,
    Ns,
    P,
    Np,
    L,
    Ge,
    Le,
    G,
}

pub fn jcc(m: Mnemonic) -> Option<Cc> {
    use Mnemonic as M;
    Some(match m {
        M::Jo => Cc::O,
        M::Jno => Cc::No,
        M::Jb => Cc::B,
        M::Jae => Cc::Ae,
        M::Je => Cc::E,
        M::Jne => Cc::Ne,
        M::Jbe => Cc::Be,
        M::Ja => Cc::A,
        M::Js => Cc::S,
        M::Jns => Cc::Ns,
        M::Jp => Cc::P,
        M::Jnp => Cc::Np,
        M::Jl => Cc::L,
        M::Jge => Cc::Ge,
        M::Jle => Cc::Le,
        M::Jg => Cc::G,
        _ => return None,
    })
}

pub fn setcc(m: Mnemonic) -> Option<Cc> {
    use Mnemonic as M;
    Some(match m {
        M::Seto => Cc::O,
        M::Setno => Cc::No,
        M::Setb => Cc::B,
        M::Setae => Cc::Ae,
        M::Sete => Cc::E,
        M::Setne => Cc::Ne,
        M::Setbe => Cc::Be,
        M::Seta => Cc::A,
        M::Sets => Cc::S,
        M::Setns => Cc::Ns,
        M::Setp => Cc::P,
        M::Setnp => Cc::Np,
        M::Setl => Cc::L,
        M::Setge => Cc::Ge,
        M::Setle => Cc::Le,
        M::Setg => Cc::G,
        _ => return None,
    })
}
```
