```rs
#[test]
fn recovers_memcmp_check_input() {
    // check(ptr) { return memcmp(ptr, target, len) == 0 }  — memcmp is a symbolic stub.
    const MEMCMP: u64 = 0xa000;
    let target = b"passw0rd";
    let mut a = CodeAssembler::new(64).unwrap();
    let mut fail_l = a.create_label();
    a.mov(rsi, TARGET_ADDR).unwrap();
    a.mov(edx, target.len() as i32).unwrap();
    a.call(MEMCMP).unwrap();
    a.test(eax, eax).unwrap();
    a.jne(fail_l).unwrap();
    a.mov(eax, 1).unwrap();
    a.ret().unwrap();
    a.set_label(&mut fail_l).unwrap();
    a.xor(eax, eax).unwrap();
    a.ret().unwrap();
    let code = a.assemble(BASE).unwrap();
    let fail = fail_addr(&code);

    let mut mem = Memory::new();
    mem.write_bytes(BASE, &code);
    mem.write_bytes(TARGET_ADDR, target);

    let mut hooks = std::collections::HashMap::new();
    hooks.insert(MEMCMP, orress_emu::Stub::Memcmp);
    let found = solve_check(
        mem,
        BASE,
        &[INPUT],
        INPUT,
        target.len() as u32,
        0,
        vec![fail],
        hooks,
        orress_sym::Abi::SysV,
    )
    .unwrap();
    assert!(
        found.result.complete,
        "incomplete: {}",
        found.result.message
    );
    assert_eq!(found.result.input, target);
}

#[test]
fn solver_handles_coupled_bytes() {
    // b0 + b1 == 0x90 and b0 == 0x30  →  b0=0x30, b1=0x60.
    let c0 = expr::rel(expr::Rel::Eq, expr::var(0), expr::konst(0x30, 8));
    let sum = expr::bin(expr::Op::Add, expr::var(0), expr::var(1));
    let c1 = expr::rel(expr::Rel::Eq, sum, expr::konst(0x90, 8));
    let r = solve(&[c0, c1], 2);
    assert!(r.complete, "{}", r.message);
    assert_eq!(r.input, vec![0x30, 0x60]);
}

#[test]
fn exports_smt2() {
    let c = expr::rel(
        expr::Rel::Eq,
        expr::bin(expr::Op::Xor, expr::var(0), expr::konst(0x5a, 8)),
        expr::konst(0x11, 8),
    );
    let smt = expr::to_smt2(&[c], 1);
    assert!(smt.contains("declare-const b0 (_ BitVec 8)"));
    assert!(smt.contains("bvxor"));
    assert!(smt.contains("check-sat"));
}

#[test]
fn simplify_preserves_value() {
    // The display simplifier must be value-preserving. Differential-test it against eval over the
    // whole single-byte input space on the noisy width-juggling the executor emits and on a rotate.
    use orress_sym::expr::{self, Op};
    let x = expr::var(0);
    let noisy = expr::extract(
        expr::zext(
            expr::bin(Op::Xor, expr::zext(x.clone(), 32), expr::konst(0x3b, 32)),
            64,
        ),
        7,
        0,
    );
    let core = expr::bin(Op::Xor, x.clone(), expr::konst(0x3b, 8));
    let rol = expr::bin(
        Op::Or,
        expr::bin(Op::Shl, core.clone(), expr::konst(1, 8)),
        expr::bin(Op::Lshr, core, expr::konst(7, 8)),
    );
    for e in [&noisy, &rol] {
        let s = expr::simplify(e);
        for b in 0u16..=255 {
            assert_eq!(
                e.eval(&[b as u8]),
                s.eval(&[b as u8]),
                "simplify changed value at {b}"
            );
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn renders_lifted_check_readably() {
    // The payoff: the captured constraint renders as the readable per-byte check, rotate and all.
    use orress_sym::expr::{self, Op, Rel};
    let x = expr::var(0);
    let core = expr::bin(Op::Xor, x, expr::konst(0x3b, 8));
    let rol = expr::bin(
        Op::Or,
        expr::bin(Op::Shl, core.clone(), expr::konst(1, 8)),
        expr::bin(Op::Lshr, core, expr::konst(7, 8)),
    );
    let check = expr::rel(Rel::Eq, rol, expr::konst(0x9a, 8));
    assert_eq!(
        expr::render(&expr::simplify(&check)),
        "rol((in[0] ^ 0x3b), 1) == 0x9a"
    );
}

// --- audit regression tests (flags, unmodelled instructions, stubs, memory) ----

use orress_sym::{SymError, SymExec};

/// Assembles `body` (which reads the input byte at [rdi] and sets flags) followed by `jcc fail`,
/// a pass block (`mov eax, 1; ret`) and the fail block (`xor eax, eax; ret`, the last 3 bytes).
fn flag_check(
    body: impl FnOnce(&mut CodeAssembler),
    jcc: impl FnOnce(&mut CodeAssembler, CodeLabel),
) -> (Vec<u8>, u64) {
    let mut a = CodeAssembler::new(64).unwrap();
    let fail_l = a.create_label();
    body(&mut a);
    jcc(&mut a, fail_l);
    finish(a, fail_l)
}

/// Appends the pass block and the fail block (the last 3 bytes) and assembles.
fn finish(mut a: CodeAssembler, mut fail_l: CodeLabel) -> (Vec<u8>, u64) {
    a.mov(eax, 1).unwrap();
    a.ret().unwrap();
    a.set_label(&mut fail_l).unwrap();
    a.xor(eax, eax).unwrap();
    a.ret().unwrap();
    let code = a.assemble(BASE).unwrap();
    let fail = BASE + code.len() as u64 - 3;
    (code, fail)
}

/// Runs a check symbolically (input at INPUT, `len` bytes), returning the executor.
fn run_sym(
    code: &[u8],
    fail: u64,
    len: u32,
    hooks: std::collections::HashMap<u64, orress_emu::Stub>,
    abi: orress_emu::Abi,
    extra: impl FnOnce(&mut Memory),
) -> Result<SymExec, SymError> {
    let mut mem = Memory::new();
    mem.write_bytes(BASE, code);
    extra(&mut mem);
    let mut sx = SymExec::new(mem, INPUT, len, 0, vec![fail]);
    sx.set_hooks(hooks);
    sx.run_check(BASE, &[INPUT, u64::from(len)], abi)?;
    Ok(sx)
}

/// Runs the check symbolically over a 1-byte input, then compares the captured constraints with
/// the concrete emulator for every byte value: the constraints must hold exactly for the inputs
/// that really pass. (Before, CF/OF after add/inc/dec/shl were constants, L/G ignored OF, and
/// O/P were always false.)
fn assert_exact(name: &str, (code, fail): (Vec<u8>, u64)) {
    use orress_emu::{Abi, Emulator};
    let sym = run_sym(&code, fail, 1, Default::default(), Abi::SysV, |_| {});
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.map(BASE, &code);
    for b in 0u16..=255 {
        let b = b as u8;
        emu.map(INPUT, &[b, 0]);
        let passes = emu.call(BASE, &[INPUT, 1], Abi::SysV).unwrap() == 1;
        let predicted = match &sym {
            Ok(sx) => sx.constraints.iter().all(|c| c.eval(&[b]) != 0),
            // Execution was forced into the avoided block: nothing passes.
            Err(SymError::HitAvoid(_)) => false,
            Err(e) => panic!("{name}: symbolic run failed: {e}"),
        };
        assert_eq!(predicted, passes, "{name}: input byte {b:#04x}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn branch_conditions_match_the_cpu_exactly() {
    let load = |a: &mut CodeAssembler| a.movzx(eax, byte_ptr(rdi)).unwrap();
    assert_exact(
        "add/jb",
        flag_check(
            |a| {
                load(a);
                a.add(al, 0xf0u32 as i32).unwrap();
            },
            |a, l| a.jb(l).unwrap(),
        ),
    );
    assert_exact(
        "add/jl",
        flag_check(
            |a| {
                load(a);
                a.add(al, 0x40).unwrap();
            },
            |a, l| a.jl(l).unwrap(),
        ),
    );
    assert_exact(
        "add/jo",
        flag_check(
            |a| {
                load(a);
                a.add(al, 0x40).unwrap();
            },
            |a, l| a.jo(l).unwrap(),
        ),
    );
    assert_exact(
        "add/ja",
        flag_check(
            |a| {
                load(a);
                a.add(al, 0x30).unwrap();
            },
            |a, l| a.ja(l).unwrap(),
        ),
    );
    assert_exact(
        "xor/jp",
        flag_check(
            |a| {
                load(a);
                a.xor(al, 0x5a).unwrap();
            },
            |a, l| a.jp(l).unwrap(),
        ),
    );
    assert_exact(
        "cmp/jo",
        flag_check(
            |a| {
                load(a);
                a.cmp(al, 0x30).unwrap();
            },
            |a, l| a.jo(l).unwrap(),
        ),
    );
    assert_exact(
        "cmp/jnp",
        flag_check(
            |a| {
                load(a);
                a.cmp(al, 0x30).unwrap();
            },
            |a, l| a.jnp(l).unwrap(),
        ),
    );
    assert_exact(
        "inc/jle",
        flag_check(
            |a| {
                load(a);
                a.inc(al).unwrap();
            },
            |a, l| a.jle(l).unwrap(),
        ),
    );
    assert_exact(
        "dec/jo",
        flag_check(
            |a| {
                load(a);
                a.dec(al).unwrap();
            },
            |a, l| a.jo(l).unwrap(),
        ),
    );
    // INC preserves the carry from the preceding CMP.
    assert_exact(
        "cmp+inc/jb",
        flag_check(
            |a| {
                load(a);
                a.cmp(al, 0x50).unwrap();
                a.inc(ecx).unwrap();
            },
            |a, l| a.jb(l).unwrap(),
        ),
    );
    assert_exact(
        "neg/jb",
        flag_check(
            |a| {
                load(a);
                a.neg(al).unwrap();
            },
            |a, l| a.jb(l).unwrap(),
        ),
    );
    assert_exact(
        "shl1/jb",
        flag_check(
            |a| {
                load(a);
                a.shl(al, 1).unwrap();
            },
            |a, l| a.jb(l).unwrap(),
        ),
    );
    assert_exact(
        "shl1/jo",
        flag_check(
            |a| {
                load(a);
                a.shl(al, 1).unwrap();
            },
            |a, l| a.jo(l).unwrap(),
        ),
    );
    assert_exact(
        "shr3/jb",
        flag_check(
            |a| {
                load(a);
                a.shr(al, 3).unwrap();
            },
            |a, l| a.jb(l).unwrap(),
        ),
    );
    // A shift by (masked) zero leaves the CMP's flags in place.
    assert_exact(
        "cmp+shl0/jb",
        flag_check(
            |a| {
                load(a);
                a.mov(ecx, 0x20).unwrap(); // masks to 0 for a 32-bit shift
                a.cmp(al, 0x50).unwrap();
                a.shl(edx, cl).unwrap();
            },
            |a, l| a.jb(l).unwrap(),
        ),
    );
}

/// A branch on flags the executor doesn't know is an error, not a guess: on entry (no flag
/// setter yet), after an unmodelled flag writer (`bt`), and on OF after a multi-bit shift.
#[test]
fn unknown_flags_are_an_error() {
    use orress_emu::Abi;
    let cases = [
        flag_check(
            |a| a.movzx(eax, byte_ptr(rdi)).unwrap(),
            |a, l| a.je(l).unwrap(),
        ),
        flag_check(
            |a| {
                a.movzx(eax, byte_ptr(rdi)).unwrap();
                a.cmp(al, 0x41).unwrap();
                a.bt(eax, 0).unwrap();
            },
            |a, l| a.jb(l).unwrap(),
        ),
        flag_check(
            |a| {
                a.movzx(eax, byte_ptr(rdi)).unwrap();
                a.shl(al, 3).unwrap();
            },
            |a, l| a.jo(l).unwrap(),
        ),
    ];
    for (i, (code, fail)) in cases.into_iter().enumerate() {
        let r = run_sym(&code, fail, 1, Default::default(), Abi::SysV, |_| {});
        assert!(
            matches!(r, Err(SymError::Unsupported { .. })),
            "case {i}: {:?}",
            r.err()
        );
    }
}

/// Unmodelled instructions that write a register conditionally (`cmovcc`) or read symbolic input
/// (`movdqu xmm0, [input]`) must stop the run instead of being skipped.
#[test]
fn unmodelled_instructions_touching_symbolic_data_bail() {
    use orress_emu::Abi;
    let cmov = flag_check(
        |a| {
            a.movzx(eax, byte_ptr(rdi)).unwrap();
            a.mov(ecx, 0x41).unwrap();
            a.cmp(al, cl).unwrap();
            a.cmove(rax, rcx).unwrap();
            a.cmp(al, 0x41).unwrap();
        },
        |a, l| a.jne(l).unwrap(),
    );
    let movdqu = flag_check(
        |a| {
            a.movdqu(xmm0, xmmword_ptr(rdi)).unwrap();
            a.movzx(eax, byte_ptr(rdi)).unwrap();
            a.cmp(al, 0x41).unwrap();
        },
        |a, l| a.jne(l).unwrap(),
    );
    for (name, (code, fail)) in [("cmove", cmov), ("movdqu", movdqu)] {
        let r = run_sym(&code, fail, 16, Default::default(), Abi::SysV, |_| {});
        assert!(
            matches!(r, Err(SymError::Unsupported { .. })),
            "{name}: {:?}",
            r.err()
        );
    }
    // A concrete-only SSE read (constant data) is still skipped.
    let ok = flag_check(
        |a| {
            a.mov(rax, TARGET_ADDR).unwrap();
            a.movdqu(xmm0, xmmword_ptr(rax)).unwrap();
            a.movzx(eax, byte_ptr(rdi)).unwrap();
            a.cmp(al, 0x41).unwrap();
        },
        |a, l| a.jne(l).unwrap(),
    );
    let sx = run_sym(&ok.0, ok.1, 1, Default::default(), Abi::SysV, |m| {
        m.write_bytes(TARGET_ADDR, &[0u8; 16]);
    })
    .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(sx.constraints.len(), 1);
}

/// Reading unmapped memory is a fault, not a silent 0 that fabricates a constraint.
#[test]
fn unmapped_reads_fault() {
    use orress_emu::Abi;
    let (code, fail) = flag_check(
        |a| {
            a.mov(rax, 0x7777_0000u64).unwrap();
            a.movzx(ecx, byte_ptr(rax)).unwrap();
            a.movzx(eax, byte_ptr(rdi)).unwrap();
            a.cmp(al, cl).unwrap();
        },
        |a, l| a.jne(l).unwrap(),
    );
    let r = run_sym(&code, fail, 1, Default::default(), Abi::SysV, |_| {});
    assert_eq!(r.err(), Some(SymError::Fault(0x7777_0000)));
}

/// `fs:[0x28]` reads the canary from the mapped thread block, so a stack-protector prologue /
/// epilogue pair works (and doesn't fault).
#[test]
fn stack_canary_reads_work() {
    use orress_emu::Abi;
    let (code, fail) = flag_check(
        |a| {
            a.db(&[0x64, 0x48, 0x8B, 0x0C, 0x25, 0x28, 0, 0, 0])
                .unwrap(); // mov rcx, fs:[0x28]
            a.db(&[0x64, 0x48, 0x33, 0x0C, 0x25, 0x28, 0, 0, 0])
                .unwrap(); // xor rcx, fs:[0x28]
            a.test(rcx, rcx).unwrap();
        },
        |a, l| a.jne(l).unwrap(),
    );
    let sx = run_sym(&code, fail, 1, Default::default(), Abi::SysV, |_| {}).unwrap();
    assert!(sx.constraints.is_empty(), "the canary check is concrete");
}

const STUB: u64 = 0xa000;
const STUB2: u64 = 0xa100;
const SLOT: u64 = 0xa800;

fn hooks(list: &[(u64, orress_emu::Stub)]) -> std::collections::HashMap<u64, orress_emu::Stub> {
    list.iter().cloned().collect()
}

/// Stubs read their arguments from the run's ABI: a Win64 memcmp takes rcx/rdx/r8 (before, the
/// executor always read rdi/rsi/rdx). The import is called through its slot (`call [slot]`).
#[test]
fn win64_memcmp_through_an_import_slot() {
    use orress_emu::{Abi, Stub};
    let target = b"s3cr3t!";
    let mut a = CodeAssembler::new(64).unwrap();
    let fail_l = a.create_label();
    // Win64: rcx = input already; rdx = target; r8 = len.
    a.mov(rdx, TARGET_ADDR).unwrap();
    a.mov(r8d, target.len() as i32).unwrap();
    a.mov(rdi, 0x1234u64).unwrap(); // junk in the SysV argument registers
    a.mov(rsi, 0x5678u64).unwrap();
    a.call(qword_ptr(SLOT)).unwrap();
    a.test(eax, eax).unwrap();
    a.jne(fail_l).unwrap();
    let (code, fail) = finish(a, fail_l);
    let sx = run_sym(
        &code,
        fail,
        target.len() as u32,
        hooks(&[(SLOT, Stub::Memcmp)]),
        Abi::Win64,
        |m| {
            m.write_bytes(TARGET_ADDR, target);
            m.write_bytes(SLOT, &0x0001_2345u64.to_le_bytes()); // hint/name RVA, not code
        },
    )
    .unwrap();
    let r = solve(&sx.constraints, target.len());
    assert!(r.complete, "{}", r.message);
    assert_eq!(r.input, target);
}

/// malloc hands out mapped memory, memcpy copies the symbolic input bytes (it returned 0 and
/// copied nothing before), and a `Return` stub no longer demands a concrete first argument.
#[test]
fn malloc_memcpy_and_return_stubs_are_modelled() {
    use orress_emu::{Abi, Stub};
    const PUTS: u64 = 0xa200;
    let mut a = CodeAssembler::new(64).unwrap();
    let fail_l = a.create_label();
    a.mov(rbx, rdi).unwrap(); // the input
    a.mov(edi, 16).unwrap();
    a.call(STUB).unwrap(); // malloc(16)
    a.mov(r12, rax).unwrap();
    a.mov(rdi, rax).unwrap();
    a.mov(rsi, rbx).unwrap();
    a.mov(edx, 4).unwrap();
    a.call(STUB2).unwrap(); // memcpy(buf, input, 4)
    a.movzx(edi, byte_ptr(rbx)).unwrap(); // symbolic first argument
    a.call(PUTS).unwrap(); // putchar-like import (Return 0)
    a.movzx(eax, byte_ptr(r12 + 2)).unwrap();
    a.cmp(al, 0x43).unwrap();
    a.jne(fail_l).unwrap();
    a.movzx(eax, byte_ptr(r12 + 8)).unwrap(); // untouched malloc memory reads as 0
    a.test(al, al).unwrap();
    a.jne(fail_l).unwrap();
    let (code, fail) = finish(a, fail_l);
    let sx = run_sym(
        &code,
        fail,
        4,
        hooks(&[
            (STUB, Stub::Malloc),
            (STUB2, Stub::Memcpy),
            (PUTS, Stub::Return(0)),
        ]),
        Abi::SysV,
        |_| {},
    )
    .unwrap();
    let r = solve(&sx.constraints, 4);
    assert!(r.complete, "{}", r.message);
    assert_eq!(r.input[2], b'C');
}

/// strlen of a non-input string is its real length (it returned the input length before).
#[test]
fn strlen_of_a_constant_string_is_concrete() {
    use orress_emu::{Abi, Stub};
    let mut a = CodeAssembler::new(64).unwrap();
    let fail_l = a.create_label();
    a.mov(rbx, rdi).unwrap();
    a.mov(rdi, TARGET_ADDR).unwrap();
    a.call(STUB).unwrap(); // strlen("abcde") = 5
    a.movzx(ecx, byte_ptr(rbx)).unwrap();
    a.cmp(rcx, rax).unwrap();
    a.jne(fail_l).unwrap();
    let (code, fail) = finish(a, fail_l);
    let sx = run_sym(
        &code,
        fail,
        3,
        hooks(&[(STUB, Stub::Strlen)]),
        Abi::SysV,
        |m| m.write_bytes(TARGET_ADDR, b"abcde\0"),
    )
    .unwrap();
    let r = solve(&sx.constraints, 3);
    assert!(r.complete, "{}", r.message);
    assert_eq!(r.input[0], 5);
}
```

`crates/orress-term/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! ORRESS integrated terminal: a real PTY-backed shell (ConPTY on Windows, a pty
//! elsewhere) whose output is parsed into a `vt100` screen the UI renders. The model is
//! UI-agnostic; the egui renderer lives in `orress-views`.

use std::io::{Read, Write};
use std::path::Path;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::thread::JoinHandle;

use portable_pty::{Child, CommandBuilder, MasterPty, PtySize, native_pty_system};

pub type Notify = Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>;

type Writer = Arc<Mutex<Box<dyn Write + Send>>>;

/// A running shell with a terminal screen model.
pub struct Terminal {
    parser: Arc<Mutex<vt100::Parser>>,
    master: Box<dyn MasterPty + Send>,
    writer: Writer,
    /// Always `Some` until dropped (taken there to be reaped).
    child: Option<Box<dyn Child + Send + Sync>>,
    rows: u16,
    cols: u16,
    alive: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    _reader: JoinHandle<()>,
}

/// The default interactive shell for this platform.
pub fn default_shell() -> (String, Vec<String>) {
    if cfg!(windows) {
        ("powershell.exe".to_string(), vec!["-NoLogo".to_string()])
    } else {
        (
            std::env::var("SHELL").unwrap_or_else(|_| "/bin/bash".to_string()),
            Vec::new(),
        )
    }
}

fn to_io(e: anyhow::Error) -> std::io::Error {
    std::io::Error::other(e.to_string())
}

/// The device queries we answer.
const CPR_QUERY: &[u8] = b"\x1b[6n";
const DA_QUERIES: [&[u8]; 2] = [b"\x1b[c", b"\x1b[0c"];

/// Which queries a chunk of PTY output contains, taking into account a query split across two
/// reads: `carry` holds the tail of the previous chunk that was an incomplete query prefix, and is
/// updated with this chunk's incomplete tail. Returns `(cursor_position, device_attributes)`.
fn scan_queries(carry: &mut Vec<u8>, chunk: &[u8]) -> (bool, bool) {
    let mut data = std::mem::take(carry);
    data.extend_from_slice(chunk);
    let cpr = find(&data, CPR_QUERY);
    let da = DA_QUERIES.iter().any(|q| find(&data, q));
    // Keep the longest suffix that is a proper prefix of some query (at most 3 bytes).
    let all = [CPR_QUERY, DA_QUERIES[0], DA_QUERIES[1]];
    let max = all.iter().map(|q| q.len() - 1).max().unwrap_or(0);
    for len in (1..=max.min(data.len())).rev() {
        let tail = &data[data.len() - len..];
        if all.iter().any(|q| q.len() > len && q.starts_with(tail)) {
            carry.extend_from_slice(tail);
            break;
        }
    }
    (cpr, da)
}

/// Replies to the terminal device queries a program sends through the PTY — without a
/// reply, ConPTY and many shells stall. Handles the cursor-position report (`ESC[6n`) and
/// primary device-attributes (`ESC[c` / `ESC[0c`), including ones split across reads.
fn answer_queries(chunk: &[u8], carry: &mut Vec<u8>, parser: &vt100::Parser, writer: &Writer) {
    let (cpr, da) = scan_queries(carry, chunk);
    let mut reply: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
    if cpr {
        let (row, col) = parser.screen().cursor_position();
        reply.extend_from_slice(format!("\x1b[{};{}R", row + 1, col + 1).as_bytes());
    }
    if da {
        // Claim to be a VT100 with advanced video.
        reply.extend_from_slice(b"\x1b[?1;2c");
    }
    if !reply.is_empty()
        && let Ok(mut w) = writer.lock()
    {
        let _ = w.write_all(&reply);
        let _ = w.flush();
    }
}

fn find(haystack: &[u8], needle: &[u8]) -> bool {
    haystack.windows(needle.len()).any(|w| w == needle)
}

impl Terminal {
    /// Spawns `shell` in a new PTY of `rows` x `cols`, reading its output on a thread.
    pub fn spawn(
        shell: &str,
        args: &[String],
        cwd: Option<&Path>,
        rows: u16,
        cols: u16,
        notify: Notify,
    ) -> std::io::Result<Self> {
        let rows = rows.max(1);
        let cols = cols.max(1);
        let pair = native_pty_system()
            .openpty(PtySize {
                rows,
                cols,
                pixel_width: 0,
                pixel_height: 0,
            })
            .map_err(to_io)?;
        let mut cmd = CommandBuilder::new(shell);
        for a in args {
            cmd.arg(a);
        }
        if let Some(cwd) = cwd {
            cmd.cwd(cwd);
        }
        let child = pair.slave.spawn_command(cmd).map_err(to_io)?;
        let mut reader = pair.master.try_clone_reader().map_err(to_io)?;
        let writer: Writer = Arc::new(Mutex::new(pair.master.take_writer().map_err(to_io)?));

        let parser = Arc::new(Mutex::new(vt100::Parser::new(rows, cols, 5000)));
        let alive = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(true));
        let (pr, al, nf, wr) = (
            Arc::clone(&parser),
            Arc::clone(&alive),
            Arc::clone(&notify),
            Arc::clone(&writer),
        );
        let reader = std::thread::Builder::new()
            .name("orress-term-read".into())
            .spawn(move || {
                let mut buf = [0u8; 8192];
                let mut carry = Vec::new();
                loop {
                    match reader.read(&mut buf) {
                        Ok(0) | Err(_) => break,
                        Ok(n) => {
                            let chunk = &buf[..n];
                            if let Ok(mut p) = pr.lock() {
                                p.process(chunk);
                                // Answer the terminal queries the shell/ConPTY sends, or it
                                // waits for a reply and produces no output.
                                answer_queries(chunk, &mut carry, &p, &wr);
                            }
                            nf();
                        }
                    }
                }
                al.store(false, Ordering::SeqCst);
                nf();
            })
            .expect("spawn terminal reader");

        Ok(Self {
            parser,
            master: pair.master,
            writer,
            child: Some(child),
            rows,
            cols,
            alive,
            _reader: reader,
        })
    }

    /// The vt100 screen model, locked by the caller for rendering.
    pub fn parser(&self) -> &Arc<Mutex<vt100::Parser>> {
        &self.parser
    }

    /// Sends bytes to the shell (keyboard input).
    pub fn input(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) {
        if let Ok(mut w) = self.writer.lock() {
            let _ = w.write_all(bytes);
            let _ = w.flush();
        }
    }

    /// Resizes the PTY and the screen model to `rows` x `cols`.
    pub fn resize(&mut self, rows: u16, cols: u16) {
        let (rows, cols) = (rows.max(1), cols.max(1));
        if (rows, cols) == (self.rows, self.cols) {
            return;
        }
        self.rows = rows;
        self.cols = cols;
        let _ = self.master.resize(PtySize {
            rows,
            cols,
            pixel_width: 0,
            pixel_height: 0,
        });
        if let Ok(mut p) = self.parser.lock() {
            p.screen_mut().set_size(rows, cols);
        }
    }

    pub fn size(&self) -> (u16, u16) {
        (self.rows, self.cols)
    }

    /// Whether the shell is still running.
    pub fn is_alive(&self) -> bool {
        self.alive.load(Ordering::SeqCst)
    }
}

impl Drop for Terminal {
    /// Kills the shell and reaps it (so it does not linger as a zombie). Reaping waits briefly
    /// inline; a process that takes longer to exit is reaped on a background thread so dropping a
    /// terminal never blocks the UI.
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let Some(mut child) = self.child.take() else {
            return;
        };
        let _ = child.kill();
        let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + std::time::Duration::from_millis(200);
        while std::time::Instant::now() < deadline {
            match child.try_wait() {
                Ok(Some(_)) | Err(_) => return,
                Ok(None) => std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(10)),
            }
        }
        let _ = std::thread::Builder::new()
            .name("orress-term-reap".into())
            .spawn(move || {
                let _ = child.wait();
            });
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn finds_queries_split_across_reads() {
        let mut carry = Vec::new();
        assert_eq!(scan_queries(&mut carry, b"hello \x1b["), (false, false));
        assert_eq!(carry, b"\x1b[");
        assert_eq!(scan_queries(&mut carry, b"6n more"), (true, false));
        assert!(carry.is_empty());

        assert_eq!(scan_queries(&mut carry, b"x\x1b"), (false, false));
        assert_eq!(scan_queries(&mut carry, b"[c"), (false, true));

        assert_eq!(scan_queries(&mut carry, b"\x1b[0"), (false, false));
        assert_eq!(scan_queries(&mut carry, b"c\x1b[6n"), (true, true));

        // An ordinary escape sequence is not carried.
        assert_eq!(scan_queries(&mut carry, b"\x1b[31m"), (false, false));
        assert!(carry.is_empty());
    }
}
```

```rs
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use orress_term::Terminal;

#[test]
fn shell_runs_and_echoes() {
    let (shell, args) = if cfg!(windows) {
        ("cmd.exe".to_string(), Vec::new())
    } else {
        ("/bin/sh".to_string(), Vec::new())
    };
    let notify: Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync> = Arc::new(|| {});
    let mut term = match Terminal::spawn(&shell, &args, None, 24, 80, notify) {
        Ok(t) => t,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("could not spawn shell: {e}; skipping");
            return;
        }
    };
    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(600));
    term.input(b"echo orress_marker\r\n");

    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(8);
    let mut contents = String::new();
    while Instant::now() < deadline {
        if let Ok(p) = term.parser().lock() {
            contents = p.screen().contents();
        }
        if contents.contains("orress_marker") {
            break;
        }
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
    }
    eprintln!("screen:\n{contents}");
    assert!(
        contents.contains("orress_marker"),
        "shell output not seen on screen"
    );
}
```

`crates/orress-theme/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! Themes. A theme is a small set of named colors, stored as JSON with `#rrggbb` values,
//! and turned into egui visuals. Besides UI colors it carries the "syntax" colors the
//! reverse-engineering views use (addresses, mnemonics, registers, ...), so every view
//! colors the same concept the same way.

use std::collections::HashMap;

use egui::{Color32, Stroke, Visuals};
use serde::{Deserialize, Deserializer, Serialize, Serializer};

/// A color written as `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa` in theme files.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Hex(pub Color32);

impl Serialize for Hex {
    fn serialize<S: Serializer>(&self, s: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
        let [r, g, b, a] = self.0.to_srgba_unmultiplied();
        if a == 255 {
            s.collect_str(&format_args!("#{r:02x}{g:02x}{b:02x}"))
        } else {
            s.collect_str(&format_args!("#{r:02x}{g:02x}{b:02x}{a:02x}"))
        }
    }
}

impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for Hex {
    fn deserialize<D: Deserializer<'de>>(d: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
        let s = String::deserialize(d)?;
        Color32::from_hex(&s)
            .map(Hex)
            .map_err(|_| serde::de::Error::custom(format!("invalid color `{s}`, expected #rrggbb")))
    }
}

/// Colors for the shell (panels, text, accents).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct UiColors {
    pub background: Hex,
    pub panel: Hex,
    pub elevated: Hex,
    pub border: Hex,
    pub text: Hex,
    pub text_muted: Hex,
    pub accent: Hex,
    pub selection: Hex,
    pub warning: Hex,
    pub error: Hex,
    pub success: Hex,
}

/// Colors shared by disassembly, decompiler, hex and debugger views.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SyntaxColors {
    pub address: Hex,
    pub bytes: Hex,
    pub mnemonic: Hex,
    pub register: Hex,
    pub immediate: Hex,
    pub string: Hex,
    pub comment: Hex,
    pub function: Hex,
    pub label: Hex,
    pub keyword: Hex,
    pub type_name: Hex,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Theme {
    pub name: String,
    pub dark: bool,
    pub ui: UiColors,
    pub syntax: SyntaxColors,
}

fn c(hex: &str) -> Hex {
    Hex(Color32::from_hex(hex).expect("built-in theme colors are valid"))
}

/// A Zed color string, or the given fallback when it is absent or unparseable.
fn pick(opt: Option<&str>, fallback: Hex) -> Hex {
    opt.and_then(|h| Color32::from_hex(h).ok())
        .map(Hex)
        .unwrap_or(fallback)
}

/// The shape of a Zed theme-family file (only the fields ORRESS maps; unknown keys are ignored).
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct ZedFamily {
    #[serde(default)]
    themes: Vec<ZedTheme>,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct ZedTheme {
    #[serde(default)]
    name: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    appearance: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    style: ZedStyle,
}

#[derive(Default, Deserialize)]
struct ZedStyle {
    #[serde(default)]
    background: Option<String>,
    #[serde(rename = "editor.background", default)]
    editor_background: Option<String>,
    #[serde(rename = "editor.foreground", default)]
    editor_foreground: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    text: Option<String>,
    #[serde(rename = "text.muted", default)]
    text_muted: Option<String>,
    #[serde(rename = "text.accent", default)]
    text_accent: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    border: Option<String>,
    #[serde(rename = "elevated_surface.background", default)]
    elevated: Option<String>,
    #[serde(rename = "surface.background", default)]
    surface: Option<String>,
    #[serde(rename = "panel.background", default)]
    panel: Option<String>,
    #[serde(rename = "element.selected", default)]
    element_selected: Option<String>,
    #[serde(rename = "editor.selection.background", default)]
    editor_selection: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    warning: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    error: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    success: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    created: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    syntax: HashMap<String, ZedSyntaxStyle>,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct ZedSyntaxStyle {
    #[serde(default)]
    color: Option<String>,
}

impl Theme {
    pub fn from_json(json: &str) -> Result<Self, serde_json::Error> {
        serde_json::from_str(json)
    }

    pub fn to_json(&self) -> String {
        serde_json::to_string_pretty(self).expect("theme serializes")
    }

    /// Imports a **Zed** theme-family JSON (the format Zed theme extensions ship: a `themes`
    /// array, each with a `style` map) into one ORRESS `Theme` per entry. Zed's style keys are
    /// mapped onto our UI and syntax colors; whatever a Zed theme omits keeps the matching ORRESS
    /// default (for the appearance), so the result is always a complete theme. Zed's `#rrggbbaa`
    /// colors are accepted (alpha is kept). This is the first, no-WASM slice of Zed-extension
    /// compatibility.
    pub fn from_zed_json(json: &str) -> Result<Vec<Theme>, serde_json::Error> {
        let family: ZedFamily = serde_json::from_str(json)?;
        Ok(family.themes.into_iter().map(Theme::from_zed).collect())
    }

    fn from_zed(z: ZedTheme) -> Theme {
        let dark = !z.appearance.eq_ignore_ascii_case("light");
        let mut t = if dark {
            Theme::rusty_dark()
        } else {
            Theme::rusty_light()
        };
        if !z.name.is_empty() {
            t.name = z.name;
        }
        t.dark = dark;
        let s = &z.style;
        // The editor surface is the truest "background"; panels sit on the surface colors.
        t.ui.background = pick(
            s.editor_background.as_deref().or(s.background.as_deref()),
            t.ui.background,
        );
        t.ui.panel = pick(s.panel.as_deref().or(s.surface.as_deref()), t.ui.panel);
        t.ui.elevated = pick(
            s.elevated.as_deref().or(s.surface.as_deref()),
            t.ui.elevated,
        );
        t.ui.border = pick(s.border.as_deref(), t.ui.border);
        t.ui.text = pick(
            s.editor_foreground.as_deref().or(s.text.as_deref()),
            t.ui.text,
        );
        t.ui.text_muted = pick(s.text_muted.as_deref(), t.ui.text_muted);
        t.ui.accent = pick(s.text_accent.as_deref(), t.ui.accent);
        t.ui.selection = pick(
            s.editor_selection
                .as_deref()
                .or(s.element_selected.as_deref()),
            t.ui.selection,
        );
        t.ui.warning = pick(s.warning.as_deref(), t.ui.warning);
        t.ui.error = pick(s.error.as_deref(), t.ui.error);
        t.ui.success = pick(s.success.as_deref().or(s.created.as_deref()), t.ui.success);
        // Syntax highlighting keys (each Zed entry is `{ "color": "#..", ... }`). RE-specific
        // concepts map to the nearest source concept: a mnemonic reads like a keyword, a register
        // like a variable, an immediate like a number, raw bytes like a comment (dim).
        let syn =
            |name: &str| -> Option<&str> { s.syntax.get(name).and_then(|v| v.color.as_deref()) };
        t.syntax.keyword = pick(syn("keyword"), t.syntax.keyword);
        t.syntax.function = pick(syn("function"), t.syntax.function);
        t.syntax.type_name = pick(syn("type"), t.syntax.type_name);
        t.syntax.string = pick(syn("string"), t.syntax.string);
        t.syntax.comment = pick(
            syn("comment").or_else(|| syn("comment.doc")),
            t.syntax.comment,
        );
        t.syntax.immediate = pick(syn("number"), t.syntax.immediate);
        t.syntax.register = pick(
            syn("variable").or_else(|| syn("variable.special")),
            t.syntax.register,
        );
        t.syntax.label = pick(syn("label").or_else(|| syn("tag")), t.syntax.label);
        t.syntax.mnemonic = pick(syn("keyword"), t.syntax.mnemonic);
        t.syntax.address = pick(s.text_muted.as_deref(), t.syntax.address);
        t.syntax.bytes = pick(syn("comment"), t.syntax.bytes);
        t
    }

    /// Default dark theme, loosely inspired by Zed's One Dark.
    pub fn rusty_dark() -> Self {
        Self {
            name: "ORRESS Dark".into(),
            dark: true,
            ui: UiColors {

        }
    }

    pub fn built_in() -> Vec<Self> {
        vec![
            Self::rusty_dark(),
            Self::rusty_light(),
            Self::high_contrast(),
        ]
    }

    pub fn visuals(&self) -> Visuals {
        let ui = &self.ui;
        let mut v = if self.dark {
            Visuals::dark()
        } else {
            Visuals::light()
        };
        v.override_text_color = Some(ui.text.0);
        v.panel_fill = ui.panel.0;
        v.window_fill = ui.elevated.0;
        v.extreme_bg_color = ui.background.0;
        v.faint_bg_color = ui.elevated.0;
        v.code_bg_color = ui.background.0;
        v.hyperlink_color = ui.accent.0;
        v.warn_fg_color = ui.warning.0;
        v.error_fg_color = ui.error.0;
        v.selection.bg_fill = ui.selection.0;
        v.selection.stroke = Stroke::new(1.0, ui.accent.0);
        v.window_stroke = Stroke::new(1.0, ui.border.0);
        v.widgets.noninteractive.bg_stroke = Stroke::new(1.0, ui.border.0);
        v.widgets.noninteractive.bg_fill = ui.panel.0;
        v.widgets.inactive.weak_bg_fill = ui.elevated.0;
        v.widgets.hovered.bg_stroke = Stroke::new(1.0, ui.accent.0);
        v.widgets.active.bg_stroke = Stroke::new(1.0, ui.accent.0);
        v
    }

    /// Applies the theme to every egui style (dark and light slots).
    pub fn apply(&self, ctx: &egui::Context) {
        let theme = if self.dark {
            egui::Theme::Dark
        } else {
            egui::Theme::Light
        };
        ctx.set_theme(theme);
        ctx.set_visuals_of(theme, self.visuals());
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn built_in_themes_round_trip_through_json() {
        for theme in Theme::built_in() {
            let back = Theme::from_json(&theme.to_json()).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(back, theme);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn bad_color_is_a_clear_error() {
        let mut json = Theme::rusty_dark().to_json();
        json = json.replacen("#61afef", "blue", 1);
        let err = Theme::from_json(&json).unwrap_err().to_string();
        assert!(err.contains("invalid color `blue`"), "{err}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn imports_a_zed_theme_family() {
        // A trimmed Zed theme family (the real files carry dozens more style keys we ignore).
        let json = r##"{
            "name": "Demo",
            "themes": [
                {
                    "name": "Demo Dark",
                    "appearance": "dark",
                    "style": {
                        "editor.background": "#101418",
                        "editor.foreground": "#c8ccd4",
                        "text.muted": "#767b85",
                        "border": "#2a2f38",
                        "editor.selection.background": "#2d4f67aa",
                        "error": "#e05252",
                        "syntax": {
                            "keyword": { "color": "#c678ddff", "font_weight": 700 },
                            "function": { "color": "#61afef" },
                            "type": { "color": "#56b6c2" },
                            "string": { "color": "#98c379" },
                            "comment": { "color": "#5c6370" },
                            "number": { "color": "#d19a66" },
                            "variable": { "color": "#e06c75" }
                        }
                    }
                },
                { "name": "Demo Light", "appearance": "light", "style": {} }
            ]
        }"##;
        let themes = Theme::from_zed_json(json).expect("imports");
        assert_eq!(themes.len(), 2);

        let dark = &themes[0];
        assert_eq!(dark.name, "Demo Dark");
        assert!(dark.dark);
        assert_eq!(dark.ui.background, c("#101418"));
        assert_eq!(dark.ui.text, c("#c8ccd4"));
        assert_eq!(dark.syntax.keyword, c("#c678dd")); // alpha ff folds to opaque
        assert_eq!(dark.syntax.mnemonic, c("#c678dd")); // mnemonic maps to the keyword color
        assert_eq!(dark.syntax.immediate, c("#d19a66")); // number → immediate
        assert_eq!(dark.syntax.register, c("#e06c75")); // variable → register
        assert_eq!(
            dark.ui.selection,
            Theme::from_json(&dark.to_json()).unwrap().ui.selection
        );

        // The light entry has an empty style, so it keeps the ORRESS light defaults but its name.
        let light = &themes[1];
        assert_eq!(light.name, "Demo Light");
        assert!(!light.dark);
        assert_eq!(light.ui.background, Theme::rusty_light().ui.background);
    }
}
```

```rs
//! Text encodings, implemented here so custom alphabets (a common CTF trick) work.

pub const BASE64_STANDARD: &str =
    "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/";
pub const BASE64_URL: &str = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-_";
pub const BASE32: &str = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ234567";
pub const BASE58: &str = "123456789ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijkmnopqrstuvwxyz";

/// Hex to bytes. Ignores whitespace, commas, `0x` and `\x` prefixes.
pub fn from_hex(input: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(input)
        .replace("0x", "")
        .replace("0X", "")
        .replace("\\x", "");
    let digits: Vec<u8> = text
        .bytes()
        .filter(|b| !b.is_ascii_whitespace() && *b != b',' && *b != b':')
        .collect();
    if let Some(bad) = digits.iter().find(|b| !b.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {
        return Err(format!("`{}` is not a hex digit", *bad as char));
    }
    if !digits.len().is_multiple_of(2) {
        return Err("odd number of hex digits".into());
    }
    Ok(digits
        .chunks(2)
        .map(|p| u8::from_str_radix(std::str::from_utf8(p).expect("ascii"), 16).expect("hex"))
        .collect())
}

pub fn to_hex(input: &[u8], separator: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
    input
        .iter()
        .map(|b| format!("{b:02x}"))
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join(separator)
        .into_bytes()
}

fn check_alphabet(alphabet: &str, len: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let a = alphabet.as_bytes().to_vec();
    if a.len() != len {
        return Err(format!(
            "the alphabet needs exactly {len} characters, it has {}",
            a.len()
        ));
    }
    let mut seen = [false; 256];
    for &c in &a {
        if std::mem::replace(&mut seen[usize::from(c)], true) {
            return Err(format!("`{}` appears twice in the alphabet", c as char));
        }
    }
    Ok(a)
}

pub fn to_base64(input: &[u8], alphabet: &str, pad: bool) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let a = check_alphabet(alphabet, 64)?;
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(input.len().div_ceil(3) * 4);
    for chunk in input.chunks(3) {
        let n = (u32::from(chunk[0]) << 16)
            | (u32::from(*chunk.get(1).unwrap_or(&0)) << 8)
            | u32::from(*chunk.get(2).unwrap_or(&0));
        for i in 0..4 {
            if i <= chunk.len() {
                out.push(a[((n >> (18 - 6 * i)) & 63) as usize]);
            } else if pad {
                out.push(b'=');
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(out)
}

pub fn from_base64(input: &[u8], alphabet: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let a = check_alphabet(alphabet, 64)?;
    let mut lookup = [255u8; 256];
    for (i, &c) in a.iter().enumerate() {
        lookup[usize::from(c)] = i as u8;
    }
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(input.len() * 3 / 4);
    let (mut buffer, mut bits) = (0u32, 0u32);
    for &c in input {
        // Look the character up first: a custom alphabet may legitimately
        // contain `=` or whitespace.
        let v = lookup[usize::from(c)];
        if v == 255 {
            if c == b'=' {
                // Padding ends a quantum: drop the leftover (zero) bits so a
                // following concatenated block ("QQ==QQ==") starts aligned.
                buffer = 0;
                bits = 0;
                continue;
            }
            if c.is_ascii_whitespace() {
                continue;
            }
            return Err(format!("`{}` is not in the base64 alphabet", c as char));
        }
        buffer = (buffer << 6) | u32::from(v);
        bits += 6;
        if bits >= 8 {
            bits -= 8;
            out.push((buffer >> bits) as u8);
            buffer &= (1 << bits) - 1;
        }
    }
    Ok(out)
}

pub fn to_base32(input: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let a = BASE32.as_bytes();
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for chunk in input.chunks(5) {
        let mut block = [0u8; 5];
        block[..chunk.len()].copy_from_slice(chunk);
        let n = block.iter().fold(0u64, |acc, &b| (acc << 8) | u64::from(b));
        let chars = (chunk.len() * 8).div_ceil(5);
        for i in 0..8 {
            if i < chars {
                out.push(a[((n >> (35 - 5 * i)) & 31) as usize]);
            } else {
                out.push(b'=');
            }
        }
    }
    out
}

pub fn from_base32(input: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let (mut buffer, mut bits) = (0u64, 0u32);
    for &c in input {
        if c.is_ascii_whitespace() || c == b'=' {
            continue;
        }
        let v = BASE32
            .bytes()
            .position(|x| x == c.to_ascii_uppercase())
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("`{}` is not a base32 character", c as char))?;
        buffer = (buffer << 5) | v as u64;
        bits += 5;
        if bits >= 8 {
            bits -= 8;
            out.push((buffer >> bits) as u8);
            buffer &= (1 << bits) - 1;
        }
    }
    Ok(out)
}

pub fn to_base58(input: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let a = BASE58.as_bytes();
    let zeros = input.iter().take_while(|&&b| b == 0).count();
    let mut digits: Vec<u8> = Vec::new(); // little-endian base-58 digits
    for &byte in &input[zeros..] {
        let mut carry = u32::from(byte);
        for d in &mut digits {
            carry += u32::from(*d) << 8;
            *d = (carry % 58) as u8;
            carry /= 58;
        }
        while carry > 0 {
            digits.push((carry % 58) as u8);
            carry /= 58;
        }
    }
    let mut out = vec![b'1'; zeros];
    out.extend(digits.iter().rev().map(|&d| a[usize::from(d)]));
    out
}

pub fn from_base58(input: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let text: Vec<u8> = input
        .iter()
        .copied()
        .filter(|b| !b.is_ascii_whitespace())
        .collect();
    let zeros = text.iter().take_while(|&&b| b == b'1').count();
    let mut bytes: Vec<u8> = Vec::new(); // little-endian
    for &c in &text[zeros..] {
        let v = BASE58
            .bytes()
            .position(|x| x == c)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("`{}` is not a base58 character", c as char))?;
        let mut carry = v as u32;
        for b in &mut bytes {
            carry += u32::from(*b) * 58;
            *b = (carry & 0xff) as u8;
            carry >>= 8;
        }
        while carry > 0 {
            bytes.push((carry & 0xff) as u8);
            carry >>= 8;
        }
    }
    let mut out = vec![0u8; zeros];
    out.extend(bytes.iter().rev());
    Ok(out)
}

/// Exactly two ASCII hex digits → one byte (no separators, no prefixes).
fn hex_pair(pair: &[u8]) -> Option<u8> {
    if pair.len() != 2 || !pair.iter().all(u8::is_ascii_hexdigit) {
        return None;
    }
    u8::from_str_radix(std::str::from_utf8(pair).ok()?, 16).ok()
}

pub fn from_url(input: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(input.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < input.len() {
        match input[i] {
            b'%' => {
                let byte = input
                    .get(i + 1..i + 3)
                    .and_then(hex_pair)
                    .ok_or("a `%` must be followed by two hex digits")?;
                out.push(byte);
                i += 3;
            }
            b'+' => {
                out.push(b' ');
                i += 1;
            }
            b => {
                out.push(b);
                i += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(out)
}

pub fn to_url(input: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for &b in input {
        if b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b"-_.~".contains(&b) {
            out.push(b);
        } else {
            out.extend(format!("%{b:02X}").bytes());
        }
    }
    out
}

/// `\x41\n\t\\` → bytes.
pub fn from_escaped(input: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < input.len() {
        if input[i] != b'\\' {
            out.push(input[i]);
            i += 1;
            continue;
        }
        let next = *input
            .get(i + 1)
            .ok_or("the text ends with a lone backslash")?;
        i += 2;
        match next {
            b'x' => {
                let byte = input
                    .get(i..i + 2)
                    .and_then(hex_pair)
                    .ok_or("`\\x` needs two hex digits")?;
                out.push(byte);
                i += 2;
            }
            b'n' => out.push(b'\n'),
            b'r' => out.push(b'\r'),
            b't' => out.push(b'\t'),
            b'0' => out.push(0),
            other => out.push(other),
        }
    }
    Ok(out)
}

pub fn to_escaped(input: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out = String::new();
    for &b in input {
        match b {
            b'\\' => out.push_str("\\\\"),
            b'\n' => out.push_str("\\n"),
            b'\r' => out.push_str("\\r"),
            b'\t' => out.push_str("\\t"),
            0x20..=0x7e => out.push(b as char),
            _ => out.push_str(&format!("\\x{b:02x}")),
        }
    }
    out.into_bytes()
}
```

```rs
//! Data transforms: decode, decrypt, decompress and hash bytes, alone or chained into
//! a [`Recipe`] such as `from_base64 | xor key=0x41 | zlib_inflate`.
//!
//! The same recipes run in ORRESS's Workbench and in `orress-cli`, and [`magic`]
//! searches for a recipe that turns unreadable input into something readable.

mod codec;
mod magic;
mod ops;
pub mod score;

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::fmt;

pub use magic::{Suggestion, magic};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub enum Category {
    Encoding,
    Text,
    Bitwise,
    Crypto,
    Compression,
    Hash,
    Data,
}

impl Category {
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Encoding => "Encoding",
            Self::Text => "Text",
            Self::Bitwise => "Bitwise",
            Self::Crypto => "Crypto",
            Self::Compression => "Compression",
            Self::Hash => "Hashes",
            Self::Data => "Data",
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ParamKind {
    /// Bytes: `0x4142`, `hex:41 42`, `text:abc` or plain text.
    Key,
    Int,
    Text,
    Choice(&'static [&'static str]),
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct Param {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub kind: ParamKind,
    pub default: &'static str,
    pub explain: &'static str,
}

pub type OpFn = fn(&[u8], &Args<'_>) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String>;

/// A transform operation.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct Op {
    pub id: &'static str,
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub category: Category,
    pub explain: &'static str,
    pub params: &'static [Param],
    pub run: OpFn,
}

/// Parameter values for one step, with typed access.
pub struct Args<'a> {
    values: &'a BTreeMap<String, String>,
    spec: &'static [Param],
}

impl Args<'_> {
    fn raw(&self, name: &str) -> &str {
        self.values
            .get(name)
            .map(String::as_str)
            .or_else(|| self.spec.iter().find(|p| p.name == name).map(|p| p.default))
            .unwrap_or("")
    }

    pub fn key(&self, name: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
        parse_key(self.raw(name)).map_err(|e| format!("{name}: {e}"))
    }

    pub fn int(&self, name: &str) -> Result<i64, String> {
        let raw = self.raw(name).trim();
        let value = match raw.strip_prefix("0x").or_else(|| raw.strip_prefix("0X")) {
            Some(hex) => i64::from_str_radix(hex, 16).ok(),
            None => raw.parse().ok(),
        };
        value.ok_or_else(|| format!("{name}: `{raw}` is not a number"))
    }

    pub fn text(&self, name: &str) -> String {
        self.raw(name).to_owned()
    }
}

/// Parses a key or other byte parameter:
/// - `0x41424344` or `hex:41 42 43` → hex bytes
/// - `text:hello` → the text's bytes
/// - anything else → the text's bytes as typed
pub fn parse_key(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let t = text.trim();
    if let Some(hex) = t.strip_prefix("hex:") {
        return codec::from_hex(hex.as_bytes());
    }
    if let Some(hex) = t.strip_prefix("0x").or_else(|| t.strip_prefix("0X"))
        && !hex.is_empty()
        && hex.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_hexdigit() || c == ' ')
    {
        return codec::from_hex(hex.as_bytes());
    }
    if let Some(raw) = t.strip_prefix("text:") {
        return Ok(raw.as_bytes().to_vec());
    }
    Ok(text.as_bytes().to_vec())
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Step {
    pub op: String,
    pub params: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    pub enabled: bool,
}

impl Step {
    /// A step with default parameters.
    pub fn new(op: &str) -> Self {
        let params = find(op)
            .map(|o| {
                o.params
                    .iter()
                    .map(|p| (p.name.to_owned(), p.default.to_owned()))
                    .collect()
            })
            .unwrap_or_default();
        Self {
            op: op.to_owned(),
            params,
            enabled: true,
        }
    }

    pub fn with(mut self, name: &str, value: &str) -> Self {
        self.params.insert(name.to_owned(), value.to_owned());
        self
    }

    pub fn apply(&self, input: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
        let op = find(&self.op).ok_or_else(|| format!("unknown operation `{}`", self.op))?;
        let args = Args {
            values: &self.params,
            spec: op.params,
        };
        (op.run)(input, &args)
    }
}

/// A chain of steps; each step's output is the next one's input.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Recipe(pub Vec<Step>);

impl Recipe {
    /// Runs the recipe, returning every enabled step's output. Stops at the first error.
    pub fn run(&self, input: &[u8]) -> Vec<Result<Vec<u8>, String>> {
        let mut outputs = Vec::new();
        let mut current = input.to_vec();
        for step in self.0.iter().filter(|s| s.enabled) {
            match step.apply(&current) {
                Ok(out) => {
                    outputs.push(Ok(out.clone()));
                    current = out;
                }
                Err(e) => {
                    outputs.push(Err(e));
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        outputs
    }

    /// The final output, or the first error.
    pub fn output(&self, input: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
        match self.run(input).pop() {
            Some(result) => result,
            None => Ok(input.to_vec()),
        }
    }

    /// Parses `op key=value | op2 key="two words"`.
    pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Result<Self, String> {
        let mut steps = Vec::new();
        for part in split_outside_quotes(text, '|') {
            let part = part.trim();
            if part.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            let tokens = split_outside_quotes(part, ' ');
            let mut tokens = tokens.iter().map(|t| t.trim()).filter(|t| !t.is_empty());
            let op = tokens.next().ok_or("empty step")?;
            let spec = find(op).ok_or_else(|| format!("unknown operation `{op}`"))?;
            let mut step = Step::new(op);
            for token in tokens {
                let (name, value) = token
                    .split_once('=')
                    .ok_or_else(|| format!("`{token}`: parameters are written name=value"))?;
                if !spec.params.iter().any(|p| p.name == name) {
                    let known: Vec<&str> = spec.params.iter().map(|p| p.name).collect();
                    return Err(format!(
                        "`{op}` has no parameter `{name}` (it has: {})",
                        if known.is_empty() {
                            "none".to_owned()
                        } else {
                            known.join(", ")
                        }
                    ));
                }
                let value = value.trim_matches('"');
                step.params.insert(name.to_owned(), value.to_owned());
            }
            steps.push(step);
        }
        Ok(Self(steps))
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for Recipe {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        let mut first = true;
        for step in self.0.iter().filter(|s| s.enabled) {
            if !first {
                f.write_str(" | ")?;
            }
            first = false;
            f.write_str(&step.op)?;
            let defaults = find(&step.op).map_or(&[][..], |o| o.params);
            for (name, value) in &step.params {
                let is_default = defaults
                    .iter()
                    .any(|p| p.name == name && p.default == value);
                if is_default {
                    continue;
                }
                if value.contains([' ', '|']) || value.is_empty() {
                    write!(f, " {name}=\"{value}\"")?;
                } else {
                    write!(f, " {name}={value}")?;
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

fn split_outside_quotes(text: &str, sep: char) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut parts = vec![String::new()];
    let mut quoted = false;
    for c in text.chars() {
        if c == '"' {
            quoted = !quoted;
        }
        if c == sep && !quoted {
            parts.push(String::new());
        } else {
            parts.last_mut().expect("non-empty").push(c);
        }
    }
    parts
}

/// All operations, in display order.
pub fn ops() -> &'static [Op] {
    ops::ALL
}

pub fn find(id: &str) -> Option<&'static Op> {
    ops::ALL.iter().find(|o| o.id == id)
}

mod tests;
```

`crates/orress-transforms/src/magic.rs`:

```rs
//! "Magic": search for a recipe that makes the input readable, like CyberChef's Magic.
//!
//! A small beam search: from the input, try every decoding that plausibly applies
//! (base64 only if the text looks like base64, zlib only if it starts like zlib, ...),
//! keep the best few results, and repeat a few levels deep.

use crate::score::{file_type, score};
use crate::{Recipe, Step};

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Suggestion {
    pub recipe: Recipe,
    pub output: Vec<u8>,
    pub score: f32,
    /// Plain-language reason, e.g. "readable text" or "a PNG image".
    pub why: String,
}

const BEAM: usize = 12;
const MAX_INPUT: usize = 1 << 20;

fn is_text(data: &[u8]) -> bool {
    !data.is_empty()
        && data
            .iter()
            .all(|b| b.is_ascii_graphic() || b.is_ascii_whitespace())
}

/// Decodings worth trying on `data`.
fn candidates(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<Step> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let text = is_text(data);
    let compact: Vec<u8> = data
        .iter()
        .copied()
        .filter(|b| !b.is_ascii_whitespace())
        .collect();
    if text && compact.len() >= 4 {
        if compact.len().is_multiple_of(2) && compact.iter().all(u8::is_ascii_hexdigit) {
            out.push(Step::new("from_hex"));
        }
        if compact
            .iter()
            .all(|b| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b"+/=".contains(b))
        {
            out.push(Step::new("from_base64"));
        }
        if compact
            .iter()
            .all(|b| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b"-_=".contains(b))
        {
            out.push(Step::new("from_base64").with("alphabet", crate::codec::BASE64_URL));
        }
        if compact
            .iter()
            .all(|b| b.is_ascii_uppercase() || (b'2'..=b'7').contains(b) || *b == b'=')
        {
            out.push(Step::new("from_base32"));
        }
        if compact
            .iter()
            .all(|b| crate::codec::BASE58.as_bytes().contains(b))
        {
            out.push(Step::new("from_base58"));
        }
        if data.contains(&b'%') {
            out.push(Step::new("from_url"));
        }
        if data.windows(2).any(|w| w == b"\\x") {
            out.push(Step::new("from_escaped"));
        }
        if data.iter().filter(|b| b.is_ascii_alphabetic()).count() * 2 > data.len() {
            out.push(Step::new("rot13"));
        }
        out.push(Step::new("reverse"));
    }
    if data.len() >= 2 && data[0] == 0x78 {
        out.push(Step::new("zlib_inflate"));
    }
    if data.starts_with(&[0x1f, 0x8b]) {
        out.push(Step::new("gzip_decompress"));
    }
    if data.len() >= 4
        && data.len().is_multiple_of(2)
        && data.iter().skip(1).step_by(2).all(|&b| b == 0)
    {
        out.push(Step::new("utf16le_to_utf8"));
    }
    // XOR can also turn text into printable gibberish, so try it on anything that does
    // not already contain a flag.
    let has_flag = orress_bytes::strings::looks_like_flag(&String::from_utf8_lossy(data));
    if !has_flag && data.len() >= 4 {
        // Best single-byte XOR key.
        let sample = &data[..data.len().min(2048)];
        if let Some((key, _)) = (1..=255u8)
            .map(|k| (k, score(&sample.iter().map(|b| b ^ k).collect::<Vec<_>>())))
            .max_by(|a, b| a.1.total_cmp(&b.1))
        {
            out.push(Step::new("xor").with("key", &format!("0x{key:02x}")));
        }
        // Known plaintext: maybe it is an XOR-encrypted flag.
        if let Some(key) = crate::ops::recover_xor_key(data, b"flag{", 0)
            && key.len() < 5
        {
            let hex: String = key.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect();
            out.push(Step::new("xor").with("key", &format!("0x{hex}")));
        }
    }
    out
}

fn describe(data: &[u8]) -> String {
    if let Some(kind) = file_type(data) {
        return kind.to_owned();
    }
    if orress_bytes::strings::looks_like_flag(&String::from_utf8_lossy(data)) {
        return "looks like a flag!".to_owned();
    }
    if is_text(data) {
        return "readable text".to_owned();
    }
    "binary data".to_owned()
}

/// Ranked suggestions, best first. `depth` is the maximum recipe length.
pub fn magic(input: &[u8], depth: usize) -> Vec<Suggestion> {
    let input = &input[..input.len().min(MAX_INPUT)];
    let base = score(input);
    let mut frontier: Vec<(Recipe, Vec<u8>)> = vec![(Recipe::default(), input.to_vec())];
    let mut found: Vec<Suggestion> = Vec::new();
    for _ in 0..depth {
        let mut next: Vec<(Recipe, Vec<u8>, f32)> = Vec::new();
        for (recipe, data) in &frontier {
            for step in candidates(data) {
                // Do not undo the previous step (reverse after reverse, rot13 twice).
                if recipe.0.last().is_some_and(|last| {
                    last.op == step.op && matches!(step.op.as_str(), "reverse" | "rot13")
                }) {
                    continue;
                }
                let Ok(out) = step.apply(data) else {
                    continue;
                };
                if out.is_empty() || out == *data {
                    continue;
                }
                let mut r = recipe.clone();
                r.0.push(step);
                let s = score(&out);
                next.push((r, out, s));
            }
        }
        next.sort_by(|a, b| b.2.total_cmp(&a.2));
        next.dedup_by(|a, b| a.1 == b.1);
        next.truncate(BEAM);
        for (recipe, output, s) in &next {
            // Longer recipes must earn their extra steps.
            let adjusted = s - 0.05 * recipe.0.len() as f32;
            if *s > base + 0.1 && !found.iter().any(|f| f.output == *output) {
                found.push(Suggestion {
                    recipe: recipe.clone(),
                    why: describe(output),
                    output: output.clone(),
                    score: adjusted,
                });
            }
        }
        frontier = next.into_iter().map(|(r, o, _)| (r, o)).collect();
        if frontier.is_empty() {
            break;
        }
    }
    found.sort_by(|a, b| b.score.total_cmp(&a.score));
    found.truncate(10);
    found
}
```

```rs
fn utf16le_to_utf8(input: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    if !input.len().is_multiple_of(2) {
        return Err("UTF-16 data must have an even number of bytes".into());
    }
    let units: Vec<u16> = input
        .chunks(2)
        .map(|c| u16::from_le_bytes([c[0], c[1]]))
        .collect();
    Ok(String::from_utf16_lossy(&units).into_bytes())
}

fn caesar(input: &[u8], shift: u8) -> Vec<u8> {
    input
        .iter()
        .map(|&b| match b {
            b'a'..=b'z' => b'a' + (b - b'a' + shift) % 26,
            b'A'..=b'Z' => b'A' + (b - b'A' + shift) % 26,
            _ => b,
        })
        .collect()
}

fn xor(input: &[u8], key: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    if key.is_empty() {
        return Err("the key is empty".into());
    }
    Ok(input
        .iter()
        .zip(key.iter().cycle())
        .map(|(a, b)| a ^ b)
        .collect())
}

fn xor_brute(input: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let sample = &input[..input.len().min(4096)];
    let mut results: Vec<(f32, u8)> = (0..=255u8)
        .map(|k| {
            let out: Vec<u8> = sample.iter().map(|b| b ^ k).collect();
            (crate::score::score(&out), k)
        })
        .collect();
    results.sort_by(|a, b| b.0.total_cmp(&a.0));
    let mut text = String::new();
    for (score, key) in results.iter().take(8) {
        let out: Vec<u8> = input.iter().take(80).map(|b| b ^ key).collect();
        text += &format!(
            "key 0x{key:02x} (score {score:.2}): {}\n",
            String::from_utf8_lossy(&codec::to_escaped(&out))
        );
    }
    text.into_bytes()
}

/// Recovers a repeating XOR key from known plaintext at the start of the data.
pub fn recover_xor_key(input: &[u8], known: &[u8], key_len: usize) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    if known.is_empty() || input.len() < known.len() {
        return None;
    }
    let lengths: Vec<usize> = if key_len == 0 {
        (1..=known.len()).collect()
    } else {
        vec![key_len]
    };
    for len in lengths {
        if len > known.len() {
            continue;
        }
        let key: Vec<u8> = input[..len].iter().zip(known).map(|(c, p)| c ^ p).collect();
        // The key must reproduce all of the known text.
        let consistent = known
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .all(|(i, &p)| input[i] ^ key[i % len] == p);
        if consistent {
            return Some(key);
        }
    }
    None
}

fn xor_known(input: &[u8], known: &[u8], key_len: i64) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let key = recover_xor_key(input, known, key_len.max(0) as usize)
        .ok_or("no repeating key fits: the data may not start with this text, or the key is longer than the known text")?;
    let mut out = format!(
        "key: 0x{} (\"{}\")\n",
        String::from_utf8_lossy(&codec::to_hex(&key, "")),
        String::from_utf8_lossy(&codec::to_escaped(&key))
    )
    .into_bytes();
    out.extend(xor(input, &key)?);
    Ok(out)
}

fn rc4(input: &[u8], key: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    if key.is_empty() || key.len() > 256 {
        return Err("RC4 keys are 1 to 256 bytes".into());
    }
    let mut s: Vec<u8> = (0..=255).collect();
    let mut j = 0u8;
    for i in 0..256 {
        j = j.wrapping_add(s[i]).wrapping_add(key[i % key.len()]);
        s.swap(i, usize::from(j));
    }
    let (mut i, mut j) = (0u8, 0u8);
    Ok(input
        .iter()
        .map(|&b| {
            i = i.wrapping_add(1);
            j = j.wrapping_add(s[usize::from(i)]);
            s.swap(usize::from(i), usize::from(j));
            b ^ s[usize::from(s[usize::from(i)].wrapping_add(s[usize::from(j)]))]
        })
        .collect())
}

enum AesKey {
    A128(aes::Aes128),
    A192(aes::Aes192),
    A256(aes::Aes256),
}

impl AesKey {
    fn new(key: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, String> {
        let bad = |_| "invalid AES key".to_owned();
        Ok(match key.len() {
            16 => Self::A128(aes::Aes128::new_from_slice(key).map_err(bad)?),
            24 => Self::A192(aes::Aes192::new_from_slice(key).map_err(bad)?),
            32 => Self::A256(aes::Aes256::new_from_slice(key).map_err(bad)?),
            n => return Err(format!("AES keys are 16, 24 or 32 bytes; this one is {n}")),
        })
    }

    fn encrypt(&self, block: &mut [u8; 16]) {
        let b: &mut aes::Block = (&mut block[..]).try_into().expect("16 bytes");
        match self {
            Self::A128(c) => c.encrypt_block(b),
            Self::A192(c) => c.encrypt_block(b),
            Self::A256(c) => c.encrypt_block(b),
        }
    }

    fn decrypt(&self, block: &mut [u8; 16]) {
        let b: &mut aes::Block = (&mut block[..]).try_into().expect("16 bytes");
        match self {
            Self::A128(c) => c.decrypt_block(b),
            Self::A192(c) => c.decrypt_block(b),
            Self::A256(c) => c.decrypt_block(b),
        }
    }
}

fn aes(input: &[u8], a: &Args<'_>, encrypt: bool) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let cipher = AesKey::new(&a.key("key")?)?;
    let mode = a.text("mode");
    let pkcs7 = a.text("padding") == "pkcs7";
    let iv: [u8; 16] = if mode == "ECB" {
        [0; 16]
    } else {
        a.key("iv")?
            .try_into()
            .map_err(|v: Vec<u8>| format!("the IV must be 16 bytes, it is {}", v.len()))?
    };
    let mut data = input.to_vec();
    if mode == "CTR" {
        let mut counter = iv;
        for chunk in data.chunks_mut(16) {
            let mut stream = counter;
            cipher.encrypt(&mut stream);
            chunk.iter_mut().zip(stream).for_each(|(b, s)| *b ^= s);
            // Big-endian increment of the whole counter block.
            for byte in counter.iter_mut().rev() {
                *byte = byte.wrapping_add(1);
                if *byte != 0 {
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        return Ok(data);
    }
    if encrypt && pkcs7 {
        let pad = 16 - data.len() % 16;
        data.extend(std::iter::repeat_n(pad as u8, pad));
    }
    if !data.len().is_multiple_of(16) {
        return Err(format!(
            "{mode} works on 16-byte blocks; the data is {} bytes",
            data.len()
        ));
    }
    let mut previous = iv;
    for chunk in data.chunks_mut(16) {
        let mut block: [u8; 16] = chunk.try_into().expect("16 bytes");
        if encrypt {
            if mode == "CBC" {
                block.iter_mut().zip(previous).for_each(|(b, p)| *b ^= p);
            }
            cipher.encrypt(&mut block);
            previous = block;
        } else {
            let saved = block;
            cipher.decrypt(&mut block);
            if mode == "CBC" {
                block.iter_mut().zip(previous).for_each(|(b, p)| *b ^= p);
            }
            previous = saved;
        }
        chunk.copy_from_slice(&block);
    }
    if !encrypt && pkcs7 {
        let pad = usize::from(*data.last().ok_or("no data")?);
        let valid = (1..=16).contains(&pad)
            && data.len() >= pad
            && data[data.len() - pad..]
                .iter()
                .all(|&b| usize::from(b) == pad);
        if !valid {
            return Err("wrong key or IV: the PKCS#7 padding is invalid (set padding=none to see the raw result)".into());
        }
        data.truncate(data.len() - pad);
    }
    Ok(data)
}

fn tea(input: &[u8], a: &Args<'_>, xtea: bool) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let key = a.key("key")?;
    if key.len() != 16 {
        return Err(format!("TEA keys are 16 bytes; this one is {}", key.len()));
    }
    if !input.len().is_multiple_of(8) {
        return Err("TEA works on 8-byte blocks".into());
    }
    let big = a.text("endian") == "big";
    let word = |b: &[u8]| {
        let arr = [b[0], b[1], b[2], b[3]];
        if big {
            u32::from_be_bytes(arr)
        } else {
            u32::from_le_bytes(arr)
        }
    };
    let k: Vec<u32> = key.chunks(4).map(word).collect();
    let rounds = if xtea {
        a.int("rounds")?.clamp(1, 1024) as u32
    } else {
        32
    };
    const DELTA: u32 = 0x9E37_79B9;
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(input.len());
    for block in input.chunks(8) {
        let (mut v0, mut v1) = (word(&block[..4]), word(&block[4..]));
        if xtea {
            let mut sum = DELTA.wrapping_mul(rounds);
            for _ in 0..rounds {
                v1 = v1.wrapping_sub(
                    ((v0 << 4 ^ v0 >> 5).wrapping_add(v0))
                        ^ sum.wrapping_add(k[(sum >> 11 & 3) as usize]),
                );
                sum = sum.wrapping_sub(DELTA);
                v0 = v0.wrapping_sub(
                    ((v1 << 4 ^ v1 >> 5).wrapping_add(v1))
                        ^ sum.wrapping_add(k[(sum & 3) as usize]),
                );
            }
        } else {
            let mut sum = DELTA.wrapping_mul(32);
            for _ in 0..32 {
                v1 = v1.wrapping_sub(
                    (v0 << 4).wrapping_add(k[2])
                        ^ v0.wrapping_add(sum)
                        ^ (v0 >> 5).wrapping_add(k[3]),
                );
                v0 = v0.wrapping_sub(
                    (v1 << 4).wrapping_add(k[0])
                        ^ v1.wrapping_add(sum)
                        ^ (v1 >> 5).wrapping_add(k[1]),
                );
                sum = sum.wrapping_sub(DELTA);
            }
        }
        for v in [v0, v1] {
            out.extend(if big {
                v.to_be_bytes()
            } else {
                v.to_le_bytes()
            });
        }
    }
    Ok(out)
}

fn inflate(input: &[u8], zlib: bool) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let result = if zlib {
        miniz_oxide::inflate::decompress_to_vec_zlib_with_limit(input, 256 << 20)
    } else {
        miniz_oxide::inflate::decompress_to_vec_with_limit(input, 256 << 20)
    };
    result.map_err(|e| format!("not valid compressed data ({:?})", e.status))
}

fn gunzip(input: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    if input.len() < 18 || input[0] != 0x1f || input[1] != 0x8b || input[2] != 8 {
        return Err("not gzip data (gzip starts with 1F 8B 08)".into());
    }
    let flags = input[3];
    let mut pos = 10;
    if flags & 4 != 0 {
        let extra = usize::from(u16::from_le_bytes([input[pos], input[pos + 1]]));
        pos += 2 + extra;
    }
    for flag in [8u8, 16] {
        if flags & flag != 0 {
            while *input.get(pos).ok_or("truncated gzip header")? != 0 {
                pos += 1;
            }
            pos += 1;
        }
    }
    if flags & 2 != 0 {
        pos += 2;
    }
    inflate(
        input
            .get(pos..input.len() - 8)
            .ok_or("truncated gzip data")?,
        false,
    )
}

pub fn crc32(input: &[u8]) -> u32 {
    let mut crc = !0u32;
    for &b in input {
        crc ^= u32::from(b);
        for _ in 0..8 {
            crc = if crc & 1 == 1 {
                (crc >> 1) ^ 0xEDB8_8320
            } else {
                crc >> 1
            };
        }
    }
    !crc
}

fn fnv1a32(input: &[u8]) -> u32 {
    input.iter().fold(0x811c_9dc5u32, |h, &b| {
        (h ^ u32::from(b)).wrapping_mul(0x0100_0193)
    })
}

fn ror13(input: &[u8]) -> u32 {
    input
        .iter()
        .fold(0u32, |h, &b| h.rotate_right(13).wrapping_add(u32::from(b)))
}

fn slice(input: &[u8], offset: i64, length: i64) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let start = usize::try_from(offset).map_err(|_| "offset cannot be negative")?;
    if start > input.len() {
        return Err(format!(
            "offset {start} is past the end ({} bytes)",
            input.len()
        ));
    }
    let end = if length <= 0 {
        input.len()
    } else {
        (start + length as usize).min(input.len())
    };
    Ok(input[start..end].to_vec())
}
```

`crates/orress-transforms/src/score.rs`:

```rs
//! How "readable" or meaningful bytes look, to rank automatic decoding results.

/// Known file signatures: (magic bytes, description).
const SIGNATURES: &[(&[u8], &str)] = &[
    (b"MZ", "a Windows program (PE)"),
    (b"\x7fELF", "a Linux program (ELF)"),
    (b"PK\x03\x04", "a ZIP archive"),
    (b"\x89PNG", "a PNG image"),
    (b"\xff\xd8\xff", "a JPEG image"),
    (b"GIF8", "a GIF image"),
    (b"%PDF", "a PDF document"),
    (b"\x1f\x8b", "gzip data"),
    (b"7z\xbc\xaf", "a 7-Zip archive"),
    (b"Rar!", "a RAR archive"),
    (b"\xca\xfe\xba\xbe", "a Java class or Mach-O file"),
    (b"dex\n", "Android DEX code"),
];

/// Describes the data if it starts with a known file signature.
pub fn file_type(data: &[u8]) -> Option<&'static str> {
    SIGNATURES
        .iter()
        .find(|(magic, _)| data.starts_with(magic) && data.len() > magic.len() + 8)
        .map(|(_, name)| *name)
}

const COMMON_WORDS: &[&str] = &[
    "the", "and", "flag", "password", "http", "key", "you", "this", "that", "with", "for",
    "secret", "user", "admin", "win", "correct", "ctf",
];

/// Readability score, roughly 0..=1, plus bonuses for flags and file signatures.
pub fn score(data: &[u8]) -> f32 {
    if data.is_empty() {
        return 0.0;
    }
    if file_type(data).is_some() {
        return 1.5;
    }
    let len = data.len() as f32;
    let printable = data
        .iter()
        .filter(|&&b| (0x20..=0x7e).contains(&b) || b == b'\n' || b == b'\r' || b == b'\t')
        .count() as f32;
    let letters = data.iter().filter(|b| b.is_ascii_alphabetic()).count() as f32;
    let spaces = data.iter().filter(|&&b| b == b' ').count() as f32;
    let mut s = printable / len * 0.6 + (letters + spaces) / len * 0.3;
    // Natural text has spaces roughly every 5–6 characters.
    if (0.05..0.3).contains(&(spaces / len)) {
        s += 0.1;
    }
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(data).to_ascii_lowercase();
    let words = COMMON_WORDS.iter().filter(|w| text.contains(*w)).count();
    s += (words as f32 * 0.05).min(0.2);
    if orress_bytes::strings::looks_like_flag(&text) {
        s += 1.0;
    }
    s
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn text_beats_noise() {
        let text = score(b"The password is hunter2, keep it secret.");
        let noise = score(&[0x8f, 0x12, 0xa0, 0x33, 0xfe, 0x01, 0x77, 0x90]);
        assert!(text > 0.8 && noise < 0.3, "{text} {noise}");
        assert!(score(b"flag{x0r_is_fun}") > 1.0);
        assert_eq!(
            file_type(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n0000000000"),
            Some("a PNG image")
        );
    }
}
```
