`crates/orress-transforms/src/tests.rs`:

```rs
use crate::*;

fn run(recipe: &str, input: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    Recipe::parse(recipe)
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{recipe}: {e}"))
        .output(input)
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{recipe}: {e}"))
}

#[test]
fn encodings_round_trip() {
    let data: Vec<u8> = (0..=255).collect();
    for (enc, dec) in [
        ("to_hex", "from_hex"),
        ("to_base64", "from_base64"),
        ("to_base32", "from_base32"),
        ("to_base58", "from_base58"),
        ("to_url", "from_url"),
        ("to_escaped", "from_escaped"),
    ] {
        assert_eq!(run(&format!("{enc} | {dec}"), &data), data, "{enc}");
    }
    assert_eq!(run("to_base58", b"\0\0abc"), b"11ZiCa");
    assert_eq!(run("to_base64", b"hello"), b"aGVsbG8=");
    assert_eq!(
        run("from_base64", b"aGVsbG8"),
        b"hello",
        "missing padding is fine"
    );
    assert_eq!(run("to_base32", b"hi"), b"NBUQ====");
    assert_eq!(run("from_hex", b"\\x48\\x69, 0x21"), b"Hi!");
    assert_eq!(
        run("utf8_to_utf16le | utf16le_to_utf8", "héllo".as_bytes()),
        "héllo".as_bytes()
    );
}

#[test]
fn custom_base64_alphabet() {
    // A shuffled alphabet, as CTF challenges and malware like to use.
    let alphabet = "ZYXWVUTSRQPONMLKJIHGFEDCBAzyxwvutsrqponmlkjihgfedcba9876543210+/";
    let encoded = run(&format!("to_base64 alphabet={alphabet}"), b"secret");
    assert_ne!(encoded, b"c2VjcmV0");
    assert_eq!(
        run(&format!("from_base64 alphabet={alphabet}"), &encoded),
        b"secret"
    );
    assert!(
        Recipe::parse("from_base64 alphabet=abc")
            .unwrap()
            .output(b"x")
            .is_err()
    );
}

#[test]
fn url_and_escape_decoding_never_panic_on_separators() {
    // `from_hex` strips separators, so "% ," used to become an empty Vec and
    // the decoders indexed `[0]` → panic. These must be clean errors.
    for (op, input) in [
        ("from_url", &b"100% , done"[..]),
        ("from_url", b"%0x"),
        ("from_url", b"%,,"),
        ("from_escaped", b"\\x0x"),
        ("from_escaped", b"\\x ,"),
        ("from_escaped", b"\\x\\x"),
    ] {
        let recipe = Recipe::parse(op).unwrap();
        assert!(recipe.output(input).is_err(), "{op} {input:?}");
    }
    assert_eq!(run("from_url", b"a%41+b"), b"aA b");
    assert_eq!(run("from_escaped", b"\\x41\\x4a"), b"AJ");
    // magic() on prose containing '%' must not panic either.
    let _ = magic(b"100% , done and 50%x complete", 2);
}

#[test]
fn base64_padding_resets_alignment() {
    assert_eq!(run("from_base64", b"QQ==QQ=="), b"AA");
    assert_eq!(run("from_base64", b"aGk=aGk="), b"hihi");
    // A custom alphabet that uses '=' as a digit must decode it as a digit.
    let alphabet = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789=/";
    let encoded = crate::codec::to_base64(b"\xfb\xff", alphabet, false).unwrap();
    assert!(encoded.contains(&b'='));
    assert_eq!(
        crate::codec::from_base64(&encoded, alphabet).unwrap(),
        b"\xfb\xff"
    );
}

#[test]
fn xor_and_friends() {
    assert_eq!(run("xor key=0x01", b"AB"), b"@C");
    assert_eq!(run("xor key=key | xor key=key", b"secret"), b"secret");
    assert_eq!(run("xor key=hex:00ff", &[1, 1]), vec![1, 0xfe]);
    assert_eq!(run("rol bits=1 | ror bits=1", b"z"), b"z");
    assert_eq!(run("add value=1 | sub value=1", b"z"), b"z");
    assert_eq!(run("not", &[0x0f]), vec![0xf0]);
    assert_eq!(run("swap_endian width=4", &[1, 2, 3, 4]), vec![4, 3, 2, 1]);
    assert_eq!(run("rot13 | rot13", b"Hello"), b"Hello");
    assert_eq!(run("caesar shift=1", b"abz"), b"bca");
    // Known-plaintext key recovery.
    let encrypted = run("xor key=K3y", b"flag{known_plaintext}");
    let out = run("xor_known known=flag{", &encrypted);
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out);
    assert!(text.starts_with("key: 0x4b3379"), "{text}");
    assert!(text.contains("flag{known_plaintext}"));
}

#[test]
fn crypto_known_answers() {
    // RC4 test vector: key "Key", plaintext "Plaintext".
    assert_eq!(
        run("rc4 key=Key | to_hex separator=", b"Plaintext"),
        b"bbf316e8d940af0ad3"
    );
    // AES-128 ECB, FIPS-197 appendix C.1.
    let ct = run(
        "aes_encrypt key=0x000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f mode=ECB padding=none | to_hex separator=",
        &codec::from_hex(b"00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff").unwrap(),
    );
    assert_eq!(ct, b"69c4e0d86a7b0430d8cdb78070b4c55a");
    // CBC and CTR round trips with padding.
    for mode in ["CBC", "CTR"] {
        let key = "0x2b7e151628aed2a6abf7158809cf4f3c";
        let iv = "0x000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f";
        let r = format!(
            "aes_encrypt key={key} iv={iv} mode={mode} | aes_decrypt key={key} iv={iv} mode={mode}"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            run(&r, b"a secret message!"),
            b"a secret message!",
            "{mode}"
        );
    }
    // Wrong key gives a clear padding error.
    let enc = run(
        "aes_encrypt key=0x00000000000000000000000000000000",
        b"hello",
    );
    assert!(
        Recipe::parse("aes_decrypt key=0x11111111111111111111111111111111")
            .unwrap()
            .output(&enc)
            .unwrap_err()
            .contains("padding")
    );
}

#[test]
fn tea_and_xtea_decrypt_known_vectors() {
    // XTEA, 32 rounds, all-zero key and block (big-endian words):
    // ciphertext DEE9D4D8F7131ED9 decrypts to zeros.
    let out = run(
        "xtea_decrypt key=0x00000000000000000000000000000000 endian=big",
        &codec::from_hex(b"dee9d4d8f7131ed9").unwrap(),
    );
    assert_eq!(out, vec![0; 8]);
    // TEA, zero key and block: ciphertext 41EA3A0A94BAA940 (big-endian words).
    let out = run(
        "tea_decrypt key=0x00000000000000000000000000000000 endian=big",
        &codec::from_hex(b"41ea3a0a94baa940").unwrap(),
    );
    assert_eq!(out, vec![0; 8]);
}

#[test]
fn compression_and_hashes() {
    let text = b"compress me compress me compress me".repeat(10);
    assert_eq!(run("zlib_deflate | zlib_inflate", &text), text);
    // gzip of "hi\n" (from the gzip tool).
    let gz = codec::from_hex(b"1f8b08000000000000ffcbc8e40200d78d2e7a03000000").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(run("gzip_decompress", &gz), b"hi\n");
    assert_eq!(run("md5", b"abc"), b"900150983cd24fb0d6963f7d28e17f72");
    assert_eq!(run("crc32", b"123456789"), b"cbf43926");
    assert_eq!(run("fnv1a32", b"a"), b"e40c292c");
    // ROR13 of "LoadLibraryA" is the well-known shellcode constant 0xec0e4e8e.
    assert_eq!(run("ror13", b"LoadLibraryA"), b"ec0e4e8e");
}

#[test]
fn data_ops() {
    assert_eq!(run("slice offset=2 length=3", b"abcdefg"), b"cde");
    assert_eq!(run("slice offset=4", b"abcdefg"), b"efg");
    assert_eq!(
        run("strings min=4", b"\x00\x01hello\x00world"),
        b"hello\nworld"
    );

            .unwrap()

    );

#[test]
fn recipe_text_round_trips() {
    let r = Recipe::parse("from_base64 | xor key=0x41 | caesar shift=5 | to_hex separator=\" \"")
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(r.0.len(), 4);
    let again = Recipe::parse(&r.to_string()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(again, r);
    assert!(
        Recipe::parse("nope")
            .unwrap_err()
            .contains("unknown operation")
    );
    assert!(
        Recipe::parse("xor colour=red")
            .unwrap_err()
            .contains("has no parameter")
    );
    let outputs = Recipe::parse("from_hex | from_base64").unwrap().run(b"zz");
    assert_eq!(outputs.len(), 1, "stops at the first error");
    assert!(outputs[0].is_err());
}

#[test]
fn every_op_is_documented_and_runs_on_empty_input() {
    for op in ops() {
        assert!(!op.explain.is_empty(), "{}", op.id);
        // Must not panic on empty or odd input; errors are fine.
        let _ = Step::new(op.id).apply(b"");
        let _ = Step::new(op.id).apply(&[0xff; 7]);
    }
}

#[test]
fn magic_finds_layered_encodings() {
    // base64(xor(flag, 0x5a))
    let encrypted = run("xor key=0x5a | to_base64", b"flag{magic_decoding_works}");
    let suggestions = magic(&encrypted, 3);
    let best = &suggestions[0];
    assert_eq!(
        String::from_utf8_lossy(&best.output),
        "flag{magic_decoding_works}"
    );
    assert_eq!(best.recipe.to_string(), "from_base64 | xor key=0x5a");

    // hex(zlib(text))
    let compressed = run(
        "zlib_deflate | to_hex",
        b"the password is swordfish and the user is admin",
    );
    let s = magic(&compressed, 3);
    assert_eq!(
        s[0].output,
        b"the password is swordfish and the user is admin"
    );

    // Already readable text: nothing much to suggest, and no panic.
    let _ = magic(b"just some normal text here", 3);
    let _ = magic(&[], 3);
}

`crates/orress-triage/src/capa.rs`:

```rs
//! Capability detection, capa-style: named, human-readable capabilities inferred from the
//! combination of imported APIs and strings a sample contains, each with the evidence that
//! triggered it and a MITRE ATT&CK technique. This is a defensive triage aid — it labels what a
//! sample *can* do so an analyst can confirm; nothing is executed.

use std::collections::BTreeSet;

/// A detected capability with the evidence behind it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Capability {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub namespace: &'static str,
    pub attack: &'static str,
    pub evidence: Vec<String>,
}

/// A matching condition over a sample's imports and strings.
enum Cond {
    /// At least one of these API names is imported.
    ApiAny(&'static [&'static str]),
    /// All of these API names are imported.
    ApiAll(&'static [&'static str]),
    /// At least one of these substrings appears in a string (case-insensitive).
    StrAny(&'static [&'static str]),
    /// Any sub-condition matches.
    Any(&'static [Cond]),
}

struct Rule {
    name: &'static str,
    namespace: &'static str,
    attack: &'static str,
    cond: Cond,
}

/// Normalises an API name for matching: drop a leading `_`, a stdcall `@N` suffix and a trailing
/// A/W wideness suffix, lower-cased.
fn norm_api(name: &str) -> String {
    let n = name.trim_start_matches('_');
    let n = n.split('@').next().unwrap_or(n);
    let n = n
        .strip_suffix('A')
        .or_else(|| n.strip_suffix('W'))
        .unwrap_or(n);
    n.to_ascii_lowercase()
}

/// Evaluates a condition, returning the matched evidence if it holds.
fn eval(
    cond: &Cond,
    imports: &[(String, String)],
    strings_lc: &[(String, &str)],
) -> Option<Vec<String>> {
    match cond {
        Cond::ApiAny(names) => {
            let want: BTreeSet<String> = names.iter().map(|n| norm_api(n)).collect();
            let matched: Vec<String> = imports
                .iter()
                .filter(|(n, _)| want.contains(n))
                .map(|(_, orig)| orig.clone())
                .collect();
            (!matched.is_empty()).then_some(matched)
        }
        Cond::ApiAll(names) => {
            let mut evidence = Vec::new();
            for name in *names {
                let target = norm_api(name);
                let found = imports.iter().find(|(n, _)| *n == target);
                match found {
                    Some((_, orig)) => evidence.push(orig.clone()),
                    None => return None,
                }
            }
            Some(evidence)
        }
        Cond::StrAny(subs) => {
            let mut evidence = Vec::new();
            for sub in *subs {
                let needle = sub.to_ascii_lowercase();
                if let Some((_, orig)) = strings_lc.iter().find(|(lc, _)| lc.contains(&needle)) {
                    evidence.push(format!("\"{}\"", truncate(orig)));
                }
            }
            (!evidence.is_empty()).then_some(evidence)
        }
        Cond::Any(conds) => {
            let mut evidence = Vec::new();
            for c in *conds {
                if let Some(e) = eval(c, imports, strings_lc) {
                    evidence.extend(e);
                }
            }
            (!evidence.is_empty()).then_some(evidence)
        }
    }
}

fn truncate(s: &str) -> String {
    if s.chars().count() > 48 {
        format!("{}…", s.chars().take(48).collect::<String>())
    } else {
        s.to_string()
    }
}

/// Detects capabilities from the sample's imported API names and strings.
pub fn detect(imports: &[&str], strings: &[&str]) -> Vec<Capability> {
    let imp: Vec<(String, String)> = imports
        .iter()
        .map(|&n| (norm_api(n), n.to_string()))
        .collect();
    let strings_lc: Vec<(String, &str)> = strings
        .iter()
        .map(|&s| (s.to_ascii_lowercase(), s))
        .collect();

    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for rule in RULES {
        if let Some(mut evidence) = eval(&rule.cond, &imp, &strings_lc) {
            evidence.sort();
            evidence.dedup();
            out.push(Capability {
                name: rule.name,
                namespace: rule.namespace,
                attack: rule.attack,
                evidence,
            });
        }
    }
    out
}

use Cond::{Any, ApiAll, ApiAny, StrAny};

/// The built-in capability rule set.

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

`crates/orress-triage/src/config.rs`:

```rs
//! A small, pluggable config-extractor framework. Each extractor recognises a malware family's
//! embedded configuration (C2 servers, keys, campaign ids, mutexes) and returns it as labelled
//! fields. New families are added by implementing [`ConfigExtractor`]; two examples ship here —
//! one signature-based (a documented demo family) and one generic heuristic.
//!
//! **No real malware-family extractors ship yet.** The built-in set is the `ExampleRAT` demo
//! (which only matches samples built for it, such as ORRESS's own test fixtures) plus a
//! `host:port` endpoint heuristic, so an empty result says nothing about whether a sample carries
//! a config — it only means neither of those two recognisers fired.
//!
//! Static, read-only: extractors parse bytes/strings the analyst already has.

use std::sync::OnceLock;

use orress_loaders::BinaryInfo;
use regex::Regex;

/// One key/value field of an extracted configuration.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ConfigField {
    pub key: String,
    pub value: String,
}

/// A configuration recovered from a sample.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Config {
    pub family: String,
    pub fields: Vec<ConfigField>,
    /// How the config was obtained (signature match, heuristic, …).
    pub note: String,
}

/// Recognises and extracts one family's configuration.
pub trait ConfigExtractor: Send + Sync {
    fn family(&self) -> &'static str;
    /// Returns the config if this sample matches the family.
    fn extract(&self, info: &BinaryInfo, data: &[u8], strings: &[&str]) -> Option<Config>;
}

/// Runs every registered extractor and collects the configs that matched.
pub fn run_all(info: &BinaryInfo, data: &[u8], strings: &[&str]) -> Vec<Config> {
    extractors()
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|e| e.extract(info, data, strings))
        .collect()
}

/// The built-in extractor set.
fn extractors() -> &'static [Box<dyn ConfigExtractor>] {
    static E: OnceLock<Vec<Box<dyn ConfigExtractor>>> = OnceLock::new();
    E.get_or_init(|| {
        vec![
            Box::new(ExampleRat) as Box<dyn ConfigExtractor>,
            Box::new(GenericC2Endpoints),
        ]
    })
    .as_slice()
}

fn field(key: &str, value: impl Into<String>) -> ConfigField {
    ConfigField {
        key: key.to_string(),
        value: value.into(),
    }
}

// --- Example 1: a signature-based extractor for a demo family -------------

/// Extractor for the demo family **ExampleRAT**. Its config is the marker `ORCFG`, a 2-byte
/// little-endian length, then that many `0x5A`-XOR-encoded bytes of `key=value;` text. Real
/// family extractors (AgentTesla, Remcos, …) follow this shape: find a signature, decode, parse.
struct ExampleRat;

const EXAMPLE_KEY: u8 = 0x5a;

impl ConfigExtractor for ExampleRat {
    fn family(&self) -> &'static str {
        "ExampleRAT (demo)"
    }

    fn extract(&self, _info: &BinaryInfo, data: &[u8], _strings: &[&str]) -> Option<Config> {
        let marker = b"ORCFG";
        let pos = data.windows(marker.len()).position(|w| w == marker)?;
        let start = pos + marker.len();
        let len_bytes = data.get(start..start + 2)?;
        let len = u16::from_le_bytes([len_bytes[0], len_bytes[1]]) as usize;
        let blob = data.get(start + 2..start + 2 + len)?;
        let decoded: Vec<u8> = blob.iter().map(|b| b ^ EXAMPLE_KEY).collect();
        let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&decoded);
        let fields: Vec<ConfigField> = text
            .split(';')
            .filter_map(|kv| {
                let (k, v) = kv.split_once('=')?;
                (!k.trim().is_empty()).then(|| field(k.trim(), v.trim().to_string()))
            })
            .collect();
        (!fields.is_empty()).then(|| Config {
            family: self.family().to_string(),
            fields,
            note: format!("signature ORCFG at {pos:#x}, XOR 0x5A"),
        })
    }
}

// --- Example 2: a generic heuristic extractor -----------------------------

/// Pulls `host:port` network endpoints out of the sample's strings (IPs and domains with an
/// explicit port) — the actionable form a C2 config usually takes.
struct GenericC2Endpoints;

fn endpoint_re() -> &'static Regex {
    static R: OnceLock<Regex> = OnceLock::new();
    R.get_or_init(|| {
        Regex::new(
            r"(?i)\b(?:(?:\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}|[a-z0-9][a-z0-9\-]*(?:\.[a-z0-9\-]+)+):\d{2,5}\b",
        )
        .unwrap()
    })
}

impl ConfigExtractor for GenericC2Endpoints {
    fn family(&self) -> &'static str {
        "Network endpoints (heuristic)"
    }

    fn extract(&self, _info: &BinaryInfo, _data: &[u8], strings: &[&str]) -> Option<Config> {
        let re = endpoint_re();
        let mut seen = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
        for s in strings {
            for m in re.find_iter(s) {
                let ep = m.as_str();
                // Drop obvious version strings like "1.2.3:4" where the port looks like a build.
                if valid_endpoint(ep) {
                    seen.insert(ep.to_string());
                }
            }
        }
        (!seen.is_empty()).then(|| Config {
            family: self.family().to_string(),
            fields: seen.into_iter().map(|ep| field("endpoint", ep)).collect(),
            note: "host:port patterns in strings".into(),
        })
    }
}

/// Accepts an endpoint only if its IPv4 octets (if any) and port are in range.
fn valid_endpoint(ep: &str) -> bool {
    let Some((host, port)) = ep.rsplit_once(':') else {
        return false;
    };
    if port.parse::<u32>().is_ok_and(|p| p == 0 || p > 65535) {
        return false;
    }
    // If the host is dotted-decimal, validate octets.
    if host.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit() || c == '.') {
        return host.split('.').count() == 4
            && host
                .split('.')
                .all(|o| o.parse::<u16>().is_ok_and(|n| n <= 255));
    }
    true
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// Encodes an ExampleRAT config blob for testing (marker + len + XOR'd text).
    fn example_blob(text: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut out = b"junk before ORCFG".to_vec();
        let enc: Vec<u8> = text.bytes().map(|b| b ^ EXAMPLE_KEY).collect();
        out.extend_from_slice(&(enc.len() as u16).to_le_bytes());
        out.extend_from_slice(&enc);
        out.extend_from_slice(b"junk after");
        out
    }

    #[test]
    fn extracts_example_rat_config() {
        let data = example_blob("c2=evil.example.com;port=4444;campaign=spring2026;mutex=ORX-01");
        let info = BinaryInfo::default();
        let configs = run_all(&info, &data, &[]);
        let rat = configs
            .iter()
            .find(|c| c.family.starts_with("ExampleRAT"))
            .expect("ExampleRAT config");
        assert!(rat.fields.contains(&field("c2", "evil.example.com")));
        assert!(rat.fields.contains(&field("campaign", "spring2026")));
    }

    #[test]
    fn extracts_generic_endpoints() {
        let info = BinaryInfo::default();
        let strings = [
            "beacon 192.168.10.5:8080",
            "fallback: c2.bad.example:443",
            "ver 1.2.3",

        let net = configs
            .iter()
            .find(|c| c.family.starts_with("Network"))

        assert!(values.contains(&"c2.bad.example:443"));
    }

    #[test]

        let info = BinaryInfo::default();

    }

`crates/orress-triage/src/fuzzy.rs`:

```rs
//! Fuzzy (similarity) hashes for a sample: TLSH and ssdeep. Unlike cryptographic hashes, these
//! stay close for files that are *similar*, so they're used to cluster variants of a family and
//! to look a sample up in a corpus. Both implementations here are pure Rust.

/// A sample's fuzzy hashes (TLSH needs ~50+ bytes with some variance, so it can be absent).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct FuzzyHashes {
    pub tlsh: Option<String>,
    pub ssdeep: String,
}

/// Computes the fuzzy hashes of `data`.
pub fn compute(data: &[u8]) -> FuzzyHashes {
    let tlsh = tlsh2::TlshDefaultBuilder::build_from(data)
        .map(|t| String::from_utf8_lossy(&t.hash()).into_owned());
    let ssdeep = fuzzyhash::FuzzyHash::new(data).to_string();
    FuzzyHashes { tlsh, ssdeep }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn computes_both_for_a_real_buffer() {
        // A varied 4 KiB buffer, enough for TLSH.
        let data: Vec<u8> = (0..4096u32)
            .map(|i| (i.wrapping_mul(2654435761) >> 13) as u8)
            .collect();
        let f = compute(&data);
        assert!(f.tlsh.is_some(), "TLSH should compute for a 4 KiB buffer");
        assert!(f.tlsh.as_ref().unwrap().starts_with('T'));
        assert!(!f.ssdeep.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn tlsh_absent_for_tiny_input() {
        let f = compute(b"too small");
        assert!(f.tlsh.is_none());
    }
}

`crates/orress-triage/src/hints.rs`:

```rs
//! A graded-hint engine for CTF/crackme challenges. From a sample's triage [`Report`] it infers
//! what *kind* of challenge it is and produces **graded hints** — a nudge, then a direction, then
//! a near-solution — so a learner is pointed forward without the answer being spoiled. Rule-based
//! (no model), so it is deterministic and testable.

use orress_loaders::apis::ApiCategory;
use orress_loaders::{BinaryInfo, DetectionCategory};

use crate::Report;

/// How much a hint gives away.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum HintLevel {
    /// A gentle push in the right direction.
    Nudge,
    /// What to look for and roughly how.
    Direction,
    /// Almost the answer.
    Solution,
}

impl HintLevel {
    pub fn label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Nudge => "Nudge",
            Self::Direction => "Direction",
            Self::Solution => "Near solution",
        }
    }
}

/// One graded hint.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Hint {
    pub level: HintLevel,
    pub text: String,
}

/// The inferred challenge category.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ChallengeKind {
    Packed,
    Crypto,
    AntiDebug,
    Network,
    StringCompare,
    Generic,
}

impl ChallengeKind {
    fn describe(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Packed => {
                "a packed or encrypted binary — the real code is hidden until it's unpacked"
            }
            Self::Crypto => "a crypto challenge built around a known algorithm",
            Self::AntiDebug => "a challenge that resists debugging",
            Self::Network => "a sample that talks to the network (often for a C2 or the flag)",
            Self::StringCompare => "a password/flag check that compares your input against a value",
            Self::Generic => "a reverse-engineering challenge",
        }
    }
}

/// The classification and graded hints for a sample.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Challenge {
    pub kind: ChallengeKind,
    /// A one-line "this looks like …" summary.
    pub summary: String,
    /// Graded hints, easiest first.
    pub hints: Vec<Hint>,
    /// Suggested techniques/tools to try.
    pub techniques: Vec<&'static str>,
}

fn looks_like_flag(s: &str) -> bool {
    let l = s.to_ascii_lowercase();
    l.contains("flag{") || l.contains("ctf{") || l.contains("key{") || l.contains("flag_")
}

/// Classifies a sample from its triage report and produces graded hints.
pub fn analyze(report: &Report, info: &BinaryInfo, strings: &[&str]) -> Challenge {
    let has = |c: ApiCategory| report.behaviors.iter().any(|b| b.category == c);
    let packed = info.entropy > 7.2
        || info
            .detections
            .iter()
            .any(|d| d.category == DetectionCategory::Packer);

    let flag = strings
        .iter()
        .find(|s| looks_like_flag(s))
        .map(|s| s.to_string());

    // Most salient classification first.
    let kind = if packed {
        ChallengeKind::Packed
    } else if has(ApiCategory::Crypto) {
        ChallengeKind::Crypto
    } else if has(ApiCategory::AntiDebug) {
        ChallengeKind::AntiDebug
    } else if has(ApiCategory::Network) {
        ChallengeKind::Network
    } else if has(ApiCategory::Compare) {
        ChallengeKind::StringCompare
    } else {
        ChallengeKind::Generic
    };

    let mut hints = Vec::new();
    // A plaintext flag already present is a near-solution regardless of kind.
    if let Some(f) = &flag {
        hints.push(Hint {
            level: HintLevel::Solution,
            text: format!(
                "A flag-format string is already in the binary: `{f}` — check the Strings view."
            ),
        });
    }
    hints.extend(kind_hints(kind));

    let flag_note = if flag.is_some() {
        " There's also a flag-looking string in it."
    } else {
        ""
    };
    Challenge {
        kind,
        summary: format!("This looks like {}.{flag_note}", kind.describe()),
        hints,
        techniques: techniques(kind),
    }
}

fn hint(level: HintLevel, text: &str) -> Hint {
    Hint {
        level,
        text: text.to_string(),
    }
}

fn kind_hints(kind: ChallengeKind) -> Vec<Hint> {
    use ChallengeKind::*;
    use HintLevel::*;
    match kind {
        Packed => vec![
            hint(
                Nudge,
                "The file looks packed or encrypted (high entropy or a known packer). You won't see the real logic until it's unpacked.",
            ),
            hint(
                Direction,
                "Find the original entry point: run it under the debugger and break after the unpacking stub (often a tail jump into another section), or step it in the Emulator.",
            ),
            hint(
                Solution,
                "Dump the unpacked image from memory once execution reaches the OEP, then re-analyze the dump. For UPX, `upx -d` restores it directly.",
            ),
        ],
        Crypto => vec![
            hint(
                Nudge,
                "Cryptographic constants were found — a known algorithm is involved.",
            ),
            hint(
                Direction,
                "Identify the algorithm from its constants (AES S-box, SHA/MD5 IVs, TEA delta, RC4 KSA, ChaCha \"expand 32-byte k\"), then find where the key and your input meet.",
            ),
            hint(
                Solution,
                "Recover the key/IV from the code or data and run the matching transform in the Workbench to decrypt.",
            ),
        ],
        AntiDebug => vec![
            hint(Nudge, "The program checks whether it's being debugged."),
            hint(
                Direction,
                "Locate the anti-debug check (IsDebuggerPresent, a PEB flag, ptrace, or a timing check) and see what branch it controls.",
            ),
            hint(
                Solution,
                "Patch the check to always take the \"not debugged\" path — invert the jump or NOP it — then continue.",
            ),
        ],
        Network => vec![
            hint(Nudge, "This sample talks to the network."),
            hint(
                Direction,
                "Follow the network APIs to the host/port and protocol; the C2 or the flag source is often in the strings or an embedded config.",
            ),
            hint(
                Solution,
                "Point it at the Sandbox fake network to capture its requests, or extract the endpoint from the config/strings directly.",
            ),
        ],
        StringCompare => vec![
            hint(
                Nudge,
                "Your input is compared against something — likely a password or flag check.",
            ),
            hint(
                Direction,
                "Break on the comparison (strcmp/strncmp/memcmp) and read the expected value, or look for a suspicious constant string.",
            ),
            hint(
                Solution,
                "The compared value is the answer — read it from the strings/data or the register at the compare. If it's computed (e.g. XOR with a key), recover it with the Emulator's side-channel solver or the symbolic solver.",
            ),
        ],
        Generic => vec![
            hint(
                Nudge,
                "Start from the strings and imports to form a hypothesis about what the program does.",
            ),
            hint(
                Direction,
                "Find `main`, follow how it reads your input, and locate the success/failure branch.",
            ),
            hint(
                Solution,
                "Work backward from the \"correct!\" message to the condition that guards it, and satisfy that condition.",
            ),
        ],
    }
}

fn techniques(kind: ChallengeKind) -> Vec<&'static str> {
    use ChallengeKind::*;
    match kind {
        Packed => vec!["unpacking", "debugger", "entropy map", "memory dump"],
        Crypto => vec![
            "crypto-constant detection",
            "Workbench transforms",
            "trace key setup",
        ],
        AntiDebug => vec!["anti-analysis detection", "patch & go", "debugger"],
        Network => vec![
            "IOC extraction",
            "fake network (Sandbox)",
            "config extractor",
        ],
        StringCompare => vec![
            "strings",
            "breakpoint on strcmp",
            "side-channel solver",
            "symbolic solver",
        ],
        Generic => vec!["strings", "functions", "disassembly", "decompiler"],
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod hint_tests {
    use super::*;
    use orress_loaders::Import;

    fn imp(name: &str) -> Import {
        Import {
            library: "k.dll".into(),
            name: name.into(),
        }
    }

    fn challenge(info: BinaryInfo, strings: &[&str]) -> Challenge {
        let report = crate::build(&info, strings, b"data");
        analyze(&report, &info, strings)
    }

    #[test]
    fn classifies_packed_by_entropy() {
        let info = BinaryInfo {
            entropy: 7.9,
            ..Default::default()
        };
        let c = challenge(info, &[]);
        assert_eq!(c.kind, ChallengeKind::Packed);
        // Three graded hints, in order.
        let levels: Vec<HintLevel> = c.hints.iter().map(|h| h.level).collect();
        assert_eq!(
            levels,
            [HintLevel::Nudge, HintLevel::Direction, HintLevel::Solution]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn classifies_network() {
        let info = BinaryInfo {
            imports: vec![imp("InternetOpenA"), imp("send")],
            ..Default::default()
        };
        let c = challenge(info, &["GET http://c2.example/gate"]);
        assert_eq!(c.kind, ChallengeKind::Network);
    }

    #[test]
    fn classifies_string_compare_and_finds_flag() {
        let info = BinaryInfo {
            imports: vec![imp("strcmp")],
            ..Default::default()
        };
        let c = challenge(info, &["enter password:", "flag{h1nt_eng1ne}"]);
        assert_eq!(c.kind, ChallengeKind::StringCompare);
        // The plaintext flag surfaces as the first, near-solution hint.
        assert_eq!(c.hints[0].level, HintLevel::Solution);
        assert!(c.hints[0].text.contains("flag{h1nt_eng1ne}"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn generic_when_nothing_stands_out() {
        let info = BinaryInfo {
            imports: vec![imp("printf")],
            ..Default::default()
        };
        let c = challenge(info, &["hello"]);
        assert_eq!(c.kind, ChallengeKind::Generic);
        assert_eq!(c.hints.len(), 3);
        assert!(!c.techniques.is_empty());
    }
}

`crates/orress-triage/src/ioc.rs`:

```rs
//! Indicator-of-compromise extraction from a sample's strings: URLs, domains, IPv4 addresses,
//! emails, registry keys, file paths, named-object namespaces (mutexes/events) and crypto wallet
//! addresses. Values can be defanged for safe sharing (`http` → `hxxp`, `.` → `[.]`).

use std::collections::BTreeSet;

use regex::Regex;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub enum IocKind {
    Url,
    Domain,
    Ipv4,
    Email,
    RegistryKey,
    FilePath,
    Namespace,
    CryptoWallet,
}

impl IocKind {
    pub fn label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Url => "URLs",
            Self::Domain => "Domains",
            Self::Ipv4 => "IPv4 addresses",
            Self::Email => "Emails",
            Self::RegistryKey => "Registry keys",
            Self::FilePath => "File paths",
            Self::Namespace => "Named objects (mutex/event)",
            Self::CryptoWallet => "Crypto wallets",
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub struct Ioc {
    pub kind: IocKind,
    pub value: String,
}

struct Patterns {
    url: Regex,
    email: Regex,
    ipv4: Regex,
    domain: Regex,
    registry: Regex,
    win_path: Regex,
    env_path: Regex,
    unc_path: Regex,
    namespace: Regex,
    btc: Regex,
    eth: Regex,
}

fn patterns() -> &'static Patterns {
    use std::sync::OnceLock;
    static P: OnceLock<Patterns> = OnceLock::new();
    P.get_or_init(|| Patterns {
        url: Regex::new(r#"(?i)\b(?:https?|ftp)://[^\s"'<>\)\]]+"#).unwrap(),
        email: Regex::new(r"\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+\-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.\-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\b").unwrap(),
        ipv4: Regex::new(r"\b(?:\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}\b").unwrap(),
        domain: Regex::new(r"(?i)\b(?:[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9\-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?\.)+[a-z]{2,24}\b")
            .unwrap(),
        registry: Regex::new(r#"(?i)\b(?:HKEY_[A-Z_]+|HKLM|HKCU|HKCR|HKU)\\[^\s"'<>]+"#).unwrap(),
        win_path: Regex::new(r#"\b[A-Za-z]:\\[^\s"'<>|*?]+"#).unwrap(),
        env_path: Regex::new(r#"%[A-Za-z0-9_]+%[\\/][^\s"'<>|*?]*"#).unwrap(),
        unc_path: Regex::new(r#"\\\\[A-Za-z0-9._\-]+\\[^\s"'<>|*?]+"#).unwrap(),
        namespace: Regex::new(r#"(?i)\b(?:Global|Local|Session)\\[^\s"'<>]+"#).unwrap(),
        btc: Regex::new(r"\b(?:bc1[ac-hj-np-z02-9]{11,71}|[13][1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{25,34})\b")
            .unwrap(),
        eth: Regex::new(r"\b0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}\b").unwrap(),
    })
}

/// File-looking "domains" that are almost always module names, not network hosts.
fn is_module_name(s: &str) -> bool {
    let lower = s.to_ascii_lowercase();
    const EXTS: &[&str] = &[
        // Binary / data / config files that look like `name.tld`.
        ".dll", ".exe", ".sys", ".drv", ".ocx", ".cpl", ".scr", ".bin", ".dat", ".tmp", ".log",
        ".txt", ".ini", ".cfg", ".obj", ".lib", ".pdb", ".so",
        // Source-file extensions that collide with TLDs (common in compiler/debug strings,
        // e.g. a Rust binary is full of `fmt.rs`, `mod.rs`). Kept out of network IOCs.
        ".rs", ".go", ".py", ".pyc", ".rb", ".c", ".h", ".cpp", ".hpp", ".cs", ".java", ".pl",
        ".rc", ".s", ".asm", ".inc", ".md", ".toml", ".json", ".xml", ".html", ".css",
    ];
    EXTS.iter().any(|e| lower.ends_with(e))
}

fn octets_valid(ip: &str) -> bool {
    ip.split('.')
        .all(|o| o.parse::<u16>().is_ok_and(|n| n <= 255))
}

/// Extracts and de-duplicates IOCs from `strings`.
pub fn extract(strings: &[&str]) -> Vec<Ioc> {
    let p = patterns();
    let mut set: BTreeSet<Ioc> = BTreeSet::new();
    let mut add = |kind: IocKind, value: &str| {
        set.insert(Ioc {
            kind,
            value: value.to_string(),
        });
    };
    for s in strings {
        // Spans already reported as a URL or email, so their hosts aren't repeated as domains.
        let mut covered: Vec<std::ops::Range<usize>> = Vec::new();
        for m in p.url.find_iter(s) {
            add(IocKind::Url, m.as_str().trim_end_matches(['.', ',', ';']));
            covered.push(m.range());
        }
        for m in p.email.find_iter(s) {
            add(IocKind::Email, m.as_str());
            covered.push(m.range());
        }
        for m in p.ipv4.find_iter(s) {
            if octets_valid(m.as_str()) {
                add(IocKind::Ipv4, m.as_str());
            }
        }
        for m in p.registry.find_iter(s) {
            add(IocKind::RegistryKey, m.as_str());
        }
        for m in p.win_path.find_iter(s) {
            add(IocKind::FilePath, m.as_str());
        }
        for m in p.env_path.find_iter(s) {
            add(IocKind::FilePath, m.as_str());
        }
        for m in p.unc_path.find_iter(s) {
            add(IocKind::FilePath, m.as_str());
        }
        for m in p.namespace.find_iter(s) {
            add(IocKind::Namespace, m.as_str());
        }
        for m in p.btc.find_iter(s) {
            add(IocKind::CryptoWallet, m.as_str());
        }
        for m in p.eth.find_iter(s) {
            add(IocKind::CryptoWallet, m.as_str());
        }
        // Domains last, skipping ones already captured as a URL/email host or module name.
        for m in p.domain.find_iter(s) {
            let d = m.as_str();
            let in_url_or_email = covered
                .iter()
                .any(|r| m.start() < r.end && r.start < m.end());
            if in_url_or_email || is_module_name(d) || octets_valid(d) {
                continue;
            }
            add(IocKind::Domain, d);
        }
    }
    set.into_iter().collect()
}

/// Defangs an IOC value for safe display/sharing.
pub fn defang(value: &str) -> String {
    value
        .replace("http", "hxxp")
        .replace("HTTP", "HXXP")
        .replace("://", "[://]")
        .replace('.', "[.]")
        .replace('@', "[@]")
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn kinds(iocs: &[Ioc], kind: IocKind) -> Vec<&str> {
        iocs.iter()
            .filter(|i| i.kind == kind)
            .map(|i| i.value.as_str())
            .collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn extracts_mixed_iocs() {
        let strings = [
            "GET http://evil.example.com/payload.bin HTTP/1.1",
            "connect to 192.168.13.37",
            "C:\\Users\\victim\\AppData\\Roaming\\svch0st.exe",
            "HKCU\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run",
            "Global\\MyEvilMutex",
            "contact: badguy@evil.example.com",
            "send BTC to 1BvBMSEYstWetqTFn5Au4m4GFg7xJaNVN2",
            "loaded kernel32.dll ok",
        ];
        let iocs = extract(&strings);
        assert!(
            kinds(&iocs, IocKind::Url)
                .iter()
                .any(|u| u.contains("evil.example.com/payload.bin"))
        );
        assert_eq!(kinds(&iocs, IocKind::Ipv4), vec!["192.168.13.37"]);
        assert!(
            kinds(&iocs, IocKind::RegistryKey)
                .iter()
                .any(|r| r.contains("CurrentVersion"))
        );
        assert!(
            kinds(&iocs, IocKind::FilePath)
                .iter()
                .any(|f| f.contains("svch0st.exe"))
        );
        assert!(
            kinds(&iocs, IocKind::Namespace)
                .iter()
                .any(|n| n.contains("MyEvilMutex"))
        );
        assert!(kinds(&iocs, IocKind::Email).contains(&"badguy@evil.example.com"));
        assert!(
            kinds(&iocs, IocKind::CryptoWallet)
                .iter()
                .any(|w| w.starts_with("1BvBM"))
        );
        // kernel32.dll must NOT be reported as a domain.
        assert!(!kinds(&iocs, IocKind::Domain).contains(&"kernel32.dll"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn source_filenames_are_not_domains() {
        // Rust/compiler debug strings are full of these — they must not pollute domain IOCs.
        let iocs = extract(&["at library/core/src/fmt.rs and mod.rs line 10"]);
        let domains = kinds(&iocs, IocKind::Domain);
        assert!(
            !domains.iter().any(|d| d.ends_with(".rs")),
            "got {domains:?}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn url_and_email_hosts_are_not_repeated_as_domains() {
        let iocs = extract(&[
            "GET http://c2.example.net/x and mail ops@drop.example.org",
            "fallback host backup.example.com",
        ]);
        assert_eq!(kinds(&iocs, IocKind::Domain), vec!["backup.example.com"]);
        assert_eq!(kinds(&iocs, IocKind::Url).len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(kinds(&iocs, IocKind::Email), vec!["ops@drop.example.org"]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn defangs() {
        assert_eq!(defang("http://evil.com"), "hxxp[://]evil[.]com");
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_bad_octets() {
        let iocs = extract(&["version 999.999.1.0 build"]);
        assert!(kinds(&iocs, IocKind::Ipv4).is_empty());
    }
}

`crates/orress-triage/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! Static malware triage: assemble a report from a file's already-computed [`BinaryInfo`]
//! (hashes, sections, imports, detections) plus IOC extraction from its strings, grouped by the
//! behaviour each import enables and mapped to MITRE ATT&CK. Pure analysis — nothing runs.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;

use orress_loaders::apis::{self, ApiCategory};
use orress_loaders::{BinaryInfo, DetectionCategory};

pub mod capa;
pub mod config;
pub mod fuzzy;
pub mod hints;
pub mod ioc;
pub mod yara;

pub use capa::Capability;
pub use config::{Config, ConfigField};
pub use fuzzy::FuzzyHashes;
pub use ioc::{Ioc, IocKind};
pub use yara::{LibHit, MemHit, MemScan, YaraHit, YaraMatch, YaraOutcome};

/// Imports that enable one behaviour.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct BehaviorGroup {
    pub category: ApiCategory,
    pub attack: &'static str,
    pub apis: Vec<String>,
    pub suspicious: bool,
}

/// A static triage report.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Report {
    /// Headline risk notes, most important first.
    pub flags: Vec<String>,
    /// Named capabilities inferred from imports + strings (capa-style).
    pub capabilities: Vec<Capability>,
    pub behaviors: Vec<BehaviorGroup>,
    pub iocs: Vec<Ioc>,
    /// Configurations recovered by the family/heuristic extractors.
    pub configs: Vec<Config>,
    /// Fuzzy/similarity hashes (TLSH, ssdeep).
    pub fuzzy: FuzzyHashes,
    /// A full Markdown rendering, for export.
    pub markdown: String,
}

/// A representative MITRE ATT&CK technique for a behaviour category.
fn attack(c: ApiCategory) -> &'static str {
    use ApiCategory::*;
    match c {
        Injection | Memory => "T1055 Process Injection",
        Network => "T1071 Application Layer Protocol",
        AntiDebug => "T1497 Sandbox Evasion / T1622 Debugger Evasion",
        Crypto => "T1573 Encrypted Channel / T1486 Data Encrypted",
        Process => "T1106 Native API",
        File => "T1005 Data from Local System",
        Registry => "T1112 Modify Registry / T1547 Autostart",
        DynamicLoading => "T1027 Obfuscation / T1620 Reflective Loading",
        Input => "T1056.001 Keylogging",
        Compare => "",
    }
}

/// Builds a triage report from `info`, the sample's extracted `strings`, and its raw bytes
/// (`data`, used for the fuzzy hashes).
pub fn build(info: &BinaryInfo, strings: &[&str], data: &[u8]) -> Report {
    // Group imports by behaviour category.
    let mut grouped: BTreeMap<ApiCategory, Vec<String>> = BTreeMap::new();
    for imp in &info.imports {
        if let Some(api) = apis::lookup(&imp.name) {
            let v = grouped.entry(api.category).or_default();
            if !v.iter().any(|n| n == &imp.name) {
                v.push(imp.name.clone());
            }
        }
    }
    let mut behaviors: Vec<BehaviorGroup> = grouped
        .into_iter()
        .map(|(category, apis)| BehaviorGroup {
            category,
            attack: attack(category),
            apis,
            suspicious: category.suspicious(),
        })
        .collect();
    // Suspicious behaviours first, then by name.
    behaviors.sort_by(|a, b| {
        b.suspicious
            .cmp(&a.suspicious)
            .then(a.category.name().cmp(b.category.name()))
    });

    let import_names: Vec<&str> = info.imports.iter().map(|i| i.name.as_str()).collect();
    let capabilities = capa::detect(&import_names, strings);
    let iocs = ioc::extract(strings);
    let configs = config::run_all(info, data, strings);
    let fuzzy = fuzzy::compute(data);
    let flags = risk_flags(info, &behaviors, &iocs);
    let markdown = render_markdown(
        info,
        &flags,
        &capabilities,
        &configs,
        &behaviors,
        &iocs,
        &fuzzy,
    );

    Report {
        flags,
        capabilities,
        behaviors,
        iocs,
        configs,
        fuzzy,
        markdown,
    }
}

fn risk_flags(info: &BinaryInfo, behaviors: &[BehaviorGroup], iocs: &[Ioc]) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut flags = Vec::new();
    for d in &info.detections {
        if d.category == DetectionCategory::Packer {
            flags.push(format!("Packed/obfuscated: {} ({})", d.name, d.evidence));
        }
    }
    if info.entropy > 7.2 {
        flags.push(format!(
            "High file entropy ({:.2}/8) — likely packed or encrypted",
            info.entropy
        ));
    }
    let suspicious: Vec<&str> = behaviors
        .iter()
        .filter(|b| b.suspicious)
        .map(|b| b.category.name())
        .collect();
    if !suspicious.is_empty() {
        flags.push(format!(
            "Suspicious capabilities: {}",
            suspicious.join(", ")
        ));
    }
    let net = iocs
        .iter()
        .filter(|i| matches!(i.kind, IocKind::Url | IocKind::Domain | IocKind::Ipv4))
        .count();
    if net > 0 {
        flags.push(format!("{net} network indicator(s) in strings"));
    }
    if let Some(pe) = &info.pe
        && !pe.has_signature
    {
        flags.push("No Authenticode signature".into());
    }
    flags
}

fn render_markdown(
    info: &BinaryInfo,
    flags: &[String],
    capabilities: &[Capability],
    configs: &[Config],
    behaviors: &[BehaviorGroup],
    iocs: &[Ioc],
    fuzzy: &FuzzyHashes,
) -> String {
    use std::fmt::Write;
    let mut s = String::new();
    let _ = writeln!(s, "# Triage report\n");

    let _ = writeln!(s, "## Overview");
    let _ = writeln!(s, "- Format: {} ({})", info.format.name(), info.arch);
    let _ = writeln!(s, "- Size: {} bytes", info.size);
    let _ = writeln!(s, "- Entropy: {:.2}/8", info.entropy);
    let _ = writeln!(s, "- MD5: `{}`", info.hashes.md5);
    let _ = writeln!(s, "- SHA-256: `{}`", info.hashes.sha256);
    if let Some(h) = &info.hashes.imphash {
        let _ = writeln!(s, "- Imphash: `{h}`");
    }
    if let Some(t) = &fuzzy.tlsh {
        let _ = writeln!(s, "- TLSH: `{t}`");
    }
    let _ = writeln!(s, "- ssdeep: `{}`", fuzzy.ssdeep);
    let _ = writeln!(s);

    if !flags.is_empty() {
        let _ = writeln!(s, "## Risk flags");
        for f in flags {
            let _ = writeln!(s, "- {f}");
        }
        let _ = writeln!(s);
    }

    if !configs.is_empty() {
        let _ = writeln!(s, "## Extracted configuration");
        for c in configs {
            let _ = writeln!(s, "### {} _({})_", c.family, c.note);
            for f in &c.fields {
                let _ = writeln!(s, "- {}: `{}`", f.key, f.value);
            }
        }
        let _ = writeln!(s);
    }

    if !capabilities.is_empty() {
        let _ = writeln!(s, "## Capabilities");
        for c in capabilities {
            let att = if c.attack.is_empty() {
                String::new()
            } else {
                format!("  _[{}]_", c.attack)
            };
            let _ = writeln!(s, "- **{}** ({}){att}", c.name, c.namespace);
            let _ = writeln!(s, "  - evidence: {}", c.evidence.join(", "));
        }
        let _ = writeln!(s);
    }

    if !behaviors.is_empty() {
        let _ = writeln!(s, "## Imports by behaviour");
        for b in behaviors {
            let mark = if b.suspicious { " ⚠" } else { "" };
            let att = if b.attack.is_empty() {
                String::new()
            } else {
                format!("  _[{}]_", b.attack)
            };
            let _ = writeln!(
                s,
                "- **{}**{mark}{att}: {}",
                b.category.name(),
                b.apis.join(", ")
            );
        }
        let _ = writeln!(s);
    }

    if !iocs.is_empty() {
        let _ = writeln!(s, "## Indicators (defanged)");
        let mut kind = None;
        for i in iocs {
            if kind != Some(i.kind) {
                let _ = writeln!(s, "\n### {}", i.kind.label());
                kind = Some(i.kind);
            }
            let _ = writeln!(s, "- `{}`", ioc::defang(&i.value));
        }
        let _ = writeln!(s);
    }
    s
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use orress_loaders::Import;

    fn imp(name: &str) -> Import {
        Import {
            library: "kernel32.dll".into(),

        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn builds_report_with_behaviors_and_iocs() {

    }
}

`crates/orress-triage/src/yara.rs`:

```rs
//! A thin wrapper over YARA-X (VirusTotal's pure-Rust YARA engine): compile a rule and scan the
//! open file, returning structured matches for the UI. The YARA workbench uses this to let an
//! analyst write a rule and test it live against the sample and their library, generate a
//! starter rule from the sample's strings, and scan against a folder of rules.

use std::ops::Range;
use std::path::Path;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

/// Per-scan time limit for a file: a pathological rule (catastrophic regex, huge loops) must not
/// hang the workbench.
const FILE_SCAN_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10);
/// Per-region time limit for process memory (regions can be large).
const REGION_SCAN_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
/// Overall budget for scanning all of a process's regions.
const MEMORY_SCAN_BUDGET: Duration = Duration::from_secs(120);

/// A readable message for a scan error, spelling out timeouts.
fn scan_error_message(e: &yara_x::ScanError, limit: Duration) -> String {
    match e {
        yara_x::ScanError::Timeout => format!(
            "scan timed out after {}s — a rule is too slow for this data (simplify regexes/loops)",
            limit.as_secs()
        ),
        other => other.to_string(),
    }
}

/// One matched location of a pattern.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct YaraMatch {
    pub pattern: String,
    pub range: Range<usize>,
    /// A short preview of the matched bytes.
    pub preview: String,
}

/// A rule that matched, with its pattern matches.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct YaraHit {
    pub rule: String,
    pub matches: Vec<YaraMatch>,
}

/// The outcome of compiling and running a rule.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum YaraOutcome {
    Hits(Vec<YaraHit>),
    CompileError(String),
    ScanError(String),
}

/// The most matches recorded per pattern (keeps the UI bounded on noisy rules).
const MAX_MATCHES: usize = 200;

/// Compiles `rule_src` and scans `data`, returning the matches (or a compile/scan error).
pub fn scan(rule_src: &str, data: &[u8]) -> YaraOutcome {
    let rules = match yara_x::compile(rule_src) {
        Ok(r) => r,
        Err(e) => return YaraOutcome::CompileError(e.to_string()),
    };
    let mut scanner = yara_x::Scanner::new(&rules);
    scanner.set_timeout(FILE_SCAN_TIMEOUT);
    let results = match scanner.scan(data) {
        Ok(r) => r,
        Err(e) => return YaraOutcome::ScanError(scan_error_message(&e, FILE_SCAN_TIMEOUT)),
    };
    let mut hits = Vec::new();
    for rule in results.matching_rules() {
        let mut matches = Vec::new();
        for pattern in rule.patterns() {
            let pid = pattern.identifier().to_string();
            for m in pattern.matches().take(MAX_MATCHES) {
                matches.push(YaraMatch {
                    pattern: pid.clone(),
                    range: m.range(),
                    preview: preview(m.data()),
                });
            }
        }
        hits.push(YaraHit {
            rule: rule.identifier().to_string(),
            matches,
        });
    }
    YaraOutcome::Hits(hits)
}

/// One rule from a scanned library that matched the file.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct LibHit {
    /// The rule file (name only).
    pub file: String,
    pub rule: String,
    pub matches: usize,
}

/// Compiles every `.yar`/`.yara` file in `dir` and scans `data` with it, aggregating the rules
/// that matched. Returns `(hits, errors)` — files that failed to compile are listed in `errors`.
pub fn scan_dir(dir: &Path, data: &[u8]) -> (Vec<LibHit>, Vec<String>) {
    let mut hits = Vec::new();
    let mut errors = Vec::new();
    let entries = match std::fs::read_dir(dir) {
        Ok(e) => e,
        Err(e) => return (hits, vec![format!("{}: {e}", dir.display())]),
    };
    for entry in entries.flatten() {
        let path = entry.path();
        let ext = path.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str()).unwrap_or("");
        if !ext.eq_ignore_ascii_case("yar") && !ext.eq_ignore_ascii_case("yara") {
            continue;
        }
        let file = path
            .file_name()
            .map(|n| n.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let src = match std::fs::read_to_string(&path) {
            Ok(s) => s,
            Err(e) => {
                errors.push(format!("{file}: {e}"));
                continue;
            }
        };
        match scan(&src, data) {
            YaraOutcome::Hits(rule_hits) => {
                for h in rule_hits {
                    hits.push(LibHit {
                        file: file.clone(),
                        rule: h.rule,
                        matches: h.matches.len(),
                    });
                }
            }
            YaraOutcome::CompileError(e) | YaraOutcome::ScanError(e) => {
                errors.push(format!("{file}: {}", e.lines().next().unwrap_or("error")));
            }
        }
    }
    (hits, errors)
}

/// Generates a starter YARA rule from a sample's distinctive strings.
pub fn generate_rule(name: &str, strings: &[&str]) -> String {
    let mut chosen: Vec<&str> = strings
        .iter()
        .copied()
        .filter(|s| {
            let n = s.chars().count();
            (8..=60).contains(&n)
                && s.is_ascii()
                && s.bytes().all(|b| (0x20..0x7f).contains(&b))
                && !s.to_ascii_lowercase().ends_with(".dll")
                && s.chars().any(|c| c.is_ascii_alphabetic())
        })
        .collect();
    chosen.sort_by_key(|s| std::cmp::Reverse(s.len()));
    chosen.dedup();
    chosen.truncate(10);

    let ident = sanitize_ident(name);
    let mut out = format!(
        "rule {ident} {{\n    meta:\n        author = \"ORRESS\"\n        description = \"auto-generated from distinctive strings\"\n    strings:\n"
    );
    if chosen.is_empty() {
        out.push_str("        $a = \"CHANGE_ME\"\n    condition:\n        $a\n}\n");
        return out;
    }
    for (i, s) in chosen.iter().enumerate() {
        out.push_str(&format!("        $s{i} = \"{}\"\n", escape_yara(s)));
    }
    let need = chosen.len().min(3);
    out.push_str(&format!("    condition:\n        {need} of them\n}}\n"));
    out
}

fn sanitize_ident(name: &str) -> String {
    let mut s: String = name
        .chars()
        .map(|c| if c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() { c } else { '_' })
        .collect();
    if s.is_empty() || s.as_bytes()[0].is_ascii_digit() {
        s.insert(0, 'r');
    }
    s
}

fn escape_yara(s: &str) -> String {
    s.replace('\\', "\\\\").replace('"', "\\\"")
}

/// A YARA match located in a running process's memory.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct MemHit {
    pub rule: String,
    pub pattern: String,
    pub address: u64,
    pub preview: String,
}

/// The outcome of an in-memory scan.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum MemScan {
    Hits(Vec<MemHit>),
    CompileError(String),
}

/// Compiles `rule_src` and scans each memory region (base address + bytes), reporting matches at
/// their absolute addresses. Matches that span a region boundary are not detected. Regions that
/// fail to scan (e.g. time out) are skipped; use [`scan_regions_report`] to see those errors.
pub fn scan_regions<'a>(
    rule_src: &str,
    regions: impl IntoIterator<Item = (u64, &'a [u8])>,
) -> MemScan {
    scan_regions_report(rule_src, regions).0
}

/// Like [`scan_regions`], but also returns the per-region scan errors (timeouts included, and a
/// note if the overall memory-scan budget ran out before every region was scanned).
pub fn scan_regions_report<'a>(
    rule_src: &str,
    regions: impl IntoIterator<Item = (u64, &'a [u8])>,
) -> (MemScan, Vec<String>) {
    let rules = match yara_x::compile(rule_src) {
        Ok(r) => r,
        Err(e) => return (MemScan::CompileError(e.to_string()), Vec::new()),
    };
    let mut scanner = yara_x::Scanner::new(&rules);
    scanner.set_timeout(REGION_SCAN_TIMEOUT);
    let started = Instant::now();
    let mut hits = Vec::new();
    let mut errors = Vec::new();
    for (base, data) in regions {
        if started.elapsed() > MEMORY_SCAN_BUDGET {
            errors.push(format!(
                "memory scan stopped after {}s; remaining regions were not scanned",
                MEMORY_SCAN_BUDGET.as_secs()
            ));
            break;
        }
        let results = match scanner.scan(data) {
            Ok(r) => r,
            Err(e) => {
                errors.push(format!(
                    "region {base:#x}: {}",
                    scan_error_message(&e, REGION_SCAN_TIMEOUT)
                ));
                continue;
            }
        };
        for rule in results.matching_rules() {
            let rname = rule.identifier().to_string();
            for pattern in rule.patterns() {
                let pid = pattern.identifier().to_string();
                for m in pattern.matches().take(MAX_MATCHES) {
                    hits.push(MemHit {
                        rule: rname.clone(),
                        pattern: pid.clone(),
                        address: base + m.range().start as u64,
                        preview: preview(m.data()),
                    });
                }
            }
        }
        if hits.len() > 2000 {
            break;
        }
    }
    (MemScan::Hits(hits), errors)
}

/// A short printable preview of matched bytes (ASCII where printable, else `.`).
fn preview(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    let shown = &bytes[..bytes.len().min(32)];
    let s: String = shown
        .iter()
        .map(|&b| {
            if (0x20..0x7f).contains(&b) {
                b as char
            } else {
                '.'
            }
        })
        .collect();
    if bytes.len() > 32 {
        format!("{s}…")
    } else {
        s
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn matches_a_string_rule() {
        let rule = r#"rule finds_malware { strings: $a = "malware" condition: $a }"#;
        let data = b"this sample contains malware right here";
        match scan(rule, data) {
            YaraOutcome::Hits(hits) => {
                assert_eq!(hits.len(), 1);
                assert_eq!(hits[0].rule, "finds_malware");
                assert_eq!(hits[0].matches.len(), 1);
                assert_eq!(hits[0].matches[0].range.start, 21);
                assert_eq!(hits[0].matches[0].preview, "malware");
            }
            other => panic!("expected hits, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn reports_compile_errors() {
        let out = scan("rule broken { condition: $nope }", b"x");
        assert!(matches!(out, YaraOutcome::CompileError(_)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn no_match_is_empty() {
        let rule = r#"rule no_hit { strings: $a = "zzzz" condition: $a }"#;
        match scan(rule, b"abcd") {
            YaraOutcome::Hits(hits) => assert!(hits.is_empty()),
            other => panic!("expected empty hits, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn generated_rule_compiles_and_matches() {
        let strings = [
            "this is a distinctive marker string",
            "AnotherUniqueToken_12345",
            "short",
        ];
        let rule = generate_rule("my sample.exe", &strings);
        assert!(rule.contains("rule my_sample_exe"));
        // Short strings are filtered out.
        assert!(!rule.contains("short"));
        let data = b"this is a distinctive marker string and AnotherUniqueToken_12345 too";
        assert!(matches!(scan(&rule, data), YaraOutcome::Hits(h) if !h.is_empty()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn generated_rule_escapes_quotes() {
        let rule = generate_rule("t", &["string with \"quotes\" and a marker"]);
        assert!(rule.contains("\\\"quotes\\\""));
        assert!(!matches!(scan(&rule, b""), YaraOutcome::CompileError(_)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn scan_regions_maps_absolute_addresses() {
        let rule = r#"rule mem { strings: $a = "INJECTED" condition: $a }"#;
        let r1: &[u8] = b"...nothing here...";
        let r2: &[u8] = b"junk INJECTED junk"; // "INJECTED" at offset 5
        let regions = [(0x10000u64, r1), (0x7fff_0000u64, r2)];
        match scan_regions(rule, regions) {
            MemScan::Hits(hits) => {
                assert_eq!(hits.len(), 1);
                assert_eq!(hits[0].rule, "mem");
                assert_eq!(hits[0].address, 0x7fff_0000 + 5);
                assert_eq!(hits[0].preview, "INJECTED");
            }
            MemScan::CompileError(e) => panic!("compile error: {e}"),
        }
        let (out, errors) = scan_regions_report(rule, [(0x1000u64, r2)]);
        assert!(matches!(out, MemScan::Hits(h) if h.len() == 1));
        assert!(errors.is_empty(), "{errors:?}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn timeouts_are_reported_clearly() {
        let msg = scan_error_message(&yara_x::ScanError::Timeout, FILE_SCAN_TIMEOUT);
        assert!(msg.contains("timed out after 10s"), "{msg}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn scan_dir_aggregates_library_hits() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("orress_yara_{}", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(
            dir.join("r.yar"),
            r#"rule lib_rule { strings: $a = "needle" condition: $a }"#,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let (hits, errors) = scan_dir(&dir, b"a haystack with a needle inside");
        assert!(errors.is_empty(), "{errors:?}");
        assert_eq!(hits.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(hits[0].rule, "lib_rule");
        assert_eq!(hits[0].file, "r.yar");
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }
}

`crates/orress-ui/src/explain.rs`:

```rs
//! Explain Mode: every widget can carry a plain-language explanation.
//!
//! ```ignore
//! ui.button("Entropy").explain(
//!     "Entropy",
//!     "How random the bytes look. Close to 8 means compressed or encrypted data.",
//! );
//! ```
//!
//! When Explain Mode is on, hovering shows the explanation as a tooltip. Whether it is
//! on or off, the last hovered explanation is remembered so the Explain panel can show it
//! in full.

use egui::{Context, Id, Response, RichText};

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Explanation {
    pub title: String,
    pub body: String,
}

fn mode_id() -> Id {
    Id::new("orress::explain_mode")
}

fn last_id() -> Id {
    Id::new("orress::last_explanation")
}

pub fn set_explain_mode(ctx: &Context, on: bool) {
    ctx.data_mut(|d| d.insert_temp(mode_id(), on));
}

pub fn explain_mode(ctx: &Context) -> bool {
    ctx.data(|d| d.get_temp(mode_id())).unwrap_or(true)
}

/// The explanation of the most recently hovered widget, if any.
pub fn last_explanation(ctx: &Context) -> Option<Explanation> {
    ctx.data(|d| d.get_temp(last_id()))
}

pub trait ExplainExt {
    /// Explanation shown in the Explain panel and, in Explain Mode, as a tooltip.
    fn explain(self, title: &str, body: &str) -> Self;
    /// Explanation shown only in the Explain panel: for large areas such as the hex grid,
    /// where a tooltip would cover what you are looking at.
    fn note(self, title: &str, body: &str) -> Self;
}

fn record(ctx: &Context, title: &str, body: &str) {
    let explanation = Explanation {
        title: title.to_owned(),
        body: body.to_owned(),
    };
    if last_explanation(ctx).as_ref() != Some(&explanation) {
        ctx.data_mut(|d| d.insert_temp(last_id(), explanation));
    }
}

impl ExplainExt for Response {
    fn note(self, title: &str, body: &str) -> Self {
        if self.hovered() {
            record(&self.ctx, title, body);
        }
        self
    }

    fn explain(self, title: &str, body: &str) -> Self {
        if !self.hovered() {
            return self;
        }
        let ctx = self.ctx.clone();
        record(&ctx, title, body);
        if explain_mode(&ctx) {
            self.on_hover_ui(|ui| {
                ui.set_max_width(320.0);
                ui.label(RichText::new(title).strong());
                ui.label(body);
            })
        } else {
            self
        }
    }
}

//! Shared egui widgets for ORRESS.

pub mod explain;
pub mod palette;
pub mod spotlight;

pub use explain::{ExplainExt, Explanation};
pub use palette::{CommandPalette, PaletteItem};

use egui::{RichText, Ui};

/// Draws a keyboard shortcut as a small "key cap" chip, e.g. `Ctrl+Shift+P`.
pub fn kbd(ui: &mut Ui, label: &str) -> egui::Response {
    let visuals = ui.visuals().clone();
    egui::Frame::new()
        .fill(visuals.extreme_bg_color)
        .stroke(visuals.widgets.noninteractive.bg_stroke)
        .corner_radius(3.0)
        .inner_margin(egui::Margin::symmetric(4, 1))
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            ui.label(RichText::new(label).monospace().small().weak());
        })
        .response
}

/// Secondary text in the theme's muted color.
pub fn muted(text: impl Into<String>) -> RichText {
    RichText::new(text).weak()
}

`crates/orress-ui/src/palette.rs`:

```rs
//! The command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P): fuzzy search over every action.

use egui::{Align, Context, Id, Key, Modifiers, RichText, Sense};
use nucleo_matcher::pattern::{CaseMatching, Normalization, Pattern};
use nucleo_matcher::{Config, Matcher, Utf32Str};
use orress_actions::ActionId;

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct PaletteItem {
    pub action: ActionId,
    pub title: String,
    pub category: String,
    pub shortcut: Option<String>,
    pub explain: String,
}

impl PaletteItem {
    fn haystack(&self) -> String {
        format!("{}: {}", self.category, self.title)
    }
}

const MAX_RECENT: usize = 8;

pub struct CommandPalette {
    open: bool,
    query: String,
    selected: usize,
    /// Set when the selection moved by keyboard, so the list scrolls to it.
    scroll_to_selected: bool,
    recent: Vec<ActionId>,
    matcher: Matcher,
}

impl Default for CommandPalette {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            open: false,
            query: String::new(),
            selected: 0,
            scroll_to_selected: false,
            recent: Vec::new(),
            matcher: Matcher::new(Config::DEFAULT),
        }
    }
}

impl CommandPalette {
    pub fn is_open(&self) -> bool {
        self.open
    }

    pub fn toggle(&mut self) {
        if self.open {
            self.close();
        } else {
            self.open = true;
            self.query.clear();
            self.selected = 0;
        }
    }

    pub fn close(&mut self) {
        self.open = false;
    }

    /// Indices into `items`, best match first. With an empty query, recently used
    /// actions come first and the rest are alphabetical.
    pub fn filter(&mut self, items: &[PaletteItem]) -> Vec<usize> {
        if self.query.trim().is_empty() {
            let mut order: Vec<usize> = (0..items.len()).collect();
            order.sort_by_key(|&i| {
                let recent_rank = self
                    .recent
                    .iter()
                    .position(|a| a == &items[i].action)
                    .unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
                (recent_rank, items[i].haystack().to_lowercase())
            });
            return order;
        }

        let pattern = Pattern::parse(&self.query, CaseMatching::Ignore, Normalization::Smart);
        let mut buf = Vec::new();
        let mut scored: Vec<(usize, u32)> = items
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .filter_map(|(i, item)| {
                let haystack = item.haystack();
                pattern
                    .score(Utf32Str::new(&haystack, &mut buf), &mut self.matcher)
                    .map(|score| (i, score))
            })
            .collect();
        scored.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.cmp(&a.1).then(a.0.cmp(&b.0)));
        scored.into_iter().map(|(i, _)| i).collect()
    }

    fn remember(&mut self, action: &ActionId) {
        self.recent.retain(|a| a != action);
        self.recent.insert(0, action.clone());
        self.recent.truncate(MAX_RECENT);
    }

    /// Shows the palette if open. Returns the action the user picked.
    pub fn show(&mut self, ctx: &Context, items: &[PaletteItem]) -> Option<ActionId> {
        if !self.open {
            return None;
        }

        let matches = self.filter(items);
        if self.selected >= matches.len() {
            self.selected = matches.len().saturating_sub(1);
        }

        // Navigation keys are consumed before the text field sees them.
        let (up, down, enter, escape) = ctx.input_mut(|i| {
            (
                i.consume_key(Modifiers::NONE, Key::ArrowUp),
                i.consume_key(Modifiers::NONE, Key::ArrowDown),
                i.consume_key(Modifiers::NONE, Key::Enter),
                i.consume_key(Modifiers::NONE, Key::Escape),
            )
        });
        if up && self.selected > 0 {
            self.selected -= 1;
            self.scroll_to_selected = true;
        }
        if down && self.selected + 1 < matches.len() {
            self.selected += 1;
            self.scroll_to_selected = true;
        }

        let mut picked = None;
        if enter {
            picked = matches.get(self.selected).map(|&i| items[i].action.clone());
        }

        let area = egui::Area::new(Id::new("orress::palette_area"))
            .anchor(egui::Align2::CENTER_TOP, [0.0, 80.0])
            .order(egui::Order::Foreground);
        let modal = egui::Modal::new(Id::new("orress::palette"))
            .area(area)
            .show(ctx, |ui| {
                ui.set_width(560.0);
                let edit = ui.add(
                    egui::TextEdit::singleline(&mut self.query)
                        .hint_text("Type a command… (try \"dock\", \"theme\" or \"open\")")
                        .desired_width(f32::INFINITY),
                );
                edit.request_focus();
                if edit.changed() {
                    self.selected = 0;
                }
                ui.separator();

                egui::ScrollArea::vertical()
                    .max_height(360.0)
                    .auto_shrink([false, true])
                    .show(ui, |ui| {
                        if matches.is_empty() {
                            ui.label(RichText::new("No matching command.").weak());
                        }
                        for (row, &index) in matches.iter().enumerate() {
                            let item = &items[index];
                            let selected = row == self.selected;
                            let response = palette_row(ui, item, selected);
                            if selected && self.scroll_to_selected {
                                response.scroll_to_me(Some(Align::Center));
                            }
                            if response.hovered()
                                && ui.input(|i| i.pointer.delta() != egui::Vec2::ZERO)
                            {
                                self.selected = row;
                            }
                            if response.clicked() {
                                picked = Some(item.action.clone());
                            }
                        }
                    });
                self.scroll_to_selected = false;

                // Beginner help: what does the highlighted command do?
                if let Some(item) = matches.get(self.selected).map(|&i| &items[i]) {
                    ui.separator();
                    ui.label(RichText::new(&item.explain).small().weak());
                }
            });

        if escape || modal.should_close() {
            self.close();
        }
        if let Some(action) = &picked {
            self.remember(action);
            self.close();
        }
        picked
    }
}

fn palette_row(ui: &mut egui::Ui, item: &PaletteItem, selected: bool) -> egui::Response {
    let fill = if selected {
        ui.visuals().selection.bg_fill
    } else {
        egui::Color32::TRANSPARENT
    };
    egui::Frame::new()
        .fill(fill)
        .corner_radius(4.0)
        .inner_margin(egui::Margin::symmetric(6, 3))
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            ui.set_width(ui.available_width());
            ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                ui.label(RichText::new(format!("{}:", item.category)).weak());
                ui.label(&item.title);
                if let Some(shortcut) = &item.shortcut {
                    ui.with_layout(egui::Layout::right_to_left(Align::Center), |ui| {
                        crate::kbd(ui, shortcut);
                    });
                }
            });
        })
        .response
        .interact(Sense::click())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn item(id: &str, category: &str, title: &str) -> PaletteItem {
        PaletteItem {
            action: id.into(),
            title: title.into(),
            category: category.into(),
            shortcut: None,
            explain: String::new(),
        }
    }

    fn items() -> Vec<PaletteItem> {
        vec![
            item("workspace::ToggleLeftDock", "workspace", "Toggle Left Dock"),
            item("workspace::Open", "workspace", "Open File…"),
            item("theme::Dark", "theme", "ORRESS Dark"),
        ]

    fn fuzzy_match_ranks_relevant_first() {
        let mut p = CommandPalette::default();
        let items = items();
        p.query = "tgl dock".into();

        assert_eq!(m.len(), 3);
    }
}

`crates/orress-ui/src/spotlight.rs`:

```rs
//! Spotlight: lessons can point at a part of the interface ("open the command
//! palette here"). Widgets register their screen area under a name with [`mark`];
//! [`paint`] dims everything else and outlines the target.
//!
//! Marks from the previous frame are used for painting, because the overlay is drawn
//! before or after the target depending on panel order.

use std::collections::HashMap;

use egui::{Color32, Context, Id, LayerId, Order, Rect, Stroke, StrokeKind};

#[derive(Clone, Default)]
struct Marks {
    current: HashMap<String, Rect>,
    previous: HashMap<String, Rect>,
}

fn id() -> Id {
    Id::new("orress::spotlight")
}

/// Call once at the start of every frame.
pub fn begin_frame(ctx: &Context) {
    ctx.data_mut(|d| {
        let marks = d.get_temp_mut_or_default::<Marks>(id());
        marks.previous = std::mem::take(&mut marks.current);
    });
}

/// Registers the screen area of a named part of the UI.
pub fn mark(ctx: &Context, name: &str, rect: Rect) {
    ctx.data_mut(|d| {
        d.get_temp_mut_or_default::<Marks>(id())
            .current
            .insert(name.to_owned(), rect);
    });
}

/// Where a named part was drawn (this frame if already, else last frame).
pub fn rect(ctx: &Context, name: &str) -> Option<Rect> {
    ctx.data(|d| {
        d.get_temp::<Marks>(id()).and_then(|m| {
            m.current
                .get(name)
                .or_else(|| m.previous.get(name))
                .copied()
        })
    })
}

/// Dims the screen around `name` (and keeps the `keep_clear` areas, such as the lesson
/// panel, undimmed) and outlines the target with a pulsing border. Returns `false` if
/// that part is not visible (e.g. its dock is closed).
pub fn paint(ctx: &Context, name: &str, label: &str, keep_clear: &[Rect]) -> bool {
    let Some(target) = rect(ctx, name) else {
        return false;
    };
    let screen = ctx.content_rect();
    let target = target.expand(4.0).intersect(screen);
    let painter = ctx.layer_painter(LayerId::new(
        Order::Foreground,
        Id::new("orress::spotlight_layer"),
    ));
    let dim = Color32::from_black_alpha(130);
    // Cut the screen into a grid along the edges of all clear areas and dim the cells
    // outside them. Painting only (no input is captured), so clicks reach everything.
    let holes: Vec<Rect> = std::iter::once(target)
        .chain(keep_clear.iter().map(|r| r.intersect(screen)))
        .filter(|r| r.is_positive())
        .collect();
    let mut xs = vec![screen.min.x, screen.max.x];
    let mut ys = vec![screen.min.y, screen.max.y];
    for h in &holes {
        xs.extend([h.min.x, h.max.x]);
        ys.extend([h.min.y, h.max.y]);
    }
    xs.sort_by(f32::total_cmp);
    xs.dedup();
    ys.sort_by(f32::total_cmp);
    ys.dedup();
    for x in xs.windows(2) {
        for y in ys.windows(2) {
            let cell = Rect::from_min_max(egui::pos2(x[0], y[0]), egui::pos2(x[1], y[1]));
            if !holes.iter().any(|h| h.contains(cell.center())) {
                painter.rect_filled(cell, 0.0, dim);
            }
        }
    }
    let t = ctx.input(|i| i.time);
    let pulse = (0.5 + 0.5 * (t * 3.0).sin()) as f32;
    let color = Color32::from_rgb(255, 200, 60);
    painter.rect_stroke(
        target,
        6.0,
        Stroke::new(2.0 + 2.0 * pulse, color),
        StrokeKind::Outside,
    );
    if !label.is_empty() {
        let below = target.max.y + 8.0 < screen.max.y - 40.0;
        let pos = if below {
            egui::pos2(target.min.x, target.max.y + 8.0)
        } else {
            egui::pos2(target.min.x, target.min.y - 30.0)
        };
        let galley = painter.layout(
            label.to_owned(),
            egui::FontId::proportional(14.0),
            Color32::BLACK,
            320.0,
        );
        let bubble = Rect::from_min_size(pos, galley.size()).expand(6.0);
        painter.rect_filled(bubble, 6.0, color);
        painter.galley(pos, galley, Color32::BLACK);
    }
    ctx.request_repaint();
    true
}
