`crates/orress-views/src/apihash.rs`:

```rs
//! Reference lookup that labels a 32-bit constant in a captured blob with the Windows API name
//! whose rotate-13 name hash it matches. A position-independent loader resolves its imports by
//! comparing such hashes; recognising them is a standard triage step (as in scdbg or the IDA
//! "shellcode hashes" plugin). Read-only: it only names constants the analyst already has.

/// The common rotate-right-13 name hash, computed over the ASCII name bytes.
fn ror13(name: &[u8]) -> u32 {
    let mut h: u32 = 0;
    for &b in name {
        h = h.rotate_right(13).wrapping_add(u32::from(b));
    }
    h
}

/// A matched constant: its offset in the blob, the value, and the API name it hashes to.
pub struct HashMatch {
    pub offset: usize,
    pub value: u32,
    pub name: &'static str,
}

/// Scans every 4-byte little-endian window of `blob` for a value equal to a reference API-name
/// hash, returning the labelled matches.
pub fn scan(blob: &[u8]) -> Vec<HashMatch> {
    let table: Vec<(u32, &'static str)> = API_NAMES
        .iter()
        .map(|&n| (ror13(n.as_bytes()), n))
        .collect();
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    if blob.len() < 4 {
        return out;
    }
    for off in 0..=blob.len() - 4 {
        let v = u32::from_le_bytes([blob[off], blob[off + 1], blob[off + 2], blob[off + 3]]);
        if let Some(&(_, name)) = table.iter().find(|&&(h, _)| h == v) {
            out.push(HashMatch {
                offset: off,
                value: v,
                name,
            });
        }
    }
    out
}

/// A modest reference set of Windows API names a loader commonly resolves.
const API_NAMES: &[&str] = &[
    "LoadLibraryA",
    "LoadLibraryW",
    "LoadLibraryExA",
    "GetProcAddress",
    "GetModuleHandleA",
    "GetModuleHandleW",
    "VirtualAlloc",
    "VirtualProtect",
    "VirtualFree",
    "GetProcessHeap",
    "HeapAlloc",
    "ExitProcess",
    "ExitThread",
    "CreateThread",
    "Sleep",
    "WaitForSingleObject",
    "CreateFileA",
    "CreateFileW",
    "ReadFile",
    "WriteFile",
    "CloseHandle",
    "GetFileSize",
    "SetFilePointer",
    "GetModuleFileNameA",
    "GetCommandLineA",
    "GetTempPathA",
    "GetProcAddress",
    "LoadLibrary",
    "WSAStartup",
    "WSASocketA",
    "socket",
    "connect",
    "send",
    "recv",
    "closesocket",
    "InternetOpenA",
    "InternetOpenUrlA",
    "InternetConnectA",
    "HttpOpenRequestA",
    "HttpSendRequestA",
    "InternetReadFile",
    "URLDownloadToFileA",
    "RegOpenKeyExA",
    "RegSetValueExA",
    "RegQueryValueExA",
    "GetUserNameA",
    "GetComputerNameA",
    "OpenProcess",
    "ReadProcessMemory",
    "WriteProcessMemory",
    "CreateRemoteThread",
    "GetThreadContext",
    "SetThreadContext",
    "ResumeThread",
    "CreateProcessA",
    "TerminateProcess",
    "MessageBoxA",
    "GetWindowsDirectoryA",
    "GetSystemDirectoryA",
    "GetCurrentProcess",
    "GetCurrentProcessId",
    "IsDebuggerPresent",
];

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn ror13_is_stable_and_scans() {
        // Encode the LoadLibraryA hash as a little-endian constant in a blob and find it.
        let h = ror13(b"LoadLibraryA");
        let mut blob = vec![0x90u8, 0x90];
        blob.extend_from_slice(&h.to_le_bytes());
        blob.push(0xc3);
        let matches = scan(&blob);
        assert!(
            matches
                .iter()
                .any(|m| m.name == "LoadLibraryA" && m.value == h)
        );
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-views/src/archive.rs`:

```rs
//! The Archive view: open a ZIP/JAR, list its members, read the JAR manifest, and open a `.class`
//! member straight into the Java disassembler — powered by the pure-Rust `orress-archive` reader.
//! The decoded content of the selected entry is cached so only a new selection does work.

use egui::{RichText, Ui};
use orress_archive::Archive;
use orress_dex::Dex;
use orress_java::ClassFile;
use orress_project::DocStore;
use orress_ui::muted;

/// Persistent UI state for the Archive tab.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct ArchiveView {
    selected: Option<String>,
    method_sel: usize,
    /// The file (path and generation) the selection and cache belong to: another file resets
    /// the selection, and a patch decodes the entry again.
    doc: Option<(std::path::PathBuf, u64)>,
    /// The decoded content of `selected`, cached by entry name.
    cache_name: Option<String>,
    cached_class: Option<Result<ClassFile, String>>,
    cached_dex: Option<Result<Dex, String>>,
    /// Raw decompressed bytes of the selected .dex (needed to disassemble a method).
    cached_dex_bytes: Option<Vec<u8>>,
    dex_method_sel: usize,
    cached_text: Option<String>,
}

/// Bytes of a non-class entry shown as a text preview.
const PREVIEW_BYTES: usize = 8192;

pub fn archive_view(ui: &mut Ui, view: &mut ArchiveView, docs: &DocStore) {
    orress_ui::spotlight::mark(ui.ctx(), "view.Archive", ui.max_rect());
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label(RichText::new("Archive").strong());
        ui.label(muted("ZIP / JAR entries · manifest · open .class members"));
    });
    ui.separator();

    let Some(doc) = docs.active() else {
        ui.label(muted("Open a .zip, .jar or .apk file to inspect it."));
        return;
    };
    let Some(bytes) = doc.bytes() else {
        ui.label(muted("Reading the file…"));
        return;
    };
    if !orress_archive::looks_like_zip(bytes) {
        ui.label(muted(format!(
            "{} is not a ZIP-based archive (no PK signature).",
            doc.file_name()
        )));
        return;
    }

    // The archive borrows the file bytes, so re-open each frame (a cheap central-directory scan).
    let ar = match Archive::open(bytes) {
        Ok(a) => a,
        Err(e) => {
            ui.colored_label(
                ui.visuals().error_fg_color,
                format!("Could not read archive: {e}"),
            );
            return;
        }
    };

    let is_apk = ar.by_name("AndroidManifest.xml").is_some()
        && ar.entries.iter().any(|e| e.name.ends_with(".dex"));
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label(RichText::new(format!("{} entries", ar.entries.len())).strong());
        if is_apk {
            let dex = ar
                .entries
                .iter()
                .filter(|e| e.name.ends_with(".dex"))
                .count();
            ui.label(muted(format!("· Android APK ({dex} dex)")));
        } else if let Some(mc) = manifest_main_class(&ar) {
            ui.label(muted(format!("· Main-Class: {mc}")));
        }
    });
    ui.add_space(4.0);

    let doc_key = (doc.path.clone(), doc.generation);
    if view.doc.as_ref().map(|(p, _)| p) != Some(&doc.path) {
        view.selected = None;
    }
    let doc_changed = view.doc.as_ref() != Some(&doc_key);
    view.doc = Some(doc_key);

    // Decode the selection (once) when it, or the file, changes.
    if doc_changed || view.cache_name != view.selected {
        view.cached_class = None;
        view.cached_dex = None;
        view.cached_dex_bytes = None;
        view.cached_text = None;
        view.method_sel = 0;
        view.dex_method_sel = 0;
        if let Some(name) = view.selected.clone()
            && let Some(entry) = ar.by_name(&name)
        {
            match ar.read(entry) {
                Ok(data) => {
                    if name.ends_with(".class") {
                        view.cached_class = Some(orress_java::parse(&data));
                    } else if name.ends_with(".dex") {
                        view.cached_dex = Some(orress_dex::parse(&data));
                        view.cached_dex_bytes = Some(data);
                    } else {
                        view.cached_text = Some(text_preview(&data));
                    }
                }
                Err(e) => view.cached_text = Some(format!("(could not extract: {e})")),
            }
        }
        view.cache_name = view.selected.clone();
    }

    ui.horizontal_top(|ui| {
        // Left: entry list.
        ui.vertical(|ui| {
            ui.set_width(320.0);
            egui::ScrollArea::vertical()
                .id_salt("archive-entries")
                .auto_shrink([false, false])
                .show(ui, |ui| {
                    for e in &ar.entries {
                        if e.is_dir() {
                            ui.label(
                                RichText::new(format!("  {}/", e.name.trim_end_matches('/')))
                                    .monospace()
                                    .weak(),
                            );
                            continue;
                        }
                        let selected = view.selected.as_deref() == Some(e.name.as_str());
                        let label =
                            format!("{}  ({}, {})", e.name, e.uncompressed_size, e.method_name());
                        if ui
                            .selectable_label(selected, RichText::new(label).monospace())
                            .clicked()
                        {
                            view.selected = Some(e.name.clone());
                        }
                    }
                });
        });
        ui.separator();
        // Right: the selected entry.
        ui.vertical(|ui| {
            let Some(name) = view.selected.clone() else {
                ui.label(muted("Select an entry to view it."));
                return;
            };
            ui.label(RichText::new(&name).strong().monospace());
            if let Some(dex) = &view.cached_dex {
                match dex {
                    Ok(d) => dex_panel(
                        ui,
                        d,
                        view.cached_dex_bytes.as_deref().unwrap_or(&[]),
                        &mut view.dex_method_sel,
                    ),
                    Err(e) => {
                        ui.colored_label(
                            ui.visuals().error_fg_color,
                            format!("Not a valid DEX: {e}"),
                        );
                    }
                }
                return;
            }
            match (&view.cached_class, &view.cached_text) {
                (Some(Ok(cf)), _) => {
                    ui.add_space(2.0);
                    crate::java::class_file_panel(ui, cf, &mut view.method_sel, "arch");
                }
                (Some(Err(e)), _) => {
                    ui.colored_label(
                        ui.visuals().error_fg_color,
                        format!("Not a valid class: {e}"),
                    );
                }
                (None, Some(text)) => {
                    egui::ScrollArea::both()
                        .id_salt("archive-preview")
                        .auto_shrink([false, false])
                        .show(ui, |ui| {
                            let mut buf = text.as_str();
                            ui.add(
                                egui::TextEdit::multiline(&mut buf)
                                    .code_editor()
                                    .desired_width(f32::INFINITY),
                            );
                        });
                }
                (None, None) => {
                    ui.label(muted("(empty)"));
                }
            }
        });
    });
}

fn dex_panel(ui: &mut Ui, d: &Dex, data: &[u8], method_sel: &mut usize) {
    ui.label(muted(format!(
        "DEX {} · {} strings · {} types · {} methods · {} classes",
        d.version, d.string_count, d.type_count, d.method_count, d.class_def_count
    )));

    // Strings (collapsed to leave room for the code).
    egui::CollapsingHeader::new(format!(
        "Strings ({})",
        d.strings.iter().filter(|s| !s.trim().is_empty()).count()
    ))
    .id_salt("dex-strings-h")
    .show(ui, |ui| {
        egui::ScrollArea::vertical()
            .id_salt("dex-strings")
            .max_height(160.0)
            .auto_shrink([false, false])
            .show(ui, |ui| {
                for s in d.strings.iter().filter(|s| !s.trim().is_empty()).take(2000) {
                    let text = RichText::new(format!("  {s:?}")).monospace();
                    ui.label(if looks_interesting(s) {
                        text.color(ui.visuals().warn_fg_color)
                    } else {
                        text.weak()
                    });
                }
            });
    });

    // Flatten (class, method) pairs that have code.
    let methods: Vec<(&str, &orress_dex::DexMethod)> = d
        .classes
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|c| {
            c.methods
                .iter()
                .filter(|m| m.code_off != 0)
                .map(move |m| (c.name.as_str(), m))
        })
        .collect();
    if methods.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    if *method_sel >= methods.len() {
        *method_sel = 0;
    }
    ui.add_space(4.0);
    ui.separator();
    ui.horizontal_top(|ui| {
        ui.vertical(|ui| {
            ui.set_width(220.0);
            ui.label(RichText::new(format!("Methods ({})", methods.len())).strong());
            egui::ScrollArea::vertical()
                .id_salt("dex-methods")
                .auto_shrink([false, false])
                .show(ui, |ui| {
                    for (i, (_, m)) in methods.iter().enumerate() {
                        if ui
                            .selectable_label(*method_sel == i, RichText::new(&m.name).monospace())
                            .clicked()
                        {
                            *method_sel = i;
                        }
                    }
                });
        });
        ui.separator();
        ui.vertical(|ui| {
            let Some((_, m)) = methods.get(*method_sel) else {
                return;
            };
            ui.label(
                RichText::new(format!("{} (smali)", m.name))
                    .strong()
                    .monospace(),
            );
            match d.disassemble_method(data, m.code_off) {
                Ok(il) => {
                    egui::ScrollArea::vertical()
                        .id_salt("dex-smali")
                        .auto_shrink([false, false])
                        .show(ui, |ui| {
                            for ins in &il {
                                let mark = if ins.is_branch_target { ">>" } else { "  " };
                                let line = format!(
                                    "{mark} {:04x}: {:<22} {}",
                                    ins.offset, ins.mnemonic, ins.operand
                                );
                                let text = RichText::new(line).monospace();
                                ui.label(if ins.is_branch_target {
                                    text.color(ui.visuals().hyperlink_color)
                                } else {
                                    text
                                });
                            }
                        });
                }
                Err(e) => {
                    ui.label(muted(e));
                }
            }
        });
    });
}

/// Highlights strings that often matter in an APK: URLs, commands, secrets.
fn looks_interesting(s: &str) -> bool {
    let l = s.to_ascii_lowercase();
    [
        "http", "://", "flag", ".so", "/data/", "exec", "http://", "token", "secret", "password",
    ]
    .iter()
    .any(|k| l.contains(k))
}

fn manifest_main_class(ar: &Archive) -> Option<String> {
    let entry = ar.by_name("META-INF/MANIFEST.MF")?;
    let bytes = ar.read(entry).ok()?;
    orress_archive::parse_manifest(&bytes)
        .into_iter()
        .find(|(k, _)| k == "Main-Class")
        .map(|(_, v)| v)
}

/// A printable preview of an entry's first bytes (non-printable bytes shown as `.`).
fn text_preview(data: &[u8]) -> String {
    let shown = &data[..data.len().min(PREVIEW_BYTES)];
    let mut s: String = shown
        .iter()
        .map(|&b| {
            if b == b'\n' || b == b'\t' || (0x20..0x7f).contains(&b) {
                b as char
            } else {
                '.'
            }
        })
        .collect();
    if data.len() > PREVIEW_BYTES {
        s.push_str("\n…");
    }
    s
}
```

`crates/orress-views/src/assistant.rs`:

```rs
//! The AI assistant panel — bring your own model. It answers questions about the open binary
//! through one of four backends: the **Claude plan** (via the `claude` CLI, no API key), the
//! **Claude API** (key), any **OpenAI-compatible** endpoint (OpenAI, Azure, or a local server like
//! Ollama/LM Studio), or **Offline** (static analysis only, nothing leaves the machine).
//!
//! The non-secret config (provider, model, base URL) is persisted to `ai.json` in the config dir;
//! the API key is session-only or taken from an environment variable. Sending context to a model
//! is opt-in, and the exact context (a summary, never raw bytes) is shown first.
//!
//! Installed Zed extensions extend the assistant: their **slash commands** (`/<name> …`) run
//! locally through the extension host and their output becomes the answer, and their **context
//! (MCP) servers** can be offered to any model backend as tool sources — the Claude CLI via its own
//! MCP config, the HTTP backends (Claude API, OpenAI-compatible) via ORRESS's built-in MCP client.

use std::fmt::Write as _;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU64, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

use egui::{RichText, Ui};
use orress_ai::{Config, Provider, SYSTEM_PROMPT};
use orress_project::DocStore;
use orress_triage::hints::Challenge;
use orress_ui::muted;

/// Cap on how much analysis context is assembled for a prompt.
const MAX_CONTEXT: usize = 8_000;

/// Persistent UI state for the AI assistant tab.
pub struct AssistantView {
    cfg: Config,
    loaded: bool,
    /// The last persisted JSON, to detect edits worth saving.
    saved_json: String,
    consent: bool,
    question: String,
    result: Arc<Mutex<Option<Result<String, String>>>>,
    running: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    claude_ok: Option<bool>,
    /// Slash commands and context (MCP) servers discovered from installed Zed extensions.
    slash: Vec<orress_ext::ZedSlashCommand>,
    servers: Vec<orress_ext::ZedContextServer>,
    discovered: bool,
    /// Let Claude use the discovered MCP servers as tools (Claude-CLI backend only).
    use_mcp: bool,
    /// Error from the last attempt to save `ai.json`.
    save_error: Option<String>,
    /// Context built for the current file: ((path, SHA-256), context, classification).
    /// Triage and hints are too slow to redo every frame.
    context: Option<((PathBuf, String), String, Challenge)>,
    /// SHA-256 of the file the consent and answer belong to.
    file_sha: String,
    /// Bumped when the file changes, so an answer still in flight for the old file is dropped.
    epoch: Arc<AtomicU64>,
}

impl Default for AssistantView {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            cfg: Config::default(),
            loaded: false,
            saved_json: String::new(),
            consent: false,
            question: String::new(),
            result: Arc::new(Mutex::new(None)),
            running: Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false)),
            claude_ok: None,
            slash: Vec::new(),
            servers: Vec::new(),
            discovered: false,
            use_mcp: false,
            save_error: None,
            context: None,
            file_sha: String::new(),
            epoch: Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0)),
        }
    }
}

fn ai_file() -> Option<PathBuf> {
    orress_settings::Paths::from_platform().map(|p| p.config_dir.join("ai.json"))
}

pub fn assistant_view(ui: &mut Ui, view: &mut AssistantView, docs: &DocStore) {
    orress_ui::spotlight::mark(ui.ctx(), "view.Assistant", ui.max_rect());
    if !view.loaded {
        if let Some(f) = ai_file() {
            view.cfg = orress_ai::load_config(&f);
        }
        view.saved_json = orress_ai::config_json(&view.cfg);
        view.loaded = true;
    }

    // Discover the slash commands and context (MCP) servers that installed Zed extensions provide,
    // once the app has told us where the extensions live.
    if !view.discovered
        && let Some(dir) = crate::extensions::extensions_dir(ui.ctx())
    {
        view.slash = orress_ext::zed_slash_commands(&dir);
        view.servers = orress_ext::zed_context_servers(&dir);
        view.discovered = true;
    }

    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label(RichText::new("AI assistant").strong());
        ui.label(muted("bring your own model · explain · graded help"));
    });
    ui.separator();

    let claude_ok = *view
        .claude_ok
        .get_or_insert_with(orress_ai::claude_available);
    backend_config(ui, view, claude_ok);

    // Persist the config when it changes (the key only if "Remember key" is on).
    let now = orress_ai::config_json(&view.cfg);
    if now != view.saved_json {
        if let Some(f) = ai_file() {
            view.save_error = orress_ai::save_config(&f, &view.cfg)
                .err()
                .map(|e| format!("could not save {}: {e}", f.display()));
        }
        view.saved_json = now;
    }
    if let Some(e) = &view.save_error {
        ui.colored_label(ui.visuals().error_fg_color, e);
    }

    ui.add_space(4.0);
    let Some(doc) = docs.active() else {
        ui.label(muted("Open a binary, then ask the assistant about it."));
        return;
    };
    let Some(analysis) = doc.analysis() else {
        ui.label(muted(
            "Analysis is still running… the assistant needs it to answer.",
        ));
        return;
    };
    // Consent and the answer belong to one file: switching files starts over.
    if view.file_sha != analysis.info.hashes.sha256 {
        view.file_sha.clone_from(&analysis.info.hashes.sha256);
        view.consent = false;
        view.epoch.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
        *lock(&view.result) = None;
    }
    let key = (doc.path.clone(), analysis.info.hashes.sha256.clone());
    if view.context.as_ref().is_none_or(|(k, ..)| *k != key) {
        view.context = build_context(doc).map(|(c, ch)| (key, c, ch));
    }
    let Some((_, context, challenge)) = view.context.clone() else {
        ui.label(muted(
            "Analysis is still running… the assistant needs it to answer.",
        ));
        return;
    };
    // The worktree an extension slash command / context server runs against.
    let worktree = orress_ext::project_root(&doc.path);

    let offline = view.cfg.provider == Provider::Offline;
    if !offline {
        ui.checkbox(
            &mut view.consent,
            "Send the analysis summary below to the model",
        )
        .on_hover_text("Only the summary shown here is sent — never the raw file bytes.");
    }
    egui::CollapsingHeader::new("Context that will be used")
        .id_salt("ai-context")
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            egui::ScrollArea::vertical()
                .max_height(160.0)
                .id_salt("ai-ctx-scroll")
                .show(ui, |ui| {
                    ui.label(RichText::new(&context).monospace().weak());
                });
        });
    ui.add_space(4.0);

    // Slash commands provided by installed extensions: click to insert `/<name> `, then Ask runs it.
    if !view.slash.is_empty() {
        ui.horizontal_wrapped(|ui| {
            ui.label(muted("Slash commands:"));
            let cmds: Vec<(String, String)> = view
                .slash
                .iter()
                .map(|c| (c.command.name.clone(), c.command.description.clone()))
                .collect();
            for (name, desc) in cmds {
                let resp = ui.small_button(format!("/{name}"));
                let resp = if desc.is_empty() {
                    resp
                } else {
                    resp.on_hover_text(desc)
                };
                if resp.clicked() {
                    view.question = format!("/{name} ");
                }
            }
        });
    }
    // Context (MCP) servers provided by installed extensions. Every model backend can use them —
    // the Claude CLI via its own MCP config, the HTTP backends via ORRESS's built-in MCP client.
    if !view.servers.is_empty() {
        let ids: Vec<String> = view.servers.iter().map(|s| s.server_id.clone()).collect();
        if view.cfg.provider == Provider::Offline {
            ui.label(muted(format!(
                "{} MCP server(s) available — switch to a model backend to use them.",
                ids.len()
            )));
        } else {
            ui.checkbox(
                &mut view.use_mcp,
                format!("Let the model use {} MCP server(s)", ids.len()),
            )
            .on_hover_text(format!("Context servers: {}", ids.join(", ")));
        }
    }

    let running = view.running.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
    let usable = offline || (view.cfg.provider != Provider::ClaudeCli) || claude_ok;
    let can_send = !running && usable && (offline || view.consent);

    ui.horizontal_wrapped(|ui| {
        for (label, q) in [
            (
                "Explain this file",
                "Explain what this program does and how its check works.",
            ),
            (
                "Suggest next steps",
                "What should I do next in ORRESS to solve this?",
            ),
            (
                "Where's the flag/key?",
                "Where is the flag or key, and how is the input validated?",
            ),
        ] {
            if ui.add_enabled(can_send, egui::Button::new(label)).clicked() {
                view.question = q.to_string();
                submit(
                    view,
                    ui.ctx().clone(),
                    &context,
                    &challenge,
                    worktree.clone(),
                );
            }
        }
    });
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.add(
            egui::TextEdit::singleline(&mut view.question)
                .hint_text("Ask about this binary…  (or /command for an extension)")
                .desired_width(ui.available_width() - 60.0),
        );
        // A slash command runs a local extension (no model, no consent needed); a plain question
        // needs a usable backend and consent.
        let is_slash = parse_slash(view.question.trim()).is_some();
        let ok = !running && !view.question.trim().is_empty() && (is_slash || can_send);
        if ui.add_enabled(ok, egui::Button::new("Ask")).clicked() {
            submit(
                view,
                ui.ctx().clone(),
                &context,
                &challenge,
                worktree.clone(),
            );
        }
    });
    if !offline && !view.consent {
        ui.label(muted("Tick the consent box to send context to the model."));
    }

    ui.add_space(6.0);
    ui.separator();
    if running {
        ui.horizontal(|ui| {
            ui.spinner();
            ui.label(muted("asking…"));
        });
        return;
    }
    if let Some(result) = lock(&view.result).as_ref() {
        match result {
            Ok(text) => {
                egui::ScrollArea::vertical()
                    .auto_shrink([false, false])
                    .id_salt("ai-answer")
                    .show(ui, |ui| {
                        let mut buf = text.as_str();
                        ui.add(
                            egui::TextEdit::multiline(&mut buf)
                                .desired_width(f32::INFINITY)
                                .desired_rows(16),
                        );
                    });
            }
            Err(e) => {
                ui.colored_label(ui.visuals().error_fg_color, format!("AI error: {e}"));
            }
        }
    }
}

/// The backend picker and provider-specific configuration.
fn backend_config(ui: &mut Ui, view: &mut AssistantView, claude_ok: bool) {
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label("Backend:");
        egui::ComboBox::from_id_salt("ai-provider")
            .selected_text(view.cfg.provider.label())
            .show_ui(ui, |ui| {
                for p in [
                    Provider::ClaudeCli,
                    Provider::ClaudeApi,
                    Provider::OpenAi,
                    Provider::Offline,
                ] {
                    ui.selectable_value(&mut view.cfg.provider, p, p.label());
                }
            });
    });

    match view.cfg.provider {
        Provider::ClaudeCli => {
            if !claude_ok {
                ui.colored_label(
                    ui.visuals().warn_fg_color,
                    "The `claude` CLI was not found — install Claude Code and sign in to use your Claude plan.",
                );
            } else {
                ui.label(muted(
                    "Runs `claude -p` on your signed-in Claude plan (Pro/Max or API) — no API key.",
                ));
            }
            model_field(ui, &mut view.cfg.model, "default (your Claude Code model)");
        }
        Provider::ClaudeApi => {
            model_field(ui, &mut view.cfg.model, "claude-opus-4-20250514");
            base_field(ui, &mut view.cfg.base_url, "https://api.anthropic.com");
            key_field(
                ui,
                &mut view.cfg.api_key,
                &mut view.cfg.remember_key,
                "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY",
            );
        }
        Provider::OpenAi => {
            ui.label(muted("OpenAI, Azure, or a local server (Ollama: http://localhost:11434/v1, LM Studio, …)."));
            model_field(ui, &mut view.cfg.model, "gpt-4o-mini (or e.g. llama3.1)");
            base_field(ui, &mut view.cfg.base_url, "https://api.openai.com/v1");
            key_field(
                ui,
                &mut view.cfg.api_key,
                &mut view.cfg.remember_key,
                "OPENAI_API_KEY",
            );
        }
        Provider::Offline => {
            ui.label(muted(
                "Answers from ORRESS's static analysis only — nothing leaves the machine.",
            ));
        }
    }
}

                .hint_text(hint)

fn key_field(ui: &mut Ui, key: &mut String, remember: &mut bool, env: &str) {
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label(muted("API key:"));
        ui.add(

/// Parses a leading slash command: `/name arg1 arg2` → `("name", ["arg1", "arg2"])`. Returns
/// `None` for input that is not a slash command (empty, or not starting with `/name`).
fn parse_slash(input: &str) -> Option<(String, Vec<String>)> {
    let rest = input.trim().strip_prefix('/')?;
    let mut parts = rest.split_whitespace();
    let name = parts.next()?.to_string();
    if name.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    Some((name, parts.map(str::to_string).collect()))
}

/// Dispatches the input: a `/command` runs an extension slash command; anything else is a model
/// question.
fn submit(
    view: &mut AssistantView,
    ctx: egui::Context,
    context: &str,
    challenge: &Challenge,
    worktree: PathBuf,
) {
    if let Some((name, args)) = parse_slash(view.question.trim()) {
        run_slash_command(view, ctx, &name, args, worktree);
    } else {
        ask(view, ctx, context, challenge, worktree);
    }
}

/// Runs an extension's slash command on a background thread; its output becomes the answer.
fn run_slash_command(
    view: &mut AssistantView,
    ctx: egui::Context,
    name: &str,
    args: Vec<String>,
    worktree: PathBuf,
) {
    let Some(sc) = view.slash.iter().find(|c| c.command.name == name).cloned() else {
        let available: Vec<String> = view
            .slash
            .iter()
            .map(|c| format!("/{}", c.command.name))
            .collect();
        *lock(&view.result) = Some(Err(format!(
            "unknown slash command /{name}. Available: {}",
            if available.is_empty() {
                "(none installed)".to_string()
            } else {
                available.join(", ")
            }
        )));
        return;
    };
    let result = Arc::clone(&view.result);
    let running = Arc::clone(&view.running);
    *lock(&result) = None;
    running.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
    let epoch = Arc::clone(&view.epoch);
    let started = epoch.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
    std::thread::spawn(move || {
        let r = orress_ext::run_zed_slash_command(
            &sc.wasm,
            &sc.command,
            &args,
            Some(worktree.as_path()),
            serde_json::json!({}),
        )
        .map(|o| o.text);
        if epoch.load(Ordering::SeqCst) == started {
            *lock(&result) = Some(r);
        }
        running.store(false, Ordering::SeqCst);
        ctx.request_repaint();
    });
}

/// Resolves each discovered context server's launch command (running its WASM) into an
/// [`orress_ai::McpServer`]. Servers that fail to resolve are skipped.
fn resolve_mcp(
    servers: &[orress_ext::ZedContextServer],
    worktree: &std::path::Path,
) -> Vec<orress_ai::McpServer> {
    let roots = [worktree.to_path_buf()];
    servers
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|s| {
            let cmd = orress_ext::resolve_context_server_command(
                &s.wasm,
                &s.server_id,
                &roots,
                serde_json::json!({}),
            )
            .ok()?;
            Some(orress_ai::McpServer {
                name: s.server_id.clone(),
                command: cmd.command,
                args: cmd.args,
                env: cmd.env,
            })
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Starts a model query: Offline answers locally; the others run on a background thread. When MCP
/// is enabled (Claude-CLI backend), the discovered context servers are resolved and passed through.
fn ask(
    view: &mut AssistantView,
    ctx: egui::Context,
    context: &str,
    challenge: &Challenge,
    worktree: PathBuf,
) {
    if view.cfg.provider == Provider::Offline {
        *lock(&view.result) = Some(Ok(offline_answer(challenge)));
        return;
    }
    let prompt = orress_ai::build_prompt(view.question.trim(), context);
    let cfg = view.cfg.clone();
    let result = Arc::clone(&view.result);
    let running = Arc::clone(&view.running);
    let mcp_servers = if view.use_mcp && cfg.provider != Provider::Offline {
        view.servers.clone()
    } else {
        Vec::new()
    };
    *lock(&result) = None;
    running.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
    let epoch = Arc::clone(&view.epoch);
    let started = epoch.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
    std::thread::spawn(move || {
        let mcp = resolve_mcp(&mcp_servers, &worktree);
        let r = orress_ai::ask(&cfg, SYSTEM_PROMPT, &prompt, &mcp);
        if epoch.load(Ordering::SeqCst) == started {
            *lock(&result) = Some(r);
        }
        running.store(false, Ordering::SeqCst);
        ctx.request_repaint();
    });
}

/// The offline answer: the challenge classification plus every graded hint, from static analysis.
fn offline_answer(c: &Challenge) -> String {
    let mut out = format!("{}\n\nGraded hints:\n", c.summary);
    for h in &c.hints {
        let _ = writeln!(out, "  [{}] {}", h.level.label(), h.text);
    }
    if !c.techniques.is_empty() {
        let _ = writeln!(out, "\nSuggested techniques: {}", c.techniques.join(", "));
    }
    out.push_str(
        "\n(Offline mode — from ORRESS's static analysis only; nothing was sent anywhere.)",
    );
    out
}

/// Locks the shared answer, recovering it if a worker panicked while holding the lock.
fn lock<T>(m: &Mutex<T>) -> std::sync::MutexGuard<'_, T> {
    m.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
}

/// Builds the compact analysis context (never the raw bytes) and the challenge classification.
fn build_context(doc: &orress_project::Document) -> Option<(String, Challenge)> {
    let analysis = doc.analysis()?;
    let bytes = doc.bytes()?;
    let strings: Vec<&str> = analysis.strings.iter().map(|s| s.text.as_str()).collect();
    let report = orress_triage::build(&analysis.info, &strings, bytes);
    let challenge = orress_triage::hints::analyze(&report, &analysis.info, &strings);

    let mut c = String::new();
    let _ = writeln!(c, "file: {}", doc.file_name());
    let _ = writeln!(
        c,
        "format: {} ({})",
        analysis.info.format.name(),
        analysis.info.arch
    );
    let _ = writeln!(
        c,
        "size: {} bytes · entropy {:.2}/8",
        analysis.info.size, analysis.info.entropy
    );
    let _ = writeln!(c, "classification: {}", challenge.summary);
    if !report.flags.is_empty() {
        let _ = writeln!(c, "risk flags: {}", report.flags.join("; "));
    }
    if !report.capabilities.is_empty() {
        let caps: Vec<String> = report
            .capabilities
            .iter()
            .map(|x| x.name.to_string())
            .collect();
        let _ = writeln!(c, "capabilities: {}", caps.join(", "));
    }
    for b in &report.behaviors {
        let _ = writeln!(c, "imports[{}]: {}", b.category.name(), b.apis.join(", "));
    }
    if !report.iocs.is_empty() {
        let iocs: Vec<&str> = report
            .iocs
            .iter()
            .take(15)
            .map(|i| i.value.as_str())
            .collect();
        let _ = writeln!(c, "indicators: {}", iocs.join(", "));
    }
    let top: Vec<&str> = strings
        .iter()
        .filter(|s| s.len() >= 5)
        .take(40)
        .copied()
        .collect();
    if !top.is_empty() {
        let _ = writeln!(c, "strings (sample):\n{}", top.join("\n"));
    }
    if c.len() > MAX_CONTEXT {
        c.truncate(crate::code::floor_char_boundary(&c, MAX_CONTEXT));
        c.push_str("\n… (truncated)");
    }
    Some((c, challenge))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::parse_slash;

    #[test]
    fn parses_slash_commands() {
        assert_eq!(parse_slash("/greet"), Some(("greet".to_string(), vec![])));
        assert_eq!(
            parse_slash("  /file  src/main.rs  --line 3 "),
            Some((
                "file".to_string(),
                vec!["src/main.rs".into(), "--line".into(), "3".into()]
            ))
        );
        // Not slash commands.
        assert_eq!(parse_slash("explain this"), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_slash(""), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_slash("/"), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_slash("/   "), None);
    }
}

```

`crates/orress-views/src/challenge.rs`:

```rs
//! The Challenge Workbench panel: author a CTF challenge from a template, build and test it with
//! the run console, and submit it to the site's Forge for review. The scaffolding, template and
//! HTTP submit live in `orress-challenge`; this is the egui front end.

use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

use egui::Ui;
use orress_challenge::{KitSource, Meta};
use orress_ui::muted;

use crate::RunConsole;

/// What to do once `main.rs` has been saved from the open editor.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum AfterSave {
    Build,
    Submit,
}

/// State for the Challenge Workbench (owned by the app; not persisted, so the password never is).
pub struct ChallengeWorkbenchView {
    /// A Build or Submit waiting for the workspace to save `main.rs`'s editor buffer (unsaved
    /// edits must not be built or submitted stale), and the outcome of that save.
    after_save: Option<AfterSave>,
    save_result: Option<Result<(), String>>,
    meta: Meta,
    /// Hints, edited as one newline-separated field.
    hints_text: String,
    project_dir: Option<PathBuf>,
    main_rs: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// Use the bundled, offline `challenge-kit` (true) or a custom dependency (false).
    use_builtin_kit: bool,
    /// The custom `challenge-kit` dependency spec, used when `use_builtin_kit` is false.
    kit_source: String,
    site_url: String,
    username: String,
    password: String,
    status: Arc<Mutex<String>>,
    busy: Arc<AtomicBool>,
}

impl Default for ChallengeWorkbenchView {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            after_save: None,
            save_result: None,
            meta: Meta::default(),
            hints_text: String::new(),
            project_dir: None,
            main_rs: None,
            use_builtin_kit: true,
            kit_source: String::new(),
            site_url: "https://ctf.okiedocus.nl".to_string(),
            username: String::new(),
            password: String::new(),
            status: Arc::new(Mutex::new(String::new())),
            busy: Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false)),
        }
    }
}

impl ChallengeWorkbenchView {
    fn sync_hints(&mut self) {
        self.meta.hints = self
            .hints_text
            .lines()
            .map(|l| l.trim().to_string())
            .filter(|l| !l.is_empty())
            .collect();
    }

    fn set_status(&self, s: impl Into<String>) {
        if let Ok(mut g) = self.status.lock() {
            *g = s.into();
        }
    }

    /// The source file the workspace should save from its editor tab before a pending Build or
    /// Submit runs (`None` when nothing waits for a save). Answer with [`Self::report_save`].
    pub fn save_request(&self) -> Option<std::path::PathBuf> {
        if self.after_save.is_some() && self.save_result.is_none() {
            self.main_rs.clone()
        } else {
            None
        }
    }

    /// The outcome of saving `main.rs` (Ok also when no editor had it open, or it was clean).
    pub fn report_save(&mut self, result: Result<(), String>) {
        self.save_result = Some(result);
    }

    /// Runs a Build or Submit once its save went through.
    fn take_ready_action(&mut self) -> Option<AfterSave> {
        self.after_save?;
        match self.save_result.take()? {
            Ok(()) => self.after_save.take(),
            Err(e) => {
                self.after_save = None;
                self.set_status(format!("Could not save main.rs, so nothing was run: {e}"));
                None
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Draws the workbench. Scaffolding pushes the generated `main.rs` to `open_requests` (the app
/// opens it in the editor); Build & test drives `run_console`; Submit runs on a background thread.
pub fn challenge_workbench(
    ui: &mut Ui,
    view: &mut ChallengeWorkbenchView,
    open_requests: &mut Vec<PathBuf>,
    run_console: &mut RunConsole,
) {
    // Build / Submit first save main.rs from the editor (via the workspace); act once it has.
    let ready = view.take_ready_action();
    if view.after_save.is_some() {
        ui.ctx().request_repaint();
    }
    egui::ScrollArea::vertical()
        .auto_shrink([false, false])
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            ui.heading("Challenge Workbench");
            ui.label(muted(
                "Build your own crackme or keygen, test it, and submit it for review. You write the \
                 check() logic; the platform owns the flag, the build and the challenge id.",
            ));
            ui.add_space(6.0);

            // 1. Metadata.
            ui.heading("1 · Describe it");
            egui::Grid::new("cw_meta")
                .num_columns(2)
                .spacing([8.0, 6.0])
                .show(ui, |ui| {
                    ui.label("Title");
                    ui.text_edit_singleline(&mut view.meta.title);
                    ui.end_row();
                    ui.label("Category");
                    ui.text_edit_singleline(&mut view.meta.category);
                    ui.end_row();
                    ui.label("Technique");
                    ui.text_edit_singleline(&mut view.meta.technique);
                    ui.end_row();
                    ui.label("Difficulty");
                    egui::ComboBox::from_id_salt("cw_level")
                        .selected_text(format!("Level {}", view.meta.level))
                        .show_ui(ui, |ui| {
                            for l in 1..=5u8 {
                                ui.selectable_value(&mut view.meta.level, l, format!("Level {l}"));
                            }
                        });
                    ui.end_row();
                    ui.label("Input label");
                    ui.text_edit_singleline(&mut view.meta.input_label);
                    ui.end_row();
                });
            ui.label("Brief");
            ui.text_edit_multiline(&mut view.meta.brief);
            ui.label("Hints (one per line)");
            ui.text_edit_multiline(&mut view.hints_text);
            ui.label("Writeup (shown after solving)");
            ui.text_edit_multiline(&mut view.meta.writeup);

            ui.add_space(6.0);
            ui.separator();

            // 2. Source.
            ui.heading("2 · Write the logic");
            ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                ui.label("challenge-kit:");
                ui.radio_value(&mut view.use_builtin_kit, true, "Built-in")
                    .on_hover_text(
                        "Use the challenge-kit bundled with ORRESS. It is vendored into the project, \
                         so it builds offline with no external repository.",
                    );
                ui.radio_value(&mut view.use_builtin_kit, false, "External")
                    .on_hover_text("Depend on your own challenge-kit checkout instead.");
            });
            if !view.use_builtin_kit {
                ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                    ui.label("    dependency:");
                    ui.add(
                        egui::TextEdit::singleline(&mut view.kit_source)
                            .desired_width(360.0)
                            .hint_text(r#"git = "https://…"  or  path = "../checkout""#),
                    )
                    .on_hover_text(
                        "A Cargo dependency spec body for challenge-kit, e.g. \
                         git = \"https://github.com/you/challenge-kit\" or path = \"../checkout\".",
                    );
                });
            }
            ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                if ui
                    .button("Scaffold & open in editor")
                    .on_hover_text("Create a challenge-kit project and open its main.rs in the editor")
                    .clicked()
                    && let Some(dir) = rfd::FileDialog::new()
                        .set_title("Choose an (empty) folder for the challenge project")
                        .pick_folder()
                {
                    view.sync_hints();
                    let kit = if view.use_builtin_kit {
                        KitSource::BuiltIn
                    } else {
                        KitSource::External(view.kit_source.clone())
                    };
                    match orress_challenge::scaffold(&dir, &view.meta, &kit) {
                        Ok(main) => {
                            view.project_dir = Some(dir);
                            open_requests.push(main.clone());
                            view.main_rs = Some(main);
                            view.set_status(
                                "Scaffolded. Edit main.rs in the editor, then Build & test or Submit.",
                            );
                        }
                        Err(e) => view.set_status(format!("Scaffold failed: {e}")),
                    }
                }
                if let Some(main) = view.main_rs.clone()
                    && ui.button("Re-open main.rs").clicked()
                {
                    open_requests.push(main);
                }
            });
            if let Some(dir) = &view.project_dir {
                ui.label(muted(format!("Project: {}", dir.display())));
            }
            let can_build =
                view.project_dir.is_some() && !run_console.is_running() && view.after_save.is_none();
            if ui
                .add_enabled(can_build, egui::Button::new("Build & test (cargo run)"))
                .on_hover_text(
                    "Save main.rs, then compile and run your challenge to try it in \
                     challenge-kit's window",
                )
                .clicked()
            {
                view.after_save = Some(AfterSave::Build);
                view.save_result = None;
            }
            if ready == Some(AfterSave::Build)
                && let Some(dir) = view.project_dir.clone()
            {
                let task = orress_editor::Task {
                    label: "cargo run".into(),
                    steps: vec![orress_editor::Command {
                        program: "cargo".into(),
                        args: vec!["run".into()],
                        cwd: dir,
                    }],
                };
                let ctx = ui.ctx().clone();
                run_console.run(task, Arc::new(move || ctx.request_repaint()));
                view.set_status("Building — see the Output panel.");
            }

            ui.add_space(6.0);
            ui.separator();

            // 3. Submit.
            ui.heading("3 · Submit for review");
            egui::Grid::new("cw_submit")
                .num_columns(2)
                .spacing([8.0, 6.0])
                .show(ui, |ui| {
                    ui.label("Site URL");
                    ui.text_edit_singleline(&mut view.site_url);
                    ui.end_row();
                    ui.label("Username");
                    ui.text_edit_singleline(&mut view.username);
                    ui.end_row();
                    ui.label("Password");
                    ui.add(egui::TextEdit::singleline(&mut view.password).password(true));
                    ui.end_row();
                });
            let busy = view.busy.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
            let can_submit = !busy
                && view.main_rs.is_some()
                && !view.username.is_empty()
                && view.after_save.is_none();
            if ui
                .add_enabled(can_submit, egui::Button::new("Submit to CTF site"))
                .on_hover_text("Save main.rs, log in and send the source + metadata for review")
                .clicked()
            {
                view.after_save = Some(AfterSave::Submit);
                view.save_result = None;
            }
            if ready == Some(AfterSave::Submit) {
                view.sync_hints();
                match view.main_rs.as_ref().map(std::fs::read_to_string) {
                    Some(Ok(source)) => {
                        let base = view.site_url.clone();
                        let user = view.username.clone();
                        let pass = view.password.clone();
                        let meta = view.meta.clone();
                        let status = Arc::clone(&view.status);
                        let busy_flag = Arc::clone(&view.busy);
                        busy_flag.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
                        view.set_status("Submitting…");
                        let ctx = ui.ctx().clone();
                        std::thread::spawn(move || {
                            let result = orress_challenge::submit(&base, &user, &pass, &meta, &source);
                            if let Ok(mut g) = status.lock() {
                                *g = match result {
                                    Ok(m) => m,
                                    Err(e) => format!("Error: {e}"),
                                };
                            }
                            busy_flag.store(false, Ordering::Relaxed);
                            ctx.request_repaint();
                        });
                    }
                    Some(Err(e)) => view.set_status(format!("Could not read main.rs (save it first?): {e}")),
                    None => view.set_status("Scaffold the challenge first."),
                }
            }
            if busy {
                ui.ctx().request_repaint();
                ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                    ui.spinner();
                    ui.label("working…");
                });
            }

            let status = view.status.lock().map(|g| g.clone()).unwrap_or_default();
            if !status.is_empty() {
                ui.add_space(4.0);
                ui.separator();
                ui.label(&status);
            }
        });
}
```

`crates/orress-views/src/code.rs`:

```rs
//! Rendering code lines as colored, clickable text, shared by the disassembly and graph
//! views. Text is monospace, so a token's position is its character column.

use std::collections::BTreeSet;
use std::ops::Range;

use egui::text::LayoutJob;
use egui::{Color32, Context, FontId, Id, TextFormat};
use orress_analysis::{Insn, Line, LineKind, Program, TokenKind};
use orress_editor::{Language, Tok};
use orress_project::Document;
use orress_theme::SyntaxColors;

/// Colour for one source token kind, mirroring the code editor's own mapping.
fn source_color(kind: Tok, c: &SyntaxColors, default: Color32) -> Color32 {
    match kind {
        Tok::Keyword => c.keyword.0,
        Tok::Type => c.type_name.0,
        Tok::Function | Tok::Macro => c.function.0,
        Tok::Attribute | Tok::Lifetime => c.label.0,
        Tok::String | Tok::Char => c.string.0,
        Tok::Number => c.immediate.0,
        Tok::Comment => c.comment.0,
        #[allow(unreachable_patterns)]
        _ => default,
    }
}

/// A syntax-highlighted layout job for `text` as `lang` source, using the same tree-sitter
/// highlighter and theme colours as the code editor. Used for read-only colored views such as
/// the decompiler's Rust-port tab, so it reads like the IDE editor. Does not wrap (the view
/// scrolls horizontally).
pub fn highlight_job(
    text: &str,
    lang: Language,
    colors: &SyntaxColors,
    font: FontId,
    default: Color32,
) -> LayoutJob {
    let tokens = orress_editor::highlight(text, lang);
    let mut job = LayoutJob::default();
    job.wrap.max_width = f32::INFINITY;
    let len = text.len();
    // A boundary at every token edge, so each emitted run has one uniform colour.
    let mut points: BTreeSet<usize> = BTreeSet::from([0, len]);
    for t in &tokens {
        points.insert(t.start.min(len));
        points.insert(t.end.min(len));
    }
    let points: Vec<usize> = points
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|p| text.is_char_boundary(*p))
        .collect();
    for w in points.windows(2) {
        let (a, b) = (w[0], w[1]);
        if a >= b {
            continue;
        }
        let col = tokens
            .iter()
            .find(|t| t.start <= a && a < t.end)
            .map_or(default, |t| source_color(t.kind, colors, default));
        job.append(&text[a..b], 0.0, TextFormat::simple(font.clone(), col));
    }
    job
}

/// What a span of text refers to, for clicks and explanations.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Target {
    Address(u64),
    Number(u64),
    Mnemonic(String),
    Register(String),
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Span {
    pub chars: Range<usize>,
    pub target: Target,
}

pub struct Rendered {
    pub job: LayoutJob,
    pub spans: Vec<Span>,
    pub chars: usize,
}

fn syntax_id() -> Id {
    Id::new("orress::syntax_colors")
}

/// The app stores the current theme's syntax colors here.
pub fn set_syntax(ctx: &Context, colors: SyntaxColors) {
    ctx.data_mut(|d| d.insert_temp(syntax_id(), colors));
}

pub fn syntax(ctx: &Context) -> SyntaxColors {
    ctx.data(|d| d.get_temp::<SyntaxColors>(syntax_id()))
        .unwrap_or_else(|| orress_theme::Theme::rusty_dark().syntax)
}

pub struct Style {
    pub font: FontId,
    pub colors: SyntaxColors,
    pub text: Color32,
    pub muted: Color32,
    pub wide: bool,
    pub show_address: bool,
    pub show_bytes: bool,
}

struct Builder<'a> {
    job: LayoutJob,
    spans: Vec<Span>,
    chars: usize,
    style: &'a Style,
}

impl Builder<'_> {
    fn push(&mut self, text: &str, color: Color32, target: Option<Target>) {
        let n = text.chars().count();
        if let Some(target) = target {
            self.spans.push(Span {
                chars: self.chars..self.chars + n,
                target,
            });
        }
        self.job.append(
            text,
            0.0,
            TextFormat::simple(self.style.font.clone(), color),
        );
        self.chars += n;
    }

    fn pad_to(&mut self, column: usize) {
        if self.chars < column {
            let pad = " ".repeat(column - self.chars);
            self.push(&pad, self.style.text, None);
        }
    }

    fn finish(self) -> Rendered {
        Rendered {
            job: self.job,
            spans: self.spans,
            chars: self.chars,
        }
    }
}

fn hex_color(c: &orress_theme::Hex) -> Color32 {
    c.0
}

pub fn address_text(addr: u64, wide: bool) -> String {
    if wide {
        format!("{addr:016x}")
    } else {
        format!("{addr:08x}")
    }
}

/// Name for an address, with an offset into a function if it is inside one:
/// `main`, `main+0x1a`, or the plain hex address.
pub fn describe_address(doc: &Document, program: &Program, addr: u64) -> String {
    if let Some(name) = doc.name_of(addr) {
        return name;
    }
    if let Some(f) = program.function_containing(addr)
        && let Some(name) = doc.name_of(f.entry)
    {
        return format!("{name}+0x{:x}", addr - f.entry);
    }
    format!("0x{addr:x}")
}

fn parse_number(text: &str) -> Option<u64> {
    let t = text.trim_start_matches('#');
    match t.strip_prefix("0x") {
        Some(hex) => u64::from_str_radix(hex, 16).ok(),
        None => t.parse::<i64>().ok().map(|v| v as u64),
    }
}

/// Text hidden in a number: compilers store short strings as immediates, e.g.
/// `mov rcx,0x7365735f6e65706f` is "open_ses" (bytes in little-endian order).
pub fn text_in_number(value: u64) -> Option<String> {
    let bytes = value.to_le_bytes();
    let len = 8 - bytes.iter().rev().take_while(|&&b| b == 0).count();
    let text = &bytes[..len];
    (len >= 3 && text.iter().all(|b| (0x20..=0x7e).contains(b)))
        .then(|| String::from_utf8_lossy(text).into_owned())
}

/// Plain-language reading of a number: hex, decimal, signed, character.
pub fn describe_number(value: u64) -> String {
    let mut s = format!("0x{value:x} = {value}");
    if (value as i64) < 0 {
        s += &format!(" = {} (signed)", value as i64);
    }
    if value <= 0xff {
        let ch = match value as u8 {
            0x20..=0x7e => format!("'{}'", value as u8 as char),
            0 => "NUL".into(),
            0x0a => "'\\n' (newline)".into(),
            0x0d => "'\\r' (carriage return)".into(),
            0x09 => "'\\t' (tab)".into(),
            _ => "not a printable character".into(),
        };
        s += &format!("\nas a character: {ch}");
    } else if let Some(text) = text_in_number(value) {
        s += &format!("\nas text (little-endian bytes): \"{text}\"");
    }
    s
}

/// Comment for an instruction: yours, a string it refers to, or text hidden in an
/// immediate number.
pub fn auto_comment(doc: &Document, program: &Program, insn: &Insn) -> Option<String> {
    if let Some(c) = doc.annotations.comments.get(&insn.address) {
        return Some(c.clone());
    }
    let string = insn.data_refs.iter().find_map(|r| {
        program.string_refs.get(r).map(|s| {
            // Rust passes strings as (pointer, length): if the next instruction loads a
            // small number, that is likely the length, so cut the text there.
            let len = following_length(program, insn)
                .filter(|&n| n > 0 && n <= s.len() && s.is_char_boundary(n));
            let s = len.map_or(s.as_str(), |n| &s[..n]);
            let mut text: String = s.chars().take(60).collect();
            if s.chars().count() > 60 {
                text.push('…');
            }
            format!("\"{text}\"")
        })
    });
    string.or_else(|| {
        insn.operands.iter().find_map(|t| match t.kind {
            TokenKind::Number => parse_number(&t.text)
                .filter(|&v| v > 0xffff)
                .and_then(text_in_number)
                .map(|text| format!("\"{text}\" (text stored in a number)")),
            _ => None,
        })
    })
}

/// Length loaded right after a string address, if any (`mov edx,0x15`). Newer Rust
/// versions store literal lengths as `len * 2 + 1`; both forms are accepted.
fn following_length(program: &Program, insn: &Insn) -> Option<usize> {
    let next = program.decode(insn.end())?;
    if next.mnemonic != "mov" {
        return None;
    }
    let value = next.operands.iter().rev().find_map(|t| match t.kind {
        TokenKind::Number => parse_number(&t.text),
        _ => None,
    })?;
    let value = if value % 2 == 1 { value >> 1 } else { value };
    usize::try_from(value).ok()
}

pub fn render_insn(doc: &Document, program: &Program, insn: &Insn, style: &Style) -> Rendered {
    let c = &style.colors;
    let mut b = Builder {
        job: LayoutJob::default(),
        spans: Vec::new(),
        chars: 0,
        style,
    };
    if style.show_address {
        b.push(
            &address_text(insn.address, style.wide),
            hex_color(&c.address),
            None,
        );
        b.push("  ", style.text, None);
    }
    if style.show_bytes {
        let bytes = program
            .memory
            .read(insn.address, insn.len.into())
            .unwrap_or(&[]);
        let mut hex: String = bytes.iter().take(8).map(|x| format!("{x:02x} ")).collect();
        if bytes.len() > 8 {
            hex.push('…');
        }
        b.push(&format!("{hex:<25}"), hex_color(&c.bytes), None);
    }
    let start = b.chars;
    b.push(
        &insn.mnemonic,
        hex_color(&c.mnemonic),
        Some(Target::Mnemonic(insn.mnemonic.clone())),
    );
    b.pad_to(start + 8);
    for token in &insn.operands {
        match token.kind {
            TokenKind::Address(addr) => {
                let (text, color) = match doc.name_of(addr) {
                    Some(name) => {
                        let color = if program.functions.contains_key(&addr)
                            || program
                                .name(addr)
                                .is_some_and(|n| n.kind == orress_analysis::NameKind::Import)
                        {
                            hex_color(&c.function)
                        } else {
                            hex_color(&c.label)
                        };
                        (name, color)
                    }
                    // Jump targets inside a function are labels, shown as in the listing.
                    None if program.labels.contains(&addr) => {
                        (format!("loc_{addr:x}"), hex_color(&c.label))
                    }
                    None => (token.text.clone(), hex_color(&c.immediate)),
                };
                b.push(&text, color, Some(Target::Address(addr)));
            }
            TokenKind::Register => b.push(
                &token.text,
                hex_color(&c.register),
                Some(Target::Register(token.text.clone())),
            ),
            TokenKind::Number => {
                let target = parse_number(&token.text).map(Target::Number);
                b.push(&token.text, hex_color(&c.immediate), target);
            }
            TokenKind::Keyword => b.push(&token.text, hex_color(&c.keyword), None),
            TokenKind::Mnemonic => b.push(&token.text, hex_color(&c.mnemonic), None),
            TokenKind::Punct | TokenKind::Text => b.push(&token.text, style.text, None),
        }
    }
    if let Some(comment) = auto_comment(doc, program, insn) {
        b.pad_to(start + 40);
        b.push(&format!("  ; {comment}"), hex_color(&c.comment), None);
    }
    b.finish()
}

/// Renders one listing line (instruction, label, function header, data or region).
pub fn render_line(doc: &Document, program: &Program, line: &Line, style: &Style) -> Rendered {
    let c = &style.colors;
    let mut b = Builder {
        job: LayoutJob::default(),
        spans: Vec::new(),
        chars: 0,
        style,
    };
    match line.kind {
        LineKind::Insn => {
            return match program.decode(line.addr) {
                Some(insn) => render_insn(doc, program, &insn, style),
                None => {
                    b.push(
                        &address_text(line.addr, style.wide),
                        hex_color(&c.address),
                        None,
                    );
                    b.push("  ??", style.muted, None);
                    b.finish()
                }
            };
        }
        LineKind::Region => {
            let name = program
                .memory
                .region(line.addr)
                .map_or_else(String::new, |r| r.name.clone());
            b.push(
                &address_text(line.addr, style.wide),
                hex_color(&c.address),
                None,
            );
            b.push(
                &format!("  ; ===== section {name} ====="),
                hex_color(&c.comment),
                None,
            );
        }
        LineKind::Function => {
            b.push(
                &address_text(line.addr, style.wide),
                hex_color(&c.address),
                None,
            );
            b.push("  ", style.text, None);
            let name = doc
                .name_of(line.addr)
                .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("sub_{:x}", line.addr));
            b.push(
                &format!("{name}:"),
                hex_color(&c.function),
                Some(Target::Address(line.addr)),
            );
            let refs = program.xrefs(line.addr).len();
            let blocks = program
                .functions
                .get(&line.addr)
                .map_or(0, |f| f.blocks.len());
            let mut info = format!(
                "   ; function · {blocks} block{}",
                if blocks == 1 { "" } else { "s" }
            );
            if refs > 0 {
                info += &format!(" · {refs} reference{}", if refs == 1 { "" } else { "s" });
            }
            if program.main == Some(line.addr) {
                info += " · program entry (main)";
            }
            if let Some(comment) = doc.annotations.comments.get(&line.addr) {
                info += &format!(" · {comment}");
            }
            b.push(&info, hex_color(&c.comment), None);
        }
        LineKind::Label => {
            b.push(
                &address_text(line.addr, style.wide),
                hex_color(&c.address),
                None,
            );
            b.push("  ", style.text, None);
            let name = doc
                .name_of(line.addr)
                .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("loc_{:x}", line.addr));
            b.push(
                &format!("{name}:"),
                hex_color(&c.label),
                Some(Target::Address(line.addr)),
            );
        }
        LineKind::Data(n) => {
            b.push(
                &address_text(line.addr, style.wide),
                hex_color(&c.address),
                None,
            );
            b.push("  ", style.text, None);
            let start = b.chars;
            b.push("db", style.muted, None);
            b.pad_to(start + 8);
            let bytes = program.memory.read(line.addr, n.into()).unwrap_or(&[]);
            let text: Vec<String> = bytes.iter().map(|x| format!("0x{x:02x}")).collect();
            b.push(&text.join(","), style.muted, None);
        }
    }
    b.finish()
}

/// Span under a character column.
pub fn span_at(spans: &[Span], column: usize) -> Option<&Span> {
    spans.iter().find(|s| s.chars.contains(&column))
}

/// The largest index `<= max` that is a char boundary of `s`, so `&s[..i]` never panics.
pub(crate) fn floor_char_boundary(s: &str, max: usize) -> usize {
    if max >= s.len() {
        return s.len();
    }
    (0..=max)
        .rev()
        .find(|&i| s.is_char_boundary(i))
        .unwrap_or(0)
}
```
