`crates/orress-views/src/debugger.rs`:

```rs
//! The debugger: a bottom-dock panel with run controls, registers, flags, the stack and
//! breakpoints, plus the glue that marks the current instruction and breakpoints in the
//! disassembly.
//!
//! [`DebugSession`] is the long-lived state the app owns; the panel and the disassembly
//! view both read and drive it. Addresses the user sees are file virtual addresses (based
//! on the file's preferred load address); the target runs at a possibly different base
//! (ASLR), so the session translates between the two.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::Arc;

use egui::{RichText, Ui};
use orress_debug::{DebugState, Debugger, Registers, Status, StopReason};
use orress_project::Document;
use orress_ui::{ExplainExt as _, muted};

const EXPLAIN: &str = "The debugger runs the program under ORRESS's control. Set breakpoints (F9 in the \
    disassembly, or click the gutter) to stop at an address; then step one instruction at a time and \
    watch the registers, flags and stack change. You can even change a register or a byte of memory \
    and continue. Debugging runs the real program, so only debug code you trust.";

/// No breakpoints (returned for a file that has none).
static NO_BREAKPOINTS: BTreeSet<u64> = BTreeSet::new();

/// Debugger state the app keeps between frames.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct DebugSession {
    active: Option<Active>,
    /// Breakpoints the user has set, per binary, as file virtual addresses. Kept even when no
    /// target is running, so Start re-applies them.
    breakpoints: BTreeMap<PathBuf, BTreeSet<u64>>,
    /// The file the path-less accessors ([`DebugSession::breakpoints`],
    /// [`DebugSession::toggle_breakpoint`]) refer to: the binary a view last asked about via
    /// [`DebugSession::current_file_rip`] or [`DebugSession::set_current_file`].
    current: Option<PathBuf>,
}

struct Active {
    path: PathBuf,
    dbg: Debugger,
    state: DebugState,
    /// The file's preferred load address, to translate file <-> runtime addresses.
    preferred_base: u64,
    /// Whether the user's breakpoints have been applied to this run.
    applied: bool,
    /// The generation we last reacted to (to refresh the stack read on each stop).
    seen_generation: u64,
}

impl DebugSession {
    /// Starts debugging `path`. `preferred_base` comes from the file's analysis.
    pub fn start(&mut self, path: &Path, preferred_base: u64, notify: Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>) {
        let dbg = Debugger::launch(path.to_path_buf(), Vec::new(), notify);
        self.active = Some(Active {
            path: path.to_path_buf(),
            dbg,
            state: DebugState {
                status: Status::Starting,
                ..empty_state()
            },
            preferred_base,
            applied: false,
            seen_generation: 0,
        });
    }

    pub fn is_active_for(&self, path: &Path) -> bool {
        self.active.as_ref().is_some_and(|a| a.path == path)
    }

    pub fn is_running_somewhere(&self) -> bool {
        self.active.as_ref().is_some_and(|a| a.state.is_alive())
    }

    /// The current target state (refreshed each frame by [`DebugSession::refresh`]), for views that
    /// read registers / memory map / pid, e.g. the heap visualizer.
    pub fn state(&self) -> Option<&DebugState> {
        self.active.as_ref().map(|a| &a.state)
    }

    /// The target pid while stopped (for pid-based memory reads via `orress_debug::read_mem`).
    pub fn stopped_pid(&self) -> Option<u32> {
        let a = self.active.as_ref()?;
        if a.state.is_stopped() {
            a.state.pid
        } else {
            None
        }
    }

    /// The base address of the loaded libc (`libc.so.6`), from the module list.
    pub fn libc_base(&self) -> Option<u64> {
        let a = self.active.as_ref()?;
        a.state
            .modules
            .iter()
            .find(|m| {
                let n = m.name.rsplit(['/', '\\']).next().unwrap_or(&m.name);
                n.starts_with("libc.so") || n.starts_with("libc-") || n == "libc.so.6"
            })
            .map(|m| m.base)
    }

    /// The generation of the current snapshot, so a view caches until the next stop.
    pub fn generation(&self) -> u64 {
        self.active.as_ref().map_or(0, |a| a.state.generation)
    }

    /// Makes `path` the file the path-less breakpoint accessors refer to.
    pub fn set_current_file(&mut self, path: &Path) {
        if self.current.as_deref() != Some(path) {
            self.current = Some(path.to_path_buf());
        }
    }

    /// The breakpoints (file VAs) of the current file (see [`DebugSession::set_current_file`]).
    pub fn breakpoints(&self) -> &BTreeSet<u64> {
        match &self.current {
            Some(path) => self.breakpoints_for(path),
            None => &NO_BREAKPOINTS,
        }
    }

    /// The breakpoints (file VAs) set in `path`.
    pub fn breakpoints_for(&self, path: &Path) -> &BTreeSet<u64> {
        self.breakpoints.get(path).unwrap_or(&NO_BREAKPOINTS)
    }

    /// The runtime instruction pointer translated to a file VA, if stopped in `path`. Also makes
    /// `path` the current file, so a view's following `breakpoints()` / `toggle_breakpoint()`
    /// calls act on the binary it shows.
    pub fn current_file_rip(&mut self, path: &Path) -> Option<u64> {
        self.set_current_file(path);
        let a = self.active.as_ref()?;
        if a.path != path || !a.state.is_stopped() {
            return None;
        }
        a.runtime_to_file(a.state.registers.rip)
    }

    /// Toggles a breakpoint at a file VA of the current file (see
    /// [`DebugSession::set_current_file`]); does nothing when no file is current.
    pub fn toggle_breakpoint(&mut self, file_va: u64) {
        if let Some(path) = self.current.clone() {
            self.toggle_breakpoint_in(&path, file_va);
        }
    }

    /// Toggles a breakpoint at a file VA of `path`; applies it immediately if that binary is the
    /// one being debugged.
    pub fn toggle_breakpoint_in(&mut self, path: &Path, file_va: u64) {
        let set = self.breakpoints.entry(path.to_path_buf()).or_default();
        let added = set.insert(file_va);
        if !added {
            set.remove(&file_va);
        }
        if set.is_empty() {
            self.breakpoints.remove(path);
        }
        if let Some(a) = &self.active
            && a.path == path
            && let Some(rt) = a.file_to_runtime(file_va)
        {
            if added {
                a.dbg.add_breakpoint(rt);
            } else {
                a.dbg.remove_breakpoint(rt);
            }
        }
    }

    /// Runs a debugger command (from the F5/F10/F11 shortcuts) on the running target. Both step
    /// commands execute one instruction (machine code has no source lines to step over). Returns
    /// whether a target took it.
    pub fn command(&mut self, action: crate::DebugAction) -> bool {
        use crate::DebugAction;
        let Some(a) = &self.active else {
            return false;
        };
        let stopped = a.state.is_stopped();
        match action {
            DebugAction::Continue if stopped => a.dbg.resume(),
            DebugAction::StepOver | DebugAction::StepInto if stopped => a.dbg.step(),
            DebugAction::Pause if a.state.status == Status::Running => a.dbg.pause(),
            DebugAction::Stop if a.state.is_alive() => a.dbg.kill(),
            _ => return false,
        }
        true
    }

    /// Pulls the latest target state and reacts to a new stop (apply breakpoints, read
    /// the stack). Call once per frame before drawing.
    pub fn refresh(&mut self) {
        let Some(a) = &mut self.active else {
            return;
        };
        a.state = a.dbg.state();
        // Apply the user's breakpoints for this binary as soon as the runtime base is known.
        if !a.applied && a.state.image_base.is_some() {
            for &va in self.breakpoints.get(&a.path).unwrap_or(&NO_BREAKPOINTS) {
                if let Some(rt) = a.file_to_runtime(va) {
                    a.dbg.add_breakpoint(rt);
                }
            }
            a.applied = true;
        }
        // On each new stop, refresh the stack and the memory pane.
        if a.state.generation != a.seen_generation && a.state.is_stopped() {
            a.seen_generation = a.state.generation;
            a.dbg.read_stack(a.state.registers.rsp, 128);
        }
    }
}

fn empty_state() -> DebugState {
    // DebugState has no public constructor; make one via a throwaway debugger would spawn
    // a thread, so build the fields we need directly through Default-like values.
    DebugState {
        status: Status::Starting,
        reason: None,
        registers: Registers::default(),
        prev_registers: Registers::default(),
        modules: Vec::new(),
        image_base: None,
        pid: None,
        breakpoints: std::collections::BTreeMap::new(),
        last_error: None,
        memory: None,
        stack: None,
        generation: 0,
    }
}

impl Active {
    fn file_to_runtime(&self, va: u64) -> Option<u64> {
        let base = self.state.image_base?;
        Some(va.wrapping_sub(self.preferred_base).wrapping_add(base))
    }

    fn runtime_to_file(&self, rt: u64) -> Option<u64> {
        let base = self.state.image_base?;
        Some(rt.wrapping_sub(base).wrapping_add(self.preferred_base))
    }
}

/// Draws the debugger panel for the active document.
pub fn debugger_panel(ui: &mut Ui, session: &mut DebugSession, doc: Option<&mut Document>) {
    session.refresh();
    let Some(doc) = doc else {
        ui.label("Open a program to debug it.");
        return;
    };
    let path = doc.path.clone();
    session.set_current_file(&path);

    // A run that ended (exited, stopped or failed) shows the start screen again, with how
    // the last run ended, so the program can be debugged as many times as needed.
    let ended = session
        .active
        .as_ref()
        .filter(|a| a.path == path && !a.state.is_alive())
        .map(|a| a.state.clone());
    if !session.is_active_for(&path) || ended.is_some() {
        if let Some(last) = &ended {
            ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                ui.label(muted("Last run:"));
                status_line(ui, last);
            });
            ui.separator();
        }
        start_screen(ui, session, doc);
        return;
    }

    // `state` is a cheap clone so we do not hold a borrow of `session` across the
    // breakpoint list, which needs `&mut session`.
    let state = session.active.as_ref().expect("active").state.clone();

    if let Some(a) = &session.active {
        controls(ui, &a.dbg, &state);
    }
    status_line(ui, &state);
    ui.separator();

    egui::ScrollArea::vertical()
        .auto_shrink([false, false])
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            if let Some(a) = &session.active {
                registers(ui, &state);
                edit_register(ui, &a.dbg, &state);
                ui.add_space(6.0);
                flags(ui, &state);
                ui.add_space(6.0);
                egui::CollapsingHeader::new("Stack")
                    .default_open(true)
                    .show(ui, |ui| {
                        stack_view(ui, &state);
                    });
                egui::CollapsingHeader::new("Memory")
                    .default_open(false)
                    .show(ui, |ui| {
                        memory_view(ui, &a.dbg, a.preferred_base, &state);
                    });
                ui.label(muted(
                    "F5 continue · F10/F11 step one instruction · Shift+F5 stop (with this panel focused)",
                ));
            }
            egui::CollapsingHeader::new("Breakpoints")
                .default_open(true)
                .show(ui, |ui| {
                    breakpoints_list(ui, session, doc);
                });
        });
}

fn start_screen(ui: &mut Ui, session: &mut DebugSession, doc: &mut Document) {
    ui.add_space(4.0);
    ui.label(RichText::new("Debugger").strong())
        .note("Debugger", EXPLAIN);
    ui.label(muted(EXPLAIN));
    ui.add_space(8.0);

    let base = doc.analysis().map(|a| a.info.image_base);
    let main = doc.program().and_then(|p| p.main);
    let is_exe = doc
        .analysis()
        .map(|a| {
            matches!(
                a.info.format,
                orress_loaders::Format::Pe
                    | orress_loaders::Format::Coff
                    | orress_loaders::Format::Elf
            )
        })
        .unwrap_or(false);

    if !cfg!(all(
        any(target_os = "windows", target_os = "linux"),
        target_arch = "x86_64"
    )) {
        ui.colored_label(
            ui.visuals().warn_fg_color,
            "Native debugging is available on Windows and Linux (x86-64). A macOS back end, and a \
             GDB-remote back end for other targets, are planned.",
        );
        return;
    }
    if !is_exe {
        ui.label(muted(
            "Open a native program (a Windows .exe or a Linux ELF) to debug it. Other formats come \
             with later back ends.",
        ));
    }

    let path = doc.path.clone();
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        let start = ui
            .button(RichText::new("▶ Start debugging").strong())
            .explain(
                "Start debugging",
                "Launches the program under the debugger and stops at the first breakpoint.",
            );
        if start.clicked()
            && let Some(base) = base
        {
            // If the user set no breakpoints, stop at main so they are not lost at once.
            if session.breakpoints_for(&path).is_empty()
                && let Some(main) = main
            {
                session.toggle_breakpoint_in(&path, main);
            }
            let ctx = ui.ctx().clone();
            let notify: Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync> = Arc::new(move || ctx.request_repaint());
            session.start(&path, base, notify);
        }
    });
    if main.is_some() {
        ui.label(muted(
            "The program will stop at main. Set more breakpoints with F9 in the disassembly.",
        ));
    }
}

fn controls(ui: &mut Ui, dbg: &Debugger, state: &DebugState) {
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        let stopped = state.is_stopped();
        let running = state.status == Status::Running;
        if ui
            .add_enabled(stopped, egui::Button::new("▶ Continue"))
            .on_hover_text("F5 (with the Debugger panel focused)")
            .clicked()
        {
            dbg.resume();
        }
        if ui
            .add_enabled(stopped, egui::Button::new("↷ Step"))
            .on_hover_text("One instruction (F10 or F11, with the Debugger panel focused)")
            .clicked()
        {
            dbg.step();
        }
        if ui
            .add_enabled(running, egui::Button::new("⏸ Pause"))
            .clicked()
        {
            dbg.pause();
        }
        if ui
            .add_enabled(state.is_alive(), egui::Button::new("⏹ Stop"))
            .on_hover_text("Shift+F5")
            .clicked()
        {
            dbg.kill();
        }
    });
}

fn status_line(ui: &mut Ui, state: &DebugState) {
    let text = match &state.reason {
        Some(r) => r.summary(),
        None => match state.status {
            Status::Starting => "starting…".into(),
            Status::Running => "running…".into(),
            Status::Exited => "the program has ended".into(),
            Status::Failed => "the debugger could not start".into(),
            Status::Stopped => "stopped".into(),
        },
    };
    let color = match state.status {
        Status::Failed => ui.visuals().error_fg_color,
        Status::Exited => ui.visuals().weak_text_color(),
        _ if matches!(state.reason, Some(StopReason::Exception { .. })) => {
            ui.visuals().error_fg_color
        }
        _ => ui.visuals().text_color(),
    };
    ui.colored_label(color, text);
    if let Some(e) = &state.last_error
        && state.status != Status::Failed
    {
        ui.colored_label(ui.visuals().warn_fg_color, e);
    }
}

fn registers(ui: &mut Ui, state: &DebugState) {
    let changed = state.is_stopped() && state.generation > 1;
    egui::Grid::new("dbg-regs")
        .num_columns(4)
        .spacing([14.0, 2.0])
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            let gp = state.registers.gp();
            let prev = state.prev_registers.gp();
            for (i, (name, value)) in gp.iter().enumerate() {
                let differ = changed && prev[i].1 != *value;
                reg_cell(ui, name, *value, differ);
                if i % 2 == 1 {
                    ui.end_row();
                }
            }
            reg_cell(
                ui,
                "rip",
                state.registers.rip,
                changed && state.prev_registers.rip != state.registers.rip,
            );
            reg_cell(ui, "rsp", state.registers.rsp, false);
            ui.end_row();
        });
}

fn reg_cell(ui: &mut Ui, name: &str, value: u64, changed: bool) {
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label(RichText::new(format!("{name:>3}")).monospace().weak());
        let color = if changed {
            ui.visuals().warn_fg_color
        } else {
            ui.visuals().text_color()
        };
        ui.label(
            RichText::new(format!("{value:016x}"))
                .monospace()
                .color(color),
        )
        .on_hover_text(format!("{value} (decimal)"));
    });
}

/// A compact "set a register" row: pick a register, type a hex value, apply.
fn edit_register(ui: &mut Ui, dbg: &Debugger, state: &DebugState) {
    if !state.is_stopped() {
        return;
    }
    let reg_id = ui.id().with("dbg-edit-reg");
    let val_id = ui.id().with("dbg-edit-val");
    let mut reg = ui.memory_mut(|m| {
        m.data
            .get_temp::<String>(reg_id)
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "rax".into())
    });
    let mut val = ui.memory_mut(|m| m.data.get_temp::<String>(val_id).unwrap_or_default());
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label(muted("set"));
        egui::ComboBox::from_id_salt(reg_id)
            .width(52.0)
            .selected_text(reg.clone())
            .show_ui(ui, |ui| {
                for name in orress_debug::GP_NAMES.iter().chain(&["rip", "rsp"]) {
                    ui.selectable_value(&mut reg, (*name).to_string(), *name);
                }
            });
        ui.label("=");
        let field = ui.add(
            egui::TextEdit::singleline(&mut val)
                .hint_text("hex")
                .desired_width(120.0),
        );
        let submit = ui.button("Set").clicked()
            || (field.lost_focus() && ui.input(|i| i.key_pressed(egui::Key::Enter)));
        if submit && let Ok(v) = u64::from_str_radix(val.trim().trim_start_matches("0x"), 16) {
            dbg.set_register(reg.clone(), v);
            val.clear();
        }
    });
    ui.memory_mut(|m| {
        m.data.insert_temp(reg_id, reg);
        m.data.insert_temp(val_id, val);
    });
}

fn flags(ui: &mut Ui, state: &DebugState) {
    ui.horizontal_wrapped(|ui| {
        ui.label(RichText::new("flags").monospace().weak());
        for f in &orress_debug::FLAGS {
            let on = orress_debug::flag_set(state.registers.rflags, f.bit);
            let color = if on {
                ui.visuals().warn_fg_color
            } else {
                ui.visuals().weak_text_color()
            };
            ui.label(RichText::new(f.short).monospace().color(color))
                .on_hover_text(format!(
                    "{} ({}): {}\nnow {}",
                    f.name,
                    f.short,
                    f.meaning,
                    if on { "set" } else { "clear" }
                ));
        }
    });
}

fn stack_view(ui: &mut Ui, state: &DebugState) {
    let Some((base, bytes)) = &state.stack else {
        ui.label(muted("(stops to show the stack)"));
        return;
    };
    let rsp = state.registers.rsp;
    egui::Grid::new("dbg-stack")
        .num_columns(2)
        .spacing([14.0, 2.0])
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            for (i, chunk) in bytes.chunks(8).enumerate() {
                let Ok(eight) = <[u8; 8]>::try_from(chunk) else {
                    break;
                };
                let addr = base + (i * 8) as u64;
                let value = u64::from_le_bytes(eight);
                let mark = if addr == rsp { "rsp>" } else { "    " };
                ui.label(
                    RichText::new(format!("{mark}{addr:016x}"))
                        .monospace()
                        .weak(),
                );
                ui.label(RichText::new(format!("{value:016x}")).monospace());
                ui.end_row();
            }
        });
}

fn memory_view(ui: &mut Ui, dbg: &Debugger, preferred_base: u64, state: &DebugState) {
    if !state.is_stopped() {
        ui.label(muted("(stops to read memory)"));
        return;
    }
    let base = match state.image_base {
        Some(b) => b,
        None => return,
    };
    let addr_id = ui.id().with("dbg-mem-addr");
    let gen_id = ui.id().with("dbg-mem-gen");
    let file_id = ui.id().with("dbg-mem-file");
    // Default to the instruction pointer, by name, so it is read as a runtime address.
    let mut addr_text = ui.memory_mut(|m| {
        m.data
            .get_temp::<String>(addr_id)
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "rip".into())
    });
    let mut request: Option<MemAddr> = None;
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label(muted("address"));
        let field = ui.add(
            egui::TextEdit::singleline(&mut addr_text)
                .desired_width(140.0)
                .hint_text("hex file address or register"),
        );
        let submit = ui.button("Show").clicked()
            || (field.lost_focus() && ui.input(|i| i.key_pressed(egui::Key::Enter)));
        if submit && let Some(addr) = parse_addr(&addr_text, &state.registers) {
            request = Some(addr);
        }
    });
    // Re-read whenever the target stops again, so the view stays live.
    let last_gen = ui.memory_mut(|m| m.data.get_temp::<u64>(gen_id).unwrap_or(0));
    if last_gen != state.generation
        && let Some(addr) = parse_addr(&addr_text, &state.registers)
    {
        request = Some(addr);
    }
    if let Some(addr) = request {
        // A register value is already a runtime address; typed hex is a file VA, so it moves
        // with the image (ASLR).
        let rt = match addr {
            MemAddr::Runtime(rt) => rt,
            MemAddr::File(va) => va.wrapping_sub(preferred_base).wrapping_add(base),
        };
        ui.memory_mut(|m| {
            m.data
                .insert_temp(file_id, matches!(addr, MemAddr::File(_)))
        });
        dbg.read_memory(rt, 128);
    }
    let as_file = ui.memory_mut(|m| m.data.get_temp::<bool>(file_id).unwrap_or(false));
    ui.memory_mut(|m| {
        m.data.insert_temp(addr_id, addr_text);
        m.data.insert_temp(gen_id, state.generation);
    });
    if let Some((rt_addr, bytes)) = &state.memory {
        if as_file {
            let file_addr = rt_addr.wrapping_sub(base).wrapping_add(preferred_base);
            ui.label(muted("addresses: file (as in the disassembly)"));
            hex_dump(ui, file_addr, bytes);
        } else {
            ui.label(muted("addresses: runtime (where the program is loaded)"));
            hex_dump(ui, *rt_addr, bytes);
        }
    }
}

/// An address typed into the memory pane.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum MemAddr {
    /// A register's value: an address in the running process.
    Runtime(u64),
    /// Typed hex: a file virtual address (as shown in the disassembly).
    File(u64),
}

/// A hex + ASCII dump, 16 bytes per row, starting at address `start`.
fn hex_dump(ui: &mut Ui, start: u64, bytes: &[u8]) {
    egui::Grid::new("dbg-mem-grid")
        .num_columns(3)
        .spacing([14.0, 2.0])
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            for (row, chunk) in bytes.chunks(16).enumerate() {
                let addr = start + (row * 16) as u64;
                ui.label(RichText::new(format!("{addr:016x}")).monospace().weak());
                let hex: String = chunk.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x} ")).collect();
                ui.label(RichText::new(hex).monospace());
                let ascii: String = chunk
                    .iter()
                    .map(|b| {
                        if b.is_ascii_graphic() || *b == b' ' {
                            *b as char
                        } else {
                            '.'
                        }
                    })
                    .collect();
                ui.label(RichText::new(ascii).monospace().weak());
                ui.end_row();
            }
        });
}

/// Parses a register name (a runtime address) or a hex file virtual address.
fn parse_addr(text: &str, regs: &Registers) -> Option<MemAddr> {
    let t = text.trim();
    if let Some(v) = regs.get(&t.to_ascii_lowercase()) {
        return Some(MemAddr::Runtime(v));
    }
    u64::from_str_radix(t.trim_start_matches("0x"), 16)
        .ok()
        .map(MemAddr::File)
}

fn breakpoints_list(ui: &mut Ui, session: &mut DebugSession, doc: &mut Document) {
    let bps: Vec<u64> = session.breakpoints_for(&doc.path).iter().copied().collect();
    if bps.is_empty() {
        ui.label(muted(
            "None yet. In the disassembly, press F9 or click the gutter.",
        ));
        return;
    }
    let program = doc.program().cloned();
    let mut remove = None;
    let mut go = None;
    for va in bps {
        ui.horizontal(|ui| {
            if ui.small_button("✕").on_hover_text("Remove").clicked() {
                remove = Some(va);
            }
            let label = program
                .as_ref()
                .map(|p| code_describe(doc, p, va))
                .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("0x{va:x}"));
            if ui.link(RichText::new(label).monospace()).clicked() {
                go = Some(va);
            }
        });
    }
    if let Some(va) = remove {
        session.toggle_breakpoint_in(&doc.path, va);
    }
    if let Some(va) = go {
        doc.navigate_to_address(va);
    }
}

fn code_describe(doc: &Document, program: &orress_project::Program, va: u64) -> String {
    crate::code::describe_address(doc, program, va)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn breakpoints_are_kept_per_binary() {
        let mut s = DebugSession::default();
        let (a, b) = (Path::new("a.exe"), Path::new("b.exe"));
        // A view showing a.exe asks about it first (as the disassembly does), then toggles.
        assert_eq!(s.current_file_rip(a), None);
        s.toggle_breakpoint(0x401000);
        assert!(s.breakpoints().contains(&0x401000));
        // Switching to b.exe shows its own (empty) set; a.exe's breakpoint is not leaked.
        s.current_file_rip(b);
        assert!(s.breakpoints().is_empty());
        s.toggle_breakpoint(0x402000);
        assert_eq!(s.breakpoints_for(a).len(), 1);
        assert!(s.breakpoints_for(b).contains(&0x402000));
        // Toggling again removes it.
        s.toggle_breakpoint_in(a, 0x401000);
        assert!(s.breakpoints_for(a).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn register_names_are_runtime_addresses() {
        let regs = Registers {
            rip: 0x7ff6_1234_0000,
            ..Registers::default()
        };
        assert_eq!(
            parse_addr("rip", &regs),
            Some(MemAddr::Runtime(0x7ff6_1234_0000))
        );
        assert_eq!(parse_addr("0x401000", &regs), Some(MemAddr::File(0x401000)));
        assert_eq!(parse_addr("zz", &regs), None);
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-views/src/decompiler.rs`:

```rs
//! Decompiler panel: the function under the cursor as Rust-style pseudocode.
//!
//! It follows the cursor of the active file: move through the disassembly and the
//! panel shows (and highlights) the matching line. Clicking a line moves the
//! disassembly there; clicking a function name goes to that function. Ctrl+F searches
//! the function's code; a right click shows what can be done with a line or name.

use std::sync::{Arc, Weak};

use egui::text::LayoutJob;
use egui::{Align, Color32, FontId, RichText, Sense, Ui};
use orress_analysis::Program;
use orress_decompiler::{Output, TokKind};
use orress_project::{DocStore, Document};
use orress_ui::{ExplainExt as _, muted};

use crate::edit::{self, EditPopup};
use crate::find::{self, FindInput, FindStep};
use crate::{ViewCommand, ViewRequest, code, menu};

type Cached = Arc<Result<Output, String>>;
type PortCached = Arc<Result<String, String>>;

/// How many decompiled functions (per mode) are kept.
const CACHE_ENTRIES: usize = 16;

/// One cached result, for `func` in a specific analysis. The `Weak` pins the identity of
/// the program without keeping it alive: a patch makes a new program, so its functions are
/// decompiled again, while renames (applied when drawing) reuse the result.
#[derive(Clone)]
struct Entry<T> {
    program: Weak<Program>,
    func: u64,
    /// The document's annotation generation the result was built at, so applying or editing
    /// a type (which bumps the generation) re-decompiles instead of reusing a stale result.
    generation: u64,
    value: Arc<T>,
}

/// Recently decompiled functions, most recently used last, bounded so browsing many
/// functions or files does not pile results up in memory.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
struct DecompCache {
    pseudo: Vec<Entry<Result<Output, String>>>,
    port: Vec<Entry<Result<String, String>>>,
    /// The highlighted port text, for the port result it was built from and the colours.
    port_job: Option<(
        PortCached,
        Color32,
        orress_theme::SyntaxColors,
        Arc<LayoutJob>,
    )>,
}

fn cache_id() -> egui::Id {
    egui::Id::new("orress::decompiler_cache")
}

/// The cached value for (`program`, `func`), moved to the most-recent end.
fn lookup<T>(
    entries: &mut Vec<Entry<T>>,
    program: &Arc<Program>,
    func: u64,
    generation: u64,
) -> Option<Arc<T>> {
    let weak = Arc::downgrade(program);
    let i = entries.iter().position(|e| {
        e.func == func && e.generation == generation && Weak::ptr_eq(&e.program, &weak)
    })?;
    let e = entries.remove(i);
    let value = Arc::clone(&e.value);
    entries.push(e);
    Some(value)
}

fn remember<T>(
    entries: &mut Vec<Entry<T>>,
    program: &Arc<Program>,
    func: u64,
    generation: u64,
    value: &Arc<T>,
) {
    // Results for programs that no longer exist (an older patch level, a closed file) go first.
    entries.retain(|e| e.program.strong_count() > 0);
    if entries.len() >= CACHE_ENTRIES {
        entries.remove(0);
    }
    entries.push(Entry {
        program: Arc::downgrade(program),
        func,
        generation,
        value: Arc::clone(value),
    });
}

const EXPLAIN: &str = "The decompiler turns the machine code of a function back into readable code. \
    ORRESS writes it as Rust: `if`, `while` and `loop` instead of jumps, parameters (a1, a2 ...) \
    instead of registers, `&[u8]` for a buffer with its length, `bool` for yes/no results. \
    It is a reconstruction, not the original source: names, types and some details are lost when \
    a program is compiled. Values the decompiler cannot type are shown as read::<u32>(address). \
    When in doubt, the disassembly is the truth.";

fn color(kind: TokKind, syntax: &orress_theme::SyntaxColors, text: Color32) -> Color32 {
    match kind {
        TokKind::Keyword => syntax.keyword.0,
        TokKind::Type => syntax.type_name.0,
        TokKind::Function => syntax.function.0,
        TokKind::Param => syntax.label.0,
        TokKind::Variable => syntax.register.0,
        TokKind::Number => syntax.immediate.0,
        TokKind::Str => syntax.string.0,
        TokKind::Comment => syntax.comment.0,
        TokKind::Punct => text,
    }
}

/// Sanitises a function label into a file-name stem (alphanumerics and `_` kept, the rest
/// replaced), so a name like `main+0x1a` becomes a usable `main_0x1a.rs`.
fn file_stem(name: &str) -> String {
    let s: String = name
        .chars()
        .map(|c| {
            if c.is_alphanumeric() || c == '_' {
                c
            } else {
                '_'
            }
        })
        .collect();
    if s.is_empty() { "function".into() } else { s }
}

/// The Copy / Open-in-editor buttons shared by both decompiler modes. `code` is the text they
/// act on; `name` is the function label used to name the editor buffer (which can then be saved
/// with File ▸ Save As). `code` is the text to act on.
fn code_actions(ui: &mut Ui, requests: &mut Vec<ViewRequest>, name: &str, code: &str) {
    if ui
        .small_button("Copy")
        .on_hover_text("Copy the code")
        .clicked()
    {
        ui.ctx().copy_text(code.to_string());
    }
    if ui
        .small_button("Open in editor")
        .on_hover_text("Open this code in a new editor tab (then save it with File ▸ Save As)")
        .clicked()
    {
        requests.push(ViewRequest::OpenInEditor {
            name: format!("{}.rs", file_stem(name)),
            contents: code.to_string(),
        });
    }
}

/// Per-panel state that lives between frames: the find bar, the right-click target and a
/// rename/comment popup.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
struct PanelState {
    find: FindInput,
    /// Index of the current match in this frame's match list.
    current: Option<usize>,
    /// What the matches belong to: (function, Rust port mode, query). When it changes the
    /// current match starts over.
    matched: Option<(u64, bool, String)>,
    /// The right-clicked line and the address under the pointer.
    menu: Option<(usize, Option<u64>)>,
    popup: Option<EditPopup>,
    /// The open "set prototype" editor, if any.
    proto: Option<crate::prototype::ProtoDraft>,
}

fn state_id() -> egui::Id {
    egui::Id::new("orress::decompiler_panel")
}

/// Something picked in the right-click menu, done after the code is drawn.
enum MenuAction {
    GoTo(u64),
    Rename(u64),
    Comment(u64),
    Xrefs(u64),
    Mode(bool),
    Find,
}

const FIND_EXPLAIN: &str = "Search the decompiled code of this function, ignoring upper/lower \
    case: a variable (a1), a function name, a number (0x5a), a keyword (while). F3 finds the \
    next match, Shift+F3 the previous one. To search the whole program, use Find in the \
    Disassembly view.";

pub fn decompiler_panel(
    ui: &mut Ui,
    docs: &mut DocStore,
    requests: &mut Vec<ViewRequest>,
    commands: Vec<ViewCommand>,
) {
    let mut state: PanelState = ui
        .ctx()
        .data(|d| d.get_temp(state_id()))
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let mut step = None;
    for command in commands {
        match command {
            ViewCommand::FindNext if state.find.needle().is_some() => step = Some(FindStep::Next),
            ViewCommand::FindPrevious if state.find.needle().is_some() => {
                step = Some(FindStep::Previous);
            }
            ViewCommand::Find | ViewCommand::FindNext | ViewCommand::FindPrevious => {
                state.find.show();
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    panel(ui, docs, requests, &mut state, step);
    ui.ctx().data_mut(|d| d.insert_temp(state_id(), state));
}

fn panel(
    ui: &mut Ui,
    docs: &mut DocStore,
    requests: &mut Vec<ViewRequest>,
    state: &mut PanelState,
    mut step: Option<FindStep>,
) {
    let Some(doc) = docs.active_mut() else {
        ui.label(
            "Open a program and put the cursor in a function: its decompiled code appears here.",
        );
        return;
    };
    let Some(program) = doc.program().cloned() else {
        ui.label(muted("Waiting for the disassembly…"));
        return;
    };
    let Some(format) = doc.analysis().map(|a| a.info.format) else {
        return;
    };
    let cursor = program.memory.address_of(doc.cursor);
    let Some(func) = cursor
        .and_then(|a| program.function_containing(a))
        .map(|f| f.entry)
    else {
        ui.label("Put the cursor inside a function in the disassembly (Ctrl+D) to decompile it.");
        return;
    };

    // Decompiling is quick, but not free: keep the result until the code changes (a patch
    // makes a new program) or a type is applied/edited (which bumps the generation). Names are
    // not part of the output; renames apply when drawing.
    let generation = doc.generation;
    let hints = build_hints(doc);
    let cached: Option<Cached> = ui.ctx().data_mut(|d| {
        lookup(
            &mut d.get_temp_mut_or_default::<DecompCache>(cache_id()).pseudo,
            &program,
            func,
            generation,
        )
    });
    let result = cached.unwrap_or_else(|| {
        let conv = orress_decompiler::convention(format);
        let r = Arc::new(
            orress_decompiler::decompile_with(&program, func, conv, &hints)
                .map_err(|e| e.to_string()),
        );
        ui.ctx().data_mut(|d| {
            let cache = d.get_temp_mut_or_default::<DecompCache>(cache_id());
            remember(&mut cache.pseudo, &program, func, generation, &r);
        });
        r
    });

    let name = code::describe_address(doc, &program, func);
    let mode_id = egui::Id::new("orress::decompiler_mode");
    let mut port_mode: bool = ui.ctx().data(|d| d.get_temp(mode_id)).unwrap_or(false);
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label(RichText::new(format!("Decompiled: {name}")).strong())
            .explain("Decompiler", EXPLAIN);
        ui.label(muted(format!("(0x{func:x})")));
        ui.separator();
        if ui.selectable_label(!port_mode, "Pseudocode").clicked() {
            port_mode = false;
        }
        if ui
            .selectable_label(port_mode, "Rust port")
            .on_hover_text("A compilable Rust scaffold for porting — un-lifted instructions kept as inline asm")
            .clicked()
        {
            port_mode = true;
        }
        ui.separator();
        if ui
            .selectable_label(state.find.open, "Find…")
            .on_hover_text("Search this function's code (Ctrl+F)")
            .clicked()
        {
            if state.find.open {
                state.find.open = false;
            } else {
                state.find.show();
            }
        }
        ui.separator();
        let has_proto = doc.annotations.func_prototypes.contains_key(&func);
        let label = if has_proto {
            "Prototype ✎"
        } else {
            "Set prototype…"
        };
        if ui
            .selectable_label(state.proto.is_some(), label)
            .on_hover_text("Pin this function's return type and parameter names/types")
            .clicked()
        {
            state.proto = if state.proto.is_some() {
                None
            } else {
                Some(crate::prototype::ProtoDraft::load(doc, func))
            };
        }
    });
    crate::prototype::window(ui, &mut state.proto, doc, &name);
    if state.find.open {
        let bar = find::bar(ui, &mut state.find, "e.g. a1, while, 0x5a", FIND_EXPLAIN);
        if bar.changed {
            state.current = None;
        }
        step = bar.step.or(step);
    }
    let needle = state.find.open.then(|| state.find.needle()).flatten();
    let key = (func, port_mode, needle.clone().unwrap_or_default());
    if state.matched.as_ref() != Some(&key) {
        state.matched = Some(key);
        state.current = None;
        if step.is_none() {
            state.find.status = None;
        }
    }

    let mut action: Option<MenuAction> = None;

    // --- Rust port mode: a compilable scaffold rather than reading pseudocode. -----
    if port_mode {
        #[cfg(feature = "compile-check")]
        let pkey = egui::Id::new(("orress::port", &doc.path, func));
        let pcached: Option<PortCached> = ui.ctx().data_mut(|d| {
            lookup(
                &mut d.get_temp_mut_or_default::<DecompCache>(cache_id()).port,
                &program,
                func,
                generation,
            )
        });
        let pres = pcached.unwrap_or_else(|| {
            let conv = orress_decompiler::convention(format);
            let r =
                Arc::new(orress_decompiler::port(&program, func, conv).map_err(|e| e.to_string()));
            ui.ctx().data_mut(|d| {
                let cache = d.get_temp_mut_or_default::<DecompCache>(cache_id());
                remember(&mut cache.port, &program, func, generation, &r);
            });
            r
        });
        ui.horizontal(|ui| {
            ui.label(muted(
                "Best-effort compilable Rust — review before porting.",
            ));
            if let Ok(s) = &*pres {
                code_actions(ui, requests, &name, s);
            }
            #[cfg(feature = "compile-check")]
            if let Ok(s) = &*pres {
                port_compile_check(ui, pkey, s);
            }
        });
        ui.separator();
        match &*pres {
            Ok(s) => {
                // Colour the port with the same tree-sitter highlighter and theme as the code
                // editor, so the tab reads like the IDE editor (and like the pseudocode tab).
                // Highlighting parses the whole text, so it is redone only when the text or
                // the colours change.
                let syntax = code::syntax(ui.ctx());
                let default = ui.visuals().text_color();
                let cached_job = ui.ctx().data(|d| {
                    d.get_temp::<DecompCache>(cache_id())
                        .and_then(|c| c.port_job)
                        .filter(|(p, c, sx, _)| {
                            Arc::ptr_eq(p, &pres) && *c == default && *sx == syntax
                        })
                        .map(|(.., job)| job)
                });
                let job = cached_job.unwrap_or_else(|| {
                    let job = Arc::new(code::highlight_job(
                        s,
                        orress_editor::Language::Rust,
                        &syntax,
                        FontId::monospace(13.0),
                        default,
                    ));
                    ui.ctx().data_mut(|d| {
                        d.get_temp_mut_or_default::<DecompCache>(cache_id())
                            .port_job =
                            Some((Arc::clone(&pres), default, syntax.clone(), Arc::clone(&job)));
                    });
                    job
                });
                let starts = needle
                    .as_deref()
                    .map(|n| find::matches(s, n))
                    .unwrap_or_default();
                let stepped = step.is_some();
                if let (Some(step), Some(n)) = (step, needle.as_deref()) {
                    state.current = find::step_index(starts.len(), state.current, step);
                    state.find.status = Some(match state.current {
                        Some(i) => Ok(format!("{} of {} in this function", i + 1, starts.len())),
                        None => Err(format!("`{n}` is not in this function")),
                    });
                }
                let len = needle.as_ref().map_or(0, String::len);
                let job = if starts.is_empty() {
                    (*job).clone()
                } else {
                    mark_matches(&job, &starts, len, state.current)
                };
                let galley = ui.fonts_mut(|f| f.layout_job(job));
                egui::ScrollArea::both()
                    .auto_shrink([false, false])
                    .id_salt("port-scroll")
                    .show(ui, |ui| {
                        let response =
                            ui.add(egui::Label::new(Arc::clone(&galley)).selectable(true));
                        if stepped && let Some(i) = state.current {
                            let char_index = s[..starts[i]].chars().count();
                            let at = galley
                                .pos_from_cursor(egui::text::CCursor::new(char_index))
                                .translate(response.rect.min.to_vec2());
                            ui.scroll_to_rect(at, Some(Align::Center));
                        }
                        response.context_menu(|ui| {
                            ui.set_min_width(220.0);
                            ui.style_mut().wrap_mode = Some(egui::TextWrapMode::Extend);
                            ui.style_mut().wrap_mode = Some(egui::TextWrapMode::Extend);
                            menu::copy_item(ui, "Copy the code", s.clone());
                            if ui.button("Open in editor").clicked() {
                                requests.push(ViewRequest::OpenInEditor {
                                    name: format!("{}.rs", file_stem(&name)),
                                    contents: s.clone(),
                                });
                                ui.close();
                            }
                            if ui.button("Show pseudocode").clicked() {
                                action = Some(MenuAction::Mode(false));
                                ui.close();
                            }
                            if ui
                                .add(egui::Button::new("Find…").shortcut_text("Ctrl+F"))
                                .clicked()
                            {
                                action = Some(MenuAction::Find);
                                ui.close();
                            }
                            menu::views_and_commands(ui, requests);
                        });
                    });
            }
            Err(e) => {
                ui.label(e.as_str());
            }
        }
        apply(ui, doc, requests, state, action, &mut port_mode);
        ui.ctx().data_mut(|d| d.insert_temp(mode_id, port_mode));
        return;
    }

    let out = match &*result {
        Ok(out) => out,
        Err(e) => {
            ui.label(e.as_str());
            ui.ctx().data_mut(|d| d.insert_temp(mode_id, port_mode));
            return;
        }
    };
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        code_actions(ui, requests, &name, &out.text());
        ui.label(muted(
            "Pseudocode reconstructed from the machine code. Names and types are best guesses.",
        ))
        .note("Decompiler", EXPLAIN);
    });
    ui.separator();

    // The text of each line as drawn (with the user's names), for searching.
    let line_text = |line: &orress_decompiler::Line| -> String {
        line.spans
            .iter()
            .map(|span| match (span.kind, span.target) {
                (TokKind::Function, Some(a)) => doc.name_of(a).unwrap_or_else(|| span.text.clone()),
                _ => span.text.clone(),
            })
            .collect()
    };
    let hits: Vec<usize> = match needle.as_deref() {
        Some(n) => out
            .lines
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .filter(|(_, l)| line_text(l).to_ascii_lowercase().contains(n))
            .map(|(i, _)| i)
            .collect(),
        None => Vec::new(),
    };
    let stepped = step.is_some();
    if let (Some(step), Some(n)) = (step, needle.as_deref()) {
        state.current = find::step_index(hits.len(), state.current, step);
        state.find.status = Some(match state.current {
            Some(i) => Ok(format!(
                "line {} · {} of {} matching lines in this function",
                hits[i] + 1,
                i + 1,
                hits.len()
            )),
            None => Err(format!("`{n}` is not in this function")),
        });
    }
    let current_hit = state.current.and_then(|i| hits.get(i).copied());

    let current = cursor.and_then(|a| out.line_for(a));
    // Scroll to the current line only when the cursor moved.
    let moved_key = egui::Id::new("orress::decompiler_cursor");
    let moved = ui.ctx().data(|d| d.get_temp::<Option<u64>>(moved_key)) != Some(cursor);
    ui.ctx().data_mut(|d| d.insert_temp(moved_key, cursor));

    let syntax = code::syntax(ui.ctx());
    let text = ui.visuals().text_color();
    let font = FontId::monospace(13.0);
    let highlight = ui.visuals().selection.bg_fill.gamma_multiply(0.35);
    let found = Color32::from_rgb(230, 180, 40);
    let mut go: Option<u64> = None;
    egui::ScrollArea::both()
        .auto_shrink([false, false])
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            ui.spacing_mut().item_spacing = egui::vec2(0.0, 1.0);
            for (i, line) in out.lines.iter().enumerate() {
                let mut targets: Vec<(egui::Rect, u64)> = Vec::new();
                let row = ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                    ui.label(RichText::new("    ".repeat(line.indent)).font(font.clone()));
                    for span in &line.spans {
                        // User renames win over the analysis' names.
                        let shown = match (span.kind, span.target) {
                            (TokKind::Function, Some(a)) => {
                                doc.name_of(a).unwrap_or_else(|| span.text.clone())
                            }
                            _ => span.text.clone(),
                        };
                        let rich = RichText::new(shown)
                            .font(font.clone())
                            .color(color(span.kind, &syntax, text));
                        let r = ui.add(egui::Label::new(rich).selectable(false));
                        if let Some(a) = span.target {
                            targets.push((r.rect, a));
                        }
                    }
                });
                let rect = row
                    .response
                    .rect
                    .with_max_x(ui.clip_rect().right().max(row.response.rect.right()));
                if Some(i) == current {
                    ui.painter().rect_filled(rect, 2.0, highlight);
                    if moved && !stepped {
                        // Only scroll vertically: keep the start of the line in view.
                        let left =
                            egui::Rect::from_min_size(rect.min, egui::vec2(1.0, rect.height()));
                        ui.scroll_to_rect(left, Some(Align::Center));
                    }
                }
                if hits.binary_search(&i).is_ok() {
                    let strength = if Some(i) == current_hit { 0.45 } else { 0.18 };
                    ui.painter()
                        .rect_filled(rect, 2.0, found.gamma_multiply(strength));
                    if stepped && Some(i) == current_hit {
                        let left =
                            egui::Rect::from_min_size(rect.min, egui::vec2(1.0, rect.height()));
                        ui.scroll_to_rect(left, Some(Align::Center));
                    }
                }
                // One click area per line; a click on a name goes to that name instead.
                let r = ui.interact(rect, ui.id().with(("line", i)), Sense::click());
                let pointer = r.hover_pos();
                let on_target = pointer
                    .and_then(|p| targets.iter().find(|(t, _)| t.contains(p)).map(|(_, a)| *a));
                if r.secondary_clicked() {
                    state.menu = Some((i, on_target));
                }
                if let Some(a) = on_target {
                    ui.ctx().set_cursor_icon(egui::CursorIcon::PointingHand);
                    if r.clicked() {
                        go = Some(a);
                    }
                } else if r.clicked() {
                    go = line.addr;
                }
                r.context_menu(|ui| {
                    if let Some((at, target)) = state.menu
                        && at == i
                    {
                        let text = line_text(line);
                        let picked =
                            line_menu(ui, doc, &program, requests, func, line, target, &text);
                        if picked.is_some() {
                            action = picked;
                        }
                    }
                });
                if let Some(a) = on_target {
                    r.on_hover_text(format!("Go to 0x{a:x}"));
                }
            }
        });
    if let Some(a) = go {
        doc.navigate_to_address(a);
    }
    apply(ui, doc, requests, state, action, &mut port_mode);
    ui.ctx().data_mut(|d| d.insert_temp(mode_id, port_mode));
}

/// The right-click menu of a pseudocode line. `target` is the function or address under
/// the pointer.
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
fn line_menu(
    ui: &mut Ui,
    doc: &Document,
    program: &Program,
    requests: &mut Vec<ViewRequest>,
    func: u64,
    line: &orress_decompiler::Line,
    target: Option<u64>,
    text: &str,
) -> Option<MenuAction> {
    ui.set_min_width(220.0);
    ui.style_mut().wrap_mode = Some(egui::TextWrapMode::Extend);
    let mut action = None;
    let mut pick = |ui: &mut Ui, label: String, a: MenuAction| {
        if ui.button(label).clicked() {
            action = Some(a);
            ui.close();
        }
    };
    if let Some(a) = target {
        let name = code::describe_address(doc, program, a);
        pick(ui, format!("Go to {name}"), MenuAction::GoTo(a));
        pick(ui, format!("Rename {name}…"), MenuAction::Rename(a));
        pick(
            ui,
            format!("Cross-references to {name}"),
            MenuAction::Xrefs(a),
        );
        ui.separator();
    }
    if let Some(addr) = line.addr {
        pick(
            ui,
            format!("Show in disassembly (0x{addr:x})"),
            MenuAction::GoTo(addr),
        );
        pick(ui, "Comment…".into(), MenuAction::Comment(addr));
    }
    if target != Some(func) {
        let name = code::describe_address(doc, program, func);
        pick(ui, format!("Rename {name}…"), MenuAction::Rename(func));
        pick(
            ui,
            format!("Cross-references to {name}"),
            MenuAction::Xrefs(func),
        );
    }
    ui.menu_button("Copy", |ui| {
        menu::copy_item(ui, "Line", text.trim().to_owned());
        if let Some(addr) = line.addr {
            menu::copy_item(ui, "Address", format!("0x{addr:x}"));
        }
        menu::copy_item(
            ui,
            "Function name",
            code::describe_address(doc, program, func),
        );
    });
    ui.separator();
    pick(ui, "Show Rust port".into(), MenuAction::Mode(true));
    if ui
        .add(egui::Button::new("Find…").shortcut_text("Ctrl+F"))
        .clicked()
    {
        action = Some(MenuAction::Find);
        ui.close();
    }
    if ui.button("Show in graph").clicked() {
        requests.push(ViewRequest::RunAction("view::Graph".into()));
        ui.close();
    }
    menu::views_and_commands(ui, requests);
    action
}

/// Does what was picked in a right-click menu, and shows the rename/comment popup.
fn apply(
    ui: &mut Ui,
    doc: &mut Document,
    requests: &mut Vec<ViewRequest>,
    state: &mut PanelState,
    action: Option<MenuAction>,
    port_mode: &mut bool,
) {
    match action {
        Some(MenuAction::GoTo(a)) => {
            if !doc.navigate_to_address(a) {
                requests.push(ViewRequest::Message(format!(
                    "0x{a:x} is not inside the file."
                )));
            }
        }
        Some(MenuAction::Rename(a)) => state.popup = Some(EditPopup::rename(doc, a)),
        Some(MenuAction::Comment(a)) => state.popup = Some(EditPopup::comment(doc, a)),
        Some(MenuAction::Xrefs(a)) => {
            doc.xref_target = Some(a);
            requests.push(ViewRequest::ShowXrefs);
        }
        Some(MenuAction::Mode(port)) => *port_mode = port,
        Some(MenuAction::Find) => state.find.show(),
        None => {}
    }
    if let Some(popup) = &mut state.popup
        && !edit::show(ui, doc, popup)
    {
        state.popup = None;
    }
}

/// `job` with the matches (byte offsets `starts`, each `len` long) given a background; the
/// `current` one stronger.
fn mark_matches(
    job: &LayoutJob,
    starts: &[usize],
    len: usize,
    current: Option<usize>,
) -> LayoutJob {
    let found = Color32::from_rgb(230, 180, 40);
    let mut out = job.clone();
    out.sections.clear();
    for section in &job.sections {
        let (start, end): (usize, usize) = (
            section.byte_range.start.into(),
            section.byte_range.end.into(),
        );
        let mut cuts = vec![start, end];
        for &m in starts {
            for b in [m, m + len] {
                if b > start && b < end {
                    cuts.push(b);
                }
            }
        }
        cuts.sort_unstable();
        cuts.dedup();
        for (k, w) in cuts.windows(2).enumerate() {
            let mut format = section.format.clone();
            // The match this piece belongs to: the last one starting at or before it.
            let i = starts.partition_point(|&m| m <= w[0]);
            if i > 0 && w[1] <= starts[i - 1] + len {
                let strength = if current == Some(i - 1) { 0.6 } else { 0.25 };
                format.background = found.gamma_multiply(strength);
            }
            out.sections.push(egui::text::LayoutSection {
                leading_space: if k == 0 { section.leading_space } else { 0.0 },
                byte_range: w[0].into()..w[1].into(),
                format,
            });
        }
    }
    out
}

/// The Rust-port "does this compile?" affordance (behind the `compile-check` feature): a
/// button that runs `rustc` over the scaffold, then a ✓ / ✗ badge with the diagnostics.
#[cfg(feature = "compile-check")]
fn port_compile_check(ui: &mut egui::Ui, pkey: egui::Id, src: &str) {
    use orress_decompiler::compile::{CompileStatus, check_source};

    let key = pkey.with("compile");
    let cached: Option<std::sync::Arc<(CompileStatus, String)>> =
        ui.ctx().data(|d| d.get_temp(key));
    if ui
        .small_button("Check compiles")
        .on_hover_text("Run rustc over this scaffold")
        .clicked()
    {
        let r = check_source(src);
        ui.ctx()
            .data_mut(|d| d.insert_temp(key, std::sync::Arc::new((r.status, r.diagnostics))));
    }
    if let Some(r) = cached {
        let (status, diags) = &*r;
        match status {
            CompileStatus::Compiles => {
                ui.colored_label(egui::Color32::from_rgb(0x4c, 0xaf, 0x50), "✓ compiles");
            }
            CompileStatus::Errors => {
                ui.colored_label(egui::Color32::from_rgb(0xe5, 0x73, 0x73), "✗ errors")
                    .on_hover_text(diags.as_str());
            }
            CompileStatus::ToolMissing => {
                ui.label(muted("rustc not found"))
                    .on_hover_text(diags.as_str());
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Builds decompiler type hints from the document's type catalog and function prototypes:
/// user struct layouts (to name recovered struct parameters and their fields) and lowered
/// prototypes (to override a function's signature).
fn build_hints(doc: &Document) -> orress_decompiler::types::TypeHints {
    use orress_decompiler::types as dt;
    use orress_project::types::UserType;

    let catalog = doc.type_catalog();
    let mut structs = Vec::new();
    for ty in catalog.types.values() {
        if let UserType::Struct { name, .. } = ty
            && let Some(laid) = catalog.layout(ty)
        {
            let fields = laid
                .iter()
                .filter(|f| f.count == 1)
                .filter_map(|f| {
                    let (w, signed) = scalar_width(&catalog, &f.ty)?;
                    Some((
                        f.offset,
                        orress_decompiler::ir::Width(w),
                        signed,
                        f.path.clone(),
                    ))
                })
                .collect();
            structs.push(dt::StructDef {
                name: name.clone(),
                fields,
            });
        }
    }

    let mut prototypes = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
    for (&addr, proto) in &doc.annotations.func_prototypes {
        let params = proto
            .params
            .iter()
            .map(|(_, t)| {
                lower_ty(&catalog, t).unwrap_or(dt::Ty::Int(orress_decompiler::ir::Width(8), false))
            })
            .collect();
        let ret = proto.ret.as_ref().and_then(|t| lower_ty(&catalog, t));
        prototypes.insert(addr, dt::Proto { ret, params });
    }

    dt::TypeHints {
        structs,
        prototypes,
    }
}

/// The integer byte-width and signedness of a scalar field type, or `None` for a type that
/// is not a fixed-width scalar (a nested struct, say) and so cannot name a recovered field.
fn scalar_width(
    catalog: &orress_project::TypeCatalog,
    ty: &orress_project::TypeRef,
) -> Option<(u8, bool)> {
    use orress_project::types::{Prim, TypeRef};
    match ty {
        TypeRef::Prim(Prim::U8 | Prim::Char | Prim::Bool) => Some((1, false)),
        TypeRef::Prim(Prim::I8) => Some((1, true)),
        TypeRef::Prim(Prim::U16) => Some((2, false)),
        TypeRef::Prim(Prim::I16) => Some((2, true)),
        TypeRef::Prim(Prim::U32) => Some((4, false)),
        TypeRef::Prim(Prim::I32) => Some((4, true)),
        TypeRef::Prim(Prim::U64) => Some((8, false)),
        TypeRef::Prim(Prim::I64) => Some((8, true)),
        TypeRef::Pointer(_) => Some((catalog.pointer_size as u8, false)),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Lowers a user type reference into a decompiler [`Ty`] for a function prototype.
fn lower_ty(
    catalog: &orress_project::TypeCatalog,
    ty: &orress_project::TypeRef,
) -> Option<orress_decompiler::types::Ty> {
    use orress_decompiler::types as dt;
    use orress_project::types::{Prim, TypeRef, UserType};

    match ty {
        TypeRef::Prim(Prim::F32) => Some(dt::Ty::Float(orress_decompiler::ir::Width(4))),
        TypeRef::Prim(Prim::F64) => Some(dt::Ty::Float(orress_decompiler::ir::Width(8))),
        TypeRef::Prim(Prim::Bool) => Some(dt::Ty::Bool),
        TypeRef::Prim(Prim::Void) => None,
        TypeRef::Prim(_) => {
            let (w, signed) = scalar_width(catalog, ty)?;
            Some(dt::Ty::Int(orress_decompiler::ir::Width(w), signed))
        }
        TypeRef::Pointer(inner) => match inner.as_ref() {
            // A pointer to a user struct becomes a named struct parameter.
            TypeRef::Named(name) => {
                let user = catalog.types.get(name)?;
                let fields = catalog
                    .layout(user)?
                    .iter()
                    .filter(|f| f.count == 1)
                    .filter_map(|f| {
                        let (w, signed) = scalar_width(catalog, &f.ty)?;
                        Some((
                            f.offset,
                            f.path.clone(),
                            dt::Field {
                                offset: f.offset,
                                width: orress_decompiler::ir::Width(w),
                                signed,
                            },
                        ))
                    })
                    .collect::<Vec<_>>();
                let field_names = fields.iter().map(|(o, n, _)| (*o, n.clone())).collect();
                let layout = dt::StructLayout {
                    name: name.clone(),
                    fields: fields.into_iter().map(|(_, _, f)| f).collect(),
                    field_names,
                };
                let mutable = matches!(user, UserType::Struct { .. });
                Some(dt::Ty::Struct(layout, mutable))
            }
            // A pointer to a scalar becomes a reference of that width.
            other => {
                let (w, _) = scalar_width(catalog, other)?;
                Some(dt::Ty::Ref(orress_decompiler::ir::Width(w), false))
            }
        },
        TypeRef::Named(_) => None,
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-views/src/diff.rs`:

```rs
//! The Binary Diff tab (M14): compare the open binary against another (a different build, or a
//! malware variant) and see which functions are identical, changed, added or removed — BinDiff-style.
//!
//! The open binary ("A") is already analyzed; its function signatures are captured on the UI thread
//! (cheap), then the comparison binary ("B") is loaded, analyzed and diffed on a background thread
//! so the UI never blocks.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

use egui::{RichText, Ui};
use orress_project::DocStore;
use orress_ui::muted;

/// The finished comparison, ready to render.
struct DiffData {
    /// The open binary ("A") this comparison was made for; the result is dropped when another
    /// file becomes active.
    a_path: PathBuf,
    b_name: String,
    a_count: usize,
    b_count: usize,
    /// (identical, changed, added, removed).
    summary: (usize, usize, usize, usize),
    /// (name in A, name in B, similarity 0..1).
    changed: Vec<(String, String, f32)>,
    added: Vec<String>,
    removed: Vec<String>,
}

type Slot = Arc<Mutex<Option<Result<DiffData, String>>>>;

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct DiffView {
    result: Slot,
    busy: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    /// The file the current (or running) comparison belongs to.
    a_path: Option<PathBuf>,
}

/// Locks the result, recovering it if the worker panicked while holding the lock.
fn lock(slot: &Slot) -> std::sync::MutexGuard<'_, Option<Result<DiffData, String>>> {
    slot.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
}

fn name_of(r: &orress_diff::FuncRef) -> String {
    r.name
        .clone()
        .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("sub_{:x}", r.entry))
}

pub fn diff_panel(ui: &mut Ui, view: &mut DiffView, docs: &DocStore) {
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label(RichText::new("Binary diff").strong());
        ui.label(muted(
            "BinDiff-style function matching between two binaries",
        ));
    });
    ui.separator();

    let Some(doc) = docs.active() else {
        ui.label(muted("Open a binary, then compare it against another."));
        return;
    };
    let Some(program) = doc.program() else {
        ui.label(muted(
            "Analysis is still running (or this file has no native code).",
        ));
        return;
    };

    // A comparison belongs to the file it was made for.
    if view.a_path.as_deref() != Some(doc.path.as_path()) {
        view.a_path = Some(doc.path.clone());
        *lock(&view.result) = None;
    }

    let a_name = file_name(&doc.path);
    ui.label(format!(
        "A: {a_name}  ({} functions)",
        program.functions.len()
    ));

    let busy = view.busy.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
    if ui
        .add_enabled(!busy, egui::Button::new("Compare against another binary…"))
        .clicked()
        && let Some(path) = rfd::FileDialog::new()
            .set_title("Pick the binary to compare against")
            .pick_file()
    {
        compare(view, program, &doc.path, path, ui.ctx().clone());
    }
    if busy {
        ui.horizontal(|ui| {
            ui.spinner();
            ui.label(muted("analyzing and diffing…"));
        });
    }

    let mut guard = lock(&view.result);
    // A comparison started for another file that finished after switching is not shown.
    if guard
        .as_ref()
        .is_some_and(|r| r.as_ref().is_ok_and(|d| d.a_path != doc.path))
    {
        *guard = None;
    }
    match guard.as_ref() {
        Some(Ok(data)) => render(ui, data),
        Some(Err(e)) => {
            ui.colored_label(ui.visuals().error_fg_color, e);
        }
        None => {}
    }
}

/// Captures A's (owned, `Send`) signatures on the UI thread, then loads, analyzes and diffs B on a
/// background thread so the UI never blocks.
/// A panic in the worker is caught and reported, so `busy` is always cleared.
fn compare(
    view: &DiffView,
    program: &orress_analysis::Program,
    a_path: &Path,
    path: PathBuf,
    ctx: egui::Context,
) {
    let a_sigs = orress_diff::signatures(program);
    let a_count = program.functions.len();
    let a_path = a_path.to_path_buf();
    let result = Arc::clone(&view.result);
    let busy = Arc::clone(&view.busy);
    *lock(&result) = None;
    busy.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
    let spawned = std::thread::Builder::new()
        .name("binary diff".into())
        .spawn(move || {
            let data = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
                analyze_and_diff(&a_sigs, a_count, &a_path, &path)
            }))
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| Err("the diff hit an internal error".into()));
            *lock(&result) = Some(data);
            busy.store(false, Ordering::Relaxed);
            ctx.request_repaint();
        });
    if let Err(e) = spawned {
        *lock(&view.result) = Some(Err(format!("could not start the diff thread: {e}")));
        view.busy.store(false, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }
}

/// Loads and analyzes the comparison binary, then diffs it against A's signatures.
fn analyze_and_diff(
    a_sigs: &[orress_diff::FuncSig],
    a_count: usize,
    a_path: &Path,
    path: &Path,
) -> Result<DiffData, String> {
    let bytes = std::sync::Arc::new(
        std::fs::read(path).map_err(|e| format!("cannot read {}: {e}", path.display()))?,
    );
    let analysis = orress_project::Analysis::run(&bytes);
    let program = orress_analysis::Program::analyze(
        &analysis.info,
        std::sync::Arc::clone(&bytes),
        &analysis.strings,
    )
    .ok_or(
        "the comparison binary has no native code ORRESS can analyze (unsupported architecture)",
    )?;

    let b_sigs = orress_diff::signatures(&program);
    let diff = orress_diff::diff(a_sigs, &b_sigs);
    let changed = diff
        .matches
        .iter()
        .filter(|m| m.kind == orress_diff::MatchKind::Changed)
        .map(|m| (name_of(&m.a), name_of(&m.b), m.similarity))
        .collect();
    Ok(DiffData {
        a_path: a_path.to_path_buf(),
        b_name: file_name(path),
        a_count,
        b_count: program.functions.len(),
        summary: diff.summary(),
        changed,
        added: diff.added.iter().map(name_of).collect(),
        removed: diff.removed.iter().map(name_of).collect(),
    })
}

fn render(ui: &mut Ui, data: &DiffData) {
    let (identical, changed, added, removed) = data.summary;
    ui.add_space(4.0);
    ui.label(format!(
        "B: {}  ({} functions; compared with {} functions in A)",
        data.b_name, data.b_count, data.a_count
    ));
    ui.label(
        RichText::new(format!(
            "identical {identical}   changed {changed}   added {added}   removed {removed}"
        ))
        .strong(),
    );

    egui::ScrollArea::vertical()
        .auto_shrink([false, false])
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            if !data.changed.is_empty() {
                ui.add_space(6.0);
                ui.label(RichText::new("Changed").strong());
                for (a, b, sim) in &data.changed {
                    let label = if a == b {
                        format!("{a}  ~{:.0}%", sim * 100.0)
                    } else {
                        format!("{a} → {b}  ~{:.0}%", sim * 100.0)
                    };
                    ui.label(RichText::new(label).monospace());
                }
            }
            if !data.added.is_empty() {
                ui.add_space(6.0);
                ui.label(RichText::new("Added (only in B)").strong());
                for n in &data.added {
                    ui.label(RichText::new(n).monospace());
                }
            }
            if !data.removed.is_empty() {
                ui.add_space(6.0);
                ui.label(RichText::new("Removed (only in A)").strong());
                for n in &data.removed {
                    ui.label(RichText::new(n).monospace());
                }
            }
        });
}

fn file_name(path: &Path) -> String {
    path.file_name()
        .map(|n| n.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
        .unwrap_or_else(|| path.display().to_string())
}
```
