`crates/orress-views/src/emulator.rs`:

```rs
//! The Emulator view: run a function from the loaded binary with arguments ("run this
//! function" — the string-decryptor / check-function workhorse), and recover an input
//! byte-by-byte with the instruction-counting side-channel solver. Built on `orress-emu`.

use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

use egui::{RichText, Ui};
use orress_analysis::Program;
use orress_arch::Isa;
use orress_emu::{Abi, Emulator, Trace, solve_by_count};
use orress_project::DocStore;
use orress_ui::muted;

/// Where the scratch buffer (the emulated input) lives in the guest address space.
const SCRATCH: u64 = 0x5000_0000;
const SCRATCH_SIZE: u64 = 0x1_0000;
/// Longest input the scratch buffer holds (one byte stays free for the NUL terminator).
const MAX_INPUT: usize = SCRATCH_SIZE as usize - 1;

/// Persistent UI state for the Emulator tab.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct EmulatorView {
    addr: String,
    input: String,
    pass_len: bool,
    run: Option<RunReport>,
    /// Time-travel debugging: a recorded trace and the step currently being inspected.
    trace: Option<Trace>,
    trace_error: Option<String>,
    scrub: usize,
    solve_len: String,
    charset: Charset,
    solve: Option<SolveReport>,
    sym_target: String,
    sym_avoid: String,
    sym: Option<SymReport>,
    /// The job running on the worker thread, if any (emulation can take seconds).
    pending: Option<Pending>,
    /// The file the results above belong to; switching files clears them.
    doc: Option<PathBuf>,
}

/// The inputs a job needs, copied out of the view so the worker owns them.
#[derive(Clone)]
struct Params {
    addr: String,
    input: String,
    pass_len: bool,
    solve_len: String,
    charset: Charset,
    sym_target: String,
    sym_avoid: String,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum JobKind {
    Run,
    Record,
    Solve,
    Symbolic,
    AutoVm,
}

impl JobKind {
    fn label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Run => "Running the function",
            Self::Record => "Recording a trace",
            Self::Solve => "Solving by instruction counting",
            Self::Symbolic => "Solving symbolically",
            Self::AutoVm => "Scanning for a VM and solving it",
        }
    }

    /// The output that reports `msg` as this job's error.
    fn failed(self, msg: &str) -> JobOutput {
        match self {
            Self::Run => JobOutput::Run(err_report(msg)),
            Self::Record => JobOutput::Record(Err(msg.to_string())),
            Self::Solve => JobOutput::Solve(SolveReport::error(msg)),
            Self::Symbolic | Self::AutoVm => JobOutput::Sym(SymReport::error(msg)),
        }
    }
}

/// What a finished job produced.
enum JobOutput {
    Run(RunReport),
    // The trace is boxed: a `Trace` carries a CPU snapshot (now including the 128-bit SSE
    // registers), so it dwarfs the other variants if stored inline.
    Record(Result<Box<Trace>, String>),
    Solve(SolveReport),
    Sym(SymReport),
}

/// A job on the worker thread. The UI polls `slot` each frame; Cancel drops the job (its
/// output is discarded) and asks the side-channel solver to stop early.
struct Pending {
    kind: JobKind,
    cancel: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    slot: Arc<Mutex<Option<JobOutput>>>,
}

impl EmulatorView {
    fn params(&self) -> Params {
        Params {
            addr: self.addr.clone(),
            input: self.input.clone(),
            pass_len: self.pass_len,
            solve_len: self.solve_len.clone(),
            charset: self.charset,
            sym_target: self.sym_target.clone(),
            sym_avoid: self.sym_avoid.clone(),
        }
    }

    fn busy(&self) -> bool {
        self.pending.is_some()
    }

    /// Stops waiting for the running job (and asks it to stop).
    fn cancel(&mut self) {
        if let Some(p) = self.pending.take() {
            p.cancel.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
        }
    }

    /// Clears results that belong to another file.
    fn reset_results(&mut self) {
        self.cancel();
        self.run = None;
        self.trace = None;
        self.trace_error = None;
        self.scrub = 0;
        self.solve = None;
        self.sym = None;
    }

    fn apply(&mut self, out: JobOutput) {
        match out {
            JobOutput::Run(r) => self.run = Some(r),
            JobOutput::Record(Ok(t)) => {
                let t = *t;
                self.scrub = t.len().saturating_sub(1);
                self.trace = Some(t);
                self.trace_error = None;
            }
            JobOutput::Record(Err(e)) => {
                self.trace = None;
                self.trace_error = Some(e);
            }
            JobOutput::Solve(s) => self.solve = Some(s),
            JobOutput::Sym(s) => self.sym = Some(s),
        }
    }

    /// Moves a finished job's output into the view.
    fn poll(&mut self) {
        let Some(p) = &self.pending else {
            return;
        };
        let done = p.slot.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).take();
        if let Some(out) = done {
            self.pending = None;
            self.apply(out);
        }
    }
}

/// Starts `kind` on a worker thread so the UI stays responsive while it emulates.
fn start(view: &mut EmulatorView, ctx: &egui::Context, program: &Arc<Program>, kind: JobKind) {
    if view.busy() {
        return;
    }
    let params = view.params();
    let program = Arc::clone(program);
    let cancel = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
    let slot = Arc::new(Mutex::new(None));
    let (worker_cancel, worker_slot, ctx) = (Arc::clone(&cancel), Arc::clone(&slot), ctx.clone());
    let spawned = std::thread::Builder::new()
        .name("emulator".into())
        .spawn(move || {
            let out = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
                run_job(kind, &params, &program, &worker_cancel)
            }))
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| kind.failed("the emulator hit an internal error"));
            *worker_slot.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) = Some(out);
            ctx.request_repaint();
        });
    match spawned {
        Ok(_) => view.pending = Some(Pending { kind, cancel, slot }),
        Err(e) => view.apply(kind.failed(&format!("could not start the emulator thread: {e}"))),
    }
}

fn run_job(kind: JobKind, params: &Params, program: &Program, cancel: &AtomicBool) -> JobOutput {
    match kind {
        JobKind::Run => JobOutput::Run(run_once(params, program)),
        JobKind::Record => JobOutput::Record(record_once(params, program).map(Box::new)),
        JobKind::Solve => JobOutput::Solve(solve_once(params, program, cancel)),
        JobKind::Symbolic => JobOutput::Sym(symbolic_solve_once(params, program)),
        JobKind::AutoVm => JobOutput::Sym(auto_vm_solve(program)),
    }
}

/// Parses the "Input length" field: 1 up to what the scratch buffer holds.
fn parse_len(s: &str) -> Result<usize, String> {
    match s.trim().parse::<usize>() {
        Ok(n) if (1..=MAX_INPUT).contains(&n) => Ok(n),
        _ => Err(format!("Enter an input length from 1 to {MAX_INPUT}.")),
    }
}

struct SymReport {
    input: Vec<u8>,
    complete: bool,
    message: String,
    constraints: usize,
    smt2: String,
    error: Option<String>,
}

impl SymReport {
    fn error(msg: &str) -> Self {
        Self {
            input: Vec::new(),
            complete: false,
            message: String::new(),
            constraints: 0,
            smt2: String::new(),
            error: Some(msg.to_string()),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Default, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Charset {
    #[default]
    Printable,
    Alnum,
    Digits,
}

impl Charset {
    fn bytes(self) -> Vec<u8> {
        match self {
            Self::Printable => (0x20u8..=0x7e).collect(),
            Self::Alnum => (b'0'..=b'9')
                .chain(b'A'..=b'Z')
                .chain(b'a'..=b'z')
                .collect(),
            Self::Digits => (b'0'..=b'9').collect(),
        }
    }
    fn label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Printable => "printable",
            Self::Alnum => "alphanumeric",
            Self::Digits => "digits",
        }
    }
}

struct RunReport {
    rax: u64,
    steps: u64,
    status: String,
    error: bool,
    /// The input buffer after the run (shows in-place decryptors' output).
    scratch: Vec<u8>,
    /// A C-string at RAX, if it points into mapped memory (shows pointer-returning decoders).
    ret_str: Option<String>,
}

struct SolveReport {
    recovered: Vec<u8>,
    rows: Vec<(usize, u8, u64, u64)>,
    error: Option<String>,
}

impl SolveReport {
    fn error(msg: &str) -> Self {
        Self {
            recovered: Vec::new(),
            rows: Vec::new(),
            error: Some(msg.to_string()),
        }
    }
}

pub fn emulator_view(ui: &mut Ui, view: &mut EmulatorView, docs: &DocStore) {
    orress_ui::spotlight::mark(ui.ctx(), "view.Emulator", ui.max_rect());
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label(RichText::new("Emulator").strong());
        ui.label(muted("run a function · side-channel solve"));
    });
    ui.separator();

    let Some(doc) = docs.active() else {
        ui.label(muted("Open a binary to emulate one of its functions."));
        return;
    };
    let Some(program) = doc.program() else {
        ui.label(muted(
            "Analysis is still running (or this file has no code).",
        ));
        return;
    };
    if program.isa != Isa::X64 {
        ui.label(muted(
            "The emulator currently supports x86-64 only; this binary is a different architecture.",
        ));
        return;
    }
    let cursor = doc.cursor_address();
    if view.doc.as_deref() != Some(doc.path.as_path()) {
        view.reset_results();
        view.doc = Some(doc.path.clone());
    }

    view.poll();
    if let Some(p) = &view.pending {
        let kind = p.kind;
        ui.horizontal(|ui| {
            ui.spinner();
            ui.label(muted(format!("{}…", kind.label())));
            if ui.button("Cancel").clicked() {
                view.cancel();
            }
        });
        ui.ctx()
            .request_repaint_after(std::time::Duration::from_millis(100));
    }

    egui::ScrollArea::vertical()
        .auto_shrink([false, false])
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            run_function_section(ui, view, program, cursor);
            ui.add_space(12.0);
            ui.separator();
            solve_section(ui, view, program, cursor);
            ui.add_space(12.0);
            ui.separator();
            symbolic_section(ui, view, program, cursor);
        });
}

fn run_function_section(
    ui: &mut Ui,
    view: &mut EmulatorView,
    program: &Arc<Program>,
    cursor: Option<u64>,
) {
    ui.heading("Run function");
    ui.label(muted(
        "Write the input string to a scratch buffer and call the function with a pointer to it.",
    ));
    egui::Grid::new("emu-run-form")
        .num_columns(2)
        .spacing([10.0, 6.0])
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            ui.label("Function address");
            ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                ui.text_edit_singleline(&mut view.addr);
                if ui.small_button("use cursor's function").clicked()
                    && let Some(f) = cursor.and_then(|a| program.function_containing(a))
                {
                    view.addr = format!("{:#x}", f.entry);
                }
            });
            ui.end_row();
            ui.label("Input (arg0 → pointer)");
            ui.text_edit_singleline(&mut view.input);
            ui.end_row();
            ui.label("");
            ui.checkbox(&mut view.pass_len, "pass input length as arg1");
            ui.end_row();
        });

    let idle = !view.busy();
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        if ui.add_enabled(idle, egui::Button::new("▶ Run")).clicked() {
            start(view, ui.ctx(), program, JobKind::Run);
        }
        if ui
            .add_enabled(idle, egui::Button::new("⏺ Record"))
            .on_hover_text("Run and record every instruction, then scrub backward and forward through the execution (time-travel debugging).")
            .clicked()
        {
            start(view, ui.ctx(), program, JobKind::Record);
        }
    });

    trace_panel(ui, view);

    if let Some(r) = &view.run {
        ui.add_space(6.0);
        let color = if r.error {
            ui.visuals().error_fg_color
        } else {
            ui.visuals().text_color()
        };
        ui.colored_label(color, &r.status);
        if !r.error {
            egui::Grid::new("emu-run-result")
                .num_columns(2)
                .spacing([10.0, 2.0])
                .show(ui, |ui| {
                    ui.label("RAX");
                    ui.label(
                        RichText::new(format!("{:#x}  ({}, {})", r.rax, r.rax, r.rax as i64))
                            .monospace(),
                    );
                    ui.end_row();
                    ui.label("instructions");
                    ui.label(RichText::new(r.steps.to_string()).monospace());
                    ui.end_row();
                    if let Some(s) = &r.ret_str {
                        ui.label("string at RAX");
                        ui.label(RichText::new(format!("{s:?}")).monospace());
                        ui.end_row();
                    }
                });
            ui.label("Scratch buffer after run:");
            ui.label(RichText::new(hex_ascii(&r.scratch)).monospace());
        }
    }
}

fn solve_section(
    ui: &mut Ui,
    view: &mut EmulatorView,
    program: &Arc<Program>,
    cursor: Option<u64>,
) {
    ui.heading("Side-channel solve");
    ui.label(muted(
        "Recover the input byte-by-byte by maximising executed instructions (instruction counting).",
    ));
    egui::Grid::new("emu-solve-form")
        .num_columns(2)
        .spacing([10.0, 6.0])
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            ui.label("Function address");
            ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                ui.text_edit_singleline(&mut view.addr);
                if ui.small_button("use cursor's function").clicked()
                    && let Some(f) = cursor.and_then(|a| program.function_containing(a))
                {
                    view.addr = format!("{:#x}", f.entry);
                }
            });
            ui.end_row();
            ui.label("Input length");
            ui.text_edit_singleline(&mut view.solve_len);
            ui.end_row();
            ui.label("Charset");
            ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                for cs in [Charset::Printable, Charset::Alnum, Charset::Digits] {
                    ui.selectable_value(&mut view.charset, cs, cs.label());
                }
            });
            ui.end_row();
            ui.label("");
            ui.checkbox(&mut view.pass_len, "pass length as arg1");
            ui.end_row();
        });

    if ui
        .add_enabled(!view.busy(), egui::Button::new("🔑 Solve"))
        .clicked()
    {
        start(view, ui.ctx(), program, JobKind::Solve);
    }

    if let Some(s) = &view.solve {
        ui.add_space(6.0);
        if let Some(e) = &s.error {
            ui.colored_label(ui.visuals().error_fg_color, e);
            return;
        }
        ui.label("Recovered input:");
        ui.label(RichText::new(format!("{:?}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&s.recovered))).monospace());
        ui.label(RichText::new(hex_ascii(&s.recovered)).monospace());
        ui.add_space(4.0);
        ui.collapsing("per-position instruction counts", |ui| {
            egui::Grid::new("emu-solve-rows")
                .num_columns(4)
                .striped(true)
                .spacing([14.0, 2.0])
                .show(ui, |ui| {
                    ui.label(muted("pos"));
                    ui.label(muted("byte"));
                    ui.label(muted("count"));
                    ui.label(muted("runner-up"));
                    ui.end_row();
                    for (i, b, c, r) in &s.rows {
                        ui.label(RichText::new(i.to_string()).monospace());
                        ui.label(RichText::new(format!("{:?}", *b as char)).monospace());
                        ui.label(RichText::new(c.to_string()).monospace());
                        ui.label(RichText::new(r.to_string()).monospace().weak());
                        ui.end_row();
                    }
                });
        });
    }
}

fn symbolic_section(
    ui: &mut Ui,
    view: &mut EmulatorView,
    program: &Arc<Program>,
    cursor: Option<u64>,
) {
    ui.heading("Symbolic solve");
    ui.label(muted(
        "Treat the input as symbolic and find a value that reaches the target block, avoiding the \
         ones you mark. Solves byte-wise transform-and-compare checks (xor/add/sub/… then equal).",
    ));
    egui::Grid::new("emu-sym-form")
        .num_columns(2)
        .spacing([10.0, 6.0])
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            ui.label("Function address");
            ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                ui.text_edit_singleline(&mut view.addr);
                if ui.small_button("use cursor's function").clicked()
                    && let Some(f) = cursor.and_then(|a| program.function_containing(a))
                {
                    view.addr = format!("{:#x}", f.entry);
                }
            });
            ui.end_row();
            ui.label("Input length");
            ui.text_edit_singleline(&mut view.solve_len);
            ui.end_row();
            ui.label("Target address");
            ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                ui.text_edit_singleline(&mut view.sym_target);
                if ui.small_button("use cursor").clicked()
                    && let Some(a) = cursor
                {
                    view.sym_target = format!("{a:#x}");
                }
            });
            ui.end_row();
            ui.label("Avoid addresses");
            ui.text_edit_singleline(&mut view.sym_avoid)
                .on_hover_text("comma- or space-separated hex addresses of the \"wrong\" blocks");
            ui.end_row();
        });

    let idle = !view.busy();
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        if ui
            .add_enabled(idle, egui::Button::new("∑ Solve symbolically"))
            .clicked()
        {
            start(view, ui.ctx(), program, JobKind::Symbolic);
        }
        if ui
            .add_enabled(idle, egui::Button::new("⚙ Solve detected VM (auto)"))
            .on_hover_text(
                "If a bytecode VM is detected, recover its key automatically — no addresses needed.",
            )
            .clicked()
        {
            start(view, ui.ctx(), program, JobKind::AutoVm);
        }
    });

    if let Some(s) = &view.sym {
        ui.add_space(6.0);
        if let Some(err) = &s.error {
            ui.colored_label(ui.visuals().error_fg_color, format!("stopped: {err}"));
        } else {
            let color = if s.complete {
                ui.visuals().text_color()
            } else {
                ui.visuals().warn_fg_color
            };
            ui.colored_label(
                color,
                format!("{} ({} constraints)", s.message, s.constraints),
            );
            ui.label("Input:");
            ui.label(RichText::new(format!("{:?}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&s.input))).monospace());
            ui.label(RichText::new(hex_ascii(&s.input)).monospace());
        }
        ui.collapsing("SMT-LIB2 (for external z3)", |ui| {
            ui.label(RichText::new(&s.smt2).monospace());
        });
    }
}

// --- engine glue ----------------------------------------------------------

fn abi_of(program: &Program) -> Abi {
    if program.memory.is_elf {
        Abi::SysV
    } else {
        Abi::Win64
    }
}

/// Seeds an emulator from the program image (regions plus zeroed `.bss` slack, so guest writes to
/// globals don't fault) and stubs imports.
fn seed(program: &Program) -> Emulator {
    let mut emu = Emulator::new();
    emu.mem = orress_vm::emu_image(program);
    for (addr, stub) in orress_vm::import_hooks(program) {
        emu.hook(addr, stub);
    }
    emu.mem.map_zeroed(SCRATCH, SCRATCH_SIZE);
    emu
}

fn parse_u64(s: &str) -> Option<u64> {
    let s = s.trim();
    s.strip_prefix("0x")
        .or_else(|| s.strip_prefix("0X"))
        .map_or_else(|| s.parse().ok(), |h| u64::from_str_radix(h, 16).ok())
}

/// General-purpose register names in the emulator's (iced-x86) index order.
const REG_NAMES: [&str; 16] = [
    "rax", "rcx", "rdx", "rbx", "rsp", "rbp", "rsi", "rdi", "r8", "r9", "r10", "r11", "r12", "r13",
    "r14", "r15",
];

/// The maximum instructions recorded for time-travel (each step keeps a small CPU snapshot).
const TRACE_LIMIT: usize = 100_000;

/// Records a time-travel trace of the function, with the same input/stack setup as `run_once`.
fn record_once(view: &Params, program: &Program) -> Result<Trace, String> {
    let func = parse_u64(&view.addr).ok_or("Enter a function address (hex, e.g. 0x401000).")?;
    let bytes = view.input.as_bytes();
    if bytes.len() > MAX_INPUT {
        return Err(format!("The input is longer than {MAX_INPUT} bytes."));
    }
    let mut emu = seed(program);
    emu.map(SCRATCH, bytes);
    emu.mem.write_bytes(SCRATCH + bytes.len() as u64, &[0]);
    let mut args = vec![SCRATCH];
    if view.pass_len {
        args.push(bytes.len() as u64);
    }
    // A fault mid-run keeps the steps leading up to it (`trace.fault`) — that's what you scrub.
    emu.record_call_with_fault(func, &args, abi_of(program), TRACE_LIMIT)
        .map_err(|e| format!("{e}"))
}

/// The time-travel scrubber: a slider over the recorded steps, showing the instruction executed and
/// the register file at that point, with the registers that changed at this step highlighted.
fn trace_panel(ui: &mut Ui, view: &mut EmulatorView) {
    if let Some(e) = &view.trace_error {
        ui.colored_label(ui.visuals().error_fg_color, e);
        return;
    }
    let Some(trace) = &view.trace else {
        return;
    };
    if trace.is_empty() {
        ui.label(muted(
            "Recorded an empty trace (the function returned immediately).",
        ));
        return;
    }
    ui.add_space(6.0);
    ui.label(RichText::new("Time-travel").strong());
    let last = trace.len() - 1;
    view.scrub = view.scrub.min(last);

    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        if ui.small_button("⏮").on_hover_text("first").clicked() {
            view.scrub = 0;
        }
        if ui.small_button("◀").on_hover_text("step back").clicked() {
            view.scrub = view.scrub.saturating_sub(1);
        }
        if ui.small_button("▶").on_hover_text("step forward").clicked() && view.scrub < last {
            view.scrub += 1;
        }
        if ui.small_button("⏭").on_hover_text("last").clicked() {
            view.scrub = last;
        }
        ui.add(egui::Slider::new(&mut view.scrub, 0..=last).text("step"));
    });

    let i = view.scrub;
    let changed: std::collections::HashSet<usize> =
        trace.changed_regs(i).into_iter().map(|(r, _)| r).collect();
    let addr = trace.addr_at(i).unwrap_or(0);
    ui.label(RichText::new(format!("step {i} / {last}   @ {addr:#x}")).monospace());

    let cpu = trace.cpu_at(i);
    egui::Grid::new("emu-ttd-regs")
        .num_columns(4)
        .spacing([14.0, 2.0])
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            for (r, name) in REG_NAMES.iter().enumerate() {
                let text = RichText::new(format!("{name} {:>#18x}", cpu.regs[r])).monospace();
                let text = if changed.contains(&r) {
                    text.strong().color(ui.visuals().warn_fg_color)
                } else {
                    text
                };
                ui.label(text);
                if r % 4 == 3 {
                    ui.end_row();
                }
            }
        });
    match &trace.fault {
        Some(e) => ui.colored_label(ui.visuals().error_fg_color, format!("stopped: {e}")),
        None => ui.label(muted(format!("stop: {:?}", trace.stop))),
    };
}

fn run_once(view: &Params, program: &Program) -> RunReport {
    let Some(func) = parse_u64(&view.addr) else {
        return err_report("Enter a function address (hex, e.g. 0x401000).");
    };
    let bytes = view.input.as_bytes();
    if bytes.len() > MAX_INPUT {
        return err_report(&format!("The input is longer than {MAX_INPUT} bytes."));
    }
    let mut emu = seed(program);
    emu.map(SCRATCH, bytes);
    emu.mem.write_bytes(SCRATCH + bytes.len() as u64, &[0]); // NUL-terminate
    let mut args = vec![SCRATCH];
    if view.pass_len {
        args.push(bytes.len() as u64);
    }
    match emu.call(func, &args, abi_of(program)) {
        Ok(rax) => {
            let scratch = emu
                .mem
                .read_vec(SCRATCH, bytes.len().max(1))
                .unwrap_or_default();
            let ret_str = emu
                .mem
                .is_mapped(rax)
                .then(|| String::from_utf8_lossy(&emu.read_cstr(rax, 256)).into_owned())
                .filter(|s| !s.is_empty());
            RunReport {
                rax,
                steps: emu.steps,
                status: format!("returned after {} instructions", emu.steps),
                error: false,
                scratch,
                ret_str,
            }
        }
        Err(e) => err_report(&format!("stopped: {e}")),
    }
}

fn solve_once(view: &Params, program: &Program, cancel: &AtomicBool) -> SolveReport {
    let Some(func) = parse_u64(&view.addr) else {
        return SolveReport::error("Enter a function address (hex, e.g. 0x401000).");
    };
    let len = match parse_len(&view.solve_len) {
        Ok(len) => len,
        Err(e) => return SolveReport::error(&e),
    };
    let abi = abi_of(program);
    let pass_len = view.pass_len;
    let mut emu = seed(program);
    let candidates = view.charset.bytes();
    let solution = solve_by_count(len, &candidates, |input| {
        // A cancelled solve finishes the sweep without emulating; its output is discarded.
        if cancel.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
            return 0;
        }
        emu.cpu = orress_emu::Cpu::new();
        emu.mem.write_bytes(SCRATCH, input);
        let mut args = vec![SCRATCH];
        if pass_len {
            args.push(len as u64);
        }
        let _ = emu.call(func, &args, abi);
        emu.steps
    });
    SolveReport {
        rows: solution
            .steps
            .iter()
            .map(|s| (s.index, s.byte, s.count, s.runner_up))
            .collect(),
        recovered: solution.input,
        error: None,
    }
}

/// Recovers the key of a detected bytecode VM with one click: finds the interpreter, derives the
/// success/avoid blocks and input from the CFG, and solves — no addresses to enter. Runs on the
/// worker thread (the VM scan + solve sweep takes a while).
fn auto_vm_solve(program: &Program) -> SymReport {
    let empty = SymReport::error;
    let Some(report) = orress_vm::scan(program).into_iter().next() else {
        return empty("No bytecode VM detected in this binary.");
    };
    match orress_vm::try_solve(program, &report) {
        Ok(sol) => SymReport {
            input: sol.key,
            complete: sol.complete,
            message: if sol.complete { "solved" } else { "partial" }.to_string(),
            constraints: sol.constraints,
            smt2: sol.smt2,
            error: None,
        },
        Err(e) => empty(&format!("Found a VM but could not solve it: {e}")),
    }
}

fn symbolic_solve_once(view: &Params, program: &Program) -> SymReport {
    let empty = SymReport::error;
    let Some(func) = parse_u64(&view.addr) else {
        return empty("enter a function address");
    };
    let len = match parse_len(&view.solve_len) {
        // MAX_INPUT fits in u32.
        Ok(len) => len as u32,
        Err(e) => return empty(&e),
    };
    let target = parse_u64(&view.sym_target).unwrap_or(0);
    let avoid: Vec<u64> = view
        .sym_avoid
        .split([',', ' ', '\t'])
        .filter_map(parse_u64)
        .collect();
    // A fresh concrete image seeds the symbolic executor; the input lives at SCRATCH.
    let mem = seed(program).mem;
    let hooks = orress_vm::import_hooks(program);
    match orress_sym::solve_check(
        mem,
        func,
        &[SCRATCH],
        SCRATCH,
        len,
        target,
        avoid,
        hooks,
        abi_of(program),
    ) {
        Ok(found) => SymReport {
            input: found.result.input,
            complete: found.result.complete,
            message: found.result.message,
            constraints: found.constraints,
            smt2: found.smt2,
            error: None,
        },
        Err(e) => empty(&e.to_string()),
    }
}

fn err_report(msg: &str) -> RunReport {
    RunReport {
        rax: 0,
        steps: 0,
        status: msg.to_string(),
        error: true,
        scratch: Vec::new(),
        ret_str: None,
    }
}

/// A compact hex + ASCII rendering of a small buffer.
fn hex_ascii(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    let hex: Vec<String> = bytes.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect();
    let ascii: String = bytes
        .iter()
        .map(|&b| {
            if (0x20..0x7f).contains(&b) {
                b as char
            } else {
                '.'
            }
        })
        .collect();
    format!("{}  |{}|", hex.join(" "), ascii)
}
```

`crates/orress-views/src/exploit.rs`:

```rs
//! The Exploit console: write a pwntools-style script against the open binary and run it on a
//! worker thread, streaming its output live. The scripting builtins (tubes, packing, cyclic, ROP,
//! symbol/GOT/PLT) live in `orress-script`'s exploit module; this is the egui front end.

use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
use std::sync::mpsc::Receiver;
use std::thread::JoinHandle;

use egui::{RichText, Ui};
use orress_analysis::FunctionKind;
use orress_project::DocStore;
use orress_script::ExploitCtx;
use orress_ui::muted;

const EXAMPLE: &str = r#"// Exploit console — a pwntools-style script over the open binary.
// Builtins: process/remote tubes, p8/p16/p32/p64, u*, flat, cyclic/cyclic_find,
// asm, str/bytes, hex/unhex, sym/got/plt/base, find_gadget.

// Find the offset to the return address with a cyclic pattern:
//   let io = process("./chall");
//   io.sendline(cyclic(200));
//   io.recvall();            // crashes; read the faulting value in the debugger,
//   print(cyclic_find(0x6161616c));   // then recover the offset

print("gadget pop rdi ; ret -> " + find_gadget("pop rdi ; ret"));
"#;

/// Persistent UI state for the Exploit console.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct ExploitView {
    src: String,
    seeded: bool,
    output: String,
    running: bool,
    cancel: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    done: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    rx: Option<Receiver<String>>,
    handle: Option<JoinHandle<()>>,
}

pub fn exploit_view(ui: &mut Ui, view: &mut ExploitView, docs: &DocStore) {
    orress_ui::spotlight::mark(ui.ctx(), "view.Exploit", ui.max_rect());
    if !view.seeded {
        view.src = EXAMPLE.to_string();
        view.seeded = true;
    }

    // Pull any streamed output.
    if let Some(rx) = &view.rx {
        while let Ok(line) = rx.try_recv() {
            view.output.push_str(&line);
        }
    }
    if view.running {
        ui.ctx().request_repaint();
        if view.done.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
            view.running = false;
            if let Some(h) = view.handle.take() {
                let _ = h.join();
            }
            view.rx = None;
        }
    }

    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label(RichText::new("Exploit").strong());
        ui.label(muted(
            "pwntools-style scripting · tubes · packing · cyclic · ROP",
        ));
    });
    ui.separator();

    let has_doc = docs
        .active()
        .map(|d| d.analysis().is_some() && d.program().is_some())
        .unwrap_or(false);

    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        if ui
            .add_enabled(!view.running && has_doc, egui::Button::new("▶ Run"))
            .clicked()
            && let Some(ctx) = docs.active().and_then(build_ctx)
        {
            start(view, ui.ctx(), ctx);
        }
        if ui
            .add_enabled(view.running, egui::Button::new("⏹ Stop"))
            .clicked()
        {
            view.cancel.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
        }
        if ui.button("Clear output").clicked() {
            view.output.clear();
        }
        if view.running {
            ui.spinner();
        }
        if !has_doc {
            ui.label(muted("Open a binary to script against it."));
        }
    });

    egui::ScrollArea::vertical()
        .id_salt("exploit-editor")
        .max_height(ui.available_height() * 0.55)
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            ui.add(
                egui::TextEdit::multiline(&mut view.src)
                    .code_editor()
                    .desired_width(f32::INFINITY)
                    .desired_rows(14),
            );
        });

    ui.separator();
    ui.label(muted("Output"));
    egui::ScrollArea::vertical()
        .id_salt("exploit-output")
        .auto_shrink([false, false])
        .stick_to_bottom(true)
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            ui.add(
                egui::Label::new(RichText::new(&view.output).monospace())
                    .wrap_mode(egui::TextWrapMode::Extend),
            );
        });
}

/// Starts the script on a worker thread; it streams output lines and sets `done` when finished.
fn start(view: &mut ExploitView, ctx: &egui::Context, exploit_ctx: ExploitCtx) {
    let (tx, rx) = std::sync::mpsc::channel();
    view.cancel = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
    view.done = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
    view.output.clear();
    view.rx = Some(rx);
    view.running = true;
    let src = view.src.clone();
    let cancel = Arc::clone(&view.cancel);
    let done = Arc::clone(&view.done);
    let egui_ctx = ctx.clone();
    view.handle = std::thread::Builder::new()
        .name("exploit".into())
        .spawn(move || {
            let result = orress_script::run_exploit(&src, exploit_ctx, tx.clone(), cancel);
            let _ = tx.send(match result {
                Ok(()) => "\n[done]\n".into(),
                Err(e) => format!("\n[error] {e}\n"),
            });
            done.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
            egui_ctx.request_repaint();
        })
        .ok();
}

/// Builds the exploit context (symbols, GOT, PLT, executable sections) from the open document.
fn build_ctx(doc: &orress_project::Document) -> Option<ExploitCtx> {
    let analysis = doc.analysis()?;
    let program = doc.program()?;
    let bytes = doc.bytes()?;
    let info = &analysis.info;

    let mut symbols = std::collections::HashMap::new();
    for s in &info.function_symbols {
        symbols.entry(s.name.clone()).or_insert(s.address);
    }
    for e in &info.exports {
        if e.address != 0 {
            symbols.entry(e.name.clone()).or_insert(e.address);
        }
    }

    let got = info
        .import_slots
        .iter()
        .map(|s| (s.name.clone(), s.address))
        .collect();

    // PLT stubs are thunk functions named "<name>@plt" in the analysis.
    let mut plt = std::collections::HashMap::new();
    for f in program.functions.values() {
        if f.kind == FunctionKind::Thunk
            && let Some(name) = program.name(f.entry)
            && let Some(base_name) = name.text.strip_suffix("@plt")
        {
            plt.entry(base_name.to_string()).or_insert(f.entry);
        }
    }

    let exec = info
        .sections
        .iter()
        .filter(|s| s.perms.execute)
        .filter_map(|s| {
            let range = s.file_range()?;
            Some((s.address, bytes.get(range)?.to_vec()))
        })
        .collect();

    let binsh = orress_bytes::search::Pattern::text("/bin/sh", false)
        .ok()
        .and_then(|p| p.find_from(bytes, 0))
        .and_then(|off| info.offset_to_address(off as u64));

    let sections = info
        .sections
        .iter()
        .map(|s| (s.name.clone(), s.address))
        .collect();

    Some(ExploitCtx {
        base: info.image_base,
        isa: program.isa,
        symbols,
        got,
        plt,
        exec,
        binsh,
        sections,
    })
}
```

```rs
//! The Extensions panel: see installed extensions, install new ones (from a git URL or a local
//! directory) and uninstall them. Install/uninstall are performed by the app (which owns the
//! extensions directory and re-registers themes and language servers afterwards); the panel emits
//! [`ViewRequest`]s and reads the installed set straight from disk.

use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::Arc;

use egui::{Id, RichText, Ui};
use orress_ui::muted;

use crate::ViewRequest;

fn dir_id() -> Id {
    Id::new("orress::extensions_dir")
}

fn cache_id() -> Id {
    Id::new("orress::extensions_installed")
}

/// The app stores the extensions directory here so the panel can scan it.
pub fn set_extensions_dir(ctx: &egui::Context, dir: PathBuf) {
    ctx.data_mut(|d| d.insert_temp(dir_id(), dir));
    refresh_extensions(ctx);
}

/// Forgets the cached list of installed extensions, so the panel re-reads the manifests from
/// disk the next time it is drawn. The app calls this after an install or uninstall.
pub fn refresh_extensions(ctx: &egui::Context) {
    ctx.data_mut(|d| d.remove_temp::<Arc<Vec<orress_ext::InstalledExtension>>>(cache_id()));
}

/// The installed extensions, read from disk once and then cached (scanning every manifest each
/// frame would hit the disk at the frame rate).
fn installed(
    ctx: &egui::Context,
    dir: &std::path::Path,
) -> Arc<Vec<orress_ext::InstalledExtension>> {
    if let Some(list) = ctx.data(|d| d.get_temp(cache_id())) {
        return list;
    }
    let list = Arc::new(orress_ext::installed(dir));
    ctx.data_mut(|d| d.insert_temp(cache_id(), Arc::clone(&list)));
    list
}

pub(crate) fn extensions_dir(ctx: &egui::Context) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    ctx.data(|d| d.get_temp::<PathBuf>(dir_id()))
}

/// Draws the Extensions panel.
pub fn extensions_panel(ui: &mut Ui, requests: &mut Vec<ViewRequest>) {
    ui.heading("Extensions");
    ui.label(muted(
        "Install ORRESS or Zed-compatible extensions: themes, tree-sitter grammars and \
         language-server adapters. Theme and server changes apply as the extension loads.",
    ));
    ui.separator();

    let Some(dir) = extensions_dir(ui.ctx()) else {
        ui.label(muted(
            "No config directory, so extensions cannot be managed here.",
        ));
        return;
    };

    // Install from a git URL or a local path.
    let src_id = Id::new("orress::ext_install_src");
    let mut src: String = ui.data(|d| d.get_temp(src_id).unwrap_or_default());
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label("Install from:");
        let edit = ui.add(
            egui::TextEdit::singleline(&mut src)
                .hint_text("git URL or local directory path")
                .desired_width(360.0),
        );
        if edit.changed() {
            ui.data_mut(|d| d.insert_temp(src_id, src.clone()));
        }
        let trimmed = src.trim().to_string();
        if ui
            .add_enabled(!trimmed.is_empty(), egui::Button::new("Install"))
            .clicked()
        {
            requests.push(ViewRequest::InstallExtension(trimmed));
            ui.data_mut(|d| d.insert_temp(src_id, String::new()));
        }
    });
    ui.add_space(8.0);

    let installed = installed(ui.ctx(), &dir);
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label(RichText::new(format!("Installed ({})", installed.len())).strong());
        if ui
            .small_button("Refresh")
            .on_hover_text("Re-read the extensions folder (e.g. after copying one in by hand)")
            .clicked()
        {
            refresh_extensions(ui.ctx());
        }
    });
    if installed.is_empty() {
        ui.label(muted("Nothing installed yet."));
    }
    for ext in installed.iter() {
        ui.horizontal(|ui| {
            ui.label(RichText::new(&ext.name).strong());
            if !ext.version.is_empty() {
                ui.label(muted(format!("v{}", ext.version)));
            }
            ui.label(muted(format!("({})", ext.id)));
            if ui.small_button("Uninstall").clicked() {
                requests.push(ViewRequest::UninstallExtension(ext.id.clone()));
            }
        });
    }

    ui.add_space(6.0);
    ui.label(muted(format!("Directory: {}", dir.display())));
}
```

`crates/orress-views/src/find.rs`:

```rs
//! The find bar shared by the code views (disassembly, decompiler): a text field with
//! Next / Previous, Enter / F3 / Shift+F3 and Esc to close.

use egui::{Key, RichText, Ui};
use orress_ui::ExplainExt as _;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum FindStep {
    Next,
    Previous,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub(crate) struct FindInput {
    pub open: bool,
    pub query: String,
    pub focus: bool,
    /// Result of the last search: where it was found, or why not.
    pub status: Option<Result<String, String>>,
}

impl FindInput {
    pub fn show(&mut self) {
        self.open = true;
        self.focus = true;
    }

    /// The query, lowercased, or `None` while it is empty.
    pub fn needle(&self) -> Option<String> {
        let q = self.query.trim();
        (!q.is_empty()).then(|| q.to_ascii_lowercase())
    }
}

/// What the bar asks for this frame.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct BarResult {
    pub step: Option<FindStep>,
    /// The query text changed (so a remembered match position is stale).
    pub changed: bool,
}

/// Draws the bar. `explain` is shown in Explain Mode on its label.
pub(crate) fn bar(ui: &mut Ui, input: &mut FindInput, hint: &str, explain: &str) -> BarResult {
    let mut result = BarResult::default();
    ui.horizontal_wrapped(|ui| {
        ui.label("Find").explain("Find", explain);
        let edit = ui.add(
            egui::TextEdit::singleline(&mut input.query)
                .hint_text(hint)
                .desired_width(260.0)
                .font(egui::TextStyle::Monospace),
        );
        if input.focus {
            edit.request_focus();
            input.focus = false;
        }
        if edit.changed() {
            input.status = None;
            result.changed = true;
        }
        let submit = edit.lost_focus() && ui.input(|i| i.key_pressed(Key::Enter));
        if ui.button("Next").on_hover_text("F3").clicked() || submit {
            result.step = Some(FindStep::Next);
            if submit {
                input.focus = true;
            }
        }
        if ui.button("Previous").on_hover_text("Shift+F3").clicked() {
            result.step = Some(FindStep::Previous);
        }
        if ui.button("×").on_hover_text("Close (Esc)").clicked()
            || (edit.has_focus() && ui.input(|i| i.key_pressed(Key::Escape)))
        {
            input.open = false;
        }
        match &input.status {
            Some(Ok(s)) => {
                ui.label(RichText::new(s).weak());
            }
            Some(Err(e)) => {
                ui.colored_label(ui.visuals().warn_fg_color, e);
            }
            None => {}
        }
    });
    result
}

/// Byte offsets where `needle` (lowercase ASCII) starts in `text`, ignoring ASCII case.
pub(crate) fn matches(text: &str, needle: &str) -> Vec<usize> {
    if needle.is_empty() {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    text.to_ascii_lowercase()
        .match_indices(needle)
        .map(|(at, _)| at)
        .collect()
}

/// The next (or previous) entry of a sorted list of match positions after (before)
/// `from`, wrapping around.
pub(crate) fn step_index(len: usize, current: Option<usize>, step: FindStep) -> Option<usize> {
    if len == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    Some(match (current, step) {
        (None, FindStep::Next) => 0,
        (None, FindStep::Previous) => len - 1,
        (Some(i), FindStep::Next) => (i + 1) % len,
        (Some(i), FindStep::Previous) => (i + len - 1) % len,
    })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn finds_ignoring_case() {
        assert_eq!(matches("if a1 == 7 { XOR }", "xor"), vec![13]);
        assert!(matches("abc", "").is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn steps_wrap_around() {
        assert_eq!(step_index(3, None, FindStep::Next), Some(0));
        assert_eq!(step_index(3, Some(2), FindStep::Next), Some(0));
        assert_eq!(step_index(3, Some(0), FindStep::Previous), Some(2));
        assert_eq!(step_index(0, None, FindStep::Next), None);
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-views/src/folder.rs`:

```rs
//! The project folder tree (left dock, top section): a Zed-style view of a folder on disk.
//! Clicking a file opens it the usual way (source to the editor, binaries to analysis); the
//! right-click menu reveals a path in the OS, makes a notes file, or extracts an executable's
//! resources into the project.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::Arc;

use egui::{RichText, Ui};
use orress_project::DocStore;

use crate::ViewRequest;

/// At most this many entries are listed per directory (a guard against pathological folders).
const MAX_ENTRIES: usize = 5000;

/// One entry in a directory listing.
#[derive(Clone)]
struct Entry {
    name: String,
    path: PathBuf,
    is_dir: bool,
}

/// Cached directory listings, so the tree does not `read_dir` every frame. Cleared when the
/// project root changes or the user presses Refresh.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
struct FolderCache {
    root: Option<PathBuf>,
    dirs: std::collections::HashMap<PathBuf, Arc<Result<Vec<Entry>, String>>>,
}

fn cache_id() -> egui::Id {
    egui::Id::new("orress::folder_cache")
}

/// Reads (and caches) the sorted listing of `dir`: directories first, then files, each
/// alphabetical and case-insensitive.
fn listing(cache: &mut FolderCache, dir: &Path) -> Arc<Result<Vec<Entry>, String>> {
    if let Some(hit) = cache.dirs.get(dir) {
        return Arc::clone(hit);
    }
    let result = read_dir_sorted(dir);
    let arc = Arc::new(result);
    cache.dirs.insert(dir.to_path_buf(), Arc::clone(&arc));
    arc
}

fn read_dir_sorted(dir: &Path) -> Result<Vec<Entry>, String> {
    let mut entries: Vec<Entry> = Vec::new();
    let read = std::fs::read_dir(dir).map_err(|e| format!("{e}"))?;
    for item in read.take(MAX_ENTRIES).flatten() {
        let path = item.path();
        let is_dir = item.file_type().map(|t| t.is_dir()).unwrap_or(false);
        let name = item.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
        entries.push(Entry { name, path, is_dir });
    }
    entries.sort_by(|a, b| {
        b.is_dir
            .cmp(&a.is_dir)
            .then_with(|| a.name.to_lowercase().cmp(&b.name.to_lowercase()))
    });
    Ok(entries)
}

/// Draws the folder tree for `root`.
pub fn folder_tree(ui: &mut Ui, root: &Path, docs: &DocStore, requests: &mut Vec<ViewRequest>) {
    let mut cache = ui
        .data_mut(|d| d.get_temp::<FolderCache>(cache_id()))
        .unwrap_or_default();
    // Reset when the project root changes.
    if cache.root.as_deref() != Some(root) {
        cache = FolderCache {
            root: Some(root.to_path_buf()),
            dirs: Default::default(),
        };
    }

    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        let name = root
            .file_name()
            .map(|n| n.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| root.display().to_string());
        ui.label(RichText::new(name).strong());
        if ui.small_button("⟳").on_hover_text("Refresh").clicked() {
            cache.dirs.clear();
        }
    });
    ui.add_space(2.0);

    let active = docs.active.as_deref().map(Path::to_path_buf);
    render_dir(ui, root, &mut cache, requests, active.as_deref());

    ui.data_mut(|d| d.insert_temp(cache_id(), cache));
}

fn render_dir(
    ui: &mut Ui,
    dir: &Path,
    cache: &mut FolderCache,
    requests: &mut Vec<ViewRequest>,
    active: Option<&Path>,
) {
    let entries = listing(cache, dir);
    match entries.as_ref() {
        Err(e) => {
            ui.colored_label(ui.visuals().warn_fg_color, e.as_str());
        }
        Ok(entries) => {
            for entry in entries.iter() {
                if entry.is_dir {
                    let path = entry.path.clone();
                    let header = egui::CollapsingHeader::new(&entry.name)
                        .id_salt(&entry.path)
                        .show(ui, |ui| {
                            render_dir(ui, &path, cache, requests, active);
                        });
                    header
                        .header_response
                        .context_menu(|ui| dir_menu(ui, &entry.path, requests));
                } else {
                    let is_active = active == Some(entry.path.as_path());
                    let label = if is_active {
                        RichText::new(&entry.name).strong()
                    } else {
                        RichText::new(&entry.name)
                    };
                    let response = ui.selectable_label(is_active, label);
                    if response.clicked() {
                        requests.push(ViewRequest::OpenPath(entry.path.clone()));
                    }
                    response.context_menu(|ui| file_menu(ui, &entry.path, requests));
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

fn file_menu(ui: &mut Ui, path: &Path, requests: &mut Vec<ViewRequest>) {
    if ui.button("Open").clicked() {
        requests.push(ViewRequest::OpenPath(path.to_path_buf()));
        ui.close();
    }
    if is_executable(path) && ui.button("Extract resources…").clicked() {
        requests.push(ViewRequest::ExtractResources(path.to_path_buf()));
        ui.close();
    }
    if ui.button("Reveal in file manager").clicked() {
        requests.push(ViewRequest::RevealInOs(path.to_path_buf()));
        ui.close();
    }
}

fn dir_menu(ui: &mut Ui, dir: &Path, requests: &mut Vec<ViewRequest>) {
    if ui.button("New notes file…").clicked() {
        requests.push(ViewRequest::NewNotesFile(dir.to_path_buf()));
        ui.close();
    }
    if ui.button("Reveal in file manager").clicked() {
        requests.push(ViewRequest::RevealInOs(dir.to_path_buf()));
        ui.close();
    }
}

/// Whether a path looks like a Windows executable image (used only to offer resource extraction;
/// the extractor itself validates the bytes).
fn is_executable(path: &Path) -> bool {
    matches!(
        path.extension()
            .and_then(|e| e.to_str())
            .map(str::to_ascii_lowercase)
            .as_deref(),
        Some(
            "exe"
                | "dll"
                | "sys"
                | "ocx"
                | "scr"
                | "cpl"
                | "efi"
                | "mui"
                | "node"
                | "drv"
                | "ax"
                | "tsp"
        )
    )
}
```

`crates/orress-views/src/functions.rs`:

```rs
//! Functions list.

use egui::{RichText, Sense, Ui};
use egui_extras::{Column, TableBuilder};
use orress_analysis::FunctionKind;
use orress_project::Document;
use orress_ui::{ExplainExt as _, muted};

use crate::{DocView, ViewCtx, ViewRequest};

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct FunctionsState {
    filter: String,
    show_thunks: bool,
    cache: Option<(String, u64, Vec<u64>)>,
}

pub fn functions(
    ui: &mut Ui,
    doc: &mut Document,
    state: &mut FunctionsState,
    cx: &mut ViewCtx<'_>,
) {
    let Some(program) = crate::program_or_message(ui, doc) else {
        return;
    };
    ui.label(muted(
        "Every function ORRESS found by following calls from the entry point and known \
         symbols. Names like sub_401000 are generated: rename them (N in the disassembly) as \
         you understand what they do. Callers: how many places call it.",
    ));
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.add(
            egui::TextEdit::singleline(&mut state.filter)
                .hint_text("Filter by name…")
                .desired_width(220.0),
        );
        ui.checkbox(&mut state.show_thunks, "Show import stubs")
            .explain(
                "Import stubs",
                "Tiny functions that only jump to a library function (PLT entries on Linux, \
             import thunks on Windows). Hidden by default because they all look the same.",
            );
        if let Some(main) = program.main
            && ui
                .button("Go to main")
                .explain(
                    "main",
                    "Jump to the program's own main function, past the start-up code.",
                )
                .clicked()
        {
            doc.navigate_to_address(main);
            cx.requests
                .push(ViewRequest::Open(doc.path.clone(), DocView::Disassembly));
        }
    });

    let key = format!("{}{}", state.filter, state.show_thunks);
    if state
        .cache
        .as_ref()
        .is_none_or(|(k, g, _)| *k != key || *g != doc.generation)
    {
        let filter = state.filter.to_lowercase();
        let list = program
            .functions
            .values()
            .filter(|f| state.show_thunks || f.kind != FunctionKind::Thunk)
            .filter(|f| {
                filter.is_empty()
                    || doc
                        .name_of(f.entry)
                        .is_some_and(|n| n.to_lowercase().contains(&filter))
            })
            .map(|f| f.entry)
            .collect();
        state.cache = Some((key, doc.generation, list));
    }
    let Some((_, _, list)) = &state.cache else {
        return;
    };
    ui.label(muted(format!(
        "{} of {} functions",
        list.len(),
        program.functions.len()
    )));

    let wide = program.isa.pointer_size() == 8;
    let current = program
        .memory
        .address_of(doc.cursor)
        .and_then(|a| program.function_containing(a))
        .map(|f| f.entry);
    let mut clicked = None;
    TableBuilder::new(ui)
        .id_salt("functions")
        .striped(true)
        .resizable(true)
        .sense(Sense::click())
        .cell_layout(egui::Layout::left_to_right(egui::Align::Center))
        .column(Column::auto().at_least(200.0))
        .column(Column::auto().at_least(if wide { 150.0 } else { 90.0 }))
        .columns(Column::auto().at_least(60.0), 3)
        .column(Column::remainder())
        .header(20.0, |mut h| {
            for (name, explain) in [
                ("Name", "The function's name: from the file's symbols, found by ORRESS (main), yours, or generated."),
                ("Address", "Where the function starts in memory."),
                ("Size", "Bytes of code."),
                ("Blocks", "Basic blocks: more blocks means more branches and loops."),
                ("Callers", "How many places call this function. Small functions with many callers are often helpers like strlen."),
                ("", ""),
            ] {
                h.col(|ui| {
                    ui.label(RichText::new(name).strong()).explain(name, explain);
                });
            }
        })
        .body(|body| {
            body.rows(18.0, list.len(), |mut row| {
                let entry = list[row.index()];
                let Some(f) = program.functions.get(&entry) else {
                    return;
                };
                row.set_selected(current == Some(entry));
                let name = doc.name_of(entry).unwrap_or_else(|| format!("sub_{entry:x}"));
                let user = doc.annotations.names.contains_key(&entry);
                row.col(|ui| {
                    let text = RichText::new(name).monospace();
                    ui.label(if user { text.strong() } else { text });
                });
                row.col(|ui| {
                    ui.label(RichText::new(crate::fmt_addr(entry, wide)).monospace());
                });
                row.col(|ui| {
                    ui.label(f.size().to_string());
                });
                row.col(|ui| {
                    ui.label(f.blocks.len().to_string());
                });
                row.col(|ui| {
                    ui.label(program.xrefs(entry).len().to_string());
                });
                row.col(|ui| {
                    if program.main == Some(entry) {
                        ui.label(RichText::new("main").small().color(ui.visuals().hyperlink_color));
                    } else if f.kind == FunctionKind::Thunk {
                        ui.label(muted("import stub"));
                    }
                });
                if row.response().clicked() {
                    clicked = Some(entry);
                }
            });
        });
    if let Some(entry) = clicked {
        doc.navigate_to_address(entry);
        cx.requests
            .push(ViewRequest::Open(doc.path.clone(), DocView::Disassembly));
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-views/src/gadgets.rs`:

```rs
//! The Gadgets panel: list the ROP gadgets in the open binary and filter them, for building
//! return-oriented chains. The finder lives in `orress-pwn`; this is the egui front end.

use std::path::PathBuf;

use egui::{RichText, Ui};
use orress_project::DocStore;
use orress_pwn::Gadget;
use orress_ui::muted;

/// Persistent UI state for the Gadgets tab.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct GadgetsView {
    /// The file (path + generation) the cache belongs to; a new file or a patch re-scans.
    doc: Option<(PathBuf, u64)>,
    gadgets: Vec<Gadget>,
    filter: String,
}

impl GadgetsView {
    fn ensure(&mut self, doc: &orress_project::Document) {
        let key = (doc.path.clone(), doc.generation);
        if self.doc.as_ref() == Some(&key) {
            return;
        }
        self.gadgets = scan(doc);
        self.doc = Some(key);
    }
}

pub fn gadgets_view(ui: &mut Ui, view: &mut GadgetsView, docs: &DocStore) {
    orress_ui::spotlight::mark(ui.ctx(), "view.Gadgets", ui.max_rect());
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label(RichText::new("Gadgets").strong());
        ui.label(muted("ROP gadgets · filter and copy for your chain"));
    });
    ui.separator();

    let Some(doc) = docs.active() else {
        ui.label(muted("Open a binary to find its ROP gadgets."));
        return;
    };
    if doc.program().is_none() {
        ui.label(muted(
            "Analysis is still running (or this file has no code).",
        ));
        return;
    }
    view.ensure(doc);

    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label("Filter");
        ui.add(
            egui::TextEdit::singleline(&mut view.filter)
                .hint_text("pop rdi ; ret")
                .desired_width(260.0),
        );
        if ui.button("Clear").clicked() {
            view.filter.clear();
        }
    });

    let needle = view.filter.to_lowercase();
    let matches: Vec<usize> = view
        .gadgets
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .filter(|(_, g)| needle.is_empty() || g.text.to_lowercase().contains(&needle))
        .map(|(i, _)| i)
        .collect();
    ui.label(muted(format!(
        "{} gadget{} ({} shown)",
        view.gadgets.len(),
        if view.gadgets.len() == 1 { "" } else { "s" },
        matches.len()
    )));
    ui.separator();

    let row_h = ui.text_style_height(&egui::TextStyle::Monospace) + 4.0;
    egui::ScrollArea::vertical()
        .auto_shrink([false, false])
        .show_rows(ui, row_h, matches.len(), |ui, range| {
            for &i in &matches[range] {
                let g = &view.gadgets[i];
                ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                    if ui
                        .button(RichText::new(format!("{:#x}", g.addr)).monospace())
                        .on_hover_text("Copy address")
                        .clicked()
                    {
                        ui.ctx().copy_text(format!("{:#x}", g.addr));
                    }
                    ui.label(RichText::new(&g.text).monospace());
                });
            }
        });
}

/// Scans the open binary's executable sections for gadgets.
fn scan(doc: &orress_project::Document) -> Vec<Gadget> {
    let (Some(analysis), Some(program), Some(bytes)) = (doc.analysis(), doc.program(), doc.bytes())
    else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    let sections: Vec<(u64, &[u8])> = analysis
        .info
        .sections
        .iter()
        .filter(|s| s.perms.execute)
        .filter_map(|s| Some((s.address, bytes.get(s.file_range()?)?)))
        .collect();
    orress_pwn::find_gadgets(&sections, program.isa, 6)
}
```
