```rs
//! Strings list with filtering and flag highlighting.

use egui::{RichText, Sense, Ui};
use egui_extras::{Column, TableBuilder};
use orress_bytes::strings::looks_like_flag;
use orress_project::Document;
use orress_ui::{ExplainExt as _, muted};

use crate::{DocView, ViewCtx, ViewRequest};

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct StringsState {
    filter: String,
    flags_only: bool,
    /// Strings inside executable code are mostly instruction bytes that happen to be
    /// printable ("D$pH"), so they are hidden unless asked for.
    show_code_strings: bool,
    min_len: Option<usize>,
    /// Cached filter result: (filter key, matching indices).
    cache: Option<(String, Vec<usize>)>,
}

pub fn strings(ui: &mut Ui, doc: &mut Document, state: &mut StringsState, cx: &mut ViewCtx<'_>) {
    let Some(analysis) = doc.analysis().cloned() else {
        return;
    };
    let all = &analysis.strings;
    ui.label(muted(
        "Readable text found in the file. Messages like \"Wrong password\" lead you to the \
         code that checks your input. Text that looks like a CTF flag is highlighted. Click a \
         row to see it in the hex view.",
    ));
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.add(egui::TextEdit::singleline(&mut state.filter).hint_text("Filter (case-insensitive)…").desired_width(240.0));
        ui.checkbox(&mut state.flags_only, "Flag-like only").explain(
            "Flag-like strings",
            "Show only strings shaped like a CTF flag, e.g. flag{...}, CTF{...} or HTB{...}.",
        );
        let mut min = state.min_len.unwrap_or(orress_project::MIN_STRING_LEN);
        ui.add(egui::Slider::new(&mut min, orress_project::MIN_STRING_LEN..=32).text("min length"))
            .explain("Minimum length", "Hide strings shorter than this. Short strings are often random bytes that happen to be printable.");
        state.min_len = Some(min);
        ui.checkbox(&mut state.show_code_strings, "Include code").explain(
            "Strings inside code",
            "By default, strings found inside executable sections are hidden: they are \
             mostly machine instructions whose bytes happen to be printable, like \"D$pH\". \
             Turn this on to see everything.",
        );
    });
    let info = &analysis.info;

    // The analysis identity and generation are part of the key: a patch re-extracts the
    // strings, and indices from the old list must never index the new one.
    let key = format!(
        "{:?}",
        (
            std::sync::Arc::as_ptr(&analysis),
            doc.generation,
            &state.filter,
            state.flags_only,
            state.min_len,
            state.show_code_strings
        )
    );
    if state.cache.as_ref().is_none_or(|(k, _)| *k != key) {
        let filter = state.filter.to_lowercase();
        let min = state.min_len.unwrap_or(0);
        let indices = all
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .filter(|(_, s)| s.text.chars().count() >= min)
            .filter(|(_, s)| !state.flags_only || looks_like_flag(&s.text))
            .filter(|(_, s)| {
                state.show_code_strings
                    || !info
                        .section_at_offset(s.offset as u64)
                        .is_some_and(|sec| sec.perms.execute)
            })
            .filter(|(_, s)| filter.is_empty() || s.text.to_lowercase().contains(&filter))
            .map(|(i, _)| i)
            .collect();
        state.cache = Some((key, indices));
    }
    let Some((_, indices)) = &state.cache else {
        return;
    };
    let capped = if all.len() >= orress_project::MAX_STRINGS {
        " (limit reached)"
    } else {
        ""
    };
    ui.label(muted(format!(
        "{} of {} strings{capped}",
        indices.len(),
        all.len()
    )));

    let wide = info.bits == Some(64);
    let program = doc.program().cloned();
    let mut clicked = None;
    let mut follow = None;
    TableBuilder::new(ui)
        .id_salt("strings")
        .striped(true)
        .resizable(true)
        .sense(Sense::click())
        .cell_layout(egui::Layout::left_to_right(egui::Align::Center))
        .column(Column::auto().at_least(80.0))
        .column(Column::auto().at_least(if wide { 150.0 } else { 90.0 }))
        .column(Column::auto().at_least(60.0))
        .column(Column::auto().at_least(50.0))
        .column(Column::auto().at_least(45.0))
        .column(Column::remainder())
        .header(20.0, |mut h| {
            for (name, explain) in [
                ("Offset", "Position in the file."),
                ("Address", "Where the string is in memory when the program runs. This is the number you will see in disassembly."),
                ("Section", "Which section the string is in. Constant strings are usually in .rdata or .rodata."),
                ("Type", "ASCII: one byte per character. UTF-16: two bytes per character (Windows wide strings)."),
                ("Refs", "How many instructions use this string. Click to jump to the code that uses it: the fastest way from \"Wrong password\" to the password check."),
                ("Text", "The string itself."),
            ] {
                h.col(|ui| {
                    ui.label(RichText::new(name).strong()).explain(name, explain);
                });
            }
        })
        .body(|body| {
            body.rows(18.0, indices.len(), |mut row| {
                let Some(s) = indices.get(row.index()).and_then(|&i| all.get(i)) else {
                    return;
                };
                let offset = s.offset as u64;
                row.set_selected(doc.cursor >= offset && doc.cursor < offset + s.byte_len as u64);
                row.col(|ui| {
                    ui.label(RichText::new(format!("0x{offset:X}")).monospace());
                });
                row.col(|ui| {
                    match info.offset_to_address(offset) {
                        Some(a) => ui.label(RichText::new(crate::fmt_addr(a, wide)).monospace()),
                        None => ui.label(muted("—")),
                    };
                });
                row.col(|ui| {
                    ui.label(info.section_at_offset(offset).map_or("", |sec| sec.name.as_str()));
                });
                row.col(|ui| {
                    ui.label(RichText::new(s.encoding.label()).small().weak());
                });
                row.col(|ui| {
                    // References to any byte of the string: Rust stores literals back
                    // to back, so one row can hold several strings.
                    let refs: Vec<orress_analysis::Xref> = program
                        .as_ref()
                        .zip(info.offset_to_address(offset))
                        .map(|(p, a)| {
                            (a..a + s.byte_len as u64)
                                .flat_map(|x| p.xrefs(x).iter().copied())
                                .collect()
                        })
                        .unwrap_or_default();
                    if let Some(first) = refs.first()
                        && ui.link(format!("{} »", refs.len())).on_hover_text("Go to the code that uses this string").clicked()
                    {
                        follow = Some(first.from);
                    }
                });
                row.col(|ui| {
                    let text = RichText::new(&s.text).monospace();
                    if looks_like_flag(&s.text) {
                        ui.label(RichText::new("FLAG?").small().strong().color(ui.visuals().warn_fg_color));
                        ui.label(text.color(ui.visuals().warn_fg_color));
                    } else {
                        ui.label(text);
                    }
                });
                if row.response().clicked() {
                    clicked = Some((offset, s.byte_len as u64));
                }
            });
        });
    if let Some(from) = follow {
        doc.navigate_to_address(from);
        cx.requests
            .push(ViewRequest::Open(doc.path.clone(), DocView::Disassembly));
    } else if let Some((offset, len)) = clicked {
        doc.select(offset, len);
        cx.requests
            .push(ViewRequest::Open(doc.path.clone(), DocView::Hex));
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-views/src/terminal.rs`:

```rs
//! The integrated terminal view: renders the `orress-term` PTY screen as a character grid
//! and sends keyboard input to the shell. Colours follow the standard ANSI palette.

use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::Arc;

use egui::text::LayoutJob;
use egui::{Color32, FontId, Pos2, Rect, Sense, Stroke, TextFormat, Ui, Vec2};
use orress_term::Terminal;

/// The terminal's persistent state (owned by the app).
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct TerminalSession {
    term: Option<Terminal>,
    /// Where to start the shell (the current project directory, if any).
    cwd: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// Scrollback offset in rows (0 = bottom / live).
    scrollback: usize,
    /// Why the shell could not be started. Kept (and shown) until the user presses Restart, so a
    /// missing shell is not re-spawned on every repaint.
    spawn_error: Option<String>,
}

impl TerminalSession {
    /// Sets the directory a newly started shell opens in (applies on the next start/Restart; a
    /// failed start keeps its directory until Restart so the error stays accurate).
    pub fn set_cwd(&mut self, cwd: Option<PathBuf>) {
        if self.term.is_none() && self.spawn_error.is_none() {
            self.cwd = cwd;
        }
    }

    pub fn is_running(&self) -> bool {
        self.term.as_ref().is_some_and(Terminal::is_alive)
    }

    fn ensure(&mut self, rows: u16, cols: u16, notify: Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>) {
        if self.term.is_none() && self.spawn_error.is_none() {
            let (shell, args) = orress_term::default_shell();
            match Terminal::spawn(&shell, &args, self.cwd.as_deref(), rows, cols, notify) {
                Ok(t) => self.term = Some(t),
                Err(e) => self.spawn_error = Some(format!("Could not start {shell}: {e}")),
            }
        }
    }

    /// Restarts the shell (after it exits, after a failed start, or on demand).
    pub fn restart(&mut self) {
        self.term = None;
        self.spawn_error = None;
        self.scrollback = 0;
    }
}

/// One ANSI palette colour (0..16), approximating a dark theme's 16-colour set.
fn ansi16(i: u8) -> Color32 {
    const P: [(u8, u8, u8); 16] = [
        (30, 30, 30),
        (205, 80, 70),
        (120, 190, 110),
        (210, 180, 90),
        (90, 150, 230),
        (190, 130, 210),
        (90, 190, 200),
        (200, 200, 200),
        (110, 110, 110),
        (235, 110, 100),
        (150, 220, 140),
        (235, 210, 120),
        (120, 175, 245),
        (215, 160, 235),
        (120, 215, 225),
        (245, 245, 245),
    ];
    let (r, g, b) = P[(i & 15) as usize];
    Color32::from_rgb(r, g, b)
}

/// The xterm 256-colour cube and greyscale ramp (indices 16..256).
fn xterm256(i: u8) -> Color32 {
    if i < 16 {
        return ansi16(i);
    }
    if i >= 232 {
        let v = 8 + 10 * (i - 232) as u32;
        return Color32::from_gray(v as u8);
    }
    let i = i - 16;
    let levels = [0u8, 95, 135, 175, 215, 255];
    Color32::from_rgb(
        levels[(i / 36 % 6) as usize],
        levels[(i / 6 % 6) as usize],
        levels[(i % 6) as usize],
    )
}

fn to_color(c: vt100::Color, default: Color32) -> Color32 {
    match c {
        vt100::Color::Default => default,
        vt100::Color::Idx(i) => xterm256(i),
        vt100::Color::Rgb(r, g, b) => Color32::from_rgb(r, g, b),
    }
}

/// Draws the terminal panel.
pub fn terminal_panel(
    ui: &mut Ui,
    session: &mut TerminalSession,
    notify: Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>,
) {
    let font = FontId::monospace(13.0);
    let (char_w, row_h) = ui.fonts_mut(|f| (f.glyph_width(&font, 'M'), f.row_height(&font)));
    let rect = ui.available_rect_before_wrap();

    // Grid size from the available area.
    let cols = ((rect.width() / char_w).floor() as u16).clamp(8, 400);
    let rows = ((rect.height() / row_h).floor() as u16).clamp(2, 200);

    session.ensure(rows, cols, Arc::clone(&notify));
    let Some(term) = &mut session.term else {
        let error = session
            .spawn_error
            .clone()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "Could not start a shell.".into());
        ui.colored_label(ui.visuals().error_fg_color, error);
        if ui.button("Restart").clicked() {
            session.restart();
        }
        return;
    };
    term.resize(rows, cols);

    let id = ui.id().with("orress-terminal");
    let response = ui.interact(rect, id, Sense::click());
    if response.clicked() {
        response.request_focus();
    }
    let focused = response.has_focus();

    // Scrollback via the wheel.
    if ui.rect_contains_pointer(rect) {
        let dy = ui.input(|i| i.smooth_scroll_delta.y);
        if dy.abs() > 0.5 {
            let step = (dy / row_h).round() as i64;
            session.scrollback = (session.scrollback as i64 + step).max(0) as usize;
        }
    }

    // Draw the grid.
    let painter = ui.painter_at(rect);
    let text_color = ui.visuals().text_color();
    let bg = ui.visuals().extreme_bg_color;
    painter.rect_filled(rect, 0.0, bg);

    let mut cursor_pos = None;
    if let Ok(mut parser) = term.parser().lock() {
        parser.screen_mut().set_scrollback(session.scrollback);
        session.scrollback = parser.screen().scrollback();
        let screen = parser.screen();
        let (srows, scols) = screen.size();
        for r in 0..srows {
            let y = rect.top() + f32::from(r) * row_h;
            // Group runs of cells with the same colours into one galley.
            let mut c = 0u16;
            while c < scols {
                let Some(cell) = screen.cell(r, c) else {
                    c += 1;
                    continue;
                };
                if cell.is_wide_continuation() {
                    c += 1;
                    continue;
                }
                let (mut fg, mut bgc) = (
                    to_color(cell.fgcolor(), text_color),
                    to_color(cell.bgcolor(), bg),
                );
                if cell.inverse() {
                    std::mem::swap(&mut fg, &mut bgc);
                }
                let x = rect.left() + f32::from(c) * char_w;
                // Background.
                if bgc != bg {
                    let w = char_w * if cell.is_wide() { 2.0 } else { 1.0 };
                    painter.rect_filled(
                        Rect::from_min_size(Pos2::new(x, y), Vec2::new(w, row_h)),
                        0.0,
                        bgc,
                    );
                }
                let contents = cell.contents();
                if !contents.is_empty() {
                    let mut job = LayoutJob::default();
                    let mut fmt = TextFormat::simple(font.clone(), fg);
                    if cell.underline() {
                        fmt.underline = Stroke::new(1.0, fg);
                    }
                    job.append(contents, 0.0, fmt);
                    let galley = ui.fonts_mut(|f| f.layout_job(job));
                    painter.galley(Pos2::new(x, y), galley, fg);
                }
                c += if cell.is_wide() { 2 } else { 1 };
            }
        }
        if !screen.hide_cursor() && session.scrollback == 0 {
            let (cr, cc) = screen.cursor_position();
            cursor_pos = Some((cr, cc));
        }
    }

    if let Some((cr, cc)) = cursor_pos {
        let x = rect.left() + f32::from(cc) * char_w;
        let y = rect.top() + f32::from(cr) * row_h;
        let cursor_rect = Rect::from_min_size(Pos2::new(x, y), Vec2::new(char_w, row_h));
        let col = ui
            .visuals()
            .text_color()
            .gamma_multiply(if focused { 0.8 } else { 0.4 });
        painter.rect(
            cursor_rect,
            0.0,
            Color32::TRANSPARENT,
            Stroke::new(1.0, col),
            egui::StrokeKind::Inside,
        );
    }

    // Keyboard input.
    if focused {
        ui.memory_mut(|m| {
            m.set_focus_lock_filter(
                id,
                egui::EventFilter {
                    horizontal_arrows: true,
                    vertical_arrows: true,
                    tab: true,
                    escape: true,
                },
            );
        });
        let bytes = collect_input(ui);
        if !bytes.is_empty() {
            term.input(&bytes);
            session.scrollback = 0;
        }
    }

    if !term.is_alive() {
        let banner = Rect::from_min_size(rect.min, Vec2::new(rect.width(), row_h + 6.0));
        let builder = egui::UiBuilder::new()
            .max_rect(banner)
            .layout(egui::Layout::left_to_right(egui::Align::Center));
        ui.scope_builder(builder, |ui| {
            ui.colored_label(ui.visuals().weak_text_color(), "[shell exited]");
            if ui.small_button("Restart").clicked() {
                session.restart();
            }
        });
    }
}

/// Takes this frame's keyboard input out of egui and translates it into terminal bytes. The
/// events are *consumed*, so the app's global shortcuts (Ctrl+W, Ctrl+Q, Ctrl+D, …) do not also
/// fire while the shell has focus. Ctrl+Shift combinations and function keys are left for the app
/// (the command palette, F1, …), since a shell has no use for them.
fn collect_input(ui: &Ui) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    ui.input_mut(|i| {
        i.events.retain(|event| {
            match event {
                egui::Event::Text(t) => out.extend_from_slice(t.as_bytes()),
                egui::Event::Paste(t) => out.extend_from_slice(t.as_bytes()),
                // egui-winit turns Ctrl+C / Ctrl+X into Copy / Cut events (no Key event), so map
                // them back to the interrupt (ETX) and Ctrl+X (CAN) control codes.
                egui::Event::Copy => out.push(0x03),
                egui::Event::Cut => out.push(0x18),
                egui::Event::Key {
                    key,
                    pressed,
                    modifiers,
                    ..
                } => {
                    if leave_for_app(*key, modifiers) {
                        return true;
                    }
                    if *pressed {
                        push_key(&mut out, *key, modifiers);
                    }
                }
                _ => return true,
            }
            false
        });
    });
    out
}

/// Keys the terminal does not take: app shortcuts with Ctrl+Shift (or Cmd+Shift), and the
/// function keys, which the shell does not use but the app does (F1 = keybindings, …).
fn leave_for_app(key: egui::Key, modifiers: &egui::Modifiers) -> bool {
    use egui::Key::*;
    let ctrl = modifiers.ctrl || modifiers.command;
    (ctrl && modifiers.shift)
        || matches!(
            key,
            F1 | F2 | F3 | F4 | F5 | F6 | F7 | F8 | F9 | F10 | F11 | F12
        )
}

fn push_key(out: &mut Vec<u8>, key: egui::Key, modifiers: &egui::Modifiers) {
    use egui::Key::*;
    // Ctrl + letter -> control code.
    if (modifiers.ctrl || modifiers.command)
        && key.name().len() == 1
        && let Some(c) = key.name().chars().next()
        && c.is_ascii_alphabetic()
    {
        out.push((c.to_ascii_uppercase() as u8) & 0x1f);
        return;
    }
    match key {
        Enter => out.push(b'\r'),
        Backspace => out.push(0x7f),
        Tab => out.push(b'\t'),
        Escape => out.push(0x1b),
        ArrowUp => out.extend_from_slice(b"\x1b[A"),
        ArrowDown => out.extend_from_slice(b"\x1b[B"),
        ArrowRight => out.extend_from_slice(b"\x1b[C"),
        ArrowLeft => out.extend_from_slice(b"\x1b[D"),
        Home => out.extend_from_slice(b"\x1b[H"),
        End => out.extend_from_slice(b"\x1b[F"),
        Delete => out.extend_from_slice(b"\x1b[3~"),
        PageUp => out.extend_from_slice(b"\x1b[5~"),
        PageDown => out.extend_from_slice(b"\x1b[6~"),
        _ => {}
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-views/src/triage.rs`:

```rs
//! The Triage view: a one-screen static malware triage of the active binary — risk flags,
//! capabilities grouped by behaviour (with MITRE ATT&CK), extracted IOCs (defanged), and
//! hashes — assembled by `orress-triage` from the already-computed analysis. Read-only; a
//! "Copy report" button exports the whole thing as Markdown.

use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

use egui::{RichText, Ui};
use orress_project::DocStore;
use orress_triage::hints::{Challenge, HintLevel};
use orress_triage::{IocKind, Report, build};
use orress_ui::muted;

/// Caches the report + challenge hints per file (keyed by SHA-256) so the analysis runs once.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct TriageView {
    cache: Option<(String, Report, Challenge)>,
    /// VM-obfuscation findings, cached by SHA-256 (computed from the disassembled CFG, which is
    /// ready a little after the static report).
    vm: Option<(String, Vec<orress_vm::VmReport>)>,
    /// The concolically-recovered key per detected VM (index-aligned with `vm`), cached by SHA-256.
    /// The solve runs a sweep of symbolic executions, so it is computed once per file, never per
    /// frame.
    keys: Option<(String, Vec<Option<orress_vm::VmSolution>>)>,
    /// The VM scan + solve running on a worker thread, with the SHA-256 it is for.
    vm_job: Option<(String, VmSlot)>,
    /// How many graded hints the user has chosen to reveal.
    revealed: usize,
}

/// VM findings: the detected interpreters and the recovered key per interpreter.
type VmFindings = (Vec<orress_vm::VmReport>, Vec<Option<orress_vm::VmSolution>>);
type VmSlot = Arc<Mutex<Option<VmFindings>>>;

/// Scans for VM interpreters and solves each one on a worker thread (a sweep of symbolic
/// executions can take seconds, far too long for the UI thread).
fn spawn_vm_scan(program: Arc<orress_analysis::Program>, ctx: egui::Context) -> VmSlot {
    let slot: VmSlot = Arc::new(Mutex::new(None));
    let out = Arc::clone(&slot);
    let spawned = std::thread::Builder::new()
        .name("vm scan".into())
        .spawn(move || {
            let findings = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
                let reports = orress_vm::scan(&program);
                let keys = reports
                    .iter()
                    .map(|r| orress_vm::solve(&program, r))
                    .collect();
                (reports, keys)
            }))
            .unwrap_or_default();
            *out.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) = Some(findings);
            ctx.request_repaint();
        });
    if spawned.is_err() {
        *slot.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) = Some(Default::default());
    }
    slot
}

pub fn triage_view(ui: &mut Ui, view: &mut TriageView, docs: &DocStore) {
    orress_ui::spotlight::mark(ui.ctx(), "view.Triage", ui.max_rect());
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label(RichText::new("Triage").strong());
        ui.label(muted("static malware triage · IOCs · capabilities"));
    });
    ui.separator();

    let Some(doc) = docs.active() else {
        ui.label(muted("Open a binary to triage it."));
        return;
    };
    let Some(analysis) = doc.analysis() else {
        ui.label(muted("Analysis is still running…"));
        return;
    };
    let sha = analysis.info.hashes.sha256.clone();
    if view.cache.as_ref().map(|(k, _, _)| k) != Some(&sha) {
        let strings: Vec<&str> = analysis.strings.iter().map(|s| s.text.as_str()).collect();
        let data: &[u8] = doc.bytes().map(|b| b.as_slice()).unwrap_or(&[]);
        let report = build(&analysis.info, &strings, data);
        let challenge = orress_triage::hints::analyze(&report, &analysis.info, &strings);
        view.cache = Some((sha.clone(), report, challenge));
        view.revealed = 0;
    }
    // VM-based obfuscation runs on the disassembled CFG, which finishes a little after the static
    // report; recompute (in the background) when it or the file changes.
    let mut scanning = false;
    if view.vm.as_ref().map(|(k, _)| k.as_str()) != Some(sha.as_str())
        && let Some(program) = doc.program()
    {
        if view.vm_job.as_ref().map(|(k, _)| k.as_str()) != Some(sha.as_str()) {
            let slot = spawn_vm_scan(Arc::clone(program), ui.ctx().clone());
            view.vm_job = Some((sha.clone(), slot));
        }
        let done = view
            .vm_job
            .as_ref()
            .and_then(|(_, slot)| slot.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).take());
        match done {
            // One concolic solve per detected VM, cached alongside the reports (same SHA key).
            Some((reports, keys)) => {
                view.vm = Some((sha.clone(), reports));
                view.keys = Some((sha.clone(), keys));
                view.vm_job = None;
            }
            None => scanning = true,
        }
    }
    let vm: Vec<orress_vm::VmReport> = view
        .vm
        .as_ref()
        .filter(|(k, _)| *k == sha)
        .map(|(_, v)| v.clone())
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let keys: Vec<Option<orress_vm::VmSolution>> = view
        .keys
        .as_ref()
        .filter(|(k, _)| *k == sha)
        .map(|(_, v)| v.clone())
        .unwrap_or_default();

    let (_, report, challenge) = view.cache.as_ref().expect("report just built");

    if ui.button("📋 Copy report (Markdown)").clicked() {
        ui.ctx().copy_text(report_markdown(report, &vm, &keys));
    }
    ui.add_space(6.0);

    challenge_section(ui, challenge, &mut view.revealed);
    ui.add_space(6.0);
    if scanning {
        ui.horizontal(|ui| {
            ui.spinner();
            ui.label(muted("Scanning for VM-based obfuscation…"));
        });
    }
    let report = &view.cache.as_ref().unwrap().1;

    egui::ScrollArea::vertical()
        .auto_shrink([false, false])
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            if !vm.is_empty() {
                ui.heading("VM-based obfuscation");
                let program = doc.program();
                for (i, r) in vm.iter().enumerate() {
                    ui.colored_label(
                        ui.visuals().warn_fg_color,
                        format!(
                            "⚠ Likely VM interpreter at {:#x} — dispatcher {:#x}, {} handlers ({:.0}% confidence)",
                            r.entry, r.dispatcher, r.handlers, r.confidence * 100.0
                        ),
                    );
                    // The concolically-recovered key: devirtualization's payoff, solved against the
                    // real bytecode (self-verifying when "verified").
                    if let Some(Some(sol)) = keys.get(i) {
                        let status = if sol.complete { "verified" } else { "partial" };
                        ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                            if ui.small_button("copy").clicked() {
                                ui.ctx().copy_text(String::from_utf8_lossy(&sol.key).into_owned());
                            }
                            ui.colored_label(
                                ui.visuals().text_color(),
                                format!(
                                    "🔑 recovered key ({status}, {} constraints): {:?}",
                                    sol.constraints,
                                    String::from_utf8_lossy(&sol.key)
                                ),
                            );
                        });
                        // The lifted per-byte logic the virtualized check performs (devirtualized
                        // by execution, so it is exact — not a guess).
                        if !sol.checks.is_empty() {
                            egui::CollapsingHeader::new("lifted checks")
                                .id_salt(("vm-checks", r.entry))
                                .show(ui, |ui| {
                                    for c in &sol.checks {
                                        ui.label(RichText::new(c).monospace().size(11.0));
                                    }
                                });
                        }
                    }
                    // The recovered instruction set and bytecode (devirtualization skeleton).
                    if let Some(p) = program {
                        egui::CollapsingHeader::new("opcode table & bytecode")
                            .id_salt(("vm", r.entry))
                            .show(ui, |ui| vm_detail(ui, p, r));
                    }
                }
                ui.add_space(8.0);
            }
            if !report.flags.is_empty() {
                ui.heading("Risk flags");
                for f in &report.flags {
                    ui.colored_label(ui.visuals().warn_fg_color, format!("⚠ {f}"));
                }
                ui.add_space(8.0);
            }

            if !report.configs.is_empty() {
                ui.heading("Extracted configuration");
                for c in &report.configs {
                    ui.horizontal_wrapped(|ui| {
                        ui.label(RichText::new(&c.family).strong());
                        ui.label(muted(format!("({})", c.note)));
                    });
                    egui::Grid::new(format!("cfg-{}", c.family))
                        .num_columns(2)
                        .spacing([12.0, 2.0])
                        .show(ui, |ui| {
                            for f in &c.fields {
                                ui.label(muted(&f.key));
                                ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                                    if ui.small_button("copy").clicked() {
                                        ui.ctx().copy_text(f.value.clone());
                                    }
                                    ui.label(RichText::new(&f.value).monospace());
                                });
                                ui.end_row();
                            }
                        });
                    ui.add_space(4.0);
                }
                ui.add_space(8.0);
            }

            ui.heading("Capabilities");
            if report.capabilities.is_empty() {
                ui.label(muted("No higher-level capabilities detected."));
            }
            for c in &report.capabilities {
                ui.horizontal_wrapped(|ui| {
                    ui.label(RichText::new(format!("• {}", c.name)).strong());
                    ui.label(muted(format!("({})", c.namespace)));
                    if !c.attack.is_empty() {
                        ui.label(muted(format!("[{}]", c.attack)));
                    }
                });
                ui.label(RichText::new(c.evidence.join(", ")).monospace().weak().size(11.0));
                ui.add_space(3.0);
            }
            ui.add_space(8.0);

            ui.heading("Imports by behaviour");
            if report.behaviors.is_empty() {
                ui.label(muted("No recognised library functions imported."));
            }
            for b in &report.behaviors {
                let title = if b.suspicious {
                    RichText::new(format!("⚠ {}", b.category.name())).strong()
                } else {
                    RichText::new(b.category.name()).strong()
                };
                ui.horizontal_wrapped(|ui| {
                    ui.label(title);
                    if !b.attack.is_empty() {
                        ui.label(muted(format!("[{}]", b.attack)));
                    }
                });
                ui.label(RichText::new(b.apis.join(", ")).monospace().weak());
                ui.add_space(4.0);
            }
            ui.add_space(8.0);

            ui.heading("Indicators (defanged)");
            if report.iocs.is_empty() {
                ui.label(muted("No IOCs found in strings."));
            }
            let mut current: Option<IocKind> = None;
            for i in &report.iocs {
                if current != Some(i.kind) {
                    ui.label(RichText::new(i.kind.label()).strong());
                    current = Some(i.kind);
                }
                ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                    let defanged = orress_triage::ioc::defang(&i.value);
                    if ui.small_button("copy").on_hover_text(&i.value).clicked() {
                        ui.ctx().copy_text(i.value.clone());
                    }
                    ui.label(RichText::new(defanged).monospace());
                });
            }
            ui.add_space(8.0);

            ui.heading("Hashes");
            let h = &analysis.info.hashes;
            egui::Grid::new("triage-hashes")
                .num_columns(2)
                .spacing([12.0, 2.0])
                .show(ui, |ui| {
                    for (label, value) in [
                        ("MD5", h.md5.as_str()),
                        ("SHA-1", h.sha1.as_str()),
                        ("SHA-256", h.sha256.as_str()),
                        ("Imphash", h.imphash.as_deref().unwrap_or("—")),
                        ("TLSH", report.fuzzy.tlsh.as_deref().unwrap_or("—")),
                        ("ssdeep", report.fuzzy.ssdeep.as_str()),
                    ] {
                        ui.label(muted(label));
                        ui.label(RichText::new(value).monospace());
                        ui.end_row();
                    }
                });
        });
}

/// Renders a detected VM's recovered opcode table and bytecode disassembly — the first stage of
/// devirtualization: the virtual instruction set and the virtual program the interpreter runs.
fn vm_detail(ui: &mut Ui, program: &orress_analysis::Program, report: &orress_vm::VmReport) {
    let dis = orress_vm::disassemble(program, report);
    if let Some(bc) = orress_vm::bytecode(program, report) {
        let prog_len = dis
            .as_ref()
            .and_then(|d| d.last())
            .map(|i| i.offset + 1 + i.operands.len());
        match prog_len.or(bc.len.map(|l| l as usize)) {
            Some(len) => ui.label(muted(format!("bytecode: {len} bytes at {:#x}", bc.base))),
            None => ui.label(muted(format!("bytecode at {:#x}", bc.base))),
        };
    }
    ui.label(RichText::new("opcode table").strong());
    for h in orress_vm::handlers(program, report) {
        ui.label(
            RichText::new(format!(
                "op {:>3}: {:<13} {:#x}  [{}]",
                h.opcode,
                orress_vm::operation(&h),
                h.address,
                h.ops.join(", ")
            ))
            .monospace()
            .size(11.0),
        );
    }
    if let Some(dis) = &dis {
        ui.add_space(4.0);
        ui.label(RichText::new("bytecode disassembly").strong());
        for ins in dis {
            let operands: Vec<String> = ins.operands.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:#04x}")).collect();
            ui.label(
                RichText::new(format!(
                    "{:04x}: op{:<3} {:<13} {}",
                    ins.offset,
                    ins.opcode,
                    ins.op,
                    operands.join(", ")
                ))
                .monospace()
                .size(11.0),
            );
        }
    }
}

/// The report's Markdown, with a VM-obfuscation section appended when any was detected (so the
/// exported report includes it too).
fn report_markdown(
    report: &Report,
    vm: &[orress_vm::VmReport],
    keys: &[Option<orress_vm::VmSolution>],
) -> String {
    let mut md = report.markdown.clone();
    if !vm.is_empty() {
        md.push_str("\n## VM-based obfuscation\n\n");
        for (i, r) in vm.iter().enumerate() {
            md.push_str(&format!(
                "- Likely VM interpreter at `{:#x}` — dispatcher `{:#x}`, {} handlers / {} blocks, {:.0}% confidence\n",
                r.entry, r.dispatcher, r.handlers, r.blocks, r.confidence * 100.0
            ));
            if let Some(Some(sol)) = keys.get(i) {
                let status = if sol.complete { "verified" } else { "partial" };
                md.push_str(&format!(
                    "  - Recovered key ({status}): `{}`\n",
                    String::from_utf8_lossy(&sol.key)
                ));
                for c in &sol.checks {
                    md.push_str(&format!("    - `{c}`\n"));
                }
            }
        }
    }
    md
}

/// The CTF/crackme hint panel: a classification, suggested techniques, and graded hints the user
/// reveals one at a time (so the answer isn't spoiled up front).
fn challenge_section(ui: &mut Ui, c: &Challenge, revealed: &mut usize) {
    ui.heading("Challenge hints");
    ui.label(RichText::new(&c.summary).strong());
    if !c.techniques.is_empty() {
        ui.label(muted(format!("Try: {}", c.techniques.join(", "))));
    }
    ui.add_space(4.0);

    let shown = (*revealed).min(c.hints.len());
    for h in &c.hints[..shown] {
        let color = match h.level {
            HintLevel::Nudge => ui.visuals().weak_text_color(),
            HintLevel::Direction => ui.visuals().text_color(),
            HintLevel::Solution => ui.visuals().warn_fg_color,
        };
        ui.horizontal_wrapped(|ui| {
            ui.label(
                RichText::new(format!("[{}]", h.level.label()))
                    .strong()
                    .color(color),
            );
            ui.label(RichText::new(&h.text).color(color));
        });
        ui.add_space(2.0);
    }

    if shown < c.hints.len() {
        let label = format!("💡 Reveal hint ({}/{})", shown + 1, c.hints.len());
        if ui
            .button(label)
            .on_hover_text("Graded: each hint gives a little more away")
            .clicked()
        {
            *revealed = shown + 1;
        }
    } else if !c.hints.is_empty() {
        ui.label(muted("All hints shown."));
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-views/src/typepick.rs`:

```rs
//! A small type-reference picker shared by the Types view and the decompiler's "set
//! prototype" editor: a base type (a primitive or a named user type) with an optional single
//! pointer. One pointer level is enough for the form; deeper nesting is out of scope.

use egui::{ComboBox, Ui};
use orress_project::types::{Prim, TypeRef};

/// A base type the dropdown can select: a primitive or another user type by name.
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum Base {
    Prim(Prim),
    Named(String),
}

/// Builds a [`TypeRef`] from a base and whether it is behind a pointer.
pub(crate) fn to_typeref(base: &Base, pointer: bool) -> TypeRef {
    let inner = match base {
        Base::Prim(p) => TypeRef::Prim(*p),
        Base::Named(n) => TypeRef::Named(n.clone()),
    };
    if pointer {
        TypeRef::Pointer(Box::new(inner))
    } else {
        inner
    }
}

/// Splits a type reference into its base and whether it is behind a pointer. A nested pointer
/// collapses to its innermost base (the one-level form).
pub(crate) fn from_typeref(ty: &TypeRef) -> (Base, bool) {
    match ty {
        TypeRef::Prim(p) => (Base::Prim(*p), false),
        TypeRef::Named(n) => (Base::Named(n.clone()), false),
        TypeRef::Pointer(inner) => match inner.as_ref() {
            TypeRef::Prim(p) => (Base::Prim(*p), true),
            TypeRef::Named(n) => (Base::Named(n.clone()), true),
            TypeRef::Pointer(_) => {
                let (b, _) = from_typeref(inner);
                (b, true)
            }
        },
    }
}

/// A dropdown over every primitive and every named type. `salt` disambiguates rows.
pub(crate) fn base_combo(ui: &mut Ui, salt: usize, base: &mut Base, names: &[String]) {
    let text = match base {
        Base::Prim(p) => p.label().to_owned(),
        Base::Named(n) => n.clone(),
    };
    ComboBox::from_id_salt(("base_combo", salt))
        .selected_text(text)
        .width(130.0)
        .show_ui(ui, |ui| {
            for p in Prim::ALL {
                ui.selectable_value(base, Base::Prim(p), p.label());
            }
            if !names.is_empty() {
                ui.separator();
                for n in names {
                    ui.selectable_value(base, Base::Named(n.clone()), n);
                }
            }
        });
}
```

`crates/orress-views/src/types.rs`:

```rs
//! The Types panel: declare `struct`/`union`/`enum`/`typedef` with a form builder and see
//! their memory layout. Types are per-binary and persist with the rest of your work
//! (names, comments) via [`orress_project::Annotations`]; applying a type to data happens
//! in the hex/inspector views. The layout maths lives in `orress_project::types`.

use egui::{ComboBox, RichText, Ui};
use orress_project::types::{FieldDef, Prim, TypeRef, UserType};
use orress_project::{DocStore, TypeCatalog};
use orress_ui::muted;

use crate::typepick::{Base, base_combo, from_typeref, to_typeref};

#[derive(Clone)]
struct FieldDraft {
    name: String,
    base: Base,
    pointer: bool,
    count: String,
}

impl FieldDraft {
    fn blank() -> Self {
        Self {
            name: String::new(),
            base: Base::Prim(Prim::U32),
            pointer: false,
            count: "1".into(),
        }
    }

    fn from_def(f: &FieldDef) -> Self {
        let (base, pointer) = from_typeref(&f.ty);
        Self {
            name: f.name.clone(),
            base,
            pointer,
            count: f.count.max(1).to_string(),
        }
    }

    fn to_def(&self) -> FieldDef {
        FieldDef {
            name: self.name.trim().to_owned(),
            ty: to_typeref(&self.base, self.pointer),
            count: self.count.trim().parse().unwrap_or(1).max(1),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Kind {
    Struct,
    Union,
    Enum,
    Typedef,
}

/// The type currently being edited, as editable buffers.
#[derive(Clone)]
struct Draft {
    /// The name the draft was loaded from, so a rename replaces the old entry. Empty for
    /// a new type.
    orig: String,
    kind: Kind,
    name: String,
    fields: Vec<FieldDraft>,
    variants: Vec<(String, String)>,
    enum_width: Prim,
    typedef_base: Base,
    typedef_pointer: bool,
}

impl Draft {
    fn new(kind: Kind) -> Self {
        Self {
            orig: String::new(),
            kind,
            name: String::new(),
            fields: vec![FieldDraft::blank()],
            variants: vec![(String::new(), "0".into())],
            enum_width: Prim::U32,
            typedef_base: Base::Prim(Prim::U32),
            typedef_pointer: false,
        }
    }

    fn from_type(ty: &UserType) -> Self {
        let mut d = Self::new(Kind::Struct);
        d.orig = ty.name().to_owned();
        d.name = ty.name().to_owned();
        match ty {
            UserType::Struct { fields, .. } => {
                d.kind = Kind::Struct;
                d.fields = fields.iter().map(FieldDraft::from_def).collect();
            }
            UserType::Union { fields, .. } => {
                d.kind = Kind::Union;
                d.fields = fields.iter().map(FieldDraft::from_def).collect();
            }
            UserType::Enum {
                width, variants, ..
            } => {
                d.kind = Kind::Enum;
                d.enum_width = *width;
                d.variants = variants
                    .iter()
                    .map(|(n, v)| (n.clone(), v.to_string()))
                    .collect();
            }
            UserType::Typedef { target, .. } => {
                d.kind = Kind::Typedef;
                let (b, p) = from_typeref(target);
                d.typedef_base = b;
                d.typedef_pointer = p;
            }
        }
        d
    }

    fn to_type(&self) -> UserType {
        let name = self.name.trim().to_owned();
        match self.kind {
            Kind::Struct => UserType::Struct {
                name,
                fields: self.fields.iter().map(FieldDraft::to_def).collect(),
            },
            Kind::Union => UserType::Union {
                name,
                fields: self.fields.iter().map(FieldDraft::to_def).collect(),
            },
            Kind::Enum => UserType::Enum {
                name,
                width: self.enum_width,
                variants: self
                    .variants
                    .iter()
                    .map(|(n, v)| (n.trim().to_owned(), v.trim().parse().unwrap_or(0)))
                    .collect(),
            },
            Kind::Typedef => UserType::Typedef {
                name,
                target: to_typeref(&self.typedef_base, self.typedef_pointer),
            },
        }
    }
}

/// Persistent UI state for the Types tab.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct TypesView {
    draft: Option<Draft>,
    error: Option<String>,
    status: Option<String>,
}

pub fn types_view(ui: &mut Ui, view: &mut TypesView, docs: &mut DocStore) {
    orress_ui::spotlight::mark(ui.ctx(), "view.Types", ui.max_rect());

    let Some(doc) = docs.active_mut() else {
        ui.heading("Types");
        ui.label(muted(
            "Open a binary to declare structs, unions, enums and typedefs, then apply them to data.",
        ));
        return;
    };

    let catalog = doc.type_catalog();
    let names: Vec<String> = catalog.types.keys().cloned().collect();

    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label(RichText::new("Types").strong());
        ui.label(muted(format!(
            "{} defined · saved with this binary",
            names.len()
        )));
    });
    ui.separator();

    ui.horizontal_top(|ui| {
        ui.vertical(|ui| {
            ui.set_width(200.0);
            ui.horizontal_wrapped(|ui| {
                if ui.button("+ Struct").clicked() {
                    view.draft = Some(Draft::new(Kind::Struct));
                    view.error = None;
                }
                if ui.button("+ Union").clicked() {
                    view.draft = Some(Draft::new(Kind::Union));
                    view.error = None;
                }
                if ui.button("+ Enum").clicked() {
                    view.draft = Some(Draft::new(Kind::Enum));
                    view.error = None;
                }
                if ui.button("+ Typedef").clicked() {
                    view.draft = Some(Draft::new(Kind::Typedef));
                    view.error = None;
                }
            });
            ui.separator();
            egui::ScrollArea::vertical().show(ui, |ui| {
                for name in &names {
                    let ty = &catalog.types[name];
                    let selected = view.draft.as_ref().is_some_and(|d| &d.orig == name);
                    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                        if ui
                            .selectable_label(selected, format!("{} {name}", ty.kind_label()))
                            .clicked()
                        {
                            view.draft = Some(Draft::from_type(ty));
                            view.error = None;
                            view.status = None;
                        }
                        if ui.small_button("🗑").on_hover_text("Delete type").clicked() {
                            doc.remove_type(name);
                            if selected {
                                view.draft = None;
                            }
                            view.status = Some(format!("Deleted {name}"));
                        }
                    });
                }
                if names.is_empty() {
                    ui.label(muted("No types yet. Start with + Struct."));
                }
            });
        });

        ui.separator();

        ui.vertical(|ui| {
            let Some(draft) = view.draft.as_mut() else {
                ui.label(muted("Select a type on the left, or create one."));
                return;
            };
            let save = editor(
                ui,
                draft,
                &names,
                view.error.as_deref(),
                view.status.as_deref(),
                &catalog,
            );
            if save {
                match commit(doc, draft) {
                    Ok(_) => {
                        view.error = None;
                        view.status = Some(format!("Saved {}", draft.name.trim()));
                        draft.orig = draft.name.trim().to_owned();
                    }
                    Err(e) => view.error = Some(e),
                }
            }
        });
    });
}

/// Draws the editor form for one draft, returning whether Save was clicked.
fn editor(
    ui: &mut Ui,
    draft: &mut Draft,
    names: &[String],
    error: Option<&str>,
    status: Option<&str>,
    catalog: &TypeCatalog,
) -> bool {
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label("Name");
        ui.text_edit_singleline(&mut draft.name);
        ui.label(muted(kind_word(draft.kind)));
    });
    ui.separator();

    match draft.kind {
        Kind::Struct | Kind::Union => fields_editor(ui, draft, names),
        Kind::Enum => enum_editor(ui, draft),
        Kind::Typedef => typedef_editor(ui, draft, names),
    }

    ui.separator();
    let save = ui.button("Save").clicked();
    if let Some(e) = error {
        ui.colored_label(ui.visuals().error_fg_color, e);
    } else if let Some(s) = status {
        ui.label(muted(s));
    }

    // Live layout preview.
    ui.add_space(6.0);
    ui.label(RichText::new("Layout").strong());
    let ty = draft.to_type();
    let mut probe = catalog.clone();
    probe.types.insert(ty.name().to_owned(), ty.clone());
    match probe.layout(&ty) {
        Some(fields) if !fields.is_empty() => {
            egui::Grid::new("types_layout")
                .num_columns(4)
                .spacing([14.0, 2.0])
                .show(ui, |ui| {
                    ui.label(muted("offset"));
                    ui.label(muted("name"));
                    ui.label(muted("type"));
                    ui.label(muted("size"));
                    ui.end_row();
                    for f in &fields {
                        ui.label(RichText::new(format!("+0x{:X}", f.offset)).monospace());
                        ui.label(&f.path);
                        let arr = if f.count > 1 {
                            format!("{}[{}]", f.ty.label(), f.count)
                        } else {
                            f.ty.label()
                        };
                        ui.label(RichText::new(arr).monospace());
                        ui.label(RichText::new(format!("0x{:X}", f.size)).monospace());
                        ui.end_row();
                    }
                });
            if let Some(total) = probe.size_of(&TypeRef::Named(ty.name().to_owned())) {
                ui.label(muted(format!("total size 0x{total:X} ({total} bytes)")));
            }
        }
        Some(_) => {
            if let Some(total) = probe.size_of(&TypeRef::Named(ty.name().to_owned())) {
                ui.label(muted(format!("size 0x{total:X} ({total} bytes)")));
            }
        }
        None => {
            ui.label(muted(
                "layout unavailable (unknown or self-referential member)",
            ));
        }
    }
    save
}

fn fields_editor(ui: &mut Ui, draft: &mut Draft, names: &[String]) {
    let mut remove = None;
    egui::Grid::new("types_fields")
        .num_columns(5)
        .spacing([8.0, 4.0])
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            ui.label(muted("name"));
            ui.label(muted("type"));
            ui.label(muted("ptr"));
            ui.label(muted("count"));
            ui.label("");
            ui.end_row();
            for (i, f) in draft.fields.iter_mut().enumerate() {
                ui.add(egui::TextEdit::singleline(&mut f.name).desired_width(120.0));
                base_combo(ui, i, &mut f.base, names);
                ui.checkbox(&mut f.pointer, "");
                ui.add(egui::TextEdit::singleline(&mut f.count).desired_width(48.0));
                if ui.small_button("✕").clicked() {
                    remove = Some(i);
                }
                ui.end_row();
            }
        });
    if let Some(i) = remove
        && draft.fields.len() > 1
    {
        draft.fields.remove(i);
    }
    if ui.button("+ Add field").clicked() {
        draft.fields.push(FieldDraft::blank());
    }
}

fn enum_editor(ui: &mut Ui, draft: &mut Draft) {
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label("Underlying");
        ComboBox::from_id_salt("enum_width")
            .selected_text(draft.enum_width.label())
            .show_ui(ui, |ui| {
                for p in [
                    Prim::U8,
                    Prim::I8,
                    Prim::U16,
                    Prim::I16,
                    Prim::U32,
                    Prim::I32,
                    Prim::U64,
                    Prim::I64,
                ] {
                    ui.selectable_value(&mut draft.enum_width, p, p.label());
                }
            });
    });
    let mut remove = None;
    egui::Grid::new("types_variants")
        .num_columns(3)
        .spacing([8.0, 4.0])
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            ui.label(muted("name"));
            ui.label(muted("value"));
            ui.label("");
            ui.end_row();
            for (i, (name, value)) in draft.variants.iter_mut().enumerate() {
                ui.add(egui::TextEdit::singleline(name).desired_width(140.0));
                ui.add(egui::TextEdit::singleline(value).desired_width(80.0));
                if ui.small_button("✕").clicked() {
                    remove = Some(i);
                }
                ui.end_row();
            }
        });
    if let Some(i) = remove
        && draft.variants.len() > 1
    {
        draft.variants.remove(i);
    }
    if ui.button("+ Add variant").clicked() {
        draft.variants.push((String::new(), "0".into()));
    }
}

fn typedef_editor(ui: &mut Ui, draft: &mut Draft, names: &[String]) {
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label("Alias for");
        base_combo(ui, usize::MAX, &mut draft.typedef_base, names);
        ui.checkbox(&mut draft.typedef_pointer, "pointer");
    });
}

fn kind_word(kind: Kind) -> &'static str {
    match kind {
        Kind::Struct => "struct",
        Kind::Union => "union",
        Kind::Enum => "enum",
        Kind::Typedef => "typedef",
    }
}

/// Validates and writes the draft to the document, handling a rename (removing the old
/// name). Returns the previous name if it changed.
fn commit(doc: &mut orress_project::Document, draft: &Draft) -> Result<Option<String>, String> {
    let ty = draft.to_type();
    doc.define_type(ty)?;
    let renamed =
        (!draft.orig.is_empty() && draft.orig != draft.name.trim()).then(|| draft.orig.clone());
    if let Some(old) = &renamed {
        doc.remove_type(old);
    }
    Ok(renamed)
}
```

`crates/orress-views/src/wasm.rs`:

```rs
//! The WebAssembly view: a structured overview of an open `.wasm` module (imports, exports,
//! functions with signatures, memories, globals) and its WAT disassembly, powered by the
//! pure-Rust `orress-wasm` loader. Parsing is cached per file so switching panels is instant.

use std::path::PathBuf;

use egui::{RichText, Ui};
use orress_project::DocStore;
use orress_ui::muted;
use orress_wasm::{WasmModule, is_wasm};

/// WAT larger than this is truncated in the display (the file can still be huge; the panel stays
/// responsive). Typical CTF/malware wasm is far smaller.
const MAX_WAT_SHOWN: usize = 800_000;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Panel {
    Overview,
    Disassembly,
}

/// Persistent UI state for the WASM tab.
pub struct WasmView {
    /// (path, byte length) of the parsed file, so we re-parse when the file changes.
    key: Option<(PathBuf, usize, u64)>,
    module: Option<WasmModule>,
    wat: Option<Result<String, String>>,
    panel: Panel,
}

impl Default for WasmView {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            key: None,
            module: None,
            wat: None,
            panel: Panel::Overview,
        }
    }
}

pub fn wasm_view(ui: &mut Ui, view: &mut WasmView, docs: &DocStore) {
    orress_ui::spotlight::mark(ui.ctx(), "view.Wasm", ui.max_rect());
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label(RichText::new("WebAssembly").strong());
        ui.label(muted(
            "module overview · WAT disassembly (pure-Rust wasm-tools)",
        ));
    });
    ui.separator();

    let Some(doc) = docs.active() else {
        ui.label(muted("Open a .wasm file to inspect it."));
        return;
    };
    let Some(bytes) = doc.bytes() else {
        ui.label(muted("Reading the file…"));
        return;
    };
    if !is_wasm(bytes) {
        ui.label(muted(format!(
            "{} is not a WebAssembly module (it does not start with the \\0asm magic).",
            doc.file_name()
        )));
        return;
    }

    // (Re)parse when the active file changes.
    let key = (doc.path.clone(), bytes.len(), doc.generation);
    if view.key.as_ref() != Some(&key) {
        view.module = Some(orress_wasm::parse(bytes));
        view.wat = Some(orress_wasm::disassemble(bytes));
        view.key = Some(key);
    }
    let Some(module) = &view.module else { return };

    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.selectable_value(&mut view.panel, Panel::Overview, "Overview");
        ui.selectable_value(&mut view.panel, Panel::Disassembly, "Disassembly (WAT)");
        ui.separator();
        ui.label(muted(format!("wasm v{}", module.version)));
    });
    if module.is_component {
        ui.colored_label(
            ui.visuals().warn_fg_color,
            "This is a WebAssembly component, not a core module — the overview may be incomplete.",
        );
    }
    if let Some(e) = &module.parse_error {
        ui.colored_label(
            ui.visuals().warn_fg_color,
            format!("Parsing stopped early: {e} (showing what was read)"),
        );
    }
    ui.add_space(4.0);

    match view.panel {
        Panel::Overview => overview(ui, module),
        Panel::Disassembly => disassembly(ui, view.wat.as_ref()),
    }
}

fn overview(ui: &mut Ui, m: &WasmModule) {
    ui.label(RichText::new(m.summary()).strong());
    if let Some(s) = m.start_func {
        ui.label(muted(format!("start function: {s}")));
    }
    ui.add_space(6.0);

    egui::ScrollArea::vertical()
        .auto_shrink([false, false])
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            // Imports
            if !m.imports.is_empty() {
                section(ui, &format!("Imports ({})", m.imports.len()));
                for imp in &m.imports {
                    let sig = match &imp.kind {
                        orress_wasm::ImportKind::Func(ti) => {
                            m.types.get(*ti as usize).map(|t| t.signature())
                        }
                        _ => None,
                    };
                    let line = match sig {
                        Some(s) => {
                            format!("  {} · {}.{}  {s}", imp.kind.label(), imp.module, imp.name)
                        }
                        None => format!("  {} · {}.{}", imp.kind.label(), imp.module, imp.name),
                    };
                    ui.label(RichText::new(line).monospace());
                }
                ui.add_space(6.0);
            }

            // Exports
            if !m.exports.is_empty() {
                section(ui, &format!("Exports ({})", m.exports.len()));
                for e in &m.exports {
                    ui.label(
                        RichText::new(format!("  {} · {} [{}]", e.kind, e.name, e.index))
                            .monospace(),
                    );
                }
                ui.add_space(6.0);
            }

            // Functions
            if !m.functions.is_empty() {
                section(ui, &format!("Defined functions ({})", m.functions.len()));
                egui::Grid::new("wasm-funcs")
                    .striped(true)
                    .num_columns(5)
                    .spacing([14.0, 3.0])
                    .show(ui, |ui| {
                        for h in ["#", "name", "signature", "locals/ops", "bytes"] {
                            ui.label(RichText::new(h).strong());
                        }
                        ui.end_row();
                        for f in &m.functions {
                            ui.label(RichText::new(f.index.to_string()).monospace());
                            ui.label(
                                RichText::new(f.name.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| "—".into()))
                                    .monospace(),
                            );
                            ui.label(
                                RichText::new(
                                    f.sig.as_ref().map(|s| s.signature()).unwrap_or_default(),
                                )
                                .monospace()
                                .weak(),
                            );
                            ui.label(
                                RichText::new(format!("{} / {}", f.locals, f.ops)).monospace(),
                            );
                            ui.label(RichText::new(f.size.to_string()).monospace());
                            ui.end_row();
                        }
                    });
                ui.add_space(6.0);
            }

            // Memories & globals
            if !m.memories.is_empty() {
                section(ui, &format!("Memories ({})", m.memories.len()));
                for mem in &m.memories {
                    let max = mem
                        .max_pages
                        .map(|x| x.to_string())
                        .unwrap_or_else(|| "∞".into());
                    let flags = [
                        mem.memory64.then_some("memory64"),
                        mem.shared.then_some("shared"),
                    ]
                    .into_iter()
                    .flatten()
                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                    .join(", ");
                    let suffix = if flags.is_empty() {
                        String::new()
                    } else {
                        format!("  ({flags})")
                    };
                    ui.label(
                        RichText::new(format!(
                            "  {} … {} pages (×64 KiB){suffix}",
                            mem.min_pages, max
                        ))
                        .monospace(),
                    );
                }
                ui.add_space(6.0);
            }
            if !m.globals.is_empty() {
                section(ui, &format!("Globals ({})", m.globals.len()));
                for (i, g) in m.globals.iter().enumerate() {
                    let mu = if g.mutable { "mut " } else { "" };
                    ui.label(RichText::new(format!("  [{i}] {mu}{}", g.ty)).monospace());
                }
                ui.add_space(6.0);
            }

            // Misc
            let mut misc = Vec::new();
            if m.table_count > 0 {
                misc.push(format!("{} table(s)", m.table_count));
            }
            if m.data_segments > 0 {
                misc.push(format!("{} data segment(s)", m.data_segments));
            }
            if !misc.is_empty() {
                ui.label(muted(misc.join(" · ")));
            }
            if !m.custom_sections.is_empty() {
                section(ui, "Custom sections");
                for (name, len) in &m.custom_sections {
                    ui.label(
                        RichText::new(format!("  {name} ({len} bytes)"))
                            .monospace()
                            .weak(),
                    );
                }
            }
        });
}

fn disassembly(ui: &mut Ui, wat: Option<&Result<String, String>>) {
    match wat {
        None => {
            ui.label(muted("No disassembly."));
        }
        Some(Err(e)) => {
            ui.colored_label(
                ui.visuals().error_fg_color,
                format!("Could not disassemble: {e}"),
            );
        }
        Some(Ok(text)) => {
            let shown = if text.len() > MAX_WAT_SHOWN {
                ui.label(muted(format!(
                    "WAT is {} bytes; showing the first {}.",
                    text.len(),
                    MAX_WAT_SHOWN
                )));
                &text[..crate::code::floor_char_boundary(text, MAX_WAT_SHOWN)]
            } else {
                text.as_str()
            };
            egui::ScrollArea::both()
                .auto_shrink([false, false])
                .show(ui, |ui| {
                    // A read-only, selectable code view (copy with Ctrl+C).
                    let mut buf = shown;
                    ui.add(
                        egui::TextEdit::multiline(&mut buf)
                            .code_editor()
                            .desired_width(f32::INFINITY),
                    );
                });
        }
    }
}

fn section(ui: &mut Ui, title: &str) {
    ui.label(RichText::new(title).strong().underline());
}
```
