`crates/orress-views/src/workbench.rs`:

```rs
//! The Workbench: decode, decrypt and decompress data with a chain of operations
//! (a recipe), with "Magic" to find the chain automatically.

use egui::{RichText, Ui};
use orress_project::DocStore;
use orress_transforms::{ParamKind, Recipe, Step, Suggestion};
use orress_ui::{ExplainExt as _, muted};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
enum Mode {
    #[default]
    Text,
    Hex,
}

/// Output (or error) of every step of a recipe.
type StepOutputs = Vec<Result<Vec<u8>, String>>;

pub struct Workbench {
    input: Vec<u8>,
    input_text: String,
    input_mode: Mode,
    output_mode: Mode,
    /// Where the input came from, e.g. "crackme01.exe 0x1200..0x1240".
    source: Option<(std::path::PathBuf, u64, u64)>,
    pub recipe: Recipe,
    recipe_text: String,
    recipe_error: Option<String>,
    filter: String,
    magic: Option<Vec<Suggestion>>,
    cache: Option<(String, StepOutputs)>,
    message: Option<String>,
}

impl Default for Workbench {
    fn default() -> Self {
        let mut wb = Self {
            input: Vec::new(),
            input_text: "ZmxhZ3t3ZWxjb21lX3RvX3RoZV93b3JrYmVuY2h9".into(),
            input_mode: Mode::Text,
            output_mode: Mode::Text,
            source: None,
            recipe: Recipe(vec![Step::new("from_base64")]),
            recipe_text: String::new(),
            recipe_error: None,
            filter: String::new(),
            magic: None,
            cache: None,
            message: None,
        };
        wb.input = wb.input_text.clone().into_bytes();
        wb.recipe_text = wb.recipe.to_string();
        wb
    }
}

impl Workbench {
    /// Loads bytes from a file region (from the hex view's selection).
    pub fn set_input(&mut self, bytes: Vec<u8>, source: Option<(std::path::PathBuf, u64, u64)>) {
        self.input_mode = if bytes
            .iter()
            .all(|b| b.is_ascii_graphic() || b.is_ascii_whitespace())
        {
            Mode::Text
        } else {
            Mode::Hex
        };
        self.input_text = render(&bytes, self.input_mode);
        self.input = bytes;
        self.source = source;
        self.magic = None;
    }

    fn outputs(&mut self) -> &[Result<Vec<u8>, String>] {
        let key = format!("{}\u{0}{}", self.recipe_with_flags(), fnv(&self.input));
        if self.cache.as_ref().is_none_or(|(k, _)| *k != key) {
            let outputs = self.recipe.run(&self.input);
            self.cache = Some((key, outputs));
        }
        &self.cache.as_ref().expect("just set").1
    }

    fn recipe_with_flags(&self) -> String {
        let flags: String = self
            .recipe
            .0
            .iter()
            .map(|s| if s.enabled { '1' } else { '0' })
            .collect();
        format!("{}#{flags}", self.recipe)
    }

    fn final_output(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
        let input = self.input.clone();
        match self.outputs().last() {
            Some(r) => r.clone(),
            None => Ok(input),
        }
    }

    fn sync_text(&mut self) {
        self.recipe_text = self.recipe.to_string();
        self.recipe_error = None;
    }
}

fn fnv(data: &[u8]) -> u64 {
    data.iter().fold(0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325u64, |h, &b| {
        (h ^ u64::from(b)).wrapping_mul(0x100_0000_01b3)
    })
}

fn render(bytes: &[u8], mode: Mode) -> String {
    match mode {
        Mode::Text => String::from_utf8_lossy(bytes).into_owned(),
        Mode::Hex => bytes
            .chunks(16)
            .map(|row| {
                row.iter()
                    .map(|b| format!("{b:02x}"))
                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                    .join(" ")
            })
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join("\n"),
    }
}

fn parse_input(text: &str, mode: Mode) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    match mode {
        Mode::Text => Ok(text.as_bytes().to_vec()),
        Mode::Hex => orress_transforms::parse_key(&format!("hex:{text}")),
    }
}

pub fn workbench(ui: &mut Ui, wb: &mut Workbench, docs: &mut DocStore) {
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.heading("Workbench");
        ui.label(muted(
            "Chain operations to decode, decrypt or decompress data. Each step works on the \
             previous step's output. Not sure where to start? Press Magic.",
        ));
    });
    ui.separator();
    ui.columns(3, |cols| {
        operations(&mut cols[0], wb);
        recipe(&mut cols[1], wb);
        data(&mut cols[2], wb, docs);
    });
}

fn operations(ui: &mut Ui, wb: &mut Workbench) {
    ui.label(RichText::new("Operations").strong()).explain(
        "Operations",
        "Click an operation to add it to the end of the recipe. Hover one to see what it does.",
    );
    ui.add(
        egui::TextEdit::singleline(&mut wb.filter)
            .hint_text("Search, e.g. base64, xor, aes")
            .desired_width(f32::INFINITY),
    );
    let filter = wb.filter.to_lowercase();
    egui::ScrollArea::vertical()
        .id_salt("wb_ops")
        .auto_shrink([false, false])
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            let mut category = None;
            for op in orress_transforms::ops() {
                if !filter.is_empty()
                    && !op.name.to_lowercase().contains(&filter)
                    && !op.id.contains(&filter)
                {
                    continue;
                }
                if category != Some(op.category) {
                    category = Some(op.category);
                    ui.add_space(4.0);
                    ui.label(RichText::new(op.category.name()).small().weak());
                }
                if ui
                    .selectable_label(false, op.name)
                    .explain(op.name, op.explain)
                    .clicked()
                {
                    wb.recipe.0.push(Step::new(op.id));
                    wb.sync_text();
                }
            }
        });
}

fn recipe(ui: &mut Ui, wb: &mut Workbench) {
    ui.label(RichText::new("Recipe").strong()).explain(
        "Recipe",
        "The steps, top to bottom. Untick a step to skip it, use the arrows to reorder. The \
         text field below holds the same recipe as text: copy it, share it, or use it with \
         orress-cli.",
    );
    let outputs: Vec<Result<usize, String>> = wb
        .outputs()
        .iter()
        .map(|r| r.as_ref().map(Vec::len).map_err(Clone::clone))
        .collect();
    let mut action: Option<(usize, i32)> = None; // (index, -1 up / +1 down / 0 remove)
    let mut changed = false;
    egui::ScrollArea::vertical()
        .id_salt("wb_recipe")
        .max_height(ui.available_height() - 90.0)
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            let mut enabled_index = 0;
            for (i, step) in wb.recipe.0.iter_mut().enumerate() {
                let Some(op) = orress_transforms::find(&step.op) else {
                    continue;
                };
                egui::Frame::group(ui.style()).show(ui, |ui| {
                    ui.set_width(ui.available_width());
                    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                        changed |= ui
                            .checkbox(&mut step.enabled, "")
                            .on_hover_text("Run this step")
                            .changed();
                        ui.label(RichText::new(op.name).strong())
                            .explain(op.name, op.explain);
                        ui.with_layout(egui::Layout::right_to_left(egui::Align::Center), |ui| {
                            if ui.small_button("x").on_hover_text("Remove").clicked() {
                                action = Some((i, 0));
                            }
                            if ui.small_button("v").on_hover_text("Move down").clicked() {
                                action = Some((i, 1));
                            }
                            if ui.small_button("^").on_hover_text("Move up").clicked() {
                                action = Some((i, -1));
                            }
                        });
                    });
                    for p in op.params {
                        let value = step
                            .params
                            .entry(p.name.to_owned())
                            .or_insert_with(|| p.default.to_owned());
                        ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                            ui.label(muted(p.name)).explain(p.name, p.explain);
                            match p.kind {
                                ParamKind::Choice(options) => {
                                    egui::ComboBox::from_id_salt((i, p.name))
                                        .selected_text(value.as_str())
                                        .show_ui(ui, |ui| {
                                            for o in options {
                                                changed |= ui
                                                    .selectable_value(value, (*o).to_owned(), *o)
                                                    .changed();
                                            }
                                        });
                                }
                                _ => {
                                    changed |= ui
                                        .add(
                                            egui::TextEdit::singleline(value)
                                                .id_salt((i, p.name))
                                                .desired_width(f32::INFINITY),
                                        )
                                        .changed();
                                }
                            }
                        });
                    }
                    if step.enabled {
                        match outputs.get(enabled_index) {
                            Some(Ok(n)) => {
                                ui.label(muted(format!("{n} bytes out")));
                            }
                            Some(Err(e)) => {
                                ui.colored_label(ui.visuals().warn_fg_color, e);
                            }
                            None => {
                                ui.label(muted("not run (an earlier step failed)"));
                            }
                        }
                        enabled_index += 1;
                    }
                });
            }
            if wb.recipe.0.is_empty() {
                ui.label(muted("Empty. Click operations on the left to add them."));
            }
        });
    if let Some((i, dir)) = action {
        match dir {
            0 => {
                wb.recipe.0.remove(i);
            }
            -1 if i > 0 => wb.recipe.0.swap(i, i - 1),
            1 if i + 1 < wb.recipe.0.len() => wb.recipe.0.swap(i, i + 1),
            _ => {}
        }
        changed = true;
    }
    if changed {
        wb.sync_text();
    }
    ui.separator();
    ui.label(muted("As text (edit or paste a recipe):"));
    let edit = ui.add(
        egui::TextEdit::singleline(&mut wb.recipe_text)
            .id_salt("wb_recipe_text")
            .desired_width(f32::INFINITY)
            .font(egui::TextStyle::Monospace),
    );
    if edit.changed() {
        match Recipe::parse(&wb.recipe_text) {
            Ok(r) => {
                wb.recipe = r;
                wb.recipe_error = None;
            }
            Err(e) => wb.recipe_error = Some(e),
        }
    }
    if let Some(e) = &wb.recipe_error {
        ui.colored_label(ui.visuals().warn_fg_color, e);
    }
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        if ui.small_button("Copy as command").explain(
            "Copy as command",
            "Copies a orress-cli command that runs this recipe on a file, for scripts and terminals.",
        ).clicked() {
            ui.ctx().copy_text(format!("orress-cli recipe \"{}\" INPUT_FILE", wb.recipe));
        }
        if ui.small_button("Clear").clicked() {
            wb.recipe.0.clear();
            wb.sync_text();
        }
    });
}

fn data(ui: &mut Ui, wb: &mut Workbench, docs: &mut DocStore) {
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label(RichText::new("Input").strong());
        let old = wb.input_mode;
        ui.selectable_value(&mut wb.input_mode, Mode::Text, "text");
        ui.selectable_value(&mut wb.input_mode, Mode::Hex, "hex").explain(
            "Hex input",
            "Type or paste bytes as hex (41 42 43). Use this for binary data.",
        );
        if wb.input_mode != old {
            wb.input_text = render(&wb.input, wb.input_mode);
        }
        if ui.small_button("From selection").explain(
            "From selection",
            "Use the bytes selected in the hex view of the current file. You can also select bytes there and use the palette command \"Hex: Send to Workbench\".",
        ).clicked() {
            match docs.active().and_then(|d| Some((d, d.selection?))) {
                Some((doc, (a, b))) => {
                    let bytes = doc.bytes().and_then(|x| x.get(a as usize..b as usize)).map(<[u8]>::to_vec).unwrap_or_default();
                    let path = doc.path.clone();
                    wb.set_input(bytes, Some((path, a, b)));
                }
                None => wb.message = Some("Select some bytes in the hex view first.".into()),
            }
        }
    });
    let edit = ui.add(
        egui::TextEdit::multiline(&mut wb.input_text)
            .id_salt("wb_input")
            .desired_rows(6)
            .desired_width(f32::INFINITY)
            .font(egui::TextStyle::Monospace),
    );
    if edit.changed() {
        match parse_input(&wb.input_text, wb.input_mode) {
            Ok(bytes) => {
                wb.input = bytes;
                wb.source = None;
                wb.message = None;
                wb.magic = None;
            }
            Err(e) => wb.message = Some(format!("Input: {e}")),
        }
    }
    ui.label(muted(format!("{} bytes", wb.input.len())));
    if let Some(m) = &wb.message {
        ui.colored_label(ui.visuals().warn_fg_color, m);
    }

    ui.add_space(6.0);
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label(RichText::new("Output").strong());
        ui.selectable_value(&mut wb.output_mode, Mode::Text, "text");
        ui.selectable_value(&mut wb.output_mode, Mode::Hex, "hex");
    });
    let output = wb.final_output();
    match &output {
        Ok(bytes) => {
            let flag = orress_bytes::strings::looks_like_flag(&String::from_utf8_lossy(bytes));
            if flag {
                ui.label(
                    RichText::new("This looks like a flag!")
                        .strong()
                        .color(ui.visuals().warn_fg_color),
                );
            }
            let shown = &bytes[..bytes.len().min(64 * 1024)];
            let mut text = render(shown, wb.output_mode);
            if shown.len() < bytes.len() {
                text += "\n… (first 64 KiB shown)";
            }
            egui::ScrollArea::vertical()
                .id_salt("wb_output")
                .max_height(180.0)
                .show(ui, |ui| {
                    ui.add(
                        egui::TextEdit::multiline(&mut text)
                            .desired_width(f32::INFINITY)
                            .font(egui::TextStyle::Monospace)
                            .interactive(true),
                    );
                });
            ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                ui.label(muted(format!("{} bytes · entropy {:.2}", bytes.len(), orress_bytes::entropy::shannon(bytes))));
                if ui.small_button("Copy").clicked() {
                    ui.ctx().copy_text(String::from_utf8_lossy(bytes).into_owned());
                }
                if ui.small_button("Save…").clicked()
                    && let Some(path) = rfd_save()
                    && let Err(e) = std::fs::write(&path, bytes)
                {
                    wb.message = Some(format!("Could not save: {e}"));
                }
                if let Some((path, start, end)) = wb.source.clone()
                    && bytes.len() as u64 == end - start
                    && ui
                        .small_button("Write back to file")
                        .explain(
                            "Write back",
                            "Replace the selected bytes in the file with this output (as a patch, the file on disk is not changed). Useful to decrypt data in place and then read it in the disassembly or hex view.",
                        )
                        .clicked()
                    && let Some(doc) = docs.get_mut(&path)
                {
                    if let Err(e) = doc.patch(start, bytes) {
                        wb.message = Some(e);
                    } else {
                        wb.message = Some(format!("Patched {} bytes at 0x{start:x}.", bytes.len()));
                    }
                }
            });
        }
        Err(e) => {
            ui.colored_label(ui.visuals().warn_fg_color, e);
        }
    }

    ui.add_space(6.0);
    if ui
        .button(RichText::new("Magic").strong())
        .explain(
            "Magic",
            "Tries common decodings (hex, base64, base32, URL, zlib, gzip, XOR, ROT13, UTF-16 ...) \
             in chains of up to 3 steps, and lists the most readable results. Click Use to \
             load a result's recipe.",
        )
        .clicked()
    {
        wb.magic = Some(orress_transforms::magic(&wb.input, 3));
    }
    if let Some(suggestions) = wb.magic.clone() {
        if suggestions.is_empty() {
            ui.label(muted("Magic found nothing more readable than the input."));
        }
        let mut chosen = None;
        egui::ScrollArea::vertical()
            .id_salt("wb_magic")
            .max_height(200.0)
            .show(ui, |ui| {
                for (i, s) in suggestions.iter().enumerate() {
                    egui::Frame::group(ui.style()).show(ui, |ui| {
                        ui.set_width(ui.available_width());
                        ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                            if ui.small_button("Use").clicked() {
                                chosen = Some(i);
                            }
                            ui.label(RichText::new(s.recipe.to_string()).monospace().strong());
                        });
                        let preview: String = String::from_utf8_lossy(&s.output)
                            .chars()
                            .take(120)
                            .collect();
                        ui.label(RichText::new(preview).monospace().small());
                        ui.label(muted(&s.why));
                    });
                }
            });
        if let Some(i) = chosen {
            wb.recipe = suggestions[i].recipe.clone();
            wb.sync_text();
        }
    }
}

fn rfd_save() -> Option<std::path::PathBuf> {
    rfd::FileDialog::new().set_title("Save output").save_file()
}
```

```rs
//! Cross-references panel: who uses an address.
//!
//! It follows the function under the cursor until a target is pinned (X in the disassembly,
//! or the Pin button); "Follow cursor" unpins it again.

use egui::{RichText, Ui};
use orress_project::DocStore;
use orress_ui::muted;

use crate::{DocView, ViewRequest, code};

pub fn xrefs_panel(ui: &mut Ui, docs: &mut DocStore, requests: &mut Vec<ViewRequest>) {
    let Some(doc) = docs.active_mut() else {
        ui.label(
            "Open a file, put the cursor on a function or address in the disassembly and press X.",
        );
        return;
    };
    let Some(program) = doc.program().cloned() else {
        ui.label(muted("Waiting for the disassembly…"));
        return;
    };
    // A pinned target (X in the disassembly), else the function under the cursor.
    let pinned = doc.xref_target.is_some();
    let target = doc.xref_target.or_else(|| {
        let addr = program.memory.address_of(doc.cursor)?;
        program.function_containing(addr).map(|f| f.entry)
    });
    let Some(target) = target else {
        ui.label("Put the cursor on code, or press X on an address in the disassembly.");
        return;
    };
    let name = code::describe_address(doc, &program, target);
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label(RichText::new(format!("References to {name}")).strong());
        ui.label(muted(format!("(0x{target:x})")));
        if pinned {
            if ui
                .small_button("Follow cursor")
                .on_hover_text("Unpin: show references to the function under the cursor again")
                .clicked()
            {
                doc.xref_target = None;
            }
        } else if ui
            .small_button("📌 Pin")
            .on_hover_text("Keep showing this target while the cursor moves")
            .clicked()
        {
            doc.xref_target = Some(target);
        }
    });
    ui.label(muted(
        "Every place in the code that calls, jumps to or reads this address. Following \
         references is how you find, for example, the code that prints \"Wrong password\".",
    ));
    let refs = program.xrefs(target).to_vec();
    if refs.is_empty() {
        ui.label(
            "No references found. It may be called indirectly (through a pointer) or not at all.",
        );
        return;
    }
    let mut go = None;
    egui::ScrollArea::vertical()
        .auto_shrink([false, false])
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            egui::Grid::new("xrefs")
                .striped(true)
                .num_columns(4)
                .spacing([12.0, 3.0])
                .show(ui, |ui| {
                    for h in ["From", "In", "Kind", "Instruction"] {
                        ui.label(RichText::new(h).strong());
                    }
                    ui.end_row();
                    for xref in &refs {
                        if ui
                            .link(RichText::new(format!("0x{:x}", xref.from)).monospace())
                            .clicked()
                        {
                            go = Some(xref.from);
                        }
                        ui.label(
                            RichText::new(code::describe_address(doc, &program, xref.from))
                                .monospace(),
                        );
                        ui.label(xref.kind.label());
                        let text = program
                            .decode(xref.from)
                            .map(|i| i.text())
                            .unwrap_or_default();
                        ui.label(RichText::new(text).monospace().weak());
                        ui.end_row();
                    }
                });
        });
    if let Some(from) = go {
        doc.navigate_to_address(from);
        requests.push(ViewRequest::Open(doc.path.clone(), DocView::Disassembly));
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-views/src/yara.rs`:

```rs
//! The YARA workbench: write a YARA rule and test it live against the open file, powered by the
//! pure-Rust YARA-X engine (`orress-triage::yara`). Matches show their rule, pattern, offset and
//! a byte preview.

use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

use egui::{RichText, Ui};
use orress_debug::read_all_memory;
use orress_project::DocStore;
use orress_triage::yara::{generate_rule, scan, scan_dir, scan_regions_report};
use orress_triage::{LibHit, MemScan, YaraOutcome};
use orress_ui::muted;

/// Cap on how much of a process's memory to read for a scan.
const MEM_CAP: usize = 256 * 1024 * 1024;

const DEFAULT_RULE: &str = r#"rule example {
    meta:
        author = "analyst"
        description = "matches the PE DOS stub"
    strings:
        $dos = "This program cannot be run in DOS mode"
        $mz  = { 4D 5A }
    condition:
        $mz at 0 and $dos
}
"#;

/// Persistent UI state for the YARA tab.
pub struct YaraView {
    rule: String,
    outcome: Option<YaraOutcome>,
    scanned: String,
    /// Results of scanning the open file against a rule folder: (hits, errors).
    library: Option<(Vec<LibHit>, Vec<String>)>,
    library_dir: String,
    pid: String,
    /// The process-scan result plus per-region errors (timeouts, budget exhausted).
    mem: Option<MemResult>,
    /// Folder and process scans run on worker threads (they read many files or up to
    /// [`MEM_CAP`] of memory); these hold their results until they finish.
    library_job: Option<Slot<(Vec<LibHit>, Vec<String>)>>,
    mem_job: Option<Slot<MemResult>>,
}

type Slot<T> = Arc<Mutex<Option<T>>>;

/// A process scan: the hits plus per-region errors, or why memory couldn't be read.
type MemResult = Result<(MemScan, Vec<String>), String>;

/// Runs `work` on a worker thread; its result (or `on_panic()` if it panicked) lands in
/// the returned slot and a repaint is requested.
fn spawn_job<T: Send + 'static>(
    ctx: &egui::Context,
    work: impl FnOnce() -> T + Send + 'static,
    on_panic: impl FnOnce() -> T + Send + 'static,
) -> Slot<T> {
    let slot: Slot<T> = Arc::new(Mutex::new(None));
    let out = Arc::clone(&slot);
    let ctx = ctx.clone();
    // If the thread cannot start, the slot is never filled; `take_done` notices that nobody
    // else holds it and gives up waiting.
    let _ = std::thread::Builder::new()
        .name("yara scan".into())
        .spawn(move || {
            let result = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(work))
                .unwrap_or_else(|_| on_panic());
            *out.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) = Some(result);
            ctx.request_repaint();
        });
    slot
}

/// Takes a finished job's result; clears `job` when it is done.
fn take_done<T>(job: &mut Option<Slot<T>>) -> Option<T> {
    let done = job
        .as_ref()?
        .lock()
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
        .take();
    if done.is_some() || job.as_ref().is_some_and(|s| Arc::strong_count(s) == 1) {
        *job = None;
    }
    done
}

impl Default for YaraView {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            rule: DEFAULT_RULE.to_string(),
            outcome: None,
            scanned: String::new(),
            library: None,
            library_dir: String::new(),
            pid: String::new(),
            mem: None,
            library_job: None,
            mem_job: None,
        }
    }
}

pub fn yara_view(ui: &mut Ui, view: &mut YaraView, docs: &DocStore) {
    orress_ui::spotlight::mark(ui.ctx(), "view.Yara", ui.max_rect());
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label(RichText::new("YARA workbench").strong());
        ui.label(muted("write a rule · scan the open file (YARA-X)"));
    });
    ui.separator();

    let file = docs
        .active()
        .map(|d| d.file_name())
        .unwrap_or_else(|| "no file".into());

    if let Some(done) = take_done(&mut view.library_job) {
        view.library = Some(done);
    }
    if let Some(done) = take_done(&mut view.mem_job) {
        view.mem = Some(done);
    }

    ui.label(muted("Rule:"));
    egui::ScrollArea::vertical()
        .max_height(240.0)
        .id_salt("yara-rule")
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            ui.add(
                egui::TextEdit::multiline(&mut view.rule)
                    .code_editor()
                    .desired_rows(10)
                    .desired_width(f32::INFINITY),
            );
        });

    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        let enabled = docs.active().and_then(|d| d.bytes()).is_some();
        if ui
            .add_enabled(enabled, egui::Button::new("▶ Scan open file"))
            .on_hover_text(format!("Scan {file} with this rule"))
            .clicked()
            && let Some(bytes) = docs.active().and_then(|d| d.bytes())
        {
            view.outcome = Some(scan(&view.rule, bytes));
            view.scanned = file.clone();
        }
        if ui
            .add_enabled(enabled, egui::Button::new("✨ Generate from strings"))
            .on_hover_text("Build a starter rule from the sample's distinctive strings")
            .clicked()
            && let Some(analysis) = docs.active().and_then(|d| d.analysis())
        {
            let strings: Vec<&str> = analysis.strings.iter().map(|s| s.text.as_str()).collect();
            view.rule = generate_rule(&file, &strings);
            view.outcome = None;
        }
        let library_busy = view.library_job.is_some();
        if ui
            .add_enabled(
                enabled && !library_busy,
                egui::Button::new("📁 Scan rule folder…"),
            )
            .on_hover_text("Scan the open file against every .yar/.yara rule in a folder")
            .clicked()
            && let Some(dir) = rfd::FileDialog::new()
                .set_title("Pick a YARA rule folder")
                .pick_folder()
            && let Some(bytes) = docs.active().and_then(|d| d.bytes()).cloned()
        {
            view.library_dir = dir.display().to_string();
            view.library = None;
            view.library_job = Some(spawn_job(
                ui.ctx(),
                move || scan_dir(&dir, &bytes),
                || {
                    (
                        Vec::new(),
                        vec!["the folder scan hit an internal error".to_string()],
                    )
                },
            ));
        }
        if library_busy {
            ui.spinner();
            ui.label(muted("scanning rule folder…"));
        }
        if !enabled {
            ui.label(muted("open a file to scan"));
        }
    });

    // In-memory scan of a running process (unpacks/decrypts show up in memory).
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.label("Running process (PID)");
        ui.add(egui::TextEdit::singleline(&mut view.pid).desired_width(80.0));
        let mem_busy = view.mem_job.is_some();
        if ui
            .add_enabled(!mem_busy, egui::Button::new("🧠 Scan process memory"))
            .on_hover_text("Read the process's committed memory and scan it with this rule")
            .clicked()
        {
            match view.pid.trim().parse::<u32>() {
                Ok(pid) => {
                    let rule = view.rule.clone();
                    view.mem = None;
                    view.mem_job = Some(spawn_job(
                        ui.ctx(),
                        move || {
                            read_all_memory(pid, MEM_CAP).map(|regions| {
                                scan_regions_report(
                                    &rule,
                                    regions.iter().map(|r| (r.base, r.data.as_slice())),
                                )
                            })
                        },
                        || Err("the process scan hit an internal error".into()),
                    ));
                }
                Err(_) => view.mem = Some(Err("enter a numeric PID".into())),
            }
        }
        if mem_busy {
            ui.spinner();
            ui.label(muted("reading process memory…"));
        }
    });

    if let Some(mem) = &view.mem {
        ui.add_space(4.0);
        match mem {
            Err(e) => {
                ui.colored_label(
                    ui.visuals().error_fg_color,
                    format!("process scan failed: {e}"),
                );
            }
            Ok((MemScan::CompileError(e), _)) => {
                ui.colored_label(ui.visuals().error_fg_color, "Rule did not compile:");
                ui.label(RichText::new(e).monospace());
            }
            Ok((MemScan::Hits(hits), errors)) => {
                for e in errors.iter().take(20) {
                    ui.colored_label(ui.visuals().warn_fg_color, format!("  {e}"));
                }
                if hits.is_empty() {
                    ui.label(muted("No matches in process memory."));
                } else {
                    ui.label(
                        RichText::new(format!("{} match(es) in process memory", hits.len()))
                            .strong(),
                    );
                    for h in hits.iter().take(500) {
                        ui.label(
                            RichText::new(format!(
                                "  {} · {} @ {:#x}  {:?}",
                                h.rule, h.pattern, h.address, h.preview
                            ))
                            .monospace()
                            .weak(),
                        );
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    if let Some((hits, errors)) = &view.library {
        ui.add_space(6.0);
        ui.separator();
        ui.label(RichText::new(format!("Library scan — {}", view.library_dir)).strong());
        if hits.is_empty() {
            ui.label(muted("No rules in the folder matched."));
        }
        for h in hits {
            ui.label(
                RichText::new(format!("  {} · {} ({} match)", h.file, h.rule, h.matches))
                    .monospace(),
            );
        }
        for e in errors {
            ui.colored_label(ui.visuals().warn_fg_color, format!("  {e}"));
        }
    }

    let Some(outcome) = &view.outcome else {
        return;
    };
    ui.add_space(6.0);
    ui.separator();
    match outcome {
        YaraOutcome::CompileError(e) => {
            ui.colored_label(ui.visuals().error_fg_color, "Rule did not compile:");
            ui.label(RichText::new(e).monospace());
        }
        YaraOutcome::ScanError(e) => {
            ui.colored_label(ui.visuals().error_fg_color, format!("Scan error: {e}"));
        }
        YaraOutcome::Hits(hits) => {
            if hits.is_empty() {
                ui.label(muted(format!("No rules matched {}.", view.scanned)));
                return;
            }
            ui.label(
                RichText::new(format!("{} rule(s) matched {}", hits.len(), view.scanned)).strong(),
            );
            egui::ScrollArea::vertical()
                .auto_shrink([false, false])
                .show(ui, |ui| {
                    for hit in hits {
                        ui.add_space(4.0);
                        ui.label(RichText::new(&hit.rule).strong().monospace());
                        for m in &hit.matches {
                            ui.label(
                                RichText::new(format!(
                                    "   {}  @ {:#x}  {:?}",
                                    m.pattern, m.range.start, m.preview
                                ))
                                .monospace()
                                .weak(),
                            );
                        }
                    }
                });
        }
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-vm/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! VM-obfuscation detection (M14): find the **dispatch loop** of a bytecode interpreter.
//!
//! VM-based protections (VMProtect, Themida, and homegrown CTF VMs) replace a function's code with
//! bytecode for a custom virtual machine, plus an interpreter that fetches an opcode and jumps to a
//! handler for it. In the CFG this interpreter has a very recognizable shape: one **dispatcher**
//! block that many handler blocks branch back to (so it has a high fan-in), inside a loop. This is
//! the entry point of any devirtualization effort — you first have to find the VM.
//!
//! This is a deterministic, CFG-only heuristic (no execution): it flags functions whose structure
//! matches an interpreter, ranked by confidence. It does not yet *lift* the bytecode.
//!
//! Precision note: a high fan-in block alone is *not* enough, and neither is a high fan-out one.
//! Ordinary loops in library code (error-handling latches in a statically-linked runtime) have a
//! high-fan-in block; an ordinary `switch` has a high-fan-out block. On their own either produces a
//! flood of false positives. The distinguishing mark of an interpreter is a **dispatch loop**: a
//! block that branches *out* to many handlers, most of which *loop back* to it to fetch the next
//! opcode. So we look for a high-fan-out block whose successors can reach it again, and count those
//! looping handlers. A one-shot `switch` fails this (its cases fall through, they don't return to
//! the switch) and so does a plain loop latch (low fan-out), while a real interpreter scores high.
//! `scan` additionally drops low-confidence matches and keeps only the strongest few.

use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};

use orress_analysis::{Block, Function, Program};

/// Functions below this many basic blocks are never interpreters (handlers make them large).
const MIN_BLOCKS: usize = 12;
/// A dispatcher must branch out to at least this many handlers that loop back to it.
const MIN_HANDLERS: usize = 6;
/// `scan` reports only matches at least this confident, so weak shapes don't flood the results.
const CONFIDENCE_FLOOR: f32 = 0.6;
/// `scan` returns at most this many candidates (the highest-confidence ones).
const MAX_REPORTS: usize = 8;

/// A function that looks like a VM interpreter.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct VmReport {
    /// The function's entry address.
    pub entry: u64,
    /// The dispatcher block: the one most handlers branch back to.
    pub dispatcher: u64,
    /// Total basic blocks (roughly: handlers + glue).
    pub blocks: usize,
    /// Handlers: blocks the dispatcher branches to that also branch back to it (≈ the opcode count).
    pub handlers: usize,
    /// In-degree of the dispatcher (how many blocks target it).
    pub max_fan_in: usize,
    /// 0.0–1.0 — how strongly the shape matches an interpreter.
    pub confidence: f32,
}

/// Tests one function for the interpreter shape.
pub fn detect(func: &Function) -> Option<VmReport> {
    let blocks = func.blocks.len();
    if blocks < MIN_BLOCKS {
        return None;
    }

    // Predecessors of every block, and the in-degree (for the report).
    let mut preds: HashMap<u64, Vec<u64>> = HashMap::new();
    let mut in_degree: HashMap<u64, usize> = HashMap::new();
    for block in &func.blocks {
        for edge in &block.succs {
            preds.entry(edge.target).or_default().push(block.start);
            *in_degree.entry(edge.target).or_default() += 1;
        }
    }

    // The dispatcher is the high-fan-out block with the most *looping* handlers: successors that can
    // reach the block again (so the loop fetches the next opcode through it). A one-shot switch has
    // high fan-out but no looping successors; a plain loop latch has looping edges but low fan-out.
    let mut best: Option<(&orress_analysis::Block, usize)> = None;
    for block in &func.blocks {
        if block.succs.len() < MIN_HANDLERS {
            continue;
        }
        let back = reach_to(&preds, block.start);
        let handlers = block
            .succs
            .iter()
            .filter(|e| back.contains(&e.target))
            .count();
        if handlers >= MIN_HANDLERS && best.is_none_or(|(_, h)| handlers > h) {
            best = Some((block, handlers));
        }
    }

    let (dispatcher, handlers) = best?;
    let fan_out = dispatcher.succs.len();
    let max_fan_in = in_degree.get(&dispatcher.start).copied().unwrap_or(0);

    Some(VmReport {
        entry: func.entry,
        dispatcher: dispatcher.start,
        blocks,
        handlers,
        max_fan_in,
        confidence: confidence(handlers, fan_out),
    })
}

/// One recovered VM opcode: the dispatch case index, the handler it runs, and a first look at what
/// that handler does. This is the opcode table — the skeleton a full devirtualization is built on.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct VmHandler {
    /// The opcode value (the dispatch index that selects this handler).
    pub opcode: usize,
    /// The handler block's address.
    pub address: u64,
    /// Instructions in the handler's entry block.
    pub insns: usize,
    /// The distinctive data operations the handler performs (e.g. `xor, add`), as a first hint of
    /// the virtual instruction's meaning. Empty when the handler is only glue/control flow.
    pub ops: Vec<String>,
    /// Net change the handler makes to the operand-stack pointer: `+1` pushes a value, `-1` is a
    /// binary operation (pop two, push one), `-2` consumes two (a comparison), `0` is unary/none.
    pub stack_delta: i64,
}

/// A best-effort name for the virtual operation a handler implements, inferred from the distinctive
/// data operations in its (dominator-isolated) body. Reliable for the arithmetic/logic opcodes — VM
/// bookkeeping only uses `add`/`inc`/`cmp`, so `xor`/`sub`/`rol`/shift/`mul` single out the real op.
/// Handlers that only move/compare (push, pop, dup, equality, length) can't be told apart from
/// bookkeeping at this level, so they are reported as `stack/control` rather than guessed.
pub fn operation(h: &VmHandler) -> &'static str {
    let has = |m: &str| h.ops.iter().any(|o| o == m);
    if has("rol") || has("ror") {
        "rotate"
    } else if has("shl") || has("shr") || has("sar") {
        "shift"
    } else if has("imul") || has("mul") {
        "multiply"
    } else if has("xor") {
        "xor"
    } else if has("sub") || has("sbb") {
        "subtract"
    } else if has("and") || has("or") || has("not") || has("neg") {
        "bitwise"
    } else if h.stack_delta >= 1 {
        // A net increase of the stack pointer means the handler pushes a value (push-immediate,
        // push-input, dup). A net decrease is NOT reliably a comparison vs a binary op here — the
        // pushed result of a binary op is often written without a tracked `sp` increment — so those
        // stay `stack/control` rather than risk a wrong label.
        "push"
    } else if h.insns <= 3 {
        "halt/return"
    } else {
        "stack/control"
    }
}

/// One decoded virtual instruction of the bytecode: its offset in the blob, the opcode byte, the
/// recovered operation name, and the operand bytes that follow it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct VmInsn {
    pub offset: usize,
    pub opcode: u8,
    pub op: &'static str,
    pub operands: Vec<u8>,
}

/// Disassembles the VM's bytecode into virtual instructions. For each opcode it recovers the
/// operand size from how far the handler advances the virtual program counter (an `add vpc, k`
/// consumes `k - 1` operand bytes after the opcode byte), names the operation, and walks the blob
/// instruction by instruction until a halt handler or the end. Turns the extracted bytecode into a
/// readable program in the recovered instruction set. `None` if the bytecode can't be located.
pub fn disassemble(program: &Program, report: &VmReport) -> Option<Vec<VmInsn>> {
    let bc = bytecode(program, report)?;
    // `Memory::read` returns *up to* the requested length (it stops at the region end), so the
    // walk must be bounded by what was actually read, not by the recovered length.
    let blob = program.memory.read(bc.base, bc.len? as usize)?.to_vec();
    let func = program.functions.get(&report.entry)?;

    // Identify the virtual program counter: the opcode fetch's address register that is not the
    // (constant) bytecode base.
    let mem = program.mem_ref(bc.fetch)?;
    let regs: Vec<u8> = [mem.base, mem.index].into_iter().flatten().collect();
    let base_reg = regs
        .iter()
        .copied()
        .find(|&r| program.register_const_at(func, bc.fetch, r) == Some(bc.base))?;
    let vpc = regs.iter().copied().find(|&r| r != base_reg)?;

    let table = handlers(program, report);
    let idom = idoms(func);
    // How far the vpc advances per instruction = the shared advance in the fetch/dispatch blocks
    // (blocks not owned by any handler — covers a uniform fixed-size encoding) plus the handler's
    // own advance (covers per-opcode operand reads). Operand bytes = total advance minus the opcode
    // byte. `vpc_advance(pred)` sums the positive constant deltas to the vpc over matching blocks.
    let handler_entries: Vec<u64> = table.iter().map(|h| h.address).collect();
    let vpc_advance = |owned: &dyn Fn(u64) -> bool| -> i64 {
        func.blocks
            .iter()
            .filter(|b| owned(b.start))
            .flat_map(|b| &b.insns)
            .filter_map(|&a| program.reg_info(a).and_then(|i| i.delta))
            .filter(|&(r, k)| r == vpc && k > 0)
            .map(|(_, k)| k)
            .max()
            .unwrap_or(0)
    };
    let in_a_handler = |blk: u64| handler_entries.iter().any(|&h| dominates(&idom, h, blk));
    let shared_advance = vpc_advance(&|blk| !in_a_handler(blk));
    let operand_size = |opcode: u8| -> usize {
        let Some(h) = table.iter().find(|h| h.opcode == opcode as usize) else {
            return 0;
        };
        let handler_advance = vpc_advance(&|blk| dominates(&idom, h.address, blk));
        let total = (shared_advance + handler_advance).max(1);
        (total as usize).saturating_sub(1)
    };
    let name = |opcode: u8| -> &'static str {
        table
            .iter()
            .find(|h| h.opcode == opcode as usize)
            .map_or("unknown", operation)
    };

    Some(walk_bytecode(&blob, operand_size, name))
}

/// Walks a bytecode blob instruction by instruction: each opcode byte, its operand bytes (clipped
/// to what is left of the blob), until a halt handler or the end. Bounded by `blob.len()` alone,
/// so a blob shorter than the recovered extent can't index out of bounds.
fn walk_bytecode(
    blob: &[u8],
    operand_size: impl Fn(u8) -> usize,
    name: impl Fn(u8) -> &'static str,
) -> Vec<VmInsn> {
    let len = blob.len();
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut pc = 0usize;
    while pc < len {
        let opcode = blob[pc];
        let op = name(opcode);
        let size = operand_size(opcode).min(len - pc - 1);
        let operands = blob[pc + 1..pc + 1 + size].to_vec();
        out.push(VmInsn {
            offset: pc,
            opcode,
            op,
            operands,
        });
        pc += 1 + size;
        if op == "halt/return" {
            break;
        }
    }
    out
}

/// The recovered location of a VM's bytecode blob: the base address the interpreter reads opcodes
/// from, and the fetch instruction that reads it. The first concrete artifact for reading the
/// virtual program itself (the next step after the opcode table).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct VmBytecode {
    /// Base address of the bytecode blob in the binary.
    pub base: u64,
    /// The opcode-fetch instruction that reads the blob.
    pub fetch: u64,
    /// Length of the blob in bytes, when the interpreter's bound (`cmp vpc, len`) is recovered.
    pub len: Option<u64>,
}

/// Locates the VM's bytecode blob. The opcode fetch is a byte-sized load `[base + index]` in the
/// dispatcher's fetch region (the dispatcher block or a direct predecessor, run before each
/// dispatch); one of its address registers is a loop-invariant pointer to a data blob — the
/// bytecode — which register dataflow resolves to a constant address. `None` if it can't be found.
pub fn bytecode(program: &Program, report: &VmReport) -> Option<VmBytecode> {
    let func = program.functions.get(&report.entry)?;
    let fetch_region: Vec<&Block> = func
        .blocks
        .iter()
        .filter(|b| {
            b.start == report.dispatcher || b.succs.iter().any(|e| e.target == report.dispatcher)
        })
        .collect();
    for block in fetch_region {
        for &a in &block.insns {
            let Some(mem) = program.mem_ref(a) else {
                continue;
            };
            if !mem.is_load || mem.size != 1 {
                continue; // the opcode fetch reads a single byte
            }
            for reg in [mem.base, mem.index].into_iter().flatten() {
                let Some(base) = program.register_const_at(func, a, reg) else {
                    continue;
                };
                if program.memory.is_code(base) {
                    continue;
                }
                // The blob runs from its base until the next referenced datum (e.g. the jump
                // table) — a reliable extent even when the interpreter has no `cmp vpc, len` bound
                // (it may just run until a HALT opcode). Capped so a missing next-ref stays sane.
                const MAX_BLOB: u64 = 4096;
                let len = program
                    .next_data_ref(base)
                    .map(|n| (n - base).min(MAX_BLOB));
                return Some(VmBytecode {
                    base,
                    fetch: a,
                    len,
                });
            }
        }
    }
    None
}

/// Mnemonics that characterise what a handler *computes* (not glue like mov/jmp/push/lea).
const SIGNAL_OPS: &[&str] = &[
    "xor", "add", "sub", "adc", "sbb", "and", "or", "not", "neg", "inc", "dec", "imul", "mul",
    "idiv", "div", "shl", "shr", "sar", "rol", "ror", "cmp", "test",
];

/// Recovers the VM's **opcode table**: for each dispatch case, the handler it runs and a summary of
/// the operations that handler performs. The first step of devirtualization — turning the detected
/// interpreter into a described instruction set. Returns empty if the dispatcher's jump table was
/// not recovered (e.g. a compare-chain dispatch with no table).
pub fn handlers(program: &Program, report: &VmReport) -> Vec<VmHandler> {
    let Some(func) = program.functions.get(&report.entry) else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    let Some(block) = func.blocks.iter().find(|b| b.start == report.dispatcher) else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    // The dispatcher block ends in the indirect jump; its recovered jump table is the opcode table.
    let Some(&jmp) = block.insns.last() else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    let Some(cases) = program.switch_tables.get(&jmp) else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    let idom = idoms(func);
    let sp = find_sp(program, func);
    cases
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(opcode, &address)| {
            // The handler's region is the blocks it dominates — its own body, not the shared fetch
            // and dispatch blocks every handler returns to. Collect the operations it performs there
            // and its net effect on the operand-stack pointer.
            let mut ops: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
            let mut insns = 0;
            let mut stack_delta = 0i64;
            for hb in func
                .blocks
                .iter()
                .filter(|b| dominates(&idom, address, b.start))
            {
                insns += hb.insns.len();
                for &a in &hb.insns {
                    let Some(info) = program.reg_info(a) else {
                        continue;
                    };
                    if let Some(insn) = program.decode(a)
                        && SIGNAL_OPS.contains(&insn.mnemonic.as_str())
                        && !ops.iter().any(|o| o == &insn.mnemonic)
                    {
                        ops.push(insn.mnemonic.clone());
                    }
                    if let (Some(sp), Some((r, k))) = (sp, info.delta)
                        && r == sp
                    {
                        stack_delta += k;
                    }
                }
            }
            VmHandler {
                opcode,
                address,
                insns,
                ops,
                stack_delta,
            }
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Identifies the operand-stack pointer: the register most often used to index a stack-slot buffer
/// (`[rsp|rbp + sp + disp]`) across the interpreter — every handler touches the operand stack.
fn find_sp(program: &Program, func: &Function) -> Option<u8> {
    let mut counts = [0usize; 16];
    for block in &func.blocks {
        for &a in &block.insns {
            if let Some(info) = program.reg_info(a)
                && let Some(mem) = info.mem
                && matches!(mem.base, Some(4) | Some(5)) // rsp / rbp
                && let Some(idx) = mem.index
            {
                counts[idx as usize] += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    counts
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .filter(|&(_, &c)| c > 0)
        .max_by_key(|&(_, &c)| c)
        .map(|(i, _)| i as u8)
}

/// Immediate-dominator map for a function's CFG (Cooper–Harvey–Kennedy). A block's handler region
/// is the set of blocks it dominates — the code reached *only* through it, i.e. its own body,
/// excluding the shared dispatcher and fetch blocks that every handler returns to.
fn idoms(func: &Function) -> HashMap<u64, u64> {
    // Reverse post-order from the entry.
    let succ: HashMap<u64, Vec<u64>> = func
        .blocks
        .iter()
        .map(|b| (b.start, b.succs.iter().map(|e| e.target).collect()))
        .collect();
    let mut post = Vec::new();
    let mut seen = HashSet::new();
    let mut stack = vec![(func.entry, 0usize)];
    while let Some((n, i)) = stack.pop() {
        if i == 0 && !seen.insert(n) {
            continue;
        }
        match succ.get(&n).and_then(|s| s.get(i)) {
            Some(&next) => {
                stack.push((n, i + 1));
                if !seen.contains(&next) {
                    stack.push((next, 0));
                }
            }
            None => post.push(n),
        }
    }
    let rpo: Vec<u64> = post.iter().rev().copied().collect();
    let order: HashMap<u64, usize> = rpo.iter().enumerate().map(|(i, &b)| (b, i)).collect();
    let mut preds: HashMap<u64, Vec<u64>> = HashMap::new();
    for b in &func.blocks {
        for e in &b.succs {
            preds.entry(e.target).or_default().push(b.start);
        }
    }
    let mut idom: HashMap<u64, u64> = HashMap::from([(func.entry, func.entry)]);
    let intersect = |idom: &HashMap<u64, u64>, mut a: u64, mut b: u64| {
        while a != b {
            while order.get(&a).copied().unwrap_or(usize::MAX)
                > order.get(&b).copied().unwrap_or(usize::MAX)
            {
                a = idom[&a];
            }
            while order.get(&b).copied().unwrap_or(usize::MAX)
                > order.get(&a).copied().unwrap_or(usize::MAX)
            {
                b = idom[&b];
            }
        }
        a
    };
    let mut changed = true;
    while changed {
        changed = false;
        for &b in rpo.iter().skip(1) {
            let mut new = None;
            for &p in preds.get(&b).into_iter().flatten() {
                if idom.contains_key(&p) {
                    new = Some(match new {
                        None => p,
                        Some(n) => intersect(&idom, p, n),
                    });
                }
            }
            if let Some(new) = new
                && idom.get(&b) != Some(&new)
            {
                idom.insert(b, new);
                changed = true;
            }
        }
    }
    idom
}

/// Whether `h` dominates `b` (so `b` is part of `h`'s handler region).
fn dominates(idom: &HashMap<u64, u64>, h: u64, b: u64) -> bool {
    let mut cur = b;
    loop {
        if cur == h {
            return true;
        }
        match idom.get(&cur) {
            Some(&p) if p != cur => cur = p,
            _ => return false,
        }
    }
}

/// Every block that can reach `target` (reverse reachability over the predecessor edges).
fn reach_to(preds: &HashMap<u64, Vec<u64>>, target: u64) -> HashSet<u64> {
    let mut seen = HashSet::new();
    let mut stack = vec![target];
    while let Some(node) = stack.pop() {
        if let Some(ps) = preds.get(&node) {
            for &p in ps {
                if seen.insert(p) {
                    stack.push(p);
                }
            }
        }
    }
    seen
}

/// Scans every function in a program for interpreters, highest-confidence first. Only matches at
/// or above `CONFIDENCE_FLOOR` are returned, capped at `MAX_REPORTS`, so the result is a short
/// list of strong candidates rather than every loop in the binary.
pub fn scan(program: &Program) -> Vec<VmReport> {
    let mut out: Vec<VmReport> = program
        .functions
        .values()
        .filter_map(detect)
        .filter(|r| r.confidence >= CONFIDENCE_FLOOR)
        .collect();
    out.sort_by(|a, b| {
        b.confidence
            .partial_cmp(&a.confidence)
            .unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal)
    });
    out.truncate(MAX_REPORTS);
    out
}

/// Weighs how many handlers the dispatcher has against the share of its out-edges that are
/// handlers (a pure dispatcher sends almost every branch to a handler that returns).
fn confidence(handlers: usize, fan_out: usize) -> f32 {
    let count = (handlers as f32 / 16.0).min(1.0);
    let purity = if fan_out == 0 {
        0.0
    } else {
        (handlers as f32 / fan_out as f32).min(1.0)
    };
    (0.6 * count + 0.4 * purity).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
}

mod lift;
pub use lift::{VmSolution, emu_image, import_hooks, solve, try_solve};

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests;
```

`crates/orress-vm/src/lift.rs`:

```rs
//! Concolic lifting of a detected VM: recover the input (key) that drives the interpreter to its
//! success return. The insight (see PLAN.md M14.53/.55) is that a VM's control flow is driven by
//! the *concrete* bytecode while the program input is symbolic, so symbolically executing the whole
//! interpreter unrolls the dispatch loop and yields the real per-byte check constraints; solving
//! them gives a valid key that passes the real binary (self-verifying).
//!
//! This module derives the symbolic-execution parameters purely from the CFG — the success/fail
//! verdict blocks and the "doomed" blocks to steer away from — then runs [`orress_sym::solve_check`]
//! over the emulator's image of the program. No per-opcode semantics are guessed; correctness comes
//! from execution.

use std::collections::HashSet;

use iced_x86::{Decoder, DecoderOptions, Mnemonic, OpKind, Register};
use orress_analysis::{Block, Function, Isa, NameKind, Program};
use orress_sym::{Abi, SymError};

use crate::VmReport;

/// The outcome of concolically lifting a VM: the recovered key and the constraints behind it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct VmSolution {
    /// The interpreter function that was solved.
    pub func: u64,
    /// The input length the solve succeeded at.
    pub input_len: u32,
    /// The recovered input bytes (the key).
    pub key: Vec<u8>,
    /// Whether every captured constraint was satisfied (a self-verifying key).
    pub complete: bool,
    /// How many path constraints the symbolic run captured.
    pub constraints: usize,
    /// The lifted per-byte checks, rendered readably (e.g. `rol(in[0] ^ 0x3b, 1) == 0x9a`) — the
    /// logic the virtualized check performs, recovered by execution rather than pattern-matching.
    pub checks: Vec<String>,
    /// The constraints as SMT-LIB2, for an external solver.
    pub smt2: String,
}

/// Input lengths to try (the VM's length check rejects wrong lengths concretely and fast).
const MAX_LEN: u32 = 48;

/// Concolically solve a detected VM, recovering the key. Returns `None` if the interpreter's
/// verdict blocks can't be identified or no length yields a solution; [`try_solve`] says why.
pub fn solve(program: &Program, report: &VmReport) -> Option<VmSolution> {
    try_solve(program, report).ok()
}

/// How informative a failed attempt's error is: a real modelling gap (unsupported instruction,
/// symbolic address, fault) explains a failure better than a budget overrun, which in turn says
/// more than "this length hit an avoided block" (the expected outcome for every wrong length).
fn error_rank(e: &SymError) -> u8 {
    match e {
        SymError::HitAvoid(_) => 0,
        SymError::BudgetExhausted => 1,
        SymError::Unsupported { .. } | SymError::SymbolicAddress(_) | SymError::Fault(_) => 2,
    }
}

/// [`solve`], but on failure returns the most relevant reason: the highest-ranked symbolic
/// execution error seen across the tried input lengths (see `error_rank`), or an
/// [`SymError::Unsupported`] naming the precondition that failed (non-x86-64 program, no
/// enclosing function, no recognisable success/fail verdict, no constraints captured).
pub fn try_solve(program: &Program, report: &VmReport) -> Result<VmSolution, SymError> {
    let unsupported = |what: &str| SymError::Unsupported {
        addr: report.entry,
        what: what.to_string(),
    };
    // The symbolic executor and `decode_block` are x86-64 only.
    if program.isa != Isa::X64 {
        return Err(unsupported(&format!(
            "VM lifting for {:?} (x86-64 only)",
            program.isa
        )));
    }
    let func = program
        .function_containing(report.entry)
        .ok_or_else(|| unsupported("VM entry outside any function"))?;
    let abi = if program.memory.is_elf {
        Abi::SysV
    } else {
        Abi::Win64
    };

    let (target, avoid) = verdict_blocks(program, func)
        .ok_or_else(|| unsupported("interpreter without a recognisable success verdict"))?;

    // Place the symbolic input above every mapped region (clear of the program, its `.bss`
    // slack, and the stack `run_check` maps near 0x7fff_0000).
    let max_end = program
        .memory
        .regions
        .iter()
        .map(|r| r.start.saturating_add(r.len))
        .max()
        .unwrap_or(0);
    let mut input_base = max_end.saturating_add(0x1_0000) & !0xfff;
    // Keep clear of the scratch stack `run_check` maps just below 0x7fff_0000.
    if (0x7fe0_0000..0x8010_0000).contains(&input_base) {
        input_base = 0x8010_0000;
    }

    let hooks = import_hooks(program);
    let base_mem = emu_image(program);

    let mut best: Option<VmSolution> = None;
    let mut worst_err: Option<SymError> = None;
    for input_len in 1..=MAX_LEN {
        let mut mem = base_mem.clone();
        mem.map_zeroed(input_base, u64::from(input_len) + 16);
        let args = [input_base, u64::from(input_len)];
        let found = match orress_sym::solve_check(
            mem,
            func.entry,
            &args,
            input_base,
            input_len,
            target,
            avoid.clone(),
            hooks.clone(),
            abi,
        ) {
            Ok(f) => f,
            // Usually: this length drove execution into a doomed/avoided block — the wrong
            // length. Remember the most telling error in case no length works.
            Err(e) => {
                if worst_err
                    .as_ref()
                    .is_none_or(|w| error_rank(&e) > error_rank(w))
                {
                    worst_err = Some(e);
                }
                continue;
            }
        };
        let sol = VmSolution {
            func: func.entry,
            input_len,
            key: found.result.input,
            complete: found.result.complete,
            constraints: found.constraints,
            checks: found.checks,
            smt2: found.smt2,
        };
        // A complete solve with real constraints is the answer; otherwise keep the richest attempt.
        if sol.complete && sol.constraints > 0 {
            return Ok(sol);
        }
        if best
            .as_ref()
            .is_none_or(|b| sol.constraints > b.constraints)
        {
            best = Some(sol);
        }
    }
    match best.filter(|b| b.constraints > 0) {
        Some(b) => Ok(b),
        None => Err(worst_err
            .unwrap_or_else(|| unsupported("VM run that captured no input-dependent constraints"))),
    }
}

/// The success block to steer toward and the set of blocks to avoid. Success = the verdict block
/// that sets the return register to a non-zero constant and flows straight to `ret`; the avoid set
/// is every block from which that success block is unreachable (the "doomed" set), so steering an
/// input-dependent branch away from `avoid` keeps execution on the passing path even when the fail
/// edge reaches the failure return only through intermediate blocks.
fn verdict_blocks(program: &Program, func: &Function) -> Option<(u64, Vec<u64>)> {
    let target = func
        .blocks
        .iter()
        .filter(|b| reaches_ret_cleanly(program, func, b.start))
        .find(|b| matches!(verdict_const(program, b), Some(k) if k != 0))
        .map(|b| b.start)?;

    // Each block's successors, augmented with its recovered switch-table targets: a dispatcher's
    // register-indirect jump has its cases in `switch_tables`, and the analysis CFG may not carry
    // every one as a `succs` edge, so reachability has to consult the table directly.
    let succs_of = |b: &Block| -> Vec<u64> {
        let mut s: Vec<u64> = b.succs.iter().map(|e| e.target).collect();
        if let Some(cases) = b.insns.last().and_then(|a| program.switch_tables.get(a)) {
            s.extend(cases.iter().copied());
        }
        s
    };

    // Reverse reachability: the blocks from which `target` is reachable over successor edges.
    let mut can_reach: HashSet<u64> = HashSet::from([target]);
    let mut changed = true;
    while changed {
        changed = false;
        for b in &func.blocks {
            if !can_reach.contains(&b.start) && succs_of(b).iter().any(|t| can_reach.contains(t)) {
                can_reach.insert(b.start);
                changed = true;
            }
        }
    }
    let avoid = func
        .blocks
        .iter()
        .map(|b| b.start)
        .filter(|a| !can_reach.contains(a))
        .collect();
    Some((target, avoid))
}

/// The constant this block leaves in the return register (rax/eax/al), if its net effect is a
/// constant — `mov eax, k` or `xor eax, eax`. Used to classify success (non-zero) vs fail (zero).
fn verdict_const(program: &Program, b: &Block) -> Option<u64> {
    let mut k = None;
    for ins in decode_block(program, b) {
        let is_ret_reg = |r: Register| r.full_register() == Register::RAX;
        match ins.mnemonic() {
            Mnemonic::Mov if is_ret_reg(ins.op0_register()) => {
                k = matches!(
                    ins.op1_kind(),
                    OpKind::Immediate8
                        | OpKind::Immediate32
                        | OpKind::Immediate32to64
                        | OpKind::Immediate8to32
                        | OpKind::Immediate8to64
                )
                .then(|| ins.immediate(1));
            }
            Mnemonic::Xor
                if is_ret_reg(ins.op0_register()) && ins.op0_register() == ins.op1_register() =>
            {
                k = Some(0);
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    k
}

/// Whether `start` flows straight to a `ret` along single-successor edges without any further
/// write to the return register (so the constant a verdict block set still holds at the return).
fn reaches_ret_cleanly(program: &Program, func: &Function, start: u64) -> bool {
    let mut cur = start;
    for _ in 0..6 {
        let Some(b) = func.blocks.iter().find(|b| b.start == cur) else {
            return false;
        };
        if decode_block(program, b)
            .last()
            .is_some_and(|i| i.mnemonic() == Mnemonic::Ret)
        {
            return true;
        }
        if b.succs.len() != 1 {
            return false;
        }
        let next = b.succs[0].target;
        if let Some(nb) = func.blocks.iter().find(|b| b.start == next)
            && verdict_const(program, nb).is_none()
            && writes_ret_reg(program, nb)
        {
            return false; // an intervening block clobbers the return register
        }
        cur = next;
    }
    false
}

/// Whether the block writes the return register (rax/eax/al) at all.
fn writes_ret_reg(program: &Program, b: &Block) -> bool {
    decode_block(program, b).iter().any(|ins| {
        matches!(
            ins.mnemonic(),
            Mnemonic::Mov | Mnemonic::Xor | Mnemonic::Movzx | Mnemonic::Add | Mnemonic::Sub
        ) && ins.op0_register().full_register() == Register::RAX
    })
}

/// Decodes all instructions in a block from the program image.
fn decode_block(program: &Program, b: &Block) -> Vec<iced_x86::Instruction> {
    let Some(bytes) = program.memory.read(b.start, (b.end - b.start) as usize) else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    let mut dec = Decoder::with_ip(64, bytes, b.start, DecoderOptions::NONE);
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    while dec.can_decode() {
        out.push(dec.decode());
    }
    out
}

/// Zero-filled slack mapped after every file-backed region. The analysis image only carries a
/// section's file bytes, so a zero-initialised tail (`.bss`, a `.data` section's virtual
/// overhang) would otherwise be unmapped — and guest writes to unmapped memory fault.
const BSS_SLACK: u64 = 0x8000;

/// Builds an emulator memory image from the program's mapped regions (each followed by
/// `BSS_SLACK` zeroed bytes where nothing else is mapped). The shared seeding step for every
/// front end that runs a loaded program in `orress-emu` / `orress-sym`.
pub fn emu_image(program: &Program) -> orress_emu::Memory {
    let mut mem = orress_emu::Memory::new();
    for r in &program.memory.regions {
        if let Some(bytes) = program.memory.read(r.start, r.len as usize) {
            mem.write_bytes(r.start, bytes);
        }
    }
    // After all file bytes are in: `map_zeroed` only adds missing pages, never clears data.
    for r in &program.memory.regions {
        mem.map_zeroed(r.start.saturating_add(r.len), BSS_SLACK);
    }
    mem
}

/// Import stubs keyed by import address (both the IAT/GOT slot and any thunk named after the
/// import), so library calls return something sensible instead of faulting. The emulator and
/// the symbolic executor match a hooked slot on `call [slot]` / `jmp [slot]` as well as a direct
/// call to a hooked address. The name → stub mapping is [`orress_emu::stub_for`].
pub fn import_hooks(program: &Program) -> std::collections::HashMap<u64, orress_emu::Stub> {
    program
        .names
        .iter()
        .filter(|(_, n)| n.kind == NameKind::Import)
        .map(|(&addr, n)| (addr, orress_emu::stub_for(&n.text)))
        .collect()
}
```

`crates/orress-vm/src/tests.rs`:

```rs
use super::*;
use orress_analysis::{Block, Edge, EdgeKind, Function, FunctionKind};

fn block(start: u64, succs: &[u64]) -> Block {
    Block {
        start,
        end: start + 8,
        insns: vec![start],
        succs: succs
            .iter()
            .map(|&t| Edge {
                target: t,
                kind: EdgeKind::Jump,
            })
            .collect(),
    }
}

fn func(entry: u64, blocks: Vec<Block>) -> Function {
    Function {
        entry,
        kind: FunctionKind::Normal,
        blocks,
        calls: Vec::new(),
    }
}

/// A classic interpreter: one dispatcher that `n` handlers each branch back to, plus the dispatcher
/// fanning out to them.
fn vm_like(handlers: usize) -> Function {
    let dispatcher = 0x1000;
    let mut blocks = Vec::new();
    // The dispatcher branches out to every handler.
    let handler_addrs: Vec<u64> = (0..handlers).map(|i| 0x1100 + i as u64 * 0x20).collect();
    blocks.push(block(dispatcher, &handler_addrs));
    // Each handler does its work, then branches back to the dispatcher (a back edge).
    for &h in &handler_addrs {
        blocks.push(block(h, &[dispatcher]));
    }
    func(dispatcher, blocks)
}

#[test]
fn detects_an_interpreter_dispatch_loop() {
    let report = detect(&vm_like(20)).expect("a VM interpreter shape is detected");
    assert_eq!(report.dispatcher, 0x1000);
    assert_eq!(report.handlers, 20);
    assert_eq!(report.max_fan_in, 20); // all 20 handlers branch back
    assert!(report.confidence > 0.7, "confidence {}", report.confidence);
}

#[test]
fn small_functions_are_not_interpreters() {
    // A short linear function: a → b → c (3 blocks).
    let f = func(
        0x400,
        vec![
            block(0x400, &[0x408]),
            block(0x408, &[0x410]),
            block(0x410, &[]),
        ],
    );
    assert!(detect(&f).is_none());
}

#[test]
fn a_big_but_flat_function_is_not_an_interpreter() {
    // 20 blocks in a straight chain: no block has a high fan-in, and no back edge.
    let blocks: Vec<Block> = (0..20)
        .map(|i| block(0x1000 + i * 8, &[0x1000 + (i + 1) * 8]))
        .collect();
    assert!(detect(&func(0x1000, blocks)).is_none());
}

#[test]
fn a_simple_loop_is_not_an_interpreter() {
    // A 15-block function with one back edge but only a small fan-in (a normal loop, not dispatch).
    let mut blocks: Vec<Block> = (0..14)
        .map(|i| block(0x1000 + i * 8, &[0x1000 + (i + 1) * 8]))
        .collect();
    // Last block loops back to the top (fan-in of the head is only 2).
    blocks.push(block(0x1000 + 14 * 8, &[0x1000]));
    assert!(detect(&func(0x1000, blocks)).is_none());
}

#[test]
fn detects_a_split_dispatch_loop() {
    // The real compiled shape: the dispatcher D fans out to 10 handlers, each handler returns to a
    // separate loop header H, and H branches to D. The handlers don't jump to D directly, but they
    // *reach* it through H — so the detector must follow reachability, not just direct back edges.
    let (d, h) = (0x1000, 0x900);
    let handlers: Vec<u64> = (0..10).map(|i| 0x1100 + i * 0x20).collect();
    let mut blocks = vec![block(h, &[d]), block(d, &handlers)];
    for &x in &handlers {
        blocks.push(block(x, &[h]));
    }
    let report = detect(&func(h, blocks)).expect("a split dispatch loop is detected");
    assert_eq!(report.dispatcher, d);
    assert_eq!(report.handlers, 10);
}

#[test]
fn a_one_shot_switch_is_not_an_interpreter() {
    // A high-fan-out block whose cases do NOT loop back (an ordinary switch, not a dispatch loop):
    // the dispatcher fans out to 10 cases that each fall through to a common exit. No looping
    // handlers, so despite the fan-out it must not be flagged.
    let sw = 0x1000;
    let exit = 0x2000;
    let cases: Vec<u64> = (0..10).map(|i| 0x1100 + i * 0x20).collect();
    let mut blocks = vec![block(sw, &cases)];
    for &c in &cases {
        blocks.push(block(c, &[exit]));
    }
    blocks.push(block(exit, &[]));
    assert!(
        detect(&func(sw, blocks)).is_none(),
        "a one-shot switch must not be flagged"
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_sprawling_loop_with_few_handlers_is_not_an_interpreter() {
    // The library-code false positive: a big function (30 blocks) with a high-fan-in latch that 8
    // blocks branch back to, but the other ~21 blocks are a non-handler chain. High fan-in, but the
    // dispatch loop does not dominate the function (handler ratio 8/30 < 0.5), so it is not a VM.
    let latch = 0x1000;
    let mut blocks = vec![block(latch, &[0x1100])];
    // 8 handlers that each return to the latch (fan-in 8, well over MIN_FAN_IN).
    for i in 0..8u64 {
        blocks.push(block(0x1100 + i * 8, &[latch]));
    }
    // A long tail of ordinary blocks that are not handlers (they don't branch to the latch).
    for i in 0..21u64 {
        blocks.push(block(0x2000 + i * 8, &[0x2000 + (i + 1) * 8]));
    }
    let report = detect(&func(latch, blocks));
    assert!(
        report.is_none(),
        "a low-handler-ratio loop must not be flagged, got {report:?}"
    );
}

#[test]
fn more_handlers_means_higher_confidence() {
    // Both are interpreters (≥ MIN_BLOCKS), but the one with more handlers scores higher.
    let strong = detect(&vm_like(20)).expect("strong VM detected");
    let weak = detect(&vm_like(11)).expect("weak VM detected");
    assert!(
        strong.confidence > weak.confidence,
        "{} vs {}",
        strong.confidence,
        weak.confidence
    );
}

/// A blob shorter than the recovered extent (`Memory::read` stops at the region end) must not be
/// indexed past its end: the walk is bounded by the bytes actually read, and an operand run that
/// overhangs the end is clipped.
#[test]
fn bytecode_walk_is_bounded_by_the_blob() {
    let blob = [0x01, 0xaa, 0xbb, 0x02, 0xcc];
    // Opcode 1 takes two operand bytes, opcode 2 claims four (only one is left).
    let size = |op: u8| if op == 1 { 2 } else { 4 };
    let insns = walk_bytecode(&blob, size, |_| "op");
    assert_eq!(insns.len(), 2);
    assert_eq!(insns[0].operands, vec![0xaa, 0xbb]);
    assert_eq!(insns[1].offset, 3);
    assert_eq!(insns[1].operands, vec![0xcc]);
    assert!(walk_bytecode(&[], size, |_| "op").is_empty());
}
```
