`crates/orress-vm/tests/lift.rs`:

```rs
//! Program-level seeding and lifting: a hand-built x86-64 binary, analysed by `orress-analysis`,
//! run through the shared `emu_image` / `import_hooks` seeding.

use std::sync::Arc;

use iced_x86::code_asm::*;
use orress_analysis::Program;
use orress_emu::{Abi, Emulator};
use orress_loaders::{BinaryInfo, Format, Kind, NamedAddress, Perms, Section};

const BASE: u64 = 0x40_1000;
const DATA: u64 = 0x40_2000;
/// The import slot for `strcmp`. In the file image it holds 0 (like an unbound GOT/IAT entry).
const SLOT: u64 = DATA + 0x100;
const INPUT: u64 = 0x50_0000;

/// `check(s) { return strcmp(s, "hunter2") == 0 }` calling strcmp through its import slot
/// (`call [slot]`, as PE and `-fno-plt` ELF code does), in an analysable binary.
fn program(arch: &str, bits: u8) -> Program {
    let mut a = CodeAssembler::new(64).unwrap();
    a.mov(rsi, DATA).unwrap();
    a.call(qword_ptr(SLOT)).unwrap();
    a.test(eax, eax).unwrap();
    a.sete(al).unwrap();
    a.movzx(eax, al).unwrap();
    a.ret().unwrap();
    let mut code = a.assemble(BASE).unwrap();
    code.resize(0x100, 0xcc);

    let mut data = vec![0u8; 0x200];
    data[..8].copy_from_slice(b"hunter2\0");

    let mut file = vec![0u8; 0x200]; // headers
    file.extend(&code); // offset 0x200 -> BASE
    file.extend(&data); // offset 0x300 -> DATA

    let section = |name: &str, offset, size, address, execute: bool| Section {
        name: name.into(),
        offset,
        file_size: size,
        address,
        virtual_size: size,
        perms: Perms {
            read: true,
            write: !execute,
            execute,
        },
        entropy: None,
    };
    let info = BinaryInfo {
        format: Format::Elf,
        kind: Kind::Executable,
        arch: arch.into(),
        bits: Some(bits),
        entry: Some(BASE),
        image_base: 0x40_0000,
        sections: vec![
            section(".text", 0x200, 0x100, BASE, true),
            section(".data", 0x300, 0x200, DATA, false),
        ],
        import_slots: vec![NamedAddress {
            address: SLOT,
            name: "strcmp".into(),
        }],
        function_symbols: vec![NamedAddress {
            address: BASE,
            name: "check".into(),
        }],
        ..BinaryInfo::default()
    };
    Program::analyze(&info, Arc::new(file), &[]).expect("supported architecture")
}

/// The hook is keyed by the import *slot*; `call [slot]` loads the slot's file contents (0 here),
/// so before the fix execution jumped to address 0 instead of running the strcmp stub.
#[test]
fn a_call_through_an_import_slot_runs_the_stub() {
    let p = program("x86-64", 64);
    let hooks = orress_vm::import_hooks(&p);
    assert_eq!(hooks.get(&SLOT), Some(&orress_emu::Stub::Strcmp));

    let run = |input: &[u8]| {
        let mut emu = Emulator::new();
        emu.mem = orress_vm::emu_image(&p);
        for (&addr, stub) in &hooks {
            emu.hook(addr, stub.clone());
        }
        emu.map(INPUT, input);
        emu.call(BASE, &[INPUT], Abi::SysV).unwrap()
    };
    assert_eq!(run(b"hunter2\0"), 1);
    assert_eq!(run(b"letmein\0"), 0);
}

/// The image maps a zeroed tail after each file-backed region (`.bss`), so guest writes there
/// work now that writes to unmapped memory fault.
#[test]
fn the_image_maps_a_zeroed_bss_tail() {
    let p = program("x86-64", 64);
    let mut mem = orress_vm::emu_image(&p);
    assert_eq!(
        mem.read(DATA, 8).unwrap(),
        u64::from_le_bytes(*b"hunter2\0")
    );
    mem.write(DATA + 0x200, 0x1234, 8).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(mem.read(DATA + 0x200, 8).unwrap(), 0x1234);
    assert!(mem.write(0, 1, 1).is_err(), "null stays unmapped");
}

/// VM lifting decodes and executes x86-64 only; any other ISA is refused with a reason rather
/// than mis-decoded.
#[test]
fn try_solve_rejects_non_x64_programs() {
    let p = program("x86 (32-bit)", 32);
    let report = orress_vm::VmReport {
        entry: BASE,
        dispatcher: BASE,
        blocks: 0,
        handlers: 0,
        max_fan_in: 0,
        confidence: 1.0,
    };
    match orress_vm::try_solve(&p, &report) {
        Err(orress_sym::SymError::Unsupported { what, .. }) => {
            assert!(what.contains("x86-64"), "{what}");
        }
        other => panic!("expected Unsupported, got {:?}", other.map(|s| s.key)),
    }
    assert!(orress_vm::solve(&p, &report).is_none());
}
```

`crates/orress-wasm/examples/wasm_info.rs`:

```rs
//! Prints a WebAssembly module's overview and the head of its WAT disassembly.
//!
//! Run with: `cargo run -p orress-wasm --example wasm_info -- path/to/module.wasm`

fn main() {
    let path = std::env::args()
        .nth(1)
        .expect("usage: wasm_info <file.wasm>");
    let data = std::fs::read(&path).expect("read file");
    if !orress_wasm::is_wasm(&data) {
        eprintln!("{path}: not a WebAssembly module");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
    let m = orress_wasm::parse(&data);
    println!("{} — {}", path, m.summary());
    if let Some(e) = &m.parse_error {
        println!("parse error: {e}");
    }
    println!("\nimports:");
    for i in m.imports.iter().take(10) {
        println!("  {} {}.{}", i.kind.label(), i.module, i.name);
    }
    println!("\nexports:");
    for e in m.exports.iter().take(10) {
        println!("  {} {} [{}]", e.kind, e.name, e.index);
    }
    println!("\nfirst functions:");
    for f in m.functions.iter().take(8) {
        println!(
            "  #{} {} {} ({} locals, {} ops, {} bytes)",
            f.index,
            f.name.as_deref().unwrap_or("—"),
            f.sig.as_ref().map(|s| s.signature()).unwrap_or_default(),
            f.locals,
            f.ops,
            f.size
        );
    }

    match orress_wasm::disassemble(&data) {
        Ok(wat) => {
            println!("\nWAT (first 20 lines):");
            for line in wat.lines().take(20) {
                println!("  {line}");
            }
        }
        Err(e) => println!("disassemble failed: {e}"),
    }
}
```

`crates/orress-wasm/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! WebAssembly loading for ORRESS: turn a `.wasm` module into a structured overview (types,
//! imports, functions with resolved signatures, exports, memories, globals, data segments) and a
//! readable **WAT** disassembly. Pure Rust, built on the `wasm-tools` parser/printer. It never
//! runs the module and tolerates truncated/hostile input — parse errors are recorded, not fatal,
//! so the overview is always populated with whatever was read before the failure.
//!
//! WASM shows up in CTF (browser/crypto challenges, custom VMs compiled to wasm) and increasingly
//! in malware; this is the first managed/bytecode format in ORRESS's M10 "managed & exotic" track.

use wasmparser::{CompositeInnerType, ExternalKind, Operator, Parser, Payload, TypeRef};

/// A function type (signature): parameter and result value types, as WAT type names.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct FuncType {
    pub params: Vec<String>,
    pub results: Vec<String>,
}

impl FuncType {
    /// A compact `(i32, i32) -> i32` rendering.
    pub fn signature(&self) -> String {
        let params = self.params.join(", ");
        let results = match self.results.len() {
            0 => "()".to_string(),
            1 => self.results[0].clone(),
            _ => format!("({})", self.results.join(", ")),
        };
        format!("({params}) -> {results}")
    }
}

/// What an import brings in.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ImportKind {
    /// A function, with its type-section index.
    Func(u32),
    Table,
    Memory,
    Global,
    Tag,
}

impl ImportKind {
    pub fn label(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Func(_) => "func",
            Self::Table => "table",
            Self::Memory => "memory",
            Self::Global => "global",
            Self::Tag => "tag",
        }
    }
}

/// An imported entity (`module.name`).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Import {
    pub module: String,
    pub name: String,
    pub kind: ImportKind,
}

/// An exported entity.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Export {
    pub name: String,
    /// `func` / `table` / `memory` / `global` / `tag`.
    pub kind: &'static str,
    pub index: u32,
}

/// A linear memory declaration.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Memory {
    pub min_pages: u64,
    pub max_pages: Option<u64>,
    pub memory64: bool,
    pub shared: bool,
}

/// A global declaration.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Global {
    pub ty: String,
    pub mutable: bool,
}

/// A defined (code-section) function.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Function {
    /// Absolute function index (imported functions come first).
    pub index: u32,
    /// Name from the `name` custom section or an export, if any.
    pub name: Option<String>,
    pub type_index: u32,
    pub sig: Option<FuncType>,
    /// Number of declared local slots (beyond parameters).
    pub locals: u32,
    /// Number of operators in the body.
    pub ops: u32,
    /// Size of the function body in bytes.
    pub size: u32,
}

/// A parsed WebAssembly module overview.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct WasmModule {
    pub version: u16,
    /// Function types from the type section (index-aligned; non-function types are empty).
    pub types: Vec<FuncType>,
    pub imports: Vec<Import>,
    pub imported_func_count: u32,
    pub functions: Vec<Function>,
    pub exports: Vec<Export>,
    pub memories: Vec<Memory>,
    pub globals: Vec<Global>,
    pub table_count: u32,
    pub data_segments: u32,
    pub start_func: Option<u32>,
    /// Custom sections as `(name, byte length)`.
    pub custom_sections: Vec<(String, usize)>,
    /// Whether a `name` custom section was present (debug names available).
    pub has_names: bool,
    /// Set if this is a component rather than a core module (overview will be sparse).
    pub is_component: bool,
    /// A parse error that stopped the walk early; the overview holds what was read before it.
    pub parse_error: Option<String>,
}

impl WasmModule {
    /// Total function count (imported + defined).
    pub fn total_funcs(&self) -> u32 {
        self.imported_func_count + self.functions.len() as u32
    }

    /// A short one-line summary for a header.
    pub fn summary(&self) -> String {
        format!(
            "{} function(s) ({} imported, {} defined) · {} export(s) · {} memor{} · {} global(s)",
            self.total_funcs(),
            self.imported_func_count,
            self.functions.len(),
            self.exports.len(),
            self.memories.len(),
            if self.memories.len() == 1 { "y" } else { "ies" },
            self.globals.len(),
        )
    }
}

/// Returns true if `data` starts with the WebAssembly magic (`\0asm`).
pub fn is_wasm(data: &[u8]) -> bool {
    data.len() >= 4 && data[..4] == [0x00, 0x61, 0x73, 0x6d]
}

fn valtype_name(t: &wasmparser::ValType) -> String {
    t.to_string()
}

/// Parses a WebAssembly module into an overview. Never panics on bad input; a parse failure is
/// recorded in [`WasmModule::parse_error`] and the partial overview is returned.
pub fn parse(data: &[u8]) -> WasmModule {
    let mut m = WasmModule::default();
    // Type indices for each defined function, in code order.
    let mut func_type_indices: Vec<u32> = Vec::new();
    // Function names by absolute index (from the name section).
    let mut names: std::collections::BTreeMap<u32, String> = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();

    for payload in Parser::new(0).parse_all(data) {
        let payload = match payload {
            Ok(p) => p,
            Err(e) => {
                m.parse_error = Some(e.to_string());
                break;
            }
        };
        match payload {
            Payload::Version { num, encoding, .. } => {
                m.version = num;
                m.is_component = matches!(encoding, wasmparser::Encoding::Component);
            }
            Payload::TypeSection(reader) => {
                for group in reader {
                    let Ok(group) = group else { continue };
                    for sub in group.types() {
                        let ft = match &sub.composite_type.inner {
                            CompositeInnerType::Func(f) => FuncType {
                                params: f.params().iter().map(valtype_name).collect(),
                                results: f.results().iter().map(valtype_name).collect(),
                            },
                            // Array/struct/cont types (GC proposal): keep the index aligned.
                            _ => FuncType::default(),
                        };
                        m.types.push(ft);
                    }
                }
            }
            Payload::ImportSection(reader) => {
                for imp in reader {
                    let Ok(imp) = imp else { continue };
                    let kind = match imp.ty {
                        TypeRef::Func(i) => {
                            m.imported_func_count += 1;
                            ImportKind::Func(i)
                        }
                        TypeRef::Table(_) => ImportKind::Table,
                        TypeRef::Memory(_) => ImportKind::Memory,
                        TypeRef::Global(_) => ImportKind::Global,
                        TypeRef::Tag(_) => ImportKind::Tag,
                    };
                    m.imports.push(Import {
                        module: imp.module.to_string(),
                        name: imp.name.to_string(),
                        kind,
                    });
                }
            }
            Payload::FunctionSection(reader) => {
                for ti in reader.into_iter().flatten() {
                    func_type_indices.push(ti);
                }
            }
            Payload::TableSection(reader) => {
                m.table_count = reader.count();
            }
            Payload::MemorySection(reader) => {
                for mem in reader.into_iter().flatten() {
                    m.memories.push(Memory {
                        min_pages: mem.initial,
                        max_pages: mem.maximum,
                        memory64: mem.memory64,
                        shared: mem.shared,
                    });
                }
            }
            Payload::GlobalSection(reader) => {
                for g in reader.into_iter().flatten() {
                    m.globals.push(Global {
                        ty: valtype_name(&g.ty.content_type),
                        mutable: g.ty.mutable,
                    });
                }
            }
            Payload::ExportSection(reader) => {
                for e in reader {
                    let Ok(e) = e else { continue };
                    let kind = match e.kind {
                        ExternalKind::Func => "func",
                        ExternalKind::Table => "table",
                        ExternalKind::Memory => "memory",
                        ExternalKind::Global => "global",
                        ExternalKind::Tag => "tag",
                    };
                    m.exports.push(Export {
                        name: e.name.to_string(),
                        kind,
                        index: e.index,
                    });
                }
            }
            Payload::StartSection { func, .. } => m.start_func = Some(func),
            Payload::DataSection(reader) => m.data_segments = reader.count(),
            Payload::CodeSectionEntry(body) => {
                let code_idx = m.functions.len();
                let index = m.imported_func_count + code_idx as u32;
                let type_index = func_type_indices.get(code_idx).copied().unwrap_or(0);
                let mut locals = 0u32;
                if let Ok(lr) = body.get_locals_reader() {
                    for (count, _) in lr.into_iter().flatten() {
                        locals = locals.saturating_add(count);
                    }
                }
                let mut ops = 0u32;
                if let Ok(or) = body.get_operators_reader() {
                    for op in or.into_iter() {
                        match op {
                            Ok(_) => ops = ops.saturating_add(1),
                            Err(_) => break,
                        }
                    }
                }
                let range = body.range();
                let sig = m.types.get(type_index as usize).cloned();
                m.functions.push(Function {
                    index,
                    name: None,
                    type_index,
                    sig,
                    locals,
                    ops,
                    size: (range.end - range.start) as u32,
                });
            }
            Payload::CustomSection(c) => {
                m.custom_sections
                    .push((c.name().to_string(), c.data().len()));
                if c.name() == "name" {
                    m.has_names = true;
                    parse_function_names(c.data(), c.data_offset(), &mut names);
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }

    // Attach names: prefer the name section, fall back to exported function names.
    for f in &mut m.functions {
        if let Some(n) = names.get(&f.index) {
            f.name = Some(n.clone());
        }
    }
    if m.functions.iter().any(|f| f.name.is_none()) {
        for e in &m.exports {
            if e.kind == "func"
                && let Some(f) = m.functions.iter_mut().find(|f| f.index == e.index)
                && f.name.is_none()
            {
                f.name = Some(e.name.clone());
            }
        }
    }
    m
}

/// Parses the function-name subsection of the `name` custom section (best-effort).
fn parse_function_names(
    data: &[u8],
    offset: usize,
    out: &mut std::collections::BTreeMap<u32, String>,
) {
    use wasmparser::{BinaryReader, Name, NameSectionReader};
    let reader = NameSectionReader::new(BinaryReader::new(data, offset));
    for sub in reader {
        let Ok(sub) = sub else { break };
        if let Name::Function(map) = sub {
            for n in map.into_iter().flatten() {
                out.insert(n.index, n.name.to_string());
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Disassembles the whole module to WAT text, with byte-offset comments (so matches in the hex
/// view line up with instructions). Returns an error message if the module can't be printed.
pub fn disassemble(data: &[u8]) -> Result<String, String> {
    let mut out = String::new();
    let mut cfg = wasmprinter::Config::new();
    cfg.print_offsets(true);
    cfg.print(data, &mut wasmprinter::PrintFmtWrite(&mut out))
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    Ok(out)
}

/// Disassembles a single defined function to a list of `(offset, text)` operator lines. `index`
/// is the absolute function index. Returns an error if the index isn't a defined function or the
/// body can't be read.
pub fn disassemble_function(data: &[u8], index: u32) -> Result<Vec<(usize, String)>, String> {
    let mut imported_funcs = 0u32;
    let mut code_idx = 0u32;
    for payload in Parser::new(0).parse_all(data) {
        let payload = payload.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        match payload {
            Payload::ImportSection(reader) => {
                for imp in reader.into_iter().flatten() {
                    if matches!(imp.ty, TypeRef::Func(_)) {
                        imported_funcs += 1;
                    }
                }
            }
            Payload::CodeSectionEntry(body) => {
                let abs = imported_funcs + code_idx;
                code_idx += 1;
                if abs != index {
                    continue;
                }
                let reader = body.get_operators_reader().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
                let mut lines = Vec::new();
                let mut depth = 0i32;
                for item in reader.into_iter_with_offsets() {
                    let (op, off) = item.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
                    if matches!(op, Operator::End | Operator::Else) {
                        depth = (depth - 1).max(0);
                    }
                    let indent = "  ".repeat(depth as usize);
                    lines.push((off, format!("{indent}{}", mnemonic(&op))));
                    if matches!(
                        op,
                        Operator::Block { .. }
                            | Operator::Loop { .. }
                            | Operator::If { .. }
                            | Operator::Else
                    ) {
                        depth += 1;
                    }
                }
                return Ok(lines);
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    Err(format!("no defined function at index {index}"))
}

/// Renders an operator as a WAT-like mnemonic (`local.get 0`, `i32.const 42`, `call 3`, …).
fn mnemonic(op: &Operator) -> String {
    use Operator::*;
    match op {
        LocalGet { local_index } => format!("local.get {local_index}"),
        LocalSet { local_index } => format!("local.set {local_index}"),
        LocalTee { local_index } => format!("local.tee {local_index}"),
        GlobalGet { global_index } => format!("global.get {global_index}"),
        GlobalSet { global_index } => format!("global.set {global_index}"),
        I32Const { value } => format!("i32.const {value}"),
        I64Const { value } => format!("i64.const {value}"),
        F32Const { value } => format!("f32.const {:#x}", value.bits()),
        F64Const { value } => format!("f64.const {:#x}", value.bits()),
        Call { function_index } => format!("call {function_index}"),
        CallIndirect { type_index, .. } => format!("call_indirect (type {type_index})"),
        Br { relative_depth } => format!("br {relative_depth}"),
        BrIf { relative_depth } => format!("br_if {relative_depth}"),
        _ => {
            // Fall back to the debug form, turned into a wasm-ish mnemonic:
            // `I32Add` -> `i32.add`, `MemoryGrow { .. }` -> `memory.grow ...`.
            let dbg = format!("{op:?}");
            debug_to_mnemonic(&dbg)
        }
    }
}

/// Turns an `Operator` debug string into a lowercase, dotted WAT-ish mnemonic.
fn debug_to_mnemonic(dbg: &str) -> String {
    // Split off any `{ fields }` payload.
    let (head, tail) = match dbg.split_once(" {") {
        Some((h, t)) => (h, Some(t.trim_end_matches('}').trim())),
        None => (dbg, None),
    };
    let mnem = split_camel(head);
    match tail {
        Some(t) if !t.is_empty() => format!("{mnem} ({t})"),
        _ => mnem,
    }
}

/// `I32TruncF64S` -> `i32.trunc_f64_s` (heuristic: dot after a leading type prefix, else snake).
fn split_camel(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    let mut first_boundary_done = false;
    let chars: Vec<char> = s.chars().collect();
    for (i, &c) in chars.iter().enumerate() {
        if c.is_ascii_uppercase() && i > 0 {
            // First boundary becomes a dot (type.op), later boundaries become underscores.
            if !first_boundary_done {
                out.push('.');
                first_boundary_done = true;
            } else {
                out.push('_');
            }
        }
        out.push(c.to_ascii_lowercase());
    }
    out
}
```

```rs
use super::*;
use wasm_encoder::{
    CodeSection, EntityType, ExportKind, ExportSection, Function, FunctionSection, GlobalSection,
    GlobalType, ImportSection, Instruction, MemorySection, MemoryType, Module, NameSection,
    TypeSection, ValType,
};

/// The canonical hand-assembled "add two i32s" module (41 bytes), exported as `add`.
const ADDER: &[u8] = &[
    0x00, 0x61, 0x73, 0x6d, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, // \0asm, version 1
    0x01, 0x07, 0x01, 0x60, 0x02, 0x7f, 0x7f, 0x01, 0x7f, // type: (i32,i32)->i32
    0x03, 0x02, 0x01, 0x00, // function: 1 func, type 0
    0x07, 0x07, 0x01, 0x03, b'a', b'd', b'd', 0x00, 0x00, // export "add" func 0
    0x0a, 0x09, 0x01, 0x07, 0x00, 0x20, 0x00, 0x20, 0x01, 0x6a,
    0x0b, // code: local.get 0/1; i32.add
];

#[test]
fn detects_magic() {
    assert!(is_wasm(ADDER));
    assert!(!is_wasm(b"MZ\x90\x00"));
    assert!(!is_wasm(b"no"));
}

#[test]
fn parses_the_adder() {
    let m = parse(ADDER);
    assert!(m.parse_error.is_none(), "{:?}", m.parse_error);
    assert_eq!(m.version, 1);
    assert!(!m.is_component);
    assert_eq!(m.types.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(m.types[0].signature(), "(i32, i32) -> i32");
    assert_eq!(m.imported_func_count, 0);
    assert_eq!(m.functions.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(m.total_funcs(), 1);

    let f = &m.functions[0];
    assert_eq!(f.index, 0);
    assert_eq!(f.type_index, 0);
    assert_eq!(f.locals, 0);
    // local.get, local.get, i32.add, end
    assert_eq!(f.ops, 4);
    // Name comes from the export.
    assert_eq!(f.name.as_deref(), Some("add"));

    assert_eq!(m.exports.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(m.exports[0].name, "add");
    assert_eq!(m.exports[0].kind, "func");
}

#[test]
fn disassembles_adder_to_wat() {
    let wat = disassemble(ADDER).unwrap();
    assert!(wat.contains("i32.add"), "{wat}");
    assert!(wat.contains("(export \"add\""), "{wat}");
    assert!(wat.contains("local.get"), "{wat}");
}

#[test]
fn disassembles_a_single_function() {
    let lines = disassemble_function(ADDER, 0).unwrap();
    let text: Vec<&str> = lines.iter().map(|(_, t)| t.trim()).collect();
    assert_eq!(text, vec!["local.get 0", "local.get 1", "i32.add", "end"]);
    // Offsets are monotonically increasing and within the file.
    assert!(lines.windows(2).all(|w| w[0].0 < w[1].0));
    assert!(lines.iter().all(|(off, _)| *off < ADDER.len()));
}

#[test]
fn records_parse_error_on_truncation() {
    // Valid header, then a bogus section id/length.
    let bad = [0x00, 0x61, 0x73, 0x6d, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 0x40];
    let m = parse(&bad);
    assert_eq!(m.version, 1);
    assert!(m.parse_error.is_some());
}

/// Build a richer module with wasm-encoder: an imported function, a memory, a mutable global,
/// two defined functions (one named via the name section), and exports.
fn rich_module() -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut types = TypeSection::new();
    types.ty().function([ValType::I32], [ValType::I32]); // type 0: (i32)->i32
    types.ty().function([], []); // type 1: ()->()

    let mut imports = ImportSection::new();
    imports.import("env", "log", EntityType::Function(0)); // imported func 0

    let mut funcs = FunctionSection::new();
    funcs.function(0); // defined func 1: (i32)->i32
    funcs.function(1); // defined func 2: ()->()

    let mut mems = MemorySection::new();
    mems.memory(MemoryType {
        minimum: 1,
        maximum: Some(16),
        memory64: false,
        shared: false,
        page_size_log2: None,
    });

    let mut globals = GlobalSection::new();
    globals.global(
        GlobalType {
            val_type: ValType::I32,
            mutable: true,
            shared: false,
        },
        &wasm_encoder::ConstExpr::i32_const(0),
    );

    let mut exports = ExportSection::new();
    exports.export("run", ExportKind::Func, 1);
    exports.export("mem", ExportKind::Memory, 0);

    let mut code = CodeSection::new();
    let mut f1 = Function::new([(1, ValType::I32)]); // one i32 local
    f1.instruction(&Instruction::LocalGet(0));
    f1.instruction(&Instruction::Call(0)); // call imported log
    f1.instruction(&Instruction::LocalGet(0));
    f1.instruction(&Instruction::End);
    code.function(&f1);
    let mut f2 = Function::new([]);
    f2.instruction(&Instruction::End);
    code.function(&f2);

    let mut names = NameSection::new();
    let mut fnames = wasm_encoder::NameMap::new();
    fnames.append(2, "do_nothing"); // name for defined func at absolute index 2
    names.functions(&fnames);

    let mut module = Module::new();
    module.section(&types);
    module.section(&imports);
    module.section(&funcs);
    module.section(&mems);
    module.section(&globals);
    module.section(&exports);
    module.section(&code);
    module.section(&names);
    module.finish()
}

#[test]
fn parses_rich_module() {
    let bytes = rich_module();
    let m = parse(&bytes);
    assert!(m.parse_error.is_none(), "{:?}", m.parse_error);

    assert_eq!(m.imported_func_count, 1);
    assert_eq!(m.functions.len(), 2);
    assert_eq!(m.total_funcs(), 3);

    assert_eq!(m.imports.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(m.imports[0].module, "env");
    assert_eq!(m.imports[0].name, "log");
    assert_eq!(m.imports[0].kind.label(), "func");

    assert_eq!(m.memories.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(m.memories[0].min_pages, 1);
    assert_eq!(m.memories[0].max_pages, Some(16));

    assert_eq!(m.globals.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(m.globals[0].ty, "i32");
    assert!(m.globals[0].mutable);

    // Defined func at absolute index 1 is exported as "run".
    let run = m.functions.iter().find(|f| f.index == 1).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(run.name.as_deref(), Some("run"));
    assert_eq!(run.sig.as_ref().unwrap().signature(), "(i32) -> i32");

    // Defined func at absolute index 2 gets its name from the name section.
    assert!(m.has_names);
    let nothing = m.functions.iter().find(|f| f.index == 2).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(nothing.name.as_deref(), Some("do_nothing"));
}

#[test]
fn disassembles_function_with_import_offset() {
    let bytes = rich_module();
    // Absolute index 1 is the first *defined* function (import occupies index 0).
    let lines = disassemble_function(&bytes, 1).unwrap();
    let text: Vec<&str> = lines.iter().map(|(_, t)| t.trim()).collect();
    assert_eq!(text, vec!["local.get 0", "call 0", "local.get 0", "end"]);
}

#[test]
fn mnemonic_fallback_formats_ops() {
    assert_eq!(debug_to_mnemonic("I32Add"), "i32.add");
    assert_eq!(debug_to_mnemonic("Nop"), "nop");
    assert_eq!(
        debug_to_mnemonic("MemoryGrow { mem: 0 }"),
        "memory.grow (mem: 0)"
    );
    assert_eq!(debug_to_mnemonic("I32TruncF64S"), "i32.trunc_f64_s");
}
```

```rs
//! The workspace, modeled on Zed: a center area of split panes with tabs, plus a left,
//! right and bottom dock. Each of the four areas is its own `egui_dock` tree, so any of
//! them can hold several tabs and be split further. The whole layout is serializable
//! and restored on the next start.

mod views;

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use egui::{Id, Ui};
use egui_dock::{DockArea, DockState, NodeIndex, NodePath, SurfaceIndex};
use orress_actions::{ActionId, ActionRegistry, KeyContext, Keymap};
use orress_project::DocStore;
use orress_views::{DocView, ViewCommand, ViewRequest, ViewState};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

/// What a tab shows.
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum TabKind {
    Welcome,
    Academy,
    /// The running lesson (right dock).
    Lesson,
    /// The Academy's CPU simulator.
    Simulator,
    /// Data transforms (decode, decrypt, decompress).
    Workbench,
    Keybindings,
    Notes {
        text: String,
    },
    /// A view of an open file.
    Doc {
        path: PathBuf,
        view: DocView,
        #[serde(skip)]
        state: Box<ViewState>,
    },
    /// A code editor buffer (center). `path` is None for a new untitled file.
    Editor {
        #[serde(default)]
        path: Option<PathBuf>,
        #[serde(skip)]
        state: Box<orress_views::EditorState>,
    },
    /// Cross-references of the current file (follows the focused document).
    Xrefs,
    /// The decompiler (right dock): the function under the cursor as Rust-style code.
    Decompiler,
    /// The machine-code debugger (bottom dock).
    Debugger,
    /// The emulator: run a function, side-channel solve.
    Emulator,
    /// The shellcode workbench: decode, disassemble, emulate a code blob.
    Shellcode,
    /// Static malware triage report.
    Triage,
    /// YARA workbench.
    Yara,
    /// WebAssembly module overview + WAT disassembly.
    Wasm,
    /// Python bytecode (.pyc) code-object tree + disassembly.
    Pyc,
    /// Java class file: constant pool, fields, methods + JVM disassembly.
    Java,
    /// ZIP/JAR archive: entries, manifest, open .class members.
    Archive,
    /// Resource extractor: native resources, embedded files, sections and overlay.
    Resources,
    /// Exploit console: pwntools-style scripting over the open binary.
    Exploit,
    /// glibc heap visualizer (chunks and bins).
    Heap,
    /// ROP gadget finder.
    Gadgets,
    /// JavaScript deobfuscation / beautify / string extraction.
    Js,
    /// .NET assembly metadata: types, methods, user strings.
    DotNet,
    /// AI assistant (Claude CLI / offline).
    Assistant,
    /// Dynamic-analysis sandbox (safety gate + launcher).
    Sandbox,
    /// Challenge Workbench: author, test and submit a user-made CTF challenge to the site.
    ChallengeWorkbench,
    ProjectTree,
    Explain,
    Inspector,
    /// User-defined types: declare structs/unions/enums/typedefs and see their layout.
    Types,
    /// Extension manager: installed extensions, install/uninstall.
    Extensions,
    /// Team collaboration: shared project over a relay, presence/follow, claims, chat, CTF.
    Collaboration,
    /// Binary diff: BinDiff-style function matching between the open binary and another.
    Diff,
    /// Scripting console: run a Rhai script against the open binary's analysis.
    Script,
    /// The integrated terminal (a real shell).
    Terminal,
    /// Build/run task output.
    Output,
    /// Source-level debugger (DAP).
    DebugSource,
    Problems,
    /// Retired (it was a placeholder). Kept only so layouts saved by older versions still load;
    /// [`Workspace::forget_open_files`] drops it at startup and nothing opens it.
    Jobs,
}

/// What to do with unsaved changes when closing an editor tab.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum CloseChoice {
    Save,
    Discard,
    Cancel,
}

/// A tab title for an editor before its buffer is created.
fn editor_title(path: Option<&Path>) -> String {
    path.and_then(|p| p.file_name())
        .map(|n| n.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
        .unwrap_or_else(|| "untitled".into())
}

impl TabKind {
    pub fn title(&self) -> String {
        match self {
            Self::Welcome => "Welcome".into(),
            Self::Academy => "Academy".into(),
            Self::Lesson => "Lesson".into(),
            Self::Simulator => "CPU Simulator".into(),
            Self::Workbench => "Workbench".into(),
            Self::Keybindings => "Keybindings".into(),
            Self::Notes { .. } => "Notes".into(),
            Self::Doc { path, view, .. } => {
                format!("{} · {}", orress_project::file_name(path), view.name())
            }
            Self::Editor { path, state } => state
                .title()
                .unwrap_or_else(|| editor_title(path.as_deref())),
            Self::Xrefs => "Cross-references".into(),
            Self::Decompiler => "Decompiler".into(),
            Self::Debugger => "Debugger".into(),
            Self::Emulator => "Emulator".into(),
            Self::Shellcode => "Shellcode".into(),
            Self::Triage => "Triage".into(),
            Self::Yara => "YARA".into(),
            Self::Wasm => "WASM".into(),
            Self::Pyc => "Python".into(),
            Self::Java => "Java".into(),
            Self::Archive => "Archive".into(),
            Self::Resources => "Resources".into(),
            Self::Exploit => "Exploit".into(),
            Self::Heap => "Heap".into(),
            Self::Gadgets => "Gadgets".into(),
            Self::Js => "JavaScript".into(),
            Self::DotNet => ".NET".into(),
            Self::Assistant => "Assistant".into(),
            Self::Sandbox => "Sandbox".into(),
            Self::ChallengeWorkbench => "Challenge Workbench".into(),
            Self::ProjectTree => "Project".into(),
            Self::Explain => "Explain".into(),
            Self::Inspector => "Inspector".into(),
            Self::Types => "Types".into(),
            Self::Extensions => "Extensions".into(),
            Self::Collaboration => "Collaboration".into(),
            Self::Diff => "Binary diff".into(),
            Self::Script => "Scripting".into(),
            Self::Terminal => "Terminal".into(),
            Self::Output => "Output".into(),
            Self::DebugSource => "Debug".into(),
            Self::Problems => "Problems".into(),
            Self::Jobs => "Jobs".into(),
        }
    }

    pub fn key_context(&self) -> KeyContext {
        match self {
            Self::Doc {
                view: DocView::Hex, ..
            } => KeyContext::Hex,
            Self::Doc {
                view: DocView::Disassembly,
                ..
            } => KeyContext::Disassembly,
            Self::Doc {
                view: DocView::Graph,
                ..
            } => KeyContext::Graph,
            Self::Editor { .. } => KeyContext::Editor,
            Self::Decompiler => KeyContext::Decompiler,
            // Both debuggers take F5 / F10 / F11 while focused.
            Self::Debugger | Self::DebugSource => KeyContext::Debugger,
            Self::Notes { .. } => KeyContext::Notes,
            Self::Terminal => KeyContext::Terminal,
            _ => KeyContext::Workspace,
        }
    }

    /// The area a tab of this kind opens in by default.
    pub fn home(&self) -> Slot {
        match self {
            Self::ProjectTree => Slot::Left,
            Self::Explain | Self::Inspector | Self::Lesson | Self::Decompiler | Self::Assistant => {
                Slot::Right
            }
            Self::Xrefs
            | Self::Terminal
            | Self::Problems
            | Self::Jobs
            | Self::Debugger
            | Self::Output
            | Self::DebugSource => Slot::Bottom,
            _ => Slot::Center,
        }
    }

    /// Whether opening this kind again should focus the existing tab instead.
    fn same_view(&self, other: &TabKind) -> bool {
        match (self, other) {
            (Self::Notes { .. }, _) | (_, Self::Notes { .. }) => false,
            // New (untitled) editors are always separate; a path focuses its tab.
            (Self::Editor { path: a, .. }, Self::Editor { path: b, .. }) => a.is_some() && a == b,
            (Self::Editor { .. }, _) | (_, Self::Editor { .. }) => false,
            (
                Self::Doc {
                    path: a, view: va, ..
                },
                Self::Doc {
                    path: b, view: vb, ..
                },
            ) => a == b && va == vb,
            _ => std::mem::discriminant(self) == std::mem::discriminant(other),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Tab {
    id: u64,
    pub kind: TabKind,
}

impl Tab {
    /// Whether this is an editor with unsaved changes.
    fn is_dirty(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(&self.kind, TabKind::Editor { state, .. } if state.is_dirty())
    }

    /// Saves an editor's unsaved changes (see [`orress_views::EditorState::save_interactive`]).
    /// `Ok(true)` for anything else.
    fn save(&mut self) -> Result<bool, String> {
        match &mut self.kind {
            TabKind::Editor { path, state } => state.save_interactive(path),
            _ => Ok(true),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Slot {
    Center,
    Left,
    Right,
    Bottom,
}

/// Things tab views need from the app, and requests they send back to it.
pub struct TabEnv<'a> {
    pub registry: &'a ActionRegistry,
    pub keymap: &'a Keymap,
    pub recent_files: &'a [PathBuf],
    /// The open project folder (Zed-style), shown as a tree at the top of the left dock. Set by
    /// the app after construction; `None` when no folder is open.
    pub project_root: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// Actions triggered from inside a view (e.g. a button on the welcome page).
    pub emitted: Vec<ActionId>,
    /// Files the user asked to open from inside a view.
    pub open_requests: Vec<PathBuf>,
    pub docs: &'a mut DocStore,
    /// Views of documents the user asked for from inside a view.
    pub view_requests: Vec<ViewRequest>,
    /// Cross-file go-to-definition targets from the editor.
    pub editor_nav: Vec<orress_views::GotoFile>,
    /// A save requested from the File menu, delivered to the focused editor tab.
    pub editor_save: Option<orress_views::SaveRequest>,
    pub academy: &'a mut orress_academy::Academy,
    pub workbench: &'a mut orress_views::Workbench,
    pub debugger: &'a mut orress_views::DebugSession,
    pub run_console: &'a mut orress_views::RunConsole,
    pub lsp: &'a mut orress_lsp::LspManager,
    pub terminal: &'a mut orress_views::TerminalSession,
    pub source_dbg: &'a mut orress_views::SourceDebug,
    pub emulator: &'a mut orress_views::EmulatorView,
    pub shellcode: &'a mut orress_views::ShellcodeView,
    pub triage: &'a mut orress_views::TriageView,
    pub yara: &'a mut orress_views::YaraView,
    pub wasm: &'a mut orress_views::WasmView,
    pub pyc: &'a mut orress_views::PycView,
    pub java: &'a mut orress_views::JavaView,
    pub archive: &'a mut orress_views::ArchiveView,
    pub resources: &'a mut orress_views::ResourcesView,
    pub exploit: &'a mut orress_views::ExploitView,
    pub heap: &'a mut orress_views::HeapView,
    pub gadgets: &'a mut orress_views::GadgetsView,
    pub js: &'a mut orress_views::JsView,
    pub dotnet: &'a mut orress_views::DotNetView,
    pub assistant: &'a mut orress_views::AssistantView,
    pub sandbox: &'a mut orress_views::SandboxView,
    pub collab: &'a mut orress_views::CollabView,
    pub diff: &'a mut orress_views::DiffView,
    pub script: &'a mut orress_views::ScriptView,
    pub challenge: &'a mut orress_views::ChallengeWorkbenchView,
    pub types: &'a mut orress_views::TypesView,
}
```
