```rs
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Workspace {
    center: DockState<Tab>,
    left: DockState<Tab>,
    right: DockState<Tab>,
    bottom: DockState<Tab>,
    pub left_open: bool,
    pub right_open: bool,
    pub bottom_open: bool,
    focused: Slot,
    next_id: u64,
    /// Commands waiting for the focused document view.
    #[serde(skip)]
    commands: Vec<ViewCommand>,
    /// An editor tab with unsaved changes the user asked to close: the app asks Save / Don't
    /// Save / Cancel, then calls [`Workspace::resolve_close`].
    #[serde(skip)]
    pending_close: Option<u64>,
}

impl Default for Workspace {
    fn default() -> Self {
        let mut next_id = 0;
        let mut tab = |kind| {
            next_id += 1;
            Tab { id: next_id, kind }
        };
        let new_dock = |tabs| {
            let mut dock = DockState::new(tabs);
            dock.set_focused_node_and_surface(NodePath {
                surface: SurfaceIndex::main(),
                node: NodeIndex::root(),
            });
            dock
        };
        let center = new_dock(vec![tab(TabKind::Welcome)]);
        let left = new_dock(vec![tab(TabKind::ProjectTree)]);
        let right = new_dock(vec![tab(TabKind::Explain), tab(TabKind::Inspector)]);
        let bottom = new_dock(vec![
            tab(TabKind::Xrefs),
            tab(TabKind::Terminal),
            tab(TabKind::Output),
            tab(TabKind::DebugSource),
            tab(TabKind::Problems),
        ]);
        Self {
            center,
            left,
            right,
            bottom,
            left_open: true,
            right_open: true,
            bottom_open: true,
            focused: Slot::Center,
            next_id,
            commands: Vec::new(),
            pending_close: None,
        }
    }
}

impl Workspace {
    fn dock(&mut self, slot: Slot) -> &mut DockState<Tab> {
        match slot {
            Slot::Center => &mut self.center,
            Slot::Left => &mut self.left,
            Slot::Right => &mut self.right,
            Slot::Bottom => &mut self.bottom,
        }
    }

    fn set_open(&mut self, slot: Slot, open: bool) {
        match slot {
            Slot::Center => {}
            Slot::Left => self.left_open = open,
            Slot::Right => self.right_open = open,
            Slot::Bottom => self.bottom_open = open,
        }
    }

    pub fn toggle(&mut self, slot: Slot) {
        let open = match slot {
            Slot::Center => return,
            Slot::Left => !self.left_open,
            Slot::Right => !self.right_open,
            Slot::Bottom => !self.bottom_open,
        };
        self.set_open(slot, open);
        if !open && self.focused == slot {
            self.focused = Slot::Center;
        }
    }

    /// Opens a tab, or focuses the existing one if this view is already open.
    pub fn open(&mut self, kind: TabKind) {
        for slot in [Slot::Center, Slot::Left, Slot::Right, Slot::Bottom] {
            let dock = self.dock(slot);
            if let Some(path) = dock.find_tab_from(|t| t.kind.same_view(&kind)) {
                let _ = dock.set_active_tab(path);
                dock.set_focused_node_and_surface(path.node_path());
                self.set_open(slot, true);
                self.focused = slot;
                return;
            }
        }
        let slot = kind.home();
        self.next_id += 1;
        let tab = Tab {
            id: self.next_id,
            kind,
        };
        let dock = self.dock(slot);
        dock.push_to_focused_leaf(tab);
        if let Some(path) = focused_leaf(dock) {
            dock.set_focused_node_and_surface(path);
        }
        self.set_open(slot, true);
        self.focused = slot;
    }

    /// Drop every file-backed tab (open documents and editor buffers) from all docks, so a
    /// restored session starts with no files loaded. The dock layout and non-file views are
    /// kept; if pruning empties the center, a fresh Welcome tab replaces them. Called once at
    /// startup, since open files are deliberately not persisted across launches.
    pub fn forget_open_files(&mut self) {
        // Retired tab kinds from older layouts go too.
        let is_file = |t: &mut Tab| {
            matches!(
                t.kind,
                TabKind::Doc { .. } | TabKind::Editor { .. } | TabKind::Jobs
            )
        };
        for dock in [
            &mut self.center,
            &mut self.left,
            &mut self.right,
            &mut self.bottom,
        ] {
            dock.retain_tabs(|t| !is_file(t));
        }
        if self.center.iter_all_tabs().next().is_none() {
            self.next_id += 1;
            let mut center = DockState::new(vec![Tab {
                id: self.next_id,
                kind: TabKind::Welcome,
            }]);
            center.set_focused_node_and_surface(NodePath {
                surface: SurfaceIndex::main(),
                node: NodeIndex::root(),
            });
            self.center = center;
        }
        self.focused = Slot::Center;
    }

    /// Closes the focused tab — unless it is an editor with unsaved changes, which is left open
    /// with a close prompt pending (see [`Workspace::close_prompt`]).
    pub fn close_active_tab(&mut self) {
        let dock = self.dock(self.focused);
        if let Some(leaf_path) = focused_leaf(dock)
            && let Ok(leaf) = dock.leaf(leaf_path)
            && let Some(tab) = leaf.tabs.get(leaf.active.0)
        {
            if tab.is_dirty() {
                self.pending_close = Some(tab.id);
                return;
            }
            let active = leaf.active;
            dock.remove_tab((leaf_path, active).into());
        }
    }

    /// The editor tab waiting for a Save / Don't Save / Cancel answer, with its title.
    pub fn close_prompt(&self) -> Option<(u64, String)> {
        let id = self.pending_close?;
        self.all_tabs()
            .find(|t| t.id == id)
            .map(|t| (id, t.kind.title()))
    }

    /// Applies the answer to a close prompt. Saving may show a file dialog (untitled buffers);
    /// cancelling that, or a failed save, keeps the tab open. Returns a save error to show.
    pub fn resolve_close(&mut self, id: u64, choice: CloseChoice) -> Option<String> {
        self.pending_close = None;
        let close = match choice {
            CloseChoice::Cancel => false,
            CloseChoice::Discard => true,
            CloseChoice::Save => match self.tab_mut(id).map(Tab::save) {
                Some(Ok(saved)) => saved,
                Some(Err(e)) => return Some(e),
                None => false,
            },
        };
        if close {
            self.remove_tab(id);
        }
        None
    }

    fn all_tabs(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Tab> {
        [&self.center, &self.left, &self.right, &self.bottom]
            .into_iter()
            .flat_map(|dock| dock.iter_all_tabs().map(|(_, t)| t))
    }

    fn all_tabs_mut(&mut self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &mut Tab> {
        [
            &mut self.center,
            &mut self.left,
            &mut self.right,
            &mut self.bottom,
        ]
        .into_iter()
        .flat_map(|dock| dock.iter_all_tabs_mut().map(|(_, t)| t))
    }

    fn tab_mut(&mut self, id: u64) -> Option<&mut Tab> {
        self.all_tabs_mut().find(|t| t.id == id)
    }

    fn remove_tab(&mut self, id: u64) {
        for slot in [Slot::Center, Slot::Left, Slot::Right, Slot::Bottom] {
            let dock = self.dock(slot);
            if let Some(path) = dock.find_tab_from(|t| t.id == id) {
                dock.remove_tab(path);
                return;
            }
        }
    }

    /// Titles of the editor tabs with unsaved changes.
    pub fn dirty_editors(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        self.all_tabs()
            .filter(|t| t.is_dirty())
            .map(|t| t.kind.title())
            .collect()
    }

    /// Saves every editor with unsaved changes (asking for a file name for untitled ones).
    /// `Ok(false)` when the user cancelled a file dialog; `Err` on the first failed save.
    pub fn save_all_editors(&mut self) -> Result<bool, String> {
        for tab in self.all_tabs_mut() {
            if tab.is_dirty() && !tab.save()? {
                return Ok(false);
            }
        }
        Ok(true)
    }

    /// Saves the open editor of `path`, if any, when it has unsaved changes (no dialog: it has a
    /// file). `Ok` also when no editor has the file open.
    pub fn save_editor(&mut self, path: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
        for tab in self.all_tabs_mut() {
            if let TabKind::Editor {
                path: Some(p),
                state,
            } = &mut tab.kind
                && p == path
                && state.is_dirty()
            {
                let mut p = Some(p.clone());
                return match state.save_interactive(&mut p) {
                    Ok(true) => Ok(()),
                    Ok(false) => Err("the save was cancelled".into()),
                    Err(e) => Err(e),
                };
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// The files open in editor tabs.
    pub fn editor_paths(&self) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
        self.all_tabs()
            .filter_map(|t| match &t.kind {
                TabKind::Editor { path: Some(p), .. } => Some(p.clone()),
                _ => None,
            })
            .collect()
    }

    /// Puts every dock back to its first-start layout. Work in progress survives: notes, code
    /// editors (with their unsaved buffers) and open file views move to the center area.
    pub fn reset_layout(&mut self) {
        let mut fresh = Workspace::default();
        let keep = |t: &mut Tab| {
            matches!(
                t.kind,
                TabKind::Notes { .. } | TabKind::Editor { .. } | TabKind::Doc { .. }
            )
        };
        let mut kept: Vec<Tab> = Vec::new();
        for dock in [
            &mut self.center,
            &mut self.left,
            &mut self.right,
            &mut self.bottom,
        ] {
            let paths: Vec<_> = dock
                .iter_all_tabs_mut()
                .filter_map(|(path, t)| keep(t).then_some(path))
                .collect();
            // Remove back to front, so earlier paths in the same leaf stay valid.
            for path in paths.into_iter().rev() {
                if let Some(tab) = dock.remove_tab(path) {
                    kept.push(tab);
                }
            }
        }
        // Tab ids must stay unique: renumber the kept tabs after both layouts' ids.
        fresh.next_id = fresh.next_id.max(self.next_id);
        for mut tab in kept.into_iter().rev() {
            fresh.next_id += 1;
            tab.id = fresh.next_id;
            fresh.center.push_to_focused_leaf(tab);
        }
        *self = fresh;
    }

    /// Splits the focused center pane and opens a fresh notes tab beside it.
    pub fn split_right(&mut self) {
        self.next_id += 1;
        let tab = Tab {
            id: self.next_id,
            kind: TabKind::Notes {
                text: String::new(),
            },
        };
        let node = focused_leaf(&self.center).map_or(NodeIndex::root(), |p| p.node);
        let surface = self.center.main_surface_mut();
        if surface.is_empty() {
            surface.push_to_first_leaf(tab);
        } else {
            surface.split_right(node, 0.5, vec![tab]);
        }
        self.focused = Slot::Center;
    }

    /// Key context of whatever has focus, used to pick key bindings.
    pub fn key_context(&mut self) -> KeyContext {
        self.active_tab()
            .map_or(KeyContext::Workspace, |tab| tab.kind.key_context())
    }

    /// Title of the focused tab, for the status bar.
    pub fn active_title(&mut self) -> Option<String> {
        self.active_tab().map(|tab| tab.kind.title())
    }

    /// Opens (or focuses) a view of a file.
    pub fn open_doc(&mut self, path: &Path, view: DocView) {
        self.open(TabKind::Doc {
            path: path.to_path_buf(),
            view,
            state: Box::default(),
        });
    }

    /// The file and view of the focused tab, if it is a document view.
    pub fn focused_doc(&mut self) -> Option<(PathBuf, DocView)> {
        match &self.active_tab()?.kind {
            TabKind::Doc { path, view, .. } => Some((path.clone(), *view)),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// Whether the decompiler panel has focus (it takes Find commands).
    pub fn decompiler_focused(&mut self) -> bool {
        self.active_tab()
            .is_some_and(|tab| matches!(tab.kind, TabKind::Decompiler))
    }

    /// The file view shown in the main (center) area, even when keyboard focus is in a
    /// dock such as the lesson panel.
    pub fn center_doc(&self) -> Option<(PathBuf, DocView)> {
        let leaf = self.center.leaf(focused_leaf(&self.center)?).ok()?;
        match &leaf.tabs.get(leaf.active.0)?.kind {
            TabKind::Doc { path, view, .. } => Some((path.clone(), *view)),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// Queues a command for the focused document view (delivered next frame).
    pub fn send(&mut self, command: ViewCommand) {
        self.commands.push(command);
    }

    /// Every file shown by some tab.
    pub fn doc_paths(&self) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
        [&self.center, &self.left, &self.right, &self.bottom]
            .into_iter()
            .flat_map(|dock| dock.iter_all_tabs())
            .filter_map(|(_, tab)| match &tab.kind {
                TabKind::Doc { path, .. } => Some(path.clone()),
                _ => None,
            })
            .collect()
    }

    /// Whether the focused tab is a code-editor buffer (so Save / Save As apply).
    pub fn active_is_editor(&mut self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            self.active_tab().map(|t| &t.kind),
            Some(TabKind::Editor { .. })
        )
    }

    fn active_tab(&mut self) -> Option<&Tab> {
        let slot = self.focused;
        let dock = self.dock(slot);
        let leaf = dock.leaf(focused_leaf(dock)?).ok()?;
        leaf.tabs.get(leaf.active.0)
    }

    pub fn show(&mut self, ui: &mut Ui, env: &mut TabEnv<'_>) {
        // The Challenge Workbench builds/submits main.rs from disk: save its editor buffer first.
        if let Some(path) = env.challenge.save_request() {
            let result = self.save_editor(&path);
            env.challenge.report_save(result);
        }
        let style = egui_dock::Style::from_egui(ui.style());
        let focused_tab = self.active_tab().map(|t| t.id);
        let mut viewer = views::Viewer {
            env,
            focused_tab,
            commands: std::mem::take(&mut self.commands),
            close_requests: Vec::new(),
        };
        let pressed_at = ui.input(|i| {
            i.pointer
                .any_pressed()
                .then(|| i.pointer.interact_pos())
                .flatten()
        });
        let mut clicked_slot = None;

        let mut dock_area = |ui: &mut Ui, slot: Slot, dock: &mut DockState<Tab>| {
            DockArea::new(dock)
                .id(Id::new(("orress::dock", slot as u8)))
                .style(style.clone())
                .show_leaf_collapse_buttons(false)
                .show_leaf_close_all_buttons(false)
                .show_inside(ui, &mut viewer);
            if pressed_at.is_some_and(|p| ui.min_rect().contains(p)) {
                clicked_slot = Some(slot);
            }
            let name = match slot {
                Slot::Center => "dock.center",
                Slot::Left => "dock.left",
                Slot::Right => "dock.right",
                Slot::Bottom => "dock.bottom",
            };
            orress_ui::spotlight::mark(ui.ctx(), name, ui.min_rect());
        };

        egui::Panel::left("orress::left_dock")
            .resizable(true)
            .default_size(240.0)
            .min_size(140.0)
            .show_collapsible(ui, &mut self.left_open, |ui| {
                dock_area(ui, Slot::Left, &mut self.left);
            });
        egui::Panel::right("orress::right_dock")
            .resizable(true)
            .default_size(440.0)
            .min_size(160.0)
            .show_collapsible(ui, &mut self.right_open, |ui| {
                dock_area(ui, Slot::Right, &mut self.right);
            });
        egui::Panel::bottom("orress::bottom_dock")
            .resizable(true)
            .default_size(200.0)
            .min_size(80.0)
            .show_collapsible(ui, &mut self.bottom_open, |ui| {
                dock_area(ui, Slot::Bottom, &mut self.bottom);
            });
        egui::CentralPanel::no_frame().show(ui, |ui| {
            dock_area(ui, Slot::Center, &mut self.center);
        });

        if let Some(slot) = clicked_slot {
            self.focused = slot;
        }
        // An editor with unsaved changes whose close button was clicked: ask first.
        if let Some(&id) = viewer.close_requests.first() {
            self.pending_close = Some(id);
        }
        // The inspector follows the last focused file.
        if let Some((path, _)) = self.focused_doc() {
            viewer.env.docs.active = Some(path);
        }
    }
}

/// The focused leaf, falling back to the main surface's last focused node: a fresh
/// `DockState` has no focused surface until the user clicks into it.
fn focused_leaf(dock: &DockState<Tab>) -> Option<NodePath> {
    dock.focused_leaf().or_else(|| {
        dock.main_surface().focused_leaf().map(|node| NodePath {
            surface: SurfaceIndex::main(),
            node,
        })
    })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn count(ws: &mut Workspace, slot: Slot) -> usize {
        ws.dock(slot).iter_all_tabs().count()
    }

    #[test]
    fn opening_singleton_twice_focuses_existing() {
        let mut ws = Workspace::default();
        ws.open(TabKind::Keybindings);
        ws.open(TabKind::Keybindings);
        assert_eq!(count(&mut ws, Slot::Center), 2); // Welcome + Keybindings
    }

    #[test]
    fn notes_can_open_many_times() {
        let mut ws = Workspace::default();
        ws.open(TabKind::Notes {
            text: String::new(),
        });
        ws.open(TabKind::Notes {
            text: String::new(),
        });
        assert_eq!(count(&mut ws, Slot::Center), 3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn opening_dock_view_opens_its_dock() {
        // Start with the bottom dock closed, so we can verify opening a bottom view reopens it.
        let mut ws = Workspace {
            bottom_open: false,
            ..Default::default()
        };
        assert!(!ws.bottom_open);
        ws.open(TabKind::Terminal);
        assert!(ws.bottom_open);
        assert_eq!(ws.key_context(), KeyContext::Terminal);
    }

    #[test]
    fn fresh_workspace_reports_welcome_as_active() {
        let mut ws = Workspace::default();
        assert_eq!(ws.active_title().as_deref(), Some("Welcome"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn forget_open_files_drops_documents_and_restores_welcome() {
        let mut ws = Workspace::default();
        // Simulate a restored session with files open (and the Welcome tab closed).
        ws.close_active_tab(); // close the default Welcome
        ws.open_doc(Path::new("crackme02.exe"), DocView::Disassembly);
        ws.open_doc(Path::new("crackme02.exe"), DocView::Info);
        assert!(count(&mut ws, Slot::Center) >= 2);

        ws.forget_open_files();

        // No document tabs survive, and the center falls back to a single Welcome tab.
        assert!(
            ws.dock(Slot::Center)
                .iter_all_tabs()
                .all(|(_, t)| !matches!(t.kind, TabKind::Doc { .. }))
        );
        assert_eq!(count(&mut ws, Slot::Center), 1);
        assert_eq!(ws.active_title().as_deref(), Some("Welcome"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn forget_open_files_keeps_non_file_layout() {
        let mut ws = Workspace::default();
        ws.open_doc(Path::new("a.bin"), DocView::Info);
        ws.forget_open_files();
        // The side/bottom docks (ProjectTree, Explain/Inspector, Terminal, …) are untouched.
        assert_eq!(count(&mut ws, Slot::Left), 1);
        assert_eq!(count(&mut ws, Slot::Right), 2);
        assert!(count(&mut ws, Slot::Bottom) >= 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn close_active_tab_removes_it() {
        let mut ws = Workspace::default();
        ws.open(TabKind::Keybindings);
        ws.close_active_tab();
        assert_eq!(count(&mut ws, Slot::Center), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn reset_layout_keeps_notes_and_restores_docks() {
        let mut ws = Workspace::default();
        ws.open(TabKind::Notes {
            text: "flag{keep me}".into(),
        });
        ws.toggle(Slot::Left);
        ws.open(TabKind::Keybindings);
        ws.reset_layout();
        assert!(ws.left_open);
        let notes: Vec<_> = ws
            .all_tabs()
            .filter_map(|t| match &t.kind {
                TabKind::Notes { text } => Some(text.clone()),
                _ => None,
            })
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(notes, vec!["flag{keep me}".to_string()]);
        // Keybindings is not work in progress, so it is not kept.
        assert!(
            !ws.all_tabs()
                .any(|t| matches!(t.kind, TabKind::Keybindings))
        );
        // Ids stay unique.
        let mut ids: Vec<u64> = ws.all_tabs().map(|t| t.id).collect();
        let n = ids.len();
        ids.sort_unstable();
        ids.dedup();
        assert_eq!(ids.len(), n);
    }

    #[test]
    fn retired_jobs_tab_is_dropped_from_old_layouts() {
        let mut ws = Workspace::default();
        ws.open(TabKind::Jobs);
        assert!(ws.all_tabs().any(|t| matches!(t.kind, TabKind::Jobs)));
        ws.forget_open_files();
        assert!(!ws.all_tabs().any(|t| matches!(t.kind, TabKind::Jobs)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn closing_a_clean_tab_needs_no_prompt() {
        let mut ws = Workspace::default();
        ws.open(TabKind::Editor {
            path: None,
            state: Box::default(),
        });
        // A buffer that was never shown has no unsaved changes.
        ws.close_active_tab();
        assert!(ws.close_prompt().is_none());
        assert!(ws.dirty_editors().is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn closing_a_dirty_editor_asks_first() {
        let mut ws = Workspace::default();
        ws.open(TabKind::Editor {
            path: None,
            state: Box::new(orress_views::EditorState::scratch(
                "solve.rs",
                "fn main() {}",
            )),
        });
        ws.close_active_tab();
        let (id, title) = ws.close_prompt().expect("a prompt for the unsaved buffer");
        assert!(title.contains("solve.rs"));
        assert_eq!(ws.dirty_editors().len(), 1);
        // Cancel keeps it; Discard closes it.
        assert!(ws.resolve_close(id, CloseChoice::Cancel).is_none());
        assert_eq!(ws.dirty_editors().len(), 1);
        assert!(ws.resolve_close(id, CloseChoice::Discard).is_none());
        assert!(ws.dirty_editors().is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn layout_serializes() {
        let mut ws = Workspace::default();
        ws.open(TabKind::Notes {
            text: "flag{?}".into(),
        });
        // eframe persists app state as RON, which (unlike JSON) keeps the infinite
        // rects egui_dock stores for tabs that were never drawn.
        let text = ron::to_string(&ws).unwrap();
        let back: Workspace = ron::from_str(&text).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(back.next_id, ws.next_id);
    }
}

```

`crates/orress-workspace/src/views.rs`:

```rs
//! What each tab draws.

use egui::{RichText, Ui, WidgetText};
use egui_dock::TabViewer;
use egui_dock::tab_viewer::OnCloseResponse;
use orress_actions::{ActionId, KeyContext};
use orress_ui::{ExplainExt as _, explain, kbd, muted};

use crate::{Tab, TabEnv, TabKind};

pub(crate) struct Viewer<'e, 'a> {
    pub env: &'e mut TabEnv<'a>,
    /// The focused tab, which receives `commands`.
    pub focused_tab: Option<u64>,
    pub commands: Vec<orress_views::ViewCommand>,
    /// Editor tabs with unsaved changes whose close button was clicked (kept open; the
    /// workspace asks Save / Don't Save / Cancel).
    pub close_requests: Vec<u64>,
}

impl TabViewer for Viewer<'_, '_> {
    type Tab = Tab;

    fn id(&mut self, tab: &mut Tab) -> egui::Id {
        egui::Id::new(("orress::tab", tab.id))
    }

    fn title(&mut self, tab: &mut Tab) -> WidgetText {
        tab.kind.title().into()
    }

    fn on_close(&mut self, tab: &mut Tab) -> OnCloseResponse {
        if tab.is_dirty() {
            self.close_requests.push(tab.id);
            OnCloseResponse::Focus
        } else {
            OnCloseResponse::Close
        }
    }

    fn ui(&mut self, ui: &mut Ui, tab: &mut Tab) {
        match &mut tab.kind {
            TabKind::Welcome => welcome(ui, self.env),
            TabKind::Academy => orress_academy::overview(ui, self.env.academy),
            TabKind::Lesson => orress_academy::lesson_panel(ui, self.env.academy),
            TabKind::Simulator => orress_academy::simulator(ui, self.env.academy),
            TabKind::Workbench => orress_views::workbench(ui, self.env.workbench, self.env.docs),
            TabKind::Keybindings => keybindings(ui, self.env),
            TabKind::Notes { text } => notes(ui, text),
            TabKind::Doc { path, view, state } => {
                orress_ui::spotlight::mark(
                    ui.ctx(),
                    &format!("view.{}", view.name()),
                    ui.max_rect(),
                );
                let commands = if self.focused_tab == Some(tab.id) {
                    std::mem::take(&mut self.commands)
                } else {
                    Vec::new()
                };
                let mut cx = orress_views::ViewCtx {
                    commands,
                    requests: &mut self.env.view_requests,
                    debugger: self.env.debugger,
                };
                orress_views::show(ui, self.env.docs, path, *view, state, &mut cx);
            }
            TabKind::ProjectTree => {
                // The project folder tree (if a folder is open) sits on top; the open-files list
                // with each file's analysis views stays below it.
                if let Some(root) = self.env.project_root.clone() {
                    orress_views::folder_tree(
                        ui,
                        &root,
                        self.env.docs,
                        &mut self.env.view_requests,
                    );
                    ui.separator();
                }
                orress_views::project_tree(ui, self.env.docs, &mut self.env.view_requests);
            }
            TabKind::Inspector => orress_views::inspector(ui, self.env.docs),
            TabKind::Types => orress_views::types_view(ui, self.env.types, self.env.docs),
            TabKind::Collaboration => orress_views::collab_panel(ui, self.env.collab),
            TabKind::Diff => orress_views::diff_panel(ui, self.env.diff, self.env.docs),
            TabKind::Script => orress_views::script_view(ui, self.env.script, self.env.docs),
            TabKind::Extensions => {
                orress_views::extensions_panel(ui, &mut self.env.view_requests);
            }
            TabKind::Editor { path, state } => {
                orress_ui::spotlight::mark(ui.ctx(), "view.Editor", ui.max_rect());
                // Only the focused editor acts on a File-menu save request.
                let save_cmd = if self.focused_tab == Some(tab.id) {
                    self.env.editor_save.take()
                } else {
                    None
                };
                let active_binary = self.env.docs.active_mut();
                orress_views::editor_view(
                    ui,
                    path,
                    state,
                    self.env.run_console,
                    self.env.lsp,
                    &mut self.env.editor_nav,
                    self.env.source_dbg,
                    save_cmd,
                    active_binary,
                );
            }
            TabKind::Xrefs => {
                orress_views::xrefs_panel(ui, self.env.docs, &mut self.env.view_requests);
            }
            TabKind::Explain => explain_panel(ui),
            TabKind::Decompiler => {
                orress_ui::spotlight::mark(ui.ctx(), "view.Decompiler", ui.max_rect());
                let commands = if self.focused_tab == Some(tab.id) {
                    std::mem::take(&mut self.commands)
                } else {
                    Vec::new()
                };
                orress_views::decompiler_panel(
                    ui,
                    self.env.docs,
                    &mut self.env.view_requests,
                    commands,
                );
            }
            TabKind::Debugger => {
                orress_ui::spotlight::mark(ui.ctx(), "view.Debugger", ui.max_rect());
                let doc = self.env.docs.active_mut();
                orress_views::debugger_panel(ui, self.env.debugger, doc);
            }
            TabKind::Emulator => {
                orress_views::emulator_view(ui, self.env.emulator, self.env.docs);
            }
            TabKind::Shellcode => {
                orress_views::shellcode_view(ui, self.env.shellcode);
            }
            TabKind::Triage => {
                orress_views::triage_view(ui, self.env.triage, self.env.docs);
            }
            TabKind::Yara => {
                orress_views::yara_view(ui, self.env.yara, self.env.docs);
            }
            TabKind::Wasm => {
                orress_views::wasm_view(ui, self.env.wasm, self.env.docs);
            }
            TabKind::Pyc => {
                orress_views::pyc_view(ui, self.env.pyc, self.env.docs);
            }
            TabKind::Java => {
                orress_views::java_view(ui, self.env.java, self.env.docs);
            }
            TabKind::Archive => {
                orress_views::archive_view(ui, self.env.archive, self.env.docs);
            }
            TabKind::Resources => {
                let root = self.env.project_root.clone();
                orress_views::resources_view(
                    ui,
                    self.env.resources,
                    self.env.docs,
                    root.as_deref(),
                    &mut self.env.view_requests,
                );
            }
            TabKind::Exploit => {
                orress_views::exploit_view(ui, self.env.exploit, self.env.docs);
            }
            TabKind::Heap => {
                orress_views::heap_view(ui, self.env.heap, self.env.debugger);
            }
            TabKind::Gadgets => {
                orress_views::gadgets_view(ui, self.env.gadgets, self.env.docs);
            }
            TabKind::Js => {
                orress_views::js_view(ui, self.env.js, self.env.docs);
            }
            TabKind::DotNet => {
                orress_views::dotnet_view(ui, self.env.dotnet, self.env.docs);
            }
            TabKind::Assistant => {
                orress_views::assistant_view(ui, self.env.assistant, self.env.docs);
            }
            TabKind::Sandbox => {
                orress_views::sandbox_view(ui, self.env.sandbox, self.env.docs);
            }
            TabKind::ChallengeWorkbench => {
                orress_views::challenge_workbench(
                    ui,
                    self.env.challenge,
                    &mut self.env.open_requests,
                    self.env.run_console,
                );
            }
            TabKind::Terminal => {
                orress_ui::spotlight::mark(ui.ctx(), "view.Terminal", ui.max_rect());
                let notify = {
                    let ctx = ui.ctx().clone();
                    std::sync::Arc::new(move || ctx.request_repaint())
                };
                orress_views::terminal_panel(ui, self.env.terminal, notify);
            }
            TabKind::Output => {
                orress_ui::spotlight::mark(ui.ctx(), "view.Output", ui.max_rect());
                orress_views::run_panel(ui, self.env.run_console);
            }
            TabKind::DebugSource => {
                orress_ui::spotlight::mark(ui.ctx(), "view.DebugSource", ui.max_rect());
                orress_views::source_debug_panel(ui, self.env.source_dbg);
            }
            TabKind::Problems => {
                orress_ui::spotlight::mark(ui.ctx(), "view.Problems", ui.max_rect());
                orress_views::problems_panel(ui, self.env.lsp);
            }
            // Retired; dropped from restored layouts at startup, so normally never drawn.
            TabKind::Jobs => {
                ui.label(muted("This tab is no longer used. Close it."));
            }
        }
    }

    fn scroll_bars(&self, tab: &Tab) -> [bool; 2] {
        // The hex view virtualizes its own scrolling.
        match tab.kind {
            TabKind::Doc { .. }
            | TabKind::Inspector
            | TabKind::Xrefs
            | TabKind::Decompiler
            | TabKind::Editor { .. }
            | TabKind::Academy
            | TabKind::Lesson
            | TabKind::Emulator
            | TabKind::Shellcode
            | TabKind::Triage
            | TabKind::Yara
            | TabKind::Wasm
            | TabKind::Pyc
            | TabKind::Java
            | TabKind::Archive
            | TabKind::Js
            | TabKind::DotNet
            | TabKind::Assistant
            | TabKind::Script
            | TabKind::Workbench => [false, false],
            _ => [true, true],
        }
    }
}

fn shortcut_label(ui: &Ui, env: &TabEnv<'_>, action: &str) -> Option<String> {
    env.keymap
        .keystroke_anywhere(&ActionId::from(action), KeyContext::Workspace)
        .map(|(k, ctx)| with_context(k.label(ui.ctx()), ctx))
}

/// A shortcut label, with the context it works in when that is not everywhere (e.g.
/// "Ctrl+Shift+C (Hex)").
fn with_context(label: String, ctx: KeyContext) -> String {
    match ctx {
        KeyContext::Global | KeyContext::Workspace => label,
        other => format!("{label} ({other:?})"),
    }
}

/// A button that emits an action, with its shortcut and explanation.
fn action_button(ui: &mut Ui, env: &mut TabEnv<'_>, action: &str, label: &str) {
    let id = ActionId::from(action);
    let explanation = env
        .registry
        .get(&id)
        .map(|a| a.explain.clone())
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let shortcut = shortcut_label(ui, env, action);
    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        if ui.button(label).explain(label, &explanation).clicked() {
            env.emitted.push(id);
        }
        if let Some(s) = shortcut {
            kbd(ui, &s);
        }
    });
}

fn welcome(ui: &mut Ui, env: &mut TabEnv<'_>) {
    // Inset the whole home screen so copy doesn't run flush to the panel edges.
    egui::Frame::NONE
        .inner_margin(egui::Margin::symmetric(36, 12))
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            ui.add_space(24.0);
            ui.vertical_centered(|ui| {
                // The logo as the centrepiece of the home screen (like Visual Studio's start page / Zed's
                // empty-pane logo). The texture is loaded at startup; fall back to a text wordmark.
                let logo = ui
                    .ctx()
                    .data(|d| d.get_temp::<egui::TextureHandle>(egui::Id::new("orress::logo")));
                if let Some(tex) = logo {
                    // Large enough that the wordmark and tagline in the logo read clearly; scales with the
                    // tab width on smaller windows.
                    let size = (ui.available_width() * 0.55).clamp(300.0, 460.0);
                    ui.image((tex.id(), egui::vec2(size, size)));
                    ui.add_space(6.0);
                } else {
                    ui.heading(RichText::new("ORRESS").size(34.0).strong());
                    ui.label(muted("Okiedocus Rusty Reverse Engineering Software Suite"));
                }
                ui.add_space(2.0);
                ui.label(muted(
                    "Reverse engineering for CTFs and malware analysis — and a place to learn it.",
                ));
            });
            ui.add_space(24.0);

            ui.columns(2, |cols| {
                let ui = &mut cols[0];
                ui.label(RichText::new("Start").strong().size(16.0));
                action_button(ui, env, "workspace::Open", "Open a file…");
                action_button(ui, env, "academy::Open", "Start the Academy");
                action_button(ui, env, "command_palette::Toggle", "Command palette");
                action_button(ui, env, "help::Keybindings", "All keyboard shortcuts");
                action_button(ui, env, "workspace::NewNotes", "New notes tab");

                ui.add_space(12.0);
                ui.label(RichText::new("Recent files").strong().size(16.0));
                if env.recent_files.is_empty() {
                    ui.label(muted("Nothing yet. Files you open show up here."));
                }
                for path in env.recent_files {
                    let name = path.file_name().map_or_else(
                        || path.display().to_string(),
                        |n| n.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
                    );
                    if ui
                        .link(name)
                        .on_hover_text(path.display().to_string())
                        .clicked()
                    {
                        env.open_requests.push(path.clone());
                    }
                }

                let ui = &mut cols[1];
                ui.label(
                    RichText::new("New to reverse engineering?")
                        .strong()
                        .size(16.0),
                );
                ui.label(
                    "Reverse engineering means figuring out how a program works when you only have \
             the program, not its source code. You read its machine code, run it under a \
             debugger, and rebuild its logic step by step.",
                );
                ui.add_space(6.0);
                ui.label(
            "In CTF competitions, \"reversing\" challenges hide a flag inside a program. In \
             malware analysis, you find out what a malicious program does so you can detect \
             and stop it.",
        );
                ui.add_space(6.0);
                ui.label(
                    "The Academy teaches all of it, from binary numbers to unpacking malware. \
             Explain Mode is on: hover over anything and the Explain panel on the right \
             tells you what it is.",
                );
            });
        });
}

fn keybindings(ui: &mut Ui, env: &mut TabEnv<'_>) {
    ui.heading("Keyboard shortcuts");
    ui.label(muted(
        "Every command in ORRESS. Change shortcuts in keymap.json (Help > Open Config Folder); \
         the format is the same as Zed's keymap.",
    ));
    ui.add_space(8.0);
    egui::Grid::new("orress::keybindings")
        .striped(true)
        .num_columns(3)
        .spacing([16.0, 6.0])
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            ui.label(RichText::new("Command").strong());
            ui.label(RichText::new("Shortcut").strong());
            ui.label(RichText::new("What it does").strong());
            ui.end_row();
            let mut actions: Vec<_> = env.registry.iter().collect();
            actions.sort_by(|a, b| a.id.cmp(&b.id));
            for action in actions {
                ui.label(&action.title)
                    .on_hover_text(RichText::new(action.id.as_str()).monospace());
                match env
                    .keymap
                    .keystroke_anywhere(&action.id, KeyContext::Workspace)
                {
                    Some((k, ctx)) => {
                        ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                            kbd(ui, &k.label(ui.ctx()));
                            if !matches!(ctx, KeyContext::Global | KeyContext::Workspace) {
                                ui.label(muted(format!("in {ctx:?}")));
                            }
                        });
                    }
                    None => {
                        ui.label(muted("—"));
                    }
                }
                ui.label(&action.explain);
                ui.end_row();
            }
        });
}

fn notes(ui: &mut Ui, text: &mut String) {
    ui.label(muted(
        "Write down what you find: addresses, ideas, the flag. In later versions notes link \
         to addresses and turn into your writeup.",
    ));
    ui.add(
        egui::TextEdit::multiline(text)
            .code_editor()
            .desired_width(f32::INFINITY)
            .desired_rows(24)
            .hint_text("# Notes\n\n- main is at 0x401000\n- input is compared with ..."),
    );
}

fn explain_panel(ui: &mut Ui) {
    // Prose wraps to the panel width; the scroll area keeps a long explanation readable in the
    // narrow dock (and gives a horizontal scrollbar for anything that can't wrap).
    let content_width = ui.available_width();
    egui::ScrollArea::both()
        .auto_shrink([false, false])
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            ui.set_max_width(content_width);
            match explain::last_explanation(ui.ctx()) {
                Some(e) => {
                    ui.heading(&e.title);
                    ui.add_space(4.0);
                    ui.label(&e.body);
                }
                None => {
                    ui.heading("Explain");
                    ui.label(
                        "Hover over a button, label or value and its explanation appears here. \
                     It stays until you hover over something else, so you can read it at \
                     your own pace.",
                    );
                }
            }
        });
}
```

`crates/orress/build.rs`:

```rs
//! Build script: on Windows, embed the ORRESS icon and version/product metadata into the
//! executable, so `orress.exe` shows the logo in Explorer and taskbar pins and carries proper
//! Details (version, product name, description). A no-op on other targets.

fn main() {
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=../../assets/icon.ico");
    if std::env::var("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_OS").as_deref() == Ok("windows") {
        #[cfg(windows)]
        {
            let mut res = winresource::WindowsResource::new();
            res.set_icon("../../assets/icon.ico");
            res.set("ProductName", "ORRESS");
            res.set(
                "FileDescription",
                "Okiedocus Rusty Reverse Engineering Software Suite",
            );
            res.set("CompanyName", "Okiedocus");
            res.set("LegalCopyright", "Licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0");
            // FileVersion / ProductVersion are filled from CARGO_PKG_VERSION automatically.
            if let Err(e) = res.compile() {
                println!("cargo:warning=could not embed Windows resources (icon/version): {e}");
            }
        }
    }
}
```

```rs
//! Every action the app knows, with a beginner-friendly explanation.

use orress_actions::{ActionRegistry, Keymap};
use orress_theme::Theme;

pub const DEFAULT_KEYMAP: &str = include_str!("../assets/default-keymap.json");

/// Prefix of the per-theme actions, e.g. `theme::Use(High Contrast)`.
pub const THEME_PREFIX: &str = "theme::Use(";

pub fn theme_action(name: &str) -> String {
    format!("{THEME_PREFIX}{name})")
}

pub fn theme_from_action(id: &str) -> Option<&str> {
    id.strip_prefix(THEME_PREFIX)?.strip_suffix(')')
}

pub fn default_keymap() -> Keymap {
    Keymap::from_json(DEFAULT_KEYMAP).expect("built-in keymap is valid")
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn default_keymap_only_uses_registered_actions() {
        let registry = registry(&Theme::built_in());
        // `null` bindings unbind a key in a context, so only real actions are checked.
        for binding in default_keymap().bindings() {
            if let Some(action) = binding.action.as_ref() {
                assert!(registry.contains(action), "unregistered action {action}");
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn theme_action_round_trip() {
        let id = theme_action("High Contrast");
        assert_eq!(theme_from_action(&id), Some("High Contrast"));
        assert_eq!(theme_from_action("theme::Next"), None);
    }
}
```
